The in vivo observation that the inhibited system becomes a transcriptional repressor is specific to this mechanism, since it requires a target-bound but nuclease-free complex.

title: A CRISPR evolutionary arms race: structural insights into viral anti-CRISPR/Cas responses.

This is also the paper behind the Ca(2+) sites in 5GNF, and it makes no claim about calcium anywhere in its text, which is the central evidence for the over-annotation call on GO:0046872.

Second, and more importantly, the paper itself declines to assign the catalytic centre, which is why the GO:0004521 row on this entry carries an explicit caveat.

review_notes: Automated Compara-based transfer from the C. elegans ortholog. Most transferred terms are appropriate, but some electronically propagated component terms (nucleolus, transcription repressor complex) over-reach relative to the established activator biology of CEP-1.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (InterPro2GO and related) annotations. Consistent with the p53-like DNA-binding domain (IPR008967, IPR012346); the generic DNA binding term is subsumed by the more specific sequence-specific DNA binding annotation.

title: Rapid coevolution of the nematode sex-determining genes fem-3 and tra-2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Haag, Wang, Kimble, Curr Biol 2002). Cached entry is abstract-only; abstract directly supports the conserved male-promoting function of C. briggsae fem-3 (IMP) and the species-specific FEM-3-TRA-2 interaction (IPI). Provides the experimental basis for the male sex-determination and TRA-2-binding annotations.

title: DNA binding and in vivo function of C.elegans PEB-1 require a conserved FLYWCH motif.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary research on PEB-1; the C. briggsae sequence is characterized here and the FLYWCH motif is shown to be required for DNA binding and in vivo function. Establishes the YDTGCCRW consensus and nuclear localization requirements. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false); quotes used are verbatim from the abstract.

title: Independent recruitment of F box genes to regulate hermaphrodite development during nematode evolution.
review_notes: Sole primary characterization of she-1 (Guo, Lang & Ellis, Curr. Biol. 2009). PMID is the reference cited by the UniProt entry (A8XDR5) for FUNCTION, DEVELOPMENTAL STAGE, DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE, and mutagenesis of Arg-49/Gly-111. Full text is not available in the local publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text is quoted and citation soundness is not independently verified here; claims are drawn from the UniProt summary and the published abstract.

title: The TRA-1 transcription factor binds TRA-2 to regulate sexual fates in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Establishes tra-1 as terminal regulator promoting female fates and reports the conserved MX-dependent TRA-1/TRA-2 physical interaction in both C. elegans and C. briggsae; directly supports the sex-determination and protein-interaction annotations for Cbr-tra-1.

title: RNA-Regulated TRA-1 nuclear export controls sexual fate.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows TRA-1 is a GLI-family TF required for female development with sex-specific nuclear distribution and CRM1-dependent nuclear export coupled to tra-2 3'UTR binding; supports the nucleus/cytoplasm localization annotations and the regulated-export mechanism.

title: Evolutionary change within a bipotential switch shaped the sperm/oocyte decision in hermaphroditic nematodes.
review_notes: Cited in the GO:0045944 annotation review as the source for TRA-1's context-dependent activating role on fog-3 (with the TRR-1/Tip60 HAT complex) in the sperm/oocyte decision. Added to references for traceability; full-text verification pending.

title: Proteolysis in Caenorhabditis elegans sex determination: cleavage of TRA-2A by TRA-3.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Establishes that the membrane protein TRA-2A is a substrate of the TRA-3 calpain-like protease and that cleavage generates a feminizing fragment; supports the IDA membrane localization. Work is in C. elegans but directly informs the conserved Cbr-TRA-2 biology.

title: The TRA-1 transcription factor binds TRA-2 to regulate sexual fates in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache, but explicitly reports an MX-dependent Cb-TRA-1/Cb-TRA-2 interaction in C. briggsae (no cross-species interaction), directly supporting the Cbr-specific TRA-1 binding and germline sex-determination (spermatogenesis) roles.

title: Rapid coevolution of the nematode sex-determining genes fem-3 and tra-2.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Directly addresses C. briggsae: FEM-3 interacts with TRA-2 in a strictly species-specific manner and the FEM-3-binding domain of TRA-2 is hypervariable and rapidly coevolving. Supports the FEM-3 sequestration/adaptor function and the comparative-evolution framing.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer of nuclear localization from the C. elegans ortholog G5EEV2; consistent with the UniProt-documented nuclear/condensed-chromosome localization of Cbr-TRR-1.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) inferences for the TRRAP/Tra1 family. The complex memberships (NuA4, SAGA), nuclear localization, and chromatin/transcription processes are all consistent with the well-characterized conserved scaffolding role of this family.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Keyword-to-GO mapping of the Nucleus subcellular location; redundant with but consistent with the IBA/ISS nucleus annotations.

title: Evolutionary change within a bipotential switch shaped the sperm/oocyte decision in hermaphroditic nematodes.
review_notes: Primary functional study for Cbr-trr-1 (Guo, Chen & Ellis, PLoS Genet 2013). Shows trr-1 acts through TRA-1 and the Tip60 HAT complex to activate fog-3 and control the germline sperm/oocyte fate decision; reduced trr-1 gives a feminized (Fog) germ line, and the gene is required for spermatogenesis and embryonic development. Full text is available in the local publications cache (content_type: full_text_pdf); the verbatim finding above is quoted directly from it.

title: Genome sequence of the nematode C. elegans: a platform for investigating biology
review_notes: This is the C. elegans genome sequencing paper; it is the source of the genomic DNA sequence for the mcm-4 locus (Y39G10AR.14) but does not provide functional characterization.

title: Alternative splicing directs dual localization of Candida albicans 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase to cytosol and peroxisomes.
review_notes: Primary C. albicans study behind the IDA cytosol and peroxisome annotations; abstract-only in the cache, so the enzyme-assay details reported by the deep-research summary (6PG + NADP+, 340 nm) could not be quoted directly.

title: Null mutants of Candida albicans for cell-wall-related genes form fragile biofilms that display an almost identical extracellular matrix proteome.
review_notes: Supports only the context-dependent biofilm-matrix detection; abstract-only in the cache.

title: The Pentose Phosphate Pathway in Yeasts-More Than a Poor Cousin of Glycolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biomolecules 2021, doi 10.3390/biom11050725); corroborates the dual localization and the fraction in peroxisomes.

title: 6-Phosphogluconate dehydrogenase and its crystal structures.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Acta Cryst F 2022, doi 10.1107/S2053230X22001091); source of the cofactor-specificity determinants tested in the bioinformatics check. Not C. albicans-specific.

title: A response to iron involving carbon metabolism in the opportunistic fungal pathogen Candida albicans.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis investigation - LPL1 monoacylglycerol lipase activity

title: Gpa2, a G-protein alpha subunit required for hyphal development in Candida albicans.

title: The cAMP phosphodiesterase encoded by CaPDE2 is required for hyphal development in Candida albicans.

title: Gpr1, a putative G-protein-coupled receptor, regulates morphogenesis and hypha formation in the pathogenic fungus Candida albicans.
review_notes: Places Gpr1/Gpa2 upstream of glucose-induced cAMP; contested by PMID:15673611. Relevant to whether the glucose-activated GPCR pathway IBA (GO:0110034) applies to C. albicans Pde1.

title: Carbon source induced yeast-to-hypha transition in Candida albicans is dependent on the presence of amino acids and on the G-protein-coupled receptor Gpr1.
review_notes: Short Biochem Soc Trans report; supports ligand ambiguity of CaGpr1, bearing on the glucose-activated qualifier of GO:0110034.

title: The G protein-coupled receptor Gpr1 and the Galpha protein Gpa2 act through the cAMP-protein kinase A pathway to induce morphogenesis in Candida albicans.
review_notes: Key evidence that the C. albicans Gpr1/Gpa2 module is not the glucose-induced cAMP route; bears on GO:0110034.

title: Farnesol and dodecanol effects on the Candida albicans Ras1-cAMP signalling pathway and the regulation of morphogenesis.
review_notes: Shows Pde1 is not required for farnesol/dodecanol repression of hyphal growth.

title: Candida albicans Pde1p and Gpa2p comprise a regulatory module mediating agonist-induced cAMP signalling and environmental adaptation.
review_notes: Key in vivo study: Pde1 terminates glucose/acidification-induced cAMP signalling; synthetic morphogenesis/stress phenotypes with GPA2. Abstract only cached.

title: Multiple roles and diverse regulation of the Ras/cAMP/protein kinase A pathway in Candida albicans.
review_notes: Review placing Pde1 among the core Ras/cAMP/PKA pathway components.

title: Sugar Sensing and Signaling in Candida albicans and Candida glabrata.
review_notes: Review summarising divergence of the C. albicans Gpr1/Gpa2 module from the S. cerevisiae glucose-sensing GPCR.

title: A Candida albicans cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase: cloning and expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and biochemical characterization of the recombinant enzyme.
review_notes: Original cloning and biochemical characterisation of C. albicans Pde1; supports cAMP/cGMP hydrolysis (IDA) and complementation (IGI). Abstract only cached.

title: The PDE1-encoded low-affinity phosphodiesterase in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae has a specific function in controlling agonist-induced cAMP signaling.
review_notes: S. cerevisiae ortholog: Pde1 specifically controls glucose/acidification-induced cAMP; notes conserved PKA site in C. albicans Pde1.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis run: PDE1 and the glucose-activated GPCR pathway (GO:0110034)
review_notes: Independent run given competing references (PMID:20558315, 15302825, 15673611) without the prior verdict. Its conclusion matches the cached primary abstracts. Two errors: it names S. cerevisiae as the source of the IBA (the PAINT donor is S. pombe cgs2), and it calls PMID:15302825 superseded rather than disputed.

title: UniProt entry P49822 (ALBU_CANLF), Serum albumin / Can f 3
review_notes: Curated UniProt record (function largely by similarity to human/bovine albumin); source for the fatty-acid/metal-ion carrier and enterobactin-binding core functions.

title: Structural and ligand binding analysis of the pet allergens Can f 1 and Fel d 7.
review_notes: PMC full text; primary structural/biophysical characterization of Can f 1 (and Fel d 7) fatty-acid binding.

title: UniProt entry O18873 (Major allergen Can f 1), Canis lupus familiaris
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; supports secreted lipocalin classification. Specific ligand/role recorded as a knowledge gap.

title: UniProt entry O18874 (Minor allergen Can f 2), Canis lupus familiaris
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; supports secreted odorant-binding lipocalin classification.

title: Characterization of the dog lipocalin allergen Can f 6: the role in cross-reactivity with cat and horse.
review_notes: Primary characterization of Can f 6 as a cross-reactive lipocalin allergen; supports secreted localization and the cross-reactive-lipocalin grouping.

title: Dog saliva - an important source of dog allergens.
review_notes: Supports the secreted/salivary (extracellular) localization of Can f 6.

title: Early evolution of the T-box transcription factor family.
review_notes: Full text cached (PMC3791752). The primary CoBra paper: phylogeny, Xenopus rescue and overexpression, XBra/CoBra chimeras and universal PBM. All functional assays except the PBM are heterologous (Xenopus). No locus ID is given for CoBra; the mapping to A0A0D2VUC6 is our inference.

title: The Dynamic Regulatory Genome of Capsaspora and the Origin of Animal Multicellularity.
review_notes: Full text cached. Provides the only in vivo evidence for CoBra: Bra-motif regulatory sites from ATAC-seq, their stage association and histone marks, and ChIP-qPCR with an anti-CoBra antibody at 20 sites. The target network is inferred from motifs, not from loss of function.

title: Which Capsaspora T-box protein is Brachyury (CoBra)?
review_notes: Our own reproducible analysis (tbox_assign.py). Assigns A0A0D2VUC6 as CoBra from T-box domain similarity and the arginine at the Xenopus Bra K149 position. Not a phylogeny, so the assignment is an inference.

title: Structural insight into dimeric interaction of the SARAH domains from Mst1 and RASSF family proteins in the apoptosis pathway.
review_notes: Human MST1 SARAH structure; used to evaluate the tetramerization IEA. Shows homodimer and 1:1 heterodimer formation, not tetramers, for the MST SARAH domain.

title: Premetazoan origin of the hippo signaling pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached. Capsaspora Hpo cDNA was tested heterologously: in Drosophila S2R+ cells it induced phosphorylation of Co-Yki, Dm-Wts T1077 and Dm-Yki S168, and GMR-driven overexpression gave a small-eye phenotype with increased endogenous Yki phosphorylation. Overexpression in a heterologous host; shows capacity, not endogenous function.

title: Structural basis of the heterodimerization of the MST and RASSF SARAH domains in the Hippo signalling pathway.
review_notes: Crystal structures of MST1-RASSF5 SARAH heterodimer and MST2 SARAH homodimer; corroborates dimeric (not tetrameric) SARAH assembly.

title: Genome editing in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki suggests a premetazoan role for the Hippo pathway in multicellular morphogenesis.
review_notes: coYki knockout paper that established Capsaspora gene disruption; mentions coHpo only in summarizing the 2012 heterologous data.

title: The Hippo kinase cascade regulates a contractile cell behavior and cell density in a close unicellular relative of animals.
review_notes: Primary loss-of-function study; full text cached. Names the targeted gene as CAOG_01932 and states that only one of three predicted isoforms carries the SARAH domain. Reports coHpo-/- phenotypes on coYki localization, proliferation, cell shape/contractility, aggregate morphology and cell packing, plus rescue and RNA-seq. No biochemical kinase assay or coHpo localization.

title: Assembling a Hippo: the evolutionary emergence of an animal developmental signaling pathway.
review_notes: Review; context on SARAH-domain retention in Hippo kinases outside fungi and on coHpo/coWts knockout phenotypes. No new data.

title: Integrin-mediated adhesion in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki
review_notes: bioRxiv preprint (February 2020) of PMID:32857975, full text cached from the PDF. Its methods identify the antigen as integrin beta 2, CAOG_05058, which matches A0A0D2WRB3. It describes the two antibodies (stalk and beta-I domain), the substrate-coating assays and the blocking result, and states that Capsaspora has no fibronectin ortholog. Being a preprint, details may differ from the published version.

title: Ancient origin of the integrin-mediated adhesion and signaling machinery.
review_notes: Full text cached. Deposited the four Capsaspora integrin beta cDNAs (GenBank GU320672-GU320675); GU320673 is "integrin beta 2 mRNA, complete cds", and its translation D7PE19 is identical in sequence to A0A0D2WRB3 (checked 2026-10-01). Reports conservation of the MIDAS/ADMIDAS/LIMBS sites, the expanded stalk, and the cytoplasmic alpha-interacting and NPXY motifs in beta 1-3.

title: Integrin-Mediated Adhesion in the Unicellular Holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki.
review_notes: Primary functional paper; only the abstract is cached. The abstract states the filopodial localization of integrin beta 2 and vinculin, the fibronectin effect and antibody inhibition of adhesion. The mapping of "integrin beta 2" to CAOG_05058 comes from the methods of the cached bioRxiv preprint of the same study (DOI:10.1101/2020.02.27.967653).

title: Genome editing in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki suggests a premetazoan role for the Hippo pathway in multicellular morphogenesis.
review_notes: coYki knockout paper (full text cached). Mentions CAOG_05058 only as an up-regulated integrin-beta gene in coYki knockout cells, which have increased substrate adhesion.

title: Integrin-mediated adhesion in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki
review_notes: bioRxiv preprint (full text cached) of the Curr Biol paper PMID:32857975, same authors and title. The only source of experimental data on coVIN. Its methods identify the vinculin antigen as CAOG_05123 residues 335-834, which matches A0A0D2WSN3 (CAOG_005123, 834 aa). Shows localisation only; no vinculin perturbation or binding data. Not peer reviewed; the published version may differ in detail.

title: Ancient origin of the integrin-mediated adhesion and signaling machinery.
review_notes: Comparative genomics of the integrin adhesome, including Capsaspora. Establishes that vinculin predates animals; argues that the scaffolds predate integrins and were co-opted. No functional data on coVIN.

title: Analysis of a vinculin homolog in a sponge (phylum Porifera) reveals that vertebrate-like cell adhesions emerged early in animal evolution.
review_notes: Sponge (Oscarella pearsei) vinculin biochemistry and structure. Used as comparative context for the predicted activities of coVIN; it contains no Capsaspora data.

title: Integrin-Mediated Adhesion in the Unicellular Holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki.
review_notes: Published version (Curr Biol 2020); cached abstract only. The abstract states the vinculin localisation; experimental details were taken from the preprint DOI:10.1101/2020.02.27.967653.

title: Premetazoan origin of the hippo signaling pathway.
review_notes: Identifies the Capsaspora Hippo pathway components including a Wts homolog and tests Co-Yki, Co-Sd and Co-Hpo in Drosophila. Capsaspora Wts was aligned but not functionally tested; Co-Hpo phosphorylated Drosophila Wts.

title: Genome editing in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki suggests a premetazoan role for the Hippo pathway in multicellular morphogenesis.
review_notes: coYki knockout paper; establishes that coYki with its predicted Warts sites mutated (4SA) is nuclear, the basis for inferring coWts substrate and mechanism. coWts itself is not studied.

title: The Hippo kinase cascade regulates a contractile cell behavior and cell density in a close unicellular relative of animals.
review_notes: Primary paper for coWts; full text cached. Methods name the targeted gene as coWts (CAOG_00619); NCBI RefSeq XP_004365490.1 carries locus_tag CAOG_00619 and is cross-referenced by UniProt A0A0D2VGR4 (new tag CAOG_000619). Reports knockout, coYki localization, proliferation, cell morphology, aggregate and RNA-seq data. No biochemical kinase or phosphorylation measurements.

title: Assembling a Hippo: the evolutionary emergence of an animal developmental signaling pathway.
review_notes: Review; summarizes the coWts knockout phenotypes without new data.

title: Premetazoan origin of the hippo signaling pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached. Identifies Co-Yki and tests it in Drosophila: eye overexpression with Co-Sd, co-IP and HRE-luciferase in S2R+ cells, and phosphorylation by Co-Hpo. Its claims of growth-promoting activity rest on fly tissue and were not borne out in Capsaspora (PMID:35659869).

title: Regulated aggregative multicellularity in a close unicellular relative of metazoa.
review_notes: Describes the aggregative stage of Capsaspora, the biological context of the coYki aggregate phenotypes. Does not mention coYki or the Hippo pathway.

title: Genome editing in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki suggests a premetazoan role for the Hippo pathway in multicellular morphogenesis.
review_notes: Primary coYki paper; full text cached. The key resources table identifies coYki as GenBank CAOG_07866, which matches the UniProt ORF name CAOG_007866 (A0A0D2WY30). Reports the knockout, rescue, localization, blebbistatin and RNA-seq data.

title: The Hippo kinase cascade regulates a contractile cell behavior and cell density in a close unicellular relative of animals.
review_notes: Full text cached. Shows that coHpo and coWts control coYki localization in Capsaspora. Uses a hyperactive coYki 4SA transgene and a TEAD-interface (F123A) mutant. The residue numbering differs from the UniProt model (see suggested questions).

title: Assembling a Hippo: the evolutionary emergence of an animal developmental signaling pathway.
review_notes: Review by the same group. Summarizes the coYki domain conservation (TEAD-binding helices, four HXRXXS motifs) and the Capsaspora findings. Adds no primary data.

title: TreeGrafter-generated GO annotations
review_notes: Source of the GO:0046933 ATP synthase row, via PANTHER:PTN000390110. review_notes: Ortholog (Salmonella); full text in the cache.

review_notes: Correctly identifies P0CAT8 as the flagellar export ATPase and notes that no direct P0CAT8 biochemistry exists. Primary papers were cited instead wherever possible.

title: Induction of a novel chicken Toll-like receptor following Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium infection.
review_notes: Full text read. First description of the receptor; used here only for the phylogenetic placement near, but not within, the TLR1/TLR2/TLR6/TLR10 clade. Its infection data are transcript-level and are not used to support any annotation.

title: Cleavage and activation of a Toll-like receptor by microbial proteases.
review_notes: Full text read. The definitive functional study of this receptor: protease-dependent activation, ectodomain cleavage, constitutive activity of the truncated receptor, cell-surface localisation, and the negative controls excluding the classical TLR ligands including acylated lipopeptides.

title: TLR15 is unique to avian and reptilian lineages and recognizes a yeast-derived agonist.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the lineage restriction, the yeast-lysate response, the failure of other agonists and the abolition of activity by heat or PMSF are all stated there. Independent support for the protease-activation model.

title: Activation of ChTLR15/ChNF-κB-ChNLRP3/ChIL-1β signaling transduction pathway mediated inflammatory responses to E. tenella infection.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the gain- and loss-of-function result in DF-1 cells and the cecal expression time course are both stated there. title: Uncovering a 500 million year old history and evidence of pseudogenization for TLR15.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. Shows that the gene is an ancient jawed-vertebrate lineage with orthologues in lungfish and holocephalan cartilaginous fish, that it forms a distinct subfamily most closely related to but outside the TLR1 subfamily, and that its ectodomain has a single-domain rather than the TLR1-family three-domain architecture. Used to correct the description and to strengthen the removal of the TLR2-derived ligand annotation.

title: Structural analysis of the Toll-like receptor 15 TIR domain.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. Crystal structures of the cytoplasmic TIR domain as a dimer, with mutational mapping of the interface and a structure-based argument that the adaptor is MyD88. Used for the signalling-complex row and the pathway row.

title: Eimeria tenella aspartyl protease is identified as a potential TLR15 ligand and activates macrophages and dendritic cells in chickens.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. The candidate ligand is a parasite aspartyl protease recovered by co-immunoprecipitation, and the authors state that the receptor's definitive role needs further work, so it is cited as consistent with the protease-activation mechanism and not as evidence of pattern binding or of a defence-response annotation.

title: Falcon deep research report on chicken TLR15
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis, read during the cross-check. Its own conclusion that protease sensing is the best-supported molecular function agrees with the deliberate decision here not to upgrade to pattern recognition receptor activity; every substantive claim taken from it was verified in the primary paper before use.

title: Chicken TLR21 acts as a functional homologue to mammalian TLR9 in the recognition of CpG oligodeoxynucleotides.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Independent demonstration of the CpG response, with chicken TLR7 and TLR15 as negative controls, plus the ER localisation of the resting receptor and the RNA interference result in HD11 macrophages.

title: Chicken TLR21 is an innate CpG DNA receptor distinct from mammalian TLR9.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the CpG-DNA response, the knockdown in chicken macrophages, the response to bacterial genomic DNA, the shared localisation with human TLR9 and the chloroquine sensitivity are all stated there. Also the clearest statement that the resemblance to TLR9 is functional rather than orthologous.

title: Toll-like receptor 9 and 21 have different ligand recognition profiles and cooperatively mediate activity of CpG-oligodeoxynucleotides in zebrafish.
review_notes: Full text read. Concerns the zebrafish orthologue, cited here only for the comparative point that TLR21 is the CpG receptor across non-mammalian vertebrates while being phylogenetically distant from TLR9.

title: Mechanisms of type I interferon production by chicken TLR21.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; fetched during the deep-research cross-check after the Falcon report cited its preprint. The claims used here are all in the abstract, namely NF-kappa-B activation and a type I interferon response in chicken macrophages, and interferon-beta transcription dependent on NF-kappa-B and IRF7 but not on TBK1. Basis for the proposed GO:0032728 annotation.

title: Falcon deep research report on chicken TLR21
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis, read during the cross-check. Cited only for the review-level consensus that the receptor is endosomal, which agrees with the primary localisation work; its substantive new content, the type I interferon mechanism, was verified in the published paper (PMID:37951324) before use, and the report cites only that paper's preprint.

title: A voltage-dependent chloride channel fine-tunes photosynthesis in plants.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Source of the experimental grounding behind the IBA chloride-channel and light reaction annotations; about the Arabidopsis homolog, not BST1.

title: A Spatial Interactome Reveals the Protein Organization of the Algal CO(2)-Concentrating Mechanism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Affinity-purification/MS interactome that first linked Cre16.g662600 to LCIB/LCIC and the other BST paralogs. Interaction data only; no functional assay of BST1.

title: Thylakoid localized bestrophin-like proteins are essential for the CO(2) concentrating mechanism of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified (PMC6708349); full text cached. The only primary functional study of BST1-3. Provides localization (Venus fusion under PSAD promoter, i.e. overexpression), CIA5-dependent induction, triple-RNAi physiology and homology modelling. No direct transport or electrophysiology assay was performed; the bicarbonate-channel role is an explicit proposal.

title: Transportation for fuel: Thylakoid membrane bestrophin channels facilitate HCO3- transport to the pyrenoid in diatoms.
review_notes: PubMed-verified commentary on PMID:38478576. It describes BST1-3 as "the main HCO3− transporters", which overstates the primary evidence (no direct transport measured). Not used as evidence.

title: Low-CO2-inducible bestrophins outside the pyrenoid sustain high photosynthetic efficacy in diatoms.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Independent genetic evidence in a diatom for the thylakoid-bestrophin CCM model; no direct transport assay; not about BST1 itself.

title: Toll-like receptor 9 and 21 have different ligand recognition profiles and cooperatively mediate activity of CpG-oligodeoxynucleotides in zebrafish.
review_notes: Full text read. The primary functional characterisation of this receptor: CpG motif preference, ectodomain determinants, TIR box 2 requirement, UNC93B1 binding and regulation, endoplasmic reticulum localisation, chloroquine sensitivity, and the in vivo cytokine and antibacterial effects. Supports every substantive call in this review.

title: Falcon deep research report on zebrafish tlr21
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis, read during the cross-check. It reaches the same conclusion as this review about the EC:3.2.2.6 annotation being an error and about the receptor being intracellular and CpG-specific, and it is cited only for that concurrence; the REMOVE argument itself rests on the UniProt family statement and the functional literature.

title: Innate immune gene expression in individual zebrafish after Listonella anguillarum inoculation.

The abstract confirms that this transcript was among those measured after bacterial inoculation but does not report its behaviour, and the genes it highlights as induced are others. This is why the GO:0009617 row is left UNDECIDED: the citation is plausible and may be supported by the figures, but it cannot be confirmed from what is cached.

title: Teleost TLR22 recognizes RNA duplex to induce IFN and protect cells from birnaviruses.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. The only functional characterisation of a TLR22 protein: in fugu, long double-stranded RNA recognised at the cell surface, TICAM-1-dependent interferon induction and protection against dsRNA viruses. Cited here for context and to frame the experiments proposed; deliberately not used to support any annotation, because it concerns a different species.

title: Positive selection pressure within teleost Toll-like receptors tlr21 and tlr22 subfamilies and their response to temperature stress and microbial components in zebrafish.

title: Toll-like receptor 9 and 21 have different ligand recognition profiles and cooperatively mediate activity of CpG-oligodeoxynucleotides in zebrafish.
review_notes: Full text read. About zebrafish tlr9 and tlr21; used here for the phylogenetic placement of tlr22 beside tlr21, tlr5b and tlr3, and for the observation that poly(I:C), which the authors describe as the TLR3 and TLR22 ligand, does not activate tlr21.

title: Falcon deep research report on zebrafish tlr22
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis, read during the cross-check. Cited for its explicit statement that the zebrafish protein has never been tested for ligand binding and that its localisation and adaptor use are unestablished, which is the basis of the conservative stance taken here; it adds no zebrafish-specific experiment beyond the papers already cited.

title: Structural basis of TLR5-flagellin recognition and signaling.
review_notes: Full text read. The crystallised receptor is the zebrafish protein: only the zebrafish ectodomain expressed in soluble form, and the 2018 paper identifies that crystallised fragment as TLR5b. This is direct structural evidence for flagellin binding by this gene product, although the paper's framing is about human TLR5, for which the structure served as a surrogate.

title: Common and specific downstream signaling targets controlled by Tlr2 and Tlr5 innate immune signaling in zebrafish.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. In vivo morpholino evidence that this gene is required for the flagellin-induced transcriptional response of zebrafish embryos, with the useful detail that knockdown of this paralogue alone gives a partial block and knockdown of both paralogues a complete one. Used as additional support for the proposed pathway term.

title: Duplicated TLR5 of zebrafish functions as a heterodimeric receptor.
review_notes: Full text read. Establishes the obligate heterodimer, the failure of either paralogue to signal as a homodimer, the UNC93B1 effect and the species-specificity of the flagellin contact site. The primary source for this gene's function.

title: Fish TLR5 develops a taste for viral RNA.
review_notes: Full text read. A commentary, not primary research, and about grass carp rather than zebrafish. Reports that teleost TLR5b homodimers can respond to double-stranded RNA and signal to interferon-stimulated response elements. Recorded as a question and a proposed experiment; no annotation rests on it.

GRs lack the analogous common ORCO coreceptor; ORCO absence is not a negative for GR channel plausibility.

title: Deep research review of DpuGr29 gustatory receptor
review_notes: Read fully. Correctly resolves identity, the Daphnia-specific expansion and lack of target electrophysiology/tissue mapping. Antennular/feeding-appendage expression is a hypothesis, not a measured target location.

title: OpenScientist focused assessment of DpuGr29 courtship and ligand-gated channel function
review_notes: Complete report, both CSVs and HTML/PDF variants read. Retains useful BmGr9 mechanism and motif lead but rejects courtship from missing target assays and donor species without inspecting topology. Actual target descent supports retention. Mislabels FBgn0032416, calls the donor support one study, double-counts preprint PMID:38187590 and final PMID:38573859, and conflates ORCO absence with GR subunit uncertainty. Corrections and remaining limits are independently documented in DpuGr29-report-assessment.md.

title: Genetic interactions of the E3 ubiquitin ligase component FbxA with cyclic AMP metabolism and a histidine kinase signaling pathway during Dictyostelium discoideum development.
review_notes: Solid genetic evidence linking dhkA to RegA/cAMP and sporulation. The authors' proposed directionality (that DhkA activates RegA phosphodiesterase) explicitly contradicts Wang et al. (PMID:10373524 / PMID:15897458), who show ligand binding to DhkA inhibits phosphorelay to RegA; the direction of DhkA-RegA regulation is therefore contested. Hand-curated expert assessment - the Wang/Anjard-Loomis inhibition model is the better-supported working model. DhkA autophosphorylation on His1395 and phosphorelay through RdeA to the RegA receiver aspartate are biochemically demonstrated, and SDF-2 binding lowers this relay so RegA is dephosphorylated and inactivated, raising intracellular cAMP and activating PKA to trigger encapsulation. The fbxA genetic-interaction study reported here infers the opposite direction only indirectly, so it is recorded as a contested minority interpretation pending direct measurement of the RegA phosphorylation state in dhkA-null versus SDF-2-treated cells.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment analysis of the IplA IP3-gated channel hypothesis
review_notes: Independent OpenScientist function-assignment run (3 iterations). Verdict PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The IP3R/RyR-superfamily intracellular Ca2+-release channel identity is well supported (RIH domain, IP3-receptor-binding-core armadillo fold, six-TM pore; single-copy in the genome, so no paralog confusion). The specific IP3-GATED molecular function is NOT directly supported - the metazoan MIR domain is absent, 0 of 9 canonical IP3-coordinating residues map, no primary study demonstrates IP3 binding or IP3-gated conductance, and the literature hedges ("putative"), with a competing Ca2+-sensing interpretation. Directly corroborates this review's MODIFY of GO:0005220 (IP3-gated channel) to the generic GO:0005262 (calcium channel activity). Best-supported MF is a generalized calcium channel term pending direct IP3-binding data.

title: The internal phosphodiesterase RegA is essential for the suppression of lateral pseudopods during Dictyostelium chemotaxis.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports the chemotaxis/pseudopod and cortical myosin localization annotations.

title: Identification and characterization of two unusual cGMP-stimulated phoshodiesterases in dictyostelium.
review_notes: Retrieved using the publication fetcher and inspected the primary full-text cache. Distinguishes substrate-selectivity estimates from demonstration of physiological cGMP turnover.

title: Genetic interactions of the E3 ubiquitin ligase component FbxA with cyclic AMP metabolism and a histidine kinase signaling pathway during Dictyostelium discoideum development.
review_notes: Supports RegA's developmental (sporulation/culmination) role via suppressor genetics linked to cAMP metabolism.

title: Adenylyl cyclase G is activated by an intramolecular osmosensor.
review_notes: Primarily about ACG, but the introduction traces RegA's role in the osmotic-stress cAMP response, supporting the osmotic-stress annotation.

title: cAMP controls cytosolic Ca2+ levels in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Links RegA-controlled intracellular cAMP to cytosolic calcium regulation; calcium effects are downstream of the core PDE function.

title: Seven Dictyostelium discoideum phosphodiesterases degrade three pools of cAMP and cGMP.
review_notes: Authoritative statement of RegA's cAMP specificity, cytosolic localization, and phosphorelay regulation; grounds the core function and the cGMP-activity REMOVE.

title: High-throughput analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: High-throughput phenotype screen; abstract does not contain a regA-specific statement, so this reference only corroborates the well-established sorocarp-development role indirectly.

title: Loss of cAMP-specific phosphodiesterase rescues spore development in G protein mutant in dictyostelium.
review_notes: Supports RegA's role in restraining spore development downstream of cAMP/PKA signaling.

title: Response of Dictyostelium discoideum to UV-C and involvement of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase.
review_notes: regA appears only as one of several developmental marker genes in an expression assay; provides weak, non-core support for a UV-C response role.

title: Differentiation-inducing factor 2 modulates chemotaxis via the histidine kinase DhkC-dependent pathway in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Abstract-only but directly supports RegA's role in DIF-2-modulated chemotaxis via the DhkC-RdeA-RegA pathway.

title: Mitogen-activated protein kinase regulation of the phosphodiesterase RegA in early Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Documents the RegA-Erk2 physical interaction underpinning the protein-binding (protein kinase binding) annotation.

title: Development of Phosphodiesterase-Protein-Kinase Complexes as Novel Targets for Discovery of Inhibitors with Enhanced Specificity.
review_notes: Retrieved using the publication fetcher and inspected the primary full-text cache. The recombinant RegA-RD assay demonstrates cGMP competition for the complex; this is not by itself proof of catalytic cGMP hydrolysis.

title: A cAMP-phosphodiesterase controls PKA-dependent differentiation.
review_notes: Establishes RegA as the cAMP phosphodiesterase controlling PKA-dependent differentiation and its stimulation by PKA-R binding.

title: An intersection of the cAMP/PKA and two-component signal transduction systems in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Defines the two-domain architecture and the Asp212 phosphoacceptor that activates the phosphodiesterase.

title: OpenScientist focused regA GO:0047555 hypothesis report
review_notes: The report omits PMID:34063491 and does not reconcile the greater-than selectivity bound in PMID:12429832 with the later ~200 claim. Another enzyme performing cGMP turnover does not establish its absence in RegA. Artifact evidence-tier plots are hardcoded summaries, not a new enzymatic or phylogenetic analysis.

title: The Dictyostelium homologue of mammalian soluble adenylyl cyclase encodes a guanylyl cyclase.
review_notes: Primary paper identifying and disrupting sgcA; establishes it as the predominant guanylyl cyclase and a class III (sAC-homologous) enzyme, not a NO-sensitive heme cyclase.

title: Chemotaxis: signalling modules join hands at front and tail.
review_notes: Review that frames the front/back modular model; supports the cGMP-myosin-pseudopod suppression role but is a secondary source.

title: Activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase at the leading edge during Dictyostelium chemotaxis.
review_notes: Establishes cytosolic resting distribution and chemoattractant-induced anterior cortical activation; cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available false) but the abstract states these localizations directly.

title: Guanylyl cyclase protein and cGMP product independently control front and back of chemotaxing Dictyostelium cells.
review_notes: Uncouples catalytic activity (sGCDeltacat) from leading-edge localization (sGCDeltaN); the strongest evidence for the dual, cGMP-dependent and cGMP-independent, roles of sgcA.

title: The role of cGMP and the rear of the cell in Dictyostelium chemotaxis and cell streaming.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports the rear/cGMP role in chemotaxis and pseudopod retraction.

title: Four key signaling pathways mediating chemotaxis in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Genetic identification of sGC as one of four key chemotaxis pathways; supports chemotaxis-to-cAMP core process.

title: Switching direction in electric-signal-induced cell migration by cyclic guanosine monophosphate and phosphatidylinositol signaling.
review_notes: Supports both leading-edge localization and an accessory role in electrotaxis directional switching.

title: Dictyostelium chemotaxis: essential Ras activation and accessory signalling pathways for amplification.
review_notes: Places sGC among accessory amplification pathways rather than the essential Ras module; supports regulation-of-chemotaxis annotation.

title: Pumilio-dependent localization of mRNAs at the cell front coordinates multiple pathways required for chemotaxis.
review_notes: Supports leading-edge/cell-front enrichment of sGC among the coordinated chemotaxis pathways.

title: Intracellular Calcium Responses to External Calcium Stimuli in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Supports a modulatory role of cGMP/sgcA in the timing of calcium responses; peripheral to the core function.

title: Comparison of molecular mechanisms mediating cell contact phenomena in model developmental systems: an exploration of universality.
review_notes: Broad review of cell-contact mechanisms across model systems; the abstract does not discuss SmlA specifically. The TAS annotation to positive regulation of aggregate size is correct on the biology but the primary support comes from the Brock/Gomer studies.

title: Exposure of cells to a cell number-counting factor decreases the activity of glucose-6-phosphatase to decrease intracellular glucose levels in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Establishes the CF-glucose-6-phosphatase-glucose axis downstream of the size-control pathway; SmlA is upstream via its control of CF secretion.

title: A protein in crude cytosol regulates glucose-6-phosphatase activity in crude microsomes to regulate group size in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Links the counting-factor pathway to glucose-6-phosphatase regulation; relevant to the glucose-6-phosphate/glucose-homeostasis annotations on smlA as downstream, non-core effects.

title: A cell number-counting factor regulates levels of a novel protein, SslA, as part of a group size regulation mechanism in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Directly ties smlA loss to counting-factor oversecretion and small group size, and provides the genetic interaction (sslA) supporting the IGI annotation.

title: Global transcriptional responses to cisplatin in Dictyostelium discoideum identify potential drug targets.
review_notes: Cisplatin sensitivity is an indirect phenotype; it does not support a direct DNA damage response function for SmlA.

title: Proteomic analysis of Legionella-containing phagosomes isolated from Dictyostelium.
review_notes: High-throughput phagosome proteomics catalog; the phagocytic-vesicle annotation is an over-annotation for a cytosolic protein.

title: A Dictystelium mutant with defective aggregate size determination.
review_notes: Primary discovery and characterization of smlA; establishes the cytosolic localization, non-secretion, undetermined molecular function, and the secretion-control/aggregate-size role.

title: Disruption of the sporulation-specific gene spiA in Dictyostelium discoideum leads to spore instability.
review_notes: Primary knockout-and-rescue study establishing the spore-coat localization and spore-stability role of Dd31/spiA. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available false); all quotes are verbatim from the abstract.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Developmental transcriptome study; supports the culmination-stage, sporulation-marker expression of spiA. Full text available and quote is verbatim.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment analysis of the SpiA SCAMP trafficking hypothesis
review_notes: The existing independent report supports SCAMP-family identity and explicitly recommends retaining vesicular-trafficking annotations as non-core. It notes that NPF-less mammalian SCAMP4/SCAMP5 still traffic, so the absent NPF repeats in SpiA do not establish loss of trafficking or of a particular compartment. The PAINT localization assertion includes NPF-less human SCAMP5, strengthening that caveat. Report findings and exact excerpts are incorporated into the three IBA reviews; no duplicate report was launched.

title: Developmentally regulated protein-tyrosine kinase genes in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Original cloning; abstract-only cached; reports PTK activity of fusion proteins and developmental regulation.

title: Identification of the kinase that activates a nonmetazoan STAT gives insights into the evolution of phosphotyrosine-SH2 domain signaling.
review_notes: Key paper identifying Pyk2 as the STATc Tyr922 kinase; abstract-only cached.

title: Two Dictyostelium tyrosine kinase-like kinases function in parallel, stress-induced STAT activation pathways.
review_notes: Full text cached; Pyk2/Pyk3 redundancy in stress-induced STATc activation, localization, autophosphorylation.

title: The MADS-box gene srfA is expressed in a complex pattern under the control of alternative promoters and is essential for different aspects of Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Establishes expression pattern and additional developmental roles (slug migration) beyond sporulation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Regulated expression of the MADS-box transcription factor SrfA mediates activation of gene expression by protein kinase A during Dictyostelium sporulation.
review_notes: Establishes PKA-dependent regulation of srfA induction at culmination; contextual background for its developmental role. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Dictyostelium discoideum developmentally regulated genes whose expression is dependent on MADS box transcription factor SrfA.
review_notes: Full text available; identifies SrfA-dependent target genes and supports the positive-regulation transcription-factor role.

title: The MADS-box transcription factor SrfA is required for actin cytoskeleton organization and spore coat stability during Dictyostelium sporulation.
review_notes: Structural analysis of srfA-null spores; documents actin-rod and spore-coat phenotypes downstream of the transcription-factor function.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Genome-wide developmental transcriptome study that does not specifically discuss srfA in the cached full text. It is cited as the IEP source for a culmination annotation, but srfA cannot be verified from this reference.

title: A Serum Response Factor homolog is required for spore differentiation in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Original characterization of srfA; establishes it as an SRF/MADS-box transcription factor required for spore differentiation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Evidence that the Dictyostelium Dd-STATa protein is a repressor that regulates commitment to stalk cell differentiation and is also required for efficient chemotaxis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary genetic evidence for the repressor role, stalk-cell differentiation, chemotaxis, and culmination phenotypes.

title: Glycogen synthase kinase-3 enhances nuclear export of a Dictyostelium STAT protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Supports nuclear localization and the GskA-dependent nuclear export mechanism.

title: The Dictyostelium prestalk cell inducer DIF regulates nuclear accumulation of a STAT protein by controlling its rate of export from the nucleus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The abstract characterizes the paralog Dd-STATc (DIF-controlled CRM1-dependent nuclear export); used by dictyBase to support nuclear activity. Nuclear localization of Dd-STATa itself is independently established (PMID:9670017, PMID:11032815).

title: Structure of an activated Dictyostelium STAT in its DNA-unbound form.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; crystal structure (PDB 1UUR/1UUS) of the activated homodimer, establishing dimerization mechanism and DNA-binding domain.

title: Identification of new modes of Dd-STATa regulation of gene expression in Dictyostelium by in situ hybridisation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports positive (activating) regulation of a subset of prestalk target genes.

title: Evidence that the Dictyostelium STAT protein Dd-STATa plays a role in the differentiation of inner basal disc cells and identification of a promoter element essential for expression in these cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports regulation of gene expression and culmination/inner basal disc differentiation.

title: High-throughput analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Genome-scale mutant screen corroborating a developmental (post-slug) phenotype for dstA/STATa.

title: STAT signaling in Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Review, abstract-only in cache; quotes taken from the abstract. Summarises the four Dictyostelium STATs and the Dd-STATa null phenotype (delayed aggregation, no phototaxis, failed culmination). Secondary to the primary null-mutant papers (PMID:10393118, PMID:15733068).

title: Comparative evolutionary genomics of the STAT family of transcription factors.
review_notes: Review with comparative-genomic analysis (full text cached, PMC3670131). Checked passages that Dictyostelium encodes four STATs (dstA-dstD) forming a distinct clade, that they lack the N-terminal and transactivation domains of metazoan STATs, and that Dictyostelium STAT signaling lies outside the Metazoa.

title: Evolution of the JAK-STAT pathway.
review_notes: Review (full text cached, PMC3670263). Checked passages that amoebozoan STAT-like proteins have coiled-coil, DNA-binding and SH2 domains but no transactivation domain or N-terminal sequence, that the first JAK-like protein appears in sponges, and that the canonical JAK-STAT pathway was assembled in bilateria. Supports the non-JAK STAT signaling term for Dictyostelium.

title: Regulation of ecmF gene expression and genetic hierarchy among STATa, CudA, and MybC on several prestalk A-specific gene expressions in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes STATa-CudA-MybC genetic hierarchy and organizer/positive-regulation roles.

title: Analysis of DrkA kinase's role in STATa activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies DrkA as a candidate direct activating kinase and provides the physical/kinase-substrate interaction basis for the protein binding IPI.

title: SH2 signaling in a lower eukaryote: a STAT protein that regulates stalk cell differentiation in dictyostelium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; founding paper identifying Dd-STATa as a STAT and SH2-signaling transcription factor.

title: Developmentally and spatially regulated activation of a Dictyostelium STAT protein by a serpentine receptor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Establishes cAR1-dependent activation and the spatial pattern of nuclear Dd-STATa in the tip organizer.

title: OpenScientist assessment of STATa proliferation regulation and defense response
review_notes: Read complete substantive report. Correctly distinguishes proliferation from differentiation and defense from osmotic stress; correctly identifies STATb among ancestral evidence. Rejection nevertheless rests on donor taxonomic composition, alternative pathway genes and missing target assays. It explicitly acknowledges untested target growth/defense and establishes no STATa-specific loss.

title: Tyrosine phosphorylation-independent nuclear translocation of a dictyostelium STAT in response to DIF signaling.
review_notes: Foundational STATc paper; establishes its transcription factor and repressor roles and DIF-induced nuclear translocation. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: OSBPa, a predicted oxysterol binding protein of Dictyostelium, is required for regulated entry into culmination.
review_notes: Study of OSBPa/osbA and culmination; abstract does not describe a STATc interaction, so the source of the generic STATc protein binding IPI is not resolvable from the cached abstract-only record.

title: The Dictyostelium prestalk cell inducer DIF regulates nuclear accumulation of a STAT protein by controlling its rate of export from the nucleus.
review_notes: Establishes that STATc nuclear accumulation is regulated at the level of nuclear export. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: A STAT-regulated, stress-induced signalling pathway in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Establishes STATc as a stress-activated transcriptional activator controlling specific target genes.

title: STATc is a key regulator of the transcriptional response to hyperosmotic shock.
review_notes: Genome-wide (microarray) evidence for STATc's central role in the hyperosmotic transcriptional response; full text available.

title: Evidence that DIF-1 and hyper-osmotic stress activate a Dictyostelium STAT by inhibiting a specific protein tyrosine phosphatase.
review_notes: Identifies PTP3 as the STATc-inactivating phosphatase and the basis of the STATc protein binding IPI; full text available.

title: Identification of the kinase that activates a nonmetazoan STAT gives insights into the evolution of phosphotyrosine-SH2 domain signaling.
review_notes: Identifies Pyk2 as a STATc-activating kinase and supports use of a STAT (non-JAK) signaling term. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: The calcineurin dependent transcription factor TacA is involved in development and the stress response of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Primarily a TacA study; corroborates STATc as the established stress-response pathway. Basis of the STATc osmotic/cation stress IMP annotations; cached record is abstract-only.

title: Comparative evolutionary genomics of the STAT family of transcription factors.
review_notes: Review with comparative-genomic analysis (full text cached, PMC3670131). Checked passages that Dictyostelium encodes four STATs (dstA-dstD) forming a distinct clade, that they lack the N-terminal and transactivation domains of metazoan STATs, and that Dictyostelium STAT signaling lies outside the Metazoa. No STATc-specific data.

title: Evolution of the JAK-STAT pathway.
review_notes: Review (full text cached, PMC3670263). Checked passages that the first JAK-like protein appears in sponges and that the canonical JAK-STAT pathway was assembled in bilateria, so amoebozoan STAT signaling is JAK-independent by descent. Supports the GO:0007259 to GO:0097696 MODIFY.

title: The arrestin-domain containing protein AdcA is a response element to stress.
review_notes: Links STATc-dependent transcription to regulation of the cellular stress response via AdcA; full text available.

title: Identification of the protein kinases Pyk3 and Phg2 as regulators of the STATc-mediated response to hyperosmolarity.
review_notes: Establishes STATc-dependent positive regulation of gene expression and additional upstream kinases; full text available.

title: Two Dictyostelium tyrosine kinase-like kinases function in parallel, stress-induced STAT activation pathways.
review_notes: Defines the Pyk2/Pyk3 kinase-STATc SH2 interaction; basis of the protein binding IPI; full text available.

title: The Dictyostelium prestalk inducer differentiation-inducing factor-1 (DIF-1) triggers unexpectedly complex global phosphorylation changes.
review_notes: High-throughput phosphoproteomic support for STATc activation by DIF-1; full text available.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Developmental transcriptome study; basis of the IEP sorocarp development annotation via expression pattern; full text available.

title: AIGR Gene Hypothesis Deep Research — Dictyostelium discoideum statC (Q54BD4)
review_notes: Primary source leads and noncanonical stress activation are supported. Refuted verdict is not: report admits statC proliferation and bacterial-clearance roles are untested, treats paralog descendants as automatic propagation error, and adds JAK/cytokine requirements absent from the broad GO definitions. TirA/NADPH oxidase necessity does not exclude a STAT transcriptional regulator. No target-specific loss is established.

title: Biosynthesis of Dictyostelium discoideum differentiation-inducing factor by a hybrid type I fatty acid-type III polyketide synthase.
review_notes: Primary paper establishing StlB (Steely2) as the DIF-1 pathway acylphloroglucinol (THPH/PCP) synthase by combined in vitro enzymology and in vivo knockout/rescue; PMID and title verified against the cached record.

title: DIF-1 induces the basal disc of the Dictyostelium fruiting body.
review_notes: Full-text mutant-phenotype study directly establishing the developmental roles (prestalk differentiation, basal disc / lower cup) that require StlB-dependent DIF-1.

title: Steely enzymes are involved in prestalk and prespore pattern formation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; supports the prestalk/pattern-formation role of Steely polyketides including DIF-1 from StlB.

title: c-di-GMP induction of Dictyostelium cell death requires the polyketide DIF-1.
review_notes: Full-text study; StlB contributes indirectly (via DIF-1) to developmental cell death.

title: Stalk cell differentiation without polyketides in the cellular slime mold.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; supports StlB (via DIF-1) acting upstream of prestalk gene expression.

title: Yellow polyketide pigment suppresses premature hatching in social amoeba.
review_notes: This paper is about PKS5/dictyodenes and does not characterize dibenzofuran metabolism by StlB; it references StlB only for DIF-1 synthesis. It does not support the dibenzofuran metabolic process annotation.

title: Evolutionary analyses of ABC transporters of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: PMC full text confirmed; an evolutionary survey classifying TagC within the ABCB family. Supports the transporter-module context but does not experimentally establish transport activity for TagC.

title: Peptide signaling during terminal differentiation of Dictyostelium.
review_notes: PMC full text confirmed. Primary functional evidence that TagC is the serine protease that processes AcbA to SDF-2; underpins the core protease and protein-processing annotations.

title: GABA induces terminal differentiation of Dictyostelium through a GABAB receptor.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache, but the abstract explicitly localizes the TagC protease domain to the prestalk cell surface and states it converts AcbA to SDF-2; supports plasma membrane localization and the protease function.

title: A multidrug resistance transporter/serine protease gene is required for prestalk specialization in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; the paper primarily characterizes the paralog tagB but establishes the tag-gene paradigm (protease plus MDR transporter) and the prestalk-specialization/encapsulation role that the dictyBase IMP annotation transfers to tagC. Full text (not cached) presumably covers tagC; per policy the experimental annotation is retained.

title: Screening of genes involved in cell migration in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Abstract-only; the paper concerns the phospholipase D gene pldB and cell migration and does not mention tgrB1. Basis for the tgrB1 cell-motility IGI annotation cannot be verified from the available text.

title: Polymorphic members of the lag gene family mediate kin discrimination in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Foundational paper identifying lagB1/tgrB1 as a polymorphic kin-discrimination determinant; full text verified.

title: Self-recognition in social amoebae is mediated by allelic pairs of tiger genes.
review_notes: Establishes allele-specific self-recognition by matched tgrB1-tgrC1 pairs; full text verified.

title: TgrC1 mediates cell-cell adhesion by interacting with TgrB1 via mutual IPT/TIG domains during development of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Biochemical identification and domain mapping of the TgrB1-TgrC1 interaction; cached record is abstract-only but the abstract directly supports the cited claims.

title: Kin recognition protects cooperators against cheaters.
review_notes: Demonstrates the population-level protective role of tgrB1/tgrC1 kin recognition; full text verified.

title: Assembly of the TgrB1-TgrC1 cell adhesion complex during Dictyostelium discoideum development.
review_notes: Defines assembly of the TgrB1-TgrC1 adhesion complex; cached record is abstract-only but supports the cited claims.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Transcriptome study; supports developmental-stage expression and the aggregation checkpoint role of tgrB1.

title: Gene discovery by chemical mutagenesis and whole-genome sequencing in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Suppressor screen of the tgrB1-tgrC1 mismatch; supports TgrB1's role in a cell-surface receptor signaling pathway.

title: A polychromatic 'greenbeard' locus determines patterns of cooperation in a social amoeba.
review_notes: Establishes the greenbeard behaviour of the Tgr locus; full text verified.

title: The polymorphic proteins TgrB1 and TgrC1 function as a ligand-receptor pair in Dictyostelium allorecognition.
review_notes: Definitive demonstration that TgrB1 is the receptor and TgrC1 the ligand; full text verified.

title: Identification of novel proteins in the Dictyostelium discoideum chemorepulsion pathway using REMI.
review_notes: REMI screen for AprA chemorepulsion components. The paper's "TgrB1" screen hit is described as encoded by DDB_G0293176, whereas this gene is DDB_G0280689; the GPCR chemorepellent-signaling annotation to tgrB1 cannot be verified and is inconsistent with TgrB1's known Ig-domain receptor biology.

title: The greenbeard gene tgrB1 regulates altruism and cheating in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Direct evidence linking TgrB1 receptor activity to altruism and cheating in chimeras; full text verified.

title: The membrane glycoprotein gp150 is encoded by the lagC gene and mediates cell-cell adhesion by heterophilic binding during Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Establishes gp150 = lagC (TgrC1) and demonstrates heterophilic, EDTA-resistant cell-cell adhesion with enrichment at cell-cell contacts. Abstract-only in cache; claims verified against abstract.

title: A cell-adhesion pathway regulates intercellular communication during Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Places lagC as the terminal node of a comC-lagC-lagD signaling pathway required for sporulation; supports the developmental (non-core) role.

title: Dictyostelium morphogenesis.
review_notes: General morphogenesis review used as TAS support for plasma membrane site of action; does not name tgrC1 specifically.

title: Regulation of cell-cell adhesion during Dictyostelium development.
review_notes: Review of Dictyostelium adhesion systems (cadA, csaA, lagC/gp150) noting adherens junction-like structures; supports membrane/junction localization.

title: Purification and partial characterization of a cell adhesion molecule (gp150) involved in postaggregation stage cell-cell binding in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Purified gp150 inhibits post-aggregation reassociation and binds cells saturably; direct evidence for cell-cell adhesion molecule function.

title: Polymorphic members of the lag gene family mediate kin discrimination in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Full text available; lagC1 (tgrC1) deletion causes strain segregation from wild type, establishing the kin-recognition role.

title: Self-recognition in social amoebae is mediated by allelic pairs of tiger genes.
review_notes: Full text available; matching tgrB1/tgrC1 allele pairs are necessary and sufficient for attractive self-recognition via differential adhesion.

title: TgrC1 mediates cell-cell adhesion by interacting with TgrB1 via mutual IPT/TIG domains during development of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Identifies TgrB1 as the heterophilic binding partner and maps the TgrC1 binding region (Ile336-Val360, TIG2). Abstract-only in cache; claims verified against abstract.

title: The green tea catechin epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) blocks cell motility, chemotaxis and development in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Full text available; tgrC expression is delayed by EGCG among late-aggregate genes. Supports a peripheral response-to-catechin annotation, not a core function.

title: Kin recognition protects cooperators against cheaters.
review_notes: Full text available; uses tgrB1/tgrC1 allele swaps to show kin recognition protects cooperators; supports the socially cooperative development (non-core) role.

title: Assembly of the TgrB1-TgrC1 cell adhesion complex during Dictyostelium discoideum development.
review_notes: Demonstrates TgrC1 cis-homodimerization and the assembly of large TgrB1-TgrC1 adhesion complexes. Abstract-only in cache; claims verified against abstract.

title: Leaps and lulls in the developmental transcriptome of Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Full text available; positions tgrB1/tgrC1 as an aggregate-to-mound developmental checkpoint; supports the IEP timing/developmental annotation.

title: TgrC1 Has Distinct Functions in Dictyostelium Development and Allorecognition.
review_notes: Full text available; suppressor genetics separate TgrC1's cell-autonomous stalk-differentiation role from its non-cell-autonomous spore and recognition roles.

title: A polychromatic 'greenbeard' locus determines patterns of cooperation in a social amoeba.
review_notes: Full text available; the tgrB1/tgrC1 locus is a polychromatic greenbeard whose binding strength predicts partner-specific segregation.

title: The polymorphic proteins TgrB1 and TgrC1 function as a ligand-receptor pair in Dictyostelium allorecognition.
review_notes: Full text available; merodiploid experiments establish TgrC1 as the non-cell-autonomous ligand and TgrB1 as the cell-autonomous receptor. Key support for the core receptor-ligand activity.

title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic insights into light-mediated unicellular-to-multicellular transition in Dictyostelium discoideum.
review_notes: Full text available; tgrC1 (lagC) is downregulated under dark in a transcriptomic screen. This is expression-based and does not indicate a TgrC1 function in light response (basis for the over-annotation call).

title: Identification of a cell surface glycoprotein involved in cell aggregation in D. discoideum.
review_notes: Founding study identifying gp150 as a developmentally regulated cell-surface glycoprotein whose antibodies block reaggregation.

title: A glycoprotein involved in aggregation of D. discoideum is distributed on the cell surface in a nonrandom fashion favoring cell junctions.
review_notes: Immuno-EM shows gp150 is closely associated with the plasma membrane and enriched at cell-cell contact/junction sites.

title: LagC is required for cell-cell interactions that are essential for cell-type differentiation in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Identifies lagC and shows null cells arrest at the loose aggregate stage with defective cell-type differentiation and sporulation.

title: High-throughput analysis of spatio-temporal dynamics in Dictyostelium.
review_notes: Full-text screen; independently corroborates a tipA developmental defect at slug/culmination stages, supporting the HMP sorocarp development annotation. It does not address molecular function.

title: Sorting of the initial cell types in Dictyostelium is dependent on the tipA gene.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment analysis of the TipA PP2C phosphatase hypothesis
review_notes: Independent OpenScientist function-assignment run (3 iterations). Verdict PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The PP2C/PPM domain membership is well supported (InterPro IPR001932 / IPR053287, PANTHER PTHR21586, confident AlphaFold PP2C fold), but the canonical catalytic-His motif (DGHxG) is absent across the entire TIPA-specific phosphatase family (0/100 members) while the metal-coordinating aspartate scaffold is conserved (~69-86 percent). Best supported computed molecular function is metal ion binding; protein Ser/Thr phosphatase activity should NOT be asserted with experimental confidence. Concordant with this review leaving molecular_function unasserted. Lead - TipA is likely a metal-binding but catalytically divergent (pseudo)PP2C; requires an enzyme assay to resolve.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.

title: OpenScientist function-assignment hypothesis: Mtpalpha (Q8IPE8) peroxisome (GO:0005777)
review_notes: In-repo OpenScientist report generated for the mitochondrion-vs-peroxisome hypothesis. Verdict SUPPORTED (retain peroxisome).
