title: UniProt entry Q8IPE8 (Mtpalpha, Trifunctional enzyme subunit alpha, mitochondrial)
review_notes: Local UniProt record used to anchor the domain/architecture, localization and complex claims. Enzymatic and MLCL-acyltransferase details are ARBA-inferred, not fly experimental.

title: Mapping organelle proteins and protein complexes in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Supports mitochondrial localization of Mtpbeta as a high-throughput organelle-proteomics assignment; the specific protein call is in the full dataset, not the abstract.

title: Impaired fatty acid oxidation in a Drosophila model of mitochondrial trifunctional protein (MTP) deficiency.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full text not available). Directly establishes the in vivo beta-oxidation function of the Drosophila Mtpbeta gene through loss-of-function genetics and acylcarnitine biomarker accumulation.

title: An inventory of peroxisomal proteins and pathways in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Prediction-based (ISM) mitochondrion localization; consistent with the experimental HDA annotation but lower confidence and tangential to the paper's peroxisome focus.

title: Maintaining Toll signaling in Drosophila brain is required to sustain autophagy for dopamine neuron survival.
review_notes: Found via the Falcon deep-research cross-check and read in the cached full text. Cell-culture evidence with overexpressed receptor TIR domains; used only for a suggested question, not for an annotation.

title: Falcon research on NtR/CG6698/Q9W288
review_notes: Read the full report. Its failure to find a ligand assay is useful, but its claim that no channel function can be inferred overlooks the published Cys-loop tree and FlyBase unclassified-channel grouping. Direct target assays are not required to accept conserved broad function. The report provides no primary evidence against the channel inference.

title: Analysis of Drosophila STING Reveals an Evolutionarily Conserved Antimicrobial Function.
review_notes: Establishes dSTING (CG1667) as the fly STING ortholog, its c-di-GMP binding, and its antibacterial (Listeria) function via Relish/IMD and antimicrobial peptides. Full text available and used for supporting quotes.

title: Inflammation-Induced, STING-Dependent Autophagy Restricts Zika Virus Infection in the Drosophila Brain.
review_notes: Demonstrates dSTING-dependent autophagy restricting Zika virus in the adult brain; grounds the positive regulation of macroautophagy annotations.

title: The Kinase IKKβ Regulates a STING- and NF-κB-Dependent Antiviral Response Pathway in Drosophila.
review_notes: Establishes ER membrane localization (cited by UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION) and the dSTING -> dIKKbeta -> Relish -> Nazo antiviral axis against picorna-like viruses.

title: 2'3'-cGAMP triggers a STING- and NF-κB-dependent broad antiviral response in Drosophila.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but internally consistent; shows 2'3'-cGAMP triggers an NF-kappaB (Relish)-dependent, interferon-independent antiviral program - central to removing the type I IFN annotation.

title: cGAS-like receptors sense RNA and control 3'2'-cGAMP signalling in Drosophila.
review_notes: Structural and functional demonstration that dSTING binds 3'2'-cGAMP (its preferred ligand), produced by cGLR1 from dsRNA.

title: Two cGAS-like receptors induce antiviral immunity in Drosophila.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; shows cGLR1/cGLR2 activate Sting- and NF-kappaB-dependent antiviral immunity against RNA and DNA viruses.

title: Orally acquired cyclic dinucleotides drive dSTING-dependent antiviral immunity in enterocytes.
review_notes: Shows a gut enterocyte CDN-dSTING-dTBK1-NF-kappaB antiviral circuit; grounds tissue-specific antiviral innate immune response annotation.

title: The virus-induced cyclic dinucleotide 2'3'-c-di-GMP mediates STING-dependent antiviral immunity in Drosophila.
review_notes: Identifies 2'3'-c-di-GMP as a potent dSTING agonist; grounds cellular response to virus and cGAS/STING signaling IDA annotations.

title: Drosophila melanogaster Sting mediates Coxiella burnetii infection by reducing accumulation of reactive oxygen species.
review_notes: Demonstrates dSTING antibacterial defense against the Gram-negative bacterium Coxiella burnetii via reduced ROS and antimicrobial peptide induction.

title: A cryptic homotypic interaction motif of insect STING is required for its antiviral signaling.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; shows a cryptic RHIM motif drives dSTING oligomerization, interaction with IMD, and antiviral signaling via Relish.

title: The Drosophila Su(var)2-10 locus regulates chromosome structure and function and encodes a member of the PIAS protein family.
review_notes: Foundational cloning and characterisation paper (full text cached).

title: A Drosophila PIAS homologue negatively regulates stat92E.
review_notes: Full text cached; genetic (LOF, overexpression, JAK-STAT mutant backgrounds) evidence for dPIAS as a negative regulator of Stat92E.

title: The JAK/STAT pathway and Drosophila development.
review_notes: Abstract-only review of Drosophila JAK/STAT; abstract does not mention dPIAS. Source of three TAS rows whose primary support is PMID:11504941 and PMID:11390354.

title: Genome-wide RNAi screen identifies genes involved in intestinal pathogenic bacterial infection.
review_notes: Genome-wide screen with targeted follow-up of PIAS; supports a peripheral role via JAK-STAT inhibition, not an innate immune effector role.

title: Su(var)2-10 and the SUMO Pathway Link piRNA-Guided Target Recognition to Chromatin Silencing.
review_notes: Primary mechanistic paper (full text cached), including in vitro auto-SUMOylation and C341S catalytic mutant.

title: The SUMO Ligase Su(var)2-10 Controls Hetero- and Euchromatic Gene Expression via Establishing H3K9 Trimethylation and Negative Feedback Regulation.
review_notes: Full text cached; genome-wide follow-up of PMID:31901446.

title: SUMOylation of Bonus, the Drosophila homolog of Transcription Intermediary Factor 1, safeguards germline identity by recruiting repressive chromatin complexes to silence tissue-specific genes.
review_notes: Full text cached; identifies a specific substrate.

title: OpenScientist deep research report for Su(var)2-10 (Drosophila melanogaster)
review_notes: Key claims (PIAS identity, piRNA/SetDB1 mechanism, genome-wide H3K9me3 dependence, Bonus substrate, Stat92E antagonism, lamina/telomere localisation) were checked against cached primary papers PMID:11390354, PMID:31901446, PMID:31901448, PMID:37999956 and PMID:11504941. Domain-mechanism claims are inferred from yeast/plant Siz orthologs and were not independently verified here.

title: cGAS-like receptors sense RNA and control 3'2'-cGAMP signalling in Drosophila.
review_notes: Slavik et al. 2021 (Nature); full text cached. Establishes cGLR1 as a dsRNA sensor that synthesizes 3',2'-cGAMP and signals through dSTING-Relish; the primary functional reference for this gene.

title: Two cGAS-like receptors induce antiviral immunity in Drosophila.
review_notes: Holleufer et al. 2021 (Nature); abstract-only in the cache. Independently identifies cGLR1/cGLR2 and confirms cGLR1 as a dsRNA-activated 3',2'-cGAMP producer signalling via Sting/NF-kappaB.

title: The virus-induced cyclic dinucleotide 2'3'-c-di-GMP mediates STING-dependent antiviral immunity in Drosophila.
review_notes: Cai et al. 2023 (Immunity); full text cached. Shows virus-induced, cGLR-dependent production of multiple CDNs in vivo (including 2',3'-cGAMP, 3',2'-cGAMP and 2',3'-c-di-GMP) and that cGLR1 contributes to 2',3'-c-di-GMP.

title: Two cGAS-like receptors induce antiviral immunity in Drosophila.
review_notes: Holleufer et al. 2021 (Nature); abstract-only in the cache. Identifies cGLR2 as producing a combination of 2',3'-cGAMP and 3',2'-cGAMP and activating Sting/NF-kappaB antiviral immunity; states cGLR2's activating stimulus was unidentified at the time.

title: The virus-induced cyclic dinucleotide 2'3'-c-di-GMP mediates STING-dependent antiviral immunity in Drosophila.
review_notes: Cai et al. 2023 (Immunity); full text cached. Shows 2',3'-c-di-GMP is the major product of Drosophila cGLR2, that dsRNA facilitates cGLR2 activity, and that cGLR-dependent CDN production is virus-induced in vivo; also notes the cGLR2 ligand remains unknown.

title: Axon guidance of Drosophila SNb motoneurons depends on the cooperative action of muscular Krüppel and neuronal capricious activities.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes Caps as a cell-surface recognition molecule regulating the RP5 motoneuron-muscle 12 connection. Directly supports the axon-guidance annotations.

title: Size isn't everything.
review_notes: Abstract-only Bioessays review on tissue size/shape control; the abstract does not mention caps or cell migration. It is the TAS basis for GO:0016477 but is only background/contextual for caps - the real support for a migration role comes from the tracheal study (PMID:16764850).

title: Pattern formation in the Drosophila wing: The development of the veins.
review_notes: Abstract-only Bioessays review on wing-vein patterning; the abstract does not mention caps. Cited as NAS support for GO:0007155 (cell adhesion); the general adhesion function is correct for caps but is not directly supported by this review - a weak/likely-inappropriate NAS citation, adjudicated identically in the trn review, which carries the same GOA row.

title: Regulation of layer-specific targeting by reciprocal expression of a cell adhesion molecule, capricious.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but content-verified: demonstrates Caps homophilic adhesion in S2 cells and reciprocal R8/R7 layer-specific targeting. Supports the homophilic-adhesion MF and photoreceptor-targeting annotations.

title: Distinct functions of the leucine-rich repeat transmembrane proteins capricious and tartan in the Drosophila tracheal morphogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; shows Caps on bridge-cells instructing dorsal-trunk branch fusion and requiring both extra- and intracellular domains. Supports GO:0035147.

title: A screen of cell-surface molecules identifies leucine-rich repeat proteins as key mediators of synaptic target selection.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; quantifies trn caps redundancy in ISNb/SNa motor-axon targeting and Caps expression on muscle 12. Supports GO:0008045.

title: A targeted gain-of-function screen identifies genes affecting salivary gland morphogenesis/tubulogenesis in Drosophila.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; implicates caps/trn in salivary gland morphogenesis and summarizes the homophilic/heterophilic adhesion-receptor hypothesis. Supports GO:0007436.

title: Target recognition at the tips of postsynaptic filopodia: accumulation and function of Capricious.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but content-verified: Caps-GFP accumulates at myopodia tips and caps/ caps trn mutants show fewer myopodia-growth-cone contacts and reduced nascent synaptic sites. Supports the muscle cell projection localization and the NMJ synapse-formation contribution.

title: Cytoneme-mediated contact-dependent transport of the Drosophila decapentaplegic signaling protein.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; Caps:GFP localizes to ASP cytonemes (enriched at tips) and caps is required for cytoneme-mediated Dpp reception. Supports GO:0035230.

title: Assessing the role of cell-surface molecules in central synaptogenesis in the Drosophila visual system.
review_notes: Full text available and reviewed; reassesses Caps in R8 targeting/synaptogenesis, finding a marginal, non-homophilic guidance role and no major direct role in R8 synapse formation. Important nuance for the synapse-assembly and photoreceptor annotations.

title: Structure of the retinal determination protein Dachshund reveals a DNA binding motif.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human DACH1 DD1 (Dachbox-N) domain; relevant to fly Dac only by homology.

title: The developments between gametogenesis and fertilization: ovulation and female sperm storage in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Review on ovulation/sperm storage; cached abstract does not mention dac; full text not available here.

title: Dachshund and C-terminal Binding Protein bind directly during Drosophila eye development.
review_notes: Shows direct Dac-CtBP binding (GST pull-down) but no DNA binding; does not support the DNA-binding TF activity TAS, supports coregulator activity.

title: Huckebein repressor activity in Drosophila terminal patterning is mediated by Groucho.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified against PubMed. Concerns Huckebein but establishes the shared WRPW/FRPW Groucho-recruitment paradigm for Hairy-related repressors; supports Hairy's transcription corepressor (Groucho) binding at the family level.

title: The origin and evolution of segmentation.
review_notes: General review on the evolution of segmentation used as a TAS source for the pair-rule/periodic-partitioning role; does not itself describe Hairy specifics.

title: Epithelial tube morphology is determined by the polarized growth and delivery of apical membrane.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; a new hairy allele causes salivary tube branching/bulging via prolonged huckebein expression. Supports non-core salivary/tube morphogenesis roles (indirect, via loss of Hairy repression).

title: Tube morphogenesis: no pipe dream in Drosophila.
review_notes: Current Biology dispatch on tube lumen size and vesicle transport; does not describe a Hairy molecular function. Basis of the over-annotated membrane organization TAS for Hairy.

title: The role of class I HLH genes in neural development--have they been overlooked?
review_notes: Generic review of HLH classes in neural development; a weak TAS source for the broad nervous system development annotation. Hairy's neural role is better supported by PMID:7958929.

title: Drosophila Topors is a RING finger-containing protein that functions as a ubiquitin-protein isopeptide ligase for the hairy basic helix-loop-helix repressor protein.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: dTopors binds the basic region of Hairy and mediates its polyubiquitination, antagonizing repression. Supports MODIFY of a bare protein-binding IPI to ubiquitin protein ligase binding.

title: The evolution of arthropod segmentation mechanisms.
review_notes: Review grouping Hairy among the primary pair-rule genes of Drosophila; TAS source for periodic partitioning, trunk, and posterior-head segmentation.

title: A molecular link between FGF and Dpp signaling in branch-specific migration of the Drosophila trachea.
review_notes: Cached full text (available) contains zero occurrences of the hairy gene name; foregrounds btl, pointed, kni/knrl. Cannot verify the Hairy tracheal IMP from the cache; annotation left UNDECIDED.

title: Physical and genetic interactions link hox function with diverse transcription factors and cell signaling proteins.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; the abstract names Hairy directly as a UBX partner and states the assays (yeast two-hybrid, phage display confirmation, immunoprecipitation for a subset). The GOA row's WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:P83949 = Ubx (hairy-uniprot.txt:131) identifies the partner as a Hox homeodomain DNA-binding transcription factor, so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0140297. Peripheral to Hairy's core repressor function, which is recorded in the annotation reason.

title: A Myc-Groucho complex integrates EGF and Notch signaling to regulate neural development.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache concerns the dMyc-Groucho complex and does not name Hairy, hence UNVERIFIED as a statement about the cached text. The partner behind this protein-binding IPI is nonetheless curated input data, since the GOA row carries WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:P16371-2, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as Groucho isoform 2 (hairy-uniprot.txt:129), so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than UNDECIDED.

title: Mechanisms underlying hypoxia tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster: hairy as a metabolic switch.
review_notes: Full text available and verified; hairy up-regulated in hypoxia-tolerant flies and acts as a metabolic switch, with hairy mutations reducing tolerance. Supports non-core response-to-hypoxia role.

title: Groucho corepressor functions as a cofactor for the Knirps short-range transcriptional repressor.
review_notes: Full text available; experimental interaction data concern Knirps-Groucho, and Hairy appears only as a long-range-repressor comparison, so the text does not itself document the Hairy interaction. The GOA row supplies the partner as WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:P16371, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as Groucho (hairy-uniprot.txt:128), so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than UNDECIDED.

title: Degringolade, a SUMO-targeted ubiquitin ligase, inhibits Hairy/Groucho-mediated repression.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: the E3 ligase Degringolade binds and ubiquitinates Hairy to inhibit Groucho recruitment. Supports MODIFY of a bare protein-binding IPI to ubiquitin protein ligase binding for the dgrn partner, and to transcription corepressor binding for the CtBP and Groucho partners that the same reference contributes as separate GOA rows (WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036 and UniProtKB:P16371).

title: Origins of context-dependent gene repression by capicua.
review_notes: Full text available and verified; uses a Hairy WRPW/Gro-dependent Sxl-repression assay. Supports Hairy's negative regulation of Pol II transcription.

title: Pair-rule expression of the Drosophila fushi tarazu gene: a nuclear receptor response element mediates the opposing regulatory effects of runt and hairy.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: Hairy represses ftz through the fDE1 element during blastoderm segmentation. Supports negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription and the segmentation role.

title: Negative regulation of proneural gene activity: hairy is a direct transcriptional repressor of achaete.
review_notes: Key primary paper: establishes Hairy as a sequence-specific DNA-binding transcriptional repressor and identifies achaete as a direct in vivo target controlling PNS/bristle patterning.

title: The WRPW motif of the hairy-related basic helix-loop-helix repressor proteins acts as a 4-amino-acid transcription repression and protein-protein interaction domain.
review_notes: Key primary paper: the WRPW motif is a sufficient active repression domain that recruits Groucho/TLE corepressors. Supports the core repression mechanism and corepressor binding.

title: A network of interacting transcriptional regulators involved in Drosophila neural fate specification revealed by the yeast two-hybrid system.
review_notes: Verified; Hairy interacts directly with Groucho but not with the tested proneural/E(spl)/Da bHLH proteins. Supports transcription corepressor binding and informs the dimerization caveat.

title: Drosophila CtBP: a Hairy-interacting protein required for embryonic segmentation and hairy-mediated transcriptional repression.
review_notes: Directly on Hairy: dCtBP binds a C-terminal region of Hairy and is required for Hairy-mediated repression and segmentation. Supports transcription corepressor binding and the pair-rule role.

title: Groucho and dCtBP mediate separate pathways of transcriptional repression in the Drosophila embryo.
review_notes: Verified; Hairy-mediated repression in vivo depends on the WRPW/Groucho interaction rather than the weak dCtBP motif. Supports Groucho as the dominant corepressor and the core repressor function.

title: UniProtKB P14003 (HAIR_DROME): Protein hairy
review_notes: UniProt record for P14003. Its SUBUNIT block records the gro (Groucho) and Topors interactions and its INTERACTION block resolves the WITH/FROM accessions carried by the GOA protein-binding rows, which is what anchors the corepressor-binding MODIFY calls on the IPI annotations whose cached papers do not themselves name the partner.

title: Subdividing cell populations in the developing limbs of Drosophila: do wing veins and leg segments define units of growth control?
review_notes: No abstract is present in the local publication cache, and PubMed returns none for this record either, so the statements behind the anterior/posterior lineage restriction and wing disc patterning annotations could not be inspected.

title: The development of the Drosophila genital disc.
review_notes: A review of genital disc development; it is the right anchor for the analia development annotation but a weak one for leg disc morphogenesis, which is annotated from the same reference.

title: Molecular organization and embryonic expression of the hedgehog gene involved in cell-cell communication in segmental patterning of Drosophila.
review_notes: Correct paper and a genuine hh study, but it is cited in GOA for nucleus and cytoplasm localisation of the Hh protein, whereas what the paper reports is localisation of the hh RNA ("This RNA is localized predominantly within nuclei until stage 10"). The same conflation has propagated into the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statement.

title: Cell migration and programmed cell death of Drosophila germ cells.
review_notes: A 2003 review cited for germ cell attraction by Hh. The claim it transmits was specifically tested and not supported by PMID:19389345, and FlyBase records a NOT annotation for primordial germ cell migration on that basis.

title: Evolution in black and white: genetic control of pigment patterns in Drosophila.
review_notes: No abstract is present in the local publication cache, and PubMed returns none for this record either, so the statement behind the developmental pigmentation annotation could not be inspected.

title: Coming to our senses.
review_notes: The identifier resolves to the intended paper, a short review of sensory organ development, but its abstract discusses Decapentaplegic, Wingless, ecdysone, atonal and eyeless and does not mention Hedgehog. It is a weak anchor for the compound eye photoreceptor differentiation annotation, which is better supported by the morphogenetic furrow work in PMID:8252628.

title: Hedgehog does not guide migrating Drosophila germ cells.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. A targeted re-examination that repeated the earlier critical experiments; it is the anchor for the NOT annotation on primordial germ cell migration.

title: Genetic and biochemical definition of the Hedgehog receptor.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. Establishes that Ihog and Ptc together constitute the Drosophila Hh receptor and that both are required for high-affinity Hh binding - the point at which fly receptor biology differs from the vertebrate SHH-PTCH1 interaction.

title: Crystal structure of a Hedgehog autoprocessing domain: homology between Hedgehog and self-splicing proteins.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. Crystal structure of the Drosophila Hedgehog autoprocessing domain with active-site identification and mutagenesis; the primary evidence for the autoprocessing and cholesterol transfer core functions, and the source of the intein-homology observation that the InterPro2GO intein-splicing mapping over-reads.

title: Rotation and asymmetry of the mitotic spindle direct asymmetric cell division in the developing central nervous system.
review_notes: Live-imaging study of neuroblast spindle rotation and anaphase spindle asymmetry directing ACD; supports the spindle-orientation role. PubMed-verified title/abstract match.

title: Multiple signalling pathways establish cell fate and cell number in Drosophila malpighian tubules.
review_notes: Malpighian tubule tip-cell study (wingless/Notch/Numb). Cached abstract does not name insc; the IMP presumably rests on full-text data not available here. Relevance to insc plausible (asymmetric tip-cell division; insc expressed in Malpighian tubules) but unverified.

title: Mechanism of glia-neuron cell-fate switch in the Drosophila thoracic neuroblast 6-4 lineage.
review_notes: Shows insc (and miranda) mutations disrupt Prospero behavior and the glia-neuron fate switch in NB6-4T; supports cortical/ACD role. Abstract explicitly names inscuteable.

title: Genetics of heart development.
review_notes: Cited (TAS) for insc sensory organ development, but this is a review of cardiac/heart development in zebrafish and Drosophila; the abstract does not mention inscuteable or sensory organs. Appears to be a wrong/mis-applied citation for this annotation; the sensory-organ-development role itself is real but should be sourced to a primary pI/SOP study (e.g. PMID:12526793).

title: Inscuteable-dependent apical localization of the microtubule-binding protein Cornetto suggests a role in asymmetric cell division.
review_notes: Directly on insc; documents apical-cortex localization (interphase-metaphase), the Insc-Cornetto interaction (2-hybrid), and inscuteable-dependent apical protein localization. PubMed-verified.

title: Apical complex genes control mitotic spindle geometry and relative size of daughter cells in Drosophila neuroblast and pI asymmetric divisions.
review_notes: Apical-complex (incl. insc pathway) control of spindle geometry and daughter-cell size in NB and pI (sensory organ precursor) divisions; supports ACD and sensory-organ roles. PubMed-verified.

title: Microtubule-induced Pins/Galphai cortical polarity in Drosophila neuroblasts.
review_notes: Defines the Inscuteable/Par pathway acting from prophase in parallel to a microtubule/Khc-73/Dlg pathway; supports apical Insc/Par localization and function. PubMed-verified.

title: Galphai generates multiple Pins activation states to link cortical polarity and spindle orientation in Drosophila neuroblasts.
review_notes: Full text states Galphai-bound Pins (GoLoco1) recruits Insc to the apical cortex; supports apical localization and the Insc-Pins(raps) relationship. PubMed/PMC-verified.

title: Genetic analysis of Drosophila melanogaster susceptibility to intestinal Vibrio cholerae infection.
review_notes: Genome-wide V. cholerae susceptibility screen; insc mutant increased susceptibility, but the authors explicitly state the immune role was not characterized. Correctly cited for a weak, peripheral IMP. Full text (PMC) confirms the insc hit.

title: Ancestry-independent fate specification and plasticity in the developmental timing of a typical Drosophila neuronal lineage.
review_notes: GOA reference for insc regulation of asymmetric cell division and regulation of nervous system development, but the cached abstract and full text concern the T-box gene mid in the RP2/sib lineage and do not describe insc experiments. Its specific support for these insc annotations could not be verified; the annotated functions are independently well established.

title: On the roles of Notch, Delta, kuzbanian, and inscuteable during the development of Drosophila embryonic neuroblast lineages.
review_notes: Directly on insc; shows lineage/stage-dependent requirement of insc for sibling cell fate specification via ACD feeding differential Notch. PubMed-verified.

title: Inscuteable and NuMA proteins bind competitively to Leu-Gly-Asn repeat-enriched protein (LGN) during asymmetric cell divisions.
review_notes: Crystal structure of Drosophila Pins(LGN) TPR bound to Insc peptide; defines the adaptor bridge (Par3 to Pins/Galphai) and raps-insc complex. Core molecular-function and complex-membership evidence. PMC full text verified.

title: The mutant not enough muscles (nem) reveals reduction of the Drosophila embryonic muscle pattern.
review_notes: nem is an allele of insc (UniProt/FlyBase synonym). Documents somatic-muscle and PNS (chordotonal) defects - peripheral, pleiotropic insc phenotypes. PubMed-verified.

title: inscuteable, a neural precursor gene of Drosophila, encodes a candidate for a cytoskeleton adaptor protein.
review_notes: Founding characterization of insc; apical submembranous localization, candidate cytoskeleton adaptor, expression in neuroblasts/trachea/Malpighian tubules. PubMed-verified.

title: Role of inscuteable in orienting asymmetric cell divisions in Drosophila.
review_notes: Foundational functional study; insc required for spindle orientation and Numb/Prospero localization; apical-cortex localization; ectopic insc reorients spindles. PubMed-verified.

title: Inscuteable and Staufen mediate asymmetric localization and segregation of prospero RNA during Drosophila neuroblast cell divisions.
review_notes: Insc nucleates the apical complex; required for protein localization, spindle orientation, and (with Staufen) prospero RNA localization; apical colocalization. PubMed-verified.

title: Identification of Miranda protein domains regulating asymmetric cortical localization, cargo binding, and cortical release.
review_notes: Miranda-focused study that documents Inscuteable among the apically localized proteins in interphase neuroblasts (apical cortex localization); notes Insc uniquely stays apical while other factors move basally. PubMed-verified.

title: The transmembrane molecule kekkon 1 acts in a feedback loop to negatively regulate the activity of the Drosophila EGF receptor during oogenesis.
review_notes: Founding study identifying Kek1 as an EGFR inhibitor acting in a negative feedback loop during oogenesis, with physical association of the extracellular/TM domains with EGFR. Directly supports the core MF and BP annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Guidance of cell migration by EGF receptor signaling during Drosophila oogenesis.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only and concerns EGFR/Gurken guidance of border-cell migration; the abstract does not mention kek1, so the kek1-specific GO:0042059 IMP annotation cannot be verified from the available text (marked UNDECIDED).

title: Mechanism of activation of the Drosophila EGF Receptor by the TGFalpha ligand Gurken during oogenesis.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only and concerns Gurken/Star/Brho-mediated EGFR activation; the abstract does not mention kek1, so the GO:0030547 IDA annotation cannot be verified from the available text (marked UNDECIDED).

title: Mechanism of inhibition of the Drosophila and mammalian EGF receptors by the transmembrane protein Kekkon 1.
review_notes: Key mechanistic study; LRRs mediate direct DER association, the cytoplasmic tail directs apical localization, Kek1 forms a heterodimer with DER, and in mammalian assays it inhibits ligand binding, autophosphorylation and ERK activation across ErbB receptors. Supports MF (binding, inhibitor), BP and localization annotations.

title: Knockouts of Kekkon1 define sequence elements essential for Drosophila epidermal growth factor receptor inhibition.
review_notes: Loss-of-function alleles map EGFR binding to LRR1/LRR2 (class I, affinity) and localization to class II alleles, and demonstrate that Kek1 inhibits EGFR in eye development. Supports the negative-regulation and binding annotations.

title: Conservation of an inhibitor of the epidermal growth factor receptor, Kekkon1, in dipterans.
review_notes: Establishes kek1 as a transcriptional EGFR target attenuating the receptor, expressed in dorsal follicle cells during D/V patterning, conserved among dipterans but absent from vertebrates and Caenorhabditis. Supports localization and BP context.

title: Bipartite inhibition of Drosophila epidermal growth factor receptor by the extracellular and transmembrane domains of Kekkon1.
review_notes: Demonstrates the bipartite mechanism (LRRs sufficient for binding, juxta/transmembrane region required for inhibition) acting via DER domain V; inhibition is unique to Kek1 among family members. Supports MF binding/inhibitor and BP annotations.

title: The Drosophila kekkon genes: novel members of both the leucine-rich repeat and immunoglobulin superfamilies expressed in the CNS.
review_notes: Original identification of kek1/kek2 as transmembrane LRR+Ig cell-surface proteins expressed in differentiating CNS neurons and in follicle cells (D/V gradient); kek1 deletion has no overt phenotype (family redundancy). Supports architecture and predicted plasma-membrane localization.

title: Molecular analysis of the klarsicht gene and its role in nuclear migration within differentiating cells of the Drosophila eye.
review_notes: Cloning of klar; perinuclear localization; null mutants viable with eye defects. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Epithelial tube morphology is determined by the polarized growth and delivery of apical membrane.
review_notes: klar mediates apical membrane delivery in salivary gland tube morphogenesis. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The functions of Klarsicht and nuclear lamin in developmentally regulated nuclear migrations of photoreceptor cells in the Drosophila eye.
review_notes: Klar needed to connect the MTOC to the nucleus; lamin needed for Klar perinuclear localization.

title: Drosophila klarsicht has distinct subcellular localization domains for nuclear envelope and microtubule localization in the eye.
review_notes: KASH domain needed for perinuclear localization and function; N-terminal region localizes to apical microtubules.

title: Organelle-specific control of intracellular transport: distinctly targeted isoforms of the regulator Klar.
review_notes: Isoform-specific targeting of Klar to the nuclear envelope (KASH) or lipid droplets (alternative exon).

title: A molecular link between FGF and Dpp signaling in branch-specific migration of the Drosophila trachea.
review_notes: Tracheal mutant screen; the cached text is partial and does not mention klar, although Europe PMC full-text search finds klarsicht in the article. The klar tracheal phenotype could not be checked here.

title: Developmental control of nuclear morphogenesis and anchoring by charleston, identified in a functional genomic screen of Drosophila cellularisation.
review_notes: Cellularisation RNAi screen focused on charleston; the abstract mentions organelle transport genes but not klar; full text not available here.

title: Drosophila klaroid encodes a SUN domain protein required for Klarsicht localization to the nuclear envelope and nuclear migration in the eye.
review_notes: Klaroid (SUN) tethers Klar to the nuclear envelope; koi and klar mutants phenocopy; both needed in R cells and cone cells. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Organelle positioning in muscles requires cooperation between two KASH proteins and microtubules.
review_notes: Klar and Msp300 KASH proteins cooperate for myonuclear spacing via an Msp300 nuclear ring and astral microtubules.

title: Klar ensures thermal robustness of oskar localization by restraining RNP motility.
review_notes: Klar-beta associates with kinesin-1 (co-IP) and restrains oskar RNP motility in oocytes.

title: Outer nuclear membrane protein Kuduk modulates the LINC complex and nuclear envelope architecture.
review_notes: Kuduk associates with the KASH domains of Klar and Msp300 and regulates LINC complex levels.

title: Developmental regulation of vesicle transport in Drosophila embryos: forces and kinetics.
review_notes: Original klar lipid droplet transport phenotype (force measurements); also nuclear migration in the eye. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Ethanol sensitivity and tolerance in long-term memory mutants of Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The klg allele (ruslan) is among the LTM mutants scored; ruslan shows increased ethanol sensitivity and reduced (rapid+chronic) tolerance. Supports the IMP behavioral response to ethanol annotation (a non-core, pleiotropic phenotype). Paper uses original mutant names; ruslan=klg per PMID:19104051.

title: The Drosophila cell adhesion molecule klingon is required for long-term memory formation and is regulated by Notch.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Establishes that rus is a klg allele encoding a homophilic CAM; Klg is acutely required for LTM but not ARM, its levels rise on LTM induction, and it acts downstream of Notch. Directly supports the homophilic adhesion, LTM (positive) and ARM (negated) annotations.

title: The long-term memory trace formed in the Drosophila α/β mushroom body neurons is abolished in long-term memory mutants.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Confirms the klg mutant (D0417) as an LTM mutant that abolishes the α/β mushroom-body LTM calcium trace; corroborates the acute LTM requirement of klg. Klg is one of 26 diverse LTM mutants, so this is supporting rather than mechanistic for klg specifically.

title: An extracellular interactome of immunoglobulin and LRR proteins reveals receptor-ligand networks.
review_notes: Source of the IPI protein-binding annotation (Drosophila IgSF/LRR extracellular interactome; UniProt IntAct records Klg/Q9VCT4 binding cDIP/Q9VDD5). The cached full text does not name klg/cDIP (pairwise hits are in supplementary tables), so no klg-specific verbatim quote is available here; the annotation is sharpened from bare protein binding to cell adhesion molecule binding.

title: klingon, a novel member of the Drosophila immunoglobulin superfamily, is required for the development of the R7 photoreceptor neuron.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available:false) but the abstract itself establishes the core findings: three C2-type Ig domains + one FN3 repeat, GPI membrane attachment, homophilic adhesion in S2 cells, and an essential role in R7 photoreceptor development. Primary reference for the core adhesion and R7 annotations.

title: Cell-cell interaction during Drosophila embryogenesis: novel mechanisms and molecules.
review_notes: Review; cited as the TAS source for the tracheal epithelial cell migration annotation, but no abstract text is available in the cache so the specific claim could not be verified against it. The underlying biology is supported by PMID:9811580.

title: dCtBP-dependent and -independent repression activities of the Drosophila Knirps protein.
review_notes: Primary structure-function study of Knirps repression; abstract available in cache. Directly supports the repressor MF (GO:0001227) and the dCtBP corepressor binding.

title: Control of endoreduplication domains in the Drosophila gut by the knirps and knirps-related genes.
review_notes: Primary paper on the gut endoreduplication role; abstract available. Shows the process is endoreduplication (endocycle), supporting the MODIFY of GO:0007088 to GO:0032875.

title: A protein interaction map of Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Genome-wide two-hybrid proteome map; abstract available. The cached record does not name the specific Knirps partner, but the GOA row supplies it as WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as dCtBP (kni-uniprot.txt:97), so the bare protein-binding annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than an uninformative non-core keep.

title: The evolution of arthropod segmentation mechanisms.
review_notes: Review of arthropod segmentation used as the TAS source for the trunk segmentation and A-P axis annotations. Supports gap-gene control of segmentation at a general level; kni's explicit gap-gene identity is documented in PMID:18271625.

title: Structurally related Arabidopsis ANGUSTIFOLIA is functionally distinct from the transcriptional corepressor CtBP.
review_notes: Arabidopsis ANGUSTIFOLIA vs dCtBP; abstract-only cache, hence UNVERIFIED as a statement about the cached text, since a direct Knirps interaction is not recoverable from the abstract. Partner identity does not depend on it, because the GOA row carries WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as dCtBP (kni-uniprot.txt:97), so the annotation is a MODIFY to GO:0001222 rather than UNDECIDED.

title: Transcription factors bind thousands of active and inactive regions in the Drosophila blastoderm.
review_notes: Full text available; explicitly names kni as a gap gene and reports in vivo Knirps ChIP. Supports the IDA DNA-binding TF activity and the trunk/A-P segmentation role.

title: Groucho corepressor functions as a cofactor for the Knirps short-range transcriptional repressor.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports Groucho (corepressor) binding, the short-range repression mechanism, and regulation of even-skipped.

title: A Comprehensive Drosophila melanogaster Transcription Factor Interactome.
review_notes: TF-TF interactome; full text available. Cited for a Knirps protein-binding IPI whose partner is supplied by the GOA row as WITH/FROM = UniProtKB:O46036, resolved by the fetched UniProt record as dCtBP (kni-uniprot.txt:97) - a corepressor, hence the MODIFY to GO:0001222. The screen's nominal restriction to sequence-specific TFs is not a safe basis for inferring the partner class, since dCtBP is itself recorded as a partner detected here; the curated WITH/FROM accession is what carries the call.

title: The transcription factors KNIRPS and KNIRPS RELATED control cell migration and branch morphogenesis during Drosophila tracheal development.
review_notes: Primary tracheal-development paper; abstract available. Supports the tracheal cell migration/branching role and direct repression of spalt.

title: UniProtKB P10734 (KNIR_DROME): Zygotic gap protein knirps
review_notes: UniProt record for P10734; confirms repressor function, nuclear localization, the NR-type C4 zinc-finger DBD, NR0 (LBD-less orphan) subfamily membership, and dCtBP/gro interactions. Used to justify the nucleus, zinc-binding, DNA-binding, and NR-activity MODIFY calls.

title: Drosophila klaroid encodes a SUN domain protein required for Klarsicht localization to the nuclear envelope and nuclear migration in the eye.
review_notes: Identifies Klaroid as the SUN protein that tethers Klarsicht; koi mutants lack eye nuclear migration. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The role of Drosophila Lamin C in muscle function and gene expression.
review_notes: Lamin C muscle study; source of the nuclear periphery IDA; abstract does not mention Koi. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Organelle positioning in muscles requires cooperation between two KASH proteins and microtubules.
review_notes: Myonuclear positioning by Klar and Msp300; koi mutants lose myonuclear rows. Full text.

title: Microtubule-driven nuclear rotations promote meiotic chromosome dynamics.
review_notes: Koi and Klar co-localize with centromeres and are required for germline chromosome motions and pairing. Abstract-only in cache; PubMed-verified via DOI.

title: Outer nuclear membrane protein Kuduk modulates the LINC complex and nuclear envelope architecture.
review_notes: Kuduk regulates LINC levels; Koi determines NE localization of KASH proteins; koi loss causes myonuclear clustering. Full text; PubMed-verified via DOI.

title: Ari-1 Regulates Myonuclear Organization Together with Parkin and Is Associated with Aortic Aneurysms.
review_notes: Ari-1 mono-ubiquitinates Koi; koi mutants show myonuclear clustering; Koi at NE. Full text.

title: A perinuclear microtubule-organizing centre controls nuclear positioning and basement membrane secretion.
review_notes: Source of UniProt MTOC/perinuclear location for Koi; shows Koi at the NE with only mild fat-body nuclear-positioning defects. Full text; PubMed-verified.

title: Premeiotic pairing of homologous chromosomes during Drosophila male meiosis.
review_notes: Koi/Klar LINC required for premeiotic centromere pairing in males; pairing reduced in koi mutants. Full text; PubMed-verified via DOI.

title: Regulation of Notch signalling by non-visual beta-arrestin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache. Directly supports the Notch-Deltex-Kurtz complex and ubiquitination-dependent Notch degradation (basis of GO:0045746 IGI and the two Reactome Notch reactions).

title: Exploratory activity in Drosophila requires the kurtz nonvisual arrestin.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports the neuronal requirement of krz for exploratory locomotor behavior (GO:0035641 IMP).

title: Regulation of smoothened by Drosophila G-protein-coupled receptor kinases.
review_notes: Full text available; primarily about Gprk2, but explicitly shows Krz over-expression reduces Smo (first evidence arrestins regulate Smo in flies), supporting GO:0048260. Notes krz LOF has no Smo phenotype.

title: β-arrestin Kurtz inhibits MAPK and Toll signalling in Drosophila development.
review_notes: Full text available; primary source for Krz-ERK binding/sequestration (MAPK, GO:0043409, GO:0120177, GO:0051019), Krz-Cactus binding and Toll inhibition (GO:0045751), and cytoplasmic localization.

title: Role of the Drosophila non-visual ß-arrestin kurtz in hedgehog signalling.
review_notes: Full text available; primary source for Krz-Smo binding, clathrin/proteasome-dependent Smo internalization and degradation (GO:0002031, GO:0031648, GO:0045879) and cytoplasmic localization. Antagonism of Hh only on over-expression.

title: Regulation of Toll signaling and inflammation by β-arrestin and the SUMO protease Ulp1.
review_notes: Full text available; supports Krz limiting Toll signalling/inflammation in larvae via the SUMO protease Ulp1 (GO:0045751 IMP).

title: SUMO regulates the activity of Smoothened and Costal-2 in Drosophila Hedgehog signaling.
review_notes: Full text available; supports excess Krz inhibiting Smo sumoylation/accumulation (GO:0045879) and Krz facilitating the Smo-Ulp1 interaction that promotes desumoylation (GO:0060189).

title: Roles of the Drosophila NudE protein in kinetochore function and centrosome migration.
review_notes: Full text: localization (kinetochore, spindle, nuclear envelope, spindle envelope; not centrosome) and null-mutant phenotypes in neuroblasts and spermatocytes.

title: Microtubules and Lis-1/NudE/dynein regulate invasive cell-on-cell migration in Drosophila.
review_notes: Border cell RNAi screen; cell-autonomous NudE requirement.

title: A genetic screen based on in vivo RNA imaging reveals centrosome-independent mechanisms for localizing gurken transcripts in Drosophila.
review_notes: Allele 11R2 (Q33 stop) of nudE causes oocyte misspecification; confirmed with nudE39A clones.

title: Dendrite arborization requires the dynein cofactor NudE.
review_notes: Full text: dendrite arborization, Golgi outpost co-transport, axonal MT polarity; Lis1 rescue.

title: The Krüppel-Like Factor Dar1 Determines Multipolar Neuron Morphology.
review_notes: Full text: nudE knockdown displaces neuronal nuclei from dendrite arbors; epistasis with dar1.

title: Nde1 promotes Lis1-mediated activation of dynein.
review_notes: Human Nde1 reconstitution (full text cached); basis for ISS to the fly ortholog.

title: Pelle Modulates dFoxO-Mediated Cell Death in Drosophila.
review_notes: Found via the Falcon deep-research cross-check and read in the cached full text. Not in GOA; used for a suggested question rather than a NEW annotation.

title: Maintaining Toll signaling in Drosophila brain is required to sustain autophagy for dopamine neuron survival.
review_notes: Found via the Falcon deep-research cross-check; cell-culture evidence with overexpressed TIR domains; not used for an annotation.

title: Subdividing cell populations in the developing limbs of Drosophila: do wing veins and leg segments define units of growth control?
review_notes: Cited as the TAS source for GO:0048099. The cached record contains the citation and DOI but no abstract text at all, so the statement attributed to it cannot be checked here. The identifier resolves to a real Dev Biol article whose subject - subdivision of the developing limb into growth-control units - is plausible for the claim, but the assertion is left unverified rather than marked VERIFIED. The A-P boundary role itself is independently supported by PMID:25231763.

title: Transcriptional regulation of atonal required for Drosophila larval eye development by concerted action of eyes absent, sine oculis and hedgehog signaling independent of fused kinase and cubitus interruptus.
review_notes: Correct paper for the Bolwig's organ annotation. Abstract-only in the cache and framed around hh, eya and so rather than ptc, so the ptc genotypes could not be inspected; the annotation is kept as non-core on the curator's full-text reading.

title: Hedgehog induces opposite changes in turnover and subcellular localization of patched and smoothened.
review_notes: Directly establishes both the plasma membrane location of Patched and its destabilisation of Smoothened in the absence of ligand, and is the source UniProt cites for the Cell membrane annotation. Also the earliest clear statement that the restraint is likely indirect.

title: Sticking together and sorting things out: adhesion as a force in development.
review_notes: The identifier is correct for the article named, but the article is a Nature Reviews Genetics review about differential adhesion and cell sorting, not a source for ptc function in wing disc A-P patterning. It touches compartment boundaries only in passing. The GO:0048100 term is retained on independent evidence (PMID:8898207), not on this citation.

title: Hedgehog acts as a somatic stem cell factor in the Drosophila ovary.
review_notes: Supports a ptc-dependent effect on the ovarian somatic stem cell pool. The phenotype is stem cell proliferation, which is why the generic GO:0007346 term was modified to GO:0072091.

title: A positive role for patched-smoothened signaling in promoting cell proliferation during normal head development in Drosophila.
review_notes: The loss-of-function phenotype in the eye-antennal disc is sound, but the paper's central claim - a non-canonical positive Ptc-Smo route acting through the Activin receptor Baboon - runs against the overwhelming evidence that Patched represses Smoothened, and has not been widely corroborated. The annotation is kept on the phenotype, not on the model.

title: Understanding human cancer using Drosophila: Tid47, a cytosolic product of the DnaJ-like tumor suppressor gene l2Tid, is a novel molecular partner of patched related to skin cancer.
review_notes: Correctly identified and does report a Patched interaction, which UniProt records as a SUBUNIT feature. Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation, which this review removes as uninformative.

title: Stability and association of Smoothened, Costal2 and Fused with Cubitus interruptus are regulated by Hedgehog.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache and written around Smo, Cos2, Fu and Ci. Supports the pathway context for the ptc annotation; the ptc-specific data are in the full text the curator read.

title: Hedgehog signal transduction via Smoothened association with a cytoplasmic complex scaffolded by the atypical kinesin, Costal-2.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Establishes the Costal-2-scaffolded complex that constitutively suppresses the pathway; the ptc IDA rests on full-text panels not visible here.

title: Drosophila Smoothened phosphorylation sites essential for Hedgehog signal transduction.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Defines the Smoothened phosphorylation cluster that reports relief of Patched repression.

title: Patched regulation of axon guidance is by specifying neural identity in the Drosophila nerve cord.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and its own conclusion is the reason the axon guidance annotation is marked as over-annotated: the defect follows from mis-specification of the pioneer neuron vMP2 rather than from any guidance activity of Patched.

title: Allocation and specification of the genital disc precursor cells in Drosophila.
review_notes: Names patched among the segment polarity genes required for allocation of the genital disc precursor cells. Supports a non-core developmental annotation.

title: Role of the Drosophila patched gene in positional signalling.
review_notes: Foundational. Establishes ptc as a permissive repressor antagonised by hedgehog and proposes, correctly, that Patched is the Hedgehog receptor acting by ligand-dependent inactivation.

title: The ihog cell-surface proteins bind Hedgehog and mediate pathway activation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache and centred on Ihog; the abstract nevertheless describes Hedgehog binding to cells coexpressing Ptc, which is the assay behind the ptc IDA to GO:0097108.

title: Epidermal growth factor receptor and transforming growth factor-beta signaling contributes to variation for wing shape in Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Correctly identified, but weak support for a ptc wing morphogenesis annotation: ptc is one of 43 loci scored as heterozygous insertional mutations in a quantitative morphometric survey, with no analysis of ptc function. The term is retained on independent grounds.

title: A large complex containing Patched and Smoothened initiates Hedgehog signaling in Drosophila.
review_notes: Reports co-immunoprecipitation and co-fractionation of Patched with Smoothened, Ci and Sex-lethal. Establishes co-membership of a large complex but does not distinguish direct from indirect association, which is why it is cited both for the removed protein-binding row and as the counter point in the GO:0005119 review.

title: Patched, the receptor of Hedgehog, is a lipoprotein receptor.
review_notes: Full text available and internally well controlled. Supports the lipoprotein particle receptor activity, the endocytic vesicle location and the lipid homeostasis annotation, and the authors themselves separate these from Hedgehog signal transduction using the SSD and Ptc14 separation-of-function alleles.

title: Genetic and biochemical definition of the Hedgehog receptor.
review_notes: Full text available. Defines the Patched-Ihog receptor and is explicit that no direct binding of Hedgehog to solubilised Patched alone was detectable, a caveat carried into the GO:0097108 review and resolved by the later genetics of PMID:25231763.

title: Dynamic phosphorylation of the kinesin Costal-2 in vivo reveals requirement of fused kinase activity for all levels of hedgehog signalling.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Provides the in situ readout of graded Hedgehog transduction against which Patched-dependent repression is measured.

title: A genetic screen for mutations affecting gonad formation in Drosophila reveals a role for the slit/robo pathway.
review_notes: Full text available; ptc appears as the com4 compaction-defect group of the screen. Supports a non-core developmental annotation without defining a gonad-specific activity.

title: Distinct phosphorylations on kinesin costal-2 mediate differential hedgehog signaling strength.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Supports the graded-signalling context in which Patched repression sets the low end of the response.

title: Non-cell autonomous control of apoptosis by ligand-independent Hedgehog signaling in Drosophila.
review_notes: Correctly cited. Its own finding - that ptc mutant cells do not protect themselves but protect neighbours through Notch and Diap-1 - is why the apoptosis annotation is marked as over-annotated.

title: Activation of Smurf E3 ligase promoted by smoothened regulates hedgehog signaling through targeting patched turnover.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes Smurf-dependent ubiquitination of Patched at K1261 and the feedback loop controlling Patched turnover; UniProt records the K1261 isopeptide bond from this work.

title: Hedgehog is a positive regulator of FGF signalling during embryonic tracheal cell migration.
review_notes: Full text available. ptc mutants are used as a Hedgehog gain-of-function tool and the migration effect is stated to be non-autonomous, so the annotation is kept only as a non-core consequence.

title: Cilia-mediated hedgehog signaling in Drosophila.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but independently corroborated: UniProt curates the cilium membrane location for ptc from this same paper. The location is real but restricted to olfactory sensory neurons, one of the few ciliated Drosophila cell types.

title: Ihog and Boi elicit Hh signaling via Ptc but do not aid Ptc in sequestering the Hh ligand.
review_notes: Decisive for two annotations in this review: it shows that Patched retains and sequesters Hedgehog without Ihog or Boi, which grounds GO:0097108 on ptc itself, and that the co-receptors act by letting Hedgehog inhibit Patched, which grounds GO:0045879.

title: Control of the dynamics and homeostasis of the Drosophila Hedgehog receptor Patched by two C2-WW-HECT-E3 Ubiquitin ligases.
review_notes: Directly about ptc. Shows that NEDD4 and SU(DX) tune Patched accumulation and that PY-motif mutation blocks internalisation without abolishing signalling activity, separating trafficking from repression.

title: PI(4)P Promotes Phosphorylation and Conformational Change of Smoothened through Interaction with Its C-terminal Tail.
review_notes: Full text available. The source for the ptc PI(4)P binding annotation, with an SSD-deletion negative control, and for the explicit statement that Patched is unlikely to inhibit Smoothened by direct association.

title: The Hippo pathway acts downstream of the Hedgehog signaling to regulate follicle stem cell maintenance in the Drosophila ovary.
review_notes: Full text available. Supports a directionally correct but entirely indirect ptc effect on Hippo signalling, via Hedgehog acting upstream of the Hippo cassette.

title: Cytoneme-mediated cell-cell contacts for Hedgehog reception.
review_notes: Full text available. Localises Patched to the basal membrane and to receiving cytonemes, and identifies cytoneme contact sites as where reception occurs, refining the plasma membrane annotation.

title: Quantitative microscopy of the Drosophila ovary shows multiple niche signals specify progenitor cell fate.
review_notes: Full text available. ptc mutant follicle stem cell clones give supernumerary, incompletely differentiated stalk cells, supporting the follicle cell development annotation as a non-core consequence of derepressed Hedgehog signalling.

title: Protein association changes in the Hedgehog signaling complex mediate differential signaling strength.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache and centred on Smo, Gprk2 and Fused. Supports the pathway context for the ptc annotation rather than a ptc-specific observation visible here.

title: Dissection of the microRNA Network Regulating Hedgehog Signaling in Drosophila.
review_notes: Full text available. Contains explicit ptc knockdown data - increased Smoothened protein and expanded Ci activator and Collier domains - that directly support the negative regulation annotation.

title: Phosphatidic acid binding to Patched contributes to the inhibition of Smoothened and Hedgehog signaling in Drosophila wing development.
review_notes: Full text available. Binding assays plus a structure-function series in which PA-motif mutants lose the ability to repress Smoothened; the strongest fly evidence tying a Patched lipid interaction to its defining activity.

title: Dual roles for patched in sequestering and transducing Hedgehog.
review_notes: Foundational. Separates the transduction and ligand-sequestration roles of Patched and is the cited source for both GO:0008158 and GO:0045879 by IMP.

title: The role of segment polarity genes during early oogenesis in Drosophila.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Supports the genetic interaction with hh in the germarium and the somatic expression of ptc. It is also the source of the GO:0045169 fusome colocalization, which the abstract does not mention and which this review leaves UNDECIDED.

title: Hedgehog stimulates maturation of Cubitus interruptus into a labile transcriptional activator.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache and centred on Fused and Su(fu). Supplies the transcriptional endpoint against which Patched repression is scored; the ptc genetics are in the full text.

title: A fine-structure genetic and chemical study of the enzyme alkaline phosphatase of E. coli. I. Purification and characterization of alkaline phosphatase.

title: RELEASE OF ALKALINE PHOSPHATASE FROM CELLS OF ESCHERICHIA COLI UPON LYSOZYME SPHEROPLAST FORMATION.
review_notes: The 1964 spheroplast-release experiment that established the periplasm as a compartment and alkaline phosphatase as its marker. Correctly cited for both periplasmic space rows; the outer-membrane-bounded child term is the more informative of the two.

title: Alkaline phosphatase of Escherichia coli: a zinc metalloenzyme.
review_notes: Identified the enzyme as a zinc metalloenzyme, the origin of the metal dependence that the family review traces from phoA through to the human isozymes.

title: A new activity for an old enzyme: Escherichia coli bacterial alkaline phosphatase is a phosphite-dependent hydrogenase.
review_notes: Genuine and carefully done: transposon genetics, purification and N-terminal sequencing establish that BAP is the phn-independent phosphite oxidase, and that the reaction evolves molecular hydrogen. Correctly cited for GO:0030613, whose definition fits the reaction literally. Also cited for GO:0033748, whose definition (H2 + A = AH2) does not cleanly match a reaction with water as co-substrate; that row is marked over-annotated. The paper's own specific-activity figures place the side activity two to three orders of magnitude below the phosphatase reaction.

title: Structural basis for signal-sequence recognition by the translocase motor SecA as determined by NMR.
review_notes: Correctly cited for a real interaction between SecA and the phoA signal peptide. Relevance to phoA's own function is low: it concerns export of the precursor, and the signal peptide is cleaved from the mature enzyme.

title: Detecting folding intermediates of a protein as it passes through the bacterial translocation channel.
review_notes: Uses phoA as the model translocation substrate. Same assessment as the other Sec papers: real interaction, about export rather than catalysis.

title: Signal peptides are allosteric activators of the protein translocase.
review_notes: The clearest of the three translocase papers about why phoA appears in this literature: proPhoA was chosen as a SecB-independent substrate that requires SecA as its essential receptor. Correctly cited, but again about export.

title: From cell membrane to nucleotides: the phosphate regulon in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Torriani's review of the Pi regulon, and the source of the explicit statement that phoA is repressed by high environmental phosphate through the Pst operon and PhoR. Cached and verified; it is the basis of the proposed GO:0016036 annotation, which is the only substantive biological process this gene has.

title: Identification of protein phosphatase 1 as a regulator of the LRRK2 phosphorylation cycle.
review_notes: Cited as an IPI source for protein binding on E. coli phoA, but the paper is a human LRRK2 and protein phosphatase 1 study and the cached record does not mention alkaline phosphatase at all. The likeliest explanation is that commercial alkaline phosphatase was used as a dephosphorylation reagent and an automated interaction import attached it to phoA, but the full text is not available to confirm that. Marked unverified rather than wrong-identifier: the citation could not be confirmed, not shown to be wrong. The corresponding annotation is left UNDECIDED.

title: Control of the phoBR Regulon in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: The current authoritative review of PhoBR regulon control, cached with full text. Cited as a secondary reference for the phosphate-starvation annotation. It concerns the regulatory system rather than phoA itself, which is why the Torriani review carries the supporting quote.

title: Refined structure of alkaline phosphatase from Escherichia coli at 2.8 A resolution.
review_notes: The refined crystal structure, defining the fold and the trinuclear metal centre that the whole family shares, and the structural basis for the homodimer proposed as a new annotation here.

title: Specific recognition of coiled coils by infrared spectroscopy: analysis of the three structural domains of type III intermediate filament proteins.
review_notes: The most serious citation problem in this gene's record. Cited as the IDA source for two molecular function terms on E. coli alkaline phosphatase, but the paper is an infrared spectroscopy study of coiled-coil structure in desmin and neurofilament proteins, and the string "alkaline phosphatase" does not appear anywhere in the cached record. Its only contact with phosphatases is that neurofilament tail domains were examined in phosphorylated and dephosphorylated forms, which in 1996 would routinely have been achieved with alkaline phosphatase as a reagent. If that is the source, it supports neither term well: using an enzyme as a tool is not a characterisation of it. GO:0004035 survives on other evidence and was accepted; GO:0004721 has no other support and was left undecided pending a full-text check.

title: Deep research report: E. coli phoA / bacterial alkaline phosphatase (BAP)
review_notes: Automated literature synthesis (Edison/falcon provider), which arrived after the annotation review was first written and prompted one addition. Its most useful contribution is the clean separation of phoA as a Pho regulon *effector* from PhoR/PhoB as the *sensors*, which is what keeps the proposed GO:0016036 annotation from overclaiming. Its primary claims were checked against the cached Torriani review rather than accepted on their own.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Standard InterPro2GO pipeline reference, correctly applied; the terms it produces for this protein are accurate but sit above the level the direct evidence supports.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: All four IBA rows on this gene hold up. Two of them list P0A7Y0 in their own WITH/FROM, which is the expected marker of a node seeded in part by the target's own experimental annotations and is not circular.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by transferring manual GO annotations between related proteins based on shared sequence features

title: Interaction network containing conserved and essential protein complexes in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. A high-throughput interaction screen, so it establishes that the rnb interaction exists (UniProt records it at NbExp=2) but carries no information about its function. That is why the row it supports is retargeted to a binding term rather than to a functional one.

title: Catalytic mechanism of Escherichia coli ribonuclease III: kinetic and inhibitor evidence for the involvement of two magnesium ions in RNA phosphodiester hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached full text available via PMC549391. The best single reference for the enzyme's mechanism, architecture and substrate specificity, and the source of the magnesium ion binding IDA.

title: Localization, annotation, and comparison of the Escherichia coli K-12 proteome under two states of growth.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. A proteome-scale localization survey; relevant to the cellular component annotation rather than to function.

title: Protein abundance profiling of the Escherichia coli cytosol.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Independent corroboration of the cytosolic localization from a different strain and a different method than PMID:15911532.

title: YmdB: a stress-responsive ribonuclease-binding regulator of E. coli RNase III activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract states the binding site and the regulatory consequence, which is what the enzyme binding IPI needs.

title: CRISPR RNA maturation by trans-encoded small RNA and host factor RNase III.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached full text available via PMC3070239. Correctly cited and scientifically sound, but the organism is Streptococcus pyogenes, so it establishes nothing about the E. coli K-12 protein's role in its own host. Relevance is marked LOW for that reason: it is context for why a housekeeping RNase appears in CRISPR pathway models, not evidence for an annotation on P0A7Y0. No annotation in this review derives from it.

title: crRNA and tracrRNA guide Cas9-mediated DNA interference in Streptococcus thermophilus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached full text available via PMC3737341. Fetched during this review because UniProt cites it for two experimental findings of the entry. It is the closest thing to E. coli evidence for the CRISPR role and is still not evidence for an annotation: the CRISPR system is a transplanted Streptococcus thermophilus type II locus, and the same paper states that E. coli K-12's own type I-E system uses a Cas6 endonuclease for this step. Cited here for the scoped prose in the ribonuclease III activity reviews and in the notes, not as support for any term.

title: RNase III is required for localization to the nucleoid of the 5' pre-rRNA leader and for optimal induction of rRNA synthesis in E. coli.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached full text available via PMC3753927. Sound and relevant to the gene's rRNA role. GOA uses it for a cytosol IDA, which is not the obvious reading of a paper whose measurements are RNA-FISH on pre-rRNA; the EcoCyc curator read the full text and the annotation is accepted, with the caveat recorded in that row's review.

title: The first step in the functional inactivation of the Escherichia coli polynucleotide phosphorylase messenger is a ribonuclease III processing at the 5' end.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract carries the quantitative half-life and abundance results. The clearest demonstration that RNase III cleavage is a quantitative determinant of gene expression in E. coli.

title: T7 early RNAs and Escherichia coli ribosomal RNAs are cut from large precursor RNAs in vivo by ribonuclease 3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. The combination of an RNase III-deficient strain in vivo and reconstitution with purified enzyme in vitro is why this row justifies the general RNA processing term: its scope spans both phage mRNA and host rRNA.

title: RNase III cleavage is obligate for maturation but not for function of Escherichia coli pre-23S rRNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. The source of the rRNA processing IMP and the clearest statement of the gene's core role, including why its loss is tolerated.

title: RNase III cleavage of single-stranded RNA. Effect of ionic strength on the fideltiy of cleavage.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. The source of the homodimerization IPI. The title's "single-stranded RNA" refers to substrates such as T7 early RNA that are single-stranded overall but contain the duplex elements the enzyme recognises; it is not a claim that the enzyme cleaves unstructured RNA, and UniProt's function statement ("Digests double-stranded RNA formed within single-strand substrates") is the accurate reading.

title: Proteomic analysis of the Escherichia coli outer membrane.
review_notes: This outer-membrane proteomics paper does not directly support SucB cytosolic localization; the cytosol call rests on independent cytosolic proteomics and SucB's soluble OGDH role.

title: Alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complexes. VI. Dissociation and reconstitution of the dihydrolipoyl transacetylase of Escherichia coli.
review_notes: The cached record is an abstract-free citation stub, and its title foregrounds E. coli dihydrolipoyl transacetylase/AceF rather than SucB; full text would be needed to verify the two SucB experimental GOA rows citing this PMID.

title: Defining the roles of the periplasmic chaperones SurA, Skp, and DegP in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports SurA-YaeT interaction and periplasmic transit of OMP clients to YaeT/BAM. Only abstract-explicit claims were used because cached full text is unavailable.

title: Impact of holdase chaperones Skp and SurA on the folding of β-barrel outer-membrane proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-cached abstract directly supports SurA stabilization of a dynamic unfolded FhuA state during stepwise membrane insertion. Only abstract-explicit claims were used.
