title: Diversity of the biosynthesis pathway for threonylcarbamoyladenosine (t<sup>6</sup>A), a universal modification of tRNA
review_notes: The cached DOI record has no full text, so the YciO-specific finding could not be verified against a verbatim local source.

title: Proteins and DNA elements essential for the CRISPR adaptation process in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match the GOA reference. Supplies precisely what the IMP row claims - that Cas2 expressed alone does not expand the array and that Cas1 plus Cas2 does - so the requirement for this gene is established genetically and independently of the structural work.

title: Cas1-Cas2 complex formation mediates spacer acquisition during CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match the IntAct reference. This is the decisive paper for this gene: it establishes both halves of the adjudication - that Cas2's catalytic activity is dispensable, and that its assembly with Cas1 is not - and it is the paper the crispr_cas_adaptive_immunity module cites for the Cas2 annoton.

title: Integrase-mediated spacer acquisition during CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match. Not cited by any GOA row for P45956, and added because it is the paper that quantifies what Cas2 contributes: Cas1 alone integrates poorly, the complex integrates well, and Cas2 active-site mutants are unimpaired. That asymmetry is the evidential basis for assigning Cas2 a non-catalytic molecular function rather than none.

title: Intrinsic sequence specificity of the Cas1 integrase directs new spacer acquisition.
review_notes: Fetched and verified against PMC; title, authors and journal match. Added because it states the adaptor interpretation of Cas2 explicitly, shows that Cas2 contributes nothing to Cas1's branched-DNA chemistry or its specificity, and records the provenance of the endoribonuclease name in archaeal and Bacillus homologues rather than in the E. coli protein. Those three points carry the MODIFY argument and the name adjudication.

title: Foreign DNA capture during CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match the IntAct reference. Supplies the DNA-bound structures and the mutational data showing that Cas2's own arginines position the protospacer, which is what makes the adaptor assignment a statement about coordinated function rather than mere subunit membership, and it is the source for the molecular-ruler behaviour raised as a proposed term.

title: Asymmetric positioning of Cas1-2 complex and Integration Host Factor induced DNA bending guide the unidirectional homing of protospacer in CRISPR-Cas type I-E system.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match the ComplexPortal reference. Supports the two IDA rows: the purified Cas1-2 complex, of which Cas2 is a subunit, is assayed integrating a protospacer into leader-containing CRISPR DNA, with IHF identified as the host factor that makes integration unidirectional.

title: A dual function of the CRISPR-Cas system in bacterial antivirus immunity and DNA repair.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; the title, author list and journal match and the biochemical and structural results on YgbT/Cas1 are reported as the GOA rows describe them. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because the paper's second headline claim - a dedicated DNA-repair function for Cas1 - has not been corroborated in the fifteen years since, and the branched-DNA nuclease activities it reports were subsequently reinterpreted as the integrase active site catalysing disintegration. The biochemistry and the crystal structure are sound; the functional interpretation of them is the contested part, which is why the three annotations it supports are demoted rather than removed.

title: Proteins and DNA elements essential for the CRISPR adaptation process in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match the GOA reference. Supplies exactly what the IMP rows claim: Cas1 and Cas2 are each individually insufficient and jointly sufficient for array expansion, and the Cas1 D221A active-site variant is inactive.

title: The binary protein-protein interaction landscape of Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Title, authors and journal verified against the cached record. Correctly cited as the source of the two IntAct rows, but it is a genome-scale yeast two-hybrid screen and the cached full text does not expose the Cas1-HprS or Cas1-Cas1 pairs at the gene level, so it informs this gene's function only weakly. Relevance LOW rather than correctness MISCITED: the citation is right, the evidence is just thin.

title: Cas1-Cas2 complex formation mediates spacer acquisition during CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match. The structural and mutational results are as the GOA rows describe them, and this is the paper that establishes the division of labour between the two subunits - Cas1 catalytic, Cas2 dispensable for catalysis but required for assembly.

title: Detection and characterization of spacer integration intermediates in type I-E CRISPR-Cas system.
review_notes: Fetched and verified against PMC; title, authors and journal match. Not cited by any GOA row, but added here because it provides the in vivo mapping of the nicking and joining sites that the core-function statement depends on, and it does so independently of the Doudna-laboratory in vitro reconstitutions.

title: Integrase-mediated spacer acquisition during CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match. This is the paper that establishes Cas1 as the catalytic subunit of an integrase-type reaction, and it is the evidence the crispr_cas_adaptive_immunity module cites for the Cas1 annoton. Added here because no GOA row cites it, yet it is the primary support for the core function.

title: Intrinsic sequence specificity of the Cas1 integrase directs new spacer acquisition.
review_notes: Fetched and verified against PMC; title, authors and journal match. Added because it is the source of the reinterpretation that decides two of the contested annotations: the branched-DNA activities are the integrase active site catalysing disintegration, not separate resolvase or flap-endonuclease functions. It also supplies the explicit statement that Cas2 acts as an adaptor protein.

title: Foreign DNA capture during CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match. Correctly cited as the source of the Cas1-Cas2 IntAct row, and supplies the DNA-bound structures that show how Cas1 and Cas2 arginines jointly clamp and measure the protospacer duplex.

title: Asymmetric positioning of Cas1-2 complex and Integration Host Factor induced DNA bending guide the unidirectional homing of protospacer in CRISPR-Cas type I-E system.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; title, authors and journal match the ComplexPortal reference. Supports the IDA rows: the purified Cas1-2 complex is assayed integrating a protospacer into leader-containing CRISPR DNA, with IHF identified as the host factor that makes integration unidirectional.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Standard InterPro2GO pipeline reference. Correctly applied, but on this protein it sees only the generic DEAD/DEAH-box helicase domain (IPR011545), which produces an accurate ATP-binding call and an uninformative nucleic-acid-binding call.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT/IBA mechanism itself is sound and the donor annotations are sound; the issue on this gene is the scope of one transferred term (RNA helicase activity) given that the Cas3 helicase module sits inside a PANTHER family dominated by DEAD-box RNA helicases.

title: Small CRISPR RNAs guide antiviral defense in prokaryotes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached full text available. This is the paper that defined the E. coli K-12 cas gene set and established the genetic requirement for Cas3 in antiviral defence. It is the source of the GO:0051607 IDA row.

title: Helicase dissociation and annealing of RNA-DNA hybrids by Escherichia coli Cas3 protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The cached record is abstract-only, so the DNA-binding and mutagenesis data that EcoCyc and UniProt annotated from this paper cannot be quoted here; UniProt's reference block for this entry records FUNCTION AS AN RNA:DNA HELICASE, FUNCTION IN FORMING R-LOOPS, COFACTOR, DNA-BINDING and mutagenesis of His74/Asp75/Lys78/317-318/Lys320/His455 from it, which is consistent with the annotations derived from it.

title: CRISPR immunity relies on the consecutive binding and degradation of negatively supercoiled invader DNA by Cascade and Cas3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached full text available via PMC3372689. This is the strongest reference for the review: it supplies the nuclease assays behind GO:0000014 and GO:0008296, the Cse1-dependent recruitment, and the pathway order. It is also the proper evidence citation for the Cas3 annoton in modules/crispr_cas_adaptive_immunity.yaml, which previously cited GO:0008296 as evidence for itself and now cites this reference together with this gene review.

title: Identification of novel protein lysine acetyltransferases in Escherichia coli.

title: Emergence of plasmid-mediated colistin resistance mechanism MCR-1 in animals and human beings in China: a microbiological and molecular biological study.

title: Structure of the catalytic domain of the colistin resistance enzyme MCR-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Stojanoski et al., BMC Biol 2016; PMC5025626, full text). 1.32 A structure of the MCR-1 catalytic domain; directly supports the pEtN-transferase MF, zinc/metal dependence, Thr285 nucleophile (phosphorylation), and the lipid A target-modification mechanism.

title: Substrate analog interaction with MCR-1 offers insight into the rising threat of the plasmid-mediated transferable colistin resistance.

title: Existing falcon function-hypothesis report
review_notes: Supports Thr285-mediated phosphoethanolamine transfer. Its EC 2.7.4.30 assignment and claim that GO:0016776 is an ancestor of the specific MCR-1 term are not consistent with the cached EC 2.7.8.43 annotation and the current GO ancestor query. Its broadness verdict is not independent proof of biological error.

title: Blinded OpenScientist function-assignment report (TreeGrafter audit)
review_notes: Supports the substituted-phosphate reaction and EC2GO branch, checked against the current GO:0043838 ancestor list. Its characterization as a wrong graft is not established by term mapping; the current broad GO:0016776 text and Falcon interpretation leave scope nuance.

title: Regulation of transcription of the mph(A) gene for macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase I in Escherichia coli: characterization of the regulatory gene mphR(A)
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Noguchi et al., J Bacteriol 2000). Characterizes the mphR(A) repressor controlling inducible mphA expression; supports the regulatory distinction from constitutive mphB.

title: Resistance phenotypes conferred by macrolide phosphotransferases
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Chesneau et al., FEMS Microbiol Lett 2007). Comparative phenotyping of mph genes; documents mph(A)'s azithromycin activity, consistent with its 14-/15-membered specificity.

title: Purification and characterization of macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase from a strain of Escherichia coli that is highly resistant to erythromycin
review_notes: PubMed-verified (O'Hara et al., Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1989). Original purification and characterization of MPH(2')I; the primary source for MphA's 14-membered (not 16-membered) substrate specificity, inducibility, and purine-NTP donor usage — the direct contrast to MphB (PMID:1330822).

title: Structural Basis for Kinase-Mediated Macrolide Antibiotic Resistance
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Fong et al., Structure 2017). Provides the MphA (MPH(2')-I) crystal structures (PDB 5IGH/5IGI), confirming the APH/protein-kinase-like fold and GTP-analog/macrolide binding.

title: The evolution of substrate discrimination in macrolide antibiotic resistance enzymes
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Pawlowski et al., Nat Commun 2018). Phylogenetic/functional survey of Mph enzymes placing MphA among the clinically mobilized, widespread Gram-negative resistance kinases.

title: Look and Outlook on Enzyme-Mediated Macrolide Resistance
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Golkar et al., Front Microbiol 2018). Authoritative review of enzyme-mediated macrolide resistance; provides a clean secondary-source statement of the MPH(2')-I vs -II substrate-specificity distinction and the GTP phosphate-donor mechanism.

title: Whole-Genome Sequencing of an Escherichia coli ST69 Strain Harboring bla(CTX-M-27) on a Hybrid Plasmid
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Wang et al., Infect Drug Resist 2024). Documents the contemporary mobile genetic context of mphA (IS26 composite transposon, IncF plasmids), supporting its horizontal dissemination.

title: Multidrug-resistant conjugative plasmid carrying mphA confers increased antimicrobial resistance in Shigella
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Asad et al., Sci Rep 2024). Experimental conjugation/MIC evidence that plasmid-borne mphA confers high-level azithromycin resistance transferable into recipient Enterobacterales.

title: Nucleotide sequence and characterization of erythromycin resistance determinant that encodes macrolide 2'-phosphotransferase I in Escherichia coli
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Noguchi et al., Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995). Cloning/sequencing of the mphA determinant; establishes mphA identity and the mphA+mrx requirement for high-level resistance.

title: abaA controls phialide differentiation in Aspergillus nidulans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sewall, Mims & Timberlake). Ultrastructural demonstration that abaA controls phialide differentiation.

title: Interactions of three sequentially expressed genes control temporal and spatial specificity in Aspergillus development.
