title: Dipeptide utilization by the periodontal pathogens Porphyromonas gingivalis, Prevotella intermedia, Prevotella nigrescens and Fusobacterium nucleatum.
review_notes: Direct organism-level evidence that F. nucleatum utilizes dipeptides as growth substrates; abstract-only in cache but PMID resolves to the intended paper. Not gene-specific for A0A133P372.

title: Crystal structure of the dinuclear zinc aminopeptidase PepV from Lactobacillus delbrueckii unravels its preference for dipeptides.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but PMID resolves to the canonical PepV crystal structure (PDB 1LFW); directly supports the di-zinc dipeptidase mechanism and broad specificity of PepV. Homolog/family inference.

title: Crystal structure and mutational analysis of aminoacylhistidine dipeptidase from Vibrio alginolyticus reveal a new architecture of M20 metallopeptidases.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but PMID resolves to the intended paper; supports M20 di-zinc architecture and PepV/PepD family relationship. Homolog/family inference.

title: Identification of a staphylococcal dipeptidase involved in the production of human body odor.
review_notes: Full-text available; biochemically characterizes a PepV homolog (M20A) as a broad metal-dependent dipeptidase. Strong homolog inference for the F. nucleatum protein's molecular function.

title: A SecA-associated protease modulates the extent of surface display of staphylococcal protein A.
review_notes: Full-text available; supports cytosolic localization and Mn-dependent dipeptidase activity of a PepV homolog. The SecA/SpA surface-display role is lineage-specific to staphylococci and is not transferred to F. nucleatum.

title: Molecular characterization of a flagellar export locus of Helicobacter pylori.
review_notes: Same species, strain CCUG 17874, not J99. Abstract only.

title: Molecular basis of the interaction between the flagellar export proteins FliI and FliH from Helicobacter pylori.
review_notes: H. pylori FliI (strain not stated in abstract). Abstract only.

title: Structural similarity between the flagellar type III ATPase FliI and F1-ATPase subunits.
review_notes: Homolog structure; explains the family-level ATP-synthase mis-propagation.

title: Distinct roles of the FliI ATPase and proton motive force in bacterial flagellar protein export.
review_notes: Salmonella homolog energetics.

title: Energy source of flagellar type III secretion.
review_notes: Salmonella homolog; PMF, not FliI ATP hydrolysis, powers translocation.

title: ATP-induced FliI hexamerization facilitates bacterial flagellar protein export.
review_notes: Salmonella homolog; ATP binding drives hexamer assembly.

title: Common architecture of the flagellar type III protein export apparatus and F- and V-type ATPases.
review_notes: Salmonella homolog; basis of the rotary-like FliI6-FliJ model.

title: An energy transduction mechanism used in bacterial flagellar type III protein export.
review_notes: Salmonella homolog; locates proton flux in the gate, not FliI.

title: Helicobacter pylori FlgN binds its substrate FlgK and the flagellum ATPase FliI in a similar manner observed for the FliT chaperone.
review_notes: In vitro H. pylori protein interaction data; full text cached.

title: Enzymatic characterization of FliI. An ATPase involved in flagellar assembly in Salmonella typhimurium.
review_notes: Homolog (Salmonella) evidence, used for ISS transfer.

title: A flagellar-specific ATPase (FliI) is necessary for flagellar export in Helicobacter pylori.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Same species, strain N6 (per UniProt O07025 citation), not J99. Abstract only.

title: Falcon deep research report for H. pylori J99 fliI
review_notes: Useful synthesis; correctly states FliI is not an ATP synthase. Several claims (E193Q monomeric, HP0256 as FliJ) derive from theses and were not relied upon.

title: Hyaluronidases and CD44 undergo differential modulation during chondrogenesis.
review_notes: The human source behind the cartilage development row, annotated IEP. The citation is correct, but an expression-pattern correlation is the weakest experimental basis for a process annotation and does not survive projection into another species. Title verified against PubMed; no quotation used.

title: BMP-7 modulates hyaluronan-mediated proximal tubular cell-monocyte interaction.
review_notes: The human source behind the heterotypic cell-cell adhesion and monocyte aggregation rows. A renal disease-model system, which is the basis for treating both projections as organ-physiology transfers. Title verified against PubMed; no quotation used.

title: Acylation of CD44 and its association with lipid rafts are required for receptor and hyaluronan endocytosis.
review_notes: The human source behind the cargo receptor activity and membrane raft rows. Title verified against PubMed; cited for provenance only, with no quotation.

title: CD44 is the signaling component of the macrophage migration inhibitory factor-CD74 receptor complex.
review_notes: Identified via QuickGO as the human IDA source behind five of the Ensembl-projected rows on this protein (cytokine receptor activity, MIF receptor complex, both p53 rows, and the ERK cascade row). Recorded so that those five rows are not mistaken for five independent lines of evidence. Title verified against PubMed; no supporting_text is quoted from it.

title: CD44-dependent intracellular and extracellular catabolism of hyaluronic acid by hyaluronidase-1 and -2.
review_notes: The human source behind the hyaluronan catabolic process row. Its title makes the key point used in that review - the catabolism is CD44-dependent but carried out by hyaluronidases, so CD44 contributes as receptor and has no enzymatic role. Title verified against PubMed; no quotation used.

title: bFGF induces changes in hyaluronan synthase and hyaluronidase isoform expression and modulates the migration capacity of fibrosarcoma cells.
review_notes: The human source behind the cellular response to fibroblast growth factor stimulus row. The study measures bFGF-driven changes in hyaluronan synthase and hyaluronidase expression in a fibrosarcoma line, which is a weak basis for asserting that CD44 itself mediates an FGF response. Title verified against PubMed; no quotation used.

title: Proinflammatory cytokines induce hyaluronan synthesis and monocyte adhesion in human endothelial cells through hyaluronan synthase 2 (HAS2) and the nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway.
review_notes: The human source behind the positive regulation of monocyte aggregation row. The gene manipulated in that system is HAS2 in endothelial cells, with CD44 acting as the monocyte-side receptor, which weakens the attribution of positive regulation to CD44. Title verified against PubMed; no quotation used.

title: Podoplanin associates with CD44 to promote directional cell migration.
review_notes: The single human source behind four projected rows (apical plasma membrane, lamellipodium membrane, wound healing cell spreading, regulation of lamellipodium morphogenesis). Recorded to make that shared provenance visible. Title verified against PubMed; no quotation used.

title: High-molecular-mass hyaluronan mediates the cancer resistance of the naked mole rat.
review_notes: The primary source of naked-mole-rat evidence for CD44 function. Contains the CD44-blocking antibody experiments on intact naked mole-rat cells, the HA/CD44/NF2 framing, and the whole-cell hyaluronan-affinity FACS comparison. Verified against the cached full text; the FACS assay is explicitly a whole-cell measurement and is cited here as corroborating rather than as a CD44-specific binding measurement.

title: The material properties of naked mole-rat hyaluronan.
review_notes: Used only for the background statement that CD44 is the main hyaluronan receptor. Its suggestion that the supercoiled structure of naked mole-rat hyaluronan may protect CD44 from proteolytic cleavage is explicitly speculative in the paper and was not used as evidence.

title: Naked mole-rat very-high-molecular-mass hyaluronan exhibits superior cytoprotective properties.
review_notes: Establishes CD44, not RHAMM, as the receptor for the cytoprotective effect of naked mole-rat hyaluronan, and shows that very-high-mass hyaluronan suppresses CD44 protein-protein interactions where ordinary high-mass hyaluronan promotes them. Important caveat verified in the full text: the experiments apply naked mole-rat hyaluronan to human IMR90 fibroblasts, so the receptor tested is human CD44. Cited here as evidence about the ligand and about the receptor requirement, not about the naked mole-rat protein.

title: Naked mole-rats are extremely resistant to post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
review_notes: Cited in the cartilage development row as the place where a naked mole-rat rescue of that projection might have been found. The paper attributes joint protection to hyaluronan polymer size and cartilage mechanics and does not implicate CD44.

title: Abundance and size of hyaluronan in naked mole-rat tissues and plasma.
review_notes: Source for the statement that very-high-mass hyaluronan reduces CD44's association with other proteins and partially attenuates p53 target gene output. This is that paper's summary of the 2020 cytoprotection study rather than new data, and is cited as such in the p53 rows.

title: The naked truth: a comprehensive clarification and classification of current 'myths' in naked mole-rat biology.
review_notes: Used for two things verified in the cached full text: that the hyaluronan-driven proliferative arrest is not a cell-autonomous contact-inhibition process, which determined the choice of GO term for the proposed proliferation annotation; and that naked mole-rat immune cell populations lack natural killer cells, which bears on the immunological projections. The latter is the review reporting Hilton et al. 2019, not primary data.

title: Dysregulation of ADAM10 shedding activity in naked mole-rat fibroblasts is due to deficient phosphatidylserine externalization.
review_notes: Abstract only. Quotations are taken from the abstract and no method detail beyond it is asserted. It establishes absence of ADAM10-mediated CD44 cleavage in naked mole-rat primary skin fibroblasts and locates the cause upstream of CD44 in phosphatidylserine externalisation, which is why it supports downgrading rather than removing the extracellular region annotation.

title: Galectin-9 promotes natural killer cells activity via interaction with CD44.
review_notes: Fetched and read for this review. It is the human source behind the signaling receptor activity and NK T cell activation rows. The identifier resolves to the intended paper and the CD44 finding is real - the galectin-9-CD44 interaction is shown in mouse and then confirmed in human NK cells - but the paper does not support GO:0051132. It studies natural killer cells throughout, and the strings NKT and natural killer T do not appear anywhere in the full text, whereas that term is defined for natural killer T cells. Marked MISCITED on that basis; the mismatch is a GOA-side question about the human annotation and is flagged rather than resolved here.

title: CD44 correlates with longevity and enhances basal ATF6 activity and ER stress resistance.
review_notes: The source of all three proposed new annotations. Contains loss- and gain-of-function on naked mole-rat CD44 in naked mole-rat oligodendrocyte progenitors, ER localisation in those cells, and the ER-retained ectodomain sufficiency experiment. Verified against the cached full text. Note that the mechanism is presented as general mammalian biology; the naked-mole-rat-specific claim is one of expression level.

title: Evolution of high-molecular-mass hyaluronic acid is associated with subterranean lifestyle.
review_notes: Independent restatement of the hyaluronan-CD44-p16 contact-inhibition axis in the naked mole rat; corroborating context rather than primary evidence for CD44.

title: Naked mole-rat hyaluronan.
review_notes: Abstract-only review. Its attribution of accelerated wound healing and cancer and arthritis resistance to CD44 signalling is a summary statement, not a demonstration, and is cited only as weak contextual support in the wound-healing row.

title: Naked mole-rat TMEM2 lacks physiological hyaluronan-degrading activity.
review_notes: Abstract only. Supports the naked mole-rat hyaluronan-accumulation phenotype through a second, independent degradation-side mechanism, which is part of the argument for downgrading the hyaluronan catabolic process and cargo receptor rows.

title: Naked mole-rat Cd44 isoform architecture and hyaluronan-binding site analysis
review_notes: Analysis performed for this review; the script and cached sequences are in the Cd44-bioinformatics folder and the result is reproducible. Establishes that the reference protein is a variant-exon-containing gene model and that the hyaluronan binding residues and Link disulfides are conserved. It does not measure binding, and says nothing about which isoforms naked mole-rat tissues express.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for CD44 (human ortholog P16070)
review_notes: A machine-generated Affinage record for the HUMAN ortholog P16070, obtained deliberately as a conserved-mechanism baseline because Affinage does not run on non-human species. Used only for mechanism; no sentence from it is cited as evidence about the naked mole-rat protein and none of its mechanism_profile GO ids were imported. Useful for the ADAM10 shedding and glycosylation-gated binding background. Its most consequential omission, recorded here as a recall observation: it contains no trace of the CD44 endoplasmic reticulum and ATF6 proteostasis function - PMID:37708026 is absent from its twenty citations and its localisation profile lists plasma membrane, nucleus and lysosome but not the ER - even though that is the only line of work in which naked mole-rat CD44 itself was manipulated.

title: UniProt entry A0AAX6R0R7 (Cd44, Heterocephalus glaber)
review_notes: Source for topology, domain boundaries and subcellular-location statements. Note that nearly all of its content is itself ARBA-propagated (PE 4, Predicted), so it is used for structural features rather than as independent functional evidence. Its CAUTION about lacking conserved residues comes from the Link-domain rule PROSITE-ProRule PRU00323 and concerns automatic disulfide-feature propagation; the sequence analysis in this review shows the hyaluronan-contact residues and Link disulfide cysteines are in fact present.

title: TreeGrafter-generated GO annotations
review_notes: The sole source of all 13 existing annotations. Traced to family PTHR10656: the 12 non-catalytic terms correspond to IBD assertions at node PTN002579681 (taxon:117571, Euteleostomi), seeded by mouse Cgas (MGI:MGI:2442261) and human CGAS (UniProtKB:Q8N884); GO:0061501 corresponds to PTN000838114 (taxon:6072, Eumetazoa) with eight seeds. The node placements are well grounded and are accepted here except where naked-mole-rat evidence contradicts them.

title: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase is a cytosolic DNA sensor that activates the type I interferon pathway.
review_notes: Primary mammalian cGAS study; comparative evidence, not an assay of naked-mole-rat A0AAX6RS70. Full text inspected for 23258413 and 24077100; 28214358 and 28363908 are abstract-only in the cache.

title: Cell intrinsic immunity spreads to bystander cells via the intercellular transfer of cGAMP.
review_notes: Primary mammalian cGAS study; comparative evidence, not an assay of naked-mole-rat A0AAX6RS70. Full text inspected for 23258413 and 24077100; 28214358 and 28363908 are abstract-only in the cache.

title: The N terminus of cGAS de-oligomerizes the cGAS:DNA complex and lifts the DNA size restriction of core-cGAS activity.
review_notes: Primary mammalian cGAS study; comparative evidence, not an assay of naked-mole-rat A0AAX6RS70. Full text inspected for 23258413 and 24077100; 28214358 and 28363908 are abstract-only in the cache.

title: Nonspecific DNA Binding of cGAS N Terminus Promotes cGAS Activation.
review_notes: Primary mammalian cGAS study; comparative evidence, not an assay of naked-mole-rat A0AAX6RS70. Full text inspected for 23258413 and 24077100; 28214358 and 28363908 are abstract-only in the cache.

title: Genome Stability Maintenance in Naked Mole-Rat.
review_notes: Background on naked-mole-rat genome maintenance, predating the cGAS work. Checked directly for cGAS/STING content and it has none, so it neither supports nor contradicts any annotation here; retained only as context for why enhanced DNA repair in this species is a well-motivated prior.

title: Extracellular cGAMP is a cancer cell-produced immunotransmitter involved in radiation-induced anti-cancer immunity.
review_notes: Primary mammalian extracellular cGAMP experiments, full text inspected: soluble cGAMP export and recipient immune effects directly support the fluid-mediated paracrine route. Comparative evidence, not a naked-mole-rat assay.

title: DNA Homeostasis and Senescence: Lessons from the Naked Mole Rat.
review_notes: Review of naked-mole-rat DNA homeostasis and senescence. Also checked and found to contain no cGAS or STING content; contextual only.

title: A cGAS-mediated mechanism in naked mole-rats potentiates DNA repair and delays aging.
review_notes: The single primary source for every species-specific claim in this review, and the only evidence that contradicts a propagated annotation. PubMed-verified (Science 2025; 390:eadp5056; doi 10.1126/science.adp5056). Cached abstract-only, so all quotes are taken from the abstract and no assay detail, cell type or residue-level mechanism is asserted beyond what the abstract states.

title: Longevity steps on the cGAS.
review_notes: Perspective piece accompanying PMID:41066557 in the same issue; it corroborates the framing but contains no independent data, and is treated as commentary rather than evidence. No annotation action rests on it.

title: Naked mole rat cGAS sticks it out.
review_notes: Nature Aging research-highlight note on the same finding. Cached with no abstract body; nothing quotable and no annotation depends on it.

title: The naked mole-rat cGAS promotes homologous recombination repair and delays aging.
review_notes: Science Bulletin research highlight on PMID:41066557 (3 pages, 2385-2387). The cache contains title and metadata only, with no abstract body, so nothing can be quoted from it and it supports no annotation. Listed because it is a genuine second discussion of the same finding, not as independent evidence.

title: Naked mole-rat cGAS (A0AAX6RS70): conservation of catalytic and chromatin-binding residues
review_notes: Own reproducible analysis written for this review (align_cgas.py, biopython global alignment against Q8N884 and Q8C6L5 with UniProt feature transfer). It answers the question the abstracts leave open — whether the catalytic machinery survives in this species — and independently resolves the numbering frame of the four divergent residues. Every quotation used as supporting_text was grep-verified against the file, since file: quotes are not checked by CI. Its stated limits are respected in the review: it establishes capability, not measured activity.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for CGAS (human)
review_notes: Human-only external synthesis, used for comparative cGAMP signaling and transfer. It contains no naked-mole-rat evidence and cannot override the target HR sign reversal. Its ontology profile was not imported; paracrine evidence is corroborated independently by primary PMID:24077100.

title: Functional Annotation Report: *Heterocephalus glaber Mb21d1* / cGAS
review_notes: The report supplies mammalian DNA sensing, cGAMP-STING signaling and nucleosome restraint, but missed the direct naked-mole-rat HR study PMID:41066557. Its human/mouse sequestration model does not demonstrate loss of naked-mole-rat immune signaling. Use conserved mechanism with this recall limitation; do not use lack of retrieved species assays to refute inherited function.

title: Focused OpenScientist report on HETGA Cgas dsRNA versus dsDNA response
review_notes: Read in full; directly adjudicates GO:0071360 as a mouse-donor dsRNA/dsDNA term-selection error rather than as evidence of a real cGAS response to exogenous dsRNA.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Method reference for the ISS annotations. All 20 ISS rows on this protein come from three named donors (human Q92819, mouse P70312, rat O35776). Sequence similarity is an appropriate basis for transferring the catalytic and localization claims, which is how most of these rows are treated here; it is a much weaker basis for transferring organ-level physiology (the two rat renal terms), which is why those are flagged.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Method reference. The five SubCell-derived CC rows mirror the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION block, which is itself entirely ECO:0000250 by similarity to human Q92819; they therefore duplicate the ISS CC rows rather than adding independent evidence.

title: TreeGrafter-generated GO annotations
review_notes: Method reference for the single TreeGrafter row (GO:0085029, via PANTHER ancestral node PTN000530842). Placing extracellular matrix assembly on the ancestral hyaluronan synthase node is phylogenetically sound - every characterised member of the family extrudes an ECM polysaccharide.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Method reference. Three rows use it; the GO:0050501 row is supported by an explicit RHEA:12528 / EC:2.4.1.212 mapping in the WITH/FROM field, which matches the CATALYTIC ACTIVITY block of the UniProt entry, so the enzymatic call is well grounded even before the naked-mole-rat literature is considered.

title: Genome sequencing reveals insights into physiology and longevity of the naked mole rat.
review_notes: Abstract only in the local cache. This is reference [1] of the UniProt entry and is the source of the genomic sequence (EMBL JH167500 / EHB01992.1) from which G5AY81 was derived. Cited for provenance of the sequence record only; it makes no functional claim about Has2.

title: High-molecular-mass hyaluronan mediates the cancer resistance of the naked mole rat.
review_notes: The primary reference for this gene; it is also reference [2] of the UniProt entry (RP FUNCTION, AND TISSUE SPECIFICITY). Full text cached and read. Verified against the UniProt record, which cites it for both the TISSUE SPECIFICITY (ECO:0000269) and the MISCELLANEOUS/HMM-HA statements. Its qualitative claims (HAS2 makes hyaluronan, HAS2 is overexpressed, HAS2 loss abolishes the phenotype) are reproduced elsewhere; its quantitative 6-12 MDa size claim is contested by PMID:33846452 and PMID:34476892 and is not relied on here for any annotation decision.

title: Molecular evolution of the hyaluronan synthase 2 gene in mammals: implications for adaptations to the subterranean niche and cancer resistance.
review_notes: Abstract only in the local cache (full_text_available false in publications/); both quotes above are taken from the abstract, and no methods-level claim is made from it. The purifying-selection result is the main reason the mouse-derived developmental terms are kept as non-core rather than removed.

title: The material properties of naked mole-rat hyaluronan.
review_notes: Full text cached. Independent group (Cambridge/Newcastle), so a useful non-Rochester corroboration that naked mole rat hyaluronan is materially unusual. Supports the extracellular matrix assembly annotation at the level of the product; makes no claim about the enzyme.

title: Naked mole-rat very-high-molecular-mass hyaluronan exhibits superior cytoprotective properties.
review_notes: Full text cached. Concerns the properties of the hyaluronan polymer rather than the enzyme, so it supports no annotation on G5AY81 directly; it is cited only to justify the proposed new term, where the point at issue is precisely whether polymer length is biologically distinguishable.

title: Naked mole-rats are extremely resistant to post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
review_notes: Full text cached. Contextual: it establishes a downstream organismal phenotype of the hyaluronan polymer and never assays Has2. Deliberately not used to support any GO annotation on this protein.

title: Abundance and size of hyaluronan in naked mole-rat tissues and plasma.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Correctly cited and methodologically careful (two independent sizing methods, quantitative cortex/medulla separation), but marked DISPUTED because its central size result directly contradicts PMID:23783513 and the discrepancy is unresolved - PMID:34476892 attributes it to isolation procedure. That dispute concerns polymer size only; the renal cortex/medulla quantification, which is what this review leans on for the two rat-derived annotations, is not contested by anyone and is the only such measurement in existence for this species.

title: The naked truth: a comprehensive clarification and classification of current 'myths' in naked mole-rat biology.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. A multi-author consensus adjudication of contested claims in this field; used here specifically as a guard against over-claiming. It is the reason the description reports both size measurements rather than asserting 6-12 MDa, and the reason no annotation in this review depends on polymer magnitude.

title: Increased hyaluronan by naked mole-rat Has2 improves healthspan in mice.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. The strongest whole-animal evidence that this specific gene product raises hyaluronan amount and mass. Note the authors' own caveat that the benefits track the polymer, not the gene ("These beneficial effects were conferred by HMM-HA and were not specific to the nmrHas2 gene"), so the downstream anti-cancer and longevity phenotypes are attributes of the product and are deliberately not annotated as processes of the protein.

title: Evolution of high-molecular-mass hyaluronic acid is associated with subterranean lifestyle.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Provides the comparative framework and the only direct transfection evidence that HAS2 sequence (not just dosage) sets polymer length. The matched-expression experiment is on blind mole rat HAS2, not naked mole rat HAS2, and is cited here as such - it is supporting analogy, not evidence about G5AY81.

title: Naked mole-rat hyaluronan.
review_notes: Abstract only in the local cache; the quote is from the abstract. A narrative review, used only for the framing statement that synthesis and degradation both contribute. No primary evidence, and no annotation rests on it.

title: Naked mole-rat TMEM2 lacks physiological hyaluronan-degrading activity.
review_notes: Abstract only in the local cache; the quote is from the abstract. Included because it guards against attributing the whole tissue hyaluronan phenotype to Has2: the degradation arm is a separate, independently evolved contribution, which is why no hyaluronan-accumulation or catabolism-related term is proposed for this gene.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for HAS2 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record for the HUMAN ortholog HAS2 (Q92819), placed in this gene folder deliberately as a conserved-mechanism baseline because Affinage does not cover non-human species. Used only for what the conserved protein does mechanistically (post-translational control of trafficking and activity, HAS1/HAS3 heteromer formation, transcriptional inputs); no sentence from it is quoted as evidence about the naked mole rat protein and none of its mechanism_profile GO ids were imported - it grounds the molecular activity at GO:0016740 transferase activity, three levels above the correct GO:0050501, so every term here was re-grounded independently. Its recall on this species-divergence question is poor: of its 32 citations only PMID:37612507 concerns the naked mole rat, and it omits PMID:23783513 entirely - i.e. it misses the one experiment that converts this gene's core molecular function from an ortholog projection into a direct assay on the naked mole rat protein. It also misses the polymer-size controversy (PMID:33846452, PMID:34476892) and the selection analysis (PMID:25948568).

title: Candidate tumor suppressor HYAL2 is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored cell-surface receptor for jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus, the envelope protein of which mediates oncogenic transformation.
review_notes: Source of the human NOT|enables GO:0004415 IDA. The apparent contradiction with the nine positive IDAs is resolved by HYAL2 being a genuinely weak, acid-requiring enzyme, not by either annotation being wrong.

title: Hyaluronidase 2 negatively regulates RON receptor tyrosine kinase and mediates transformation of epithelial cells by jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus.
review_notes: Anchor for GO:0030971, GO:0030294 and GO:0051898. Corroborated on the naked mole rat record itself by the UniProt ARBA subunit line naming MST1R, which is why these are kept as non-core rather than marked over-annotated.

title: Amino acid residues that are important for Hyal2 function as a receptor for jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus.
review_notes: Decisive for the GO:0001618 and GO:0046718 calls. Not a naked mole rat paper, but the only rodent-ortholog test of HYAL2 receptor function that exists. The affinage human record cites this paper but frames it only as a quantitative difference and omits the outright loss of Env binding in mouse.

title: Skeletal and hematological anomalies in HYAL2-deficient mice: a second type of mucopolysaccharidosis IX?
review_notes: The in vivo counterweight to the weak in vitro activity, and the basis for treating the skeletal terms as genuine but peripheral.

title: Transforming growth factor beta1 signaling via interaction with cell surface Hyal-2 and recruitment of WWOX/WOX1.
review_notes: Sole anchor for the whole nuclear and transcriptional annotation cluster projected from mouse Hyal2 (GO:0003713, GO:0090575, GO:0045944, GO:0042307) and for GO:0050431 and GO:0005829. Single-laboratory, reporter- and imaging-based; correctly cited, but too thin a base for projecting a transcription-complex membership onto an untested species.

title: High-molecular-mass hyaluronan mediates the cancer resistance of the naked mole rat.
review_notes: Establishes the tissue-level hyaluronidase deficit but does not attribute it to an isoenzyme. Its Hyal2 experiments use the human cDNA (verified in Methods), so they must not be read as evidence about naked mole rat Hyal2.

title: Naked mole-rat very-high-molecular-mass hyaluronan exhibits superior cytoprotective properties.
review_notes: Background for why the product-size axis matters biologically; motivates the proposed new term. No Hyal2-specific data.

title: Abundance and size of hyaluronan in naked mole-rat tissues and plasma.
review_notes: Explicitly identifies the attribution gap that makes several calls in this review cautious; the authors state that the HYAL1/HYAL2 distinction could not be made in the naked mole rat.

title: Evolution of high-molecular-mass hyaluronic acid is associated with subterranean lifestyle.
review_notes: The single most decisive reference for this gene. It is the only study that has cloned and functionally assayed the naked mole rat HYAL2 protein itself, and it is titled for a phenotype rather than for the gene, so it is easy to miss. Its result establishes that the naked mole rat enzyme is catalytically active and only modestly attenuated, which is what keeps GO:0004415 an ACCEPT rather than a REMOVE.

title: Naked mole-rat TMEM2 lacks physiological hyaluronan-degrading activity.
review_notes: Abstract only in the cache; nothing here is drawn from unseen Methods or Results. It concerns TMEM2 (G8/GG domains, PbH1 repeats), not the GH56 family, so its conclusion must not be transferred to Hyal2. Its value for this review is indirect but real - it gives the naked mole rat degradation deficit a documented owner elsewhere, which removes the pressure to explain that deficit by inactivating HYAL2.

title: HYAL2, a human gene expressed in many cells, encodes a lysosomal hyaluronidase with a novel type of specificity.
review_notes: Defines the catalytic character of the family; explains why cell-based assays at neutral pH can score HYAL2 as inactive.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for HYAL2 (human ortholog), used as a conserved-mechanism baseline
review_notes: Human-ortholog record, fetched deliberately as a conserved-mechanism baseline because affinage refuses non-human species; its frontmatter and heading both say human. Accurate and well-cited for human HYAL2 and genuinely useful for the RON and WWOX modules. Not cited as evidence for any naked-mole-rat claim. Three recall and grounding limitations are recorded in the notes - it contains nothing on the naked mole rat, so it misses PMID:38052795, the one paper that assays this species' protein; it frames PMID:16191204 as a quantitative difference without recording that mouse Hyal2 does not bind Env at all; and its mechanism_profile grounding is unusable, listing GO:0140098 catalytic activity acting on RNA as a molecular activity for a glycoside hydrolase. Its GO ids were deliberately not imported.

title: UniProt record for naked mole rat Hyal2 (A0A0P6J1Y4)
review_notes: The only species-specific sequence-level record. Entirely rule-derived (PE 3, inferred from homology), but the feature annotations are checkable against the deposited sequence - residue 135 is the glutamate of the conserved GH56 DWEHW motif, confirming an intact catalytic centre.

title: Selective inflammatory pain insensitivity in the African naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber).
review_notes: Full text available. The phenotype paper, and the source of the only positive naked-mole-rat evidence for the neurite-outgrowth annotations. Its Figure S2 legend is an explicit demonstration that the NGF receptor is functional in this species, which is what makes ACCEPT rather than REMOVE the right call on the core molecular function terms.

title: Hypofunctional TrkA Accounts for the Absence of Pain Sensitization in the African Naked Mole-Rat.
review_notes: Full text available and read in full. The primary and decisive source for every species-specific call in this review. Verified that the paper's central claim is a reduction in signalling efficiency, not a loss of receptor function: ligand binding is excluded as the lesion by the chimeric-receptor experiment, the kinase domain autophosphorylates basally, and the NGF dose-response reaches rat-equivalent output at 1,000 ng/mL. The residue position 774 is stated with rat numbering; the naked mole-rat UniProt entry independently carries a cysteine at its own position 774, which is recorded separately in the notes rather than inferred from the paper.

title: Independent evolution of pain insensitivity in African mole-rats: origins and mechanisms.
review_notes: Full text available. Review by authors of the primary work; used here as a concise independent restatement of the chimeric-receptor result and of TrkA expression in naked mole-rat sensory neurons. Adds no primary data on this gene, so all quantitative claims are anchored to PMID:27732851 instead.

title: The naked mole-rat has a functional purinergic pain pathway despite having a non-functional peptidergic pain pathway.
review_notes: Full text available. Background context only; no TrkA data. Cited to support the point that naked mole-rat nociceptive signalling is selectively, not globally, disabled, which is part of the argument against negating the NGF signalling pathway annotation.

title: Artemin sensitises mouse (Mus musculus) and naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber) sensory neurons in vitro.
review_notes: Full text available. Independent 2025 confirmation that TrkA marks a defined sensory neuron population in this species, and important for bounding the TrkA deficit: artemin does sensitise naked mole-rat sensory neurons, so the failure of sensitisation is specific to the NGF/TrkA route rather than a general inability of these neurons to be sensitised.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for NTRK1 (human)
review_notes: This is the Affinage record for the HUMAN orthologue NTRK1/P04629, fetched deliberately as a conserved-mechanism baseline because Affinage covers human genes only. It is a dense, well-cited map of the conserved receptor - D5 NGF-binding hot spot, ordered bi-bi kinetics, Y490/Y785 docking, IRS-mediated p85-PI3K recruitment, N-glycosylation gating of surface delivery, STX8 and GGA3 trafficking, retrograde signalling endosomes, TRAF4 and Nedd4-2 ubiquitin control - and it is what makes the endosome-membrane and receptor-complex transfers in this GOA set credible at the family level. It contains zero mentions of naked mole-rat, Heterocephalus, or PMID:27732851 across all 34 citations, so it is unusable as evidence for any species-specific claim, and no sentence of it is quoted as supporting_text anywhere in this review. Its mechanism_profile GO ids were not imported: they collapse to coarse parents and one of them, GO:0048018 receptor ligand activity, is wrong for a receptor. One useful lead it did surface is PMID:24623787, a KFG-deletion knock-in mouse in which raised TrkA activity produces enhanced thermal sensitivity - the mirror image of the naked mole-rat, recorded as a lead in the notes rather than as evidence.

title: UniProtKB record for Heterocephalus glaber Ntrk1 (A0AAX6QC09)
review_notes: The sequence and feature table were used directly to verify that the catalytic apparatus and both phosphotyrosine docking sites are intact in this species, and that position 774 of this entry is a cysteine. All quoted fragments were grep-verified as single-physical-line substrings of the file.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Standard GO reference for InterPro2GO. The four cited InterPro signatures are all present in the entry's DR lines, so the provenance checks out.

title: TreeGrafter-generated GO annotations
review_notes: The entry's PANTHER assignment is PTHR10037:SF221, the NaV1.7 subfamily, so this is a within-subfamily transfer rather than a cross-paralog one. All three transferred process terms are corroborated by naked-mole-rat literature on this protein.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
An SCN9A channelopathy causes congenital inability to experience pain.
review_notes: Human paper, cited as the sequence-similarity basis for the NEW annotation rather than as evidence about the naked mole-rat protein.

title: The molecular basis of acid insensitivity in the African naked mole-rat.
review_notes: Abstract only in the cache; every quotation used here is from the abstract. The identifier is anchored independently of the abstract text: the UniProt record for G9DCX3 cites this exact PubMed ID and DOI for its nucleotide-sequence reference, with the same author list. No residue-level claim in this review is taken from this paper, precisely because the abstract gives none.

title: Repeated functional convergent effects of NaV1.7 on acid insensitivity in hibernating mammals.
review_notes: Abstract only. Used for the convergence claim and for independent corroboration of the naked-mole-rat mechanism, not for any residue numbering. Note that the one hibernator sequence I sampled independently (Ictidomys tridecemlineatus) retains the ancestral KKV triplet, so this paper's survey should not be read as implying that every hibernator carries the variant.

title: Investigation into the role of an extracellular loop in mediating proton-evoked inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels.
review_notes: Abstract only; fetched during this review after the falcon report surfaced it, as it was not previously in the publication cache. Marked VERIFIED rather than DISPUTED because it confirms rather than contradicts the central claim (EKE increases proton block of NaV1.7); what it disputes is the simple charge-and-pore-occlusion explanation, which this review therefore does not assert. Its quantitative values come from human channel mutagenesis, not from recordings of the naked mole-rat protein.

title: Structures of human Na(v)1.7 channel in complex with auxiliary subunits and animal toxins.
review_notes: Human structural paper, used only to justify the complex term for the conserved alpha subunit. No naked-mole-rat structure exists.

title: Defining the Functional Role of Na(V)1.7 in Human Nociception.
review_notes: Cited for what it does not license rather than for what it supports; no naked mole-rat cellular component annotation was derived from it.

title: Rapid molecular evolution of pain insensitivity in multiple African rodents.
review_notes: Abstract only. Establishes the comparative context; the specific EKE/EKD motif detail attributed to this study is quoted from the full-text review PMID:32206859 rather than from this abstract, which does not state it.

title: Acid and inflammatory sensitisation of naked mole-rat colonic afferent nerves.
review_notes: Full text available. Cited here only for its statement of the NaV1.7 mechanism and for the somatic/visceral distinction, both of which are explicit in its own introduction and discussion. Its primary experimental subject, colonic afferent electrophysiology, is not used as evidence for any annotation on this protein.

title: Independent evolution of pain insensitivity in African mole-rats: origins and mechanisms.
review_notes: Full text available and used as the primary source for the motif description, since the primary papers are abstract-only in this cache. It is a review by the same group, so it is not evidentially independent of PMID:22174253; the motif it describes was nonetheless verified directly against the sequences rather than taken on trust.

title: The Somatosensory World of the African Naked Mole-Rat.
review_notes: Abstract only; used solely for the attribution of the species' pain phenotype to this gene, which the abstract states explicitly.

title: The naked truth: a comprehensive clarification and classification of current 'myths' in naked mole-rat biology.
review_notes: Full text available. Consulted specifically to check whether it corrects any over-claim about NaV1.7. It does not dispute the NaV1.7 mechanism; what it corrects is the broader claim that this species feels no pain, and that correction has been incorporated here.

title: Domain IV pore-loop motif and fragment extent for naked mole-rat Scn9a
review_notes: Analysis written for this review; the script is deterministic, uses only the standard library, and caches its UniProt downloads, so the table can be regenerated. Results are not hardcoded.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for human SCN9A used as a conserved-mechanism baseline
review_notes: Human-ortholog record used only as a conserved-mechanism baseline, never as evidence about the naked mole-rat protein, and no sentence from it is quoted as supporting_text anywhere in this review. Marked LOW_QUALITY rather than VERIFIED because the record tripped a soft trust gate: its own frontmatter reports self_evaluation_pairwise as tie rather than win against the curated UniProt reference, so it did not demonstrate an advantage over the curated source it was scored against. Its coarse GO grounding, transporter activity for a voltage-gated sodium channel, is consistent with that self-assessment.

title: Falcon deep research report for naked mole-rat Scn9a
review_notes: LLM-generated deep-research report, so its narrative is a lead rather than evidence. Every claim taken from it that matters to an annotation is separately anchored to a PMID or to the UniProt record; the quotations used from it are restricted to statements of general channel biology and to its own explicit statements about what the retrieved literature does not show. Its quantitative proton-block figures were traced to their source (PMID:28939386) and cited from there rather than from the report.

title: UniProt record for Scn9a
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record, not edited. Its FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements are RuleBase/ARBA-derived rather than experimental for this species, which is why each is corroborated with naked-mole-rat literature wherever it supports an annotation here.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Keyword-based pipeline behind the GO:0005576 row (UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0243, Secreted). The underlying UniProt assertion is itself ARBA/RuleBase-derived, but it is corroborated independently by the SignalP-predicted signal peptide at 1..19 and by the fact that the mature tachykinins act on cell-surface receptors.

title: TreeGrafter-generated GO annotations
review_notes: TreeGrafter placement onto PANTHER ancestral node PTN000134172 (family PTHR11250 TACHYKININ, subfamily PTHR11250:SF3 PROTACHYKININ-1). Supplies the GO:0031835 and GO:0006954 rows. The corresponding human annotations on P20366 are PAINT IBAs (GO_REF:0000033), i.e. the node placement rests on a curator's reading of the family tree, not on a pairwise similarity score; checked via QuickGO.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Supplies the GO:0007217 row (InterPro2GO from IPR008215/IPR008216 plus the PANTHER node) and the GO:0007204 row (Ensembl Compara projection from human TAC1, UniProtKB:P20366 / ENSP00000321106, plus the PANTHER node). Human P20366 carries GO:0007204 with an IDA (PMID:8957234) in addition to a PAINT IBA, so the projected term has experimental grounding upstream.

title: Selective inflammatory pain insensitivity in the African naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber).
review_notes: The primary source for the naked mole-rat phenotype and the single most important paper for this gene. Two things matter here beyond the famous headline: the absence of substance P is stated as being in the skin innervation specifically, and the authors reintroduced the preprotachykinin gene into naked mole-rat sensory neurons with an HSV vector and recovered capsaicin-induced thermal hyperalgesia. The construct carried a rat beta-PPT cDNA, so this shows the naked mole-rat downstream pathway is competent rather than assaying the naked mole-rat protein.

title: Absence of histamine-induced itch in the African naked mole-rat and "rescue" by Substance P.
review_notes: Intrathecal substance P restores histamine-evoked scratching in an animal that otherwise shows none. Together with PMID:21200438 this is the functional demonstration that the naked mole-rat neurokinin system responds normally to its ligand, which is what keeps the molecular-function annotation defensible.

title: Functional neurokinin and NMDA receptor activity in an animal naturally lacking substance P: the naked mole-rat.
review_notes: The title is the over-simplification this review has to correct, and the paper's own discussion corrects it: it states that substance P and CGRP have been identified in presumptive visceral sensory fibres and that peptidergic neurotransmission does occur in this species. Read past the title. The pharmacology (SP sensitises, GR-82334 reverses, APV reverses) is the strongest evidence that the naked mole-rat NK1 receptor is functional.

title: Acid and inflammatory sensitisation of naked mole-rat colonic afferent nerves.
review_notes: Direct immunohistochemical demonstration of CGRP-positive extrinsic sensory fibres in naked mole-rat colonic mesentery and myenteric plexi. Corroborates the tissue-restricted, rather than global, loss of peptidergic innervation. It shows CGRP, not substance P, so it supports the general claim by analogy rather than directly.

title: Independent evolution of pain insensitivity in African mole-rats: origins and mechanisms.
review_notes: Review by the groups that did the primary work. Valuable for the precise wording of the phenotype (skin fibres virtually devoid of immunostaining, small-diameter somata essentially absent of it) and for stating that naked mole-rats have visceral fibres positive for CGRP. Being a review, its visceral claim is a citation to Park et al. 2003 and Hockley et al. 2020 rather than a primary figure.

title: The naked mole-rat has a functional purinergic pain pathway despite having a non-functional peptidergic pain pathway.
review_notes: Qualifies its own title in its abstract: the neuropeptides are absent from cutaneous C-fibres, which makes the peptidergic pathway hypofunctional. Also shows that intrathecal substance P enhances the formalin-induced response, i.e. the inflammatory-pain capability is retained and merely unmasked. This is the paper that decides KEEP_AS_NON_CORE rather than REMOVE on GO:0006954.

title: Naked mole-rats lack cold sensitivity before and after nerve injury.
review_notes: Cited only for its one-line restatement that naked mole-rats lack CGRP and substance P in nociceptive C fibres, which is background rather than new evidence about this gene. The paper itself is about cold sensitivity.

title: The Somatosensory World of the African Naked Mole-Rat.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the local cache (full_text_available is false). The abstract is about TrkA and NaV1.7 and does not mention substance P or tachykinins at all, so nothing in this review is drawn from it. Retained as general background on naked mole-rat somatosensation; no supporting_text is quoted from it.

title: The naked truth: a comprehensive clarification and classification of current 'myths' in naked mole-rat biology.
review_notes: Does not list "naked mole-rats lack substance P" among its 28 myths, so it does not adjudicate that specific claim; stated here rather than implied, because it would be easy to over-read this paper. What it does supply is the adjacent correction (Myth 10, feeling no pain, answered by emphasising selectivity) and the observation that substance P signalling under hypercapnia is diminished rather than absent. Both support treating the substance P story as tissue- and condition-restricted.

title: Tac1 (HETGA, A0A0P6JY17): where are the processed tachykinin peptides?
review_notes: Analysis performed for this review. Gap-free comparison of A0A0P6JY17 against the reviewed human entry P20366 (both are the same length bar one C-terminal residue), transferring the human PEPTIDE coordinates and independently re-checking each transferred peptide against the tachykinin F-x-G-L-M consensus and its downstream Gly-amide plus dibasic site. Reproducible from peptide_boundaries.py; output.txt is the verbatim run.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for TAC1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated record for the HUMAN ortholog (P20366), supplied as a conserved-mechanism baseline because affinage does not run on non-human species. Two limitations, recorded because provider recall is being measured. First, it contains no naked mole-rat content: none of its 36 citations is a naked mole-rat paper, and none of the six papers that actually decide this review appears in it, so it contributed nothing to any curation call. Second, its corpus is contaminated by symbol collisions - roughly a third of its findings table describes C. elegans TAC-1 (a TACC microtubule-associated protein), Candida Tac1 (a zinc-cluster transcription factor) or rice TAC1 (tiller angle control) rather than the tachykinin precursor. It flags this itself, but the table is unsafe to consume wholesale. Its mechanism_profile GO grounding was not imported; every term here was re-grounded against QuickGO. Genuinely useful for the mouse Tac1-knockout pleiotropy literature it collects.

title: Functional annotation report: Heterocephalus glaber Tac1
review_notes: Species-specific deep-research report (Edison/falcon). Unlike the affinage human-ortholog record it is about the naked mole rat, it correctly excludes Tac2 and the unrelated symbol collisions, and it reaches the same central conclusion reached independently here from the primary papers: the locus is intact and the absence of substance P is a cutaneous expression restriction rather than a change in the protein. Its own reasoning was spot-checked against the cached primary papers before use and matched. Two leads it supplied that the cached corpus does not contain are recorded in the notes rather than curated here, because neither is verifiable from the local cache: a 2025 book chapter devoted to this exact question (Zhao et al., "Life without substance P: The naked mole rat", doi:10.1016/b978-0-443-22194-1.00013-6), and CAP-TAC1, a capped TAC1-derived circulating tachykinin-receptor agonist reported in mouse and human (doi:10.1038/s41467-023-43857-0) and explicitly not shown in this species. Its orthology-based sections are appropriately labelled as such by the report itself.

title: UniProt record for naked mole-rat Tac1 (A0A0P6JY17)
review_notes: TrEMBL, unreviewed, PE 3 (inferred from homology); all FUNCTION and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements are ARBA/RuleBase-derived rather than curated for this protein. Its sequence and its SignalP/SMART features are primary data and are used as such; its FUNCTION prose is used only where it agrees with the sequence or with an independent source. Note that it carries no PEPTIDE features, so it does not by itself say whether substance P is in this isoform.

title: Selective inflammatory pain insensitivity in the African naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber).
review_notes: The foundational naked mole-rat nociception paper; full text cached. Its capsaicin calcium-imaging and skin-nerve data are the primary species-specific evidence for the channel-activity annotations here. Quoted passages were checked verbatim against the cached full text.

title: Absence of histamine-induced itch in the African naked mole-rat and "rescue" by Substance P.
review_notes: Full text cached. Cited only for its independent demonstration of capsaicin-evoked calcium responses in naked mole-rat DRG neurons; the paper's main subject is histamine itch and substance P rescue.

title: Functional neurokinin and NMDA receptor activity in an animal naturally lacking substance P: the naked mole-rat.
review_notes: Full text cached. Supports the interpretation that the missing capsaicin-induced thermal hyperalgesia is a spinal and neuropeptide phenomenon; it makes no claim about TRPV1 protein function itself.

title: The molecular basis of acid insensitivity in the African naked mole-rat.
review_notes: This is the paper whose mRNA submission (EMBL JF912492 / AEV53346.1) created the UniProt entry G9DCX1 being reviewed, so the annotated protein is the one characterised here; the link is verifiable in the RN/RX block of Trpv1-uniprot.txt. Only the abstract is cached, so the quoted passage is from the abstract and no methods detail is cited from it. The detailed TRPV1 gating characterisation attributed to this paper is quoted at second hand via PMID:27732851 and PMID:32206859.

title: Hypofunctional TrkA Accounts for the Absence of Pain Sensitization in the African Naked Mole-Rat.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. The single most informative reference for this gene: the only paper that isolates the naked mole-rat TRPV1 protein from its cellular context and measures its gating directly, and the source of the only documented species-specific substitution. Quoted passages verified verbatim against the cache.

title: Acid and inflammatory sensitisation of naked mole-rat colonic afferent nerves.
review_notes: Full text cached. Cited only for its restatement of naked mole-rat TRPV1 proton sensitivity and afferent expression; the paper's own new data concern colonic afferent firing rather than TRPV1 directly, so it corroborates rather than establishes.

title: Independent evolution of pain insensitivity in African mole-rats: origins and mechanisms.
review_notes: Full text cached. The best single synthesis of naked mole-rat nociception, and the clearest statement anywhere that the TRPV1 channel itself is unremarkable in this species. Written by the same group that did the primary work, so it is a well-informed secondary source rather than an independent one; the primary claims it summarises are separately cited to PMID:18232734 and PMID:27732851.

title: The naked mole-rat has a functional purinergic pain pathway despite having a non-functional peptidergic pain pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached. Supports the downstream (neuropeptide) explanation of the capsaicin phenotype, which is why no pain-perception term was proposed for this gene. It also quantifies TRPV1 immunoreactivity in naked mole-rat DRG.

title: Naked mole-rats lack cold sensitivity before and after nerve injury.
review_notes: Full text cached. Important as a control on the thermosensation question: the naked mole rat's genuine thermal difference is in cold, and this paper places that difference in TRPM8/TRPA1 while explicitly finding TRPV1 transcript levels normal. Nothing here supports a cold-sensing role for TRPV1.

title: The naked truth: a comprehensive clarification and classification of current 'myths' in naked mole-rat biology.
review_notes: Full text cached. Directly relevant because TRPV1 claims about this species are a known source of over-statement. Its Myth 10 section corrects the blanket "no pain" claim and affirms normal noxious-heat nocifension, which is why the heat-related terms proposed here are cellular-response terms rather than organism-level pain terms.

title: Artemin sensitises mouse (Mus musculus) and naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber) sensory neurons in vitro.
review_notes: Full text cached. The most recent independent confirmation that naked mole-rat TRPV1 is a working capsaicin-gated channel, recorded by whole-cell voltage clamp rather than calcium imaging. Also a useful counterweight to the TrkA story: sensitisation of this channel is not globally lost in the species, only the NGF/TrkA arm is impaired.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for TRPV1 (human ortholog record)
review_notes: This is the Affinage record for the HUMAN ortholog (Q8NER1), fetched deliberately as a conserved-mechanism baseline because Affinage does not run on non-human species; its frontmatter and heading both say human. It is used only for family-level mechanism, and no sentence from it is cited as evidence about the naked mole-rat protein. Its mechanism_profile GO ids (GO:0005215, GO:0060089, GO:0008289, GO:0140299) were not imported: they are coarse parents and, for the sensor and transducer terms, not what a curator would assert for a channel whose gating has been measured directly. Its recall gap on the species question is total - none of its 22 citations is a naked mole-rat paper, and it therefore misses the functionally silent Ser502Thr substitution and the TrkA-not-TRPV1 dissociation, both of which are decisive here.

title: UniProt record G9DCX1 for naked mole rat Trpv1
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record, not edited. Used for sequence, domain architecture and the provenance of the SubCell keyword annotation. Both quoted strings were grep-checked against the file and each lies within a single physical line.

title: UniProt entry P35747 (ALBU_HORSE), Serum albumin / Equ c 3
review_notes: Curated UniProt record (function largely by similarity to human/bovine albumin); source for the carrier and enterobactin-binding core functions.

title: A novel RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain phosphatase that preferentially dephosphorylates serine 5.
review_notes: One of the two primary sources behind the human CTDSP2 FUNCTION annotation. Abstract-only in the local cache, and the abstract foregrounds SCP1; it cannot establish by itself which assays were performed on CTDSP2/SCP2. The human experimental annotation is retained under that access limitation rather than questioned - the curator read the full text.

title: Small CTD phosphatases function in silencing neuronal gene expression.
review_notes: The REST/neuronal-silencing source behind the curated human record. Abstract-only in the local cache; it addresses the SCP family (SCPs 1 to 3) rather than CTDSP2 in isolation. Cited for pathway context, not as equine evidence.

title: CTDSP2 human-horse sequence comparison
review_notes: Reproducible Biopython global alignment with retained full output, sequence hashes and scoring parameters; computed, not hardcoded. The per-feature table records that both human catalytic-aspartate positions are unaligned or deleted in the horse model - the central reason this review withholds a catalytic claim.

title: UniProtKB F7A4N8: selected horse CTDSP2 protein model
review_notes: Source record for the reviewed protein form. Naming is computational (Ensembl model plus VGNC symbol); it fixes the locus identity but establishes no equine function. The absence of a domain signature is noted as an observation about this record, not as proof of lost activity.

title: UniProtKB O14595: human CTDSP2 catalytic features
review_notes: Curated Swiss-Prot record for the human ortholog. Used as the source of the characterized biology under consideration for transfer and, critically, of the residue-level coordinates that make the transfer unsafe for this truncated protein form.

title: Tctex1d2 associates with short-rib polydactyly syndrome proteins and is required for ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Full text cached. The original identification of TCTEX1D2 as a dynein light chain and the source of the ciliary-base localization claim. The localization is a separate observation from complex assembly and carries its own transfer limits, as the gene notes record.

title: Interaction of WDR60 intermediate chain with TCTEX1D2 light chain of the dynein-2 complex is crucial for ciliary protein trafficking.
review_notes: Full text cached. One of the two experimental sources behind the human FUNCTION annotation. The auxiliary-role conclusion is worth carrying forward, since it tempers how much phenotypic weight a divergent DYNLT2B form would be expected to carry.

title: Structure and tethering mechanism of dynein-2 intermediate chains in intraflagellar transport.
review_notes: Full text cached. The source of the structural context for the human Tctex fold referenced in the notes. Cited for complex composition and the explicit stoichiometry caveat, not for the WDR34/WDR60 tethering results, which concern the intermediate chains rather than DYNLT2B.

title: TCTEX1D2 is essential for sperm flagellum formation in mice.
review_notes: Full text cached. Mouse in vivo evidence; cited for the tissue-restricted phenotype and the second (axonemal dynein) interaction set, both of which shape what an equine experiment should measure. Transfer to horse is not asserted.

title: DYNLT2B: horse–human sequence comparison
review_notes: Reproducible Biopython global alignment (BLOSUM62, gap open -10, extension -0.5) with retained sequence hashes and mapped human structural features; computed, not hardcoded. It localizes the model discrepancy to a specific beta-strand, which is why this review treats the alteration as consequential rather than as generic percentage-identity noise - while still not establishing a folding or binding defect.

title: UniProtKB A0A9L0SWY1: selected horse DYNLT2B protein model
review_notes: Source record for the reviewed protein form. Naming and domain assignment are computational (Ensembl/InterPro/Pfam); they establish family identity but no equine function, and they do not adjudicate the 245-versus-142-residue discrepancy.

title: UniProtKB Q8WW35: human DYNLT2B/TCTEX1D2 (curated reference ortholog)
review_notes: Curated Swiss-Prot record for the human ortholog with experimental ECO codes. Used as the source of characterized mammalian biology under consideration for transfer; the dimer/intermediate-chain architecture is what makes the horse C-terminal difference worth flagging.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Procedural GO reference for combined automated annotation. Correctly applied at the family level; it is a rule-based mapping rather than evidence, which is why the annotation it produced is left UNDECIDED for a model missing the anchoring motif.

title: PtdIns4P synthesis by PI4KIIIα at the plasma membrane and its impact on plasma membrane identity.
review_notes: Full text cached. The primary experimental source for EFR3A palmitoylation and plasma-membrane anchoring, and the direct basis for the UNDECIDED action - the mutant that loses exactly the residues missing from the horse model goes to the cytosol. Human and rodent cell work; equine transfer is not asserted.

title: EFR3A: horse–human sequence comparison
review_notes: Reproducible Biopython global alignment (match 2, mismatch -1, gap open -10, extension -0.5) with retained sequence hashes; computed, not hardcoded. The very high downstream identity is what makes this a localized N-terminal question rather than a doubt about orthology.

title: EFR3A horse-human pairwise alignment
review_notes: Reproducible pairwise alignment emitted by the same Biopython script that generated RESULTS.md. This file shows directly where the N-terminal gap falls: horse Met1 aligns to human Met1, human residues 2-26 are deleted, and the horse sequence resumes at human residue 27.

title: UniProtKB A0A9L0S4L8: selected horse EFR3A protein model
review_notes: Source record for the reviewed protein form. Naming is ARBA rule-based and domain assignment is InterPro/Pfam-based; together they establish family identity but no equine function, and they do not adjudicate the missing N-terminal motif. The sequence start quoted here establishes the selected horse record's N-terminus.

title: UniProtKB Q14156: human EFR3A (curated reference ortholog)
review_notes: Curated Swiss-Prot record for the human ortholog, with experimental ECO codes on the localization and palmitoylation annotations. Used as the source of characterized mammalian biology under consideration for transfer; the membrane-anchoring role is what makes the missing N-terminal motif consequential rather than incidental.

title: UniProt entry Q95182 (Major allergen Equ c 1), Equus caballus

review_notes: Read the entire report and computational artifact. Its decisive O-versus-N clade exclusion and non-pathway/storage-branch argument are contradicted by PMID:42151135 and PMID:41928514. The very tobacco accession the report calls an O-glucosyltransferase is explicitly assayed as UGT1/NaGT in the primary supplement. Automated names and missing annotations were treated as experimental proof. Its no-known-plant-nicotinate-enzyme assertion conflicts with PMID:31611893. Code uses average linkage rather than the claimed neighbor joining and can omit terminal overhangs from identity calculations; independent results use the published assayed sequence. Retain the report as provenance, not as negative functional evidence.

An initial version of this review declined to use this table directly, citing unresolved row-to-gene alignment, and instead sourced the 76% figure to Suzuki-Hashido et al. 2015 (PMID:26201026) below; that alignment is now resolved as described here, and this paper's own table row is the primary source for the figure, with Suzuki-Hashido's restatement retained only as corroboration.

The annotation is kept as curator-made; the earlier supporting quote was the article title and has been removed.

title: Mapping the dynamics of epigenetic adaptation in S. pombe during heterochromatin misregulation.
review_notes: Larkin et al. 2024 (Dev Cell). The quote used is the cached statement that deleting Epe1 together with Mst2 causes aberrant genome-wide H3K9 methylation (relieved only by adaptive clr4 silencing), which is consistent with, but less specific than, a boundary-formation result.

review_notes: The report directly evaluates the contested GO:0032452 IBA and its domain/sequence analysis supports removal. title: Carboxypeptidase yscS: gene structure and function of the vacuolar enzyme.
review_notes: PubMed abstract verified. Direct Saccharomyces cerevisiae CPS1 gene rescue, synthetic-dipeptide utilization and loss of carboxypeptidase activity after disruption; source evidence, not a fission-yeast assay.

review_notes: PubMed abstract verified. Mammalian PM20D1 bidirectional N-acyl-amino-acid catalysis and uncoupling; does not establish target activity or loss of carboxypeptidase function.

review_notes: Its SpCPS trafficking lead was independently verified in full PMID:17660439. Distinguish engineered Ub-GFP routing from native soluble processing and fungal homolog biochemistry from direct target enzyme assays.

title: Deep research on SPAC24C9.08 vacuolar carboxypeptidase (Perplexity)
review_notes: Conserved vacuolar-carboxypeptidase synthesis agrees with verified fungal PAINT ancestry and target location; quantitative substrate/processing descriptions are homolog-derived.

title: UniProt O13968 (SPAC24C9.08) target record
review_notes: Curated target record supports predicted zinc coordination and observed vacuolar localization.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Standard InterPro2GO reference. For SPBC3H7.04 the InterPro entry driving three of the IEA annotations (SOD activity, superoxide metabolic process, metal ion binding) is IPR019832 (Iron/manganese superoxide dismutase, C-terminal domain), a fold/superfamily match only — see geneontology/go-annotation#6474.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: IBA `cytoplasm` propagated from PANTHER family PTHR43595, whose characterized members are cytoplasmic/matrix Fe/Mn-SODs (SOD2, SodA). title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mapping of the UniProt "SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Mitochondrion" statement (SL-0173) to GO:0005739; correct location call.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology inference from GO:0004784 (SOD activity) → GO:0019430 (removal of superoxide radicals). The inference chain is mechanically correct but its input premise (SOD activity for SPBC3H7.04) is wrong, so the derived BP annotation is also wrong and inherits the same fate as the parent IEA.

title: Bot1p is required for mitochondrial translation, respiratory function, and normal cell morphology in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary characterization paper for the S. pombe mS42 mitoribosomal protein (named Bot1p in the paper). Establishes the mitochondrial-ribosome localization and the mitochondrial translation role, and is the ComplexPortal-cited NAS reference for the mt-SSU annotations under review.

title: UniProtKB entry O74379 (RT26_SCHPO) — Small ribosomal subunit protein mS42
review_notes: Authoritative UniProt curation of the protein as a mitoribosomal mS42 family member, not a SOD; primary evidence anchor for this review's core-function assignment.

title: SPBC3H7.04 (mS42 / bot1) — S. pombe mitoribosomal small subunit protein
review_notes: Local reviewer notes file which reproduces the upstream go-annotation curator issue (geneontology/go-annotation#6474) and integrates it with the UniProt-level and PANTHER subfamily evidence and with the pseudoenzyme detection pattern used elsewhere in this repo (Cu/Zn-SOD fold-match without PROSITE PS00087 active-site match; see projects/PSEUDOENZYMES.md).

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Genome-wide GFP localization screen that underlies the mitochondrial localization call for acn1 (via the UniProt SubCell inference and PomBase HDA annotation). Cached entry is abstract-only and does not name acn1 in the abstract, so it is supporting/contextual rather than a direct functional characterization.

title: Broad functional profiling of fission yeast proteins using phenomics and machine learning.
review_notes: Large-scale dark-gene phenomics study; the source of most acn1 FYPO phenotype annotations (broad drug/stress resistance and sensitivity). Frames the conserved-unknown ("unknome") problem that acn1 exemplifies. Provides pleiotropic screen phenotypes, not mechanism.

title: Formation of giant ER sheets by pentadecanoic acid causes lipotoxicity in fission yeast.
review_notes: Lipotoxicity screen contributing the FYPO annotation that acn1 deletion shows normal growth on pentadecanoic acid (a negative result). acn1 is not discussed in the paper's body text; relevant only as screen context linking acn1 to lipid metabolism datasets.

title: UniProtKB entry O74380 (YNV5_SCHPO), Uncharacterized membrane protein C3H7.05c
review_notes: Primary record for the reviewed protein. Establishes the Wax_synthase_dom / MBOAT_2 domain (IPR032805 / PF13813), the nine predicted transmembrane helices, the mitochondrial-membrane subcellular-location inference, and the "Predicted" (PE 4) status. All supporting_text quotes are verbatim from the cached UniProt record.

title: Deep research report (falcon/Edison): acn1 / SPBC3H7.05c functional annotation
review_notes: Automated deep-research synthesis. Its acn1-specific conclusion (no primary functional characterization exists; function inferable only from the MBOAT/wax-synthase domain) is consistent with independent inspection of UniProt, PomBase, and the primary literature. Its DOI citations are MBOAT-family reviews, not acn1-specific studies, and are treated as family background only. Note it double-lists IPR032805 and PF13813 as two domains; they are the same domain.

title: Genome-wide identification of fungal GPI proteins.
review_notes: PubMed/DOI-verified (Yeast 2003; De Groot, Hellingwerf, Klis). Abstract-only in cache; the per-gene assignment of SPAC19G12.16c to the 33 S. pombe GPI candidates underlies the PomBase TAS cell-surface annotation. Establishes a predicted GPI-anchored cell-surface role, not an experimentally demonstrated molecular function.

title: The cell cycle-regulated genes of Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS Biol 2005; Oliva et al.; PMID 15966770). Full text cached. The cell-separation role of adg2 is a cluster-level co-regulation inference (shared Ace2 sites + expression timing + a cell-surface-glycoprotein descriptor); adg2 itself was not functionally assayed here, so this supports a plausible process association, not a demonstrated adg2 function.

title: ORFeome cloning and global analysis of protein localization in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed/DOI-verified (Nat Biotechnol 2006; Matsuyama et al.). Genome-scale YFP localization screen; the specific adg2 ER call is in the dataset rather than the abstract. ER is a transit/secretory compartment consistent with a secretory glycoprotein, not confirmation of a mature GPI-anchored cell-wall product.

title: Deciphering the transcriptional-regulatory network of flocculation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS Genet 2012; Kwon et al.; PMID 23236291). Full text cached. Provides transcriptional-network context (adg2 as an Ace2 target linked to the Adn2/Adn3 flocculation program) but does not establish an Adg2 molecular activity; cited for regulatory placement, not for a function claim, so no verbatim supporting_text is attached.
