review_notes: Reactome pathway context (serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) containing the AANAT-catalyzed step.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Early proteome-scale two-hybrid map; source of the first AAR2-EAPP protein-binding annotation, which has no functional follow-up.

title: Crystallization and biochemical characterization of the human spliceosomal Aar2-Prp8(RNaseH) complex.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. This is the paper that justifies transferring the yeast Aar2p mechanism to the human protein, and therefore underpins the IBA and ISS annotations. It is also the UniProt SUBUNIT evidence (ECO:0000269|PubMed:26527271). Abstract-only, but the orthology claim quoted is explicit there.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. Large-scale interactome; second recovery of AAR2-EAPP.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. BioPlex AP-MS; third and methodologically orthogonal recovery of AAR2-EAPP, which makes the physical interaction credible without making it informative.

title: TSSC4 is a component of U5 snRNP that promotes tri-snRNP formation.
review_notes: Cached full text matches the cited title. This is the reference that distinguishes the TSSC4 protein-binding annotation from the three EAPP ones: it is a dedicated functional study rather than a screen, and it establishes TSSC4 as a U5 snRNP assembly chaperone, making the AAR2-TSSC4 interaction mechanistically expected.

title: Structural and functional investigation of the human snRNP assembly factor AAR2 in complex with the RNase H-like domain of PRPF8.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation; abstract-only, but the quoted results are stated there. Flagged in this review because GOA codes all three of its annotations (GO:0000387, GO:0005682, GO:0048025) as NAS, whereas the paper reports a crystal structure, designed interface variants that fail to bind PRPF8, and SEC interaction mapping - direct experimental results on the human protein.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AAR2 (human)
review_notes: Trust gate TRIPPED, but on inspection this is a false positive worth recording. The gate fires when the narrative's opening names a non-human organism in a human record - the ADA symbol-collision failure mode - and here it names yeast. It is not a collision: the narrative correctly covers yeast Aar2p, in which the mechanism was established structurally, and human AAR2, its genuine ortholog. UniProt itself annotates the human FUNCTION as ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:P32357, by similarity to the yeast protein, so a yeast-centred account is the correct description of this gene's literature. Every claim used here was re-verified against the cited PMIDs. The gate did its job by prompting the check; it simply needs curator adjudication for genes whose mechanism was worked out in yeast.

title: Aard is specifically up-regulated in Sertoli cells during mouse testis differentiation.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Establishes the expression pattern that is essentially all that is known about this gene, and describes it plainly as "a gene of unknown function". Expression data only - deliberately not converted into a GO process annotation.

title: Alanine and arginine rich domain containing protein, Aard, is directly regulated by androgen receptor in mouse Sertoli cells.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. Important for what it does not license: being a direct transcriptional target of androgen receptor signalling is a downstream relationship, not participation in that pathway, so it does not support an androgen-receptor-signalling process annotation for AARD. This is the same conflation identified for the mouse A1bg growth-hormone annotation earlier in this campaign, and it is avoided here rather than repeated. The paper's own "important in spermatogenesis" is a statement about the AR programme, not a demonstrated AARD requirement - no AARD loss-of-function experiment has been reported.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. The HuRI binary interactome, and the sole source of every GO annotation AARD has. The study itself is sound and large-scale; the caution here concerns what its data support for this particular prey, whose 15 partners show the coiled-coil bias and compartment scatter characteristic of a promiscuous two-hybrid prey.

title: Are AARD's reported interactors a coherent partner set?
review_notes: Reproducible analysis written for this review (analyze_partners.py), re-runnable, with partner accessions read from the gene's own AARD-goa.tsv so they cannot drift from the record under review, and all protein data fetched from the UniProt REST API at run time. Failed fetches are reported rather than silently counted as absence. It tests one specific falsifiable hypothesis - coiled-coil bias - against a fetched background rate, rather than asserting either the bias or the enrichment. Extended after PR review to add that null model, to collapse UniProt's hierarchical location strings to top-level compartments (which reduced an inflated "20 locations" to 14), and to enumerate AARD's PANTHER family.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AARD (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; both claims used were re-verified against the cited PMIDs. Notable as a negative signal done well: its mechanism_profile reports no molecular activity, no localisation and no partners, and the narrative says so in prose rather than manufacturing a plausible function. For a gene this dark that restraint is the useful contribution. It also did not attempt to convert the androgen-receptor target relationship into a pathway role.

title: Editing-defective tRNA synthetase causes protein misfolding and neurodegeneration.
review_notes: Mouse sticky mutation links AlaRS editing failure to serine mischarging and proteostasis defects. PubMed identity and abstract verified; cited to trace the mouse tRNA-modification source, not as direct human evidence.

title: The C-Ala domain brings together editing and aminoacylation functions on one tRNA.
review_notes: Full-text mechanistic study. It supports conserved Gly/Ser-tRNA(Ala) editing specificity and functional conservation of human C-Ala, but the human evidence is a cross-species domain graft rather than a direct full-length human Gly-tRNA(Ala) deacylation assay; it therefore supports only a cautious ISS claim.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. This high-throughput fractionation study is relevant only to the HDA membrane tuple. Its abstract does not expose the AARS1-specific result; neither a stable nor a transient association can be independently adjudicated from the accessible evidence.

title: Alanyl-tRNA synthetase from Escherichia coli, Bombyx mori and Ratus ratus. Existence of common structural features.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identity and abstract verified on 2026-09-27 at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2040280/; the normally recovered cache is abstract-only. This compares bacterial, Bombyx mori and rat-liver enzymes, not human AARS1. Proteolysis reduces aminoacylation while largely retaining pyrophosphate exchange; alanine plus ATP protects against digestion. These measurements corroborate the legacy donor biochemical context, but the abstract does not resolve every binding assay underlying the existing donor annotations. No full body was recovered or read, and the curated transfer judgments retain their independent human support. The exact machine-fetched title, including Ratus ratus, is preserved.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. This source supports context-specific proteomic survey of a B-cell exosome preparation. The AARS1-specific supplementary result was inaccessible, so its annotation remains UNDECIDED.

title: Deficiencies in tRNA synthetase editing activity cause cardioproteinopathy.
review_notes: Mouse editing-defect study underlying current Q8BGQ7 annotation rows. PubMed identity and abstract verified; full-text PMC retrieval failed. Supports a proofreading interpretation rather than nucleotide modification.

title: Loss-of-function alanyl-tRNA synthetase mutations cause an autosomal-recessive early-onset epileptic encephalopathy with persistent myelination defect.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. Direct human genetic and functional evidence for recessive loss of AARS1 charging function; the cache is abstract-only, so no more detailed assay interpretation is asserted.

title: Evolutionary Gain of Alanine Mischarging to Noncognate tRNAs with a G4:U69 Base Pair.
review_notes: Full-text primary study with recombinant human enzyme, cellular reporter data, and structural analysis. It establishes a noncanonical mischarging capacity, but this is secondary to cognate tRNA(Ala) charging and editing.

title: Two crystal structures reveal design for repurposing the C-Ala domain of human AlaRS.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. Direct structural and binding evidence for human C-Ala architecture, but the isolated-domain DNA-binding result does not by itself establish a physiological DNA-binding function for full-length AARS1.

title: Deficient activity of alanyl-tRNA synthetase underlies an autosomal recessive syndrome of progressive microcephaly, hypomyelination, and epileptic encephalopathy.
review_notes: Full-text primary study directly assaying recombinant human AARS1 alanine charging and Ser-tRNA(Ala) editing. It strongly supports both canonical enzymatic functions and loss-of-function disease mechanisms.

title: Double mimicry evades tRNA synthetase editing by toxic vegetable-sourced non-proteinogenic amino acid.
review_notes: Full-text primary study directly characterizing human AlaRS substrate activation and editing selectivity. It corroborates the editing function but addresses a dietary nonproteinogenic amino acid rather than the normal Ser/Gly error substrates.

title: ANKRD16 prevents neuron loss caused by an editing-defective tRNA synthetase.
review_notes: Full-text primary mouse study and PubMed identity verified. ANKRD16 accepts misactivated serine from AlaRS and limits serine-tRNA(Ala) formation; used to evaluate the mouse source term, without assigning an AARS1-specific ANKRD16 process.

title: Hypermorphic and hypomorphic AARS alleles in patients with CMT2N expand clinical and molecular heterogeneities.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. It establishes heterogeneous dominant neuropathy mechanisms and prevents overgeneralizing all pathogenic AARS1 alleles as simple loss of charging activity.

title: Protein instability associated with AARS1 and MARS1 mutations causes trichothiodystrophy.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. Direct patient-cell evidence for an AARS1 disease mechanism combining protein instability with impaired charging; the source is not needed to define the normal catalytic reaction.

title: Expanded phenotype of AARS1-related white matter disease.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/title identity verified, and the exact source12 abstract-only record read. The cross-sectional series contains 11 individuals with biallelic AARS1 variants; the later-onset subgroup is defined as onset after the first year of life. Five tested affected individuals had reduced AlaRS activity in available fibroblasts. This supports the range of recessive AARS1 disease, but does not itself establish adult-onset ALSP, a specific editing defect, or a general disease-process GO function. Full original body was not recovered/read for this closure.

title: A humanized yeast model reveals dominant-negative properties of neuropathy-associated alanyl-tRNA synthetase mutations.
review_notes: PubMed/Europe PMC identity and abstract verified. The cached abstract directly supports interaction-dependent dominant-negative effects and identifies the affected ARSs as homodimeric. The PMC full-text XML/HTML retrieval failed; detailed cellular dimer quantitation is therefore not quoted as cached evidence.

title: The alanyl-tRNA synthetase AARS1 moonlights as a lactyltransferase to promote YAP signaling in gastric cancer.
review_notes: Full-text primary study with purified-protein, cellular, and tumor-model evidence for AARS1 lactyltransferase activity and lactate-responsive nuclear YAP1/TEAD1 activation. This downstream activation does not by itself establish either positive or negative regulation of the GO-defined MST/LATS cascade.

title: Alanyl-tRNA synthetase, AARS1, is a lactate sensor and lactyltransferase that lactylates p53 and contributes to tumorigenesis.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. Direct mechanistic support for the lactate-AMP intermediate, protein lactyltransferase activity, and TP53 inhibition. Its tumor-cell global-lactylation framing is context dependent in light of PMID:40835008; the substrate-specific findings remain supported.

title: AARS1 and AARS2 sense L-lactate to regulate cGAS as global lysine lactyltransferases.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. It independently supports shared ATP-dependent AARS1/AARS2 lactyltransferase chemistry. The downstream cGAS mechanism is explicitly AARS2-specific and must not be assigned to AARS1.

title: Yeast models for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease-causing aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase alleles reveal the cellular basis of disease.
review_notes: The PubMed identity and recovered full PMC11953622 review were checked. Its AARS1 section usefully distinguishes yeast ALA1 complementation, human cytosolic function and allele-dependent assay limitations. It is a review, not a new direct human activity experiment. The generalization that human AlaRS is predominantly monomeric under normal cellular conditions is not adopted: the original purified-protein observation and separately examined humanized-yeast interference data have different assay scopes, as documented for PMID:7654687 and PMID:40491354. This assessment disputes that generalization, not the bibliographic identity or the existence of the reported yeast phenotypes.

title: Recessive, pathogenic AARS1 variants display variable loss-of-function and dominant-negative effects.
review_notes: Full-text primary study and PubMed identity verified. Tests 16 recessive-disease missense variants in humanized yeast and evaluates dominant-negative effects of severe alleles. The authors explicitly note false negatives and limited genotype-phenotype prediction; model interference is not evidence that every heterozygous carrier develops neuropathy.

title: Class I histone deacetylases catalyze lysine lactylation.
review_notes: Full-text independent counter-scope study. It does not refute purified-enzyme activity or high-lactate substrate-specific effects, but shows that AARS1 is not required for basal global lactylation in HEK293T cells and constrains broad claims.

title: AARS1 and AARS2: From Protein Synthesis to Lactylation-Driven Oncogenesis.
review_notes: Primary PubMed-derived DOI/title identity and full PMC12467997 review inspected. This is a secondary synthesis covering both AARS1 and AARS2; organellar and substrate-specific mechanisms are kept separate. Its broad global-lactylation framing is read in the tumor/high-lactate context and does not override the directly measured untreated-HEK293T knockdown result in PMID:40835008. The existing annotation decisions remain grounded in their primary reaction/localization experiments, not the review alone.

title: The role of Alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 lactylation in tumors and other diseases.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identity and full PMC12961078 review inspected. Bibliographic identity is correct, but the disease-mechanism narrative is not used as independent evidence: Figure 1 and the body expand ALSP differently, and its detailed proofreading/ER-stress disease claims require their original experimental sources. The newly cached biallelic series PMID:34446925 is independently scoped and is not equated to every adult-onset leukoencephalopathy claim. This flags the review narrative and nomenclature, without rejecting the separately established AARS1 charging or conditional lactyltransferase chemistry.

title: Comprehensive pan-cancer analysis of AARS1, a newly identified lactyltransferase in human cancers.
review_notes: Primary PubMed-derived DOI/title identity and full PMC13214215 Methods/Results/Figure 12 inspected. The paper combines pan-cancer expression/outcome associations with human renal-cancer-cell perturbations, total/TP53 lactylation measurements and wild-type versus AARS1-5A rescue. Its five-alanine mutant is specified in Methods; the examined experiments do not independently measure preservation of aminoacylation by that construct. Moreover, the Methods, Results prose and Figure 12 caption differ in naming the rescue cell lines, so this assessment retains renal-cancer-cell scope rather than certifying one inconsistent line assignment. The positive phenotype and lactylation observations support tumor-context involvement without treating association or non-rescue alone as proof that all effects are uniquely separated from canonical charging. No new annotation/core is added from these results.

title: Excess intracellular lactate represses mRNA translation and tumor progression through lactate-tRNA charging.
review_notes: PubMed/Europe PMC identifier, title and abstract verified. Full text was inaccessible from the publisher. Record as an emerging substrate-class finding and follow-up question; do not add a new GO activity/process or reinterpret established proofreading annotations from this abstract alone.

title: Covalent allosteric inhibition of AARS1 lactyltransferase.
review_notes: Full-text primary study and PubMed identity verified. Lactate binding, pyrophosphate-generation assays, structures and cellular YAP lactylation support the mechanism. XY353-1 shows a bounded selectivity window: alanine-substrate activity was not significantly affected at 5–20 micromolar, with 33.5% inhibition at 40 micromolar; U2OS global lactylation and protein-synthesis IC50 values were 12.9 and 34.7 micromolar. Protein synthesis was unaffected at 10 micromolar but inhibited at 20 and 40 micromolar in the separate dose assay. This is concentration- and assay-dependent pharmacological selectivity, not complete enzyme-intrinsic separation or universal AARS1 dependence of basal lactylation.

title: Human alanyl-tRNA synthetase: conservation in evolution of catalytic core and microhelix recognition.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. The study supports human AARS1 tRNA binding, aminoacylation, acceptor-helix recognition, and monomeric behavior of the purified enzyme. Later humanized-yeast co-expression evidence (full-text PMID:40491354) limits generalization to all cellular contexts, without refuting the purified preparation. It does not establish pre-tRNA processing, so its source GO:0008033 use is miscited. The separate cytoplasm TAS annotation is retained with curator deference because only the abstract is available locally and independent localization evidence is concordant.

title: Wide cross-species aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase replacement in vivo: yeast cytoplasmic alanine enzyme replaced by human polymyositis serum antigen.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract verified. This is direct in-vivo complementation evidence that human AARS1 supports cytoplasmic alanyl-tRNA aminoacylation, although the experimental cellular context is yeast.

title: Cytosolic tRNA aminoacylation
review_notes: Curated human Reactome pathway entry for cytosolic tRNA aminoacylation. It provides pathway context; the AARS1-specific reaction is captured in R-HSA-379864.

title: alanine + tRNA(Ala) + ATP => Ala-tRNA(Ala) + AMP + pyrophosphate
review_notes: Curated human Reactome reaction entry representing canonical AARS1 charging and cytosolic location. Its monomeric description follows the purified-enzyme study PMID:7654687; later humanized-yeast co-expression effects (full-text PMID:40491354) are interpreted using a homodimer model and prevent treating this preparation-specific observation as universal.

title: Falcon/Edison deep research report for human AARS1 (2026-09-25)
review_notes: Provider-authored research aid that completed after the wrapper timeout; not independent experimental support. Its canonical charging and AARS1/AARS2 distinction are consistent with primary evidence. Physiological monomer predominance, direct full-length human Gly-tRNA(Ala) editing, and neomorphic interaction claims are not adopted without primary verification. Annotation judgments use the separately cached primary publications.

title: UniProtKB record for human AARS1 (P49588)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProtKB record for human cytosolic alanyl-tRNA synthetase. It consolidates the alanine-charging and editing reactions, conditional lactyltransferase activity, cytoplasmic and lactate-responsive nuclear localization, isoforms, and disease variants, while preserving evidence provenance for each assertion. The monomeric subunit statement is not comprehensive in light of cellular self-association and dominant-negative evidence in PMID:37010095 and PMID:40491354.

title: Exome sequencing identifies mitochondrial alanyl-tRNA synthetase mutations in infantile mitochondrial cardiomyopathy.
review_notes: Full text recovered with the supported publication fetcher on 2026-09-25. Figure 3D directly shows AARS2-GFP targeting mitochondria in HEK293T cells. Variant-specific aminoacylation and editing defects were proposed by homology modeling, while cultured patient cells had no detected mitochondrial translation defect under the conditions tested. Later direct biochemistry supports the enzyme identity; the 2011 modeling must not be quoted as measured variant kinetics.

title: Novel (ovario) leukodystrophy related to AARS2 mutations.
review_notes: Establishes the broader human AARS2 disease spectrum, but its functional assay is yeast complementation and respiratory-chain analysis rather than direct human AARS2 charging or editing. Disease phenotypes are not core molecular functions.

title: Editing activity for eliminating mischarged tRNAs is essential in mammalian mitochondria.
review_notes: Primary direct evidence using recombinant mature human AARS2. The biochemical Ser-editing assays are human in vitro experiments; evidence that editing is essential in vivo comes from homozygous editing-deficient mouse knock-ins.

title: Overexpression of human mitochondrial alanyl-tRNA synthetase suppresses biochemical defects of the mt-tRNA(Ala) mutation in cybrids.
review_notes: Human-cell evidence supporting mitochondrial mt-tRNAAla charging and downstream translation. The system consists of transmitochondrial cybrids carrying pathogenic m.5655A>G plus AARS2 overexpression, so it is rescue evidence rather than a basal wild-type kinetic assay. The cached text itself contains the word form "incharged" and it is retained verbatim.

title: Instability of the mitochondrial alanyl-tRNA synthetase underlies fatal infantile-onset cardiomyopathy.
review_notes: Includes human patient fibroblast, skeletal-muscle and cardiac-tissue data, recombinant human enzyme assays, and HEK293T stability assays. The conclusion is variant-specific and must not be generalized to all AARS2 disease alleles.

title: The G3-U70-independent tRNA recognition by human mitochondrial alanyl-tRNA synthetase.
review_notes: Strongest direct support for human Gly-tRNAAla editing. Enzymology used recombinant human AARS2 and in-vitro-transcribed human mt-tRNAAla. Monomeric state was additionally tested by co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293T cells; the data do not support a stable-complex core function.

title: Relaxed sequence constraints favor mutational freedom in idiosyncratic metazoan mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: Direct human charging and substrate-discrimination evidence using purified mature AARS2 and unmodified in-vitro-transcribed tRNAs. Crystal structures concern isolated human C-Ala fragments; the full-length AARS2-tRNA complex was modeled rather than crystallized.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: The primary HuRI supplement and UniProt/IntAct independently confirm the EHHADH-AARS2 and PTPA-AARS2 binary pairs. The source provides no native-complex context or AARS2-specific mechanism, so it validates pair provenance but not a useful core molecular function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Full Supplementary Table S1 directly identifies Q5JTZ9/AARS2 in this dataset and assigns it to MitoCoP, with concordant subtractive, spatial and importomics classifications. This is valid high-throughput mitochondrial-localization evidence and is independently corroborated by targeted and biochemical studies.

title: Hypoxia induces mitochondrial protein lactylation to limit oxidative phosphorylation.
review_notes: Direct support for conditional AARS2 lactyltransferase activity, with hypoxia and high lactate as central contexts. Cellular physiology and in-vivo evidence are predominantly from mouse cells and mice. Cytoplasmic AARS2 detected during hypoxia was also in mouse cells and is not direct basal human localization evidence.

title: AARS1 and AARS2 sense L-lactate to regulate cGAS as global lysine lactyltransferases.
review_notes: PubMed metadata and publisher full text were independently read on 2026-09-25; the standard cache remains abstract-only because PubMed supplies no PMC record. Figure 3 and Extended Data Figure 4 document purified human AARS2 chemistry. Extended Data Figure 5h tests human THP1 cells; 5g reports endogenous AARS2-cGAS proximity in HeLa cells after 25 mM NaLac for 24 h. These support the conditional human mechanism but do not identify the precursor/mature AARS2 species or route to cGAS. Mouse conditional genetics supplies the in-vivo immune evidence. See notes for the publisher URL and assay boundaries.

title: AARS2-catalyzed lactylation induces follicle development and premature ovarian insufficiency.
review_notes: Human-cell and recombinant-protein evidence for conditional substrate-specific lactyltransferase activity, centered on ovarian disease variants and supported in vivo by mouse ovarian models. The prose calls the line COV343 whereas the adjacent figure legend calls it COV434; the cached quote is preserved while the internal model-label inconsistency is flagged.

title: Class I histone deacetylases catalyze lysine lactylation.
review_notes: Essential counter-scope for the global-lactyltransferase framing. This result concerns global basal Kla in untreated proliferating HEK293T cells and does not refute target-specific AARS2 activity under hypoxia, high lactate, glucose starvation, or other induced conditions.

title: PCBP1 regulates alternative splicing of AARS2 in congenital cardiomyopathy.
review_notes: Human AARS2 exon-16 minigenes were tested in HEK293T cells and hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes; extensive causal heart-development and OXPHOS evidence comes from mouse conditional genetics. This supports regulated transcript processing and a loss-of-function disease mechanism, not a distinct stable AARS2 protein isoform with a proven alternative activity.

title: alanine + tRNA(Ala) + ATP => Ala-tRNA(Ala) + AMP + pyrophosphate
review_notes: The reaction chemistry and mitochondrial substrate are correct and match later direct human biochemical evidence. Reactome explicitly states that this event was originally inferred computationally from other characterized mitochondrial tRNA synthetases, so it is pathway/database support rather than independent experimental evidence for AARS2.

title: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record for human AARS2 (Q5JTZ9)
review_notes: Authoritative reviewed record for Q5JTZ9. Its charging/editing and mitochondrial localization summary agrees with the direct literature. Its lactyltransferase summary is correctly restricted to high lactate, and its explicit compartmental caution is retained; the entry is not used to infer basal global lactylation or routine extramitochondrial localization.

title: Vertebrate Acyl CoA synthetase family member 4 (ACSF4-U26) is a β-alanine-activating enzyme homologous to bacterial non-ribosomal peptide synthetase.
review_notes: Cached record title matches the citation. The defining biochemical study of this enzyme and the basis for removing the fatty-acid ISS and for all three proposed annotations. The work was done on the mouse recombinant protein; the human protein is annotated by UniProt from that ortholog (ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:Q80WC9, mouse Aasdh), which is a genuine ortholog relationship - unlike the paralog ACSF3 that the removed ISS came from. Abstract-only cache, but every claim used is stated explicitly in the abstract.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AASDH (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; every claim used was re-verified against PMID:24467666. Accurate and appropriately restrained - it identifies the beta-alanine specificity, the phosphopantetheine requirement and the domain carrying the activity, and states plainly that no downstream role is established rather than inventing one. Its GO grounding (GO:0140657 ATP-dependent activity, GO:0016874 ligase activity) is correct but two levels too general and was not imported. Notably it says nothing about fatty acids, which is consistent with removing the fatty-acid ISS here, though as with A1BG earlier in this campaign the provider gives no positive signal that a bad annotation exists - its silence only corroborates after the fact.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: This is method provenance for the InterPro-to-GO electronic annotations, not experimental evidence about AASDHPPT itself. The source identifier and mapping role agree with the seeded GOA records.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: This is PAINT/IBA method provenance. The inferred transferase and protein- maturation annotations require evaluation against direct human biochemistry; this reference is not independent biological evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: This documents the automated UniProt subcellular-location mapping. It explains the cytosol IEA but does not add evidence beyond the reviewed UniProt record and the primary localization study.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: This is provenance for a combined electronic call supported by family, reaction, and EC mappings. The catalytic assignment is independently supported by direct human biochemical studies.

title: Identification of the alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde dehydrogenase-phosphopantetheinyl transferase gene, the human ortholog of the yeast LYS5 gene.
review_notes: The PMID and title are verified in the local PubMed cache. Functional evidence comes from complementation of Saccharomyces cerevisiae lys5, so it supports conserved activity but is not direct biochemical characterization in human cells or with purified human substrates. Only the abstract is cached.

title: Cloning, expression, and characterization of a human 4'-phosphopantetheinyl transferase with broad substrate specificity.
review_notes: Foundational direct human cloning and biochemical evidence for broad-substrate phosphopantetheinyl-transferase activity and cytosolic localization. The local cache is abstract-only. Its historical 329-residue description differs from the current reviewed 309-residue UniProt sequence, so the obsolete length is not used as a functional conclusion.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: The PMID, title, and high-throughput binary-screen design are verified. GOA records an AASDHPPT-TRAF2 IPI from this source, but the cached abstract does not expose the individual pair and supplies no substrate, regulatory, or stable- complex mechanism. Only the abstract is cached.

title: Mechanism and substrate recognition of human holo ACP synthase.
review_notes: Direct structural and kinetic characterization of recombinant human AASDHPPT, including CoA, Mg2+, and human FASN ACP complexes. This is the strongest source for catalytic residues, Mg2+ coordination, and the physiological enzyme-substrate interface; full text is cached.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: GOA records AASDHPPT as an HDA identification in urinary exosomes, and the PMID, title, sample, and proteomic scale are verified. The cached text contains only the abstract and not the protein-identification table, so the individual AASDHPPT peptide hit cannot be independently re-read here. Detection in this preparation does not establish exosomal function or selective secretion.

title: Defining the human deubiquitinating enzyme interaction landscape.
review_notes: The PMID, title, and CompPASS interaction-screen scope are verified. GOA records an AASDHPPT-USP22 IPI from this source, but the cached abstract does not identify the individual pair or establish direct binding, regulation, or stable-complex membership. Only the abstract is cached.

title: Acyl carrier protein-specific 4'-phosphopantetheinyl transferase activates 10-formyltetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Direct purified-human-protein and human A549 knockdown evidence identifies AASDHPPT as the ALDH1L1 phosphopantetheinyl transferase, establishes the Ser354 acceptor, and links modification to FDH activity. Full text is cached.

title: Enzymatic properties of ALDH1L2, a mitochondrial 10-formyltetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Direct recombinant human-substrate evidence for AASDHPPT modification of ALDH1L2 and the Ser375 acceptor, with A549 lysate knockdown corroboration in the full text. This supports a substrate-specific downstream effect on folate catabolism, not folate-catabolic chemistry by AASDHPPT itself.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: The PMID, title, and binary-screen scope are verified. GOA records interactions with TRAF2, SIAH1, and USP22 from this map. Those pairs preserve useful provenance but do not establish that the proteins are AASDHPPT substrates, regulators, or stable complex members.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: The PMID, title, and AP-MS co-association design are verified. GOA records an AASDHPPT-USP22 isoform-2 association, but the screen alone does not demonstrate direct binding, a stable AASDHPPT complex, or a functional consequence.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: The PMID, title, and Y2H-based binary-map scope are verified. GOA records AASDHPPT pairs with CRX, TRAF2, EFHC2, and USP22 isoform 2. The paper's own scope cautions that most individual PPI functions remain unresolved, so these records do not define AASDHPPT's molecular function.

title: Chemical Proteomic Profiling of Protein 4'-Phosphopantetheinylation in Mammalian Cells.
review_notes: Human HepG2 chemical-proteomic evidence supports the cellular substrate/PTM landscape and reports a candidate DHRS2 site. The cached abstract does not include the protein/site table or directly perturb AASDHPPT, so it corroborates phosphopantetheinylation targets rather than independently assigning every site to this enzyme. Only the abstract is cached.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ABHD14A (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record. Gates passed, but it must not be used as it stands, for a reason worth recording for the whole campaign: its two most substantive claims - that a truncated ABHD14A hydrolyses short-chain esters with CoA enhancement, and that the full-length protein localises to the Golgi - both cite 'PMID:bio_10.1101_2025.11.28.691245', which is not a PubMed identifier at all but a bioRxiv DOI encoded in a PMID-shaped field. The provider's citation slot can therefore contain non-PMID identifiers formatted to look like PMIDs, and a reader skimming for PMIDs would take preprint claims for peer-reviewed ones. Those claims are excluded here; if the preprint is published they would justify a hydrolase molecular function and a Golgi location, neither of which is annotated now.

review_notes: Crude NK-cell membrane-fraction proteomics. Its own abstract reports only ~40% of hits as plausible membrane proteins, which is the basis for marking the GO:0016020 row over-annotated. Cited for the caveat, not for the localisation.

title: Regulation of synaptic Rac1 activity, long-term potentiation maintenance, and learning and memory by BCR and ABR Rac GTPase-activating proteins.
review_notes: The key synaptic paper: PSD-95 interaction, enhanced basal Rac1, selective loss of LTP maintenance. Full text available and read.

title: Control of local Rho GTPase crosstalk by Abr.
review_notes: Xenopus single-cell wound repair; the clearest in vivo demonstration of the GEF and GAP domains acting on different GTPases in one zone. Carries an ordinary author erratum (Curr Biol 21(7):623), not a retraction.

title: Abr, a negative regulator of Rac, attenuates cockroach allergen-induced asthma in a mouse model.
review_notes: Single abr-/- knockout with elevated GTP-bound Rac in CD4+ T cells; valuable because it does not depend on the redundant double mutant.

title: Deciphering the Molecular and Functional Basis of RHOGAP Family Proteins: A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TOWARD SELECTIVE INACTIVATION OF RHO FAMILY PROTEINS.
review_notes: Systematic RHOGAP-versus-RHO-protein survey. Its conclusion that the RHOGAP domain is nonselective in cell-free conditions is what reconciles the RHOB and Rac/Cdc42 substrate claims. Cached abstract does not name ABR, so the ABR-specific RHOB result could not be verified here.

title: Mapping the proximity interaction network of the Rho-family GTPases reveals signalling pathways and regulatory mechanisms.
review_notes: BioID proximity map cited by Reactome as supporting ABR as a RHOB GAP. Cached abstract does not name ABR and the assay measures proximity to active RHOB, not GAP activity. Carries an author erratum (Nat Cell Biol 22(3):353), not a retraction.

title: EspH interacts with the host active Bcr related (ABR) protein to suppress RhoGTPases.
review_notes: Full text available. Supplies the only human-cell loss-of-function result in the set: ABR knockdown in HeLa raises active Rac1 but not Cdc42. Also independently describes ABR's C-terminal PDZ-binding motif.

title: Abr and Bcr are multifunctional regulators of the Rho GTP-binding protein family.
review_notes: The defining biochemistry for both of ABR's catalytic modules, with Rap1A/Ha-Ras negative controls. Verified against the cached abstract; note the assays used isolated recombinant domains, which is what reconciles them with Amin et al. 2016.

title: The human active breakpoint cluster region-related gene encodes a brain protein with homology to guanine nucleotide exchange proteins and GTPase-activating proteins.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms an actual E. coli fusion-protein GAP assay against Rac1 and Cdc42, so the two TAS rows citing it are better supported than the evidence code implies.

title: Human ABR encodes a protein with GAPrac activity and homology to the DBL nucleotide exchange factor domain.
review_notes: Independent 1993 confirmation of Rac-directed GAP activity, and the source of the observation that ABR lacks BCR's serine/threonine kinase region.

title: ABR WITH/FROM resolution and donor-evidence audit
review_notes: Generated by the committed resolve_withfrom.py; RESULTS.md regenerates byte-identically from results.json, and the dead-accession and multi-hit guards were break-tested.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ABR (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched LLM-generated survey, treated as a set of leads. Used only for the corpus-level direction of the literature and for locating PMIDs; no mechanistic claim in this review rests on a provider sentence. Its individual findings that were used were re-verified against the cited PMIDs.

title: UniProtKB entry Q12979 (ABR_HUMAN)
review_notes: Source for the domain boundaries, the R683 arginine finger, the R683A/N795A and V859A mutagenesis, and the subcellular location evidence tags. Residues 683 (R), 795 (N) and 859 (V) were confirmed against the SQ block.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Source of five rows, all transfers from mouse Q8BUZ1 or rat Q8K4K7. Both are genuine one-to-one orthologs within a single-subfamily PANTHER family, so the curator judgement of sequence similarity is not in doubt here.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The three PAINT rows are the best part of this record. Node PTN001100454 lies in an ortholog-only family, and the terms chosen (sarcomere, Rho signalling, positive regulation of Pol II transcription) match the mouse experimental evidence without over-reaching.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Generated the bare GO:0005856 cytoskeleton row from UniProt's "Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton" statement. Mechanically correct, but the mapping stops at a top-level term where the underlying biology is actin-specific.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of intracellular localizations of expressed fusion proteins in living cells
review_notes: The LIFEdb GFP-fusion survey, and the sole source of the plasma-membrane call. Its own title states the method: localisation of expressed fusion proteins. For a muscle-restricted protein assayed in a non-muscle line at non-native levels this is a weak basis for a located_in annotation, and it is recorded as IDA, which reads as far stronger than it is.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Correct in what it transferred into human (actin cytoskeleton, actin cytoskeleton organization, both from mouse experimental annotations). Noted for the reverse direction: the same pipeline carried the human LIFEdb plasma-membrane call back into the mouse record.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Duplicates three calls already present from curator and PAINT sources. No new information, no error; its WITH/FROM chains resolve to the same two rodent orthologs and to the family-specific InterPro signature IPR026111.

title: STARS, a striated muscle activator of Rho signaling and serum response factor-dependent transcription.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Cloned both the mouse and the human cDNA (the human clone AF503617 is cited in the human UniProt entry), but the functional experiments are attributed by UniProt to the mouse protein, which is why the human record carries the results as ISS rather than IDA. Abstract-only in the cache; the localisation and Rho claims are taken as stated and the overexpression caveat is recorded rather than used to reject them.

title: Muscle-specific signaling mechanism that links actin dynamics to serum response factor.
review_notes: Cached title matches. The key paper for the proposed GO:0042307 addition, and the one that shows the mouse GO:0006606 protein import into nucleus annotation has the causation backwards - STARS causes MRTF import, it is not the imported cargo. Also the source of the caveat on GO:0035025: RhoA is described as required for the STARS effect, not as its target.

title: Two novel members of the ABLIM protein family, ABLIM-2 and -3, associate with STARS and directly bind F-actin.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Worth noting for the record: these are ABRA's best-supported protein interactions, with functional consequences in both directions, and none of them appears in the human GOA file - the only interaction annotation human ABRA has is the Y2H hit with PPP1R18.

title: Modulation of adverse cardiac remodeling by STARS, a mediator of MEF2 signaling and SRF activity.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Independent statement of the MRTF nuclear-translocation step, supporting the proposed GO:0042307 addition. It is also the source of the Z-disc localisation that conflicts with the I-band report, which is why sarcomere is kept as the annotated compartment. Its regulatory findings concern control of STARS expression, which is deliberately not converted into a process annotation for ABRA.

title: Regulation of STARS and its downstream targets suggest a novel pathway involved in human skeletal muscle hypertrophy and atrophy.
review_notes: Cached title matches, full text available. Representative of what the human literature on this gene actually consists of - expression profiling in muscle biopsies. Informative about physiological context, but it measures transcript and protein abundance rather than testing ABRA's function, so it supports no GO annotation on its own.

title: Actin-binding rho activating protein (Abra) is essential for fluid shear stress-induced arteriogenesis.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Important as a corrective to the muscle-specific framing carried by the older literature - ABRA has a functional role in vascular smooth muscle too. Deliberately not converted into an arteriogenesis process annotation for human ABRA: the loss-of-function is mouse, the mechanism runs through expression control by shear stress, and the human record has no independent support.

title: Costars, a Dictyostelium protein similar to the C-terminal domain of STARS, regulates the actin cytoskeleton and motility.
review_notes: Cached title matches and the paper is sound; the problem is the use made of it. The affinage record cites it for the claim that ABRA's actin-cytoskeleton-regulating activity is conserved through the C-terminal Costars domain. The rescue construct is the small standalone Costars protein, whose human counterpart is ABRACL (Q9P1F3, 81 aa) - and ABRACL and ABRA are the only two reviewed human proteins carrying Pfam PF14705, with ABRACL being essentially the domain alone. A phenotype for the domain-only protein is not a phenotype for ABRA, so nothing from this paper is used to support an ABRA annotation.

title: STARS is essential to maintain cardiac development and function in vivo via a SRF pathway.
review_notes: Cached title matches, full text available. Strong in vivo support for the STARS-SRF axis in a third species, but a zebrafish morphant phenotype is not converted into a human cardiac development annotation here - the phenotype is organismal and the human record has no independent support for a developmental role.

title: Overexpression of Striated Muscle Activator of Rho Signaling (STARS) Increases C2C12 Skeletal Muscle Cell Differentiation.
review_notes: Cached title matches, full text available. Cited for the negative result, which is the interesting part - it is the one piece of evidence that ABRA does something the current mechanistic model does not explain. Its introduction is also the source of the "I-band, Z-disk and M-line" summary that motivates keeping the parent sarcomere term.

title: Striated muscle activator of Rho signalling (STARS) is reduced in ageing human skeletal muscle and targeted by miR-628-5p.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Included for the description's account of how ABRA levels are controlled. Like the other human papers it is regulation of ABRA rather than function by ABRA, so it generates no annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached title matches. The HuRI binary interactome, and the source of ABRA's only interaction annotation, the pair with PPP1R18. IntAct records three rows for that pair, all from this publication and all yeast two-hybrid variants, so the interaction has not been confirmed by an orthogonal method. A sound large-scale study; the caution here is about what a single technology can establish for one pair, not about the resource. The partner is compartment-consistent with ABRA, which is why the annotation is retained rather than called artefactual.

title: Where does the human ABRA GO record come from, and does its one plasma-membrane call have any support?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review (audit_abra_record.py), re-runnable, with the annotation rows read from this gene's own ABRA-goa.tsv so they cannot drift from the record under review and all other data fetched from the UniProt, QuickGO and InterPro REST APIs at run time. Failed fetches are reported rather than counted as absence, and the membrane-feature check names the four feature classes queried so that an empty result cannot be misread as a question that was never asked.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ABRA (human)
review_notes: External precomputed LLM research, treated as a preliminary source; every claim used was re-checked against the cited PMIDs. Its self_evaluation_pairwise is win and no bioRxiv DOI appears in a PMID-shaped field. One over-attribution was found and is recorded against PMID:20940261: the record credits ABRA with the Costars-domain actin/motility phenotype, which belongs to the domain-only protein ABRACL. Its own mechanism_profile is coarse as expected - GO:0140110 transcription regulator activity would be an error for a protein that never touches DNA - and none of its GO ids were imported.

title: Costars, a Dictyostelium protein similar to the C-terminal domain of STARS, regulates the actin cytoskeleton and motility.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Abstract only, but the three claims used here are all stated in the abstract itself, so no full-text access is needed to support them. This is the donor evidence behind the IBA and the source of the cross-species complementation result; it is also the source of the sign discrepancy with the human data, which is why it is cited on both sides of that argument rather than only in support.

title: Solution structure of the human HSPC280 protein.
review_notes: Cached title matches; PDB 2L2O and the secondary-structure features in the UniProt feature table correspond to it. Abstract only, but the two claims drawn from it are stated there. Cited here mainly for a negative that matters: a winged-helix fold invites a DNA-binding annotation, and this paper rules one out explicitly. The abstract contains a typo, HEPC280 for HSPC280, which is reproduced verbatim in the quote above.

title: HSPC280, a winged helix protein expressed in the subventricular zone of the developing ganglionic eminences, inhibits neuronal differentiation.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Abstract only; not used to support any annotation. Recorded because it reports a nuclear pool of the protein in neural progenitors and an anti-differentiation effect on overexpression in Neuro2a cells, both of which sit awkwardly with the lamellipodial pool that the human functional work establishes. At 9 kDa the protein would enter nuclei by passive diffusion regardless of any targeting, so an overexpression result is a weak basis for a nuclear location and none is proposed. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED because the localisation claim was not checkable from the abstract.

title: A Dynamic Protein Interaction Landscape of the Human Centrosome-Cilium Interface.
review_notes: Cached title matches. Identified as the actual primary source at the far end of the cilium annotation's citation chain, and confirmed independently: querying IntAct for Q9P1F3 returns five interactions, all proximity-dependent biotin identification, all from this one publication, with baits SASS6, CNTRL, DCTN1 and RPGRIP1L. The screen is a legitimate and well-executed piece of work; the error lies in a proximity-labelling prey list being read downstream as a subcellular localisation.

title: Human Costars Family Protein ABRACL Modulates Actin Dynamics and Cell Migration and Associates with Tumorigenic Growth.
review_notes: The one substantial functional paper on human ABRACL, full text available and read in full. Title matches the cached record. Its central claims are supported by the figures described, and it is unusually candid about the internal inconsistency between its in vitro and cellular results, which is why this review declines to give the process annotation a sign. Note that the F-actin binding it reports is explicitly weak and the cofilin interaction is established in cells rather than by a binary assay on purified proteins.

title: Characterization of the Abracl-Expressing Cell Populations in the Embryonic Mammalian Telencephalon.
review_notes: Cached title matches and the paper itself is sound - a careful expression and co-labelling study of mouse and cat embryonic forebrain. It is marked MISCITED for the use made of it elsewhere, not for anything it does wrong: UniProt cites it as the evidence for Cell projection, cilium on human ABRACL, and it contains no such observation. It reports somebody else's proteomics result in its Discussion and, in the same paragraph, data that argue against the protein being in the ciliated ventricular zone. It is also a mouse and cat study, so even a genuine localisation finding would need an ISS-style transfer rather than a direct human location. Note on the enum: MISCITED is defined as 'right paper, but it does not support the claim', which strictly describes how a citation is used rather than a property of the paper. It is applied here to record that this reference is cited elsewhere in GOA for something it does not show; within this document the paper is cited only for what it does report. Flagged because a reader aggregating correctness values could otherwise read it as a defect in this review's own use of the reference.

title: What actually places ABRACL in the cilium?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review; the script queries IntAct and UniProt live and hard-codes no results. It was designed to be able to fail: had the family turned out to be absent from angiosperms, or had IntAct returned affinity-capture or two-hybrid evidence alongside the BioID hits, the cilium annotation would have been left standing. It also records the one observation that cuts against a tidy story - Costars is not cross-referenced in the Chlamydomonas proteome - and declines to lean on it, since a cross-reference count is not a homology search.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ABRACL (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record; gates passed, all eight citations are genuine numeric PMIDs, and the mechanistic narrative matches the primary literature on the points this review uses. Two cautions. Its own GO grounding proposes GO:0005634 nucleus as a localisation, which rests on the abstract-only Neuro2a overexpression study and is not adopted here. And its narrative asserts the cofilin-inhibition mechanism without recording the authors' own statement that their in vitro and cellular results conflict, which is the single most important caveat for annotating this gene.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for ABRAXAS1 GO:0008017
review_notes: Provenance tracing to PTN001272083 and ABRAXAS2 is useful and agrees with the PAINT cache. The conclusion of refutation relies on primary nuclear localization, missing ABRAXAS1 assays and a single paralog source, none of which establishes loss of an ancestral function. The 2015 BRISC paper confirms the source mechanism but does not supply a direct negative ABRAXAS1 comparison.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline; yields correct-but-generic acyltransferase terms superseded by the specific thiolase activity.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer from rat peroxisomal thiolase (UniProtKB:P21775); recovers the core thiolase activity, beta-oxidation process, and peroxisome localization, plus non-core acetoacetyl-CoA/myristoyltransferase and bile-acid annotations.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers core thiolase activity, peroxisome, and fatty acid beta-oxidation, but also over-propagates phenylacetate catabolic process.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniPathway vocabulary mapping
review_notes: UniPathway mapping to peroxisomal beta-oxidation; correct process.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence; correct peroxisome localization.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: RHEA/EC-based electronic annotation; recovers the core thiolase activity and peroxisome localization plus non-core acetoacetyl-CoA/myristoyltransferase activities.

title: Identification of the peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of docosahexaenoic acid.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; establishes ACAA1's role (alongside SCPx) in DHA-forming peroxisomal beta-oxidation. Note the Reactome-derived EXP "acetate CoA-transferase" annotation to this PMID is a mis-typed MF (the paper describes thiolase, not CoA-transferase, activity).

title: Subcellular localisation and processing of non-specific lipid transfer protein are not aberrant in Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata fibroblasts.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports peroxisome localization (IDA).

title: Peroxisomes in human and mouse testis: differential expression of peroxisomal proteins in germ cells and distinct somatic cell types of the testis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports peroxisome localization (IDA).

title: Contribution of peroxisome-specific isoform of Lon protease in sorting PTS1 proteins to peroxisomes.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Cited by GOA as a "protein binding" IPI for ACAA1, but the paper's finding is essentially negative (pLon does not process thiolase); the bare protein-binding annotation is uninformative/over-annotated.

title: Pex3p-dependent peroxisomal biogenesis initiates in the endoplasmic reticulum of human fibroblasts.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports peroxisome localization (IDA).

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; high-throughput membrane-proteomics co-detection producing a spurious membrane localization for a soluble matrix enzyme.

title: Structural requirements for interaction of peroxisomal targeting signal 2 and its receptor PEX7.
review_notes: Full text available; supports peroxisome localization (IDA) and the PTS2/PEX7 import mechanism, and frames ACAA1 as the terminal (thiolase) enzyme of beta-oxidation.

title: Bile acid profiles in peroxisomal 3-oxoacyl-coenzyme A thiolase deficiency.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports very-long-chain fatty acid metabolic process (IMP) and (non-core) bile acid metabolic process, though the bile-acid thiolase role is now attributed to SCPx.

title: Rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata. Deficiency of 3-oxoacyl-coenzyme A thiolase in peroxisomes and impaired processing of the enzyme.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports fatty acid beta-oxidation (IMP) and peroxisome localization (IDA).

title: Mechanistic insights into PTS2-mediated peroxisomal protein import: the co-receptor PEX5L drastically increases the interaction strength between the cargo protein and the receptor PEX7.
review_notes: Full text available; supports peroxisome localization (IDA) via the PTS2/PEX7-PEX5L import mechanism.

title: Human peroxisomal 3-oxoacyl-coenzyme A thiolase deficiency.
review_notes: Abstract/full-abstract in cache; the foundational human genetic evidence for ACAA1's role in peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation and EC 2.3.1.16 identity. The GO:0120524 (oxidase) IMP call to this PMID is a mis-typed MF (over-annotation).

title: Immunocytochemical demonstration of peroxisomal enzymes in human kidney biopsies.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports peroxisome localization (IDA).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Full text available; systematic Y2H screen with no functional context for the ACAA1 interactions, so the derived bare protein-binding annotations are uninformative/over-annotated.

title: Immunocytochemical localization of peroxisomal proteins in human liver and kidney.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports peroxisome localization (IDA).

title: alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) metabolism
review_notes: Reactome pathway; ACAA1 participates in peroxisomal chain-shortening within n-3 PUFA metabolism.

title: Formation of DHA-CoA catalysed by 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly attributing DHA-CoA formation to the ACAA1 thiolase step in the peroxisomal matrix.

title: Beta-oxidation of very long chain fatty acids
review_notes: Reactome pathway for peroxisomal VLCFA beta-oxidation, the core process ACAA1 completes.

title: 3-ketohexacosanoyl-CoA + CoASH => tetracosanoyl-CoA + acetyl-CoA
review_notes: Reactome reaction encoding the ACAA1 thiolase step on a specific VLCFA substrate.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation pathway; source of extracellular-region and specific-granule-lumen localizations that are bystander/proteomics-based, not functional sites for ACAA1.

title: PEX7 binds cargo proteins containing PTS2
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the cytosolic PTS2-cargo recognition step; source of a transient cytosol localization, not the functional compartment.

title: Cargo of PEX5L:PEX7 translocates from the cytosol to the peroxisomal matrix
review_notes: Reactome translocation reaction; source of both a transient cytosol localization and the correct peroxisomal-matrix localization.

title: Acetyl-Coenzyme A acyltransferase 2 attenuates the apoptotic effects of BNIP3 in two human cell lines.
review_notes: Abstract verified; supports the BNIP3 interaction (GO:0005515) and the apoptosis/hypoxia process annotations. Single-lab overexpression study, so the apoptosis-regulation role is contextual/non-core.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Abstract verified; a high-throughput screen only. Supports the RNA-binding annotation as a moonlighting candidate, not a characterized ACAA2 function.

title: The crystal structure of human mitochondrial 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (T1): insight into the reaction mechanism of its thiolase and thioesterase activities.
review_notes: Abstract verified against UniProt (PDB 4C2J/4C2K, Cys92/Cys382 active site, kinetics). Primary structural/biochemical reference establishing ACAA2's core and side activities.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Supports mitochondrial localization; corroborative high-throughput evidence only.

title: Cloning and sequence analysis of a full length cDNA encoding human mitochondrial 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Supports gene identity and mitochondrial thiolase assignment; does NOT support the NAS cholesterol-biosynthesis annotation, which is recommended for removal.

title: BRCA1 affects lipid synthesis through its interaction with acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; verbatim quotes used. Establishes the BRCA1-ACC1 regulatory interaction (basis for the GO:0005515 IPI annotations).

title: TRB3 links the E3 ubiquitin ligase COP1 to lipid metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only; the with/from for the IPI is mouse Trib3 (Q8K4K2). ACC is the substrate targeted for degradation; supports a regulatory protein interaction.

title: Aldo-keto reductase family 1 B10 affects fatty acid synthesis by regulating the stability of acetyl-CoA carboxylase-alpha in breast cancer cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only; directly reports AKR1B10-ACCA co-immunoprecipitation and cytoplasmic co-localization (basis for the O60218 IPI).

title: Identification and characterization of proteins interacting with SIRT1 and SIRT3: implications in the anti-aging and metabolic effects of sirtuins.
review_notes: Abstract-only and does not name ACACA in the abstract; the SIRT1 (Q96EB6) interaction is IntAct-curated from the full interactome. Supports only a generic protein binding annotation.

title: Induced polymerization of mammalian acetyl-CoA carboxylase by MIG12 provides a tertiary level of regulation of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports both the acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity IDA and the MID1IP1 interaction, and the citrate/polymerization activation mechanism.

title: Crystal structure of Spot 14, a modulator of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only; primarily a S14 structure paper but reports the MIG12-ACC polymerization mechanism (basis for the ISS carboxylase activity and MID1IP1 IPI annotations).

title: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibition by ND-630 reduces hepatic steatosis, improves insulin sensitivity, and modulates dyslipidemia in rats.
review_notes: Abstract-only; directly assays ACC enzymatic activity (basis for the IDA acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity annotation) and establishes ACC as a metabolic-disease drug target.

title: Structural basis for regulation of human acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but the abstract itself is rich; verbatim quotes support the catalytic activity, cytosolic ACC1 vs mitochondrial ACC2 distinction, and the citrate/BRCA1 filament regulation.

title: Pin1 Exacerbates Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease by Enhancing Its Activity through Binding to ACC1.
review_notes: Full text available; Co-IP, GST pull-down and IF establish the direct Pin1-ACC1 interaction (basis for the Q13526 IPI) and its activating effect on ACC1.

title: Cloning of human acetyl-CoA carboxylase cDNA.
review_notes: Abstract-only; original human ACC cloning paper, basis for the TAS acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity annotation.

title: The subcellular localization of acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Establishes ACC2 mitochondrial (outer membrane) localization and the CPT1-inhibition rationale. Note the GOA nuclear IDA derived from this paper is not supported by the abstract.

title: TRB3 links the E3 ubiquitin ligase COP1 to lipid metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Concerns ACC regulation broadly; the ACACB IPI is with mouse Trib3 (Q8K4K2, BHF-UCL). Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Expression, purification, and characterization of human and rat acetyl coenzyme A carboxylase (ACC) isozymes.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Direct biochemical characterization of human ACC2 activity; basis for the EXP catalytic-activity annotation.

title: Characterization of recombinant human acetyl-CoA carboxylase-2 steady-state kinetics.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Direct malonyl-CoA-formation assay on human ACC2; strong support for the core catalytic function.

title: Molecular mechanism for the regulation of human ACC2 through phosphorylation by AMPK.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Structural/mechanistic study of human ACC2 activity and its AMPK regulation; supports the EXP catalytic-activity annotation.

title: The N-terminal domain of human holocarboxylase synthetase facilitates biotinylation via direct interaction with the substrate protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only and general (does not name ACACB). Cited for the ACACB-HLCS (P50747) IPI (biotinylation enzyme-substrate); supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Induced polymerization of mammalian acetyl-CoA carboxylase by MIG12 provides a tertiary level of regulation of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Establishes the ACC-MIG12 interaction and citrate-dependent polymerization/activation; basis for IPI, identical-protein-binding, and IDA activity annotations.

title: Crystal structure of Spot 14, a modulator of fatty acid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Supports the ACC2 IDA activity, acetyl-CoA metabolic process, protein homotetramerization, and IPI (MIG12) annotations attributed to this PMID.

title: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibition by ND-630 reduces hepatic steatosis, improves insulin sensitivity, and modulates dyslipidemia in rats.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Direct demonstration of ACC2 catalytic inhibition and its therapeutic relevance; supports the IDA activity annotation.

title: Isolation and characterisation of a cDNA encoding the precursor for a novel member of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase gene family.
review_notes: Identifier/title verified against fetched metadata. The abstract establishes cloned sequence and family similarity; later source papers, not this abstract, establish catalytic specificity. Full text unavailable.

title: Isolated 2-methylbutyrylglycinuria caused by short/branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: identification of a new enzyme defect, resolution of its molecular basis, and evidence for distinct acyl-CoA dehydrogenases in isoleucine and valine metabolism.
review_notes: Identifier/title verified against the fetched publication metadata and original GOA source. The cached abstract explicitly reports the ACAD8 experiments; full text was unavailable in this session.

title: Identification of isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase and its deficiency in humans.
review_notes: Identifier/title verified against the fetched publication metadata and original GOA source. The cached abstract explicitly reports the ACAD8 experiments; full text was unavailable in this session.

title: Variations in IBD (ACAD8) in children with elevated C4-carnitine detected by tandem mass spectrometry newborn screening.
review_notes: Identifier/title verified against the fetched publication metadata and original GOA source. The cached abstract explicitly reports the ACAD8 experiments; full text was unavailable in this session.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: The cache is marked full_text_available and includes article narrative.
