review_notes: Cached PubMed abstract and primary PubMed page https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27642048/ verified on 2026-09-27. The abstract explicitly identifies a mouse neuronal interactome and m-AAA–MAIP1/EMRE regulation. Publisher PDF access failed, the university repository marks its copy restricted, and ResearchGate offered a request rather than recovered full text. Exact human MAIP1/EMRE interaction assays and axonogenesis evidence remain unresolved; no wrong-species conclusion is drawn. Core enzyme and calcium-regulation assignments have independent human support in PMID:28396416.

title: Proteolytic control of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex.
review_notes: Cache is abstract-only. Primary full original https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410796/ read on 2026-09-27, including Figures 1–5 and supplementary descriptions. HEK293 experiments show AFG3L2/SPG7-dependent degradation of unassembled EMRE, ATP dependence, and context-dependent calcium leak when MICU gatekeeping is limiting. The main text explicitly distinguishes AFG3L2 homohexamers from AFG3L2–SPG7 heterohexamers. All machine-checkable quotations are from the cached abstract.

title: m-AAA and i-AAA complexes coordinate to regulate OMA1, the stress-activated supervisor of mitochondrial dynamics.
review_notes: Cached abstract and primary PubMed entry verified. The abstract explicitly assigns pre-pro-OMA1 N-terminal maturation to AFG3L2; the downstream OPA1 proteases are OMA1/YME1L1. Full experimental details were not recovered, so no precise cleavage site, universal species context or direct OPA1 cleavage by AFG3L2 is inferred.

title: Dissecting Substrate Specificities of the Mitochondrial AFG3L2 Protease.
review_notes: Cached full original read: engineered soluble coiled-coil-hexamerized human AFG3L2, ATPase/protein degradation and short-peptide cleavage assays, and human MRPL32 precursor processing. The precursor lacks its first 30 residues; mass spectrometry defines the processed product. This establishes biochemical capacity, while the physiological contribution to native human ribosome maturation remains a separate question.

title: Concurrent AFG3L2 and SPG7 mutations associated with syndromic parkinsonism and optic atrophy with aberrant OPA1 processing and mitochondrial network fragmentation.
review_notes: Official PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30252181/ identifies the study; its linked accepted manuscript at https://air.unimi.it/handle/2434/591381 was read (Methods, Results and Discussion). Human AFG3L2-V5 and Yta10(1-63)-human paraplegin(59-795)-HA are expressed in m-AAA-null yeast. Figure 3C-D supports AFG3L2 self-maturation and paraplegin maturation, including the E575Q inactive-protease control and R468C processing defect despite retained complex assembly. The engineered paraplegin targeting segment does not directly establish native human MPP cleavage. MrpL32/Ccp1 processing in yeast concerns yeast substrates; patient fibroblasts retain normal MRPL32 processing. Abnormal patient OPA1 processing does not establish direct AFG3L2 cleavage of OPA1. The normal abstract cache was recovered through verified source run 36289953066. It corroborates the study identity, yeast functional analysis and patient OPA1 phenotype, but does not include Figure 3. The detailed construct and self-maturation assessment comes from the independently read accepted manuscript; full_text_unavailable remains true for the abstract-only local cache. The accepted manuscript explicitly reserves all rights (PDF page 1 and repeated footers); its public availability does not establish a redistribution license. The existing short supporting_text_fulltext excerpt was reverified verbatim on manuscript page 16, Results 3.3/Figure 3C, and is retained.

title: Mitochondrial stress response triggered by defects in protein synthesis quality control.

Distinguish substrate-bound inactive structure from functional ATPase/protease measurements. title: Sustained OMA1-mediated integrated stress response is beneficial for spastic ataxia type 5.
review_notes: Primary identifier/title/DOI verified in the source-12 identity audit (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37804316/); the exact normal record is now available locally. Original Methods, Results and Discussion read. Human SPAX5 patient fibroblasts, AFG3L2-reduced HEK293T cells expressing human DELE1-HA, and Afg3l2-null mice are separate experimental systems. DELE1/HRI knockdown impairs patient-cell growth; Sephin-1 improves patient-cell growth, mouse Purkinje-neuron survival/arborization and mouse survival and mitochondrial readouts. DELE1 cleavage was measured after tagged overexpression in HEK293T cells, not endogenously in patient fibroblasts or mouse cerebellum because suitable antibodies were unavailable. OMA1 performs the inferred stress-dependent cleavage; the work does not establish AFG3L2 as the DELE1-cleaving enzyme, an eIF2alpha kinase, or a transcription factor. It corroborates consequences of defective proteostasis without requiring another core process or NEW annotation.

Its OMA1 ATPase/AAA wording, broad MRPL32 degradation phrasing and mixed calcium-flux descriptions are not adopted as mechanistic evidence; OMA1-mediated OPA1 cleavage and limited MRPL32 maturation remain distinguished from direct AFG3L2 substrate destruction. review_notes: Reclassified from MISCITED to VERIFIED after review. title: Structural characteristics of alpha-fetoprotein, including N-glycosylation, metal ion and fatty acid binding sites.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; clean. This is the single most function-relevant paper on human AFP and it is absent from GOA and absent from the affinage record, which is the campaign's recall lesson in concrete form. title: Copper(II)-binding ability of human alpha-fetoprotein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; clean. Old but directly on point, and performed on protein purified from human tissue rather than on a recombinant or a family member. UniProt already encodes this as a Cu(2+) binding feature at residue 22 with ECO:0000269 evidence to this PMID, yet GOA carries no copper term, which is the clearest single coverage gap on this gene.

title: Expression of serum albumin and of alphafetoprotein in murine normal and neoplastic primitive embryonic structures.
review_notes: PubMed-verified identifier and title; clean for retraction. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than MISCITED because only the abstract is cached. It is the sole basis of the mouse Afp cytoplasm IDA that Ensembl Compara projects onto human AFP, and the abstract reports that AFP protein was not detected by immunostaining here, with the intracellular-AFP statement appearing as a background citation to earlier work. I cannot see the full text, so this is recorded as support that cannot be confirmed from the available record, not as an error.

title: alpha-Fetoprotein as a carrier protein in plasma and its bilirubin-binding ability.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; clean. Directly measured on human protein. It cannot currently be expressed in GO because no bilirubin binding molecular function term exists - see proposed_new_terms.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AFP (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated provider record; the script reported trust gates clear, and all 17 of its citations are numeric PubMed identifiers with no bioRxiv DOIs in PMID-shaped fields. Precision is therefore fine. Recall and framing are not, and both were measured rather than asserted. Of its 17 citations, 0 appear in AFP's GOA record and 1 are cited in this review (PMID:33009373). It misses PMID:38678117, the cryo-EM structure of human AFP that resolves the fatty acid and metal sites and is the single most function-relevant paper on this gene, and it misses both direct ligand-binding measurements, PMID:80265 for copper and PMID:89900 for bilirubin, although UniProt flags both. More important than the omissions is what the record is about: a large part of its narrative concerns the transcriptional regulation of the AFP gene by FOXM1, HBP1/HBx and gp96/NR5A2 and the -119 HNF1 promoter variant. Those are functions of the regulators, not of alpha-fetoprotein, and the rest is hepatocellular carcinoma cell biology in which AFP concentration is the readout. Ligand binding, which is what the protein does, is absent from the record entirely. Nothing in this review rests on it, and no sentence from it is used as supporting_text; it is recorded here because the curatorial assessment of a provider record belongs in references[].reference_review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go route, and the source of the only molecular-function row in GOA. Which signature supplies the term was checked rather than assumed: of AGFG1's four InterPro signatures, only IPR001164 (the pan-ArfGAP catalytic-domain entry) maps to GO:0005096. The signature correctly identifies the conserved domain but cannot distinguish the AGFG subfamily, whose members examined here lack two of three residues required for efficient GAP catalysis; the AGFG-specific IPR052248 maps to no GO term. The row is therefore retained but marked as over-annotated rather than dismissed as a spurious domain match.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: All five IBA rows. Every protein donor named in their WITH/FROM fields was resolved and its own evidence for the propagated term queried; each row's chain contains at least one donor with its own experimental annotation at the exact term, so no row rests on family-level inference alone. The defect these rows do carry is node reach, not evidence quality - see the GO:0001675 entry.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SL-0191 Nucleus and SL-0088 Cytoplasmic vesicle, both of which derive from the same UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statement (evidenced by PubMed:10613896 and PubMed:7634337) that the EXP rows already record independently.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA00026971. All 2414 of the rule's condition sets were evaluated against AGFG1's own signature and taxon profile: exactly one fires, and it requires both FunFam 1.10.220.150:FF:000005 and FunFam 3.30.450.50:FF:000005, two FunFams named for AGFG1 itself. A second set mentioning IPR001164 does not fire because it also requires IPR051718, which AGFG1 does not have. So this is a gene-specific rule granting one location AGFG1 independently has by experiment.

title: The eps15 homology (EH) domain-based interaction between eps15 and hrb connects the molecular machinery of endocytosis to that of nucleocytosolic transport.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Supplies the nucleus and cytoplasmic-vesicle localisations, the EPS15/EPS15R interaction and its NPF/EH dependence, and - directly against the nuclear-pore row - the statement that AGFG1's status as an NPC constituent is not established.

title: Two closely related human nuclear export factors utilize entirely distinct export pathways.
review_notes: Cited for the AGFG1-NXF3 IPI row. Not retrievable (Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess N, inEPMC N, no PMC id), so the interaction's mechanism cannot be read. The reference-projection test argues it is considered curation rather than pipeline output: it annotates four proteins (AGFG1, NXF3, NXF1, XPO1) with five different terms. IntAct holds no record of the pair, consistent with a curator reading the paper directly.

title: Lack of acrosome formation in Hrb-deficient mice.
review_notes: The decisive orthologue phenotype and the basis of the acrosome-assembly IBA. Also the source of the mouse cytoplasmic-vesicle IDA. Absent from the affinage record.

title: hRIP, a cellular cofactor for Rev function, promotes release of HIV RNAs from the perinuclear region.
review_notes: Establishes that the export defect is specific to Rev-directed RNA and that bulk host poly(A)+ mRNA distribution is unaffected. This is the result that makes GO:0006406 mRNA export from nucleus the wrong branch for this gene.

title: The acroplaxome is the docking site of Golgi-derived myosin Va/Rab27a/b- containing proacrosomal vesicles in wild-type and Hrb mutant mouse spermatids.
review_notes: The donor evidence for both the acrosome-assembly and the intermediate-filament IBAs. It supports the latter specifically: the mutant acroplaxome retains F-actin but is deficient in keratin 5, an intermediate-filament protein.

title: The cellular HIV-1 Rev cofactor hRIP is required for viral replication.
review_notes: Corroborates the Rev-cofactor role with two independent ablation methods and a rescue, and adds that AGFG1 is not required for cell viability. Not cited by any GOA row.

title: Changes in intranuclear chromatin architecture induce bipolar nuclear localization of histone variant H1T2 in male haploid spermatids.
review_notes: This is the sole reference behind mouse Agfg1's GO:0007289 IMP, from which the human IBA descends, and its result for hrb is a NEGATIVE: H1T2 polar localisation is unaltered in hrb-null spermatids, which the authors use to argue that acrosome development is not required for nuclear polarity. The mouse spermatid nuclear phenotype (nucleopodes) is reported in PMID:14724135 instead, so the term is defensible for the orthologue but attached to the wrong reference.

title: Molecular basis for the sorting of the SNARE VAMP7 into endocytic clathrin-coated vesicles by the ArfGAP Hrb.
review_notes: The strongest molecular study on this gene and the basis for most of the proposed new annotations: cargo-binding region mapped to residues 136-176, ITC affinity, a crystal structure, reciprocal mutations that abolish binding on both sides, colocalisation with clathrin and AP-2 in coated pits and vesicles, and a depletion phenotype. In all of GOA it has produced only two annotations, both bare protein binding. Absent from the affinage record.

title: Consensus nomenclature for the human ArfGAP domain-containing proteins.
review_notes: The family reference, used for two opposite purposes. It supplies the published catalytic-spacing anchor (CX2CX16CX2CX4R) and ArfGAP1's residue numbers, which the motif scan reproduces as a positive control; and it supplies the disconfirming control, since it reports that the ADAP subfamily lacks in vitro GAP activity although ADAP1's motif is complete. Both clauses of that sentence are used: the same sentence also asserts, at subfamily level and without a citation, that at least one member of every non-ADAP subfamily - which includes AGFG - has demonstrated in vitro GAP activity. Its AGFG section names no such measurement for either paralogue, so the blanket clause is treated as raising the prior rather than as the evidence.

title: Role of HRB in clathrin-dependent endocytosis.
review_notes: Supports the clathrin-dependent-endocytosis role by knockdown, and is one of only two papers the affinage record returned. Marked DISPUTED because its generality is contested rather than because the paper is unsound: it reports transferrin uptake strongly reduced on HRB knockdown, while PMID:18775314 reports no effect of HRB depletion on EGF internalisation or degradation and reads AGFG1 as a SNARE-specific adaptor. Both results are recorded; this review does not adjudicate between them. The cache's Full Text section holds only page boilerplate, so only the abstract is used.

title: Distinct and separable activities of the endocytic clathrin-coat components Fcho1/2 and AP-2 in developmental patterning.
review_notes: An independent second laboratory classifying AGFG1 as a CLASP and showing concentration-dependent binding of Hrb to the FCHO1 mu-homology domain in HeLa lysates, with controls excluding an indirect, Asn-Pro-Phe-mediated route. The source of UniProt's FCHO1 SUBUNIT line, which has no GOA counterpart.

title: Ancient complexity, opisthokont plasticity, and discovery of the 11th subfamily of Arf GAP proteins.
review_notes: The paper that reverses this review's verdict on GO:0005096, and it was nearly missed: it was fetched, judged to be a family-classification paper with nothing resting on it, deleted before the first commit, and came back only through the concurrent AGFG2 review. Full text available and read. It names three catalytically required ASAP3 positions with the statement that mutating any one severely impairs activity, reports that only 2 of 40 AGFG sequences retain the aspartate and that the AGFG consensus uniquely lacks the tryptophan, and concludes that the AGFG subfamily is predicted to have lost substantial GAP activity while explicitly warning that this must not be confused with loss of Arf binding. Every claim used from it was re-measured here on AGFG1's own sequence with GAP-competent positive controls, rather than transferred from the paper's consensus analysis or from the sibling review.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: The HuRI yeast two-hybrid screen behind the POLE2 and NYAP2 rows. Correctly cited; the objection is evidence strength, not identity. Its projection test is uninformative by construction - it carries 24,599 annotations, too many to enumerate honestly - so no entity count is reported for it.

title: The temporally controlled expression of Drongo, the fruit fly homolog of AGFG1, is achieved in female germline cells via P-bodies and its localization requires functional Rab11.
review_notes: The donor evidence for the cytoplasm IBA: Drosophila drongo holds GO:0005737 by its own IDA from this paper. Cited to show that the cytoplasm row's chain is not empty of experimental evidence.

title: The ArfGAP Drongo Promotes Actomyosin Contractility during Collective Cell Migration by Releasing Myosin Phosphatase from the Trailing Edge.
review_notes: The only functional evidence anywhere that an AGFG-family GTPase-activating function matters in vivo, and it names a specific Arf class. Abstract-only, so what is used is the abstract's statement that the GTPase-activating function is essential; the assay that established it is not asserted here.

title: Arf GTPase-activating proteins SMAP1 and AGFG2 regulate the size of Weibel-Palade bodies and exocytosis of von Willebrand factor.
review_notes: Cited only for the paralogue argument. It gives AGFG2 its own characterised function in endothelial von Willebrand factor secretion and does not mention AGFG1 anywhere, which is what makes the spermatid terms reaching AGFG2 by IBA look like node over-reach rather than genuine shared biology.

title: Mapping the global interactome of the ARF family reveals spatial organization in cellular signaling pathways.
review_notes: The only human dataset placing AGFG1 in the ARF orbit, and it is proximity labelling rather than a GAP assay - evidence for association, not catalysis. Absent from GOA and from the affinage record. It supports retained Arf binding while leaving the catalytic prediction untested.

title: AGFG1 increases cholesterol biosynthesis by disrupting intracellular cholesterol homeostasis to promote PDAC progression.
review_notes: Recorded as an uncurated human result, not used to propose terms. A single cancer-cell study reporting a CAV1 interaction and altered cholesterol biosynthesis is not a basis for new process annotations here.

title: Identification of a novel cellular cofactor for the Rev/Rex class of retroviral regulatory proteins.
review_notes: A sound paper cited for two things it does not establish. Its own abstract has Rev binding the RNA and Rab/AGFG1 binding Rev's protein activation domain, so it cannot support GO:0003723 RNA binding; and the RNA it concerns is RRE-containing viral RNA, not host mRNA, so GO:0006406 mRNA export from nucleus reads more broadly than the evidence. The nucleus localisation it also carries is correct. This reference annotates exactly one entity in all of GOA, with three rows, which is the legacy ProtInc import signature.

title: A human nucleoporin-like protein that specifically interacts with HIV Rev.
review_notes: The abstract's nucleoporin claim is explicitly one of sequence homology, yet it is the sole support for GO:0005643 nuclear pore, a term whose definition asserts membership of the nuclear pore complex. A primary paper states outright that it is not certain whether AGFG1 is an authentic NPC constituent, and UniProt, curating this same paper, records Nucleus rather than nuclear envelope or nuclear pore. This reference annotates exactly one entity in all of GOA, with one row.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGFG1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated provider record, gates_passed True, and its two citations (PMID:10613896 and PMID:18819912) are real and correctly quoted - so its precision is fine. Its recall is not, and that was measured rather than asserted: it returned neither of the two papers that decide this review (PMID:18775314, the VAMP7 structure and depletion phenotype, and PMID:11711676, the mouse null with no acrosome), nor PMID:18809720, the family reference supplying the catalytic-motif anchor, nor PMID:38606629, the only human dataset placing AGFG1 with ARF1/ARF3/ARF6. It also states the general clathrin-mediated-endocytosis requirement as settled when PMID:18775314 contradicts it for EGF. Cited here for exactly one thing: its explicit statement about the extent of its own corpus, used as a statement about that corpus and corroborated independently.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: IPR001164 supplies the catalytic inference. Domain recognition is real; target-specific catalysis remains uncertain because the functional significance of divergent residues is not universal.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Actual PTHR46134 target lineage and current IBD assertions verified. Donor counts and closer unassayed orthologs do not refute the ancestral judgment.

title: The eps15 homology (EH) domain-based interaction between eps15 and hrb connects the molecular machinery of endocytosis to that of nucleocytosolic transport.
review_notes: Full text available and read in full around every sentence quoted. Titled for Hrb, but Hrbl is co-assayed throughout the functional experiments, which is exactly the pattern where a paper titled for a paralogue holds evidence about the gene under review. Care was taken to separate what was measured on Hrbl (Rev reporter, synergy, Rev levels) from what was measured only on Hrb (localisation, fractionation, the NPF-to-NPV mutant).

title: GIT proteins, A novel family of phosphatidylinositol 3,4, 5-trisphosphate-stimulated GTPase-activating proteins for ARF6.
review_notes: Abstract directly reports measured GIT1/GIT2 ARF GAP activity and ARF6 hydrolysis. This counterexample limits inference from loss of the ASAP3 Asp-homologous site; it does not demonstrate AGFG2 catalysis.

title: Lack of acrosome formation in Hrb-deficient mice.
review_notes: Abstract-only source biology supports mouse Hrb vesicle docking/fusion. Actual ancestral placement, not pairwise donor identity, grounds the AGFG2 IBA.

title: The acroplaxome is the docking site of Golgi-derived myosin Va/Rab27a/b- containing proacrosomal vesicles in wild-type and Hrb mutant mouse spermatids.
review_notes: Abstract-only primary explicitly describes altered keratin-5 distribution and later nuclear protrusions. This supports the source biology without identifying a direct filament-polymerizing activity.

title: Changes in intranuclear chromatin architecture induce bipolar nuclear localization of histone variant H1T2 in male haploid spermatids.
review_notes: The abstract explicitly includes hrb-null spermatids and shows preserved early H1T2 polarity. Full-text source-specific details remain unavailable; neither the H1T2 title nor this individual negative marker refutes spermatid differentiation roles.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only membrane-fraction proteomics; accepts transient/peripheral association. No transmembrane helix is required for the annotated broad membrane location.

title: The structure of an Arf-ArfGAP complex reveals a Ca2+ regulatory mechanism.
review_notes: Abstract-only structural study of the ASAP3-Arf6 complex. Catalytic architecture and calcium regulation inform the anchor protein; target AGFG2 activity cannot be read directly from this structure.

title: Organization patterns of the AGFG genes: an evolutionary study.
review_notes: The mammals-only claim conflicts with the broader AGFG phylogeny in PMID:23433073. This is a claim-specific disagreement, not a judgment that the entire study is low quality; the sequence-symbol census is corroboration rather than an orthology proof.

title: Ancient complexity, opisthokont plasticity, and discovery of the 11th subfamily of Arf GAP proteins.
review_notes: Full relevant phylogeny and conserved-site Results/Discussion read. AGFG catalytic reduction is a prediction. The same analysis finds loss of the Asp-homologous residue in all GIT sequences, a limitation on universal Asp-based inactivity claims.

title: Genome-wide shRNA screening identifies host factors involved in early endocytic events for HIV-1-induced CD4 down-regulation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Primary human-cell shRNA evidence for AGFG2 that has produced no annotation in GOA. Note that the affinage record's table row for the companion paper PMID:26701340 states AGFG2 knockdown raises CD4 in Vpu-expressing but not Nef-expressing cells; that is contradicted both by this paper's Nef-specific result and by the companion abstract's own dual-role conclusion, so the affinage row was not used.

title: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) Rev-binding protein (HRB) is a co-factor for HIV-1 Nef-mediated CD4 downregulation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, and only the abstract is relied on. Titled for HRB (AGFG1) while carrying the decisive AGFG2 result, which is why a symbol-keyed search would not surface it. The affinage record's rendering of this paper - that AGFG2 knockdown raises CD4 in Vpu- but not Nef-expressing cells - misstates the abstract, which concludes a dual role in both; the affinage narrative section states it correctly, so the provider's own two summaries disagree.

title: The temporally controlled expression of Drongo, the fruit fly homolog of AGFG1, is achieved in female germline cells via P-bodies and its localization requires functional Rab11.
review_notes: Cited only to identify the donor evidence on the cytoplasm row; the drongo annotations were read from QuickGO, not from this paper. Abstract-only in the cache and nothing beyond the annotation attribution is claimed. Note that FB:FBgn0020304 resolves to seven UniProt entries, none reviewed, so the curated GO evidence is real but the entry name has no Swiss-Prot authority.

title: Arf GTPase-activating proteins SMAP1 and AGFG2 regulate the size of Weibel-Palade bodies and exocytosis of von Willebrand factor.
review_notes: Full primary Results/Discussion and relevant Methods checked. Secretion perturbation and expression establish a trafficking role; the R75Q phenotype is data not shown and is not a GAP assay. Modest VWF-processing differences prevent claims that every maturation measure was unchanged.

title: Binding specificity and in vivo targets of the EH domain, a novel protein-protein interaction module.
review_notes: Cited only as UniProt reference 1 for the AGFG2 sequence and as the source PMID:10613896 attributes the Hrbl-EH interaction to. Full text is not available from PMC even after a forced re-fetch, so the AGFG2-specific content is taken on PMID:10613896's word and flagged as such rather than asserted.

title: AGFG2 reproducible bioinformatics results
review_notes: The stored residue coordinates, identity calculations and source counts were inspected. The interpretive sections were corrected: PAINT is ancestral inference, absent target experiments are not negative assays, and the Asp substitution is not a universal GAP-inactivity diagnostic.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGFG2 (human)
review_notes: Full body and table read. Useful dual Nef/Vpu narrative agrees with primary evidence. The table contradicts that narrative, detailed binding/localization is partly extrapolated from Hrb, the mammals-only statement conflicts with broader phylogeny, and the report omits the endothelial secretion study.

title: OpenScientist review of AGFG2 ArfGAP catalysis versus trafficking-cofactor function
review_notes: Focused report evaluated on 2026-10-05; it corroborates the UNDECIDED call for the InterPro-derived GTPase activator activity by finding no direct AGFG2 hydrolysis assay, while explicitly rejecting sequence-only refutation from the Thr89 position.

title: AGFG2 primary, PAINT and ontology scope check (2026-09-20)
review_notes: Actual target lineage, primary assay scope, role comparators and limitations recorded; read alongside the saved tree/ontology snapshots.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Correctly identified as the provenance of the row. The objection recorded against it is to the domain-to-term inference, not to the pipeline's execution - the G-patch signature is genuinely present and intact in AGGF1.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Both rows were checked by resolving the WITH/FROM column and querying each donor's own evidence in QuickGO. No paralogue transfer, and no propagation landing above its donor.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mechanically correct and redundant with the corresponding IDA rows.

title: Identification of an angiogenic factor that when mutated causes susceptibility to Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
review_notes: The source of seven of AGGF1's twenty-four GOA rows, and the biochemistry it reports - secretion, endothelial binding, CAM angiogenesis, proliferation, TWEAK interaction - has been independently reproduced and extended. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED for one specific reason: its human-genetic claim, that E133K is a gain-of-function KTS mutation, was contradicted by PMID:16443853 and PMID:17103452 and effectively withdrawn by the originating laboratory in PMID:18564129, and ClinVar now classifies the variant Benign/Likely benign. None of the GO rows sourced from this paper depends on that claim, which is why they are all accepted.

title: Biomedicine and diseases: the Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome, vascular anomalies and vascular morphogenesis.
review_notes: The identifier and title are right and the paper is real, but it does not support the annotation it was cited for. GO:0001570 is vasculogenesis; this review discusses angiogenesis and restates a primary paper that assayed angiogenesis. The term survives on zebrafish knockdown data published seven years later (PMID:23197652), which this reference could not have cited.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: A high-throughput screen correctly cited. Too large to test for reference-level projection - QuickGO returns 2124 annotations for it, past the page limit, so the entity count is reported as unavailable rather than estimated from one page.

title: Is the E133K allele of VG5Q associated with Klippel-Trenaunay and other overgrowth syndromes?
review_notes: Absent from the affinage deep-research record and from GOA, and decisive for how the gene should be described. Full text cached and both quotes verified against it. ClinVar independently classifies the variant Benign/Likely benign.

title: The G397A (E133K) change in the AGGF1 (VG5Q) gene is a single nucleotide polymorphism in the Spanish population.
review_notes: A two-page letter with no abstract indexed in PubMed or Europe PMC, closed access and not in PMC, so the body could not be retrieved and no quote is taken from it. Frequency figures circulating in secondary sources were deliberately not used. The identifier, title and journal were confirmed against PubMed; the conclusion is the title.

title: Identification of association of common AGGF1 variants with susceptibility for Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome using the structure association program.
review_notes: Author overlap with PMID:14961121 (Wang, Timur, Driscoll), which is what makes it the strongest item in the E133K story. The cached record is abstract-only; the paper's Discussion reportedly gives P = 0.59 for E133K between 163 cases and 465 controls, but that sentence is not in the cached text and is therefore not quoted here.

title: Dynamic protein-protein interaction wiring of the human spliceosome.
review_notes: Cited in GOA only for a self-interaction row, but the more useful fact is which screen it is. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Functional characterization of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome gene AGGF1 identifies a novel angiogenic signaling pathway for specification of vein differentiation and angiogenesis during embryogenesis.
review_notes: Verified as the donor evidence behind the GO:0001525 IBA by querying QuickGO for ZFIN:ZDB-GENE-060929-836. The work is in zebrafish, so it supports the IBA but would be ISO, not IMP, if transferred to human directly.

title: Aggf1 acts at the top of the genetic regulatory hierarchy in specification of hemangioblasts in zebrafish.
review_notes: Zebrafish work, cited only in prose as supporting context for the GO:0001570 row. No annotation rests on it and no quote is taken from it.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
Angiogenic Factor AGGF1 Activates Autophagy with an Essential Role in Therapeutic Angiogenesis for Heart Disease.
review_notes: Full text cached and quotes verified. Produced no GO annotation on any gene product; two NEW rows in this review come from it.

title: Haploinsufficiency of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome gene Aggf1 inhibits developmental and pathological angiogenesis by inactivating PI3K and AKT and disrupts vascular integrity by activating VE-cadherin.
review_notes: Cited in prose only; no supporting_text is taken from this reference and no row depends on it.

title: Aggf1 attenuates neuroinflammation and BBB disruption via PI3K/Akt/NF-κB pathway after subarachnoid hemorrhage in rats.
review_notes: Added after the PR reviewer pointed out that it was cached with full text, is AGGF1 primary research, and was missing from both the review and lab_independence.py's paper set - which meant this review's independence count described its own list rather than the literature. Senior author Zhang JH appears on no paper from the dominant group, so lab_independence.py counts this paper among the independent set - one of the papers in that set that this review cites. The work is in Sprague-Dawley rats, so it is cited as corroboration of the PI3K/AKT axis and not as evidence for any human evidence code.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
Structural basis for DEAH-helicase activation by G-patch proteins.
review_notes: Does not study AGGF1, and is cited only for what a G-patch domain is. That distinction is deliberate: it grounds the objection to the IPR000467 to GO:0003676 mapping without asserting anything measured about AGGF1.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Correctly cited. Its weight is easy to overstate: expanding the IntAct records shows two hybrid array, two hybrid prey pooling approach and validated two hybrid are sub-methods of a single screen, which is what UniProt's NbExp=3 is counting.

title: Angiogenic factor AGGF1 acts as a tumor suppressor by modulating p53 post-transcriptional modifications and stability via MDM2.
review_notes: Full text cached and all three quotes verified against it. Produced no GO annotation on any gene product. The mutational pattern independently corroborates the residue-level prediction that G437-R438, S454 and N478 form AGGF1's phosphothreonine-recognition surface - but corroborates only that the surface matters, not that it binds a phosphopeptide.

title: [ole of AGGF1 in DNA damage repair and modulating chemotherapy resistance in human colon cancer cells in vitro].
review_notes: Added after the PR reviewer pointed out that excluding it was a judgement layered on top of a measurement: lab_independence.py counts it as independent (senior author Liao S appears on no dominant-group paper), it is cached with full text, and it bears directly on the review's largest proposal. The DNA-damage-repair interpretation rests on siRNA knockdown changing phospho-gammaH2AX and NBS1 levels and is not annotated here; only the localisation is used. MEDIUM rather than HIGH for three reasons that agree: it is a small study, the article is Chinese-language with an English abstract (Nan Fang Yi Ke Da Xue Xue Bao), and the affinage record independently rates it Low confidence. Note also a fetcher defect rather than a curation one: the cached title begins '[ole of AGGF1' - a bracket-stripping step in the publication fetcher has eaten the R of '[Role', which would affect every translated PubMed title of this form. The YAML deliberately reproduces the cached title verbatim so that title validation passes; hand-correcting it here would mask the bug rather than fix it.

title: FHA domain of AGGF1 is essential for its nucleocytoplasmic transport and angiogenesis.
review_notes: Absent from the affinage deep-research record despite being titled for the FHA domain, and absent from GOA. Cached record is abstract-only; the full text could not be retrieved, so no claim is made about experiments the abstract does not describe. In particular, a secondary source asserting the 14-3-3 interaction is phosphorylation-dependent was checked and found to be an inference, not a statement in the paper, and is not used.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: 9514 annotations, so the reference-level projection test cannot be run without pagination and is reported as unavailable rather than estimated.

title: Receptor and Molecular Mechanism of AGGF1 Signaling in Endothelial Cell Functions and Angiogenesis.
review_notes: Full text cached and all quotes verified. Produced no GO annotation on any gene product, which is why two of the three molecular-function proposals in this review come from it.

title: Angiogenic factor AGGF1 blocks neointimal formation after vascular injury via interaction with integrin α7 on vascular smooth muscle cells.
review_notes: Cited in prose only, and specifically to record why it is NOT used: the species check is the point. No quote is taken from it.

title: Identification and characterization of a special type of subnuclear structure: AGGF1-coated paraspeckles.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only and does not name the cell system, which a curator making the paraspeckle and RNA-binding annotations should confirm. From the Wang QK laboratory, which discovered AGGF1. An earlier draft hedged this by anchoring the nucleus proposal on PMID:33069768 instead - but that paper has the same senior author, so the hedge was empty and is withdrawn. The honest statement is that AGGF1's mechanistic literature is dominated by one group. Of the 27 cached AGGF1 primary studies reachable from this review's own inputs, 18 have Wang Q or Wang QK as senior author; a further 5 have a senior author who is themselves an author on one of those papers (Tian XL twice, plus Xu Y, Zhou B and Lu Q), i.e. trainee or collaborator lineage rather than an independent investigator; and 4 have a senior author who appears on no Wang-group paper at all - Qi J (PMID:17884784), Zhang JH (PMID:29885663), Liao S (PMID:33168501) and Chen L (PMID:39905000). Three of those four are used by this review: PMID:39905000 for the TNFSF12 interaction and the extracellular pool, PMID:29885663 on the PI3K/AKT row, and PMID:33168501 on the GO:0005634 nucleus row, where it supplies the only line of support that is neither Wang-group nor lineage. The nucleus proposal is therefore anchored on PMID:33069768 because that paper's imaging is in a named human cell line (HCT116) and its cached record is full text, not because it is independent of this one. Independent replication of the paraspeckle result remains the single most useful thing anyone could do for this gene's annotation.

title: Protein therapy of skeletal muscle atrophy and mechanism by angiogenic factor AGGF1.
review_notes: Not disputed as a citation - the paper says what it says - but its central mechanistic claim is contradicted in direction by PMID:39905000. Recording both, and annotating neither, is the honest treatment. No quote is taken from it.

title: AGGF1 therapy inhibits thoracic aortic aneurysms by enhancing integrin α7-mediated inhibition of TGF-β1 maturation and ERK1/2 signaling.
review_notes: Mouse work, cited for completeness of the integrin alpha7 story. No quote is taken from it.

title: Systematic identification of post-transcriptional regulatory modules.
review_notes: The study is sound; the derived annotation is not. IntAct records AGGF1 as experimentalRoleA bait in all 635 proximity records, and a BirA fusion biotinylates itself, so the self-proximity datum carries no information about homodimerisation. The paper also carries an unflagged Author Correction (PMID:39468017); reading it shows the correction adds a missing author affiliation and affects no data.

title: Endothelial AGGF1 promotes retinal angiogenesis by coordinating TNFSF12/FN14 signalling.
review_notes: Full text cached and quotes verified. Produced no GO annotation on any gene product despite independently re-confirming AGGF1's best-supported interaction - the only replication of the TNFSF12 result by a group outside the dominant one.

title: Angiogenic factor AGGF1 is a general splicing factor regulating angiogenesis and vascular development by alternative splicing of SRSF6.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only but the human cell system (HPAECs) and the perturbation (silencing) are both stated in it, which is what the IMP code requires. The reference-projection check found no projection pattern, but it did sharpen the coverage point: QuickGO shows this paper produced 10 annotations over 10 entities, and every one of them is GO:0048514 blood vessel morphogenesis in ZEBRAFISH - four on aggf1 by IMP and six on srsf6a/srsf6b by IGI. So a paper whose entire finding is that AGGF1 is a general splicing factor regulating 436 genes produced ten GO annotations, all about vessel morphogenesis in fish, and not one about splicing in any species. Nothing reached human AGGF1.

title: A novel acylglycerol kinase that produces lysophosphatidic acid modulates cross talk with EGFR in prostate cancer cells.
review_notes: Full local Results and Methods checked: human cDNA expressed in mammalian cells, positive MAG/DAG assays, negative ceramide/sphingosine assays and mitochondrial enrichment. Figure 2 measures protein and MOG activity across fractions, with highest AGK-specific activity in P2. The smaller P4 protein signal and unresolved P4-specific activity/purity do not establish either a functional plasma-membrane pool or contamination. The manuscript explicitly discusses the conflicting bacterial mouse-MuLK result.

title: Further characterization of mammalian ceramide kinase: substrate delivery and (stereo)specificity, tissue distribution, and subcellular localization studies.

title: Substrate chirality and specificity of diacylglycerol kinases and the multisubstrate lipid kinase.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18004883/. The abstract compares MuLK phosphorylation of sn-1,2- and sn-2,3-dioleoylglycerol, with lower stereoselectivity than the compared DAG kinases. Species and enzyme-preparation details are not explicit in this cache. This is positive lipid-substrate evidence, but not an independent human ceramide-phosphorylation assay.

title: Role of acylglycerol kinase in LPA-induced IL-8 secretion and transactivation of epidermal growth factor-receptor in human bronchial epithelial cells.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19112101/. The abstract reports human bronchial epithelial AGK knockdown and lentiviral wild-type overexpression, intracellular LPA changes and altered LPA-induced IL8, EGFR and MAPK responses. Microscopy localizes overexpressed AGK to mitochondria. These cellular results support contextual lipid-signaling regulation; they do not isolate direct AGK phosphorylation of EGFR.

title: A suppressor/enhancer screen in Drosophila reveals a role for wnt-mediated lipid metabolism in primordial germ cell migration.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22069480/. Relevant Results, Figures 6–8, transgenic-line and lipid-MS Methods were read. Drosophila CG31873/Dmulk coding sequence is expressed from UASp constructs; Dcerk/Dmulk genetics affect primordial-germ-cell migration, and Dmulk overexpression increases whole-embryo C1P approximately 3.3-fold. This is genuine positive fly evidence. The inspected experiments do not isolate purified Dmulk or human AGK ceramide phosphorylation, and cited human/mouse enzymology is background. The XML repeats nested sections; linked supplements were not independently read. This source does not erase the distinct human negative-substrate assays.

title: Lack of the mitochondrial protein acylglycerol kinase causes Sengers syndrome.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract establishes the human genotype association and reduced muscle ANT abundance. Its proposed lipid-based mechanism is a historical interpretation, not evidence that later kinase-independent import findings are false.

title: Expression of lysophosphatidic acid, autotaxin and acylglycerol kinase as biomarkers in diabetic retinopathy.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22864860/. The abstract describes 42 human proliferative-diabetic-retinopathy vitreous samples, 35 nondiabetic controls and diabetic rat retinas, using ELISA and immunoblotting. Expression and biomarker associations do not establish a new AGK substrate or direct angiogenic mechanism. Full Methods and Results are unavailable locally.

title: Mitochondrial citrate synthase crystals: novel finding in Sengers syndrome caused by acylglycerol kinase (AGK) mutations.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identifier/title/DOI verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23266196/. Cached source inspected: Abstract only; no full Methods/Results. Human Sengers syndrome pedigrees with p.M1I and p.K327* variants. Electron microscopy, citrate synthase activity, tissue-specific respiratory-chain measurements and MnSOD abundance support disease and mitochondrial dysfunction. The abstract's lipid/redox explanation is an interpretation, not a new direct AGK substrate assay or a separation of kinase and TIM22 functions.

title: Proteomic mapping of the human mitochondrial intermembrane space in live cells via ratiometric APEX tagging.
review_notes: PubMed identity was verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25002142/. The normal fetch artifact recovered on 2026-09-27 now supplies XML full text from PMC4743503. Relevant Results and Methods describe ratiometric IMS-targeted APEX labeling and controls for cytosolic labeling through outer-membrane porins; detected peptides on selected established IMM proteins map to IMS-facing domains. The individual AGK supplementary record is not present in the extracted main text and was not independently inspected. These methods support IMS proximity but do not independently establish the AGK membrane anchor. PMID:28712726 supplies a separate interpretation and topology evidence. Local full_text_unavailable is false while the unresolved AGK-specific supplementary scope remains explicit.

title: The role of AGK in thrombocytopoiesis and possible therapeutic strategies.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identifier/title/DOI verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32202634/. Cached source inspected: Abstract only; no full Methods/Results. Mouse megakaryocyte/platelet-specific AGK loss impairs platelet production; G126E retains platelet-count and differentiation phenotypes. AGK–JAK2 binding and enhanced JAK2/STAT3 signaling are reported. This is positive context-specific, kinase-independent regulatory evidence; it neither assigns JAK2 protein phosphorylation to AGK nor demonstrates the same mechanism in normal human physiology.

review_notes: Primary PubMed identifier/title/DOI verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34948281/. Cached source inspected: Full XML body: Results 2.1–2.3, Methods 4.1–4.8 and Conclusions read. title: AGK Potentiates Arterial Thrombosis by Affecting Talin-1 and αIIbβ3-Mediated Bidirectional Signaling Pathway.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37051931/. The structured abstract describes transgenic mouse platelet activation and thrombosis experiments, co-immunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry, staining, immunoblots and PA/LPA measurements. AGK deficiency or mutation reduces activation, while measured PA/LPA output is unchanged; Talin1 Ser425 phosphorylation is implicated. The authors report kinase-dependent effects, but the abstract does not resolve a purified direct AGK-to-Talin1 phosphotransfer reaction. This platelet-activation outcome differs from the kinase-independent platelet-production phenotype in PMID:32202634; neither result is discarded.

title: Ceramide kinase-mediated C1P metabolism attenuates acute liver injury by inhibiting the interaction between KEAP1 and NRF2.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38556546/. Relevant local Methods, Results and Figures 2–8 concern CERK/C1P in mouse CCl4 and ischemia-reperfusion liver injury, mouse AML12 cells and human primary hepatocytes. Mouse KEAP1/domain-deletion constructs are expressed in HEK293T cells. C1P-coated beads and domain deletions implicate the lipid as the KEAP1 ligand, not the CERK protein or AGK. Docking and lysate pulldown are not a purified binding-constant assay. Supplementary-only methods were not independently recovered. This is a distinct-enzyme comparator, not direct AGK evidence. Retained to adjudicate the research summary's CERK-versus-AGK attribution, not as evidence for an AGK reaction.

title: Aberrantly Expressed Mitochondrial Lipid Kinase, AGK, Activates JAK2-Histone H3 Axis and BCR Signal: A Mechanistic Study with Implication in CLL Therapy.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39636206/. Patient/cell, siRNA, co-immunoprecipitation and microscopy Methods and the AGK/JAK2 Results were read. Primary untreated human CLL samples and normal B cells show cellular AGK/HSP90 and AGK/JAK2 associations, AGK-siRNA effects on phosphorylated JAK2, and cytoplasmic/nuclear AGK localization. JAK2 performs the proposed H3 Tyr41 phosphorylation; AGK is not demonstrated to be a histone kinase. These native-AGK observations are independent of the AGK–BRAF fusion events and do not make those events evidence for native-AGK localization. Supplements were not independently read.

title: Ceramide kinase suppresses ferroptosis and protects against alcohol-associated liver disease through the p38 MAPK-HSPB1 pathway.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40536506/. CERK perturbation changes p38/HSPB1 phosphorylation, and SB203580 reverses protective cellular effects. This is pathway epistasis, not purified CERK phosphorylation of p38 or HSPB1, and not an AGK experiment. Human transcriptomic associations do not change the experimental protein/model scope. Retained to adjudicate the research summary's CERK-versus-AGK attribution, not as evidence for an AGK reaction.

Retained to adjudicate the research summary's CERK-versus-AGK attribution, not as evidence for an AGK reaction.

The enzyme assay is not purified human CERK and does not identify AGK as its catalyst. cAMP/PKA effects and assay temperature/pH optima do not establish a new human AGK function. title: Case Report: Sengers syndrome caused by a novel 7.6 kb AGK deletion misdiagnosed as isolated congenital cataract.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identifier/title/DOI verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41695748/. Cached source inspected: Full XML body: Case report, genotyping, Figure 3 and Discussion read. The Discussion explicitly states that patient-derived functional validation was not performed. The deletion mechanism is an inference; no new AGK catalytic, splicing or TIM22 experiment is established.

title: Oocyte-specific acylglycerol kinase loss leads to infertility in mice via mitochondrial dysfunction.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42026151/. Conditional-allele/animal Methods and mitochondrial, fertility and metabolomic Results use mouse Agk exon-3 flox crossed with Dppa3-Cre. Oocyte loss and mitochondrial defects establish a physiological requirement; PA rises despite knockout and LPA is undetectable. No direct human AGK or TIM22 import assay is performed. Unchanged TIM22 transcript abundance does not exclude a protein-complex contribution, and kinase-dead knock-in is proposed as future work. The measured requirement does not by itself establish an additional catalytic core.

title: Acylglycerol kinase contributes to cell proliferation by activating NF‑κB signaling pathway in pancreatic cancer.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42212382/. Local Methods explicitly identify full-length human AGK in N-terminal Flag-pcDNA3.1, human AsPC1/PANC1 cells and pancreatic tissues; PANC1 xenografts use mouse hosts. Knockdown/overexpression, NF-kappaB reporter, p65 localization/phosphorylation and partial epistasis support cellular pathway regulation. They do not isolate direct AGK phosphorylation of p65 or IKK. Supplementary/raw data were not independently assessed.

title: Ceramide kinase/ceramide 1-phosphate signaling regulates LC3B expression and autophagosome formation.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42285305/. Local Methods and Results use HeLa CERK knockout/siRNA/inhibitor models, HA-tagged wild-type versus kinase-dead G198D rescue, and separate mouse Cerk-knockout cerebellar proteomics. Wild type restores NBD-C1P production and LC3B-II where G198D does not. The inspected Methods do not establish the rescue-insert species accession from the human host alone. The GFP/RFP reporter lacked a significant starvation difference, and the authors limit conclusions to LC3B-associated autophagosome formation rather than global autophagy. These are CERK experiments, not AGK evidence. Retained to adjudicate the research summary's CERK-versus-AGK attribution, not as evidence for an AGK reaction.

title: Acylglycerol Kinase Sensitizes Glioblastoma to Temozolomide via Limiting Mitochondrial Damage Related Cellular Senescence.
review_notes: Primary identifier, title and DOI independently verified at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42391447/. Local cell/construct Methods and Results 3.1–3.6 use human GBM lines U251/LN299 (as printed), shRNAs, a full-length AGK cDNA without an explicit species accession, and 82 human GBM cases. Quantitative Results show reduced basal proliferation but increased temozolomide resistance and senescence after AGK depletion. Some concluding wording reverses that direction; the assessment follows the actual Results and corresponding Discussion. The AGK-to-ROS mechanism remains unresolved, and no purified lipid- or protein-substrate assay is presented. Human host is not treated as proof of an unspecified insert origin.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for AGK ceramide kinase activity
review_notes: Read and reused the existing report. Its human ceramide-kinase conclusion is supported by direct negative substrate assays. However, the report incorrectly presents the PAINT assertion as CERK-to-AGK propagation: PTN008994514 is supported by mouse Agk and fly Mulk. It also does not independently resolve ceramide/sphingosine biosynthetic-process annotations. Retain the biochemical observations and exact report excerpt while rejecting those overextended phylogenetic/pathway explanations. The report also says Bektas did not mention ceramide and describes limited human testing; the cached human Results explicitly tested it. The metazoan debranching-family assignment is credible, but its glycogen-formation mapping is removed because the demonstrated AGL reactions perform glycogen breakdown. This is a pathway-role error, not evidence of a plant-family misassignment.

title: A redox switch in angiotensinogen modulates angiotensin release.
review_notes: The single most important paper for this gene and absent from the deep research report. Crystal structures of angiotensinogen at 2.1 A and of the human angiotensinogen-renin complex at 4.4 A. Verified against the cached full text: it states in its own abstract that angiotensinogen is a non-inhibitory serpin, which is the basis for removing the three GO:0004867 rows, and it supplies the 670 A^2 renin interface behind the GO:0002020 MODIFY. Its redox-switch model is treated as structurally sound but physiologically contested, because PMID:25691624 tested it in vivo.

title: Protein microarrays discover angiotensinogen and PRKRIP1 as novel targets for autoantibodies in chronic renal disease.
review_notes: Cited as an IDA for GO:0003014 renal system process. The cached full text is complete and contains no renal-process experiment: it is an autoantibody biomarker screen, and the authors state they cannot tell whether the antibodies target angiotensinogen or angiotensin I, nor establish pathogenicity. Correct paper, correct title, wrong use.

title: Proteomic analysis of microvesicles from plasma of healthy donors reveals high individual variability.
review_notes: Correctly cited HDA detection, but the starting material is plasma, where angiotensinogen is present at microgram-per-millilitre concentrations, so its appearance in a plasma-derived vesicle fraction carries no localisation information.

title: Structural basis of peptide recognition by the angiotensin-1 converting enzyme homologue AnCE from Drosophila melanogaster.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a good structural paper, but what it shows about AGT is a 10-residue cleavage product sitting in the active site of a Drosophila enzyme. UniProt flags the pair 'Xeno'. Recorded on human AGT as bare protein binding, where it carries no interpretive weight.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Correctly cited HDA detection. Abundant body-fluid proteins routinely co-purify with extracellular vesicles, and no vesicle-associated function or sorting signal is known for angiotensinogen.

title: Extracellular matrix signatures of human primary metastatic colon cancers and their metastases to liver.
review_notes: Correctly cited HDA detection. The objection is to the inference, not the citation: an abundant plasma protein detected in a tissue ECM proteome is the expected blood background, and no matrix function has been reported for angiotensinogen.

title: Cys18-Cys137 disulfide bond in mouse angiotensinogen does not affect AngII-dependent functions in vivo.
review_notes: The measured negative that kept a GO term out of this review. AAV delivery of wild-type versus Cys18Ser/Cys137Ser angiotensinogen into hepatocyte-specific Agt-null mice gave equivalent plasma angiotensin II, systolic blood pressure and atherosclerotic lesion size. Directly tests the PMID:20927107 redox model in vivo and finds the disulfide dispensable. Also the gain-of-function counterpart to the PMID:7989296 knockout.

title: Extracellular matrix remodelling in response to venous hypertension: proteomics of human varicose veins.
review_notes: Correctly cited HDA detection, assigned to the broad and unobjectionable GO:0005576 rather than to a specific structure. Accepted.

title: Angiotensin-(1-7) regulates angiotensin II-induced matrix metalloproteinase-8 in vascular smooth muscle cells.
review_notes: The only row in the record representing the counter-regulatory angiotensin-(1-7)/MAS1 limb, which is why it is kept. Correctly cited; the IMP evidence code is loose, since the perturbations are peptide agonists and the MAS1 antagonist A779 rather than mutations in AGT.

title: Structural basis for the specificity of renin-mediated angiotensinogen cleavage.
review_notes: Also missed by the deep research report. Four structures including loop-cleaved AGT, solved specifically to test whether the reactive centre loop triggers the stressed-to-relaxed transition; it does not. This is the experimental demonstration, rather than the assertion, that AGT lacks the serpin inhibitory mechanism, and it is what makes the GO:0004867 removals safe. Also the source of the tail-into-mouth mechanism and of the finding that specificity is set outside renin's active-site cleft.

title: Novel role of the clustered miR-23b-3p and miR-27b-3p in enhanced expression of fibrosis-associated genes by targeting TGFBR3 in atrial fibroblasts.
review_notes: Correctly cited. Three AGT rows, all properly qualified 'acts_upstream_of'. The most immediate observation - angiotensin II raises miR-23b-3p and miR-27b-3p in primary human atrial fibroblasts - is direct; the matrix row is three steps downstream, since the collagen induction is driven by miRNA over-expression rather than by angiotensin II.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: A competent large-scale study whose output is unsuitable for functional annotation of this gene. It yields ten bare protein-binding rows on AGT, a protein unrelated to neurodegeneration; the paper itself calls the results candidate interactions. None of the ten partners shares AGT's secreted compartment (0/10, computed in AGT-bioinformatics), and eight of them carry a curated intracellular location, while AGT is secreted; the remaining two, NPHP1 and PRRG2, have no annotated location at all. UniProt's NbExp=3 on each is replicates within this study.

title: Molecular cloning of the mouse angiotensinogen gene.
review_notes: Cited by GOA as a TAS for GO:0004867 serine-type endopeptidase inhibitor activity, which it does not assert. Its own abstract says only that angiotensinogen is homologous to serpins and that the authors aligned a putative reactive centre - and then notes that the human site differs from the rodent one. A sequence-alignment observation in a mouse gene-cloning paper became a molecular function annotation on the human gene. Correctly identified and correctly titled; it simply does not support the claim made from it.

title: Enzymatic degradation and electrophoresis of human angiotensin I.
review_notes: A 1968 paper cited by UniProt for the signal peptide and the 'Secreted' location, and by GOA as the IDA behind is_active_in extracellular region. PubMed holds no abstract for it, so the experiment cannot be inspected here. The conclusion is not in doubt and is corroborated many times over, but the evidence itself is unread.

title: Angiotensinogen-deficient mice with hypotension.
review_notes: The foundational loss-of-function evidence, cited by GOA for this gene nowhere at all. Homozygous Agt-null mice have no plasma immunoreactive angiotensin I and a systolic pressure of 66.9 mm Hg against 100.4 in wild-type. Supports the core blood-pressure functions. Abstract only; the quantitative result is in the abstract.

title: A molecular variant of angiotensinogen associated with preeclampsia.
review_notes: A historically important genetic association study, cited on AGT as a TAS for the generic term 'cell-cell signaling', which it contains no experiment bearing on. The variant it identifies is also now understood to act through angiotensinogen concentration rather than function.

title: AGT (P01019) - bioinformatics support for the annotation review
review_notes: Three analyses written for this review, all fetching live from UniProt, QuickGO and the committed PANTHER PAINT slice. They establish that AGT is MEROPS I04.953 while all 7 resolvable seeds of the donating IBD node are MEROPS inhibitors; that AGT has no UniProt reactive bond and a proline-blocked hinge at P12 (Pro430); and that 0 of the 10 partners from the large-scale yeast two-hybrid screen share a compartment with a secreted protein. The document states its own limits, including that the receptor-binding rows are deliberately excluded from the compartment metric.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGT (human)
review_notes: The script's trust gate tripped (self_evaluation_pairwise: tie, not win), and the record fails independently of that. It confuses AGT with AGXT: the narrative asserts that AGT has peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase activity, citing a primary hyperoxaluria type 1 study in AgxtQ84-/- rats. 'AGT' is also the common abbreviation for that enzyme, whose HGNC symbol is AGXT (P21549) - a different gene, a different protein, a different compartment. The error propagates into its own GO grounding, which lists GO:0016740 transferase activity and GO:0005777 peroxisome for a secreted plasma serpin; none of that grounding was imported. Recall is also poor: none of its 11 citations appears in AGT's GOA record, and it misses every paper that matters for the molecular biology (PMID:20927107, PMID:30563843, PMID:7989296, PMID:25691624, PMID:12045255). Nothing from it is used as supporting_text for a mechanistic claim.

title: UniProtKB P01019 (ANGT_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: The curated record, used for the signal peptide and chain boundaries, the eight angiotensin PEPTIDE features, the Cys42-Cys162 disulfide, the four N-glycosylation sites, the 'Secreted' location, the serpin similarity statement, the MEROPS I04.953 cross-reference, and the IntAct entries. The last of those matter for the review's framing: UniProt attaches the receptor interactions to PRO_ chain identifiers (PRO_0000032458 with AGTR1, PRO_0000032459 with AGTR2) rather than to full-length angiotensinogen.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro mapping provenance retained. Domain-based peptidase and metal-binding assertions are assessed against direct target assays; broad proteolysis is refined to the measured modification processes.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Original curator-mediated similarity transfers are preserved. Q641K1 is mouse Agtpbp1, not a paralog. The MGI graph read on 2026-09-27 identifies itself as a 2023-03-10 snapshot; term-specific donor references and remaining full-text limits are documented in the annotation reviews and notes.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT is an ancestral-node inference, not a count of pairwise donors. PTN007589887 and PTN002654088 are recorded as proximate sources; their exact IBD placements were not independently reconstructed. Positive target evidence supports retained judgments and human self-evidence is not circular.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Source vocabulary mappings match explicit Q9UPW5 locations. Evidence provenance is inherited from the underlying UniProt record, including similarity-based cytosol and mitochondrion assignments; the mappings are not new localization assays.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: The HPA primary AGTPBP1 subcellular page was read on 2026-09-27 (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000135049-AGTPBP1/subcellular). Nucleoplasm is supported with antibody HPA071094 in SH-SY5Y, SK-MEL-30 and U2OS; the additional locations have uncertain reliability. The seeded compartment is supported, without adding the other locations.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods

title: Purkinje cell degeneration (pcd) phenotypes caused by mutations in the axotomy-induced gene, Nna1.
review_notes: Verified PubMed identity https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11884758/ and DOI 10.1126/science.1068912. The source11 cache is abstract-only. The original Science 295:1904–1906 main text was read in the author-uploaded ResearchGate copy on 2026-09-27 (publication/11477921): mouse allele mapping, postweaning degeneration and one-month-old in-situ expression, not a direct developmental progression assay. The linked supplementary material was not recovered. PubMed and the original PDF cover identify a correction at Science 2002;297:337, legacy URL https://www.sciencemag.org/content/297/5580/337.2.full.html; its body and an exact separate PMID/DOI were not verified. No retraction, identifier remapping or specific correction to the biological result is inferred.

title: The Purkinje cell degeneration 5J mutation is a single amino acid insertion that destabilizes Nna1 protein.
review_notes: Verified primary PubMed abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16465590/, DOI 10.1007/s00335-005-0096-x; historical MGI J:105316. It reports the mouse pcd5J mutation and protein destabilization. Full text was not recovered, including after the author-page route returned request-only access. Photoreceptor/Purkinje differentiation cannot be adjudicated from the accessible degeneration summary. Source11 recovered the exact normal-fetched record; the local record is abstract-only, and no full body was recovered or read for this paper.

title: A novel subfamily of mouse cytosolic carboxypeptidases.
review_notes: Verified primary abstract and DOI 10.1096/fj.06-7329com. The cache is abstract-only and the original full paper was not recovered. The abstract explicitly studies the mouse CCP family and reports cytosolic CCP1; it does not establish every human construct detail. The proposed detyrosination mechanism in that early work is not substituted for later demonstrated deglutamylation.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in NnaD mutant flies and Purkinje cell degeneration mice reveals a role for Nna proteins in neuronal bioenergetics.
review_notes: Verified primary PubMed identity and indexed full PMC3101252, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3101252/, read 2026-09-27. Figure 5A is rat brain/spinal-cord fractionation; Figure 5B is mouse liver submitochondrial fractionation with compartment markers. Fly and mouse loss-of-function experiments concern mitochondrial physiology. These are positive donor data, not a direct human topology assay. Historical MGI J:163166 links the mouse localization/organization annotations to this paper. title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go route, and the source of the GO:0038166 row. Which signature supplies it was checked rather than assumed: AGTRAP has exactly one InterPro entry, IPR009436, which is the AGTRAP family itself (PTHR16521 / PF06396 - one subfamily, 1380 member proteins of which 5 are Swiss-Prot and all 5 are AGTRAP orthologues). So the signature match is correct and specific; the defect is that the GO term attached to it names the pathway AGTRAP inhibits.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Both IBA rows. PTHR16521 has exactly two IBD annotations family-wide (PTHR16521-paint.tsv), both seeded from MGI:MGI:1339977, and each was traced to the mouse donor's own evidence in QuickGO rather than accepted on identity. GO:0005886 rests on a mouse IDA and is sound; GO:0008217 rests on an IMP whose cited paper is about Agtr2.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The three membrane-location rows. Not a prediction: UniProt's endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and cytoplasmic vesicle SUBCELLULAR LOCATION lines all carry ECO:0000269|PubMed:12960423, so the keyword mapping is downstream of a real microscopy result.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: The single HPA immunofluorescence IDA, and the only IDA anywhere in this gene's GO record. Independently reproduces the Golgi localisation curated from PubMed:12960423.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Four Ensembl Compara rows from two donors, both resolved and both true orthologues (Q9WVK0 mouse, Q642A2 rat; no paralogue is available to transfer from, since PTHR16521 has none). The pipeline is working as designed, and two of the four rows are nonetheless wrong because the donor annotations they faithfully copy are themselves defective - GO:0004945 from an Agtr2-knockout paper and GO:0001666 from a single rat IEP. A demonstration that orthology-projection quality is bounded by donor quality.

title: Cloning and characterization of ATRAP, a novel protein that interacts with the angiotensin II type 1 receptor.
review_notes: The founding characterisation and the single most informative paper on this gene: AT1a-tail binding, its selectivity against five other receptor tails, and inhibition of AT1a-mediated phospholipase C. The work is on the mouse protein (mouse kidney library, murine AT1a bait), which is why it corroborates rather than supplies the human GO:0031702 proposal. Also the source of the mouse plasma membrane and cell cortex IDAs that Compara projects into human.

title: Increased vasoconstrictor response of the mouse lacking angiotensin II type 2 receptor.
review_notes: Relevant to this review only as the defect it documents. The paper is an Agtr2-knockout study and its abstract never mentions Agtrap, yet MGI attached two annotations on mouse Agtrap to it: GO:0004945 enables by IMP and GO:0008217 by IMP. Querying QuickGO by this reference returns 13 annotations over 3 entities (Agt, Agtr2, Agtrap), with Agtr2 correctly receiving GO:0004945 by IGI; the Agtrap rows look like a confusion between two adjacent symbols. MISCITED with respect to Agtrap - it is sound work about a different gene.

title: ATRAP, novel AT1 receptor associated protein, enhances internalization of AT1 receptor and inhibits vascular smooth muscle cell growth.
review_notes: The receptor-internalization result. An over-expression experiment in vascular smooth muscle cells whose species the abstract does not state, which is why the proposed GO:0002092 row is ISS rather than IMP.

title: Identification and characterization of AGTRAP, a human homolog of murine Angiotensin II Receptor-Associated Protein (Agtrap).
review_notes: The human AGTRAP cloning paper and the source of the RACK1 interaction, validated by yeast two-hybrid, GST pull-down, co-immunoprecipitation and surface plasmon resonance. Read carefully because UniProt's SUBUNIT line bundles it with PubMed:12960423: this paper supports the RACK1 half and does not itself assay AGTR1. The RACK1 interaction is absent from GOA.

title: The angiotensin II type I receptor-associated protein, ATRAP, is a transmembrane protein and a modulator of angiotensin II signaling.
review_notes: The topology, localisation and signalling-modulation paper, and the reference UniProt tags with ECO:0000269 on the human entry for FUNCTION, SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION. Supplies the C-terminal deletion result that maps AT1 binding, the ER/Golgi/endocytic vesicle localisation behind three IEA rows, and the inhibition of inositol lipid generation, c-fos activity and proliferation.

title: The novel angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R)-associated protein ATRAP downregulates AT1R and ameliorates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.
review_notes: Cardiomyocyte counterpart of PubMed:11162453: ATRAP over-expression lowers surface AT1 receptor number and attenuates the hypertrophic response. Corroborating, not decisive.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: CCSB HI-1; contributes 2 binding rows (PITPNC1 and PBX3). One of nine screen publications behind 188 of this gene's 199 GOA rows. IntAct logs it under two hybrid pooling only, with 3 pairs - the third is an AGTRAP self-pair that GOA did not import, which is why the IntAct evidence count and the GOA row count differ here by one.

title: Vascular response to hypoxic preconditioning in the immature brain.
review_notes: Cited only as the sole donor evidence for the response-to-hypoxia row. A neonatal rat brain hypoxic-preconditioning study; in all of GOA it produces exactly two annotations, rat Agtrap and rat Angptl4, both IEP. Correctly cited by RGD, and too thin to project into human.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: CCSB assay-framework paper, 2 binding rows, re-testing the same ORF pairs in the same two-hybrid system. Not independent replication of the screen it re-tests.

title: Atrap deficiency increases arterial blood pressure and plasma volume.
review_notes: The Atrap-knockout phenotype: elevated systolic blood pressure, expanded plasma volume, low plasma renin and enhanced renal cortical surface AT1 receptor. It rescues the GO:0008217 row whose curated evidence points at the wrong paper, and it is cited by no GO annotation in any species.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: CCSB sequencing-based interactome method paper, 4 binding rows, logged by IntAct under '2 hybrid'.

title: The phosphatidylinositol transfer protein RdgBβ binds 14-3-3 via its unstructured C-terminus, whereas its lipid-binding domain interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I receptor-associated protein).

Shows the PITP domain of RdgB-beta/PITPNC1 engaging AGTRAP on PMA treatment and being recruited to membranes as a result: the only published experiment that yields an informative molecular function for AGTRAP itself.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HI-II-14, the larger of the two dominant sources: 66 binding rows here, and 202 IntAct evidences that decompose as 68 + 67 + 67 across three two-hybrid sub-method terms - the arithmetic that shows the apparent triplicate is one experiment. Not worthless: it is also the source of the FAM114A1 hit that PubMed:35671117 later validated. Unreplicated rather than wrong.
