title: The angiotensin receptor-associated protein Atrap is a stimulator of the cardiac Ca2+-ATPase SERCA2a.
review_notes: Titled for SERCA2a. Pull-down/MALDI-MS, co-immunoprecipitation and surface plasmon resonance for the Atrap-SERCA2a interaction, plus a functional calcium-uptake increase and a knockout relaxation phenotype. Entirely mouse, hence the ISS proposal.

title: FAM114A1 influences cardiac pathological remodeling by regulating angiotensin II signaling.
review_notes: Titled for FAM114A1. The clearest case in this review of a high-throughput hit earning its keep: the authors start from the published two-hybrid candidates, validate AGTRAP-FAM114A1 by immunoprecipitation in mouse heart lysates and primary cardiac fibroblasts, and show the interaction controls AT1R abundance. Missed by the affinage record.

review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Human wild-type and G82E kinetic/cofactor experiments directly support the glyoxylate-to-glycine reaction and PLP dependence. title: Reactions of human liver peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase with beta-chloro-L-alanine and L-cysteine: spectroscopic and kinetic analysis.
review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Product/coenzyme analyses and kinetic comparisons support cysteine beta-elimination, half-transamination and amino-acid binding. The abstract also explicitly compares these reactions with physiological L-alanine transamination. The generic transaminase row is refined to the established alanine:glyoxylate activity; distinct cysteine chemistry remains non-core and physiological hepatic flux unresolved. The local record is abstract-only.

title: Molecular defects of the glycine 41 variants of alanine glyoxylate aminotransferase associated with primary hyperoxaluria type I.
review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. The abstract supports G41-dependent changes in conformation, stability, dimer-monomer equilibrium, cofactor binding and catalytic efficiency, but does not expose the full substrate-specific assay. The reaction refinement is explicitly corroborated by independent cached PMID:17696873, not attributed to an absent cached Results section. Prior external inspection of indexed PMC2840350 Results is documented in notes; the local cache remains abstract-only. Apo/holo and allele distinctions preclude a universal mutant dimerization-failure claim.

review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. N-terminal-deleted human enzyme remains dimeric and peroxisomally targeted but aggregates and loses much activity. Therefore the extension supports a functional conformation, not an absolute ability to dimerize or enter peroxisomes. Product/substrate processes are independently corroborated by the measured AGXT reaction. Local evidence is abstract-only unless external access is specified.

title: Molecular requirements for peroxisomal targeting of alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase as an essential determinant in primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Full Results, Discussion and relevant Methods read. Purified human proteins form a PEX5-(AGXT)2-PEX5 complex, with preserved AGXT activity and PLP. Direct C-terminal recognition makes a required extra adaptor unlikely in this reconstituted system; no universal claim excluding cellular cofactors is made.

title: Four of the most common mutations in primary hyperoxaluria type 1 unmask the cryptic mitochondrial targeting sequence of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase encoded by the polymorphic minor allele.
review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Local metadata marks full text available, but the extraction contains Abstract, Introduction and Discussion, not Methods/Results. These sections explicitly compare normal/variant activity, dimerization and targeting in CHO cells and discuss differences from COS cells and human liver; no uninspected image-level result is asserted.

review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Human cDNA and missing ancestral N-terminal sequence support the enzyme identity and early targeting model. The suggested mechanism for disease mistargeting is historical, not the later complete P11L/G170R mechanism. Local evidence is abstract-only unless external access is specified.

review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Human Gly161 mutant study describes cytosolic apo-protein aggregation and degradation. It does not establish mitochondrial mistargeting as the mechanism for these variants. Exact wild-type localization images are outside the abstract. Local evidence is abstract-only unless external access is specified.

review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Human binary interactome study and Y2H methodology read. title: Immunocytochemical localization of human hepatic alanine: glyoxylate aminotransferase in control subjects and patients with primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Local evidence is abstract-only unless external access is specified.

title: Peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase deficiency in primary hyperoxaluria type I.
review_notes: Identifier and title match the cached PubMed record. Patient/control human liver activity and fractionation directly support loss of the peroxisomal AGXT pool in PH1. title: Evolution of alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase 1 peroxisomal and mitochondrial targeting. A survey of its subcellular distribution in the livers of various representatives of the classes Mammalia, Aves and Amphibia.

review_notes: Cached PubMed identifier/title/abstract and seeded ATXN1 interaction record inspected. The paper reports a yeast two-hybrid network with mammalian validation of a subset. AHDC1-specific full experiments were not recovered, so no pair-specific validation or mechanism is asserted. Generic binding is removed for lack of informative function, not because the interaction is disproven.

title: De novo truncating mutations in AHDC1 in individuals with syndromic expressive language delay, hypotonia, and sleep apnea.
review_notes: Cached PubMed metadata and full founding human genetic study inspected. Four unrelated probands carried de novo truncating AHDC1 variants and shared developmental features. The paper suggests escape from nonsense-mediated decay and possible dominant-negative effects; it does not experimentally establish haploinsufficiency as the unique molecular mechanism.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Cached PubMed identifier/title/abstract inspected; full primary author PDF independently read at https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/id/eprint/19322/1/19322oa.pdf (local /tmp/ACTA1-PMID32814053.txt). The paper uses Y2H and validates a selected subset by DULIP. Pair-specific orthogonal evidence for AHDC1-HTT or AHDC1-ATXN1 was not established here. The historical IntAct construct/submethod decomposition is retained in notes, without equating record counts with biological replicates or declaring the pairs false. The publication cache remains abstract-only.

title: Phenotypic and protein localization heterogeneity associated with AHDC1 pathogenic protein-truncating alleles in Xia-Gibbs syndrome.
review_notes: Cached PubMed metadata and full primary Results sections 3.3-3.4 inspected. Tagged wild-type and mutant human AHDC1 were imaged in HeLa and, for selected constructs, 293T cells. Wild-type nuclear foci and truncation-dependent changes are direct findings. In the coexpression assay, tested mutant proteins did not redirect wild-type localization; this does not settle all dominant-negative mechanisms.

title: 1,6-Hexanediol, commonly used to dissolve liquid-liquid phase separated condensates, directly impairs kinase and phosphatase activities.
review_notes: Cached PubMed metadata and full primary assay text inspected. This methodological study tests effects of 1,6-hexanediol on enzymes and model condensates; it does not assay AHDC1. Its concentration-dependent findings caution against assuming that the AHDC1 pretreatment selectively eliminates particular interactions or constitutes a condensate-specific control.

title: AHDC1 missense mutations in Xia-Gibbs syndrome.
review_notes: Cached PubMed metadata and full primary text inspected. Clinical and computational analyses identify candidate missense-variant clusters, including the AT-hook-2 region, with explicit limitations on functional interpretation. Clustering is not a biochemical DNA-binding assay, and gain-of-function/dominant-negative explanations are hypotheses.

title: Gibbin mesodermal regulation patterns epithelial development.
review_notes: Cached PubMed metadata and full primary Results, Methods, Discussion and extended-figure legends inspected. Human differentiation, tagged AHDC1 ChIP-seq, GATA3 epistasis, BASU proximity labeling, methylation arrays, CTCF ChIP and cohesin HiChIP support chromatin-associated transcriptional regulation; mouse mutagenesis supplies separate developmental evidence. BASU does not resolve direct binding pairs. The Discussion explicitly leaves direct DNMT regulation versus indirect transcriptional effects unresolved. The hESC ChIP used 5% 1,6-hexanediol for 60 seconds; consequences for individual AHDC1 interactions were not measured. GATA3 motif analysis must not be mistaken for an AHDC1 recognition assay.

title: AT-hook DNA-binding motif-containing protein one knockdown downregulates EWS-FLI1 transcriptional activity in Ewing's sarcoma cells.
review_notes: Primary PubMed record (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36194562/) and full PLOS article DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0269077 were independently verified on 2026-09-27. The normal fetch artifact recovered that day now supplies XML full text from PMC9531837. Figure 2 reports tagged/endogenous and endogenous co-immunoprecipitation; Figure 3 and the Figure S5 caption support transcriptional effects and regulatory-region occupancy in Ewing sarcoma cells. These corroborate complex-associated coregulation without isolating intrinsic sequence recognition. Discussion of cycloheximide and MG-132 experiments explicitly leaves the protein-stability mechanism unresolved. The recovered record corroborates the earlier external reading, with no change to annotation decisions or core synthesis.

title: Ahdc1 is a potent regulator of obesity and energy metabolism.
review_notes: Cached primary PubMed abstract explicitly describes an Ahdc1-deficient mouse model with obesity and altered energy expenditure. It supplies organismal context, not a demonstrated human biochemical mechanism. Full text was not recovered; no metabolic NEW is proposed from these phenotypes.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: The 13 original ISS assertions preserve mouse Q8K3E5. Historical MGI comparative GO records independently resolve the principal process and localization donors; each decision distinguishes the original source from additional human corroboration.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Two seeded IBA annotations descend from PTN002893387. The node is an ancestral source, not an irrelevant token. Experimental target evidence can legitimately seed its ancestor. The current PAINT slice was unavailable after a normal DNS-failed fetch; neither donor count nor UniProt review status is used as negative evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: The seeded HPA IDA records centrosomal immunofluorescence for human AHI1. Accept the curator-supplied source-level location without inventing a more precise compartment.

title: Jouberin localizes to collecting ducts and interacts with nephrocystin-1.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract supports endogenous/exogenous NPHP1 co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293 and identifies mouse mIMCD3 and canine MDCK localization systems. Host-cell species does not establish the species of an exogenous Jouberin construct. Original full methods were not recovered; human construct localization is independently corroborated by PMID:23532844.

title: AHI-1 interacts with BCR-ABL and modulates BCR-ABL transforming activity and imatinib response of CML stem/progenitor cells.
review_notes: Full cached study tests human CML cells and primitive progenitors as well as murine systems. AHI1–BCR-ABL–JAK2 complex association and signaling/TKI phenotypes are supported. Ternary co-recovery alone does not identify an AHI1-dependent bridge between BCR-ABL and JAK2.

title: Ahi1, whose human ortholog is mutated in Joubert syndrome, is required for Rab8a localization, ciliogenesis and vesicle trafficking.
review_notes: Full cached primary source explicitly uses mouse Ahi1 constructs, including in human HEK293 host cells. It directly establishes Rab8a stability/localization and selective vesicular-trafficking/ciliogenesis defects. Its ciliation results are context-specific, not proof that every Ahi1-null cell must lack cilia.

title: Impaired Wnt-beta-catenin signaling disrupts adult renal homeostasis and leads to cystic kidney ciliopathy.
review_notes: Full cached Results support Jouberin–beta-catenin association, nuclear accumulation and potentiation of stimulated Wnt reporter/endogenous cyclin D1 expression. Cilia remain in the tested knockout contexts. Supplementary construct-species details remain unresolved; no inference that a human host automatically means a human construct.

title: AHI1 is required for photoreceptor outer segment development and is a modifier for retinal degeneration in nephronophthisis.
review_notes: Full cached primary study separates early outer-segment/opsin defects from later photoreceptor apoptosis. Reduced opsin dosage delays death without restoring outer segments. This establishes causal context, not a logical disproof of a negative-regulation-of-apoptosis process.

title: Retinal degeneration and failure of photoreceptor outer segment formation in mice with targeted deletion of the Joubert syndrome gene, Ahi1.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract supports mouse photoreceptor outer-segment failure, mislocalized opsin and reduced Rab8a. Historical MGI records independently verify outer-segment and assembly donor annotations; abstract access does not resolve every assay detail.

title: Neuronal Abelson helper integration site-1 (Ahi1) deficiency in mice alters TrkB signaling with a depressive phenotype.

The original four mouse process donor links are verified in the MGI comparative graph. The exact Pol II transcription readout remains unresolved after the cached abstract and externally recovered Results inspected here and is not substituted with a kinase readout.

title: Subcellular spatial regulation of canonical Wnt signalling at the primary cilium.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract supports ciliary sequestration of Jouberin and limitation of beta-catenin nuclear signaling. Used at that stated scope; a title-based explanation of why prior pipelines omitted it is not evidence.

title: Defective Wnt-dependent cerebellar midline fusion in a mouse model of Joubert syndrome.
review_notes: Full cached primary study supports reduced mouse midline Wnt response and disease-variant effects in reporter/interaction assays. Human fetal imaging and variant numbering do not independently determine expression-construct species. Normal ciliation in cerebellar granule neurons is a cell-context result, not a universal contradiction of assembly phenotypes.

title: Modelling a ciliopathy: Ahi1 knockdown in model systems reveals an essential role in brain, retinal, and renal development.
review_notes: Full cached primary source uses mouse IMCD3 knockdown and zebrafish morpholinos with mouse-mRNA rescue of gross phenotypes. It supports ciliary biology including motile Kupffer's-vesicle cilia. The human IMP source-code provenance deserves curator review, while the biological assembly assertion is independently corroborated in human fibroblasts; this is not a wrong identifier or unsound paper.

title: A ciliopathy complex at the transition zone protects the cilia as a privileged membrane domain.
review_notes: Cached abstract plus independently consulted author full text support Ahi1 affinity recovery and co-fractionation within the transition-zone complex in mouse systems. Other-subunit perturbations establish complex organization/barrier properties. They do not invalidate structural participation by Ahi1, but exact AHI1-specific localization of other transition-zone proteins remains unresolved.

title: Molecular and structural characterization of the SH3 domain of AHI-1 in regulation of cellular resistance of BCR-ABL(+) chronic myeloid leukemia cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract supports AHI1-SH3/DNM2 interaction and effects of SH3 deletion on TKI response in BCR-ABL-positive cells. The solved SH3 structure and modeled PI3K-derived peptide do not constitute a solved AHI1–DNM2 complex. Generic-binding removal does not dispute the physical interaction.

title: The Joubert syndrome-associated missense mutation (V443D) in the Abelson-helper integration site 1 (AHI1) protein alters its localization and protein-protein interactions.
review_notes: Full cached primary source explicitly tests human AHI1 constructs and human Joubert fibroblasts. It supports basal-body/junction localization, altered ciliation and ARL13B, NPHP1/HAP1 interactions and self-association. Larger complex stoichiometries are tentative migration-based assignments, not direct molecular counts.

title: Cby1 promotes Ahi1 recruitment to a ring-shaped domain at the centriole-cilium interface and facilitates proper cilium formation and function.
review_notes: Full cached primary study provides superresolution Ahi1 ring localization, Cby1-dependent recruitment and Ahi1-depletion effects on ciliary ARL13B rescued with human AHI1. Ahi1 is the recruited protein in the Cby1 experiment; that observation alone does not make Ahi1 the recruiter of other transition-zone proteins.

title: Preferred SH3 domain partners of ADAM metalloproteases include shared and ADAM-specific SH3 interactions.
review_notes: Full cached primary source directly tests isolated SH3 domains against proline-rich ADAM tails by phage display and peptide arrays. The AHI1 result supports binding specificity; lack of a full-length cellular follow-up limits physiological interpretation rather than invalidating domain binding.

title: The Ciliopathy Gene ahi1 Is Required for Zebrafish Cone Photoreceptor Outer Segment Morphogenesis and Survival.
review_notes: The cached primary PubMed/PMC record was read on 2026-09-27. Methods, Results and Figures 9–10 confirm TALEN-mutant zebrafish, preserved photoreceptor connecting cilia and Cc2d2a/Cep290 localization, with reduced Cc2d2a staining intensity. Wild-type human AHI1 RNA rescues distal pronephric cilia and cone outer-segment phenotypes; the tested human R589X RNA does not. This confirms the previously external primary result and closes its cache gate. It is human-construct rescue in zebrafish, not a native human motile-cell assay. The paper does not establish that AHI1 is unnecessary for every transition-zone substrate or tissue.

title: Missense mutations in the WD40 domain of AHI1 cause non-syndromic retinitis pigmentosa.
review_notes: Read the genuine cached PubMed/PMC5574394 full record on 2026-09-27: cDNA constructs and immunocytochemistry Methods, Results Figures 4–5 and Discussion. The synthetic human isoform 1 accession AM393493 was adapted to reference NM001134831.1, and resulting wild-type/variant sequences were Sanger-validated. N-terminal mRFP constructs were expressed in human hTERT-RPE1 cells; full-length fusion expression was checked in HEK293T. Direct human localization and mutant enrichment measurements support the ciliary-base synthesis. Preserved ciliation in the tested RPE1 and patient-fibroblast comparisons does not imply all AHI1 alleles or tissues retain function; the proposed molecular explanation for RP-versus-Joubert differences remains a hypothesis. Cache identity/title and full-text metadata are preserved exactly; original cache-recovery provenance is recorded in the notes.

title: Ahi1 promotes Arl13b ciliary recruitment, regulates Arl13b stability and is required for normal cell migration.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract supports mouse-fibroblast ARL13B recruitment/stability and altered cilia length/composition. It is corroboration of cargo biology, not a direct human experiment.

title: The Transition Zone Protein AHI1 Regulates Neuronal Ciliary Trafficking of MCHR1 and Its Downstream Signaling Pathway.
review_notes: Full cached mouse-neuron study measures loss of ciliary MCHR1 despite preserved total and surface receptor levels, and altered cAMP/ERK responses. This distinguishes ciliary targeting from global receptor synthesis or plasma-membrane delivery.

title: Depression compromises antiviral innate immunity via the AVP-AHI1-Tyk2 axis.
review_notes: Full cached primary study supports AHI1-dependent OTUD1–Tyk2 association in knockout mouse macrophages and human A549 corroboration. Figure 4C specifies RAW264.7 for the endogenous interaction panel, whereas Figure 4G provides the primary-macrophage dependency assay. This is adaptor activity, not AHI1 deubiquitinase catalysis or a ciliary bridging experiment.

title: Ciliopathy-associated protein, CEP290, is required for ciliary necklace and outer segment membrane formation in retinal photoreceptors.
review_notes: Primary PubMed and PMC records confirm the title, DOI and bioRxiv preprint identity. The cached Methods and Results distinguish global Cep290 knockout/near-null mice and wild-type controls from a separate human retinal sample from one subject. AHI1 and NPHP1 distributions were measured by superresolution fluorescence in mouse photoreceptors; the human imaging examines CEP290 and RPGR. No AHI1 perturbation or human AHI1 recruitment mechanism is inferred. Full-text sections are present, with duplicated extraction paragraphs; availability does not imply peer review. This source does not resolve the existing transition-zone recruitment uncertainty.

title: RAB3IP stimulates nucleotide exchange on RAB8A
review_notes: Cached reaction identity and the independently inspected live AHI1-containing participant are consistent with the seeded cytosol TAS. This compartment assertion does not make AHI1 the catalytic actor of the named reaction. RAB3IP is the exchange factor acting on RAB8A.

title: Recruitment of transition zone proteins
review_notes: Cached reaction identity and the independently inspected live AHI1-containing participant are consistent with the seeded cytosol TAS. This compartment assertion does not make AHI1 the catalytic actor of the named reaction. The event recruits transition-zone assemblies.

title: CEP164 recruits RAB3IP-carrying Golgi-derived vesicles to the basal body
review_notes: Cached reaction identity and the independently inspected live AHI1-containing participant are consistent with the seeded cytosol TAS. This compartment assertion does not make AHI1 the catalytic actor of the named reaction. The event concerns CEP164-dependent vesicle recruitment.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AHI1 (human)
review_notes: Genuine existing affinage output is preserved unchanged and used as a lead, not primary evidence. Its incorrectly PMID-shaped bioRxiv identifier resolves to the real CEP290 preprint PMID:39896654 (DOI 10.1101/2025.01.20.633784), identified through the primary PubMed/PMC pages and now read in the normal cached Methods and Results. The AHI1 localization experiment uses CEP290-mutant mouse retina; separate human retinal imaging concerns CEP290 and RPGR. It does not establish the converse AHI1-dependent recruitment mechanism. The other fourteen cited publications and five broad Reactome summaries are now cached and individually assessed in the notes. The report omits the established beta-catenin/Wnt literature. No provider-generated sentence substitutes for primary evidence; the recovered paper remains a preprint.

title: A human gene (AHNAK) encoding an unusually large protein with a 1.2-microns polyionic rod structure.
review_notes: The gene's founding paper, correctly cited for the nuclear NAS. PubMed records an erratum for it with no PMID in the record, so the erratum's scope could not be established; the nuclear localisation it is cited for was reproduced independently (PMID:8381120).

title: AHNAK1 and AHNAK2 are costameric proteins: AHNAK1 affects transverse skeletal muscle fiber stiffness.
review_notes: The source of the costamere IDA and the elasticity IMP that reach human AHNAK by projection, and also the only published test of AHNAK in plasma membrane repair, which was negative. Both results are in the abstract and both are used here.

title: Self-regulated alternative splicing at the AHNAK locus.
review_notes: Correctly cited for GO:0043484 and for the IDA localisation rows. Flagged here because UniProt/CAFA used it as the reference for all five ISS rows on this gene, including GO:0043034 costamere and GO:0097493 elasticity, whose donor evidence is in PMID:20833135 instead. The paper itself is sound; the block referencing is not.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Correctly cited for GO:0003723. The paper's own caveat - that the HeLa mRNA interactome is enriched for highly disordered, repeat-rich proteins - describes AHNAK precisely, and no orthogonal evidence for AHNAK RNA binding exists.

title: Structure of an asymmetric ternary protein complex provides insight for membrane interaction.
review_notes: The paper is correctly identified and is a genuine, important AHNAK structure (3.5 A, S100A10/annexin A2/AHNAK ternary complex, ~30 nM). It is miscited for the annotation that uses it: GO:1905686 positive regulation of plasma membrane repair. Membrane repair appears only in the paper's framing sentence; no repair experiment is performed. The row is one of ten identical NAS annotations that ComplexPortal attached to four complexes and six proteins from this single reference.

title: The submembranous location of p11 and its interaction with the p36 substrate of pp60 src kinase in situ.
review_notes: Osborn et al. 1988 concerns p11 and p36 (S100A10 and annexin A2) and contains no AHNAK experiment - it could not, since the AHNAK gene was first reported in 1992 (PMID:1608957). It supports GO:0005886 for its actual subjects and reaches AHNAK only as a ComplexPortal complex-to-subunit projection across eight entities. The plasma membrane term is correct for AHNAK on other evidence.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: A sound systematic study, correctly cited. Recorded here because it is the single source of eight of AHNAK's twenty-six GO:0005515 rows: IntAct holds 415 AHNAK records from it, all by holdup assay between AHNAK's isolated PDZ domain and synthetic C-terminal decapeptides. Carries an unflagged 2022 Author Correction (PMID:36477203) whose scope could not be established from the cached record.

title: Systematic identification of post-transcriptional regulatory modules.
review_notes: A proximity-labelling screen correctly cited for a U2AF2 interaction row. Carries an unflagged 2024 Author Correction (PMID:39468017); the annotation it supports is kept as non-core regardless.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AHNAK (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched external LLM-generated record, listed so its assessment is on the record. Its trust gates passed and all 45 citations are numeric PubMed ids; spot checks against the cached papers found the narrative accurate, with one slip - it describes PMID:26466345 as BMP2-driven where the paper reports BMP4/SMAD1. It supplied the decisive reference of this review, PMID:20833135, which appears nowhere in AHNAK's GOA reference set. Per campaign policy no sentence of it is quoted as supporting_text: every claim it contributed was re-grounded on the primary paper, which is why no annotation cites this file.

title: UniProt entry Q09666 (AHNK_HUMAN) as downloaded for this review
review_notes: Quoted for the SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and SUBUNIT lines. Note the entry's FUNCTION line reads only 'May be required for neuronal cell differentiation', which is a much narrower statement than the entry's own reference list and the wider literature support; that gap is raised in suggested_questions.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The GO_REF itself is sound; the per-row assessment is in each annotation's propagation_review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The pipeline did what it says; the defect is in the UniProt statement it consumed.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Reliability tier confirmed directly against the HPA API for AHNAK2 (ENSG00000185567) rather than assumed.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: The terms are right and independently supported by IDA, but the rule provenance could not be reproduced from the public rule definitions, so this is recorded as unverified rather than verified.

title: The AHNAKs are a class of giant propeller-like proteins that associate with calcium channel proteins of cardiomyocytes and other cells.
review_notes: Read specifically to test whether the T-tubule row could be removed. It could not: this paper is independent T-tubule evidence for AHNAK2 in a tissue the contrary study did not examine, which is why that row is marked over-annotated rather than removed. Mouse Ahnak2 holds GO:0030018 and GO:0030659 by IDA from this paper.

title: AHNAK, a novel component of the dysferlin protein complex, redistributes to the cytoplasm with dysferlin during skeletal muscle regeneration.
review_notes: The identifier and title are correct and the paper is genuinely the source of five AHNAK2 rows. Its abstract, which is all that is publicly available (Europe PMC inEPMC:N, hasPDF:N), reports only AHNAK. UniProt's AHNAK2 entry nevertheless carries the DYSF interaction at ECO:0000269|PubMed:17185750, so a curator with the full text did find AHNAK2 data; the DYSF row is therefore kept and the MYOF row, which UniProt did not carry across, is left UNDECIDED. Not marked MISCITED: the citation is not wrong, it is unverifiable at the level of detail the rows assert.

title: AHNAK1 and AHNAK2 are costameric proteins: AHNAK1 affects transverse skeletal muscle fiber stiffness.
review_notes: Source of the costamere proposal. One caution recorded because the affinage record got it wrong: the abstract says "no AHNAK expression was detected in the T-tubule system", not "no AHNAK2 expression". The paper concerns both proteins and calls them AHNAK1 and AHNAK2, so the generic usage plausibly covers both, but the stronger paraphrase is not what is written and is not relied on here.

title: Self-regulated alternative splicing at the AHNAK locus.
review_notes: Read because it is the single donor-evidence paper behind the splicing IBA. It produced 17 GO annotations over exactly two entities, mouse Ahnak and human AHNAK, and none on AHNAK2. The transfer the curator chose was one species step within one gene - mouse Ahnak IDA to human AHNAK ISS - and they did not extend it to AHNAK2 or to PRX. PAINT did. The same paper is also where human AHNAK acquired GO:0043034 costamere by ISS.

title: Periaxin and AHNAK nucleoprotein 2 form intertwined homodimers through domain swapping.
review_notes: The single most informative paper about human AHNAK2's molecular function, and the source of the GO:0042803 proposal. PDB accession and resolution cross-checked against the UniProt cross-reference line. Note for anyone citing it downstream: it reports a homodimer of periaxin and a homodimer of AHNAK2, not an AHNAK2-periaxin heterodimer, and AHNAK is not in the structure.

title: AHNAK2 Participates in the Stress-Induced Nonclassical FGF1 Secretion Pathway.
review_notes: The only loss-of-function study of AHNAK2 outside cancer cell lines, and it produced no GO annotation anywhere. Full text read; the methods are what determined the ISS and IPI evidence codes rather than IMP and IDA.

title: Linkage analysis and whole exome sequencing reveals AHNAK2 as a novel genetic cause for autosomal recessive CMT in a Malaysian family.
review_notes: The genetic finding is sound and correctly cited. The disputed element is the background claim that AHNAK2 binds directly to periaxin: a Europe PMC search for AHNAK2 and periaxin returns nothing earlier than PMID:24675079, which reports domain-swapped homodimers of each protein separately rather than a heterodimer. No annotation in this review rests on the interaction claim; it is raised in suggested_questions instead. Separately, the affinage record describes these as compound heterozygous variants, whereas the abstract describes a consanguineous autosomal recessive family - not load-bearing, but noted.

title: The Obscure Potential of AHNAK2.
review_notes: Never used as evidence for an annotation. Its NLS claim for AHNAK2 sits in a paragraph the authors frame as hypothesis from similarity to AHNAK, and UniProt annotates no MOTIF or NLS feature on Q8IVF2, so it is not used here.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Pipeline reference. Verified by retrieving the IPR015317 block from the EBI interpro2go file; the signature is orthogroup-specific rather than fold-level, which is why these IEAs are accepted rather than discounted.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The cleanest PAINT set encountered in this campaign. Donor identity, donor evidence and term level were each checked at QuickGO (13 annotations returned, numberOfHits equal to the number of results, so not truncated). PTHR15914 has one subfamily and no human paralogue, so no propagation_review is warranted on any row.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Pipeline reference; its mouse source is the same orthologue as the IBA rows and holds cytoplasm by its own IDA.

title: An abundant erythroid protein that stabilizes free alpha-haemoglobin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the source of eight annotations across two species (QuickGO reference scan: 8 annotations over 2 distinct entities - human AHSP and mouse Ahsp - so not a ComplexPortal-style projection). Its abstract refutes the GO:0005833 NAS row that cites it, which is the basis for that REMOVE. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern.

title: Biophysical characterization of the alpha-globin binding protein alpha-hemoglobin stabilizing protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Missed by the affinage report despite supplying the stoichiometry that the proposed complex term rests on.

title: NMR structure of the alpha-hemoglobin stabilizing protein: insights into conformational heterogeneity and binding.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; solution structure of free AHSP (PDB 1W09, 1W0A, 1W0B), cited here as part of the structural record rather than for any specific annotation. Missed by affinage.

title: Molecular mechanism of AHSP-mediated stabilization of alpha-hemoglobin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. A co-crystal structure, which is why the GO:0005515 row citing it cannot be left as bare protein binding.

title: Structure of oxidized alpha-haemoglobin bound to AHSP reveals a protective mechanism for haem.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The structural rearrangement it reports is also the evidence that AHSP's client is folded rather than unfolded, which is what excludes GO:0140309.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. A CCSB yeast two-hybrid screen; supports one screen-level row (ZC3H12A) with no orthogonal method and no biological context.

title: Biochemical fates of alpha hemoglobin bound to alpha hemoglobin-stabilizing protein AHSP.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes that the endpoint of AHSP binding is delivery to beta-globin rather than sequestration, which is why GO:0140313 molecular sequestering activity is the wrong framing.

title: Reduction of AHSP synthesis in hemin-induced K562 cells and EPO-induced CD34(+) cells leads to alpha-globin precipitation, impairment of normal hemoglobin production, and increased cell death.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The one human loss-of-function study on this gene; used deliberately because the abundant knockout literature is murine and would only license ISS or ISO.

title: A cis-proline in alpha-hemoglobin stabilizing protein directs the structural reorganization of alpha-hemoglobin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached, no retraction or erratum. Found only by recounting the co-crystal structures from PDBe (which entries map both Q9NZD4 and P69905) rather than reading UniProt's reference labels - it is absent from UniProt's RN list, absent from GOA, and absent from the affinage report, despite being a crystal structure of the complex plus the mutagenesis establishing the Pro30 mechanism.

title: AHSP (α-haemoglobin-stabilizing protein) stabilizes apo-α-haemoglobin in a partially folded state.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. The single most important reference for the ontology question, because it shows AHSP's client is neither unfolded nor natively folded, which is exactly the state GO's two chaperone MF terms do not cover.

title: Kinetics of α-globin binding to α-hemoglobin stabilizing protein (AHSP) indicate preferential stabilization of hemichrome folding intermediate.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Kinetic measurements showing the ferric complex dissociates about 100-fold more slowly than the ferrous one, so AHSP preferentially traps the oxidized intermediate; cited as mechanistic context rather than behind a specific annotation.

title: α-Hemoglobin stabilizing protein (AHSP) markedly decreases the redox potential and reactivity of α-subunits of human HbA with hydrogen peroxide.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Quantitative, human, purified-component evidence for the redox arm; the anchor reference for the proposed GO:1903427 row.

title: HSP70 sequestration by free α-globin promotes ineffective erythropoiesis in β-thalassaemia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The cached record is abstract-only and its abstract concerns HSP70, not AHSP; the AHSP-alpha-globin datum it supports is a bio-layer interferometry measurement curated in IntAct (EBI-16247582, typed "direct interaction", MI-score 0.71). Per CLAUDE.md this is not treated as a mis-attribution - the curator read a full text that is not in the cache.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supplies three screen-level rows (FKBP1A, UBE3A isoform 2, ZC3H12A). IntAct logs each partner three times as "two hybrid array", "two hybrid prey pooling approach" and "validated two hybrid" - three sub-methods of one screen, which is what UniProt's NbExp=3 counts.

title: Oxidative instability of hemoglobin E (β26 Glu→Lys) is increased in the presence of free α subunits and reversed by α-hemoglobin stabilizing protein (AHSP): Relevance to HbE/β-thalassemia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Supporting evidence for the proposed ROS row; also the clearest statement that the protection is a property of the bound client's haem, not of AHSP itself, which is the argument against GO:0016209.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The HuRI screen; supplies four screen-level rows (ZNF20, PSMB1, CLVS1, VPS9D1), each logged as three sub-methods of one experiment at MI-score 0.56.

title: Stage Specific Expression Pattern of Alpha-Hemoglobin-Stabilizing-Protein (AHSP) Portrayed in Erythroblast Chronology.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as a citation, but the nuclear localisation claim itself is marked UNVERIFIED rather than accepted: it is a single antibody-based imaging study from one laboratory, AHSP has no NLS and at 11.8 kDa can enter the nucleus passively, and every measured activity of the protein is on a cytoplasmic ligand. Recorded as a knowledge gap and a suggested experiment rather than carried into a GO:0005634 annotation.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Carries an unflagged Publisher Correction (PMID:41039152) found by reading CommentsCorrections/RefType on the article's own record; the correction's scope was read rather than assumed and it concerns a duplicated equation in the Methods, not the interaction data. QuickGO returns 3026 annotations for this reference, which paginates beyond a readable limit, so its distinct-entity count is unavailable and no projection test was run on it - stated rather than estimated from a single page.

title: Publisher Correction: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Cited only to record that the erratum on PMID:40205054 was located and its scope read.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro-to-GO method source. The exact source domain IDs are retained; target biochemistry determines reaction specificity.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT ancestral inference method. Each IBA is traced to its PTN node; full IBD/tree evidence was not recovered, and target-in-WITH is not treated as circular.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt location-vocabulary mapping method, corroborated with independent AID localization evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of intracellular localizations of expressed fusion proteins in living cells
review_notes: Fusion-protein localization curation method; original individual image not re-inspected, with broad cytoplasmic location independently corroborated.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA inference method, not an experimental publication. Specific rule predicates remain uninspected.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined electronic methods. Source entities are assessed separately and independent human evidence is distinguished from a recovered donor chain.

title: Specific expression of activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID), a novel member of the RNA-editing deaminase family in germinal center B cells.
review_notes: The cached abstract matches the primary PubMed identity. The recovered abstract explicitly describes murine CH12F3-2 discovery, positive GST-AID free-cytidine deaminase activity, zinc-chelation inhibition, and negative apoB RNA-editing/AU-rich RNA-binding tests. The previously inspected indexed original Results remain external; the local record is abstract-only. An RNA-editing-family name alone does not identify an endogenous AID RNA target.

title: Isolation, tissue distribution, and chromosomal localization of the human activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) gene.
Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) deficiency causes the autosomal recessive form of the Hyper-IgM syndrome (HIGM2).
Activation-induced cytidine deaminase deaminates deoxycytidine on single-stranded DNA but requires the action of RNase.
review_notes: The cached abstract matches the primary PMC153055 identity. The local abstract supports ssDNA deamination and acknowledges free-deoxycytidine activity. Original public Methods/Results, inspected externally, establish the human Ramos-derived GST-AID/Sf9 construct and Figure 4b free-nucleoside assay. The exact short Results excerpt is in the annotation reasons with its public URL; ordinary supporting_text quotes the cached abstract. Full text remains unavailable in the local record.

title: Activation-induced cytidine deaminase shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm like apolipoprotein B mRNA editing catalytic polypeptide 1.
PKA-mediated phosphorylation regulates the function of activation-induced deaminase (AID) in B cells.
Interaction between antibody-diversification enzyme AID and spliceosome-associated factor CTNNBL1.
AID can restrict L1 retrotransposition suggesting a dual role in innate and adaptive immunity.
review_notes: The full-text extraction matches primary PMC2665220. Actual Methods/Results include human AID NM_020661.1 among eight vertebrate cDNAs; L1 restriction is independent of cytidine deaminase activity. Mobile-element restriction is distinguished from infectious retrovirus restriction. Main-text extraction contains repeated sections and does not establish complete supplementary availability.

title: Active nuclear import and cytoplasmic retention of activation-induced deaminase.
Speckled-like pattern in the germinal center (SLIP-GC), a nuclear GTPase expressed in activation-induced deaminase-expressing lymphomas and germinal center B cells.
The RNA exosome targets the AID cytidine deaminase to both strands of transcribed duplex DNA substrates.
CTNNBL1 is a novel nuclear localization sequence-binding protein that recognizes RNA-splicing factors CDC5L and Prp31.
Hydroxylation of 5-methylcytosine by TET1 promotes active DNA demethylation in the adult brain.
Histone chaperone Spt6 is required for class switch recombination but not somatic hypermutation.
Thymine DNA glycosylase is essential for active DNA demethylation by linked deamination-base excision repair.
Optimal functional levels of activation-induced deaminase specifically require the Hsp40 DnaJa1.
Solubility-based genetic screen identifies RING finger protein 126 as an E3 ligase for activation-induced cytidine deaminase.
RNA editing of hepatitis B virus transcripts by activation-induced cytidine deaminase.
review_notes: The cached abstract matches primary PMC3568302 and supports nucleocapsid RNA editing. Public original Results inspected externally identify the unfused human AID vector and distinguish parallel human/mouse AID-ER assays, with polymerase/RNase-H and immunoprecipitation controls. The human-vector excerpt is in the annotation reason with its public URL; the ordinary supporting quote is verbatim from the local abstract. This contextual viral result does not establish physiological immunoglobulin RNA editing.

title: Non-coding RNA Generated following Lariat Debranching Mediates Targeting of AID to DNA.
review_notes: The full-text extraction matches primary PMC4426339; its fetched title capitalization is retained exactly. Actual Methods/Results use mouse CH12 cells and purified MBP-tagged mouse AID, with G133V RNA-binding/class-switching rescue experiments. Human patient genetics motivates the study but does not turn these experiments into direct human protein assays. Main text is available locally; complete supplements are not asserted.

title: TGF-β triggers HBV cccDNA degradation through AID-dependent deamination.
AID Recognizes Structured DNA for Class Switch Recombination.
review_notes: The full-text extraction matches primary PMC5771415. Actual Results/Methods distinguish engineered soluble human AID constructs for biochemistry from full-length untagged internal mutants used for class-switching rescue in mouse splenic B cells. Positive G4-dependent cooperative oligomerization is also explicit in the cached abstract and attached to the self-binding row as ordinary supporting_text. The experiments do not establish a fixed native homodimer.

title: Disease-associated CTNNBL1 mutation impairs somatic hypermutation by decreasing nuclear AID.
Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Method identity is fixed by the seeded GO_REF. InterPro redox/dimerization mappings are supported; target chemistry is refined without alleging family misclassification.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Seeded curated ortholog-transfer method; Q9Z0X1 is mouse Aifm1. Original PMID:21467298/18056262 distinguish protein species from cell hosts. Nuclear/cytosolic/PAR/ER-stress transfers are bounded; necroptosis mechanism is unresolved.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Seeded PAINT method/PTN nodes preserved. Reviewer source entities name ancestral nodes, not donor votes. Human target grounding is legitimate; peroxide-product evidence remains unresolved, not a demonstrated node-placement failure.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mapped SL identifiers and source locations are explicit in seeded annotations/UniProt. Mitochondrial/nuclear sites and stimulus/isoform-specific cytoplasmic pools are distinguished without replacing source CC resolution.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: The seeded source identifies curated immunofluorescence. Original image not recovered; independent human topology supports mitochondrion without claiming image-level subcompartment verification.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Seeded Compara method; rat donor identity checked via NCBI Gene83533. Specific source response experiments remain untraced. H2O2 response has independent target support; other contexts remain unresolved.

title: Automatic Gene Ontology annotation based on Rhea mapping
review_notes: Seeded Rhea method and RHEA:11356 match the human UniProt reaction A + NADH + H(+) = AH2 + NAD(+): generic acceptor reduction, not a proton pump.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: The broad ARBA positive-death assertion has human target corroboration. Exact rule conditions were not independently reconstructed; no rule-scoping defect is asserted.

title: Export of mitochondrial AIF in response to proapoptotic stimuli depends on processing at the intermembrane space.
review_notes: Full cached primary Results/Methods read: HeLa endogenous/tagged AIF and rat mitochondrial preparations establish topology, processing and redistribution. Matrix-facing N-terminal exposure is not matrix catalytic localization.

title: AIFsh, a novel apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) pro-apoptotic isoform with potential pathological relevance in human cancer.
review_notes: Cached primary identifier/DOI/abstract read. AIFsh is a short cytosolic product with nuclear redistribution/death on HeLa overexpression. Full body not recovered; explicit isoform scope preserved.

title: Identification and characterization of AIFsh2, a mitochondrial apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) isoform with NADH oxidase activity.
review_notes: Cached primary identifier/DOI/abstract read. AIFsh2 is mitochondrial and redox-active but lacks nuclear death activity. Reactive-oxygen-species language does not identify peroxide as the product.

title: A protein-protein interaction network for human inherited ataxias and disorders of Purkinje cell degeneration.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity/abstract verified. Network methodology is described; individual TSC22D4 pair not independently recovered. Generic-term removal does not imply a false interaction.

title: Apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) inhibits protein synthesis by interacting with the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit p44 (eIF3g).
review_notes: Official PubMed abstract verified. Binding, functional translation inhibition and competitive EIF3G rescue support the specific MF refinement. Full images were inaccessible; UniProt records source-linked nuclear/perinuclear localization.

title: Scythe regulates apoptosis-inducing factor stability during endoplasmic reticulum stress-induced apoptosis.
review_notes: Source14 recovered the unchanged normal abstract cache. PubMed identity and the previously inspected author-uploaded original full text support human AIF constructs in mouse fibroblast thapsigargin/Scythe experiments, with separate human-cell interaction steps. The abstract does not itself resolve these construct details; local full text remains unavailable.

title: No death without life: vital functions of apoptotic effectors.
review_notes: Original PMC2917777 identity and indexed AIF/Table2 text checked externally. Local cache is abstract-only. IMM/apoptosis support is distinct from unresolved peroxide-product specificity.

title: Apoptosis-inducing factor plays a critical role in caspase-independent, pyknotic cell death in hydrogen peroxide-exposed cells.
review_notes: Source14 recovered the unchanged normal abstract cache. Official PubMed identity and abstract support glucose-oxidase-generated H2O2, AIF perturbation, nuclear redistribution and stimulus-dependent death. Human UniProt explicitly links this study to target function; the exact rat donor chain remains untraced. The full body remains unavailable; this is a response to peroxide, not proof of peroxide synthesis by AIF.

title: A brain-specific isoform of mitochondrial apoptosis-inducing factor: AIF2.
review_notes: Cached primary identity/abstract read. Alternative-exon-2b AIF2 (UniProt O95831-3) and AIF1 have different membrane retention but shared IMS orientation. AIF2 is not the newer exon-skipping AIF3 product.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: Human muscle mitochondrial-proteomics source read. Metadata full_text_available is true but body extraction is partial and target supplement entry uninspected. This access limit does not turn an accessible partial body into no full text.

title: Vital function of PRELI and essential requirement of its LEA motif.
review_notes: Original indexed PMC3032331 Figure6/co-IP Methods inspected externally. AIF association with PRELI and LEA-deleted PRELI is real; PRELI protection is not transferred to AIF. Local cache remains abstract-only.

title: Poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR) binding to apoptosis-inducing factor is critical for PAR polymerase-1-dependent cell death (parthanatos).
review_notes: Source14 recovered the unchanged normal PMC3086524 full-text cache; Results and Methods were read. Purified mouse AIF, mouse constructs expressed in HeLa, and mouse neuronal rescue remain distinct. PAR-binding mutations impair release and parthanatos while preserving other assayed properties. This does not resolve RIPK/MLKL necroptosis or identify peroxide as a redox product. Primary identity remains verified.

title: Comprehensive proteomic analysis of influenza virus polymerase complex reveals a novel association with mitochondrial proteins and RNA polymerase accessory factors.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity/abstract verified. Human AIFM1 is expressly identified among influenza PA-associated proteins; possible apoptotic consequences are proposed. Local cache remains abstract-only.

title: Steroid receptor coactivator-interacting protein (SIP) inhibits caspase-independent apoptosis by preventing apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) from being released from mitochondria.
review_notes: Original indexed PMC3339961 Figures2-5/Results inspected: reciprocal HeLa co-IP, GST/in-vitro-translated AIF binding and U2OS perturbation show KANK2/SIP regulation of release. Local cache remains abstract-only.

title: Cowchock syndrome is associated with a mutation in apoptosis-inducing factor.
review_notes: Full original Milan author PDF read: recombinant human WT/E493V acceptor-reduction Table1, DNA-retardation Figure3E and human patient/cell results. Oxygen-dependent flavin reoxidation is not a peroxide-product measurement. Local cache is abstract-only.

title: Structural insights into the coenzyme mediated monomer-dimer transition of the pro-apoptotic apoptosis inducing factor.
review_notes: Cached primary identifier/DOI/abstract read: explicit human protein, coenzyme/FAD occupancy, dimer-interface mutants and solution binding. Full body not independently recovered; physiological acceptor not inferred.

title: Interaction between AIF and CHCHD4 Regulates Respiratory Chain Biogenesis.
review_notes: Full original Glasgow author manuscript inspected. Human interactions, mouse stem-cell loss/rescue and engineered import bypass are distinguished. Import support is established; exact respiratory-assembly placement unresolved. Local cache is abstract-only.

title: Structure/Function Relations in AIFM1 Variants Associated with Neurodegenerative Disorders.
review_notes: Primary identifier/abstract and publisher introduction verified. Human variant redox/FAD/NADH evidence is explicit; full peroxide assay not recovered. DNA binding is curated and corroborated by separate full human assays. Identity correctness does not settle every term.

title: The 89-kDa PARP1 cleavage fragment serves as a cytoplasmic PAR carrier to induce AIF-mediated apoptosis.
review_notes: Full cached Results/Methods read: HeLa caspase-activated PARP1 cleavage produces PAR-bearing fragments engaging AIF. This tested apoptosis route is distinct from a universal caspase-independent claim.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Full cached BioPlex methodology read. AP-MS in human293T/HCT116 establishes association; KANK2 supplementary pair not independently reconstructed. Direct binary binding is not inferred from AP-MS alone.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Full cached mitochondrial-proteome methodology read. Orthogonal human-cell approaches support MitoCoP. Target supplement details uninspected; source organelle resolution retained.

title: AIFM1 beyond cell death: An overview of this OXPHOS-inducing factor in mitochondrial diseases.
review_notes: Full cached review read, including CHCHD4/import, respiratory consequences and redox uncertainty. Secondary synthesis is not primary replication; newer human activation evidence is separated.

title: NADH-bound AIF activates the mitochondrial CHCHD4/MIA40 chaperone by a substrate-mimicry mechanism.
review_notes: Full cached original read. Engineered human structures have solution/mutant/cellular/folding corroboration. AIF anchors/activates CHCHD4; CHCHD4/ALR catalyze relay chemistry. Figure5 peroxide is from relay regeneration, not an AIF peroxide assay.

title: AIF3 splicing variant elicits mitochondrial malfunction via the concurrent dysregulation of electron transport chain and glutathione-redox homeostasis.
review_notes: Source14 recovered unchanged normal PMC11842818 full text. Results, Methods and the official supplement were inspected. Methods includes human AIF/truncated AIF in pGEX-6p-1, mouse AIF/AIF3 cellular constructs, and Figure 6n explicitly labels purified mouse AIF mutants. The supplement does not resolve species for every purified-protein panel; the former blanket mouse-only description is too broad. Figures 6h-i report purified-protein glutathione-reductase activity, distinct from mouse-cell rescue and human tissue/splicing observations. The physiological human contribution remains a question without a new enzyme assertion. Exon-2/3-skipping AIF3 is not UniProt O95831-3 AIF2.

title: Molecular characterization of mitochondrial apoptosis-inducing factor.
review_notes: Cached primary identifier/DOI/abstract read: confinement, translocation and chromatin effects. Later human localization corroborates the CCs; isolated-nucleus fragmentation is not intrinsic nuclease evidence.

title: UniProtKB O95831 (AIFM1_HUMAN): apoptosis-inducing factor 1, mitochondrial
review_notes: The human seed machine record was read directly for six alternative products, catalytic reaction and source-linked location/interaction identities. This is curated synthesis, not a primary experiment.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go route applied here uses IPR006838, the family-specific ADTRP/AIG1 entry integrated with PANTHER PTHR10989 and Pfam PF04750, and maps it to a cellular component only. Appropriately restrained for an entry spanning thousands of unstudied proteins.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT methodology is sound and correctly cited; the defect found on the GO:0016787 row is a GOA ingest lag, not a problem with this reference. Verified by reading PANTHER's current IBD.gaf and leaf GAF directly rather than by reading the node's terms off GOA's own WITH/FROM column.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The mapping route is correct and names its source (SL-0039). The problem with the resulting plasma-membrane row is in the UniProt statement being mapped, not in this reference.

title: Automatic Gene Ontology annotation based on Rhea mapping
review_notes: Twelve RHEA reactions in the WITH/FROM field, matching the twelve GO:0120573 RHEA cross-references and the twelve UniProt CATALYTIC ACTIVITY lines one for one, each of the latter carrying ECO:0000269|PubMed:27018888.

title: Cloning of androgen-inducible gene 1 (AIG1) from human dermal papilla cells.
review_notes: Cited as the origin of the gene name, not as evidence of function. Induction by a hormone is an expression observation and is neither a molecular function nor a biological process; GOA correctly carries no annotation from this paper.

title: AIG1 is a novel Pirh2-interacting protein that activates the NFAT signaling pathway.
review_notes: Two reservations, so nothing in this review rests on it. First, the abstract is internally inconsistent: it reads 'identified a novel Pirh2-interacting protein, AIG1, by yeast two-hybrid screening and confirmed its interaction with p53 both in vitro and in vivo', which literally attributes the confirmation to an AIG1-p53 interaction rather than to AIG1-Pirh2; the full text is not cached. Second, it shares an author with PMID:21988832 and is from the same institution, so the two yeast two-hybrid reports are not independent screens. Its HCC survival analysis is a biomarker correlation and is not treated as evidence of function.

title: Novel protein ADTRP regulates TFPI expression and function in human endothelial cells in normal conditions and in response to androgen.
review_notes: Cited for the paralogue rather than for AIG1, but load-bearing here: the whole AIG1-versus-ADTRP divergence on GO:0005886 rests on ADTRP having surface evidence that AIG1 does not. Checked rather than relayed from the merged ADTRP review - the cached record contains the colocalisation sentence quoted above plus one occurrence each of 'lipid raft', 'triton' and 'x-114'. It says nothing about AIG1 and is not used to support any AIG1 annotation.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: Erratum check fired here: the PubMed record carries ErratumIn PMID:29254952. It was read - the correction is to a misspelled author name only, with no data change, so the interaction row is unaffected. Reference projection check: QuickGO reports 756 annotations for this reference and the result is paginated, so the entity count is unavailable and was not substituted with a single-page total; the paper is plainly a systematic interactome.

title: AIG1 and ADTRP are atypical integral membrane hydrolases that degrade bioactive FAHFAs.
review_notes: The defining paper for this gene and the source of every experimental annotation on it. Full text cached and read in full. No retraction, erratum or expression of concern on the PubMed record. Reference projection check is negative: QuickGO returns eight annotations over exactly two entities, Q9NVV5 and Q96IZ2, so this is per-protein curation of the two proteins the paper characterises rather than a distribution across a set. One limitation, which is the basis of the two plasma-membrane verdicts: the paper contains no localisation experiment, so the GO:0005886 rows attributed to it are not supported by it.

title: Androgen-inducible gene 1 increases the ER Ca(2+) content and cell death susceptibility against oxidative stress.
review_notes: Directly relevant because it is the only study that examined where AIG1 is, and it contradicts the plasma-membrane call. Marked unverified rather than verified because full_text_available is false: the abstract does not state the species of the topology construct or the identity of the two cell lines, and the claim is unreplicated. Used as grounds for marking the plasma-membrane rows over-annotated and for a knowledge gap, not as the basis for an ER annotation.

title: AIG1 and ADTRP are endogenous hydrolases of fatty acid esters of hydroxy fatty acids (FAHFAs) in mice.
review_notes: The in vivo confirmation that this family sets endogenous FAHFA tone, quoted with its own limitation intact rather than truncated at the convenient point. Murine, so it supports no experimental evidence code on a human annotation. Absent from GOA entirely.

title: Inflammation causes insulin resistance in mice via interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3)-mediated reduction in FAHFA levels.
review_notes: Full text read. Every AIG1-specific experiment is murine - FI3KO/FI3OE adipocytes, mouse brain and kidney membrane proteomes, high-fat-diet mice - and the human SGBS adipocyte work concerns IRF3, not AIG1; the only hAIG1 strings in the text are inside the construct name shAIG1. Hence ISS rather than IMP on the annotation it supports. Absent from GOA.

title: AIG1 protects against doxorubicin-induced cardiomyocyte ferroptosis and cardiotoxicity by promoting ubiquitination-mediated p53 degradation.
review_notes: Full text read. Murine throughout - C57BL/6 mice, AAV9 cardiac transduction and the HL-1 mouse cardiomyocyte line - with the HEK293T truncation co-IPs not stating the species of the constructs, hence ISS. It is from a different Fudan department and author group than the 2011 yeast two-hybrid work, 14 years later and with different methods, so it is genuine corroboration of the Pirh2 interaction rather than a restatement. Absent from GOA.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AIG1 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates passed and all seven citations are numeric PMIDs that resolve to papers genuinely about AIG1, with no bioRxiv identifiers in a PMID-shaped field and no retraction or expression of concern among them. Recall was good here: it surfaced four papers absent from GOA (PMID:27040980, PMID:32152231, PMID:38816388, PMID:40303337), two of which changed this review. Marked LOW_QUALITY solely for its own GO grounding block, which is wrong and was not imported - it lists GO:0140098 'catalytic activity, acting on RNA' for a lipid hydrolase, and asserts GO:0005783 endoplasmic reticulum as the localisation without noting that this contradicts UniProt. It also paraphrases PMID:21622095's ambiguous 'confirmed its interaction with p53' as confirmation of the Pirh2 interaction. Used as a lead only; no sentence from it is quoted as supporting_text anywhere in this review, per the campaign rule that a provider sentence is a lead rather than evidence.

This directly supports substrate recruitment without assigning aminoacyl-transfer chemistry to AIMP1. Full experimental text remains unavailable locally.

title: Nucleolar localization of human methionyl-tRNA synthetase and its role in ribosomal RNA synthesis.

The externally read original Figures 5 and 6 show TNF-dependent endothelial coagulation potentiation, including recombinant 22- and 34-kDa forms; hypoxic conditioned medium alone did not significantly elevate coagulation. The short full-text support is the Figure 6 caption recorded in the linked notes, not the cached abstract's introductory tumor background. Original author upload accessed 2026-09-27 at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/12468958_Prostate_adenocarcinoma_cells_release_the_novel_proinflammatory_polypeptide_EMAP-II_in_response_to_stress .
