Source4 recovered the normal abstract-only cache; full article remains unavailable. The positive biochemical binding is not denied because later targeting models differ, nor is motif selectivity treated as proof of endogenous promoter selection.

title: NMR structure of the first PHD finger of autoimmune regulator protein (AIRE1). Insights into autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy (APECED) disease.
review_notes: Primary PubMed abstract and author-institution record inspected: human PHD1 structure, negative intrinsic E3 and E2-interaction results. Source4 recovered the normal abstract-only cache. Full assay comparison to PMID:14734522 remains incomplete; absence of activity in this preparation does not erase the positive report.

title: Two novel mutations of the AIRE protein affecting its homodimerization properties.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract directly identifies human patient variants and mutant-versus-wild-type yeast two-hybrid assays; it supports self-association without fixing native stoichiometry. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: Systematic identification of SH3 domain-mediated human protein-protein interactions by peptide array target screening.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract establishes the human SH3 peptide-array study; AIRE/NCK1 partner attribution is from GOA, not a pair-specific validation recovered from the abstract. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: The autoimmune regulator PHD finger binds to non-methylated histone H3K4 to activate gene expression.
review_notes: Cached full experimental text inspected: direct human H3/PHD1 biochemistry and promoter occupancy/activation in HEK293 cells. Later targeting models refine the physiological interpretation without reversing the binding result. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: Aire controls the differentiation program of thymic epithelial cells in the medulla for the establishment of self-tolerance.
review_notes: Primary PubMed/MGI J:141379 identity and newly recovered full text inspected. Aire-locus GFP knock-in/disruption distinguishes mTECs committed to Aire expression from cells retaining functional Aire. Figures 2 and 3 show altered morphology/distribution and reduced involucrin-positive terminal differentiation/Hassall-like structures in mutant mouse thymus; Figure 1 shows nuclear Aire staining. These support the existing contextual process and compartment judgments. Source4 recovered full text; this is mouse evidence, not a direct human developmental experiment.

title: Aire.
review_notes: Cached review abstract supports the established central-tolerance synthesis. It is secondary evidence, not an additional primary experiment. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: Structure and site-specific recognition of histone H3 by the PHD finger of human autoimmune regulator.
review_notes: Cached full structural report inspected; human PHD1-H3 solution structure and two structural zinc sites support the histone-reader mechanism. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: Autoimmune regulator deficiency results in decreased expression of CCR4 and CCR7 ligands and in delayed migration of CD4+ thymocytes.
review_notes: Primary PubMed/MGI J:157503 identity and newly recovered full Methods/Results inspected. Mouse thymic qPCR/ELISA, adenoviral Aire expression in the 1C6 thymic epithelial line, conditioned-medium migration and chemokine-blocking assays support regulation of chemokine production and thymocyte migration. AIRE is not assigned intrinsic chemokine or motility activity. Source4 recovered full text; the donor and host scope remains explicit.

title: Aire's partners in the molecular control of immunological tolerance.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract reports coimmunoprecipitation/mass spectrometry and RNAi analysis of AIRE partners in transcription and pre-mRNA processing. The abstract describes no assay of ribosomal translation and does not refute such a capacity or establish AIRE kinase activity. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: DAXX is a new AIRE-interacting protein.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract verifies DAXX interaction and repression of AIRE transactivation. GOA supplies the separate AIRE-AIRE assertion; its exact panel was not inspected. The listed erratum corrects an author given name, not the scientific result. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: Unmodified histone H3K4 and DNA-dependent protein kinase recruit autoimmune regulator to target genes.
review_notes: Primary PMC abstract and indexed experimental/discussion sections inspected. Chromatin versus episomal reporter and DNA-PKcs-deficient cell experiments support cooperative recruitment. AIRE is not assigned DNA-PK catalytic activity. Source4 recovered a normal abstract-only cache despite the PMC link; prior external reading and local availability remain distinct.

title: Extrathymic Aire-expressing cells are a distinct bone marrow-derived population that induce functional inactivation of CD4+ T cells.
review_notes: Primary PMC Results and newly recovered full text inspected. Human lymph-node expression is measured; functional tolerance experiments use mouse Aire-promoter-directed antigen expression. The AdBDC construct directs a mimetope in invariant chain under the Aire promoter, testing the tolerogenic cell population rather than isolating endogenous AIRE protein participation. Source4 recovered full text. The normal cache renders CD4+ as CD4⁺; this typographic difference identifies the same PMID, DOI and paper, and the original reference title is preserved. The separate MGI J:208220 bibliographic mapping remains unresolved.

title: Dominant Mutations in the Autoimmune Regulator AIRE Are Associated with Common Organ-Specific Autoimmune Diseases.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract verifies human dominant PHD1 variants and suppression of wild-type-driven expression. Exact localization images are not visible in the cache. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: A new mutation site in the AIRE gene causes autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract verifies human Q69P and yeast two-hybrid loss of mutant/wild-type interaction, with expression assays; no fixed native oligomer stoichiometry is inferred. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: A Germinal Center Checkpoint of AIRE in B Cells Limits Antibody Diversification.
review_notes: Primary PMC preprint Results/Methods inspected, including human B cells and mouse functional experiments. Source4 recovered the original bioRxiv preprint (DOI:10.1101/2024.01.10.574926; PMC10802573), not the revised eLife article. The separately inspected eLife reviewed-preprint version 2, dated 2026-09-21 (https://elifesciences.org/reviewed-preprints/110530v2; DOI:10.7554/eLife.110530.2), has a public assessment rating the evidence convincing. The current B-cell-context judgment uses that explicitly identified version; the older cache is not represented as its complete text. Detailed revision-by-revision experimental replication was not undertaken.

title: AIRE relies on Z-DNA to flag gene targets for thymic T cell tolerization.
review_notes: Primary PubMed and newly recovered full article inspected. F1-hybrid mouse cis-regulatory analysis, genome-wide Z-DNA mapping and promoter-poising experiments support the reported targeting model. The study does not measure purified AIRE-Z-DNA recognition or negatively replicate the historical recombinant motif-binding assay. Source4 recovered full text; no independent reanalysis of its genome-wide datasets was performed.

title: Mechanism for controlled assembly of transcriptional condensates by Aire.
review_notes: PubMed and full Nature Immunology article inspected, now also available in the normal source4 cache. Human WT and domain-mutant AIRE in 4D6 cells establish transcription-linked condensates, including CARD dependence; Figure 1 specifies human AIRE unless otherwise stated. Selected CTT/CBP and PHD1 biochemical/domain panels explicitly use mouse constructs. PHD1 dispersal and CTT targeting cooperate with CARD assembly; PHD1 is not simply an autonomous positive promoter selector. The six existing abstract quotations now have a local verbatim-checkable source.

title: Positional cloning of the APECED gene.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract verifies the human positional-cloning study and disease variants. Transcription-factor-like motifs are predictive, not direct localization evidence. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: An autoimmune disease, APECED, caused by mutations in a novel gene featuring two PHD-type zinc-finger domains.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract verifies the human genetic discovery. It calls AIRE a putative nuclear protein; later direct localization and functional evidence are independently cited. Identifier/title checked against the cached primary PubMed record.

title: AIRE manual deep research fallback
review_notes: Historical local curation/projection artifact, inspected as provenance rather than independent experimental support. The 2026-09-27 notes supersede its unsupported blanket E3 and immune-function conclusions.

title: AIRE PN batch curation notes
review_notes: Historical local curation/projection artifact, inspected as provenance rather than independent experimental support. The 2026-09-27 notes supersede its unsupported blanket E3 and immune-function conclusions.

title: Proteostasis PN projected annotations report
review_notes: Historical local curation/projection artifact, inspected as provenance rather than independent experimental support. The 2026-09-27 notes supersede its unsupported blanket E3 and immune-function conclusions.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: Full text cached. A methods paper demonstrating next-generation sequencing readout of Y2H screens; source of 3 GO:0005515 rows.

title: Identification and characterization of a novel gene, c1orf109, encoding a CK2 substrate that is involved in cancer cell proliferation.
review_notes: Full text cached. The original characterisation, predating any knowledge of the 55LCC complex. Its localisation data are the basis for the nucleus and cytoplasm IDA rows and have held up. Its proliferation claims are not relied on in this review. The CK2 phosphorylation finding is not currently captured by any GO annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Full text cached. Source of 43 GO:0005515 rows. Same assessment as HuRI: sound dataset, uninformative as a functional annotation for this gene.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Full text cached. Contributes one GO:0005515 row, and notably its partner is CINP - a real 55LCC subunit - so unlike the Y2H screens this row is modified to complex membership rather than removed. An AP-MS network independently corroborating the complex.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Full text cached. A high-quality systematic dataset, correctly cited, and the source of 121 of this gene's GO:0005515 rows. Relevance to AIRIM's function is LOW precisely because it is unbiased and proteome-wide: it says AIRIM touches many proteins, not what AIRIM does. Removing the derived annotations is not a criticism of the dataset.

title: C1orf109L binding DHX9 promotes DNA damage depended on the R-loop accumulation and enhances camptothecin chemosensitivity.
review_notes: Full text cached. Added after review. Important caveat recorded rather than folded in: this work is on the LONG isoform C1orf109L specifically, so it should not be treated as a property of the gene product reviewed here without isoform evidence. It is also a different activity from the 55LCC roles - DHX9 binding and R-loop accumulation - and is not currently captured by any GO annotation on this gene. Flagged, not annotated.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Full text cached. Like BioPlex 2.0, its single AIRIM row is with CINP and is therefore modified to complex membership rather than removed.

title: Labeling of heterochronic ribosomes reveals C1ORF109 and SPATA5 control a late step in human ribosome assembly.
review_notes: Full text cached. Primary evidence for the ribosome biogenesis annotations and the source of the GO:0042273 IDA. Unbiased discovery, which is the strongest kind of support for a previously dark gene.

title: The SPATA5-SPATA5L1 ATPase complex directs replisome proteostasis to ensure genome integrity.
review_notes: Full text cached. The structural and mechanistic paper for the 55LCC complex; source of the ATPase complex, DNA replication and regulation of ribosome biogenesis rows. It is also what makes the 174 generic protein-binding rows redundant: the four interactions that matter are complex membership, which this study establishes directly.

title: Cryo-EM structure of the AAA+ SPATA5 complex and its role in human cytoplasmic pre-60S maturation.
review_notes: Full text cached. The highest-resolution structural account of the complex and the source of three things this review depends on: the 4:2:2:2 stoichiometry (so 'heterohexameric', which UniProt and PMID:38554706 use, describes the SPATA5-SPATA5L1 motor rather than the whole assembly); the N-terminal ring that grounds GO:0005198; and the adapter conclusion that grounds GO:0060090. Its two statements about AIRIM and the pre-60S particle must be kept apart, because conflating them is easy and this review did it once: AIRIM makes no direct contact with the PARTICLE, which is CINP's docking job, but AIRIM does bind the SUBSTRATE RLP24 inside the funnel, which the paper states outright in a section headed 'CINP and C1orf109 are adapter proteins for the SPATA5 complex'.

title: A programmed decline in ribosome levels governs human early neurodevelopment.
review_notes: Full text cached. Added after review. The description asserted that hypomorphic AIRIM variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder while citing nothing; this is the source, and it was sitting in the same diff. It does not change any annotation action - no GO term here covers the disease association - but the claim should not have been made uncited.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AIRIM (human)
review_notes: Automated trust gates passed. Unlike the ADIG and ADM5 records reviewed in this campaign, this one is accurate and well framed: it correctly identifies the 55LCC complex, names AIRIM's role as structural, and separates the ribosome and replisome activities. It also surfaced three papers absent from GOA (PMID:40268917, PMID:40760247, PMID:32761833). Used for orientation; every annotation decision is anchored to a PMID.

title: Cooperative regulation of AJM-1 controls junctional integrity in Caenorhabditis elegans epithelia.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only. This is the donor paper for essentially the whole human annotation set, so its scope matters: every claim in it is about C. elegans. Cited here as the evidence behind the propagations, not as evidence about the human protein.

title: A Conserved Role for Girdin in Basal Body Positioning and Ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only. Found by searching the donor's annotations rather than the human gene - it is the source of worm ajm-1's only experimental ciliary annotation (GO:0036064 ciliary basal body, IDA). Decisive for removing the human cilium row, because the authors scope the AJM-1 mechanism to nematodes and reserve the conserved claim for Girdin.

title: Falcon deep research report for human AJM1
review_notes: Fallback provider, used because affinage REFUSED to write a record for this gene: its symbol-collision trust gate tripped BLOCKING, and inspection of the quarantined output confirmed the gate was right - every claim and every PMID in it described C. elegans AJM-1. That record was not written into the gene folder. Falcon, given the same ambiguous symbol, handled it correctly: it verified the identity, stated that the human protein is poorly characterized, and kept worm evidence explicitly separate from human inference. Its citation keys are internal rather than PMIDs, so it is used here for its assessment of the evidence STATE, which is checkable against the file, and not as a source of biological claims - those are anchored to PMIDs.

title: QuickGO snapshot of C. elegans ajm-1 (A0A1C3NSL9) GO annotations
review_notes: Committed for this review, following the genes/human/SAMD8/SAMD8-reaction-donor-check.json convention. Six load-bearing facts about the donor's own GOA appeared only as prose in an earlier version, so nothing let the next reader re-check them - including 'worm GO:0005929 is itself only IEA', which IS the cilium removal. The file is a QuickGO annotation-search snapshot for A0A1C3NSL9 carrying the query URL, retrieval timestamp and a sha256 of the raw response, plus a claims_this_supports block in which every claim has a 'check' field naming the row that would falsify it. The supporting_text values here quote those claim strings rather than the data rows, which is only legitimate because of that 'check' field; if this format is reused, the field should stay mandatory.

title: UniProtKB C9J069 (AJM1_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record. The important detail is the evidence codes: FUNCTION and all three SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements carry ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:A0A1C3NSL9, so they are curator inferences from the worm protein, not human observations.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro mapping provenance; human record confirms the cited adenylate-kinase signatures. Independent enzymology resolves target specificity.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT phylogenetic propagation. The four term-specific IBD records in cached PTHR23359/PTHR23359-paint.tsv were inspected. Its three GO:0004017 IRD records are documented separately in the notes; the file does not contain the complete tree/MSA needed to reconstruct their ancestry. Direct human catalytic evidence supports the retained kinase assertion, and target self-evidence is legitimate descendant grounding.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by transferring manual GO annotations between related proteins based on shared sequence features
review_notes: UniRule propagation method. Exact rule internals were not retrieved; human catalytic and compartment evidence supports retained target judgments independently.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog propagation. Mouse Ak2 donor Q9WTP6/ENSMUSP00000030583 and the sperm-localization IDA chain were resolved; the evidence is not a direct human sperm experiment.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA mapping method; rule conditions were not independently inspected. Generic metabolism is refined using direct human chemistry, not a claim of invalid rule construction.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined electronic sources are separated in propagation_review. Reaction/signature mappings have target support; unread ARBA and UniRule internals remain unresolved.

title: Release of adenylate kinase 2 from the mitochondrial intermembrane space during apoptosis.
review_notes: The recovered source14 PubMed abstract reports AK2 release to the cytosol with cytochrome c during apoptosis, while cytosolic AK1 and matrix-associated AK3 remain unchanged. This source confirms a contextual mitochondrial-to-cytosol redistribution. Its abstract describes mammalian cells without identifying every experimental species or isoform; full Methods were not recovered. It is not used as a direct human isoform-specific localization assay or evidence for constitutive core cytosol residence.

title: Adenylate kinases 1 and 2 are part of the accessory structures in the mouse sperm flagellum.
review_notes: The normal source14 record now provides the PubMed abstract, DOI 10.1095/biolreprod.106.053512, and exact machine-fetched title. The abstract directly distinguishes mouse AK2 in the sperm-midpiece mitochondrial sheath from AK1 at other flagellar structures. The historical MGI comparative graph (snapshot 2023-03-10) supplies the term-specific donor chain. The full article was not recovered; this remains a bounded mouse-to-human compartment inference, not a direct human sperm, axonemal-structure or motility assay.

title: AK2 activates a novel apoptotic pathway through formation of a complex with FADD and caspase-10.
review_notes: The recovered source14 PubMed abstract reports AK2 knockdown effects on etoposide- or staurosporine-induced apoptosis in human cells, AK2-FADD-caspase-10 association, and activation after purified AK2 addition to cell extracts. These are positive stress-dependent signaling observations, distinct from the AK2-DUSP26 complex in PMID:24548998. Full construct, stoichiometry and mechanistic controls remain unread; no additional apoptosis or adaptor annotation is manufactured from this abstract.

title: Human adenylate kinase 2 deficiency causes a profound hematopoietic defect associated with sensorineural deafness.
review_notes: The source14 XML record contains the original Results, Methods and figure legends, now read locally. Human patient genetics and loss of AK2 protein are complemented by lentiviral human AK2A/B rescue in patient bone-marrow CD34-positive cells (Figure 3), and knockdown in human CD34-positive cells. In contrast, Figure 4 inner-ear immunolocalization used mice: postnatal stria-vascularis capillary-lumen staining is not a human-ear localization assay. Human disease and rescue support a requirement for hematopoietic differentiation, without by themselves identifying a direct developmental step or justifying a new process annotation.

title: Reticular dysgenesis (aleukocytosis) is caused by mutations in the gene encoding mitochondrial adenylate kinase 2.
review_notes: PubMed identity and cached abstract verified. Human reticular-dysgenesis genetics and zebrafish knockdown are distinct evidence; neither is recast as a direct human developmental enzymatic step.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed identity and cached abstract verified. External original author-uploaded main text at ResearchGate publication 44588150 was inspected on 2026-09-27. The AK2 supplementary target row was not recovered; HDA exosome localization stays UNDECIDED without alleging contamination or equating the total proteome with the MHC-II co-IP subset.

title: The DUSP26 phosphatase activator adenylate kinase 2 regulates FADD phosphorylation and cell growth.
review_notes: The normal source14 XML record now contains the primary Results, Methods and figure legends; it corroborates the earlier external Nature/PMC3948464 reading. Human AK2 was expressed and purified from bacteria. Figures 1 and 3 distinguish lack of AK2 phosphatase activity from stimulation of purified DUSP26 on pNPP and Plk-phosphorylated FADD; AK3/FADD controls do not stimulate, and kinase-defective K28E retains stimulation. Figure 4 provides purified tagged-protein association and activity in gel-filtration fractions, not a fixed native stoichiometry. Human-cell experiments, human-tumor xenografts in mice and heterozygous mouse fibroblast experiments are distinct contexts. DUSP26 performs dephosphorylation; these data support the retained activator MF without adding a proliferation, apoptosis or differentiation process.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: PubMed identity and cached abstract verified. Original full institutional PDF https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/id/eprint/19322/1/19322oa.pdf was read: repeated human Y2H screens and integrated interaction evidence, not a single unreplicated assay. AK2 partners are also in the immutable UniProt interaction section, but target-specific supplementary panels were not reanalyzed. Generic-binding removals concern informativeness, not false interactions.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Cached full human MitoCoP study inspected. AK2-specific supplementary measurements were not separately extracted; the seeded HTP mitochondrion assertion is retained with curator deference and independent human mitochondrial biochemistry. This does not supply an IMS topology assay.

title: Failure of metabolic checkpoint control during late-stage granulopoiesis drives neutropenia in reticular dysgenesis.
review_notes: The normal source14 record contains the primary PubMed abstract and exact DOI 10.1182/blood.2024024123; it remains abstract-only despite its PMC identifier. The abstract explicitly combines patient single-cell transcriptomics with a CRISPR model in primary human hematopoietic stem cells and describes different early-versus-late metabolic checkpoint responses. Earlier externally indexed PMC11830988 Results access was documented on 2026-09-27; that access is separate from this cache. Neither source is recast as a direct differentiation molecular function or a new process assertion.

title: Adenosine triphosphate-adenosine-5'-monophosphate phosphotransferase from normal human liver mitochondria. Isolation, chemical properties, and immunochemical comparison with Duchenne dystrophic serum aberrant adenylate kinase.
review_notes: PubMed identity verified. Local record has no abstract/full text. Original JBC full text was read externally at ResearchGate publication 17011438 on 2026-09-27, DOI 10.1016/S0021-9258(18)33631-7: Methods specify normal human autopsy liver, paired coupled-enzyme assays, and Results/Table III establish purified mitochondrial adenylate-kinase activity. External full-text access does not change the immutable cache availability flag.

title: Cloning and expression of human adenylate kinase 2 isozymes: differential expression of adenylate kinase 1 and 2 in human muscle tissues.
review_notes: PubMed identity and cached abstract verified. Human AK2A and AK2B were expressed in E. coli and purified as active enzymes. Tissue expression findings do not establish all six isoforms or an absolute lack of AK2 in every skeletal-muscle context; full source was not recovered.

title: ADP + ADP <=> AMP + ATP [AK2]
review_notes: Exact cached human reaction read. Human catalytic evidence and rat-derived IMS localization inference are explicitly distinguished. Both are used within their stated scope.

title: AMP + ATP <=> ADP + ADP [AK2]
review_notes: Exact cached forward reaction read: AMP + ATP forms ADP. Its IMS assignment explicitly uses homologous rat-enzyme evidence, not an additional independent human localization experiment.

title: Interconversion of nucleotide di- and triphosphates
review_notes: Exact cached nucleotide-interconversion pathway summary read; AK2-specific reaction records provide the direct step. No whole-pathway mechanism beyond adenylate transfer is assigned.

title: UniProt P54819 human AK2 record
review_notes: Immutable normal-fetched source3 record checked for identity, six alternative products, reaction, compartment, InterPro mappings and interaction pairs. This is curated database evidence, not an additional independent experiment.

title: Long-read cDNA sequencing identifies functional pseudogenes in the human transcriptome.
review_notes: Full text cached. The only AK4P3-specific experimental paper found, and it is in no GO annotation on this gene. It is what moves the locus from 'predicted ORF' to 'transcribed and translation-competent', which is the single most decision-relevant fact available. Note carefully what it does not show: the translation was from a transfected construct, so endogenous protein production remains unproven, and no activity was assayed.

title: Is human AK4P3 an over-annotated pseudogene, or a functional AK4 duplicate?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review; script, raw output and limitations are in genes/human/AK4P3/AK4P3-bioinformatics/. Sequences are fetched live from the UniProt REST API and the comparison and tryptic digest are computed, so nothing is hardcoded. Its most useful result is the negative one: there is no sequence-level evidence of pseudogenisation, so the automatic annotations are not misfiring on a decayed relic the way they would for a frameshifted remnant. Its limitations are stated in the file - it says nothing about the genomic context on which HGNC's pseudogene call presumably rests, and an intact active site is not evidence of activity.

title: Falcon deep research report for human AK4P3
review_notes: Fallback provider: affinage has no record for this locus at all, which is consistent with its human protein-coding gene set excluding pseudogenes. Falcon handled the nomenclature trap well - it separated AK4P3 from canonical AK4/AK3L1 explicitly, warned that the AK4 literature cannot be reassigned, and surfaced PMID:33971925, which is the paper this review turns on and which no GO annotation cites. Its citation keys are internal rather than PMIDs, so it is cited here for its assessment of the evidence state, which is checkable against the file, with the biology anchored to the PMID.

title: UniProtKB A0A8I5KW96 (AK4P3, unreviewed) flat file
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record, unreviewed (TrEMBL). Its functional content is applied by HAMAP-Rule MF_03170, which is a sequence rule rather than curation of this protein, and that rule is the proximate source of most of the GO annotations under review. The PE=1 is cross-referenced to PeptideAtlas.

title: Hypothetical gene C18orf42 encodes a novel protein kinase A-binding protein.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only; every quote is from the abstract. The only functional study of this gene - an independent PubMed search on AKAIN1 and C18orf42 found no other. Its endogenous-protein work is in mouse Neuro2a cells, and its PKA-displacement result is from expression of the protein, so the 'endogenous disruptor' framing is the authors' proposal rather than a demonstrated physiological function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Full text cached. Correctly cited, and the AKAIN1-ROPN1 pair it reports is mechanistically suggestive, but as an unbiased screen it does not characterise the interaction.

title: The Inflammatory Gene PYCARD of the Entorhinal Cortex as an Early Diagnostic Target for Alzheimer's Disease.
review_notes: Full text cached. Found by an independent PubMed search for AKAIN1 run to check affinage's recall. AKAIN1 appears only in a differentially-expressed gene list; it is context, not evidence for any annotation. Two other hits from that search were examined and excluded: PMID:29275994 does not mention AKAIN1 in its full text, and PMID:32799782 concerns AKIP1, a different gene caught by name similarity.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AKAIN1 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates passed; a faithful summary of PMID:25653177. An independent PubMed search turned up no functional paper it missed, so recall was not a problem for this gene.

title: UniProtKB P0CW23 (AKAI1_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record; its functional statements carry ECO:0000269 pointing at PMID:25653177.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Supplies one row, GO:0051018 from IPR037719. The signature is family-specific for the AKAP10 A-kinase-binding domain rather than a bare fold, which makes it well founded; the only problem is that the mapped term is one level more general than the domain warrants. Recorded as an upstream interpro2go refinement rather than a gene-level error.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Supplies three rows, all from the single PANTHER node PTN001775426 in PTHR13155. Every protein-level donor was checked individually in QuickGO rather than assumed: mouse Akap10 (O88845) carries its own IDA for all three terms, and yeast RAX1 (Q08760) carries two IMP rows for GO:0008104. All three transfers are sound for human AKAP10. The reciprocal direction is not. The same node pushes GO:0005739 onto two fungal bud-site proteins whose own experimental localisations are plasma membrane, bud neck and endoplasmic reticulum. That is a PAINT node-scope issue, recorded in suggested_questions and not held against these rows.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Supplies the GO:0016020 membrane row. Traces correctly to UniProt's CC SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line, whose Membrane term carries ECO:0000269|PubMed:11248059, so it is not a fabricated call - but it names no compartment and the protein has no transmembrane segment.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence in human cell lines - the only human IDA localisation this gene has, and it agrees with the independent subcellular fractionation of endogenous protein in PMID:19797056. It is the evidence that makes the cytosol call robust rather than Reactome-derived.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Supplies two rows, GO:0043495 and GO:0005739, both transferred from mouse Akap10 O88845. Correct, but both duplicate the PAINT rows' donor and evidence, so they should not be counted as independent support.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Supplies GO:0005737 and a second GO:0005739 row. Both are correct and both are redundant with better-evidenced rows on the same gene.

title: Cloning and mitochondrial localization of full-length D-AKAP2, a protein kinase A anchoring protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. It is the ultimate source of three GOA rows via the mouse orthologue and of UniProt's Mitochondrion, Membrane and Cytoplasm subcellular-location terms, so it is load-bearing out of proportion to its visibility - GOA cites it nowhere on the human gene directly. Not cited by the seeded stub; recovered from the affinage record and from the mouse donor's QuickGO evidence.

title: Domain organization of D-AKAP2 revealed by enhanced deuterium exchange-mass spectrometry (DXMS).
review_notes: Abstract-only. Background architecture rather than a GO-annotatable result, and it produced no annotation on any gene. Used here only to describe the domain organisation.

title: PDZK1: II. an anchoring site for the PKA-binding protein D-AKAP2 in renal proximal tubular cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Species caution recorded rather than glossed: this is mouse D-AKAP2 (the 372-residue renal isoform) assayed in transfected opossum kidney cells, so it cannot support a human experimental evidence code on its own - it is used here as corroboration of the PDZK1 interaction, whose human evidence comes from PMID:36115835 and PMID:25348485. Note also that its second partner is NHERF-1 (SLC9A3R1), which is a different protein from the NHERF2 (SLC9A3R2) in GOA.

title: Gene-trapped mouse embryonic stem cell-derived cardiac myocytes and human genetics implicate AKAP10 in heart rhythm regulation.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The source of UniProt's VARIANT 646 I->V entry. Relevance is deliberately MEDIUM rather than HIGH: it is the best-known AKAP10 paper and it supports no GO annotation on the human gene, because the perturbation is mouse, the allele is dominant-interfering and the human evidence is statistical association. Kept in the reference list precisely so that the reason for not annotating from it is on the record.

title: D-AKAP2 interacts with Rab4 and Rab11 through its RGS domains and regulates transferrin receptor recycling.
review_notes: Full text available and read in full. The single most informative paper on this gene, and QuickGO returns ZERO annotations for reference=PMID:19797056 across all of GOA - not on AKAP10, not on RAB4A, RAB11A or TFRC, not on any gene in any species. Three of this review's NEW rows come from it. It is also the source of the explicit negative on Galpha activation and of the challenge to the mitochondrial localisation. Absent from the seeded stub; recovered from the affinage record. No retraction, no erratum.

title: Structure of D-AKAP2:PKA RI complex: insights into AKAP specificity and selectivity.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but the structural fact needed here is independently checkable in the UniProt entry, which cross-references PDB 3IM4 with chain C mapped to human AKAP10 residues 623-662 and records the resulting HELIX 629..653. That is what establishes the anchoring claim on the human sequence rather than by family inference. The GOA row citing it lists bovine PRKAR1A (P00514) as the partner, which UniProt's own INTERACTION block flags as Xeno.

title: A systematic evaluation of protein kinase A-A-kinase anchoring protein interaction motifs.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Supplies three GOA rows. Checked by reference in QuickGO: 26 annotations over 8 distinct entities, with GO:0032991 given by IDA to all 8 AKAPs in the study. That has the shape of a complex-membership projection but is benign here, because each AKAP was individually assayed rather than inheriting one gene's phenotype.

title: D-AKAP2:PKA RII:PDZK1 ternary complex structure: insights from the nucleation of a polyvalent scaffold.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Produces no GO annotation on this gene despite being a structure of AKAP10 with two partners simultaneously - part of the coverage defect this review documents. Absent from the seeded stub; recovered from the affinage record.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP, built from subcellular fractions of HEK293T, HeLa, Huh7 and U2OS cells by subtractive, spatial and import proteomics. Supplies the GO:0005739 HTP row, which matters more than its evidence code suggests: it is the only mitochondrial evidence for this gene that uses no AKAP10 antibody, and so is not touched by the antibody-specificity objection PMID:19797056 raises against PMID:11248059. This reference contributes 1235 annotations across GOA; the result set is paginated, so a distinct-entity count was not obtainable and is reported as unavailable rather than substituted with the annotation total.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Full text available. The largest single contributor to this gene's GOA, supplying 21 of 39 rows. Carries an Author Correction, PMID:36477203, which states that the original version contained errors in Figures 2, 4 and 5 - missing correlation coefficients, absent axis labels and panel ordering. It changes no affinity measurement and no PDZ datum, so nothing used here is affected; flagged because a correction has to be checked rather than assumed cosmetic. IntAct shows every one of these partners under holdup assay only, with 2-9 replicate rows each, which is why the UniProt NbExp figures for this gene must not be read as independent experiments.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Systematic multimodal cell map contributing 3026 annotations across GOA. Its single AKAP10 row, NHERF2, is valuable out of proportion to its size because IntAct logs it under a different method (anti tag coip) from the holdup measurement of the same pair, making NHERF2 the only PDZ partner supported by two independent techniques. Carries a Publisher Correction, PMID:41039152, which corrects duplicated variable names in an equation in the Methods loss-function section and affects no interaction data. Entity counts unavailable because the QuickGO result is paginated.

title: D-AKAP2, a novel protein kinase A anchoring protein with a putative RGS domain.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Two cautions for anyone reusing it. First, it is mouse work: the two-hybrid screen used a mouse embryonic library and the full-length clone came from a mouse testis library, so its 372-residue protein is not the 662-residue human entry, and the "residues 333-372" R-binding fragment is in mouse numbering. Second, its signal-transduction framing was explicitly speculative about the RGS domain, which is why the GO:0007165 TAS row derived from it is marked over-annotated. No retraction, no erratum, no expression of concern.

title: Dual-specific AKAPs bind type I and II PKA regulatory subunits
review_notes: A binding reaction, not a localisation experiment, so the cytosol GO term derived from it reflects the compartment Reactome assigns to the reaction rather than a measurement of where AKAP10 is. The identifier is correct and the biology it describes is correct; it is the inference from reaction compartment to gene localisation that is weak. The term survives on other evidence, which is why the row is accepted rather than demoted.

title: AKAP10 RGS domains: are the Galpha GAP contact residues present?
review_notes: Reproducible analysis committed alongside this review. Verified that a fresh run reproduces the committed RESULTS.md, results.json and stdout byte-for-byte, and that both of the script's guards fire when deliberately broken - mutating the RGS4 site table aborts on the sequence mismatch, and pointing a positive control at haemoglobin alpha aborts on the control check. The RGS-B identity of 24.3% is below the range where a residue call is safe on alignment alone, which the report states explicitly; the conclusion therefore rests on RGS-A plus the two published statements, with the computation as corroboration.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AKAP10 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record, trust gates reported clear, faith_pct 100, eight citations and every one a real numeric PMID (no preprint identifiers in a PMID-shaped field). Its recall on this gene was well above the campaign average: it surfaced PMID:19797056, PMID:25348485, PMID:12206784, PMID:14531807, PMID:17485678 and PMID:11248059, six references absent from GOA and from the seeded stub, including the one that supplies all three NEW rows. Recorded because provider recall is only ever measured when a reviewer writes it down. Two defects found and not imported. It names the PDZ partner as NHERF-1 (SLC9A3R1), whereas the annotated partner is NHERF2 (SLC9A3R2) - different proteins. And it describes the Rab work without noting that every construct in that study carried the 646V variant. Per campaign practice no sentence from this record is used as supporting_text; each lead was re-verified against the cited PMID or against UniProt before use, which is how both defects were found.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The two InterPro signatures involved were checked directly. IPR028540 is an AKAP12-only family (1185 proteins, integrated with the single-subfamily PANTHER orthogroup PTHR23209) and IPR001573 is the AKAP calmodulin-binding WSK motif shared with AKAP5 - both are specific signatures rather than bare folds, so the four IEA rows they generate are well founded.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Both IBA rows were checked by resolving every WITH/FROM token and querying each donor's own evidence in QuickGO. The zebrafish donor carries two independent IDA annotations to GO:0005737, so neither row is a family-level guess without measurement.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mechanically correct, but all three source UniProt subcellular-location statements carry ECO:0000305 and one is explicitly hedged as something the protein may be part of, so the rows inherit curator inference rather than measurement. Noted per row.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Checked against the Human Protein Atlas API, which returns exactly two subcellular main locations for AKAP12 - Plasma membrane and Cytosol - and no additional locations. Both GO_REF:0000052 rows are therefore main calls.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: The orthology itself is sound - Q5QD51 is reviewed rat Akap12 in the same single-gene PANTHER subfamily as human AKAP12, so these are ortholog and not paralog transfers. The donor annotations are mixed in quality, and the pipeline propagates them without distinction: three of the eleven transferred rows rest on expression correlation or, in the GO:0043116 case, invert the sign of the experiment they cite. Marked DISPUTED for that reason rather than for any identifier problem.

title: Developmental expression of the protein kinase C substrate/binding protein (clone 72/SSeCKS) in rat testis identification as a scaffolding protein containing an A-kinase-anchoring domain which is expressed during late-stage spermatogenesis.
review_notes: Rat, and reached by an independent route (interactive cloning with the PKA type II regulatory subunit as bait). Corroborates the human RII mapping in PMID:9000000 from a different species and method; not used as human evidence.

title: Gravin-mediated formation of signaling complexes in beta 2-adrenergic receptor desensitization and resensitization.
review_notes: Source of all three TAS rows on this gene. The TAS code understates it - the paper reports antisense knockdown experiments, not an author assertion - but the terms chosen are correct, so the rows were accepted or kept rather than modified. The cell system is not named in the abstract and the full text is not cached, so no species-specific claim was built on it beyond what the GOA row already asserts.

title: SSeCKS, a major protein kinase C substrate with tumor suppressor activity, regulates G(1)-->S progression by controlling the expression and cellular compartmentalization of cyclin D.
review_notes: Mouse NIH3T3 and rat embryo fibroblasts. Cited for the cyclin-sequestration mechanism, which is recorded in suggested_questions rather than annotated, because no human experiment tests it. Note the G1 arrest is a tetracycline-induced over-expression phenotype, which is why no cell-cycle BP term was proposed from it.

title: SSeCKS immunolabeling in rat primary sensory neurons.
review_notes: The rat IDA underlying the GO:0043025 Compara transfer. Verified through QuickGO on the donor accession rather than assumed. Rat, and cell-type restricted, so the transferred row is kept as non-core.

title: Calmodulin and cyclin D anchoring sites on the Src-suppressed C kinase substrate, SSeCKS.
review_notes: The biochemical basis of the GO:0005516 row. Explicitly about the rodent protein - the abstract frames it as SSeCKS and its human orthologue Gravin - so it supports the term by orthology, not as a human measurement; recorded as a knowledge gap in core_functions.

title: Mitogen-induced, FAK-dependent tyrosine phosphorylation of the SSeCKS scaffolding protein.
review_notes: NIH3T3 and rodent embryo fibroblasts. Supports the cell cortex row. Its F-actin co-sedimentation result would license GO:0051015 but is opposed by PMID:9885289 from the same laboratory, so it was not used to propose a term.

title: Molecular cloning and preliminary characterization of a novel cytoplasmic antigen recognized by myasthenia gravis sera.
review_notes: The original description of the human protein. Cited here for the cytoplasmic localisation and tissue distribution that UniProt's TISSUE SPECIFICITY line summarises; not load-bearing for any annotation action.

title: SSeCKS/Gravin/AKAP12 metastasis suppressor inhibits podosome formation via RhoA- and Cdc42-dependent pathways.
review_notes: Mouse NIH3T3, and a re-expression rather than loss-of-function design. Used only to support the PAINT suggestion that the Rho axis is conserved between the zebrafish orthologue's own IMP and the mammalian literature; no Rho term was annotated on this gene from it, because the human protein has no such measurement.

title: An anchored PKA and PDE4 complex regulates subplasmalemmal cAMP dynamics.
review_notes: The strongest human functional evidence on this gene and the basis of the proposed GO:0035591 row. IntAct records the AKAP12-PRKAR2A pair from this study under detection method "filter binding", a direct in-vitro assay rather than a screen, which is why the PRKAR2A rows were promoted to GO:0034237 rather than left as bare protein binding.

title: Role of protein kinase C-dependent A-kinase anchoring proteins in lysophosphatidic acid-induced cAMP signaling in human diploid fibroblasts.
review_notes: A genuinely human experimental study, which is scarce for this gene. Supports both GO:0008179 rows as they stand, with the AC2 negative control giving unusual specificity for an interaction row. The only issue is directional: the paper's conclusion is explicitly bidirectional, which is why the GO:0007193 row was modified to the neutral parent GO:0007188.

title: Src suppressed C kinase substrate regulates the lipopolysaccharide-induced TNF-alpha biosynthesis in rat astrocytes.
review_notes: One of the two rat IMPs behind GO:0032760, identified by querying the donor accession in QuickGO. Genuine loss-of-function evidence, in rat.

title: G-protein-coupled receptor-associated A-kinase anchoring proteins AKAP5 and AKAP12: differential signaling to MAPK and GPCR recycling.
review_notes: The double dissociation between two AKAPs in the same human cell lines is what makes this stronger than an ordinary knockdown, and it is the basis of the proposed GO:0001921 row. Cell lines are human, so IMP is species-correct.

title: A critical role of SRC-suppressed C kinase substrate in rat astrocytes after chronic constriction injury.
review_notes: The rat IMP behind both GO:0070374 and the second GO:0032760 annotation. Its ERK result runs opposite to the fibroblast literature, which is recorded in the GO:0070374 row rather than resolved.

title: SSeCKS/Gravin/AKAP12 inhibits cancer cell invasiveness and chemotaxis by suppressing a protein kinase C- Raf/MEK/ERK pathway.
review_notes: Rat MAT-LyLu prostate carcinoma cells and a re-expression design, so it is rodent and gain-of-function. Cited only to show that AKAP12's effect on the ERK cascade is context-dependent, which is why the transferred GO:0070374 row is non-core rather than core. Its invasion and metastasis results are deliberately not annotated: forced re-expression in a cancer line does not establish a normal physiological process.

title: Regulation of epidermal growth factor receptor trafficking by lysine deacetylase HDAC6.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but it is a screen resource for this gene rather than a study of it - AKAP12 is not named anywhere in the cached text. Shares platform and authors (Curak, Stagljar) with PMID:31980649, so the two EGFR rows are not independent.

title: Involvement of Src-suppressed C kinase substrate in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis: a link between release of astrocyte proinflammatory factor and oligodendrocyte apoptosis.
review_notes: The rat IMP behind GO:1900143. The perturbation is real but the effect is non-cell-autonomous and observed only in an EAE model, which is why the transferred row is non-core.

title: A comprehensive resource of interacting protein regions for refining human transcription factor networks.
review_notes: An mRNA-display interacting-region resource built around 50 transcription factors, in which AKAP12 appears as a prey for beta-catenin. The core data set is reported at a 70 percent verification rate. A second, orthogonal method (OpenCell endogenous-tag co-IP) recovered the same pair, so the interaction is replicated; replication makes it credible rather than informative, and the row is removed as generic binding.

title: Role of src-suppressed C kinase substrate in rat pulmonary microvascular endothelial hyperpermeability stimulated by inflammatory cytokines.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and the source of three transferred rows. The paper itself is sound; what is wrong is the sign of the GO:0043116 annotation drawn from it, which asserts negative regulation of vascular permeability while the paper reports the protein promoting permeability. Assessed from the abstract, whose RESULTS and CONCLUSIONS sentences are unambiguous; the full text was not available.

title: Analysis of the myosin-II-responsive focal adhesion proteome reveals a role for β-Pix in negative regulation of focal adhesion maturation.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a sound paper, but as a GO source it supplies GO:0005925 to 285 annotations, all HDA and all UniProt-assigned, including RPLP0, RPLP1 and RPLP2 - cytoplasmic large-ribosomal-subunit proteins that are not focal adhesion components. Flagged LOW_QUALITY as an annotation source, not as science: a proteomic inventory of isolated adhesions is not per-protein validation.

title: A directed protein interaction network for investigating intracellular signal transduction.
review_notes: Automated yeast-two-hybrid interaction mating covering more than 450 signalling proteins and yielding 2626 interactions. Screen-level support for the AKAP12-FHL1 pair; AKAP12 is not individually discussed.

title: Control of protein kinase C activity, phorbol ester-induced cytoskeletal remodeling, and cell survival signals by the scaffolding protein SSeCKS/GRAVIN/AKAP12.
review_notes: The mechanistic basis for GO:0090036. The experiments are rodent (SSeCKS-null mouse embryo fibroblasts, rat MAT-LyLu cells alongside human LNCaP), so it is not used as human evidence. Its published motif consensus was tested against the human sequence independently for this review and matches at residues 605-633 and 754-782, which is how the human protein was shown to carry the same determinants.

title: A human skeletal muscle interactome centered on proteins involved in muscular dystrophies: LGMD interactome.
review_notes: Independent Y2H recovery of the AKAP12-FHL1 pair from a human skeletal-muscle library, from a different laboratory than PMID:21900206. Its value here is replication, not characterisation.

title: Vagal efferent fiber stimulation ameliorates pulmonary microvascular endothelial cell injury by downregulating inflammatory responses.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but a poor basis for GO:0051602 response to electrical stimulus: the electrode was on the vagus nerve of a whole animal and Akap12 was measured in lung tissue several causal steps downstream. The GO:0032496 row from the same paper is the defensible one.

title: Increased SSeCKS expression in rat hepatic stellate cells upon activation in vitro and in vivo.
review_notes: Correctly cited. The concern is what was drawn from it: RGD records an IMP to GO:0061870 from a paper whose abstract describes no perturbation and no migration assay, alongside an IEP to GO:0035733. Both transferred rows were marked over-annotated. Assessed from the abstract; full text not accessible, so the question is passed to a curator rather than settled.

title: PKA compartmentalization via AKAP220 and AKAP12 contributes to endothelial barrier regulation.
review_notes: The abstract states the study analysed human, mouse and rat material, which would invite an IMP. Reading the methods shows the AKAP12 knockdown itself used mouse-specific siRNA in MyEnd mouse cells, so the proposed GO:0061028 row is ISS with mouse Akap12 as the supporting entity. Checking which reagent was human is the difference between a correct and an incorrect evidence code here.

title: AKAP12 mediates PKA-induced phosphorylation of ATR to enhance nucleotide excision repair.
review_notes: RETRACTED. The retraction notice (PMID:33091128) states the authors requested retraction after a University of Kentucky investigation determined the paper contains fabricated and/or falsified data, including substituted blank panels in negative controls. The affinage record cites this paper as a high-confidence finding with no flag, and it is the sole source of that record's DNA-repair claims and of its Reactome R-HSA-73894 grounding. No annotation in this review rests on it, and no nucleotide excision repair or ATR-related term was proposed. Listed here so the retraction is recorded rather than silently omitted.

title: Extensive rewiring of the EGFR network in colorectal cancer cells expressing transforming levels of KRAS(G13D).
review_notes: Correctly cited but methodologically redundant with PMID:20029029 for this gene: the same split-ubiquitin membrane-Y2H platform, overlapping authors, and no mention of AKAP12 in the text. Treating the two EGFR rows as independent replication would repeat the NbExp error.

title: Retraction: AKAP12 mediates PKA-induced phosphorylation of ATR to enhance nucleotide excision repair.
review_notes: Cited only to document the retraction of PMID:27683220. Found by checking CommentsCorrections RefType on every candidate PMID rather than by searching for retraction-type publications.

title: AKAP12 Supports Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity against Ischemic Stroke.
review_notes: A mouse system throughout (cultured cerebral endothelial cells plus Akap12 knockout mice), so it corroborates the ISS-coded GO:0061028 row from a second laboratory and a second vascular bed without converting it to an IMP. Read in full rather than taken from the provider summary, because the species of the perturbed cells is what decides the evidence code.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Endogenous tagging plus IP-MS, so free of the over-expression artefact that weakens most interactome sources; but QuickGO shows it supplies 2872 GO:0005515 annotations, so any one edge remains a high-throughput call. Used here as the orthogonal confirmation behind the PRKAR2A MODIFY, not as standalone evidence. It does not carry the CTNNB1 or FHL1 rows, which are removed as uninformative generic binding.

title: Gravin, an autoantigen recognized by serum from myasthenia gravis patients, is a kinase scaffold protein.
review_notes: The decisive paper for this gene, and it is absent from the affinage record entirely - the provider's citation list starts in 1997 with PMID:9187136 and never reaches this one, presumably because the title names an autoimmune disease rather than a function. Found instead in the UniProt RN list. It is the only publication that maps both the PKA and the PKC determinant on the human protein, and it is the basis of UniProt's 266-557 PKC-binding region. PubMed record verified; the round-numbered PMID is a coincidence, not a placeholder.

title: Control of cytoskeletal architecture by the src-suppressed C kinase substrate, SSeCKS.
review_notes: Mouse NIH3T3 and an over-expression system, so the result is an IMP-class observation in rodent, not a human direct assay - relevant to the cytoskeleton and focal adhesion location rows but not usable as human evidence. Note this is an ectopic-expression phenotype: it shows what happens when the protein's level is raised, which is weaker evidence for a normal physiological process than for a localisation.

title: Involvement of the protein kinase C substrate, SSeCKS, in the actin-based stellate morphology of mesangial cells.
review_notes: Read for the cytoskeleton rows. Its observation that the network is distinct from F-actin is the reason no GO:0051015 actin filament binding term was proposed despite the co-sedimentation result in PMID:12083796 - the two findings from the same laboratory are in tension and the question was recorded rather than resolved.

title: Alternative splicing regulates the subcellular localization of A-kinase anchoring protein 18 isoforms.
review_notes: Full text cached. Establishes the isoform-specific locations, and that gamma is cytosolic - which matters because gamma is a separate UniProt entry.

title: AKAP proteins anchor cAMP-dependent protein kinase to KvLQT1/IsK channel complex.
review_notes: Abstract-only; publisher full text returned 403. A heterologous reconstitution in which AKAP15/18 is one of three interchangeable AKAPs. The four IDA rows from it are kept but marked non-core, and the action-potential row is UNDECIDED because the abstract reports currents only.

title: A novel leucine zipper targets AKAP15 and cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinase to the C terminus of the skeletal muscle Ca2+ channel and modulates its function.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Not cited by any GO annotation on this gene; surfaced by the affinage record. The defining mechanistic paper for AKAP15 in skeletal muscle.

title: Beta-adrenergic regulation requires direct anchoring of PKA to cardiac CaV1.2 channels via a leucine zipper interaction with A kinase-anchoring protein 15.
review_notes: Full text cached. Not cited by any GO annotation on this gene; found by an independent PubMed search. Grounds the NEW molecular adaptor row. Its peptide-disruption result conflicts with the genetic knockout in PMID:23035250.

title: The A-kinase anchoring protein 15 regulates feedback inhibition of the epithelial Na+ channel.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Cited by UniProt but by no GO annotation. A single heterologous study of a PKA-independent effect, so raised as a question rather than proposed as an annotation.

title: Cardiomyocytes from AKAP7 knockout mice respond normally to adrenergic stimulation.
review_notes: Abstract-only. A genetic negative that directly conflicts with the peptide-disruption result in PMID:14569017. Neither is wrong on its own terms; the conflict is recorded as a knowledge gap rather than resolved here.

title: AKAP18:PKA-RIIα structure reveals crucial anchor points for recognition of regulatory subunits of PKA.
review_notes: Full text cached. Structural evidence for RII binding on this entry's own beta isoform; grounds the GO:0034237 refinement.

title: Targeted deletion of AKAP7 in dentate granule cells impairs spatial discrimination.
review_notes: Full text cached. The mouse ortholog carries synaptic-transmission terms from this paper by IDA and IMP; human does not - recorded as a curation gap.

title: A novel lipid-anchored A-kinase Anchoring Protein facilitates cAMP-responsive membrane events.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The cloning paper; source of the PKA-binding IDA and the curator's localization inference.

title: AKAP15 anchors cAMP-dependent protein kinase to brain sodium channels.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Supports AKAP15 as a channel-associated PKA anchor beyond CaV1; not used to ground any annotation.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AKAP7 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates passed. Unusually strong recall here: it surfaced the CaV1.1 leucine-zipper paper, the knockout negative and the mossy-fiber work, none cited by GOA. One trap it does not flag: much of its narrative - the 2H phosphoesterase activity, RNase L antiviral function, and USP4/SERCA2 in the heart - belongs to the long gamma/delta isoforms in UniProt Q9P0M2, and must not be read onto this entry. None of that is imported here.

title: UniProtKB O43687 (AKAP7_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: Machine-fetched. Establishes the isoform scope of the entry under review.

title: A-kinase-interacting protein localizes protein kinase A in the nucleus.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The discovery paper; grounds the catalytic-subunit binding refinement and the nuclear location.

title: Breast cancer-associated gene 3 (BCA3) is a novel Rac1-interacting protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only. A single study in osteoclasts; recorded as a question rather than annotated.

title: AKIP1 enhances NF-kappaB-dependent gene expression by promoting the nuclear retention and phosphorylation of p65.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The paper UniProt cites with an experimental evidence code for AKIP1's NF-kappaB function, yet cited by no GO annotation. It supplies the direct p65 contact, which with the catalytic-subunit binding grounds the signaling adaptor row.

title: A-kinase-interacting protein 1 (AKIP1) acts as a molecular determinant of PKA in NF-kappaB signaling.
review_notes: Full text cached. The best-characterized function. Not cited by any GO annotation; it is what shows the InterPro mapping chose the wrong NF-kappaB branch.

title: A kinase interacting protein (AKIP1) is a key regulator of cardiac stress.
review_notes: Full text cached. The mitochondrial localization is shown in rat myocytes and is curated for no species; given the modest rodent-human conservation it is recorded as a knowledge gap rather than added.

title: AKIP1 promotes early recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma through activating the Wnt/β-catenin/CBP signaling pathway.
review_notes: Abstract-only. A single cancer-cell study; recorded as a question rather than annotated.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Full text cached. Source of one generic protein-binding row (FHL2).

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Source of three generic protein-binding rows (FGFR3, GSN and the uncharacterised GW128).

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Full text cached, but AKIP1 is never named in the text - its data are supplementary. Supports PDZ domain binding as what was measured; these are peptide-domain affinities, not cellular interactions.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AKIP1 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates passed; a wide and accurate summary that surfaced the NF-kappaB, mitochondrial, Rac1 and beta-catenin papers, none cited by GOA.

title: Akirins are highly conserved nuclear proteins required for NF-kappaB-dependent gene expression in drosophila and mice.
review_notes: Full relevant Results/Discussion read. Direct human HsAkirin1 nuclear localization is supported; fly immune rescue used HsAkirin2, and mouse Akirin1-null MEFs retained tested cytokine responses. This does not directly establish a human AKIRIN1 NF-kappaB mechanism.

title: Mighty is a novel promyogenic factor in skeletal myogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract only; full article unavailable. Supports earlier C2C12 cell-cycle exit and enhanced myogenesis. MGI maps both negative satellite terms to this paper; related Dyer primary thesis corroborates reserve-cell interpretation, but is not substituted for the journal full text.

title: Akirin1 (Mighty), a novel promyogenic factor regulates muscle regeneration and cell chemotaxis.
review_notes: Abstract and publisher preview checked; complete article unavailable. Exact mouse Akirin1 source supports macrophage/myoblast chemotaxis, PI3K-dependent actin reorganization and lamellipodia; not a direct human experiment.

title: Myostatin suppression of Akirin1 mediates glucocorticoid-induced satellite cell dysfunction.
review_notes: Full Methods/Results read. Direct Akirin1 overexpression is in C2C12 myoblasts under dexamethasone, whereas satellite-cell and upstream myostatin experiments are separate. Positive proliferation in this condition does not refute earlier withdrawal in another condition.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Cache full-text flag overstates coverage (mainly Introduction/Discussion). Exact IntAct records independently verify AKIRIN1-GOPC binary two-hybrid interactions from this paper; no protein-containing-complex binding assay established.

title: Role of Akirin1 in the regulation of skeletal muscle fiber-type switch.
review_notes: Abstract only. Mouse Akirin1 promoter-reporter and fiber-type phenotypes support transcriptional/muscle function despite an outwardly normal knockout; physical mechanism remains limited.

title: AKIRIN2 controls the nuclear import of proteasomes in vertebrates.
review_notes: Abstract only: AKIRIN2 nuclear proteasome import. Existing UniProt AKIRIN1 curation explicitly contrasts that activity. Not evidence for a new AKIRIN1 proteasome-binding annotation or universal absence of contacts.

title: miR-224 activates cancer-associated fibroblasts to enhance lung cancer cell migration and invasion by targeting Akirin1.
review_notes: Full relevant Methods/Results checked. Human/mouse models coexist, but the Akirin1 cDNA and perturbation/rescue in lung fibroblast-cancer coculture are mouse. Cancer-cell movement in coculture does not contradict macrophage cell-autonomous chemotaxis.

title: CircEPDR1 regulates proliferation and differentiation of goat skeletal muscle satellite cells through miR-345-3p/Akirin1 axis.
review_notes: Full relevant Methods/Results read. Direct goat Akirin1 overexpression reduces proliferation readouts while promoting differentiation; miRNA cotransfection modifies the effect. Gene-specific experiment distinguished from upstream circRNA manipulations.

Full study uses repeated Y2H screens and pairwise retesting, not a single experiment. ALDH4A1-RBBP4 pairing is recorded in the seeded assertion/UniProt (NbExp=3); the exact supplementary pair result was not independently recovered. title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Cached full PMC8664129 main text inspected, including subtractive/spatial proteomics and importomics. Exact ALDH4A1 supplementary entry not separately inspected; retained HTP is curator-deferred and concordant with independent HPA/P5CDH compartment evidence. No mitochondrial-matrix specificity is inferred from this broad row.

title: Structure of mitochondrial pyruvate carrier and its inhibition mechanism.
review_notes: Cached full PMC12043432 Methods/Results inspected: co-expressed human MPC1/MPC2 in HEK293 cells, affinity purification and nanobody/Legobody-assisted structures define their translocation pathway. This preparation is not a controlled test of native ALDH4A1 occupancy; failure to model ALDH4A1 does not refute accessory association. Endogenous host proteins cannot be declared absent merely because their transgenes were not co-expressed.

title: Structures and mechanism of the human mitochondrial pyruvate carrier.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract and Nature publisher record (DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-08873-8) inspected. Six human MPC structures support a heterodimeric alternating-access pathway; full Methods were not recovered here. This source does not directly test ALDH4A1 association or transporter activation.

title: Biochemical genetic analysis of human and rodent aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH).
review_notes: Primary PubMed abstract verified on 2026-09-27 at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4015840/ . Original CACAO page https://gowiki.tamu.edu/wiki/index.php/PMID:4015840 records AL4A1 annotation 8806 from Table 1 gel assays with propionaldehyde or benzaldehyde. Full primary table remains unavailable; exact isozyme attribution is not independently confirmed. The broad source claim is curator-deferred. The identifier and curator record are verified, but the exact primary support for this isozyme remains unverified. Retain the broad experimental assay as non-core; independent GSA evidence in PMID:22516612 does not reassign this reference to a different substrate.

title: ALDH4A1 functions as an active component of the MPC complex maintaining mitochondrial pyruvate import for TCA cycle entry and tumour suppression.
review_notes: Cached full PMC12188464 and Nature primary record (DOI 10.1038/s41556-025-01651-8) inspected. Figures 5-7 and Extended Data 8 provide human-cell association/rescue, recombinant complex formation, and increased MPC1-MPC2 proteoliposome transport upon WT/S352L addition. These establish a bounded noncatalytic contribution beyond loss phenotypes. Reconstitution Methods specify PC/cardiolipin and lipid:protein ratio but do not clearly establish identical incorporated MPC amount/orientation for every comparison; apparent unit/residue typos are not silently repaired. Native occupancy/stoichiometry and the detailed enhancement mechanism remain open. Separate two-subunit structures and lack of a second report are not a documented scientific dispute, so the supported source is VERIFIED rather than DISPUTED. This assessment supports the measured binding and transport enhancement used for GO:0141109; it does not endorse the paper's uncorroborated universal third-subunit framing.

title: Structure of human mitochondrial pyruvate carrier MPC1 and MPC2 complex.
review_notes: Cached full PMC12280002 inspected: human MPC1/MPC2 co-expression, 1:1 purified heterodimer, MBP/DARPin-assisted structural preparation and yeast growth rescue. Supports the two-subunit transport pathway, without testing whether accessory ALDH4A1 associates in native human mitochondria. Do not equate the engineered preparation with a quantitative exclusion assay.

title: Cloning, characterization, and expression of cDNAs encoding human delta 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract inspected: two human cDNAs encode the same protein and complement activity/proline growth in deficient yeast; matrix localization is explicitly stated. Full primary Methods were not recovered. The TAS assertions are retained at the scope of this accessible evidence.

title: Mutations in the Delta1-pyrroline 5-carboxylate dehydrogenase gene cause type II hyperprolinemia.
review_notes: The exact source6 normal record supplies the primary title, DOI 10.1093/hmg/7.9.1411 and abstract. Local access is abstract-only.

title: ALDH4A1 converts 1PYR-3OH-5COOH to 4-OH-L-glutamate
review_notes: Cached human reaction summary identifies mitochondrial ALDH4A1 in the NAD+-dependent hydroxyproline-catabolic reaction. Supports pathway chemistry; matrix location is the preserved curated assertion corroborated independently by UniProt and the original P5CDH paper.

title: ALDH4A1 oxidises L-GluSS to Glu
review_notes: Cached human reaction summary identifies ALDH4A1 oxidation of GSA/NAD+ to glutamate/NADH and dimeric enzyme. Supports the catalytic pathway and mitochondrial compartment; separate matrix evidence is explicit in the human primary abstract and UniProt.

title: ALDH4A1 oxidizes 1PYR-3OH-5COOH
review_notes: Cached human reaction summary identifies the hydroxylated pyrroline-derived substrate and erythro-hydroxyglutamate product with ALDH4A1 as catalyst. This is curated pathway evidence, not an independently inspected historical patient assay.

title: UniProt P30038 ALDH4A1 record
review_notes: Immutable fetched human UniProt record inspected for identity, catalytic reaction, matrix localization, dimeric assembly, interaction count and three alternative products. Curated reaction/location evidence is distinguished from newly inspected primary experiments.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: GOA identifies InterPro2GO mappings for the SSADH family and aldehyde-dehydrogenase domains. Their broader MF assertions are refined using human substrate/cofactor measurements; the current mapping predicates were not independently reconstructed.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
