title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: GOA combines named electronic sources. RHEA/EC and UniProt location/pathway assertions were checked in the cached human record; the ARBA predicate set was not inspected.

title: Pharmacologic rescue of lethal seizures in mice deficient in succinate semialdehyde dehydrogenase.
review_notes: The recovered cached primary abstract was read. Mouse GO-CAM 68d5ebd600002976 uses this IMP reference for Aldh5a1 catalysis and GABA-shunt participation. The knockout study reports increased GABA/GHB in urine, brain and liver, lethal seizures, and pharmacologic rescue. These mouse metabolic and neurological phenotypes corroborate the donor pathway context; they do not replace direct human enzyme measurements. The complete paper remains unavailable.

title: Therapeutic intervention in mice deficient for succinate semialdehyde dehydrogenase (gamma-hydroxybutyric aciduria).
review_notes: The recovered cached primary abstract was read; MouseMine resolves MGI J:125589 to this mouse treatment study. Interventions extend survival, and high-dose vigabatrin raises brain GABA without a parallel decrease in GHB. These are treatment/metabolite observations, not a resolved succinate-flux assay. Source provenance is verified; human succinate-metabolism participation rests independently on the measured product-forming reaction. Full text remains unavailable.

title: Structure of human succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase gene: identification of promoter region and alternatively processed isoforms.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract read. Human gene/transcript analysis and natural variants support SSADH identity and its NAD+-dependent GABA-catabolic reaction. Alternative-polyadenylation reporter results do not establish functional equivalence of all protein isoforms. Full text not recovered.

title: Mutational spectrum of the succinate semialdehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH5A1) gene and functional analysis of 27 novel disease-causing mutations in patients with SSADH deficiency.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract read. Human variant expression supports SSADH activity. The reported below-5% result explicitly has one exception among missense alleles judged causative, while six other variants did not strongly affect activity. Full text not recovered; no universal severity claim.

title: Integrated analysis of protein composition, tissue diversity, and gene regulation in mouse mitochondria.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract read. Mouse mitochondrial proteomics is the source of the Aldh5a1 compartment assertion in MGI/GO-CAM. The abstract does not expose the individual protein entry, so it verifies study scope and donor provenance rather than re-identifying a peptide. Full text not recovered.

title: Proton MR spectroscopy in succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract read. This is a human MRS case report showing elevated GABA and traces of GHB in brain, corroborating pathway disruption rather than directly assaying enzyme chemistry. Full text not recovered.

title: High-level expression and characterization of the recombinant enzyme, and tissue distribution of human succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract read. Human brain cDNA expressed in E. coli yields an active purified enzyme, substrate/NAD+ kinetics, and an apparent homotetramer. Supports catalytic and assembly claims directly; full text not recovered.

title: Altered cerebral glucose and acetate metabolism in succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase-deficient mice: evidence for glial dysfunction and reduced glutamate/glutamine cycling.
review_notes: The recovered cached primary abstract was read alongside the prior primary PubMed/publisher assessment. MGI J:128716 is the mouse glutamate-process IMP source. The study measures cerebral glucose/acetate isotope incorporation and cortical metabolite pools in 17-day-old deficient and wild-type mice. This is pathway physiology, not direct glutamate turnover by SSADH. Its introductory NADP-dependent wording does not report a cofactor assay and cannot override direct human NAD+ enzymology. Full text remains unavailable.

title: Redox-switch modulation of human SSADH by dynamic catalytic loop.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract and externally indexed original PMC2670868 Results/Methods read. Supports human structures and catalytic/redox assays. The ligand structures contain SSA and the visible ADP moiety of NAD+, not succinate product and a separate ADP cofactor. Cell redox work uses overexpression, oxidant treatment and lysate assays; physiological neural flux remains a question. Local cache is abstract-only.

review_notes: Cached human mitochondrial phosphoproteomics abstract and Discussion read. The metadata flag is true, but the local extraction lacks the individual ALDH5A1 table and much of the experimental body. Citation/study identity is verified; the gene-specific HDA record is retained by curator deference plus independent localization evidence, not claimed as re-extracted.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Cached full human MitoCoP study read. Supports the source and methods of the curated mitochondrial inventory. The specific supplementary ALDH5A1 entry was not independently extracted; general proteome-size statements are not gene-specific proof. Independent human SSADH location supports acceptance.

review_notes: Cached primary abstract read. Bacterial activity and purified brain sequence validate rat SSADH; human liver cDNA clones and sequence comparison support transfer. Later human recombinant assays corroborate it. Do not assign the original rat expression experiment to human protein. Full text not recovered.

title: Two exon-skipping mutations as the molecular basis of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (4-hydroxybutyric aciduria).
review_notes: Cached abstract plus the original institutional PDF read: https://art.torvergata.it/retrieve/e291c0d3-7a76-cddb-e053-3a05fe0aa144/Chambliss_AJHG_1998.pdf . title: ALDH5A1 dehydrogenates SUCCSA to SUCCA

title: UniProtKB P51649 (SSDH_HUMAN), Succinate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase, mitochondrial
review_notes: Machine UniProt P51649 record read, including reaction RHEA:13217, mitochondrial targeting, homotetramer, pathway, two alternative products and variant annotations. The record is preserved verbatim; its bibliography is not treated as a substitute for primary-source reading.

review_notes: Cached PMID/title and primary abstract support ALDH7A1 mutation-associated AASA/P6C dehydrogenase loss and PLP adduct chemistry. Local cache is abstract-only and full assay details were not recovered. The finding is scoped to the studied mutations, not every pathogenic variant.

title: Non-P450 aldehyde oxidizing enzymes: the aldehyde dehydrogenase superfamily.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping verified in the source12 audit and exact abstract-only review record read. It summarizes the human aldehyde-dehydrogenase superfamily. Family-wide catalytic/noncatalytic roles, xenobiotic activity, embryogenesis and UV absorption are not assigned to ALDH7A1 without target-specific evidence. title: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 7A1 (ALDH7A1) is a novel enzyme involved in cellular defense against hyperosmotic stress.
review_notes: Cached identifier/title and abstract verified; external full primary PMC2881771 Results, Table 1 and Figures 3–5 were read through indexed PMC searches. Human recombinant substrate assays, human HUVEC nuclear staining and human v1 expression in CHO cells are distinct from mouse tissue fractionation. Structural substrate placement includes docking; it is not all experimentally bound substrate. Local cache remains abstract-only.

title: Genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy (ALDH7A1 deficiency).
review_notes: Cached full Methods and clinical results support genotype-associated AASA accumulation. The original AASA enzyme assignment is also discussed from earlier work; this study is not described here as a fresh purified-enzyme kinetic assay.

title: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 7A1 (ALDH7A1) attenuates reactive aldehyde and oxidative stress induced cytotoxicity.
review_notes: Cached full primary Methods/Results support human-enzyme aldehyde oxidation and human-protein cytoprotection in CHO cells. The recombinant 4HNE assay requires BME reactivation under the tested conditions; the chemical assay and heterologous-cell survival results are distinguished.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: Cached full human liver interactome supports the study identity and interaction-screen context. The seeded EPS8 partner is preserved; removing generic protein binding does not deny this interaction or assume screen contamination.

review_notes: Cached full primary main article and indexed PMC record support EPS-urine exosome-enrichment proteomics. Supplemental Table 2 is identified, but the ALDH7A1/P49419 target row was not recovered. Reference identity is verified; target-level localization support remains unresolved, with no contamination inference.

title: Identification of a novel biomarker for pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy: Implications for newborn screening.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping verified in the source12 identity audit and exact abstract-only record read. The study identifies accumulated 6-oxo-pipecolate in human PDE samples and an isotope-standard LC-MS/MS assay, including persistence in urine at room temperature. The full body was not read in this closure; detailed provider-reported concentrations and diagnostic-performance claims are not independently adopted. Biomarker accumulation is not ALDH7A1-catalyzed synthesis of that metabolite.

title: Structural and biochemical consequences of pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy mutations that target the aldehyde binding site of aldehyde dehydrogenase ALDH7A1.
review_notes: Cached full Methods, kinetics and structures read. Human AASA/NAD+ assays resolve variant-dependent impairment, with residual activity in several mutants; G174V could not be purified. Abstract efficiency ratios are rounded relative to the detailed table.

title: ALDH7A1 inhibits the intracellular transport pathways during hypoxia and starvation to promote cellular energy homeostasis.
review_notes: Cached full primary Results and Methods show direct BARS interaction, COPI reconstitution, catalytic E268Q and BARS G172E controls, and Golgi/liposome NADH generation. Main cellular studies use HeLa, with selected replication elsewhere. Independently read fractionation shows membrane recruitment; the precise plasma-membrane assertion retains curated-source attribution. A construct UniProt isoform accession was not independently resolved.

title: Structural analysis of pathogenic mutations targeting Glu427 of ALDH7A1, the hot spot residue of pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy.
review_notes: Cached full source assays human Glu427 variants with AASA/NAD+ and examines NAD+ geometry and oligomerization. The resulting catalytic defect is experimentally measured; NAD+ occupancy alone is not treated as catalysis.

title: Impact of missense mutations in the ALDH7A1 gene on enzyme structure and catalytic function.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping verified in the source12 audit; full cached structural/biochemical review read. It explicitly distinguishes 539-residue isoform-1/HGVS numbering from the 28-residue-shorter structural convention. It summarizes variant-specific effects, including relatively retained activity for some active-site variants and impaired tetramer formation for several interface variants. These are a synthesis of original studies, not a new experiment on all alleles. It corroborates the existing human chemistry/assembly interpretation without transferring every variant effect or changing the seeded isoform records.

title: Untargeted metabolomics and infrared ion spectroscopy identify biomarkers for pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy.
review_notes: Primary PubMed title/DOI and abstract rechecked. The local record is abstract-only despite a PMC identifier. Human plasma/brain and dried-bloodspot biomarker observations are distinct from accumulation in Aldh7a1-knockout mouse brain and epilepsy-like behavior in a zebrafish model. These findings concern 2-OPP/6-oxoPIP identification and possible downstream toxicity; they do not establish that ALDH7A1 makes the biomarkers or directly performs a new neuronal process. No full Methods or supplementary assay claim is made.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Cached full main study supports the MitoCoP identity and mitochondrial-proteomics method. The target supplementary entry was not independently recovered. Existing HTP mitochondrial localization is corroborated by independent target experiments, without asserting a peptide count or matrix resolution.

title: Metabolomics analysis of antiquitin deficiency in cultured human cells and plasma: Relevance to pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy.
review_notes: Cached full primary Methods/Results read: two selected exon-2 human neural-progenitor knockout clones accumulate PA and AASA/P6C in lysine-containing media. Broader metabolomic changes include indirect effects and are not automatically direct ALDH7A1 processes. The revised result quote is from Results rather than the introductory pathway statement.

title: New Therapeutic Approaches to Inherited Metabolic Pediatric Epilepsies.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping verified in the source12 audit and exact abstract-only record read. This is a therapeutic overview of inherited metabolic epilepsies, despite the automated broad publication-type classification. Its abstract discusses dietary, enzyme and gene-directed approaches generally, without exposing an ALDH7A1-specific treatment experiment. The full body was not read here; the provider narrative is not promoted to evidence that ALDH7A1 replacement or editing was tested successfully.

title: Utility and limitations of EEG in the diagnosis and management of ALDH7A1-related pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy. A retrospective observational study.
review_notes: Primary PubMed title/DOI identity verified and full cached Methods/Results read. This is a retrospective Norwegian human cohort: 13 patients, 163 EEGs and variable acute pyridoxine responses. Twelve patients were genetically confirmed; the deceased older sibling was clinically assigned. The recordings span different eras/protocols, with some available only as written reports. Diagnostic-response observations do not establish an additional molecular function or prove that every ALDH7A1 genotype shares one neurodevelopmental trajectory.

title: Biochemical, structural, and computational analyses of two new clinically identified missense mutations of ALDH7A1.
review_notes: Cached full recombinant-protein kinetics, solution oligomerization and structures read. R134S and R441C use mature-protein numbering, corresponding to HGVS Arg162 and Arg469. The source supports catalytic impairment and a tetramer defect specifically for R134S.

title: Case report: Early (molecular) diagnosis is the clue: report on ALDH7A1 deficiency in newborns.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping verified in the source12 audit; full cached Case report, molecular analysis and biomarker discussion read. This single human newborn has two segregating truncating alleles. The reported analytical problem is levetiracetam masking the urinary 6-oxo-PIP peak in the employed GC-MS method. That source-specific interference does not invalidate every assay for the biomarker. Genotyping, clinical response and follow-up are distinct from direct enzyme measurements; no new substrate or developmental activity is inferred.

title: Case report: Clinical and genetic characterization of a novel ALDH7A1 variant causing pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy, developmental delay, and intellectual disability in two siblings.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping verified in the source12 audit; full cached Methods, family results and clinical discussion read. Two human siblings carry homozygous p.Gly390Arg, identified by exome analysis and segregation with computational pathogenicity assessment. The source explicitly states that alpha-AASA testing was inaccessible. Seizure control and developmental outcomes are observed clinically; the inspected work does not measure purified mutant activity or prove a particular folding/oligomerization defect. It is retained as disease context rather than new functional evidence.

title: Precision diagnosis and treatment of vitamin metabolism-related epilepsy.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping is verified; full cached clinical review and its ALDH7A1 section were read. The ALDH7A1 subsection switches to ALDH4A1 in its treatment paragraph and uses inconsistent metabolite names, including piperonylic acid in the lysine-pathway caption. These secondary-source wording problems are not adopted as target mechanism. The section is useful clinical context, but proposed glial/neurogenesis roles and broad therapeutic claims are not new experiments. DISPUTED is limited to the identified mechanistic/gene-attribution wording, not the identifier or all disease observations.

title: ALDH7A1 protects against ferroptosis by generating membrane NADH and regulating FSP1.
review_notes: Cached primary abstract verified; indexed full PMC12085291 Results, Figures 1–6 and Methods independently read. Reconstitution separates ALDH7A1 aldehyde oxidation/NADH production from FSP1 quinone reduction, with additional FSP1 recruitment. Main experiments include human cell lines; results are not generalized to every tissue. Local cache remains abstract-only. Curated plasma-membrane placement is distinguished from the total-membrane fractionation independently read.

title: An ancient conserved gene expressed in the human inner ear: identification, expression analysis, and chromosomal mapping of human and mouse antiquitin (ATQ1).
review_notes: Live PubMed identity and abstract verified; original publisher full text was not recovered. Human fetal cochlear/tissue expression and rat hair-cell transcript measurements support the source identity and hypothesis, but the complete TAS hearing claim remains unresolved.

title: ALDH7A1 oxidises BETALD to BET
review_notes: Cached reaction explicitly assigns ALDH7A1 the betaine-aldehyde oxidation step in mitochondria. A valid additional substrate activity and curated matrix context; not a direct measurement of normal human flux.

title: Choline catabolism
review_notes: Cached pathway places aldehyde oxidation within choline-to-betaine catabolism. ALDH7A1 performs that reaction, so pathway participation is direct despite its secondary physiological scope.

title: alpha-aminoadipoate semialdehyde + NAD+ => alpha-aminoadipate + NADH + H+
review_notes: Cached summary and live primary Reactome event checked. Current catalyst is an ALDH7A1 tetramer in mitochondrial matrix; the older narrative retains a homodimer statement that is not used over the later human solution/structure evidence. Reaction identity and core compartment are supported.

title: Crystal structure of human muscle aldolase complexed with fructose 1,6-bisphosphate: mechanistic implications.

GOA cites it only as an NAS source for the enzymatic activity, which understates it: it is the gene-defining paper for this protein and the direct evidence behind the proposed GO:0009897 annotation.

It correctly grades most cofactor and localisation claims for this gene as family inference rather than direct evidence, which matches the ISS codes used on the proposed metal-binding annotations. Its structural and enzymological claims were checked against the primary literature and UniProt.

The finding is about how ALPI is regulated rather than about what ALPI does, and it rests on a single cell line, which is why the annotation is kept as non-core.

title: Sequence and characterization of the human intestinal alkaline phosphatase gene.
review_notes: The gene-defining paper for ALPI: complete genomic sequence, 11-exon structure, promoter characterisation, and the demonstration that intron positions are shared across the intestinal, placental and liver/bone/kidney genes. Cited in GOA only as an NAS source for the enzymatic activity, but its lasting value is in establishing the common ancestry and chromosomal arrangement that make isozyme misattribution such a persistent hazard in this family.

title: Human ALPI deficiency causes inflammatory bowel disease and highlights a key mechanism of gut homeostasis.
review_notes: The single most informative paper on human ALPI, and conspicuously absent from GOA's annotation set for this gene. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in two unrelated patients cause severe inflammatory bowel disease; every variant was reconstituted in HEK293T cells and shown to impair stability, dimerization, catalytic activity, surface expression or GPI anchoring, LPS dephosphorylating activity was measured directly, ALPI staining was reduced in patient biopsies, and faecal ALPI activity was undetectable in the deficient patient. Full text available and verified. Four of the five proposed new annotations rest on it.

title: Pathogenesis of Cardiomyopathy Caused by Variants in ALPK3, an Essential Pseudokinase in the Cardiomyocyte Nucleus and Sarcomere.
review_notes: Primary identifier and DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.122.059688 verified. Full PMC Methods, Results and Figures 2-6 read. Human isogenic cardiomyocytes, mouse knockout and human tissue show myomesin mislocalization and sarcomere disruption. Tagged ALPK3 in human cardiomyocytes localizes to M bands and nuclear envelope; HEK293T co-IP supports MYOM2 association, while MYOM1 co-IP was negative despite colocalization. Cellular catalytic-cleft mutations and overexpression support the pseudokinase interpretation, but do not establish absence of catalysis under every biochemical condition. PMID:39196058 reports a conflicting positive domain assay. Historical residue numbers use the article sequence rather than current 1705-aa UniProt coordinates. Primary access route: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9698156/ . The normal publication record is now cached and its actual contents were independently read. Actual extracted Methods, relevant Results/Figures and Discussion read: isogenic human hiPSC-CMs with truncations, G1777E/D1784A dual-cleft and D1774A single-cleft variants; cellular phosphoproteomics and HEK293T overexpression support a noncatalytic model within those conditions. Tagged ALPK3 is at M-bands and predominantly nuclear envelope in these models; endogenous antibody specificity is problematic. MYOM2 co-IP is positive in HEK293T, while MYOM1 co-IP is negative despite colocalization. Mouse knockout supplies separate in-vivo structural evidence. Cellular negative phosphoproteomics does not universally disprove a biochemical activity under other conditions.

title: ALPK3 Functions as a Pseudokinase.
review_notes: Primary identifier and DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.123.065993 verified. Full PMC research letter and Figure 1 read. Recombinant mouse ALPK3 residues 1339-1608 fail to phosphorylate heat-inactivated rat H9c2 or human cardiomyocyte lysates containing SQSTM1; mouse TRPM7 is a positive control. Mouse K1420R knock-in retains cardiac function and SQSTM1 phosphosignal. These negative results are substantive but concern a mouse isolated domain and a mouse mutation, rather than every full-length human context. They conflict with PMID:39196058; neither a proven contaminant nor universal inactivity is asserted. Primary access route: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10697696/ . The normal publication record is now cached and its actual contents were independently read. Entire actual experimental research-letter body and Figure 1 caption read, despite its short format/no PubMed abstract: murine ALPK3 domain 1339–1608, murine TRPM7 positive control, heat-inactivated rat H9c2/human hiPSC-CM lysates and radiolabeled ATP; no ALPK3 activity under tested conditions. Mouse K1420R preserves adult cardiac function and SQSTM1 T269/S272 ratio. Modeled nucleotide pockets are not measured binding. This is real negative evidence, not a universal inactivity proof.

Bacterially expressed His-tagged ALPK3 domain, reported residues 1577-1828, increases lysate phosphopeptides after irreversible endogenous-kinase inhibition. The SQSTM1-HA assay uses HEK293FT immunoprecipitates, active versus heat-denatured domain and phosphatase controls; it is not a wholly purified two-protein reaction. Positive phosphorylation evidence is retained, while intrinsic activity and the combined T269/S272 readout remain unresolved against PMID:38048395. Neither host-cell species nor old residue numbering is silently equated to a current canonical construct. Primary access route: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11358020/ . The normal publication record is now cached and its actual contents were independently read. Actual Methods, relevant Results/Figures and Discussion read: human tagged hPSC cardiomyocytes and mouse W1538X models; live tagged localization supports M-band and lacks a detected nuclear signal in that model. Recombinant domain 1577–1828 is expressed in E. coli BL21 and Ni-NTA purified. CM lysates are treated with fluorosulfonylbenzoyladenosine and dialyzed before addition of recombinant domain versus water. The targeted assay uses SQSTM1-HA immunoprecipitated from HEK293FT, active versus heat-denatured domain and lambda-phosphatase controls. These are positive kinase results that must be retained; the target is not a purified two-protein system and T269/S272 antibody does not isolate the residue class. Recombinant-domain species is not assigned merely from the bacterial or human host. Cellular proteomic changes include downstream effects.

title: Mitochondrial TNAP controls thermogenesis by hydrolysis of phosphocreatine.
review_notes: Primary identity and actual full Methods/Results read. Commercial recombinant human TNAP (R&D 2909-AP) directly hydrolyzes phosphocreatine at 37 degrees C, pH 7.8, with substrate kinetics. Detailed mitochondrial APEX/protease-protection/fractionation and thermogenic-flux physiology use mouse TNAP/adipocytes and mice. Thus human phosphocreatine chemistry is direct, whereas human tissue targeting is not newly established. This corrects the prior blanket mouse-only characterization without assigning human mitochondrial localization or thermogenesis as a new assertion.

title: Gene Therapy Using Recombinant AAV Type 8 Vector Encoding TNAP-D(10) Improves the Skeletal Phenotypes in Murine Models of Osteomalacia.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identity/title/DOI 10.1002/jbm4.10709 independently verified. The publication record is now cached; its actual available sections are described below. XML Methods, vector construction heading, mouse models, Results/Figures1-8 and relevant Discussion/CKD limits read. Methods explicitly identify human TNAP-D10 cDNA packaged in AAV8 using HEK293 cells. This human engineered mineral-targeted enzyme is tested in AlplPrx1/Prx1 and Phospho1-null mouse hosts with AAV8-GFP controls. Serum activity/PPi and skeletal morphology improve, while dentoalveolar changes are limited. No treatment-associated ectopic calcification increase was seen in the bounded observation window, including CKD challenge; this does not establish that native ALPL intrinsically inhibits nonskeletal mineralization or that lifetime treatment is risk-free. Construct identity is now resolved beyond the prior abstract-only assessment. The explicit human TNAP-D10 cDNA Methods resolves the prior abstract-only construct uncertainty. This is an engineered mineral-targeted human protein delivered to mouse hosts, not native human compartment localization. No increase in ectopic calcification over the tested short window is a treatment-safety result, not evidence that native ALPL inhibits non-skeletal mineralization.

title: TNAP dephosphorylates phosphocholine and phosphoethanolamine and participates in triglyceride transport from the liver to the bloodstream.

Growth rescue is consistent with choline availability but is not a direct labeled uptake measurement. Whole-animal fasting, metabolite and hepatic-lipid experiments are mouse; liver/blood ethanolamine was below NMR detection. The structures directly resolve metal sites and dimer organization; PC/PEA poses are docking, phosphate derives from crystallization and inhibitor cryo-EM supplies observed density. RCSB 9SH5 belongs to this study; 7YIV/7YIW are prior models. No TNAP membrane-transport MF is inferred.

title: Crystal structure of alkaline phosphatase from human placenta at 1.8 A resolution. Implication for a substrate specificity.

title: Mutation of a single amino acid converts germ cell alkaline phosphatase to placental alkaline phosphatase.
review_notes: Direct activity measurements on PLAP, GCAP, GCAP point mutants and GCAP/PLAP chimeras expressed in COS-1 cells. The key result -- that position 429 alone accounts for the differential L-leucine, EDTA and heat sensitivity that historically distinguished the two isozymes -- is what justifies treating ALPP and ALPG as separate functional entities despite their seven-residue difference. Correctly cited for both ALPP and ALPG.

A transcript survey in another species cannot be direct evidence of the human enzyme's catalytic activity, and the gene it tracks is the mouse embryonic AP rather than a human ALPP orthologue in any strict sense. The annotated term is nonetheless correct on other evidence, so the annotation was accepted and only the citation flagged.

Used here as the direct evidence for the proposed GO:0009897 annotation, since it shows both that the mature protein is glycolipid-anchored and that blocking the attachment traps it in the endoplasmic reticulum with little activity.

review_notes: Donor-side only. The IDA and IMP behind human AP2S1's GO:0048488 per QuickGO. Confirms that the human AP-2 sigma donor of this node carries its own experimental grounding, in endocytosis rather than TGN sorting -- the divergence that makes the general term correct at the node.

title: Recognition of dileucine-based sorting signals from HIV-1 Nef and LIMP-II by the AP-1 gamma-sigma1 and AP-3 delta-sigma3 hemicomplexes.
review_notes: The original yeast-three-hybrid demonstration that dileucine signals bind the gamma-sigma1 combination and not the analogous AP-2 or AP-4 combinations. The AP-4 negative is what makes the AP4S1 control in this review's bioinformatics meaningful. Verified against the cached full text; missed by affinage.

title: Crystal structure of the clathrin adaptor protein 1 core.
review_notes: Crystal structure of the AP-1 core. Directly establishes that sigma1 is an intact chain of the assembled complex and that AP-1 functions at the TGN, with Arf1 and PI-4-P as localisation determinants. Cited in GOA only as NAS, which understates it. Abstract-only in the cache, but every claim used is in the abstract.

title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of rhabdomyosarcoma cells reveal differential cellular gene expression in response to enterovirus 71 infection.
review_notes: Correctly identified, but a single-cell-line infection microarray in which 191 transcripts moved more than twofold and AP1S1 is not named in the abstract. Supports 'the transcript responds' and not 'the protein participates'. Projects to 20 distinct gene products in QuickGO.

title: Fab1p and AP-1 are required for trafficking of endogenously ubiquitylated cargoes to the vacuole lumen in S. cerevisiae.
review_notes: Donor-side only, and a good one: QuickGO records it as the IMP behind budding-yeast Aps1's GO:0006896, and the title confirms it is an AP-1 trafficking study rather than a generic one. Independent experimental grounding for an AP-1-clade donor of the IBD node.

title: Molecular determinants for the interaction between AMPA receptors and the clathrin adaptor complex AP-2.
review_notes: Donor-side only. The IDA/IMP/EXP evidence behind rat Ap2s1's GO:0098884 per QuickGO; title confirms an AP-2 cargo-interaction study. An AP-2-clade grounding.

title: The gamma/sigma1 and alpha/sigma2 hemicomplexes of clathrin adaptors AP-1 and AP-2 harbor the dileucine recognition site.
review_notes: The paper that settled which subunits carry the dileucine site, by expressing AP-1 and AP-2 subunits singly and as hemicomplexes. Establishes that gamma/sigma1 binds strongly while beta1/mu1 and the individual chains do not, which is what makes the contributes_to reading of the molecular function correct. Missed by the affinage report. Abstract-only in the cache; the quoted result is in the abstract.

title: Disruption of AP1S1, causing a novel neurocutaneous syndrome, perturbs development of the skin and spinal cord.
review_notes: The founding MEDNIK paper and UniProt's DISEASE source. Verified against the cached full text. Its zebrafish rescue is a clean loss-of-function demonstration in both directions: wild-type human AP1S1 mRNA rescues, the truncated form does not. Not used by GOA for any annotation on this gene.

title: Deletion mutants of AP-1 adaptin subunits display distinct phenotypes in fission yeast.
review_notes: Donor-side only, and the most on-point of the fungal donors: QuickGO records it as the IDA behind pombe vas2's GO:0042147 and GO:0099638, and it is explicitly a study of AP-1 adaptin subunit deletions. Grounds the deepest AP-1-clade donor of the node.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Bulk NK-cell membrane proteomics. Correctly cited but maximally generic: QuickGO returns 1142 annotations over 1142 distinct gene products for this reference, one per protein identified. The authors themselves note many recovered proteins are only transiently membrane-associated, which is sigma1A's case.

title: AP-1/sigma1B-adaptin mediates endosomal synaptic vesicle recycling, learning and memory.
review_notes: Titled for sigma1B but the source of the MGI IDA rows on mouse Ap1s1 that the Ensembl Compara presynapse and terminal-bouton transfers rest on, and its abstract makes a clear statement about sigma1A: the ubiquitous AP-1-sigma1A complex sorts between the TGN and early endosomes. Correctly cited. Abstract-only in the cache, which is precisely why the curator's sigma1A annotations are not second-guessed here.

title: AP17 and AP19, the mammalian small chains of the clathrin-associated protein complexes show homology to Yap17p, their putative homolog in yeast.
review_notes: The original cDNA characterisation of AP19, the small chain of AP-1, predicting a 158-residue protein of Mr 18,733 -- matching P61966 exactly. One correction to the affinage record, which presents this as human: the abstract states the clones came from rat and mouse brain libraries. Historical context only.

title: Endosomal and AP-3-dependent vacuolar trafficking routes make additive contributions to Candida albicans hyphal growth and pathogenesis.
review_notes: Donor-side only. The IMP behind C. albicans Aps3's GO:0006896 per QuickGO; title confirms AP-3-dependent vacuolar trafficking. A second, independent AP-3-clade grounding for the node.

title: Conservation and diversification of dileucine signal recognition by adaptor protein (AP) complex variants.
review_notes: Supplies the residue-level evidence used in this review: sigma1A V88D and I103S, homologous to sigma2 V88D and L103S, abolish signal binding, and sigma1A Arg 15 is the equivalent of sigma2 Arg 15. Also shows all three sigma1 isoforms recognise the signals, so the activity is shared across sigma1A/B/C rather than private to AP1S1. Verified against the cached full text; the residue positions were checked independently against the live P61966 sequence. Missed by affinage.

title: AP1S1 dileucine-site residue conservation analysis (this review)
review_notes: Analysis written for this review. Fetches nine AP-complex sigma subunits live from UniProt, asserts their lengths, and maps the structurally defined sigma2 dileucine pocket onto each. Confirms all five literature-named sigma1A positions and reproduces the homologies the literature states. Its most useful output is negative: the verified non-binder sigma4 retains the same 4/5 residues as the binders, so conservation at this pocket is not by itself evidence of the activity.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP1S1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated deep-research record whose own head-to-head self-evaluation scored pairwise = tie rather than win, tripping the trust gate; marked LOW_QUALITY on that basis and every claim taken from it was re-verified against its PMID. It does describe the right protein and found the disease and cell-biology literature well. Two errors: it presents PMID:2040623 as though the cDNA were human when the paper used rat and mouse brain libraries, and it states sigma1A nucleates a complex with Rabex-5 when PMID:27411398 explicitly reports Rabex-5 binds sigma1B and not sigma1A. It missed the entire dileucine literature and every structural paper, i.e. the whole molecular-function story. It is cited exactly once in this review, as the last of six supports for the structural core function, and only for the uncontested identity statement that AP1S1 is the small subunit of the Golgi-localized AP-1 complex -- a claim the five primary supports beside it already establish. It carries no mechanistic weight anywhere, which is the condition under which a LOW_QUALITY source can legitimately be cited at all.

No condition set is satisfied by this protein. The resulting term (GO:0005737) is nonetheless biologically true, so this is recorded as an untraceable propagation rather than a false annotation; marked UNVERIFIED because the trace could not be completed, not because the citation resolves to the wrong object.

review_notes: Correctly cited for AP-1 core architecture and TGN localization, but complex-level: the small chain in the structure is sigma1A, not sigma1B. title: Mutations in the gene encoding the Sigma 2 subunit of the adaptor protein 1 complex, AP1S2, cause X-linked mental retardation.
review_notes: The founding disease-gene paper for AP1S2, cited by UniProt for involvement in Pettigrew syndrome. Establishes loss-of-function as the mechanism. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Mutations in the AP1S2 gene encoding the sigma 2 subunit of the adaptor protein 1 complex are associated with syndromic X-linked mental retardation with hydrocephalus and calcifications in basal ganglia.
review_notes: Identifies AP1S2 as the Fried syndrome gene and establishes basal ganglia calcification as a recognisable feature. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Clinical, cellular, and neuropathological consequences of AP1S2 mutations: further delineation of a recognizable X-linked mental retardation syndrome.
review_notes: Carries the key negative cellular result for this review - patient fibroblasts lacking sigma1B show no AP-1 stability, localization or function defect - which is what makes the ubiquitous AP-1 process terms non-core for this isoform. Cached record is abstract-only, so the redundancy interpretation is quoted as the authors state it rather than re-derived.

title: AP-1/sigma1B-adaptin mediates endosomal synaptic vesicle recycling, learning and memory.
review_notes: The single most informative paper on sigma1B biology, full text available and read. Two caveats recorded in the notes: the AP-1 localization is by anti-gamma1 antibody, not an isoform-specific reagent, because the authors could not localize tagged sigma constructs; and all perturbations are in mouse, which is why the derived annotations are coded ISS.

title: Conservation and diversification of dileucine signal recognition by adaptor protein (AP) complex variants.
review_notes: Found by independent search, not returned by affinage. The only human experiment showing sigma1B assembling into AP-1 and not into AP-2, AP-3 or AP-4, and the only functional test of a sigma1B-containing hemicomplex against sorting signals. Also the source of the sigma-side residue numbers used in the residue_claims. Full text read.

title: Cell type-specific Rab32 and Rab38 cooperate with the ubiquitous lysosome biogenesis machinery to synthesize specialized lysosome-related organelles.

Two of those, platelet dense granule organization and melanosome assembly, are not supported by what the paper says: its only platelet sentence is an explicit prediction about Rab38, and its AP-1 experiments use pan-AP-1 reagents that cannot distinguish sigma isoforms. Reference projection: 178 annotations across 48 distinct gene products from five terms. Marked MISCITED for those two rows; the early endosome and vesicle-mediated transport rows it also supports are independently correct.

title: AP1S2 is mutated in X-linked Dandy-Walker malformation with intellectual disability, basal ganglia disease and seizures (Pettigrew syndrome).
review_notes: Unifies the separately named X-linked syndromes as one AP1S2 disorder and contributes the only reported non-truncating allele. Full text available and read.

title: Clinical, cellular, and neuropathological consequences of AP1S2 mutations: further delineation of a recognizable X-linked mental retardation syndrome.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. Three signatures are used on this gene and each was checked against AP2S1's own DR lines: IPR000804 (clathrin small-chain signature) and IPR016635 (AP complex small subunit) are family-wide and supply the generic transport and membrane-coat terms, while IPR027156 (APS2) is specific to the AP-2 sigma subunit and supplies GO:0035615 and GO:0072583. Every mapped term is true of AP2S1 and the subfamily-specific entry is not over-generalised.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Manual ISS transfer. Correctly identified, and the destination it reaches (plasma membrane) is right. Worth flagging that its source here, UniProtKB:P63010, is AP2B1 -- a co-complex subunit rather than a sequence orthologue or paralogue of sigma2 -- so the evidence code implies a similarity argument the relationship does not actually supply.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/GO_Central phylogenetic annotation. Traced to node PTN000204281 of PTHR11753 in the refreshed PAINT slice -- the family's only PTN node -- and all eleven gene-level donors were resolved individually. Because the seeds span AP-1, AP-2 and AP-3 sigma subunits acting in different vesicle pathways, the curator's choice of the vesicle-mediated-transport parent is the correct last common ancestor rather than an under-call.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location vocabulary mapping. Both terms used here were checked against the record: SL-0039 (Cell membrane) and SL-0162 (Membrane) are both carried by AP2S1's SUBCELLULAR LOCATION lines, and both map to the GO term actually used.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog transfer. The donor UniProtKB:P62743 was verified to be mouse Ap2s1, the 1:1 orthologue and the same subunit; human and mouse sigma2 are identical over all 142 residues, so the orthology step is as safe as it can be. What it delivers is nonetheless a tissue-restricted rather than a core location.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: GOC inter-ontology logical inference. Both rows it supplies here are location terms derived from process annotations (presynapse from GO:0048488, postsynapse from GO:0098884) rather than from any observation of the protein, so each is only as good as its input; both inputs are complex-level annotations of AP-2.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated IEA methods. The single row it supplies, GO:0030122, was traced to its ARBA component: ARBA00027293 was fetched from the UniProt endpoint and its firing condition set is FunFam 3.30.450.60:FF:000004 within Chordata, which AP2S1 satisfies exactly. Correctly applied.

title: Clathrin coat construction in endocytosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as a real and correctly-identified review, but it is a poor basis for the three UniProt TAS rows it uniquely supplies to AP2S1 (it is the only reference in GOA that projects to exactly one entity for these terms). The cached record is abstract-only and its abstract concerns the clathrin cage, the mu2 subunit and the alpha-appendage; the sigma subunit is not mentioned. Marked MISCITED specifically for GO:0030100 regulation of endocytosis, where the review is used to cast core endocytic machinery as a regulator of its own process.

title: A conserved clathrin assembly motif essential for synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the SynGO reference for the three GO:0048488 rows. Cited correctly, but the assayed material is AP-2 purified from bovine brain plus a peptide from the beta2 subunit, microinjected into squid giant synapse; sigma2 is not assayed individually. That is why the rows are kept as complex-level and non-core rather than challenged.

title: Molecular architecture and functional model of the endocytic AP2 complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the 2.6 A AP2 core structure in which sigma2 is one of the four resolved chains, so the ComplexPortal GO:0030122 projection genuinely speaks to this subunit. Cache is abstract-only.

title: The mu2 subunit of the clathrin adaptor AP-2 binds to FDNPVY and YppØ sorting signals at distinct sites.

title: Analysis of the AP-2 adaptor complex and cargo during clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the live-imaging study behind the coated-pit NEW row and behind the recorded tension over whether AP-2 travels in the budded vesicle. Cache is abstract-only, so the quotes used are abstract sentences that state the result directly.

title: A structural explanation for the binding of endocytic dileucine motifs by the AP2 complex.
review_notes: The decisive paper for this gene's molecular function and the one affinage missed. PubMed-verified by exact-title search on Europe PMC; the AP2-core/CD4-peptide co-crystal plus liposome-binding mutagenesis establishes that the dileucine motif's two leucines bind pockets built from sigma2 residues, with a YxxPhi/PtdIns(4,5)P2 specificity control. Every residue claim in this review traces to it. Note that the parent task brief cited PubMed:18497731 for this structure; that identifier resolves to an unrelated FAAH gene-variant paper.

title: AP2S1 sigma2 dileucine-pocket residue check and sigma-paralogue alignment
review_notes: Own analysis, reproducible from check_sigma2_pockets.py; all sequences fetched live from UniProt at run time and no result hardcoded. Confirms the eight pocket/patch residues in P53680, confirms that human, rat and mouse sigma2 are identical over the full chain so the rodent-structure numbering transfers exactly, and quantifies conservation across the eight human sigma paralogues.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP2S1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record; trust gates clear, self_evaluation_pairwise 'win', faith_pct 100.0, and the record describes the correct protein (P53680, sigma2). Used as a lead only. Two limits recorded: it never cites PMID:19140243, the structure paper that is the sole source for the pocket residues it alludes to via Nesbit, and it misses both AP-2 assembly chaperones (AAGAB, CCDC32) that explain the eight protein-binding rows. Its citation list also contains one non-numeric identifier, 'PMID:bio_10.1101_2024.07.22.24310683', which is a bioRxiv preprint and was not used. Its mechanism_profile GO ids were not imported; GO:0038024 cargo receptor activity in particular is defined for proteins that span membranes, which sigma2 does not.

title: UniProtKB P53680 (AP2S1_HUMAN) curated record
review_notes: The fetched Swiss-Prot record. Accession asserted to be the expected one, not a merged redirect: the file opens 'ID AP2S1_HUMAN Reviewed; 142 AA.' with 'AC P53680;' first. Used for the subunit composition, the coated-pit and cell-membrane locations, the PANTHER family assignment, the Arg15 variant features and the extracellular-calcium-homeostasis statement.

title: Assembly and function of AP-3 complexes in cells expressing mutant subunits.
review_notes: Full text verified. Supports the functional clathrin-box caveat using a beta3A/AP3B1 rescue assay; recorded as indirect for neuronal beta3B/AP3B2, because the clathrin-site mutant was beta3A.

title: A structure-based mechanism for initiation of AP-3 coated vesicle formation.
review_notes: Full text verified. Final PNAS paper superseding the preprint PMID:38895279 cited by the OpenScientist report; resolves AP-3 bound to Arf1 and cargo and supports an Arf1/cargo-driven coat-initiation model.

title: Architecture of clathrin-independent AP3:ARF1-coated carriers.
review_notes: Full text verified. Direct cryo-electron tomography and reconstitution paper showing that AP3:ARF1 can assemble cargo carriers without a clathrin lattice; this is the decisive follow-up for generalizing clathrin-coated AP-3 rows.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. Two of its three uses here run through the delta-specific entries IPR010474 and IPR017105, which is as tight as an InterPro mapping gets; the third runs through IPR002553, a domain shared with all four adaptin large-subunit families, and can only support top-level terms.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Curator sequence-similarity transfer. Both uses take mouse Ap3d1 (O54774) as donor, and human/mouse delta are reciprocal 1:1 orthologs in PTHR22781:SF12 that align residue-for-residue across the ARF1 and VAMP7 interfaces, so the similarity judgement is easy to sustain.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA. The ten IBA rows trace to exactly ten IBD rows in the committed PTHR22781 PAINT slice, split between a Eukaryota node (PTN000513025) and a Bilateria node (PTN000513028); every seed resolves to a real experimental annotation on an AP-3 delta ortholog. Nine of the ten are sound; only GO:0006896 carries a compartment that does not transfer to mammals.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location keyword mapping. Both uses are faithful to the UniProt record; the Golgi-membrane statement it maps is itself flagged By similarity (ECO:0000250), which is why that row is kept as non-core.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara orthology transfer, mouse Ap3d1 -> human. Fourteen rows, all with the same donor pair (UniProtKB:O54774 plus its Ensembl translation ENSMUSP00000020420 - one donor under two identifiers). Most transfer genuine mouse experimental annotations; the GO:1990742 row transfers a donor annotation whose GO term is mis-scoped, and the GO:0035651 row transfers a part/whole inversion.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learned rules. Of the six uses, four fire on a single AP3D1-specific CATH FunFam (3.30.450.50:FF:000001) and give reasonable terms; one (ARBA00092758, GO:0010496 intercellular transport) gives a term with the wrong topology from the same evidence; and one (ARBA00028739, GO:0032502) cannot be reproduced from any of the rule's 893 published condition sets.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated annotation. The five uses bundle ARBA and Ensembl arms; where they disagree in strength the Ensembl arm (mouse experimental donor) is the one carrying the claim, as noted per row.

title: The neuronal form of adaptor protein-3 is required for synaptic vesicle formation from endosomes.
review_notes: Shows that only the NEURONAL form of AP-3 makes synaptic vesicles from endosomes in vitro - the result that makes the SV terms a beta-3B property shared with delta rather than a delta-specific one. The IDA/IMP behind the mouse GO:0016182 seed.

title: Localization of the AP-3 adaptor complex defines a novel endosomal exit site for lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Immuno-EM localisation of AP-3 to budding profiles on a tubular endosomal compartment, and the LAMP-1/LAMP-2 recycling phenotype. The central evidence that the mammalian AP-3 exit site is endosomal rather than Golgi.

title: Gravity receptor function in mice with graded otoconial deficiencies.
review_notes: A gravity-receptor study across five otoconia-deficient mouse strains, one of which is mocha; the IMP behind the mouse GO:0048840 annotation. Correctly cited, but it is a vestibular-physiology paper, not an AP-3 paper, so it says nothing about mechanism.

title: Genetic analysis of the neuronal and ubiquitous AP-3 adaptor complexes reveals divergent functions in brain.
review_notes: The beta3A vs beta3B knockout comparison. Correctly cited and important, but it is also the source of the mis-scoped GO:0016183 synaptic-vesicle-coating NAS: nothing in the paper concerns clathrin-coated pits at the presynaptic membrane.

title: AP-1 and AP-3 facilitate lysosomal targeting of Batten disease protein CLN3 via its dileucine motif.
review_notes: CLN3 dileucine-motif binding to AP-1 and AP-3 and the sequential sorting requirement. The IPI partner (UniProtKB:Q13286) resolves to CLN3/battenin. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Vglut1 and ZnT3 co-targeting mechanisms regulate vesicular zinc stores in PC12 cells.
review_notes: Vglut1/ZnT3 co-targeting in PC12 cells; the IMP behind the mouse GO:0048499 seed. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Functions of adaptor protein (AP)-3 and AP-1 in tyrosinase sorting from endosomes to melanosomes.
review_notes: Direct localisation of AP-3 to clathrin-coated buds on tubular early endosomes in melanocytes, plus the tyrosinase mis-sorting phenotype. The IDA on human AP3D1 for endosome membrane, and one of the descendant evidences behind the PTN000513025 IBD. Full text is now cached; this availability correction does not claim a new full-text assessment.

title: BLOC-1 complex deficiency alters the targeting of adaptor protein complex-3 cargoes.
review_notes: Sound cell biology - AP-3 and BLOC-1 on shared small vesicles, and mistargeting of LAMP1, PI4KIIalpha and VAMP7-TI. What is disputed is the GO term derived from it: the paper's 'microvesicles' are intracellular transport intermediates, whereas GO:1990742 denotes an extracellular vesicle shed from the plasma membrane.

title: Zinc transporter 2 (SLC30A2) can suppress the vesicular zinc defect of adaptor protein 3-depleted fibroblasts by promoting zinc accumulation in lysosomes.
review_notes: AP3D1-specific siRNA in human fibroblastoid cells; the IMP behind GO:0140916. Correctly cited and methodologically sound - the objection is to the term, not the experiment, since the paper's own rescue result shows ZnT2 is the importer and AP-3 the delivery machinery.

title: The subcellular localization of the Niemann-Pick Type C proteins depends on the adaptor complex AP-3.
review_notes: Yeast and mammalian NPC protein targeting via AP-3; the IMP behind the GO:0006623 IBD seed. Title foregrounds Niemann-Pick disease, which is why affinage did not surface it.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Placental lysosomal-membrane proteome. Correctly cited for the HDA, but it projects onto 242 distinct gene products, so it is a compartment survey.

title: Sorting of the v-SNARE VAMP7 in Dictyostelium discoideum: a role for more than one Adaptor Protein (AP) complex.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome protein complexes associate with phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase type II alpha in neuronal and non-neuronal cells.

title: Roles of BLOC-1 and adaptor protein-3 complexes in cargo sorting to synaptic vesicles.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak protein complexes, AP-3 and BLOC-1, differentially regulate presynaptic composition in the striatum and hippocampus.

title: The schizophrenia susceptibility factor dysbindin and its associated complex sort cargoes from cell bodies to the synapse.
review_notes: BLOC-1/AP-3 sorting of PI4KIIalpha from cell bodies to the synapse; the IMP behind the mouse GO:0008089 and GO:0048490 annotations.

title: BLOC-2, AP-3, and AP-1 proteins function in concert with Rab38 and Rab32 proteins to mediate protein trafficking to lysosome-related organelles.

Abstract-only in the cache, so the experimental detail behind the AP3D1 IMPs was not verifiable here and the curator is deferred to.

title: Structural basis of the intracellular sorting of the SNARE VAMP7 by the AP3 adaptor complex.
review_notes: The crystal structure of the delta-adaptin hinge bound to the VAMP7 longin domain (PDB 4AFI; UniProt maps chains A/B to O14617 680-729), with interface mutagenesis and rescue in mocha fibroblasts. The primary evidence for the NEW SNARE-binding row and the only structurally defined delta-specific cargo receptor.

title: Adaptor protein complexes 1 and 3 are essential for generation of synaptic vesicles from activity-dependent bulk endosomes.
review_notes: AP-1 and AP-3 requirement for generating synaptic vesicles from activity-dependent bulk endosomes in rat neurons; the IDA/IMP behind the rat RGD:1308659 seed of GO:0016182. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Cell type-specific Rab32 and Rab38 cooperate with the ubiquitous lysosome biogenesis machinery to synthesize specialized lysosome-related organelles.
review_notes: A short review, correctly cited by ComplexPortal for four NAS rows. It projects onto 48 distinct gene products, so it is a general-machinery citation; its statements about AP-3 are accurate but second-hand, and the platelet dense-granule claim in particular is about HPS generally rather than about AP-3 directly.

title: Chemical-genetic disruption of clathrin function spares adaptor complex 3-dependent endosome vesicle biogenesis.
review_notes: Acute chemical-genetic inactivation of clathrin leaving AP-3 endosomal budding intact. The decisive functional test against the clathrin-dependence premise of GO:0035654.

title: Stargazin regulates AMPA receptor trafficking through adaptor protein complexes during long-term depression.
review_notes: Stargazin-AP-3A routing of AMPA receptors to late endosomes/lysosomes during LTD; the IDA/IEP/IMP behind the mouse GO:0098943 and GO:0098978 annotations and the postsynaptic localisation. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Mutations in AP3D1 associated with immunodeficiency and seizures define a new type of Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome.
review_notes: The HPS10 paper: homozygous AP3D1 mutation, AP-3 destabilisation, impaired CD8+ T-cell and NK-cell degranulation, and full rescue by retroviral AP3D1 reconstitution. Primary evidence for both NEW degranulation rows and the source of UniProt's FUNCTION and DISEASE blocks. Full text available.

title: Biallelic mutations in AP3D1 cause Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 10 associated with immunodeficiency and seizure disorder.
review_notes: Second HPS10 family, confirming the platelet storage-pool defect that the first report could not assess. Abstract-only in the cache but the abstract states the platelet finding directly.

title: Adaptor protein-3 complex is required for Vangl2 trafficking and planar cell polarity of the inner ear.
review_notes: AP-3 is required for Vangl2 trafficking and inner-ear planar cell polarity in mouse. Cited only in a knowledge gap, as the current best lead for the cochlear cargo; it does not support any annotation in this review.

title: A BLOC-1-AP-3 super-complex sorts a cis-SNARE complex into endosome-derived tubular transport carriers.
review_notes: Shows in melanocytes that sorting of the STX13-VAMP7 cis-SNARE complex into transport carriers requires recognition of VAMP7 by the AP-3 delta subunit or of STX13 by BLOC-1 pallidin. The in vivo counterpart to the 4AFI structure; supports the NEW SNARE-binding row.

title: A homozygous AP3D1 missense variant in patients with sensorineural hearing loss as the leading manifestation.
review_notes: A homozygous AP3D1 missense variant presenting as sensorineural hearing loss, extending the HPS10 phenotypic spectrum. Cited as corroboration for the inner-ear/otolith row rather than as its basis.

title: A structure-based mechanism for initiation of AP-3 coated vesicle formation.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of reconstituted human AP-3 with Arf1 and cargo, including the hemicomplex pulldowns that localise the primary Arf1 site to delta and the stepwise activation series. PDB 9C58/9C59/9C5B/9C5C map to O14617, confirming human numbering.

title: Architecture of clathrin-independent AP3:ARF1-coated carriers.
review_notes: Cryo-ET of the AP3:ARF1 coat, naming both delta ARF1 interfaces by residue, testing them in HeLa cells, and demonstrating carrier formation without a clathrin lattice. The basis for the NEW small-GTPase-binding row, the GO:0035654 modification and the NEW lysosomal-targeting row.

title: Characterization of the adaptor-related protein complex, AP-3.
review_notes: The paper that named AP-3 and identified delta as the p160 subunit, with an antibody raised against delta itself. Source of the Golgi-apparatus TAS, the intracellular-protein-transport TAS and the AP-3-complex NAS. Projects to only 14 distinct gene products in QuickGO, so it is a genuine subunit-level citation rather than a mass projection.

title: Suppressors of YCK-encoded yeast casein kinase 1 deficiency define the four subunits of a novel clathrin AP-like complex.
review_notes: Yeast suppressor screen defining the four subunits of yeast AP-3; the experimental grounding (IMP+IPI on APL5) behind the GO:0030123 IBD seed. Title foregrounds casein kinase suppression, which is why a symbol-based search does not find it.

title: Altered expression of a novel adaptin leads to defective pigment granule biogenesis in the Drosophila eye color mutant garnet.
review_notes: Identified human delta-adaptin, showed it is an AP-3 subunit, and linked it to the Drosophila garnet pigment-granule phenotype. Cited for complex membership and for the melanosome/pigment-granule rows.

title: The AP-3 adaptor complex is essential for cargo-selective transport to the yeast vacuole.
review_notes: The yeast ALP-pathway screen; the IMP behind the GO:0006896 IBD seed. Correctly cited and scientifically sound - the reason the IBA is modified is that the Golgi-to-vacuole route it establishes is yeast-specific, not that the paper is wrong.

title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: Correctly cited for AP-3 binding clathrin, and the binding is real, but its functional inference ('AP-3 function in protein sorting may depend on clathrin') has been superseded: PMID:23761069 shows the association is dispensable and PMID:42139345 shows AP3:ARF1 builds carriers with no clathrin lattice. Also note the interaction it maps is beta3's appendage, not delta's.

title: ADP-Ribosylation factor 1 (ARF1) regulates recruitment of the AP-3 adaptor complex to membranes.
review_notes: Established that ARF1 controls AP-3 membrane recruitment. Does not resolve which subunit, which the 2024/2026 structures do; cited as background to the NEW small-GTPase-binding row.

title: Mutation in AP-3 delta in the mocha mouse links endosomal transport to storage deficiency in platelets, melanosomes, and synaptic vesicles.
review_notes: The mocha mouse: a null allele of AP-3 delta linking endosomal transport to storage deficiency in platelets, melanosomes and synaptic vesicles. The single most important loss-of-function reference for this gene, and one the affinage record missed.

title: AP3D1 bioinformatics: delta-adaptin interface conservation and GOA reconciliation
review_notes: This review's own reproducible analysis: MAFFT conservation of the three mapped delta interfaces across the PTHR22781 family versus out-of-family adaptin large subunits, plus the GOA-to-YAML reconciliation. Scripts fetch live from UniProt and assert every claimed residue before aligning.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP3D1 (human)
review_notes: Affinage LLM deep-research record. Trust gates clear (.affinage.log), self_evaluation_pairwise 'win', faith 100%, and the narrative is genuinely about AP-3 delta with no symbol collision - its recent-cargo material (IFNGR1/OPTN, DRAM2, RNF13, TGFbeta2, zebrafish crasher) is useful context. Marked LOW relevance because it is precision-not-recall: it missed the mocha mouse, the garnet/delta-adaptin discovery, the entire AP-3 structural literature (both the ARF1 and VAMP7 interfaces), the clathrin papers and every PAINT donor paper. No claim in this review rests on it; the ones it suggested were re-verified against their own PMIDs.

title: UniProt entry O14617 (AP3D1_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt O14617 (AP3D1_HUMAN, entry version 224, 1153 aa). Accession and identifier checked against the fetched record, so this is not a merged-accession redirect. Quoted for complex composition and for the HPS10 disease statement.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: interpro2go, behind three rows from the same signature pair IPR001392 plus IPR018240. The pair is a family signature covering every AP medium subunit, so the two generic outputs (intracellular protein transport, vesicle-mediated transport) are safe while the third (clathrin adaptor complex) asserts membership of a class GO explicitly does not place AP-3 in. Same instructive pattern as the IBA node: correct pipeline, over-broad signature-to-term map.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Manual ISS transfer from mouse Ap3m1 for the two anterograde transport rows, duplicating what GO_REF:0000107 transfers automatically. Same donor, same underlying mocha experiment, so the two routes are not independent confirmations of each other.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT route behind all five IBA rows. The family slice was fetched and committed as interpro/panther/PTHR10529/PTHR10529-paint.tsv. Two of the five sit on PTN002237676 and PTN002575745, clade-specific nodes whose seeds are AP-3 mu subunits and the target's own mouse orthologue respectively, and are accepted. Three sit on PTN000055849, the family-level node ancestral to all AP medium subunits; two of those transfer safely and one, GO:0035615, carries a clathrin- and endocytosis-specific term from an entirely AP-1/AP-2 seed set onto a non-clathrin coat. The pipeline is applied correctly throughout; the defect is the term's placement at that node.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location mapping, behind the Golgi apparatus and cytoplasmic vesicle membrane rows. Both faithfully reproduce the SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line of Q9Y2T2, so neither is independent of the UniProt record; the cytoplasmic vesicle membrane row is nonetheless the core location and is now directly visualised in the AP-3 structures.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara automatic orthology transfer, behind five rows, all from mouse Ap3m1 (Q9JKC8). The orthology is 1:1 and the cargo-binding site is identical between the two species at all 14 tested positions, so the transfer step itself is sound. What varies is the donor evidence: two rows rest on a mouse IMP obtained with the Ap3d1 mocha allele, two on SynGO IDAs that really are about mu3A, and one recasts complex membership as complex binding.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Logical inter-ontology inference, behind the axon cytoplasm row. It is correctly applied; it simply inherits whatever confidence attaches to the GO:0008089 row it is computed from, which in this case is a mouse phenotype obtained on a different subunit.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning annotation, behind the single cytoplasm row. The rule cited, ARBA00026971, has 2388 condition sets and one output term; none of the two that mention an AP3M1 signature can fire for this protein, so the row is not reproducible from the published rule even though its conclusion is correct.

title: Altered trafficking of lysosomal proteins in Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome due to mutations in the beta 3A subunit of the AP-3 adaptor.
review_notes: The Hermansky-Pudlak type 2 paper behind both TAS rows. Abstract-only in the cache. Its abstract names mu3A explicitly as the reason AP-3 cargo selection is specific, which is why the curator placed the rows on this gene; in GOA the reference annotates AP3M1 and nothing else. The process row is accepted; the location row is marked over-annotated because the paper shows targeting to lysosomes, not residence in them.

title: Multiple C-terminal motifs of the 46-kDa mannose 6-phosphate receptor tail contribute to efficient binding of medium chains of AP-2 and AP-3.
review_notes: Two-hybrid mapping of the MPR46 cytoplasmic tail onto mu2 and mu3A, showing mu3A needs a composite tyrosine-plus-dileucine-plus-acidic structure. Abstract-only. Used as a third independent cargo tail for mu3A rather than for its mechanistic detail.

title: Genomic organization and linkage via a bidirectional promoter of the AP-3 (adaptor protein-3) mu3A and AK (adenosine kinase) genes: deletion mutants of AK in Chinese hamster cells extend into the AP-3 mu3A gene.
review_notes: Genomic organisation of the mu3A locus, which shares a bidirectional CpG-island promoter with adenosine kinase. Abstract-only. Used only in the notes, for the observation that large ADK-region deletions can remove AP3M1 - a possible but unreported route to human AP3M1 loss.

title: Genetic analysis of the neuronal and ubiquitous AP-3 adaptor complexes reveals divergent functions in brain.
review_notes: Mouse genetics separating beta3A- from beta3B-containing AP-3, with opposite synaptic zinc and ZnT3/ClC-3 phenotypes. Full text cached. The evidence that the neuronal AP-3 jobs belong mostly to the complex that does not contain AP3M1, and the main support for treating the neuronal rows on this gene as non-core.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Placental lysosomal membrane proteomics, the HDA source for GO:0005765. Abstract-only in the cache. Projects over 242 distinct gene products, and the paper itself distinguishes integral lysosomal proteins from proteins merely enriched in or partially associated with the fraction. Correctly cited; low relevance to AP3M1's function.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome protein complexes associate with phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase type II alpha in neuronal and non-neuronal cells.
review_notes: Cross-linking and affinity purification of AP-3 with mass spectrometry, the mouse IDA behind the GO:0035651 'AP-3 adaptor complex binding' row. Correctly cited; the issue is the role the term assigns, not the experiment. Projects over 26 gene products in GOA, consistent with a complex-purification study.

title: Localization to mature melanosomes by virtue of cytoplasmic dileucine motifs is required for human OCA2 function.
review_notes: The OCA2 melanosomal targeting study, source of the one low-throughput GO:0005515 row. Abstract-only in the cache, which is why the row is marked over-annotated rather than converted: the motifs the abstract describes are acidic dileucine signals, read by the sigma3/delta site rather than by the mu3A tyrosine pocket, and I cannot see from the abstract which AP-3 construct was used.

title: The schizophrenia susceptibility factor dysbindin and its associated complex sort cargoes from cell bodies to the synapse.
review_notes: The mouse IMP source for both anterograde transport rows. Full text read, and the reading is the reason those rows are non-core: every AP-3 genotype in the paper is the mocha Ap3d1 allele, and the strings Ap3m1, mu3A and AP3M do not occur in the text at all. Correctly cited for what it shows; it simply does not show it for this subunit.

title: BLOC-2, AP-3, and AP-1 proteins function in concert with Rab38 and Rab32 proteins to mediate protein trafficking to lysosome-related organelles.
review_notes: Melanocyte co-immunoprecipitation and cargo trafficking showing Rab32/Rab38 working with BLOC-2, AP-1 and AP-3; the source of both GO:0031267 rows. Abstract-only in the cache. Projects over only 7 gene products - the complexes and the two Rabs - so it is a focused, complex-scoped reference rather than a screen. Which AP-3 subunit contacts the Rab is not stated in the abstract.

title: Cell type-specific Rab32 and Rab38 cooperate with the ubiquitous lysosome biogenesis machinery to synthesize specialized lysosome-related organelles.
review_notes: The Rab32/Rab38 review that ComplexPortal cites for four NAS rows. Full text cached and read. A review rather than primary data, which is what NAS records; it is accurate about the shared LRO machinery and about tyrosinase packaging at early/recycling endosome tubules.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HI-II-14 yeast two-hybrid interactome. Correctly cited for five binding rows; none has AP3M1-specific follow-up.

title: Upregulation of μ3A Drives Homeostatic Plasticity by Rerouting AMPAR into the Recycling Endosomal Pathway.
review_notes: The only paper that manipulates mu3A itself in neurons - mouse visual cortex pyramidal cells - and the source of the SynGO IDA rows for postsynaptic recycling endosome and receptor internalization. Full text read. Two caveats recorded in the rows: the sufficiency experiments are overexpression, and the authors conclude the effect is AP-3-independent.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 affinity-purification mass spectrometry. Three binding rows, no follow-up.

title: Interaction of the Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus matrix protein with cellular adaptor protein complex 3 plays a critical role in trafficking.
review_notes: Shows HRSV matrix protein engaging AP-3 specifically through mu3A, dependent on the tyrosine of a YXXL motif at M residues 197-200. Full text cached. UniProt cites it as reference [6] for this entry, and affinage missed it. An independent functional line for the YxxPhi activity, in a host-virus context, which is why it supports the NEW row rather than generating one of its own.

title: Widespread Post-transcriptional Attenuation of Genomic Copy-Number Variation in Cancer.
review_notes: The single citation in the affinage record. A CPTAC/TCGA proteogenomics study showing that AP3B1 depletion lowers AP3M1 abundance, i.e. complex assembly stoichiometry. Real, correctly cited, and not a function of AP3M1; cited here only to characterise what affinage returned.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome: Mutation update.
review_notes: The Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome mutation update, used for two checkable facts: that the AP-3 disease genes are AP3B1 (HPS-2) and AP3D1 (HPS-10), and that all ten described HPS subtypes have an assigned gene. Full text cached and searched - the string AP3M1 does not occur anywhere in it, which is the cleanest available support for the review's statement that no human AP3M1 disorder has been described.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI all-by-all yeast two-hybrid reference interactome. Correctly cited for ten binding rows, the largest single block on this gene; no functional follow-up for any pair.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration-focused yeast two-hybrid map; the source of the single HTT binding row. Correctly cited, no AP3M1-specific follow-up.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0, two cell lines. Two binding rows that re-detect BioPlex 2.0 partners; cell-line replication within one platform rather than independent confirmation.

title: Flexible open conformation of the AP-3 complex explains its role in cargo recruitment at the Golgi.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the yeast AP-3 complex, establishing the constitutively open conformation and cargo-dependent membrane recruitment. Cited only as the precedent that the human structures later confirmed; no yeast mechanism is stated here as a human fact.

title: A structure-based mechanism for initiation of AP-3 coated vesicle formation.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of reconstituted human AP-3, including a cargo-engaged state with a LAMP1 YxxPhi peptide in the mu3 pocket. Full text in the cache and read. Cross-referenced from the UniProt record itself via PDB 9C58-9C5C with chain M = AP3M1 1-418, and PDB 9C5B is the structure measured in this review's bioinformatics. The anchor for the NEW molecular function row.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: Solute-carrier interaction proteomics; source of one SLC12A4 binding row curated into IntAct. AP3M1 does not appear in the cached article text, so the pairing lives in the supplementary interaction tables rather than in the narrative.

title: Architecture of clathrin-independent AP3:ARF1-coated carriers.
review_notes: Cryo-electron tomography of AP3:ARF1 coats, demonstrating carrier formation without a clathrin lattice and placing mammalian AP-3 on early/tubular endosomes. Full text read. One detail recorded for accuracy: the reconstituted complex is a chimera - the mu3 subunit used was rat AP3M1(1-418), with human delta and sigma and chimpanzee beta3 - while the cell-based experiments are in human HeLa cells with an anti-AP3M1 antibody.

title: Sequence requirements for the recognition of tyrosine-based endocytic signals by clathrin AP-2 complexes.
review_notes: Boll et al. 1996, the mu2 tyrosine-signal selectivity study that human AP2M1's own GO:0005048 IDA row cites. Cached and read (abstract-only) so that the precedent the NEW GO:0005048 row rests on is auditable from the repository rather than only from a QuickGO query.
