It is about mu2, not mu3A; it is cited for the curation precedent and for the assay type, not as evidence about AP3M1, whose own evidence is the five lines listed on that row.

title: AP-3: an adaptor-like protein complex with ubiquitous expression.
review_notes: Companion paper identifying sigma3A/sigma3B and showing directly that the p47A chain - AP3M1 - binds the TGN38 YQRL tyrosine signal. Abstract-only in the cache, but the binding result and the TGN localisation are both stated in the abstract and are what is quoted.

title: Characterization of the adaptor-related protein complex, AP-3.
review_notes: The paper that defined AP-3 as a heterotetramer and named mu3/p47A as its ubiquitous medium subunit. Read in full from the cache. It is the source of the NAS complex-membership row, of the ubiquitous-versus-neuronal isoform distinction this review leans on, and of the original 'not clathrin associated' position. Projects over 14 gene products in GOA, which is the AP-3 subunits and orthologues rather than a mass projection.

title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: The in vitro clathrin-binding result behind the NAS GO:0035654 row. Correctly cited and a real experiment, but its central claim is contested: the interaction is with beta3 rather than mu3A, the authors' own conclusion is hedged ('may depend on clathrin'), the 2024 review of the field calls the question open, and the 2026 reconstitution shows carrier formation without a clathrin lattice. DISPUTED rather than MISCITED - the paper says what the annotation says it says.

title: The medium subunits of adaptor complexes recognize distinct but overlapping sets of tyrosine-based sorting signals.
review_notes: The combinatorial XXXYXXO two-hybrid screen that gives mu3A its own YxxPhi residue preferences, distinct from mu1 and mu2. Abstract-only in the cache; the quoted claims are abstract-level. This is the strongest evidence that mu3A is a signal reader with its own specificity rather than a generic one, and it underpins the NEW GO:0005048 row.

title: Specificity of interaction between adaptor-complex medium chains and the tyrosine-based sorting motifs of TGN38 and lgp120.
review_notes: Shows the lgp120 (LAMP1) cytoplasmic tail binding mu3A almost exclusively among the medium chains, via the YQTI motif - the same motif resolved in the mu3 pocket by cryo-EM 26 years later. Abstract-only in the cache; the quoted statements are in the abstract. Also the source for mu4 binding tyrosine motifs only weakly, which is useful context for the family node.

title: AP3M1 bioinformatics: the YxxPhi cargo pocket of the AP-3 mu subunit
review_notes: Written for this review. Downloads PDB 9C5B and 1BXX and the seven mu-subunit sequences live, asserts that each modelled chain matches its UniProt sequence at every author-assigned position before measuring anything, and computes heavy-atom contacts to the bound cargo peptides. Establishes that AP3M1 contacts the LAMP1 YxxPhi peptide at ten residues, that nine of them lie on AP2M1 cargo-pocket alignment columns, that AP3M1 matches AP2M1 at only 5 of 14 of those columns, and that mouse and human AP3M1 are identical at all 14. States its own limits: the AP2M1 pocket is projected onto the other subunits by pairwise alignment, not by structural superposition.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP3M1 (human)
review_notes: The script's trust gate tripped (self_evaluation_pairwise: loss, faith_pct 50.0), and the record is thin rather than wrong: one citation, PMID:29032074, reporting that AP3B1 depletion lowers AP3M1 abundance. That observation is real and correctly cited, but it is complex stoichiometry rather than function, and the record's own claim that no further mechanistic detail has been characterised is false for this gene. It missed the entire YxxPhi literature, both AP-3 cryo-EM papers - one of them cross-referenced straight from the UniProt record via PDB 9C58-9C5C - the clathrin dispute, the HPS2 cargo phenotype, the mu3A neuronal paper, the beta3A/beta3B genetic dissection, and the HRSV matrix interaction that UniProt itself cites. Nothing from it is used as supporting_text for a mechanistic claim.

title: UniProtKB Q9Y2T2 (AP3M1_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: The curated record for Q9Y2T2, verified to be AP3M1_HUMAN, 418 aa, not a merged accession. Used for the complex composition, the MHD domain boundaries (176-417), the 'not clathrin-associated' FUNCTION statement, the subcellular location, the PANTHER and ComplexPortal cross-references that establish AP3M1 as a subunit of the ubiquitous AP-3A variants only, and the PDB cross-references to the 2024 cryo-EM series. Its INTERACTION block also supplied the partner symbols for the binding rows.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO mapping checked against the InterPro API: IPR001392 and IPR018240 carry GO:0006886, GO:0016192 and GO:0030131. The transport terms describe the established adaptor role. The broad clathrin-adaptor-complex term is retained as non-core after reconsidering AP-3/clathrin association; this does not infer obligate clathrin dependence.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: UniProt curator ISS. Both rows name mouse Q8R2R9 as donor; the donor annotations were checked against QuickGO and trace to PMID:21998198, whose limitation is recorded on each row.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA. The PTHR10529 slice was fetched and committed; node identities, seeds and the two IRD blocks were read from it rather than assumed.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Both SubCell rows reproduce the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line faithfully.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Seven rows come through this route. Each donor annotation was pulled from QuickGO and read; they differ sharply in strength, which is recorded row by row rather than being treated uniformly.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Used once, to derive axon cytoplasm from anterograde axonal transport. Mechanically correct; contributes no evidence of its own.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA00026971 was fetched from rest.uniprot.org and its 2,388 condition sets were filtered against the seven InterPro signatures InterPro reports for P53677 and against PTHR10529. The two sets that match a signature also require taxon Saccharomyces, or the sigma-subunit families IPR016635/IPR027156, so none can fire on this protein. The conferred term happens to be true.

title: Signal-binding specificity of the mu4 subunit of the adaptor protein complex AP-4.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The mu4 signal-binding screen. Cited for the ontology proposal rather than for AP3M2 itself: it shows a mu-bound YxxPhi signal routing a reporter to the endosomal-lysosomal system without plasma-membrane internalisation, which is the clearest demonstration that recognition of the motif by mu subunits is not an endocytic-only activity.

title: The neuronal form of adaptor protein-3 is required for synaptic vesicle formation from endosomes.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The single most important paper for this gene and the one affinage missed most consequentially: it separates neuronal from ubiquitous AP-3 and shows only the neuronal form makes synaptic vesicles from endosomes.

title: Localization of the AP-3 adaptor complex defines a novel endosomal exit site for lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Full immuno-EM Results read. Establishes predominant tubular-endosome localization, 4% TGN labeling and partial clathrin coating. These data do not prove exclusive endosome residence or absence of clathrin association.

title: Defective function of GABA-containing synaptic vesicles in mice lacking the AP-3B clathrin adaptor.
review_notes: Full text available and read in full. The mu3B knockout, and the source of every gene-specific in vivo statement in this review. Verified that it is the paper cited by the SynGO donor annotations on mouse Ap3m2.

title: Genetic analysis of the neuronal and ubiquitous AP-3 adaptor complexes reveals divergent functions in brain.
review_notes: Full paper newly retrieved and read. Mouse beta3A/beta3B genetics and cargo sorting; Discussion describes preferential/complex beta-mu pairing and is not proof that every pairing is universally obligate.

title: Mutation screening of AP3M2 in Japanese epilepsy patients.
review_notes: Abstract-only. A negative result: no coding mutations in 190 epilepsy patients. Included because it is the only dedicated human mutation screen of AP3M2 found in this search, and it delimits the knowledge gap about human disease relevance.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome protein complexes associate with phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase type II alpha in neuronal and non-neuronal cells.
review_notes: Abstract and source donor identifier verified; full text remains inaccessible after official fetch and PMC attempt. Cross-linked AP-3 complexes are analyzed. The GO term has no external-ligand-only restriction.

title: The schizophrenia susceptibility factor dysbindin and its associated complex sort cargoes from cell bodies to the synapse.
review_notes: Full AP-3 complex-level axonal cargo-sorting evidence; mocha affects AP3D1. This limits target-specific attribution but does not by itself invalidate inference to a functional AP-3 subunit.

title: Cell type-specific Rab32 and Rab38 cooperate with the ubiquitous lysosome biogenesis machinery to synthesize specialized lysosome-related organelles.
review_notes: Full text available and read. A review; cited by ComplexPortal for the early-endosome row and useful for AP-3's role at early/recycling endosome tubules in pigment cells. Corroborated with the primary immuno-EM paper rather than relied on alone.

title: Genetic characterization and in vivo image analysis of novel zebrafish Danio rerio pigment mutants.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Zebrafish pigment mutant work listing ap3m2 among candidate genes. Background for the pigment-cell knowledge gap only; no annotation rests on it.

title: Identification of a QTL in Mus musculus for alcohol preference, withdrawal, and Ap3m2 expression using integrative functional genomics and precision genetics.
review_notes: Full text available. Maps an alcohol-preference and withdrawal QTL to Ap3m2 with regulatory rather than coding variation. Context for the knowledge gaps; no annotation rests on it.

title: Candidate-based screening via gene modulation in human neurons and astrocytes implicates FERMT2 in Aβ and TAU proteostasis.
review_notes: Abstract-only. AP3M2 knockdown reduces astrocyte IL-6 in a candidate screen; a non-neuronal human phenotype with no mechanism attached. Cited only in support of the non-neuronal expression gap.

title: Hidden proteome of synaptic vesicles in the mammalian brain.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The deep synaptic-vesicle proteome behind the rat GO:0008021 annotation. Verified that the authors themselves name AP-3 among likely SV visitors rather than residents; the per-protein dataset is not in the cached text.

title: Flexible open conformation of the AP-3 complex explains its role in cargo recruitment at the Golgi.
review_notes: Full text available. Yeast AP-3 structure showing the constitutively open conformation; corroborates the human structural work and the Golgi-versus-endosome contrast between AP-3 in fungi and metazoa.

title: AP3M2: A key regulator from the nervous system modulates autophagy in colorectal cancer.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Knockdown of AP3M2 in three colorectal-cancer lines reduces viability and correlates with autophagy and ROS genes; no mechanism and no rescue. Cited only as evidence that human AP3M2 is functionally relevant outside neurons.

title: A structure-based mechanism for initiation of AP-3 coated vesicle formation.
review_notes: Full primary Results/Discussion read. PDB9C5B mu subunit is AP3M1; existing reproducible alignment supports transfer of cargo contacts to AP3M2. Paper explicitly discusses BOTH clathrin-dependent and independent AP3 functions.

title: Seizures, increased interhemispheric synchrony, altered brain transcriptomics and a leaky blood-brain barrier result from loss of ap3b2 in a CRISPR tadpole model of DEE48.
review_notes: Full text available. A Xenopus model of DEE48, the epilepsy caused by loss of AP3B2 - AP3M2's obligate partner subunit. Cited for context on the neuronal AP-3B pathway, not as evidence about AP3M2 itself.

title: Lysosome-related organelles orchestrate guanine crystal formation in pigment cells.
review_notes: Full text available. Zebrafish ap3m2 is required for guanine-crystal formation in iridophores. The orthology of the zebrafish gene to human AP3M2 rather than AP3M1 was not established here, so this supports a knowledge gap rather than an annotation.

title: Two rat homologs of clathrin-associated adaptor proteins.
review_notes: The cloning paper for rat p47B, the AP3M2 orthologue. Verified it is the source of the 'neuron-specific' claim that the later literature repeats; its own GO-relevant assertion is homology-level, which is why the TAS row it supports is modified rather than accepted.

title: AP-3: an adaptor-like protein complex with ubiquitous expression.
review_notes: Establishes AP-3 as a ubiquitously expressed adaptor-like complex and shows the p47A medium chain binding the TGN38 YQRL tyrosine signal - the paralogue-level precedent for the mu3 cargo-binding function.

title: Characterization of the adaptor-related protein complex, AP-3.
review_notes: Completed the AP-3 subunit inventory by co-immunoprecipitation and named the complex. Full text available and read; also the source of the mu subunit / tyrosine-signal statement and of the Golgi-region localisation that the SubCell row reflects.

title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Reports AP-3 association with clathrin through the beta3 appendage. This is relevant to the retained contextual clathrin-adaptor-complex inference, without establishing that every AP-3 coat requires clathrin.

title: A function for the AP3 coat complex in synaptic vesicle formation from endosomes.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The original demonstration that AP-3 coats bud small vesicles from PC12 endosomes; the foundation for the endosomal-budding reading of AP-3B.

title: The medium subunits of adaptor complexes recognize distinct but overlapping sets of tyrosine-based sorting signals.
review_notes: Abstract-only, but decisive: the only direct molecular-function assay found in this search in which mu3B itself is one of the tested subunits. Affinage did not return it.

title: AP3M2 (mu3B) bioinformatics results
review_notes: Analyses written for this review. Every number is recomputed live from UniProt, PDBe/SIFTS, RCSB and the Human Protein Atlas by AP3M2-bioinformatics/analyze.py; accessions are asserted against the fetched records, which caught one wrong accession on the first run.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP3M2 (human)
review_notes: Read all six cited findings. Useful neuronal/pigment-cell context, but calling AP3M2 mu-2 is inaccurate (mu3B); zebrafish and mouse findings are not direct human assays. It does not settle clathrin or TGN questions.

title: OpenScientist report on AP3M2 clathrin and Golgi contexts
review_notes: Focused hypothesis review that agrees with retaining AP-3 membership, mu3B cargo-signal recognition, and AP-3-mediated trafficking, and usefully documents AP-3/AP-4 scope concerns on GO:0035615. It is treated as disputed rather than adopted outright because the local review preserves AP-3/clathrin evidence as contextual and non-core, while leaving GO:0035615 unresolved pending curator review.

title: UniProt entry P53677 (AP3M2_HUMAN)
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProt record for P53677. Verified it is the intended protein (AP3M2_HUMAN, 418 aa, GN Name=AP3M2) and not a merged accession. Quotations are taken one physical line at a time because the record hard-wraps its CC blocks.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. Four signatures on this protein feed seven rows. Three of the four mappings (IPR000804 -> GO:0006886/GO:0016192/GO:0030117, IPR016635 -> GO:0015031) are correct and appropriately general; IPR027155 -> GO:0006896 carries the fungal donor compartment and is modified in this review. Mappings read from the InterPro API, not assumed.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Curator ISS from mouse Ap3s1. The donor is the 1:1 ortholog and is sequence-identical to the human protein, so the transfer step is sound; the rows are graded non-core on the nature of the mouse experiment, not on the transfer.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/GO_Central phylogenetic annotation. Traced to node PTN000204281 of PTHR11753 in the family PAINT slice in this repository; all eleven gene-level donors resolved individually. The node is the pan-AP-sigma ancestor and the term is its correct LCA.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location vocabulary mapping. Both location terms used here (SL-0132, SL-0089) were checked against the UniProt locations API and map to exactly the GO terms annotated.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog transfer from mouse Ap3s1. The pipeline step is faithful and the orthology is perfect (identical sequences), which is why three of the four rows are kept; the fourth, GO:0035651, is removed because the defect it inherits is in the source term's relation type, not in the transfer.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology logical inference. Both rows derived under it are mechanically correct given their GO-term inputs; one of those inputs is itself modified in this review, which is noted on the derived row.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automatic annotation. The ARBA rule behind it (ARBA00033921) was fetched and its condition set read; the FunFam it keys on was checked against all seven human sigma paralogs and is discriminative for AP-3 sigmas.

title: Altered trafficking of lysosomal proteins in Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome due to mutations in the beta 3A subunit of the AP-3 adaptor.
review_notes: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 2: beta3A mutations, AP-3 loss and mislocalised CD63, LAMP-1 and LAMP-2. Complex-level, used for the lysosomal-sorting argument behind the GO:0006896 modification. Cached abstract-only.

title: Assembly and function of AP-3 complexes in cells expressing mutant subunits.
review_notes: The subunit-assembly genetics: in delta-null cells sigma3 is left monomeric, in beta3A-null cells delta and sigma3 coassemble. The clearest genetic statement of sigma3's structural partner, and also the source of the finding that the beta3 clathrin box is dispensable for function. Full text available and read.

title: Recognition of dileucine-based sorting signals from HIV-1 Nef and LIMP-II by the AP-1 gamma-sigma1 and AP-3 delta-sigma3 hemicomplexes.
review_notes: The decisive paper for this gene's molecular function: yeast three-hybrid demonstration that acidic dileucine signals bind the delta-sigma3 hemicomplex of AP-3 and the gamma1-sigma1A hemicomplex of AP-1, and not the AP-2 or AP-4 equivalents. Also the only source that tests sigma3A and sigma3B side by side. Full text available and read. Not found by affinage.

title: Localization of the AP-3 adaptor complex defines a novel endosomal exit site for lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Immuno-EM localisation of AP-3 to budding profiles on tubular sorting endosomes, and the basis for treating the mammalian AP-3 route as endosome-to-lysosome rather than Golgi-to-vacuole. Full text available and read.

title: An ear-core interaction regulates the recruitment of the AP-3 complex to membranes.
review_notes: A sigma3-specific regulatory mechanism: the delta ear binds sigma3 and blocks Arf binding without affecting dileucine-signal binding, inhibiting membrane recruitment. Used for a knowledge gap and a suggested experiment rather than for an annotation, since it describes regulation of sigma3 rather than an activity of sigma3. Cached abstract-only; the abstract carries the claims used.

title: Genetic analysis of the neuronal and ubiquitous AP-3 adaptor complexes reveals divergent functions in brain.
review_notes: The beta3A/beta3B genetic comparison in mouse brain, cited by ComplexPortal for the two synaptic rows. Supports the existence of a neuronal AP-3 variant containing sigma3A and its role in synaptic vesicle composition; does not address coated-pit formation, which is why the synaptic-vesicle-coating term is modified. Full text is now cached; this availability correction does not claim a new full-text assessment.

title: Functions of adaptor protein (AP)-3 and AP-1 in tyrosinase sorting from endosomes to melanosomes.
review_notes: The source of this gene's protein-binding IPI, and the paper that identifies the partner as a dileucine cargo rather than a generic interactor: the tyrosinase tail binds the delta-sigma3 hemicomplexes, and AP-3-deficient melanocytes missort tyrosinase into endosomes. Full text available and read. Not found by affinage.

title: BLOC-1 interacts with BLOC-2 and the AP-3 complex to facilitate protein trafficking on endosomes.
review_notes: BLOC-1/AP-3 interaction on early-endosome tubules; the source of the mouse CACAO IMP behind the transferred 'membrane' row. Cited to show that the source experiment supports a far more specific location than the root-level term transferred from it. Cached abstract-only.

title: The gamma/sigma1 and alpha/sigma2 hemicomplexes of clathrin adaptors AP-1 and AP-2 harbor the dileucine recognition site.
review_notes: Independent biochemical confirmation that the dileucine site sits on the large/sigma hemicomplex rather than on beta or mu, using purified AP-1 and AP-2 subunits. Not about AP-3, and cited only for that shared architectural point. Cached abstract-only.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome protein complexes associate with phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase type II alpha in neuronal and non-neuronal cells.
review_notes: The AP-3 cross-linking/mass-spectrometry study that is the proximate source of the mouse GO:0035651 IDA. Cited to show what the experiment actually was -- AP-3 as bait, BLOC-1, BLOC-2, HOPS, clathrin and PI4KIIalpha as the associated proteins -- while the argument for removing the transferred row rests on the term's relation type, not on the assay. Cached abstract-only, and the review says so explicitly rather than second-guessing it.

title: Combined zebrafish-yeast chemical-genetic screens reveal gene-copper-nutrition interactions that modulate melanocyte pigmentation.
review_notes: A zebrafish-yeast chemical-genetic screen in which partial knockdown of the ap3s1 orthologue itself sensitises melanocytes to hypopigmentation under low copper. The only gene-level in vivo perturbation of this gene's orthologue in the corpus, which is why it is cited on the melanosome row. Found by affinage; re-read and verified. Full text available.

title: Conservation and diversification of dileucine signal recognition by adaptor protein (AP) complex variants.
review_notes: The mutagenesis paper that maps the dileucine site onto AP-3 and names the sigma3A residues directly (V94D and L109S abolish binding; Arg 15 and Leu 107 contribute). The single most important reference for this gene's molecular function, and the basis for the residue claims and the bioinformatics analysis. Full text available and read. Not found by affinage.

title: The schizophrenia susceptibility factor dysbindin and its associated complex sort cargoes from cell bodies to the synapse.
review_notes: The source of the mouse IMP behind the axonal and synaptic-vesicle transport rows. Read in full to establish what was perturbed: the genetics is the mocha Ap3d1 null, with sigma3 appearing as an immunoblot readout. Correctly cited; the review grades the derived rows non-core on that basis rather than disputing them. Full text available.

title: Differential recognition of a dileucine-based sorting signal by AP-1 and AP-3 reveals a requirement for both BLOC-1 and AP-3 in delivery of OCA2 to melanosomes.
review_notes: OCA2 dileucine-signal mutagenesis separating AP-1-preferring from AP-3-preferring variants, showing that AP-3 binding is required for steady-state melanosome localisation. Cited in a knowledge gap about what distinguishes AP-1 from AP-3 signal preference. Full text available.

title: Cell type-specific Rab32 and Rab38 cooperate with the ubiquitous lysosome biogenesis machinery to synthesize specialized lysosome-related organelles.
review_notes: A Small GTPases commentary on Bultema et al. 2012, and the reference ComplexPortal uses for four of this gene's rows. Correctly cited but broad: a QuickGO query by this reference returns 178 annotations over 48 entities across AP-1, AP-3 and BLOC-2 in human and mouse. Full text available and read; graded LOW for relevance to AP3S1 specifically because it says nothing about sigma3A.

title: A structure-based mechanism for initiation of AP-3 coated vesicle formation.
review_notes: The human AP-3 cryo-EM study. Contains this protein: UniProt maps PDB 9C58, 9C59, 9C5B and 9C5C to Q92572 with chain S over residues 1-193. Source of the NEW structural molecule activity row and of the observation that the sigma3 dileucine pocket is occupied by the beta3 N-terminal extension in the cargo-free state. Full text available and read. Not found by affinage; located by resolving the UniProt PDB cross-references through the RCSB API.

title: Cloning, expression pattern and mapping to 12p 13.2 --> p13.1 of CLAPS3, a gene encoding a novel clathrin-adaptor small chain.
review_notes: The CLAPS3 cloning paper and the source of the AP-type-complex TAS row. Establishes the 193-residue ORF and ubiquitous expression, which is what the annotation rests on. Its title asserts a 12p13.2-p13.1 FISH assignment that is superseded -- HGNC places AP3S1 at 5q22.3-q23.1 and UniProt files it under Chromosome 5 -- so the locus in the citation trail is stale while the protein-level content is sound. Flagged rather than penalised.

title: AP-3: an adaptor-like protein complex with ubiquitous expression.
review_notes: The paper that identified sigma3A and sigma3B and named AP-3. Source of the only IDA on this gene. Projection checked: QuickGO returns 3 annotations over 2 entities for this reference, exactly the two sigma3 proteins, so the row is specific rather than a complex-wide projection. Cached abstract-only.

title: Characterization of the adaptor-related protein complex, AP-3.
review_notes: The companion 1997 characterisation, which raised antibodies against recombinant delta and sigma3 and showed they are the remaining AP-3 subunits. Also the source of the Golgi-region localisation this review treats as superseded-in-resolution rather than wrong. Full text available and read.

title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: Establishes the AP-3/clathrin association through the beta3 appendage. Cited by ComplexPortal for the AP-3-mediated cargo-loading row, which this review accepts as core. Cached abstract-only; the abstract carries the claim used.

title: Mutation in AP-3 delta in the mocha mouse links endosomal transport to storage deficiency in platelets, melanosomes, and synaptic vesicles.
review_notes: The mocha paper: a delta-subunit null linking AP-3 to melanosome, platelet dense granule and synaptic vesicle cargo. Complex-level evidence, used here to support the LRO rows as real biology while grading them non-core for this subunit. Cached abstract-only.

title: Interaction of insulin receptor substrate-1 with the sigma3A subunit of the adaptor protein complex-3 in cultured adipocytes.
review_notes: The sole source of the insulin-receptor-signalling row. Correctly cited and the interaction is real as reported, but the paper itself frames the functional claim as a hypothesis and nothing has confirmed it in 28 years: 5 PMC-indexed citing papers, and UniProt's SUBUNIT line for Q92572 does not list IRS1. Graded LOW_QUALITY for the annotation it supports, not for the biochemistry it reports. Cached abstract-only.

title: AP3S1 (sigma3A): the AP-3 dileucine pocket, and whether sigma3A differs from sigma3B
review_notes: This review's own analysis. Fetches ten sigma subunits live from UniProt, asserts every sequence length, verifies the five literature-named sigma3A residues, reproduces the published sigma2-to-sigma3A correspondences by independent alignment, and reports two deliberately unflattering controls: the verified non-binder sigma4 scores as well at the pocket as the binders, and sigma3A and sigma3B are identical at every pocket position.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP3S1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record. Trust gates clear (self_evaluation_pairwise: win, faith_pct 100.0) and the record describes the right protein -- it names CLAPS3/AP3S1, gives uniprot_accession Q92572 and correctly places it in AP-3 -- so there is no symbol collision. All four of its citations are numeric PMIDs and all four were re-read. Its mechanism_profile GO grounding (GO:0060090) was not imported; the molecular function was re-grounded from the primary literature. Graded MEDIUM because it missed the entire dileucine literature, the AP-3 structure and the subunit-assembly genetics -- the whole molecular-function story for this gene.

title: UniProtKB record Q92572 (AP3S1_HUMAN), AP-3 complex subunit sigma-1
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProt record for Q92572, asserted to be the expected protein (AP3S1_HUMAN, 193 aa) rather than a merged accession. Used for the subcellular location, the PDB and ComplexPortal cross-references, the PANTHER, PROSITE, FunFam and InterPro signatures and the chromosome assignment. Every quoted line is a single physical line of the flat file.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. Correctly applied on all five rows that cite it; four map family-level generalities that hold, and the fifth (GO:0006896) maps a term whose compartment reflects the fungal AP-3 pathway rather than the human one, which is a defect of the mapping target rather than of the reference.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Manual ISS transfer by curator judgment of sequence similarity. Used twice here, both times from mouse Ap3s2, a protein identical in sequence to the human target - about as safe as the method gets. The reservation recorded on those rows is about the scope of the donor experiment, not about the transfer.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA. The node behind the single IBA row was traced in the committed PTHR11753 PAINT slice and its ten seeds resolved individually; two are AP-3 sigma orthologs and the target sits inside the clade. The inference and the level of the term are both right.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt SubCell mapping. Both rows reproduce the SUBCELLULAR LOCATION block faithfully. That block is itself ECO:0000250 by-similarity, so the rows are no stronger than the UniProt inference - but the inference is supported by the 1997 immunofluorescence of the sigma-3-containing complex.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog transfer. Four rows; the orthology calls are correct (mouse and rat Ap3s2). Two of the four inherit a defect from the donor side - a part-versus-binder mis-typing on GO:0035651 and a proteomic visitor detection on GO:0008021 - which is a source problem, not a failure of the transfer method.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology logical inference. Correctly derives axon cytoplasm from the anterograde axonal transport row; it adds no independent evidence and inherits that row's non-core grade.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated IEA methods. Both components of its WITH/FROM were checked against their sources: InterPro IPR027155 is the AP-3-sigma-specific APS3 signature, and ARBA00033921 was fetched from the UniProt ARBA service and its FunFam condition shown to discriminate AP-3 sigma subunits from all other human AP-complex sigmas.

title: Recognition of dileucine-based sorting signals from HIV-1 Nef and LIMP-II by the AP-1 gamma-sigma1 and AP-3 delta-sigma3 hemicomplexes.
review_notes: The single most important paper for this gene and the one the automated deep research missed: it is the only study that assays sigma-3B in a functional readout, cloning sigma-3A and sigma-3B separately and showing that both form delta-sigma3 hemicomplexes that bind the LIMP-II dileucine signal with identical sequence requirements. Full text verified; the title names the hemicomplexes and HIV-1 Nef, which is why a symbol-driven search does not reach it.

title: Genetic analysis of the neuronal and ubiquitous AP-3 adaptor complexes reveals divergent functions in brain.
review_notes: Correctly cited mouse genetics comparing beta-3A and beta-3B AP-3 complexes. Highly relevant to AP-3 in neurons; relevant to AP3S2 only through complex membership, since the isoform variable in the study is beta-3 and the paper says nothing about which sigma paralog is present. Full text is now cached; this availability correction does not claim a new full-text assessment.

title: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome protein complexes associate with phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase type II alpha in neuronal and non-neuronal cells.
review_notes: Correctly cited; it is the source of the mouse GO:0035651 IDA that reaches the human gene by Ensembl transfer. Cached record is abstract-only, and the abstract is sufficient to establish the assay type - cross-linking, AP-3 purification and mass spectrometry - which is what the over-annotation call rests on. The paper's own subject, PI4KIIalpha, is not at issue.

title: Conservation and diversification of dileucine signal recognition by adaptor protein (AP) complex variants.
review_notes: Full text verified. Supplies the composite-site mechanism for all three AP complexes and the substitution map that makes the paralogy argument testable (sigma-3A V94D and L109S). Its statement that it is not known whether the subunit-isoform combinations differ functionally is quoted as the field's own admission of the central gap for this gene.

title: Genome-wide association study in individuals of South Asian ancestry identifies six new type 2 diabetes susceptibility loci.
review_notes: Correctly cited, full text verified. Relevant to the gene's name recognition rather than its function: it labels a 15q26 type 2 diabetes locus AP3S2 while stating that the lead variant is an eQTL for C15orf38 and that PLIN1 is also a candidate. Used only in knowledge_gaps, to record that the disease association is not evidence about this protein.

title: The schizophrenia susceptibility factor dysbindin and its associated complex sort cargoes from cell bodies to the synapse.
review_notes: Correctly cited, full text verified, and the source annotation behind the human GO:0008089 and GO:0048490 rows via mouse Ap3s2. Reading it is what establishes that those rows are complex-level: the AP-3 loss is an Ap3d1 mocha mutant and the sigma subunit is detected with a pan-sigma-3 antibody. Not a criticism of the paper, which makes no sigma-paralog claim.

title: Cell type-specific Rab32 and Rab38 cooperate with the ubiquitous lysosome biogenesis machinery to synthesize specialized lysosome-related organelles.
review_notes: A commentary by the authors on their own primary study, not primary research, which is the right weight for the four NAS rows drawn from it. Its statements about AP-3 at endosomal tubules and about HPS are accurate. One passage is now out of date - it reports as settled that AP-3 acts as a clathrin-binding adaptor - and that is noted where it matters rather than being used as support.

title: Hidden proteome of synaptic vesicles in the mammalian brain.
review_notes: Correctly cited, full text verified. Source of the rat SynGO synaptic-vesicle annotation that reaches the human gene. Quoted for the authors' own statement that AP3 is among the endosomal proteins whose presence in the synaptic-vesicle proteome is explained by visitors or preparation carry-over, which is the basis for marking the transferred row over-annotated.

title: A structure-based mechanism for initiation of AP-3 coated vesicle formation.
review_notes: Full text verified. The human AP-3 cryo-EM core, and the source of two facts used here: that ARF1 is bound principally through delta with the delta-sigma3 hemicomplex binding nearly as well as the whole complex, and that the dileucine site on sigma-3 is occluded by the beta-3 N-terminal extension in the resting state. Built on sigma-3A, which is recorded as a limit rather than glossed.

title: A dileucine motif in TMEM163 is essential for its binding with both AP-3 and BLOC-1 complex.
review_notes: Correctly cited, full text verified. Recent primary evidence that AP-3 selects a cargo through an acidic dileucine motif and that this matters for a lysosome-related organelle, which is the mechanism this subunit contributes to. Relevant to AP3S2 at complex level only: the study works with AP3B1 and does not test which subunit contacts the motif, so it is cited for the cargo and the signal type, not for a sigma-specific claim.

title: Architecture of clathrin-independent AP3:ARF1-coated carriers.
review_notes: Full text verified. Decides the clathrin question for AP-3 by direct reconstitution and cryo-electron tomography, which is what makes two GOA rows modifiable rather than acceptable and rules out GO:0035615 as this gene's complex-level molecular function. Its methods section is also the source for the statement that the structure used AP3S1.

title: AP-3: an adaptor-like protein complex with ubiquitous expression.
review_notes: The founding paper for this gene and the source of its only experimental annotation. PubMed-verified; it cloned human sigma-3A and sigma-3B, showed both are components of AP-3, and measured their expression by Northern and Western blot. Cached record is abstract-only, but every claim drawn from it here is stated in the abstract.

title: Characterization of the adaptor-related protein complex, AP-3.
review_notes: Independent contemporaneous identification of the same subunits, with full text available. Directly relevant because it raised a sigma-3B-specific antibody and reports the sigma-3 doublet in AP-3 immunoprecipitates - the observation that sets the limit on every later pan-sigma-3 antibody experiment.

title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and its in vitro finding that the beta-3 appendage binds the clathrin heavy chain is not in question. The conclusion built on it - that AP-3 function involves clathrin coats - has been contested by direct reconstitution and coat tomography [PMID:42139345], which is why the annotation it supports is modified to a coat-agnostic term rather than accepted as written. Flagged DISPUTED for the downstream claim, not for the citation.

title: AP3S2 bioinformatics: dileucine pocket conservation, WITH/FROM resolution and ARBA rule specificity
review_notes: Local analysis written for this review. Fetches sequences, the ARBA rule and the donor records live, caches nothing that is not regenerable, and asserts no result that its scripts do not compute. Its three conclusions - the dileucine pocket is retained in sigma-3B, human and mouse AP3S2 are identical, and ARBA00033921 discriminates AP-3 sigmas - are each reproducible by deleting cache/ and re-running.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP3S2 (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated deep-research record; trust gates clear, self-evaluation 'win', and it describes the correct protein with no symbol collision. Both of its citations resolve and are about AP3S2. It is accurate as far as it goes and honest that it found no mechanism beyond complex membership, but its recall is narrow: it missed PMID:14691137, the only functional assay on sigma-3B, and with it PMID:21097499, PMID:39705307 and PMID:42139345. Its mechanism_profile GO grounding was not imported; of its three suggestions two were re-derived independently and the third, NTRK3 as a partner, is a fusion-transcript artefact rather than a protein interaction.

title: UniProtKB entry P59780 (AP3S2_HUMAN), AP-3 complex subunit sigma-2
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProt record for P59780, confirmed to be the expected accession and protein. Note that every FUNCTION, SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statement in it carries ECO:0000250 (by similarity), so it is a source for what UniProt asserts rather than for experimental fact. One defect worth reporting upstream: the SUBUNIT line gives the sigma slot as 'APS1 or AP3S2', where APS1 is the yeast AP-1 sigma gene name and the intended human symbol is AP3S1.

title: OpenScientist report on AP4B1-bound tepsin and AP-4 coat assembly
review_notes: Focused AP4B1 knowledge-gap review. It agrees with the local review that AP4B1 is an obligate AP-4 structural subunit, that its clearest subunit-specific interaction is beta4-ear recruitment of tepsin, and that the tepsin/AP-4 coat-assembly mechanism has not been directly reconstituted.

title: AP-4, a novel protein complex related to clathrin adaptors.
review_notes: Canonical abstract read; original full body unavailable. Human-cell complex biochemical evidence is described at abstract scope.

title: Characterization of a fourth adaptor-related protein complex.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity/title verified on 2026-09-28; Targeted cloning, localization and Discussion read. Human epsilon construct is distinguished from mouse beta4 and Rat1 assay hosts.

title: Functional and physical interactions of the adaptor protein complex AP-4 with ADP-ribosylation factors (ARFs).
review_notes: Official PubMed identity/title verified on 2026-09-28; Actual targeted human-epsilon construct Methods, ARF1 nucleotide/switch-mutant Results and deletion controls read.

title: Sorting of the Alzheimer's disease amyloid precursor protein mediated by the AP-4 complex.
review_notes: Canonical abstract only; APP cytoplasmic-tail recognition is by mu4.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: Screen-specific TEPSIN pair table not audited; no wrong-gene claim.

title: Bivalent Motif-Ear Interactions Mediate the Association of the Accessory Protein Tepsin with the AP-4 Adaptor Complex.
review_notes: Canonical abstract plus actual original targeted Methods, ITC/motif binding and cell recruitment Results independently read. Human epsilon ear established; hypothetical coat crosslinking remains a model.

title: The FTS-Hook-FHIP (FHF) complex interacts with AP-4 to mediate perinuclear distribution of AP-4 and its cargo ATG9A.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity/title verified. Canonical abstract and separately preserved original full-body candidate targeted Results/Figure 3 and human-reagent Methods read. The epsilon–tepsin Y2H positive control establishes this interaction; direct HOOK binding is assigned to mu4. The public original-body locator and exact short result are recorded in notes. Canonical cache remains abstract-only and unchanged.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Screen-specific TEPSIN pair table not audited; independent binding corroboration is kept distinct.

title: Structural basis for the dynamic conformations of AP-4 and its association with ARF1.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity verified and canonical full-text targeted human construct Methods, structural, interface-mutant, liposome, bead and cellular Results read. Cellular rescue uses AP4B1 knockout; epsilon interface is tested biochemically.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The interpro2go pipeline. Its two signatures on this protein, IPR001392 and IPR018240, both map to GO:0006886, GO:0016192 and GO:0030131 (checked at the InterPro API). The first two transfer correctly; the third does not, because the signatures are pan-mu-subunit while clathrin adaptor complex membership is not.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: UniProt curator ortholog transfer. The three ISS rows here cite dog AP4M1 (E2RED8) and mouse Ap4m1 (Q9JKC7); QuickGO confirms each donor carries the corresponding experimental annotation, so the transfers are traceable rather than dangling.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO_Central PAINT. Four of the five IBA rows on this gene are placed at the AP-4 mu node PTN000242612 or at nodes seeded by AP-4 subunits including AP4M1 itself. The fifth, GO:0035615, is seeded entirely by AP-1 and AP-2 mu subunits at the deep pan-mu node PTN000055849 and does not survive review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mapping of the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION block. Both rows it supports here (early endosome, Golgi apparatus) correspond to locations the UniProt record states with experimental evidence.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: The inference itself is sound; it is applied here to a molecular function (GO:0008320) that AP4M1 should not carry, so the derived biological process inherits that error. The defect is upstream, not in this GO_REF.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA. The single row it supports here (GO:0005737 cytoplasm, ARBA00026971) is a broad true parent, but of that rule's 2388 condition sets none is fully satisfied by AP4M1's own InterPro, PANTHER, FunFam and taxonomic conditions - see the bioinformatics RESULTS.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combines ARBA with Ensembl Compara orthology projection. Its three rows here each name mouse Ap4m1 or a derived GO term alongside the ARBA rule, and the two ARBA rules involved (ARBA00028630, ARBA00028253) do reproduce on AP4M1's signatures.

title: AP-4, a novel protein complex related to clathrin adaptors.
review_notes: One of the two independent 1999 identifications of AP-4. Establishes the four-subunit composition including mu4 and the trans-Golgi network localization.

title: Characterization of a fourth adaptor-related protein complex.
review_notes: The other 1999 identification. Carries the two facts this review leans on hardest: immunogold EM placing AP-4 on nonclathrin-coated vesicles, and the demonstration that mu4 is the subunit that reads tyrosine-based sorting signals.

title: Signal-binding specificity of the mu4 subunit of the adaptor protein complex AP-4.
review_notes: The mu4 peptide-library screen. Defines the mu4 signal preference and the LAMP-2 signal, and supplies the Tac chimera experiment behind the two lysosomal-transport rows. The chimera result is about what a mu4-selected signal can do, which is why those rows are kept as non-core rather than as core lysosomal sorting.

title: Functional and physical interactions of the adaptor protein complex AP-4 with ADP-ribosylation factors (ARFs).
review_notes: Direct mu4-ARF1 binding, mapped to the mu4 signal-binding domain and explicitly nucleotide-independent. Absent from the entire 53-row GOA set; it is the basis of the NEW GO:0031267 row here. Found by independent PubMed search, not by affinage.

title: AP-4 binds basolateral signals and participates in basolateral sorting in epithelial MDCK cells.
review_notes: MDCK is a canine cell line, and QuickGO shows dog AP4M1 (E2RED8) carrying GO:1903361 IMP and GO:0005769/GO:0005802 IDA from this very PMID. That is what makes the human ISS rows citing E2RED8 traceable to a real experiment in the matching species.

title: Adaptor protein complex-4 (AP-4) is expressed in the central nervous system neurons and interacts with glutamate receptor delta2.
review_notes: Direct mu4-GluRdelta2 binding through motifs other than classical tyrosine-based signals - the clearest statement that mu4's ligand repertoire is not confined to YXXPhi.

title: Accumulation of AMPA receptors in autophagosomes in neuronal axons lacking adaptor protein AP-4.
review_notes: Mouse. The AP-4 beta subunit was the gene disrupted, but MGI annotates mouse Ap4m1 GO:0006605 and GO:0008104 IMP from this paper (checked in QuickGO), consistent with the paper's separate disruption of the AP-4-TARP interaction. Cited here only for the neuronal somatodendritic role, which the human record carries by ISS.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Shotgun proteomics of urinary exosomes. Correctly cited for detection; carries no information about AP4M1 function or steady-state localization.

title: Mutation in the AP4M1 gene provides a model for neuroaxonal injury in cerebral palsy.
review_notes: The founding SPG50 description. Used for disease context and for the glutamate receptor mislocalization phenotype; no GO annotation is proposed from the phenotype itself.

title: Sorting of the Alzheimer's disease amyloid precursor protein mediated by the AP-4 complex.
review_notes: The APP co-crystal with mu4 (PDB 3L81, 4MDR) and the source of UniProt's F255 and R283 mutagenesis features. It is also the sole source of the claim that mu4's binding site is located differently from the other signal-adaptor interactions - a structural claim, which is why this review does not try to substitute a sequence alignment for it.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Binary yeast two-hybrid interactome. Its single AP4M1 edge (USP47) has no follow-up anywhere in the AP-4 literature.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: GFP-tagged affinity purification across a HeLa cell-line library. Its AP4M1 edge is TEPSIN, which is co-complex membership rather than a mu4 binding surface.

title: Bivalent Motif-Ear Interactions Mediate the Association of the Accessory Protein Tepsin with the AP-4 Adaptor Complex.
review_notes: Maps tepsin's two motifs onto the beta-4 and epsilon ear domains, which is what disqualifies the three TEPSIN protein-binding rows as mu4 molecular function. Also states the non-clathrin nature of the AP-4 coat in its opening sentence.

title: Association between Rare Variants in AP4E1, a Component of Intracellular Trafficking, and Persistent Stuttering.
review_notes: The title and the genetics are about AP4E1, but the paper contains a mu4-specific biochemical result - the mu4-NAGPA interaction - which is what both GOA rows citing it record. Not a mis-citation.

title: AP-4 mediates export of ATG9A from the trans-Golgi network to promote autophagosome formation.
review_notes: Identifies ATG9A as the specific AP-4 cargo and places the step at trans-Golgi network export. The single most important functional reference for this gene.

title: Altered distribution of ATG9A and accumulation of axonal aggregates in neurons from a mouse model of AP-4 deficiency syndrome.
review_notes: An AP4E1 knockout mouse, but the ATG9A mislocalization is also shown in fibroblasts from patients carrying mutations in the mu4 subunit specifically. That is the AP4M1-level human evidence for the ATG9A phenotype.

title: AP-4 vesicles contribute to spatial control of autophagy via RUSC-dependent peripheral delivery of ATG9A.
review_notes: Unbiased organellar proteomics reaching the same cargo independently, in AP4M1 patient cells among others, and adding SERINC1/SERINC3 and RUSC1/2. Its reservoir model, rather than direct phagophore delivery, is why no phagophore-assembly-site localization term is proposed here.

title: Axonal autophagosome maturation defect through failure of ATG9A sorting underpins pathology in AP-4 deficiency syndrome.
review_notes: Independent mouse confirmation that ATG9A is an AP-4 cargo retained at the trans-Golgi network when AP-4 function is lost. Used as corroboration only; the annotations rest on the human experiments.

title: The FTS-Hook-FHIP (FHF) complex interacts with AP-4 to mediate perinuclear distribution of AP-4 and its cargo ATG9A.
review_notes: States direct mu4 binding to the Hook1/Hook2 coiled-coil domains, which is the one protein-binding row on this gene that is unambiguously a mu4 surface and unambiguously domain-specific.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Its two AP4M1 edges (FNTA and a USP47 isoform) have no functional follow-up.

title: The role of AP-4 in cargo export from the trans-Golgi network and hereditary spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: Authoritative review by the group that did much of the primary work. Used for the consensus statement of the pathway; every mechanistic claim in this review is also anchored to a primary paper.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 affinity-purification mass spectrometry. Its AP4M1 edge is TEPSIN, i.e. co-purification of the AP-4 coat.

title: Intrathecal AAV9/AP4M1 gene therapy for hereditary spastic paraplegia 50 shows safety and efficacy in preclinical studies.
review_notes: Preclinical gene therapy. Relevant to this review only as evidence that restoring AP4M1 alone restores AP-4 function, i.e. that mu4 is the limiting subunit in patient cells. No GO annotation is proposed from it.

title: Identification of two new mu-adaptin-related proteins, mu-ARP1 and mu-ARP2.
review_notes: The cloning paper that named mu-ARP2, later renamed mu4/AP4M1. Used here only for the paralog identity figure, which this review reproduces independently by alignment.

title: trans-Golgi Network Vesicle Budding
review_notes: The pathway's own summary (cached in reactome/R-HSA-199992.md) describes clathrin coats nucleated by AP-1, not the AP-4 coat. The GO term it carries here, post-Golgi vesicle-mediated transport, is nonetheless correct for AP-4 as a broad parent.

title: AP4 transports APP from trans-Golgi network to endosome lumen
review_notes: The biology in the cached summary is right - mu4 recognizes the APP tyrosine signal and APP moves from the trans-Golgi network to endosomes. Two of the three GO terms derived from it are not: transmembrane protein transporter activity reads the reaction class as a translocase step, and endosome lumen assigns the adaptor the compartment of its cargo.

title: AP4 binds APP
review_notes: Cached summary correctly describes AP-4 composition and mu4 signal recognition. The single GO term it carries here, trans-Golgi network membrane, is right.

title: AP4M1 bioinformatics - cargo-signal site, GOA reconciliation and ARBA rule reproducibility
review_notes: Written for this review. All sequences and rules are fetched live from UniProt at run time; the scripts assert the sequence length and the two UniProt mutagenesis residues before drawing any conclusion, and the one negative result (F255 is conserved in every mu paralog, so it carries no mu4-specific information) is reported rather than suppressed.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP4M1 (human)
review_notes: Trust gate tripped - the record's own head-to-head self-evaluation scored pairwise = tie against the curated UniProt reference, and the narrative bears that out. Its six citations are the cloning paper plus five clinical/genetic/iPSC-line papers, and it states that the cargo-recognition mechanism has not been further characterized in the available corpus, which is the opposite of the truth for this gene. Its GO grounding (GO:0060090) was not imported; nothing in this review rests on this record.

title: UniProtKB O00189 (AP4M1_HUMAN) flat-file record
review_notes: The curated record, entry version 194 (2026-09-02), sequence version 2, 453 aa. Accession checked: it returns AP-4 complex subunit mu-1 and not a merged entry.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO pipeline reference behind the GO:0015031 row. Verified as applicable rather than assumed: the InterPro API returns exactly three entries for Q9Y587 and IPR016635 is among them, so unlike the two ARBA rows this annotation is reproducible from its stated source.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT phylogenetic-inference reference behind the single IBA. Verified against the family's own PAINT slice: PTHR11753 has exactly one annotated node, PTN000204281, carrying two IBD rows and no IRD or IKR, and the GO:0016192 IBD seed list matches the row's WITH/FROM apart from one fly gene that seeds the node's other IBD row.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The UniProt subcellular-location mapping reference behind the GO:0005794 row. SL-0132 is Golgi apparatus and the entry's own location line reads 'Golgi apparatus, trans-Golgi network membrane', so the mapping faithfully restates a curated statement, losing only the TGN refinement.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: The ARBA machine-learning reference behind the GO:0005737 and GO:0012505 rows. Marked LOW_QUALITY on the basis of a specific check rather than a prior about machine learning: fetching both rules from https://rest.uniprot.org/arba/ and intersecting all 2388 and 533 condition sets against AP4S1's three real InterPro matches shows that neither annotation can be reproduced from its own rule's published conditions. Both terms are biologically correct, so the objection is to the traceability of the derivation, not to the calls.

title: AP-4, a novel protein complex related to clathrin adaptors.
review_notes: One of the two 1999 papers that discovered AP-4, and the original_reference_id of the IDA complex row and both IC rows. Abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract itself carries the load-bearing statements: sigma4 as a component of the tetramer by gel filtration, sedimentation velocity and immunoprecipitation, and AP-4 at the TGN with brefeldin-A-sensitive membrane association. Reference projection checked: QuickGO returns 13 annotations over exactly 4 entities for this reference, the four AP-4 subunits, which is the expected per-subunit projection of one complex characterisation.

title: Characterization of a fourth adaptor-related protein complex.
review_notes: The other 1999 discovery paper and the original_reference_id of all three ComplexPortal NAS rows. Abstract-only in the cache; the abstract supplies the immunogold localisation to non-clathrin-coated vesicles at the TGN and, importantly for this review, attributes tyrosine-signal recognition to mu4 rather than to sigma4. Reference projection checked: 32 annotations over 10 entities, including the human and mouse AP-4 ComplexPortal complexes and mouse subunit orthologues.

title: Similar subunit interactions contribute to assembly of clathrin adaptor complexes and COPI complex: analysis using yeast three-hybrid system.
review_notes: The single most AP4S1-specific mechanistic result in the literature, and the basis of the proposed GO:0005198 row: epsilon and beta4 interact only in the presence of sigma4. Abstract-only in the cache, but the statement is in the abstract verbatim. Absent from the deep-research report, which is unsurprising - the title names clathrin adaptor complexes and COPI, not this gene. Verified on PubMed as Takatsu et al., Biochem Biophys Res Commun 2001.

title: Functional and physical interactions of the adaptor protein complex AP-4 with ADP-ribosylation factors (ARFs).
review_notes: Establishes AP-4 as an ARF1 effector and, decisively for the endosome-lumen row, states in its own abstract that the four-subunit complex localises to the cytoplasmic face of the TGN. It also shows the direct ARF1 contacts are made by epsilon and mu4, which is the same division of labour the 2026 cryo-EM structure confirms and another place where sigma4 is not the binding subunit. Abstract-only in the cache, and all three of those statements are in the abstract. Missed by the deep-research report.

title: AP-4 binds basolateral signals and participates in basolateral sorting in epithelial MDCK cells.
review_notes: Basolateral sorting by AP-4 in MDCK cells; the source of the basolateral clause in UniProt's FUNCTION text. Abstract-only. Relevant as context for what AP-4 does, but the functional depletion was of mu4, not sigma4, so nothing is annotated to AP4S1 from it.

title: Recognition of dileucine-based sorting signals from HIV-1 Nef and LIMP-II by the AP-1 gamma-sigma1 and AP-3 delta-sigma3 hemicomplexes.
review_notes: The 2003 yeast three-hybrid paper often cited as establishing that the epsilon-sigma4 hemicomplex does not bind dileucine signals. Correctly cited but weaker than it is usually taken to be, which is why it is MEDIUM rather than HIGH: it tested two signals and scored alphaC-sigma2 negative alongside epsilon-sigma4, and the alphaC-sigma2 half did not hold. Its GST pull-down arm is weaker still for AP-4, since the input preparation contained only traces of AP-4. The paper says as much itself in the discussion. The load-bearing citation for the sigma4 negative is PMID:21097499.

title: Sorting of the Alzheimer's disease amyloid precursor protein mediated by the AP-4 complex.
review_notes: The APP-AP-4 interaction paper, and the primary source behind both Reactome reactions cited in this record. Abstract-only. Cited here for what it settles about subunit division of labour - the YKFFE signal binds mu4 - rather than for anything it says about sigma4, which is nothing.

title: Conservation and diversification of dileucine signal recognition by adaptor protein (AP) complex variants.
review_notes: The decisive paper for the question of whether sigma4 contributes to cargo-signal recognition. Three canonical dileucine signals bind gamma1-sigma1A, alphaC-sigma2 and delta-sigma3A but not epsilon-sigma4, in one assay with working positive controls - including alphaC-sigma2, whose negative in the 2003 predecessor did not survive. It also supplies the two-part basic patch model and the large-subunit anchor residues used in the bioinformatics here. Verified against the cached full text.

title: Adaptor protein complex 4 deficiency causes severe autosomal-recessive intellectual disability, progressive spastic paraplegia, shy character, and short stature.
review_notes: The founding SPG52 report and the source of UniProt's DISEASE line. Cited here for the disease association and, in the isoform knowledge gap, for numbering its variant on NM_007077.3, the non-canonical isoform frame. Verified against the cached full text.

title: Structural and functional characterization of cargo-binding sites on the μ4-subunit of adaptor protein complex 4.
review_notes: Structural and functional dissection of the two cargo-binding sites on mu4. Cited for the same reason as PMID:20230749 - it locates AP-4's cargo recognition on the medium subunit - and not for any claim about sigma4.

title: Recessive loss-of-function mutations in AP4S1 cause mild fever-sensitive seizures, developmental delay and spastic paraplegia through loss of AP-4 complex assembly.
review_notes: The key AP4S1 loss-of-function paper: sigma4 absent in patient fibroblasts, all other subunits reduced, hemicomplex and complete-complex assembly both lost, tepsin membrane recruitment abolished, AP-1 assembly normal as an internal control. Full text cached and every quoted sentence verified against it. Present in the deep-research report, and confirmed independently.

title: AP-4 vesicles contribute to spatial control of autophagy via RUSC-dependent peripheral delivery of ATG9A.
review_notes: The Dynamic Organellar Maps study that identified ATG9A, SERINC1 and SERINC3 as AP-4 cargo and RUSC1/RUSC2 as accessory proteins. Cited for the cargo repertoire in the description. The perturbations were of AP4B1 and AP4E1, so it supports complex-level statements rather than AP4S1-specific ones.

title: Axonal autophagosome maturation defect through failure of ATG9A sorting underpins pathology in AP-4 deficiency syndrome.
review_notes: The Ap4e1 knockout mouse showing that TGN retention of ATG9A depletes axonal ATG9A and produces distal axonal swellings. Cited only in the knowledge gap about the missing causal step, because the perturbation is mouse Ap4e1 rather than human AP4S1 and so supports no annotation on this gene. Full text cached and verified.

title: Utilizing RNA and outlier analysis to identify an intronic splice-altering variant in AP4S1 in a sibling pair with progressive spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: An intronic AP4S1 variant causing exon 5 skipping, identified by RNA outlier analysis. Cited for the isoform knowledge gap, where it supplies a third naming frame: it calls NM_001128126.3 the 'canonical isoform 2', while UniProt calls that transcript's product isoform 1 and reserves Q9Y587-2 for the NM_007077 product. Abstract-only in the cache, and the statement quoted is in the abstract.

title: Adaptor protein complex 4 deficiency: a paradigm of childhood-onset hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by defective protein trafficking.
review_notes: The source of the proposed GO:0006892 row, and the only paper that provides human AP4S1 loss-of-function evidence for a transport phenotype: four AP4S1 fibroblast lines among fifteen, ATG9A retained in the TGN in all patient lines without exception, rescued by re-expressing an AP-4 subunit. It is also the source of the measured negative that keeps an autophagy term off this gene, since autophagic flux was intact in those same cells. Full text cached and verified.

title: Loss of ap4s1 in zebrafish leads to neurodevelopmental defects resembling spastic paraplegia 52.
review_notes: The zebrafish ap4s1 morpholino model, plus patient fibroblasts showing reduced AP-4 complex formation. Supports the gene's neurodevelopmental role but is not annotated on the human gene, since morpholino knockdown in zebrafish would be an ISS or ISO transfer rather than an IMP on human AP4S1.

title: Defining the clinical, molecular and imaging spectrum of adaptor protein complex 4-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: The international AP-4-HSP cohort paper establishing that the four genetic subtypes share one phenotype. Cited for the disease framing in the description. Clinical rather than mechanistic, hence MEDIUM.

title: High-throughput imaging of ATG9A distribution as a diagnostic functional assay for adaptor protein complex 4-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: Turns the ATG9A ratio into a quantitative functional assay validated on AP4S1 probands; corroborates the proposed GO:0006892 row. Also the source of the observation that AP4S1's domain figure is drawn on Q9Y587-2. One slip noted rather than relied on: its methods say the AP4S1 alignment was transferred from isoforms of Q9Y6B7, which is AP4B1's accession, not AP4S1's. That does not affect the functional data quoted here.

title: The adaptor protein chaperone AAGAB stabilizes AP-4 complex subunits.
review_notes: AAGAB binds and stabilises epsilon and sigma4 specifically, showing AP-4 assembly is chaperoned rather than spontaneous. One of the few papers that names sigma4 as a direct participant in a molecular event, and therefore supporting evidence for the structural-molecule function. Full text cached and verified. Missed by the deep-research report.

title: Ap4s1 truncation leads to axonal defects in a zebrafish model of spastic paraplegia 52.
review_notes: CRISPR truncation of zebrafish ap4s1 giving motor impairment and distal axonal degeneration. Abstract-only in the cache, and the cache confirms full text is unavailable. Cited only in the knowledge gap about the missing causal step, as evidence that the axonal phenotype is reproducible in a second organism.

title: Heterozygous variants in AP4S1 are not associated with a neurological phenotype.
review_notes: A measured negative worth recording: 28 heterozygous carriers of the AP4S1 p.Arg97Ter allele, none with the proposed dominant phenotype. It refutes a 2024 case report and fixes the inheritance as strictly recessive, which is what the description states. Full text cached and verified. Missed by the deep-research report.

title: Uncovering cargo clients and accessory factors of AP-1 and AP-4 through vesicle proteomics.
review_notes: Vesicle proteomics defining AP-1 and AP-4 cargo repertoires, and the source of the statement that AP-4-mediated TGN export is clathrin-independent and its vesicle-biogenesis factors uncharacterised - the premise of the ontology knowledge gap. The AP-4 arm used AP4E1-deficient cells, so it is complex-level evidence.

title: Structural basis for the dynamic conformations of AP-4 and its association with ARF1.
review_notes: The cryo-EM structures of the AP-4 core and the AP-4/ARF1 complex. Found through the EMDB cross-references in the UniProt entry rather than through the deep-research report, which predates or missed it. It states the sigma4 construct as UniProt Q9Y587 explicitly, shows the epsilon trunk wrapping sigma4, places both ARF1 sites away from sigma4, and measures the ATG9A peptide against mu4-CTD by ITC - so it settles both what sigma4 does structurally and what it does not do in cargo binding. Full text cached and verified.

title: AP4 transports APP from trans-Golgi network to endosome lumen
review_notes: The reaction itself is a reasonable model of APP transport, but as a source of a cellular-component annotation for AP4S1 it is miscited: its output entity is the AP4:APP complex placed in compartment 'endosome lumen', and the Reactome-to-GO mapping hands that compartment to all four AP-4 subunits, which are cytosolic coat proteins. Verified through the Reactome ContentService (it is a BlackBoxEvent) and through QuickGO, which returns 11 annotations over 5 entities for this reference. The trans-Golgi network membrane row from the same reaction is fine; the endosome lumen row is not.

title: AP4 binds APP
review_notes: The better-modelled of the two reactions: inputs and output all at the trans-Golgi network membrane, which is where AP-4 is, and a summary that attributes tyrosine-signal recognition to AP4M1 rather than to this subunit. Verified through the Reactome ContentService.

title: AP4S1 (sigma4): is the large-subunit half of the dileucine basic patch present in AP-4 epsilon?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review: does epsilon carry the large-subunit half of the dileucine basic patch? All eight sequences fetched live from UniProt with lengths asserted; a 6/6 method control on the three published anchors gates the answer; the finding is that all three anchors map to epsilon Thr44 while sigma4 retains the sigma-side Arg15. It supports no annotation - no cargo-binding function is proposed for AP4S1 either way - and the write-up states explicitly that it is a hypothesis consistent with the measured negative rather than a test of it.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP4S1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record. Trust gates clear per .affinage.log, self_evaluation_pairwise 'win', faith_pct 100, and all eight citations are numeric PMIDs with no preprints. It describes the right protein - no symbol collision - and each of its eight dated findings checks out against the cited paper. Its weakness is recall, not accuracy: it missed every paper that bears on sigma4's own molecular function (PMID:11409905, PMID:41565640, PMID:21097499, PMID:35976721), the mu4 cargo-site work, and the 2025 negative on heterozygous carriers. Its mechanism_profile GO ids were not imported; both molecular-function terms used here were re-grounded from the primary literature and placed in different slots than a direct import would have given.

title: UniProtKB Q9Y587 (AP4S1_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: UniProtKB flat file for Q9Y587, entry version 188, sequence version 1, 144 aa. Confirmed to be the expected accession and protein (AP4S1_HUMAN) rather than a merged redirect. Its SUBUNIT, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and DR lines are quoted directly; its FUNCTION text is treated as curator summary and its claims are traced to the primary papers rather than quoted as evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO pipeline reference behind the single IEA row. Checked at source rather than assumed: the InterPro API returns IPR038741 as a family-type entry named "AP-5 complex subunit beta-1" whose only GO mapping is GO:0016197 endosomal transport. The signature is AP5B1-specific, not a pan-adaptin one, so the mapping cannot reach proteins outside this orthologue group.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT reference behind both IBA rows. The committed family slice interpro/panther/PTHR34033/PTHR34033-paint.tsv shows a single node, PTN002145545, at taxon:2759, carrying exactly the two IBD assertions that appear as IBAs here, each seeded by UniProtKB:Q2VPB7 alone.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Source of the HDA lysosomal-membrane row. Abstract-only in the cache. A broad proteomics projection - QuickGO returns 246 annotations across 242 distinct entities for this reference - so it would be weak on its own, but the assignment it made in 2007 for a then-anonymous protein has since been confirmed three times by targeted work on AP-5. The abstract's "12 novel proteins of unknown functions" is where AP5B1 sat at the time. Missed by the deep research report.

title: A genome-scale DNA repair RNAi screen identifies SPG48 as a novel gene associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: Supplies four of the twelve IPI rows and is the study that identified zeta-5 and sigma-5. Its title is about a DNA repair screen, which is exactly why it is easy to dismiss: the full text shows reciprocal BAC-tagged immunoprecipitations in which AP5B1 (as DKFZp761E198) was itself one of the baits, establishing a five-protein complex. It also contains a measured negative for this gene - AP5B1 knockdown had no effect in the homologous-recombination assay, unlike three of its complex partners - which is why no DNA repair annotation belongs here. Not cited by the deep research report.

title: The fifth adaptor protein complex.
review_notes: The single most important paper for this gene and the source of every AP5B1-specific experiment in GOA: the two-hybrid interaction mapped to residues 16-229, the destabilisation of mu-5 on AP5B1 knockdown, the CIMPR/Vps26 knockdown phenotype with four independent siRNAs, the electron microscopy, the clathrin-motif analysis, and the renaming of the protein to beta-5. It also corrected the database sequence, adding the missing N-terminal 57 residues to give the 878 aa entry that UniProt now carries. Has a published erratum (PLoS Biol 2012;10(3)) which does not touch any claim used here. Not cited by the deep research report, which cites the 2013 follow-up instead.

title: Adaptor protein complexes AP-4 and AP-5: new players in endosomal trafficking and progressive spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: A review, cited by the deep research report as its lowest-confidence item. Resolves to the paper described and is accurate, but it is secondary and pre-dates everything that decides this review. Retained for provenance of the deep-research assessment; no claim rests on it.

title: Interaction between AP-5 and the hereditary spastic paraplegia proteins SPG11 and SPG15.
review_notes: Establishes the native hexamer and its 1:1:1:1:1:1 stoichiometry, the shared CIMPR phenotype across all six knockdowns, the late endosomal/lysosomal colocalisation, and the coat model in which AP-5 sorts, spastizin docks and spatacsin scaffolds. Abstract-only in the cache, but every claim used here is stated in the abstract. A narrow reference - QuickGO returns 8 annotations across 4 entities - so it is a targeted study, not a projection.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary yeast two-hybrid map; source of the CAMK2B and NIF3L1 IPI rows. Correctly cited and methodologically sound, but a 937-entity projection (24,599 annotations) in which AP5B1 contributes two cells. Neither partner appears anywhere in the AP-5 literature, which is why both rows are marked over-annotated rather than promoted or removed.

title: Loss of AP-5 results in accumulation of aberrant endolysosomes: defining a new type of lysosomal storage disease.
review_notes: Cited by the deep research report and independently verified. Supplies the loss-side counterpart to the lysosome-organisation annotation: patient fibroblasts and siRNA-treated HeLa cells accumulate multilamellar endolysosomal storage material. The evidence is on AP-5 zeta and mu, not on beta-5 specifically, so it supports the complex-level claim and is used that way.

title: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Type 2 (HIV-2) Gag Is Trafficked in an AP-3 and AP-5 Dependent Manner.
review_notes: Cited by the deep research report; resolves to the paper described and its finding is real. Deliberately not annotated. The siRNA used is against AP5M1 ("AP-5u ON-TARGETplus AP5M1 J-015523-09"), not AP5B1, and a virus exploiting a host trafficking route is not a function of the host gene product. Recorded so that a later reviewer does not add a viral-process term on the strength of the title.

title: Role of the AP-5 adaptor protein complex in late endosome-to-Golgi retrieval.
