review_notes: The paper that resolved the direction of the trafficking defect, by CRISPR knockout of AP5Z1 with subcellular fractionation profiling and quantitative mass spectrometry. It is the basis for refining endosomal transport to retrograde transport, endosome to Golgi. It is also the clearest statement of what remains unknown - that nothing was known about AP-5's cargo - which is what keeps a cargo-adaptor molecular function out of this review. Evidence is at the level of the complex (AP5Z1 knockout), not of AP5B1.

title: Rag GTPases and phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate mediate recruitment of the AP-5/SPG11/SPG15 complex.
review_notes: The recruitment mechanism, and the paper that names AP5B1 explicitly as one of the four AP-5 subunits assembling with SPG11 into the SPG15-GFP complex. Important for what it places elsewhere: the PI3P contact is made by the spastizin FYVE domain, so no lipid-binding function is attributed to AP5B1 here. Also useful for its honest survey of conflicting localisation reports for this complex.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex affinity-purification mass spectrometry; source of two IPI rows. A 2,196-entity projection across 9,514 annotations. Its SPG11 row is treated as informative only because that partner is independently established by four targeted studies; its CAMK2B row is marked over-annotated, as is the two-hybrid row for the same partner. Agreement between two high-throughput methods is not the same as independent functional support.

title: Bi-allelic variants in three genes encoding distinct subunits of the vesicular AP-5 complex cause hereditary macular dystrophy.
review_notes: The newest reference the deep research report caught, and the basis for the NEW retina homeostasis row. Two families with bi-allelic AP5B1 alleles, all truncating and removing more than two-thirds of the protein, within a 19-family AP-5 cohort. It also contains the first subunit-specific localisation of AP5B1 protein, by immunofluorescence in human RPE explants and iPSC-RPE, showing puncta overlapping Rab7 and partially TGN46.

title: Structural basis for membrane remodeling by the AP5-SPG11-SPG15 complex.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the SPG11-SPG15 and AP5-SPG11-SPG15 assemblies; AP5B1 residues 1-878 are chain B of PDB 8YAB and 8YAH. Source of the in vitro membrane-remodelling and curvature-sensing activity and of the autolysosome-tubulation role, and the reference ComplexPortal cites for four of the six NAS rows. Abstract-only in the cache, which is a real limitation here: it is why this review does not state which subunit provides the curvature-sensing surface or which one contacts SPG11.

title: Bi-allelic variants in AP5Z1 and AP5B1 lead to retinal degeneration.
review_notes: Independent replication cohort, five probands from Europe and Iran, including two carrying the recurrent AP5B1 p.Leu785Pro allele and one compound heterozygote with a frameshift. Published after the deep research run and found by independent Europe PMC searching. Corroborates the NEW row without being its primary citation.

title: The AP5B1 p.Leu785Pro variant is a frequent cause of late-onset macular dystrophy with variable extraocular manifestations.
review_notes: The largest AP5B1-specific cohort, 22 affected individuals from 20 families, and the paper that establishes p.Leu785Pro as a founder allele in European and Ashkenazi Jewish populations with an odds ratio of 11.9 against gnomAD controls. Published after the deep research run and found by independent Europe PMC searching; it is the strongest single piece of human evidence that AP5B1 loss of function has a phenotype.

title: AP5B1 (beta-5 adaptin): does it carry the beta-adaptin clathrin-binding apparatus?
review_notes: Analysis written for this review, fetching sequences from UniProt and domain boundaries and structural features from InterPro and UniProt at run time, with the four classical beta adaptins as controls. It re-tests the four 2011 claims about clathrin binding rather than repeating them, and confirms all four. The fourth, that the AP5B1 WDW is unavailable to clathrin, is confirmed by a PDBe polymer-coverage check showing residues 223-229 modelled inside 8YAB chain B's 7-631 span, between a solenoid helix and a disordered region - so the motif is an ordered island in an inter-helical loop of the trunk. An earlier revision of this document read the same position as lying outside the solenoid, on the strength of no Pfam domain and no UniProt feature covering residue 223; that was an over-reading of an absence, since neither database annotates inter-helical loops, and the document now records the correction rather than having overwritten it. The analysis also establishes the PANTHER family separation that makes beta-adaptin term leakage impossible on this gene, and it states its own caveats: the family-specific versus pan-family Pfam model asymmetry, and the fact that the appendage region carrying the one clathrin-box consensus match is itself unmodelled in the structure.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP5B1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched provider record used as a lead, not as evidence. Trust gates clear (self_evaluation_pairwise win, faith 100%), the accession matches the local UniProt entry, the narrative describes the right protein with no symbol collision, and all seven citations are numeric PMIDs that resolve to the papers described. Its mechanism_profile GO grounding was not imported and would have been wrong if it had been: it proposes GO:0060090 molecular adaptor activity, which overstates what has been shown, given that AP-5's cargo interaction is explicitly unknown. Recall was the weak point - it missed PMID:22022230 and PMID:20613862, the two papers containing every AP5B1-specific experiment in GOA, and the two 2026 disease cohorts. No supporting_text anywhere in this review cites this file, which leaves the "no annotations reference available deep research files" best-practice warning standing deliberately: a provider synthesis is a lead, and every claim it suggested was re-anchored to the primary source or to the UniProt record before being used.

title: UniProtKB Q2VPB7 (AP5B1_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: The curated record, checked to be the expected accession and not a merged one. Used for the 878-residue length, the PANTHER family assignment (PTHR34033, not the beta-adaptin family PTHR11134), the four AP5B1-specific InterPro/Pfam signatures, the ComplexPortal CPX-5181 cross-reference, the PDB 8YAB chain assignment, the IntAct NbExp counts used to weigh the IPI rows, and the absence of any ACT_SITE or BINDING feature. Its FUNCTION line is notably hedged ("a probable fifth adaptor protein complex it may be involved in endosomal transport"), which matches how little is established about the molecular activity.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT/IBA reference behind all five IBA rows. Traced to its node: the committed slice interpro/panther/PTHR16082/PTHR16082-paint.tsv shows five IBDs on PTN002699615, all seeded by UniProtKB:Q9H0R1 and placed at taxon:2759, with no IRD or IKR in the family.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Behind the three SubCell IEA rows. Each maps faithfully onto a subcellular location line of the UniProt record; the two membrane terms inherit that record's ECO:0000305 curator inference from PubMed:22022230, which is the correct strength.

title: A novel protein, MUDENG, induces cell death in cytotoxic T cells.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt for the cell-death function. The evidence is ectopic overexpression in Jurkat and HeLa cells arising from a randomised ribozyme screen, with no mechanism and no link to AP-5. Abstract-only in cache. Correctly cited, methodologically weak for a function claim.

title: The fifth adaptor protein complex.
review_notes: The founding AP-5 paper and the source of nine of the twenty GOA rows. Full text cached. It is also the only paper that perturbs mu-5 itself for a trafficking readout, by siRNA with both a SMARTpool and individual oligos.

title: MUDENG is cleaved by caspase-3 during TRAIL-induced cell death.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Reports caspase-3 cleavage at D276 and D290; both are aspartates inside the annotated MHD in Q9H0R1 sequence version 2, checked in AP5M1-bioinformatics. Being a caspase substrate is something done to the protein rather than an activity of it, so nothing is annotated from it.

title: Interaction between AP-5 and the hereditary spastic paraplegia proteins SPG11 and SPG15.
review_notes: Establishes the 1:1:1:1:1:1 hexamer and that knocking down any of the six components, mu-5 included, traps the CIMPR in early endosomes. The cache is abstract-only, so only abstract sentences are quoted from it.

title: Spastic paraplegia proteins spastizin and spatacsin mediate autophagic lysosome reformation.
review_notes: Abstract-only. The primary autophagic lysosome reformation paper. It is about the two partner proteins, spastizin and spatacsin, not about AP5M1, so nothing is annotated to this gene from it; it is cited only as evidence that the process the proposed new term names is real and named in the literature, and to align this term request with the one already made in the ZFYVE26 review.

title: Loss of AP-5 results in accumulation of aberrant endolysosomes: defining a new type of lysosomal storage disease.
review_notes: Full text cached. Provides the direct evidence that mu-5 is an obligate subunit, its protein level falling both in AP5Z1-nonsense patient fibroblasts and on spastizin knockdown, which the authors attribute to instability of unassembled AP subunits.

title: Characterization of MUDENG, a novel anti-apoptotic protein.
review_notes: Full text cached. Reports the opposite sign to PMID:18395520 and PMID:31427081, with MuD depletion sensitising astroglioma cells to TRAIL. Its endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial localisation rests on a crude microsomal preparation made with a commercial ER isolation kit, a fraction that co-purifies endosomes and lysosomes, so it is not resolution enough to contradict the endolysosomal localisation and no ER or mitochondrion term is proposed from it.

title: Role of the AP-5 adaptor protein complex in late endosome-to-Golgi retrieval.
review_notes: Full text cached. Identifies the transport step AP-5 acts in. The perturbation is a CRISPR knockout of AP5Z1, not of AP5M1, which is why it is used here together with the mu-5-specific knockdowns rather than on its own. It also states plainly that the conserved AP cargo-binding sites are absent from AP-5.

title: BAX is an essential key mediator of AP5M1-induced apoptosis in cervical carcinoma cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Overexpression of AP5M1 is pro-apoptotic and BAX-dependent in cervical carcinoma lines. The same overexpression limitation as PMID:18395520, and the opposite sign to PMID:27136675 and PMID:41915273.

title: Bi-allelic variants in three genes encoding distinct subunits of the vesicular AP-5 complex cause hereditary macular dystrophy.
review_notes: Full text cached. First disease association for AP5M1 itself, in three families carrying p.Arg33Ter, p.Trp389Ter and p.Tyr313Cys, with an independent immunofluorescence localisation in human RPE and iPSC-RPE. Its statement that AP4M1 Tyr284 corresponds to AP5M1 Tyr313 was used as the positive control for the alignment in AP5M1-bioinformatics.

title: Structural basis for membrane remodeling by the AP5-SPG11-SPG15 complex.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the AP5-SPG11-SPG15 assembly and the only source of a molecular activity for the complex. The cache is abstract-only. The depositions were checked directly via the RCSB REST API, and in both 8YAB and 8YAH the mu-5 and zeta entities map to the mouse orthologues Q8BJ63 and Q3U829 while beta-5, sigma-5 and spatacsin are human, so the reconstitution is mixed-species and no PDB entry maps to human Q9H0R1. That is why no gene-level GO annotation is proposed from it here.

title: MUDENG, a component of adaptor complex 5, mediates TRAIL- and TMZ-triggered apoptosis in glioblastoma (GBM) via multiple pathways.
review_notes: Abstract-only, 2026. The first paper to join the MUDENG and AP-5 literatures, confirming by TurboID proximity labelling that MuD associates with AP-5 subunits. Reports MuD as anti-apoptotic for TRAIL in glioblastoma, agreeing with PMID:27136675 and not with PMID:18395520.

title: AP5M1 bioinformatics - mu2 cargo-pocket mapping and sequence checks
review_notes: Analysis written for this review. The mu2 YxxPhi pocket is derived from PDB 1BXX contacts rather than recalled, the PDB author numbering is verified against Q96CW1 residue by residue, and the alignment is controlled against a correspondence published independently in PMID:40081374. The scripts fetch live and hardcode no results.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP5M1 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates clear and self_evaluation_pairwise win, and each of its five cited findings is correctly summarised, but all five are MUDENG cell-death papers and the record returned nothing at all on AP-5. Its closing scope statement, that no adaptor-complex trafficking function has been characterised for AP5M1, is false: PMID:22022230 is the source of nine GOA rows and of the UniProt function line. This is a recall failure of the kind produced when the decisive papers are titled for the complex or for a partner rather than for the gene. Its mechanism_profile grounding, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondrion and Programmed Cell Death, was not imported.

title: UniProtKB Q9H0R1 (AP5M1_HUMAN) flat-file record
review_notes: Machine-fetched record, entry version 167, sequence version 2, 490 aa. The accession was asserted to be Q9H0R1 before use. Source of the MHD boundaries, the PANTHER family assignment and the subcellular-location lines the GO_REF:0000044 IEAs are mapped from.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. One signature is used on this gene, IPR029392, and it was fetched from the InterPro API and checked: it is the AP-5 sigma-1 family (PANTHER PTHR16120 + Pfam PF15001), AP5S1 is the only human gene it contains (a UniProt query for the signature in taxon 9606 returns Q9NUS5 plus two unreviewed TrEMBL records of the same gene), and it maps to GO:0000724, GO:0016197 and GO:0030119 - exactly the three terms that appear on this gene through this reference. Two of the three are sound. The third, GO:0000724, is cited in the InterPro entry to PMID:20613862 and therefore propagates a single human RNAi phenotype family-wide; that row is marked over-annotated and the mapping is raised with InterPro in suggested_questions.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/GO_Central. All five IBA rows trace to node PTN000413531 of PTHR16120, and the local PAINT slice contains exactly five IBD rows, one per term, each seeded by UniProtKB:Q9NUS5 alone. Because AP5S1 is the only human gene in the family and its own experimental annotations are the seeds, these IBAs restate the target's own evidence as an ancestral property of the sigma-5 orthology group. No IRD or IKR appears in the slice.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location mapping. All three location identifiers used here were resolved at the UniProt locations endpoint and each maps to exactly the GO term used: SL-0157 Lysosome membrane to GO:0005765, SL-0091 Cytosol to GO:0005829 and SL-0151 Late endosome membrane to GO:0031902. All three correspond to lines on AP5S1's own record; the two membrane statements carry ECO:0000305 (curator inference from PMID:22022230) rather than ECO:0000269, which is recorded in the row reviews.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence curation. A projection count in QuickGO gives 3,640 distinct gene products annotated through this reference, so it is a systematic screen rather than a statement about AP5S1. Its single row here, cytosol, agrees with the fractionation data on AP-5 and is kept as non-core.

title: A structural explanation for the binding of endocytic dileucine motifs by the AP2 complex.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Not about AP-5: it is the AP-2 co-crystal study that defines the acidic dileucine site on sigma2 and names the pocket residues whose mutation abolishes binding. It is cited here because it supplies the comparator for the structural test of whether sigma-5 has that site - both the functional roles attached to the residue_claims and, through PDB 2JKR, the structure from which the site is defined empirically rather than from a typed-in residue list.

title: A genome-scale DNA repair RNAi screen identifies SPG48 as a novel gene associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Genuinely the discovery paper for this protein's membership in the complex: tagged KIAA0415 (AP5Z1) co-precipitates SPG11, SPG15, C20orf29 (AP5S1) and DKFZp761E198 (AP5B1), and reciprocal pulldowns with three baits confirm a five-protein core. It supplies both the four protein-binding IPI rows and the homologous-recombination IMP; the recombination result is correctly reported for C20orf29 with two independent esiRNAs, which is why that row is demoted rather than removed. QuickGO shows the reference annotating exactly five entities, the five members of the complex.

title: The fifth adaptor protein complex.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The paper that names C20orf29 sigma-5 and supplies almost all of the subunit-level evidence used here: the GFP-sigma-5 co-immunoprecipitation of mu5 and beta5, the LAMP1 colocalisation quantitation, and the knockdown phenocopy. Also the source of two negative statements that constrain the review - AP-5 does not associate with clathrin, and mu5 lacks the residues needed to bind YxxPhi signals. QuickGO shows it annotating 10 entities: the four human subunits, four mouse orthologues and two ComplexPortal complexes, i.e. a complex-scoped paper rather than a catalogue deposition.

title: Mutations in AP2S1 cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type 3.
review_notes: Full text available. Cited for one narrow purpose: it establishes that sigma2 Arg15, the residue that reads the acidic position of the dileucine motif, is a human disease locus, which is what makes its replacement by tyrosine in sigma-5 worth recording as a residue claim. Says nothing about AP-5 and is not used for any annotation on this gene.

title: Interaction between AP-5 and the hereditary spastic paraplegia proteins SPG11 and SPG15.
review_notes: Abstract only in the cache (full_text_available: false), and used only for statements the abstract itself makes: the ~1:1:1:1:1:1 stoichiometry of the six proteins, that all six knockdowns trap the CIMPR in early endosome clusters, and that AP-5, SPG11 and SPG15 colocalise on a late endosomal/lysosomal compartment. The first two are the reason sigma-5 can be treated as an equal member of the assembly rather than an inferred one.

title: Loss of AP-5 results in accumulation of aberrant endolysosomes: defining a new type of lysosomal storage disease.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Complex-level rather than subunit-level: the experiments are AP5Z1 patient fibroblasts and AP-5 zeta knockdown in HeLa, not sigma-5. Used for the consequence of losing AP-5 (enlarged multilamellar endolysosomes filled with storage material) and for its statement that sigma-5 is one of the core members of the stable assembly. Cited in support of a non-core process row, not of a core one.

title: Role of the AP-5 adaptor protein complex in late endosome-to-Golgi retrieval.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The study that identifies the pathway, and the basis for the NEW GO:0034499 row - but its perturbation is a CRISPR knockout of AP5Z1, not of AP5S1, so it is cited as an additional reference for that row rather than as the source of an experimental code on this gene. Also the source of the clearest statement that cargo binding in this system is attributed to SPG15 rather than to the heterotetramer, and of the field's own admission that how the complex binds cargo is unknown.

title: Rag GTPases and phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate mediate recruitment of the AP-5/SPG11/SPG15 complex.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Supplies the recruitment mechanism (coincidence detection on PI3P via the SPG15 FYVE domain plus Rag GTPases, enhanced by starvation, ARF1-independent) and, from the same authors who discovered AP-5, the decisive statement for this review's position on cargo binding: the sorting-signal-binding regions are different in AP-5 and cargo recognition, assuming it occurs, must work by another mechanism.

title: Bi-allelic variants in three genes encoding distinct subunits of the vesicular AP-5 complex cause hereditary macular dystrophy.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Human genetics of the complex: 23 bi-allelic variants in AP5Z1, AP5M1 and AP5B1 cause a macular dystrophy, and the authors state explicitly that it remains unclear whether AP5S1 variants cause disease. Used for the knowledge gap about this subunit rather than for any annotation row.

title: Structural basis for membrane remodeling by the AP5-SPG11-SPG15 complex.
review_notes: Abstract only in the cache (full_text_available: false); quotes used here are from the abstract. The structures it reports, 8YAB and 8YAH, are public, and the structural statements this review relies on were measured directly from 8YAB rather than taken from the paper - see the bioinformatics directory. It is also the source of the IntAct interaction with mouse Ap5z1, which is the reconstituted zeta/sigma-5 pair rather than a heterologous artefact. QuickGO shows it annotating 10 entities including the hexameric ComplexPortal complex CPX-20045.

title: AP5S1 (sigma-5): what the AP-5 structure says the subunit does
review_notes: Structural analysis written for this review. Measures sigma-5's interfaces in 8YAB and carries the empirically-defined sigma2 dileucine site (contacts with the CD4 peptide in 2JKR) onto sigma-5 by sequence-independent structural superposition, with positive (second sigma2 copy), negative (beta5 solenoid) and shuffled-sequence controls. All inputs are fetched live and sequence lengths and residue numbering are asserted per chain, which caught a one-residue offset in the deposited zeta numbering.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP5S1 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched affinage record. It is empty for this gene - n_discoveries: 0, citation_count: 0, and the narrative reads 'No mechanistic discoveries found in literature' - even though the trust gates passed, which is consistent with those gates measuring precision rather than recall. It contributed nothing to this review; all eight papers used were found by independent Europe PMC searches on the symbol, the complex and the partner proteins. Marked VERIFIED in the sense that the record is faithfully what the API returned, and NONE for relevance.

title: UniProtKB entry Q9NUS5 (AP5S1_HUMAN)
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProt record for the gene. Cited only for the PANTHER family assignment line, which establishes that AP5S1 is in PTHR16120 (not PTHR11753, the family of the AP-1 to AP-4 sigma subunits) and is therefore inside the clade of the IBD node.

title: A genome-scale DNA repair RNAi screen identifies SPG48 as a novel gene associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia.
review_notes: Targeted original repair, fractionation, reciprocal complex-isolation Results and corresponding Methods were read. Two knockdowns and mouse-orthologue rescue support the human-cell repair phenotype; helicase activity was predicted, not assayed. Electrophoretic bands are not mapped to current isoform accessions.

title: The fifth adaptor protein complex.
review_notes: Targeted subunit, endosomal-perturbation Results, Methods and Discussion were read. AP5Z1 knockdown is direct; tagged localization panels primarily examine other AP-5 subunits. The authors accept the earlier repair phenotype while suggesting an indirect explanation.

title: Interaction between AP-5 and the hereditary spastic paraplegia proteins SPG11 and SPG15.
review_notes: Canonical record is abstract-only. A separate intact normal-source full-text candidate supplied targeted human-cell QUBIC, endogenous-zeta localization, SPG11 pull-down Methods/Results and coat/cargo Discussion; read provenance is in notes. Stable assembly is measured, whereas cargo recognition was a proposal.

title: Loss of AP-5 results in accumulation of aberrant endolysosomes: defining a new type of lysosomal storage disease.
review_notes: Targeted human patient/control fibroblast localization, antibody-specificity and ultrastructure Results, HeLa AP5Z1 knockdown and corresponding Methods/Discussion were read. Specific AP5Z1 puncta are distinguished from persistent cross-reactive Golgi staining.

title: Role of the AP-5 adaptor protein complex in late endosome-to-Golgi retrieval.
review_notes: Targeted human knockout/retrieval, cargo pull-down and native co-IP Results, Figure8/S2 legends, relevant Methods and Discussion were read. SPG15 N-terminal cargo binding excludes zeta from that fragment; native complexes independently contain zeta and CIMPR. Cargo retrieval does not establish an isolated zeta interface.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PMID and human binary-interaction resource identity checked from the actual source. The AP5Z1–NUP93 pair-level experiment and construct/control details were not adjudicated; the annotation remains uncertain.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Actual record identifies the BioPlex human-interactome resource. The specific screen pair was not adjudicated. AP5Z1–SPG11 association is supported independently by the 2010 and 2013 targeted studies, not by assigning their experiments to this screen.

title: Spatacsin regulates directionality of lysosome trafficking by promoting the degradation of its partner AP5Z1.
review_notes: Targeted motor-association, lysosomal recruitment/tubulation Results and construct/cell Methods were read. Mouse fibroblast and neuronal contexts are explicit; AP5Z1 p150Glued coassociation may be indirect through another AP-5 subunit. No motor-binding activity is assigned to isolated human AP5Z1.

title: Structural basis for membrane remodeling by the AP5-SPG11-SPG15 complex.
review_notes: Canonical abstract and published Figures 3–5 captions were read; full Methods/body were inaccessible. RCSB8YAH identifies mouse zeta in the resolved AP-5 assembly. The mixed-species structural and assembled-complex membrane evidence is distinct from earlier human-cell cargo observations.

title: A soluble version of the receptor-like protein tyrosine phosphatase kappa stimulates neurite outgrowth via a Grb2/MEK1-dependent signaling cascade.
review_notes: PubMed resolves this PMID to Drosopoulos et al. 1999 on soluble receptor-like PTP-kappa and neurite outgrowth; it does not support APAF1 nucleotide binding.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary exosome proteomics source; not relevant to APAF1 apoptosome biology beyond a high-throughput location hit.

title: RIAM, an Ena/VASP and Profilin ligand, interacts with Rap1-GTP and mediates Rap1-induced adhesion.
review_notes: Abstract-only; founding paper.

title: RIAM links the ADAP/SKAP-55 signaling module to Rap1, facilitating T-cell-receptor-mediated integrin activation.
review_notes: Full text; T cells.

title: RIAM activates integrins by linking talin to ras GTPase membrane-targeting sequences.
review_notes: Full text; human RIAM constructs.

title: Different levels of the Tripartite motif protein, Anomalies in sensory axon patterning (Asap), regulate distinct axonal projections of Drosophila sensory neurons.
review_notes: Abstract-only; Drosophila Asap/Pico study. Whether human proteins were tested cannot be checked, so correctness is left unset.

title: Focal adhesion disassembly is regulated by a RIAM to MEK-1 pathway.
review_notes: Abstract-only; melanoma and breast carcinoma cells.

title: The structure of Rap1 in complex with RIAM reveals specificity determinants and recruitment mechanism.
review_notes: Full text.

title: The palmitoyl acyltransferase HIP14 shares a high proportion of interactors with huntingtin: implications for a role in the pathogenesis of Huntington's disease.
review_notes: HIP14 yeast two-hybrid interactome; APBB1IP not followed up.

title: Conformational activation of talin by RIAM triggers integrin-mediated cell adhesion.
review_notes: Full text.

title: Rap1 and its effector RIAM are required for lymphocyte trafficking.
review_notes: Full text; mouse knockout.

title: Loss of the Rap1 effector RIAM results in leukocyte adhesion deficiency due to impaired β2 integrin function in mice.
review_notes: Full text; mouse knockout.

title: A RIAM/lamellipodin-talin-integrin complex forms the tip of sticky fingers that guide cell migration.
review_notes: Full text.

title: Phosphorylation of RIAM by src promotes integrin activation by unmasking the PH domain of RIAM.
review_notes: Full text.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APBB1IP (human)
review_notes: Trust gates clear; accurate, well-dated synthesis; key findings checked against the cached papers.

title: UniProt entry Q7Z5R6 (AB1IP_HUMAN)
review_notes: Rap1 effector, integrin activation, membrane and lamellipodium location.

title: PTHR11243 PAINT annotations
review_notes: MRL node PTN000133590 (cytosol, plasma membrane); deep Grb7/10/14 + MRL node PTN001343226 (adaptor, intracellular signal transduction).

title: The APC-hDLG complex negatively regulates cell cycle progression from the G0/G1 to S phase.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Overexpression and domain-mutant phenotypes support the existing cell-cycle context, without an autonomous APC cyclin-kinase inhibitor claim.

title: Regulation and function of the interaction between the APC tumour suppressor protein and EB1.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. C-terminal bacterial fusion, HCT116 and SW480 experiments are distinguished; precise fusion-species provenance is not inferred from host cells.

title: Structural basis of the Axin-adenomatous polyposis coli interaction.
review_notes: The complete normal abstract and targeted original indexed Results, Fig2/3/5/6 legends and GST pull-down Methods were inspected. The original AXIN RGS-domain/APC SAMP3 experiment and official PDB1EMU AXIN organism field and APC peptide mapping to human P25054 support domain-specific binding. The canonical cache remains abstract-only; the RGS-like fold does not assign APC G-protein-regulatory activity.

title: Asef, a link between the tumor suppressor APC and G-protein signaling.
review_notes: Complete abstract and targeted indexed original binding Results read. Mouse colon/neuronal colocalization and canine MDCK morphological assays are explicit; source construct identity and modern partner-isoform correspondence are not fully reconstructed.

title: Adenomatous polyposis coli protein contains two nuclear export signals and shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Reporter/NES mutation and leptomycin observations directly support the localization context; no independent transcription-factor activity is inferred.

title: Binding of the adenomatous polyposis coli protein to microtubules increases microtubule stability and is regulated by GSK3 beta phosphorylation.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Direct binding and stabilization are explicitly reported, but detailed original reagent provenance was not reconstructed.

title: A role for the Adenomatous Polyposis Coli protein in chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Min truncation, kinetochore localization and Bub-complex association are explicit. The separate centrosomal annotation remains unadjudicated; Bub association does not make APC a kinase.

title: Siah-1 mediates a novel beta-catenin degradation pathway linking p53 to the adenomatous polyposis coli protein.
review_notes: Complete abstract read, including mammalian-cell degradation and Xenopus phenotype context. This is not APC ubiquitin-ligase catalysis.

title: Synergistic activation of the Wnt signaling pathway by Dvl and casein kinase Iepsilon.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. DVL/CKIepsilon/AXIN ternary-complex work does not expose the particular APC target assay; the original interaction remains unresolved, not disproved.

title: Pin1 regulates turnover and subcellular localization of beta-catenin by inhibiting its interaction with APC.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. Pin1 modulation of beta-catenin turnover and APC association supports the existing beta-catenin-binding context; no APC isomerase chemistry is inferred.

title: Involvement of the telomeric protein Pin2/TRF1 in the regulation of the mitotic spindle.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. Pin2/TRF1 spindle findings do not adjudicate the original APC–EB1 pair. This is incomplete target evidence, not a wrong-paper conclusion.

title: Association and regulation of casein kinase 2 activity by adenomatous polyposis coli protein.
review_notes: Complete abstract plus indexed original recombinant-protein Methods, binding Fig2 and dose-inhibition Fig5 read. Human fetal-fibroblast cDNA establishes the APC fragment source. Pig-brain full-length APC is separate. CK2alpha-prime binding is weaker than alpha; holoenzyme association does not establish direct beta binding.

title: Subcellular distribution of Wnt pathway proteins in normal and neoplastic colon.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Whole-mount human colon crypt/polyp/carcinoma confocal imaging is explicit; no inference from cell-line species is needed for this tissue observation.

title: Wnt-5a inhibits the canonical Wnt pathway by promoting GSK-3-independent beta-catenin degradation.
review_notes: Complete abstract and previously scoped body context read. Existing APC process assertions are retained; no new claim that APC supplies ubiquitin chemistry or proteolysis.

title: Nuclear accumulation of full-length and truncated adenomatous polyposis coli protein in tumor cells depends on proliferation.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Both full-length and truncated APC are considered; the result is not restricted to a single nuclear-localization sequence.

title: N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine-induced senescence-like growth arrest in colon cancer cells is associated with loss of adenomatous polyposis coli protein, microtubule organization, and telomeric DNA.
review_notes: Identity, complete abstract and source-owner scoped full-text passages reviewed. MNNG-induced senescence and loss of APC expression are described; a functional APC contribution to the DNA-damage response remains unresolved.

title: Comprehensive proteomic analysis of interphase and mitotic 14-3-3-binding proteins.
review_notes: Identity and complete 14-3-3 proteomics abstract read. The individual APC–YWHAZ experimental record and controls were not inspected.

title: Mechanism of phosphorylation-dependent binding of APC to beta-catenin and its role in beta-catenin degradation.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Structural and biochemical evidence supports this paper’s own beta-catenin-binding assertions; mixed-species beta-catenin partners remain as originally annotated.

title: Crystal structure of a beta-catenin/APC complex reveals a critical role for APC phosphorylation in APC function.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. The specific structure and affinity observations support beta-catenin binding, not an APC kinase activity.

title: The adenomatous polyposis coli protein (APC) exists in two distinct soluble complexes with different functions.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Dynamic pool distribution and GSK3 inhibition are reported; the composition of every partially assembled intermediate is not inferred.

title: Biosensor-based micro-affinity purification for the proteomic analysis of protein complexes.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. An APC beta-catenin-binding region is an affinity-purification reagent, but the original target-specific pair result remains unadjudicated.

title: Thermodynamics of beta-catenin-ligand interactions: the roles of the N- and C-terminal tails in modulating binding affinity.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. The source independently supports beta-catenin binding; the annotated nonhuman partner is preserved, not relabeled as a human construct.

title: Differential use of functional domains by coiled-coil coactivator in its synergistic coactivator function with beta-catenin or GRIP1.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. CoCoA beta-catenin/GRIP1 transcriptional assays supply Wnt context, while the exact APC intervention is not independently reconstructed. Existing well-established APC negative-Wnt function is retained with separately identified direct evidence, without relabeling this source as a new APC experiment.

title: Human scribble, a novel tumor suppressor identified as a target of high-risk HPV E6 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, interacts with adenomatous polyposis coli.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Human SCRIB and domain interfaces are explicit. Hippocampal neuron species is not inferred, and the source’s direct PDZ result is not transferred to unread screen records.

title: The third 20 amino acid repeat is the tightest binding site of APC for beta-catenin.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. ITC and CD/NMR observations directly support this paper’s binding annotation; no generalized affinity is assigned to all repeats.

title: Asef2 functions as a Cdc42 exchange factor and is stimulated by the release of an autoinhibitory module from a concealed C-terminal activation element.
review_notes: Complete abstract, original Fig4–5 captions/Results and indexed APC-ARM cloning Methods read. APC ARM205–885 came from pancreatic tumor-cell cDNA; endogenous human SW480/Panc04-03 association and purified fusion assays are separate evidence. Modern isoform mapping remains unverified; the source-specific CDC42 and Asef1-isoform binding rows remain uncertain.

title: Lack of adenomatous polyposis coli protein correlates with a decrease in cell migration and overall changes in microtubule stability.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Existing microtubule/migration/protrusion assertions are retained alongside direct binding evidence; this is not a new necessity-only process proposal.

title: Modeling of a human circadian mutation yields insights into clock regulation by PER2.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. The PER2/CKI clock emphasis does not disprove an APC experiment elsewhere; the specific APC partner result remains uninspected.

title: Loss of APC induces polyploidy as a result of a combination of defects in mitosis and apoptosis.
review_notes: Complete abstract and source-owner targeted human-cell body scope reviewed. Checkpoint and apoptosis phenotypes are distinguished; apoptosis is a secondary effect rather than a new APC enzymatic function.

title: Energetics of peptide recognition by the second PDZ domain of human protein tyrosine phosphatase 1E.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Its own APC result supports PDZ-domain binding despite weak affinity. Full assay/construct details remain uninspected; no physiological phosphatase regulation is assigned to APC.

title: Regulated binding of adenomatous polyposis coli protein to actin.
review_notes: Entire recovered abstract read; the normal cache is abstract-only. Human APC domain identity is explicit. Detailed Methods were not recovered; microinjection, microtubule competition and EB1 modulation are reported in the abstract rather than reconstructed as complete assays.

title: Bcr-Abl stabilizes beta-catenin in chronic myeloid leukemia through its tyrosine phosphorylation.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. BCR-ABL regulation of beta-catenin/AXIN/GSK3 does not expose the annotated APC target assay. Other APC structures cannot refine this source-specific pair.

title: Wilms tumor suppressor WTX negatively regulates WNT/beta-catenin signaling.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Tandem affinity/MS complex membership is explicit; the source’s APC–beta-catenin pair-specific assay remains unadjudicated and is not upgraded using other papers.

title: APC inactivation associates with abnormal mitosis completion and concomitant BUB1B/MAD2L1 up-regulation.
review_notes: Complete structured abstract read. Video microscopy and modulation evidence support the existing mitotic process, without assigning APC motor or contractile catalysis.

title: Htid-1, the human homolog of the Drosophila melanogaster l(2)tid tumor suppressor, defines a novel physiological role of APC.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Endogenous association in colon/cancer cells and mouse NIH3T3, plus GST assays, are explicit. Molecular chaperone activity belongs to the chaperone, not APC.

title: Identification and characterization of Asef2, a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor specific for Rac1 and Cdc42.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Truncated tumor APC in HeLa/MDCK experiments is explicitly distinguished from a wild-type purified APC activator assay. The Rac1/Cdc42 interpretation differs from PMID17145773; no specific APC GTPase-exchange chemistry is inferred.

title: AMER1 regulates the distribution of the tumor suppressor APC between microtubules and the plasma membrane.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Lipid binding is assigned to AMER1, not automatically to its APC partner.

title: Putative tumor suppressor EDD interacts with and up-regulates APC.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. EDD stabilization and perinuclear/cytoplasmic context are distinct from the later SCF-beta-TrCP interaction and do not confer E3 activity on APC.

title: Trabid, a new positive regulator of Wnt-induced transcription with preference for binding and cleaving K63-linked ubiquitin chains.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. This direct target statement supports non-core binding. No detailed reagent reconstruction or APC deubiquitinase activity is claimed.

title: The armadillo repeat domain of the APC tumor suppressor protein interacts with Striatin family members.
review_notes: Complete abstract plus original publisher Results2.1 read: FLAG-human APCarm in HEK293T, empty-tag comparison and MS identify Striatin, SG2NA and zinedin. Junctional and PC12 neurite contexts remain distinct.

title: Activated protein C ligation of ApoER2 (LRP8) causes Dab1-dependent signaling in U937 cells.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract plus actual author-uploaded Methods/SPR/Fig3 read. The reagent is enzymatically activated protein C, including APC-V5/Gla-domain constructs, in ApoER2 signaling experiments; it is not the APC tumor suppressor P25054. Actual assay identity, not title emphasis, establishes the misattribution.

title: The Axin1 scaffold protein promotes formation of a degradation complex for c-Myc.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. The AXIN1/MYC degradation-complex description does not expose the annotated APC–AXIN1 experiment; preserve uncertainty.

title: Asef2 and Neurabin2 cooperatively regulate actin cytoskeletal organization and are involved in HGF-induced cell migration.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Human HeLa HGF experiments explicitly report localization and perturbation; neuronal protein naming does not make the host neuronal.

title: An EB1-binding motif acts as a microtubule tip localization signal.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Reconstitution/structural context supports tip targeting through EB1, which is distinct from direct APC basic-region microtubule binding.

title: Binding of APC and dishevelled mediates Wnt5a-regulated focal adhesion dynamics in migrating cells.
review_notes: Complete abstract and indexed original Interaction of Dvl with APC Results/Fig2 read. Direct recombinant Dvl1 assays and endogenous Dvl2 association in HeLaS3 are distinct from MDCK/COS7 experiments. The separately annotated P54792 partner remains unadjudicated.

title: Adenomatous polyposis coli protein nucleates actin assembly and synergizes with the formin mDia1.
review_notes: Actual recovered targeted assembly/latrunculin/deletion Results and purification Methods read. Plasmids trace to the2007 human-domain study; NIH3T3 host, bacterial expression and rabbit actin are distinct. Nucleation is separated from severing, capping and accelerated elongation.

title: A human MAP kinase interactome.
review_notes: Identity and complete MAPK-interactome abstract read. Individual APC–plakoglobin, alpha-catenin and ERBIN pairs remain uninspected.

title: ErbB2 receptor controls microtubule capture by recruiting ACF7 to the plasma membrane of migrating cells.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. The work performed by ACF7 and the upstream enzymes is distinguished from APC structural/regulatory participation.

title: Rho GTPase Cdc42 is a direct interacting partner of Adenomatous Polyposis Coli protein and can alter its cellular localization.
review_notes: Actual cached Methods and targeted interaction Results read. Human brain/testis-library APC222–653, Y2H/translation and nucleotide-state controls support this source’s small-GTPase-binding refinement. Bacterial GST and in-vitro translation are distinct from purified full-length APC.

title: Deconstructing the ßcatenin destruction complex: mechanistic roles for the tumor suppressor APC in regulating Wnt signaling.
review_notes: Complete abstract and source-owner mechanistic context reviewed. Drosophila and human colon-cell systems are explicit; the proposed disassembly model is not collapsed with the different PMID22682247 intact-complex account.

title: Molecular basis for the recognition of adenomatous polyposis coli by the Discs Large 1 protein.
review_notes: Actual cached Methods and Results/Fig1–3 read. PDZ2 binding is strongest, PDZ1 weaker and PDZ3 negligible under the tested conditions. This does not establish each independently annotated screen pair.

title: Crystal structures of the armadillo repeat domain of adenomatous polyposis coli and its complex with the tyrosine-rich domain of Sam68.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Structure and mutation/phosphorylation tests establish the interaction; APC does not thereby acquire RNA-processing catalysis. Full reagent provenance was not reconstructed.

title: Nuclear PKM2 regulates β-catenin transactivation upon EGFR activation.
review_notes: Identity and complete abstract read. Nuclear PKM2/beta-catenin signaling does not adjudicate the source-local APC target pair; no wrong-gene claim is made.

title: Amer2 protein is a novel negative regulator of Wnt/β-catenin signaling involved in neuroectodermal patterning.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Lipid binding is AMER2’s property; Xenopus developmental experiments are not relabeled human.

title: Rocket launcher mechanism of collaborative actin assembly defined by single-molecule imaging.
review_notes: Complete recovered main body read; supplementary Methods are absent. TIRF recruitment, latrunculin controls and APC/formin separation identify APC’s physical contribution to nucleation.

title: Wnt signaling through inhibition of β-catenin degradation in an intact Axin1 complex.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. This model differs from a disassembly account; it supports general destruction-complex context without resolving every target pair or every sequential handoff.

title: Structure of the human discs large 1 PDZ2- adenomatous polyposis coli cytoskeletal polarity complex: insight into peptide engagement and PDZ clustering.
review_notes: Actual cached Methods/Fig1 and primary PDB4G69 human APC chain metadata read. This establishes a source-specific PDZ binding refinement, not independent APC scaffold catalysis.

title: The regulation and deregulation of Wnt signaling by PARK genes in health and disease.
review_notes: Identity, complete abstract and source-owner targeted Wnt-signalosome review passages assessed. The review discusses PARK proteins/DVL/LRP6 but the original APC-specific signalosome location remains unresolved.

title: Large extent of disorder in Adenomatous Polyposis Coli offers a strategy to guard Wnt signalling against point mutations.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Structural disorder and phosphorylation provide kinase-association context; accepting the curator’s kinase-binding assertion does not assign APC kinase activity.

title: Adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) membrane recruitment 3, a member of the APC membrane recruitment family of APC-binding proteins, is a positive regulator of Wnt-β-catenin signalling.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Explicit AMER3–APC and AMER3–AMER1 results do not reconstruct this paper’s separately annotated APC–AMER1 experiment.

title: Using an in situ proximity ligation assay to systematically profile endogenous protein-protein interactions in a pathway network.
review_notes: Identity and complete pathway-network/proximity-ligation abstract read. Individual APC pair records and antibody specificity were not adjudicated; proximity is distinct from a purified binary interface.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: Identity and complete quantitative-interactome abstract read. Individual APC pull-down/stoichiometry records remain uninspected.

title: Extensive metabolic disorders are present in APC(min) tumorigenesis mice.
review_notes: Complete normal and official PubMed abstract read; full Methods and control experiments remain unavailable after bounded primary-source lookup. The mouse phenotype does not by itself settle direct regulation versus systemic effects. The GO term is regulatory and does not require APC to generate heat chemically.

title: Insulin signaling regulates a functional interaction between adenomatous polyposis coli and cytoplasmic dynein.
review_notes: Actual complete-cache construct Methods, interaction Results and Fig6 captions read. Human APC fragments, rat intermediate chain, bovine dynein, COS7 hosts and mouse-brain co-IP are distinguished. Bacterial APC-containing lysate is not independently purified full-length human APC.

title: Adenomatous polyposis coli nucleates actin assembly to drive cell migration and microtubule-induced focal adhesion turnover.
review_notes: Complete abstract and targeted Results/Fig1–2 plus plasmid-construction and protein-purification Methods read. Methods explicitly identify RNAi-refractory full-length human APC/Addgene16507; U2OS human hosts, E.coli-expressed APC fragments and rabbit skeletal-muscle actin are distinct. Results call m4 L2539A/I2541A whereas Methods call it L2539A/P2541A twice; this within-paper discrepancy is preserved by using only the mutant name m4, with no residue-specific assertion. Repeated XML sections and supplementary experiments were not comprehensively read.

title: Proteome-wide analysis of phospho-regulated PDZ domain interactions.
review_notes: Identity and complete PDZ phosphoregulation-screen abstract read. APC–DLG1 and APC–SCRIB peptide/affinity records were not independently inspected. Their direct experiments in other papers do not supply this screen with a more specific source-local assertion.

title: TMEM9 promotes intestinal tumorigenesis through vacuolar-ATPase-activated Wnt/β-catenin signalling.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. The source manipulates APC abundance through TMEM9/v-ATPase; it does not confer proton-pump activity on APC.

title: HENA, heterogeneous network-based data set for Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: Identity and complete Alzheimer heterogeneous-network abstract read. The underlying APC interaction evidence has not been traced to its original experiment.

title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
review_notes: Identity and complete kinase-network abstract read. Specific APC pairs and constructs remain unadjudicated.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Identity and complete BioPlex abstract read. The individual APC target pairs/construct records are not exposed by a general description of the large cell-line interactomes.

title: Reconstitution of the destruction complex defines roles of AXIN polymers and APC in β-catenin capture, phosphorylation, and ubiquitylation.
review_notes: Actual targeted Results, cloning/purification Methods and SCF gel-filtration experiment read. APC shifts SCF only when beta-TrCP is present, without resolving every binary contact. APC increases processing efficiency but is neither kinase nor ubiquitin-transfer catalyst.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Identity and complete OpenCell abstract read. Target-specific APC interaction records remain uninspected; general access to the article is not access to each pair.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Identity and complete fragmentomics abstract read. Quantitative APC-peptide/PDZ-partner records remain uninspected. Independent APC PDZ structures do not establish the assay in this source.

title: Protein interaction studies in human induced neurons indicate convergent biology underlying autism spectrum disorders.
review_notes: Identity and complete induced-neuron network abstract read. Its individual APC–beta-catenin experiment remains unadjudicated.

title: Proteome-scale characterisation of motif-based interactome rewiring by disease mutations.
review_notes: Identity and complete motif-rewiring abstract read. Exact APC construct and partner experiments remain uninspected.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Identity and complete multimodal cell-map abstract read. The APC target interaction record remains uninspected.

title: E-cadherin and APC compete for the interaction with beta-catenin and the cytoskeleton.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Binding/complex association does not make APC a cadherin-binding adhesion receptor.

title: The APC protein and E-cadherin form similar but independent complexes with alpha-catenin, beta-catenin, and plakoglobin.
review_notes: Complete abstract explicitly reports purified-protein and two-hybrid tests. Alpha-catenin can be indirect, plakoglobin direct, and cadherin negative under the tested conditions; preserve the original NOT.

title: Association of the APC gene product with beta-catenin.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. The proposed adhesion connection is contextual and retained as non-core rather than a new direct adhesion mechanism.

title: The tumour suppressor gene product APC blocks cell cycle progression from G0/G1 to S phase.
review_notes: Complete abstract read. Cyclin/CDK rescue and kinase activity support a cellular regulation context, not purified direct APC inhibition of a CDK.

title: Binding of GSK3beta to the APC-beta-catenin complex and regulation of complex assembly.

title: Downregulation of beta-catenin by human Axin and its association with the APC tumor suppressor, beta-catenin and GSK3 beta.

title: Agonist-induced internalization and desensitization of the apelin receptor.

The receptor studied is mouse APJ expressed in HEK293 cells and the agonist is the human peptide.
