title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APOBEC4 (human)
review_notes: Its symbol-collision trust gate tripped on the word 'yeast'. That refers to expression of human APOBEC4 in yeast (PMID:21568845), not a different protein; written with --force after checking. Accurate summary.

title: UniProt entry Q8WW27 (ABEC4_HUMAN)
review_notes: Putative deaminase, substrate unknown; catalytic residues by PROSITE rule only.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT/IBA methods reference for the four phylogenetic rows. Traced to the actual IBD assertions in interpro/panther/PTHR32288/PTHR32288-paint.tsv rather than taken on trust; node, seeds, taxon and dates are recorded in each row's propagation_review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The UniProt subcellular-location-to-GO mapping reference. The source term SL-0243 was resolved to 'Secreted' against the UniProt locations service, and the underlying keyword is independently supported by isolation of the protein from plasma.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: The Ensembl Compara ortholog-transfer reference. Correctly applied - the donor really is the mouse orthologue - but in this instance it re-derives a term the target already holds by direct experiment from the same publication, which is why the row's propagation_review records EVIDENCE_CIRCULAR_OR_REDUNDANT.

title: DNA sequence variation in human apolipoprotein C4 gene and its effect on plasma lipid profile.
review_notes: The APOC4 coding-variant study cited in UniProt for VAR_012081, VAR_012082 and VAR_012068. Abstract-only in cache; verified that the triglyceride association is reported for Leu36Pro and Leu96Arg in women specifically. Graded MEDIUM because the effect is small - a later review puts APOC4 variation at about 2% of plasma triglyceride variance - and because the paper itself frames the functional role as unknown. The verbatim quote used here retains the original's typographical error ('reveled'). Cited by the affinage report.

title: Human apoC-IV: isolation, characterization, and immunochemical quantification in plasma and plasma lipoproteins.
review_notes: The decisive experimental paper for this gene and the anchor of the review. Cached abstract only (full_text_available: false), but the abstract itself carries the quantitative claims used here: purification of human apoC-IV from apoVLDL, identification by microsequencing four tryptic peptides, the >80% VLDL / remainder HDL distribution, and the 0.1-1.9 mg/dl concentration range tracking plasma triglyceride. It also supplies the mouse-plasma observation that grounds the MGI:87878 IBA donor. Absent from the affinage report.

title: Proteomic analysis of human very low-density lipoprotein by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis and MALDI-TOF/TOF.
review_notes: Independent 2-DE/MALDI-TOF-TOF confirmation that apoC-IV is present on human VLDL, in three isoforms. Abstract-only in cache; the abstract states the identification explicitly. Its main subject is the VLDL proteome generally rather than apoC-IV, so it corroborates rather than establishes. Absent from the affinage report.

title: Expression of apolipoprotein C-IV is regulated by Ku antigen/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma complex and correlates with liver steatosis.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Correctly cited for the GO:0019915 IMP: the ApoC-IV transfection experiment and its 2.7-fold triglyceride increase are real and statistically supported. The relevance grade is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the paper is principally about what regulates APOC4 transcription (HCV core protein, Ku antigen, PPARgamma/RXRalpha) rather than about APOC4's own function; APOC4 is the readout in most of it. Absent from the affinage report.

title: Gain and loss events in the evolution of the apolipoprotein family in vertebrata.
review_notes: Full text available. Vertebrate-wide phylogeny of the apolipoprotein family, cited for the single claim that apoC-IV arose in Eutheria - which independently corroborates the taxon:9347 placement of the PAINT node PTN000792756 and the family taxonomic span computed here. The paper is a comparative-genomics survey, not an experimental study of apoC-IV, and is used for nothing else. Absent from the affinage report.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI, the CCSB yeast two-hybrid reference interactome. Correctly cited - the 23 APOC4 GO:0005515 rows really do come from it - but it is a maximal-projection reference: a full QuickGO export returns 85,343 annotations over 6,769 gene products, 84,937 of them GO:0005515. Full text read to confirm the assay (Y2H, Gal4 fusions) and the single-screen caveat. Not miscited; simply uninformative about this gene, which is why relevance is LOW rather than the correctness flag being set.

title: High-Density Lipoprotein Carries Markers That Track With Recovery From Stroke.
review_notes: Full text available. A second, independent human HDL proteomic dataset in which APOC4 is among the HDL cargo proteins measured. Used only as corroboration that apoC-IV is detectable on HDL; the paper's stroke-recovery correlations are not used and support no annotation here. Absent from the affinage report.

title: Differences in HDL-Bound Apolipoproteins in Patients With Advanced Liver Fibrosis Due to Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Independent human HDL proteomics detecting ApoC-IV as an HDL-bound apolipoprotein, used here to corroborate the GO:0034364 rows, which otherwise rest on one clause of one 2003 abstract. Its own subject is NAFLD fibrosis rather than apoC-IV; it states it found no prior reports on apoC-IV in liver disease. Absent from the affinage report.

title: Quartet of APOCs and the Different Roles They Play in Diabetes.
review_notes: Full text available and read; a 2023 review of the four apoCs. Secondary source, cited here for statements it makes explicitly and that no primary paper on apoC-IV makes: the supraphysiological-dose caveat on the transgenic result, the apoE-displacement mechanism and its explicit contrast with a lipase effect, the order-of-magnitude abundance gap, and the field's own assessment that almost nothing is known about APOC4. Because it is a review, the mechanistic claims it reports are treated as hypotheses and are deliberately not annotated. Absent from the affinage report.

title: Identification and characterization of a new human gene (APOC4) in the apolipoprotein E, C-I, and C-II gene locus.
review_notes: The gene-identification paper, correctly cited by both TAS rows. Its contribution is sequence-level prediction - 127 residues, a putative 25-residue signal peptide (UniProt now places the cleavage after residue 27 by similarity to the rabbit protein), two potential amphipathic helices - plus the locus structure and the observation that apoC-IV mRNA is low in human liver. TAS is the right evidence code for it. This is the paper the affinage report leads with.

title: Identification, characterization, cloning, and expression of apolipoprotein C-IV, a novel sialoglycoprotein of rabbit plasma lipoproteins.
review_notes: The rabbit apoC-IV characterisation, and the only direct lipid-binding measurement anywhere in this family. Abstract-only in cache; the abstract states the discoidal-micelle result, the VLDL/HDL association, liver-restricted expression, secretion from transfected cells and the mammalian conservation claim. Basis of the proposed ISS row. Absent from the affinage report, and - more consequentially - absent from the GO record for P55057 entirely.

title: Expression of a novel human apolipoprotein (apoC-IV) causes hypertriglyceridemia in transgenic mice.
review_notes: The transgenic-mouse study behind two IMP rows. Abstract-only in cache. Verified that its own abstract states the lipid-binding conclusion and the hypertriglyceridaemia phenotype, and also the earlier negative - apoC-IV not detectable in normal adult human plasma by immunoblot - which PMID:12700345 later superseded. Graded here as gain-of-function evidence at supraphysiological dose rather than as evidence about endogenous protein. Absent from the affinage report.

title: APOBR dimer binds VLDLs
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction 'APOBR dimer binds VLDLs'. APOC4 participates as a VLDL constituent; supports only the extracellular-region assignment. Verified that the cached summary is about VLDL and macrophage APOBR as the display name states.

title: VLDLR binds VLDL
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction 'VLDLR binds VLDL'. Its summary names APOC4 explicitly as a minor VLDL constituent and cites Kotite et al. 2003, the same primary evidence as the IDA row, so this is not a generic pathway projection.

title: VLDL binds APOC1 and APOC4
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction 'VLDL binds APOC1 and APOC4' - the one Reactome event in which APOC4 is the acting participant rather than a bystander component, again citing Kotite et al. 2003.

title: Expression of APOC4 regulated by NR1H2 or NR1H3
review_notes: Cached Reactome event 'Expression of APOC4 regulated by NR1H2 or NR1H3'. A gene-expression event; it records that liver X receptors induce the APOE/APOC1/APOC2/APOC4 cluster in macrophages, which is about APOC4 regulation rather than APOC4 function, and supports only the extracellular-region assignment for the product.

title: APOC4 (P55056) - bioinformatics support for the annotation review
review_notes: Bioinformatics performed for this review. Two live analyses: the taxonomic span of PTHR32288, which corroborates the Eutheria placement of the PAINT node, and a hydrophobic-moment scan of mature chains, which places human apoC-IV inside the exchangeable-apolipoprotein band. Both fetch inputs at run time and assert on them; neither is an experiment, and RESULTS.md says so explicitly where it matters.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APOC4 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates cleared (.affinage.log records 'APOC4: trust gates clear'), faith_pct 100.0, self_evaluation_pairwise empty, and the narrative describes the correct protein with no symbol collision - so no LOW_QUALITY flag is warranted on correctness. Its problem is recall, not accuracy: its four citations are PMID:8530039, PMID:10996355, PMID:29580721 and PMID:33705959, so it missed every paper that measured the protein: none of its citations is among the four references (PMID:12700345, PMID:8827523, PMID:18809223, PMID:17154273) behind all six of APOC4's experimental GOA rows outside the 23-row HuRI two-hybrid set. Its mechanism_profile is empty, so no GO grounding was available to import even had that been appropriate. Cited cited once, in the GO:0006629 row, where its independent arrival at the same conclusion about how little is established corroborates a KEEP_AS_NON_CORE that already stands on the primary literature. No mechanistic or grounding claim in this review rests on it, and none of its GO ids was imported.

title: UniProtKB P55056 (APOC4_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProtKB flat file for P55056. Confirmed to be the expected entry (APOC4_HUMAN, reviewed, 127 aa) and not a merged redirect. Used for the signal peptide boundary, the N-glycosylation site, the secreted location, the liver-and-plasma tissue specificity, and the PANTHER family assignment. Its FUNCTION line is a single hedged sentence, which is itself informative about the state of knowledge.

title: Apolipoprotein specificity for lipid efflux by the human ABCAI transporter.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports APOE as an exchangeable apolipoprotein acceptor for ABCA1-mediated cholesterol and phospholipid efflux.

title: Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) isoform-dependent lipid release from astrocytes prepared from human ApoE3 and ApoE4 knock-in mice.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports APOE-containing HDL-like particle release from astrocytes and APOE isoform effects on cholesterol release.

title: The binding of apolipoprotein E to oligomers and fibrils of amyloid-β alters the kinetics of amyloid aggregation.
review_notes: Cached full-text record supports APOE binding to amyloid-beta oligomers/fibrils and modulation of aggregation kinetics; this supports non-core Alzheimer-context annotations.

title: TREM2 Binds to Apolipoproteins, Including APOE and CLU/APOJ, and Thereby Facilitates Uptake of Amyloid-Beta by Microglia.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports APOE-containing lipoproteins as TREM2 ligands and links APOE to microglial uptake of amyloid-lipoprotein complexes.

title: Low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein mediates uptake of cholesteryl esters derived from apoprotein E-enriched lipoproteins.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports receptor-mediated uptake and lysosomal processing of apoE-enriched lipoprotein particles through LRP.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT/IBA method reference for both of this gene's phylogenetic annotations. Verified against the committed PAINT slice interpro/panther/PTHR15011/PTHR15011-paint.tsv, which shows the single node PTN002687490 at taxon:117571 and the two IBD assertions the IBAs descend from.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The UniProt subcellular-location mapping reference. Verified against the UniProt locations REST record for SL-0243, which declares "Secreted" and its GO mapping to GO:0005576. The mapping is correct and the underlying UniProt annotation is experimentally supported, so this electronic row adds no unsupported claim.

title: Lipid transfer inhibitor protein defines the participation of lipoproteins in lipid transfer reactions: CETP has no preference for cholesteryl esters in HDL versus LDL.
review_notes: Decisive for the mechanism and for the molecular function analysis: it shows that the preference of CETP for HDL seen in plasma is created by this protein rather than being a property of CETP, and that the protein does not change CETP's selection of lipid or its mechanism. That last finding is what rules out describing apolipoprotein F as an enzyme or transporter inhibitor in the GO sense. Missed by the deep research report; verified against PubMed.

title: Lipid transfer inhibitor protein defines the participation of high density lipoprotein subfractions in lipid transfer reactions mediated by cholesterol ester transfer protein (CETP).
review_notes: The reason this review describes the protein as retargeting CETP rather than simply inhibiting it: within HDL the effect changes sign, with VLDL-to-HDL3 transfer stimulated while VLDL-to-HDL2 is inhibited. Cited on the GO:0006869 MODIFY row as the caveat attached to the negative-regulation replacement term. Missed by the deep research report; verified against PubMed.

title: CETP and lipid transfer inhibitor protein are uniquely affected by the negative charge density of the lipid and protein domains of LDL.
review_notes: Separates binding from activity - oleate abolishes inhibitory activity without reducing binding to LDL - which is why the molecular function added in this review is a binding term and the inhibition is recorded as a separate, currently unrepresentable activity. Also establishes that LDL surface lipid charge, not protein charge, controls the activity. Missed by the deep research report; verified against PubMed.

title: Control of cholesteryl ester transfer protein activity by sequestration of lipid transfer inhibitor protein in an inactive complex.
review_notes: Resolves the long-standing conflict between the HDL and LDL literature by showing there are two pools with opposite activity, and characterises the 470 kDa particle well enough (density 1.134 g/ml, apolipoprotein A-I-containing) to match the GO:0034364 definition. Used as the primary reference for the new HDL particle row. Missed by the deep research report, whose GO grounding nonetheless contains GO:0140313 molecular sequestering activity, apparently drawn from this paper's title - an inversion, since the protein is what gets sequestered, not the sequestering agent. Verified against PubMed.

title: Overexpression of apolipoprotein F reduces HDL cholesterol levels in vivo.
review_notes: Cited here for its human protein biochemistry rather than for its mouse overexpression result. The full text contains the mutagenesis that fixes the proprotein cleavage site at Arg-164, the demonstration that the secreted protein is Endo H-resistant and therefore Golgi-matured, the site-by-site N-glycosylation analysis identifying Asn-118 and Asn-139 in the proprotein and Asn-267 in the mature chain, and the fractionation putting more than 90% of human plasma apoF on HDL3. The overexpression result itself is AAV-driven ectopic expression in a CETP-free animal and is treated as IMP-grade context, not as evidence for a human function; no annotation in this review rests on it.

title: Isolation and partial characterization of a new acidic apolipoprotein (apolipoprotein F) from high density lipoproteins of human plasma.
review_notes: The original isolation of apolipoprotein F, and one of the three ECO:0000269 citations behind UniProt's Secreted line. This 1978 Biochemistry paper has no abstract in PubMed, so the cached record contains only the citation and title; the supporting_text used for it is taken from the title, which itself states the isolation from human plasma HDL. Historically important and correctly cited, but it cannot support anything finer than the localisation claim it is used for here.

title: Conversion of lipid transfer inhibitor protein (apolipoprotein F) to its active form depends on LDL composition.
review_notes: Shows that the active and inactive pools interconvert and that the trigger is modification of LDL rather than release from the complex, which is the basis for the knowledge gap about the inactive particle. Missed by the deep research report; verified against PubMed.

title: The effects of apolipoprotein F deficiency on high density lipoprotein cholesterol metabolism in mice.
review_notes: The source of the mouse IMP that seeds the GO:0008203 IBD node, confirmed by querying QuickGO for Q91V80, which returns GO:0008203 IMP from this PMID with allele MGI:3800154. Its introduction is also the clearest published statement that apolipoprotein F is unrelated to the classical apolipoproteins and lacks their amphipathic helices, and that the family's conservation in CETP-free species implies a second function. The lipid phenotype is modest and sex-specific, which is recorded in the propagation review rather than used against the transfer.

title: Genetic manipulation of the ApoF/Stat2 locus supports an important role for type I interferon signaling in atherosclerosis.
review_notes: Cited only for the caveat it supplies: the non-lipid phenotypes of the ApoF knockout line are attributable to hypomorphic Stat2 expression from a gene 425 base pairs downstream. The authors invoke this for the interferon and macrophage phenotypes, not for hepatic cholesteryl ester, so it does not void the GO:0008203 seed, but it means the line is confounded and the 39% lesion reduction in the double knockout should not be read as an apolipoprotein F lipid effect. Verified against the cached full text.

title: Is there a link between proprotein convertase PC7 activity and human lipid homeostasis?
review_notes: Identifies PCSK7/PC7 as a protease that processes apolipoprotein F. Relevant to the description of precursor maturation and cited there; deliberately not used to generate any annotation, because apolipoprotein F is the substrate of this cleavage, not its agent. Verified against the cached full text.

title: Inhibition of lipid transfer by a unique high density lipoprotein subclass containing an inhibitor protein.
review_notes: The original purification of lipid transfer inhibitor protein, published ten years before anyone knew it was apolipoprotein F. Missed by the deep research report, which is the general pattern for this gene: the mechanistic literature is titled for LTIP. Verified against PubMed. Supplies the 29 kDa mass, the pI of 4.6, the demonstration that inhibition covers cholesteryl ester, triglyceride and phospholipid transfer, and the measurement that 85% of functional activity is in the HDL density range - the last of which is the earliest evidence for the HDL pool annotated in this review.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0. Correctly cited for a real affinity-purification observation, but a whole-proteome projection: full pagination of QuickGO by reference gives 3731 annotations across 2324 distinct gene products, every one of them to GO:0005515. Contains no APOF-specific text - a grep of the cached full text for APOF or GALNT returns nothing - so the partner identity was resolved from the GOA WITH/FROM column and UniProt rather than from the paper.

title: Absolute quantitation of disease protein biomarkers in a single LC-MS acquisition using apolipoprotein F as an example.
review_notes: A methods paper that happens to be a clean direct detection of the protein in human serum and plasma, which is what the IDA row rests on. Also an unexpectedly useful source on glycosylation: it records that the tryptic peptide DANISQPETTK had to be excluded because it was glycosylated, and that peptide maps to precursor positions 265-275, spanning both the mature chain's only N-glycosylation sequon and its mapped O-GalNAc site. Its biomarker conclusion, that apoF falls across NAFLD stages, is not used for any annotation.

title: ApoF knockdown increases cholesteryl ester transfer to LDL and impairs cholesterol clearance in fat-fed hamsters.
review_notes: The in vivo validation of the inhibitory function, in the hamster because it expresses CETP and the mouse does not. Supports the negative-regulation replacement term. It also supplies the reverse cholesterol transport result that inverts with diet, which is why no RCT term appears anywhere in this review. Verified against PubMed.

title: Apolipoprotein F: a natural inhibitor of cholesteryl ester transfer protein and a key regulator of lipoprotein metabolism.
review_notes: The authoritative review, by the group responsible for most of the mechanistic work, with full text available. Used for the mechanism statement, the two-pool resolution, the precursor architecture and the field's own admission of what remains unknown. One internal discrepancy is recorded rather than smoothed over: it describes the precursor as 308 amino acids with a 286-residue proprotein, whereas UniProt and PMID:19008531 give 326 and 290; all sources agree on 162 residues for the mature chain. Being a review, it is used for framing and for statements it makes in its own voice, with primary references cited alongside wherever an annotation depends on the claim. Missed by the deep research report.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0, and the larger of the two projections: 9514 annotations across 4757 distinct gene products by full QuickGO pagination, of which 9508 are GO:0005515. Reports the same GALNT4 partner as PMID:28514442 from a successor release of the same pipeline, so the two rows are one interaction seen twice, consistent with UniProt's NbExp=2 for the pair. Contains no APOF-specific text.

title: Apolipoprotein F concentration, activity, and the properties of LDL controlling ApoF activation in hyperlipidemic plasma.
review_notes: The primary reference for the new GO:0030169 low-density lipoprotein particle binding row. Quantifies LDL-bound apolipoprotein F by ELISA across 200 donors, states that the activity requires LDL binding, and identifies LDL particle size as the sole correlate of binding capacity among the physicochemical properties surveyed - which is also the positive argument against the cholesterol binding annotation. Present in the deep research report.

title: Apolipoprotein F is reduced in humans with steatosis and controls plasma triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism.
review_notes: Reports that hepatic APOF expression is the strongest negative correlate of plasma triglyceride among liver-regulated genes in two obese cohorts, and that adenoviral human apolipoprotein F in mice increases VLDL-triglyceride secretion and remnant clearance. The human data are correlative and the functional data are ectopic overexpression in a CETP-free animal, so no annotation in this review rests on it; it is cited as evidence that CETP-independent roles exist, which is one of the knowledge gaps.

title: Isolation and characterization of simple and complex lipoproteins containing apolipoprotein F from human plasma.
review_notes: Correctly cited and scientifically sound for what it did, which was to resolve three apoF-containing particles and determine their lipid composition by thin-layer chromatography. It is the sole source of four GOA rows, and its own conclusion is an explicit suggestion about the particles rather than a measurement of the protein. Used here to support the cholesterol metabolic process row, which its conclusion does reach, and cited against the lipid carrier activity and cholesterol binding rows, which it does not support.

title: Regulation of lipid transfer between lipoproteins by an endogenous plasma protein: selective inhibition among lipoprotein classes.
review_notes: Establishes the selectivity that defines this protein - the inhibition order VLDL-LDL > LDL-HDL > VLDL-HDL - and the consequence that inhibiting LDL transfers enhances cholesteryl ester removal from HDL. Missed by the deep research report. Verified against PubMed; published under the LTIP name, five years before the identity with apoF was established.

title: Purification and molecular cloning of human apolipoprotein F.
review_notes: The cloning paper, and the source of three GOA rows. Correctly cited for extracellular localisation and for lipid metabolic process. Its use for GO:0005102 signaling receptor binding is the problem: the abstract describes purification from HDL, cDNA cloning, a Northern blot and chromosome mapping, with no receptor experiment of any kind, and no receptor for this protein has been reported since. The paper is sound; the annotation drawn from it is not.

title: Molecular cloning and expression of lipid transfer inhibitor protein reveals its identity with apolipoprotein F.
review_notes: The single most important paper for this gene, and it carries zero GO annotations anywhere in the GO corpus - checked directly against QuickGO by reference, which returns no hits. It establishes that LTIP and apolipoprotein F are the same protein, that recombinant human apoF secreted from transfected cells has CETP inhibitor activity, and that the protein is associated almost exclusively with LDL. The one caution: UniProt cites it for the statement that apoF also associates to a lesser degree with VLDL, Apo-AI and Apo-AII, and the abstract does not mention VLDL, so that part of the UniProt summary could not be verified from the cached record and no VLDL annotation was made on it.

title: APOF (Q13790) sequence analysis — results
review_notes: Local reproducible analysis written for this review; all sequences fetched live from the UniProt REST API at run time, with feature boundaries asserted against the record rather than assumed. Supports the amphipathicity deficit cited on the cholesterol binding row and the precursor arithmetic cited on the IBA row. Its N-glycosylation sequon inventory was computed independently and was afterwards found to match, site for site, the experimental mutagenesis in PMID:19008531, which is the strongest available check on it.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APOF (human)
review_notes: Trust gates clear per .affinage.log, self_evaluation_pairwise win, faith_pct 100, 16 citations all with numeric PMIDs, and the record describes the correct protein with no symbol collision. Accurate and useful on transcriptional regulation and the in vivo mouse and hamster work. Two limitations were worked around rather than inherited. Its mechanism_profile GO grounding was not imported: GO:0140313 molecular sequestering activity inverts the finding it comes from, since apolipoprotein F is sequestered into the inactive complex rather than being the sequestering agent. And its recall is poor on the mechanism: of the ten Morton-group papers that carry the mechanistic argument, it cites one, because they are titled for lipid transfer inhibitor protein rather than for apolipoprotein F. No supporting_text in this review is taken from it.

review_notes: Abstract-only.

review_notes: Abstract-only; APS T-cell study.

review_notes: Abstract-only; single cell-culture study.

title: The role of beta2-glycoprotein I (beta2GPI) in the activation of plasminogen.
review_notes: Abstract-only.

review_notes: Abstract-only.

title: Self-interaction of soluble and surface-bound beta2-glycoprotein I and its enhancement by lupus anticoagulants.
review_notes: Abstract-only.

title: {beta}2 Glycoprotein I ({beta}2GPI) binds platelet factor 4 (PF4): implications for the pathogenesis of antiphospholipid syndrome.
review_notes: Abstract-only.

review_notes: Abstract-only.

review_notes: No abstract in the cache; only the title is available, so the lipoprotein-distribution data cannot be checked here.

review_notes: Full text.

review_notes: Abstract-only.

review_notes: Abstract-only; rat infusion.

review_notes: No abstract in the cache; only the title is available, so the lipoprotein lipase activation data cannot be checked here.

title: Novel interaction of apolipoprotein(a) with beta-2 glycoprotein I mediated by the kringle IV domain.
review_notes: Abstract-only.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APOH (human)
review_notes: Trust gates clear; mostly genetic-association and APS findings. Its PMID:25081279 row includes functional clotting assays and is used for the anticoagulant call.

title: UniProt entry P02749 (APOH_HUMAN)
review_notes: Binds negatively charged substances; may prevent intrinsic coagulation activation.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Actual InterPro source IPR008405 is preserved. Target membrane interaction supports lipid binding, while the two process mappings remain unresolved. The current primary entry and mapping rationale were not retrieved; no family-name failure mechanism is inferred.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The exact seeded ancestral node PTN001422588 is retained. Target membrane/lipid experiments independently corroborate the two functions; the PAINT tree and ancestral placement were not reconstructed. Target self-inclusion is legitimate descendant evidence.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: The combined InterPro/UniProt extracellular-location inference agrees with human plasma isolation and serum rescue. Historical rule construction was not reconstructed, and localization is not assigned indiscriminately to every alternative product.

title: Apolipoprotein L-I is the trypanosome lytic factor of human serum.
review_notes: The original IPI and IMP source objects match the complete cached abstract: human APOL1/SRA helix interaction, APOL1 depletion and native/recombinant add-back, and trypanosome lysis are explicit. Full Methods remain unread. The exact add-back result supports the protozoan-defense refinement.

title: Apolipoprotein L-I promotes trypanosome lysis by forming pores in lysosomal membranes.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract read: pore-forming and membrane-addressing domains, bilayer anion conductance, and parasite lysosomal effects. Target membrane/lipid interaction is supported. Original constructs and full Methods remain unread, so chloride selectivity is not rejected using the later cation assay.

title: Proteomic analysis of human very low-density lipoprotein by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis and MALDI-TOF/TOF.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract directly identifies apoL-I in human VLDL. Seven proteomic forms and a phosphorylation site are reported; these forms are not equated with the three seeded UniProt sequence products. Detailed proteomic tables and physiological contribution were not independently adjudicated.

title: Human Trypanosoma evansi infection linked to a lack of apolipoprotein L-I.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity and complete abstract independently checked. Human biallelic APOL1 frameshifts accompany absent serum trypanolysis, restored by recombinant APOL1. This supports the extracellular immune-effector role and T. evansi defense; full clinical Methods were not read.

title: Proteomic analysis of microvesicles from plasma of healthy donors reveals high individual variability.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract describes 161 proteins associated with sub-220-nm human plasma microvesicles and donor variability. The APOL1-specific protein table remains unread; neither detection nor contamination is inferred from the general study description.

title: Secreted kinase phosphorylates extracellular proteins that regulate biomineralization.
review_notes: The original main text establishes secretory-pathway FAM20C kinase activity and named biomineralization substrates. The APOL1-specific IPI experiment is not resolved from that body; its supplementary PDF could not be read through the available download route. Later UniProt PTM evidence is explicitly separate corroboration.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Complete abstract and bounded target-record search of the human binary-interaction study were inspected. The APOL1–CDC23 assay record remains uninspected, despite the curated UniProt interaction trace. No binding mechanism or source error is inferred.

title: Human trypanolytic factor APOL1 forms pH-gated cation-selective channels in planar lipid bilayers: relevance to trypanosome lysis.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity/abstract and targeted indexed original Results and purification/bilayer Methods were read. Mature human O14791 residues 28–398 were assayed; acidic bilayer association is separated from channel opening on neutralization. The normal cache remains abstract-only; supplementary Methods and earlier 2005 construct details were not read.

title: Apolipoprotein L, a new human high density lipoprotein apolipoprotein expressed by the pancreas. Identification, cloning, characterization, and plasma distribution of apolipoprotein L.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity and complete abstract independently checked. Human plasma APOL1 was identified by isolation and sequencing from apoA-I-containing HDL; plasma distribution and particle characterization are explicit. This is particle membership evidence, not demonstration that APOL1 transports lipid cargo.

title: Haptoglobin-related Protein binds Hemoglobin
review_notes: Complete normal event summary read. TLF-1 contains APOL1, APOA1 and HDL3 in human serum. Hemoglobin binding is performed by HPR in the described event; APOL1 complex membership supports location without transferring that binding function.

title: FAM20C phosphorylates FAM20C substrates
review_notes: Complete normal event summary describes FAM20C phosphorylation of secreted substrates. Its APOL1-specific entity and ER-lumen compartment assignment are not exposed in the summary, so the exact source-local localization remains unresolved.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. The two source entries were fetched from the InterPro API: IPR019166 'MICOS complex subunit MIC26/MIC27' and IPR033182 'MICOS complex subunit MIC26/MIC27, animal', each mapping to exactly GO:0042407 and GO:0061617. Both contain APOO as a core member and neither maps to anything APOO does not do, so this is a precise rather than a promiscuous domain-to-term mapping.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT. The family slice was fetched to interpro/panther/PTHR14564/PTHR14564-paint.tsv and confirms exactly one node, PTN001803267, carrying exactly the two IBD annotations that appear as IBAs on APOO. Seeds and dates were read from that file, not assumed.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The UniProt subcellular-location mapping itself operates correctly; what it maps is unreliable for this protein. One of the four rows it generates (mitochondrial inner membrane) is accepted; the other three (Secreted, Golgi apparatus membrane, endoplasmic reticulum membrane) are removed because the UniProt statements behind them rest on a protein species PMID:37279200 showed is not MIC26. Flagged DISPUTED rather than MISCITED because the defect is in the upstream UniProt record, not in this GO_REF's procedure, and it will resolve when that record is updated.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence. Assigns the mitochondrion, agreeing with five other lines of evidence on this gene; nothing in it depends on the disputed secretory identity.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automatic annotation. All three components were checked: ARBA00026962 was fetched from rest.uniprot.org/arba (380 condition sets, one of which is exactly InterPro IPR019166 plus taxon Eukaryota, both of which APOO satisfies); UniProtKB:Q9DCZ4 is the reviewed 198-residue mouse orthologue; ENSMUSP00000109531 was confirmed by Ensembl REST to be that same mouse protein. All converge on the mitochondrion.

title: ApoO, a novel apolipoprotein, is an original glycoprotein up-regulated by diabetes in human heart.
review_notes: The paper that named APOO, and the origin of every secretory annotation on this gene. Correctly cited and historically important, but its central protein assignment has been overturned: the 55 kDa immunoreactive species on which the secretion, glycosylation, lipoprotein-association and cholesterol-efflux observations all rest is unchanged by MIC26 knockdown and knockout and contains no MIC26 peptides (PMID:37279200). Cached abstract only; the GOA EXP annotation on it is nevertheless removed here, because the refutation is a direct, knockout-controlled re-examination of that exact band and not an inference from the abstract.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: Phosphoproteomics of mitochondria purified from human skeletal muscle. Supports mitochondrial localisation only; the identification itself is in the supplementary tables rather than the cached text, which is normal for a high-throughput dataset and is not a citation problem.

title: Proteomics analysis of cardiac extracellular matrix remodeling in a porcine model of ischemia/reperfusion injury.
review_notes: A porcine cardiac extracellular-matrix proteomics study. It does not concern APOO, and APOO is not discussed in it; it entered this gene's record only because pig APOO was among the proteins identified in the ECM fraction, which then became an HDA on F1SPZ9 and an ISS on the human protein. Flagged MISCITED in the sense that the paper does not support the claim made from it: a single detection in an enriched fraction of an organ dense with mitochondria is not evidence of secretion.

title: APOOL is a cardiolipin-binding constituent of the Mitofilin/MINOS protein complex determining cristae morphology in mammalian mitochondria.
review_notes: The complexome-profiling study that first placed APOO and APOOL in the Mitofilin/MINOS complex, and the source of the cardiolipin-binding result - which belongs to APOOL/MIC27, not to APOO. Cited here for both purposes, and in particular to keep the paralogue's lipid-binding activity off this gene. Missed by the affinage record, which is the classic failure mode: the decisive paper is titled for the paralogue.

title: Apolipoprotein O is mitochondrial and promotes lipotoxicity in heart.
review_notes: The study that relocated APOO from the secretory pathway to mitochondria, by in vivo fluorescent labelling and subcellular fractionation. Its cardiac lipotoxicity phenotype comes from human APOO transgenic mice and is not annotated on the human gene here. Cached abstract only.

title: The non-glycosylated isoform of MIC26 is a constituent of the mammalian MICOS complex and promotes formation of crista junctions.
review_notes: The single most heavily used reference on this gene, supplying nine GOA rows. Its mitochondrial conclusions - inner-membrane MIC26 as a MICOS subunit interacting with MIC60, MIC27 and MIC10, and required for crista junction number - are accepted in full. Its three-form model is not: the glycosylated/secreted 55 kDa species and its ER/Golgi precursor were withdrawn by the same laboratory in PMID:37279200 (Anand and Reichert are authors of both). Hence its nine rows split three ACCEPT, three MODIFY and three REMOVE. Cached abstract only, but the refutation is explicit and author-confirmed.

title: Detailed analysis of the human mitochondrial contact site complex indicate a hierarchy of subunits.
review_notes: Independent confirmation of MICOS/MIB membership by radiolabelled import and co-immunoprecipitation with MIC60, and the source of the alternative name Mic23. Also the one paper reporting a negative cristae result for ApoO depletion, which is why it is cited on the cristae rows as well: later CRISPR knockout data (PMID:32788226) resolve the disagreement in favour of a real but MIC27-redundant contribution. Full text available and read. Missed by the affinage record.

title: QIL1 is a novel mitochondrial protein required for MICOS complex stability and cristae morphology.
review_notes: The QIL1/MIC13 paper. Its relevance to APOO is that MIC26 appears in systematic human MICOS proteomics and is degraded when MICOS disassembles - subunit behaviour. Also the reference ComplexPortal attaches its four NAS statements to. Full text available and read.

title: Mass spectrometry analysis of K63-ubiquitinated targets in response to oxidative stress.
review_notes: Recorded here only to document a citation defect in the machine-generated deep research record, and used to support nothing. The affinage report cites PMID:26217776 twice for MIC26 crista-junction and MIC26/MIC27-antagonism findings and labels it Biochimica et biophysica acta; the identifier in fact resolves to a Data Brief paper on K63-ubiquitinated targets in oxidative stress, with no relation to MIC26. The intended reference is almost certainly PMID:26217777, one digit away, by the authors of PMID:25764979 and with exactly the claimed content. Both were fetched and compared.

title: Data supporting the role of the non-glycosylated isoform of MIC26 in determining cristae morphology.
review_notes: The companion data paper to PMID:25764979. Valuable in hindsight: it records that MIC26 depletion lowers the 22 kDa mitochondrial form but not the 55 kDa 'secreted' one - the diagnostic of a non-specific antibody signal, available in 2015 and not acted on until 2023. Retrieved independently after noticing the affinage off-by-one citation.

title: Evolution and structural organization of the mitochondrial contact site (MICOS) complex and the mitochondrial intermembrane space bridging (MIB) complex.
review_notes: Complexome profiling defining the MICOS, membrane-bridging and MIB assemblies, and establishing that Mic23/MIC26 and Mic27 are opisthokont-restricted - the fact that explains the shape of PANTHER family PTHR14564. Source of four GOA rows on this gene, three of which are accepted; the fourth, SAM complex, is a projection over all 12 co-migrating MIB proteins and is removed. Cached abstract only. Missed by the affinage record.

title: Assembly of the Mitochondrial Cristae Organizer Mic10 Is Regulated by Mic26-Mic27 Antagonism and Cardiolipin.
review_notes: Yeast Mic26 destabilises Mic10 oligomers, antagonising Mic27. Cited here for what it does not license: this is Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and the human counterpart reported by Koob and Anand is reciprocal control of steady-state protein levels, which is a different claim. No human annotation is made from it. Cached abstract only.

title: Mutation in the MICOS subunit gene APOO (MIC26) associated with an X-linked recessive mitochondrial myopathy, lactic acidosis, cognitive impairment and autistic features.
review_notes: The first pathogenic APOO variant, I117T, with patient fibroblasts plus yeast and Drosophila models. Supplies human loss-of-function evidence for cristae junction disruption, and is also the experimental basis of the Drosophila IMP that seeds one side of the MICOS-complex IBD. Full text available and read.

title: MIC26 and MIC27 cooperate to regulate cardiolipin levels and the landscape of OXPHOS complexes.
review_notes: The decisive functional study: CRISPR single and double knockouts of MIC26 and MIC27 in human HAP1 cells, with crista junction counts, complexome profiling, respiration, mitochondrial morphology and cardiolipin lipidomics side by side. It is what separates MIC26's own contribution from MIC27's and from the complex's, and it supplies the single NEW annotation proposed here. Full text available and read.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP, the high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome. Supports mitochondrial localisation with explicit contaminant discrimination, which is why it is graded above a bare proteomic detection, but it says nothing about function.

title: Loss of APOO (MIC26) aggravates obesity-related whitening of brown adipose tissue via PPARα-mediated functional interplay between mitochondria and peroxisomes.
review_notes: Adipocyte-specific Apoo knockout mouse: impaired oxidative phosphorylation and brown adipose whitening. Real physiology, but mouse and tissue-specific, and downstream of the cristae defect; cited as context and in a knowledge gap, not annotated on the human gene. Cached abstract only.

title: MIC26 and MIC27 are bona fide subunits of the MICOS complex in mitochondria and do not exist as glycosylated apolipoproteins.
review_notes: The paper that settles this gene's central ambiguity, and the basis for eight REMOVE actions. Knockdown with three siRNAs, CRISPR knockout in four human cell lines, four independent antibodies, GFP- and myc-tagged constructs, glycosylation site mutagenesis and mass spectrometry of the excised 47-63 kDa gel region all agree that the 55 kDa species is not MIC26. Weight is increased, not reduced, by the authorship: Anand and Reichert are authors of the 2015 paper whose three-form model this withdraws. Full text available and read in full.

title: A X-linked nonsense APOO/MIC26 variant causes a lethal mitochondrial disease with progeria-like phenotypes.
review_notes: Second pathogenic APOO variant, the C-terminal nonsense E178*. Useful because the residual mutant protein still reaches mitochondria and still binds MICOS subunits yet cannot restore cristae - separating localisation and complex membership from function. Cached abstract only.

title: Macrophage-specific deletion of MIC26 (APOO) mitigates advanced atherosclerosis by increasing efferocytosis.
review_notes: Macrophage-specific Mic26 knockout mouse; increased efferocytosis via lowered OPA1 and increased fission. Cited for the mitochondrial-morphology knowledge gap, where it corroborates the human knockout phenotype by an independent route. Mouse and tissue-specific; not annotated on the human gene. Cached abstract only.

title: The molecular basis of mitochondrial crista formation by the MIC10 complex.
review_notes: The current structural model of the MIC10 subcomplex, and the only source making any cardiolipin-recruitment claim about MIC26 itself. Graded LOW_QUALITY not because the work is poor - it is careful and explicit about its limits - but because the evidence class is AlphaFold 3 models plus coarse-grained and all-atom molecular dynamics, with no experimental measurement. Cited here to define a knowledge gap and to justify NOT annotating cardiolipin binding on APOO. Human sequences were used (Mic26 residues numbered to 198, Mic27 to 268). Missed by the affinage record.

title: APOO / MIC26 (Q9BUR5) - N-terminal targeting sequence and paralogue architecture
review_notes: This review's own analysis, reproducible from genes/human/APOO/APOO-bioinformatics/targeting_sequence_analysis.py with all sequences and feature spans fetched live from UniProt. It is corroborating sequence evidence, not an experiment, and RESULTS.md states its limits: two hand-chosen ten-protein panels, a descriptive distance rather than a calibrated classifier, and one metric (Arg content) on which MIC26 does not match presequences - though neither does the paralogue UniProt already calls a transit peptide.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APOO (human)
review_notes: Machine-generated deep research (Affinage, LLM-authored). Trust gates clear and self_evaluation_pairwise 'win'; the narrative is about the right protein, with no symbol collision, and it correctly leads with the 2023 refutation of the secreted isoform, which is the most important fact for this gene's annotations. Graded LOW_QUALITY for two defects: it cites PMID:26217776 twice for MIC26 content when that identifier resolves to an unrelated K63-ubiquitination Data Brief (the intended paper is PMID:26217777), and its citation list omits five references this review needed - PMID:23704930, PMID:26477565, PMID:42647630, PMID:25781180 and PMID:25997101, the first of which is the source of the cardiolipin-binding result that must be kept on the paralogue. No claim in this review is supported by an affinage sentence; every mechanistic claim is quoted from a primary paper or from UniProt.

title: UniProtKB entry Q9BUR5 (MIC26_HUMAN)
review_notes: The fetched Q9BUR5 record; accession asserted to be the expected protein (MIC26_HUMAN, 198 aa), not a merged accession resolving elsewhere. Its function, subunit and mitochondrial inner-membrane sections are current and correct. Three things in it are stale: the Secreted / Golgi apparatus membrane / endoplasmic reticulum membrane locations and the chondroitin-sulfate PTM line, all traceable to the species refuted in PMID:37279200; and SIGNAL 1..25 (ECO:0000255, prediction only) where the paralogue Q6UXV4 carries TRANSIT 1..27. The mouse orthologue's record Q9DCZ4 already lists only the inner membrane.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping method. The two signatures cited on this gene, IPR019166 and IPR033182, were fetched from the InterPro API and both carry exactly GO:0042407 and GO:0061617, which is what the IEA rows assert. The mapping is sound for APOOL, since IPR033182 is the animal-restricted MIC26/MIC27 family and APOOL is one of its two human members.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT/IBA method. Both IBA rows on this gene descend from a single node, PTN001803267 in PTHR14564; the local PAINT slice was fetched and confirms exactly two IBD rows at that node and no IRD or IKR anywhere in the family.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The SubCell-to-GO mapping. SL-0168 was fetched from the UniProt locations API and maps to GO:0005743 mitochondrial inner membrane, matching the row. The underlying Swiss-Prot SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line is itself ECO:0000269-backed by PubMed:23704930 and PubMed:25764979.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: The Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence curation method. Its mitochondrial call for APOOL agrees with the antibody immunofluorescence and subcellular fractionation in PMID:23704930.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automatic annotation. The rule cited in this row, ARBA00026962, was fetched from the UniProt ARBA API. It confers GO:0005739 and has 380 condition sets, of which set 26 (IPR019166 AND taxon Eukaryota) is the one APOOL satisfies. That is a defensible condition for a MIC26/MIC27-family protein.

title: Characterization of the proteins released from activated platelets leads to localization of novel platelet proteins in human atherosclerotic lesions.
review_notes: Not an APOOL paper, and cited here only as provenance. It is the single PubMed-backed literature reference behind Reactome R-HSA-114608 Platelet degranulation, the pathway whose membership generates the GO:0005576 and GO:0031093 rows on this gene. Reading it shows what those rows rest on, namely a 2004 shotgun screen of the thrombin-induced platelet releasate returning over 300 proteins, nine years before APOOL was shown to be mitochondrial.

title: APOOL is a cardiolipin-binding constituent of the Mitofilin/MINOS protein complex determining cristae morphology in mammalian mitochondria.
review_notes: The defining paper for this gene and the source of every experimental claim about the protein itself. Mitochondrial localisation by immunofluorescence and fractionation, membrane integration by alkaline carbonate extraction, intermembrane-space topology by graded-digitonin protease protection, specific cardiolipin binding by lipid strip with a GST-only negative control, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation with Mitofilin/MIC60, MINOS1/MIC10 and SAMM50, and cristae and respiration phenotypes on both overexpression and miRNA knockdown. Full text read from the cache.

title: The non-glycosylated isoform of MIC26 is a constituent of the mammalian MICOS complex and promotes formation of crista junctions.
review_notes: Titled for MIC26, but the source of three APOOL annotations and of the antagonistic level-regulation result that makes single-gene depletion of either paralogue hard to interpret. Cache is abstract-only, so the co-immunoprecipitation details behind the three GO:0005515 IPI rows and the EXP inner-membrane row were not readable here; the partner accessions Q16891, Q5TGZ0 and Q9BUR5 were instead resolved against UniProt and all three are MICOS subunits, which is consistent with what the abstract states.

title: Detailed analysis of the human mitochondrial contact site complex indicate a hierarchy of subunits.
review_notes: Source of the MICOS-complex and mitochondrion IDA rows, and also the one human study reporting a negative cristae result for MIC27 knockdown. Correctly cited and methodologically fine; it is superseded on the cristae question by PMID:32788226, which counts crista junctions in CRISPR knockouts rather than scoring morphology in shRNA knockdowns, and which removes the paralogue compensation this study could not control for. Recorded as VERIFIED rather than DISPUTED because the disagreement is about sensitivity, not about correctness of the observation.

title: MICOS coordinates with respiratory complexes and lipids to establish mitochondrial inner membrane architecture.
review_notes: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Establishes the Mic27/Mic10/Mic12 subcomplex and its cardiolipin and respiratory-complex dependence. Used only as family context; no yeast mechanism is asserted as a human fact in this review.

title: QIL1 is a novel mitochondrial protein required for MICOS complex stability and cristae morphology.
review_notes: Human 293T and HCT116 interaction proteomics. Source of the MICOS-complex and mitochondrion IDA rows and of the four ComplexPortal NAS rows, and the study that places MIC27 in the MIC13/QIL1-dependent module rather than the MIC60 module. Full text read from the cache.

title: Evolution and structural organization of the mitochondrial contact site (MICOS) complex and the mitochondrial intermembrane space bridging (MIB) complex.
review_notes: Complexome profiling and comparative genomics; the source of the three HDA complex rows and of the IC row on this gene. The paper is correctly cited, but one of the annotations drawn from it is not supported by it. Its own resolution of the profile puts MIC27 in the MICOS complex, with SAMM50 and the metaxins appearing only in the bridging and full MIB forms, so the derived part_of SAM complex row conflicts with the reference it cites. Cache is abstract-only, but the abstract states the three-form model explicitly.

title: Distinct Roles of Mic12 and Mic27 in the Mitochondrial Contact Site and Cristae Organizing System.
review_notes: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The origin of the claim that Mic27 stabilises Mic10 oligomers. Cited here as family context and as the reason NOT to promote the bare protein-binding IPI rows to an oligomer-stabilisation molecular function, since the human knockouts in PMID:32788226 show MIC27 is dispensable for the stability and integration of the other MICOS subunits.

title: Mic13 Is Essential for Formation of Crista Junctions in Mammalian Cells.
review_notes: Human CRISPR MIC13 knockout. Independent confirmation, in a different laboratory from PMID:25997101, that MIC27 requires MIC13 to be assembled into MICOS. Full text read from the cache.

title: Cristae architecture is determined by an interplay of the MICOS complex and the F(1)F(O) ATP synthase via Mic27 and Mic10.
review_notes: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Reports that deletion of yeast Mic27 impairs crista junction formation and alters cristae curvature, and proposes a MICOS-ATP synthase link through Mic10 and Mic27. Consistent with the human phenotype but not evidence for it; used as context only.

title: Assembly of the Mitochondrial Cristae Organizer Mic10 Is Regulated by Mic26-Mic27 Antagonism and Cardiolipin.
review_notes: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The antagonistic Mic26/Mic27 effect on Mic10 oligomers, and a stabilising role for cardiolipin. Family context; the human paralogue antagonism is instead documented at the level of protein abundance in PMID:25764979 and PMID:32788226.

title: MIC26 and MIC27 cooperate to regulate cardiolipin levels and the landscape of OXPHOS complexes.
review_notes: The decisive human loss-of-function study and the one that reconciles the earlier disagreement about whether MIC27 depletion affects cristae. HAP1 single and double CRISPR knockouts with quantified electron microscopy. Crista junctions and cristae per mitochondrial section are significantly reduced in the MIC27 single knockout, while the full onion-stack MICOS phenotype requires the double knockout. Also the source of the constraint that MIC26 and MIC27 are dispensable for the stability and integration of the other MICOS subunits. Full text read from the cache. Not currently cited by any GOA row for this gene.

title: Drosophila MICOS knockdown impairs mitochondrial structure and function and promotes mitophagy in muscle tissue.
review_notes: Drosophila. Characterises CG5903/Mic26-27, the single-copy invertebrate family member whose FlyBase identifier FB:FBgn0038400 is one of the seeds of the PTN001803267 IBD node behind the MICOS-complex IBA on this gene. Read to check that the seed has real experimental grounding; it does.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP, a high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome. The APOOL call lives in the supplementary tables, not the cached text, and the reference supports 1235 GO:0005739 annotations over 1234 distinct gene products (QuickGO, paginated), so it is a bulk resource projection rather than an APOOL-specific observation, but a well-controlled one whose conclusion for this protein is independently established.

title: MIC26 and MIC27 are bona fide subunits of the MICOS complex in mitochondria and do not exist as glycosylated apolipoproteins.
review_notes: The paper that retires the secreted-apolipoprotein reading of this family, using knockouts in four human cell lines, four anti-MIC26 antibodies and GFP- and myc-tagged constructs. It is the positive evidence behind removing the extracellular region and platelet alpha granule lumen rows. Full text read from the cache. Not currently cited by any GOA row for this gene.

title: The molecular basis of mitochondrial crista formation by the MIC10 complex.
review_notes: Computational, not experimental. AlphaFold3 models with coarse-grained and atomistic molecular dynamics. Proposes that MIC10, MIC26 and MIC27 recruit cardiolipin at a conserved basic inter-transmembrane loop and thereby stabilise membrane curvature, reporting 83% cardiolipin occupancy at the MIC27 connecting loop. Graded MEDIUM and flagged as modelling throughout. It supplies a mechanism to test, not evidence of binding, and the binding itself rests on PMID:23704930. Published August 2026, after the affinage run, which is why that report does not contain it.

title: Exocytosis of platelet alpha granule contents
review_notes: The Reactome reaction is a real and correctly described reaction; what is wrong is APOOL's presence in it. Reactome still lists Q6UXV4 among the 27 participants of Platelet degranulation (R-HSA-114608) as entities R-HSA-8863003 and R-HSA-8862979, on the strength of a 2004 platelet releasate proteomics screen (PMID:14630798). The same database now also carries Q6UXV4 as R-HSA-8949612 APOOL (MIC27) in the mitochondrial inner membrane under Cristae formation, so the platelet placement is a stale duplicate. The reference supports 134 annotations over 67 gene products, two terms each, so nothing in it is APOOL-specific.

title: APOOL bioinformatics, inter-transmembrane loop conservation across PTHR14564
review_notes: Analysis performed for this review. Fetches the nine PTHR14564 representative members plus the Drosophila PAINT seed Q9VEY5 live from UniProt, asserts every length against the local family index, reads the human transmembrane boundaries from the UniProt flat file rather than re-predicting them, and aligns with FAMSA. Result, the human inter-TM loop is residues 130-137 RKGSKFKK, net charge +5, and all ten members carry a net-positive block with at least two basic residues. The document states its own limits, chiefly that conservation and charge are not a binding demonstration.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for APOOL (human)
review_notes: LLM-generated deep research. Trust gates cleared (self_evaluation_pairwise win, faith 100%) and the record describes the correct protein with no symbol collision, which is why it is listed at all; graded LOW_QUALITY because it is machine-authored and unreviewed, so nothing in it is used as supporting text. Its dated-findings table checked out against the primary papers wherever tested. It missed PMID:42647630 (published after its run date), PMID:14630798 (reachable only by chasing Reactome provenance, not by a gene-centred search), PMID:33053165 and PMID:40751083. Its mechanism_profile proposes GO:0008289 and GO:0005198; neither was imported, since GO:1901612 is the specific term the data support and structural molecule activity is contradicted for human MIC27 by PMID:32788226. Its citation list contains one non-numeric identifier, PMID:bio_10.1101_2025.05.20.655052, a bioRxiv preprint, which is not citable and was not used.

title: UniProtKB entry Q6UXV4 (MIC27_HUMAN), entry version 154, 02-SEP-2026
review_notes: The machine-fetched Swiss-Prot record. Confirmed to be the intended protein and not a merged accession, with ID line MIC27_HUMAN, GN Name=APOOL, 268 aa. Used for the topology features, the family assignment (PTHR14564, PF09769, IPR019166/IPR033182) and the curated FUNCTION, SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION blocks.

title: Falcon deep research report for APP
review_notes: Generated deep-research report used as synthesis support for APP processing, trafficking, synaptic, adhesion, and metal-homeostasis framing.

title: UniProt text export for APP (P05067)
review_notes: Local UniProt record supports APP receptor/adhesion, synaptogenic, proteolytic-fragment, isoform, copper/metal-binding, trafficking, and localization biology.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: UniProt manual ortholog-transfer pipeline; the source of all 24 ISS rows, every one of them from mouse Appl2 (Q8K3G9). Verified by inspecting the WITH/FROM of each row.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT phylogenetic annotation; the source of both IBA rows. Verified against the family's own PAINT slice (interpro/panther/PTHR46415/PTHR46415-paint.tsv), which shows the two IBD nodes, their taxon levels and their seeds.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location keyword projection; five CC rows. Each keyword id was resolved against the UniProt locations API (SL-0191 Nucleus, SL-0100 Endosome membrane, SL-0093 Early endosome membrane, SL-0205 Phagosome membrane, SL-0206 Phagosome). These restate UniProt's own curated locations rather than adding evidence.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara orthology projection; 19 rows, all with WITH/FROM UniProtKB:Q8K3G9|ensembl:ENSMUSP00000020500. I confirmed via UniProt that ENSMUSP00000020500 maps to Q8K3G9, so these are one donor under two identifiers, not two.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learned rules. Each cited rule was fetched from rest.uniprot.org/arba and its condition sets counted; they range from 4 (ARBA00093152) to 171 (ARBA00027281), and that span is what separates the rules I kept from the ones I marked over-annotated.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined multi-method IEA pipeline; the rows mix an ARBA rule, the mouse ortholog and a subcellular-location keyword in a single WITH/FROM. For GO:0005886 the ARBA component (ARBA00027801, 686 condition sets) is what drives the call.

title: APPL proteins link Rab5 to nuclear signal transduction via an endosomal compartment.
review_notes: The founding characterisation of APPL endosomes and of APPL1/APPL2 as Rab5 effectors; source of the EXP, TAS and two IDA rows plus a complex-binding row. The cache is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), and the abstract foregrounds APPL1's nuclear translocation, so the APPL2-specific details behind the NuRD row were read by the curator in the full text, not by me. QuickGO projection test: 20 annotations over 4 gene products, so this is not a bulk reference.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale yeast two-hybrid map (Rual et al.). Two rows, partners APPL1 and RAB22A. Systematic-screen evidence with no APPL2-specific follow-up.

title: APPL1, APPL2, Akt2 and FOXO1a interact with FSHR in a potential signaling complex.
review_notes: FSHR complex study. Beyond the two interaction rows, this is the source of the single cleanest functional distinction between the paralogs - APPL1 binds Akt2, APPL2 does not - which is what corroborates PAINT's decision to place the protein-kinase-B-binding IBD at the APPL1-only node. Cache is abstract-only but the relevant statement is in the abstract.

title: Membrane targeting by APPL1 and APPL2: dynamic scaffolds that oligomerize and bind phosphoinositides.
review_notes: Domain-level membrane-targeting and oligomerisation study; the source of most MF and several CC rows. Full text cached. Note the record lists an erratum (Traffic 2008;9(4):623-4) whose content is not in the cache, so quotes are taken from main-text sections only. The paper's own distinction between full-length protein and isolated domains is what separates the phosphatidylinositol row (accepted) from the phosphatidylserine and plasma-membrane rows (non-core).

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary exosome proteomics. Correctly cited and methodologically fine, but a whole-fraction inventory: the QuickGO projection test returns 1016 annotations over 1016 distinct gene products, all GO:0070062. Relevance to APPL2 function is nil.

title: Endosomal adaptor proteins APPL1 and APPL2 are novel activators of beta-catenin/TCF-mediated transcription.
review_notes: APPL proteins as activators of beta-catenin/TCF transcription via Reptin; full text cached. Source of two IPI rows and of the NEW GO:0090263 row. The APPL2 evidence is entirely gain-of-function because APPL2 is practically undetectable in the HEK293 cells used, which the paper states plainly - that limitation is recorded wherever the paper is used.

title: Yin-Yang regulation of adiponectin signaling by APPL isoforms in muscle cells.
review_notes: The Yin-Yang adiponectin paper: APPL2 as a negative regulator of adiponectin signalling, with both RNAi and overexpression directions in C2C12 myotubes. Not in the GOA reference list - it is the experimental basis of the mouse annotations that the ISS/IEA rows transfer. Retrieved and read for this review.

title: Biochemical characterization of APPL endosomes: the role of annexin A2 in APPL membrane recruitment.
review_notes: Biochemical characterisation of APPL endosomes and of annexin A2 as the recruitment factor; full text cached. Source of endosome, endosome-membrane and vesicle IDA rows, and the one paper providing a loss-of-function control on APPL2's own localisation.

title: Membrane curvature protein exhibits interdomain flexibility and binds a small GTPase.
review_notes: Crystal and solution structures of the APPL2 BAR-PH module plus the Rab-binding screen and Rab31 thermodynamics; full text cached. Correctly cited for the Rab31 interaction. It is MISCITED nowhere, but it does not support the homotetramerization row attributed to it - the word tetramer does not appear in the paper and all its solution data give a dimer. Recorded as VERIFIED because the citation resolves to the intended, supporting paper; the problem is with what one annotation claims it says, which is argued in that row's review.

title: A human skeletal muscle interactome centered on proteins involved in muscular dystrophies: LGMD interactome.
review_notes: Skeletal-muscle LGMD yeast two-hybrid interactome. One row, partner APPL1. Systematic screen.

title: A Y2H-seq approach defines the human protein methyltransferase interactome.
review_notes: Y2H-seq protein-methyltransferase interactome. One row, partner SUV39H2, no follow-up.

title: The adaptor protein APPL2 inhibits insulin-stimulated glucose uptake by interacting with TBC1D1 in skeletal muscle.
review_notes: APPL2-TBC1D1 and insulin-stimulated glucose uptake; the best-evidenced APPL2 function, with overexpression, knockdown and a muscle-specific conditional knockout. Cache is abstract-only, but the abstract states every result the annotations rest on.

title: Absence of Appl2 sensitizes endotoxin shock through activation of PI3K/Akt pathway.
review_notes: Appl2 knockout mice in endotoxin shock; the loss-of-function basis for the innate-immune and cytokine rows. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome map. Five rows; the two Rab partners are informative, the rest are unfollowed screen hits.

title: Rab31 and APPL2 enhance FcγR-mediated phagocytosis through PI3K/Akt signaling in macrophages.
review_notes: Rab31/APPL2 in FcgammaR-mediated phagocytosis; the experimental basis for the phagosome, ruffle, cytoplasm, phagocytosis and FcgammaR-signalling annotations that reach human APPL2 by orthology. Uses APPL2-only siRNA. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: Phospho-tyrosine dependent protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Phospho-tyrosine-dependent interaction screen. One row, partner MAPRE3, no follow-up.

title: Appl1 and Appl2 are Expendable for Mouse Development But Are Essential for HGF-Induced Akt Activation and Migration in Mouse Embryonic Fibroblasts.
review_notes: Appl1/Appl2 knockout mice and MEFs. Important as a control on a paralog-conflation suspicion: the title reads as a double-knockout result, but single Appl2 KO MEFs also show the HGF-induced Akt defect. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: APPL proteins promote TGFβ-induced nuclear transport of the TGFβ type I receptor intracellular domain.
review_notes: APPL proteins in TGF-beta-induced nuclear transport of TbetaRI-ICD; full text cached. Correctly cited, but every functional experiment is a simultaneous APPL1+APPL2 knockdown and the receptor interaction is mapped to APPL1 alone, so it cannot establish an APPL2-specific role. Recorded as VERIFIED rather than MISCITED because the paper does support the claim that the gene product is required - the limitation is one of attribution, argued in the affected rows.

title: Distinct Roles for APPL1 and APPL2 in Regulating Toll-like Receptor 4 Signaling in Macrophages.
review_notes: TLR4 signalling in macrophages with APPL1 and APPL2 depleted separately; the basis for the TLR4, cytokine and macropinosome annotations. Cache is abstract-only but the abstract states the separate-depletion design explicitly. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 affinity-purification mass spectrometry. One row, partner APPL1.

title: Adaptor Protein APPL2 Affects Adult Antidepressant Behaviors and Hippocampal Neurogenesis via Regulating the Sensitivity of Glucocorticoid Receptor.
review_notes: APPL2 transgenic mice, glucocorticoid-receptor sensitivity and hippocampal neurogenesis; the basis for the neurogenesis rows. Gain-of-function in vivo. Abstract-only cache. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: Activation of hypothalamic RIP-Cre neurons promotes beiging of WAT via sympathetic nervous system.
review_notes: Conditional APPL2 ablation in VMH RIP-Cre neurons and beiging of white adipose tissue; the basis for the thermogenesis and cold-acclimation rows. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Interaction disruption by coding variants. Five rows; two Rab partners plus unfollowed hits.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome. Seven rows, the largest single block of unfollowed screen hits on this gene.

title: APPL2 Negatively Regulates Olfactory Functions by Switching Fate Commitments of Neural Stem Cells in Adult Olfactory Bulb via Interaction with Notch1 Signaling.
review_notes: APPL2 and olfactory neurogenesis via Notch1; supplies the in vitro knockdown direction that the transgenic-mouse work lacks. Not in the GOA reference list; retrieved for this review.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 dual proteome-scale networks. One row, partner APPL1.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous tagging. One row, partner APPL1. Endogenous tagging makes this a better class of screen than overexpression Y2H, but there is still no APPL2-specific follow-up.

title: APPL2 (Q8NEU8) sequence checks: orthology, paralogy and residue-level verification
review_notes: Sequence analysis written for this review: live UniProt fetches with asserted lengths, pairwise global identities, and residue-level checks of the positions the structural paper names. Reproducible via appl_orthology.py.

title: UniProtKB record Q8NEU8 (DP13B_HUMAN), DCC-interacting protein 13-beta
review_notes: The UniProt Swiss-Prot record for Q8NEU8 (DP13B_HUMAN, 664 aa), fetched by the pipeline. Accession checked against the review's own id before use - this matters here because the Affinage service returned Q06481 (APLP2) for the symbol 'APPL2'. No affinage deep-research record exists for APPL2 and none is cited. The affinage prefetch refused to write one because its wrong-protein trust gate tripped: the record returned by the service was built on UniProt accession Q06481, which is APLP2 (amyloid-beta precursor-like protein 2), a different gene that carries 'APPL2' as a legacy alias, rather than Q8NEU8. This review therefore rests entirely on UniProt, GOA, the PANTHER PAINT slice and primary literature retrieved directly. The same symbol collision was filtered out of every literature search.

title: An integrated physical and gene map of the 3.5-Mb chromosome 3p21.3 (AP20) region implicated in major human epithelial malignancies.
review_notes: Abstract-only; the gene's identification in the AP20 region map. Its cell-adhesion suggestion rests on an RGD sequence motif only.

review_notes: Abstract-only; transcript-level correlation in breast cancer, with no functional test, so it does not support a GO annotation.

review_notes: PE2; C-terminal transmembrane helix by prediction.

title: Proteomics of human umbilical vein endothelial cells applied to etoposide-induced apoptosis.
review_notes: Large-scale HUVEC proteomic study; APRT is among the catalogued cytoplasmic proteins. Source of the cytoplasm TAS annotation; contextual only.

review_notes: Function and AQP2 interaction from the two MIAC papers.
