title: Cloning and characterization of androgen receptor coactivator, ARA55, in human prostate.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly reports ARA55/HIC5 binding in two-hybrid and co-IP assays and enhancement of AR transcription in DU145 cells; it supports the coactivator-binding interpretation. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Isolation and characterization of ARA160 as the first androgen receptor N-terminal-associated coactivator in human prostate cells.
review_notes: The complete abstract supports human AR N-terminal association with ARA160/TMF and coactivation. Targeted original Methods and Results around Figure6 additionally distinguish positive wild-type AR estradiol responses from E708K and T877A variant responses; the canonical cache remains abstract-only. Figure captions and text were read, not a new pixel-level quantification. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Glucocorticoids can promote androgen-independent growth of prostate cancer cells through a mutated androgen receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly concerns a doubly mutated AR that responds to cortisol/cortisone in patient-derived prostate cancer cells. It supports the retained mutant-specific signaling context, not normal wild-type glucocorticoid physiology. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Androgen receptor interacts with a novel MYST protein, HBO1.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports ligand-enhanced HBO1/KAT7 association with AR and suppression of AR-mediated transcription in CV1 and PC3 cells, supporting corepressor binding without assigning acetyltransferase chemistry to AR. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Beta-catenin affects androgen receptor transcriptional activity and ligand specificity.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports androgen-enhanced beta-catenin/AR co-IP in LNCaP and enhanced receptor transcription; complex association and functional coactivation are both stated. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: DJ-1 positively regulates the androgen receptor by impairing the binding of PIASx alpha to the receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract describes the AR–PIASxalpha regulatory complex and AR reporter inhibition in monkey CV1 cells, relieved by DJ1. The DJ1–PIAS assay is not silently recast as a direct AR–DJ1 experiment. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Inhibition of androgen receptor (AR) function by the reproductive orphan nuclear receptor DAX-1.
review_notes: The complete abstract expressly reports direct DAX1–AR domain interactions and inhibition of AR transcription/N–C interaction. This supports receptor binding with the inhibitory cellular context retained. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Conformational analysis of the androgen receptor amino-terminal domain involved in transactivation. Influence of structure-stabilizing solutes and protein-protein interactions.
review_notes: The complete abstract supports RAP74-induced folding of an AR activation-domain polypeptide. It does not by itself resolve the annotated multicomponent adaptor mechanism; the original adaptor assertion remains uncertain, despite correct citation identity. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Novel ATPase of SNF2-like protein family interacts with androgen receptor and modulates androgen-dependent transcription.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports ARIP4 association with AR in vitro and cells and separately demonstrates ARIP4 DNA-dependent ATPase activity. It supports ATPase binding by AR, not ATP hydrolysis by AR. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: DJBP: a novel DJ-1-binding protein, negatively regulates the androgen receptor by recruiting histone deacetylase complex, and DJ-1 antagonizes this inhibition by abrogation of this complex.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly reports testosterone-dependent DJBP–AR association, nuclear colocalization and repression through an HDAC complex. Monkey Cos1 reporter context is stated; no human construct species is inferred solely from cell origin. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: A direct beta-catenin-independent interaction between androgen receptor and T cell factor 4.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports GST-AR DNA-binding-domain capture of Tcf4, transfected/endogenous co-IP and AR occupancy of a Tcf4-responsive promoter. It distinguishes direct TF association from beta-catenin-dependent recruitment. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Isolation and identification of L-dopa decarboxylase as a protein that binds to and enhances transcriptional activity of the androgen receptor using the repressed transactivator yeast two-hybrid system.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports AR N-terminal interaction with DDC confirmed in vitro/in vivo and enhancement of ligand-dependent transcription in prostate cells. The coactivator interpretation does not transfer DDC enzymatic activity to AR. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Identification of glucocorticoid receptor domains involved in transrepression of transforming growth factor-beta action.
review_notes: Although the paper foregrounds GR, its complete abstract explicitly reports repression of TGF-beta transactivation by liganded AR. GR/Smad3 domain and physical-contact results are not transferred to AR.

title: The scaffolding protein RACK1 interacts with androgen receptor and promotes cross-talk through a protein kinase C signaling pathway.
review_notes: The complete abstract identifies human AR–RACK1 association and PKC-dependent nuclear translocation with transcriptional suppression. Nuclear presence is distinct from activation of target transcription. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Androgen regulation of the human FERM domain encoding gene EHM2 in a cell model of steroid-induced differentiation.
review_notes: The complete abstract specifies HT1080-derived HT-AR1 cells engineered with human AR, with DHT-induced growth arrest, cytoskeletal changes and differentiation-associated expression. These are retained as contextual cell responses. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Interactions between activating signal cointegrator-2 and the tumor suppressor retinoblastoma in androgen receptor transactivation.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly calls ASC2–AR binding indirect and describes Rb-dependent coactivation. Coactivator association is supported without claiming a purified direct ASC2–AR interface. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: The molecular mechanisms of coactivator utilization in ligand-dependent transactivation by the androgen receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports activated AR ligand-binding-domain structures with FXXLF/LXXLL recruitment motifs and SRC-dependent transcription. Peptide-domain recognition supports the coactivator interface within that assay scope. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Negative modulation of androgen receptor transcriptional activity by Daxx.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports Daxx binding to AR N-terminal/DNA-binding domains, suppression of AR transcription and impaired AR DNA binding. SUMO-dependent regulation is separated from a new AR SUMO-ligase activity. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Androgen receptor function is modulated by the tissue-specific AR45 variant.
review_notes: The complete abstract establishes human AR45 and its domain composition, tissue expression and context-dependent modulation of AR. It supports the intended isoform paper; the exact nuclear-localization experiment was not independently reconstructed from this abstract. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Huntingtin interacting protein 1 modulates the transcriptional activity of nuclear hormone receptors.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports HIP1 association with AR, androgen-dependent response-element recruitment and reporter changes after HIP1 depletion/overexpression. HIP1 trafficking mechanisms are not assigned as AR enzymatic functions. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: hZimp7, a novel PIAS-like protein, enhances androgen receptor-mediated transcription and interacts with SWI/SNF-like BAF complexes.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports hZimp7–AR nuclear complex formation and enhancement of AR transcription. Its separate hZimp7–BRG1/BAF57 association is not treated as an independently tested AR interface. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Modulation of androgen receptor transactivation by FoxH1. A newly identified androgen receptor corepressor.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly reports FoxH1–AR physical association, repression and nuclear interaction in LNCaP. It supports both TF/corepressor context without asserting that AR performs FoxH1 signaling functions. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Differential use of functional domains by coiled-coil coactivator in its synergistic coactivator function with beta-catenin or GRIP1.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly identifies beta-catenin as an AR-binding coactivator while focusing its new assays on CoCoA. It supports the intended AR/beta-catenin biological context; the original source's precise AR-binding assay was not reaudited in full. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Cyclin D1b variant influences prostate cancer growth through aberrant androgen receptor regulation.
review_notes: The complete abstract distinguishes cyclin D1b retention of AR association from compromised AR repression relative to D1a. The original partner isoform remains intact; reduced regulatory potency is not loss of binding. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Androgen receptor auto-regulates its expression by a negative feedback loop through upregulation of IFI16 protein.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports ligand-dependent IFI16–AR binding, an AR DNA-binding-domain interaction and inhibition of AR target expression after IFI16 re-expression. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Small carboxyl-terminal domain phosphatase 2 attenuates androgen-dependent transcription.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports SCP2–AR association and transcriptional attenuation, with ligand-dependent promoter recruitment and RNAi effects. The phosphatase acts on the transcription machinery; AR is not assigned its chemistry. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Glucocorticoid and androgen activation of monoamine oxidase A is regulated differently by R1 and Sp1.
review_notes: The complete abstract distinguishes AR binding to an androgen-response element and indirect Sp1-mediated promoter association from GR/R1 mechanisms. Only the AR-specific MAOA transcription evidence is used. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Male germ cell-associated kinase, a male-specific kinase regulated by androgen, is a coactivator of androgen receptor in prostate cancer cells.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports MAK–AR co-IP, nuclear/promoter colocalization and androgen/kinase-dependent coactivation. MAK catalytic activity and AR transcriptional receptor activity remain distinct. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Receptor for activated C kinase 1 (RACK1) and Src regulate the tyrosine phosphorylation and function of the androgen receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract supports a RACK1-mediated AR/Src signaling association and altered AR phosphorylation/transcription. It does not resolve every component into isolated binary contacts. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: A novel function of caspase-8 in the regulation of androgen-receptor-driven gene expression.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports Casp8–AR interaction motifs and repression independently of Casp8 apoptotic protease activity. The binding/refinement does not require AR to activate apoptosis or proteolysis. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Control of prostate cell growth: BMP antagonizes androgen mitogenic activity with incorporation of MAPK signals in Smad1.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports MAPK-regulated Smad1 physical interaction with androgen-activated AR and transcriptional repression. The source-specific inhibitory TF context supports the retained refinement. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Insulin-like growth factor 1/insulin signaling activates androgen signaling through direct interactions of Foxo1 with androgen receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports ligand-dependent Foxo1 interaction with the AR C terminus, recruitment to target chromatin and interference with AR-DNA association. IGF1/insulin relief of repression is kept as regulatory context. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Cooperative demethylation by JMJD2C and LSD1 promotes androgen receptor-dependent gene expression.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports AR association with JMJD2C and assembly with JMJD2C/LSD1 on target chromatin. The demethylases catalyze H3K9 demethylation; the receptor organizes ligand-dependent transcription. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: A novel variant of the putative demethylase gene, s-JMJD1C, is a coactivator of the AR.
review_notes: The complete abstract explicitly identifies a human AR fragment and human s-JMJD1C interaction by two-hybrid, GST capture and mammalian assays. The source's putative demethylase designation is not upgraded to AR catalytic activity. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Androgen-dependent gene expression of prostate-specific antigen is enhanced synergistically by hypoxia in human prostate cancer cells.
review_notes: The abstract alone emphasizes ChIP and transcriptional cooperation. Targeted original publisher Cross Talk Results and Figure6A legend independently verify reciprocal endogenous AR/HIF1alpha co-IP in LNCaP at 1% oxygen with 10nM DHT for20h. This positive association, rather than ChIP alone, supports TF binding; a complete Methods audit is not claimed.

title: Sirtuin 1 is required for antagonist-induced transcriptional repression of androgen-responsive genes by the androgen receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports antagonist-bound AR recruitment of SIRT1/corepressor to target promoters and transcriptional repression. Receptor chromatin occupancy is separated from SIRT1 deacetylation. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: DJ-1 binds androgen receptor directly and mediates its activity in hormonally treated prostate cancer cells.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports DJ1–AR association and modulation of transcription. The previously independently inspected original publisher Figure4 establishes the positive direction used for coactivator binding; full-paper experimental closure is not implied. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: PRMT2, a member of the protein arginine methyltransferase family, is a coactivator of the androgen receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports PRMT2 interaction/coactivation and hormone-dependent AR/PRMT2 movement from cytoplasm to nucleus. It explicitly separates hydroxyflutamide-induced AR nuclear entry from PRMT2 entry. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Peroxiredoxin 1 interacts with androgen receptor and enhances its transactivation.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports reciprocal IP, ChIP and in-vitro capture supporting Prx1–AR interaction and enhanced transcription. Prx1 antioxidant activity is expressly dispensable for this receptor effect. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Interaction between the androgen receptor and a segment of its corepressor SHP.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports an AR ligand-binding-domain crystal complex with an SHP NR-box peptide. The structural fragment evidence supports the repressor-associated complex without claiming that an isolated peptide is the complete cellular assembly. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Isosilybin B causes androgen receptor degradation in human prostate carcinoma cells via PI3K-Akt-Mdm2-mediated pathway.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports antibody capture of Akt/MDM2/AR complexes under isosilybin B in human prostate cancer models, alongside receptor ubiquitination/degradation. This supports E3-ligase binding in that treatment context; AR remains the regulated substrate. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Leupaxin, a novel coactivator of the androgen receptor, is expressed in prostate cancer and plays a role in adhesion and invasion of prostate carcinoma cells.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports ligand-dependent leupaxin–AR interaction and transcriptional activation in prostate cancer cells. Focal-adhesion and export observations concern leupaxin and are not transferred wholesale to AR. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: TRIM68 regulates ligand-dependent transcription of androgen receptor in prostate cancer cells.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports TRIM68–AR interaction and enhanced DHT-dependent transcription. TIP60/p300 cooperation is described separately; their catalytic activities are not assigned to AR. Detailed full-paper Methods, figures and supplements were not independently inspected unless separately stated.

title: Blood pressure is regulated by an alpha1D-adrenergic receptor/dystrophin signalosome.
review_notes: Actual construct/TAP purification Methods, complete Table3, signalosome Results and Figures4–5 were inspected and independently corroborated. The placement is the substantive curation act here: PANTHER puts Drosophila Arc1 in the same family and subfamily, but the node excludes it, which is correct because the fly and tetrapod genes are independent Ty3/gypsy domestications. Confirmed empirically - dArc1 receives no IBA from this node.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Supplies nine CC rows from SubCell keywords. The mapping mechanism is sound; the variable is what each keyword is anchored to on the human record. Two are anchored to citations that do not support them: SL-0090 Cytoskeleton (ECO:0000269|PubMed:21834987, a paper showing diffuse cytoplasmic GFP-ARC plus an actin phenotype, not cytoskeletal localisation) and SL-0071 Clathrin-coated vesicle membrane (ECO:0000269|PubMed:24945773, which reports coated-PIT association). Both are handled on the corresponding rows.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Eight rows, all projected from mouse Arc (Q9WV31 / ENSMUSP00000023268). Note that UniProtKB:Q9WV31 and ensembl:ENSMUSP00000023268 in these WITH/FROM columns are the same entity under two identifiers, so a two-item list here is one donor, not two. Most of the projections are well founded; GO:0071598 inherits the weakness of its mouse source.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Three rows combining Compara projection from mouse Arc with a SubCell keyword and, for GO:0050804, the InterPro signature. All three land on terms that the manual evidence independently supports.

title: Inhibition of activity-dependent arc protein expression in the rat hippocampus impairs the maintenance of long-term potentiation and the consolidation of long-term memory.
review_notes: One of the two IMP seeds behind the GO:1900271 IBD, and the donor evidence behind the rat-sourced long-term memory ISS. The design carries the argument: antisense knockdown dissociates LTP maintenance from LTP induction and memory consolidation from acquisition, which is what justifies the regulation-of formulation rather than a bare participation claim. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Developmental association of the synaptic activity-regulated protein arc with the mouse acrosomal organelle and the sperm tail.
review_notes: The entire basis of the acrosomal vesicle annotation, reached via UniProt's ECO:0000250|UniProtKB:Q9WV31 SubCell entry. A single 2003 mouse immunofluorescence study with no follow-up; nothing human, and nothing connecting the germ-cell pool to Arc's characterised functions. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Synaptic targeting by Alzheimer's-related amyloid beta oligomers.
review_notes: An amyloid-beta oligomer paper, not an Arc paper: Arc appears as a readout of aberrant synaptic induction. It carries four ARUK-UCL TAS rows on the human gene plus the rat IGI behind GO:0061001. A reference-projection check (QuickGO by reference, paginated) returns 16 annotations over only four entities, so it is gene-specific rather than boilerplate - but its Arc statements are second-hand citations of Guzowski, Steward and Kelly. Marked MISCITED for the GO:0060997 row specifically: the sentence used there reports that chronic overexpression 'has been suggested' to distort spine structure, which does not support an involved_in dendritic spine morphogenesis annotation. The long-term memory and LTP statements it also supports are accurate.

title: Arc/Arg3.1 is essential for the consolidation of synaptic plasticity and memories.
review_notes: The germline Arc/Arg3.1 knockout. Supplies the loss-of-function direction for long-term memory, LTP and LTD, and the biphasic LTP phenotype (enhanced early, absent late) that makes 'regulation of' the right formulation. Abstract-only in cache, which is enough for the claims used here.

title: Arc/Arg3.1 interacts with the endocytic machinery to regulate AMPA receptor trafficking.
review_notes: The mechanistic core of the synaptic half of this gene, and the donor evidence behind more rows in this file than any other paper - GO:0014069, GO:0031901, GO:0005886, GO:0045202, GO:0098978 and GO:0099149 all trace here. Full text verified: separate endophilin and dynamin interaction regions, immunogold EM at the PSD and its lateral margins, early-endosome co-localisation with transferrin receptor but not LAMP1, and bidirectional perturbation.

title: Arc/Arg3.1 mediates homeostatic synaptic scaling of AMPA receptors.
review_notes: Establishes the homeostatic-scaling arm with both perturbation directions in one paper: overexpression blocks the inactivity-induced rise in surface AMPARs, knockout abolishes scaling. Not cited by any GOA row, but it is what makes GO:0048168 and GO:0050804 defensible beyond their recorded seeds.

title: Sustained Arc/Arg3.1 synthesis controls long-term potentiation consolidation through regulation of local actin polymerization in the dentate gyrus in vivo.
review_notes: Donor evidence behind rat Arc's GO:0045202 rows and the strongest in vivo support for the actin/spine-regulation claims. Full text verified. It is the reason GO:0061001 is kept while GO:0060997 is not: Arc regulates local actin polymerisation, and spine and PSD expansion follow, rather than Arc executing spine morphogenesis.

title: Identification and characterization of a set of conserved and new regulators of cytoskeletal organization, cell morphology and migration.
review_notes: The source of both human IDAs in this file (GO:0005737, GO:0005886) and, via UniProt, of the cytoskeleton SubCell keyword. Full text verified. Two problems, neither fatal: the localisation data are GFP-ARC overexpressed in PC3 prostate carcinoma cells, which do not express ARC, and the paper carries a 2024 author correction stating that the siARC panels of Fig. 6 duplicated the siZRANB1 panels. The correction affects the knockdown figure rather than the localisation figure and the authors state the conclusions are unaffected, but it is a data-integrity event on this gene's panels and the rows resting on it are graded accordingly. It is also the source of the useful and independently checkable fact that ARC has no closely related mammalian paralogue.

title: Arc/Arg3.1 regulates an endosomal pathway essential for activity-dependent beta-amyloid generation.
review_notes: Donor evidence behind mouse Arc's GO:0005886 and GO:0045211 rows. Its one-sentence statement of the mechanism - Arc recruits endophilin2/3 and dynamin to early/recycling endosomes trafficking AMPA receptors - is the cleanest summary of the postsynaptic function in the literature. Also the origin of UniProt's PSEN1/APP statements. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Inverse synaptic tagging of inactive synapses via dynamic interaction of Arc/Arg3.1 with CaMKIIbeta.
review_notes: Donor evidence behind a rat Arc GO:0045202 EXP row, and the explanation for UniProt's otherwise cryptic 'Targeted to inactive synapses following interaction with CAMK2B in the kinase inactive state'. Full text verified. It is why Arc's synaptic targeting is counter-intuitive: the protein goes to synapses that have gone quiet, not to active ones.

title: Arc in the nucleus regulates PML-dependent GluA1 transcription and homeostatic plasticity.
review_notes: The basis of the NEW GO:0005634 row. Full text verified: activity-regulated nuclear expression in vivo and in vitro, a mapped NLS, nuclear retention domain and NES, and a PML-dependent transcriptional route to synaptic downscaling. The absence of any nuclear CC term for human ARC in GOA is the clearest compartment gap in this record.

title: Arc/Arg3.1 is a postsynaptic mediator of activity-dependent synapse elimination in the developing cerebellum.
review_notes: The basis of the NEW GO:0098883 row, and the source of UniProt's by-similarity statement about climbing-fibre synapse elimination. Purkinje-cell-specific knockdown with an occlusion experiment placing Arc downstream of P/Q-type VDCCs, which is stronger than a correlative developmental observation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Conditional knockout of tumor overexpressed gene in mouse neurons affects RNA granule assembly, granule translation, LTP and short term habituation.
review_notes: The sole gene-level seed behind the GO:0071598 IBD, and the reason that row is downgraded. Full text verified. The paper is about TOG/Ckap5; Arc enters it as the A2RE reporter TRANSCRIPT used to count granules, with Arc protein measured only as nascent translation output near granules and as bulk immunostaining intensity. It is a real Arc observation but it is about Arc mRNA as granule cargo, so it does not establish the Arc protein as a constituent of a neuronal RNP granule. Marked MISCITED for that specific claim; the paper is not itself flawed. Found only by donor tracing - its title makes it unreachable from any Arc keyword search.

title: Triad3A regulates synaptic strength by ubiquitination of Arc.
review_notes: UniProt's cited source for the Lys-268/Lys-269 ubiquitination sites and for the clathrin-coated vesicle membrane location. Full text verified. Supports the first unreservedly; the second is the basis for the MODIFY to GO:0005905, because what the paper reports is transient association with clathrin-coated PITS, plus a large fraction of surface Arc events with no CCP co-localisation at all.

title: Arc is a flexible modular protein capable of reversible self-oligomerization.
review_notes: The only paper in this set that worked on purified recombinant HUMAN Arc. Full text verified. It demonstrates reversible self-association into large soluble oligomers by DLS, AFM and EM, and a large conformational change on presenilin-1 peptide binding. GOA does not cite it anywhere, so GO:0051260 sits as an ISS from rat when direct human evidence exists.

title: Structural basis of arc binding to synaptic proteins: implications for cognitive disease.
review_notes: Crystal structures of both Arc lobes, establishing the bi-lobar Gag architecture and naming the N-lobe and C-lobe. Full text verified. Also records the functional corollary of the convergence argument: insect Arc domestication followed a different path, with a role in stress-induced behaviour rather than learning and memory.

title: Arc/Arg3.1 governs inflammatory dendritic cell migration from the skin and thereby controls T cell activation.
review_notes: The basis of the NEW GO:0036336 row and the source of UniProt's immune-system FUNCTION statement, which GO does not currently reflect at all. Mouse work; the mechanism given is myosin II-dependent actin dynamics, which is the one demonstrated functional payoff of the protein's 'cytoskeleton-associated' name outside neurons. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Palmitoylation and Membrane Binding of Arc/Arg3.1: A Potential Role in Synaptic Depression.
review_notes: Donor evidence behind three separate rows (GO:0045121, GO:0050804, GO:1900452) and the mechanistic explanation for why a protein with no transmembrane segment is annotated to membranes at all. Full text verified: the 94-CLCRC-98 motif, ~50% of detergent-insoluble synaptosomal Arc in raft fractions, and abolition of Arc-dependent synaptic depression when the cysteines are mutated. Reachable only through the mouse donor, not by keyword search on the gene.

title: Retrovirus-like Gag Protein Arc1 Binds RNA and Traffics across Synaptic Boutons.
review_notes: The Drosophila companion paper. Not evidence for the human protein and not cited by any row here, but it is what makes the PANTHER family question answerable: dArc1 independently earned IDA annotations for capsid formation, mRNA binding, intercellular vesicle transport and regulation of neuronal synaptic plasticity - nearly the same term set human ARC holds - which is why placing the IBD node at Tetrapoda rather than at the family root matters.

title: The Neuronal Gene Arc Encodes a Repurposed Retrotransposon Gag Protein that Mediates Intercellular RNA Transfer.
review_notes: The single most important paper for this gene, and the donor evidence behind five human ISS rows (GO:0003729, GO:0051028, GO:0051260, GO:0110077, GO:1903561). Full text verified. Capsid assembly, RNA dependence of assembly, non-selective RNA packaging, EV release requiring an intact C-terminal domain, neuron-to-neuron mRNA transfer with Arc-null recipients as the control, and the phylogenomic analysis placing tetrapod Arc orthologues throughout tetrapods and absent from fish - which is exactly the clade boundary the PAINT node uses. All experiments used rat Arc, so it is ISS-grade for human.

title: Arc Oligomerization Is Regulated by CaMKII Phosphorylation of the GAG Domain: An Essential Mechanism for Plasticity and Memory Formation.
review_notes: Donor evidence behind mouse Arc's GO:0007616, GO:1900271, GO:0043197, GO:0030425 and GO:0050804 rows. Full text verified. One caveat recorded on the GO:1900271 ISS row: in the knock-in model hippocampal LTP was explicitly normal and it was mGluR-LTD that changed, so this paper is a stronger source for the LTD terms than for the LTP ones.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI. The source of all four GO:0005515 rows. The identifications are correct and reproducible - UniProt records NbExp=3, which is three assay replicates within this one screen rather than three independent studies - but none of the four partners (TBX18, S100P, CSRP2, SH2D4A) has any follow-up with Arc. Correctly cited, uninformative for function.

title: Arc self-association and formation of virus-like capsids are mediated by an N-terminal helical coil motif.
review_notes: The reference behind all three human IDAs and, through human ARC's own accession, behind two of the six IBD seeds. Cache is abstract-only and the abstract says 'mammalian Arc' without naming a species for the capsid preparations, which is the one thing that could not be checked directly. The human anchor is nonetheless solid: UniProt cross-references PDB 6YTU (0.95 A, chains A/B = residues 99-132) to Q7LC44, and the RCSB entry gives the source organism as Homo sapiens with the sequence XQETIANLERWVKREMHVWREVFYRLERWADRLES, which is the human 99-132 segment. Accepted per project policy on experimental annotations whose full text is unavailable.

title: Author Correction: Identification and characterization of a set of conserved and new regulators of cytoskeletal organization, cell morphology and migration.
review_notes: The 2024 correction to PMID:21834987, recorded here because it concerns this gene's panels specifically. Full text verified: the siARC images in Fig. 6 duplicated the siZRANB1 images and have been replaced; the authors state the conclusions are unaffected. It does not touch Fig. 8, which is where the GO:0005737 and GO:0005886 IDAs come from, but it is why those rows are graded non-core rather than accepted at face value.

title: Arc, a growth factor and activity-regulated gene, encodes a novel cytoskeleton-associated protein that is enriched in neuronal dendrites.
review_notes: The discovery paper, and the sole recorded seed behind the GO:0048168 IBD via rat Arc's RGD IEP row. Verified against the fetched PubMed record. It establishes activity-dependent induction, dendritic enrichment of mRNA and protein, F-actin co-precipitation and subplasmalemmal-cortex localisation - so it correctly underpins the cell cortex and cytoskeleton claims - but its own plasticity conclusion is explicitly hypothetical, which is why an IEP code from it is thin support for a process annotation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: ARC gene expression
review_notes: A Reactome expression pathway, the source of the cytosol TAS row. Correct and uncontroversial as a compartment assignment for a newly translated protein with no signal peptide or transmembrane segment, but it is a pathway-diagram statement rather than an observation, and it says nothing about function.

title: UniProtKB Q7LC44 (ARC_HUMAN) flat file
review_notes: The Swiss-Prot record fetched by the pipeline, entry version 156 of 02-SEP-2026. Used for sequence length, feature table, subcellular locations, PTMs and the DOMAIN block's statement of independent tetrapod and fly domestication. Accession verified as Q7LC44 (ARC_HUMAN, 396 aa), which matters here because the affinage prefetch returned O60936 (NOL3) under the same symbol. Note that most of its FUNCTION and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements are ECO:0000250 by-similarity from rat Q63053 and mouse Q9WV31, and that two of its ECO:0000269 anchors over-read their citations (see GO_REF:0000044).

title: Purification and cloning of a brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein for ADP-ribosylation factors.
review_notes: The BIG1/BIG2 cloning paper. Correctly identified and a real primary source for the gene, but the GO:0006887 exocytosis TAS drawn from it is not supported - its statements about secretion are background about the ARF family and about brefeldin A, and its only nucleotide-exchange assay was performed on BIG2.

title: p200 ARF-GEP1: a Golgi-localized guanine nucleotide exchange protein whose Sec7 domain is targeted by the drug brefeldin A.
review_notes: The defining molecular-function experiment on human BIG1 - a Sec7-domain fragment loading GTP-gamma-S onto class I ARFs, with brefeldin A shown to be an uncompetitive inhibitor at Ki 7 microM. Verified against the cached abstract. It carries no GO annotation anywhere in GOA, which is the clearest single instance of the curation-coverage gap on this gene.

title: Identification and localization of two brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange proteins for ADP-ribosylation factors in a macromolecular complex.
review_notes: Supports the Golgi membrane, cytosol and perinuclear localisations and the BIG1-BIG2 co-complex. Note that the >670 kDa co-purification was from bovine brain cytosol while the imaging was in human HeLa S3 and HepG2 cells; both are stated in the abstract.

title: Protein kinase A-anchoring (AKAP) domains in brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 2 (BIG2).
review_notes: Titled and framed for the paralogue BIG2; the AKAP domain mapping in the abstract is that of BIG2. The BIG1 results sit in the full text, which is not cached. UniProt curators assert the PRKAR1A and PRKAR2A interactions for the human BIG1 entry with experimental evidence from this reference, so the GO:0034237 IDA and the Golgi EXP are accepted on that basis rather than second-guessed from the abstract.

title: Nuclear localization and molecular partners of BIG1, a brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein for ADP-ribosylation factors.
review_notes: Establishes the nuclear, nucleolar and nuclear-matrix pools in serum-starved HepG2 cells. Also the source of the important negative that ARF was never detected in nuclear BIG1 immunoprecipitates, which is why the nuclear rows are kept as non-core.

title: BIG1 is a binding partner of myosin IXb and regulates its Rho-GTPase activating protein activity.
review_notes: Correctly cited for the MYO9B interaction, the NOT GO:0005096 and the GO:0034260 negative regulation. The separate question of whether it supports the MYO9A partner attribution could not be resolved - the cached record is abstract-only and the publisher full text returns HTTP 403 - so that row is left UNDECIDED rather than marked MISCITED.

title: Hem-1 complexes are essential for Rac activation, actin polymerization, and myosin regulation during neutrophil chemotaxis.
review_notes: ARFGEF1 appears only as one of the mass-spectrometry identifications in Hem-1 leading-edge complexes, with no BIG1-specific follow-up. The reference annotates fifteen entities across thirteen terms in GOA, consistent with a complex-composition study rather than a study of this gene.

title: Effect of protein kinase A on accumulation of brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 1 (BIG1) in HepG2 cell nuclei.
review_notes: Establishes that PKA phosphorylation of Ser-883, together with the 711-715 NLS, is required for cAMP-induced nuclear accumulation of BIG1. Cited to keep that consequence distinct from the separate PKA effect on exchange activity in PMID:17360629; the provider record conflates the two. Contributes no GO annotation.

title: AMY-1 (associate of Myc-1) localization to the trans-Golgi network through interacting with BIG2, a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor for ADP-ribosylation factors.
review_notes: Supports a BIG1-MYCBP interaction in vitro but explicitly assigns the TGN-targeting function to BIG2 rather than BIG1.

title: BIG1, a brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein, is required for correct glycosylation and function of integrin beta1.
review_notes: Paralogue-controlled siRNA in human HepG2 cells. Supports both the Golgi organization IMP and the glycoprotein biosynthetic process row, the latter correctly qualified as acts_upstream_of_positive_effect.

title: Regulation of brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 1 (BIG1) and BIG2 activity via PKA and protein phosphatase 1gamma.
review_notes: The measurement behind the cAMP control of BIG1 catalysis - PKA-phosphorylated BIG1 has significantly decreased GEP activity against recombinant ARF1, restored by PP1gamma. Its Discussion also refutes the widely repeated shorthand that Ser-883 is the site responsible - BIG2 carries alanine at the corresponding position and its activity falls in parallel, and the authors state the mechanism is unresolved. Read in full for this review; no GO annotation exists from it anywhere in GOA.

title: Interactions between conserved domains within homodimers in the BIG1, BIG2, and GBF1 Arf guanine nucleotide exchange factors.
review_notes: Source of the homodimer NEW row. UniProt records the homodimer for the human entry with experimental evidence from this reference. No GO annotation exists from it anywhere in GOA.

title: Association of guanine nucleotide-exchange protein BIG1 in HepG2 cell nuclei with nucleolin, U3 snoRNA, and fibrillarin.
review_notes: The reference behind the GO:0030532 row. The paper is unambiguous that the RNA is U3 small nucleolar RNA, which is why the term is modified to GO:0005732. The authors hedge the complex as one the components may exist together in, and the co-immunoprecipitation is abolished by RNase or DNase.

title: Redundant roles of BIG2 and BIG1, guanine-nucleotide exchange factors for ADP-ribosylation factors in membrane traffic between the trans-Golgi network and endosomes.
review_notes: Source of the GO:0042147 NEW row. Cell line confirmed as HeLa from the Materials and Methods of the PMC full text, so an IMP on the human gene is species-correct. The knockdown was double, so the requirement is shared redundantly with BIG2. No GO annotation exists from this reference on any gene.

title: Interaction of brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein (BIG) 1 and kinesin motor protein KIF21A.
review_notes: Directed study of the BIG1-KIF21A interaction with reciprocal immunoprecipitation of endogenous proteins and domain-level mapping. Supports replacing the bare binding rows with GO:0019894 kinesin binding.

title: Interaction of phosphodiesterase 3A with brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange proteins BIG1 and BIG2 and effect on ARF1 activity.
review_notes: Supports the PDE3A and BIG2 interactions and the cAMP-regulation context, but contributes only uninformative GO:0005515 rows.

title: A role of histone H3 lysine 4 methyltransferase components in endosomal trafficking.
review_notes: BIG1 appears as the factor that targets mDpy-30 to the TGN. The GOA row names UniProtKB:Q8K3E7, a 99-residue rat Dpy30 entry, as the partner of an annotation made against the human gene; the species mismatch is recorded in the row review.

title: Specific functions of BIG1 and BIG2 in endomembrane organization.
review_notes: The best evidence for a BIG1 role that is structural rather than catalytic - Golgi mini-stacks that remain export-competent. Directly comparative between BIG1 and BIG2 in human cells.

title: Effects of brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange (BIG) 1 and KANK1 proteins on cell polarity and directed migration during wound healing.
review_notes: Supports the GO:2000114 polarity row directly. The GO:0090303 wound-healing row drawn from it overshoots the assay, which is a scratch-wound migration experiment in HeLa cells rather than tissue repair; the authors are also explicit that the KANK1 co-immunoprecipitation involves only small fractions of each protein.

title: The small G protein Arl1 directs the trans-Golgi-specific targeting of the Arf1 exchange factors BIG1 and BIG2.
review_notes: Establishes the ARL1 requirement for BIG1 trans-Golgi targeting in mammalian cells. In GOA it produced six annotations, all on Drosophila Arl1 and Sec71 from FlyBase and none on human ARFGEF1.

title: The PI(3)P interactome from a colon cancer cell.
review_notes: Recorded only to document a check that came back negative. IntAct holds a PI(3)P small-molecule pull-down record naming ARFGEF1 from this study, but it is a 681-protein lipid-affinity screen, ARFGEF1 has no FYVE, PX or PH domain in its InterPro content, and there is no GOA row. No lipid-binding term was imported.

title: ACBD3 interaction with TBC1 domain 22 protein is differentially affected by enteroviral and kobuviral 3A protein binding.
review_notes: ARFGEF1 is an affinity-purification co-purification here, with a strong specificity argument (peptides in six of more than 2,100 runs) but no functional follow-up. Contributes only uninformative GO:0005515 rows.

title: Arf guanine nucleotide-exchange factors BIG1 and BIG2 regulate nonmuscle myosin IIA activity by anchoring myosin phosphatase complex.
review_notes: Source of the GO:0030674 adaptor NEW row and independent corroboration of the GO:0030837 actin row. Experiments in HeLa cells. Crucially it controls for exchange activity, showing the myosin IIA association survives without it. No GO annotation exists from this reference anywhere in GOA.

title: BIG1, a brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange factor, is required for GABA-gated Cl⁻ influx through regulation of GABAA receptor trafficking.
review_notes: Establishes a requirement for BIG1 GEF activity in GABA-A receptor surface delivery, which connects to the seizure phenotype of ARFGEF1 haploinsufficiency. Not used for an annotation because the abstract does not state the species of the neurons, and an experimental evidence code asserts the experiment was done in the annotated species.

title: Structural Insights into Arl1-Mediated Targeting of the Arf-GEF BIG1 to the trans-Golgi.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human ARL1 bound to the BIG1 DCB domain, with the contact residues shown to be required for Golgi localisation in cells; four UniProt MUTAGEN entries cite it. Source of the GO:0031267 NEW row. No GO annotation exists from this reference anywhere in GOA.

title: Structural basis for targeting BIG1 to Golgi apparatus through interaction of its DCB domain with Arl1.
review_notes: An independent second crystal structure of the same DCB-ARL1 interaction, cited here so the GO:0031267 NEW row does not rest on a single structure. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Arfgef1 haploinsufficiency in mice alters neuronal endosome composition and decreases membrane surface postsynaptic GABA(A) receptors.
review_notes: Mouse model linking Arfgef1 haploinsufficiency to altered recycling-endosome composition, reduced surface GABA-A receptors and a lowered seizure threshold. Cited as background for the disease connection; no annotation is drawn from it, since the experiments are murine.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex. Supports 9,514 annotations across GOA; a proteome-scale screen rather than a study of this gene. Every row it contributes to ARFGEF1 is GO:0005515; the full set is paginated and was not enumerated. Provides independent replication for the MYCBP interaction.

title: Haploinsufficiency of ARFGEF1 is associated with developmental delay, intellectual disability, and epilepsy with variable expressivity.
review_notes: The human genetics behind the DEDISB disease entry, and the reason the neuron projection development row is kept despite being an ortholog transfer. Contributes no GO annotation.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Supports 2,876 annotations across GOA, of which the ARFGEF1 rows are all GO:0005515 (the full set is paginated and was not enumerated). Proteome-scale; replicates the MYCBP and ARFGEF2 interactions.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Supports 3,026 annotations across GOA. Proteome-scale; a fourth independent observation of the MYCBP interaction.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARFGEF1 (human)
review_notes: LLM-generated provider record, cited here only as a statement about its own citation corpus (citation_count 26), never as evidence for a mechanistic claim. Its trust gates passed and all 26 citations are numeric PubMed ids, but every claim used in this review was re-verified against the cited paper or UniProt; the provider also missed both ARL1 crystal structures (PMID:27373159, PMID:27436755), which is a recall failure the gates do not measure.

title: Purification and cloning of a brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein for ADP-ribosylation factors.
review_notes: The founding biochemical characterisation. Direct in vitro exchange assay on recombinant BIG2 with a brefeldin A specificity control; anchors GO:0005085.

title: Identification and localization of two brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange proteins for ADP-ribosylation factors in a macromolecular complex.
review_notes: Establishes the BIG1-BIG2 macromolecular complex and the Golgi localisation. The co-immunoprecipitations are from bovine brain cytosol; the imaging is in human HeLa S3 and HepG2.

title: Overexpression of an ADP-ribosylation factor-guanine nucleotide exchange factor, BIG2, uncouples brefeldin A-induced adaptor protein-1 coat dissociation and membrane tubulation.
review_notes: Companion overexpression study showing BIG2 acts on AP-1 but not COPI. Produces no GO annotation anywhere.

title: Dominant-negative mutant of BIG2, an ARF-guanine nucleotide exchange factor, specifically affects membrane trafficking from the trans-Golgi network through inhibiting membrane association of AP-1 and GGA coat proteins.
review_notes: The dominant-negative E738K result establishing that BIG2 is required for AP-1 and GGA1 membrane association at the TGN and not for COPI. Produces no GO annotation anywhere.

title: Protein kinase A-anchoring (AKAP) domains in brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 2 (BIG2).
review_notes: Maps the three AKAP regions to residues and confirms the interaction on endogenous proteins from human HepG2 cytosol.

title: Mutations in ARFGEF2 implicate vesicle trafficking in neural progenitor proliferation and migration in the human cerebral cortex.
review_notes: The disease-founding paper. Verified and central to the gene's biology, but its cell experiments use brefeldin A and a dominant-negative construct, neither of which isolates BIG2 from BIG1 or GBF1 - which is why no neurodevelopmental BP term is proposed from it. Produces no GO annotation anywhere.

title: The brefeldin A-inhibited GDP/GTP exchange factor 2, a protein involved in vesicular trafficking, interacts with the beta subunits of the GABA receptors.
review_notes: The origin of 17 of ARFGEF2's 66 GOA rows, via two independent projection pipelines. A real BIG2 study in rat brain and HEK293 cells. Full text is subscription-only, which is why the GO:0005879 axonemal-microtubule row derived from it could not be resolved.

title: BIG2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for ADP-ribosylation factors: its localization to recycling endosomes and implication in the endosome integrity.
review_notes: Establishes class I ARF (ARF1/ARF3) specificity in cells and the recycling-endosome pool, using the catalytically dead E738K mutant.

title: BIG1 is a binding partner of myosin IXb and regulates its Rho-GTPase activating protein activity.
review_notes: The paper is correctly identified and scientifically sound; it simply does not support a myosin-binding annotation on ARFGEF2. Its subject, its yeast two-hybrid screen and its antibodies are all BIG1/ARFGEF1, and across GOA it placed six annotations on human ARFGEF1 and none on human ARFGEF2; human ARFGEF2's row reaches it only through a rat intermediate. Coded MISCITED rather than WRONG_IDENTIFIER because the identifier resolves to exactly the intended paper - the schema reserves WRONG_IDENTIFIER for a PMID pointing at a different article.

title: Interaction of BIG2, a brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein, with exocyst protein Exo70.
review_notes: The EXOC7/Exo70 interaction and the MTOC/centrosome localisation, both in human HepG2 cells.

title: Overlapping expression of ARFGEF2 and Filamin A in the neuroependymal lining of the lateral ventricles: insights into the cause of periventricular heterotopia.
review_notes: Filamin A transport from Golgi to cell membrane requires BIG2 and not BIG1 - a second cargo for the Golgi-to-surface route. Produces no GO annotation anywhere.

title: Association of brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 2 (BIG2) with recycling endosomes during transferrin uptake.
review_notes: Transferrin receptor recycling, with a BIG1 negative control. Note the cells are COS7 and the siRNAs are human-designed, which is a mild species caveat on the human IDA.

title: AMY-1 (associate of Myc-1) localization to the trans-Golgi network through interacting with BIG2, a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor for ADP-ribosylation factors.
review_notes: MYCBP/AMY-1 interaction and the RNAi result that AMY-1 needs BIG2 to reach the TGN. The abstract does not name the cell system and the full text was unavailable, which is why no IMP row was added from it.

title: The brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein, BIG2, regulates the constitutive release of TNFR1 exosome-like vesicles.
review_notes: Correctly identified and scientifically sound, but it is cited in GOA for GO:0032760 positive regulation of tumour necrosis factor production, and it measures release of the TNF receptor TNFR1, not production of TNF. Flagged as MISCITED for that specific annotation, not as a defect of the paper.

title: Redundant roles of BIG2 and BIG1, guanine-nucleotide exchange factors for ADP-ribosylation factors in membrane traffic between the trans-Golgi network and endosomes.
review_notes: Establishes that BIG1 and BIG2 are redundant for AP-1-dependent retrograde transport, which is the counterweight to the non-redundant endosomal function. Produces no GO annotation anywhere.

title: Interaction of phosphodiesterase 3A with brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange proteins BIG1 and BIG2 and effect on ARF1 activity.
review_notes: PDE3A in the BIG1/BIG2 AKAP complexes, in human HeLa cells.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: A proteome-scale membrane survey; the reference assigns GO:0016020 to 1142 distinct entities across GOA, so the ARFGEF2 row is a sweep rather than a result about this protein.

title: Specific functions of BIG1 and BIG2 in endomembrane organization.
review_notes: The cleanest BIG1-versus-BIG2 comparison; explicitly states the siRNA was done on human cells. Anchors the non-redundant endosome-organisation function.

title: Effects of brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange (BIG) 1 and KANK1 proteins on cell polarity and directed migration during wound healing.
review_notes: A BIG1-centred study; ARFGEF2 receives 1 of its 14 annotations, recording the BIG1-BIG2 association already established elsewhere.

title: Brefeldin A-inhibited ADP-ribosylation factor activator BIG2 regulates cell migration via integrin β1 cycling and actin remodeling.
review_notes: Independent human HeLa corroboration of the migration phenotype through integrin beta1 recycling. Produces no GO annotation anywhere.

title: Arf guanine nucleotide-exchange factors BIG1 and BIG2 regulate nonmuscle myosin IIA activity by anchoring myosin phosphatase complex.
review_notes: The correct human reference for BIG2 myosin binding and for the two NEW cytoskeletal rows. Full text available and read; produces no GO annotation anywhere at present.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS; supplies one MYCBP interaction row.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous tagging; supplies MYCBP and ARFGEF1 interaction rows at endogenous expression levels.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell maps; supplies one MYCBP interaction row.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARFGEF2 (human)
review_notes: LLM-generated provider record. All 24 citations are numeric PubMed ids and none is retracted. Its recall is the limitation, not its precision: it did not surface PMID:15198677, the rat paper behind 17 of the 66 GOA rows, nor PMID:15644318, the BIG1 paper behind the myosin-binding row - both were found only by resolving WITH/FROM and querying QuickGO by reference. The record has no gates_passed field; its faith_pct and self_evaluation_pairwise values are precision signals and say nothing about coverage. Used here bibliographically and as corroboration, never as the sole source of a mechanistic claim.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The pipeline itself is sound and correctly applied: ARFGEF3 genuinely carries InterPro IPR000904 (Sec7 domain). What is disputed is the inference the mapping encodes for this entry, namely that presence of the Sec7 domain implies exchange factor activity. ARFGEF3's Sec7 domain has lost the catalytic glutamate, so both GO terms this reference supplies (GO:0005085 and GO:0032012) overstate what the domain can do here. Recorded as DISPUTED rather than MISCITED because the defect is in a domain-to-activity rule, not in the citation.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Verified by resolving every WITH/FROM token on both IBA rows: 19 tokens each, 10 shared, so 28 distinct (32 across all seven GOA rows that carry one), with zero unresolved. The node placements are well founded: every one of the 18 protein donors of the GO:0005085 row carries its own experimental evidence for that term and 15 carry their own IDA. The GO:0016192 row's donors are heterogeneous in process, so that broad term is the genuine LCA. The problem on the GO:0005085 row is target-side loss of the catalytic residue, not a defect in this reference or in the node.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The SL-0086 (Cytoplasm) mapping is exact. The SL-0244 and SL-0245 mappings are not: UniProt's own definition of SL-0244 describes regulated exocytosis of hormones and neurotransmitters, but the mapping sends it to GO:0030133 transport vesicle, which GO defines as the constitutive secretory pathway. GO:0030141 secretory granule and GO:0030133 are disjoint sibling branches under GO:0031410, verified against QuickGO's is_a/part_of closure, so this is a wrong-branch mapping rather than a coarse one. Affects the vocabulary rule, not this gene alone.

title: Cloning and characterization of a novel WD-40 repeat protein that dramatically accelerates osteoblastic differentiation.
review_notes: The original cloning paper for the unrelated BIG-3, cited here only as the evidence that establishes the name collision: a 3 kb mRNA encoding a 34 kDa, seven-WD-40-repeat protein. Correctly cited for that purpose and not relevant to ARFGEF3's function.

title: Yeast Ysl2p, homologous to Sec7 domain guanine nucleotide exchange factors, functions in endocytosis and maintenance of vacuole integrity and interacts with the Arf-Like small GTPase Arl1p.
review_notes: Not about ARFGEF3 and supports no annotation on this gene. Cited only in the PAINT question, as the single reference behind the GO:0005085 support of MON2, a WITH/FROM donor on ARFGEF3's IBA row that carries no annotated SEC7 domain. It matters because the paper claims a potential rather than a demonstrated exchange activity, which is what makes the node's donation to Mon2-like members worth re-examining. Identified by the committed reciprocal_donor_check.py rather than by hand, and cached here so the claim rests on the record instead of on a transcript.

title: BIG-3, a novel WD-40 repeat protein, is expressed in the developing growth plate and accelerates chondrocyte differentiation in vitro.
review_notes: Not this gene. The affinage record presents this paper's chondrocyte differentiation results as ARFGEF3 findings, but its "BIG-3" is BMP-2-induced gene 3 kb, a 34 kDa protein with seven WD-40 repeats (PMID:11551928). ARFGEF3/BIG3 is 2177 residues with Sec7 and armadillo-type repeats and no WD-40 domain. A pure symbol collision. Nothing in this review rests on it; listed so the collision is recorded rather than silently dropped.

title: The effects of BIG-3 on osteoblast differentiation are not dependent upon endogenously produced BMPs.
review_notes: Same symbol collision as PMID:14657013 and by the same authors: the abstract states plainly that BIG-3, BMP-2-induced gene 3 kb, encodes a WD-40 repeat protein. Not ARFGEF3. The Smad1 result the affinage record attributes to this gene belongs to a different protein.

title: Activation of an estrogen/estrogen receptor signaling by BIG3 through its inhibitory effect on nuclear transport of PHB2/REA in breast cancer.
review_notes: The founding functional paper on human BIG3 and the source of the single EXP annotation in GOA. Human cell lines and human tumour tissue throughout; localisation rests on endogenous protein with a validated antibody. The negative BIG3-ERalpha result is recorded because it constrains which terms are defensible.

title: Targeting BIG3-PHB2 interaction to overcome tamoxifen resistance in breast cancer cells.
review_notes: The loss-of-interaction complement to PMID:19496786: a targeted disruption of the interface releases the ligand and reverses the downstream effect, which is stronger evidence for a sequestering function than either knockdown or overexpression alone.

title: BIG3 inhibits insulin granule biogenesis and insulin secretion.
review_notes: The principal functional characterisation of the protein, but performed in mouse (MIN6 cells, BIG3-knockout mice), which is why the granule-pathway annotations proposed from it carry ISS with the mouse accession rather than IMP. Note the paper does contain a human element - exogenous human BIG3 rescues the knockdown phenotype - but that is a rescue experiment in a mouse cell line, not a measurement of the human protein's own behaviour in human cells.

title: Brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide-exchange protein 3 (BIG3) is predicted to interact with its partner through an ARM-type α-helical structure.
review_notes: The decisive sequence analysis for this review, and independently reproduced in ARFGEF3-bioinformatics/ as a precondition of that script running at all (7/7 of the paper's other Sec7 domains score positive, BIG3 negative). Two caveats recorded rather than glossed. First, the Methods give GEP100 as Swiss-Prot Q6ND90, which is a Rhodopseudomonas palustris succinate dehydrogenase subunit; the intended accession is Q6DN90. Second, the paper states its conclusion is consistent with a previous GST-GAT pull-down demonstration and the PMC cross-reference resolves that to PMID:24711543, but no such assay is locatable in that paper's accessible text, so the direct experimental demonstration of absent GEF activity remains unverified here.

title: Detection of insulin granule exocytosis by an electrophysiology method with high temporal resolution reveals enlarged insulin granule pool in BIG3-knockout mice.
review_notes: Corroborates PMID:24711543 by localising the defect to granule number rather than to release kinetics, which is what makes "regulates biogenesis" preferable to "regulates exocytosis". Abstract-only in the cache and mouse-based, so nothing in this review rests on it alone.

title: Xanthohumol suppresses oestrogen-signalling in breast cancer through the inhibition of BIG3-PHB2 interactions.
review_notes: A chemically distinct disruptor of the same interface, so it is genuine corroboration rather than a repeat of the peptide result. Absent from the affinage record; found by independent search.

title: Therapeutic advances in BIG3-PHB2 inhibition targeting the crosstalk between estrogen and growth factors in breast cancer.
review_notes: Downstream pharmacology of the released PHB2 rather than a statement about BIG3's own activity. Retained for context; no annotation rests on it.

title: Increased biogenesis of glucagon-containing secretory granules and glucagon secretion in BIG3-knockout mice.
review_notes: Important because it generalises the granule phenotype beyond insulin: the same negative regulation applies to glucagon granules in a different islet cell type. That is what licenses the broader GO:1904410 rather than an insulin-specific term. Mouse throughout, hence ISS.

title: BIG3 Inhibits the Estrogen-Dependent Nuclear Translocation of PHB2 via Multiple Karyopherin-Alpha Proteins in Breast Cancer Cells.
review_notes: This is what converts "BIG3 keeps PHB2 cytoplasmic" into a specific molecular function: BIG3 prevents PHB2 from engaging its import receptors, which is the GO:0140311 definition almost word for word. Human cell lines throughout.

title: Brefeldin A-inhibited guanine nucleotide exchange protein 3 is localized in lysosomes and regulates GABA signaling in hippocampal neurons.
review_notes: The single most compartment-informative paper on this gene, and affinage did not return it; it was found only by an independent PubMed sweep. It adds a fourth localisation and an entire tissue context (brain) that GOA does not cover. Not annotated here because it is mouse, abstract-only in the cache, and the lysosomal assignment has not been replicated; recorded instead as a knowledge gap and a question.

title: Stapled BIG3 helical peptide ERAP potentiates anti-tumour activity for breast cancer therapeutics.
review_notes: Peptide engineering of the ERAP inhibitor. Corroborates that the 165-173 helix is the functional interface, but adds nothing about BIG3's own activity. Absent from the affinage record; found by independent search.

title: A-kinase anchoring protein BIG3 coordinates oestrogen signalling in breast cancer cells.
review_notes: The source of three molecular functions that GOA does not record at all, all of them measured on endogenous human proteins in human cells. Note the level at which each claim is safe: the PKA interaction was measured but the RII-subunit specificity is predicted, so this review annotates the parent GO:0051018 rather than GO:0034237.

title: Biophysical characterization of the breast cancer-related BIG3-PHB2 interaction: Effect of non-conserved loop region of BIG3 on the structure and the interaction.
review_notes: Biophysics of the BIG3-PHB2 interaction, supporting that the binding is direct and measurable. Abstract-only in the cache, so no quantitative claim is drawn from it.

title: The survival and proliferation of osteosarcoma cells are dependent on the mitochondrial BIG3-PHB2 complex formation.
review_notes: A genuine fourth compartment, and the paper itself frames it as cell-type dependent rather than as a correction of the earlier work. Raised as a question rather than annotated, because it rests on one paper in one tumour lineage and would otherwise import a mitochondrial localisation into the gene's general record.

title: Arfgef3 knockout ameliorates ischemia reperfusion-induced acute kidney injury via mitochondrial dysfunction alleviation in mice.
review_notes: A whole-animal disease-model phenotype in a tissue where the protein's molecular role is unknown. Protection by knockout describes what happens when the gene is removed under injury, not a wild-type molecular function, so no term is proposed from it.

title: Overexpression of Brefeldin A-inhibited Guanine Nucleotide-exchange Protein 3 in Patients with Extramammary Paget's Disease.
review_notes: Expression survey in a further tumour type, extending the pattern of ectopic BIG3 expression in carcinoma. Descriptive; no molecular function claimed. Absent from the affinage record; found by independent search.

title: ARFGEF3 (BIG3) - computed evidence for the GO review
review_notes: This review's own reproducible analyses: the Sec7 glutamic-finger check with active and known-dead controls, the WITH/FROM resolution with per-donor evidence query, and the SubCell-to-GO branch check. Every quoted figure was re-derived from the committed scripts rather than transcribed, and the supporting_text drawn from this file is a computed table row rather than prose, because file: quotes are not machine-validated by CI.

title: Arginase I is constitutively expressed in human granulocytes and participates in fungicidal activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only cache but the myeloid-arginase/azurophil-granule findings are the source for the neutrophil localization and antimicrobial annotations. Complete canonical abstract read for this followup; no new whole-paper read is claimed.

title: Crystal structure of human arginase I at 1.29-A resolution and exploration of inhibition in the immune response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source for the binuclear Mn cluster and experimental arginase-activity annotations. Complete canonical abstract read for this followup; no new whole-paper read is claimed.

title: Suppression of T-cell functions by human granulocyte arginase.
review_notes: Official PMID/title and complete cached abstract checked. Original indexed publisher Results/Figure 6C–D and relevant human-cell/recombinant-protein Methods were also inspected: reduced IFN-gamma protein output with unchanged transcript abundance supports production regulation. This is a targeted original-body read, not a complete supplemental audit. The local cache remains abstract-only; see the public body locator in the notes. The public publisher URL and Figure 6C legend are retained in the notes so the original-body support can be checked independently of the immutable cache.

title: Expression, purification, assay, and crystal structure of perdeuterated human arginase I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; direct experimental support for arginase activity and Mn dependence. Complete canonical abstract read for this followup; no new whole-paper read is claimed.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Identifier/title and complete abstract checked. Authors report nuclear preparation purity above 99.9%, but the ARG1-specific proteomic table and peptide assignment are uninspected. The prior carryover inference was unsupported; lack of a known nuclear function does not refute localization.

title: Binding of α,α-disubstituted amino acids to arginase suggests new avenues for inhibitor design.
review_notes: Official identity/title and cached abstract plus targeted full-text introduction, human inhibitor-binding/crystallography and enzyme-inhibition Methods inspected. Human arginase I undergoes SPR inhibitor-binding and structural characterization; the inspected urea-production inhibition assay uses Plasmodium falciparum arginase. Do not describe that assay as human reaction kinetics.

title: Analysis of novel ARG1 mutations causing hyperargininemia and correlation with arginase I activity in erythrocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source for the L-arginine catabolic process IMP annotation and homotrimer quaternary structure. Complete canonical abstract read for this followup; no new whole-paper read is claimed.

title: CMTM6 maintains the expression of PD-L1 and regulates anti-tumour immunity.
review_notes: Identifier/title, complete abstract and targeted CMTM6 co-IP/MS Methods, Results and Extended Data 6c legend read. The ARG1–CMTM6 pair is a retained original IPI assertion; its target entry in Extended Data 6c/Supplementary Table 1 was not inspected. A full-text cache and lack of a body-text hit do not establish the pair or its absence. No wrong-paper or genericity-based removal conclusion is made.

title: Molecular cloning and nucleotide sequence of cDNA for human liver arginase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; original cloning paper, foundational for arginase activity, cytoplasmic localization, and urea-cycle/L-arginine-catabolism annotations. Complete canonical abstract read for this followup; no new whole-paper read is claimed.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Stable ID, title, human species and complete normal event summary were checked. UNVERIFIED records the still-uninspected ARG1-specific participant inventory; the event identity itself is established. The summary describes a granule class and exocytosis, not a target-specific assay. Independent granulocyte observations are distinguished from this original curated source in the annotation reasons.

title: Exocytosis of azurophil granule lumen proteins
review_notes: Stable ID, title, human species and complete normal event summary were checked. UNVERIFIED records the still-uninspected ARG1-specific participant inventory; the event identity itself is established. The summary describes a granule class and exocytosis, not a target-specific assay. Independent granulocyte observations are distinguished from this original curated source in the annotation reasons.

title: arginine + H2O => ornithine + urea [ARG1]
review_notes: Exact normal Source39 cache identity, human species, title and complete summary checked against the prior official event assessment; canonical bytes match the independently validated archive. Explicit human cytosolic ARG1-trimer catalyst and arginine-to-ornithine/urea reaction in the complete event summary.

title: ARG1 variants don't synthesize urea and ornithine
review_notes: Exact normal Source39 cache identity, human species, title and complete summary checked against the prior official event assessment; canonical bytes match the independently validated archive. Human deficient variants, with candidate/member and structural/catalytic distinctions. The short summary is not a direct assay of each variant and does not display the cytosolic graph field; that scope comes from the earlier official graph read. The earlier official graph participant/compartment read was performed by the coordinating reviewer and recorded separately; the present short normal summary does not itself expose that field.

title: ARG1 gene expression
review_notes: Exact normal Source39 cache identity, human species, title and complete summary checked against the prior official event assessment; canonical bytes match the independently validated archive. TP53 repression of ARG1 expression and downstream nitrogen/polyamine effects. ARG1 is the expression product, not transcriptional machinery. The summary does not show the product compartment; the cytosolic output was identified in the earlier official graph read. The coordinating reviewer previously inspected the official graph input/output and compartment fields; the present normal summary is not substituted for that graph evidence.

title: Arginine and glutamate-rich 1 (ARGLU1) interacts with mediator subunit 1 (MED1) and is required for estrogen receptor-mediated gene transcription and breast cancer cell growth.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum flags. Establishes the direct MED1 interaction, ligand-dependent promoter recruitment and ChIP-reChIP co-occupancy that the new GO:0036033 annotation rests on. Cached copy is abstract-only, so all claims drawn from it here are taken from the abstract, which states them explicitly.

title: Dynamic protein-protein interaction wiring of the human spliceosome.
review_notes: Targeted yeast two-hybrid map of the human spliceosome; one of three independent studies recovering the ARGLU1-SRPK2 pair. Cached abstract-only. Used only for the SRPK2 interaction and for the scale of the screen, both of which the abstract states.

title: The three clades of the telomere-associated TLO gene family of Candida albicans have different splicing, localization, and expression features.
review_notes: Not a paper about ARGLU1, but the sole experimental source of the GO:0005739 mitochondrion annotation that reaches human ARGLU1 by IBA, so it is decisive for this review. Verified against PubMed; no retraction or erratum. Cached abstract-only, and the abstract states the clade-restricted localisation and the Med2 domain content directly, which is all this review relies on.

title: The protein interaction landscape of the human CMGC kinase group.
review_notes: Source of the ARGLU1-SRPK2 record that IntAct types as phosphorylation by protein kinase assay in vitro, which is the strongest single piece of evidence for the GO:0019901 replacement term. Cached abstract-only; the substrate-identification claim is stated in the abstract and the per-pair detail was taken from IntAct rather than from the text.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: The paper is sound and correctly identified; the problem is the use made of it. It reports proteins in the vicinity of the E-cadherin cytoplasmic tail by proximity biotinylation, and that result has been converted into 272 cadherin binding annotations over 272 distinct gene products. For a nuclear protein such as ARGLU1 the inference from proximity to binding is not supported. Full text is cached and was read.

title: An Ultraconserved Element (UCE) controls homeostatic splicing of ARGLU1 mRNA.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Establishes the autoregulatory circuit and its direction, in human HeLa, HEK293 Flp-In T-REx and MCF7 cells including a CRISPR protein-null line, which is what licenses the human IMP on the proposed GO:0048025 annotation. No retraction or erratum.

title: ARGLU1 is a transcriptional coactivator and splicing regulator important for stress hormone signaling and development.
review_notes: The primary paper on this gene and the source of most of its experimental GO annotations. Full text cached and read, including the results and figure legends. No retraction or erratum.
