Two things in it are easy to misread and are handled explicitly in this review: the LXXLL motifs are shown to be dispensable rather than required, and the cellular RNA immunoprecipitation was performed in mouse Neuro-2a cells with tagged human constructs, so the human and mouse annotations derived from it are not independent.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0. Correctly cited, but very large: the committed reference-scope audit finds 9509 GO:0005515 annotations from this reference, too many to enumerate entity counts for, so it is treated as corroborating rather than establishing. It independently recovers SRPK2, PUF60 and JMJD6, which is its value here.

title: miR-335-5p Inhibits Progression of Uterine Leiomyoma by Targeting ARGLU1
review_notes: RETRACTED. PubMed lists this record with publication type Retracted Publication and a RetractionIn pointer to PMID:37503407. The affinage deep-research record for this gene cites it as a dated finding with no retraction flag, which is a provider defect worth recording. Nothing in this review rests on it, and it is listed here solely so that the retraction is on the record for the next reviewer.

title: Distinct biogenesis pathways may have led to functional divergence of the human and Drosophila Arglu1 sisRNA.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only. Supplies the sisRNA arm of the autoregulatory circuit and the statement that ARGLU1 protein has splicing-inhibitory activity on its host gene, which is the direction evidence behind the proposed GO:0048025 annotation. Worth noting for anyone reading the nucleoplasm IBA: this paper shows the human and Drosophila sisRNA mechanisms differ in both biogenesis and sign, so the fly ortholog being a WITH/FROM donor does not imply mechanistic identity.

title: Deletion of ARGLU1 causes global defects in alternative splicing in vivo and mouse cortical malformations primarily via apoptosis.
review_notes: Full text cached. Mouse conditional knockout, so it supports the mouse annotations directly and the human ones only by orthology; cited here for the in vivo splicing phenotype that corroborates the Compara transfer, not as human evidence.

title: ARGLU1 enhances promoter-proximal pausing of RNA polymerase II and stimulates DNA damage repair.
review_notes: Full text cached. Correctly cited and not retracted. Used for two things only: the explicit statement that ARGLU1 has no known structural or functional domains, and the pausing mechanism that motivates the recorded ontology gap. Its DNA repair claims rest on adenoviral overexpression rather than loss of function and no annotation is proposed from them.

title: Systematic identification of post-transcriptional regulatory modules.
review_notes: Correctly cited. Two caveats recorded rather than acted on: it carries an erratum (PMID:39468017), and its ARGLU1-U2AF2 record is proximity-dependent biotin identification, which reports neighbourhood rather than binding. Nothing in this review depends on either point.

title: PAK1 mediated phosphorylation of ARGLU1 promotes tumorigenic potential of Breast cancer.
review_notes: Found by an independent PubMed sweep, not by the deep-research provider, and not present in GOA. Cached abstract-only. Cited here only for the kinase-substrate relationship and the Ser-77 site, which the abstract states; no GO annotation is proposed from it because the downstream readouts are cancer-cell proliferation phenotypes rather than a molecular function.

title: ARGLU1 bioinformatics results
review_notes: Committed analyses supporting the PANTHER mitochondrion-node removal, the high-throughput cadherin-binding demotion, the SRPK2/U2AF2/PUF60/JMJD6 partner audit, the GO:1990935 splicing-factor-binding replacement term, and the RS-repeat composition call. The report is hand-written from JSON artifacts regenerated by the scripts in ARGLU1-bioinformatics/.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The pipeline itself is sound; its application to this gene is not. IPR000198 is the RhoGAP domain signature, and it matches ARHGAP11B partly because UniProt's Rho-GAP DOMAIN feature on this protein extends into non-homologous frameshift sequence. See the GO:0007165 row.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Maps UniProt's curated SUBCELLULAR LOCATION (Mitochondrion matrix, itself ECO:0000269|PubMed:31883789) onto GO:0005759. Agrees with the independent IDA row.

title: Human-specific gene ARHGAP11B promotes basal progenitor amplification and neocortex expansion.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch. Cached record is ABSTRACT-ONLY, and the abstract does not mention the RhoGAP assay that this paper is cited for in two GOA rows. I did not overrule those rows on that basis; the negative result is independently restated in the full text of PMID:27957544, which cites this paper as its reference (23). Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern via CommentsCorrections on the article's own PubMed record: none.

title: A single splice site mutation in human-specific ARHGAP11B causes basal progenitor amplification.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch; full text available and read. The single most important reference for this gene, because it is the only one that separates the GAP-activity question from the progenitor question experimentally. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none.

title: The evolution and population diversity of human-specific segmental duplications.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch. Background only; cited by UniProt's MISCELLANEOUS line for the duplication timing. No annotation in this review depends on it. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none.

title: Human-specific ARHGAP11B induces hallmarks of neocortical expansion in developing ferret neocortex.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch. Not cited by any GOA row; included because it is one of the systems establishing the progenitor phenotype, and because naming the system matters for how the cerebral-cortex rows should be read. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none.

title: Human-Specific ARHGAP11B Acts in Mitochondria to Expand Neocortical Progenitors by Glutaminolysis.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch. Cached record is ABSTRACT-ONLY. Six GOA rows rest on it, including both protein-binding rows, the mitochondrial matrix IDA and the glutamine catabolism row. Every one of those claims is stated in the abstract, and all six are accepted or refined rather than challenged; I did not second-guess a full text I have not read. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none.

title: Human-specific ARHGAP11B increases size and folding of primate neocortex in the fetal marmoset.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch. Abstract-only cache. Not cited by any GOA row. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none. PubMed lists an accompanying Science commentary, which is a Comment-in rather than a correction.

title: Expression of human-specific ARHGAP11B in mice leads to neocortex expansion and increased memory flexibility.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch; full text available. The experimental system is a transgenic MOUSE carrying the human gene, so the phenotype is a property of the human protein acting in mouse neocortex, not a measurement in human tissue. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none.

title: Human-specific ARHGAP11B ensures human-like basal progenitor levels in hominid cerebral organoids.
review_notes: Title verified against PubMed by efetch. This paper supports no GOA row at all, which is the clearest coverage gap in this gene's record: every existing cerebral-cortex annotation is gain-of-function, and the loss-of-function evidence, uniquely obtained in human cells, is uncurated. It is the basis of the NEW GO:2000179 row. Quotes here are taken from the abstract because the reference validator resolves this record to abstract-only (the publisher full text returns HTTP 403), even though a PMC copy is cached locally. Checked for erratum, retraction and expression of concern: none.

title: RHOA GAPs stimulate RHOA GTPase activity
review_notes: The reaction is real and correctly describes RHOA GAPs as a class, and for genuine members such as ARHGAP11A the resulting annotation is right. Marked MISCITED for ARHGAP11B specifically: including this protein in the catalyst set asserts an activity that two independent IDA annotations on the same gene explicitly negate, and that UniProt's recommended protein name denies. The defect is set membership, not the reaction.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: Same defect as R-HSA-8981637, one level up: ARHGAP11B is listed as a participant in the RHO GTPase cycle on the strength of its RhoGAP domain, and every participant receives GO:0051056. The gene has no measured role in small GTPase signalling.

title: ARHGAP11B: a GAP-dead RhoGAP that still has its arginine finger
review_notes: Generated report from the committed ARHGAP11B structural audit. The report corroborates, but does not replace, the direct experimental evidence that modern ARHGAP11B is GAP-dead by showing that residue-identity screening would miss this pseudoenzyme, that the human-specific frameshift starts at residue 221, and that UniProt's Rho-GAP DOMAIN feature overruns the last ARHGAP11A-homologous residue.

title: ARHGAP10, a novel human gene coding for a potentially cytoskeletal Rho-GTPase activating protein.
review_notes: The cloning paper. Cited here only for the domain architecture (PDZ + PH + Rho-GAP, i.e. no ArfGAP domain) and for the fact that this gene was named ARHGAP10 before HGNC reassigned that symbol to a different gene.

title: Comprehensive proteomic analysis of interphase and mitotic 14-3-3-binding proteins.
review_notes: One of four independent studies recovering ARHGAP21 as a 14-3-3 interactor; together they justify modifying the generic binding rows to GO:0071889.

title: Targeted proteomic analysis of 14-3-3 sigma, a p53 effector commonly silenced in cancer.
review_notes: 14-3-3 sigma interactome. Supports GO:0071889 alongside three other studies.

title: Golgi-localized GAP for Cdc42 functions downstream of ARF1 to control Arp2/3 complex and F-actin dynamics.
review_notes: The gene's founding paper and the source of its only experimental MF annotation. Abstract-only in cache. Calls the protein ARHGAP10 (this gene's former symbol). Says Cdc42 is the PREFERRED substrate, not the only one -- which is why it does not actually contradict PMID:16184169.

title: ARHGAP10 is necessary for alpha-catenin recruitment at adherens junctions and for Listeria invasion.
review_notes: Title verified against the cached PubMed record. Calls the protein ARHGAP10, which is this gene's former symbol, not the modern ARHGAP10 (A1A4S6) -- confirmed by querying QuickGO by reference, which shows this paper's two annotations sit on CTNNA1 and none on A1A4S6. Drives all three NEW rows. Cached copy is abstract-only, so the quotes used are from the abstract; the GAP-activity and knockdown statements are explicit there. PubMed types it a 'Letter' (hence publication_type COMMENT_EDITORIAL in the cache), but it is a Nature Cell Biology primary research Letter, not a commentary.

title: Role of the Arf6 GDP/GTP cycle and Arf6 GTPase-activating proteins in actin remodeling and intracellular transport.
review_notes: Titled for Arf6 and its GAPs, not for ARHGAP21, which is why it is easy to miss. Load-bearing here for one point: it classifies ARHGAP21 (as ARHGAP10) an Arf6 EFFECTOR and contrasts it with the two Arf GAPs assayed in the same experiment, which is the cleanest evidence that ARHGAP21 is not an ArfGAP.

title: Structural basis for ARF1-mediated recruitment of ARHGAP21 to Golgi membranes.
review_notes: 2.1 A crystal structure of ARF1-GTP bound to ARHGAP21's ArfBD. IntAct records this pair by x-ray diffraction against ARHGAP21's PH domain, confirming which module was assayed. Currently contributes only a bare GO:0005515 row, which this review modifies to GO:0031267.

title: Wilms tumor suppressor WTX negatively regulates WNT/beta-catenin signaling.
review_notes: Titled for WTX; ARHGAP21 appears only as a co-purifying protein with no follow-up. Supports removal of the generic binding row.

title: A comprehensive resource of interacting protein regions for refining human transcription factor networks.
review_notes: Display-technology screen aimed at transcription-factor networks. Weakest interaction row on the gene: single publication, single method class, no domain mapping in IntAct.

title: Cdc42 regulates microtubule-dependent Golgi positioning.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Source of five of ARHGAP21's GOA rows and the only paper contributing more than one. Explicitly reconciles the nomenclature ('ARHGAP21 (also referred to as ARHGAP10)').

title: β-Arrestin 1 inhibits the GTPase-activating protein function of ARHGAP21, promoting activation of RhoA following angiotensin II type 1A receptor stimulation.
review_notes: Full text available. Named in the description for the beta-arrestin 1 inhibition of GAP activity. One of the RhoA-side papers, and one of the seven primary papers that produced zero GO annotations anywhere in GOA.

title: Post-translational modification of the RhoGTPase activating protein 21, ARHGAP21, by SUMO2/3.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Named in the description and knowledge_gaps for SUMO2/3 modification at K1444 (UniProt numbers the site K1444; the abstract says K1443). Produced zero GO annotations anywhere in GOA; no PTM term is proposed here because SUMOylation is recorded by UniProt rather than as a GO function of this protein.

title: ARHGAP21 is a RhoGAP for RhoA and RhoC with a role in proliferation and migration of prostate adenocarcinoma cells.
review_notes: One of the two poles of the substrate disagreement. Abstract-only in cache. Reports GAP activity for RhoA and RhoC in PC3 but not the same phenotype in LNCaP, which is the main evidence that substrate engagement may be cell-context dependent rather than one group simply being wrong. Produced zero GO annotations anywhere in GOA.

title: ARHGAP21 protein, a new partner of α-tubulin involved in cell-cell adhesion formation and essential for epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
review_notes: Independent knockdown support for the adherens-junction NEW row, and the source of the junction-localised Cdc42 inactivation. Abstract-only in cache. Also reports an alpha-tubulin interaction and a requirement for alpha-tubulin acetylation in EMT, neither of which is annotated anywhere; not proposed here because the acetylation is a downstream readout rather than an ARHGAP21 activity. Produced zero GO annotations anywhere in GOA.

title: ARHGAP21 prevents abnormal insulin release through actin rearrangement in pancreatic islets from neonatal mice.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Cited on the GO:0032956 row solely to show that the sign of ARHGAP21's effect on F-actin is not fixed across systems: here antisense knockdown REDUCES F-actin ('F-actin was reduced in AS-islets'), the opposite of the stress-fibre accumulation UniProt records on depletion. MOUSE islets, so it supports the choice of a sign-agnostic regulation term and is not evidence for the human annotation.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: Large-scale quantitative interactome; three ARHGAP21 rows, none followed up.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS; contributes one YWHAZ row supporting GO:0071889.

title: Hematopoietic defects in response to reduced Arhgap21.
review_notes: Full text available. Named in knowledge_gaps as one of the seven uncurated primary papers, and it is the RhoC-substrate report. The experiments are in MOUSE (Arhgap21 haploinsufficiency), with human CMP/MEP knockdown recapitulating the erythroid phenotype, so it is cited as literature context and not used to support any human experimental code.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0. 9,514 annotations in GOA, so per-gene counts from a single QuickGO page are unreliable for this reference and were not used.

title: Differential CFTR-Interactome Proximity Labeling Procedures Identify Enrichment in Multiple SLC Transporters.
review_notes: CFTR-centred proximity labelling. Proximity is not binding, and the study's subject is CFTR; supports removal of the generic row.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Source of ten of the twenty-four GO:0005515 rows. Carries an Author Correction (PMID:36477203) whose scope is missing PCC values, axis labels, legends and panel ordering in Figs 2, 4 and 5 -- cosmetic, no data changed, so the reported interactions stand. The full text never names ARHGAP21, so the claim that these rows measure its PDZ domain was verified against IntAct participant ranges (all map to residues 50-159) rather than assumed.

title: Author Correction: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: The Author Correction on PMID:36115835, named in that reference's review notes and in the knowledge_gaps discussion. Scope is missing PCC values, axis labels, legends and panel ordering in Figs 2, 4 and 5 -- cosmetic, no data changed, so the ARHGAP21 interactions it reports stand. Listed here so every PMID the document names resolves to a reference entry.

title: A central chaperone-like role for 14-3-3 proteins in human cells.
review_notes: Paralog-resolved 14-3-3 interactome; contributes both an SFN and a YWHAZ row.

title: ARHGAP21 enhances metastasis in hepatocellular carcinoma by inhibiting ubiquitination of filamin A.
review_notes: Full text available. Added in round 2 after review: it reports the only cellular ligand yet assigned to ARHGAP21's PDZ domain (filamin A), which refutes the MF_DARK framing the first draft put on the PDZ knowledge gap. Supports the NEW GO:0031005 row. The domain mapping is hedged in the paper as a 'potential mediator', so the row is scoped to the binding rather than to PDZ-dependence. Human HCC cell lines.

title: ARHGAP21 provenance analyses - results
review_notes: Committed provenance analyses supporting the GO-specific curation choices in the review: obsolete substrate-specific GAP and small-GTPase-binding term resolution, PDZ/PBM term coverage, QuickGO-by-reference coverage, IntAct partner/domain/method checks, PAINT WITH/FROM interpretation, and PubMed correction checks.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGAP21 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched Affinage record, gates_passed true, 15 numeric PMIDs, no bioRxiv DOIs in PMID fields, and no retraction on any cited PMID (checked via CommentsCorrections on each record). Its narrative is accurate where it overlaps the primary papers I read. Its RECALL is the problem: it returned neither founding 2005 paper (PMID:15793564, PMID:16184169) nor PMID:20525016, i.e. it missed every paper that actually carries a GOA row on this gene, and the alpha-catenin paper that drives the largest curation gap here. Consistent with gates certifying precision and not recall. It is cited exactly once, at core_functions level, for a corpus-level statement about what the literature collectively reports; no mechanistic claim in this review rests on it, and its own coarse GO grounding was not imported.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The standard InterPro2GO mapping reference. Cited here for the IPR000198 (RhoGAP domain) to GO:0007165 mapping. Correct as a domain-level inference; the issue raised in this review is that the mapped term is on the wrong branch, not that the mapping is misapplied.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The standard PAINT/IBA reference. The specific IBA row it supports here is well founded: the node's named donor, ARHGAP21, carries its own experimental GO:0005096 IDA.

title: Identification and characterization of human ARHGAP23 gene in silico.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only, which is sufficient for what it is cited for here (gene structure and domain architecture). Contributes no evidence about activity.

title: Golgi-localized GAP for Cdc42 functions downstream of ARF1 to control Arp2/3 complex and F-actin dynamics.
review_notes: Cited only to trace what the IBA node rests on; not used to support any substrate claim for ARHGAP23. Cached record is abstract-only. The evidence code was checked against genes/human/ARHGAP21/ARHGAP21-goa.tsv, which carries "enables GO:0005096 IDA PMID:15793564".

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: Correctly cited for what it is - a mass-spectrometry inventory. It supports detection in an exosome preparation, not residence in a compartment where the protein does anything.

title: The human PDZome: a gateway to PSD95-Disc large-zonula occludens (PDZ)-mediated functions.
review_notes: Title-verified against the cached full text. Cited to delimit a knowledge gap rather than to support an annotation.

title: A lateral signalling pathway coordinates shape volatility during cell migration.
review_notes: Title-verified against the cached full text; in NCBI's curated gene2pubmed set for GeneID 57636. The single most informative paper for this gene, and the automated provider missed it because the title names a phenotype rather than the gene. Loss and gain of function are both reported, with a pharmacological comparator.

title: Deciphering the Molecular and Functional Basis of RHOGAP Family Proteins: A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TOWARD SELECTIVE INACTIVATION OF RHO FAMILY PROTEINS.
review_notes: Title verified, so the identifier resolves to the intended paper; UNVERIFIED refers to the claim, not the citation. The cached record is abstract-only, so the non-selection of ARHGAP23 could not be confirmed from the cache and rests on an external full-text check. What is independently verifiable, and what the negative claim actually leans on, is that the Müller 2020 supplementary table of RhoGEF/RhoGAP specificities leaves its "in vitro" literature columns empty for ARHGAP23 while filling the "in vivo" and "reference" columns. That substitute is no longer a manual reading either: analyze_arhgap23.py parses Supplementary Table 2, reads the column groups from the header rows rather than assuming them, and aborts if the "in vitro" block cannot be found - so an absent column can never be reported as an empty one, which is the way this particular negative could go wrong.

title: RhoGTPase Regulators Orchestrate Distinct Stages of Synaptic Development.
review_notes: Title-verified against the cached full text. The title names the family, not the gene, which is why the automated provider missed it. This is the source Reactome cites for ARHGAP23's membership in the RAC1 GAP set (as "Martin Vilchez et al. 2017").

title: Systems analysis of RhoGEF and RhoGAP regulatory proteins reveals spatially organized RAC1 signalling from integrin adhesions.
review_notes: Title verified. Main text is paywalled and absent from PMC, so no quote from it is used here; every claim attributed to this paper comes from the publisher's open Supplementary Information and Source Data, which the committed analysis downloads and parses. The residue-numbering discrepancy above is recorded as a discrepancy, not as a correction of the paper - the structural argument favours R942 but only an experiment settles it.

title: Shear stimulation of FOXC1 and FOXC2 differentially regulates cytoskeletal activity during lymphatic valve maturation.
review_notes: Cited for context only - it is the nearest thing to an in-vivo phenotype in the literature, and even that is indirect. No annotation here depends on it.

title: Replication and meta-analyses nominate numerous eosinophilic esophagitis risk genes.
review_notes: Background only. Deliberately not used to support any GO annotation: a GWAS locus assigns a gene to a region, not a function to a protein.

title: Pan‑cancer analysis identified ARHGAP23 as a potential biomarker for pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
review_notes: Listed so that its absence from the evidence base is deliberate rather than accidental: it is one of only two papers with ARHGAP23 in the title, so an automated pass is likely to weight it heavily. It states that ARHGAP23 is known to activate RHO-GTPase, which is the opposite of what a GTPase-activating protein does, and it contains no primary data.

title: Plakophilin 4 controls the spatio-temporal activity of RhoA at adherens junctions to promote cortical actin ring formation and tissue tension.
review_notes: Title-verified against the cached full text. One of the three papers the automated provider did return, and it is genuinely central. Note that the paper's own framing of why ARHGAP23 was tested is a family-level guess ("ARHGAP23 is similar to ARHGAP21"); the result then separated the two proteins rather than confirming the analogy.

title: VE-cadherin interaction proteomics identifies ARVCF as stabilizer of endothelial adherens junctions.
review_notes: Title-verified against the cached full text. Supports a junctional association in a second cell type (endothelium) alongside the keratinocyte data, but carries no functional or localization experiment specific to ARHGAP23, so it is not used to support any annotation here on its own.

title: RHOA GAPs stimulate RHOA GTPase activity
review_notes: The reaction is sound and the set membership is justified: the cited source is the RhoGEF/RhoGAP FRET specificity screen, which scores ARHGAP23 significantly active on RhoA. Marked MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the GO term the reaction emits cannot carry the RHOA specificity that is the whole content of the reaction.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: Correctly cited, and true of this gene. Its weakness is granularity, not accuracy - the direct evidence supports a specific negative-regulation term that this projection cannot reach.

title: RAC1 GAPs stimulate RAC1 GTPase activity
review_notes: Sound and sourced, but the underlying Rac1 evidence is less consistent than the RhoA evidence. PMID:28114311 and PMID:32203420 both report Rac1 activity, while PMID:27226243 found active Rac1 decreased rather than increased on ARHGAP21/23 knockdown. Recorded here because the GO row that results is indistinguishable from the RhoA one.

title: ARHGAP23 retains the RhoGAP arginine finger — and that is not evidence of activity
review_notes: Committed, reproducible analysis in genes/human/ARHGAP23/ARHGAP23-bioinformatics. Every number is emitted by analyze_arhgap23.py from fetched UniProt records, PDB 1TX4 and the publisher's supplementary files; the script carries a --self-test and a separate committed mutation_test.py that breaks each guard and asserts the self-test catches it, with a silent negative control.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGAP23 (human)
review_notes: Cited both for what it got right and for what it missed. Every citation it returned resolves and is correctly used, so nothing here is a citation error; the defect is coverage, and the resulting explicit assertion that no experimental characterization exists is contradicted by three papers found by an independent search of Europe PMC and NCBI gene2pubmed. Flagged LOW_QUALITY rather than MISCITED for that reason.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Retained original automated or phylogenetic evidence source. Target biology assessed independently; historical complete rule or ancestral placement not reconstructed.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Retained original automated or phylogenetic evidence source. Target biology assessed independently; historical complete rule or ancestral placement not reconstructed.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: Retained original automated or phylogenetic evidence source. Target biology assessed independently; historical complete rule or ancestral placement not reconstructed.

title: PARG1, a protein-tyrosine phosphatase-associated RhoGAP, as a putative Rap2 effector.
review_notes: Official PMID/DOI and complete normal abstract verified. Human PARG1 ZPH-dependent Rap2 interaction follows an initial worm two-hybrid screen; the fibroblast phenotype supports putative regulation, not a universal activation mechanism. Full original Methods remain unread.

title: Blood vessel tubulogenesis requires Rasip1 regulation of GTPase signaling.
review_notes: Official PMID/DOI and complete abstract verified. Actual normal XML-derived body was read for HUVEC 3D-matrix depletion, GTPase/ROCK/myosin and RhoA-rescue Results and complete main Experimental Procedures. Mouse MS1 affinity purification/colocalization and mouse Rasip1 knockout are distinguished from human ARHGAP29 depletion. Supplementary protocols and image pixels were not independently audited.

title: Expression and mutation analyses implicate ARHGAP29 as the etiologic gene for the cleft lip with or without cleft palate locus identified by genome-wide association on chromosome 1p22.
review_notes: Official PMID/DOI and complete abstract verified. Actual normal XML-derived expression, sample, sequencing and statistics Methods and target Results were read. Human rare-variant observations and mouse craniofacial/Irf6-expression experiments are distinct. Truncating alleles occur in unaffected relatives and aggregate associations do not survive the stated multiple-testing threshold; this early study alone does not establish complete penetrance or direct human IRF6 regulation.

title: KIF14 negatively regulates Rap1a-Radil signaling during breast cancer progression.
review_notes: Complete abstract and targeted PDZ interaction Results, figures and construct/MS Methods read. ARHGAP29-specific Figure3B pixels and TablesS1/S2 remain unread. No wrong-gene conclusion follows from the KIF14-centered narrative.

title: Rasip1 mediates Rap1 regulation of Rho in endothelial barrier function through ArhGAP29.
review_notes: Official PMID/DOI and complete normal abstract verified. Separately inspected primary target Results, Discussion and short main Methods describe A549-Epac1 and human endothelial assays. The authors could not consistently demonstrate reduced bulk Rho-GTP after Rap1 activation. Local signaling is proposed; detailed supplementary protocols remain unread. Normal recovery remains abstract-only despite a PMCID.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: Canonical abstract and partial body read; the separate recovered XML was consulted for the localization-screen Results and Methods. Existing cache retained. Target-specific Supplemental Table2 has not been read, so the historical microscopy assignment remains unverified.

title: Heart of glass anchors Rasip1 at endothelial cell-cell junctions to support vascular integrity.
review_notes: Actual cached target Results, Figure 3 supplement 3 and construct Methods were read. The reported coassociation is positive evidence; an unreported construct accession is not evidence against it. An isolated binary interface and exact stoichiometry were not established.

title: A novel GTPase-activating protein for Rho interacts with a PDZ domain of the protein-tyrosine phosphatase PTPL1.
review_notes: Official PubMed identifier/title and complete abstract independently verified. Normal cache is abstract-only. Targeted publisher-indexed GAP Results/Fig5 were read during source preparation; complete cloning/Methods were not recovered. UniProt associates the cloning record with human ARHGAP29.

title: RHOA GAPs stimulate RHOA GTPase activity
review_notes: Cached summary and current official human event identity/participant description read. ARHGAP29 is in the supported group; binding-only versus GAP-activity evidence is explicitly distinguished.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: Cached pathway summary and GDP/GTP-cycle regulator definitions read. The GAP role is explicit; not every participant, linked reaction or cited paper has been independently audited.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The pipeline is sound and IPR000198 genuinely matches this protein: ARHGAP36 has a structurally intact Rho-GAP fold. What the signature cannot see is that the fold has lost its catalytic residue, so the GO:0007165 it supplies is true of ARHGAP36 for reasons unrelated to the domain that triggered it. See the GO:0007165 row.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Actual PTHR12635 lineage inspected: Q6ZRI8 PTN002489201 descends from IBD PTN000973894 for all three rows. Catalytic loss is assessed separately from retained process/location; donor count and the existence of an ND placeholder do not refute IBA.

title: Arhgap36-dependent activation of Gli transcription factors.
review_notes: Full text retrieved from PMC4121843 on re-fetch with --force after an initial abstract-only cache. This is the founding functional paper for the gene and one of the two independent full-text sources for the arginine-finger loss. Its T246 numbering is mouse canonical numbering; that correspondence was not assumed but derived, and is shown in section 4 of the bioinformatics report.

title: Deciphering the Molecular and Functional Basis of RHOGAP Family Proteins: A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TOWARD SELECTIVE INACTIVATION OF RHO FAMILY PROTEINS.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only even after a forced re-fetch, so only the abstract is quoted. The body, read at PMC5034035, names ARHGAP36 first in its list of RHOGAP-domain proteins that lack an arginine finger, under the section heading "Not all RHOGAP Domain-containing Proteins Are GAPs", and states that the serine, threonine or glutamine found there cannot substitute for the arginine function. It also gives OCRL1 as the documented case of a RHOGAP-domain protein that binds GTP-bound RAC1 without stimulating hydrolysis, which is the precedent this review uses to keep the UniProt RAC1 interaction separate from the catalytic claim. That body text is deliberately not quoted as supporting_text because it is not in the cache.

title: Bimodal antagonism of PKA signalling by ARHGAP36.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The single most important reference for this gene's molecular function: it is the only one that measures an activity of ARHGAP36 on purified components, and it identifies the responsible domain as the N-terminal arginine-rich region rather than the Rho-GAP domain. Notably this paper does not discuss GAP activity at all; the same laboratory later published the systematic screen (PMID:32203420) that reported none.

title: Patched1-ArhGAP36-PKA-Inversin axis determines the ciliary translocation of Smoothened for Sonic Hedgehog pathway activation.
review_notes: Full text retrieved from PMC6338837. Important for two reasons that pull in different directions, and the review states both: it is independent confirmation that ARHGAP36 negatively regulates PKA, and it is the one paper in which ARHGAP36 restrains rather than promotes a Hedgehog pathway step, namely Smoothened ciliary translocation.

title: Critical roles of ARHGAP36 as a signal transduction mediator of Shh pathway in lateral motor columnar specification.
review_notes: Full text cached. Establishes the developmental context and an in vivo requirement, but the system is mouse spinal cord, so it informs the biology rather than supplying a human experimental annotation.

title: Systems analysis of RhoGEF and RhoGAP regulatory proteins reveals spatially organized RAC1 signalling from integrin adhesions.
review_notes: The primary source of the negative functional result on this gene: a systematic screen of RhoGEF and RhoGAP regulatory proteins, in which ARHGAP36 had no effect on RAC1, CDC42 or RHOA activity. The article is not open access -- Europe PMC returns no PMC id and isOpenAccess N -- so the cached record is abstract-only and no supporting_text is quoted from it anywhere in this review. The identity of PMID:33999959's reference [25] as this paper was verified against the PLOS bibliography rather than inferred. The supplementary workbook, however, is freely downloadable, and the result was read from it directly by ARHGAP36-bioinformatics/scan_muller_supplementary.py rather than taken on the citation. Supplementary Table 2, activity-screen columns: ARHGAP36 negative for RhoA, Rac1 and Cdc42, with ARHGAP35 and ARHGAP1 positive in the same run. Supplementary Table 1: the screened construct is human isoform 2, 517 aa, and the authors' own domain call is "GAP-like (arginine finger missing)". Those readings are recorded here and in the GO:0005096 reason rather than as supporting_text, because supporting_text is validated as a substring of the cached publication and a quote from a supplementary file could not be checked there. The findings above are attached to this reference and not to the bioinformatics report, because they are statements about what this paper contains. They carry no supporting_text for the reason just given. The re-derivation lives in ARHGAP36-bioinformatics/scan_muller_supplementary.py and its committed output muller2020_arhgap36.json. Listed HIGH because it is the decisive experiment, and flagged as one an ARHGAP36-titled literature search does not return: its title names RAC1 signalling at integrin adhesions.

title: Structure-activity mapping of ARHGAP36 reveals regulatory roles for its GAP homology and C-terminal domains.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Its citation [25], resolved against the journal's own bibliography at journals.plos.org (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0251684), is Muller et al. 2020 Nat Cell Biol, PMID:32203420. Recording that resolution matters because it is the only route from this review to the primary negative GAP result, whose own cached record is abstract-only.

title: Germline intergenic duplications at Xq26.1 underlie Bazex-Dupré-Christol basal cell carcinoma susceptibility syndrome.
review_notes: The only functional reference in the UniProt entry for this protein, and the source of UniProt's SUBUNIT line recording an interaction with the active form of RAC1 via the Rho-GAP domain on ECO:0000269. The cached record is abstract-only and the abstract does not mention RAC1, so that interaction is not quoted or relied on as evidence here; it is discussed in the GO:0005096 row only to state explicitly what the REMOVE does and does not cover. Not returned by the deep-research provider, whose title-based retrieval had no reason to surface a dermatology genetics paper.

title: Enhancer hijacking at the ARHGAP36 locus is associated with connective tissue to bone transformation.
review_notes: Full text cached. A misexpression phenotype rather than a statement about the normal function of the gene, so it informs the description but supports no annotation. An Author Correction exists, PMID:37813867.

title: Molecular and genetic characterization of sex-linked orange coat color in the domestic cat.
review_notes: Full text cached. The organism is the domestic cat, so it supplies no human annotation, but it is a useful third-party statement of how the field now reads the GAP domain and it shows the PKA relationship holding in a whole animal. Published version of the preprint the deep-research record cited without a PMID; the companion paper is PMID:40378840.

title: ARHGAP36 imposes a bifurcate activation of adherens junction and actomyosin to promote entosis.
review_notes: Main text remains subscription/PMC-embargoed. Read full PubMed abstract, accessible main images7/8, supplementary figures S6-S8 and the complete supplementary legend DOCX. These include actual actin-associated target imaging and target-depletion effects on polarized F-actin/pMLC2, reversing the earlier claim that no study places ARHGAP36 in the actin cytoskeleton. Source URLs, hashes and bounded observations are preserved in the primary-evidence note and project artifact. No inference of purified binary actin binding.

title: Mechanistic insights into transcriptional regulation of ARHGAP36 expression identify a factor predictive of neuroblastoma survival.
review_notes: Full text cached. Independent confirmation of the PKA-to-Hedgehog mechanism in a different system, and the clearest statement in the literature that the Smoothened-independence is a property of the ARHGAP36 route rather than an artefact of one assay. Published version of the preprint the deep-research record cited without a PMID.

title: ARHGAP36: the arginine finger UniProt annotates, and the residue that is there
review_notes: Generated by analyze_arhgap36.py in the same directory, which fetches everything live from UniProt, RCSB and PROSITE and has a --self-test asserting 16 propositions including two negative controls that must stay silent. The report states explicitly that a missing arginine finger is not on its own proof of inactivity, because the sibling ARHGAP11B analysis measured the converse, and the review's conclusion does not rest on it alone.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGAP36 (human)
review_notes: Full report reviewed. Its PKA, GLI and entosis narrative provides useful primary leads; its broad catalytic/transcription-regulator GO grounding is not direct evidence that ARHGAP36 catalyzes a protein reaction or acts at DNA. Coverage omissions and a provider self-score alone do not establish low scientific quality. Primary structural, catalytic-screen and new accessible entosis data determine the judgments.

title: ARHGAP36 primary figure, screen and PAINT evidence recheck
review_notes: Reviewer evidence record based on direct inspection of named public primary figures and supplementary materials; includes source URLs. Machine-readable project artifact preserves source hashes, actual target ancestry and current residue versions.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping behind the GO:0007165 IEA row. Correct as a rule, uninformative as an annotation; all seven RhoGAP comparators carry the same row.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The PAINT reference behind five IBA rows. Its node placements were checked against the PANTHER PAINT export for PTHR14166 rather than taken on trust.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Restates the curated UniProt Cytoplasm subcellular-location keyword.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence; one of only two experimental annotations on the human protein.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of intracellular localizations of expressed fusion proteins in living cells
review_notes: LIFEdb fusion-protein localisation; the other of the two experimental annotations on the human protein.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Source of six rows, every one of which projects a curated rat row traceable to PMID:12414125 or PMID:17804252. Verified by querying the donor accession directly; these are not free-floating electronic inferences.

title: Compound deletion of the rhoGAP C1 and V2 vasopressin receptor genes in a patient with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
review_notes: The single most informative human loss-of-function study on this gene, and the source of the redundancy hypothesis this review adopts. Affinage did not return it. Its negative result is unusually strong because the immunologic and hematologic testing was targeted at the tissue where ARHGAP4 is enriched rather than being a generic workup, and it spans 16 years.

title: Cloning of rat ARHGAP4/C1, a RhoGAP family member expressed in the nervous system that colocalizes with the Golgi complex and microtubules.
review_notes: The decisive biochemical paper, and it is about the RAT protein, which matters for every conclusion drawn from it. It produced four GO rows on rat Arhgap4 and none on human ARHGAP4; the human entry receives them by Ensembl Compara projection. Its title reports Golgi localisation, for which no GO annotation exists in any species. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Hem-1 complexes are essential for Rac activation, actin polymerization, and myosin regulation during neutrophil chemotaxis.
review_notes: Source of the GO:0005515 IPI with NCKAP1L and of the only UniProt SUBUNIT statement for this gene. The cached record is abstract-only and does not name ARHGAP4; the component list is in the full text, which is the normal situation for a proteomic inventory and is not a reason to doubt the annotation. Biologically the most interesting interaction on the gene, since it places a hematopoietic RhoGAP inside the machinery that activates RAC.

title: Severe combined immunodeficiency associated with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and a deletion in the Xq28 region.
review_notes: The most informative human loss-of-function datum for this gene, and a negative one. Affinage did not return it. It is the reason this review treats the absence of a phenotype as a finding rather than an absence of study.

title: ARHGAP4 is a novel RhoGAP that mediates inhibition of cell motility and axon outgrowth.
review_notes: The best structure-function work on this gene, and the source of three rat GO rows (GO:0010764 IMP, GO:0030517 IMP, GO:0030426 IDA) that reach human only by projection. Every result is gain-of-function. Cached record is abstract-only; PMC2111057 exists but the publisher does not release the text.

title: Immunological profile in a family with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus with a novel 11 kb deletion in AVPR2 and ARHGAP4 genes.
review_notes: Affinage did not return it. Its expression-profiling result is the only direct test of the compensation hypothesis proposed by PMID:10425039, and it refutes the transcriptional version of that hypothesis while leaving protein-level redundancy open. Both are cited in the knowledge gap rather than only the one that fits. Note that these patients retain roughly half of ARHGAP4, so the study bounds partial loss, not null.

title: A novel contiguous gene deletion of AVPR2 and ARHGAP4 genes in male dizygotic twins with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and intellectual disability.
review_notes: Affinage did not return it. Cited for its explicit statement that the field does not know what losing ARHGAP4 does, which is what makes the knowledge gap a gap rather than an absence of study. The intellectual disability in these twins is not attributable to ARHGAP4 on this evidence, since the deletion also removes AVPR2 and the cohort is two siblings.

title: ARHGAP4 mutated in a Chinese intellectually challenged family.
review_notes: A single-family exome study with no functional assay, whose candidate was selected by database filtering and SIFT. T491 lies outside the Rho-GAP domain (507-695). Recorded because it is one of only two ARHGAP4 variant reports in humans, not because it establishes a function. It produced no GO annotation.

title: Deciphering the Molecular and Functional Basis of RHOGAP Family Proteins: A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TOWARD SELECTIVE INACTIVATION OF RHO FAMILY PROTEINS.
review_notes: The family-level reference frame for every substrate claim in this review, and the source of the arginine-finger-less control set used in the bioinformatics. Affinage did not return it. Two things were checked in the PMC full text rather than assumed: ARHGAP4 appears exactly once, as entry 42 of Table 1 under its old name p115, so it is inside the 57 predicted-catalytic RHOGAPs but outside the 14 that were assayed; and the seven proteins reported to lack the arginine finger are ARHGAP36, ARAP2, DEPDC1, DEPDC1B, FAM13B, INPP5B and OCRL1. A web-search summary claiming this paper measured an ARHGAP4-R543K mutant by FRET is false and was not used.

title: ARHGAP4-SEPT2-SEPT9 complex enables both up- and down-modulation of integrin-mediated focal adhesions, cell migration, and invasion.
review_notes: The strongest interaction result in the ARHGAP4 literature, and fully uncurated: it produced no GO annotation on ARHGAP4, SEPT2 or SEPT9. Cited here as corroboration for the GO:0030336 IBA row and as a concrete instance of the coverage gap, not as the basis of any new annotation.

title: ARHGAP4 variants are associated with X-linked early-onset temporal lobe epilepsy.
review_notes: Indexed by PubMed as a Letter, and the PubMed record carries no abstract, so nothing beyond the title could be verified and no claim in this review rests on it. Recorded because it is the second of the two ARHGAP4 variant reports and because affinage did not return it. It produced no GO annotation. Assessing it would need the full text.

title: WITHDRAWN: ARHGAP4/ MYH9/ β-catenin/ c-Jun positive feedback loop regulates colorectal cancer stemness.
review_notes: Recorded as a citation hazard. The affinage deep-research record cites PMID:40817404, the republished version of this work in NPJ Precision Oncology, which is the correct identifier to use. This withdrawn version is flagged so that a later reviewer encountering either identifier knows the relationship. No claim in this review depends on the finding.

title: ARHGAP4/MYH9/β-catenin/c-Jun positive feedback loop promotes colorectal cancer stemness.
review_notes: The republished version of the work withdrawn as PMID:40553870, and the identifier a curator should use. Listed for that mapping and because affinage cites it. Like the other cancer papers it produced no GO annotation, and no claim in this review rests on it.

title: An X chromosome-linked gene encoding a protein with characteristics of a rhoGAP predominantly expressed in hematopoietic cells.
review_notes: The original human cloning paper and the source of all four TAS rows. Cached text is the abstract plus an abbreviated full text. No GAP assay is reported here; the GAP assignment is from sequence homology plus a stress-fibre phenotype, which is why the TAS rows carry less weight than the rat IDA.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: Basis of the GO:0051056 TAS row, which is the best-pitched process term on the gene.

title: RAC1 GAPs stimulate RAC1 GTPase activity
review_notes: The reaction name is itself the finding. Reactome commits to RAC1 as the substrate, a commitment GO:0005096 cannot carry, so the Reactome identifier is the only machine-readable place in GOA where the ARHGAP4 substrate is named.

title: ARHGAP4 bioinformatics analyses
review_notes: Seven rerunnable analyses committed alongside this review, each with a self-test that breaks its input or its anchor on purpose and requires every guard to fire, with negative controls that must stay silent. They supply the arginine-finger alignment against the PDB 1TX4 anchor, the cross-service GO merge check, the per-reference coverage counts, the WITH/FROM and PAINT-node resolution, the comparator check that refuted three of four candidate term replacements, the IMPC query that distinguishes a tested-and-clean knockout from an untested one, and an offline audit of this document (GOA row reconciliation, duplicate YAML keys, verbatimness of both PMID and file quotes, folded-hyphen damage, and reference completeness).

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGAP4 (human)
review_notes: The provider record used as the starting point. Its trust gates were clear (accession P98171, no non-human organism token, self-evaluation pairwise win, faith 100 percent) and its narrative is accurate as far as it goes, so the two statements cited from it are used as corroboration. It returned 11 citations and missed every human-genetics paper (PMID:16781893, PMID:18489790, PMID:10425039, PMID:22965914, PMID:26707211, PMID:39060771) and the family-wide RHOGAP kinetics survey (PMID:27481945), all of which were found instead by PubMed queries on the symbol and its synonyms. It also cites PMID:40817404 without noting that an earlier version of the same work was withdrawn. Its GO grounding was not imported.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. The domain assignment (IPR000198) is correct; the mapped term (signal transduction) is too general to inform.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA. The node's descendant evidence includes mouse Arhgap6's own IDA rows for the propagated terms, so the calls are experimentally anchored rather than inferred from similarity alone.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location keyword mapping; tracks the experimentally attributed Cytoplasm line in the UniProt record.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence. A real observation of a generic compartment.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog transfer from mouse O54834. Sound, and largely redundant with the IBA and ISS rows; the GO:1902533 row is the one case where it brings in a term the human record does not otherwise hold.

title: Functional analysis of ARHGAP6, a novel GTPase-activating protein for RhoA.
review_notes: The primary functional paper and the source of most of the experimental annotations. Verified against PubMed: Prakash et al., Hum Mol Genet 2000. Cached abstract only (full_text_available: false), so full-text-only details such as the focal adhesion measurement are accepted on the curator's authority rather than re-derived.

title: Expression in Escherichia coli of human ARHGAP6 gene and purification of His-tagged recombinant protein.
review_notes: A methods paper: expression of recombinant His-tagged ARHGAP6 isoform 4 in E. coli and its purification. It makes no functional claim, so no annotation follows from it. Cached because affinage's dated-findings table cites it; listed here so that decision is explicit.

title: Regulation of phospholipase C-delta1 by ARGHAP6, a GTPase-activating protein for RhoA: possible role for enhanced activity of phospholipase C in hypertension.
review_notes: The source of the three BHF-UCL phospholipase annotations that are in UniProt but not in current GOA. Verified against PubMed: Ochocka et al., Int J Biochem Cell Biol 2008. Note the title misspells the gene as ARGHAP6, which is why symbol-driven searches and the affinage report both miss it. Abstract only in cache; the quoted claims are all in the abstract.

title: Genetic screening in C. elegans identifies rho-GTPase activating protein 6 as novel HERG regulator.
review_notes: Independent evidence that an ARHGAP6 output is GAP-independent and PLC-dependent, and the source of the explicit R433G identification of the arginine finger. Full text available via PMC. Titled for HERG and for C. elegans, which is why it is absent from a EuropePMC title search on the gene symbol and from the affinage citation list.

title: Inhibitory effects of Arhgap6 on cervical carcinoma cells.
review_notes: Cited by Reactome R-HSA-9018806 as establishing RAC3-directed GAP activity for ARHGAP6. The paper itself reports a co-immunoprecipitation between Arhgap6 and Rac3 and never measures GTPase activity, so the GAP-activity reading is not supported by it. The paper is correctly cited as a Rac3 interaction; what is disputed is the inference drawn from it.

title: ARHGAP6 regulates the proliferation, migration and invasion of lung cancer cells.
review_notes: Tumour-suppressor phenotype in lung cancer cell lines: raising ARHGAP6 suppresses IL-6-induced migration and invasion and lowers phospho-STAT3. No annotation is proposed. The readouts are several steps downstream of anything ARHGAP6 does molecularly, they are cell-line phenotypes under manipulated expression, and STAT3 regulation is a consequence of altered RhoA/ROCK signalling rather than a distinct activity - the kind of indirect effect the repository guidance asks not to annotate.

title: Systems analysis of RhoGEF and RhoGAP regulatory proteins reveals spatially organized RAC1 signalling from integrin adhesions.
review_notes: Family-wide RhoGEF/RhoGAP substrate-specificity screen, cited by Reactome as its second source for ARHGAP6 as a RHOA GAP. Abstract only in cache, so it is cited here for the existence and scope of the screen rather than for a per-protein result.

title: ARHGAP6 Promotes Apoptosis and Inhibits Glycolysis in Lung Adenocarcinoma Through STAT3 Signaling Pathway.
review_notes: Same family of claims as PMID:30816546 in DDP-resistant lung adenocarcinoma: apoptosis, glycolysis and cisplatin sensitivity, all attributed to STAT3. Full text is cached. No annotation proposed, for the same reason - these are downstream cellular phenotypes of a manipulated expression level, not molecular functions or direct processes.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Quantitative fragmentomics/holdup assay; the single source of all 22 GO:0005515 rows. A PDZ-directed assay by design, so the all-PDZ partner list reflects the method as much as ARHGAP6's selectivity - which is a reason to treat the rows as one determinant, not to doubt them.

title: ARHGAP6 Suppresses Breast Cancer Tumor Growth by Promoting Ferroptosis via RhoA-ROCK1-p38 MAPK Signaling.
review_notes: Ferroptosis in breast cancer cells, placed downstream of RhoA-ROCK1-p38 MAPK. Consistent with ARHGAP6 being a RhoA GAP, and that consistency is worth noting, but ferroptosis is three signalling steps removed from the GAP activity and is measured only under manipulated expression in cell lines. No annotation proposed.

title: Cloning and characterization of a novel rho-type GTPase-activating protein gene (ARHGAP6) from the critical region for microphthalmia with linear skin defects.
review_notes: Original cloning and characterisation from the MLS critical region. Establishes the gene, the rhoGAP domain and alternative splicing; the functional claims that GO records from it were confirmed later by PMID:10699171.

title: RHOA GAPs stimulate RHOA GTPase activity
review_notes: Places ARHGAP6 among the RHOA GAPs on two citations, PMID:10699171 and PMID:32203420. Well grounded.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: RHO GTPase cycle; a generic parent process.

title: RAC3 GAPs stimulate RAC3 GTPase activity
review_notes: Places ARHGAP6 in the tier of GAPs shown to stimulate RAC3 GTPase activity, citing only PMID:26628301, which shows binding and not catalysis. The GO term it produces is still true of ARHGAP6 for a different substrate, so the row is kept; the pathway assertion behind it is what is disputed.

title: ARHGAP6 bioinformatics: what PMID:36115835 measured, per partner
review_notes: Generated by the committed check_binding_evidence.py, which reads IntAct's curated record of PMID:36115835 for each GOA partner and reports the PSI-MI detection method and interaction type. It refuses to report when zero partners match, because an earlier version read the wrong id field and returned a clean-looking zero that would have been mistaken for an absence of evidence. Quotes taken from it here were grep-verified verbatim and exactly once.

title: ARHGAP6 bioinformatics: UniProt vs GOA, and what depends on the gap
review_notes: Generated by the committed check_goa_uniprot_divergence.py. Obsolescence is checked against two independent services and a disagreement would be reported rather than resolved. Quotes taken from it here were grep-verified verbatim and exactly once.

title: ARHGAP6 bioinformatics: are the `protein binding` rows many findings or one?
review_notes: Generated by the committed check_pdz_interactome.py. Partner accessions and both row counts are parsed from the repository's own GOA TSV rather than hardcoded. Quotes taken from it here were grep-verified verbatim and exactly once.

title: ARHGAP6 bioinformatics: the RhoGAP catalytic arginine finger, with controls
review_notes: Generated by the committed check_arginine_finger.py in this gene's bioinformatics folder; regenerate with `uv run check_arginine_finger.py`. The anchor position is verified against PDB 1TX4 rather than asserted, and the script exits non-zero rather than reporting an unverifiable number. Every supporting_text quoted from it here was grep-verified as a verbatim, exactly-once match - CI checks supporting_text only for PMID references, so file: quotes are otherwise unchecked.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGAP6 (human)
review_notes: Affinage deep-research record. Trust gates clear: accession O43182 matches the local UniProt file, organism human, self_evaluation_pairwise win, faith_pct 100. Its narrative is accurate and it correctly foregrounds the separability of the GAP and actin arms. Its weakness is recall, not accuracy: its 11-PMID citation list omits PMID:18434237 and PMID:19038263, the two papers carrying the most GO-relevant experimental content, and both are omitted for the same reason - neither title names the gene in a searchable form (18434237 misspells it ARGHAP6, 19038263 spells it out and leads with HERG and C. elegans). Cited here only for the separability framing, which it states plainly.

title: UniProtKB entry O43182 (RHG06_HUMAN)
review_notes: The machine-fetched UniProtKB record for O43182 (entry version 202, sequence version 3), not edited. Used for the Rho-GAP domain bounds, the arginine-finger SITE, the SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line and the C-terminal sequence. The quote used here was grep-verified as a verbatim single-line match.

title: EphA4-mediated Rho activation via Vsm-RhoGEF expressed specifically in vascular smooth muscle cells.
review_notes: The founding paper and the source of the human GO:0005085 IDA and the EPHA4 IPI. Cache is abstract-only, so the quoted evidence here is from the abstract; the curated IDA rests on the full text. Its VSMC-specificity claim is contradicted in mouse retina by PMID:23029280 and that is recorded rather than resolved.

title: EphB-mediated degradation of the RhoA GEF Ephexin5 relieves a developmental brake on excitatory synapse formation.
review_notes: Not returned by affinage; found by searching the alias Ephexin5. It is the experimental basis of mouse Arhgef15 GO:0005085 IDA and GO:2000297 IMP, and therefore of every ISS and Ensembl row in the human record that cites UniProtKB:Q5FWH6. Full text available. Its RhoA-specificity conclusion is superseded on the CDC42 half by PMID:40138406 and PMID:32203420, which is recorded in the review rather than treated as an error.

title: Arhgef15 promotes retinal angiogenesis by mediating VEGF-induced Cdc42 activation and potentiating RhoJ inactivation in endothelial cells.
review_notes: Full text available. The CDC42 result includes a knockdown in human HUVECs, so it is not a mouse-only observation. Also the source of the endothelial-specific expression claim that conflicts with PMID:12775584; both are reported here with their systems attached.

title: Exome sequencing reveals new causal mutations in children with epileptic encephalopathies.
review_notes: Absent from GOA but present in UniProt's reference list. Contains a G-LISA RhoA activation assay on the human protein comparing wild type with R604C, which is one of only three direct measurements of human ARHGEF15 exchange activity, alongside PMID:12775584 and PMID:32203420. Relevance is MEDIUM not HIGH because the epilepsy association itself is a single de novo variant of uncertain significance; the assay is what matters.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid interactome screen. Correctly cited for the interactions it reports; it attaches no biology to any of them for this gene.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Isoform-resolved two-hybrid screen; same status as the other interactome papers.

title: ARHGEF15 overexpression worsens the prognosis in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma through enhancing the motility and proliferative activity of the cancer cells.
review_notes: Cited here only because Reactome lists it alongside PMID:32203420 as evidence for ARHGEF15 in its RHOA and CDC42 GEF reactions. The findings are about overexpression in tumour cells and support no GO annotation in this review.

title: A dual role for the RhoGEF Ephexin5 in regulation of dendritic spine outgrowth.
review_notes: Not returned by affinage. It is the experimental basis of the mouse GO:0150052, GO:0098794 and GO:0098978 rows that Ensembl Compara projects into human, so the human IEA rows are traceable to a real mouse experiment. Full text available.

title: Systems analysis of RhoGEF and RhoGAP regulatory proteins reveals spatially organized RAC1 signalling from integrin adhesions.
review_notes: A family-wide substrate-specificity screen of all 145 human RhoGEFs and RhoGAPs, and the source Reactome cites for ARHGEF15 in both its RHOA and CDC42 GEF reactions. It is absent from ARHGEF15's GOA. The cached record is abstract-only and the article is paywalled, but the supplementary tables are free; Supplementary Table 2 row 85 reads RhoA plus, Rac1 minus, Cdc42 plus and is extracted reproducibly by ARHGEF15-bioinformatics/muller2020_specificity.py. The screen's library entry for this gene is the human protein at its full 841 residues. The column mapping is corroborated by six textbook-specificity read-controls read from the same columns, of which five recover their expected GTPase and ITSN1 recovers nothing; that failure is retained rather than dropped, because it is what establishes that a minus in this table means not detected rather than does not act.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Correctly cited; no mechanism attached for this gene.

title: Mutations in ARHGEF15 cause autosomal dominant hereditary cerebral small vessel disease and osteoporotic fracture.
review_notes: Source of the human GO:0005085, GO:0032956 and GO:0035025 IMP rows and of the BSVD5 disease association. Cache is abstract-only; UniProt's statement that the protein does not activate RAC1 or CDC42 comes from the full text and is not second-guessed here, although it is in tension with PMID:32203420 and PMID:40138406 on the CDC42 half.

title: Activity-dependent regulation of Cdc42 by Ephexin5 drives synapse growth and stabilization.
review_notes: Not returned by affinage. It revises the RhoA-only substrate claim of PMID:21029865 in the same system and identifies phosphorylation of the EphB2 site Y361, human Y353, as the selectivity switch. Full text available. Mouse brain, so it informs but does not establish the human substrate range on its own.

title: RHOA GEFs activate RHOA
review_notes: Cached Reactome entry. Its ARHGEF15 entry cites Fukushima et al. 2016 (PMID:27145964) and Mueller et al. 2020 (PMID:32203420); following that citation is how the family-wide specificity screen was found.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: A pathway-membership statement at the level of the whole RHO cycle; it adds no substrate-level information.

title: CDC42 GEFs activate CDC42
review_notes: Cached Reactome entry. ARHGEF15 is in its confirmed list, not its candidate list, on the same two citations as R-HSA-8980691. This is the only place in the entire GO record where CDC42 is named for this gene.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGEF15 (human)
review_notes: Trust gates clear, 11 citations, self-evaluation win. The gates are a precision statement and not a recall one: the record missed PMID:21029865, PMID:40138406, PMID:28185854 and PMID:32203420, which between them decide the substrate question and ground every mouse-derived row in the GO record. What it did contribute, and nothing else surfaced, is the endothelial CDC42 and RhoJ literature. Its mechanism_profile carries no molecular-activity or localization GO grounding, so nothing was imported from it; the one sentence quoted below is attached to a claim that PMID:23029280 independently establishes in the same block.

title: Comprehensive proteomic analysis of interphase and mitotic 14-3-3-binding proteins.
review_notes: Systematic 14-3-3 interactome; ARHGEF16 appears as one of many 14-3-3-zeta partners. Supports retyping the generic protein-binding row to GO:0071889, nothing more.

title: Targeted proteomic analysis of 14-3-3 sigma, a p53 effector commonly silenced in cancer.
review_notes: 14-3-3 sigma (SFN) interactome screen. Same status as the other 14-3-3 references.

title: Analogues of Y27632 increase gap junction communication and suppress the formation of transformed NIH3T3 colonies.
review_notes: A ROCK-inhibitor pharmacology paper in which ARHGEF16-transformed NIH3T3 cells are used as a model; the cached full text names ARHGEF16 twice and identifies it as a Tip-1 partner in work then unpublished. Cited by the affinage report and verified here as genuinely about this protein, but it is a tool-compound study and supports no GO term for the gene product.

title: Ephexin4 and EphA2 mediate cell migration through a RhoG-dependent mechanism.
review_notes: The decisive paper for this gene, and the source of 8 of its 12 experimental GO rows. Establishes RhoG as the exchange substrate on purified DH-PH protein and reports the Rac1, Cdc42 and RhoA negatives with Dock180, Zizimin1 and Ephexin1 as positive controls. Full text retrieved from PMC2922637 and all quotations checked against it. Notably absent from the affinage deep-research record, whose retrieval is keyed on the symbol while this title says Ephexin4.

title: The HPV16 E6 binding protein Tip-1 interacts with ARHGEF16, which activates Cdc42.
review_notes: Correctly cited and the source of four GO rows, including the TAX1BP3 PDZ interaction which is sound. Marked DISPUTED for its Cdc42 arm alone: PMID:20679435 reports no cellular Cdc42 activation and no binding to nucleotide-free Cdc42 in HEK293T cells, with Zizimin1 as positive control. The two reconcile if Cdc42 activation is conditional on Tip-1 and HPV16 E6, which is how this review treats it. Separately, the GO:0005096 molecular function drawn from this paper is a term-choice error on GOA's side, not a defect of the paper, which calls ARHGEF16 a GEF throughout. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Ephexin4 and EphA2 mediate resistance to anoikis through RhoG and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase.
review_notes: Knockdown plus rescue in HeLa cells establishing anoikis suppression through RhoG, PI3K and Akt. Basis for the proposed NEW annotation to GO:2000811. Abstract-only in the cache; the quotation used is from the abstract. Not retrieved by affinage.

title: Ephexin4-mediated promotion of cell migration and anoikis resistance is regulated by serine 897 phosphorylation of EphA2.
review_notes: Places Ephexin4 on the ligand-independent, Akt-driven arm of EphA2 signalling and corroborates the anoikis role through an orthogonal perturbation of the receptor rather than of ARHGEF16. Full text available. Not retrieved by affinage.

title: Arhgef16, a novel Elmo1 binding partner, promotes clearance of apoptotic cells via RhoG-dependent Rac1 activation.
review_notes: Establishes efferocytosis for the MOUSE protein: murine Arhgef16 expressed in LR73 phagocytes, synergistic with Elmo1, abolished without it, RhoG-dependent and Dock1-independent. Relevant to human ARHGEF16 only by orthology, which is why this review records it as a curation gap on mouse rather than proposing a human annotation. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Binary yeast two-hybrid interactome. Contributes three generic protein-binding rows with no mechanistic follow-up for this gene.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: Affinity pulldown of E-cadherin complexes, which reports co-purification rather than direct contact. Basis for the cadherin-binding row, which this review marks over-annotated because the method cannot separate direct binding from capture via the junctional PDZ scaffolds ARHGEF16 does bind.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex-style affinity-purification interactome; contributes one 14-3-3 row.

title: Intermolecular steric inhibition of Ephexin4 is relieved by Elmo1.
review_notes: Mechanism of the N-terminal autoinhibitory mode: the SH3 domain of one Ephexin4 molecule occludes the N20 region of another, and Elmo1 competes it off, making the protein accessible to RhoG. Gives the ELMO interaction a regulatory meaning that GO:0005515 cannot express. Not retrieved by affinage.

title: Proteome-wide analysis of phospho-regulated PDZ domain interactions.
review_notes: PDZ-domain interaction screen; two of the 42 rows retyped to GO:0030165.

title: GLI2 promotes cell proliferation and migration through transcriptional activation of ARHGEF16 in human glioma cells.
review_notes: ARHGEF16 as a GLI2 transcriptional target promoting glioma migration and proliferation via CKAP5. Genuinely about this gene, but it is expression-level and disease-context biology and supports no GO process term for the gene product itself.

title: The Intermolecular Interaction of Ephexin4 Leads to Autoinhibition by Impeding Binding of RhoG.
review_notes: Defines the autoinhibition interface by point mutation and states plainly that Ephexin4 acts on RhoG rather than RhoA, unlike its siblings. Important caveat recorded in the review: the mutants are MURINE (methods cite cDNA NM_001112744, UniProt Q3U5C8, 713 aa), so the published E295A is human E291A - human position 295 is a serine. Not retrieved by affinage.

title: Emerging Roles of Ephexins in Physiology and Disease.
review_notes: Family review; useful for keeping the five ephexins apart, which is the standing confusion risk for this gene. Secondary literature, used for orientation rather than as evidence.

title: Systems analysis of RhoGEF and RhoGAP regulatory proteins reveals spatially organized RAC1 signalling from integrin adhesions.
review_notes: Systematic RhoGEF/RhoGAP interaction and localisation survey. The three ARHGEF16 rows it contributes are PDZ-scaffold partners reported in supplementary data; the cached text does not name ARHGEF16 directly.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Four generic protein-binding rows whose partners carry no PDZ domain, so they cannot be attributed to the C-terminal motif and remain uninformative.

title: FYN is required for ARHGEF16 to promote proliferation and migration in colon cancer cells.
review_notes: FYN as an ARHGEF16 partner required for its proliferative and migratory effects in colon cancer. Genuinely about this gene; disease-context, and the effect on ARHGEF16 protein levels makes the epistasis hard to read as a direct molecular function.

title: Double inhibition and activation mechanisms of Ephexin family RhoGEFs.
review_notes: Crystal structures of partially and fully autoinhibited Ephexin4, establishing two independent inhibitory modes and their relief by N-terminal tyrosine phosphorylation and by PDZ-protein binding to the C-terminal motif. This is what converts the PDZ rows from incidental interactions into a regulatory switch. Abstract-only in the cache (PNAS restricts full-text access through PMC); quotations are from the abstract. Not retrieved by affinage.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0; contributes one 14-3-3-zeta row.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Holdup-based PDZ-domain affinity mapping, and the single largest contributor to this gene's GO record: 37 of the 77 GOA rows. All 37 partners carry PDZ domains and bind one C-terminal motif, so the set reports one determinant measured 37 times rather than 37 findings.

title: A central chaperone-like role for 14-3-3 proteins in human cells.
review_notes: 14-3-3 interactome; three rows, all retyped to GO:0071889.

title: ARHGEF16 expression correlates with proliferation, migration and invasion of colon cancer cells.
review_notes: Expression-correlation study in colon cancer. Named in the review for completeness of the disease literature; supports no annotation.

title: Phosphorylation of Ephexin4 at Ser-41 contributes to chromosome alignment via RhoG activation in cell division.
review_notes: Knockdown, rescue and a phospho-mimic allele in human HeLa and A549 cells, linking Ephexin4 to metaphase chromosome alignment through cortical RhoG. Ser41 is already a UniProt-annotated phosphosite from two independent mass-spectrometry studies. No GO annotation resulted; this review records it as a curation gap rather than proposing a process term, because the entity that positions chromosomes is not this one. Not retrieved by affinage.

title: p75NTR indirectly activates RAC and Cdc42 via a guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor
review_notes: Source of one cytosol TAS row. DISPUTED rather than MISCITED, because the claim GOA actually draws from this reaction is GO:0005829 cytosol and that claim is correctly supported; what is contested is the reaction's own set-level GTPase output, which never reaches GOA. ARHGEF16 is one of 52 protein participants in a set-level GEF catalyst whose asserted outputs are Rac and Cdc42 - both of which PMID:20679435 specifically failed to detect for Ephexin4 in cells, with Dock180 and Zizimin1 as positive controls.

title: GEFs activate RhoA,B,C
review_notes: Source of the other cytosol TAS row, and DISPUTED for the same reason as R-HSA-205039: the cytosol claim it supports is fine, the substrate claim it makes is contested and never reaches GOA. The catalyst is a 54-participant DefinedSet of Dbl-family GEFs assembled by domain rather than by measured specificity - it contains TIAM1 and TIAM2 (Rac-only), FGD1-FGD4 and ITSN1 (Cdc42-only), SOS1, SOS2 and RASGRF2 (Ras), and all five ephexins - and its output is RHOA/B/C:GTP. PMID:20679435 could not detect RhoA activation by Ephexin4.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGEF16 (human)
review_notes: Machine-fetched provider record; trust gates clear, self_evaluation_pairwise win, faith_pct 100.0, and all six of its citations verified here as genuinely about this protein - so nothing in it is miscited, and MISCITED would say something the rest of this note disclaims.
