LOW_QUALITY instead, for a methodological reason: its retrieval is keyed on the symbol ARHGEF16 and so returned none of the seven mechanistic papers whose titles say Ephexin4, including PMID:20679435, the source of 8 of the gene's 12 experimental GO rows. Working from that incomplete base it names direct exchange on Cdc42 as this protein's core biochemical activity and never mentions RhoG, its actual substrate. Its non-literature grounding is also coarse: molecular_activity GO:0098772 molecular function regulator activity, pathway R-HSA-162582 Signal Transduction, no localization. A useful first pass on the disease and partner literature; not usable as the basis for the molecular function.

title: Identification and characterization of a novel Rho-specific guanine nucleotide exchange factor.
review_notes: The founding paper for this gene and the source of UniProt's p114-Rho-GEF AltName and of its FUNCTION statement. Verified against PubMed and the cached abstract. It produced zero GO annotations in any species, and the automated deep-research provider did not return it, because its title names the function rather than the gene.

title: G Protein betagamma subunits stimulate p114RhoGEF, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for RhoA and Rac1: regulation of cell shape and reactive oxygen species production.
review_notes: Correctly cited and it is the source of the gene's only curated molecular-function annotation, but its Rac1 conclusion is contradicted by the purified-protein experiment in PMID:11085924 and by the depletion experiment in PMID:21258369. Marked DISPUTED for that reason, not for any citation defect. No free full text was found, so the assessment rests on the abstract plus the two contradicting papers.

title: Cytoskeletal modification of Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factor activity: identification of a Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factor as a binding partner for Sept9b, a mammalian septin.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. Missed by the automated provider because the title names the partner rather than the gene, even though it is in UniProt's own RN list and supplies one of the gene's two alternative names. Abstract only; no free route to the full text was found.

title: Proteomic analysis of exosomes from human neural stem cells by flow field-flow fractionation and nanoflow liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.
review_notes: A bulk exosome proteomics survey contributing 66 GO annotations, one of them the extracellular exosome row on this gene. Correctly cited; the issue is what a single mass-spectrometry identification licenses, not whether the citation is right.

title: Involvement of p114-RhoGEF and Lfc in Wnt-3a- and dishevelled-induced RhoA activation and neurite retraction in N1E-115 mouse neuroblastoma cells.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed, full text available. Places ARHGEF18 downstream of Wnt planar-cell-polarity signalling in a neuronal cell line, one of the few contexts outside junction assembly. Produced zero GO annotations in any species. Not used as the basis of any annotation action here, because the only rows it could support are process terms with no existing counterpart in this gene's record.

title: Spatially restricted activation of RhoA signalling at epithelial junctions by p114RhoGEF drives junction formation and morphogenesis.
review_notes: The paper that defines this gene's central cell-biological role, with full text available. Verified against PubMed. It has produced no GO annotation in any species, which is the single largest gap in this gene's record, and it is the source of the three annotations proposed here as NEW.

title: Lulu2 regulates the circumferential actomyosin tensile system in epithelial cells through p114RhoGEF.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed; abstract only in the cache but the abstract carries both load-bearing claims. Source of the apical plasma membrane EXP and apical part of cell IDA rows.

title: Stimulation of cortical myosin phosphorylation by p114RhoGEF drives cell migration and tumor cell invasion.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed, full text available. Produced zero GO annotations in any species; a candidate source for cell-migration process terms that this review does not propose because no existing GOA row covers the area.

title: Activated RhoA is a positive feedback regulator of the Lbc family of Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factor proteins.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. The abstract states the finding at family level and does not name p114RhoGEF, so the gene-specific claim in this review is anchored on the companion structure paper PMID:29876405, which names it explicitly and deposits the coordinates. Missed by the automated provider because the title names the family.

title: LKB1 controls human bronchial epithelial morphogenesis through p114RhoGEF-dependent RhoA activation.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed; abstract only, but the abstract carries the claim. Adds a third independent epithelial system, bronchial, to the junction assembly role. Produced zero GO annotations in any species.

title: ArhGEF18 regulates RhoA-Rock2 signaling to maintain neuro-epithelial apico-basal polarity and proliferation.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed; abstract only. A whole-organism loss-of-function study with a human rescue, and it has produced no GO annotation in any species, including on the medaka gene.

title: ZO-1 controls endothelial adherens junctions, cell-cell tension, angiogenesis, and barrier formation.
review_notes: Title names ZO-1, not ARHGEF18, but the full text contains substantial p114RhoGEF experiments and the ARUK-UCL curator clearly read them; all three GOA rows derived from it check out against the cached full text.

title: CRB3A Controls the Morphology and Cohesion of Cancer Cells through Ehm2/p114RhoGEF-Dependent Signaling.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed; abstract only. Adds the Crumbs polarity module to the list of tissue-specific recruitment mechanisms, and pairs with the Drosophila result that the Crumbs complex recruits Cysts. Produced zero GO annotations in any species.

title: p114RhoGEF governs cell motility and lumen formation during tubulogenesis through a ROCK-myosin-II pathway.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed; abstract only. A stage-specific requirement, which is why it is useful for separating junction assembly from junction maintenance in the suggested experiments. Produced zero GO annotations in any species.

title: Biallelic Mutation of ARHGEF18, Involved in the Determination of Epithelial Apicobasal Polarity, Causes Adult-Onset Retinal Degeneration.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. The disease finding itself licenses no GO term, but the variant characterisation supports the direction of the process annotation. Abstract only in the cache, and it produced zero GO annotations in any species.

title: The FERM protein EPB41L5 regulates actomyosin contractility and focal adhesion formation to maintain the kidney filtration barrier.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed. Extends the FERM-protein recruitment mechanism from EPB41L4B in epithelium to EPB41L5 in podocytes. Note that the abstract spells the gene ARGHEF18, which is why symbol-based retrieval misses it; the quoted text preserves the misspelling because it is verbatim.

title: Expression of novel "LOCGEF" isoforms of ARHGEF18 in eosinophils.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed, full text available. Defines the five UniProt isoforms and the only localisation evidence outside epithelium and endothelium. The p114 isoform is not detected in eosinophils, so the junctional mechanism cannot be assumed to apply there.

title: Crystal structures of the PH domains from Lbc family of RhoGEFs bound to activated RhoA GTPase.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed; open access, full text and coordinates freely available. Missed by the automated provider because the title names the family. It has produced zero GO annotations in any species, so the only structural information about this gene is absent from its GO record.

title: A Gα12-specific Binding Domain in AKAP-Lbc and p114RhoGEF.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed, full text available. The second heterotrimeric G protein input to this gene alongside the G beta-gamma stimulation in PMID:14512443. Produced zero GO annotations in any species.

title: Apical polarity proteins recruit the RhoGEF Cysts to promote junctional myosin assembly.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed, full text available. Establishes the orthology that underwrites this gene's exchange-factor IBD. Missed by the automated provider because the title names the fly gene.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: A high-throughput interactome contributing 2876 GO annotations, one of them the AKAP13 protein binding row on this gene. Correctly cited; the limitation is what a single untargeted interaction licenses.

title: Septin-mediated RhoA activation engages the exocyst complex to recruit the cilium transition zone.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed, full text available. The open-access precursor to the 2025 mitochondrial-fission study, and the paper that turns the septin interaction from a single 2005 result into a reproducible one. Missed by the automated provider because the title names the partner. Produced zero GO annotations in any species.

title: Roles of protein-protein interactions and monolayer mechanics in tricellulin localization to tricellular tight junctions.
review_notes: Not about ARHGEF18. Cited only to decide the granularity of the proposed tight-junction compartment term, which is why it is marked LOW relevance to this gene. Identifier verified against PubMed by esummary (Biology Open, 15 Sep 2025) and the full text is cached. Reading it changed the claim it was cited for, which is the reason it is in references rather than left as free-text prose. The first draft said occludin is not confined to bicellular junctions; the paper is more equivocal, since occludin is in proximity to tricellulin and required for its localisation at tricellular junctions but is not itself enriched there. The term choice does not depend on this, resting instead on the resolution limits of the imaging.

title: p75NTR indirectly activates RAC and Cdc42 via a guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor
review_notes: ARHGEF18 is returned among this reaction's participants only as a member of a generic GEFs catalyst set. The reaction's declared substrate is RAC1 and its name additionally invokes Cdc42, which every primary source agrees ARHGEF18 does not act on. Recorded as miscited in the sense that the protein is placed in a reaction it has not been shown to catalyse; the cytosol annotation derived from it is kept as non-core because a cytosolic pool is independently real.

title: Disassembly of tight junctions
review_notes: ARHGEF18 participates as a component of Reactome's Tight Junction Complex entity. The junctional localisation is independently true; the row is a participant-compartment assignment rather than an observation.

title: SMURF1 binds phosphorylated PARD6A
review_notes: Same participant-compartment mechanism as the other Reactome cell-junction rows.

title: SMURF1 ubiquitinates RHOA
review_notes: Same participant-compartment mechanism. RHOA appears here as the SMURF1 substrate, not as this protein's exchange substrate.

title: GEFs activate RhoA,B,C
review_notes: The biologically apt Reactome reaction for this gene, with RhoA, RhoB and RhoC bound to GDP as input and bound to GTP as output. ARHGEF18 still enters it as a member of a generic GEFs set rather than as a named catalyst.

title: TGFBR1 is recruited to tight junction by binding Pard6a
review_notes: An inferred, non-species-specific event; same participant-compartment mechanism as the R-HSA rows.

title: TGFBR2 is recruited to tight junctions-associated, Pard6a-bound, TGFBR1 after TGF-beta stimulation
review_notes: An inferred, non-species-specific event; same participant-compartment mechanism.

title: TGFBR2 phosphorylates Pard6a
review_notes: An inferred, non-species-specific event; same participant-compartment mechanism.

title: ARHGEF18 (p114RhoGEF) bioinformatics
review_notes: Reproducible analysis committed alongside this review. Resolves the two published loss-of-function substitutions onto the current canonical sequence (Thr-458, Tyr-606), shows that the conserved Dbl tyrosine is pan-family and therefore uninformative about substrate, validates a structure-anchored substrate classifier at 8 of 8 on held-out proteins and then shows why its ARHGEF18 answer should not be pushed, and maps the ten RhoA-contacting PH residues of PDB 6BCB onto the human protein. Both scripts carry self-tests with positive and negative controls, all passing.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGEF18 (human)
review_notes: Blocking trust gates passed (accession Q6ZSZ5, human), but the soft gate tripped. Affinage's own head-to-head self-evaluation scored this record as a tie rather than a win against the curated UniProt reference. Precision was good, since every PMID it returned resolves to a real paper about this gene, and the three identifiers checked most closely (20810787, 23648482, 26483385) match the papers it described. Recall was the problem. It missed the founding biochemistry (PMID:11085924), the paper that named the protein SA-RhoGEF (PMID:15558029), the only structure of the protein (PMID:29876405), the family-level positive-feedback study (PMID:23493395), the podocyte recruitment mechanism (PMID:28536193), the open-access septin precursor (PMID:36912772) and the Drosophila ortholog work (PMID:31409654). It also states the substrate as RhoA and Rac1 citing only PMID:14512443, without the contradicting purified-protein result.

title: WGEF is a novel RhoGEF expressed in intestine, liver, heart, and kidney.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Wang et al., Biochem Biophys Res Commun 324:1053-8 (2004), and independently corroborated as the ARHGEF19 evidence cited by Reactome R-HSA-8980691. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because its substrate claim is contradicted by the later side-by-side retest in PMID:18256687, not because the citation is wrong. Cached as abstract only; the full text was not consulted.

title: WGEF activates Rho in the Wnt-PCP pathway and controls convergent extension in Xenopus gastrulation.
review_notes: The single most important paper on this gene, and the one the review's molecular-function conclusion rests on. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC2262038); full text cached and read. Anchored independently to a checkable fact: it is the GOA reference for the existing GO:0005515 IPI with UniProtKB:P61586, and the RhoA co-precipitation it describes is exactly what that IPI records. Note that the human-specific experiments (Figs 2A-C, 5B-D, 6) are substantial despite the Xenopus-forward title.

title: Role of the C-terminal SH3 domain and N-terminal tyrosine phosphorylation in regulation of Tim and related Dbl-family proteins.
review_notes: Retrieval note worth recording: this paper is titled for Tim, a paralogue, and is returned by no ARHGEF19 query - it surfaces only on a WGEF search. It is nevertheless one of only two studies that assay Wgef autoinhibition biochemically, and it is the source later work cites for the human Y295E phosphomimetic being autoinhibition-free. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC2655348); cached as abstract only, so both quotes are taken from the abstract and no figure-level claim is made from it.

title: Epigenetic regulation of adipocyte differentiation by a Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factor, WGEF.
review_notes: Mouse 3T3-L1 only, and no human counterpart has been reported, so it informs the gene's regulation rather than supporting any human annotation. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC2686168); full text cached. Listed here chiefly because it is one of the eleven primary papers that have produced no GO annotation in any species.

title: Epidermal wound repair is regulated by the planar cell polarity signaling pathway.
review_notes: The source of both the human IGI (GO:0032956 with GRHL3) and, via mouse Arhgef19, of the human wound-healing IBA. Anchored to a checkable fact: MGI:1925912, the sole gene-product donor on the IBA row, resolves at MGI to mouse Arhgef19 itself, whose IMP for GO:0042060 comes from this paper. A correction worth recording for anyone who works from the cache: this entry was originally cached abstract-only, and on that basis an earlier revision of this review stated that no human wound-healing experiment on ARHGEF19 existed. The abstract says "keratinocytes" without a species and the paper is framed around mouse genetics, so the inference was natural and wrong - the full text, re-fetched from PMC2965174 and now cached, names the line as human HaCaT and carries a knockdown-with-rescue scratch assay. Every quote used here is from the cached full text. Note the published erratum adding an author, which does not affect any content used.

title: Involvement of p114-RhoGEF and Lfc in Wnt-3a- and dishevelled-induced RhoA activation and neurite retraction in N1E-115 mouse neuroblastoma cells.
review_notes: The only published negative result on this gene, and a well-controlled one. It is mouse neuroblastoma, so it cannot license a human NOT annotation, but it does establish that the Wnt-Dishevelled-RhoA role is context-dependent rather than universal. PubMed- and PMC-verified; full text cached and read.

title: Grhl3 and GEF19 in the front rho.
review_notes: Secondary commentary, carrying no new data, and cited here for one reason: its title spells the gene "GEF19", so no ARHGEF19 or WGEF PubMed query returns it. It is recorded as a retrieval blind spot for anyone re-running literature discovery on this gene. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC3116594); cached as abstract only.

title: Pronephric tubulogenesis requires Daam1-mediated planar cell polarity signaling.
review_notes: Amphibian and fish only; supports the developmental role of the Daam1-WGEF-Rho module but provides no human or mammalian evidence. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC3171937); cached as abstract only. QuickGO shows this paper produced six annotations, all on zebrafish daam1a and none on any ARHGEF19 orthologue.

title: miR-503 regulates metastatic function through Rho guanine nucleotide exchanger factor 19 in hepatocellular carcinoma.
review_notes: Establishes post-transcriptional regulation of the gene rather than a function of the protein, so it supports no GO annotation directly. PubMed-verified; cached as abstract only, no PMC record.

title: Wnt signaling in midbrain dopaminergic neuron development and regenerative medicine for Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: The identifier resolves to the intended paper - title and journal match - but whether it supports the annotation could not be checked: only the abstract is cached, and that abstract mentions neither ARHGEF19 nor planar cell polarity. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than MISCITED for exactly that reason; the curator who made the NAS read the full text and I did not. The substantive point stands regardless of how it resolves, which is that a review is doing work the primary literature (PMID:18256687) could do far better.

title: ARHGEF19 interacts with BRAF to activate MAPK signaling during the tumorigenesis of non-small cell lung cancer.
review_notes: The strongest of the three MAPK papers and the only one that maps the requirement to specific domains. PubMed-verified; cached as abstract only (no PMC record), so all claims used here are abstract-level and no figure is cited. The mechanism remains unexplained - nothing beyond co-immunoprecipitation supports a direct DH-PH:BRAF interface - which is why the proposed annotation is non-core.

title: Emerging Roles of Ephexins in Physiology and Disease.
review_notes: A family review, used only for two things this review states on its authority: that Ephexin-2 is sparsely characterised relative to its paralogues, and that the Ephexin name is homology-based rather than evidence of an Eph receptor partner. Both are corroborated independently - the first by the measured annotation counts in ARHGEF19-bioinformatics, the second by the absence of any Eph-ARHGEF19 paper in the PubMed sweep. PubMed- and PMC-verified; full text cached and read.

title: Divergent roles of the Wnt/PCP Formin Daam1 in renal ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Dog (MDCKII) and mouse (IMCD3) cell lines, and the paper's own Xenopus arm gives a discordant result, which the title's word divergent reflects. No cilium or ciliogenesis term is proposed for human ARHGEF19 on this basis. PubMed- and PMC-verified; full text cached and read.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: A proteome-scale screen, not a study of this gene; the source of the second GO:0005515 IPI row. UniProt records the ARHGEF19-PAK5 pair with NbExp=3 so it is not a single-assay artefact, but nothing has followed it up and it stays non-core. PubMed-verified.

title: ARHGEF19 regulates MAPK/ERK signaling and promotes the progression of small cell lung cancer.
review_notes: Corroborates the domain requirement reported for BRAF in PMID:29164615, with a different partner and a different tumour type. Two caveats: it shares an institution with that paper, so the two are not fully independent, and the abstract's "-PD domain" is a typographical error for the PH domain - read as written it names a domain ARHGEF19 does not have. PubMed-verified; cached as abstract only.

title: Double inhibition and activation mechanisms of Ephexin family RhoGEFs.
review_notes: Structural work on Ephexin-4; ARHGEF19 is discussed as a family member but is not assayed, so this supports the architectural framing and nothing gene-specific. Cached as abstract only - the publisher restricts PMC full-text access - so both quotes are from the abstract, and statements this review takes from the full text (that Ephexin-2's biological functions remain elusive, and that the activating input for the non-Ephexin-4 members is undefined) are attributed in the notes file rather than quoted as supporting_text here.

title: ARHGEF19 promotes the growth of breast cancer in vitro and in vivo by the MAPK pathway.
review_notes: The third independent tumour type showing the same MAPK effect, which is why it is cited, but it is the weakest of the three: a low-visibility journal, no mechanism beyond immunoblot, and no domain mapping. Marked LOW_QUALITY for that reason rather than because the citation is wrong - PubMed-verified, cached as abstract only. It contributes convergence, not evidence.

title: Dishevelled2 activates WGEF via its interaction with a unique internal peptide motif of the GEF.
review_notes: Important and carefully done, but it contradicts PMID:18256687 on where Dishevelled binds and neither mapping has been reproduced independently, so DISPUTED records a live disagreement rather than a fault. Two things a reader of the database rather than the paper would get wrong: the activity measurements are on Xenopus protein, and PDB 8YR7 - which UniProt lists under Q8IW93, implying a human ARHGEF19 structure - is the failed fusion, with the WGEF peptide not usefully resolved. The residue claims were checked against the current UniProt sequence: position 295 is Y and residues 349-359 read GSTFSLWQDIP. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC11076555); full text cached and read.

title: ANKK1 Is a Wnt/PCP Scaffold Protein for Neural F-ACTIN Assembly.
review_notes: One of the small number of human-cell interaction studies on this protein, alongside PMID:18256687, the interactome screen, and the BRAF and HRAS co-immunoprecipitations in PMID:29164615 and PMID:32993957. It is the only source of a human localisation observation of any kind - qualitative, and in a neuroblastoma line, so it is recorded as context rather than annotated. It has produced no GO annotation in any species, and neither ANKK1 nor the human WGEF-RhoA interaction it reports is in the GO record. PubMed- and PMC-verified; full text cached and read.

title: p75NTR indirectly activates RAC and Cdc42 via a guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor
review_notes: The reaction itself is fine; using it as a source for ARHGEF19 is not. Its output is RAC1-GTP and human WGEF does not activate Rac1 (PMID:18256687, Fig. 2B), so the protein is attached here by set membership rather than by evidence. The derived GO annotation is only the cytosol compartment, which is why the row is marked over-annotated rather than removed.

title: GEFs activate RhoA,B,C
review_notes: Appropriate pathway assignment for this protein. The cytosol compartment it carries is a Reactome modelling convention for GEF catalytic activity, not a localisation observation, which is why the derived cellular-component row is kept as non-core.

title: RHOA GEFs activate RHOA
review_notes: Verified by reading the reaction's own summary, which names its evidence protein by protein; for ARHGEF19 it cites Wang et al. 2004, which is PMID:15485661. That paper has produced no GO annotation in any species, so this Reactome TAS is currently the only route by which its content reaches GO at all.

title: RHO GTPase cycle
review_notes: Correct pathway placement. Because both the pathway and the reaction through which ARHGEF19 enters it are RHO-specific and describe activation, the derived GO:0051056 row is refined to the Rho-specific positive-regulation term rather than left at the small-GTPase level.

title: ARHGEF19 bioinformatics: DH-PH exchange-surface panel and GO literature coverage
review_notes: Analyses written for this review; both scripts fetch every input live and exit non-zero if an assertion fails. The panel test carries five positive comparators with substrate co-crystals and measured activity plus three negative controls, and selftest_guards.py mutation-tests all seventeen guards - twelve against the panel test and five against the quote checker - including two negative controls that must stay silent. Every quote above is checked against the committed file by verify_quotes.py, which also checks the file: and Reactome: quotes CI does not.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGEF19 (human)
review_notes: The machine-fetched Affinage record, run with its trust gates clear (accession Q8IW93 matched, organism human, self-evaluation "win"). Its eleven citations were checked one by one against PubMed and all resolve to real papers about this gene, so as a precision claim it holds. Recall is a different matter and the gate says nothing about it. Those eleven citations omit three of the fourteen primary papers, plus one commentary. Their titles were checked against the gene's synonyms by go_coverage_by_reference.py rather than characterised by hand, because an earlier revision of this note generalised that every miss had an unfindable title and the list below contains a counterexample. Two of the four are genuinely unfindable by symbol: PMID:20643356 "Epidermal wound repair is regulated by the planar cell polarity signaling pathway", which is the one paper that has produced informative GO annotations for this gene in any species, and PMID:18537266, titled for Tim, a paralogue, and load-bearing for the regulatory section of this review. A third, the commentary PMID:21686262, names the gene only as the abbreviation "GEF19", which no ARHGEF19 or WGEF query returns. The fourth has no retrieval explanation at all: PMID:34813497 is titled "ARHGEF19 promotes the growth of breast cancer in vitro and in vivo by the MAPK pathway", the symbol is its first word, and the simplest possible query returns it. The record's GO grounding is not imported either: the molecular-function terms it offers (GO:0098772, GO:0060089) are less specific than what GOA already carries, and its localisation terms rest on non-human evidence. Used here as a literature index and a cross-check on the narrative, not as an evidence source.

title: Truncating mutations in BBS10 and BBS12 impair proteostasis and ciliary architecture in Bardet-Biedl Syndrome.

The publisher full-text request returned403, so complete Methods/Results, figures and construct controls were not inspected. Primary-cilium localization does not distinguish basal body from shaft and no nucleotide/folding assay is established.

title: Falcon deep research report for BBS12
review_notes: Preserved LLM-generated lead map, with primary evidence assessed separately. Assembly and intermediate-stability claims are supported independently by PMID:20080638 and PMID:22500027; basal-body localization is checked against PMID:19190184. The report's vertebrate-only origin is superseded by PMID:24010126. Its absolute absence-from-axoneme claim, absent intrinsic nucleotide activity and assignment of a substrate-binding/folding mechanism to BBS12 are not established by those primary studies. Downstream signaling-pathway assignments, variant totals, prevalence percentages and other quantitative claims are not adopted. The report remains MEDIUM/UNVERIFIED rather than direct evidence for these claims.

title: a-ketoisocaproate, a-keto-b-methylvalerate, or a-ketoisovalerate + glutamate <=> leu, ile, or val + alpha-ketoglutarate [BCAT2]
review_notes: The complete recovered normal summary and frontmatter were read. The separately saved official page was inspected for species, compartment, reaction participants and BCAT2-dimer catalyst fields; those fields are not present in the short normal cache. This human reverse reaction regenerates leucine, isoleucine or valine from their existing ketoacid skeletons and glutamate. The page assigns the reaction and homodimer to the mitochondrial matrix. It supports reversibility and canonical-product localization, without demonstrating net human tissue flux or de novo carbon-skeleton synthesis.

title: leu, ile, or val + alpha-ketoglutarate <=> a-ketoisocaproate, a-keto-b-methylvalerate, or a-ketoisovalerate + glutamate [BCAT2]

The separately saved official page was inspected for species, compartment, reaction participants and BCAT2-dimer catalyst fields; those fields are not present in the short normal cache. This human reaction transfers the BCAA amino group to 2-oxoglutarate and produces the matching ketoacid plus glutamate. Its matrix-localized homodimer initiates catabolism upstream of BCKDH and does not itself perform the committed downstream oxidative decarboxylation.

title: AP-64, Encoded by C5orf46, Exhibits Antimicrobial Activity against Gram-Negative Bacteria.
review_notes: Cached full text read in full. The sole functional characterisation of this gene in any organism, and the basis for both proposed new terms. Retraction, erratum and expression-of-concern checks clean by two independent routes - the PubMed record's PublicationType and CommentsCorrections fields, and Crossref relation/update-to/updated-by on DOI 10.3390/biom11040485. Identity of the assayed molecule verified computationally rather than assumed: the paper's stated 64 residues, MW 7.2 and PI 4.54 are all reproduced from UniProt's annotated mature CHAIN 24..87, so this is the gene's physiological secreted product and not a synthetic sub-fragment. Two reading cautions recorded. First, the paper is careful that the killing mechanism is unresolved, and the deep-research record's framing invites a membrane-permeabilisation reading the paper declines to support; no molecular function is proposed here as a result. Second, the Jurkat/Raji cytotoxicity must not be reported without the immediately following result that normal T cells, HaCaT keratinocytes and mouse embryonic fibroblasts are equally susceptible - it is general cytotoxicity at micromolar concentration, not selective anti-tumour activity. Notably, a QuickGO query by reference returns zero annotations citing this PMID anywhere in GOA (positive control: PMID:19199708 returns 396), so none of it has ever been curated.

title: Preliminary study on the role of the C5orf46 gene in renal cancer.
review_notes: Cached full text read; retraction and correction checks clean. Marked LOW_QUALITY on methodological grounds rather than citation grounds - the identifier and title are correct and the paper is honestly presented, its own title beginning 'Preliminary study'. The in vitro part is siRNA knockdown in two lines with proliferation, migration and apoptosis read-outs, no rescue, no mechanism, and no molecular function assayed; the remainder is TCGA bioinformatics. Sufficient to record a cancer-cell-line dependency as a knowledge gap, not sufficient to support a GO process term, and no term is proposed from it. Its background sentence that the gene has 'antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects via sequencing and microarray technologies' garbles the antibacterial finding, which came from purified protein assays, not sequencing; that sentence is not relied on.

title: C5orf46 bioinformatics results (mature-peptide identity; partner-set composition; annotation coverage gap)
review_notes: Generated by analyze_c5orf46.py in the same folder, with the fetched records cached under data/ so the numbers reproduce without network access. Every reported zero in it is paired with a non-zero positive control from the same endpoint in the same call pattern - ADGRA2 and ACTB for the IBA count, PMID:19199708 for the reference-coverage count, IPR001879 for the interpro2go lookup - because a rejected query and a genuine negative are indistinguishable downstream. Its guards are break-tested in both directions with the failure message asserted, and one of them caught a real defect in the script's own first version: a single-request IntAct fetch silently dropped 32 of AQP6's 1032 interaction records, and the self-test now re-runs that exact call and requires it to raise. Quotations into this file are deliberately taken from computed table rows rather than from prose, because a file: quote into a generated artifact is a two-way dependency and prose gets reworded.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for C5orf46 (human)
review_notes: A machine-generated secondary source, assessed rather than trusted. Its value here was real: it surfaced all three of the papers that GOA does not cite, including the sole functional characterisation of the gene, so both proposed terms trace to a lead it provided. Marked LOW_QUALITY on two grounds, neither of which is a fabricated citation. First, the cytotoxicity finding is framed without the disconfirming result that follows it in the same paper, which turns general micromolar cytotoxicity into an apparent anti-tumour selectivity - exactly the kind of error a verbatim-quote gate cannot catch, because the sentence itself is true. Second, the narrative's shape invites a membrane-permeabilisation reading of the mechanism, which the source explicitly leaves open between envelope damage and an intracellular target; no molecular function is proposed anywhere in this review as a result. The record's own GO grounding offers no molecular activity and only GO:0005576, which agrees with the conclusion reached here independently. Nothing from it is used as evidence for any mechanistic claim - it is cited once, for a corpus-level negative that three independent sources corroborate.

review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Human skeletal-muscle cultures, including rat-spinal-cord innervation, distinguish alpha1C plasma-membrane expression from predominantly cytoplasmic alpha1S. Full target cytoplasmic images were not inspected; independent trafficking evidence is used for the broad cytoplasm assertion.

title: Direct interaction of the Rab3 effector RIM with Ca2+ channels, SNAP-25, and synaptotagmin.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read, with bounded consultation. Explicit weaker alpha1C/RIM binding is retained despite alpha1B emphasis. Full construct-level Methods and native target assays were not inspected.

title: Skeletal and cardiac ryanodine receptors bind to the Ca(2+)-sensor region of dihydropyridine receptor alpha(1C) subunit.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Surface-plasmon-resonance experiments concern RyR1/2 binding to alpha1C calcium-sensor/C-terminal regions. Full paper was not recovered; this supports intracellular channel coupling, while the separately sourced intercellular-electrical-coupling TAS assertion remains unresolved.

title: A novel long N-terminal isoform of human L-type Ca2+ channel is up-regulated by protein kinase C.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Human long-N-terminal splice product expressed in Xenopus oocytes shows PKC modulation differing from the short-N-terminal comparator. This is channel regulation and splice-context evidence, not alpha1C kinase activity.

title: Effects of methylmercury on human neuronal L-type calcium channels transiently expressed in human embryonic kidney cells (HEK-293).
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Human neuronal alpha1C-1 with alpha2b and beta3a in HEK293 cells; whole-cell barium currents and methylmercury modulation. The channel preparation is calcium-channel specific, but barium is the stated recording charge carrier.

title: alpha(1C) (Ca(V)1.2) L-type calcium channel mediates mechanosensitive calcium regulation.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Human intestinal alpha1C in HEK/CHO expression systems supports mechanosensitive channel behavior, with auxiliary-subunit/cytoskeletal context. Full traces and all native-tissue experiments were not inspected.

title: Molecular cloning and characterization of the human voltage-gated calcium channel alpha(2)delta-4 subunit.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Although the title foregrounds alpha2delta4, it explicitly tests association with CaV1.2/beta3 and calcium influx in HEK293 cells. It is not a wrong-paralog basis for rejecting the target plasma-membrane assertion.

title: [A FORM OF TACHYCARDIA CAUSED BY DIGITALIS (PAROXYSMAL AURICULAR TACHYCARDIA WITH BLOCK)].
review_notes: The legitimate machine-fetched identity is a 1964 Dutch digitalis-associated tachycardia paper. No abstract or full text was available, and its support for a postsynaptic-density annotation was not verified. PMID:15140941 independently supports postsynaptic CaV1.2 and is a plausible intended citation, but an official identifier replacement has not been established. Keep the original ID/title and GOA reference; do not manufacture a remapping.

title: Ca2+-binding protein-1 facilitates and forms a postsynaptic complex with Cav1.2 (L-type) Ca2+ channels.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and bounded consultation of available sections read. The canonical HTML omits Results despite its full-text flag. Direct primary PMC Results were separately inspected by the consultant. Human short CaBP1, rbcII channel constructs, HEK293T binding assays and native rat postsynaptic preparations support CaBP1/calmodulin association and neuronal location. Purified calmodulin does not distinguish three CALM gene-specific assays; no images were independently inspected.

title: Ca(V)1.2 calcium channel dysfunction causes a multisystem disorder including arrhythmia and autism.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected author-uploaded primary clinical/developmental and expression/electrophysiology text read. Human G406R channel dysfunction is directly established; congenital and multisystem phenotypes are distinguished from individual developmental mechanisms. The normal cache remains abstract-only; supplemental web text is paraphrased with explicit access bounds. Full immune/eye developmental assays and supplementary material were not inspected.

title: Severe arrhythmia disorder caused by cardiac L-type calcium channel mutations.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. G406R/G402S channel functional expression and modeled cardiac consequences support altered inactivation. Computational cardiomyocyte modeling is not described as a native action-potential recording.

title: Insights into voltage-gated calcium channel regulation from the structure of the CaV1.2 IQ domain-Ca2+/calmodulin complex.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract plus selected actual Methods/Results read. Human IQ-domain/calmodulin structure and human full-length channel recordings with auxiliary subunits in Xenopus oocytes support gating regulation. The channel is the regulated pore; calmodulin supplies calcium-sensing feedback.

title: Atherosclerosis-related molecular alteration of the human CaV1.2 calcium channel alpha1C subunit.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Human vascular disease-associated alpha1C splicing and channel-expression comparisons inform surface channel function. Full target images and all vascular assays were not inspected; a universal splice pattern is not inferred.

title: Molecular coupling of a Ca2+-activated K+ channel to L-type Ca2+ channels via alpha-actinin2.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and bounded consultation read. It explicitly includes alpha-actinin-2 association with CaV1.2/CaV1.3, while highlighted knockout physiology concerns CaV1.3. Full target Methods were inaccessible, and the latter phenotype is not transferred to CACNA1C.

title: Loss-of-function mutations in the cardiac calcium channel underlie a new clinical entity characterized by ST-segment elevation, short QT intervals, and sudden cardiac death.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and source context read. Human WT/mutant alpha1C with beta2b/alpha2delta1 in CHO-K1 cells, trafficking/current defects and patient ECG findings. These support broad cardiac-channel function but do not independently resolve the precise atrial-cell action-potential annotation. Historical association statements are not treated as a new disease-validity classification.

title: Calmodulin-dependent gating of Ca(v)1.2 calcium channels in the absence of Ca(v)beta subunits.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and consultant-inspected indexed primary Methods/Results read. Human vascular alpha1C, human cardiac beta2d and calmodulin were tested in COS1 cells, including beta-free conditions. Exact original beta1/beta3 source assays were not independently resolved; the retained partner edges use explicit UniProt corroboration and curator deference.

title: New molecular components supporting ryanodine receptor-mediated Ca(2+) release: roles of junctophilin and TRIC channel in embryonic cardiomyocytes.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. This is a review of junctophilin/TRIC/RyR contributions to embryonic cardiomyocyte calcium handling. The target TAS calcium-import assertion is independently corroborated by alpha1C electrophysiology rather than attributed to a new target transport assay in this review.

title: Multiple C-terminal tail Ca(2+)/CaMs regulate Ca(V)1.2 function but do not mediate channel dimerization.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Structural tail/calmodulin assemblies and electrophysiology support regulation, while the paper rejects channel dimerization as the physiological inference. The indexed official correction, DOI:10.1038/emboj.2010.277, corrects an affiliation; it is supplementary context, not a new cached reference or an invalidation of the experiments.

title: Protein interactome reveals converging molecular pathways among autism disorders.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and consultant-selected Results/Discussion read. Human-cDNA/fragment Y2H screening includes independent retesting and a mammalian validation subset. Exact ACTN1/PICK1 edges are corroborated in UniProt, but individual supplementary target entries and pair-specific validation were not inspected. Partner identity supports the ACTN1 refinement without transferring an ACTN2-specific mechanism.

title: Long QT syndrome type 8: novel CACNA1C mutations causing QT prolongation and variant phenotypes.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Patient ascertainment and functional human channel comparisons, including distinct R858H and A582D effects, support calcium-channel/cardiac roles. Not every reported variant is represented as independently established disease causality.

title: Novel Timothy syndrome mutation leading to increase in CACNA1C window current.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. I1166T produces mixed current-density and window-current effects; the phenotype is not reduced to a single direction of channel activity. Full images were not inspected.

title: Identification and Functional Characterization of a Novel CACNA1C-Mediated Cardiac Disorder Characterized by Prolonged QT Intervals With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy, Congenital Heart Defects, and Sudden Cardiac Death.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected unique actual Methods/Results/Discussion read. Human EYFP-alpha1C-77 R518C/H in HEK293 cells, current-density/gating and surface fluorescence measurements, plus clinical first-degree AV block. Direct AV-node-cell assays were not resolved, and supplements/images were not inspected. Clinical AV evidence is preserved while AV-cell specificity remains uncertain.

title: Molecular and Functional Characterization of Rare CACNA1C Variants in Sudden Unexplained Death in the Young.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Rare variants from a sudden-death cohort were tested by HEK293 patch clamp. Functional pore evidence is separated from a universal causal classification of rare variants.

title: The α2δ-1 subunit remodels CaV1.2 voltage sensors and allows Ca2+ influx at physiological membrane potentials.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected unique actual Methods/Results read. Human alpha1C-77 with beta3 and alpha2delta1 in Xenopus oocytes, engineered cysteine voltage-clamp fluorometry and barium currents establish auxiliary modulation of channel activation. The preparation is not equated with every native subunit combination or a direct molecular contact map.

title: Ser1928 phosphorylation by PKA stimulates the L-type Ca2+ channel CaV1.2 and vasoconstriction during acute hyperglycemia and diabetes.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected actual Results read, including human arterial myocyte channel activity in the glucose/PKA/Ser1928 context. Mouse genetic and human cellular observations are distinguished; kinase activity belongs to PKA, not the channel.

title: Structural insights into binding of STAC proteins to voltage-gated calcium channels.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected actual channel Methods read. Human CaV1.2 alpha1C-77, human STAC3 and auxiliary constructs in Xenopus oocytes support calcium-dependent-inactivation modulation; the paper also contains CaV1.1 structural work, which is not substituted for the target assay.

title: Alternative Splicing at N Terminus and Domain I Modulates Ca(V)1.2 Inactivation and Surface Expression.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected unique Methods/Results read. Human N-terminal/exon-8 splice constructs with rat auxiliaries in HEK cells, surface biotinylation and current measurements support expression/gating differences. The indexed official correction DOI:10.1016/j.bpj.2018.06.001 replaces duplicated exemplary Figure 7 traces for one construct; corrected images were not inspected. The correction is not represented as replacing all expression data, and artificial splice combinations are not assumed to be named native products.

review_notes: The normal record has bibliographic metadata without an abstract, but actual full XML provides Methods/Results. Selected S643F experiments were read and show mixed loss- and gain-related current effects. Access is not described as abstract-only simply because the abstract is absent.

title: Expanding clinical phenotype in CACNA1C related disorders: From neonatal onset severe epileptic encephalopathy to late-onset epilepsy.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected actual clinical/interpretive text read. Three affected individuals in two families and structural interpretation support neurological association; direct electrophysiology was not established in the inspected text. The broadly correct channel process is retained with independent target functional evidence.

review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Patient-derived and isogenic human induced-pluripotent-stem-cell cardiomyocytes support R518C-associated action-potential prolongation and L-type channel perturbation. Full cell-subtype characterization, traces and supplementary data were not inspected.

title: Mechanisms and Regulation of Cardiac Ca(V)1.2 Trafficking.
review_notes: Complete normal canonical abstract read; canonical cache is abstract-only and was preserved despite a fuller fetched variant. This review describes dyadic CaV1.2 calcium entry, RyR2 release, contraction and intracellular channel reservoirs. The review is supporting synthesis, not a newly inspected primary experiment.

review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and selected actual Methods/Results read. Human L614R channels were tested with human auxiliaries in HEK cells, while other variants used a mouse channel backbone and rat auxiliaries. Clinical, construct and species boundaries are retained. The indexed official correction DOI:10.1038/s41436-021-01306-7 adds an author middle initial; it does not replace experimental data.

Selected Gi/o receptor/G-protein manipulations fail to modulate this preparation, which is not a general exclusion of all native GPCR signaling. Full Methods/figures not inspected.

review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. Human neuronal alpha1D with beta2 and alpha2b in Xenopus oocytes supports L-type channel reconstitution; absence of current without beta2 is specific to the tested system. Canonical cache preserved despite a fetched whitespace/metadata variant. Full Methods/figures not inspected.

title: Molecular coupling of a Ca2+-activated K+ channel to L-type Ca2+ channels via alpha-actinin2.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract read. CaV1.3 and CaV1.2 associate with alpha-actinin2, which links them to SK2 without direct SK2-L-type channel binding. CaV1.3 deletion perturbs SK2 and atrial repolarization. Full construct-level Methods and images were not inspected; the original human partner assertion is retained with curator deference, and the deletion physiology is not called an endogenous human experiment.

title: Modulation of voltage- and Ca2+-dependent gating of CaV1.3 L-type calcium channels by alternative splicing of a C-terminal regulatory domain.
review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique Methods/Results/Discussion read. Human channel backbone with rat exon42A sequence identical to the human amino-acid sequence, HEK/tsA-201 recordings, C-terminal fragments and FRET test splice-dependent gating and calmodulin modulation. Mouse tissue expression and human RT-PCR are separated from heterologous functional assays. Images and all supplementary data were not inspected; 42A is not automatically equated with the distinct 43s construct used in a later paper.

title: Loss of Ca(v)1.3 (CACNA1D) function in a human channelopathy with bradycardia and congenital deafness.
review_notes: Complete normal abstract and official publisher identity read. Human SANDD families and nonconducting glycine-insertion channel, with explicit mouse SAN and hair-cell mechanism context. Canonical text is abstract-only; a publisher cookie redirect prevented direct full-text access. No direct human SAN-cell recording or full Methods/image inspection is claimed. Existing broad and tissue-context annotations use this convergent evidence with curator deference.

title: Defects in ankyrin-based membrane protein targeting pathways underlie atrial fibrillation.
review_notes: Complete abstract plus selected unique Methods, Results and Discussion read. Mouse atrial/fibroblast targeting and electrophysiology, CaV1.3 fragment/motif binding, human atrial lysates/expression and computational action-potential modeling are distinguished. The channel construct/motif numbering is not silently remapped to the current canonical human sequence. Supplementary Methods and images were not inspected; ankyrin-dependent targeting is not the sole membrane-delivery route.

title: Somatic and germline CACNA1D calcium channel mutations in aldosterone-producing adenomas and primary aldosteronism.
review_notes: Complete abstract and selected primary functional Results/Methods read. Human WT and pore-region variants coexpressed with beta2a/alpha2delta1 in HEK293T cells show altered activation/inactivation. Peak-current differences vary among variants and are interpreted cautiously by the authors. Adrenal disease interpretation is distinguished from direct channel measurement; no aldosterone-synthetic enzyme function is transferred to alpha1D. Images/supplements not inspected.

title: CACNA1D de novo mutations in autism spectrum disorders activate Cav1.3 L-type calcium channels.
review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique Methods/Results/Discussion read. Human long-C-terminal channel constructs in tsA-201 cells, calcium-current recordings and WT/mutant coexpression show distinct A749G and G407R mechanisms. Reduced peak amplitude can coexist with persistent current gain. Historical ASD-risk interpretation is not promoted to an independently updated disease-validity or treatment claim. Supplementary figures not inspected.

title: New gain-of-function mutation shows CACNA1D as recurrently mutated gene in autism spectrum disorders and epilepsy.
review_notes: Complete abstract and selected unique Methods/Results/Discussion read. Human long and 43s short splice constructs carrying V401L were compared in tsA-201 cells; gating, inactivation and inferred surface-expression effects depend on splice context. The 43s construct is not relabeled as current named product42A. Historical clinical interpretation is kept separate from directly measured channel function. Images and supplements not inspected.

title: Solution structures of the SH3 domains from Shank scaffold proteins and their interactions with Cav1.3 calcium channels.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and bounded consultant publisher-access assessment read. Shank SH3 domains bind a channel-derived arginine-rich region; the exact human SHANK3-1 edge is also present in GOA/UniProt. The consultant inspected supplementary descriptions, not underlying experiments; main text/figures were inaccessible. Domain binding does not imply native full-channel scaffold assembly or isoform-exclusive binding.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Complete canonical abstract and bounded consultant assessment of selected primary Results/Methods read. Protein-derived motifs and recombinant human PDZ domains were tested by equilibrium holdup assays; exact GOA/UniProt edges identify the supported target interactions. Individual CACNA1D supplement values, domain numbers, motif sequence and pair-specific orthogonal validation were not inspected. The complete indexed official correction DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-35177-6 repairs omitted correlation values/axis labels, a Figure4a column and Figure5 labels/panel ordering; corrected images were not inspected. It does not state withdrawal of the target interactions. The canonical cache is preserved despite an alternate metadata/whitespace variant.

title: Calcium Influx through Voltage-gated Calcium Channels
review_notes: Complete normal human event summary read. It explicitly describes calcium movement across plasma membrane and includes CaV1.3 in beta-cell secretion context. It is pathway synthesis, not a new isolated target assay or proof of one invariant auxiliary-subunit combination.

title: UniProtKB Q01668 CAC1D_HUMAN source record
review_notes: Authenticated normal Reviewed human record read for identity, channel mechanism, interaction partners and four named products. Names, IDs and sequence notes are preserved literally. Additional splice products can exist; the four records are not represented as four individually assayed native proteins in every tissue.

title: De Novo Pathogenic Variants in CACNA1E Cause Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy with Contractures, Macrocephaly, and Dyskinesias.
review_notes: Complete normal cached abstract and official PubMed identity read; human disease cohort and heterologous functional testing support variant-specific changes in CaV2.3 gating. Full original Methods/figures were not inspected. The linked 2019 correction was read in an author-institution publication record and concerns author spelling and omissions, not functional results; canonical metadata remain unchanged.

review_notes: Normal cached full text read for CaV3.1-specific Results, Discussion and Methods. Adult female mice aged 2–4 months and isolated AVNC recordings at 36 degrees C were used. CaV3.1-null cells retain irregular slower spontaneous pacing and reduced maximal isoproterenol-stimulated rates; CaV1.3-null cells are quiescent under the tested baseline conditions but can show initiated activity with negative current injection. Figures and supplemental tables were not independently inspected. This supports the specialized ISS context without making CaV3.1 the sole action-potential generator.

Short NM_198382.2 cDNA was tested; c.5075G>A corresponds to c.5144G>A in the longer transcript. The IRES-EGFP reporter is not a demonstrated channel fusion. Wild-type and mutant channels localize to cytoplasm and plasma membrane. Mutant gating is positively shifted; Purkinje-cell differentiation morphology was not obviously different. Supplementary images were not separately inspected.

This supports the historical amine-response context as enzyme activity rather than an inferred transcript-only measurement. It supports receptor signaling and localization; this family-specific presentation does not redefine the usual recessive severe-disease association. The cache is abstract-only.

This is a particular allele/family with apparent recessive mild disease, not a universal inheritance rule. The cache is abstract-only.

title: The cargo receptor p24A facilitates calcium sensing receptor maturation and stabilization in the early secretory pathway.
review_notes: Human CaSR and human TMED2/p24A constructs were tested in HEK293 cells after a human-kidney yeast two-hybrid screen. Selected complete Methods, Results and Discussion passages show reciprocal coimmunoprecipitation of immature CaSR, truncation and p24A-mutant comparisons, surface/total expression controls and Sar1 perturbations. TMED2 is the trafficking cargo receptor; CASR is its cargo. Direct purified-protein binding and a chaperone activity of CASR were not established.

title: Calcium sensing receptor mutations implicated in pancreatitis and idiopathic epilepsy syndrome disrupt an arginine-rich retention motif.
review_notes: Selected complete Methods, Results and Discussion passages from the normal HTML cache show FLAG-tagged human CaSR expressed in HEK293 cells, background-corrected surface/total ELISA, ERK responses, arginine-motif mutants and phosphorylation-site substitutions. They support regulated surface abundance. The historical epilepsy implication is not accepted as current gene-disease validity; the frozen ClinGen record classifies that association as refuted. Cellular trafficking results and disease causality are separate claims. Direct 14-3-3 binding was explicitly left unresolved by the authors.

review_notes: The complete abstract reports reduced inositol-phosphate signaling by human T550I CaSR in COS7 cells and an intermediate cotransfection response. It supports GPCR signaling; dominant-negative interpretation remains qualified. The cache is abstract-only.

title: CASR gene activating mutations in two families with autosomal dominant hypocalcemia.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports Q681R and P221L in hypocalcemic families and functional testing of Q681R in HEK293 cells, with increased calcium sensitivity despite similar expression and surface targeting. It supports receptor localization and signaling. The cache is abstract-only.

title: Two novel mutations of the calcium-sensing receptor gene affecting the same amino acid position lead to opposite phenotypes and reveal the importance of p.N802 on receptor activity.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports human N802I and N802S CaSR in COS7 cells, MAPK signaling and allosteric modulation. This supports receptor signaling and the tested localization observations, not a conclusion that all hypercalcemic families have CASR variants. The cache is abstract-only.

title: A novel mutation in calcium-sensing receptor gene associated to hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria.
review_notes: Selected complete Results, Methods and Discussion passages show Myc-tagged human T972M CaSR in HEK293 cells, wild-type and F351V controls, altered mature glycosylation and reduced calcium-evoked ERK phosphorylation. The father/son hypercalciuric presentation is an atypical family-specific finding. Tissue-selective effects on parathyroid versus kidney are an interpretation rather than directly measured tissue signaling.

title: Novel activating mutation of human calcium-sensing receptor in a family with autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports human P136L CaSR in HEK293 cells, surface localization, increased intracellular-calcium and MAPK responses, and segregation with hypocalcemia in a family. This supports the tested receptor localization and signaling. The cache is abstract-only.

title: Identification and functional analysis of a novel CaSR mutation in a family with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports human G571W CaSR in COS7 cells, surface expression comparable to wild type and reduced Fura-2 calcium responses. This supports receptor signaling and localization, with no claim to have inspected the complete imaging controls. The cache is abstract-only.

title: Structural mechanism of ligand activation in human calcium-sensing receptor.
review_notes: Selected complete structural, ligand-binding, mutational and cellular-assay passages were read. Human extracellular-domain constructs were expressed in insect cells, whereas full-length human receptors were tested in HEK293 cells with surface-expression controls, IP1 and calcium readouts. Scintillation proximity directly demonstrated tryptophan binding; anomalous diffraction supported calcium-binding sites. The paper interprets amino acids as agonists, but later controlled-membrane work distinguishes positive allosteric modulation. Amino-acid binding remains supported irrespective of this activation-model dispute.

title: Illuminating the allosteric modulation of the calcium-sensing receptor.
review_notes: Selected complete Results and Discussion passages describe a SNAP-tag TR-FRET receptor sensor, cellular IP1/calcium assays, cell-surface controls, cross-linking and dialyzed membrane preparations. Under the controlled membrane conditions calcium alone drove the full conformational transition, whereas amino acids potentiated calcium responses. This differs from a universal amino-acid-alone agonist interpretation. Detailed experimental protocols delegated to the separate SI Appendix were not independently read.

title: Calcium-sensing receptor-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome response to calciprotein particles drives inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis.
review_notes: Selected complete Results, captions, Discussion and Methods passages were read, including human monocytes, one sequenced CaSR-deficient THP-1 clone and a non-targeting clone, myeloid-specific mouse deletion, pharmacological controls, calciprotein-particle uptake, NLRP3 dependence, IL-1beta release and ASC-speck methodology. CaSR contributes upstream to inflammatory activation under calcium/phosphate/particle conditions; residual CaSR-independent activation is explicit. This does not make CASR a structural inflammasome component or establish a universal receptor output. Figures and supplementary data were not independently reanalyzed.

title: Structural mechanism of cooperative activation of the human calcium-sensing receptor by Ca(2+) ions and L-tryptophan.
review_notes: Selected complete cryo-EM interpretation, construct and cellular-assay passages were read. Full-length human CaSR with substituted signal sequence/tags was expressed in insect cells; HEK293T mutant assays measured IP1 with surface-expression controls. Tryptophan closes the Venus flytrap domain but does not alone complete transmembrane activation; calcium and amino acids cooperate in the authors' model. Ambient ligands and conformational intermediates limit absolute ligand-sufficiency conclusions.

title: Asymmetric activation of the calcium-sensing receptor homodimer.
review_notes: Selected complete structural, engineered-dimer, BRET, IP1 and expression-method passages were read. Human CaSR residues 20-894 were used for structural and cellular assays, with signaling competence assessed; forced dimers used GABAB-derived targeting elements. The results support GPCR signaling, asymmetric activation and allosteric modulation, but engineered targeting constructs and the C-terminal truncation must not be presented as unmodified endogenous receptor behavior.

title: Structural insights into the activation of human calcium-sensing receptor.
review_notes: Selected complete structural, ligand, mutational, expression-control and Discussion passages were read. A human 1-870 construct was purified for structures and full-length mutant receptors were tested in cells. Inhibitory nanobody stabilization and calcium/TNCA/cinacalcet conditions define the structural states. The authors acknowledge that cryo-EM density alone does not uniquely identify calcium and that amino-acid activation terminology remains contested. Cellular calcium responses and expression controls support receptor activity.

title: Allosteric modulation and G-protein selectivity of the Ca(2+)-sensing receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract and selected complete Results/Methods paragraphs were read. Two complementary cellular BRET approaches primarily support Gi/o and Gq/11 activation, with receptor surface-expression controls. Human receptor constructs include a 20-894 truncation; structural preparations additionally use GABAB-derived tails, tethering and engineered G proteins. These experiments support receptor coupling in the tested systems, not a universal native-tissue G-protein preference or a direct cAMP measurement.

title: Promiscuous G-protein activation by the calcium-sensing receptor.
review_notes: The complete abstract and selected complete construct/functional Methods paragraphs were read. Structures use truncated human receptor and dominant-negative or mini/chimeric G proteins, whereas cellular assays use full-length receptor. Gi/Gs-tail chimeras redirect coupling to an IP1 readout in Gq/11-deficient cells; this is not native Gi/Gs second-messenger measurement. Separate TRUPATH assays address Gi1, Gi3 and Gq. The authors report no detectable CaSR-induced Gs activity in HEK293T or MCF7, although that method paragraph names a Gq donor, an unresolved internal description ambiguity. Surface-expression controls and calcium-dependent FRET-background subtraction are explicit. No universal physiological Gs claim is justified.

title: Molecular cloning and functional expression of human parathyroid calcium receptor cDNAs.
review_notes: The complete abstract reports cloning of a 1078-residue human parathyroid calcium-sensing receptor, a rare insertion-containing transcript and functional cation responses in Xenopus oocytes. This supports receptor function and calcium sensing. A complete primary body was not retrieved, and organismal chemosensory behavior cannot be adjudicated from the abstract alone.

title: Cloning and functional expression of a rat kidney extracellular calcium/polyvalent cation-sensing receptor.
review_notes: The authenticated normal cache contains the complete abstract only despite PMCID PMC42831. It directly describes rat kidney RaKCaR cRNA in Xenopus oocytes and phospholipid-dependent, intracellular-calcium-induced chloride currents. Separately read selected original-paper Results and Figure 3 caption supply water-injected controls and persistence of the response in calcium-free extracellular solution with EGTA; these external sections are not presented as cached full text or a whole-paper reading. The dated official rat donor graph links this paper to the chloride-transport assertion. These observations support receptor-mediated channel activation, with the human transport transfer assessed as excessive; they do not establish a specific human chloride-transport regulatory subtype. The abstract describes earlier bovine parathyroid receptor/PTH work as background, not a new human PTH-secretion assay.

review_notes: Complete abstract read. Explicit human wild-type and deletion-mutant CAV3 adenoviral constructs were tested in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes with agonist-induced hypertrophy and signaling readouts. Supports contextual growth regulation, not a demonstrated human developmental or T-tubule process. Cache remains abstract-only.

title: Insulin resistance in skeletal muscles of caveolin-3-null mice.
review_notes: Complete normal cached abstract and selected complete external primary Methods, Results, Discussion and captions read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC515114/. Mouse Cav3-null muscle glucose uptake, tolerance and fasting lipid concentrations support bounded homeostasis phenotypes; re-expression restores insulin signaling, not a demonstrated glucose-uptake rescue. The measured serum triglyceride concentration does not establish a CAV3 triglyceride chemical step or flux. No raw figure analysis. Normal cache remains abstract-only despite the external body access.

title: Behavior of caveolae and caveolin-3 during the development of myocyte hypertrophy.
review_notes: Complete normal cached abstract and official primary identity read. Neonatal rat cardiomyocytes show increased caveolae and CAV3 after ionomycin; BAPTA, calcineurin and CaMKII inhibition statements concern the phenylephrine experiments and are not silently reassigned to ionomycin. Pressure-overloaded rat hearts are a separate endpoint. The source supports the bounded stimulus-response transfer, not CAV3 calcium-sensing activity. Full body unavailable.

title: Caveolin isoform expression during differentiation of C6 glioma cells.
review_notes: Complete normal cached abstract and official publisher/PubMed identity read. C6 glioma differentiation experiments report temporal caveolin expression and localization; the rat model was established in the primary metadata/available source context. The full body remains inaccessible. This resolves donor provenance but not the precise CAV3 differentiation contribution, so the two corresponding transfers remain undecided. No wrong-paralog conclusion or claim that expression evidence is intrinsically invalid.

title: Caveolin regulates microtubule polymerization in the vascular smooth muscle cells.
review_notes: Complete normal abstract plus actual indexed publisher Methods/Results excerpts read at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0006291X06001513. The excerpts explicitly distinguish adeno-Cav3 from adeno-Cav1/GFP in rat aortic vascular smooth muscle cells and increased polymerized tubulin after strong overexpression. The publisher excerpts are incomplete sections, not a full-paper read. The abstract alone does not assign every scaffolding-peptide or downregulation result to CAV3. No intrinsic polymerase or universal physiological effect is inferred.

title: Mutant caveolin-3 induces persistent late sodium current and is associated with long-QT syndrome.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract and external university-hosted primary Methods, relevant Results, Discussion, limitations and captions read. Human CAV3/Nav1.5 HEK293 experiments show mutant late-current increases with no measurable WT-versus-vector effect; controlled co-IP and human ventricular colocalization support association/location. T78M pacemaking reasoning was extrapolated from separate SCN5A work, not tested here. No supplement or image-pixel analysis; canonical cache remains abstract-only. Historical disease claims do not upgrade frozen Limited long-QT validity. External primary URL: https://www.sfu.ca/~tibbits/courses/K812/2104.pdf.

title: Novel mechanism for sudden infant death syndrome: persistent late sodium current secondary to mutations in caveolin-3.
review_notes: Complete canonical HTML Methods, Results, Discussion and limitations read. Human tagged CAV3 variants with SCN5A Q1077del in HEK293 cells increased late current; the WT increase and peak-current/gating differences were not significant. Anonymous SIDS cohort and noncardiac expression-model limits are explicit. Manuscript typographical inconsistencies are not a verified correction or justification to rewrite source identifiers.

review_notes: Complete abstract identifies a human rippling-muscle-disease family with an in-frame CAV3 deletion. Full functional body was unavailable; the abstract does not settle the cited skeletal-muscle contraction mechanism. No wrong-gene claim is inferred.

Supports caveola assembly and model-specific ischemic protection. Mouse Cav3 constructs in C2C12 cells and mouse muscle, control-IgG co-IP, MG53/dysferlin localization, transgenic and acute P104L perturbations, R26Q/C71W comparisons and injury-dye assays support coordinated repair-protein trafficking. Overexpression effects and the MG53-dependent injury response are separated from CAV3 fusion catalysis. Figures and supplementary movies were not independently reanalysed.

Human tagged CAV3 myopathy variants show distinct surface/Golgi distributions in heterologous cells and context-dependent effects on TrkA/EGFR signaling. title: Caveolin-3 regulates protein kinase A modulation of the Ca(V)3.2 (alpha1H) T-type Ca2+ channels.

CAV3 is caveolin-3, not the similarly written calcium-channel designation. Direct pore inhibition and a universal channel effect are not claimed.

title: Chemical biology. A small-molecule inhibitor of the aberrant transcription factor CBFβ-SMMHC delays leukemia in mice.

title: Heterozygous pathogenic variants involving CBFB cause a new skeletal disorder resembling cleidocranial dysplasia.
review_notes: Complete normal metadata/abstract and selected full XML Methods/Results/Discussion were read. Eight subjects from five families carry heterozygous variants with skeletal features resembling cleidocranial dysplasia; RNA was tested in two subjects. Clinical overlap and proposed RUNX interactions do not establish a single molecular mechanism for every allele. The new-transcript/neomorphic proposal is distinguished from demonstrated RNA effects and the frozen ClinGen classification.

title: CBFβ Regulates RUNX3 ADP-Ribosylation to Mediate Homologous Recombination Repair.
review_notes: Complete metadata/abstract and selected unique cached Results/Methods were read. Human HEK293T/U2OS coassociation, Runt-region and interface-mutant tests, controlled proximity ligation, CBFB depletion/rescue and RUNX3 stability assays support the complex. Proximity ligation is not a solved direct interface. RUNX3 ADP-ribosylation/repair effects do not make CBFB an ADP-ribosyltransferase or independently establish every repair step.

title: A Cryptic CBFB Deletion-Inversion Expands the Mutational Spectrum of Variants Associated With Cleidocranial Dysplasia.
review_notes: Complete normal metadata/abstract and selected full XML Methods/Results/Discussion were read. A mother/daughter deletion-inversion-deletion removes CBFB exons 1–2; breakpoint and RNA evidence support reduced expression for this structural allele. Their phenotype lacks the earlier cohort's reported developmental delay. The paper's introductory 187-amino-acid statement is not substituted for the reviewed canonical 182-amino-acid UniProt product. No universal haploinsufficiency-versus-neomorph conclusion is made.

title: Fusion between transcription factor CBF beta/PEBP2 beta and a myosin heavy chain in acute myeloid leukemia.

Later human experiments establish transcriptional regulation without resolving that exact boundary. This is not a claim of wrong-gene attribution, miscitation or reference invalidity. The canonical cache remains abstract-only.
