title: Expression of frizzled-related protein and Wnt-signalling molecules in invasive human breast tumours.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Wong et al., J Pathol 2002). An IHC/ISH survey of Wnt-pathway components in breast tumours; it reports elevated cyclin D1 but contains no cyclin D1 mechanism, so it is weak support for the nuclear localisation row it underpins.

title: Self-assembling protein microarrays.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Ramachandran et al., Science 2004); a self-assembling-protein-microarray method paper mapping pairwise interactions among replication proteins. Correctly cited as the source of an interaction row, but it carries no cyclin D1-specific functional analysis; the cyclin D1-CDK6 complex is supported independently by PMID:8114739.

title: Cyclin D1b variant influences prostate cancer growth through aberrant androgen receptor regulation.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Burd et al., PNAS 2006). Establishes AR corepression by cyclin D1a and the compromised activity of the D1b variant; cited for resolving the AR protein-binding row, with the isoform caveat noted in suggested_questions.

title: INSM1 functions as a transcriptional repressor of the neuroD/beta2 gene through the recruitment of cyclin D1 and histone deacetylases.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Liu et al., Biochem J 2006). Primary evidence for the CDK-independent corepressor role: cyclin D1 suppresses the neuroD/beta2 promoter with INSM1 and mediates INSM1-HDAC1/3 association.

title: Cyclin D1 repression of nuclear respiratory factor 1 integrates nuclear DNA synthesis and mitochondrial function.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Wang et al., PNAS 2006). Cyclin D1 represses NRF-1 expression and activity, supporting resolution of the NRF1 binding row to transcription factor binding.

title: leptin-induced growth stimulation of breast cancer cells involves recruitment of histone acetyltransferases and mediator complex to CYCLIN D1 promoter via activation of Stat3.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Saxena et al., JBC 2007); abstract-only. The CYCLIN D1 promoter is the object acted upon by leptin-activated STAT3, so this does not establish cyclin D1 participation in the leptin response.

title: CDK4 and CDK6 delay senescence by kinase-dependent and p16INK4a-independent mechanisms.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Ruas et al., Mol Cell Biol 2007). The paper is centred on CDK4/CDK6 and senescence; the cyclin D1 holoenzyme row it supports is sound, but the abstract does not analyse cyclin D1 directly, so the complex annotation rests mainly on PMID:8114739 and PMID:19237565.

title: Sulindac suppresses beta-catenin expression in human cancer cells.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Han et al., Eur J Pharmacol 2008). Shows cyclin D1 downregulation as a beta-catenin-target readout after sulindac; an expression-change observation, not evidence that cyclin D1 acts in a xenobiotic response.

title: Identification of an INSM1-binding site in the insulin promoter: negative regulation of the insulin gene transcription.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Wang et al., J Endocrinol 2008). Shows recruitment of cyclin D1 and HDAC3 to the insulin promoter and the effect of anti-cyclin D1 morpholino, supporting the corepressor MF, BP and complex annotations.

title: UVA-induced cell cycle progression is mediated by a disintegrin and metalloprotease/epidermal growth factor receptor/AKT/Cyclin D1 pathways in keratinocytes.
review_notes: Cached record verified (He et al., Cancer Res 2008). Knockdown, not merely induction, of cyclin D1 blocked UVA-induced progression - the reason GO:0070141 is kept as non-core while the other stimulus-response rows are marked over-annotated.

title: Zinc finger transcription factor INSM1 interrupts cyclin D1 and CDK4 binding and induces cell cycle arrest.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Zhang et al., JBC 2009). Maps the cyclin box/proline-rich interface with INSM1 and shows RB hypophosphorylation on CDK4 displacement. Note the paper concerns G1, not G2/M, which is the basis for modifying the GO:0010971 row.

title: Crystal structure of human CDK4 in complex with a D-type cyclin.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Day et al., PNAS 2009). Provides the 2.3 A crystal structure of the CDK4-cyclin D1 heterodimer, i.e. direct structural evidence for the cyclin D1-CDK4 complex and for cyclin binding as an activating interaction.

title: F-box protein FBXO31 mediates cyclin D1 degradation to induce G1 arrest after DNA damage.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Santra et al., Nature 2009). Establishes Thr286-dependent, FBXO31-mediated degradation of cyclin D1 causing G1 arrest after DNA damage. Note that it supports cyclin D1 as the ligase SUBSTRATE, which is why the DNA-damage process rows derived from it are marked over-annotated.

title: Structural basis of the phosphorylation-independent recognition of cyclin D1 by the SCF(FBXO31) ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Li et al., PNAS 2018); abstract-only. Cited for the phosphorylation-dependent export and cytoplasmic proteolysis framework behind the cytoplasm/cytosol annotations.

title: AMBRA1 regulates cyclin D to guard S-phase entry and genomic integrity.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Maiani et al., Nature 2021). AMBRA1-mediated degradation of D-type cyclins guards S-phase entry; supports the G1/S involvement and the turnover mechanism.

title: CRL4(AMBRA1) is a master regulator of D-type cyclins.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Simoneschi et al., Nature 2021); abstract-only in the cache. Identifies CRL4(AMBRA1) as the ligase for all three D-cyclins and shows that their accumulation causes RB hyperphosphorylation.

title: The AMBRA1 E3 ligase adaptor regulates the stability of cyclin D.
review_notes: Cached record verified (Chaikovsky et al., Nature 2021). Its opening statement of the cyclin D-CDK4/6-RB axis is the quote used for the core activator function.

review_notes: Cached record verified (Li et al., Nat Commun 2025); abstract-only. FBXO32 K27-linked ubiquitination stabilises cyclin D1 - relevant to turnover, and another case where cyclin D1 is the substrate rather than a participant.

review_notes: Cached record verified. The paper is about p16INK4a and pRB, but its conclusion that pRB is "the critical target acted upon by cyclin D-dependent kinases in the G1 phase" is the claim cited here; it is a NAS-grade statement for CCND1 rather than direct CCND1 experimentation.

title: Plasticity and rigidity in adaptor protein-2-mediated internalization of the TCR:CD3 complex.
review_notes: Abstract only. 293T reconstitution showing AP-2-mediated TCR internalization needs both the CD3G (D/E)xxxLL signal and YxxL motifs, with an absolute requirement for CD3G K128. The falcon report's residue-level percentages (D127 abolishing uptake, L131/L132 ~60%) could not be checked against the abstract.

title: Patients with CD3G mutations reveal a role for human CD3γ in T(reg) diversity and suppressive function.
review_notes: Full text cached. Six CD3G-deficient patients, all with autoimmunity; Treg TRB repertoire with ~log10 fewer unique productive reads, reduced diversity and suppressive function. Phenotypic (necessity) evidence downstream of reduced TCR-CD3 signalling.

title: A Novel CD3G Mutation in a Taiwanese Patient With Normal T Regulatory Function Presenting With the CVID Phenotype Free of Autoimmunity-Analysis of all Genotypes and Phenotypes.
review_notes: Full text cached. Single patient homozygous c.del213A with near-absent CD3 gamma, one-log lower surface CD3, CVID-like B cell deficiency and preserved Treg suppression without autoimmunity.

title: Structures of human γδ T cell receptor-CD3 complex.
review_notes: Full text cached. Cryo-EM of human Vgamma9Vdelta2 and Vgamma5Vdelta1 TCR-CD3 complexes (reconstituted with all CD3 chains co-expressed) shows CD3 epsilon-gamma packed against TCR gamma and CD3 epsilon-delta against TCR delta. Cited by the falcon report (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07439-4).

title: The protein interactions of the immunoglobulin receptor family tyrosine-based activation motifs present in the T cell receptor zeta subunits and the CD3 gamma, delta and epsilon chains.
review_notes: Abstract only. Phosphopeptide pull-downs; doubly phosphorylated CD3 gamma ITAM binds ZAP-70 (equal to zeta1 and delta) and also Shc, Grb-2 and PI3K p85. In vitro binding capacity only.

title: Falcon deep research report for human CD3G
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/falcon, 2026-10-01) drawing on primary papers (Rowe 2018 PMID:29653965, Lee 2019 PMID:31921117, Szymczak and Vignali 2005 PMID:15778375, Osman 1996 PMID:8647168, Xin 2024 PMID:38657677, Li 2024 sepsis, Menon 2024 aptamers) and reviews (Xu 2020, Shah 2021). All DOIs resolve to the stated papers; quantitative claims checked against cached text (Treg ~log10 read reduction, all six patients autoimmune, one-log lower CD3 in Lee 2019) are correct. It omits that the human gamma-delta structures also contain CD3 epsilon-delta, and residue-level internalization percentages from Szymczak 2005 could not be verified (abstract only). Careful about separating complex-level from CD3G-specific evidence; no hallucinated citations detected.

title: Crystal structure of the human CD4 N-terminal two-domain fragment complexed to a class II MHC molecule.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Crystal structure of the CD4 D1D2 fragment bound to class II MHC; source for the Phe43 contact, for the V-shaped ternary model that excludes a direct CD4-TCR contact, and for the similarity between the gp120 and pMHCII binding modes.

title: CD4 dimers constitute the functional component required for T cell activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified for the dimerization mapping (K318, Q344 in D4) and its requirement for coreceptor function. GOA also uses this paper for an extracellular matrix structural constituent NAS row on CD4, which the paper does not support; that row is removed.

title: A zinc clasp structure tethers Lck to T cell coreceptors CD4 and CD8.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Solution structures of the ternary CD4-Lck-Zn2+ and CD8alpha-Lck-Zn2+ complexes; the primary source for the zinc clasp that underlies the coreceptor's kinase-delivery function, and for the masking of the CD4 dileucine endocytosis motif by Lck.

title: Lymphocyte chemoattractant factor induces CD4-dependent intracytoplasmic signaling in lymphocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified and correctly cited for CD4-dependent calcium/IP3 signaling by lymphocyte chemoattractant factor (IL-16), including loss of the response in cells lacking the CD4 cytoplasmic domain. Marked DISPUTED because PMID:27231345 later failed to detect any IL-16-CD4 interaction by NMR or on CD4-expressing cells; the two annotations GO:0042011 and GO:0042012 rest on this contested relationship.

title: Proteomic-based identification of CD4-interacting proteins in human primary macrophages.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Proteomic identification of CD4-interacting proteins in human primary macrophages; cited only for the constitutive recycling of CD4 in macrophages, not for any interaction-based annotation (the dataset is a large-scale affinity proteomic screen).

title: Affinity maturation of human CD4 by yeast surface display and crystal structure of a CD4-HLA-DR1 complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Crystal structure of an affinity-matured human CD4 bound to HLA-DR1; gives the atomic description of the CD4-binding site on MHC class II (invariant alpha-2 and beta-2 residues) and states the wild-type affinity as >400 uM. Cited by UniProt for the D1-MHCII domain assignment.

title: CD4 ligation on human blood monocytes triggers macrophage differentiation and enhances HIV infection.
review_notes: PubMed-verified for the monocyte work: MHC class II ligation of CD4 drives MAPK- and Src-kinase-dependent macrophage differentiation of human blood monocytes. Cached abstract-only, and the abstract does not mention IL-15 or GM-CSF, for which GOA nonetheless carries IDA rows citing this paper; those rows are left UNDECIDED.

title: Remarkably low affinity of CD4/peptide-major histocompatibility complex class II protein interactions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Two-dimensional and SPR measurement of the CD4/peptide-MHC class II interaction, reported as the weakest such interaction studied; the quantitative basis for treating CD4 as co-recruited rather than independently ligating.

title: The CD4 and CD3δε Cytosolic Juxtamembrane Regions Are Proximal within a Compact TCR-CD3-pMHC-CD4 Macrocomplex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. FRET between CD4 and CD3-delta cytosolic juxtamembrane regions on concurrent engagement of the same agonist pMHC. Supports the proximity argument used to mark the part_of T cell receptor complex row over-annotated: CD4 is brought close to CD3 on ligand binding rather than being a subunit.

title: Structure of a Potential Therapeutic Antibody Bound to Interleukin-16 (IL-16): MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS AND NEW THERAPEUTIC OPPORTUNITIES.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Structure of an anti-IL-16 Fab; also reports, by NMR with CD4 D1-D4 and D3D4 and by flow cytometry on CD4-expressing cells, that no IL-16-CD4 interaction could be detected. It is cited in GOA as the basis of a leukocyte chemotaxis NAS annotation on CD4, which is the opposite of what it concludes about CD4 binding; that row is removed.

title: Dual Role of CD4 in Peripheral T Lymphocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified review (Dual Role of CD4 in Peripheral T Lymphocytes). Source for microvillar-tip accumulation of CD4 and its dependence on LCK association; also the source of the caution that stable CD4 oligomers and discrete raft localization are not firmly established in living cells.

title: Complete Multilineage CD4 Expression Defect Associated With Warts Due to an Inherited Homozygous CD4 Gene Mutation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Human autosomal recessive CD4 deficiency (immunodeficiency 79) with recalcitrant HPV warts and double-negative T cells substituting for the CD4+ compartment; used for the loss-of-function phenotype in the description, not for any annotation action.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. A large yeast two-hybrid neurodegeneration interactome; the CD4-LAMP2 and CD4-SH3GLB1 rows are screen-level hits with no CD4-directed follow-up.

title: Helper T cell immunity in humans with inherited CD4 deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Seven patients from five families with biallelic deleterious CD4 variants: no detectable CD4+ T cells, expanded helper-like TCRab CD4-CD8- double-negative cells, retained but reduced HLA-II-restricted responses. Also characterises the short isoform 2, which binds LCK but not HLA class II. Used for the description and for two suggested questions; no annotation action rests on it.

title: Oligomerization of CD4 is required for stable binding to class II major histocompatibility complex proteins but not for interaction with human immunodeficiency virus gp120.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Shows by dominant-negative F43I co-expression that CD4 oligomerization is required for stable class II binding but not for gp120 binding -- the key distinction between the physiological and the viral interaction.

title: Role of CD4 and CD8 in T cell activation and differentiation.
review_notes: A 1993 Advances in Immunology review, cached abstract-only. GOA uses it for four NAS rows (immune response, coreceptor activity, MHC class II protein binding, T cell receptor complex). Its assertions are consistent with the primary literature except the T cell receptor complex part_of row, which is marked over-annotated.

title: A Zn2+ ion links the cytoplasmic tail of CD4 and the N-terminal region of Lck.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Demonstrates a single Zn2+ ion linking the CD4 tail and the Lck N-terminal region, with EDTA-sensitive assembly and a cysteine requirement; the biochemical companion to PMID:14500983.

title: CD4 deep research report (falcon / Edison Scientific)
review_notes: Falcon deep-research report generated for this review (Edison Scientific, 40 citations). Its substantive claims were checked against primary literature: the coreceptor/LCK mechanism, the weak pMHCII affinity, the CD4-CD3 macrocomplex, microvillar localization, macrophage recycling and the 2024 inherited-deficiency cohort all trace to papers now cached here. It correctly insists that CCR5/CXCR4, not CD4, are the HIV entry coreceptors and that LCK, not CD4, is the kinase. It contains no claim that changed an annotation action; its main caveats (that raft and oligomerization models are incompletely established in living cells) are recorded in the notes.

title: CDH23: catenin, neuronal and calcium process scope

title: Falcon deep research report for CDK2
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/Falcon) of recent CDK2 reviews and primary literature. Accurately summarizes the canonical CDK2 biology already captured in this review (cyclin E/A binding, Thr160/CAK activation, nuclear G1/S and S-phase roles, RB1/E2F pathway, NPAT/histone and centrosome substrates). Useful additions that strengthen specific annotations: (1) the proline-directed S/T-P substrate motif with quantitative support from an analog-sensitive in situ nuclear phosphorylation screen (Chi et al. 2020, Sci Adv) and a kinome-wide specificity atlas (Johnson et al. 2023, Nature); (2) a broad nuclear CDK2 substrate landscape (~117 candidates). Several cited PMIDs (Chi 2020, Johnson 2023, Fagundes & Teixeira 2021) are NOT in the local publications cache and were not independently verified here, so correctness is left UNVERIFIED; the report also occasionally over-states (e.g., framing CDK2 as the "canonical" Rb kinase, whereas CDK4/6 initiate and CDK2 completes Rb hyperphosphorylation, and CDK2 is dispensable for the mitotic cell cycle).

title: Falcon deep research report for CDK4
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/Falcon) of CDK4 reviews and primary literature. Accurately captures canonical CDK4 biology used in this review (D-cyclin binding, Thr172/T-loop activation, INK4 and CIP/KIP regulation, nuclear G1/S RB-kinase role, RB1/RBL1/RBL2 substrates, Hsp90-Cdc37 chaperoning). Several cited secondary reviews are not in the local publications cache and were not independently verified, so correctness is left UNVERIFIED.

title: Mechanism of CDK5/p25 binding by CDK inhibitors.

title: Microtubule association of the neuronal p35 activator of Cdk5.

title: Cdk5: multitasking between physiological and pathological conditions.

title: Memory enhancement by targeting Cdk5 regulation of NR2B.
review_notes: Cached full-text record supports CDK5 phosphorylation of NR2B/GluN2B and regulation of NMDA receptor surface expression, synaptic transmission, and memory.

title: CDK5-cyclin B1 regulates mitotic fidelity.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified (PMID:39232161, Nature 2024). title: p35 is a neural-specific regulatory subunit of cyclin-dependent kinase 5.

title: Conversion of p35 to p25 deregulates Cdk5 activity and promotes neurodegeneration.

title: Identification of a novel, membrane-associated neuronal kinase, cyclin-dependent kinase 5/p35-regulated kinase.
review_notes: Cached full-text record supports p35 interaction with a membrane-associated neuronal kinase and CDK5/p35-dependent regulation, useful for non-core binding/regulatory context.

title: Mechanism of CDK5/p25 binding by CDK inhibitors.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports the CDK5/p25 structural complex and inhibitor-binding context; relevant to p25-containing CDK5R1 complexes.

title: Microtubule association of the neuronal p35 activator of Cdk5.

title: Myristoylation of p39 and p35 is a determinant of cytoplasmic or nuclear localization of active cyclin-dependent kinase 5 complexes.

title: p35 is a neural-specific regulatory subunit of cyclin-dependent kinase 5.

title: Falcon deep research report for CDKN1B
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/Falcon). Its account of the canonical biology matches the primary literature reviewed here: the intrinsically disordered Cip/Kip architecture and KID (~residues 25-93), inhibition of cyclin E/A-CDK2, the context-dependent cyclin D-CDK4/6 assembly role, Ser10/CRM1 export, Thr157/Thr198-14-3-3 cytoplasmic retention, and CDK2-dependent Thr187 phosphorylation feeding CKS1-SCF(SKP2) degradation. It is cited here only for the cytoplasmic non-CDK functions it summarises. Left UNVERIFIED because its citations are to internal document keys (e.g. 'cusan2018landscapeofcdkn1b', 'bencivenga2025p27kip1andtumors') rather than PMIDs and could not be resolved against the publication cache; its clinical/prognostic sections were not used for any annotation decision.

title: Cysteine dioxygenase: modulation of expression in human cell lines by cytokines and control of sulphate production.

title: Functional characterization and regulation of the taurine transporter and cysteine dioxygenase in human hepatoblastoma HepG2 cells.

title: An insight into the mechanism of human cysteine dioxygenase. Key roles of the thioether-bonded tyrosine-cysteine cofactor.

title: Covariation MS uncovers a protein that controls cysteine catabolism.

title: Molecular and functional characterization of the Drosophila melanogaster conserved smORFome.
review_notes: Establishes fly orthology and a conditional organismal phenotype; no molecular mechanism.

title: Survivin and the inner centromere protein INCENP show similar cell-cycle localization and gene knockout phenotype.

title: Synergistic interaction of lovastatin and paclitaxel in human cancer cells.

title: GW182 is critical for the stability of GW bodies expressed during the cell cycle and cell proliferation.

title: Centromere protein F includes two sites that couple efficiently to depolymerizing microtubules.
review_notes: Direct MT binding and force coupling by both CENP-F termini.

title: Mutations in centrosomal protein CEP152 in primary microcephaly families linked to MCPH4.
review_notes: PubMed record and cached abstract were checked; the study links biallelic CEP152 variants to microcephaly and tests centrosome localization of a truncating allele.

title: Architectural basis for cylindrical self-assembly governing Plk4-mediated centriole duplication in human cells.

title: Upstream of growth and differentiation factor 1 (uog1), a mammalian homolog of the yeast longevity assurance gene 1 (LAG1), regulates N-stearoyl-sphinganine (C18-(dihydro)ceramide) synthesis in a fumonisin B1-independent manner in mammalian cells.

title: Impairment of ceramide synthesis causes a novel progressive myoclonus epilepsy.
review_notes: EPM8-defining study; CerS1 is an ER transmembrane protein catalyzing C18-ceramide biosynthesis, and the H183Q variant reduces C18-ceramide with impaired activity. Supports core MF/BP/CC and disease.

title: Eleven residues determine the acyl chain specificity of ceramide synthases.
review_notes: Maps the acyl-chain-length specificity determinants of the CerS family (context for CERS1 C18 selectivity). Cited for a sphingomyelin-biosynthesis IDA that is a contributory/non-core process.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Identification and characterization of a set of conserved and new regulators of cytoskeletal organization, cell morphology and migration.

title: Axonemal structures reveal mechanoregulatory and disease mechanisms.
review_notes: Cryo-EM atomic model of the human respiratory-cilia axoneme (PDB 8J07) directly resolves CFAP61 as a structural subunit at the base of radial spoke 3 (RS3), confirming its axonemal localization and radial-spoke association; the GTP/GDP/Mg ligands in the structure belong to axonemal tubulin, not CFAP61, so no GTPase/ nucleotide-binding function is attributable to CFAP61.

title: Interaction mapping of endoplasmic reticulum ubiquitin ligases identifies modulators of innate immune signalling.

title: Falcon deep research report for CGRRF1
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis; not independently verified for every claim. title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Cholesterol 25-Hydroxylase inhibits SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses by depleting membrane cholesterol.

title: Cholesterol 25-hydroxylase suppresses SARS-CoV-2 replication by blocking membrane fusion.

title: cDNA cloning of mouse and human cholesterol 25-hydroxylases, polytopic membrane proteins that synthesize a potent oxysterol regulator of lipid metabolism.

title: Cholesterol is hydroxylated to 25-hydroxycholesterol
review_notes: Reactome reaction correctly capturing the cholesterol->25-HC step. However it is the source of the "cytosol" location TAS annotation, which mislocalizes this ER multi-pass membrane enzyme; the reaction chemistry is right but the compartment assignment is not.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.

title: CHAC1/MGC4504 is a novel proapoptotic component of the unfolded protein response, downstream of the ATF4-ATF3-CHOP cascade.

title: Falcon deep research report for CHAF1B
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon); claims are machine-aggregated and not independently verified, so marked UNVERIFIED. The report's own summary table usefully distinguishes CHAF1B/p60 subunit-specific evidence from broader CAF-1 holo-complex inference. The strongest subunit-specific claims trace to the Liu et al. 2023 Science cryo-EM structure (add8673): that the p60 subunit is the principal H3-H4 binding component, contacting histone H4 through its ventral beta-propeller surface and engaging a partially unfolded H3 region, and that CHAF1B is required for CAF-1 histone binding and nucleosome assembly activity. The report also surfaces a CHAF1B-specific genome-stability function (Shrestha et al. 2023, jcs.260944): CHAF1B depletion causes CENP-A mislocalization and chromosomal instability. Many other statements (PCNA recruitment, heterochromatin/H3K9me3-H3K27me3 maintenance, viral latency, transcriptional/cell-fate control, cancer overexpression) are attributed to the CAF-1 holo-complex or to CHAF1B knockdown phenotypes rather than to a direct, isolated p60 molecular activity, and should not be transferred to CHAF1B as subunit-specific molecular functions without primary-source verification. None of the underlying primary papers are in the publications cache; supporting_text quotes below are verbatim from this report, not from the primary articles.

However, the report's annotation-set enumeration is wrong in two ways that undercut its recommendations, so its verdict was not adopted. (1) It reports the GO:0042026 ISS (GO_REF:0000024) as positive supporting evidence; in CRYAA-goa.tsv that row is NOT|involved_in from bovine UniProtKB:P02470, i.e. it refutes rather than supports the hypothesis. This is the single most decisive datum for the seed hypothesis and the run missed it. (2) Its headline recommendation, ADD the "missing" GO:0051082 (unfolded protein binding), is a no-op -- GOA already carries three GO:0051082 annotations for P02489 (IBA GO_REF:0000033; IPI PMID:8943244 with UniProtKB:P07320; IMP PMID:18407550) -- and is also obsolete advice, since GO:0051082 is now a formally obsolete term whose GO obsoletion note directs replacement to GO:0044183 or GO:0140309 -- neither of which fits an in-situ holdase, so the run's "add GO:0051082" advice is doubly unusable. Pathway/disease claims (ATF4/ISR, JAK2/IFN-gamma immunity, mitotic translation, RAN-translation suppression, neurodevelopment) are largely heterodimer- or MCTS1-centric inferences and not DENR-only molecular functions. title: Overexpression of human diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1, acyl-coa:cholesterol acyltransferase 1, or acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase 2 stimulates secretion of apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins in McA-RH7777 cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Overexpression of human DGAT1 in rat hepatoma cells increases TG synthesis and VLDL/apoB secretion. Supports a contributory role in VLDL assembly / lipid transport, but the effect is via TG loading in an overexpression system, not a demonstrated physiological requirement.

title: Acyl coenzyme A dependent retinol esterification by acyl coenzyme A: diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Biochemically demonstrates DGAT1 acyl-CoA:retinol acyltransferase (ARAT) activity (EC 2.3.1.76) with defined Km values; DGAT1 is the major ARAT in Caco-2 cells. Establishes the secondary retinol-esterifying activity.

title: AGPAT6 is a novel microsomal glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract is about AGPAT6/GPAT4, a different enzyme; DGAT1 GO:0019432 (IDA) is attributed here (likely DGAT1 assayed as a comparator in the full text, which is not in the cache). The assigned function (TAG biosynthesis) is DGAT1's true core function.

title: Molecular identification of a novel mammalian brain isoform of acyl-CoA:lysophospholipid acyltransferase with prominent ethanolamine lysophospholipid acylating activity, LPEAT2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract is about LPEAT2 (AYTL3/AGPAT7), a different enzyme; DGAT1 GO:0004144 (IDA, MGI) and GO:0019432 (IDA) are attributed here, presumably from DGAT1 used as a positive control in the full text (not in cache). Assigned DGAT function is correct for DGAT1; not removed per experimental-annotation policy.

title: Diacylglycerol acyltransferase-1 localizes hepatitis C virus NS5A protein to lipid droplets and enhances NS5A interaction with the viral capsid core.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. DGAT1 forms a complex with HCV NS5A and core proteins and guides them to lipid droplets; supports the GO:0005515 protein binding (IPI) annotation (physical interaction with viral NS5A). A host-pathogen interaction, not a core cellular function.

title: Synthesis of neutral ether lipid monoalkyl-diacylglycerol by lipid acyltransferases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. DGAT1 uses 1-monoalkylglycerol as an acyl acceptor to synthesize monoalkyl-mono/di-acylglycerol; DGAT1 is the predominant enzyme for intracellular MADAG synthesis in CHO-K1 cells. Demonstrates broad acyl-acceptor specificity including a monoacylglycerol-acylation step.

title: Structure and mechanism of human diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Cryo-EM structure of human DGAT1 in complex with oleoyl-CoA; defines the nine-TM MBOAT fold, the ER-membrane reaction chamber, the catalytic His415/Glu416, and the homodimer/homotetramer states. Primary source for the MF (GO:0004144), CC, and IPI (self) annotations.

title: Structure and catalytic mechanism of a human triacylglycerol-synthesis enzyme.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Independent cryo-EM structure of dimeric human DGAT1; establishes the catalytic mechanism, MBOAT-family assignment, and broad acyl-acceptor specificity. Primary source for the MF (GO:0004144), CC, and IPI (self) annotations.

title: Characterization of two human genes encoding acyl coenzyme A:cholesterol acyltransferase-related enzymes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Original characterization of human ARGP1 (=DGAT1) as an ACAT-related gene product predicted to perform the last acylation in triglyceride biosynthesis. Source of the TAS acyltransferase and triglyceride-metabolism annotations.

title: Identification of a gene encoding an acyl CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase, a key enzyme in triacylglycerol synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Original cloning of a DGAT (mouse ortholog) establishing that DGAT catalyzes the terminal and only committed step of TAG synthesis (EC 2.3.1.20). Source of the TAS GO:0004144 annotation for the human gene.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation pathway; used to place DGAT1 at the plasma membrane and specific granule membrane. These localizations do not reflect the physiological ER-membrane site of DGAT1 catalysis and drive over-annotated CC terms.

title: 1,2-diacyl-glycerol + acyl-CoA => triacylglycerol + CoASH [DGAT1]
review_notes: Reactome reaction correctly describing tetrameric DGAT1 at the ER membrane catalyzing DAG + acyl-CoA -> TAG + CoASH. Supports the core MF and ER-membrane CC.

title: Cloning of DGAT2, a second mammalian diacylglycerol acyltransferase, and related family members.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original cloning/characterization of DGAT2; directly supports the core diacylglycerol O-acyltransferase activity and TAG biosynthesis annotations.

title: A novel diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT2) is decreased in human psoriatic skin and increased in diabetic mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports ER localization (IDA) and the terminal role of DGAT2 in triglyceride synthesis.

title: Acyl coenzyme A dependent retinol esterification by acyl coenzyme A: diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1.
review_notes: Abstract foregrounds DGAT1 as the major ARAT, but the paper establishes the ARAT side activity for DGAT-family enzymes; the EXP DGAT2 annotations reflect the full assay set. Not removable on abstract grounds.

title: Biochemical characterization of human acyl coenzyme A: 2-monoacylglycerol acyltransferase-3 (MGAT3).
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the paper characterizes MGAT3 but explicitly assays and compares DGAT2 (DGAT activity, ER membrane/lipid droplet localization), supporting the IDA annotations for DGAT2.

title: Synthesis of neutral ether lipid monoalkyl-diacylglycerol by lipid acyltransferases.
review_notes: Full text available; supports the minor monoacylglycerol/ether-lipid side activity (IDA GO:0006640). DGAT2 is a minor contributor (~35-fold selective for 1-MOG).

title: The ER-Localized Protein DFCP1 Modulates ER-Lipid Droplet Contact Formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; underlies the DGAT2-SLC27A1 IPI (WITH UniProtKB:Q6PCB7) and the UniProt SUBUNIT statement about SLC27A1/ZFYVE1.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput NK-cell membrane proteome; supports only a generic membrane localization, not a specific function of DHCR7.

title: Identification and pharmacological characterization of cholesterol-5,6-epoxide hydrolase as a target for tamoxifen and AEBS ligands.
review_notes: Establishes that DHCR7 with EBP forms the AEBS carrying cholesterol-5,6-epoxide hydrolase activity; a genuine secondary (moonlighting) activity, non-core.

title: The terminal enzymes of cholesterol synthesis, DHCR24 and DHCR7, interact physically and functionally.
review_notes: Full-text available; demonstrates DHCR7-DHCR24 physical/functional interaction and the cholesterol/vitamin D3 partitioning role of DHCR7.

title: TMEM147 interacts with lamin B receptor, regulates its localization and levels, and affects cholesterol homeostasis.
review_notes: Reports a physical interaction between DHCR7 and TMEM147 affecting DHCR7 protein levels and cholesterol homeostasis.

title: 7-Dehydrocholesterol is an endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis.
review_notes: Establishes DHCR7 as pro-ferroptotic via depletion of the anti-ferroptotic metabolite 7-DHC; includes active-site mutagenesis confirming reductase activity.

title: 7-Dehydrocholesterol dictates ferroptosis sensitivity.
review_notes: Full-text available; independent confirmation of DHCR7's pro-ferroptotic role and its 7-DHC reductase function in distal cholesterol biosynthesis.

title: Molecular cloning and expression of the human delta7-sterol reductase.
review_notes: Primary cloning/characterization; directly establishes the NADPH-dependent 7-DHC reductase (EC 1.3.1.21) core function.

title: The human lamin B receptor/sterol reductase multigene family.
review_notes: Establishes DHCR7 as a member of the LBR/sterol-reductase family localized to the endoplasmic reticulum.

title: Identification and characterization of a cDNA encoding a long-chain cis-isoprenyltranferase involved in dolichyl monophosphate biosynthesis in the ER of brain cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; establishes hCIT/DHDDS as the ER cis-isoprenyltransferase for Dol-P biosynthesis (rescues yeast rer2 and sec59 defects; colocalizes with calnexin in the ER). Supports the ER localization (IDA) and dolichyl monophosphate biosynthesis annotations.

title: In vivo interaction between the human dehydrodolichyl diphosphate synthase and the Niemann-Pick C2 protein revealed by a yeast two-hybrid system.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; documents the DHDDS-NPC2 (P61916) interaction by Y2H and co-IP. Supports the ancillary protein-binding annotation but not the core catalytic function.

title: Mutation of Nogo-B receptor, a subunit of cis-prenyltransferase, causes a congenital disorder of glycosylation.
review_notes: Full text available. Although titled around NgBR/NUS1, the study reconstitutes cis-PTase from human hCIT (DHDDS) plus NgBR in a yeast triple-KO and shows both are required, directly supporting the DHDDS catalytic-activity and complex annotations.

title: A conserved C-terminal RXG motif in the NgBR subunit of cis-prenyltransferase is critical for prenyltransferase activity.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; first purification of the heteromeric cis-PT, showing both NgBR and hCIT (DHDDS) subunits function in catalysis and substrate binding. Supports the catalytic-activity, complex, and Dol-P biosynthesis annotations.

title: Structural elucidation of the cis-prenyltransferase NgBR/DHDDS complex reveals insights in regulation of protein glycosylation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but the abstract explicitly frames cis-PTase as the rate-limiting step in glycosyl carrier lipid synthesis and reports the human NgBR/DHDDS crystal structure. Supports MF, complex, and ER localization annotations.

title: Structural basis of heterotetrameric assembly and disease mutations in the human cis-prenyltransferase complex.
review_notes: Full text available. Crystal structure and enzymology of the human cis-PT heterotetramer; shows the sole active site is within DHDDS (FPP/IPP/Mg2+ binding). Strongly supports the DHDDS catalytic-activity core function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput BioPlex interactome study; source of an IPI capturing the DHDDS-NUS1 (Q96E22) interaction. Correct but uninformative as bare protein binding.

title: Identification and characterization of short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase 3 (DHRS3) deficiency, a retinoic acid embryopathy of humans.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read; directly establishes DHRS3's physiological role in retinoic-acid homeostasis and development, its ER-membrane RDH10 complex, and the effect of loss-of-function on retinoid levels. Source of the IMP annotation for retinoic acid biosynthetic process.

title: Molecular characterization of a novel short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase that reduces all-trans-retinal.
review_notes: Abstract only (full_text_available: false), but the abstract itself supports the reductase activity, Rossmann-fold nucleotide binding, cone-photoreceptor localization and broader retinol-metabolism role. Establishes EC 1.1.1.300 (per UniProt CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, ECO:0000269|PubMed:9705317).

title: A nonsense mutation in DHTKD1 causes Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 in a large Chinese pedigree.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes DHTKD1 loss-of-function in CMT2Q and reports mitochondrial localization and impaired ATP/NAD(H) on silencing. Cited correctly for the mitochondrion (IDA) and energy (IMP) annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 AP-MS interactome. Correctly cited as the source of a high-throughput protein-binding IPI, but not a directed study of DHTKD1 function; the recorded partner is not functionally informative.

title: The mitochondrial 2-oxoadipate and 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes share their E2 and E3 components for their function and both generate reactive oxygen species.
review_notes: Primary biochemical characterization of human E1a (DHTKD1): ThDP-dependent 2-oxoadipate decarboxylation, ~49x preference for 2-oxoadipate over 2-oxoglutarate, and recruitment of shared E2/E3. Anchors the core MF and complex annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary Y2H interactome. Source of a high-throughput protein-binding IPI; not a directed DHTKD1 study and functionally uninformative for this gene.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex-derived proteome-scale interactome. Source of a high-throughput protein-binding IPI; not functionally informative for DHTKD1.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP high-confidence mitochondrial proteome; independently confirms DHTKD1 mitochondrial localization.

review_notes: Core DIABLO/SMAC apoptosis evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract.

review_notes: Core DIABLO/SMAC apoptosis evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract.

review_notes: Core DIABLO/SMAC apoptosis evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract.

title: Structural and biochemical basis of apoptotic activation by Smac/DIABLO.
review_notes: Core DIABLO/SMAC apoptosis evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract.

review_notes: Supports a specific IAP-family or IAP-antagonist interaction context in the DIABLO review.

review_notes: Supports a specific IAP-family or IAP-antagonist interaction context in the DIABLO review.

review_notes: Supports a specific IAP-family or IAP-antagonist interaction context in the DIABLO review.

review_notes: Supports a specific IAP-family or IAP-antagonist interaction context in the DIABLO review.

review_notes: Supports a specific IAP-family or IAP-antagonist interaction context in the DIABLO review.

review_notes: Supports a specific IAP-family or IAP-antagonist interaction context in the DIABLO review.

review_notes: Core DIABLO/SMAC apoptosis evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract.

review_notes: Recent BIRC6 structural evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract and used to interpret the BRUCE/BIRC6 antagonist row.

review_notes: Recent BIRC6 structural evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract and used to interpret the BRUCE/BIRC6 antagonist row.

title: Structural basis for SMAC-mediated antagonism of caspase inhibition by the giant ubiquitin ligase BIRC6.
review_notes: Recent BIRC6 structural evidence verified against the cached PubMed abstract and used to interpret the BRUCE/BIRC6 antagonist row.

title: Crystal structure of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 3 bound to lipoyl domain 2 of human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Structurally characterizes the DLAT lipoyl-domain-2/PDK3 interaction; supports the (uninformative) protein-binding IPI but not a core function.

title: Distinct structural mechanisms for inhibition of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase isoforms by AZD7545, dichloroacetate, and radicicol.
review_notes: PDK3-inhibitor structural study using DLAT lipoyl domain 2; source of a bare protein-binding IPI, peripheral to DLAT's core function.

title: Extended polypeptide linkers establish the spatial architecture of a pyruvate dehydrogenase multienzyme complex.
review_notes: Establishes the E2 central core architecture and the shuttling role of E2 lipoyl domains; supports the structural core function.

title: Structures of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex cores: a highly conserved catalytic center with flexible N-terminal domains.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the human E2 core; identifies E2 as the central component forming the PDC catalytic core.

title: Binding of pyruvate dehydrogenase to the core of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Maps the E1(beta)-E2 subunit-binding interaction; supports E1 assembly onto the E2 core.

title: Subunit and catalytic component stoichiometries of an in vitro reconstituted human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Establishes DLAT (E2p) as part of the 60-meric dodecahedral PDC core and its stoichiometry.

title: Interaction of E1 and E3 components with the core proteins of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Source of the UniProt EC 2.3.1.12 catalytic-activity assignment; describes E2 transferring the acetyl moiety to CoA to form acetyl-CoA.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial phosphoproteome; supports mitochondrial localization only.

title: Component co-expression and purification of recombinant human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex from baculovirus infected SF9 cells.
review_notes: Functional reconstitution of the recombinant human PDC; supports DLAT's role in the pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA reaction and complex membership.

title: Sirtuin 4 is a lipoamidase regulating pyruvate dehydrogenase complex activity.
review_notes: Identifies DLAT K132/K259 lipoyl sites and the SIRT4 delipoylation regulatory mechanism; explicitly states DLAT constitutes the PDH catalytic core.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex); source of a bare protein-binding IPI, not informative for core function.

title: Nucleotide sequence of a cDNA for the dihydrolipoamide acetyltransferase component of human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Founding cDNA report identifying DLAT as the E2 (dihydrolipoamide acetyltransferase) component of the human PDC.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex 3.0); source of bare protein-binding IPIs, not informative for core function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization only.

title: Assembly and full functionality of recombinantly expressed dihydrolipoyl acetyltransferase component of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Recombinant human E2 with high acetyltransferase activity assembling into the pentagonal dodecahedron core; supports both catalytic and structural-core functions.

title: Dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase-binding protein of the human pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. DNA-derived amino acid sequence, expression, and reconstitution of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.
review_notes: Title foregrounds E3BP (protein X), but the full-text reconstitution assays the E2 core; the associated IDA/IC annotations to DLAT are curator-derived from that work and are accepted.

title: Physical interaction of Delta1, Jagged1, and Jagged2 with Notch1 and Notch3 receptors.
review_notes: Abstract confirms direct DSL ligand-Notch binding assays.

title: Delta proteins and MAGI proteins: an interaction of Notch ligands with intracellular scaffolding molecules and its significance for zebrafish development.
review_notes: Mostly zebrafish/mouse proteins; supports PDZ-binding, not Tat binding.

title: Intrinsic selectivity of Notch 1 for Delta-like 4 over Delta-like 1.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; biochemical binding and reporter assays.

title: Regulated release of ERdj3 from unfolded proteins by BiP.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches; Results show ERdj3 binds unfolded substrates and stimulates BiP ATPase, supporting DNAJB11's core ER co-chaperone/Hsp70-recruitment function.

title: Monoallelic Mutations to DNAJB11 Cause Atypical Autosomal-Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJB11 is a BiP co-factor whose monoallelic loss-of-function causes atypical ADPKD with PC1/PKD1 maturation and trafficking defects, supporting the gene's in-vivo ER co-chaperone function.

title: Mutations in DNAJB13, Encoding an HSP40 Family Member, Cause Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia and Male Infertility.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms biallelic DNAJB13 mutations cause PCD and male infertility via axonemal/radial-spoke and sperm flagellar defects, and GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0031514/GO:0036126/GO:1904158 (IDA/IMP), supporting DNAJB13's core cilium/flagellum axoneme role.

title: Differential requirements of IQUB for the assembly of radial spoke 1 and the motility of mouse cilia and flagella.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJB13 is a radial-spoke-1 stalk component in mammalian sperm flagella. Corroborates the RS1/cilium-motility role (GOA anchors this PMID as NAS for radial spoke and sperm flagellum); supporting rather than primary functional evidence.

title: The diverse members of the mammalian HSP70 machine show distinct chaperone-like activities.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; the study characterizes mammalian HSP40/HSP70 co-chaperones' anti-aggregation/refolding activities. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0051087 (protein-folding chaperone binding, IPI) and GO:0005829 (cytosol, IDA), supporting DNAJB4's core co-chaperone function.

title: Binding of human nucleotide exchange factors to heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) generates functionally distinct complexes in vitro.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DnaJB4 acts as a J-protein co-chaperone stimulating Hsp70 ATPase activity, and GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0001671 (ATPase activator activity, IDA) - the core MF.

title: Loss of function variants in DNAJB4 cause a myopathy with early respiratory failure.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms biallelic DNAJB4 loss-of-function causes a myopathy with respiratory failure and that DNAJB4 localizes to the Z-disc with a role in myofibril proteostasis. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0030018 (Z disc, IDA), supporting the in-vivo function.

title: Hsc40, a new member of the hsp40 family, exhibits similar expression profile to that of hsc70 in mammalian cells.
review_notes: Original characterization of DNAJB5/Hsc40 (title plausibly supports HSP40-family membership and stress-inducible expression; GOA cites it for GO:0006986 response to unfolded protein, IEP), but the publication is not cached so the supporting text could not be confirmed against a checkable source.

title: The diverse members of the mammalian HSP70 machine show distinct chaperone-like activities.
review_notes: Anchored to GOA evidence - this PMID is cited for DNAJB5's GO:0051087 (protein-folding chaperone binding, IPI) and GO:0005829 (cytosol, IDA) - establishing DNAJB5's core cytosolic HSP70 co-chaperone function. Cached text is the family-wide HSP70-machine study; gene-specific detail confirmed via the GOA annotation rather than the cached abstract.

title: The SANT2 domain of the murine tumor cell DnaJ-like protein 1 human homologue interacts with alpha1-antichymotrypsin and kinetically interferes with its serpin inhibitory activity.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC1/MTJ1/ERdj1's lumenal J-domain stimulates BiP/GRP78 ATPase and its SANT2 domain binds SERPINA3. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0001671 (ATPase activator activity, TAS) and GO:0050708/GO:0045861, supporting the gene's core ER co-chaperone function.

title: ERdj4 and ERdj5 are required for endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein degradation of misfolded surfactant protein C.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms ERdj5/DNAJC10 is required for ERAD of misfolded substrate and acts via stimulation of BiP ATPase. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0036503 (ERAD pathway, IMP), GO:0034663 and GO:0051787, supporting DNAJC10's ER-chaperone/ERAD role.

title: ERdj5 is the ER reductase that catalyzes the removal of non-native disulfides and correct folding of the LDL receptor.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms ERdj5/DNAJC10 is the ER protein-disulfide reductase that removes non-native disulfides and folds LDLR in a BiP-dependent manner. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0015035 (protein-disulfide reductase activity, IDA) - the core MF.

title: A splicing mutation in the novel mitochondrial protein DNAJC11 causes motor neuron pathology associated with cristae disorganization, and lymphoid abnormalities in mice.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC11 localizes to the mitochondrial outer membrane in a high-MW complex and that a hypomorphic mutation causes cristae disorganization. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0005741 (mitochondrial outer membrane, EXP) - the core localization/function.

title: QIL1 is a novel mitochondrial protein required for MICOS complex stability and cristae morphology.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC11 associates with the MICOS/SAM (MIB) complex. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0140275 (MIB complex, IDA) and GO:0005739, supporting DNAJC11's MIB-complex membership.

title: Evolution and structural organization of the mitochondrial contact site (MICOS) complex and the mitochondrial intermembrane space bridging (MIB) complex.
review_notes: Cached publication confirms DNAJC11 as a MICOS/MIB component; GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0140275 (MIB complex, HDA). Title corrected to verbatim PubMed.

title: The co-chaperone DNAJC12 binds to Hsc70 and is upregulated by endoplasmic reticulum stress.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC12 binds Hsc70 (HSPA8) and is a cytoplasmic stress-upregulated co-chaperone. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0005737 (cytoplasm, IDA) and GO:0005515, supporting DNAJC12's core J-domain co-chaperone function.

title: Biallelic Mutations in DNAJC12 Cause Hyperphenylalaninemia, Dystonia, and Intellectual Disability.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC12 is an HSP70 co-chaperone of the aromatic amino acid hydroxylases (PAH, TH, TPH) whose biallelic loss-of-function causes hyperphenylalaninemia with neurotransmitter deficiency, establishing the gene's in-vivo specific-client chaperone function.

title: Human RME-8 is involved in membrane trafficking through early endosomes.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC13/RME-8 localizes to early endosomes and is required for transferrin recycling and EGFR trafficking. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0005769/GO:0031901 (early endosome, EXP/IDA) and GO:2001135/GO:2000641 (IMP), supporting the core role.

title: RME-8 coordinates the activity of the WASH complex with the function of the retromer SNX dimer to control endosomal tubulation.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; body confirms DNAJC13/RME-8 binds FAM21/WASH and coordinates retromer SNX1 to control endosomal tubulation. GOA anchors this PMID to GO:0071203 (WASH complex, IDA), GO:0007032 (endosome organization, IMP) and GO:0010008, supporting the core endosomal-sorting role.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Cached; this PMID is cited only for a high-throughput membrane proteomics inclusion (GOA GO:0016020 membrane, HDA) and does not establish DNAJC14's core dopamine-receptor-export function, which in this review rests on the UniProt record rather than any literature PMID present here.

title: Methylation-controlled J-protein MCJ acts in the import of proteins into human mitochondria.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; Results confirm MCJ is an inner-membrane J-protein whose soluble J domain 'stimulates the ATPase activity of the human mtHsp70 chaperone, mortalin' and that interacts with the TIM23 translocase, supporting the import co-chaperone core function. Anchors the GOA IPI annotation (PMID:23263864).

title: MCJ/DnaJC15, an endogenous mitochondrial repressor of the respiratory chain that controls metabolic alterations.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; Results repeatedly establish MCJ as a 'respiratory chain' repressor that impairs supercomplex formation and negatively regulates complex I, supporting the negative-regulator-of-respiratory-chain core function (this PMID is cited in core_functions.supported_by).

title: ERdj8 governs the size of autophagosomes during the formation process.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; Results establish ERdj8 as an ER-membrane DnaJ protein that 'governs the size of autophagosomes', with overexpression enlarging autophagosomes via its DnaJ and TRX domains and ablation impairing engulfment of larger targets. Sole experimental reference establishing the core function (regulation of autophagosome size, GO:0016243) and ER-membrane localization (cited in core_functions.supported_by).

title: OpenScientist report on DNAJC16 J-domain and TRX activity
review_notes: Focused hypothesis review; its core topological premise follows UniProt's predicted type-IV topology for residues 26-535, but that conflicts with PMID:32492081's type-1 and ER-luminal wording and UniProt also retains a predicted cleaved signal peptide that is difficult to reconcile with a cytoplasmic 26-535 region. Treat the topology as unresolved pending direct experimental mapping.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Cached title matches the YAML title; this is a high-throughput endogenous-tagging cell-map study (not a DNAJC17-focused paper). It contributes only an IPI protein-binding annotation (to EFTUD2/Q15029, a spliceosome component), which is corroborating but background; it does not directly establish the core RNA-binding/spliceosome function.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Cached title matches the YAML title; large-scale multimodal cell-mapping study, not DNAJC17-specific. Supplies only an IPI protein-binding annotation (to EFTUD2/Q15029); background/corroborating relevance, does not establish the core function.

title: Mutation of DNAJC19, a human homologue of yeast inner mitochondrial membrane co-chaperones, causes DCMA syndrome, a novel autosomal recessive Barth syndrome-like condition.

title: DNAJC21 Mutations Link a Cancer-Prone Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome to Corruption in 60S Ribosome Subunit Maturation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; this is a systematic binary-interactome (Y2H) map, not a DNAJC22-focused study. The sole literature reference for this poorly characterized gene, and only background relevance.

title: Structure and mechanistic insights into novel iron-mediated moonlighting functions of human J-protein cochaperone, Dph4.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; the text establishes DPH4 as a J-protein cochaperone whose J-domain stimulates HSP70 ATPase activity, with an iron/zinc-binding redox-active CSL domain, supporting the ATPase-activator MF and diphthamide-biosynthesis role. Primary reference cited in core_functions.supported_by.

title: Immunotoxin resistance via reversible methylation of the DPH4 promoter is a unique survival strategy.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; the text confirms DPH4 is required for diphthamide biosynthesis on EF2 and that DPH4 silencing renders EF2 refractory to immunotoxins, corroborating the diphthamide-biosynthesis biological-process role (functional/disease context rather than direct MF characterization).

title: Falcon deep research report for DNAJC25
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report. The report itself warns "no contexts were retrieved, so this answer is not grounded in evidence" and that evidence gathering "experienced technical difficulties". SAFE, family-level claims that are usable: DNAJC25 is a J-domain/HSP40 protein inferred to act as an HSP70 co-chaperone (stimulating HSP70 ATPase to assist protein folding/quality control) with no intrinsic enzymatic activity and no experimentally identified clients — this only corroborates the existing IBA/IEA framing and adds no independent experimental weight. SPECULATIVE / NOT incorporated: (1) cytoplasmic localization (attributed to "review literature discussing DNAJC subfamily members", not to DNAJC25 directly, and it contradicts the UniProt multi-pass membrane / IBA ER-membrane evidence); (2) RNF149 substrate / hepatocellular-carcinoma tumor-suppressor role (Guo et al. 2023, cancers15215203) — a gene-specific functional claim drawn from an abstract in an ungrounded report and not independently verified here, so not added to existing_annotations or core_functions. Cited DOIs were not PubMed-verified in this review.

title: RJLs: a new family of Ras-related GTP-binding proteins.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; the text defines the RJL family of Ras-related GTP-binding proteins (DNAJC27/RBJ) and notes the chordate chimeric architecture with a C-terminal J domain, supporting the GTP-binding molecular function and J-domain co-chaperone framing of this gene.

title: Small GTPase RBJ mediates nuclear entrapment of MEK1/MEK2 in tumor progression.

Primary experimental reference for the MEK-ERK scaffold/positive-regulator core function; cited in core_functions.supported_by.

title: Promyelocytic leukemia protein interacts with the apoptosis-associated speck-like protein to limit inflammasome activation.

Sole literature reference for this poorly characterized gene; background relevance only.

title: Absence of BiP co-chaperone DNAJC3 causes diabetes mellitus and multisystemic neurodegeneration.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_25466870.md) PubMed title matches the YAML title exactly and establishes the in vivo physiological role of DNAJC3 as a BiP (HSPA5) co-chaperone: loss-of-function causes recessive diabetes mellitus with multisystemic neurodegeneration, corroborating the ER chaperone/UPR core function.

title: The P58 cellular inhibitor complexes with the interferon-induced, double-stranded RNA-dependent protein kinase, PKR, to regulate its autophosphorylation and activity.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_8576172.md) PubMed title matches the YAML title exactly and directly establishes that P58/DNAJC3 complexes with PKR and regulates its autophosphorylation/activity, supporting the core MF protein kinase inhibitor activity (GO:0004860). Full text not cached, but the title/abstract anchor the inhibitory-complex claim.

title: The 7q11.23 protein DNAJC30 interacts with ATP synthase and links mitochondria to brain development.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_30318146.md, full text available) title matches and establishes DNAJC30 as a mitochondrial inner-membrane protein that interacts with ATP synthase, supporting the enzyme binding core function and its role in the ATP-synthase machinery.

title: Impaired complex I repair causes recessive Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_33465056.md, full text available) title matches and establishes DNAJC30 as a chaperone required for complex I N-module subunit repair, with biallelic mutations causing recessive LHON, supporting the complex I repair chaperone core function.

title: Characterisation of a new human and murine member of the DnaJ family of proteins.
review_notes: Cached abstract verified. It establishes MCG18/DNAJC4 as a J-domain family member and predicts a membrane-spanning region, but reports no DNAJC4-specific folding, unfolded-protein-response, client-binding, HSP70-binding, or ATPase assay.

title: OpenScientist report on DNAJC4 HSP70 co-chaperone activity

title: Cysteine-string protein isoform beta (Cspbeta) is targeted to the trans-Golgi network as a non-palmitoylated CSP in clonal beta-cells.

title: Falcon deep research report for DNAJC5G
review_notes: LLM deep-research synthesis (no contexts retrieved per its own header; "this answer is not grounded in evidence but is instead a direct response from the agent model"), so all claims are UNVERIFIED pending primary-source checking. SAFE to use for DNAJC5G: J-domain HSP70 co-chaperone family inference and palmitoylated cysteine-string membrane anchoring (both family-level), plus the gene-specific testis/sperm detection and ring-shaped headpiece staining (attributed to Carapito et al. 2017 / Duek et al. 2016 proteomics, not yet independently verified here). title: Auxilin depletion causes self-assembly of clathrin into membraneless cages in vivo.

title: Endocytosis and clathrin-uncoating defects at synapses of auxilin knockout mice.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_20160091.md) PubMed title matches the YAML title exactly; abstract states auxilin acts as a co-chaperone supporting HSC70-dependent clathrin uncoating, and auxilin-knockout synapses accumulate clathrin-coated vesicles/empty cages with impaired endocytosis, directly supporting the clathrin-uncoating and synaptic-vesicle-recycling core functions (cited in core_functions).

title: Cofactor Tpr2 combines two TPR domains and a J domain to regulate the Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperone system.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_12853476.md) PubMed title matches the YAML title exactly; abstract states Tpr2/DNAJC7 recognizes both Hsp70 and Hsp90 via its TPR domains and that its J domain stimulates Hsp70 ATP hydrolysis, directly supporting the J-domain Hsp70-ATPase-stimulation and dual-TPR Hsp70/Hsp90-binding core functions (cited in core_functions).

title: Role of the cochaperone Tpr2 in Hsp90 chaperoning.

Full text not cached but abstract anchors the claim.

title: HDJC9, a novel human type C DnaJ/HSP40 member interacts with and cochaperones HSP70 through the J domain.

title: DNAJC9 integrates heat shock molecular chaperones into the histone chaperone network.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_33857403.md, full text available) PubMed title matches the YAML title exactly; establishes DNAJC9 as a histone H3-H4 chaperone that binds H3-H4 in a complex with MCM2 and recruits HSP70 via its J domain for nucleosome assembly, directly supporting all three core functions (cited as their primary supported_by).

title: Delta/notch-like epidermal growth factor (EGF)-related receptor, a novel EGF-like repeat-containing protein targeted to dendrites of developing and adult central nervous system neurons.

title: Genetic regulation of dihydropyrimidinase and its possible implication in altered uracil catabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Site-directed mutagenesis/expression of DPYS variants shows inactivating mutations reduce DHP activity and impair uracil catabolism; supports MF and BP annotations.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.

review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI binary interactome. Source of a bare protein-binding IPI; a high-throughput datapoint that is not functionally informative for DHP.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: PubMed-verified neurodegenerative-disease Y2H interactome. Source of a bare protein-binding IPI; high-throughput and not functionally informative for DHP.

title: Dihydropyrimidinase deficiency: structural organization, chromosomal localization, and mutation analysis of the human dihydropyrimidinase gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Characterizes the human DPYS gene and the first DHP-deficiency mutations; eukaryotic expression shows all mutations reduce enzyme activity. Supports MF, BP, zinc-binding (NAS), and disease context.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for DPYSL2 GO:0016812
review_notes: Focused OpenScientist report independently supports removal of GO:0016812 as CRMP pseudoenzyme over-propagation from active dihydropyrimidinases.

title: Collapsin response mediator protein 3 deacetylates histone H4 to mediate nuclear condensation and neuronal death.
review_notes: PMID/title and full article verified against PMC/Nature. Directly supports controlled mouse-CRMP3-associated deacetylation. This verifies the source and reported findings, not exclusive intrinsic catalytic attribution or an unambiguous human reagent assay.

title: OpenScientist assessment of CRMP3 deacetylase and broad hydrolase activity
review_notes: Read entire report and compared Methods/Results to the full primary article. Enzyme-attribution and replication uncertainties are useful, but full-length constructs were tested; HEK293 and Sf9 tags/purification differ; TSA sensitivity does not demonstrate contamination; NOT dihydropyrimidinase does not negate parent hydrolase terms. Exact reported sequence identities/residue maps lack delivered code or alignment artifacts and are not adopted as independently verified measurements.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Source of the two domain-based IEA hydrolase annotations (GO:0016787, GO:0016810). The InterPro2GO mapping fires on the metallo-hydrolase fold but DPYSL5 lacks the catalytic metal site; the activity annotations are not supported for this member.

title: Identification of CRAM, a novel unc-33 gene family protein that associates with CRMP3 and protein-tyrosine kinase(s) in the developing rat brain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary identification of CRMP5/CRAM; abstract read. Establishes CRMP-family membership and neuronal/developmental context.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports generic protein binding only.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput neurodegenerative-disease interactome; generic protein binding only.

title: Missense variants in DPYSL5 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with corpus callosum agenesis and cerebellar abnormalities.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary human genetics paper supporting the IMP negative-regulation-of-dendrite-morphogenesis annotation.

title: The Jumonji-C oxygenase JMJD7 catalyzes (3S)-lysyl hydroxylation of TRAFAC GTPases.
review_notes: Cached publication (publications/PMID_29915238.md) PubMed title matches the YAML title exactly; body explicitly names developmentally regulated GTP-binding proteins 1 and 2 (DRG1/2) as TRAFAC-family GTPases and JMJD7 substrates, supporting DRG2's core GTPase molecular function and the JMJD7 hydroxylation/RNA-binding context.

title: A novel GTP-binding protein which is selectively repressed in SV40 transformed fibroblasts.
review_notes: Original DRG2 cloning paper. Verified against a checkable anchor: UniProt P55039 (DRG2_HUMAN, 364 AA) cites PubMed=7929244 as its nucleotide sequence reference, and the cached abstract (364-aa, ~41 kDa GTP-binding protein with conserved G1-G5 motifs defining a new GTPase subfamily) matches DRG2. Establishes DRG2 as a GTP-binding protein, the basis for its core GTPase MF.

title: Falcon deep research report for DRG2
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) deep-research report; treated as UNVERIFIED pending primary-source checking. DRG2-SPECIFIC, well-anchored claims: DRG2 forms an obligate heterodimer with DFRP2/RWDD1 that stabilizes it against degradation; DRG2 is a JMJD7 substrate hydroxylated at Lys21 in the N-terminal HTH domain, which promotes RNA binding without altering stability/GTPase activity (Markolovic 2018, PMID:29915238); DRG2 localizes to cytoplasm, nucleus and Rab5-positive early endosomes; the DRG2-specific endosomal/Rab5 and PD-L1 recycling role derives from a genuine DRG2 paper (Choi 2024, doi:10.1038/s41420-024-02027-x). GENERALIZED / EXTRAPOLATED-FROM-PARALOG claims to treat cautiously: the 'general translation factor that rescues stalled/paused ribosomes and stimulates peptidyl transfer' mechanism rests on DRG1, bacterial Obg, and yeast Rbg2 orthologs plus 2024 preprints (jin2024/hawk2024, westrip2024), and the report itself states direct biochemical characterization of human DRG2 GTPase activity (e.g. K+-dependence) is limited and inferred from DRG1. The Gcn1-mediated collided-ribosome recruitment and DNAJC2/co-chaperone links are speculative. No annotation was added or removed on the basis of this report alone; it is used only to corroborate the existing ribosome/translation framing.

title: Structure and function of the c-myc DNA-unwinding element-binding protein DUE-B.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: Mechanism of chiral proofreading during translation of the genetic code.

title: A family of diverse Cul4-Ddb1-interacting proteins includes Cdt2, which is required for S phase destruction of the replication factor Cdt1.
review_notes: Establishes DTL/Cdt2 as a DCAF/substrate receptor of CUL4-DDB1; source of DDB1/CUL4 interaction, complex membership and DNA-damage-response annotations. R246A DDB1-binding mutant in UniProt.

title: CUL4-DDB1 ubiquitin ligase interacts with multiple WD40-repeat proteins and regulates histone methylation.
review_notes: Source of the DTL-DDB1 IntAct interaction; confirms DTL as a WD40 substrate receptor of CUL4-DDB1.

title: DTL/CDT2 is essential for both CDT1 regulation and the early G2/M checkpoint.
review_notes: Establishes both the CDT1-degradation and the G2/M checkpoint roles in zebrafish and human DTL; source of checkpoint and cell-cycle annotations.

title: Role of L2DTL, cell cycle-regulated nuclear and centrosome protein, in aggressive hepatocellular carcinoma.
review_notes: Source of the IDA nucleus and centrosome localizations and the APC/C-Cdh1 mitotic degradation; also documents an oncogenic overexpression phenotype (non-core).

title: PCNA-dependent regulation of p21 ubiquitylation and degradation via the CRL4Cdt2 ubiquitin ligase complex.
review_notes: Key mechanistic study of CRL4(CDT2) targeting p21 in a PCNA-dependent manner; source of polyubiquitination, transferase-activity (contributes_to), catabolism and response-to-UV annotations.

title: CRL4(Cdt2) E3 ubiquitin ligase monoubiquitinates PCNA to promote translesion DNA synthesis.

title: Selective ubiquitylation of p21 and Cdt1 by UBCH8 and UBE2G ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes via the CRL4Cdt2 ubiquitin ligase complex.
review_notes: Source of the IDA CRL4A(CDT2) complex membership; defines the E2 enzymes used by the complex for different substrates.

title: TRIM39 regulates cell cycle progression and DNA damage responses via stabilizing p21.
review_notes: Full text available; primarily about TRIM39 but documents the DTL-CDKN1A interaction (p21 is a CRL4(CDT2) substrate).

title: CUL4-DDB1-CDT2 E3 Ligase Regulates the Molecular Clock Activity by Promoting Ubiquitination-Dependent Degradation of the Mammalian CRY1.
review_notes: Establishes CRY1 as a CRL4(CDT2) substrate (circadian role) and provides IDA nuclear localization and IMP ubiquitin-dependent catabolism evidence.

title: PCNA-Dependent Cleavage and Degradation of SDE2 Regulates Response to Replication Stress.
review_notes: Full text available; identifies SDE2 as a CRL4(CDT2) substrate in the replication-stress response; source of the DTL-SDE2 interaction.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.

review_notes: Cell-specific interactome; captures the DTL-DDB1 association as a bare protein binding annotation.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Endogenous-tagging interactome; captures the DTL-DDB1 association as a bare protein binding annotation.

title: A central chaperone-like role for 14-3-3 proteins in human cells.
review_notes: 14-3-3 interactome; captures DTL-YWHAE interaction (consistent with DTL phosphorylation) as a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Falcon deep research report for human DTL
review_notes: Falcon synthesis (Tirado-Class 2023 Life Sci Alliance, Tang 2023 BMC Cancer, plus 2024 cancer studies) of DTL/CDT2 as the PCNA-coupled CRL4(CDT2) substrate receptor; the substrate-receptor mechanism, PIP-degron, and CDT1/p21/SET8 substrate set are fully consistent with the experimentally curated annotations and UniProt record. The DCAF14-regulation and oncogenic-substrate (SLTM, RUVBL1) claims are recent and context-specific. Citations are author-year/DOI rather than PMIDs.

title: Structures of human thymidylate kinase in complex with prodrugs: implications for the structure-based design of novel compounds.
review_notes: Structural/kinetic characterisation of human TMPK; directly supports dTMP kinase activity, ATP binding, and dTDP formation. Abstract quotes verified verbatim.

review_notes: Cloned human dTMP kinase; complementation of yeast cdc8-type mutant and dTMP kinase activity on expression establish the molecular function. Quotes verified verbatim.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP high-throughput mitochondrial proteomics dataset; source of the HTP mitochondrion call. DTYMK is not discussed in the prose; the enzyme is established as cytosolic, so this localization is treated as an over-annotation.

title: DTYMK is essential for genome integrity and neuronal survival.

title: Human dTMP kinase: gene expression and enzymatic activity coinciding with cell cycle progression and cell growth.
review_notes: Human dTMP kinase catalysing dTMP phosphorylation; S-phase-regulated expression and activity. Supports MF and cell-cycle context. Quotes verified verbatim.

title: dUMP or TMP + ATP <=> dUDP or TDP + ADP [DTYMK]

title: dUDP or TDP + ADP <=> dUMP or TMP + ATP [DTYMK]

title: UniProtKB entry P23919 (KTHY_HUMAN), thymidylate kinase

title: Nitric oxide down-regulates MKP-3 mRNA levels: involvement in endothelial cell protection from apoptosis.
review_notes: Abstract checked; NO destabilises MKP-3 mRNA; MKP-3 promotes TNFalpha-induced endothelial apoptosis via ERK dephosphorylation.

title: Solution structure of ERK2 binding domain of MAPK phosphatase MKP-3: structural insights into MKP-3 activation by ERK2.

review_notes: Full text cached; siRNA knockdown of endogenous MKP-3 raises ERK1/2 phosphorylation in Ras-transformed human cells (IMP support).
