title: The identification of novel proteins that interact with the GLP-1 receptor and restrain its activity.
review_notes: GLP-1R interactome (MYTH Y2H + CO-IP). FDFT1 is one of many co-detected interactors; supports only a bare GO:0005515 protein-binding annotation, not SQS function.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-scale edgotyping study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI for FDFT1.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome (Y2H); source of multiple bare GO:0005515 protein-binding calls for FDFT1, many with ER/membrane partners but no defined molecular function.

title: Conservation between human and fungal squalene synthetases: similarities in structure, function, and regulation.
review_notes: Cloning/characterization of human hepatic squalene synthase; establishes conservation, membrane topology, and role in sterol biosynthesis (basis of the TAS annotations).

title: The molecular mechanism of nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates as antiosteoporosis drugs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the EXP molecular-function annotations (EC 2.5.1.1 and 2.5.1.10) and Mg(2+) cofactor for human FPPS. Abstract-only in cache but the abstract explicitly states the two sequential condensations. UniProt cites this PMID for both catalytic-activity statements.

title: A protein-protein interaction network for human inherited ataxias and disorders of Purkinje cell degeneration.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput ataxia interactome; source of an IntAct FDPS-ATXN1 "protein binding" annotation. No FDPS-specific functional characterization; relevant only as interaction evidence, not to core function.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; proteome-wide RBP capture, no gene-specific validation for FDPS. Supports only a non-core moonlighting-candidate RNA-binding annotation.

title: Cloning, analysis, and bacterial expression of human farnesyl pyrophosphate synthetase and its regulation in Hep G2 cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original human FPPS cloning/expression paper. Abstract-only in cache. Supports the enzyme identity and its pathway context; cited for the (non-core) TAS cholesterol-biosynthesis annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI reference interactome; source of several IntAct FDPS "protein binding" annotations. High-throughput binary interactions, not core function.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: PubMed-verified neurodegeneration interactome map; source of an IntAct FDPS-ATXN1 "protein binding" annotation. Not relevant to FDPS core enzymatic function.

title: UniProt entry P14324 (FPPS_HUMAN), farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase
review_notes: Authoritative UniProt record for human FDPS (P14324); source for function, catalytic activities, cofactor, subcellular location (Cytoplasm) and pathway steps.

title: A molecular defect in human protoporphyria.
review_notes: Identifies the F417S EPP1 variant and confirms FECH catalyses the last step of heme biosynthesis; supports disease and pathway framing.

title: Frataxin-mediated iron delivery to ferrochelatase in the final step of heme biosynthesis.
review_notes: Demonstrates frataxin as an iron donor to FECH at the matrix-side site of the homodimer for the terminal heme-synthesis step.

title: Substrate interactions with human ferrochelatase.
review_notes: Crystal structure with protoporphyrin IX bound; establishes homodimeric, inner-membrane-associated enzyme with an essential [2Fe-2S] cluster.

title: The molecular defect of ferrochelatase in a patient with erythropoietic protoporphyria.
review_notes: EPP molecular-defect study; describes FECH as the terminal enzyme of heme biosynthesis catalysing ferrous iron insertion into protoporphyrin IX.

title: Molecular cloning and sequence analysis of cDNA encoding human ferrochelatase.
review_notes: Original human FECH cDNA cloning; 423-aa precursor with 54-aa leader.

title: A Novel Role for Progesterone Receptor Membrane Component 1 (PGRMC1): A Partner and Regulator of Ferrochelatase.
review_notes: Establishes PGRMC1 as a FECH partner that decreases FECH activity in vitro; FECH is the terminal enzyme of the heme pathway.

title: Dimeric ferrochelatase bridges ABCB7 and ABCB10 homodimers in an architecturally defined molecular complex required for heme biosynthesis.
review_notes: Defines the FECH-ABCB7-ABCB10 metabolon; dimeric FECH bridges the two ABC transporter homodimers in a complex required for heme biosynthesis.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex) source of high-throughput protein binding IPIs; not a defined FECH functional interaction.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization of FECH.

title: Proteomic Analysis of Ferrochelatase Interactome in Erythroid and Non-Erythroid Cells.
review_notes: Maps the FECH interactome/heme metabolon (ABCB10, mitoferrin-1, PPOX, PGRMC1/2) across erythroid and non-erythroid cells.

title: Mammalian ferrochelatase. Expression and characterization of normal and two human protoporphyric ferrochelatases.
review_notes: Primary experimental characterization of recombinant human FECH activity and EPP mutants (F417S <2% activity); anchors the core catalytic annotation.

title: Site-directed mutagenesis and spectroscopic characterization of human ferrochelatase: identification of residues coordinating the [2Fe-2S] cluster.
review_notes: Identifies C403/C406/C411 as [2Fe-2S] cluster ligands required for activity; supports the cofactor-binding secondary function.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as a real NK-cell membrane proteome study, but it does not support membrane localization of FEN1. The authors state that only ~40% of identified proteins were plausible membrane proteins and that the rest were proteins transiently or adventitiously associated with the membrane fraction. Basis for the REMOVE on GO:0016020.

title: Flap Endonuclease 1 Endonucleolytically Processes RNA to Resolve R-Loops through DNA Base Excision Repair.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Assays human and yeast FEN1 side by side on RNA:DNA hybrid intermediates and demonstrates R-loop resolution through BER; the basis for the proposed GO:0062176 annotation.

title: Structural and functional homology between mammalian DNase IV and the 5'-nuclease domain of Escherichia coli DNA polymerase I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies human DNase IV as the FEN1/rad2 homolog and reports both endonucleolytic incision at the flap bifurcation and RNase H activity, supporting GO:0004523 and the nuclear localization annotation.

title: Structural and functional conservation of the human homolog of the Schizosaccharomyces pombe rad2 gene, which is required for chromosome segregation and recovery from DNA damage.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false). The abstract reports cloning of the human homolog of S. pombe rad2 and complementation of the UV sensitivity of a rad2 null mutant, and describes no damaged-DNA-binding experiment. The GO:0003684 REMOVE therefore rests primarily on the positive argument that FEN1 discriminates branch geometry rather than base damage, not on a claim about the unread full text; the GO:0009650 'UV protection' annotation rests only on heterologous complementation of a fission yeast phenotype.

title: The characterization of a mammalian DNA structure-specific endonuclease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The founding characterization of mammalian FEN-1: defines 5'-flap strand specificity, absence of Holliday junction cleavage, and a dsDNA-specific 5'-3' exonuclease activity. Directly supports the flap endonuclease and exonuclease annotations.

title: Structure of the DNA repair and replication endonuclease and exonuclease FEN-1: coupling DNA and PCNA binding to FEN-1 activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Crystal structure of Pyrococcus furiosus FEN-1 with active-site metals plus analysis of the conserved PCNA-binding C terminus; supports the exonuclease/endonuclease mode switch and the Okazaki fragment role, though the structure itself is archaeal rather than human.

title: Colocalization of kindlin-1, kindlin-2, and migfilin at keratinocyte focal adhesion and relevance to the pathophysiology of Kindler syndrome.
review_notes: Cached full text supports kindlin-2 focal-adhesion localization and relationship to kindlin/migfilin cell-matrix adhesion complexes.

title: Kindlin-2 regulates podocyte adhesion and fibronectin matrix deposition through interactions with phosphoinositides and integrins.
review_notes: Abstract directly supports integrin binding, phosphoinositide binding, integrin activation, podocyte matrix adhesion, fibronectin deposition, and focal-adhesion localization, but full text is unavailable in cache.

title: Kindlin-1 and -2 have overlapping functions in epithelial cells implications for phenotype modification.
review_notes: Cached full text supports kindlin-2 roles in epithelial focal adhesions, actin organization, beta1 integrin activation, adhesion, survival, and migration.

title: Analysis of the myosin-II-responsive focal adhesion proteome reveals a role for β-Pix in negative regulation of focal adhesion maturation.
review_notes: Cached full text is a focal-adhesion proteome study; supports focal-adhesion detection/context but is not direct FERMT2 mechanistic evidence.

title: Structural basis of phosphoinositide binding to kindlin-2 protein pleckstrin homology domain in regulating integrin activation.
review_notes: Abstract directly supports kindlin-2 PH-domain PIP3 binding and the role of phosphoinositide binding in talin-cooperative integrin activation.

title: Kindlin 2 forms a transcriptional complex with β-catenin and TCF4 to enhance Wnt signalling.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports beta-catenin/TCF4 complex formation and Wnt signaling enhancement; full text unavailable.

title: Kindlin-2 mediates activation of TGF-β/Smad signaling and renal fibrosis.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports TGF-beta type I receptor and Smad3 interaction and renal fibrosis signaling; full text unavailable.

title: Kindlin-2 regulates renal tubular cell plasticity by activation of Ras and its downstream signaling.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports Ras/ERK/AKT activation and renal tubular EMT context; full text unavailable.

title: Molecular basis of kindlin-2 binding to integrin-linked kinase pseudokinase for regulating cell adhesion.
review_notes: Cached abstract maps high-affinity kindlin-2 binding to ILK and shows its requirement for focal-adhesion localization and spreading; full text unavailable.

title: Kindlin-2 interacts with endothelial adherens junctions to support vascular barrier integrity.
review_notes: Cached full text supports endothelial adherens-junction localization, beta/gamma-catenin and actin interaction, and vascular-barrier maintenance.

title: The WD40-domain containing protein CORO2B is specifically enriched in glomerular podocytes and regulates the ventral actin cytoskeleton.
review_notes: Cached full text is primarily about CORO2B/podocyte focal adhesions; FERMT2 support is focal-adhesion/proteomic context rather than direct function.

title: Kindlin-2 regulates mesenchymal stem cell differentiation through control of YAP1/TAZ.
review_notes: Cached full text supports RhoA/MLCK/stress-fiber/focal-adhesion assembly and MSC fate phenotypes.

title: Kindlin-2 interacts with a highly conserved surface of ILK to regulate focal adhesion localization and cell spreading.
review_notes: Cached full text directly supports the ILK-kindlin-2 interaction, focal-adhesion localization, and cell-spreading output.

title: Fermitin family homolog-2 (FERMT2) is highly expressed in human placental villi and modulates trophoblast invasion.
review_notes: Cached full text supports placental FERMT2 expression and trophoblast adhesion/migration/invasion context.

title: Structural interactions of fibroblast growth factor receptor with its ligands.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human FGF1 with human FGFR2 D2-D3.

title: Compensation by fibroblast growth factor 1 (FGF1) does not account for the mild phenotypic defects observed in FGF2 null mice.
review_notes: Fgf1 knockout: essentially no abnormalities in mice lacking only FGF1.

title: Crystal structures of two FGF-FGFR complexes reveal the determinants of ligand-receptor specificity.
review_notes: FGF1-FGFR1 and FGF2-FGFR2 crystal structures; basis for FGF1 as universal FGFR ligand.

title: Copper induces the assembly of a multiprotein aggregate implicated in the release of fibroblast growth factor 1 in response to stress.
review_notes: Abstract supports Cu2+-dependent FGF1-S100A13-Syt1 aggregate formation.

title: Multiple fibroblast growth factors support growth of the ureteric bud but have different effects on branching morphogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract supports in vitro effects of exogenous FGF1 on rat ureteric bud branching and elongation.

title: S100A13 mediates the copper-dependent stress-induced release of IL-1alpha from both human U937 and murine NIH 3T3 cells.
review_notes: Abstract focuses on IL-1alpha but restates Cu2+/S100A13-dependent stress release of FGF1; abstract-only.

title: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) homologous factors share structural but not functional homology with FGFs.
review_notes: Abstract confirms FGF1 used as the FGFR-activating reference ligand with mutational analysis.

title: Insights into the molecular basis for fibroblast growth factor receptor autoinhibition and ligand-binding promiscuity.
review_notes: FGF1-FGFR3c three-Ig structure; explains FGF1 promiscuity.

title: Fibroblast growth factor 16 and 18 are expressed in human cardiovascular tissues and induce on endothelial cells migration but not proliferation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; study focuses on FGF16/FGF18 and the abstract does not mention FGF1, which was presumably used as a comparator in the full text.

title: Alternative splicing generates two forms of mRNA coding for human heparin-binding growth factor 1.
review_notes: Gene structure/splicing paper; functional statements are background/speculative.

title: betaKlotho is required for fibroblast growth factor (FGF) 21 signaling through FGF receptor (FGFR) 1c and FGFR3c.
review_notes: Full text; FGF1 is used as the pan-FGFR positive control in BaF3 proliferation assays (source of the IGI rows).

title: The release of fibroblast growth factor-1 from melanoma cells requires copper ions and is mediated by phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt intracellular signaling pathway.
review_notes: Abstract supports FGF-1 secretion from A375 melanoma cells under serum deprivation.

title: Direct binding of integrin alphavbeta3 to FGF1 plays a role in FGF1 signaling.
review_notes: Full text read; integrin alphaVbeta3 binding and mutagenesis separating FGFR, heparin and integrin binding surfaces. Integrin model mainly from one laboratory.

title: FGF-1 induces expression of LXRalpha and production of 25-hydroxycholesterol to upregulate the apoE gene in rat astrocytes.
review_notes: Full text; exogenous FGF-1 effects on apoE/LXR and cholesterol synthesis in rat astrocytes (downstream, cell-type-specific).

title: Gentisic acid, a compound associated with plant defense and a metabolite of aspirin, heads a new class of in vivo fibroblast growth factor inhibitors.
review_notes: Full text; FGF-1 mitogenesis, heparin-site crystal structures and sponge angiogenesis used to characterize gentisic acid inhibitors.

title: Nuclear import of exogenous FGF1 requires the ER-protein LRRC59 and the importins Kpnα1 and Kpnβ1.
review_notes: LRRC59 and importins required for nuclear import of exogenous FGF1.

title: A PPARγ-FGF1 axis is required for adaptive adipose remodelling and metabolic homeostasis.
review_notes: Mouse Fgf1 knockout develops insulin resistance and aberrant adipose remodelling on high-fat diet; PPARgamma induces FGF1.

title: A dominant-negative FGF1 mutant (the R50E mutant) suppresses tumorigenesis and angiogenesis.
review_notes: Full text; R50E dominant-negative suppresses FGF1-induced angiogenesis and endothelial migration/tube formation.

title: Endocrinization of FGF1 produces a neomorphic and potent insulin sensitizer.
review_notes: Pharmacological insulin-sensitizing activity of recombinant FGF1 in mice, mediated predominantly via FGFR1.

title: AHNAK2 Participates in the Stress-Induced Nonclassical FGF1 Secretion Pathway.
review_notes: AHNAK2 participates in stress-induced non-classical FGF1 export.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI proteome-scale Y2H; source of the FGF1-VBP1 interaction only.

title: Nuclear Localization Sequence of FGF1 Is Not Required for Its Intracellular Anti-Apoptotic Activity in Differentiated Cells.
review_notes: NLS of FGF1 dispensable for its intracellular anti-apoptotic activity.

title: Intracellular FGF1 protects cells from apoptosis through direct interaction with p53.
review_notes: Intracellular FGF1 anti-apoptotic activity requires wild-type p53 and involves direct binding to the p53 DBD; single laboratory.

title: Amino acid sequence of human acidic fibroblast growth factor.
review_notes: Protein sequence paper; no functional data supporting signal transduction.

title: Receptor specificity of the fibroblast growth factor family.
review_notes: Classic BaF3 receptor-specificity study; abstract states FGF1 is the only FGF that activates all FGFR splice variants.

title: KGF and FGF-10 stimulate liquid secretion in human fetal lung.
review_notes: Human fetal lung explants; FGF10 increases luminal liquid volume. Abstract only.

title: Randomized trial of topically applied repifermin (recombinant human keratinocyte growth factor-2) to accelerate wound healing in venous ulcers.
review_notes: Clinical trial of topical recombinant FGF10 (repifermin) in venous ulcers; pharmacological, not endogenous role.

title: Fibroblast growth factor-10 is a mitogen for urothelial cells.
review_notes: Human lamina propria fibroblasts make FGF10; recombinant FGF10 is a urothelial mitogen with heparin-dependent receptor phosphorylation. Abstract only.

title: Structural basis by which alternative splicing confers specificity in fibroblast growth factor receptors.
review_notes: Crystal structure of FGF10-FGFR2b and structure-based mutagenesis; establishes FGFR2b specificity.

title: Fibroblast growth factor-10 upregulates Na,K-ATPase via the MAPK pathway.
review_notes: FGF10 recruits Na,K-ATPase to alveolar epithelial plasma membrane via Ras/MAPK; indirect downstream effect.

title: Fibroblast growth factor-10 attenuates H2O2-induced alveolar epithelial cell DNA damage: role of MAPK activation and DNA repair.
review_notes: FGF10 protection against oxidant DNA damage via ERK; DNA-repair role only suggested.

title: Fibroblast growth factors 7 and 10 are expressed in the human embryonic pancreatic mesenchyme and promote the proliferation of embryonic pancreatic epithelial cells.
review_notes: Human embryonic pancreatic mesenchyme expresses FGF10, which stimulates epithelial proliferation.

title: The fibroblast growth factor binding protein is a novel interaction partner of FGF-7, FGF-10 and FGF-22 and regulates FGF activity: implications for epithelial repair.
review_notes: FGFBP1 binds FGF10 and potentiates low-dose activity.

title: Stimulation of human hair growth by the recombinant human keratinocyte growth factor-2 (KGF-2).
review_notes: Recombinant FGF10 stimulates hair follicle cell proliferation in organ culture.

title: FGF-10 and its receptor exhibit bidirectional paracrine targeting to urothelial and smooth muscle cells in the lower urinary tract.
review_notes: FGF10 synthesized by fibroblasts, secreted and targeted to urothelium/smooth muscle; surface, cytoplasmic and nuclear localization. Abstract only.

title: Receptor specificity of the fibroblast growth factor family. The complete mammalian FGF family.
review_notes: Mitogenesis-based receptor specificity survey of FGF10-23 in BaF3 cells; cached text is abstract only and does not state FGF10 specificity explicitly.

title: FGF-10 is decreased in bronchopulmonary dysplasia and suppressed by Toll-like receptor activation.
review_notes: FGF10 reduced in bronchopulmonary dysplasia; TLR activation suppresses FGF10 expression and saccular development.

title: Fibroblast growth factor-10 prevents H2O2-induced cell cycle arrest by regulation of G1 cyclins and cyclin dependent kinases.
review_notes: FGF10 prevents H2O2-induced alveolar epithelial G1 arrest; full text available.

title: FGF10 missense mutations in aplasia of lacrimal and salivary glands (ALSG).
review_notes: FGF10 missense mutations in ALSG families (human genetics).

title: Cortactin involvement in the keratinocyte growth factor and fibroblast growth factor 10 promotion of migration and cortical actin assembly in human keratinocytes.
review_notes: FGF7 and FGF10 promote keratinocyte migration via Src/PI3K and cortactin.

title: Translocation of fibroblast growth factor-10 and its receptor into nuclei of human urothelial cells.
review_notes: Recombinant FGF10 accumulates in urothelial nuclei; NLS-like motif. Single-lab observation.

title: Cathespin H is an Fgf10 target involved in Bmp4 degradation during lung branching morphogenesis.
review_notes: Mouse lung: Fgf10-Fgfr2b induces Ctsh which controls Bmp4; abstract does not describe the migration data underlying the GO annotation.

title: Heparanase cleavage of perlecan heparan sulfate modulates FGF10 activity during ex vivo submandibular gland branching morphogenesis.
review_notes: Heparanase releases FGF10 from perlecan HS to promote SMG branching; SPR binding of FGF10 to HS; mouse ex vivo.

title: FGFR2IIIb signaling regulates thymic epithelial differentiation.
review_notes: Mouse thymus: ectopic FGF10 and FGFR2IIIb blockade alter thymic epithelium.

title: Involvement of FGF and BMP family proteins and VEGF in early human kidney development.
review_notes: Immunohistochemistry of FGF10 in human embryonic meso/metanephros; expression only.

title: An intronic alteration of the fibroblast growth factor 10 gene causing ALSG-(aplasia of lacrimal and salivary glands) syndrome.
review_notes: Full text; FGF10 intronic splice mutation in ALSG; supports haploinsufficiency.

title: FGF-10 and specific structural elements of dermatan sulfate size and sulfation promote maximal keratinocyte migration and cellular proliferation.
review_notes: Dermatan sulfate potentiates FGF10 activity on FGFR2IIIb reporter cell lines and keratinocyte migration; full text not retrievable to confirm the reporter cell line.

title: Construction and characterization of a high activity mutant of human keratinocyte growth factor-2.
review_notes: High-activity FGF10 mutant; receptor binding and tracheal epithelial proliferation.

title: Using an in situ proximity ligation assay to systematically profile endogenous protein-protein interactions in a pathway network.
review_notes: High-throughput proximity ligation screen in HeLa; FGF10 not discussed in abstract.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI Y2H map; FGF10 partners SREK1IP1 and THAP1 lack known functional relevance.

title: FGF-10 is a chemotactic factor for distal epithelial buds during lung development.
review_notes: FGF10 is a chemoattractant for distal lung epithelial buds in explants.

title: FGF-19, a novel fibroblast growth factor with unique specificity for FGFR4.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Xie 1999, Cytokine). Establishes FGF19 as a high-affinity, FGFR4-exclusive ligand; the primary IPI source for GO:0005104.

title: Definition of a novel growth factor-dependent signal cascade for the suppression of bile acid biosynthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Holt 2003, Genes Dev). Full text confirms FGF19 represses CYP7A1 in human hepatocytes and mouse liver and activates JNK; source for the bile-acid and JNK annotations.

title: Fibroblast growth factor 15 functions as an enterohepatic signal to regulate bile acid homeostasis.
review_notes: PubMed abstract verified (Inagaki 2005, Cell Metab). Mouse Fgf15-null shows the bile-acid/CYP7A1 feedback function of the ortholog; supporting reference for GO:0070858.

title: Molecular insights into the klotho-dependent, endocrine mode of action of fibroblast growth factor 19 subfamily members.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Goetz 2007, MCB). Structural basis for reduced heparin binding and endocrine mode; supports extracellular/endocrine framing.

title: Tissue-specific expression of betaKlotho and fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor isoforms determines metabolic activity of FGF19 and FGF21.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kurosu 2007, JBC). Full text confirms betaKlotho requirement, ERK/FRS2 signaling, adipocyte glucose uptake and CYP7A1 repression.

title: Liver-specific activities of FGF19 require Klotho beta.
review_notes: PubMed abstract verified (Lin 2007, JBC; full text not cached). Establishes KLB requirement for FGF19-FGFR4 binding and signaling.

title: betaKlotho is required for fibroblast growth factor (FGF) 21 signaling through FGF receptor (FGFR) 1c and FGFR3c.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Suzuki 2008, Mol Endocrinol). Full text: FGF19 fully activated BaF3 cells expressing betaKlotho with FGFR1c/2c/3c/4; source for the IGI proliferation/signaling annotations.

title: C-terminal tail of FGF19 determines its specificity toward Klotho co-receptors.
review_notes: PubMed abstract verified (Wu 2008, JBC). Chimera experiments map FGF19 C-terminal tail as the Klotho-recognition region and show binding to alpha- and betaKlotho; supports the receptor-binding MODIFY.

title: Bile acids activate fibroblast growth factor 19 signaling in human hepatocytes to inhibit cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase gene expression.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Song 2009, Hepatology). Full text: FGF19 represses CYP7A1 via ERK1/2 and, notably, did NOT activate JNK here, contradicting Holt 2003.

title: FGF19 as a postprandial, insulin-independent activator of hepatic protein and glycogen synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kir 2011, Science). Full text: human FGF19 stimulates insulin-independent hepatic glycogen synthase activity/glycogen synthesis; basis for the NEW GO:0045725 annotation.

title: Structure and expression of a novel human FGF, FGF-19, expressed in the fetal brain.
review_notes: PubMed abstract verified (Nishimura 1999, BBA). Cloning/expression report (fetal brain); does not establish a nervous-system developmental function for human FGF19.

title: Structural basis for FGF receptor dimerization and activation.
review_notes: FGF2-FGFR1 crystal structure; abstract verified.

title: Crystal structures of two FGF-FGFR complexes reveal the determinants of ligand-receptor specificity.
review_notes: FGF1-FGFR1 and FGF2-FGFR2 structures; abstract verified.

title: Crystal structure of a ternary FGF-FGFR-heparin complex reveals a dual role for heparin in FGFR binding and dimerization.
review_notes: 2:2:2 FGF2-FGFR1-heparin ternary structure; supports heparin binding.

title: Evidence that bone morphogenetic protein 4 has multiple biological functions during kidney and urinary tract development.
review_notes: BMP4 kidney study; FGF2 used as a supplement in explants.

title: The zinc-finger transcription factor, early growth response 3, mediates VEGF-induced angiogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract concerns VEGF/Egr3; FGF2 annotations presumably from full-text comparator experiments.

title: Differential involvement of TGF-beta1 in mediating the motogenic effects of TSP-1 on endothelial cells, fibroblasts and oral tumour cells.
review_notes: TSP-1 study; FGF-2 used as migration stimulus. Basis for a negative-regulation annotation on FGF2 unclear.

title: bFGF induces changes in hyaluronan synthase and hyaluronidase isoform expression and modulates the migration capacity of fibrosarcoma cells.
review_notes: bFGF effects on HA metabolism and migration in fibrosarcoma cells; indirect.

title: A phosphoinositide 3-kinase/phospholipase Cgamma1 pathway regulates fibroblast growth factor-induced capillary tube formation.
review_notes: FGF-2 activates PI3K/PLCgamma1 in HUVEC.

title: Tec-kinase-mediated phosphorylation of fibroblast growth factor 2 is essential for unconventional secretion.
review_notes: Tec kinase and unconventional secretion of FGF2.

title: A murine fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor expressed in CHO cells is activated by basic FGF and Kaposi FGF.
review_notes: bFGF binds and activates mouse FGFR1 in CHO cells.

title: Nuclear import of exogenous FGF1 requires the ER-protein LRRC59 and the importins Kpnα1 and Kpnβ1.
review_notes: Title focuses on FGF1 but abstract explicitly reports FGF2 nuclear import via CEP57 and importins.

title: Dynamic modulation of FGFR1-5-HT1A heteroreceptor complexes. Agonist treatment enhances participation of FGFR1 and 5-HT1A homodimers and recruitment of β-arrestin2.
review_notes: FGF2 as agonist in FGFR1-5-HT1A heteroreceptor BRET study; receptor-receptor MF belongs to the receptors.

title: The integrin-binding defective FGF2 mutants potently suppress FGF2 signalling and angiogenesis.
review_notes: FGF2-integrin alphaVbeta3 binding; single-laboratory model.

title: Receptor specificity of the fibroblast growth factor family.
review_notes: FGF receptor-specificity mitogenic panel; FGF2-specific data in full text.

title: Neuregulins promote survival and growth of cardiac myocytes. Persistence of ErbB2 and ErbB4 expression in neonatal and adult ventricular myocytes.
review_notes: Neuregulin study; FGF2 not mentioned in abstract (presumably a comparator in full text).

title: Neuronal defects and delayed wound healing in mice lacking fibroblast growth factor 2.
review_notes: Fgf2 knockout: viable, cortical neuron and wound-healing defects.

title: Identification of a novel FGF, FGF-21, preferentially expressed in the liver.
review_notes: Discovery of FGF21; abstract only. Supports secretion (signal peptide) and liver expression; does not itself test signaling.

title: FGF-21 as a novel metabolic regulator.
review_notes: Discovery of FGF21 as an adipocyte glucose-uptake regulator; establishes non-mitogenic character.

title: BetaKlotho is required for metabolic activity of fibroblast growth factor 21.
review_notes: Shows beta-Klotho is required for FGF21 activity, FGFR binding and MAPK activation.

title: Hepatic fibroblast growth factor 21 is regulated by PPARalpha and is a key mediator of hepatic lipid metabolism in ketotic states.
review_notes: Establishes hepatic, PPARalpha/fasting-induced FGF21 as a circulating hormone; abstract only cached.

title: Tissue-specific expression of betaKlotho and fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor isoforms determines metabolic activity of FGF19 and FGF21.
review_notes: Full text cached. Directly supports beta-Klotho-dependent FGFR1 signaling, ERK activation and glucose uptake in adipocytes, and weak FGF21 action on FGFR4/hepatocytes.

title: betaKlotho is required for fibroblast growth factor (FGF) 21 signaling through FGF receptor (FGFR) 1c and FGFR3c.
review_notes: Reconstitution in BaF3 cells: FGF21 activates FGFR1c/FGFR3c only with beta-Klotho.

title: C-terminal tail of FGF19 determines its specificity toward Klotho co-receptors.
review_notes: Abstract only; chimera data show the FGF21 C-terminal tail specifies beta-Klotho binding.

title: FGF21 N- and C-termini play different roles in receptor interaction and activation.
review_notes: Abstract only; direct Biacore binding of FGF21 C-terminus to beta-Klotho.

title: Different roles of N- and C- termini in the functional activity of FGF21.
review_notes: Abstract only; C-terminus binds beta-Klotho, N-terminus engages FGFR; MAPK and GLUT1/glucose uptake readouts.

title: FGF21 regulates PGC-1α and browning of white adipose tissues in adaptive thermogenesis.
review_notes: Full text cached; mouse loss- and gain-of-function data on FGF21 in cold-induced WAT browning.

title: Fibroblast growth factor-21 (FGF21) regulates low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) levels in cells via the E3-ubiquitin ligase Mylip/Idol and the Canopy2 (Cnpy2)/Mylip-interacting saposin-like protein (Msap).
review_notes: Single cell-culture study of FGF21 effects on IDOL/CNPY2/LDLR; in vivo relevance not established.

title: FGF21 regulates metabolism and circadian behavior by acting on the nervous system.
review_notes: Shows central (SCN, hindbrain) beta-Klotho mediates FGF21 neuroendocrine and metabolic effects (mouse).

review_notes: Correctly cited - FLG does appear in this sperm nuclear proteome - but a shotgun catalogue of a tissue where FLG is not the relevant biology is weak support for nuclear localisation, and large abundant skin proteins are a standard contamination confound. The nucleus annotation is retained on the strength of PMID:9800950 and PMID:12230510 instead.

title: Caspase-14 is required for filaggrin degradation to natural moisturizing factors in the skin.
review_notes: Maps two caspase-14 cleavage sites in the FLG repeat unit and shows that defective degradation reduces urocanic acid and pyrrolidone carboxylic acid. Establishes the terminal catabolic fate of filaggrin, in which FLG is the substrate rather than the actor.

title: Defects of filaggrin-like proteins in both lesional and nonlesional atopic skin.
review_notes: Genotyped case-control cohort showing reduced FLG, HRNR and FLG2 in atopic skin independent of FLG genotype. Appropriate basis for an IEP annotation to establishment of skin barrier.

title: Kallikrein-related peptidase 5 functions in proteolytic processing of profilaggrin in cultured human keratinocytes.
review_notes: Correctly cited for a real KLK5-profilaggrin interaction, but the relationship is enzyme-substrate, so it supports a protein-binding row rather than any informative molecular function of FLG.

title: Crystal Structure of Human Profilaggrin S100 Domain and Identification of Target Proteins Annexin II, Stratifin, and HSP27.
review_notes: 2.2 A crystal structure (PDB 4PCW) of the profilaggrin N-terminal S100 domain with bound calcium; also establishes the stable dimer, the two hydrophobic target pockets, and three partner proteins. The load-bearing evidence for GO:0005509, and - by reporting only calcium in the very domain concerned - the strongest evidence against GO:0046914.

title: Proteomic characterization of human multiple myeloma bone marrow extracellular matrix.
review_notes: A myeloma bone-marrow ECM proteome. FLG's appearance there is best explained by skin-derived sample contamination; it is an intracellular epidermal protein with no signal peptide and no reported expression in bone marrow. Not a credible basis for the extracellular matrix annotation.

title: Liquid-liquid phase separation drives skin barrier formation.
review_notes: Shows that filaggrin assembles keratohyalin granules by liquid-liquid phase separation, that repeat number sets the critical concentration and disease alleles raise it, that the S100 domain lowers it by dimerising, and that pH-triggered dissolution drives enucleation. The primary basis for the proposed GO:0140693 annotation.

title: Structural properties of target binding by profilaggrin A and B domains and other S100 fused-type calcium-binding proteins.
review_notes: Shows the profilaggrin B domain cooperates with the S100 domain to bind annexin II and keratin intermediate filaments in a calcium-dependent manner, giving functional meaning to the EF-hand calcium binding. Surfaced by the OpenScientist calcium hypothesis run and verified against PubMed.

title: Characterization of a class of cationic proteins that specifically interact with intermediate filaments.
review_notes: The paper that named filaggrin and demonstrated its defining activity: specific association with intermediate filaments, macrofibril formation, and a stoichiometry of about two filaggrin molecules per three-chain filament building block. Primary evidence for repointing GO:0005198 to a filament-binding term.

title: Histidine-rich proteins (filaggrins): structural and functional heterogeneity during epidermal differentiation.
review_notes: Direct in vitro demonstration that filaggrins aggregate keratin filaments specifically into bundles, and that their basic arginines are progressively converted to citrulline during maturation - i.e. the binding activity is switched off rather than made permanent. Surfaced by the OpenScientist structural-versus-binding hypothesis run and verified against PubMed. Covers guinea pig, rat, mouse and human epidermis.

title: The proteins elafin, filaggrin, keratin intermediate filaments, loricrin, and small proline-rich proteins 1 and 2 are isodipeptide cross-linked components of the human epidermal cornified cell envelope.
review_notes: Peptide-level demonstration that filaggrin is covalently isodipeptide cross-linked into human cornified envelopes. Supports the cornified envelope location, the cornification process, and the one genuinely structural molecular function of filaggrin.

title: The mechanism of interaction of filaggrin with intermediate filaments. The ionic zipper hypothesis.
review_notes: Establishes the mechanism of filament binding - charge-complementary contacts between cationic beta-turns of the repeat and the packed filament rod domains - and shows that short synthetic peptides reproduce it. Directly relevant to whether the repeat's molecular function is structural or a binding activity.

title: Profilaggrin is a major epidermal calcium-binding protein.
review_notes: Provides the in vitro demonstration that the two N-terminal EF-hands bind calcium, and states the terminal fate of filaggrin as complete degradation to free amino acids. The experimental basis for GO:0005509 that PMID:1429717 only conjectured.

title: Translocation of profilaggrin N-terminal domain into keratinocyte nuclei with fragmented DNA in normal human skin and loricrin keratoderma.
review_notes: Immuno-electron microscopy showing the profilaggrin N-terminal domain moves from keratohyalin granules into the nuclei of transition-layer keratinocytes while the filaggrin repeat domains stay cytoplasmic. The proper support for the nucleus annotation.

title: The crystal structure of human protein farnesyltransferase reveals the basis for inhibition by CaaX tetrapeptides and their mimetics.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; PubMed-verified. Crystal structure of the human FNTA:FNTB heterodimer; source of the FNTA:FNTB IPI and the DisProt molecular-adaptor EXP annotation.

title: 3-Aminopyrrolidinone farnesyltransferase inhibitors: design of macrocyclic compounds with improved pharmacokinetics and excellent cell potency.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. FTase-inhibitor crystallography with purified enzyme; supports FTase activity (EXP) and the FNTA:FNTB interaction.

title: Dual protein farnesyltransferase-geranylgeranyltransferase-I inhibitors as potential cancer chemotherapeutic agents.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Dual FTase/GGTase-I inhibitor structural study; supports FTase activity (EXP).

title: Crystal structures of the anticancer clinical candidates R115777 (Tipifarnib) and BMS-214662 complexed with protein farnesyltransferase suggest a mechanism of FTI selectivity.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. FTase inhibitor crystal structures; source of an FNTA:FNTB IPI.

title: Crystallographic analysis reveals that anticancer clinical candidate L-778,123 inhibits protein farnesyltransferase and geranylgeranyltransferase-I by different binding modes.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Structural comparison of FTase and GGTase-I inhibitor binding; source of an FNTA:FNTB IPI.

title: Crystallographic analysis of CaaX prenyltransferases complexed with substrates defines rules of protein substrate selectivity.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Defines CaaX substrate-selectivity rules for FTase and GGTase-I; informative on the shared enzymology of the FNTA-containing complexes.

title: Conversion of protein farnesyltransferase to a geranylgeranyltransferase.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Human enzyme crystallography/kinetics; the source of multiple UniProtKB IDA annotations (FTase and GGTase activities, both complexes, farnesylation and geranylgeranylation).

title: The protein farnesyltransferase regulates HDAC6 activity in a microtubule-dependent manner.
review_notes: Abstract-only (PMC2665085); PubMed-verified. Directly shows FNTA (the alpha subunit) binds microtubules and is required for HDAC6 activity; source of the BHF-UCL microtubule-binding, alpha-tubulin-binding, microtubule-associated-complex, enzyme- binding and regulation-of-microtubule-movement annotations. The acetyltransferase- activator MF label it is cited for does not match the described HDAC6 (deacetylase) biology.

title: Structural basis for binding and selectivity of antimalarial and anticancer ethylenediamine inhibitors to protein farnesyltransferase.
review_notes: Full text available; PubMed-verified. FTase enzymology and structure, including FNTA (alpha) contributions to the CaaX substrate pocket; supports FTase activity (EXP).

title: Human-chromatin-related protein interactions identify a demethylase complex required for chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Large-scale chromatin AP-MS interactome; source of bare protein-binding IPIs with FNTB and PGGT1B (the expected heterodimer partners), uninformative about FNTA molecular function.

title: GGTase3 is a newly identified geranylgeranyltransferase targeting a ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Primarily about a distinct alpha subunit (PTAR1) forming GGTase3; provides IntAct FNTA interactions with FNTB, PGGT1B and RAS substrates (bare protein-binding IPIs).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HuRI binary interactome; source of bare protein-binding IPIs (FNTB, PGGT1B, AP4M1). Uninformative about molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. BioPlex proteome-scale interactome; source of bare protein-binding IPIs (FNTB, PGGT1B). Uninformative about molecular function.

title: A Proteomic Approach Identifies Isoform-Specific and Nucleotide-Dependent RAS Interactions.
review_notes: Full text available; PubMed-verified. RAS-isoform interactome; FNTA appears as a RAS interactor consistent with RAS being a prenylation substrate. Source of bare protein-binding IPIs (HRAS, KRAS, NRAS).

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Multimodal cell-maps interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (PGGT1B). Uninformative about molecular function.

title: cDNA cloning and expression of rat and human protein geranylgeranyltransferase type-I.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Establishes that GGTase-I shares the FTase alpha subunit (FNTA) and that FNTA plus the GGTase-I beta subunit reconstitutes active enzyme; supports GGTase-I activity, geranylgeranylation and complex membership.

title: cDNA cloning of the two subunits of human CAAX farnesyltransferase and chromosomal mapping of FNTA and FNTB loci and related sequences.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Cloning of the two human CAAX farnesyltransferase subunits (FNTA/FNTB); supports FTase activity (TAS).

title: Mutational analysis of alpha-subunit of protein farnesyltransferase. Evidence for a catalytic role.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Alpha-subunit mutagenesis (K164) showing the alpha subunit stabilizes the beta subunit and plays a direct catalytic role; anchors the contributes_to framing for FTase activity.

title: Characterization of recombinant human farnesyl-protein transferase: cloning, expression, farnesyl diphosphate binding, and functional homology with yeast prenyl-protein transferases.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Recombinant human FPTase characterization; FPP binds the beta subunit of the holoenzyme and alpha-subunit substitutions impair activity. Supports FTase enzymology and farnesylation.

title: The p21(RAS) farnesyltransferase alpha subunit in TGF-beta and activin signaling.
review_notes: Abstract-only; PubMed-verified. Identifies FNTA as a cytoplasmic interactor of the ligand-free TGF-beta/activin type I receptors, phosphorylated and released on ligand binding; basis for the cytoplasm and TGF-beta-signaling TAS annotations (a moonlighting role).

title: The crystal structure of human protein farnesyltransferase reveals the basis for inhibition by CaaX tetrapeptides and their mimetics.
review_notes: First human FTase crystal structure; confirms the FNTA:FNTB heterodimer, catalytic Zn2+ in the beta subunit and FPP binding site. IntAct source for the FNTA-binding IPI.

title: 3-Aminopyrrolidinone farnesyltransferase inhibitors: design of macrocyclic compounds with improved pharmacokinetics and excellent cell potency.
review_notes: FTase inhibitor co-crystal/enzymology; UniProt EXP source for FTase activity/function.

title: Dual protein farnesyltransferase-geranylgeranyltransferase-I inhibitors as potential cancer chemotherapeutic agents.
review_notes: Dual FTase/GGTase-I inhibitor study; UniProt EXP source for FTase activity.

title: Crystal structures of the anticancer clinical candidates R115777 (Tipifarnib) and BMS-214662 complexed with protein farnesyltransferase suggest a mechanism of FTI selectivity.
review_notes: FTI (tipifarnib/BMS-214662) co-crystal structures; IntAct source for FNTA binding.

title: Crystallographic analysis reveals that anticancer clinical candidate L-778,123 inhibits protein farnesyltransferase and geranylgeranyltransferase-I by different binding modes.
review_notes: FTI (L-778,123) co-crystal structures; IntAct source for FNTA binding.

title: Crystallographic analysis of CaaX prenyltransferases complexed with substrates defines rules of protein substrate selectivity.
review_notes: Defines CaaX substrate-selectivity rules from co-crystal structures; supports FTase MF.

title: Conversion of protein farnesyltransferase to a geranylgeranyltransferase.
review_notes: Maps FPP-vs-GGPP selectivity to beta-subunit residues W102/Y365; UniProt IDA source for GO:0004660, GO:0008270, GO:0018343 and GO:0005965.

title: The protein farnesyltransferase regulates HDAC6 activity in a microtubule-dependent manner.
review_notes: Source for the moonlighting HDAC6/microtubule annotations. Abstract attributes microtubule binding to the alpha subunit (FNTA); FNTB roles here are complex-level and non-core.

title: Structural basis for binding and selectivity of antimalarial and anticancer ethylenediamine inhibitors to protein farnesyltransferase.
review_notes: Full text available. States FTase modifies >60 CaaX signal-transduction proteins including Ras/Rho GTPases; UniProt EXP source for FTase activity/function.

title: Human-chromatin-related protein interactions identify a demethylase complex required for chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Chromatin AP-MS interactome; FNTB captured as interactor (with FNTA), no new FNTB function.

title: GGTase3 is a newly identified geranylgeranyltransferase targeting a ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Paper is about GGTase3 (PTAR1/RabGGTB); FNTB appears only in comparison/IntAct context. Used as IntAct source for the FNTA-binding IPI, not a functional FNTB finding.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; high-throughput protein-binding data only.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome; high-throughput protein-binding data only.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex interactome; high-throughput protein-binding data only.

title: Characterization of recombinant human farnesyl-protein transferase: cloning, expression, farnesyl diphosphate binding, and functional homology with yeast prenyl-protein transferases.
review_notes: Original human FPTase characterization; shows FPP photo-cross-links specifically to the beta subunit and maps catalytic mutants (D200/G249/G349). Strongly supports the core catalytic function.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the core complex I assembly process and a broad cytoplasmic localization (the latter general relative to the inner-membrane experimental data).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot keyword mapping
review_notes: UniProt keyword-to-GO mapping (Oxidoreductase, FAD/Flavoprotein); supports the generic oxidoreductase MF and the flavoprotein FAD-binding function.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell keyword mapping to mitochondrial inner membrane; consistent with the experimental IDA/EXP localization.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence mitochondrial localization; correct but general.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of intracellular localizations of expressed fusion proteins in living cells
review_notes: LIFEdb expressed-fusion-protein mitochondrial localization; correct but general.

title: FOXRED1, encoding an FAD-dependent oxidoreductase complex-I-specific molecular chaperone, is mutated in infantile-onset mitochondrial encephalopathy.
review_notes: Original disease study establishing FOXRED1 as a complex I-specific assembly chaperone and localizing it to mitochondria/inner membrane. Abstract-only cache.

title: Characterization of mitochondrial FOXRED1 in the assembly of respiratory chain complex I.
review_notes: Definitive mechanistic characterization (IMP source for the core assembly process and the inner-membrane IDA localization). Abstract-only cache; the curator read the full text.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: HTP mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization but is general.

title: The signaling adapter FRS-2 competes with Shc for binding to the nerve growth factor receptor TrkA. A model for discriminating proliferation and differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract verified; FRS-2 PTB binds Trk receptors at the SHC site; rescues NGF-induced differentiation.

title: FRS2 proteins recruit intracellular signaling pathways by binding to diverse targets on fibroblast growth factor and nerve growth factor receptors.
review_notes: Abstract/full text cached; PTB of FRS2alpha/beta binds FGFR1 constitutively and TrkA pY490-dependently.

title: Structural basis of SNT PTB domain interactions with distinct neurotrophic receptors.
review_notes: Full text cached; NMR basis for mutually exclusive FGFR vs TRK recognition by the SNT-1 PTB domain.

title: Stimulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase by fibroblast growth factor receptors is mediated by coordinated recruitment of multiple docking proteins.
review_notes: Cached with full text; FRS2alpha-GRB2-GAB1 assembly recruits and activates PI3K.

title: EGFR and FGFR signaling through FRS2 is subject to negative feedback control by ERK1/2.
review_notes: Abstract verified; FRS2 role in EGFR signalling in A-431 cells and ERK1/2 negative feedback.

title: TrkA alternative splicing: a regulated tumor-promoting switch in human neuroblastoma.
review_notes: Abstract (TrkAIII splice variant) does not mention FRS2; IPI with TrkA must derive from full text, not checked.

title: ALK activation induces Shc and FRS2 recruitment: Signaling and phenotypic outcomes in PC12 cells differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract verified; FRS2 recruited/phosphorylated by activated ALK in PC12 cells.

title: Nedd4-1 binds and ubiquitylates activated FGFR1 to control its endocytosis and function.
review_notes: Abstract verified; FRS2alpha used as a downstream readout of FGFR1 signalling; Nedd4-1 study.

title: Overexpression of microRNA-1 promotes cardiomyocyte commitment from human cardiovascular progenitors via suppressing WNT and FGF signaling pathways.
review_notes: Abstract verified; FRS2 as a miR-1 target in cardiovascular progenitor fate choice.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: E-cadherin proximity proteomics; FRS2 not named in cached main text (presumably in supplementary tables).

title: LuTHy: a double-readout bioluminescence-based two-hybrid technology for quantitative mapping of protein-protein interactions in mammalian cells.
review_notes: LuTHy methods paper; FRS2-PTPN11 pair not found in cached text (likely supplementary).

title: Physical and functional interactome atlas of human receptor tyrosine kinases.
review_notes: RTK interactome atlas; FRS2-FGFR1 pair not found in cached text (likely supplementary).

title: A lipid-anchored Grb2-binding protein that links FGF-receptor activation to the Ras/MAPK signaling pathway.
review_notes: Original purification/cloning of FRS2; abstract verified in cache; establishes lipid-anchored docking-protein function and myristoylation requirement.

title: Binding of Shp2 tyrosine phosphatase to FRS2 is essential for fibroblast growth factor-induced PC12 cell differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract verified; FRS2 binds SHP2 N-SH2; SHP2 recruits additional GRB2.

title: Novel recognition motif on fibroblast growth factor receptor mediates direct association and activation of SNT adapter proteins.
review_notes: Abstract verified; direct PTB-FGFR1 juxtamembrane binding. Does not support the GPCR or receptor-PTP pathway TAS rows attributed to it.

title: FRS2 proteins recruit intracellular signaling pathways by binding to diverse targets on fibroblast growth factor and nerve growth factor receptors.
review_notes: Full text cached; shows PTB domains of both FRS2alpha and FRS2beta (FRS3) bind FGF and NGF receptors directly.

title: The signaling adapters fibroblast growth factor receptor substrate 2 and 3 are activated by the thyroid TRK oncoproteins.
review_notes: Abstract-only; FRS3 recruited and activated by TRK oncoproteins.

title: FRS2 family docking proteins with overlapping roles in activation of MAP kinase have distinct spatial-temporal patterns of expression of their transcripts.
review_notes: Abstract-only; UniProt cites for FRS3 function; FRS2beta rescues MAPK activation in Frs2alpha-null MEFs.

title: SNT-2 interacts with ERK2 and negatively regulates ERK2 signaling in response to EGF stimulation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; FRS3 binds ERK2 via residues 186-252.

title: Direct interaction of Rnd1 with FRS2 beta regulates Rnd1-induced down-regulation of RhoA activity and is involved in fibroblast growth factor-induced neurite outgrowth in PC12 cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only; FGFR1 phosphorylates FRS2beta and recruits Shp2; Rnd1 binding.

title: Context-specific requirements for Fgfr1 signaling through Frs2 and Frs3 during mouse development.
review_notes: Abstract-only; Fgfr1 mutant lacking the Frs2/3 binding site.

title: Trk receptor binding and neurotrophin/fibroblast growth factor (FGF)-dependent activation of the FGF receptor substrate (FRS)-3.
review_notes: Abstract-only; FRS3-specific evidence for Trk binding and GRB2/SHP2 recruitment and MAPK support.

title: Unique role of SNT-2/FRS2beta/FRS3 docking/adaptor protein for negative regulation in EGF receptor tyrosine kinase signaling pathways.
review_notes: Abstract-only; FRS3 PTB binds EGFR; negative regulation of EGFR signalling.

title: UNC-51-like kinase regulation of fibroblast growth factor receptor substrate 2/3.
review_notes: Abstract-only; ULK2 binds FRS2/3 PTB domain.

title: Hepatitis C virus infection protein network.
review_notes: HCV-host yeast two-hybrid screen; FRS3 is one hit; no functional information for FRS3.

title: Prominent expression of FRS2beta protein in neural cells and its association with intracellular vesicles.
review_notes: Abstract-only; neural-restricted FRS2beta expression.

title: The fibroblast growth factor receptor substrate 3 adapter is a developmentally regulated microtubule-associated protein expressed in migrating and differentiated neurons.
review_notes: Abstract-only; Frs3 antibody, localization and microtubule binding in neurons.

title: FRS2beta, a potential prognostic gene for non-small cell lung cancer, encodes a feedback inhibitor of EGF receptor family members by ERK binding.
review_notes: Abstract-only; maps FRS3 D-domain-like ERK docking motifs.

title: Structural basis for the recognition of nucleophosmin-anaplastic lymphoma kinase oncoprotein by the phosphotyrosine binding domain of Suc1-associated neurotrophic factor-induced tyrosine-phosphorylated target-2.
review_notes: Abstract-only; NMR structure of SNT-2 PTB domain with NPM-ALK peptide.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput yeast two-hybrid interactome; source of uninformative protein-binding IPIs.

title: Phospho-tyrosine dependent protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput phosphotyrosine-dependent yeast two-hybrid screen; source of protein-binding and self-interaction IPIs.

title: FGF-Dependent, Context-Driven Role for FRS Adapters in the Early Telencephalon.
review_notes: Full text; Frs2/Frs3 compound mutants in telencephalon; Frs3-null viable.

title: Neurotrophin and FGF Signaling Adapter Proteins, FRS2 and FRS3, Regulate Dentate Granule Cell Maturation and Excitatory Synaptogenesis.
review_notes: Full text; Frs2/Frs3 double mutants in hippocampal dentate granule cell maturation.

title: Developmental stage-specific role of Frs adapters as mediators of FGF receptor signaling in the oligodendrocyte lineage cells.
review_notes: Full text; Frs adapters in oligodendrocyte lineage; FRS2 dominant.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source of most protein-binding IPIs.

title: Missense variants in FRS3 affect body mass index in populations of diverse ancestries.
review_notes: Full text; FRS3 missense variants associated with BMI (association only).

title: Broadly expressed SNT-like proteins link FGF receptor stimulation to activators of Ras.
review_notes: Abstract-only; describes SNT-like proteins before molecular identification of FRS3, supporting FGF-induced phosphorylation and Grb2/Sos association of the family.

title: Novel recognition motif on fibroblast growth factor receptor mediates direct association and activation of SNT adapter proteins.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; UniProt cites it for FRS3 cloning and FGFR1 interaction. Supports direct PTB-mediated FGFR1 binding by SNT-2/FRS3.

title: Deep research report on FRS3 (Falcon/Edison)
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis; microtubule/kinesin/PSD claims rest largely on an unpublished 2012 thesis and were not used as primary evidence.

title: Formiminotransferase cyclodeaminase is an organ-specific autoantigen recognized by sera of patients with autoimmune hepatitis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes human FTCD identity (cytosolic, liver-specific, oligomeric) and the LC1 autoantigen link; used for the cytoplasm and folate-metabolism TAS annotations.

title: The molecular basis of glutamate formiminotransferase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary experimental basis for the GO:0030409 IDA and for the disease association (formiminoglutamic aciduria / FIGLU excretion).

title: Characterization of the antigenicity of the formiminotransferase-cyclodeaminase in type 2 autoimmune hepatitis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the human cytosol/Golgi IDA localizations and the key caveat that human FTCD does not bind cytoskeleton, undercutting the microtubule-binding annotations.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports the HDA extracellular-exosome annotation but is a bystander detection.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Large-scale interactome map; the resulting GO:0005515 annotation is non-informative for FTCD function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Large-scale interactome map; the resulting GO:0005515 annotation is non-informative for FTCD function.

title: N-formiminoglutamate + tetrahydrofolate => glutamate + 5-formiminotetrahydrofolate
review_notes: Reactome pathway step for FTCD; supports cytosolic localization and the formimidoyltransferase reaction.

title: The obesity-associated FTO gene encodes a 2-oxoglutarate-dependent nucleic acid demethylase.
review_notes: Founding enzymology paper; establishes the Fe(II)/2OG chemistry and nuclear localization, in mouse Fto. Correctly used as the ISS source for the human nucleus annotation.

title: Oxidative demethylation of 3-methylthymine and 3-methyluracil in single-stranded DNA and RNA by mouse and human FTO.
review_notes: Direct human FTO biochemistry on ssDNA/ssRNA alkylation lesions. Supports the activity but not the in vivo repair process terms derived from it.

title: Loss-of-function mutation in the dioxygenase-encoding FTO gene causes severe growth retardation and multiple malformations.
review_notes: Human genetic proof that FTO catalytic activity is essential - homozygous R316Q causes a lethal recessive polymalformation syndrome. PubMed-verified (Am J Hum Genet 2009). Not currently used as a GOA source for this gene but decisive for the in vivo importance of the enzyme.

title: Crystal structure of the FTO protein reveals basis for its substrate specificity.
review_notes: Structural basis for single-strand selectivity. Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract does not state ferrous iron binding explicitly, so the GO:0008198 IDA is taken on the curator's reading of the full structure.

title: N6-methyladenosine in nuclear RNA is a major substrate of the obesity-associated FTO.
review_notes: The in vitro m6A demethylation is not in question and the paper is correctly cited. Its central inference - that nuclear mRNA m6A is the major physiological substrate - is what the direct-sequencing reassessment (PMID:41279954) and the m6Am literature contest.

title: Meclofenamic acid selectively inhibits FTO demethylation of m6A over ALKBH5.
review_notes: Sound inhibitor biochemistry and structure. Supports in vitro m6A turnover; the cellular m6A readout is antibody-based and so inherits the substrate dispute.

title: FTO Obesity Variant Circuitry and Adipocyte Browning in Humans.
review_notes: Excellent paper, wrong gene for these annotations. It dissects the FTO locus and concludes the causal mechanism runs through IRX3 and IRX5; FTO protein is never perturbed. Used in GOA as the IMP source for two FTO biological-process annotations, which conflates locus with gene product. The annotations would be better re-homed to IRX3 and IRX5.

title: Fluorescein Derivatives as Bifunctional Molecules for the Simultaneous Inhibiting and Labeling of FTO Protein.
review_notes: Inhibitor and co-crystal study; supports in vitro FTO demethylase activity. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Dynamic m(6)A mRNA methylation directs translational control of heat shock response.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a genuine mutant-phenotype experiment, but the m6A readout is antibody-based, which is the methodology under challenge. It is the IMP leg of the contested GO:1990931 annotation.

title: Reversible methylation of m(6)A(m) in the 5' cap controls mRNA stability.
review_notes: Establishes cap m6Am as a preferred FTO substrate over m6A - one of the pillars of the substrate reassessment. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Differential m(6)A, m(6)A(m), and m(1)A Demethylation Mediated by FTO in the Cell Nucleus and Cytoplasm.
review_notes: The most informative single reference for this gene. Establishes the snRNA, U6 and tRNA m1A substrates alongside mRNA, and is candid that the tRNA m1A effect size dwarfs the mRNA m6A and cap m6Am effects in Fto-knockout cells.

title: Decoding m(6)Am by simultaneous transcription-start mapping and methylation quantification.
review_notes: Describes CROWN-seq, the quantitative m6Am method used as the FTO-activity positive control in PMID:41279954. Background rather than direct FTO evidence.

title: FTO degrader impairs ribosome biogenesis and protein translation in acute myeloid leukemia.
review_notes: Peer-reviewed 2025 support for the m6A-eraser model in AML, and the stronger of the two pro-m6A 2025 papers because degradation does not depend on active-site occupancy, so it is not vulnerable to the inhibitor-specificity objection. Its m6A quantification is still antibody-dependent.

title: Evidence human FTO catalyses hydroxylation of N6-methyladenosine without direct formation of a demethylated product contrasting with ALKBH5/2/3 and bacterial AlkB.
review_notes: Peer-reviewed comparative MS and real-time NMR study (Nucleic Acids Res 2025). Grounds the chemistry layer of the dispute - isolated FTO forms the hemiaminal hm6A rather than releasing formaldehyde itself. Its own caveat "at least in isolated form" is why the GO demethylase terms were not downgraded on this basis.

title: Structure-Based Design of a Highly Potent Dual-Competitive FTO Inhibitor for Targeted m(6)A Demethylase Inhibition in AML.
review_notes: Representative of the active drug-discovery literature that assumes the m6A-eraser model. Cited here to show that side of the dispute is current, not superseded. Its cellular m6A readouts are antibody-based, and the claim that FTO inhibitors act through FTO is exactly what PMID:41279954 challenges. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: FTO depletion does not alter m(6)A stoichiometry in AML mRNA: a reassessment using direct RNA nanopore sequencing.
review_notes: PREPRINT (bioRxiv, Oct 2025) - not peer reviewed, and marked UNVERIFIED for that reason rather than for any identified defect. Weighed as substantial but not decisive: it is methodologically orthogonal to MeRIP rather than a failed replication, it carries an internal positive control (snRNA m6Am rises as expected, confirming FTO activity was abolished), and it converges with peer-reviewed prior work (PMID:28002401, PMID:30197295) and with an independent chemistry result (PMID:40874592). Used here to demote GO:1990931 from core, never to remove an annotation.

title: Accumulation of cyclin B1 requires E2F and cyclin-A-dependent rearrangement of the anaphase-promoting complex.
review_notes: Abstract only; cyclin A/CDK2 phosphorylation controls Cdh1-APC assembly.

title: MAD2B is an inhibitor of the anaphase-promoting complex.
review_notes: Abstract only; MAD2B inhibits CDH1-APC and CDC20-APC by targeting the coactivators.

title: E2F-dependent accumulation of hEmi1 regulates S phase entry by inhibiting APC(Cdh1).
review_notes: Abstract only; Emi1 inhibits APC(Cdh1) to permit S-phase entry, Cdh1 overexpression causes a G1 block.

title: Mitotic degradation of human thymidine kinase 1 is dependent on the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome-CDH1-mediated pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached; establishes KEN-box-dependent TK1 binding and reconstituted APC/C-Cdh1 ubiquitination. Basis of the GO:1990756 IDA.

title: The anaphase-promoting complex: a key factor in the regulation of cell cycle.
review_notes: General APC review; source of NAS rows.

title: Emi1 stably binds and inhibits the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome as a pseudosubstrate inhibitor.
review_notes: Full text cached; Emi1 is a pseudosubstrate that occupies the D-box receptor of APC/C-Cdh1.

title: A bacterial effector targets Mad2L2, an APC inhibitor, to modulate host cell cycling.
review_notes: Abstract only; Shigella IpaB targets Mad2L2; FZR1 appears as the Mad2L2-bound coactivator.

title: The Cdc14B-Cdh1-Plk1 axis controls the G2 DNA-damage-response checkpoint.
review_notes: Full text cached; Cdc14B-Cdh1-Plk1 axis in the G2 DNA-damage checkpoint, Claspin as a G1 substrate, phosphorylation-site mutants.

title: Hypoxia and cell cycle regulation of the von Hippel-Lindau tumor suppressor.
review_notes: Full text cached; pVHL-Cdh1 association reported with hedged substrate status.

title: Substrate binding on the APC/C occurs between the coactivator Cdh1 and the processivity factor Doc1.
review_notes: Full text cached; bipartite coactivator-Doc1 substrate receptor.

title: Nuclear PTEN regulates the APC-CDH1 tumor-suppressive complex in a phosphatase-independent manner.
review_notes: Full text cached; nuclear PTEN promotes APC/C-CDH1 assembly; source of the mouse senescence/proliferation IMPs.

title: Deubiquitinase USP37 is activated by CDK2 to antagonize APC(CDH1) and promote S phase entry.
review_notes: Abstract only; USP37 antagonises APC(CDH1) on cyclin A and becomes a K11-ubiquitinated substrate in mitosis.

title: Cyclin F-mediated degradation of ribonucleotide reductase M2 controls genome integrity and DNA repair.
review_notes: Abstract only and centred on cyclin F/RRM2 in G2; FZR1 content not visible in the cache.

title: Molecular mechanism of APC/C activation by mitotic phosphorylation.
review_notes: Full text cached; cryo-EM of human APC/C with coactivators, C-box/IR-tail docking, Cdh1 versus Cdc20 regulation by phosphorylation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS network (BioPlex 3.0); interaction context only.

title: De novo FZR1 loss-of-function variants cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
review_notes: Full text cached; DEE109 variants, nuclear localisation of FZR1 by immunofluorescence.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Proteome-scale U2OS cell-map AP-MS; interaction context only.

title: Transmembrane topology of human glucose 6-phosphate transporter.
review_notes: Primarily about the G6P transporter (SLC37A4/G6PT); establishes that the glucose-6-phosphatase active site is situated in the ER lumen. Supports the luminal-active-site location of the G6PC1 system.

title: Glucose-6-phosphatase mutation G188R confers an atypical glycogen storage disease type 1b phenotype.
review_notes: G188R loss-of-function G6PC1 variant; supports glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic activity and the GSD1a disease association.

title: The catalytic center of glucose-6-phosphatase. HIS176 is the nucleophile forming the phosphohistidine-enzyme intermediate during catalysis.
review_notes: Defines the catalytic mechanism (His-176 nucleophile, His-119 proton donor); primary support for glucose-6-phosphatase activity.

title: Glycogen storage disease type Ia in Argentina: two novel glucose-6-phosphatase mutations affecting protein stability.
review_notes: T16R and Y209C variants abolish enzymatic activity in expression assays; supports glucose-6-phosphatase activity and GSD1a.

title: Brain contains a functional glucose-6-phosphatase complex capable of endogenous glucose production.
review_notes: Abstract foregrounds glucose-6-phosphatase-beta (G6PC3) in astrocytes; cited by MGI for a G6PC1 IDA of glucose-6-phosphatase activity. Function is correct for G6PC1, but the abstract does not directly assay G6PC1.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome screen; source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations (WFS1, RNF11). No functional consequence established for G6PC1.

title: Mutations in the glucose-6-phosphatase gene that cause glycogen storage disease type 1a.
review_notes: Cloning and expression of human G6Pase; inactivating GSD1a mutations. Primary support for glucose-6-phosphatase activity, gluconeogenesis, and glucose homeostasis.

title: Glycogen storage disease type 1a in Israel: biochemical, clinical, and mutational studies.
review_notes: States G6Pase catalyzes the final common step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; V166G variant causes complete inactivation.

title: Transmembrane topology of glucose-6-phosphatase.
review_notes: Establishes nine-TM ER membrane topology with luminal active site and His-176 as catalytic phosphoryl acceptor; primary support for ER membrane location.

title: Histidine 167 is the phosphate acceptor in glucose-6-phosphatase-beta forming a phosphohistidine enzyme intermediate during catalysis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but directly establishes the catalytic mechanism and active-site residues of G6PC3 (G6Pase-beta); supports the core MF.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Generic high-throughput membrane proteomics; supports only a non-specific membrane localization, superseded by ER membrane. Not G6PC3-specific.

title: Functional analysis of mutations in a severe congenital neutropenia syndrome caused by glucose-6-phosphatase-β deficiency.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC4794745). Directly supports G6PC3 catalytic activity, ER-membrane localization, SLC37A4/G6PT partnership, and the SCN4 disease mechanism. Basis of the IMP GO:0004346 annotation.

title: Cell growth and cholesterol metabolism in human glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient lymphomononuclear cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports an indirect NADPH-supply role of G6PD in cholesterol synthesis (G6PD-deficient PBMC show reduced cholesterol synthesis).

title: Structural studies of glucose-6-phosphate and NADP+ binding to human glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified human G6PD structural study; directly supports catalytic activity, NADP binding (catalytic and structural sites), substrate binding, and homo-oligomerization.

title: Production of inflammatory molecules in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from severely glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase-deficient subjects.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports only an indirect lipid/inflammatory phenotype of G6PD deficiency, not a direct lipid-metabolic function.

title: Mutation in G6PD gene leads to loss of cellular control of protein glutathionylation: mechanism and implication.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; strongly supports G6PD's role in glutathione metabolism and the cellular oxidative-stress response via NADPH.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; incidental localization of an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteomics; peripheral/incidental membrane association, not a primary functional site.

title: ATM activates the pentose phosphate pathway promoting anti-oxidant defence and DNA repair.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; documents HSPB1/Hsp27 binding and direct stimulation of G6PD activity in the ATM oxidative-stress/DNA-damage response.

title: Quantitative proteomic analysis of human substantia nigra in Alzheimer's disease, Huntington's disease and Multiple sclerosis.
review_notes: Disease proteomics survey; detection/altered expression does not support a substantia nigra developmental role for G6PD (HEP annotation over-interpreted).

title: Sex steroid hormone modulation of NADPH pathways in MCF-7 cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; measures G6PD activity and NADPH-generating pathways, supporting the pentose phosphate shunt annotation.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; incidental localization of an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Ribose metabolism and nucleic acid synthesis in normal and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase-deficient human erythrocytes infected with Plasmodium falciparum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; deficiency-based evidence for the oxidative-branch PPP role, glutathione maintenance, and ribose-phosphate contribution.

title: Regulation of G6PD acetylation by SIRT2 and KAT9 modulates NADPH homeostasis and cell survival during oxidative stress.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports catalytic activity, K403 acetylation-dependent regulation, homodimerization requirement, and the SIRT2 interaction.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; corroborates G6PD self-interaction (identical protein binding).

title: Severe G6PD Deficiency Due to a New Missense Mutation in an Infant of Northern European Descent.
review_notes: PubMed-verified case report; very low enzymatic activity of a novel variant supports the catalytic function and X-linked deficiency phenotype.

title: Aldolase B suppresses hepatocellular carcinogenesis by inhibiting G6PD and pentose phosphate pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies G6PD as the rate-limiting PPP enzyme, directly assays its activity, and documents the ALDOB-G6PD-TP53 ternary complex.

title: Substitution of arginine 219 by glycine compromises stability, dimerization, and catalytic activity in a G6PD mutant.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text; direct biochemical/biophysical evidence for catalytic activity, dimerization, and substrate binding of human G6PD.

title: Biochemical variants of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase giving rise to congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified classic study; variant enzymes causing CNSHA support the catalytic function and erythrocyte oxidative-defense role.

title: Glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity in membranes of erythrocytes from normal individuals and subjects with Mediterranean G6PD deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports catalytic activity, cytosolic localization, and a minor peripheral membrane-associated pool in erythrocytes.

title: Mutation profile of the GAA gene in 40 Italian patients with late onset glycogen storage disease type II.
review_notes: Late-onset Pompe mutation-profile study; establishes that GAA deficiency impairs glycogen degradation with lysosomal accumulation. Supports the disease context but the diaphragm-contraction annotation derived from it is a disease consequence, not a molecular function.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Placental lysosomal-membrane proteome; basis for UniProt's lysosome and lysosome-membrane location. GAA co-purifies with lysosomal membranes though it is a soluble lumenal enzyme.

title: Molecular and functional characterization of eight novel GAA mutations in Italian infants with Pompe disease.
