review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. Native human erythrocyte protein, activity measurements, mass spectrometry, and simulation support cytosolic catalysis and redox-dependent regulation.

title: Design and evaluation of azaindole-substituted N-hydroxypyridones as glyoxalase I inhibitors.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The curated activity and zinc annotations are consistent with the inhibitor-bound structure; full text was unavailable.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity, full text, and the GOA HDA record were checked. The result supports exosome cargo detection without establishing secretion or extracellular catalytic function for GLO1.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and the GOA IPI record were checked. GOA reports a GLO1-PUS10 binary interaction, but no GLO1-specific functional consequence is established; generic protein binding is therefore uninformative.

title: Human glyoxalase I. cDNA cloning, expression, and sequence similarity to glyoxalase I from Pseudomonas putida.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This is the founding human-cDNA and heterologous-function study and directly supports catalytic activity and methylglyoxal detoxification; full text was unavailable.

title: Crystal structure of human glyoxalase I--evidence for gene duplication and 3D domain swapping.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The structure establishes homodimer architecture, domain swapping, and the intersubunit zinc active site; full text extraction was unavailable.

title: Involvement of an active-site Zn2+ ligand in the catalytic mechanism of human glyoxalase I.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Mutagenesis, metal analysis, activity measurements, and structure directly establish zinc-dependent catalysis and the catalytic glutamate; full text was unavailable.

title: Manual literature synthesis for human GLO1 (Q04760)
review_notes: Manual synthesis produced after both configured automated providers failed; conclusions are anchored to reviewed UniProt, GOA, Reactome, and primary literature.

title: Manual literature and annotation review notes for human GLO1
review_notes: Manual journal of source inspection, term checks, evidence boundaries, annotation decisions, and open questions.

title: UniProtKB record for human GLO1 (Q04760)
review_notes: The reviewed UniProtKB record was checked directly for catalytic reaction, zinc cofactor, dimerization, active-site residues, structures, isoforms, post-translational modifications, and source provenance.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Correctly cited exosome proteomics study; supports detection of GLOD4 in that preparation but says nothing about its function.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Guo Z et al., Sci Signal 2014;7(354):rs7, doi 10.1126/scisignal.2005473. The paper is real and correctly identified, but it does not support a cadherin binding molecular function for GLOD4: it is a BioID proximity-labelling survey that reported 561 proteins near the E-cadherin tail, and proximity within a labelling radius is not binding. Flagged MISCITED for that mismatch between what the paper measured and what the annotation asserts, not for any defect in the study.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP. A high-quality, multi-criteria mitochondrial proteome; appropriate support for the mitochondrion location and independently consistent with the fractionation reported in PMID:41628334.

title: Selective peroxynitrite-mediated protein nitration catalyzed by glyoxalase domain containing protein 4.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Wright S, Dang VC, Hussain S, et al., Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2026 Feb 2;123(6):e2515002123, doi 10.1073/pnas.2515002123, PMC12890929; full text cached. The sole source for every functional claim about GLOD4, and internally well controlled: kinetics, MS site mapping, cosubstrate exclusion, active-site mutants, a 23,000-protein selectivity screen, knockout cells and gene-dose-dependent knockout mice. Marked VERIFIED because the citation and the science are sound as far as one study can be, but two limitations should travel with it. Most authors are employees of Nitrase Therapeutics and the paper declares a patent application on GLOD4 activity; and the enzyme class is presented by the authors themselves as a proposal, with the catalytic mechanism explicitly unresolved. Independent replication is not yet available.

title: Isolation, characterization and expression of a human brain mitochondrial glutaminase cDNA.
review_notes: Cloning of the human brain mitochondrial glutaminase cDNA; recombinant enzyme is active and carries an N-terminal mitochondrial targeting signal. Abstract-only in cache; supports glutaminase activity and mitochondrial localization.

title: Cloning and analysis of unique human glutaminase isoforms generated by tissue-specific alternative splicing.
review_notes: Defines the human KGA, GAC and GAM splice isoforms and their tissue expression; GAC is the high-glutaminase-activity isoform in breast cancer cells. GAM (isoform 2) lacks catalytic activity per UniProt.

title: Brain-specific BNIP-2-homology protein Caytaxin relocalises glutaminase to neurite terminals and reduces glutamate levels.
review_notes: Establishes the direct ATCAY (Caytaxin, Q86WG3)-KGA interaction and shows ATCAY inhibits KGA activity and lowers glutamate. Supports the protein-binding IPI and the mitochondrial IDA; the derived GO:0062133 process term describes ATCAY's regulatory effect rather than a GLS function (flagged as over-annotation).

title: The nuclear receptor FXR regulates hepatic transport and metabolism of glutamine and glutamate.
review_notes: Primarily about FXR regulation of hepatic glutamine/glutamate metabolism; only contextually supports glutaminase producing glutamate. Basis for a TAS annotation of L-glutamate biosynthetic process.

title: Full-length human glutaminase in complex with an allosteric inhibitor.
review_notes: First full-length human GAC crystal structure with kinetic assays; directly supports glutaminase activity, glutamine catabolism/glutamate biosynthesis, and the homotetramer.

title: Mitochondrial localization and structure-based phosphate activation mechanism of Glutaminase C with implications for cancer metabolism.
review_notes: Demonstrates GAC is mitochondrial and describes the phosphate/tetramerization activation mechanism relevant to cancer metabolism. Supports the mitochondrial localization annotation.

title: Structural basis for the allosteric inhibitory mechanism of human kidney-type glutaminase (KGA) and its regulation by Raf-Mek-Erk signaling in cancer cell metabolism.
review_notes: KGA crystal structures with glutamate/glutamine, catalytic-activity assays, active-site mutagenesis, and RAF1/MAP2K2 interaction; supports the EXP glutaminase activity annotation and the homotetramer/regulation biology.

title: Structural basis for the active site inhibition mechanism of human kidney-type glutaminase (KGA).
review_notes: Full text available; cKGA:DON structure and active-site mutagenesis (Ser286, Lys289, Tyr249, Tyr466) confirm catalytic residues and glutaminase activity.

title: Design and evaluation of novel glutaminase inhibitors.
review_notes: Glutaminase-inhibitor design study with KGA/GAC structures and activity assays; supports the EXP glutaminase activity annotation.

title: The origin and evolution of human glutaminases and their atypical C-terminal ankyrin repeats.
review_notes: Full-length KGA structure and evolutionary/ANK-repeat analysis; determines catalytic activity and subunit structure. Supports the EXP glutaminase activity annotation and the homotetramer/filament biology.

title: Characterization of the interactions of potent allosteric inhibitors with glutaminase C, a key enzyme in cancer cell glutamine metabolism.
review_notes: GAC allosteric-inhibitor (UPGL00004/CB-839/BPTES) structural and enzymatic characterization; supports the EXP glutaminase activity annotation.

title: GLS hyperactivity causes glutamate excess, infantile cataract and profound developmental delay.
review_notes: Gain-of-function Ser482Cys GLS variant (CASGID) causing glutamate excess; functional basis for the intracellular glutamate homeostasis IMP annotation.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome study; corroborates GLS mitochondrial localization (HTP evidence).

title: Molecular cloning, sequencing and expression studies of the human breast cancer cell glutaminase.
review_notes: Original cloning of the human liver-type (GLS2) glutaminase from ZR-75 breast-cancer cells; establishes the 602-aa protein, the mitochondrial import presequence, and liver/brain/pancreas tissue distribution. Supports the TAS glutaminase-activity and mitochondrion annotations.

title: The C-terminus of human glutaminase L mediates association with PDZ domain-containing proteins.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid identification of PDZ-domain interactors (alpha1-syntrophin/SNTA1 and GIP/TAX1BP3) binding the GLS2 C-terminal -ESXV motif. Supports the IPI protein-binding annotation; interaction is real but the GO term itself is uninformative.

title: Phosphate-activated glutaminase (GLS2), a p53-inducible regulator of glutamine metabolism and reactive oxygen species.
review_notes: Suzuki et al. companion paper identifying GLS2 as a p53 target regulating glutamine metabolism, GSH synthesis, ROS levels, and the apoptotic response. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available:false); source of the IDA mitochondrion and IMP ROS/apoptosis annotations.

title: Glutaminase 2, a novel p53 target gene regulating energy metabolism and antioxidant function.
review_notes: Hu et al. companion paper; full text available. States GLS2 is a mitochondrial glutaminase catalyzing glutamine-to-glutamate hydrolysis, a p53 target that boosts glutamate/alpha-ketoglutarate, mitochondrial respiration and GSH while lowering ROS, and is lost in HCC. Primary support for the core function synthesis.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI proteome-scale binary interactome; GLS2 (with HIP1 and XAF1) appears in the dataset, not in the cached narrative text. Basis for a high-throughput IPI protein-binding annotation; contextual only.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale AP-MS interactome; source of a high-throughput IPI protein-binding annotation (GLS2-HIP1). Data are in the large-scale network, not the cached narrative; contextual only.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports the HTP mitochondrion localization of GLS2. GLS2 is in the dataset rather than the cached narrative text.

title: Nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) and housekeeping (GLUD1) human glutamate dehydrogenases are regulated by distinct allosteric mechanisms: implications for biologic function.
review_notes: Primary characterization of human GLUD1-derived GDH: dual-cofactor activity, potent GTP inhibition (IC50 ~0.2 microM), and ADP/leucine activation. Directly supports the catalytic and allosteric-regulation annotations.

title: Structures of bovine glutamate dehydrogenase complexes elucidate the mechanism of purine regulation.
review_notes: Bovine GDH structures (with human HHS-mutant kinetics) establishing the shared mechanism of oxidative deamination and dual NAD(H)/NADP(H) usage and the ADP/GTP allosteric sites; used by UniProt as experimental evidence for EC 1.4.1.3.

title: Acute insulin responses to leucine in children with the hyperinsulinism/hyperammonemia syndrome.
review_notes: Clinical study of HI/HA (HHF6) patients; establishes the mechanistic link between loss of GTP inhibition of GDH and leucine-stimulated insulin secretion. Supports the positive-regulation-of-insulin-secretion annotation.

title: Expression, purification and characterization of human glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH) allosteric regulatory mutations.
review_notes: Purified human GDH; states the reversible oxidative deamination reaction in the mitochondrial matrix and characterizes ADP/GTP allosteric sites via mutants. Anchors the catalytic-activity, location, and ADP-binding annotations.

title: Importance of glutamate 279 for the coenzyme binding of human glutamate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Photoaffinity-labeling and mutagenesis identifying Glu279 at the NAD(+) coenzyme-binding site of human GDH. Supports the NAD+ binding annotation.

title: Study of structure-function relationships in human glutamate dehydrogenases reveals novel molecular mechanisms for the regulation of the nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) isoenzyme.
review_notes: Structure-function/mutagenesis of human GDH isoenzymes (GLUD1 vs GLUD2) mapping allosteric (ADP/leucine/GTP) determinants. Supports ADP- and L-leucine-binding annotations.

title: Molecular basis of human glutamate dehydrogenase regulation under changing energy demands.
review_notes: Characterizes GLUD1-derived GDH activity/regulation and confirms mitochondrial localization by GFP fusion. Supports the catalytic-activity and mitochondrion annotations.

title: Identification of ADP-ribosylation site in human glutamate dehydrogenase isozymes.
review_notes: Measures human GDH activity and its inhibition by ADP-ribosylation; establishes one-subunit-per-hexamer stoichiometry and the reactive Cys. Supports catalytic activity and the ADP-ribosylation PTM.

title: SIRT4 inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase and opposes the effects of calorie restriction in pancreatic beta cells.
review_notes: Shows SIRT4 ADP-ribosylates and downregulates GDH, linking GDH activity to amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion in beta-cells. Supports catalytic-activity and the SIRT4-interaction/regulation annotations.

title: Mitochondrial targeting adaptation of the hominoid-specific glutamate dehydrogenase driven by positive Darwinian selection.
review_notes: Full-text-available; directly states GLUD1 localizes to both mitochondria and cytoplasm (vs mitochondria-specific GLUD2). Supports the cytoplasm annotation.

title: Human GLUD1 and GLUD2 glutamate dehydrogenase localize to mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: Experimental subcellular localization: most GDH translocates into mitochondria, with a minor ER pool. Supports the mitochondrion and endoplasmic-reticulum location annotations.

title: Quantitative proteomic analysis of human substantia nigra in Alzheimer's disease, Huntington's disease and Multiple sclerosis.
review_notes: Proteomic abundance survey of substantia nigra in neurodegenerative disease. Detection/differential abundance does not support a role in substantia nigra development; the derived GO annotation is an over-interpretation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale BioPlex interactome. Correctly cited as source of a high-throughput protein-protein interaction, but yields only an uninformative protein-binding term for GLUD1.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 interactome; source of a high-throughput interaction giving only a generic protein-binding annotation.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization of GLUD1.

title: Cryo-EM structure of the KLHL22 E3 ligase bound to an oligomeric metabolic enzyme.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure of CUL3(KLHL22)-RBX1 bound to the GDH1 hexamer; KLHL22 polyubiquitinates GDH1 in vitro. Biologically meaningful KLHL22 interaction, but recorded in GOA only as generic protein binding.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map/interactome; source of a generic protein-binding annotation.

title: Abnormal glutamate metabolism in an adult-onset degenerative neurological disorder.
review_notes: Human patients with partial GDH deficiency show elevated plasma glutamate and reduced alpha-ketoglutarate, indicating decreased glutamate catabolism. Supports the L-glutamate catabolic process annotation.

title: Nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) and housekeeping (GLUD1) human glutamate dehydrogenases are regulated by distinct allosteric mechanisms: implications for biologic function.
review_notes: Primary characterization of recombinant human GLUD2 vs GLUD1: GLUD2 is GTP-insensitive, strongly activated by ADP and L-leucine. Supports the catalytic activity and allosteric-effector binding annotations. Abstract-only in cache; annotations defer to the original curator's reading of the full text.

title: Study of structure-function relationships in human glutamate dehydrogenases reveals novel molecular mechanisms for the regulation of the nerve tissue-specific (GLUD2) isoenzyme.
review_notes: Structure-function/mutagenesis study identifying Arg443Ser and Gly456Ala as the adaptive substitutions underlying GLUD2's GTP resistance and ADP dependence. Supports ADP and L-leucine binding annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Molecular basis of human glutamate dehydrogenase regulation under changing energy demands.
review_notes: Characterizes GLUD1/GLUD2 regulation under changing energy demands; GLUD2 has low basal activity, is GTP-resistant, and is fully activatable by ADP/L-leucine, functioning under acidification and high ADP. Supports the catalytic-activity annotation. Abstract-only.

title: Mitochondrial targeting adaptation of the hominoid-specific glutamate dehydrogenase driven by positive Darwinian selection.
review_notes: Full-text available. Establishes GLUD2 as a hominoid retrogene specifically targeted to mitochondria (unlike cytoplasm+mitochondria GLUD1) via a positively selected E7K MTS substitution. Directly supports the mitochondrion IDA and the NOT-cytosol IDA.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). GLUD2 appears only in supplementary interaction data (WITH GLUD1/P00367); yields a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex 3). Same situation as PMID:28514442: bare "protein binding" with WITH GLUD1/P00367.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial-proteome study; identifies GLUD2 as mitochondrial (HTP), corroborating its mitochondrial-matrix localization.

title: Novel human glutamate dehydrogenase expressed in neural and testicular tissues and encoded by an X-linked intronless gene.
review_notes: Founding GLUD2 paper: cloning of the X-linked intronless GLUD2, expression in retina, testis and brain, and recombinant enzyme catalyzing oxidative deamination of glutamate. Supports the catalytic-activity and glutamate-metabolism annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H interactome map; source of a GLUL self-interaction (identical protein binding). Cached full text does not mention GLUL by name (hit in supplementary data). Consistent with the known homo-oligomer.

title: Congenital glutamine deficiency with glutamine synthetase mutations.
review_notes: Establishes human GS activity and disease (congenital glutamine deficiency) via R324C/R341C variants; abstract-only cache but directly supports the EXP glutamine synthetase activity annotation.

title: Glutamine synthetase is essential for proliferation of fetal skin fibroblasts.
review_notes: Shows GS activity is required for fetal fibroblast proliferation (downstream of glutamine supply). Supports GO:0008283 IDA.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary-exosome proteomics; source of the extracellular exosome HDA localization. Over-annotation for an abundant cytosolic enzyme.

title: Shifted Transversal Design smart-pooling for high coverage interactome mapping.
review_notes: Smart-pooling interactome screen; source of a GLUL self-interaction. Consistent with homo-oligomerization but uninformative on its own.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteomics; source of the nucleus HDA localization. Bulk proteomic detection of an abundant cytosolic protein; over-annotation.

title: The nuclear receptor FXR regulates hepatic transport and metabolism of glutamine and glutamate.
review_notes: Describes hepatic (perivenous) glutamine synthesis by GS and glutamate uptake; supports the TAS glutamine-biosynthesis and glutamate-catabolism annotations. Main focus is FXR regulation of the pathway.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: Human liver interactome study; source of a GLUL self-interaction. Consistent with homo-oligomerization; uninformative bare-binding hit.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome map; source of a GLUL self-interaction. Consistent with the decameric assembly.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Parallel variant-cloning / interaction study; source of a GLUL self-interaction. Uninformative bare-binding hit.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Interactome perturbation study; source of the GLUL-TAT (P17735) bare protein binding annotation. No functional context; over-annotation.

title: Genome-wide RNAi Screening Identifies Protein Modules Required for 40S Subunit Synthesis in Human Cells.
review_notes: Genome-wide RNAi screen showing intracellular glutamine synthesis (GLUL) supports 40S subunit production; supports the ribosome-biogenesis and nucleolar-localization IMP annotations. Effect attributed to glutamine synthesis (downstream of core activity).

title: Role of glutamine synthetase in angiogenesis beyond glutamine synthesis.
review_notes: Establishes the glutamine-synthesis-independent moonlighting role: GS autopalmitoylates and palmitoylates RHOJ to control endothelial migration and sprouting angiogenesis; also confirms cytosol/plasma-membrane localization and GS catalytic activity.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Allele-frequency interactome perturbation study; source of a GLUL self-interaction consistent with homo-oligomerization.

title: Bestrophin-2 and glutamine synthetase form a complex for glutamate release.
review_notes: Shows GLUL-BEST2 complex formation gating glutamate release; confirms GS catalytic activity (R299E abolishes it) and cytosolic localization. Cached abstract failed to fetch (error blob); claims grounded to UniProt CC lines.

title: Physiological substrates for human lysosomal beta -hexosaminidase S.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; abstract explicitly states that hydrolysis of membrane-bound SM2 by Hex S was synergistically stimulated by the GM2 activator protein, supporting GM2A's activator/lipid-chaperone role in glycosphingolipid catabolism.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary-exosome proteomics; supports only the non-core extracellular-exosome localization of GM2A, not its function.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports only the non-core extracellular-exosome localization.

title: Endolysosomes Are the Principal Intracellular Sites of Acid Hydrolase Activity.
review_notes: Establishes endolysosomes as the principal sites of acid hydrolase activity; used as the basis for the curator IC placing GM2A at the endolysosomal ILV membrane. Not GM2A-specific but contextually apt.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 high-throughput AP-MS interactome; underlies a generic protein-binding IPI (partner ACTA2) that is over-annotated for GM2A.

title: Membrane lipids and their degradation compounds control GM2 catabolism at intralysosomal luminal vesicles.
review_notes: Primary reconstitution study directly demonstrating GM2A-assisted GM2 catabolism and its regulation by membrane lipids; strongest support for the lipid chaperone / ganglioside catabolic core functions.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 high-throughput AP-MS interactome; underlies a generic protein-binding IPI (partner ACTA2) that is over-annotated for GM2A.

title: Biochemical characterization of human GMP synthetase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary biochemical/kinetic characterization of purified human GMP synthetase (Nakamura & Lou 1995, JBC); directly supports the glutamine-hydrolyzing GMP synthase activity. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Enhanced in vitro growth of glomerular cells derived from rats with immune-mediated mesangial injury.
review_notes: Cited by the MGI GO:0003921 (GMP synthase activity) IDA annotation, but this PMID resolves to a rat glomerular mesangial-cell growth paper (Harendza et al. 1993, Exp Nephrol) with no relation to GMP synthase. Wrong/transposed identifier; the intended reference is almost certainly PMID:8089153 (human GMP synthetase cloning). The annotated function is correct and independently supported, so the annotation is retained.

title: Human GMP synthetase. Protein purification, cloning, and functional expression of cDNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary paper purifying human GMP synthetase, cloning its cDNA, and showing functional complementation of an E. coli guaA mutant. This is the UniProt evidence for EC 6.3.5.2, function, and cytosolic localization. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Reduction of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine 2-epimerase/N-acetylmannosamine kinase activity and sialylation in distal myopathy with rimmed vacuoles.
review_notes: Identified pathogenic GNE mutations in distal myopathy with rimmed vacuoles and showed reduced epimerase and kinase activities and reduced muscle sialylation; source of the core MF (both activities) and BP (sialic acid biosynthesis) IMP annotations. Abstract-only in cache; claims verified against the abstract and UniProt.

title: Influence of UDP-GlcNAc 2-epimerase/ManNAc kinase mutant proteins on hereditary inclusion body myopathy.
review_notes: Recombinant expression and enzymatic assay of GNE HIBM mutants; each mutant reduced both GNE activities. Supports the core ManNAc kinase (EXP) function. Abstract-only in cache.

title: UDP-N-acetylglucosamine 2-epimerase/N-acetylmannosamine kinase (GNE) binds to alpha-actinin 1: novel pathways in skeletal muscle?
review_notes: Full text available. Demonstrates a specific GNE-alpha-actinin 1 (ACTN1) interaction in skeletal muscle by SPR, in vitro binding and co-IP. Supports the ACTN1 IPI, but only via the uninformative protein binding term; no functional consequence for GNE catalysis established, so annotation is marked over-annotated.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome map (Rolland et al.); source of multiple generic protein binding IPI annotations with no established functional relevance to GNE. Correctly cited but low informativeness for GNE function.

title: Mechanism and inhibition of human UDP-GlcNAc 2-epimerase, the key enzyme in sialic acid biosynthesis.
review_notes: Full text available. Crystal structure of the human epimerase domain with UDP and CMP-Neu5Ac plus catalytic-residue mutagenesis; establishes the epimerase mechanism and the CMP-Neu5Ac feedback-inhibition / sialuria basis. Primary support for the core epimerase MF (IDA).

title: Identification of the metabolic defect in sialuria.
review_notes: Direct assay of the rate-limiting UDP-GlcNAc 2-epimerase; identified the sialuria defect as loss of CMP-Neu5Ac feedback inhibition. Supports the core epimerase MF and its allosteric regulation. Abstract-only in cache; claims verified against abstract and UniProt.

title: Activity of N-acylneuraminate-9-phosphatase (NANP) is not essential for de novo sialic acid biosynthesis.
review_notes: GNE knockout cell lines show reduced cell-surface sialylation and dramatically reduced CMP-sialic acid, directly demonstrating GNE's requirement for de novo sialic acid biosynthesis. Supports the BP (IMP) annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Systematic interactome variant-disruption study; source of a generic protein binding IPI with no established functional relevance to GNE's sialic-acid function.

title: Effect of naturally occurring mutations in human glycine N-methyltransferase on activity and conformation.
review_notes: Kinetic/conformational characterization of recombinant WT and disease-mutant human GNMT; supports the enzyme activity annotation and KM values.

title: Glycine N -methyltransferase deficiency: a new patient with a novel mutation.
review_notes: Case report of GNMT deficiency; diagnostic metabolite pattern (elevated methionine/AdoMet, normal N-methylglycine) and near-abolished activity of the N140S variant.

title: Glycine N-methyltransferases: a comparison of the crystal structures and kinetic properties of recombinant human, mouse and rat enzymes.
review_notes: Crystal structures and kinetics of recombinant human GNMT; supports activity, glycine binding, SAM metabolism, and homotetramer.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale Y2H screen (CCSB-HI1); source of a generic protein-binding IPI, not functionally specific for GNMT.

title: Destabilization of human glycine N-methyltransferase by H176N mutation.
review_notes: Biophysical/structural study of human GNMT tetramer and the destabilizing H176N disease variant; supports activity and homotetramerization.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: Human liver interactome screen; source of a generic protein-binding IPI, not functionally specific for GNMT.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Clone-seq/Y2H interactome-scanning pipeline; GNMT (Gnmt) appears in a self-interaction/stability panel, consistent with homotetramer.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Alternative-splicing interactome study; source of generic protein-binding and self-interaction IPIs for GNMT.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Population-scale interaction-disruption study; source of generic protein-binding and self-interaction IPIs for GNMT.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; multiple generic protein-binding IPIs for GNMT, not individually functionally validated.

title: Mammalian glycine N-methyltransferases. Comparative kinetic and structural properties of the enzymes from human, rat, rabbit and pig livers.
review_notes: Comparative kinetic/structural study establishing human liver GNMT as an abundant homotetramer with cooperative SAM kinetics.

title: GNMT tetramer transfers methyl group from AdoMet to Gly to form AdoHyc and SARC
review_notes: Reactome reaction for cytosolic GNMT tetramer catalyzing AdoMet-to-glycine methyl transfer; supports catalytic function and cytosol localization.

title: UniProtKB entry GNMT_HUMAN (Q14749)
review_notes: Primary source for catalytic activity (EC 2.1.1.20, RHEA:19937), SAM:SAH regulatory function, homotetramer, cytoplasmic localization, kinetics, and disease variants.

title: Identification and characterization of the mouse cDNA encoding acyl-CoA:dihydroxyacetone phosphate acyltransferase.
review_notes: Establishes DHAPAT catalytic activity (EC 2.3.1.42) via heterologous expression of the ortholog cDNA in yeast; used by UniProt as an EC:2.3.1.42 catalytic-activity reference. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Impaired membrane traffic in defective ether lipid biosynthesis.
review_notes: Characterizes RCDP2 disease variants, catalytic activity, and pathway; cited by UniProt for FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, and PATHWAY. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Role of dihydroxyacetonephosphate acyltransferase in the biosynthesis of plasmalogens and nonether glycerolipids.
review_notes: Functional-rescue study establishing that peroxisomal DHAPAT is essential for plasmalogen biosynthesis and does not normally contribute to nonether glycerolipids; source of FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION, and PATHWAY in UniProt. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Large-scale NK-cell membrane proteome; supports only a generic membrane localization for GNPAT.

title: PEX14 is required for microtubule-based peroxisome motility in human cells.
review_notes: Native peroxisomal-membrane-complex study; the associated HDA dataset places GNPAT at the peroxisomal membrane. The paper's focus is PEX14/tubulin, not GNPAT function.

title: Purification of peroxisomal acyl-CoA: dihydroxyacetonephosphate acyltransferase from human placenta.

title: Ether lipid biosynthesis: isolation and molecular characterization of human dihydroxyacetonephosphate acyltransferase.
