title: Acyl-CoA:dihydroxyacetonephosphate acyltransferase: cloning of the human cDNA and resolution of the molecular basis in rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata type 2.
review_notes: Cloning of human DHAPAT cDNA and demonstration that RCDP type 2 is caused by GNPAT/DHAPAT mutations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Structural and kinetic differences between human and Aspergillus fumigatus D-glucosamine-6-phosphate N-acetyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available false); the abstract plus UniProt CATALYTIC ACTIVITY and BIOPHYSICOCHEMICAL PROPERTIES sections directly support the EC 2.3.1.4 core function and kinetics.

title: Acceptor substrate binding revealed by crystal structure of human glucosamine-6-phosphate N-acetyltransferase 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract-only in cache. Supports the core catalytic MF and the homodimer/self-interaction (GO:0042802) annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome map (HuRI). Source of a GNPNAT1 self-interaction (identical protein binding) call; consistent with the known homodimer but not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome study; source of a bare protein binding call (with FABP1). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary (Y2H) interactome map; source of a bare protein binding call (with PSMB8). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome study (BioPlex); source of a bare protein binding call (with FABP1). Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Acetylation of glucosamine 6-phosphate to GlcNAc6P
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing the GNPNAT1 catalytic step in the cytosol; supports the core MF, BP, and cytosolic location.

title: A cDNA clone for human glucosamine-6-sulphatase reveals differences between arylsulphatases and non-arylsulphatases.
review_notes: Primary cloning/characterization paper; directly establishes the core molecular function and biological role. Source of the UniProt EC 3.1.6.14 and FUNCTION evidence.

title: Purification of a 75 kDa protein from the organelle matrix of human neutrophils and identification as N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulphatase.
review_notes: Provides direct (IDA) support for the molecular function, heparan sulfate catabolic process, and the neutrophil primary-granule / secreted locations.

title: Sulphatase activities are regulated by the interaction of sulphatase-modifying factor 1 with SUMF2.
review_notes: GNS is one of seven sulphatases co-transfected/assayed; supports the FGly/SUMF1 dependence of GNS activity but the paper's main focus is SUMF1/SUMF2 regulation, not GNS specifically.

title: Systematic identification of SH3 domain-mediated human protein-protein interactions by peptide array target screening.
review_notes: High-throughput SH3 peptide-array screen; citation is correct but supports only an uninformative "protein binding" annotation with no evidence of biological relevance to GNS.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Large-scale exosome proteomics; supports only a non-core secreted-vesicle location.

title: Human liver N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulphate sulphatase. Catalytic properties.
review_notes: Detailed enzymology; supports the molecular function and the glycosaminoglycan catabolic process (exolytic mechanism).

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline. Correctly assigns PLP binding and the transaminase family MF, but also produces the uninformative parents (catalytic activity, amino acid metabolic process).

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS pipeline (mostly transfer from rat P13221 / bovine P00508). Correctly recovers the core aspartate/glutamate/2-oxoglutarate metabolism and secondary cysteine transaminase activity.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the core aspartate aminotransferase MF, cytosol localization and aspartate biosynthesis.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell keyword mapping to cytoplasm; consistent with experimental data.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara transfer from the rat ortholog (UniProtKB:P13221). Recovers a few correct metabolic terms (oxaloacetate metabolism, glutamate biosynthesis) but also over-propagates many rat-physiology and signaling/regulation terms that are not appropriate for the human enzyme (e.g. TGF-beta signaling, collagen biosynthesis, calcium regulation, transdifferentiation).

title: Automatic Gene Ontology annotation based on Rhea mapping
review_notes: Rhea-based mapping of the (2S)-2-aminobutanoate transaminase reaction; a genuine promiscuous activity.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA assignment of L-aspartate catabolic process; consistent with the reaction direction.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (ARBA/EC/Rhea) for the core aspartate aminotransferase and cysteine transaminase activities; consistent with curated data.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: MS detection of GOT1 in urinary exosomes; supports a secondary/incidental extracellular-exosome localization only.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: MS detection in parotid-gland exosomes; incidental localization.

title: Regulation of epidermal growth factor receptor trafficking by lysine deacetylase HDAC6.
review_notes: Membrane yeast two-hybrid screen of EGFR interactors; source of a bare protein-binding (GO:0005515) IPI, uninformative for GOT1 function.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: MS detection in B-cell exosomes; incidental localization.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: MS detection of GOT1 in a sperm-nucleus proteome; a non-canonical localization, likely a contaminant/minor pool.

title: New automated measurement of mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase with use of protease 401.
review_notes: Abstract-only; assays cytosolic vs mitochondrial AST activity via selective inactivation of the cytosolic form, supporting GOT1 catalytic activity and the GOT1/GOT2 distinction.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies genetic variants in GOT1 determining serum aspartate aminotransferase levels.
review_notes: GWAS + recombinant-protein functional study. Directly establishes GOT1 as the gene encoding cytosolic AST and provides EXP evidence for the core catalytic activity (p.Asn389del abolishes activity; ASTQTL1).

title: The amino acid sequence of cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase from human liver.
review_notes: Purification and full amino-acid sequence of human liver cytosolic AST; foundational identity/activity evidence.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: MS detection in prostatic-secretion exosomes; incidental localization.

title: Effects of therapeutic coronary reperfusion on aspartate aminotransferase isoenzymes in sera of patients with acute myocardial infarction.
review_notes: Abstract-only; measures cytosolic (soluble) AST catalytic activity in serum, distinguished from the mitochondrial isoenzyme.

title: 2-Aminobutyric acid modulates glutathione homeostasis in the myocardium.
review_notes: Shows AST generates 2-aminobutyrate from 2-oxobutyrate (cysteine-biosynthesis by-product); supports the promiscuous (2S)-2-aminobutanoate transaminase activity. Assay uses generic AST rather than isoform-resolved GOT1.

title: Extensive rewiring of the EGFR network in colorectal cancer cells expressing transforming levels of KRAS(G13D).
review_notes: EGFR-network interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding (GO:0005515) IPI, uninformative for GOT1 function.

title: Systematic discovery of mutation-directed neo-protein-protein interactions in cancer.
review_notes: Systematic neo-PPI screen (EGFR/BRAF); source of bare protein-binding (GO:0005515) IPIs, uninformative for GOT1 function.

title: The malate-aspartate shuttle is important for de novo serine biosynthesis.
review_notes: MAS-component knockout panel in HEK293. Full text not cached (abstract-only); abstract foregrounds MDH1/serine but GOT1 is a canonical MAS enzyme included in the disrupted-component panel. Supports the malate-aspartate shuttle IMP.

title: Enzyme immunoassay of human cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase.
review_notes: Specific immunoassay for human cytosolic AST with no cross-reactivity to the mitochondrial isoenzyme; supports GOT1 identity/activity.

title: Multiple molecular forms of human heart cytoplasmic aspartate aminotransferase.
review_notes: Purification of cytoplasmic AST from human heart; supports the cytoplasmic/cytosol localization (IDA).

title: Regulation of the cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase housekeeping gene promoter by glucocorticoids, cAMP, and insulin.
review_notes: Promoter study establishing transcriptional regulation of GOT1 by glucocorticoids (induction), cAMP (potentiation) and insulin (inhibition); underlies the IEP hormone-response annotations (regulation of expression, non-core).

title: oxaloacetate + glutamate <=> aspartate + alpha-ketoglutarate [GOT1]
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the GOT1-catalyzed transamination in the cytosol.

title: PXLP-K259-GOT1 transaminates 2-OG and L-Asp
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the PLP-Lys259 mechanism of GOT1; supports both the catalytic activity and PLP-binding core functions.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline. Correctly assigns PLP binding and the transaminase-family MF, but also produces the uninformative parents (catalytic activity, transaminase activity, amino acid metabolic process).

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS pipeline (transfer from bovine P00508). Correctly recovers the core aspartate aminotransferase MF, mitochondrial localization and aspartate/glutamate/2-oxoglutarate metabolism.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the core aspartate aminotransferase MF, mitochondrial localization and aspartate catabolism.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell keyword mapping to mitochondrial matrix (core) and plasma membrane (the moonlighting FABPpm pool); both consistent with experimental data.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA assignment of L-aspartate catabolic process; consistent with the reaction direction.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (EC/Rhea) for the core aspartate aminotransferase (EC 2.6.1.1) and the secondary kynurenine aminotransferase (EC 2.6.1.7) activities; consistent with curated data.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: MS detection of GOT2 in B-cell exosomes; supports a secondary/incidental extracellular-exosome localization only.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial phosphoproteome of human muscle; supports the core mitochondrial localization (HDA).

title: New automated measurement of mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase with use of protease 401.
review_notes: Abstract-only; assays mitochondrial vs cytosolic AST activity via selective inactivation of the cytosolic form, supporting GOT2 catalytic activity and the GOT1/GOT2 distinction.

title: Structural and biochemical studies of human 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase: implications for hydroxyproline metabolism in primary hyperoxaluria.
review_notes: Full text available. Primarily about HOGA1, but establishes that mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase is one of the four enzymes of the 4-hydroxy-L-proline degradation pathway (basis for the BHF-UCL TAS GO:0019470). A minor, non-core branch for GOT2.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: RNA interactome capture; source of a high-throughput RNA-binding (GO:0003723) HDA call. Incidental for an abundant mitochondrial enzyme; not an informative/core molecular function.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: MS detection in prostatic-secretion exosomes; incidental localization.

title: Serum mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase activity: not useful as a marker of excessive alcohol consumption in an unselected population.
review_notes: Abstract-only; immunochemically measures mitochondrial AST (mAST) catalytic activity in serum (EC 2.6.1.1). The clinical conclusion is negative (mAST not a useful alcohol marker), but it directly assays the mitochondrial isoenzyme activity.

title: Recombinant expression, purification and crystallographic studies of the mature form of human mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Recombinant human mAspAT expressed, purified, characterized (pH/temperature optima) and crystallized (PDB 5AX8); EXP support for the core EC 2.6.1.1 activity. Also explicitly describes GOT2 as a moonlighting enzyme with an LCFA-binding site and a role in kynurenic acid biosynthesis.

title: Effects of therapeutic coronary reperfusion on aspartate aminotransferase isoenzymes in sera of patients with acute myocardial infarction.
review_notes: Abstract-only; measures mitochondrial AST (m-AST) catalytic activity in serum, distinguished from the cytosolic isoenzyme.

title: Bi-allelic GOT2 Mutations Cause a Treatable Malate-Aspartate Shuttle-Related Encephalopathy.
review_notes: Abstract-only (full text at PMC6732527). Defines the disease (DEE82), establishes GOT2 as the mitochondrial glutamate-oxaloacetate transaminase and an essential malate-aspartate shuttle/NAD(H)-redox enzyme, and provides EXP enzyme-activity evidence (deficient in patient fibroblasts; loss-of-function variants). Key reference for GOT2 function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome; HTP support for the core mitochondrial localization of GOT2.

title: The malate-aspartate shuttle is important for de novo serine biosynthesis.
review_notes: MAS-component knockout panel in HEK293 (abstract-only cached). The abstract foregrounds MDH1/OGC/serine, but GOT2 is a canonical MAS enzyme included in the disrupted-component panel. Supports the malate-aspartate shuttle IMP.

title: Ethanol up-regulates fatty acid uptake and plasma membrane expression and export of mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferase in HepG2 cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Primary experimental basis for GOT2's moonlighting FABPpm role: ethanol up-regulates mAspAT mRNA and plasma-membrane expression, and plasma-membrane mAspAT correlates with increased long-chain fatty-acid uptake Vmax. Supports the plasma-membrane localization (IDA), fatty-acid transport (IEP) and response-to-ethanol (IDA) annotations.

title: PXLP-K279-GOT2 dimer transaminates 4-OH-L-glutamate to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate (HOG)
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the GOT2 step of hydroxyproline catabolism in the mitochondrial matrix; captures the PLP-Lys279 mechanism. Non-core metabolic branch.

title: GOT2 dimer transaminates L-Asp
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the core GOT2-catalyzed L-aspartate transamination in the mitochondrial matrix.

title: GOT2 transaminates OA and L-Glu
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the reverse (oxaloacetate + L-glutamate -> aspartate) direction of the core GOT2 transamination.

title: Gaa1p and gpi8p are components of a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) transamidase that mediates attachment of GPI to proteins.
review_notes: Establishes that GAA1 and GPI8 are the core transamidase components and that GPI8 (PIGK) is the catalytic cysteine-protease subunit; GAA1 KO abolishes carbonyl-intermediate formation. Abstract-only cache.

title: PIG-S and PIG-T, essential for GPI anchor attachment to proteins, form a complex with GAA1 and GPI8.
review_notes: Defines the GAA1/GPI8/PIG-S/PIG-T complex and its ER localization; source of the direct protein-sequence and complex-assembly annotations. Abstract-only.

title: Structural requirements for the recruitment of Gaa1 into a functional glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase complex.
review_notes: Concerns ER retention/sorting of GAA1 itself and complex assembly via its luminal domain; does NOT support 'protein retention in ER lumen' (GO:0006621) as a GPAA1 function acting on other proteins - that annotation is a term/paper mismatch. Relevant for localization/assembly. Abstract-only.

title: Two subunits of glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase, GPI8 and PIG-T, form a functionally important intermolecular disulfide bridge.
review_notes: GPI8-PIG-T disulfide bridge and confirmation the five-component complex holds substrate; supports complex membership. Abstract-only.

title: Human PIG-U and yeast Cdc91p are the fifth subunit of GPI transamidase that attaches GPI-anchors to proteins.
review_notes: Establishes PIG-U as the fifth subunit alongside GAA1; affinity-purified complex; supports complex membership and attachment BP. Abstract-only.

title: A conserved proline in the last transmembrane segment of Gaa1 is required for glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) recognition by GPI transamidase.
review_notes: Direct functional link between GAA1 and GPI recognition/binding by the complex (co-IP of GPI abolished by GAA1 C-terminal TM mutation); basis of the GPI anchor binding (contributes_to) IMP annotation. Abstract-only.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum localization of Gaa1 and PIG-T, subunits of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase complex.
review_notes: Shows GAA1 is passively retained in the ER by a signalless mechanism; supports ER-membrane localization and complex membership. Abstract-only.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane-proteome MS; only supports the generic 'membrane' HDA term, which is over-annotated relative to the specific ER membrane.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex 2.0 proteome-scale AP-MS; source of bare 'protein binding' IPIs (PIGK/PIGT/MOXD1). Interactions plausible but term uninformative.

title: Mutations in GPAA1, Encoding a GPI Transamidase Complex Protein, Cause Developmental Delay, Epilepsy, Cerebellar Atrophy, and Osteopenia.
review_notes: Defines GPIBD15 disease; biallelic GPAA1 variants reduce surface GPI-APs; supports the attachment BP and disease context. Abstract-only.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 proteome-scale AP-MS; bare 'protein binding' IPI source.

title: Functional Analysis of the GPI Transamidase Complex by Screening for Amino Acid Mutations in Each Subunit.
review_notes: Full text cached; systematic mutagenesis of all five subunits. Confirms PIGK is catalytic, GPAA1 has M28-peptidase-like fold, GPAA1 D250A reduces activity, and GPAA1 proposed to form the amide bond with the bridging EtNP.

title: Structure of human glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure of the human GPI-T; PIGK C206-H164-N58 catalytic triad; TM cleft as GPI substrate-binding site. Abstract-only cache.

title: Molecular insights into biogenesis of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor proteins.
review_notes: 2.53-Å cryo-EM structure of the equimolar heteropentameric GPI-T; legumain- like proprotein cleavage mechanism; GPAA1 His354 mutation reduces activity. Abstract-only cache.

title: Structures of liganded glycosylphosphatidylinositol transamidase illuminate GPI-AP biogenesis.
review_notes: Full text cached; substrate/product-bound GPI-T structures. Directly shows GPAA1 binding the GPI lipid (EtNP1-His354/Mg2+, EtNP2-Gln355/Ser51, EtNP3-Ser51/Asn53); basis of the GPI anchor binding IDA and core MF.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Proteome-scale multimodal cell-map interactome; bare 'protein binding' IPI source (PIGK/PIGT).

title: Molecular cloning of human homolog of yeast GAA1 which is required for attachment of glycosylphosphatidylinositols to proteins.
review_notes: Original cloning of human GAA1; antisense knockdown reduces reporter GPI-AP; basis of the attachment BP and complex-component annotations. Abstract-only.

title: AGPAT6 is a novel microsomal glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase.
review_notes: Cached entry is abstract-only and the abstract describes AGPAT6/GPAT4 (a microsomal paralog). UniProt cites PubMed:18238778 with ECO:0000269 for GPAM's FUNCTION and multiple catalytic-activity reactions, so the full text also characterizes GPAT1; the GPAM annotations sourced from it are experimental and retained per policy.

title: The microsomal cardiolipin remodeling enzyme acyl-CoA lysocardiolipin acyltransferase is an acyltransferase of multiple anionic lysophospholipids.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache foregrounds ALCAT1, but UniProt uses this paper (ECO:0000269) for a GPAM catalytic activity; the derived GPAM annotations are experimental (IMP) and represent a secondary lysophospholipid-remodeling activity, retained as non-core.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome map; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation, which is uninformative for GPAT1's molecular function (marked over-annotated).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: HTP support for mitochondrial localization, consistent with the specific mitochondrial-outer-membrane placement.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Standard InterPro→GO electronic-annotation reference; the G-patch domain (IPR000467) legitimately maps to nucleic acid binding.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard PAINT IBA reference. Here it propagates an erroneous kinetochore call inherited from PMID:20813266; flagged upstream in geneontology/go-annotation#6450.

title: The protein composition of mitotic chromosomes determined using multiclassifier combinatorial proteomics.
review_notes: Source of the disputed kinetochore IDA. Genuine proteomics paper but the per-protein localization assignment for GPATCH11 is based on a low-resolution image, and a dedicated 2024 study (PMID:39572588) contradicts the kinetochore call. Upstream GO curators have flagged the derived annotations in geneontology/go-annotation#6450.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Correctly cited for the IntAct IPI evidence, but the listed partners are not mechanistically informative about GPATCH11's splicing role.

title: GPATCH11 variants cause mis-splicing and early-onset retinal dystrophy with neurological impairment.
review_notes: Dedicated patient + mouse study with high-resolution localization data. Strongest available evidence for the gene's nucleoplasm/centrosome localization and splicing role; directly contradicts the kinetochore IDA.

title: GPATCH11 ortholog Sap34 regulates pre-mRNA splicing by interacting with early spliceosomal complexes in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
review_notes: Direct ortholog functional characterization. Strongly supports the pre-mRNA splicing core function. Abstract-only in the cache; full text not yet available.

title: Falcon deep research report for GPATCH11
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon). It is almost entirely a synthesis of the primary Zanetti/Perrault 2024 study (PMID:39572588) plus G-patch family reviews (Bohnsack 2021, Karika 2026), and is consistent with the independently reviewed primary literature already cited here. The individual constituent PMIDs were not all independently re-verified against PubMed for this synthesis, so correctness is left UNVERIFIED; quoted supporting_text below is verbatim from this report. No claims unique to the report (i.e. not traceable to PMID:39572588 / PMID:42260140) were used to change any annotation action.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Abstract-verified urinary-exosome proteome (1132 proteins by LC-MS/MS). GPD1 is detected but no function is assigned; supports only the extracellular-exosome HDA location, which is a proteome-detection artefact rather than functional localization for this soluble cytosolic enzyme.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome (yeast two-hybrid). Basis for the bare GPD1-FAM25A 'protein binding' IPI. Correctly cited but the interaction is high-throughput with no established functional consequence for GPD1.

title: Molecular cloning, sequencing and expression of a cDNA encoding a human liver NAD-dependent alpha-glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Primary characterization of human liver GPD1: cloning, sequencing and expression of the NAD-dependent alpha-glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.8). Basis for the core catalytic-activity and cytoplasmic-localization annotations. Abstract only in cache (full_text_available: false).

title: DHAP is converted to G3P by GPD1/GPD1L
review_notes: Reactome reaction modelling the physiological DHAP -> G3P step catalysed by the GPD1 homodimer with NADH as electron donor; supports the core catalytic activity, biosynthetic direction and cytosolic localization.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP) study; GPD2/P43304 is a MitoCoP member. Corroborates mitochondrial localisation (HTP) but does not resolve sub-mitochondrial location or function.

title: Mutation in the calcium-binding domain of the mitochondrial glycerophosphate dehydrogenase gene in a family of diabetic subjects.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Abstract-only (full_text_available: false). Source of the UniProt catalytic-activity, activity-regulation (calcium enhances activity), and beta-cell glucose-sensing FUNCTION statements, and of the GOA IDA on GO:0004368. Establishes GPD2 as the Ca2+-sensitive FAD-linked mitochondrial glycerophosphate dehydrogenase.

title: Gly-3-P+FAD->DHAP+FADH2 (catalyzed by mitochondrial Gly-Phos dehydrogenase)
review_notes: Reactome reaction for GPD2 catalysis; supports the core catalytic activity, the glycerol-phosphate shuttle role, and inner-membrane localisation.

title: Structural models of DYNLL1 with interacting partners: African swine fever virus protein p54 and postsynaptic scaffolding protein gephyrin.
review_notes: Structural-modelling paper of DYNLL1 (LC8) with gephyrin; supports a gephyrin-DYNLL1 interaction but is not about gephyrin's core function. Basis of one IPI protein-binding annotation.

title: Expression and subcellular distribution of gephyrin in non-neuronal tissues and cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Establishes cytoplasmic/cytosolic localization of gephyrin in non-neuronal (liver/hepatocyte) cells and its role in MoCo biosynthesis there; basis of the IDA cytosol annotation.

title: Metal insertion into the molybdenum cofactor: product-substrate channelling demonstrates the functional origin of domain fusion in gephyrin.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Reconstitutes in-vitro MoCo synthesis; shows G domain adenylylates molybdopterin and E domain catalyses metal insertion, with >300-fold enhancement in the fused protein. Directly supports the two core catalytic MFs.

title: Palmitoylation of gephyrin controls receptor clustering and plasticity of GABAergic synapses.
review_notes: Full text available. Demonstrates gephyrin palmitoylation (Cys212/Cys284 by DHHC-12/ZDHHC12) controlling membrane association and GABAAR clustering; basis of the adaptor-activity and GABAAR-clustering IMP/IDA annotations.

title: Simultaneous impairment of neuronal and metabolic function of mutated gephyrin in a patient with epileptic encephalopathy.
review_notes: Full text available. Characterizes the Dravet-like G375D variant that abolishes both the MoCo-synthetic and the receptor-clustering functions; the single most informative reference showing gephyrin's bifunctionality in human.

title: An organelle-specific protein landscape identifies novel diseases and molecular mechanisms.
review_notes: Large-scale organelle/interactome proteomics; source of an IntAct IPI (DYNLL1) protein- binding annotation. Does not inform gephyrin's core function specifically.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex interactome; source of an IntAct IPI (DYNLL1) protein-binding annotation. Not specific to gephyrin function.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging interactome; source of an IntAct IPI (DYNLL1) protein-binding annotation. Not specific to gephyrin function.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome; source of an IntAct IPI (DYNLL1) protein-binding annotation. Not specific to gephyrin function.

title: The neurotransmitter receptor-anchoring protein gephyrin reconstitutes molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis in bacteria, plants, and mammalian cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Foundational paper: gephyrin binds molybdopterin and reconstitutes MoCo biosynthesis across bacteria, plant and mammalian cells; basis of the MoCo IMP, molybdopterin-binding IDA, and (as assay readout) the nitrate-reductase IMP.

title: Tumor autocrine motility factor is an angiogenic factor that stimulates endothelial cell motility.
review_notes: Establishes the secreted AMF/angiogenic moonlighting role and cytoplasm/secreted localization; supports the EXP extracellular region and cytoplasm annotations.

title: Enzymes of the human erythrocyte. IV. Phosphoglucose isomerase, purification and properties.
review_notes: Classic purification/characterization of the human erythrocyte enzyme; supports the core catalytic activity (EXP GO:0004347).

title: Purification of human tumor cell autocrine motility factor and molecular cloning of its receptor.
review_notes: Purified AMF stimulates tumor-cell migration and its receptor gp78 was cloned; supports the moonlighting motility/migration function.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Large-scale exosome proteomic survey detecting GPI; supports extracellular exosome (HDA) but not a specific function.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: Large-scale exosome proteomic survey detecting GPI; supports extracellular exosome (HDA) but not a specific function.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: NK-cell membrane proteome survey; the study notes many hits are only transiently membrane-associated, arguing GPI's membrane annotation is over-stated.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Large-scale B-cell exosome proteomic survey detecting GPI; supports extracellular exosome (HDA) but not a specific function.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Large-scale exosome proteomic survey detecting GPI; supports extracellular exosome (HDA) but not a specific function.

title: Polyubiquitylation of AMF requires cooperation between the gp78 and TRIM25 ubiquitin ligases.
review_notes: Full text confirms GPI/AMF directly binds the gp78 (AMFR) ubiquitin ligase cytoplasmic domain and is a ubiquitylation substrate; supports the IPI ubiquitin protein ligase binding annotation and frames GPI as a moonlighting protein.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial affinity-enrichment interactome screen; basis of the uninformative bare protein-binding (TAMM41) IPI annotation.

title: Two novel mutations (p.(Ser160Pro) and p.(Arg472Cys)) causing glucose-6-phosphate isomerase deficiency are associated with erythroid dysplasia and inappropriately suppressed hepcidin.
review_notes: Patient enzyme-activity measurements in GPI deficiency confirm the core catalytic function and the disease association (CNSHA4).

title: Neuroleukin: a lymphokine product of lectin-stimulated T cells.
review_notes: Establishes neuroleukin (=GPI) as a T-cell lymphokine inducing immunoglobulin secretion; supports the moonlighting immune-related annotations.

title: The first stable variant of erythrocyte glucose-phosphate isomerase associated with severe hemolytic anemia.
review_notes: Describes a stable GPI variant causing hemolytic anemia with altered F6P/G6P kinetics; it does not support a role in hemostasis, so the TAS hemostasis annotation appears mis-mapped.

title: Human glucose phosphate isomerase: exon mapping and gene structure.
review_notes: Reports the GPI gene/exon structure; cited (NAS) for the generic carbohydrate metabolic process term.

title: GPR158/179 regulate G protein signaling by controlling localization and activity of the RGS7 complexes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Cell Biol 2012, Orlandi et al.). Founding demonstration that GPR158 recruits R7-family RGS complexes to the plasma membrane.

title: GPR158, an orphan member of G protein-coupled receptor Family C: glucocorticoid-stimulated expression and novel nuclear role.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS One 2013). Source of the nucleus annotation. Correctly cited, but the nuclear-localisation claim is unreplicated outside this group and is flagged as mechanistically unexplained by UniProt.

title: Orphan Receptor GPR158 Is an Allosteric Modulator of RGS7 Catalytic Activity with an Essential Role in Dictating Its Expression and Localization in the Brain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2015). Establishes the enzyme-activator function towards RGS7 in the native nervous system.

title: Gpr158 mediates osteocalcin's regulation of cognition.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Exp Med 2017, Khrimian et al.). The osteocalcin-receptor assignment rests on mouse genetics, electrophysiology and behaviour; no direct high-affinity binding site has been defined, and UniProt annotates the osteocalcin role only by similarity. Included to document the competing ligand model, not as established fact.

title: GPR158 in the Visual System: Homeostatic Role in Regulation of Intraocular Pressure.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Ocul Pharmacol Ther 2019). Second source of the nucleus and plasma membrane EXP annotations; same group as PMID:23451275, so not independent for the nuclear claim.

title: Nonclassical Ligand-Independent Regulation of Go Protein by an Orphan Class C G-Protein-Coupled Receptor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Pharmacol 2019, Hajj et al.). Abstract-only in the cache. Key negative result - no constitutive or canonical Go activation - which is why the generic GPCR-activity terms are downgraded here.

title: Cryo-EM structure of human GPR158 receptor coupled to the RGS7-Gβ5 signaling complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2021, Patil et al.). Structural basis of the GPR158-RGS7-Gbeta5 complex and of the extracellular Cache domain.

title: Structure of the class C orphan GPCR GPR158 in complex with RGS7-Gβ5.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2021, Jeong et al.). Independent cryo-EM structure from a different laboratory, agreeing on the homodimer and the RGS7-binding platform.

title: Orphan receptor GPR158 serves as a metabotropic glycine receptor: mGlyR.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2023, Laboute et al.). Source of the GO:0160079, GO:0008047 and GO:0008277 IDA annotations. The competing-interest statement discloses a GPR158-focused startup, so the independent replication in PMID:38884814 is what makes the ligand assignment convincing.

title: Glycine: a long-sought novel ligand for GPR158.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Trends Pharmacol Sci 2023). Independent commentary treating the deorphanization as accepted.

title: Glycine-induced activation of GPR158 increases the intrinsic excitability of medium spiny neurons in the nucleus accumbens.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Mol Life Sci 2024, Aceto et al.). Independent laboratory and independent brain region; the key replication supporting the metabotropic glycine receptor assignment.

title: Osteocalcin and GPR158: linking bone and brain function.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Front Cell Dev Biol 2025). A review that states the osteocalcin-receptor role as settled; cited here to document that framing, not to support it. The primary evidence it rests on is mouse genetic rather than direct binding.

title: A postsynaptic GPR158-PLCXD2 complex controls spine apparatus abundance and dendritic spine maturation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Dev Cell 2025, Verpoort et al.). Abstract-only in the cache. Describes a ligand-independent GPR158 signalling module, the third of the three competing models.

title: Functional exploration of metabotropic glycine receptors in cultured rat hippocampal slices.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuroreport 2026). Demonstrates Gi/o-dependent metabotropic glycine responses in CA3 pyramidal cells, but does not itself manipulate GPR158, so it supports the existence of mGlyR signalling rather than GPR158's identity as the receptor.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro-to-GO mapping. Correct for the generic class A GPCR signature on this protein, but two of the three rows it drives (GO:0007186, GO:0016020) are broader than the evidence for GPR161 supports and are modified to their established children.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Curator ortholog transfer. Every ISS row on this record was traced through QuickGO to an experimental (IDA or IMP) annotation on mouse Gpr161, so none of them is a propagation from another inference.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER PAINT phylogenetic inference. Both IBA rows resolve to real IBD nodes in the local slice interpro/panther/PTHR22752/PTHR22752-paint.tsv: PTN002733799 for GO:0004930 and the Chordata-scoped PTN004562730 for GO:0007189 and GO:0055037.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt subcellular-location-to-GO mapping. Both rows it drives (plasma membrane, ciliary membrane) are correct at the granularity the SubCell vocabulary can express.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learned annotations. All four rows land on terms independently supported by direct human evidence, which is unusually specific for this source and reflects that GPR161's UniProt entry carries the AKAP and cilium features explicitly.

title: TULP3 bridges the IFT-A complex and membrane phosphoinositides to promote trafficking of G protein-coupled receptors into primary cilia.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Genes Dev 2010, Mukhopadhyay S et al.) and the title matches the cached record. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false). The abstract does not name GPR161, so it is cited here only for the TULP3/IFT-A ciliary-GPCR trafficking mechanism; UniProt cites this paper with ECO:0000269 for the GPR161 cilium membrane location and Reactome R-HSA-5610725 states the GPR161-specific case.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Nature 2020, Luck K et al.) and the title matches the cached record. Correctly cited: it really is the source of the five GO:0005515 IntAct rows. Relevance to GPR161 function is low, however - it contributes five high-throughput Y2H partners (UPK1B, COMT, EFNA5, CLDN19, SLC30A2), none of which appears in any described GPR161 mechanism and none of which was followed up, so the rows support no informative molecular function.

title: GPR161 structure uncovers the redundant role of sterol-regulated ciliary cAMP signaling in the Hedgehog pathway.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Nat Struct Mol Biol 2024, Hoppe N et al.) and the title matches the cached record. Full text available in the cache and read; it is the anchor for all four IDA rows in the GOA file and supports each of them, including the separation of Gs coupling from PKA anchoring that justifies GPR161 carrying two distinct molecular functions.

title: β-Arrestin mediates the export of ciliary GPR161 but not Smoothened together with the BBSome and intraflagellar transport machinery.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (J Cell Sci 2025, Fujii T et al.) and the title matches the cached record. Only the abstract is cached (full_text_available: false), so the quoted support here is abstract-level; UniProt cites this paper with ECO:0000269 for the cilium membrane location and the ARRB1/ARRB2 interactions, i.e. the curator read the full text. Note that GPR161 is the cargo of the export machinery this paper characterises, not one of its actors.

title: TULP3 is required for GPR161 localization in the cilium
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction (reactome/R-HSA-5610725.md); its author statement that TULP3 and IFT-A recruit GPR161 to the cilium matches PMID:20889716 and the UniProt subcellular-location note. Supports the ciliary membrane TAS row.

title: GPR161 is internalized
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction (reactome/R-HSA-5635102.md). Correctly describes Hedgehog-induced removal of GPR161 from the cilium and its internalisation, which is the basis of both the ciliary membrane and the endocytic vesicle membrane TAS rows. The endocytic vesicle is a transit compartment, which is why that row is kept as non-core.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell 2014, Rolland et al.). High-throughput binary interactome screen; correctly cited but contributes only uninformative protein binding annotations.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2019, Fragoza et al.). Variant-interactome study; contributes an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2020, Luck et al.). HuRI; the single largest contributor of bare protein binding rows for this gene, none of them functionally informative.

title: Multiplexed mapping of the interactome of GPCRs with receptor activity-modifying proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Adv 2024). GPCR-RAMP interactome screen. A RAMP interaction could be functionally meaningful for a receptor, but no consequence for GPR25 trafficking or pharmacology is established, so the annotation remains uninformative.

title: A lymphocyte chemoaffinity axis for lung, non-intestinal mucosae and CNS.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2024, Ocón et al.). The founding deorphanization, with in vivo adoptive-transfer homing in wild-type and Cxcl17-null recipients. Full text available in the cache and read for this review; it is the source of the finding that GPR25 does not direct homing to lymph nodes or spleen, which is why the lymphoid-organ migration term is modified here.

title: Identification of orphan GPR25 as a receptor for the chemokine CXCL17.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (FEBS J 2025, Hu et al.). Abstract-only in the cache. Independent confirmation by beta-arrestin recruitment and TGF-alpha shedding, with pocket mutagenesis identifying Trp95 and Arg178.

title: CXCL17 activates three MAS-related G protein-coupled receptors independently of its conserved C-terminal fragment.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Arch Biochem Biophys 2026, same group as PMID:40279398). Documents CXCL17 promiscuity towards MRGPRX1, MRGPRX2 and MAS1 at micromolar concentrations. Cited here to record the residual controversy accurately - it is about the ligand, not about GPR25, and the different structural requirement (C-terminal fragment dispensable for the MRGPRs, essential for GPR25) argues that the two interactions are mechanistically distinct.

title: GPR25 promotes the formation of lung and liver tissue-resident memory CD8 T cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Immunol 2025, Feng et al.). Independent in vivo genetics from a fourth laboratory, showing a TGF-beta-induced requirement for GPR25 in tissue-resident memory CD8 T cell formation that is separable from tissue entry.

title: Evidence for a Two-Step Model for Activation of GPR25 by the Chemoattractant CXCL17.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Basic Clin Pharmacol Toxicol 2026, Yang, Giblin and Pease, Imperial College). Abstract-only in the cache. Third independent laboratory, different cell background, independently recovering Trp95 and Arg178 as essential; explicitly verifies GPR25 as a bona fide CXCL17 receptor.

title: Discovery of a novel human G protein-coupled receptor gene (GPR25) located on chromosome 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biochem Biophys Res Commun 1997, Jung et al.). Original cloning paper; supports family membership and the seven-transmembrane prediction only, with no functional data.

title: An unfolded putative transmembrane polypeptide, which can lead to endoplasmic reticulum stress, is a substrate of Parkin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell 2001;105:891-902, Imai et al.). The founding Pael-R/parkin paper; the most reproducible molecular observation about this protein.

title: CHIP is associated with Parkin, a gene responsible for familial Parkinson's disease, and enhances its ubiquitin ligase activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Cell 2002;10:55-67). Source of the CHIP/Hsp70/parkin/Pael-R complex annotations.

title: A product of the human gene adjacent to parkin is a component of Lewy bodies and suppresses Pael receptor-induced cell death.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. PACRG interaction; recorded only as bare protein binding.

title: The neuropeptide head activator is a high-affinity ligand for the orphan G-protein-coupled receptor GPR37.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Cell Sci 2006, Rezgaoui et al.). The head-activator deorphanization. Marked DISPUTED because the pairing was not reproduced by Dunham et al. 2009, was not a hit in a genome-wide orphan screen, and the ligand has no human gene; the WITH/FROM entity of the derived GOA row is the Hydra vulgaris peptide UniProtKB:P69251. Its localisation observations remain usable.

title: A ubiquitin ligase HRD1 promotes the degradation of Pael receptor, a substrate of Parkin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HRD1/SYVN1 as a second E3 for Pael-R; independent support for the ER quality-control axis.

title: GPR37 associates with the dopamine transporter to modulate dopamine uptake and behavioral responses to dopaminergic drugs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Dopamine transporter association; recorded only as bare protein binding.

title: Structural basis for endosomal trafficking of diverse transmembrane cargos by PX-FERM proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as a real paper (PNAS 2013;110:E643-52), but GPR37 does not appear anywhere in the cached text, so the basis of the GO:0043235 IDA could not be checked from here - presumably a supplementary cargo table. Flagged rather than acted on.

title: GPR37 and GPR37L1 are receptors for the neuroprotective and glioprotective factors prosaptide and prosaposin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2013;110:9529-34, Meyer et al.). The prosaposin/prosaptide deorphanization that underlies GO:0036505 and the core function.

title: The identification of novel proteins that interact with the GLP-1 receptor and restrain its activity.
review_notes: GLP-1 receptor interaction screen; bare protein binding only.

title: CASPR2 forms a complex with GPR37 via MUPP1 but not with GPR37(R558Q), an autism spectrum disorder-related mutation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. CASPR2-MUPP1-GPR37 complex; supports the dendrite, synapse, PDZ-domain-binding and plasma membrane annotations.

title: Drug Discovery Opportunities at the Endothelin B Receptor-Related Orphan G Protein-Coupled Receptors, GPR37 and GPR37L1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Front Pharmacol 2015, Smith NJ). The authoritative critical review of GPR37/GPR37L1 pharmacology. It is the source for the head-activator refutation and for the reservations about the prosaposin pairing; both are quoted verbatim rather than paraphrased.

title: The Parkinson's-disease-associated receptor GPR37 undergoes metalloproteinase-mediated N-terminal cleavage and ectodomain shedding.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Constitutive metalloproteinase cleavage and ectodomain shedding; establishes that most surface GPR37 is N-terminally truncated.

title: Systematic protein-protein interaction mapping for clinically relevant human GPCRs.
review_notes: Systematic GPCR interaction map; bare protein binding only.

title: GPR37 regulates macrophage phagocytosis and resolution of inflammatory pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Clin Invest 2018;128:3568-82, Bang et al.). Independent reproduction of TX14 binding to GPR37, and the origin of the protectin D1/NPD1 claim. Important because it is the paper in which one laboratory reports a peptide and a lipid activating the same receptor.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegenerative-disease interactome; bare protein binding only.

title: Activation of GPR37 in macrophages confers protection against infection-induced sepsis and pain-like behaviour in mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2021). GPR37 in macrophage defence against infection and sepsis; supports the protectin D1 arm and the macrophage biology.

title: Osteocalcin attenuates oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination via GPR37 signaling in the mouse brain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Adv 2021;7:eabi5811, Qian et al.). Original osteocalcin-GPR37 pairing. Marked DISPUTED because osteocalcin already has two other claimed receptors and because the only follow-up study shares its senior authors.

title: Neuroprotectin D1 and GPR37 protect against chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy and the transition from acute to chronic pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Pharmacol Res 2025). NPD1/GPR37 in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy; knockout-dependent.

title: Role and regulatory mechanism of GPR37 in neurological diseases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified review (Front Cell Neurosci 2025). Useful as a statement that the field currently treats prosaposin, neuroprotectin D1 and osteocalcin as co-existing ligands, which is precisely the situation this review adjudicates.

title: A bone-derived hormone permits rapid visual escape via GPR37 receptor in a subpopulation of VTA GABAergic neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neuron 2026;114:1594-1608, Liu et al.). Osteocalcin-GPR37 in VTA GABAergic neurons. Marked DISPUTED on independence grounds (shared senior authors with PMID:34678058) and because it carries a four-page published erratum, PMID:42001851.

title: A bone-derived hormone permits rapid visual escape via GPR37 receptor in a subpopulation of VTA GABAergic neurons.
review_notes: The published erratum to PMID:41679312, Neuron 2026;114:1695-1698. Cited so that the correction is visible alongside the claim.

title: The response to danger: Is it in your bones?
review_notes: PubMed-verified commentary by Karsenty, the senior figure of the osteocalcin field, accompanying PMID:41679312. Supportive but not independent data.

title: Spinal-level activation of GPR37 in TRPV1-expressing sensory neurons erases nociceptive system sensitization in murine models.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Pain 2026). Conditional knockout of GPR37 in TRPV1-lineage sensory neurons abolishes the effects of intrathecal TX14A - the strongest in vivo evidence that prosaptide acts through GPR37. Also uses protectin D1 as a second agonist in the same study.

title: Distinct localization and potential functions of GPR37 signaling mediated by prosaposin and protectin D1 in the rat pituitary gland.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Reprod Dev 2026). Cited specifically as evidence of how the field now states the ligand question - it asserts in a single sentence that both prosaposin and protectin D1 are endogenous ligands of GPR37, without reconciling the chemical-class difference.

title: A novel endothelin receptor type-B-like gene enriched in the brain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The cloning paper; source of the TAS rows. Records ancestry from the endothelin-B receptor family, not pharmacology - GPR37 was never shown to bind endothelins.

title: The orphan GPR50 receptor specifically inhibits MT1 melatonin receptor function through heterodimerization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO J 2006;25:3012-23, Levoye et al.). Establishes the MT1-inhibitory heterodimer that underlies the core_functions entry.

title: GPR50 interacts with neuronal NOGO-A and affects neurite outgrowth.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the postsynaptic-density localisation. Note that its overexpression result (GPR50 increases neurite length) is opposite in sign to the later knockout result; the loss-of-function direction is the more reliable one.

title: GPR50 interacts with TIP60 to modulate glucocorticoid receptor signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports the plasma membrane EXP annotation and the KAT5/TIP60 interaction.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; the GPR50-ZNF572 pair has no follow-up.

title: Importance of the second extracellular loop for melatonin MT(1) receptor function and absence of melatonin binding in GPR50.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Br J Pharmacol 2018;175:3281-97, Clement et al.). The mechanistic explanation for why GPR50 does not bind melatonin, and the basis for removing GO:0008502. The cached title is missing a space after 'MT' because the PubMed record drops the subscript.

title: GPR50-Ctail cleavage and nuclear translocation: a new signal transduction mode for G protein-coupled receptors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the nucleus EXP annotation and of the C-terminal domain core function.

title: GPR50 Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression via the Notch Signaling Pathway through Direct Interaction with ADAM17.
review_notes: Single-study cancer-cell result; recorded but not used for a core function.

title: Orphan GPR50 Restrains Neurite Outgrowth and Cell Migration by Activating the G(12/13) Protein-RhoA Pathway in Neural Progenitor Cells and Tanycytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Pineal Res 2025;77:e70041, Ahmad et al.). Knockout-mouse evidence for constitutive, ligand-independent G12/13-RhoA signalling.

title: Photo-cross-linking-assisted deorphanization deciphers GPR50-L-LEN pairing in metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2026;22:1132-43, Wu et al.). Technically strong single-laboratory deorphanization proposing L-LEN as the endogenous agonist, with Galphai coupling. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because a cryo-EM study published five weeks later states that no endogenous agonist has been characterized without engaging this result, and because the reported transducer (Galphai) conflicts with the Galpha12/13 coupling reported by two other groups. No GO annotation has been made on this basis, and none should be until it is independently replicated.

title: Structure of the melatonin-related orphan receptor, GPR50.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Cells 2026;49:100331, Shin et al.). Cryo-EM structure of the ligand-free receptor plus BRET2 basal-activity profiling. Its statement that endogenous agonists have not been characterized is what puts it in direct tension with the L-LEN paper.

title: Cloning of a melatonin-related receptor from human pituitary.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (FEBS Lett 1996;386:219-24, Reppert et al.). The founding description of GPR50/H9. Directly reports the absence of melatonin binding, which is the key evidence against the GO:0008502 IEA.

title: Cloning and characterization of a novel orphan G-protein-coupled receptor localized to human chromosome 2p16.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biochem Biophys Res Commun 1999, Tarttelin et al.). Original human GPR75 cloning paper; source of the TAS plasma membrane annotation, which is a sequence-based author statement rather than a measurement.

title: RANTES stimulates Ca2+ mobilization and inositol trisphosphate (IP3) formation in cells transfected with G protein-coupled receptor 75.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Br J Pharmacol 2006, Ignatov et al.). This is the single experimental study behind every C-C chemokine receptor annotation on human GPR75, reaching it via the mouse Gpr75 IDA. Correctly cited, but the deorphanization it claims has not been adopted by IUPHAR and is described as controversial in 2025-2026 reviews.

title: The orphan G-protein-coupled receptor 75 signaling is activated by the chemokine CCL5.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Neurochem 2018, Dedoni et al.). Independent support for CCL5-evoked, GPR75-dependent signalling in cells lacking CCR1/CCR3/CCR5, and the source of the IC plasma membrane annotation. Cited as the strongest evidence for the chemokine model; still short of demonstrating direct chemokine binding, which the 2026 structures make harder to envisage.

title: GPR75: Advances, Challenges in Deorphanization, and Potential as a Novel Drug Target for Disease Treatment.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Int J Mol Sci 2025). Current, balanced review; states the IUPHAR orphan classification explicitly and records the family relationships that place GPR75 outside the chemokine receptor clade.

title: Orphan G-protein coupled receptor 75 (GPR75), a unique and controversial potential therapeutic target.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Recept Signal Transduct Res 2025, Stratulat, Babes and Tunaru). Abstract-only in the cache. Independent review stating that the agonist status of both proposed GPR75 ligands remains controversial.

title: Cryo-EM structures of GPR75 reveal an occluded orthosteric pocket challenging conventional drug discovery paradigms for an anti-obesity target.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Acta Pharmacol Sin 2026). Abstract-only in the cache because PMC full text is restricted. Establishes Gq coupling and a collapsed extracellular domain with no conventional orthosteric pocket - the structural argument against any orthosteric agonist, chemokine included.

title: Falcon deep research report for human GRAP2
review_notes: Generated 2026-10-03 (Edison/Falcon). Used as leads only. Key claims checked against primary papers and cached: HuT78 knockdown (PMID:25636200), Gads-SLP-76 Kd 9 nM and quaternary complex (PMID:30510001), Jurkat GRB2-family knockouts / 100% SLP76-GADS occupancy (PMID:37006259), FLT3 pY955/pY969 (PMID:26895103), Yablonski review (PMID:31402911). LAT Y171/Y191 are given in short-isoform numbering without noting canonical Y200/Y220. The HPK1 attribution of GADS T262 phosphorylation was not verified in a cached primary paper; PMID:25452106 reports T262 phosphorylation by mass spectrometry without naming the kinase in its abstract.

title: Recruitment of the class II phosphoinositide 3-kinase C2beta to the epidermal growth factor receptor: role of Grb2.
review_notes: GRB2 SH3 domains bind PI3K-C2beta and GRB2 is required to link it to phosphorylated EGFR.

title: A proteomics strategy to elucidate functional protein-protein interactions applied to EGF signaling.
review_notes: SILAC pulldown over GRB2 SH2; only EGFR and Shc are stated to bind the bait directly, other co-purifying proteins are indirect.

title: The SH2 and SH3 domain-containing protein GRB2 links receptor tyrosine kinases to ras signaling.
review_notes: GRB2 cloning paper; abstract states SH2-mediated association with tyrosine-phosphorylated EGFR/PDGFR and cooperation with Ras. Supports EGFR signalling annotations.

title: NKG2D-mediated signaling requires a DAP10-bound Grb2-Vav1 intermediate and phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase in human natural killer cells.
review_notes: GRB2-Vav1 binding to DAP10 required for NKG2D-mediated cytotoxicity in human NK cells.

title: GAREM, a novel adaptor protein for growth factor receptor-bound protein 2, contributes to cellular transformation through the activation of extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling.
review_notes: GAREM1 proline-rich motifs bound by GRB2 SH3 domains; basis of the GO:0017124 row, which has the direction reversed.

title: Tarp regulates early Chlamydia-induced host cell survival through interactions with the human adaptor protein SHC1.
review_notes: SH2-domain microarray against Chlamydia Tarp phosphopeptides; supports GRB2 phosphotyrosine binding.

title: Selected reaction monitoring mass spectrometry reveals the dynamics of signaling through the GRB2 adaptor.
review_notes: AP-SRM GRB2 interactome dynamics (abstract only cached); defines ~90 GRB2-associated proteins without resolving binding modes per partner.

title: Tespa1 is involved in late thymocyte development through the regulation of TCR-mediated signaling.
review_notes: Tespa1 study; abstract reports Tespa1 association with GRB2 in the TCR signalosome, not GRB2 as a COP9 signalosome subunit.

title: Inhibition of basal FGF receptor signaling by dimeric Grb2.
review_notes: Dimeric GRB2 binds FGFR2 C-termini and restrains basal receptor signalling; supports homodimerization.

title: GRB2-mediated recruitment of THEMIS to LAT is essential for thymocyte development.
review_notes: Abstract shows GRB2 C-SH3 binding a THEMIS PxRPxK motif and recruiting THEMIS to LAT.

title: Threshold-controlled ubiquitination of the EGFR directs receptor fate.
review_notes: Cbl recruited to EGFR in complex with GRB2 via EGFR pY1068/pY1086 plus pY1045; GRB2 as the Cbl-EGFR adaptor.

title: A THEMIS:SHP1 complex promotes T-cell survival.
review_notes: Abstract shows GRB2 bridging SHP1 (N-SH3) and THEMIS (C-SH3) and recruiting the complex to LAT via its SH2 domain.

title: Phospho-tyrosine dependent protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale pY-dependent Y2H screen; the TSPAN2-GRB2 pair is characterised in detail (SH2- and TSPAN2 pY124-dependent).

title: GRB2 Nucleates T Cell Receptor-Mediated LAT Clusters That Control PLC-γ1 Activation and Cytokine Production.
review_notes: Full text cached; supports GRB2 adaptor activity in LAT microcluster formation in CD4+ T cells. Contains no NK-cell data, so it does not support the GO:0045953 annotation attributed to it.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
