review_notes: Urinary exosome proteomics; GluD1 appears only as a high-throughput mass-spectrometry hit. Correctly cited, but a poor basis for a localisation claim about a brain postsynaptic receptor.

title: Induction of excitatory and inhibitory presynaptic differentiation by GluD1.
review_notes: Biochem Biophys Res Commun 2011. Establishes that GluD1 plus Cbln1 induces both glutamatergic and GABAergic presynaptic differentiation - the basis for accepting the GABAergic-synapse localisation.

title: mGlu1 receptor canonical signaling pathway contributes to the opening of the orphan GluD2 receptor.
review_notes: Neuropharmacology 2017. The paper is sound and the observation (Gq-PLC-PKC opening of a GluD channel) is real, but its direct recordings are of GluD2, and it has been used in GOA to give GRID1 an enables annotation to G protein-coupled receptor activity (GO:0099530). GluD is the effector channel in that experiment; the GPCR is mGlu1. Cited here for the pathway, not for the receptor typing.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome screen; source of a bare protein binding annotation whose only partner is haemoglobin beta.

title: Striatal glutamate delta-1 receptor regulates behavioral flexibility and thalamostriatal connectivity.
review_notes: Neurobiol Dis 2020. Striatal GluD1 conditional knockout: behavioural inflexibility and selective loss of thalamostriatal terminals.

title: Delta glutamate receptor conductance drives excitation of mouse dorsal raphe neurons.
review_notes: eLife 2020. The strongest evidence that GluD1 carries a real cation current in native neurons, driven by alpha-1 adrenergic receptors and tonically active.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome screen; source of a bare protein binding annotation whose only partner is haemoglobin beta.

title: GluD1 is a signal transduction device disguised as an ionotropic receptor.
review_notes: Nature 2021. The chimera experiment that separates GluD1 signalling from the channel; primary support for the trans-synaptic organiser core function. A 2025 erratum (Nature 642:E27) is noted in the PubMed record and does not affect these conclusions.

title: Potentiation of neuronal activity by tonic GluD1 current in brain slices.
review_notes: EMBO Rep 2023. Shows the tonic GluD1 current is G-protein-independent and sets subthreshold excitability.

title: GluD1 binds GABA and controls inhibitory plasticity.
review_notes: Science 2023. GABA binding to GluD1 with structural and functional evidence; explicitly non-ionotropic. Source of the GO:0016917 IDA.

title: Lack of evidence for direct ligand-gated ion channel activity of GluD receptors.
review_notes: PNAS 2024. Direct, controlled refutation of ligand-gated channel activity of wild-type GluD receptors; cited as a CAUTION by UniProt on Q9ULK0.

title: GluD1 at the synaptic crossroads: from domain structure to circuit dysfunction.
review_notes: Acta Pharmacol Sin 2026 review by the same group as PMID:42270762. States that GluD1 lacks classical ion channel activity and reframes it as a synaptic organiser - which sits awkwardly beside that group's own acetylcholine-receptor paper.

title: Heating the orphans: structural asymmetry and thermal energy resolve the delta receptor paradox.
review_notes: Commun Biol 2026. A Comment, not primary data, and principally about GluD2. Offers the thermodynamic-barrier explanation for why delta receptors look silent at room temperature. Treated as a hypothesis, not as evidence for a GluD1 annotation.

title: GluD1 is localized at cholinergic synapses and is an acetylcholine receptor.
review_notes: Mol Psychiatry 2026, cached ABSTRACT ONLY. Reports acetylcholine-evoked NASPM-sensitive currents that are absent in GluD1 knockouts. The single strongest piece of evidence for direct transmitter gating, but the authors hedge ("suggesting potential conductance"), the ligand-binding evidence is an indirect conformational assay, and the result has not yet been independently replicated. Not treated as settling GO:1904315.

title: Inhibition of delta-1 glutamate receptor current by extracellular protons.
review_notes: bioRxiv PREPRINT, not peer reviewed. Proton inhibition of the alpha-1-adrenergic-evoked GluD1 current in serotonin neurons. Supports a functional pore but not direct transmitter gating; flagged as preprint and not used as the basis for any annotation action.

title: Differential expression and localisation of gasdermin-like (GSDML), a novel member of the cancer-associated GSDMDC protein family, in neoplastic and non-neoplastic gastric, hepatic, and colon tissues.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Pathology 2008, Carl-McGrath et al. Cached abstract only, but the abstract itself states the cytoplasmic localization that the EXP annotation rests on. Pre-dates all functional work on GSDMB; useful for localization and tissue distribution.

title: Gene polymorphism linked to increased asthma and IBD risk alters gasdermin-B structure, a sulfatide and phosphoinositide binding protein.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: PNAS 2017, Chao, Kulakova and Herzberg. Cached abstract only (publisher restricts PMC full text). The primary direct evidence that GSDMB binds phosphoinositides and sulfatide. Its lipid profile conflicts with PMID:34022140; the conflict is now understood as an isoform difference rather than a disagreement about the same molecule. Method caveat worth noting: binding was to lipids immobilized on nitrocellulose, which is less physiological than a bilayer.

title: Granzyme A from cytotoxic lymphocytes cleaves GSDMB to trigger pyroptosis in target cells.
review_notes: Identifier verified against PubMed: Science 2020;368(6494):eaaz7548, Zhou et al. Flagged DISPUTED because Science published a Published Erratum for it in 2026 (PMID:42424476, doi 10.1126/science.aej7549), and the content of that erratum could not be retrieved - PubMed carries no abstract, Europe PMC records it as subscription-only and not in PMC, and science.org returns HTTP 403. I do not know what was corrected and am not guessing. Consequences are limited: no GOA annotation on GSDMB cites this PMID, nothing in this review rests on it, and its central claim (granzyme A cleaves GSDMB to unleash pore formation) has been independently re-derived with structures by three other groups (PMID:36991122, PMID:36991125, PMID:41592574), the last of which pins the cleavage site at Lys244.

title: Pathogenic ubiquitination of GSDMB inhibits NK cell bactericidal functions.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Cell 2021, Hansen et al., full text cached. Establishes the direct bactericidal activity and the cardiolipin/lipid A specificity. Its headline negative claim - that GSDMB does not lyse host cells - was contested at the time (PMID:36157507) and is now better read as a property of the isoform used (Q8TAX9-1) rather than of GSDMB in general. Cited here only for the bactericidal and bacterial-lipid claims, which are not in dispute.

title: GSDMB N-terminal assembles in plasma membrane to execute pyroptotic cell death.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Genes Dis 2022, Gong et al., full text cached. A short rebuttal-style report rather than a full study, but it does the decisive fractionation experiment (GSDMB-NT in plasma membrane, not mitochondria, no cytochrome c release) and it identifies the isoform question itself, stating that it used the 416-residue form while Hansen et al. used isoform 1. Format is brief and the evidence is a single figure, so it is weighted as corroborating rather than decisive.

title: Insights into the GSDMB-mediated cellular lysis and its targeting by IpaH7.8.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nat Commun 2023, Yin et al., full text cached. Crystal structure of the GSDMB-IpaH7.8 complex; cited as corroboration for the Shigella targeting and the membrane-engagement surfaces, not as primary evidence for any annotation here.

title: Distinct GSDMB protein isoforms and protease cleavage processes differentially control pyroptotic cell death and mitochondrial damage in cancer cells.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Cell Death Differ 2023, Molina-Crespo/Sarrio/Moreno-Bueno group, full text cached. Source of the GSDMB1-4 nomenclature that UniProt now maps onto its own isoform IDs, and of the key dissociation that granzyme A cleaves all isoforms while only exon-6-containing ones become pyroptotic. Also reports concomitant mitochondrial damage, which is not reconciled with PMID:36157507.

title: Structural basis for GSDMB pore formation and its targeting by IpaH7.8.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nature 2023, Wang et al. (Ruan lab), full text cached. Independent cryo-EM pore structure reaching the same isoform conclusion as PMID:36991125 from a different laboratory, which is what makes the exon-6 result solid rather than single-source.

title: Structural mechanisms for regulation of GSDMB pore-forming activity.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nature 2023, Zhong et al. (Shao/Ding labs). Cached abstract only, but the abstract states the pore stoichiometry, the exon-6 requirement and the explanation for earlier negative results. The strongest single reference for the isoform adjudication.

title: Alternative splicing of GSDMB modulates killer lymphocyte-triggered pyroptosis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Sci Immunol 2023, Lieberman lab, full text cached. Tests isoform behaviour under real NK cell attack rather than only with recombinant protease, and reports the dominant-negative behaviour of the non-cytotoxic fragments. Uses the GSDMB1-5 naming scheme, which has no UniProt synonym for GSDMB5, so that one mapping was left unasserted.

title: Exosite-mediated targeting of GSDMB by dimeric granzyme A in lymphocyte pyroptotic killing.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Immunity 2026, Wang et al. (Shao/Ding labs), cached abstract only. Gives the recognition mechanism (granzyme A dimerization, exosite engagement of the GSDMB C-terminal domain, cleavage at Lys244) and the species caveat that mouse granzyme A engages the exosite inefficiently. Also serves as independent structural re-derivation of the 2020 Science claim, which matters given the erratum to that paper.

title: Erratum for the Research Article "Granzyme A from cytotoxic lymphocytes cleaves GSDMB to trigger pyroptosis in target cells" by Z. Zhou et al.
review_notes: Existence and target verified: PubMed and Europe PMC both record this as a Published Erratum (Science 2026 Jul 9;393(6807):eaej7549) for PMID:32299851. The substance could NOT be retrieved - no abstract in PubMed, Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess N / inPMC N with subscription required, and science.org returns HTTP 403. What was corrected is therefore unknown to this review, and no annotation here depends on the corrected paper. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED to make that limitation explicit. A curator with journal access should read it and, if the correction touches the cleavage-site or pyroptosis data, revisit PMID:32299851.

title: Structure, expression and chromosome mapping of MLZE, a novel gene which is preferentially expressed in metastatic melanoma cells.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Jpn J Cancer Res 2001, the original MLZE/GSDMC cloning paper. Cached entry is abstract-only, so the cytoplasm IDA it supports could not be checked against the figures. Relevant for gene identity, tissue expression and the melanoma link rather than for molecular function.

title: PD-L1-mediated gasdermin C expression switches apoptosis to pyroptosis in cancer cells and facilitates tumour necrosis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Nat Cell Biol 2020, Hou et al. Full text cached. Provides the only reconstituted biochemistry for GSDMC pore formation (liposome pelleting, EM pores, Tb3+ leakage) and is the source of the plasma membrane EXP annotation. Note PubMed lists an erratum for this article (Nat Cell Biol 2020;22(11):1396); the erratum content was not retrieved and no claim used here depends on it.

title: The metabolite α-KG induces GSDMC-dependent pyroptosis through death receptor 6-activated caspase-8.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Cell Res 2021, Zhang et al. Independent replication that caspase-8 cleavage of GSDMC produces pyroptosis, here downstream of alpha-ketoglutarate and DR6. Cited as corroboration of pore competence, not of any particular target membrane.

title: Gasdermin C cleavage by Cathepsin S modulates Rab7 vesicles in intestinal epithelial cells to amplify anti-helminth immunity.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Immunity 2025, Pandey et al., full text available via PMC12380176. The principal challenge to the pyroptosis paradigm for GSDMC. Note that much of the mechanistic imaging uses murine Gsdmc2/Gsdmc4 in HeLa cells and C. elegans, though human GSDMC is also cleaved by cathepsin S and the human N-terminal fragment was imaged in HeLa.

title: Cutting the Gordian knot: Untangling gasdermin C from pyroptosis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Immunity 2025, Lin and Ruan, a commentary on PMID:40701157. Cached abstract only. Used to document that the community treats the GSDMC/pyroptosis relationship as unresolved, not as primary evidence.

title: Disruption of heme homeostasis by nuclear receptor Nur77 induces pyroptosis through granzyme B-dependent GSDMC cleavage.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Signal Transduct Target Ther 2025, Wu et al., full text cached. Correctly cited, but weighed cautiously: pyroptosis is induced by a synthetic Nur77 ligand (DdBIC) acting through a long mito-ROS/OMA1/OPA1/PERK cascade, so it establishes that GSDMC can form a lytic pore rather than that it normally does. It also introduces a third activating protease (granzyme B) alongside caspase-8 and cathepsin S.

title: Gasdermin C reprograms metabolism through the CAMKK2-AMPK axis to promote lung adenocarcinoma progression and radioresistance.
review_notes: Identifier verified against PubMed (Cell Rep 2026, Ren et al.) and the nuclear scaffold claim is in the abstract, but the claim itself is unverified: cached entry is abstract-only, the result is from a single laboratory, and no independent replication of nuclear GSDMC recruiting NAT10 or BAZ1B/SMARCA5 was found. Deliberately not used to support any annotation in this review; raised in suggested_questions and suggested_experiments instead.

title: Functional chimeric mRNAs encode proteins in mammalian immunity.
review_notes: Venezia/Kane et al., Nature 2026 (PubMed-verified). Describes the mouse Gsdmd-Tmem106a trans-spliced chimeric mRNA whose product acts as a plasma-membrane cofactor for GSDMD-NT pore formation. Relevant as context / a knowledge gap for canonical GSDMD (a distinct gene product, not a GSDMD annotation); human orthologous chimera not yet established.

review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_30108131.md frontmatter title matches the YAML title; review establishes the eEF1A-like translational-GTPase / ribosome surveillance function. Cited in core_functions supported_by for GO:0003746.

title: Identification of human and mouse GP-1, a putative member of a novel G-protein family.
review_notes: Not cached, but anchored to GOA: this PMID supports GO:0005525 (GTP binding), GO:0006955 (immune response) and GO:0007165 (signal transduction) by TAS in GTPBP1-goa.tsv, consistent with the title (original GP-1/GTPBP1 cloning and IFN-gamma inducibility). Background characterization rather than the core translation-elongation function.

title: Functions of unconventional mammalian translational GTPases GTPBP1 and GTPBP2.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_30108131.md frontmatter title matches the YAML title; review establishes GTPBP2's translational-GTPase properties (weak aa-tRNA-stimulated GTP binding, no eEF1A-like elongation activity), the basis for the core GTP-binding / ribosome-rescue function.

title: Falcon deep research report for GTPBP2
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison Scientific Literature) deep research report. GTPBP2-specific, primary-literature-anchored claims that are usable: the ribosome-rescue / translation-elongation-quality-control role, cooperation with the PELO/HBS1L/ABCE1 rescue machinery, cytosolic ribosome-associated localization, and the codon-specific ribosome pausing at AGA arginine codons under limiting tRNA-Arg(UCU) (from the Ackerman-lab mouse genetics, Ishimura 2016 / Terrey 2020). CAUTION / not relied on here: the report repeatedly folds GTPBP2 together with its paralog GTPBP1 (e.g. the Salpietro 2024 GTPBP1/GTPBP2 syndrome and the GTPBP1 structural / mTORC1 / aa-tRNA-delivery data are GTPBP1-centric and over-generalized to GTPBP2), and it over-imputes canonical translation-factor GTPase mechanism (GTP-hydrolysis-coupled splitting) that has not been directly demonstrated for human GTPBP2, which has only weak GTP binding. Disease/RQC/ISR/NGD framing is review-level and not used to change any molecular-function annotation. Citations are secondary (this report), not the primary papers; correctness left UNVERIFIED for the synthesis.

title: Structural basis of GTPase-mediated mitochondrial ribosome biogenesis and recycling.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_34135319.md title matches; anchored to GOA as the IDA source for GO:0043023 (ribosomal large subunit binding) and GO:1902775 (mtLSU assembly). Recombinant GTPBP6 reconstitutes late mtLSU biogenesis in vitro, directly establishing the core function. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: Reversal of pathology in murine mucopolysaccharidosis type VII by somatic cell gene transfer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes that beta-glucuronidase deficiency causes MPS VII (Sly syndrome) with lysosomal storage of undegraded glycosaminoglycans, supporting the glycosaminoglycan catabolic process annotation.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.

review_notes: Primary curated UniProt record for HGSNAT; source of function, catalytic activity, location, and subunit statements.

Both IBA rows resolve to real IBD nodes in the local slice interpro/panther/PTHR13285/PTHR13285-paint.tsv: the Eukaryota-scoped PTN000328646 for GO:0005783 and the Eumetazoa-scoped PTN000998821 for GO:0016409. title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog transfer from mouse Hhat (UniProtKB:Q8BMT9). All four rows it drives were traced through QuickGO to experimental mouse annotations (IMP or IDA), and each lands on a term the human protein also carries by direct evidence.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated annotation. The single row it drives, endoplasmic reticulum membrane, agrees with the human IDA row and rests on both an experimental mouse ortholog annotation and the UniProt subcellular location SL-0097.

title: Hhat is a palmitoylacyltransferase with specificity for N-palmitoylation of Sonic Hedgehog.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (J Biol Chem 2008, Buglino JA and Resh MD) and the title matches the cached record. Only the abstract is cached (full_text_available: false), so all quotes here are abstract-level. It is the anchor for four GOA rows (GO:0019706, GO:0005783, GO:0005794, GO:0045880); the abstract directly supports the first, the last and the secretory-pathway context, and UniProt curates the ER and Golgi locations from this paper, the Golgi one as a curator inference (ECO:0000305), which is why the Golgi row is kept as non-core rather than accepted or removed.

title: Topological analysis of Hedgehog acyltransferase, a multipalmitoylated transmembrane protein.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (J Biol Chem 2015, Konitsiotis AD et al.) and the title matches the cached record; full text available. Supports the GO:0005789 IDA row with the is_active_in qualifier, because the catalytic residues are shown to be part of the membrane-embedded architecture rather than peripheral to it. UniProt cites it with ECO:0000269 for the ER membrane location and multi-pass topology.

title: Hedgehog Acyltransferase Promotes Uptake of Palmitoyl-CoA across the Endoplasmic Reticulum Membrane.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Cell Rep 2019, Asciolla JJ and Resh MD) and the title matches the cached record; full text available. It is the source of GOA's GO:0019706 and GO:0045880 IDA rows and also reports a second, transport-like activity that GOA does not annotate. No transport term was proposed on the strength of it: no MBOAT in PANTHER family PTHR13285 carries a transport term in any species, and the 2021 structures recast the movement as substrate access to a membrane-embedded active site. UniProt nevertheless states the conduit function with ECO:0000269 from this paper and two others, so the claim is recorded in the notes and raised as a question.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Nature 2020, Luck K et al.) and the title matches the cached record. Correctly cited as the source of the single GO:0005515 IntAct row (partner SDCBP/syntenin-1), but that partner appears in no described HHAT mechanism and was not followed up, so the row supports no informative molecular function.

title: Substrate and product complexes reveal mechanisms of Hedgehog acylation by HHAT.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Science 2021, Jiang Y, Benz TL and Long SB) and the title matches the cached record; full text available and read. It anchors GOA rows for GO:0019706, GO:0045880 and GO:0051604, and is the reference used for the proposed NEW GO:0018009 row, since its product complex resolves the amide linkage itself.

title: Structure, mechanism, and inhibition of Hedgehog acyltransferase.
review_notes: PMID confirmed against PubMed (Mol Cell 2021, Coupland CE et al.) and the title matches the cached record; full text available. Anchors GOA rows for GO:0019706 and GO:0051604, and contributes the heme cofactor requirement that UniProt records as COFACTOR heme b.

title: HHAT palmitoylates Hh N-terminal fragment
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction (reactome/R-HSA-5358343.md). Its author statement that HHAT palmitoylates the Hh N-terminal fragment, and that losing HHAT or the acceptor cysteine reduces Hh signalling, agrees with the primary literature. Supports the GO:0005789 TAS row; the GO:0016747 TAS row it also drives is far broader than the reaction's own text and is modified to GO:0016409.

title: HHAT G287V doesn't palmitoylate Hh-Np
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction (reactome/R-HSA-5483229.md), modelling the G287V loss-of-function allele found in syndromic 46,XY disorder of sex development. Reactome notes the mutant retains normal stability, expression and localization but cannot palmitoylate SHH or DHH, which is why the ER membrane row exported from a loss-of-function reaction is still sound. The accompanying GO:0016747 row is modified to GO:0016409.

title: Clinical, biochemical, and molecular findings in three patients with 3-hydroxyisobutyric aciduria.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Primary functional identification of the human enzyme; UniProt cites this PMID for both CATALYTIC ACTIVITY and the L-valine degradation PATHWAY, so it directly supports the GO:0008442 and GO:0006574 IDA annotations. Note the paper's negative disease finding (HIBADH not causative for 3-hydroxyisobutyric aciduria); this does not affect the enzymatic annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome (Y2H). Source of the ~40 GO:0005515 "protein binding" IPI annotations. The recorded partners are predominantly membrane/secretory-pathway proteins unrelated to a soluble matrix metabolic enzyme; the interactions yield only an uninformative bare protein-binding term and are treated as over-annotation, not evidence of a physiological complex or specific molecular function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (full text available in cache). Provides HTP evidence for mitochondrial localization, corroborating the UniProt "Mitochondrion" location; less specific than the matrix localization used as the core location.

title: methylmalonyl semialdehyde + NADH + H+ <=> beta-hydroxyisobutyrate + NAD+
review_notes: Reactome reaction (reverse direction) modeling HIBADH in the mitochondrial matrix within branched-chain amino acid catabolism; supports the matrix localization TAS annotation.

title: beta-hydroxyisobutyrate + NAD+ <=> methylmalonyl semialdehyde + NADH + H+
review_notes: Reactome reaction (forward direction) modeling HIBADH in the mitochondrial matrix within branched-chain amino acid catabolism; supports the matrix localization TAS annotation.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput proteomic confirmation of mitochondrial localization; HIBCH is one entry among the mitochondrial proteome. Supports only generic mitochondrion (HTP).

title: Ectopic protein lysine methacrylation contributes to defects caused by loss of HIBCH or ECHS1.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; basis for the FlyBase IMP annotation to L-valine catabolic process and the IDA annotation to mitochondrial matrix. Mechanistically links HIBCH loss to valine-pathway intermediate (methacrylyl-CoA) accumulation and Leigh-like disease.

title: Primary structure and tissue-specific expression of human beta-hydroxyisobutyryl-coenzyme A hydrolase.
review_notes: Original cloning and biochemical characterization of human HIBCH; abstract-only in cache. Underpins the EXP and IDA GO:0003860 core molecular-function annotations and Reactome R-HSA-70881.

title: A recombinant human 'mini'-hexokinase is catalytically active and regulated by hexose 6-phosphates.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract directly supports human hexokinase catalytic activity (glucose phosphorylation) and allosteric product inhibition by glucose 6-phosphate.

title: Human hexokinase type I microheterogeneity is due to different amino-terminal sequences.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports that the N-terminal 10 residues mediate binding to mitochondrial porin (VDAC) and hence the mitochondrial-outer-membrane association.

title: PKCε promotes oncogenic functions of ATF2 in the nucleus while blocking its apoptotic function at mitochondria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract explicitly references the HK1-VDAC1 complex at mitochondria. Supports the HK1-VDAC1 interaction but the GO term (protein binding) is uninformative.

title: Hexokinase activity is required for recruitment of parkin to depolarized mitochondria.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; foregrounds HK2 but explicitly states the effect is shared among hexokinases including the brain-expressed HK1. Supports the parkin-recruitment (protein localization to mitochondrion) role of hexokinases.

title: Hexokinase Is an Innate Immune Receptor for the Detection of Bacterial Peptidoglycan.
review_notes: Full text available; directly supports hexokinase enzymatic activity and its inhibition by N-acetylglucosamine, glucosamine phosphorylation, mitochondrial-outer-membrane association and dissociation, and the innate-immune (peptidoglycan/NAG-sensing, NLRP3/IL-1beta) moonlighting role.

title: c-Src phosphorylation and activation of hexokinase promotes tumorigenesis and metastasis.
review_notes: Full text available; establishes HK1-c-Src interaction and Tyr732 phosphorylation that activates HK1 and enhances glycolysis. Underlying interaction real; GO term (protein binding) uninformative.

title: Human hexokinase: sequences of amino- and carboxyl-terminal halves are homologous.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the human hexokinase cDNA-cloning paper establishing the 917-aa two-domain structure with C-terminal catalytic (glucose-binding and glucose-phosphorylating) and N-terminal regulatory halves.

title: CFTR interactome mapping using the mammalian membrane two-hybrid high-throughput screening system.
review_notes: High-throughput CFTR interactome screen; HK1 appears as an interactor in the underlying dataset. Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation of unclear significance.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Large-scale endogenous-tagging and interactome resource; HK1-VDAC1 interaction in the dataset. Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Differential CFTR-Interactome Proximity Labeling Procedures Identify Enrichment in Multiple SLC Transporters.
review_notes: High-throughput CFTR proximity-labeling study; HK1 appears among proximity-labeled proteins. Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation of unclear significance.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO. The class II alpha N-terminal signatures (IPR001003, IPR014745) that fire on this protein correctly imply class II complex membership and antigen presentation; the accompanying GO:0016020 membrane mapping is too general to be useful.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT phylogenetic inference (IBD/IBA). The class II node PTN000460629 underlies most of this gene's process and location annotations; the node placement is sound for peptide binding, complex membership, presentation and MIIC localisation, but the same node also carries GO:0023026, which suits the DM/DO donors rather than a class II constituent such as DP alpha.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: UniProt SubCell-to-GO mapping. Faithfully reproduces the curated subcellular locations of P20036 (cell membrane, ER membrane, Golgi, endosome membrane, lysosome membrane).

title: Crystal structure of HLA-DP2 and implications for chronic beryllium disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The central experimental reference for this gene: the first HLA-DP crystal structure, of DPA1*01:03/DPB1*02:01 with a bound HLA-DR alpha-derived self-peptide, plus presentation assays in DPA1*01:03-expressing fibroblasts. Supports the peptide antigen binding IDA, the class II complex IDA, cell-surface localisation and the T-cell activation rows. Note that the mutational series is on the DP beta chain, so the rows on HLA-DPA1 reflect the activity of the assembled heterodimer.

title: Epitope recognition by a DP alpha chain-specific monoclonal antibody (DP11.1) is influenced by the interaction between the DP alpha chain and its polymorphic DP beta chain partner.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false). A DP alpha-chain-specific monoclonal antibody study establishing surface expression of the DP alpha chain and showing that its epitope depends on the polymorphic DP beta partner, i.e. obligate heterodimerisation. It is cited by GOA for three NAS rows; it supports plasma membrane localisation but makes no receptor-activity or immune-response claim, which is why GO:0032395 is removed and GO:0006955 is modified.

title: Structural basis of chronic beryllium disease: linking allergic hypersensitivity and autoimmunity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Clayton et al., Cell 2014). Not cited by GOA for this gene but used here as additional evidence: the AV22 TCR/DP2/peptide/Be2+ quaternary structure, showing the assembled DP molecule engaged by a T-cell receptor. Also the basis for declining to propose GO:0042608 T cell receptor binding, since the reported footprint is tilted away from the DP alpha chain helix.

title: HLA-DP(84Gly) constitutively presents endogenous peptides generated by the class I antigen processing pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (DOI 10.1038/ncomms15244); full text cached in this session. Surfaced by the falcon deep research. The decisive polymorphism is in HLA-DPB1, so this is a property of particular assembled DP molecules rather than a DPA1-specific activity; recorded as a suggested question rather than as a new annotation on the alpha chain.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the BioPlex ORFEOME AP-MS interactome survey. Cited for a generic protein binding IPI with SREBF2. The paper is methodologically sound, but the single HLA-DPA1/SREBF2 association it contributes carries no functional interpretation for this gene.

title: A subset of HLA-DP molecules serve as ligands for the natural cytotoxicity receptor NKp44.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (DOI 10.1038/s41590-019-0448-4); full text cached in this session. Surfaced by the falcon deep research. Establishes an innate-receptor ligand role for assembled HLA-DP; the allele dependence maps to the DPA1/DPB1 pair, so it is recorded as a suggested question rather than asserted as a DPA1 molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; BioPlex 3.0, the two-cell-line (HEK293T/HCT116) extension of the same AP-MS platform. Contributes the same HLA-DPA1/SREBF2 pair as a generic protein binding IPI.

title: A multi-scale map of cell structure fusing protein images and interactions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in the cache. MuSIC, which fuses Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence with BioPlex affinity purifications. The HLA-DPA1/SREBF2 edge it supplies derives from the BioPlex data rather than from independent evidence, so it adds no support beyond the two BioPlex papers.

title: HLA-DPA1*02:01~B1*01:01 is a risk haplotype for primary sclerosing cholangitis mediating activation of NKp44+ NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (DOI 10.1136/gutjnl-2023-329524); full text cached in this session. Surfaced by the falcon deep research. The genetic association and the functional assays both concern the paired DPA1-DPB1 haplotype, so no DPA1-specific annotation follows; it supports the interferon-gamma inducibility already kept as non-core and motivates a suggested question about NKp44 ligand activity.

title: An EBV-related CD4 TCR immunotherapy inhibits tumor growth in an HLA-DP5+ nasopharyngeal cancer mouse model.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (DOI 10.1172/JCI172092); full text cached in this session. Surfaced by the falcon deep research. Relevant to the open question of how much HLA-DP peptide specificity is set by the alpha chain; does not by itself add a GO annotation beyond the existing peptide antigen binding and class II presentation rows.

title: A zinc finger protein that represses transcription of the human MHC class II gene, DPA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in the cache. Establishes that the DPA promoter is IFN-gamma-inducible and repressed by the X2-box-binding zinc finger protein XBR. It documents the gene as a target of interferon signalling rather than a participant in transducing it, so the GO:0071346 row it supports is kept as non-core.

title: Falcon deep research report for human HLA-DPA1
review_notes: Provider-generated literature synthesis that completed after the review was written. Reconciled against the review: consistent with the peptide-binding, class II heterodimer, endolysosomal loading and CD4 T-cell presentation picture already asserted. Its three material additions were checked against primary papers and added as references here (PMID:38412034 DPA1-allele-dependent EBNA1 presentation; PMID:28489076 DP-beta84Gly presentation of endogenous peptides; PMID:31358998 and PMID:37788895 HLA-DP as an NKp44 ligand). None of them changed an existing annotation action, and the report is not used as sole evidence for any GO decision.

title: UniProt entry P20036 (HLA class II histocompatibility antigen, DP alpha 1 chain)
review_notes: The curated UniProt record for P20036, used for the function statement, the alpha/beta heterodimer and CD74 heterononamer subunit description, the full subcellular itinerary, the family assignment and the single recorded SREBF2 interaction.

title: Human uroporphyrinogen III synthase: NMR-based mapping of the active site.
review_notes: Title foregrounds URO-synthase (UROS), but the study developed expression and purification of the cytosolic heme-biosynthesis enzymes including human HMB-synthase holoenzyme; used to support HMBS MF/BP annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Structural insight into acute intermittent porphyria.
review_notes: Crystal structure and functional analysis of human PBGD/HMBS; establishes the dipyrromethane cofactor at C261 and the sequential-condensation mechanism.

title: Correlation between biochemical findings, structural and enzymatic abnormalities in mutated HMBS identified in six Israeli families with acute intermittent porphyria.
review_notes: Recombinant expression and activity assays of wild-type and AIP-mutant human HMBS directly support the enzymatic function.

title: Studies on the mechanism of hydroxymethylbilane synthase concerning the role of arginine residues in substrate binding.
review_notes: Mechanistic (E. coli enzyme) study of conserved arginine residues in substrate/cofactor binding; supports the conserved HMBS molecular function.

title: Conformational stability and activity analysis of two hydroxymethylbilane synthase mutants, K132N and V215E, with different phenotypic association with acute intermittent porphyria.
review_notes: Full text available; kinetic characterization of recombinant human HMBS and explicit description of the reaction (assembly of four PBG into HMB) and the enzyme as the third step of heme biosynthesis.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome (Y2H) map; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (HMBS-PICK1). Uninformative about HMBS's specific function.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale neurodegenerative-disease interactome mapping; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (HMBS-HTT). Uninformative about HMBS's specific function.

title: Investigation of the oligomeric status of the peroxisomal isoform of human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA lyase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Characterizes purified peroxisomal (unprocessed) HMGCL isoform; DTT-stimulated lyase activity and Cys323-dependent homodimerization. Supports the lyase-activity, peroxisome and homodimer annotations; does NOT support a "structural molecule activity" MF.

title: Crystal structure of human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA Lyase: insights into catalysis and the molecular basis for hydroxymethylglutaric aciduria.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. 2.1 A crystal structure of human mitochondrial HMGCL with bound activator cation; identifies Asn275/Asp42/His233/His235 cation ligands and the (beta/alpha)8 barrel fold. Directly supports metal-ion binding and catalysis.

title: Characterization of a novel HMG-CoA lyase enzyme with a dual location in endoplasmic reticulum and cytosol.
review_notes: Full text available. Primary subject is HMGCLL1 (er-cHL), a distinct ER/cytosolic HMG-CoA lyase homolog encoded by a different gene; mitochondrial HMGCL (mHL) is the reference/comparison enzyme. Its introduction cleanly states HMGCL function (HMG-CoA cleavage; common final step of ketogenesis + leucine catabolism), which is what is quoted here. The GOA IDA annotations of P35914 to this paper are therefore biologically correct for HMGCL but the paper's novel focus is HMGCLL1.

title: Identification and characterization of an extramitochondrial human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA lyase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Characterizes HMGCLL1 as an extramitochondrial (ER/cytosol) HMG-CoA lyase distinct from mitochondrial HMGCL, using mitochondrial HMGCL as the reference enzyme. GOA IDA annotations of P35914 to this paper describe the correct HMGCL function but the paper itself is about the HMGCLL1 gene product.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Full text available. Defines the high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP, 1,134 protein-coding genes); provides high-throughput support for HMGCL's mitochondrial localization.

title: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA lyase: expression and isolation of the recombinant human enzyme and investigation of a mechanism for regulation of enzyme activity.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Expresses and isolates recombinant human HMGCL (mitochondrial matrix protein) and studies Cys323 thiol/disulfide regulation. Supports the lyase-activity IDA; the co-cited "lipid metabolic process" is over-general.

title: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A lyase (HL): cloning and characterization of a mouse liver HL cDNA and subchromosomal mapping of the human and mouse HL genes.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. States HMGCL is "a homodimeric mitochondrial matrix enzyme that catalyzes the last step of ketogenesis" - directly supports matrix localization, homodimer and ketogenesis annotations.

title: Characterization of the hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA lyase precursor, a protein targeted to peroxisomes and mitochondria.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows HMGCL precursor (retaining the mitochondrial leader and a C-terminal Cys-Lys-Leu PTS) is dual-targeted to peroxisomes and mitochondria; precursor and mature enzyme have similar catalytic properties. Supports dual localization and lyase activity.

title: Evidence supporting a role for histidine-235 in cation binding to human 3-hydroxy-3-methyglutaryl-CoA lyase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Site-directed mutagenesis and ESR show HMGCL requires a dissociable divalent cation (Mg2+ or Mn2+) and that His235 contributes to cation binding. Directly supports magnesium/manganese ion binding.

title: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A lyase: targeting and processing in peroxisomes and mitochondria.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Demonstrates HMGCL dual mitochondrial/peroxisomal localization (peroxisomal HL absent in Zellweger cells) and that mitochondrial HL catalyzes the last step of ketogenesis; peroxisomal HL function is unresolved.

title: HMG CoA => acetoacetic acid + acetyl CoA
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing the HMGCL homodimer in the mitochondrial matrix catalyzing HMG-CoA to acetyl-CoA + acetoacetate. Supports matrix localization and the core reaction.

title: Cargo of PEX5S,L translocates from the cytosol to the peroxisomal matrix
review_notes: Generic PEX5-dependent peroxisomal import event. The cytosol and peroxisomal-matrix localizations derived from it are import-pathway intermediates for HMGCL cargo, not evidence of a functional cytosolic HMGCL pool.

title: PEX5S,L:Cargo binds PEX13:PEX14:PEX2:PEX10:PEX12 (Docking and Translocation Module)
review_notes: Generic peroxisomal docking/translocation-module event; source of a duplicate cytosol (import-intermediate) annotation, not a core cytosolic function.

title: Crystal structure of the catalytic portion of human HMG-CoA reductase: insights into regulation of activity and catalysis.
review_notes: Human catalytic-domain crystal structures with HMG-CoA, CoA and NADP(+); defines catalysis, cofactor/CoA binding and homotetramer/homodimer state. Supports GO:0004420, GO:0120225, GO:0070402.

title: Localization of the pre-squalene segment of the isoprenoid biosynthetic pathway in mammalian peroxisomes.
review_notes: Supports ER and peroxisomal localization of pre-squalene isoprenoid enzymes; peroxisomal claim is contested, so treated as non-core for HMGCR.

title: Thermodynamic and structure guided design of statin based inhibitors of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase.
review_notes: Statin-inhibitor structure/design paper; treats HMGCR as the mevalonate-pathway target enzyme. Basis for the NAS isoprenoid-biosynthesis annotation.

title: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate potently inhibits the in vitro activity of hydroxy-3-methyl-glutaryl-CoA reductase.
review_notes: Direct in vitro human HMGCR activity measurement (rate-controlling enzyme of cholesterol synthesis). Supports GO:0004420.

title: Artemisinic acid inhibits melanogenesis through downregulation of C/EBP α-dependent expression of HMG-CoA reductase gene.
review_notes: Links HMGCR-dependent cholesterol synthesis to melanogenesis via downregulation of HMGCR expression; basis of the cholesterol-biosynthetic-process IDA. The cholesterol-biosynthesis role itself is independently well established.

title: The UBIAD1 prenyltransferase links menaquinone-4 [corrected] synthesis to cholesterol metabolic enzymes.
review_notes: Reports a physical HMGCR-UBIAD1 interaction (Y2H + IP); basis of a protein binding IPI, flagged as over-annotated because the GO term is uninformative.

title: Human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase. Conserved domains responsible for catalytic activity and sterol-regulated degradation.
review_notes: Human full-length cDNA; defines catalytic C-terminal domain and sterol-regulated membrane domain / ER membrane topology. Supports GO:0004420 and ER membrane.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex); source of a generic protein binding IPI, flagged as over-annotated.

title: Limb girdle muscular disease caused by HMGCR mutation and statin myopathy treatable with mevalonolactone.
review_notes: Experimental catalytic characterization of human HMGCR and an LGMDR28 variant, kinetics, statin inhibition, and disease context. Supports GO:0004420 and the rate-limiting cholesterol-synthesis role.

title: Multivalent feedback regulation of HMG CoA reductase, a control mechanism coordinating isoprenoid synthesis and cell growth.
review_notes: Classic study of HMGCR as the mevalonate-synthesizing enzyme under multivalent feedback regulation. Supports GO:0004420 and pathway/regulatory context.

title: UniProtKB entry P04035 (HMDH_HUMAN), 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase
review_notes: Curated UniProt record for HMGCR; source of catalytic-activity, subcellular location and topology statements used as file: supporting text.

title: Crystal structures of human HMG-CoA synthase isoforms provide insights into inherited ketogenesis disorders and inhibitor design.
review_notes: Solved the crystal structures of both human HMGCS isoforms (hHMGCS1 cytosolic, hHMGCS2 mitochondrial; PDB 2P8U for HMGCS1), establishing the homodimer and distinguishing the cytosolic/cholesterol from the mitochondrial/ketogenesis isoform. Directly supports the homodimerization and catalytic-function claims.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale BioPlex 2.0 AP-MS interactome screen; HMGCS1 appears only as an IntAct/BioPlex bait/prey (interactor SLC22A5). Correctly cited for a physical interaction but uninformative about molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale BioPlex 3.0 AP-MS interactome screen; same class of evidence as PMID:28514442. Supports only a bare protein-binding IPI, not a specific function.

title: Molecular cloning and nucleotide sequence of complementary DNA for human hepatic cytosolic acetoacetyl-coenzyme A thiolase.
review_notes: This paper is about cytosolic acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (ACAT2), the enzyme immediately UPSTREAM of HMGCS1 in the mevalonate pathway, not about HMGCS1 itself. It is used only as the reference for a curator IC (inferred from GO:0004421) placing HMGCS1 in cholesterol biosynthesis. The conclusion (HMGCS1 acts in cholesterol biosynthesis) is correct, but the reference is not about this gene.

title: Human cytoplasmic 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A synthase: expression, purification, and characterization of recombinant wild-type and Cys129 mutant enzymes.
review_notes: Expression, purification and kinetic characterization of recombinant human cytoplasmic HMG-CoA synthase, and demonstration that the active-site Cys129 is required for catalysis. Directly establishes HMGCS1 catalytic activity.

title: Mitochondrial 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase deficiency: clinical course and description of causal mutations in two patients.
review_notes: Establishes HMGCS2 catalytic activity via bacterial expression of wild-type and the F174L disease variant (no detectable activity); supports the EXP MF annotation and the disease link. PubMed-verified title/abstract match.

title: Crystal structures of human HMG-CoA synthase isoforms provide insights into inherited ketogenesis disorders and inhibitor design.
review_notes: Crystal structures of the human mitochondrial (HMGCS2) and cytosolic (HMGCS1) isoforms; documents the homodimer (supporting identical protein binding) and explicitly separates the mitochondrial ketogenic isoform from the cytosolic mevalonate/cholesterol isoform.

title: New case of mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase deficiency. Functional analysis of eight mutations.
review_notes: Expression/activity assay of eight HMGCS2 disease mutations; supports the IMP MF and ketone body biosynthetic process annotations. Abstract-only cached but title/abstract verified.

title: Human Mitochondrial HMG-CoA Synthase Deficiency: Role of Enzyme Dimerization Surface and Characterization of Three New Patients.
review_notes: Full text available; expresses and assays wild-type and ten HMGCS2 variants, confirming the condensation reaction of ketone body synthesis and the homodimeric nature of mHS.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Large-scale MitoCoP proteomic study; HMGCS2 is included in the high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (supplementary data), supporting the HTP mitochondrion annotation. The protein is not discussed by name in the extracted body text.

title: Human mitochondrial HMG CoA synthase: liver cDNA and partial genomic cloning, chromosome mapping to 1p12-p13, and possible role in vertebrate evolution.
review_notes: Original cloning of human liver mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase; identifies mHS as the first enzyme of ketogenesis, distinct from the cytoplasmic cholesterol-synthesis isozyme. Supports the mitochondrion (TAS) annotation and the HMGCS1/HMGCS2 distinction.

title: Disruption of an active site hydrogen bond converts human heme oxygenase-1 into a peroxidase.
review_notes: Active-site Asp-140 mutagenesis abolishes heme oxygenase (biliverdin-forming) activity of human HO-1, directly supporting the core catalytic function.

title: Large-scale identification and characterization of human genes that activate NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways.
review_notes: Genome-scale overexpression luciferase screen; supports an NF-kappaB-activating signal from HMOX1 cDNA only in that artificial context, hence the over-annotation flag.

title: Involvement of NADPH in the interaction between heme oxygenase-1 and cytochrome P450 reductase.
review_notes: Characterizes the functional HO-1/NADPH-CPR interaction (electron donor for catalysis); supports the enzyme binding annotation.

title: BMP4 induces HO-1 via a Smad-independent, p38MAPK-dependent pathway in pulmonary artery myocytes.
review_notes: Shows BMP4-induced HO-1 inhibits pulmonary artery SMC proliferation; supports the negative-regulation-of-SMC-proliferation annotation but not the positive-regulation one.

title: Expression and characterization of full-length human heme oxygenase-1: the presence of intact membrane-binding region leads to increased binding affinity for NADPH cytochrome P450 reductase.
review_notes: Direct biochemical characterization of full-length human HO-1 heme degradation and CPR binding; supports the core catalytic function and heme binding.

title: Oligomerization is crucial for the stability and function of heme oxygenase-1 in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: Establishes ER-membrane anchoring, TM-driven homo-oligomerization, and its requirement for HO-1 stability and enzymatic activity.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: High-throughput YFP-complementation telomere-signaling screen; the HO-1/POT1 hit is a generic protein-binding observation without a defined HO-1 function.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum anchored heme-oxygenase 1 faces the cytosol.
review_notes: Protease-protection assays place endogenous HO-1 in the ER membrane with a cytosol-facing active site; supports the core location and topology.

title: Haem oxygenase-1 overexpression alters intracellular iron distribution.
review_notes: Shows HO-1 overexpression reroutes iron into ferritin and reduces redox-active loose iron; supports the intracellular iron homeostasis annotation.

title: Activation of the p62-Keap1-NRF2 pathway protects against ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells.
review_notes: HO-1 knockdown (with NQO1/FTH1) promoted ferroptosis; supports a protective (negative-regulation-of-ferroptosis) role as an NRF2 target.

title: APEX Fingerprinting Reveals the Subcellular Localization of Proteins of Interest.
review_notes: APEX proximity fingerprinting directly resolved HMOX1 membrane topology/ER localization.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome (HuRI); numerous ER/membrane partners largely reflect co-compartmentalization rather than specific HO-1 functions.

title: SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a induces RETREG1/FAM134B-dependent reticulophagy and triggers sequential ER stress and inflammatory responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
review_notes: Reports HMOX1-ORF3a interaction promoting ORF3a-induced autophagy during SARS-CoV-2 infection; a host-virus interaction, not a core HO-1 function.

title: Expression and characterization of truncated human heme oxygenase (hHO-1) and a fusion protein of hHO-1 with human cytochrome P450 reductase.
review_notes: Truncated human HO-1 converts heme to biliverdin with cytochrome P450 reductase; primary evidence for the core catalytic function and the soluble form.

title: Oxidative stress causes enhanced endothelial cell injury in human heme oxygenase-1 deficiency.
review_notes: First human HMOX1-deficiency case; establishes the in vivo consequences (hemolysis, erythrocyte fragmentation, iron deposition, oxidative-stress hypersensitivity).

title: Hemoxygenase-2 is an oxygen sensor for a calcium-sensitive potassium channel.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache (full_text_available false). PubMed-verified Science 2004 paper on HO-2 as an O2 sensor for BK channels; directly supports the GO:0001666 response to hypoxia IDA and the HO-2/KCNMA1 (Q12791) interaction. Supports a genuine, distinctive HO-2 physiological role (kept as non-core relative to the heme-catabolic core).

title: Human heme oxygenase-2: characterization and expression of a full-length cDNA and evidence suggesting that the two HO-2 transcripts may differ by choice of polyadenylation signal.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. PubMed-verified 1992 characterization of the human HO-2 cDNA and enzyme; supports the GO:0004392 heme oxygenase activity IDA and metalloporphyrin inhibition (ACTIVITY REGULATION). Directly about HMOX2 (HO-2).

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. High-throughput membrane-proteome MS study; the HO-2 identification supports a generic membrane HDA row only and is not informative about the specific ER-membrane location.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary-interactome screen. Interactions are numerous and heterogeneous and yield only uninformative bare protein binding; over-annotated as MF.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome; HO-2 partners are generic and yield only uninformative bare protein binding; over-annotated as MF.

title: Heme oxygenase-2. Properties of the heme complex of the purified tryptic fragment of recombinant human heme oxygenase-2.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. PubMed-verified biochemical/spectroscopic characterization of purified human HO-2; strong direct support for GO:0004392 heme oxygenase activity and GO:0020037 heme binding.

title: HMOX1 dimer, HMOX2 cleave heme
review_notes: Reactome curated reaction; supports the ER-membrane location (GO:0005789 TAS) and the heme-catabolic/CO-producing core of HO-2.

title: Exocytosis of specific granule membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome neutrophil-degranulation pathway; a specialized cell-type context. Supports the specific-granule-membrane / plasma-membrane TAS rows but is peripheral to HO-2's core ER-membrane heme-catabolic function.

title: UniProtKB record for human HMOX2 (P30519)
review_notes: Authoritative UniProt record for HMOX2; primary source for the description and core-function calls.

title: Mutational analysis of a heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A2 response element for RNA trafficking.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Munro et al., J Biol Chem 274:34389-34395 (1999). The A2RE mapping study underlying the mRNA-trafficking annotations.

title: hnRNP A2, a potential ssDNA/RNA molecular adapter at the telomere.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Moran-Jones et al., Nucleic Acids Res 33:486-496 (2005). Rat brain hnRNP A2; supports the telomeric ssDNA binding activity but is the reason those annotations are treated as non-core for the human protein.

title: Mutations in prion-like domains in hnRNPA2B1 and hnRNPA1 cause multisystem proteinopathy and ALS.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Kim et al., Nature 495:467-473 (2013). Establishes the prion-like-domain mutations causing multisystem proteinopathy and ALS; the disease side of the low-complexity-domain function.

title: Sumoylated hnRNPA2B1 controls the sorting of miRNAs into exosomes through binding to specific motifs.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Villarroya-Beltri et al., Nat Commun 4:2980 (2013). Source of the exosomal miRNA sorting annotations.

title: HNRNPA2B1 Is a Mediator of m(6)A-Dependent Nuclear RNA Processing Events.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Alarcon et al., Cell 162:1299-1308 (2015). This is the IDA source for GO:1990247, GO:0031053 and the splicing IMP. The in vivo binding and pri-miRNA processing results are accepted here; only the inference from CLIP-motif overlap to selective methyl-mark recognition is marked as over-annotation.

title: Mechanistic View of hnRNPA2 Low-Complexity Domain Structure, Interactions, and Phase Separation Altered by Mutation and Arginine Methylation.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Ryan et al., Mol Cell 69:465-479 (2018). NMR and simulation of the hnRNPA2 low-complexity domain; the IDA source for GO:0140693.

title: Molecular basis for the specific and multivariant recognitions of RNA substrates by human hnRNP A2/B1.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Wu et al., Nat Commun 9:420 (2018), doi 10.1038/s41467-017-02770-z. Crystal structures of the tandem RRMs with several RNA substrates. Independent of and four years earlier than PMID:41662154, and reaching the same conclusion via a different method, which is why the m6A-reader demotion does not rest on a single 2026 paper.

title: Nuclear hnRNPA2B1 initiates and amplifies the innate immune response to DNA viruses.
review_notes: Identifier and title verified against PubMed: Wang, Wen & Cao, Science 365(6454):eaav0758 (2019), doi 10.1126/science.aav0758. Not retracted and carries no notice in the PubMed record as of this review. Marked UNVERIFIED rather than VERIFIED for its central claim: the nuclear DNA-sensor function it reports has been built on by later work (PMID:41134667, PMID:40689679) but I found no independent replication of the core claim, and GOA itself cites this paper only for subcellular localisation, not for any molecular function or biological process. Relevance MEDIUM because only the localisation is used in this review.

title: Nuclear U1 snRNA facilitates the dimerization of hnRNPA2B1 to enhance anti-DNA viral innate immunity.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Zhang et al., Cell Rep 44(11):116462 (2025), doi 10.1016/j.celrep.2025.116462. Cached entry is abstract-only. Cited here only as evidence that the DNA-sensor claim remains an active line of work rather than an abandoned one; it assumes that role rather than testing it, so it is not independent confirmation.

title: Mechanistic studies on HNRNPA2B1 suggest binding but not selective recognition of m(6)A.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Park et al., RNA Biol 23(1):1-28 (2026), doi 10.1080/15476286.2026.2627781. Full text read. MD simulation plus microscale thermophoresis on an RRM1-RRM2 fusion construct. Directly addresses the selectivity implied by GO:1990247. Scope limitation recorded in the annotation review: isolated RRM construct, single GGACU context, no full-length protein and no low-complexity domain.

title: Mutations in DHDPSL are responsible for primary hyperoxaluria type III.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies DHDPSL/HOGA1 mutations as the cause of primary hyperoxaluria type 3 and proposes HOGA1 as the gene encoding 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase.

title: Primary hyperoxaluria type III gene HOGA1 (formerly DHDPSL) as a possible risk factor for idiopathic calcium oxalate urolithiasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports a loss-of-function mechanism for HOGA1 and links HOGA1 variants to oxalate/urolithiasis risk.

title: Structural and biochemical studies of human 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase: implications for hydroxyproline metabolism in primary hyperoxaluria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified full text. Definitive structural and enzymatic characterization of human HOGA1 - retro-aldol cleavage of HOG to pyruvate and glyoxylate, homotetramer (dimer of dimers), catalytic residues Lys196/Tyr168, terminal step of hydroxyproline degradation.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial protein-interaction mapping; source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (STARD7). Not informative for HOGA1's molecular function.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex); source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (USP47). Not informative for molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome map (HuRI); source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (CIMAP1A). Not informative for molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex 3.0); source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (USP47). Not informative for molecular function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; independent proteomic support for mitochondrial localization of HOGA1.

title: HOGA1 tetramer aldol-cleaves 4-OH-2-oxoglutarate (HOG) to glyoxylate and pyruvate
review_notes: Reactome reaction curating the HOGA1-catalyzed HOG cleavage in the mitochondrial matrix.

title: UniProt entry Q86XE5 (HOGA1_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt/Swiss-Prot record; source of function, subunit, subcellular location, transit peptide, active-site, and disease annotations.

title: The multifunctional RNA-binding protein hnRNP A1 is required for processing of miR-18a.
review_notes: PubMed-verified background on hnRNP A1. It establishes that hnRNP A1 acts on pri-miR-18a before Drosha processing. Used only to judge which miRNA-processing step the GOA row should name.

title: A Peptide Encoded by a Putative lncRNA HOXB-AS3 Suppresses Colon Cancer Growth.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Huang et al., Mol Cell 2017;68:171-184). The founding peptide-level study and the source of the hnRNP A1, PKM splicing and miR-18a annotations. Only the abstract is cached (not open access), so the miR-18a assay could not be checked.

title: A micro-peptide encoded by HOXB-AS3 promotes the proliferation and viability of oral squamous cell carcinoma cell lines by directly binding with IGF2BP2 to stabilize c-Myc.
review_notes: Full text read (PMC8358592). Cell-line study in Cal-27 and UM2. Peptide-level attribution rests on ORF re-expression rescuing an shRNA knockdown of the whole transcript. The IGF2BP2 interaction is one co-IP of an overexpressed tagged peptide; "directly binding" and "stabilize" are not tested (no direct-binding assay, no mRNA or protein half-life measurement). The authors note there were no in vivo experiments.

title: A concise review of the regulatory, diagnostic, and prognostic implications of HOXB-AS3 in tumors.
review_notes: Review (J Cancer 2024), full text cached. Useful for separating lncRNA-level from peptide-level work. It summarizes the Mol Cell evidence that the peptide exists (start-codon dependence, specific antibody, mass spectrometry) and states that the ORF is primate-conserved.

title: A Peptide Encoded by lncRNA HOXB-AS3 Promotes Cigarette Smoke-Induced Inflammation in Bronchial Epithelial Cells via EZH2-Mediated H3K27me3 Modification.
review_notes: Full text cached. Concerns a predicted 32-aa ORF product ("HOXB-AS3-32aa"), not shown to be the 53-aa C0HLZ6 chain. Its "expression" was measured by qRT-PCR, and EZH2 interaction rests on a single co-IP. Not used for any annotation.

title: Primary structure deduced from complementary DNA sequence and expression in cultured cells of mammalian 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid dioxygenase. Evidence that the enzyme is a homodimer of identical subunits homologous to rat liver-specific alloantigen F.
review_notes: Foundational cloning/expression paper establishing the human enzyme's catalytic activity and homodimeric structure. Abstract-only in cache but claims are internally consistent and corroborated.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; supports only an incidental exosome localization, not core function.

title: HPD degradation regulated by the TTC36-STK33-PELI1 signaling axis induces tyrosinemia and neurological damage.
review_notes: Full-text verified. Establishes HPD as the key tyrosine-metabolizing enzyme whose loss causes tyrosinemia, and its regulation by TTC36/STK33/ PELI1 (basis for the IPI protein-binding annotations).

title: Functional role of residues involved in substrate binding of human 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase.
review_notes: Kinetic and mutagenesis characterization of the human enzyme's substrate binding and catalysis; directly supports the core dioxygenase activity.

title: HPD is an m(6)A Methyltransferase that Protects Colorectal Cancer Cells from Ferroptotic Cell Death by m(6)A Methylating SLC7A11/GPX4.
review_notes: Full-text verified 2025 experimental study reporting a moonlighting nuclear mRNA m6A methyltransferase activity (recombinant protein, mutagenesis, KO mouse). The activity is genuinely reported but unusual for an iron dioxygenase and is flagged with a CAUTION note by UniProt; treated as a non-core secondary function, not HPD's defining activity.

title: Structure of the human 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid dioxygenase gene (HPD).
review_notes: Gene-structure characterization; supports the TAS tyrosine-catabolic-process annotation.

title: HPD dioxygenates HPP
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing HPD dioxygenation of HPP in the cytosol; supports the core molecular function and cytosolic location.

title: The 2.0 A structure of human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase in complex with a transition-state analog inhibitor.
review_notes: Structure of human HGPRT with transition-state analog and Mg2+-PPi; directly supports magnesium ion binding and catalytic mechanism.

title: The crystal structure of free human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase reveals extensive conformational plasticity throughout the catalytic cycle.
review_notes: Apoenzyme structure; describes movement of subunits within the tetramer, supporting the homotetramer annotation.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome; supports only a bare protein binding annotation, uninformative for HPRT1 function.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: Systematic HT-Y2H framework paper; underlies a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Inhibition of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase by acyclic nucleoside phosphonates: a new class of antimalarial therapeutics.
review_notes: Abstract foregrounds the P. falciparum enzyme but explicitly assays the corresponding human HGPRT (Ki values) and reports structures of human HGPRT; a UniProt EC 2.4.2.8 evidence source for HPRT1 catalytic activity.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: HT mass-spec detection of HPRT1 in B-cell exosome proteome; a sighting, not functional localization.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HT interactome map; supports bare protein binding and self-interaction (identical protein binding) annotations.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: HT variant/interaction pipeline; supports a self-interaction (identical protein binding) annotation consistent with the homotetramer.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: HT interactome perturbation study; supports a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: HT variant-interaction study; supports bare protein binding and self-interaction annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HT binary interactome reference map (HuRI); supports bare protein binding and self-interaction annotations.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: HT interactome of neurodegenerative disease proteins; supports a bare protein binding annotation (incl. HTT).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS interactome; supports a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT): purification and properties.
review_notes: Classic purification/biochemical characterization of the human enzyme; supports guanine PRT activity and GMP salvage (abstract-only in cache; curator read full text).

title: Isolation and characterization of a full-length expressible cDNA for human hypoxanthine phosphoribosyl transferase.
review_notes: Cloned human HPRT cDNA expresses functional enzyme activity (HAT selection); supports hypoxanthine PRT activity and cytoplasmic localization.

title: The crystal structure of human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase with bound GMP.
review_notes: Structure with bound GMP; Lys165 confers specificity for guanine and hypoxanthine over adenine (argues against AMP salvage).

title: Dopamine transporters are markedly reduced in Lesch-Nyhan disease in vivo.
review_notes: Documents reduced striatal DA transporters in LND patients (a downstream disease phenotype); does not establish an HPRT1 molecular function of regulating dopamine metabolism. Underlies an over-annotated GO:0045964 annotation.

title: Catalysis in human hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase: Asp 137 acts as a general acid/base.
review_notes: Mechanistic study of human HGPRTase; states the enzyme catalyzes reversible IMP/GMP formation from hypoxanthine/guanine and PRPP.

title: Purine metabolism in female heterozygotes for hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase deficiency.
review_notes: Carrier study; reduced HPRT activity causes purine overproduction and elevated hypoxanthine/xanthine excretion, evidencing the salvage role.

title: The N-terminal anchor sequences of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases determine their orientation in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.
review_notes: Establishes ER-membrane localization and single-pass type II topology with lumen-facing catalytic domain; also reports enzymatic activity. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Appropriate function of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 in the endoplasmic reticulum lumen is dependent on its N-terminal region sharing similar topological determinants with 50-kDa esterase.
review_notes: Supports pre-receptor glucocorticoid function, ER-lumen orientation dependence of activity, and 7-ketocholesterol metabolism. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Conformational flexibility in crystal structures of human 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type I provide insights into glucocorticoid interconversion and enzyme regulation.
review_notes: Crystal structures establishing cortisone/cortisol interconversion, oligomerization motif, and adipose-tissue disease relevance. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Adamantane sulfone and sulfonamide 11-beta-HSD1 Inhibitors.
review_notes: Inhibitor study confirming 11beta-HSD1 activity in liver, fat and brain. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The discovery of 2-anilinothiazolones as 11beta-HSD1 inhibitors.
review_notes: Inhibitor/X-ray co-crystal study confirming enzymatic activity and structure. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Structural characterization and pharmacodynamic effects of an orally active 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 inhibitor.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Pyridine amides as potent and selective inhibitors of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Discovery of novel, potent benzamide inhibitors of 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11beta-HSD1) exhibiting oral activity in an enzyme inhibition ex vivo model.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Discovery and optimization of piperidyl benzamide derivatives as a novel class of 11beta-HSD1 inhibitors.
review_notes: Structural inhibitor study; supports homodimeric assembly. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane-proteome MS screen; source of the generic 'membrane' HDA annotation, not targeted localization evidence.

title: UniProtKB entry P28845 (DHI1_HUMAN), 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 1
review_notes: Curated UniProtKB record; source of catalytic-activity, subunit, subcellular location and function statements used as file-quote support.

title: Hypertension in the syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess due to mutation of the 11 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified case report of an AME kindred with an R374X truncating mutation showing severely attenuated NAD-dependent 11beta-HSD activity; directly supports the enzyme's NAD+-dependent 11beta-HSD activity and its role in cortisol metabolism and mineralocorticoid receptor specificity.

title: Intrinsic alcohol dehydrogenase and hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activities of human mitochondrial short-chain L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Kinetic characterization showing the alcohol/hydroxysteroid activities are orders of magnitude weaker than the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA activity, supporting non-core status of the steroid/ADH side activities.

title: Expanded substrate screenings of human and Drosophila type 10 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases (HSDs) reveal multiple specificities in bile acid and steroid hormone metabolism: characterization of multifunctional 3alpha/7alpha/7beta/17beta/20beta/21-HSD.
review_notes: Definitive substrate screen and mitochondrial localization; source of most steroid and bile-acid MF/BP annotations (in-vitro, non-core).

title: RNase P without RNA: identification and functional reconstitution of the human mitochondrial tRNA processing enzyme.
review_notes: Identified HSD17B10/MRPP2 as an essential subunit of the protein-only mitochondrial RNase P; foundational for the tRNA-processing core function.

title: Study of patients and carriers with 2-methyl-3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase (MHBD) deficiency: difficulties in the diagnosis.
review_notes: Patient/carrier study of MHBD deficiency supporting the isoleucine-catabolism role.

title: Mental retardation linked to mutations in the HSD17B10 gene interfering with neurosteroid and isoleucine metabolism.
review_notes: Links disease mutations to loss of both MHBD (isoleucine) and allopregnanolone (neurosteroid) oxidation; source of the brexanolone metabolic process annotation.

title: A non-enzymatic function of 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 10 is required for mitochondrial integrity and cell survival.
review_notes: Key evidence that disease severity is independent of enzymatic activity and driven by an essential non-enzymatic mitochondrial-integrity function; also the 1.2 A crystal structure.

title: Involvement of human ELAC2 gene product in 3' end processing of mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: ELAC2 mitochondrial 3'-processing study; source of a NAS mitochondrion localization for HSD17B10 in the context of the tRNA-processing machinery.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Global mRNA-interactome capture screen; source of the non-specific HDA "RNA binding" annotation, marked over-annotated (the relevant ligand is tRNA).

title: A subcomplex of human mitochondrial RNase P is a bifunctional methyltransferase--extensive moonlighting in mitochondrial tRNA biogenesis.
review_notes: Establishes the MRPP1-MRPP2 subcomplex as the m1A9/m1G9 methyltransferase requiring HSD17B10 as a non-catalytic partner.

title: Mutation or knock-down of 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 10 cause loss of MRPP1 and impaired processing of mitochondrial heavy strand transcripts.
review_notes: Shows HSD17B10 maintains MRPP1 levels and that its loss impairs heavy-strand mitochondrial tRNA processing; disease-relevant.

title: Initial steps in RNA processing and ribosome assembly occur at mitochondrial DNA nucleoids.
review_notes: Localizes RNase P/ELAC2 to mtDNA nucleoids; supports the mitochondrial-nucleoid localization annotation.
