title: Mitochondrial energy failure in HSD10 disease is due to defective mtDNA transcript processing.
review_notes: Supports that HSD10 disease pathology stems from defective mtDNA transcript (tRNA) processing rather than the metabolic defect. Cited in notes; not an existing GOA annotation source.

title: Molecular insights into HSD10 disease: impact of SDR5C1 mutations on the human mitochondrial RNase P complex.
review_notes: Shows disease mutations impair dehydrogenation, tRNA processing, methylation, homotetramerization and TRMT10C interaction; source of several core annotations.

title: Myxococcus CsgA, Drosophila Sniffer, and human HSD10 are cardiolipin phospholipases.
review_notes: Establishes the cardiolipin phospholipase C-like (cardiolipin dehydrogenase) activity, inhibited by Aβ; a distinct in-vitro moonlighting activity (non-core).

title: A novel HSD17B10 mutation impairing the activities of the mitochondrial RNase P complex causes X-linked intractable epilepsy and neurodevelopmental regression.
review_notes: K212E patient mutation impairing SDR5C1-dependent RNase P activities; source of an EXP dehydrogenase annotation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding (TRMT10C) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Novel patient missense mutations in the HSD17B10 gene affect dehydrogenase and mitochondrial tRNA modification functions of the encoded protein.
review_notes: V12L/V176M patient mutations reduce dehydrogenase, methyltransferase and tRNA processing; clean statement of the dual catalytic/non-catalytic functions.

title: The MRPP1/MRPP2 complex is a tRNA-maturation platform in human mitochondria.
review_notes: Shows MRPP1/2 retains tRNA after 5'-cleavage, enhances ELAC2 3'-processing and presents tRNA to the CCA-adding enzyme; source of tRNA-binding and processing annotations.

title: A Map of Human Mitochondrial Protein Interactions Linked to Neurodegeneration Reveals New Mechanisms of Redox Homeostasis and NF-κB Signaling.
review_notes: Mitochondrial interactome map; source of bare protein-binding IPIs (EEF2, TRAP1) of unclear functional significance, marked over-annotated.

title: Structural insight into the human mitochondrial tRNA purine N1-methyltransferase and ribonuclease P complexes.
review_notes: Structural study of the MRPP1/MRPP2 and RNase P complexes; source of RNase P complex, mitochondrion and 5'-processing annotations.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome; source of a bare protein-binding (APP/Aβ) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Study of Biomolecular Interactions of Mitochondrial Proteins Related to Alzheimer's Disease: Toward Multi-Interaction Biomolecular Processes.
review_notes: Alzheimer-related mitochondrial interaction study; source of a bare protein-binding (Aβ peptide) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; source of a bare protein-binding (TRMT10C) IPI, marked over-annotated.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrion localization.

title: Structural basis for human mitochondrial tRNA maturation.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the four mt-tRNA maturation steps; supports the maturation-platform, CCA-addition and catalytic-complex annotations.

title: Structural basis of 3'-tRNA maturation by the human mitochondrial RNase Z complex.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the mitochondrial RNase Z (ELAC2/SDR5C1/TRMT10C) complex; supports the 3'-processing and endoribonuclease-complex annotations.

title: An intracellular protein that binds amyloid-beta peptide and mediates neurotoxicity in Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: The original ERAB/Aβ discovery paper. Establishes the Aβ (APP) interaction, but its cytoplasm/plasma-membrane/ER localization and bile-acid TAS assignments are legacy mis-assignments superseded by later mitochondrial-matrix work.

title: A human brain L-3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase is identical to an amyloid beta-peptide-binding protein involved in Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: Cloning and biochemical characterization establishing the core NAD+-dependent (3S)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity; identical to ERAB.

title: Identification of two mammalian reductases involved in the two-carbon fatty acyl elongation cascade.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available:false); PubMed-verified. Basis for the core KAR molecular function and ER membrane localization; full text read by the original EXP/IDA curators.

title: Characterization of type 12 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, an isoform of type 3 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase responsible for estradiol formation in women.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; PubMed-verified. Documents a real in-vitro steroid (estradiol dehydrogenase) activity, treated here as non-core because the physiological substrate is fatty-acyl-CoA.

title: ELOVL1 production of C24 acyl-CoAs is linked to C24 sphingolipid synthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache and abstract does not name KAR/HSD17B12; the ELOVL1/LASS2 interaction is a UniProt SUBUNIT assertion (full text read by curators). Supports the fatty acid elongase complex annotation.

title: Elucidating novel hepatitis C virus-host interactions using combined mass spectrometry and functional genomics approaches.
review_notes: High-throughput HCV host-factor screen; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (HCV protein partner). No bearing on HSD17B12 biochemical function.

title: Two modes of regulation of the fatty acid elongase ELOVL6 by the 3-ketoacyl-CoA reductase KAR in the fatty acid elongation cycle.
review_notes: Full text available; verified. Direct source for the IDA KAR activity, fatty acid elongation process, and fatty acid elongase complex annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (UBQLN1).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (UBQLN1 isoform).

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome; source of bare protein-binding IPIs (HRAS, GSN, FGFR3, CHAT, UBQLN1). No functional content for HSD17B12.

title: Physical and functional interactome atlas of human receptor tyrosine kinases.
review_notes: RTK interactome atlas; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (FGFR3).

title: HSD17B3,12 hydrogenates 3OOD-CoA to 3HODC-CoA
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing HSD17B12 at the KAR reduction step in the ER; supports the ER membrane localization annotation.

title: Synthesis of very long-chain fatty acyl-CoAs
review_notes: Reactome pathway for VLCFA-CoA synthesis; supports the long-chain fatty-acyl-CoA biosynthetic process annotation.

title: Biochemical analyses and molecular modeling explain the functional loss of 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 mutant G133R in three Tunisian patients with 46, XY Disorders of Sex Development.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Directly measures wild-type 17beta-HSD3 androstenedione-> testosterone conversion and ER localization in HEK-293 cells; basis for the IDA MF and ER-localization annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Source of a generic IPI protein-binding annotation (interactor NCS1/P62166); uninformative for molecular function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome (BioPlex 3.0). Source of a second generic IPI protein-binding annotation (interactor NCS1/P62166); uninformative for molecular function.

title: Male pseudohermaphroditism caused by mutations of testicular 17 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Landmark paper identifying HSD17B3, its testis-predominant expression, NADPH cofactor use, and disease-causing mutations; basis for the MF, testis tissue, disease, and male-genitalia-development annotations.

title: UniProtKB entry P37058 (DHB3_HUMAN), 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source for catalytic activity (RHEA:14981/EC 1.1.1.64 testosterone/androstenedione; RHEA:24616/EC 1.1.1.62 estradiol/estrone), NADPH cofactor use, ER subcellular location, testis tissue specificity, and the 46,XY DSD disease association.

title: Enoyl-CoA hydratase deficiency: identification of a new type of D-bifunctional protein deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Defines an isolated hydratase-domain deficiency of DBP (Asn457Tyr) and states DBP's role in beta-oxidation of VLCFA, branched-chain and bile-acid intermediates.

title: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation disorders and 58 kDa sterol carrier protein X (SCPx). Activity measurements in liver and fibroblasts using a newly developed method.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Uses recombinant human D-bifunctional protein to generate the bile-acid enoyl-CoA substrate; supports DBP hydratase/dehydrogenase activity on bile-acid intermediates. Primary focus is SCPx, so relevance is medium.

title: Identification of the peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of docosahexaenoic acid.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows DBP is among the main enzymes in the peroxisomal beta-oxidation of C24:6n-3 to DHA (C22:6n-3). Cited by UniProt for the PUFA/DHA function; supports the DHA-synthesis role.

title: Identification of the peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzymes involved in the degradation of long-chain dicarboxylic acids.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Direct enzyme measurements with recombinant human DBP; identifies DBP as one of the main enzymes in peroxisomal beta-oxidation of C16 dicarboxylic acid.

title: Peroxisomal branched chain fatty acid beta-oxidation pathway is upregulated in prostate cancer.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows DBP is upregulated with increased activity in prostate cancer; supports peroxisomal localization/activity. Physiological/disease context rather than core mechanism.

title: Crystal structure of 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase 2 from human peroxisomal multifunctional enzyme type 2.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Crystal structure of the human MFE-2 hydratase-2 domain; explains accommodation of bulky C26, pristanic and DHCA/THCA CoA esters and supports homodimerization.

title: Differential expression profiling of membrane proteins by quantitative proteomics in a human mesenchymal stem cell line undergoing osteoblast differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. High-throughput membrane-proteomics screen; DBP detected as a differentially expressed protein. Basis of the osteoblast-differentiation and membrane annotations, both of which are over-annotations (expression change / co-fractionation).

title: PEX14 is required for microtubule-based peroxisome motility in human cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Study of PEX14 and peroxisome motility, not HSD17B4; DBP appears only as a co-purified peroxisomal-membrane-preparation protein. Basis of an over-annotated peroxisomal-membrane location.

title: Molecular cloning of a novel widely expressed human 80 kDa 17 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase IV.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Original cloning of the 736-aa protein as 17-beta-HSD IV; reports a unidirectional oxidative 17-beta-HSD activity. Source of the steroid-activity annotations, which are in-vitro side activities relative to the enzyme's physiological fatty-acid role.

title: Structure of D-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydratase/D-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase bifunctional protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Shows the full-length human enzyme is bifunctional (dehydratase + dehydrogenase), a truncated C-terminal fragment retains only dehydratase, and the native enzyme is a homodimer; cDNA identical to 17-beta-HSD IV. Directly supports both core MFs.

title: Peroxisomal D-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: resolution of the enzyme defect and its molecular basis in bifunctional protein deficiency.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC19272). First case of DBP deficiency; Gly16Ser in the NAD+-binding loop abolishes the dehydrogenase activity while hydratase activity is normal; DBP is essential and non-redundant, and likely the main VLCFA beta-oxidation enzyme.

title: Structure and expression of a new complementary DNA encoding the almost exclusive 3 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/delta 5-delta 4-isomerase in human adrenals and gonads.
review_notes: Original type-II 3beta-HSD cloning and kinetic characterization; PubMed-verified. Directly establishes the bifunctional dehydrogenase/isomerase activity and the adrenal/gonad-specific expression of HSD3B2.

title: A novel missense mutation in the HSD3B2 gene, underlying nonsalt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia. new insight into the structure-function relationships of 3β-hydroxysteroid dehidrogenase type II.
review_notes: Functional study of the G250V CAH variant; PubMed-verified. Supports the bifunctional NAD+-dependent activity, the ER-membrane localization, and the steroid/androgen biosynthetic role of HSD3B2.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale neurodegenerative-disease yeast two-hybrid interactome; PubMed-verified. Source of the IntAct "protein binding" IPIs (GLE1, SPRED1) but does not inform the steroidogenic function of HSD3B2.

title: The bile acid synthetic gene 3beta-hydroxy-Delta(5)-C(27)-steroid oxidoreductase is mutated in progressive intrahepatic cholestasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified defining paper; expression cloning shows the C27 3beta-HSD acts on four 7-alpha-hydroxylated sterols, does not metabolize C19/21 steroids, and that loss of activity causes neonatal cholestasis. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available false); quotes taken verbatim from the abstract.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map (HuRI/CCSB); source of bare protein-binding IPI. Correctly cited but uninformative for HSD3B7's molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; source of numerous bare protein-binding IPIs. Correctly cited but uninformative for HSD3B7's molecular function.

title: A family of ubiquitin-like proteins binds the ATPase domain of Hsp70-like Stch.
review_notes: Primary abstract checked. GO:0032182 denotes small conjugating ubiquitin-like proteins; binding to ubiquilin/BAG6-like proteins through a different region does not establish that activity.

title: Differential Effects of STCH and Stress-Inducible Hsp70 on the Stability and Maturation of NKCC2.
review_notes: Full text read; human STCH was screened with murine NKCC2 in a heterologous system. Client degradation does not refute all chaperone mechanisms.

title: Heat shock protein Hspa13 regulates endoplasmic reticulum and cytosolic proteostasis through modulation of protein translocation.
review_notes: Full text read; overexpression/ATPase-mutant and knockout phenotypes are distinguished. Cytosolic TTR accumulation is not cytosolic HSPA13 localization.

title: Stch encodes the 'ATPase core' of a microsomal stress 70 protein.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_8131751.md title matches; also anchored to GOA (TAS, GO:0043231). The defining characterization of STCH/HSPA13 as a microsomal HSP70 with peptide-independent ATPase activity and a truncated substrate-binding domain; supports core_function GO:0016887. (Gene is poorly characterized overall, but this paper is directly on-target.)

title: GOA annotation export for HSPA13
review_notes: Local GOA export row directly identifies the contested GO:0044183 IBA source for HSPA13.

title: OpenScientist focused review of HSPA13 secondary localization, 2026-09-21
review_notes: Focused localization audit evaluated on 2026-10-05. The nucleus, plasma-membrane and cytosol critiques are incorporated as over-annotation calls; cytosol is kept softer than hard removal because PMID:10675567 leaves an unresolved cytosol-facing topology question.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis investigation - HSPA13 protein folding chaperone
review_notes: Structural divergence is supported. Its universal impossibility/refutation language goes beyond the GO definition and assays; promoting degradation does not generally exclude a chaperone role, and positive ER localization is nonexclusive. The recent papers were read independently.

title: The chaperones MPP11 and Hsp70L1 form the mammalian ribosome-associated complex.
review_notes: Full primary mRAC purification, complex assembly, localization and yeast complementation read. Supports the folding complex but does not directly demonstrate a DNAJC2-stimulated HSPA14 ATPase cycle.

title: The diverse members of the mammalian HSP70 machine show distinct chaperone-like activities.
review_notes: Abstract verified; author accepted manuscript located but body font extraction/figure reading could not resolve the HSPA14-specific refolding result. Cytosolic source annotation retained; focused adjudication requests exact Figure4/5 assays.

title: The chaperone network connected to human ribosome-associated complex.
review_notes: Full Methods, Results and Discussion read. Direct human Hsp70L1 nucleotide-binding and mRAC ATP-turnover assays; hydrolysis explicitly inconclusive. Separate Hsp70 is stimulated by the complex; ATP binding is required but hydrolysis dispensable in heterologous complementation.

title: Intracellular HSP70L1 inhibits human dendritic cell maturation by promoting suppressive H3K27me3 and H2AK119Ub1 histone modifications.
review_notes: Full text cached and primary claims checked; supports a distinct dendritic-cell intracellular chromatin lead with nuclear HSP70L1, but whether the chromatin effect is a direct HSPA14 function remains a separate curation question.

title: OpenScientist focused review of HSPA14 ATPase, refolding and secondary compartments, 2026-09-21
review_notes: Focused report evaluated on 2026-10-05. Its ATPase, refolding and plasma-membrane critiques are incorporated. The report's stronger ATPase removal call is recorded as over-annotation because direct human hydrolysis remains weak and inconclusive rather than directly disproved.

title: UniProt entry Q0VDF9 (HSP7E_HUMAN), Heat shock 70 kDa protein 14 / HSP70L1
review_notes: The record correctly identifies mRAC and cytosolic location, but its statement that DNAJC2 stimulates HSPA14 ATPase is not established by full PMID:21245388. Direct nascent-chain contact by HSPA14 is also proposed rather than resolved.

title: OpenScientist SSZ1 ATPase adjudication (comparative scope)
review_notes: Actual report read for homolog coverage. It explicitly calls HSPA14 activity untested and omits PMID:21245388, which performed the inconclusive near-background assay; it cannot adjudicate the human target. No direct transfer of fungal ATPase loss is made.

title: Structural basis for the cooperation of Hsp70 and Hsp110 chaperones in protein folding.
review_notes: Crystal structure (PDB 3D2E/3D2F) of the ATP-bound Hsp110 NEF (yeast Sse1p) embracing the Hsp70 nucleotide-binding domain, defining how Hsp110 drives ADP release and nucleotide exchange on Hsp70 during chaperone-assisted folding.

title: Characterization of the Cardiac Overexpression of HSPB2 Reveals Mitochondrial and Myogenic Roles Supported by a Cardiac HspB2 Interactome.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_26465331.md title matches; anchored to GOA as an IPI protein-binding source. Provides the validated GAPDH client and cardiac/mitochondrial interactome supporting the holdase core function. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: MKBP, a novel member of the small heat shock protein family, binds and activates the myotonic dystrophy protein kinase.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_9490724.md title matches; anchored to GOA as the TAS source for GO:0008047 (enzyme activator activity) and GO:0005829 (cytosol). Directly establishes the HSPB2/MKBP DMPK-binding-and-activation core function. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: Mutant small heat shock protein B3 causes motor neuropathy: utility of a candidate gene approach.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_20142617.md title matches and confirms the dominant HSPB3 R7S variant causing distal hereditary motor neuronopathy (HMND4); establishes the in vivo physiological importance of HSPB3 chaperone function. Not GOA-anchored but cached content is on-target.

title: Terminal Regions Confer Plasticity to the Tetrameric Assembly of Human HspB2 and HspB3.
review_notes: Cached full-text (publications/PMID_29969581.md) confirms the crystal structure (PDB 6F2R) of the full-length human HspB2/HspB3 hetero-tetramer (3:1), directly establishing the HspB2-HspB3 hetero-oligomeric assembly and supporting the cytoprotective sHSP chaperone function.

title: HspB3, the most deviating of the six known human small heat shock proteins.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_9858786.md title matches; anchored to GOA as a TAS source for GO:0006986 (response to unfolded protein). The defining characterization of HspB3 as a divergent small HSP (HSP20 family); supports the core sHSP holdase/proteostasis function. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: Falcon deep research report for HSPB3
review_notes: LLM (Edison/Falcon) synthesis. CROSS-CHECKABLE claims that agree with independently verified sources: (i) HSPB3 is the divergent sHSP with a unique N-terminal region and essentially no canonical C-terminal extension (matches cached PMID:9858786 and UniProt); (ii) HSPB3 forms an obligate hetero-oligomer with HSPB2, a 3:1 HSPB2:HSPB3 heterotetramer in which four ACDs form a flattened tetrahedron (matches cached full-text PMID:29969581 / PDB 6F2R); (iii) disease-associated R7S variant in the N-terminus (matches cached PMID:20142617, UniProt HMND4). SPECULATIVE or PARALOG-GENERALIZED claims NOT independently verified here and treated cautiously: the LBR-substrate / lamin-B-receptor / MYOD-driven myogenesis / LBR-LMNA tether-switch narrative and the R116P variant all derive from a single un-cached preprint (tiago2021/cam.69495) plus reviews and are NOT in the publications cache (so cited PMIDs could not be checked against full text); the 'moderate/selective chaperone activity', mitochondrial-exclusion, and BAG3-pathway statements are review-level and partly generalized from HSPB1/HSPB4/HSPB5/HSPB8. Marked UNVERIFIED overall because the primary papers underpinning the novel HSPB3-specific functional claims are not in the cache and the source is an LLM synthesis.

title: Identification and characterization of cvHsp. A novel human small stress protein selectively expressed in cardiovascular and insulin-sensitive tissues.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_10593960.md title matches; anchored to GOA as a TAS source for GO:0006986 (response to unfolded protein) and GO:0008016 (regulation of heart contraction). Identifies cvHsp/HSPB7 and its alpha-filamin binding, supporting core_function GO:0031005 (filamin binding). Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: HSPB7 is a SC35 speckle resident small heat shock protein.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_19464326.md title matches; anchored to GOA as the IDA source for GO:0005634 (nucleus) and GO:0005737 (cytoplasm). Shows HSPB7 does not support substrate refolding, which argues against GO:0044183 (protein folding chaperone) but does not by itself establish GO:0140309 (unfolded protein holdase activity).

title: HSPB7 is the most potent polyQ aggregation suppressor within the HSPB family of molecular chaperones.
review_notes: The cached abstract directly reports HSPB7-dependent suppression of polyQ aggregation and toxicity, while also confirming that HSPB7 does not improve refolding of heat-denatured luciferase. It supports substrate-selective antiaggregation but not GO:0044183 protein folding chaperone activity.

title: The N terminus of the small heat shock protein HSPB7 drives its polyQ aggregation-suppressing activity.
review_notes: Full text is cached. Recombinant HSPB7 directly delays polyQ aggregation, and HSPB7 binds early profibrillar/polyQ species through its N-terminal domain. These experiments establish substrate-selective antiaggregation activity but do not demonstrate escort to an acceptor or location as required by GO:0140309; they remain inconsistent with GO:0044183 protein folding chaperone activity.

title: Some properties of human small heat shock protein Hsp22 (H11 or HspB8).
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_14985082.md title matches; the cached Results establish ATP-independent holdase activity (suppresses heat aggregation of ADH and rhodanese), supporting the holdase core function. Notably the same paper reports negligible kinase activity, which contradicts the GOA IDA GO:0004672 (protein kinase activity) tied to this PMID - a likely over-annotation. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: HspB8 chaperone activity toward poly(Q)-containing proteins depends on its association with Bag3, a stimulator of macroautophagy.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_18006506.md title matches; richly anchored in GOA as the source for GO:1905337 (positive regulation of aggrephagy, IMP), GO:0034620 (cellular response to unfolded protein, IMP), GO:0101031 (protein folding chaperone complex, IDA) and GO:0042803 (homodimerization). Establishes the HSPB8-BAG3 CASA/aggrephagy core function. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: Chaperone-assisted selective autophagy is essential for muscle maintenance.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_20060297.md title matches and confirms HSPB8 as a small-HSP component of the BAG3/HSPA8/CHIP chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA) machinery degrading damaged Z-disk filamin in muscle; supports the CASA/aggrephagy core function. Not directly GOA-anchored for HSPB8 but cached content is on-target.

title: Characterization of two novel human small heat shock proteins: protein kinase-related HspB8 and testis-specific HspB9.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_11470154.md title matches; the original identification establishing HSPB9 as a rapidly-evolving, testis-restricted small HSP expressed in spermatogenic cells. Foundational for the gene's spermatogenesis-associated identity, though chaperone activity is inferred not demonstrated. Not GOA-anchored for HSPB9 but cached content is on-target.

title: Testis-specific human small heat shock protein HSPB9 is a cancer/testis antigen, and potentially interacts with the dynein subunit TCTEL1.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_15503857.md title matches; anchored to GOA as the IPI protein-binding source. Provides the only experimental molecular interaction for this poorly characterized paralog (HSPB9-TCTEL1/DYNLT1), supporting core_function GO:0045503 (dynein light chain binding). Title notes the interaction is 'potential', so the evidence is suggestive rather than definitive. Cited in core_functions supported_by.

title: Falcon deep research report for HSPB9
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon) built from family-level reviews (Tedesco 2022, Vos 2008, Sun 2005, Gu 2023). SAFE, directly-citable claims used here: (1) HSPB9 carries the conserved alpha-crystallin/HSP20 domain placing it in the ATP-independent sHSP chaperone family; (2) HSPB9 lacks a canonical NLS, so nuclear entry may depend on binding partners; (3) the TCTEL1/DYNLT1 interaction is reported to occur via the HSPB9 C-terminus; (4) HSPB9 is among the least functionally characterized HSPBs and direct experimental evidence for its chaperone activity/substrates is lacking. SPECULATIVE / paralog-generalized claims NOT imported into annotations: that HSPB9 itself performs holdase/anti-aggregation activity, forms regulatory oligomers, or participates in CASA/apoptosis/cytoskeletal roles (these are HSPB1/5/8 functions, not evidenced for HSPB9); and any specific spermatogenesis transport mechanism, which the report itself flags as hypothetical. Underlying primary refs not independently re-verified here, hence UNVERIFIED.

title: OpenScientist report on HSPB9 small-HSP holdase activity
review_notes: Focused hypothesis review that corroborates the current conservative boundary: HSPB9 is an alpha-crystallin-domain small-HSP-family member, but ATP-independent holdase or generic unfolded-protein-binding activity should remain unassigned until direct HSPB9 assays exist.

title: HYPK, a Huntingtin interacting protein, reduces aggregates and apoptosis induced by N-terminal Huntingtin with 40 glutamines in Neuro2a cells and exhibits chaperone-like activity.
review_notes: Cached publications/PMID_17947297.md title matches; richly anchored in GOA as the IDA source for GO:0050821 (protein stabilization), GO:0043066 (negative regulation of apoptotic process), GO:0032991 (protein-containing complex) and the cytoplasm/nucleus localizations. Establishes the HYPK chaperone-like anti-polyQ-aggregation core function.

title: Huntingtin interacting protein HYPK is intrinsically unstructured.
review_notes: Not cached, but anchored to GOA: this PMID is the EXP/IDA source for GO:0044183 (protein folding chaperone) for HYPK, consistent with the title. Directly supports the intrinsically-disordered-chaperone core function.

title: The chaperone-like protein HYPK acts together with NatA in cotranslational N-terminal acetylation and prevention of Huntingtin aggregation.
review_notes: Not cached, but anchored to GOA: this PMID is the EXP source for the cytoplasm (GO:0005737) and nucleus (GO:0005634) localizations of HYPK, consistent with the title. Establishes the HYPK-NatA (NAA10/NAA15) complex that underpins the acetyltransferase-modulating core function.

title: Human-chromatin-related protein interactions identify a demethylase complex required for chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Large AP-MS interactome (Marcon et al.) that is the GOA IPI source for an HYPK interaction; relevant only as a network/interaction record, not a functional characterization. Title corrected to verbatim PubMed (the prior title was a fabricated description).

title: Falcon deep research report for HYPK
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) report; not independently verified, so marked UNVERIFIED. HYPK-specific, well-anchored claims it surfaces: (i) HYPK is a non-catalytic regulator of the human NatA (NAA10-NAA15) complex that stabilizes the complex and allosterically inhibits NAA10 (citing Klein et al. 2024 Nat Commun and Deng & Marmorstein 2021); (ii) HYPK is ribosome/polysome-associated near the exit tunnel together with NatA, NAC and MAP1/MAP2 (Klein 2024; Lentzsch 2024); and (iii) a distinct, HYPK-specific role as a selective autophagy receptor for polyneddylated cargo via a C-terminal UBA domain (NEDD8 binding) and an atypical N-terminal LIR (Y49AEE52, LC3/GABARAP binding), citing the HYPK-specific primary paper Ghosh & Ranjan 2022 Autophagy (PMID:34320889). CAUTION: the report at points over-generalizes NAC-complex and general co-translational-processing functions onto HYPK, and over-reads the huntingtin connection (HYPK was named for HTT interaction; the polyQ anti-aggregation/NEDD8-aggrephagy links are HYPK-specific but the broader Huntington's disease relevance is inferential). The autophagy-receptor and NatA-allosteric-inhibition mechanisms are not yet captured by GOA annotations and are flagged for expert follow-up rather than used to add or remove annotations here.

title: Activation of integrin alpha(V)beta(3) regulates cell adhesion and migration to bone sialoprotein.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Direct adhesion and migration assays establish BSP as an alpha-V/beta-3 ligand.

title: Factor H binding to bone sialoprotein and osteopontin enables tumor cell evasion of complement-mediated attack.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The paper directly supports integrin binding, factor-H recruitment, and a context-specific complement- evasion process.

title: Structural characterization of human recombinant and bone-derived bone sialoprotein. Functional implications for cell attachment and hydroxyapatite binding.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This is the most direct human- protein evidence for hydroxyapatite binding, cell attachment, structure, and post-translational modification.

title: Differential expression profiling of membrane proteins by quantitative proteomics in a human mesenchymal stem cell line undergoing osteoblast differentiation.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked, but the full text and IBSP- specific quantitative result were unavailable. The experimental HDA annotations are therefore left undecided rather than overruled.

title: Expression of bone sialoprotein (BSP) in developing human tissues.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Human immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization directly establish developmental cell and matrix context.

title: Matrix vesicles are carriers of bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and noncollagenous matrix proteins.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This is the direct rat evidence underlying the orthology-transferred vesicle annotation; extracellular vesicle is the more informative human replacement.

title: Structure-activity relationship of human bone sialoprotein peptides.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and the open-access full text were checked. The study directly supports integrin-dependent cell attachment but does not assay a generic structural-molecule activity.

title: Skeletal development of mice lacking bone sialoprotein (BSP)--impairment of long bone growth and progressive establishment of high trabecular bone mass.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Mouse knockout supplies causal conserved support for the human IBA bone-mineralization and matrix roles.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. HuRI reports IBSP-FAM9B and IBSP-FXYD3 screening interactions, but no endogenous mechanism is established and generic protein binding is uninformative.

title: A molecular interactome of the glioblastoma perivascular niche reveals integrin binding sialoprotein as a mediator of tumor cell migration.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. The work directly supports a disease-context positive effect on cell migration.

title: MatrisomeDB 2.0: 2023 updates to the ECM-protein knowledge database.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. The database classification supports the noncollagenous interstitial-matrix component annotation.

title: Characterization of native and recombinant bone sialoprotein: delineation of the mineral-binding and cell adhesion domains and structural analysis of the RGD domain.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Direct biochemical and cell- attachment experiments establish mineral binding and integrin-dependent adhesion; full text was unavailable locally.

title: Interaction of integrin alphaVbeta3 with IPSP (Bone sialoprotein 2)
review_notes: The cached Reactome event was checked. Despite the IPSP display-name typo, the event explicitly models human IBSP binding extracellular alpha-V/beta-3.

title: Manual literature synthesis for human IBSP (P21815)
review_notes: Manual synthesis prepared after both configured research providers failed; claims are anchored to reviewed records and primary studies.

title: Manual literature and annotation review notes for human IBSP
review_notes: Manual review journal integrating GOA, QuickGO, UniProt, Reactome, and primary publications, including explicit uncertainty boundaries.

title: UniProtKB record for human IBSP (P21815)
review_notes: The reviewed UniProt record was checked directly for sequence, processing, localization, modifications, tissue expression, and primary provenance.

title: The carboxyl methyltransferase modifying G proteins is a metalloenzyme.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; PubMed-verified. Supports the core methyltransferase activity (GO:0004671) and the metalloenzyme character used in Reactome (ICMT:Zn2+).

title: Topology of mammalian isoprenylcysteine carboxyl methyltransferase determined in live cells with a fluorescent probe.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; PubMed-verified. Supports core ER membrane localization (GO:0005789) and multi-pass topology.

title: Regulation of NOTCH signaling by RAB7 and RAB8 requires carboxyl methylation by ICMT.
review_notes: Full text available; supports core methyltransferase activity (GO:0004671) and extends substrate range to RAB7/RAB8.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI high-throughput yeast two-hybrid interactome (Luck et al. 2020). Source of the bare GO:0005515 protein-binding IPI; partners are not functionally connected to ICMT's methyltransferase activity, so contributes only an uninformative interaction annotation.

title: Mammalian prenylcysteine carboxyl methyltransferase is in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; PubMed-verified. Original molecular characterization; basis for UniProt EC 2.1.1.100 and core ER localization.

title: Molecular basis for the function of the αβ heterodimer of human NAD-dependent isocitrate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Crystal structures (PDB 6KDF apo, 6KDE Ca2+-bound, 6KDY NAD-bound, 6KE3 NADH-bound) of the human IDH3 αβ heterodimer establish IDH3B (β) as an assembled subunit whose small domain helps form the active-site cleft and whose β3-α3/β12-α8 loops build a pseudo-allosteric site, defining β's structural/regulatory contribution to NAD/NADH binding, metal-ion geometry, and allosteric control of the holoenzyme rather than any catalytic activity of β alone.

title: Structures of a constitutively active mutant of human IDH3 reveal new insights into the mechanisms of allosteric activation and the catalytic reaction.
review_notes: Structures of the constitutively active α-Q139A mutant, including the (αβαγ)2 holoenzyme (PDB 8GRB) and the first pseudo-Michaelis complex of HsIDH3, place IDH3B as an integral β subunit of the active heterooctamer and define the cofactor/substrate/metal-binding residues at the complex level, supporting β's role in holoenzyme assembly, allosteric activation, and the catalytic reaction.

title: Localization of the pre-squalene segment of the isoprenoid biosynthetic pathway in mammalian peroxisomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache. Supports peroxisomal localization of the pre-squalene cholesterol biosynthetic segment (including IDI1) in human cells; basis for the IDA peroxisome annotation.

title: IDI2, a second isopentenyl diphosphate isomerase in mammals.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Although titled for the paralog IDI2, the abstract explicitly states both IDI1 and IDI2 are localized to the peroxisome by a PTS1-dependent pathway, directly supporting the IDI1 peroxisome IDA annotation.

title: Human isopentenyl diphosphate: dimethylallyl diphosphate isomerase: overproduction, purification, and characterization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Definitive biochemical characterization of recombinant human IDI1 (IPP->DMAPP isomerization, Mg2+ dependence, Km/Vmax); experimental basis for GO:0004452 (IDA) and the IC cholesterol biosynthesis annotation.

title: IDI2, a second isopentenyl diphosphate isomerase in mammals.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Definitive primary characterization of human IDI2: skeletal-muscle-restricted expression, IPP-to-DMAPP isomerase activity (Km 22.8 uM, pH optimum 8.0), yeast idi1 complementation, PTS1-dependent peroxisomal localization, and PPARalpha-linked regulation. Experimental basis for the GO:0004452 (IDA), peroxisome, and isoprenoid-process annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Genome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Cached full text does not name IDI2, but the IDI2-LDB1 (Q86U70-2) interaction it supports is recorded in the UniProt INTERACTION block. Supports only a bare "protein binding" annotation with no established functional role for IDI2; marked over-annotated.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid binary interactome (HuRI). Cached full text does not name IDI2, but the IDI2-LDB1 (Q86U70-2) interaction it supports is recorded in the UniProt INTERACTION block. Supports only a bare "protein binding" annotation; marked over-annotated.

title: Evolution of vertebrate indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache. UniProt cites this paper (ECO:0000269) for the catalytic activity and biophysicochemical properties (Km 21.23 uM L-Trp vs 4.6 mM D-Trp). Directly supports the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase MF for IDO1.

title: Molecular cloning, sequencing and expression of human interferon-gamma-inducible indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase cDNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Establishes the tryptophan-catabolizing (kynurenine-pathway) function and IFN-gamma inducibility. Does NOT establish electron transfer activity; the GO:0009055 TAS from this paper is an over-annotation.

title: Human renal tubular epithelial cells suppress alloreactive T cell proliferation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Supports the IMP annotations for indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase activity and positive regulation of T cell apoptotic process, and is consistent with the NOT annotation for regulation of activated T cell proliferation (IDO inhibitor failed to restore proliferation).

title: Prevention of allogeneic fetal rejection by tryptophan catabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Classic maternal-fetal tolerance study (mouse model). Supports the female pregnancy / maternal-fetal immune tolerance role annotated by TAS.

title: IDO1 dioxygenates L-Trp to NFK
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing the IDO1-catalyzed L-Trp -> N-formyl-L-kynurenine step and its cytosolic localization. Title left as fetched.

title: Expression of five iduronate-2-sulfatase site-directed mutations.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; supports IDS iduronate-2-sulfatase activity (residual activity of R88H/R88P mutants), the CXPSR formylglycine motif, and poor lysosomal transport of mutants. PubMed-verified title.

title: The effect of four mutations on the expression of iduronate-2-sulfatase in mucopolysaccharidosis type II.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; transient-expression/activity study of IDS MPS II mutations, supporting the iduronate-2-sulfatase activity annotation. PubMed-verified title.

title: Sulphatase activities are regulated by the interaction of sulphatase-modifying factor 1 with SUMF2.
review_notes: Full text available; source of the IDS-SUMF2 (Q8NBJ7) IntAct IPI. SUMF2 stably associates with IDS and modulates SUMF1/FGE-mediated sulfatase activation in the ER. Supports a real but peripheral interaction; the protein binding term is uninformative.

title: Hunter syndrome: isolation of an iduronate-2-sulfatase cDNA clone and analysis of patient DNA.
review_notes: Original IDS cDNA cloning paper; establishes IDS (EC 3.1.6.13) as required for lysosomal degradation of heparan and dermatan sulfate, and defines the precursor processing. PubMed-verified title.

title: Insights into Hunter syndrome from the structure of iduronate-2-sulfatase.
review_notes: Full text available; crystal structure (PDB 5FQL) of human IDS. Defines the catalytic mechanism (formylglycine at Cys84, active-site Ca2+), specific activity on iduronide-2-sulfate substrate, and role in stepwise GAG (HS/DS) degradation. Primary support for the MF, calcium binding, and GAG catabolism annotations.

title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I, unique structure of accumulated heparan sulfate and increased N-sulfotransferase activity in mice lacking α-l-iduronidase.
review_notes: Murine Idua-knockout study directly demonstrating loss of terminal iduronate removal from heparan sulfate; supports the HS/heparin catabolic-process annotations.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.

title: Human α-L-iduronidase uses its own N-glycan as a substrate-binding and catalytic module.

title: Insights into mucopolysaccharidosis I from the structure and action of α-L-iduronidase.
review_notes: Definitive structural and mechanistic study of human IDUA; primary support for the molecular function and HS/DS catabolic processes.

title: Immunopurification and characterization of human alpha-L-iduronidase with the use of monoclonal antibodies.
review_notes: Early biochemical characterization of the human enzyme; supports catalytic activity but its disaccharide-metabolic-process annotation reflects the assay substrate rather than the in vivo polymeric substrate.

title: Regulation of signal transduction by enzymatically inactive antiviral RNA helicase proteins MDA5, RIG-I, and LGP2.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Bamming & Horvath, J Biol Chem 284:9700-9712 (2009). title: Ribose 2'-O-methylation provides a molecular signature for the distinction of self and non-self mRNA dependent on the RNA sensor Mda5.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Zuest et al., Nat Immunol 12:137-143 (2011). One of the two IDA sources for GO:0038187; demonstrates MDA5-dependent interferon induction by coronavirus mRNA lacking 2'-O-methylation.

title: Cooperative assembly and dynamic disassembly of MDA5 filaments for viral dsRNA recognition.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Peisley et al., PNAS 108:21010-21015 (2011). Source of the ATP-driven filament assembly/disassembly proofreading model.

title: Structural basis for dsRNA recognition, filament formation, and antiviral signal activation by MDA5.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Wu et al., Cell 152:276-289 (2013). The other IDA source for GO:0038187; crystal structure of MDA5 on dsRNA plus filament and CARD-oligomerisation model. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so quoting is limited to the abstract.

title: Gain-of-function mutations in IFIH1 cause a spectrum of human disease phenotypes associated with upregulated type I interferon signaling.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Rice et al., Nat Genet 46:503-509 (2014). Establishes IFIH1 gain-of-function variants as a cause of Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome and related interferonopathies, with increased RNA binding - used here as evidence bearing on self-RNA sensing.

title: RNA editing by ADAR1 prevents MDA5 sensing of endogenous dsRNA as nonself.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Liddicoat et al., Science 349:1115-1120 (2015). Mouse genetics, not human IFIH1 biochemistry, hence MEDIUM: it shows that ADAR1 editing of endogenous dsRNA exists to prevent MDA5 activation, which is relevant background for the ligand question rather than direct evidence about the human protein.

title: Loss of cellular RNA homeostasis contributes to MDA5 activation during virus infection.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed: Sampaio et al., Nat Immunol 27:1815-1828 (2026), doi 10.1038/s41590-026-02614-3. Full text read. The central claim used here - that endogenous MDA5 iCLIP in SARS-CoV-2- and EMCV-infected cells recovers host, not viral, RNA - is quoted verbatim. title: Substitutions for hydrophobic amino acids in the N-terminal domains of IGFBP-3 and -5 markedly reduce IGF-I binding and alter their biologic actions.

title: The human plasma proteome: a nonredundant list developed by combination of four separate sources.

title: Insulin-like growth factor binding protein-5 (IGFBP-5) interacts with thrombospondin-1 to induce negative regulatory effects on IGF-I actions.
review_notes: IGFBP-5/thrombospondin-1 interaction modulating TS-1/IAP; abstract only.

title: MiR-137 inhibited cell proliferation and migration of vascular smooth muscle cells via targeting IGFBP-5 and modulating the mTOR/STAT3 signaling.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: MatrisomeDB 2.0: 2023 updates to the ECM-protein knowledge database.

title: IGFBP5 is an ROR1 ligand promoting glioblastoma invasion via ROR1/HER2-CREB signaling axis.

title: Insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-binding protein 5 forms an alternative ternary complex with IGFs and the acid-labile subunit.

title: Falcon deep research report for human IGFBP5
review_notes: Quoting corrected 2026-10-06: two quotes attributed to this file were not in it and now quote it verbatim, and a finding that the profibrotic response is IGF-independent and needs no nuclear entry was withdrawn. The file says nuclear localization is not required for every phenotype, including fibrosis, but never that the profibrotic response is IGF-independent; its nuclear-entry passage concerns a survival phenotype in which IGF binding was required. Generated late (after the review was drafted); the file's own claims are consistent with the review and do not contradict existing actions. Key primary claims (Kalus 1998 PMID:9822601, Jones 1993 PMID:7683690, Su 2015 PMID:26103640) were already cited and verified in the review.

title: Identification of Sef, a novel modulator of FGF signalling.

title: hSef inhibits PC-12 cell differentiation by interfering with Ras-mitogen-activated protein kinase MAPK signaling.

title: hSef potentiates EGF-mediated MAPK signaling through affecting EGFR trafficking and degradation.

title: Interleukin-17 receptor D (Sef) is a multi-functional regulator of cell signaling.

title: IL17RD binds p-2S MAP2Ks and MAPKs

title: MAP2Ks phosphorylate MAPK at the Golgi membrane

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for IL23R prolactin receptor activity

title: Inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase binds nucleic acids in vitro and in vivo.

title: Two distinct cDNAs for human IMP dehydrogenase.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.

title: ANKRD9 is a metabolically-controlled regulator of IMPDH2 abundance and macro-assembly.
