title: Mutations in KDSR Cause Recessive Progressive Symmetric Erythrokeratoderma.
review_notes: Disease-gene identification; biallelic KDSR mutations cause progressive symmetric erythrokeratoderma, with yeast complementation showing loss of KDSR function.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale yeast two-hybrid interactome; source of four uninformative protein-binding interactions for KDSR (KIF1B, HSPB1, TTR, WFS1). No established functional relevance to KDSR's enzymatic role.

title: Glucosylceramide and galactosylceramide, small glycosphingolipids with significant impact on health and disease.
review_notes: Review of glucosyl-/galactosylceramide biology; does not mention or assay KDSR. Cited for a glycosphingolipid biosynthesis annotation that is several enzymatic steps downstream of KDSR - a pathway-level over-annotation.

title: De novo sphingolipid biosynthesis necessitates detoxification in cancer cells.
review_notes: Full text available; shows KDSR reduces 3KDS to sphinganine and that KDSR loss causes toxic 3KDS accumulation, ER dysfunction and proteotoxic stress, highlighting KDSR as a cancer therapy target.

title: FVT-1, a novel human transcription unit affected by variant translocation t(2;18)(p11;q21) of follicular lymphoma.
review_notes: Original FVT-1 cloning paper describing the follicular-lymphoma translocation and predicting a "putatively secreted protein"; the secretion prediction (basis of the extracellular-region annotation) was later superseded by ER membrane topology.

title: UniProtKB entry Q06136 (KDSR_HUMAN)
review_notes: UniProt record for human KDSR; source of catalytic activity (EC 1.1.1.102, RHEA:22640), ER membrane multi-pass topology, NADPH-binding sites, and disease associations.

title: Properties of normal and mutant recombinant human ketohexokinases and implications for the pathogenesis of essential fructosuria.
review_notes: Primary enzymology of recombinant human KHK; establishes ketohexokinase activity (EC 2.7.1.3), that both KHK-A and KHK-C isoforms are active, kinetic parameters, and the disease mechanism of essential fructosuria (G40R null, A43T thermolabile). Directly supports the core catalytic function and fructose metabolic process annotations. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available false).

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteomics; source of the extracellular exosome HDA localization. Detection of a highly expressed cytosolic enzyme in exosomes, not a functional localization. Abstract-only cache does not name KHK individually (part of the 1132-protein dataset).

title: Structures of alternatively spliced isoforms of human ketohexokinase.
review_notes: Full-text-available crystal structures of KHK-A and KHK-C and the KHK-A ternary complex with fructose and AMP-PNP. Directly supports ATP binding, fructose binding, homodimerization/identical protein binding, and the committed fructolysis role. Verified against cached full text.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale Y2H interactome; source of the bare "protein binding" IPI (KHK-LHX9, Q9NQ69). The cached full text does not mention KHK or LHX9 specifically (the interaction lives in the supplementary dataset). Low information value for KHK's molecular function; retained as over-annotated.

title: Molecular basis of essential fructosuria: molecular cloning and mutational analysis of human ketohexokinase (fructokinase).
review_notes: Original cloning and mutational analysis defining KHK as hepatic fructokinase (EC 2.7.1.3) and the molecular basis of essential fructosuria (compound heterozygous G40R / A43T). Supports ketohexokinase activity and disease role. Abstract-only cache.

title: Histone Interaction Landscapes Visualized by Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry in Intact Cell Nuclei.
review_notes: PubMed title/identifier verified; cached abstract and discussion read (full_text_available true but methods/results absent). IntAct IM-26653-2713 independently verifies Q5VZ46-Q93079 crosslink association. Supports a nuclear pool with high-throughput limits; not a KIAA1614-specific functional mechanism.

title: Deep research report on KIAA1614
review_notes: Useful unknown-function summary, but treating IPR051741 as a physical PAR6 domain and asserting no detected partners/localization omits independently curated high-throughput evidence. Lack of target studies does not refute IBA.

title: OpenScientist KIAA1614 Par6-like polarity-scaffold hypothesis report
review_notes: Substantive report read and reused. InterPro confirms divergent annotated architecture, but also a PTHR14102:SF12 match (reported score 4.6e-32); a four-mer Jaccard comparison does not refute homology. IBA is not circular just because the target lacks experimental GO rows. Missing domains or interaction-database edges do not establish inability to bind. AlphaFold numeric claims lack delivered computational provenance and were not adopted. IntAct nuclear H2B and PTPRR associations were independently confirmed; no duplicate report needed.

title: Kinesin 3 and cytoplasmic dynein mediate interkinetic nuclear migration in neural stem cells.
review_notes: Rat brain RNAi identifies Kif1a as the basal interkinetic nuclear migration motor; rescue with human KIF1A.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput neurodegenerative-disease interactome; KIF1A interactions not functionally followed up.

title: Genotype and defects in microtubule-based motility correlate with clinical severity in KIF1A-associated neurological disorder.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; human KAND variant biophysics (microtubule binding, velocity, processivity).

title: The neuron-specific kinesin superfamily protein KIF1A is a unique monomeric motor for anterograde axonal transport of synaptic vesicle precursors.
review_notes: Original mouse KIF1A characterization as anterograde motor for synaptic vesicle precursors (abstract-only cache).

title: Defect in synaptic vesicle precursor transport and neuronal cell death in KIF1A motor protein-deficient mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; Kif1a knockout mouse shows specific loss of synaptic vesicle precursor transport.

title: Falcon deep research report for KIF1A
review_notes: Retrieval support only; consistent with primary sources on plus-end motor activity and SVP/DCV cargo. Does not discuss interkinetic nuclear migration (that NEW row rests on PMID:21037580).

title: The kinesin protein Kif7 is a critical regulator of Gli transcription factors in mammalian hedgehog signaling.
review_notes: Independent 2009 demonstration that Kif7 binds Gli proteins and controls their proteolysis and stability, acting in both directions. Abstract-only. Cited by mouse GOA for IMP rows on both GO:0045879 and GO:0045880, which anchors the ISS transfers reviewed here.

title: The mammalian Cos2 homolog Kif7 plays an essential role in modulating Hh signal transduction during development.
review_notes: The paper GOA cites for the KIF7-GLI/SMO/SUFU interactions and for ciliary localisation. Cached record is abstract-only; every claim used here is quoted from that abstract, and the interaction set is independently corroborated by the UniProt SUBUNIT line derived from the same paper.

title: Mouse Kif7/Costal2 is a cilia-associated protein that regulates Sonic hedgehog signaling.
review_notes: Mouse genetics establishing that Kif7 acts downstream of Smo with both regulatory signs, and the source of the base-to-tip redistribution and of the ciliary-base localisation behind the ISS GO:0036064 row. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: KIF7 mutations cause fetal hydrolethalus and acrocallosal syndromes.
review_notes: Human disease genetics: hydrolethalus and acrocallosal syndromes, plus the modifier-allele result. Used here for the human GLI3-processing phenotype, which independently supports the smoothened pathway annotations. Full text in the cache.

title: Mutations in KIF7 link Joubert syndrome with Sonic Hedgehog signaling and microtubule dynamics.
review_notes: Source of the JBTS12 locus, the NPHP1 interaction and the GO:0003777 IDA. Verified against PubMed. Abstract-only in the cache. Its framing of KIF7 as "a putative ciliary motor protein" is explicitly provisional, which is why the motor annotation derived from it is modified rather than treated as an established assay result.

title: Kif7 promotes hedgehog signaling in growth plate chondrocytes by restricting the inhibitory function of Sufu.
review_notes: The genetic separation of the positive arm: halving the Sufu dose rescues Kif7-null chondrocytes. Abstract-only in the cache, but the rescue result is stated explicitly in the abstract and is the strongest single piece of evidence that the positive role of KIF7 is SUFU-directed.

title: Kif7 regulates Gli2 through Sufu-dependent and -independent functions during skin development and tumorigenesis.
review_notes: Keratinocyte counterpart of the chondrocyte result, showing the same Sufu-dependent and -independent split in a second tissue. Abstract-only. Corroborating rather than load-bearing.

title: Positive and negative regulation of Gli activity by Kif7 in the zebrafish embryo.
review_notes: Zebrafish loss-of-function analysis; source of the cytoplasmic-puncta observation and of the Costal-2-substitutes-for-Kif7 experiment that supports the PANTHER sister-subfamily orthology. Full text in the cache.

title: The kinesin-4 protein Kif7 regulates mammalian Hedgehog signalling by organizing the cilium tip compartment.
review_notes: The central mechanistic paper for KIF7: purified-protein plus-end assays, cilium tip compartment organisation, and the negative results on intraflagellar transport. Full text available in the cache and quoted directly. Reactome R-HSA-5610733 cites the same work for the same conclusions.

title: Altered chemomechanical coupling causes impaired motility of the kinesin-4 motors KIF27 and KIF7.
review_notes: Kinetic dissection of the whole kinesin-4 family, including side-by-side motility and ATPase measurements on KIF7 and Drosophila Cos2. Full text in the cache. This is the reference that makes the immotility of KIF7 a measured property of both orthologues rather than an inference about one protein.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex affinity-purification interactome. Contributes one KIF7-P4HA2 row. The measurement is not disputed and has since been validated by targeted experiments.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging interactome. Contributes one KIF7-P4HA2 row; endogenous tagging makes this the least overexpression-prone of the three screen detections.

title: P4HA2 hydroxylates SUFU to regulate the paracrine Hedgehog signaling and promote B-cell lymphoma progression.
review_notes: Validates the KIF7-P4HA2 interaction that the three interactome screens reported, maps it to the KIF7 GLI-binding domain, and shows P4HA2 ciliary localisation is KIF7-dependent. Full text in the cache. This is what converts three bare protein-binding rows into an adaptor-activity call; the paper itself names the three screens as its prior support.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome. Contributes the third independent KIF7-P4HA2 detection.

title: KIF7 is recruited to the ciliary tip through interaction with axonemal microtubules
review_notes: Reactome reaction behind the TAS ciliary-tip row. The cached summary is current with the primary literature - it describes plus-end binding and ATP-dependent growth inhibition and cites He et al. 2014 - so the author statement is accurate even though the reaction title retains motor-protein nomenclature.

title: Tumor necrosis factor-alpha-converting enzyme controls surface expression of c-Kit and survival of embryonic stem cell-derived mast cells.
review_notes: Shows TACE/ADAM17-mediated shedding of the KIT ectodomain; supports the soluble extracellular-region annotation.

title: Activation of the human c-kit product by ligand-induced dimerization mediates circular actin reorganization and chemotaxis.
review_notes: Shows SCF-induced dimerization/kinase activation, actin reorganization and chemotaxis; supports cytoskeletal/chemotaxis outputs.

title: Structural basis for activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase KIT by stem cell factor.
review_notes: Structural paper establishing SCF-induced KIT dimerization and kinase activation; directly supports receptor activity and Kit signaling.

title: Induction of microRNA-221 by platelet-derived growth factor signaling is critical for modulation of vascular smooth muscle phenotype.
review_notes: Primarily a miR-221/PDGF study; c-Kit appears as a downregulated target, so KIT's role in vSMC differentiation is indirect/peripheral.

title: CD72 negatively regulates KIT-mediated responses in human mast cells.
review_notes: CD72 study that also assays KIT/SCF-dependent mast cell chemotaxis, cytokine production and degranulation; supports mast cell effector annotations.

title: Expression of a truncated form of KIT tyrosine kinase in human spermatozoa correlates with sperm DNA integrity.
review_notes: Shows cytoplasmic TR-KIT in human spermatozoa (sub-acrosomal/equatorial); supports the cytoplasm/isoform localization.

title: Mechanisms of STAT protein activation by oncogenic KIT mutants in neoplastic mast cells.
review_notes: Demonstrates STAT1/3/5 activation and direct STAT phosphorylation downstream of oncogenic KIT; supports JAK-STAT/STAT annotations.

title: Mechanism of activation of human c-KIT kinase by internal tandem duplications of the juxtamembrane domain and point mutations at aspartic acid 816.
review_notes: Establishes ligand-independent constitutive kinase activation by JM ITDs and D816Y; supports RTK activity and autophosphorylation.

title: Activating and dominant inactivating c-KIT catalytic domain mutations in distinct clinical forms of human mastocytosis.
review_notes: Identifies D816V activating mutations in mastocytosis with spontaneous receptor activation; supports the general signal transduction annotation.

title: Parathyroid hormone-regulated production of stem cell factor in human osteoblasts and osteoblast-like cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes that osteoblasts express the exon-6-omitted, membrane-associated SCF isoform, supporting plasma-membrane localization of KITLG.

title: Structural basis for activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase KIT by stem cell factor.
review_notes: Crystal structures of the KIT ectodomain before/after SCF binding; establishes that SCF's role is to dimerize KIT. Directly supports stem cell factor receptor binding.

title: Developmental changes in human fetal testicular cell numbers and messenger ribonucleic acid levels during the second trimester.
review_notes: Abstract-only; KITL is measured as a Sertoli-cell transcript rising through the second trimester, supporting the IEP male gonad development annotation.

title: Monocytic cells derived from human embryonic stem cells and fetal liver share common differentiation pathways and homeostatic functions.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache foregrounds hESC/fetal-liver monocyte differentiation; SCF is a standard component of such hematopoietic differentiation systems. Basis for the IDA embryonic hemopoiesis annotation; retained as non-core (experimental annotation, full text not accessible).

title: Primary structure and functional expression of rat and human stem cell factor DNAs.
review_notes: Primary cloning and functional-expression paper; demonstrates recombinant SCF is biologically active and augments hematopoietic progenitor proliferation synergistically with CSFs. Supports receptor binding, cytokine activity and hematopoietic roles.

title: Allelic Mutations of KITLG, Encoding KIT Ligand, Cause Asymmetric and Unilateral Hearing Loss and Waardenburg Syndrome Type 2.
review_notes: Full text available; immunofluorescence directly localizes transmembrane KITLG to cytoplasm, cell membrane, lamellipodia and filopodia, and links loss of membrane localization/reduced secretion to disease. Supports the IDA localization annotations.

title: Insulin-like growth factor-I augments erythropoietin-induced proliferation through enhanced tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT5.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache foregrounds IGF-I/EPO/STAT5 in the SCF-responsive F-36P cell line; full text not accessible. Basis for the IDA positive-regulation-of-proliferation annotation, retained by deferring to the curator's full-text reading.

title: Establishment of the anti-Klotho monoclonal antibodies and detection of Klotho protein in kidneys.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Monoclonal antibodies detect 130 kDa Klotho in human and mouse kidney membranes and in transfected CHO supernatant, supporting both plasma-membrane and extracellular location.

title: Association of klotho gene polymorphism with bone density and spondylosis of the lumbar spine in postmenopausal women.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. This is an association study of a non-coding CA-repeat polymorphism with bone density, negative in the overall population; it does not establish that KL acts in bone mineralization, so it is weak support for the IMP process annotation it underpins.

title: Klotho is a novel beta-glucuronidase capable of hydrolyzing steroid beta-glucuronides.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. This is the source of the beta-glucuronidase EC assignment. The activity was not reproduced with the human ectodomain in PMID:29342138, and no physiological substrate has been established, so the claim is genuinely contested rather than miscited.

title: Secreted Klotho protein in sera and CSF: implication for post-translational cleavage in release of Klotho protein from cell membrane.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. First detection of circulating Klotho in human serum and CSF; the 130 kDa size indicates the shed ectodomain rather than the predicted splice product.

title: Suppression of aging in mice by the hormone Klotho.
review_notes: Full text cached. Mouse overexpression study supporting an FGF23-independent humoral role for soluble Klotho; used as background only, since the receptor and mechanism are undefined and no such annotation is proposed.

title: Regulation of fibroblast growth factor-23 signaling by klotho.
review_notes: Full text cached. Co-immunoprecipitation of Klotho with FGFRs and demonstration that both full-length and soluble Klotho act as cofactors for FGF23 signaling.

title: Klotho converts canonical FGF receptor into a specific receptor for FGF23.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Foundational demonstration that Klotho converts FGFR1c into the FGF23 receptor and that Klotho alone cannot signal.

title: A homozygous missense mutation in human KLOTHO causes severe tumoral calcinosis.
review_notes: Full text cached. The H193R homozygous patient establishes the physiological requirement for KL in human FGF23-dependent phosphate and vitamin D control.

title: C-terminal tail of FGF19 determines its specificity toward Klotho co-receptors.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Chimera study supports direct binding of endocrine FGFs to alpha-Klotho and localizes specificity to the FGF C-terminal tail.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Large-scale urinary exosome proteomics; KL detection is a high-throughput observation.

title: RNAi silencing of brain klotho potentiates cold-induced elevation of blood pressure via the endothelin pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached. This rat study is the experimental source behind the blood-pressure and norepinephrine annotations transferred to human KL by Ensembl Compara; the effects are systemic and indirect.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Prostatic-secretion exosome proteomics; KL detection comes from the proteomic inventory rather than from a targeted experiment.

title: α-Klotho is a non-enzymatic molecular scaffold for FGF23 hormone signalling.
review_notes: Full text cached. Human FGF23-FGFR1c-alphaKlotho ternary crystal structure with signaling and enzyme assays; the primary source for the coreceptor molecular function and against intrinsic glycosidase activity.

title: Mutation of the mouse klotho gene leads to a syndrome resembling ageing.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. The mouse klotho discovery paper reports sequence similarity to beta-glucosidases only, with no enzyme assay, so it does not support the beta-glucosidase activity annotation drawn from it.

title: Identification of the human klotho gene and its two transcripts encoding membrane and secreted klotho protein.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Human KL gene structure and the two transcripts encoding membrane-bound and putative secreted forms.

title: Liver-specific activities of FGF19 require Klotho beta.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper directly supports the curated FGFR-binding record and mammalian FGF19-KLB-FGFR4 signaling; its physiological CYP7A1 experiment is in mouse, so the human process proposal uses ISS.

title: C-terminal tail of FGF19 determines its specificity toward Klotho co-receptors.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. Chimera experiments directly support endocrine-FGF recognition by KLB; only the abstract is cached.

title: FGF21 N- and C-termini play different roles in receptor interaction and activation.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper supports replacing generic protein binding with fibroblast growth factor binding; only the abstract is cached.

title: Different roles of N- and C- termini in the functional activity of FGF21.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. Binding and deletion experiments independently support FGF21 recognition by KLB; only the abstract is cached.

title: Structures of β-klotho reveal a 'zip code'-like mechanism for endocrine FGF signalling.
review_notes: PubMed identity, PMC full text, human crystal structures, quantitative binding assays, mutagenesis, and cell-signaling experiments were verified. This is the decisive source for pseudoenzyme status and KLB coreceptor mechanism.

title: Structures of ligand-occupied β-Klotho complexes reveal a molecular mechanism underlying endocrine FGF specificity and activity.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper supplies direct human structural support for FGF19 binding to KLB; locally accessible content is abstract-only.

title: Manual deep-research synthesis for human KLB
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the fetched UniProt record, complete GOA set, and cached primary literature, including explicit evidence boundaries and provider failures.

title: Manual KLB curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored annotation decision log with inline provenance and explicit handling of the inactive GH-like domains.

title: UniProtKB record for human KLB (Q86Z14)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project; used for accession, sequence, membrane topology, family, and domain metadata.

title: Functional characterization and mechanism of action of recombinant human kynurenine 3-hydroxylase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Characterizes recombinant human KMO: NADPH-dependent flavin monooxygenase, one non-covalently bound FAD per enzyme, pH optimum 7.5, kinetics; documents peroxide-forming uncoupling. Directly supports the core catalytic, FAD-binding and OMM annotations.

title: Structural basis of kynurenine 3-monooxygenase inhibition.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Reports the first KMO crystal structures (yeast KMO +/- inhibitor) validated against human KMO, confirms FAD-dependence and outer mitochondrial membrane localization, and documents inhibitor-accelerated H2O2 formation (basis of the non-core NAD(P)H oxidase activity).

title: Kynurenine-3-monooxygenase inhibition prevents multiple organ failure in rodent models of acute pancreatitis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Kmo-knockout metabolic profiling establishes KMO as the gatekeeper of kynurenine metabolism (loss diverts flux to kynurenic acid); characterizes human KMO activity and a potent inhibitor. Supports the tryptophan-catabolism/gatekeeper role and refutes a kynurenic-acid-biosynthesis role.

title: Biochemistry and structural studies of kynurenine 3-monooxygenase reveal allosteric inhibition by Ro 61-8048.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Biochemical/structural study of human KMO with active-site mutagenesis (R85, Y99, N363, E366, M367, Y398 abolish/strongly reduce activity) and evidence that the C-terminal region is essential; supports the core catalytic MF annotation.

title: Structural Basis for Inhibitor-Induced Hydrogen Peroxide Production by Kynurenine 3-Monooxygenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Human KMO structure (PDB 5X68) in complex with FAD; defines FAD-binding residues and inhibitor-induced H2O2 production. Supports the core FAD-binding annotation and the non-core NAD(P)H oxidase side activity.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified large-scale quantitative mitochondrial proteome dataset. Provides HTP-level support for mitochondrial localization of KMO but is not KMO-specific; less informative than the experimental outer-mitochondrial-membrane evidence.

title: Cloning and functional expression of human kynurenine 3-monooxygenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Original cloning and functional expression of human KMO; establishes it as an NADPH-dependent flavin monooxygenase hydroxylating L-kynurenine, tissue expression (liver/placenta/kidney), and OMM localization. Foundational support for the core catalytic and localization annotations.

title: Combining SSH and cDNA microarrays for rapid identification of differentially expressed genes.
review_notes: KRT19 identified only as differentially expressed between ER+ and ER- breast cancer lines; does not show response to estrogen.

title: Proteomic profiling of cellular proteins interacting with the hepatitis C virus core protein.
review_notes: HCV core pull-down; K19 identified among bound proteins, validation focused on K8 and vimentin.

title: Specific interaction of the actin-binding domain of dystrophin with intermediate filaments containing keratin 19.
review_notes: Abstract verified: dystrophin ABD binds K19 directly and specifically; K8/K19 at costameres. Basis for muscle IDA annotations.

title: Absence of keratin 19 in mice causes skeletal myopathy with mitochondrial and sarcolemmal reorganization.
review_notes: K19-null mouse skeletal myopathy with costamere disruption; key in vivo genetic evidence for muscle role.

title: EGF potentiated oncogenesis requires a tissue transglutaminase-dependent signaling pathway leading to Src activation.
review_notes: Full text: K19 bridges tTG and Src in SKBR3 cells; single cancer cell line study.

title: Expression of caspase-14 and keratin-19 in the human epidermis and appendages during fetal skin development.
review_notes: IHC expression study in fetal skin; supports expression pattern, not membrane localization specifically (abstract only).

title: Sequence of the human 40-kDa keratin reveals an unusual structure with very high sequence identity to the corresponding bovine keratin.
review_notes: Original human K19 sequence paper; documents lack of tail domain. Supports TAS structural IF annotations.

title: KRT19 directly interacts with β-catenin/RAC1 complex to regulate NUMB-dependent NOTCH signaling pathway and breast cancer properties.
review_notes: Cancer-cell study reporting KRT19-beta-catenin/RAC1 interaction and NOTCH modulation; single lab.

title: Purification and biochemical characterization of some of the properties of recombinant human kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; biochemical characterization establishing kynureninase activity and the strong 3-hydroxykynurenine preference. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Crystal structure of Homo sapiens kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; structural and kinetic characterization establishing PLP dependence, fold-type I superfamily membership and substrate preference. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Xanthurenic aciduria due to a mutation in KYNU encoding kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; links KYNU deficiency to hydroxykynureninuria (HYXKY). Abstract-only in cache.

title: High-performance liquid chromatographic assay of human lymphocyte kynureninase activity levels.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the vitamin-B6 (PLP) dependence of kynureninase activity (basis for the response-to-vitamin-B6 annotation). Abstract-only.

title: NAD Deficiency, Congenital Malformations, and Niacin Supplementation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes the NAD-deficiency/VCRL2 disease mechanism and in-vitro activity of mutant KYNU. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Intracellular localization and characterization of 3-hydroxykynureninase in human liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; early biochemical localization/characterization of the human liver enzyme. Basis for both cytosol and mitochondrion IDA annotations. Abstract-only.

title: Isolation and expression of a cDNA clone encoding human kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary cloning and functional expression of human kynureninase establishing the catalytic activity and PLP dependence. Abstract-only.

title: Cloning and recombinant expression of rat and human kynureninase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; independent cloning/kinetic characterization of human kynureninase. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Different kynurenine pathway enzymes limit quinolinic acid formation by various human cell types.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the quinolinate-biosynthesis and IFN-gamma-response annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Falcon deep research report for human LAT
review_notes: Provider-generated literature synthesis (Edison/falcon) drawing mostly on two reviews (Shah 2021, Fernandez-Aguilar 2023) and three preprints (Rubin 2024 bioRxiv, Rainwater 2025 bioRxiv, Saez bioRxiv). Its core scaffold, docking-site and pathway claims agree with the primary papers already cited here. Its vesicular-trafficking claims were verified against peer-reviewed primary papers (PMID:29789604, PMID:23666293, PMID:29440364, and the published Saez paper PMID:33572370). Errors noted: it gives LAT as ~233 residues without saying this is the short isoform (UniProt canonical O43561-1 is 262 aa, so Y132/Y171/Y191/Y226 are short-isoform numbers); it attributes a 2026 Yamane et al. SLP-76/PLCgamma1 study to the 2021 Shah review; DNA-PKcs phosphorylation of S224/S241 rests on a single preprint. Not used as sole evidence for any annotation decision.

title: A fast and robust gene knockout method for Salpingoeca rosetta informs the genetics of choanoflagellate multicellular development
review_notes: bioRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed), full text cached; used for evolutionary context only.

title: The Hippo kinase cascade regulates a contractile cell behavior and cell density in a close unicellular relative of animals.
review_notes: Full text cached; primary genetic study of the Capsaspora Warts ortholog, used for evolutionary context only.

title: Lck bound to coreceptor is less active than free Lck.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1073/pnas.1913334117 (cited by the falcon report); full text cached. Mouse T hybridoma system.

title: CD28-CAR-T cell activation through FYN kinase signaling rather than LCK enhances therapeutic performance.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.100917 (cited by the falcon report). Engineered-receptor context; shows FYN redundancy, not a new LCK function.

title: A partial human LCK defect causes a T cell immunodeficiency with intestinal inflammation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1084/jem.20230927 (cited by the falcon report). Human genetic necessity evidence; does not change molecular function assignments.

title: Molecular determinants of differential substrate selection between the Src family kinases Lck and Src.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1880421 (cited by the falcon report); full text cached. The report's "~90% kinase-domain identity" is not what the paper says (it states 60-90% identity across SFK catalytic sites).

title: Falcon deep research report for human LCK
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis built mostly on three 2023-2024 reviews (De Sanctis 2024 Cancers, PMID:39123358; Fernandez-Aguilar 2023 Biology, PMID:37759563; Zhang 2023 Front Cell Dev Biol, PMID:36910149) plus four primary papers (Wei 2020 PMID:32571924, Lui 2023 PMID:37962568, Karpouzou 2026 PMID:42638732, Wu 2023 PMID:36696897), which were resolved from DOIs and cached here. Core biochemistry (Y394/Y505 regulation, CSK/CD45, zinc clasp, ITAM and ZAP70 phosphorylation, free vs coreceptor-bound pools) agrees with the review. Minor inaccuracies: "~90% kinase-domain identity" with Src (the cited paper says 60-90% across SFKs), and the 2023 JEM study is not the first human LCK deficiency report (the paper itself refers to earlier LCK variants). Claims on nuclear LCK, ZDHHC2/21 palmitoylation, Y192 feedback, CD5/CD2/CD44/CD146/CD160 signaling and therapeutics rest on reviews only and were not used as annotation evidence. title: Identification of a putative lysosomal cobalamin exporter altered in the cblF defect of vitamin B12 metabolism.

title: The brain-specific kinase LMTK3 regulates neuronal excitability by decreasing KCC2-dependent neuronal Cl(-) extrusion.

title: LMTK3 regulation of EV biogenesis and cargo sorting promotes tumour growth by reducing monocyte infiltration and driving pro-tumourigenic macrophage polarisation in breast cancer.

It is a disease-context mechanism, not evidence that every LRIF1 activity is long-isoform-specific. The project fetcher could obtain only the abstract.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: PubMed title and abstract were verified. Six LRIF1 interaction candidates are supplied by IntAct/GOA, but the cached narrative does not name LRIF1 or show that it participates in neurodegeneration or protein aggregation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and full text were verified. The BioPlex dataset supplies a recurrent LRIF1-CBX3 interaction, while the paper emphasizes that AP-MS networks are cell-line- and state-dependent; the pair should not be generalized without focused endogenous validation.

title: SMCHD1 and LRIF1 converge at the FSHD-associated D4Z4 repeat and LRIF1 promoter yet display different modes of action.
review_notes: PubMed identity and full text were verified. The study refines LRIF1's human D4Z4 mechanism, distinguishes auxiliary repression from establishment of the underlying chromatin state, and provides long-isoform/autoregulatory evidence across human myoblast, myocyte, fibroblast, and cell-line contexts.

title: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record for human LRIF1 (Q5T3J3)
review_notes: Reviewed source record for LRIF1 identity, the C1orf103/RIF1/HBiX1 aliases, two alternative splice products, PXVxL HP1-binding motif, nuclear and chromosome locations, and primary-reference cross-links. CAF-1 is not listed as an LRIF1 alias and is a distinct chromatin-assembly complex.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Machine-source reference for the IBA annotations; it documents the phylogenetic inference method rather than direct LRIG1 experiments.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Machine-source reference for the UniProt subcellular-location mapping; it is not primary experimental evidence.

title: LRIG1 restricts growth factor signaling by enhancing receptor ubiquitylation and degradation.
review_notes: Direct human mechanistic evidence for ErbB association, c-Cbl recruitment, receptor ubiquitylation/degradation, and membrane topology.

title: The leucine-rich repeat protein LRIG1 is a negative regulator of ErbB family receptor tyrosine kinases.
review_notes: Direct human ErbB-family evidence, but only the abstract is cached; detailed assay interpretation should remain bounded to the reported transfection systems.

title: LRIG1 is a novel negative regulator of the Met receptor and opposes Met and Her2 synergy.
review_notes: Direct human MET evidence with both LRIG1 overexpression and knockdown; the paper explicitly distinguishes this mechanism from CBL-dependent ErbB regulation.

title: Lrig1 is an endogenous inhibitor of Ret receptor tyrosine kinase activation, downstream signaling, and biological responses to GDNF.
review_notes: Direct RET-pathway evidence, but only the abstract is cached. The reported mechanism suppresses ligand binding and activation and does not establish RET degradation.

title: LRIG1 negatively regulates the oncogenic EGF receptor mutant EGFRvIII.
review_notes: Direct evidence in human glioblastoma cells; the oncogenic EGFRvIII context and Cbl-independent mechanism must not be generalized to every ErbB receptor.

title: Paracrine regulation of growth factor signaling by shed leucine-rich repeats and immunoglobulin-like domains 1.
review_notes: Direct evidence for a soluble, non-cell-autonomous LRIG1 product; abstract-only evidence does not establish a single obligatory protease or isoform.

title: The pan-ErbB negative regulator Lrig1 is an intestinal stem cell marker that functions as a tumor suppressor.
review_notes: Strong in vivo mouse intestinal evidence. It supports a context-specific tumor-suppressor role but is not direct evidence for a universal human cancer function.

title: Leucine-rich repeat and immunoglobulin domain-containing protein-1 (Lrig1) negative regulatory action toward ErbB receptor tyrosine kinases is opposed by leucine-rich repeat and immunoglobulin domain-containing protein 3 (Lrig3).
review_notes: The abstract verifies functional opposition and cross-talk. Because the cache is abstract-only, full physical-interaction details underlying curated IPI records are deferred to the original curator rather than rejected.

title: USP8 modulates ubiquitination of LRIG1 for Met degradation.
review_notes: Direct human-cell mechanistic evidence, specifically in an antibody-induced MET degradation paradigm; it should not be presented as the sole basal mechanism.

title: LRIG1 extracellular domain: structure and function analysis.
review_notes: Important direct negative result that makes LRIG1-EGFR interaction and inhibition assay-dependent; it does not erase positive evidence from other systems.

title: A protein interaction network centered on leucine-rich repeats and immunoglobulin-like domains 1 (LRIG1) regulates growth factor receptors.
review_notes: Useful LRIG1-centered network study, but most interactions are screen-derived and the receptor assays use triple overexpression in HEK293 cells.

title: LRIG1 negatively regulates RET mutants and is downregulated in thyroid cancer.
review_notes: Direct RET-mutant biochemistry plus human tumor expression and a negative mouse-model result; together these prevent an unconditional pan-cancer tumor-suppressor claim.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Valid machine-source interaction paper, but the LRIG1-LRIG3 hit is screen-level and does not by itself define a specific LRIG1 molecular function.

title: Lrig1 and Lrig3 cooperate to control Ret receptor signaling, sensory axonal growth and epidermal innervation.
review_notes: In vivo mouse evidence for tissue-specific LRIG1/LRIG3 redundancy in RET signaling; it does not imply that paralogs are interchangeable in human ErbB regulation.

title: MET binds LRIG1
review_notes: Current Reactome event text, cross-checked against its cited primary MET studies; it combines basal and SAIT301-induced contexts that should remain distinguishable.

title: LRIG1 undergoes ubiquitination
review_notes: Correct human pathway event; LRIG1 is the ubiquitination substrate, not the ubiquitin ligase.

title: USP8 deubiquitinates LRIG1
review_notes: Correct human pathway event supported by the primary USP8 study; it describes regulation of LRIG1 rather than an LRIG1 catalytic activity.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Live Gene Ontology reference page verified. This is the provenance method for LRIG2's three IBA rows; the individual PANTHER/WITH-FROM source sets were adjudicated in the annotation reviews rather than treated as LRIG2-specific experiments.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Live Gene Ontology reference page verified. This mapping method accounts for LRIG2's cytoplasm and plasma-membrane IEA rows; it is method provenance, not an independent experiment.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Live Gene Ontology reference page verified. This is the method source for six LRIG2 IEA rows, all transferred from mouse Lrig2 rather than LRIG1 or LRIG3; species transfer remains explicit in their reviews.

title: Characterization and tissue-specific expression of human LRIG2.
review_notes: PubMed record and cached abstract verified; full text is unavailable in the cache. This is direct human LRIG2 characterization, although the localization and glycosylation experiments used heterologous COS-7 expression.

title: LRIG2 mutations cause urofacial syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed record and cached abstract verified; full text is unavailable in the cache. The human genetics and fetal-bladder localization support developmental importance but do not identify LRIG2's molecular activity.

title: In vivo analysis of Lrig genes reveals redundant and independent functions in the inner ear.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC record and cached full text verified. This is direct mouse Lrig2 genetics supporting same-ortholog auditory transfer, not direct human evidence; it also supplies an explicit warning against transferring LRIG1/LRIG3 mechanisms.

title: Soluble LRIG2 ectodomain is released from glioblastoma cells and promotes the proliferation and inhibits the apoptosis of glioblastoma cells in vitro and in vivo in a similar manner to the full-length LRIG2.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC record and cached full text verified. The direct EGFR interaction is informative, but signaling and growth conclusions are bounded to engineered human U87/U251 glioblastoma cells and mouse xenografts; they do not establish a general role in normal human physiology. The paper explicitly reports the LRIG2 phenotype as opposite to LRIG1 in these glioblastoma models.

title: Lrig2 Negatively Regulates Ectodomain Shedding of Axon Guidance Receptors by ADAM Proteases.
review_notes: PubMed record and cached abstract verified; full text is unavailable in the cache. This is direct Lrig2 neuronal mechanism evidence, but it is not direct normal-human evidence and should support mouse-ortholog transfers only within that species/context boundary.

title: LRIG2 promotes the proliferation and cell cycle progression of glioblastoma cells in vitro and in vivo through enhancing PDGFRβ signaling.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC record and both corrigenda were reviewed. PMID:30942453 corrects only the second author's given name. PMID:35014687 replaces duplicated p-Akt and Cyclin D1 panels in Fig. 7 after repeating the experiment and states that the conclusions remain supported; it does not alter the Fig. 8 colocalization/co-IP evidence. Direct PDGFRB interaction and signaling effects remain supported in engineered human U87 glioblastoma cells and mouse xenografts, not normal physiology. The paper's mouse-MEF comparison makes cell-type transfer unsafe.

title: [Corrigendum] LRIG2 promotes the proliferation and cell cycle progression of glioblastoma cells in vitro and in vivo through enhancing PDGFRβ signaling.
review_notes: The notice changes Minghai Dong to Minhai Dong and reports no figure, data, or conclusion correction.

title: [Corrigendum] LRIG2 promotes the proliferation and cell cycle progression of glioblastoma cells in vitro and in vivo through enhancing PDGFRβ signaling.
review_notes: The notice identifies Fig. 7 p-Akt/Cyclin D1 panels as the corrected material and states that the main conclusions remain supported. It does not correct Fig. 8 colocalization or reciprocal co-IP.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Supports mapped membrane locations, not autonomous receptor activity.

title: Lrig3 regulates neural crest formation in Xenopus by modulating Fgf and Wnt signaling pathways.
review_notes: Primary Xenopus evidence; useful developmental context but not a direct human annotation or proof of a single receptor mechanism.

title: Cross-repressive interactions between Lrig3 and netrin 1 shape the architecture of the inner ear.
review_notes: Decisive mouse developmental genetics; species and tissue boundaries are retained.

title: Inhibition of LRIG3 gene expression via RNA interference modulates the proliferation, cell cycle, cell apoptosis, adhesion and invasion of glioblastoma cell (GL15).
review_notes: Direct human glioma-cell perturbation, but not normal physiology or a specific molecular target.

title: Vertebrate Lrig3-ErbB interactions occur in vitro but are unlikely to play a role in Lrig3-dependent inner ear morphogenesis.
review_notes: Supports ERBB association while experimentally separating it from the inner-ear developmental mechanism.

title: Comparison of tear protein levels in breast cancer patients and healthy controls using a de novo proteomic approach.
review_notes: Pooled human tear-fluid proteomics; it does not establish constitutive secretion of intact LRIG3.

title: Leucine-rich repeat and immunoglobulin domain-containing protein-1 (Lrig1) negative regulatory action toward ErbB receptor tyrosine kinases is opposed by leucine-rich repeat and immunoglobulin domain-containing protein 3 (Lrig3).
review_notes: Direct human-cell study of LRIG1-LRIG3 cross-talk and ERBB stability; detailed assays remain under curator deference because the cache is abstract-only.

title: The Prognostic and Therapeutic Potential of LRIG3 and Soluble LRIG3 in Glioblastoma.
review_notes: Direct glioma-cell, xenograft, and patient-fluid evidence; tumor and therapeutic contexts are not generalized into normal physiology.

title: LRIG3 Suppresses Angiogenesis by Regulating the PI3K/AKT/VEGFA Signaling Pathway in Glioma.
review_notes: Direct glioma-model evidence bounded to tumor and xenograft systems.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Credible screen evidence, but not a standalone mechanism or stable endogenous complex.

title: Glioma-derived LRIG3 interacts with NETO2 in tumor-associated macrophages to modulate microenvironment and suppress tumor growth.
review_notes: Targeted interaction and functional NETO2 perturbation support a tumor-microenvironment mechanism, not a universal physiological pathway.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: This is the correct method reference for manual ISS transfer. The rat Lrit1 donor and its experimental ER evidence were reviewed separately.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: This is the correct PANTHER IBA method reference. Its LRIT1-family sources were checked against exact mouse, rat, and human SF9 members.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: This correctly documents the UniProt subcellular-location mapping. The dendrite result is marked over-annotated and source-weak because apposition to bipolar-cell dendritic tips does not establish LRIT1 protein within dendrites.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: This is the correct Ensembl Compara method reference; Q8K099 is the exact mouse Lrit1 ortholog with direct synaptic-cleft and synapse evidence.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: The combined IEA uses the rat ortholog and ER vocabulary mapping. It is mechanically sound but represents a non-core localization context.

title: Molecular cloning of a novel membrane glycoprotein, pal, specifically expressed in photoreceptor cells of the retina and containing leucine-rich repeat.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. Direct localization and topology experiments concern rat Pal or rat Pal expressed in HeLa cells; the human result is cloning and chromosomal mapping only.

title: Lrit1, a Retinal Transmembrane Protein, Regulates Selective Synapse Formation in Cone Photoreceptor Cells and Visual Acuity.
review_notes: Title and abstract were checked. The paper directly studies mouse Lrit1; the human annotations derived here are explicit orthology transfers. The local cache is abstract-only, so detailed assay claims defer to the source curator.

title: LRIT1 Modulates Adaptive Changes in Synaptic Communication of Cone Photoreceptors.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. The study directly establishes mouse Lrit1 binding, localization, and cone-synaptic physiology; human claims must remain explicit orthology transfers.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: This is the correct method reference for mapping the UniProt membrane controlled vocabulary to GO:0016020. The mapping is mechanically sound but broad and based on predicted type-I topology rather than direct human LRIT2 localization.

title: The status, quality, and expansion of the NIH full-length cDNA project: the Mammalian Gene Collection (MGC).
review_notes: PubMed metadata and the cached paper were checked. UniProt uses an MGC cDNA from this resource to support LRIT2 isoform 2 and its sequence variation, but the article is a collection-wide resource paper and does not compare LRIT2 isoform expression, localization, or function.

title: The full-ORF clone resource of the German cDNA Consortium.
review_notes: PubMed metadata and full cached text were checked. UniProt links the retinal isoform-1 LRIT2 cDNA to this human ORF resource; the publication itself does not establish endogenous retinal protein localization or function.

title: Lrit1, a Retinal Transmembrane Protein, Regulates Selective Synapse Formation in Cone Photoreceptor Cells and Visual Acuity.
review_notes: The title and cached abstract were checked. They directly concern mouse Lrit1, not human LRIT2. UniProt transfers an LRIT1-LRIT2 association from the mouse Lrit2 record linked to this paper, but the abstract-only cache does not expose that assay; no LRIT1 synaptic mechanism is transferred to LRIT2 here.

title: Novel eye genes systematically discovered through an integrated analysis of mouse transcriptomes and phenome.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. The Lrit2 result is a zebrafish morpholino phenotype selected from a mouse coexpression prediction, not a targeted human or mouse LRIT2 mechanism. It supports a bounded ocular-development hypothesis but not a human core function.

title: Efficient in vivo labeling of endogenous proteins with SMART delineates retina cellular and synaptic organization.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. This is direct mouse LRIT3 localization evidence and is included only as a paralog boundary after a broader LRIT-family literature search; it does not support LRIT2 localization or function.

title: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record for human LRIT2 (A6NDA9)
review_notes: Reviewed source for human sequence, type-I topology, domain boundaries, two alternative products, retinal cDNA provenance, and the mouse-orthology-derived LRIT1 association. The subunit statement is explicitly ECO:0000250 and therefore is not direct evidence for a human complex or function.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Correct method reference for manual ISS transfer. W8DXL4 is the exact mouse Lrit3 ortholog, but perikaryon is marked over-annotated because current tagging supports the presynaptic photoreceptor terminal instead of a somatic pool.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Correct UniProt subcellular-location mapping reference. ER membrane is retained as biosynthetic non-core context, whereas perikaryon is marked over-annotated for lack of positive support under the current presynaptic model.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Correct Ensembl Compara method reference and exact mouse ortholog. The generic cell-tip result is retained as non-core because later endogenous tagging resolves LRIT3 to the presynaptic photoreceptor side.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: The combined IEA sources are mechanically traceable, and direct human antibody staining supports retaining dendrite as non-core. Later mouse tagging refines the functional protein to the presynaptic photoreceptor side.

title: Leucine-rich repeat, immunoglobulin-like and transmembrane domain 3 (LRIT3) is a modulator of FGFR1.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. This is direct human HEK293 overexpression evidence for FGFR1 trafficking/signaling modulation, but it is context-limited and independent of the retinal loss-of-function mechanism.

title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies LRIT3 mutations as a cause of autosomal-recessive complete congenital stationary night blindness.
review_notes: PubMed metadata and the cached abstract were checked. This is the decisive direct human disease and retinal-localization source. The cache is abstract-only, and later mouse endogenous-tagging data refine the puncta to a presynaptic origin.

title: LRIT3 Differentially Affects Connectivity and Synaptic Transmission of Cones to ON- and OFF-Bipolar Cells.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. Human physiology is included, but the detailed structural and mechanistic experiments are in the mouse nob6 model.

title: Presynaptic Expression of LRIT3 Transsynaptically Organizes the Postsynaptic Glutamate Signaling Complex Containing TRPM1.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. Photoreceptor-specific rescue supplies the strongest causal evidence for the presynaptic organizer model in mouse retina; human process annotations remain explicit orthology transfers.

title: LRIT3 is Required for Nyctalopin Expression and Normal ON and OFF Pathway Signaling in the Retina.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. The study supplies mouse co-IP, localization, knockout, and electrophysiology evidence; it does not establish a purified binary interface or direct human retinal mechanism.

title: Efficient in vivo labeling of endogenous proteins with SMART delineates retina cellular and synaptic organization.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. Endogenous tagging resolves the cell-side ambiguity left by earlier puncta apposed to bipolar dendritic tips.

title: Domain-specific functions of LRIT3 in synaptic assembly and retinal signal transmission.
review_notes: Full text and title were checked. The 2026 mouse rAAV deletion-rescue study is strong structure-function evidence, but its proposed LRR-nyctalopin and Ig-TRPM1 contacts remain mechanistic models rather than purified direct interfaces.

title: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record for human LRIT3 (Q3SXY7)
review_notes: Reviewed source for human sequence, topology, domains, alternative products, disease, localization, and curated literature links. Mouse-orthology statements and direct human evidence are distinguished explicitly in the record.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: This is the current GO reference for PANTHER phylogenetic inference. It documents the annotation method rather than primary LRMDA biology; the biological transfer still requires LRMDA-subfamily and species review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: This is the current GO reference for Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence curation. It explains the provenance of the nucleoplasm record, but PMID:36334630 reports that available anti-OCA7 antibodies gave suspect nuclear and random cytoplasmic signal. The row is therefore retained only as a source record and marked over-annotated.

title: Mutations in c10orf11, a melanocyte-differentiation gene, cause autosomal-recessive albinism.
review_notes: Foundational primary evidence combining human genetics and fetal-tissue localization with zebrafish morpholino/rescue experiments. The functional perturbation is zebrafish, not human or mouse, and the result supports pigment-cell development/differentiation without isolating a direct melanin-synthesis reaction. The local cache is abstract-only.

title: OCA7 is a melanosome membrane protein that defines pigmentation by regulating early stages of melanosome biogenesis.
review_notes: Direct human MNT1-cell evidence for melanosomal localization and a cell-autonomous role in organelle maturation and pigmentation. These data define a pigment-synthesis/biogenesis mechanism in differentiated cells; they do not independently establish embryonic melanocyte differentiation or normal in-vivo human physiology. Full text was reviewed. The direct RAB32/RAB38-binding and localization constructs used the 226-residue form amplified from MNT1 cells; the relationship of that tested form to reviewed Q9H2I8 is unresolved, while the knockout phenotype itself remains gene-level evidence.

title: Identification of a RAB32-LRMDA-Commander membrane trafficking complex reveals the molecular mechanism of human oculocutaneous albinism type 7.
review_notes: Direct biochemical, cell-biological, and mechanistic evidence for an RAB32-LRMDA-Commander adaptor complex in human-cell models. A critical proteoform boundary applies: every experiment used A0A087WWI0 (226 aa), whereas the reviewed Q9H2I8 record is 198 aa. The source files do not establish how these forms are related, so sequence-numbered interfaces belong directly to the tested longer construct and should not be asserted as endogenous Q9H2I8 results without further evidence.

title: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record for human LRMDA (Q9H2I8)
review_notes: Reviewed record for the 198-residue human target, its LRR architecture, OCA7 association, and absence of a curated alternative-products section. It does not by itself establish a molecular activity, and it must not be conflated with the 226-residue forms used for the direct interaction and localization work in PMID:36334630 and PMID:41038817; their sequence relationship is not established by the reviewed record.

title: HIV-tat induces formation of an LRP-PSD-95- NMDAR-nNOS complex that promotes apoptosis in neurons and astrocytes.
review_notes: NeuroAIDS paper supports LRP-containing postsynaptic/NMDAR/nNOS complex formation but is infection/toxicity context rather than core LRP1 function.

title: SRF and myocardin regulate LRP-mediated amyloid-beta clearance in brain vascular cells.
review_notes: Full-text AD vascular paper supporting LRP-mediated amyloid-beta cerebrovascular clearance.

title: Prion protein-mediated toxicity of amyloid-β oligomers requires lipid rafts and the transmembrane LRP1.
review_notes: Full-text AD Aβ oligomer paper supporting LRP1-dependent Aβ oligomer internalization/toxicity context.

title: The LDL-receptor-related protein, LRP, is an apolipoprotein E-binding protein.
review_notes: Primary paper supporting LRP as an apolipoprotein E-binding cell-surface receptor.

title: The dynamic uptake and release of SOD3 from intracellular stores in macrophages modulates the inflammatory response.
review_notes: Full-text macrophage SOD3 paper supports inflammatory/endocytic ligand handling context, non-core for LRP1.

title: Surface location and high affinity for calcium of a 500-kd liver membrane protein closely related to the LDL-receptor suggest a physiological role as lipoprotein receptor.
review_notes: Primary LDL receptor-related protein paper supporting cell-surface localization, calcium binding, and recycling lipoprotein receptor function.

title: Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and vitronectin promote the cellular clearance of thrombin by low density lipoprotein receptor-related proteins 1 and 2.
review_notes: Primary endocytosis paper supporting LRP1/LRP2-mediated clearance of thrombin-PAI-1 complexes.

title: Manual LRP1 review notes
review_notes: Manual notes document the deep-research timeout and summarize cached UniProt, PANTHER, GOA, and publication evidence used for this review.

title: UniProt text export for LRP1 (Q07954)
review_notes: Local UniProt record directly supports LRP1 endocytic receptor function, ligand classes, tau/MAPT receptor activity, localization, subunit processing, and tissue expression.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Canonical PAINT provenance for the two IBA annotations. The LRP10 lipoprotein-receptor inference has a narrow mouse-ortholog donor, whereas the plasma-membrane inference uses a broad mixed LDLR-family donor set; those different propagation scopes are handled in the annotation reviews.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Correct method provenance for the Ensembl Compara transfer from mouse Lrp10. Orthology is appropriate, but the transferred LDL-particle term is broader than the beta-VLDL cargo tested in the source experiment.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: Correct provenance for the ARBA vesicle-mediated-transport annotation. It is an automated rule rather than independent experimental evidence, but the broad process is consistent with direct LRP10 trafficking studies.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Correct combined-IEA provenance for generic membrane localization. The ordered sources include an ARBA rule, mouse Lrp10 identifiers, and a UniProt subcellular-location statement.

title: A novel low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein mediating cellular uptake of apolipoprotein E-enriched beta-VLDL in vitro.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary study and the decisive experimental source for the mouse-ortholog lipoprotein-uptake inference. It supports transfer of a beta-VLDL receptor activity within the narrow LRP10 subfamily, not direct human evidence or blanket LDL-particle receptor activity.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed identifier and title are verified, and this is the stated source of the seeded HDA membrane annotation. Only the abstract is cached and it does not name LRP10 or provide the protein/peptide table, so the gene-specific detection cannot be independently checked here; curator deference is retained.

title: LDLR-related protein 10 (LRP10) regulates amyloid precursor protein (APP) trafficking and processing: evidence for a role in Alzheimer's disease.
review_notes: Direct human primary evidence for APP binding, TGN/endosome/plasma-membrane cycling, DXXLL-dependent retrograde trafficking, and effects on APP processing. Most assays use tagged or overexpressed proteins in cultured HEK293, HeLa, or SH-SY5Y cells, so the disease interpretation is not a universal in-vivo mechanism.

title: LRP10 genetic variants in familial Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies: a genome-wide linkage and sequencing study.
review_notes: PubMed-verified human genetic and functional study. It supports variant-specific effects and a proposed loss-of-function model, but the segregation evidence is explicitly limited, one carrier occurred among controls, and disease association does not establish LRP10's normal core molecular function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Correct HuRI source for the 21 IntAct/GOA LRP10 interaction partners. The paper establishes a high-throughput binary-screen resource; it does not by itself establish native-tissue complexes or a shared mechanistic function for the diverse partner set.

title: LRP10 interacts with SORL1 in the intracellular vesicle trafficking pathway in non-neuronal brain cells and localises to Lewy bodies in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies.
review_notes: Strong direct human evidence using post-mortem brain and control iPSC-derived cells with knockout-validated antibodies. It establishes cell-type and trafficking-compartment context plus an SORL1 association; Lewy-body localization and disease hypotheses remain pathological context, not proof of a normal neuronal core function.

title: LRP10 and α-synuclein transmission in Lewy body diseases.
review_notes: Direct mechanistic evidence for extracellular-vesicle release, uptake, and context-dependent effects on α-synuclein, plus a patient splice-variant model. The authors explicitly frame the work as initial and identify major model limitations; it should not be generalized into a constitutive normal LRP10 secretion or α-synuclein-regulation function.

title: UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot record for human LRP10 (Q7Z4F1)
review_notes: Current reviewed human record used for identity, topology, domain, alternative-product, interaction, and family boundaries. Isoform 2 deletes residues 557-713, but the record supplies no demonstrated isoform-specific function. There is no experimental PDB cross-reference; the structure link is AlphaFoldDB only. The function comment assigns apoE-lipoprotein uptake by similarity and should not be mistaken for direct human evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: This is the current UniProt subcellular-location mapping source for the membrane IEA. Live QuickGO and the local TSV both carry SL-0162, and the reviewed Q86VZ4 topology independently supports the broad location.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: This is the current Ensembl Compara source for seven stress-process IEAs. Live donor tracing resolves both WITH/FROM identifiers to mouse Lrp11 and the source terms to IEP evidence from PMID:25262641.

title: The status, quality, and expansion of the NIH full-length cDNA project: the Mammalian Gene Collection (MGC).
review_notes: The paper is a cDNA-resource report rather than an LRP11 functional study. Its relevance is limited to the brain- and skin-derived full-length cDNA sequences cited by the reviewed UniProt record for isoforms 1 and 2.

title: Functional specialization of beta-arrestin interactions revealed by proteomic analysis.
review_notes: The PMID and paper identity are verified, but the LRP11-specific hit and its phosphorylation/localization interpretation reside in supplementary tables absent from the cache. The experimental GO rows therefore remain undecided.

title: Genetic regulatory network analysis reveals that low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 11 is involved in stress responses in mice.
review_notes: Verified as the actual mouse donor evidence behind all seven human stress IEAs. The paper supports stress-associated expression and a candidate gene network, but not causal human LRP11 involvement in seven distinct processes.

title: The role of low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 11 as a tumor promoter in cervical cancer.
review_notes: Direct human knockdown and xenograft evidence is available in full text. These are strong disease-context phenotypes but should not be promoted to a constitutive receptor function without a defined ligand or proximal mechanism.

title: LRP11 activates β-catenin to induce PD-L1 expression in prostate cancer.
review_notes: Direct human perturbation supports a cancer-context LRP11-beta-catenin-PD-L1 regulatory axis. Only the abstract is cached, so mechanistic details beyond the stated gain/loss and antibody experiments are not inferred.

title: LRP11 promotes stem-like T cells via MAPK13-mediated TCF1 phosphorylation, enhancing anti-PD1 immunotherapy.
review_notes: Full text verifies mouse tumor/T-cell experiments, a mouse Lrp11 chimeric receptor, and selected human PBMC assays. It is the strongest ligand-linked mechanistic study, but species and immunotherapy context must remain explicit.

title: Reviewed UniProtKB entry for human LRP11 (Q86VZ4)

review_notes: Classic study linking low serum MBP (a Ca2+-dependent serum lectin) to a common opsonic defect that purified MBP corrects dose-dependently. Supports MBL as a Ca2+-dependent lectin acting at the pathogen surface and in opsonization/innate defense.
