review_notes: Higher oligomers (tetramers) of the MBL homotrimer bind microbes and MASPs more strongly and activate complement better than trimers/dimers - establishing oligomerization as central to MBL function. Supports identical-protein (self) association and the complement-activation role.

title: C1q and Mannose-Binding Lectin Interact with CR1 in the Same Region on CCP24-25 Modules.
review_notes: Localizes the MBL (and C1q) binding site on CR1 to CCP24-25; supports a specific receptor interaction.

title: C1q/TNF-Related Protein 6 Is a Pattern Recognition Molecule That Recruits Collectin-11 from the Complement System to Ligands.
review_notes: Primarily about CTRP6/collectin-11; MBL appears as part of the broader collectin system. Background relevance.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome (HuRI). Generic, low-specificity source of the GO:0005515 protein-binding IPI; not informative about MBL molecular function.

title: Complement Activation and Thrombin Generation by MBL Bound to β2-Glycoprotein I.
review_notes: MBL binds beta2-glycoprotein I and can trigger complement/thrombin generation; a specific ligand interaction linking MBL to coagulation crosstalk.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Generic source of the protein-binding IPI; not informative about MBL molecular function.

title: Recognition and inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 by humoral innate immunity pattern recognition molecules.
review_notes: MBL binds SARS-CoV-2 trimeric spike (including VoC) in a glycan- and calcium-dependent manner, activates the lectin pathway after binding, and inhibits the virus in vitro; MBL2 polymorphisms associate with COVID-19 severity. Strong support for calcium-dependent carbohydrate/glycoprotein recognition, PRR activity, antiviral innate immunity and lectin-pathway activation.

title: Isolation and characterization of a mannan-binding protein from human serum.
review_notes: Original isolation of human serum MBP; defines it as a Ca2+-dependent serum lectin specific for mannose and N-acetylglucosamine with high-affinity, saturable, reversible mannan binding (Kd ~2.3e-9 M). Foundational support for the core D-mannose/carbohydrate binding MF.

title: Structure and function of mannan-binding proteins isolated from human liver and serum.
review_notes: Purifies liver and serum MBP; shows both are liver-synthesized, secreted, differ in oligomer number (L-MBP ~9, S-MBP ~18 subunits), and that complement activation requires higher oligomerization and the collagen-like-domain N-terminus. Supports secreted location and oligomer-dependent complement activation.

title: Binding of mannan-binding protein to various bacterial pathogens of meningitis.
review_notes: MBP (a Ca2+-dependent plasma lectin) binds bacterial surfaces; binding inhibited by mannose and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine. Supports Ca2+-dependent carbohydrate recognition at the microbial cell surface and defense against bacteria.

title: A second serine protease associated with mannan-binding lectin that activates complement.
review_notes: Identifies MASP-2 and establishes that MBL binds microbial carbohydrates and activates complement through associated serine proteases (analogous to C1r/C1s), with MBL structurally related to C1q. Foundational support for PRR activity and lectin-pathway initiation.

title: MBL binds to repetitive carbohydrate structures on the surfaces of viruses, bacteria, fungi, and protozoa
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the core MBL recognition event - binding repetitive microbial surface carbohydrate. Supports the carbohydrate-binding MF and extracellular location.

title: MBL2 binds SARS-CoV-2 S
review_notes: Reactome reaction for MBL2 binding SARS-CoV-2 spike; consistent with PMID:35102342.

title: FutureHouse Falcon deep-research report for MBL2 (P11226)
review_notes: AI deep-research synthesis used as a starting point. Its core conclusions (Ca2+-dependent carbohydrate binding, lectin-pathway complement activation, innate defense/opsonization as core; cytoplasm/cytosol/nucleus/synapse/apoptosis-execution/pyroptosis/neuronal roles as high-risk and unsupported) agree with the primary literature reviewed here, and all its cited sources resolve to real published papers (no preprint-only/unresolvable PMIDs). Used to corroborate, not as primary evidence.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for MBL2 GO:0043129
review_notes: Focused OpenScientist report supports removing GO:0043129 as collectin-family surfactant-homeostasis over-propagation from pulmonary surfactant collectins to serum MBL2.

title: The molecular basis of 3-methylcrotonylglycinuria, a disorder of leucine catabolism.
review_notes: Primary molecular characterization of the human MCCA (MCCC1) gene; PubMed-verified. Establishes the alpha subunit as biotin-containing and the leucine-catabolic role of MCC.

title: The molecular basis of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency.
review_notes: Independent primary characterization of MCCA/MCCB and disease-causing mutations; PubMed-verified.

title: Human biotin-containing subunit of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase gene (MCCA): cDNA sequence, genomic organization, localization to chromosomal band 3q27, and expression.
review_notes: Defines the domain architecture (biotin carboxylase + biotin-carrier) and mitochondrial localization of MCCC1; PubMed-verified.

title: Mitochondrial targeting signals and mature peptides of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Direct experimental evidence for mitochondrial matrix localization and transit peptide cleavage; PubMed-verified.

title: Expression, purification, characterization of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (MCCC).
review_notes: Biochemical characterization of the assembled MCC holoenzyme; basis for the IDA carboxylase-activity, complex, and matrix-localization annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Structure and function of biotin-dependent carboxylases.
review_notes: Family-level structure/function review; supports the modular BC/CT/BCCP architecture but is not gene-specific experimental evidence for MCCC1.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial protein-interaction mapping; source of an IntAct protein-binding IPI. MCCC1 is one node in a high-throughput dataset; not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex high-throughput AP-MS interactome; source of an IntAct protein-binding IPI (partner OXCT2). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Leucine regulates autophagy via acetylation of the mTORC1 component raptor.
review_notes: Knockdown/autophagy study confirming MCCC1's role as the leucine-metabolizing enzyme; it does not itself assay carboxylase catalytic activity (UniProt attaches the ECO:0000269 catalytic-activity claim to this paper alongside PMID:17360195).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 dual proteome-scale interactome; source of IntAct protein-binding IPIs (partners OXCT2, MCCC2). High-throughput, not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteomics; supports mitochondrial localization at proteome scale (HTP evidence code).

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-mapping resource; source of an IntAct protein-binding IPI (partner MCCC2). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: The molecular basis of 3-methylcrotonylglycinuria, a disorder of leucine catabolism.
review_notes: Full text cached and verified. Establishes MCC as a heteromeric alpha/beta biotin-dependent carboxylase of leucine catabolism, that the beta subunit binds the acyl-CoA substrate, characterizes the human MCCB gene (563-residue polypeptide), and demonstrates in vivo involvement of MCC in leucine catabolism via a fungal MCCA-null model.

title: The molecular basis of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified title matches; parallel molecular characterization of human MCC deficiency and MCCC2 disease variants. Cache is abstract-only; claims (carboxylase activity, complex membership) are consistent with the well-established enzymology and corroborated by the IDA evidence.

title: Mitochondrial targeting signals and mature peptides of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase.
review_notes: Abstract-cached; directly supports mitochondrial matrix import of MCCbeta via a cleavable N-terminal presequence (cleavage Ala22/Tyr23), grounding the matrix localization annotations.

title: Expression, purification, characterization of human 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (MCCC).
review_notes: Abstract-cached. Direct enzymatic characterization of purified recombinant human MCC (alpha/beta complex, ~500-800 kDa, 1:1 stoichiometry, kcat ~4.0 s-1, KM values), grounding the carboxylase-activity and complex-membership annotations.

title: Structure and function of biotin-dependent carboxylases.
review_notes: Review of biotin-dependent carboxylase structure/function; supports the multi-subunit (BC/CT/BCCP) architecture of MCC and the carboxyltransferase role of the beta subunit.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial interaction mapping; the MCCC2-MCCC1 interaction it captures is real but only supports a generic protein-binding annotation better represented by the carboxylase complex term.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MCCC1). Contextual, not function-establishing for MCCC2.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP); corroborates mitochondrial localization of MCCC2 by high-throughput proteomics.

title: CFTR interactome mapping using the mammalian membrane two-hybrid high-throughput screening system.
review_notes: High-throughput CFTR-interactome screen; the CFTR-MCCC2 IPI has no established biological relationship to this matrix enzyme and is likely non-specific.

title: Differential CFTR-Interactome Proximity Labeling Procedures Identify Enrichment in Multiple SLC Transporters.
review_notes: CFTR proximity-labeling screen; source of a generic CFTR-MCCC2 protein-binding IPI, not indicative of MCCC2 function.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map genomics study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (MCCC1). Contextual.

title: 3-Methylcrotonyl-coenzyme A carboxylase deficiency in Amish/Mennonite adults identified by detection of increased acylcarnitines in blood spots of their children.
review_notes: Abstract-cached. Documents isolated MCC deficiency in humans, underpinning the IMP link between loss of MCC and disrupted leucine catabolism.

review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) inference for the MCEE ortholog group; consistent with the well-established epimerase function and mitochondrial localisation.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt

review_notes: EC 5.1.99.1 / RHEA:20553 to GO:0004493 mapping; the EC and Rhea assignments are experimentally supported (PMID:11481338) so this electronic mapping is correct.

title: Identification of the human methylmalonyl-CoA racemase gene based on the analysis of prokaryotic gene arrangements. Implications for decoding the human genome.

review_notes: Establishes MCEE deficiency as a human disease (MIM:251120); referenced in UniProt (INVOLVEMENT IN MCEED). Not cited as an existing GOA annotation but relevant to MCEE's biological role. Cached publication not available (abstract-only); title matches the UniProt cross-reference.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Systematic proteome-scale binary (Y2H) interactome map (HI-II-14). Source of a high-throughput "protein binding" IPI; no MCEE-specific functional insight.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome-perturbation study; source of a high-throughput "protein binding" IPI, uninformative for MCEE molecular function.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Large-scale variant/PPI screen; source of a high-throughput "protein binding" IPI, not a targeted study of MCEE.

review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome (Y2H); source of a high-throughput "protein binding" IPI, uninformative for MCEE function.

title: D-methylmalonyl-CoA <=> L-methylmalonyl-CoA

title: Propionyl-CoA catabolism
review_notes: Reactome pathway placing MCEE in propionyl-CoA catabolism; supports the short-chain fatty acid catabolic process annotation.

title: MCT-1 protein interacts with the cap complex and modulates messenger RNA translational profiles.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; biochemical study establishing MCTS1 cap-complex association and DENR/SUI1 recruitment, supporting its translation-reinitiation role.

title: Activities of Ligatin and MCT-1/DENR in eukaryotic translation initiation and ribosomal recycling.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; reconstitution study establishing the MCTS1/DENR (Ligatin-like) role in eIF2-independent initiator-tRNA recruitment and 40S ribosomal recycling, the gene's core molecular function.

title: DENR-MCTS1 heterodimerization and tRNA recruitment are required for translation reinitiation.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; demonstrates that MCTS1-DENR heterodimerization and tRNA recruitment are required for translation reinitiation, directly supporting the core function.

title: Human MCTS1-dependent translation of JAK2 is essential for IFN-γ immunity to mycobacteria.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; provides the in vivo physiological significance of MCTS1-DENR reinitiation (JAK2 translation, IFN-gamma immunity).

title: Falcon deep research report for MCTS1
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) summary, marked UNVERIFIED pending source-by-source checking. The core MCTS1-specific claims it makes (cytoplasmic, 40S-/ribosome-associated non-canonical reinitiation+recycling factor obligately partnered with DENR; JAK2 5'UTR uORF dependence; impaired recycling on MCTS1 loss) are independently corroborated by the cached full text of Bohlen 2023 (PMID:37875108) and by the existing experimental annotations, so they are reliable. CAVEATS: (1) much of the mechanistic and target-class detail (uORF re-initiation, ATF4, mitotic translation, ~200-240 targets) derives from DENR-centric or MCTS1-DENR-complex work (Castelo-Szekely 2019, Meurs 2024/2025, von Hohenberg 2022, Vasudevan 2020) and should be read as properties of the heterodimer, not of MCTS1 in isolation. (2) The oncogene/cancer claims (PA2G4-P48 stabilization in HNSCC, IL-6/IL-6R/STAT3, EMT/stemness; Sun 2023, Weng 2019) are phenotypic/association-level and do not by themselves establish a distinct MCTS1 molecular function beyond translational control; not used to add or strengthen molecular-function annotations here. None of these cited papers (except PMID:37875108) are in the local publications cache, so their supporting_text was not independently verified.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Large-scale urinary-exosome proteomics; MDH1 detected as one of many abundant cytosolic proteins. Supports only the (over-annotated) exosome localization.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: Genome-wide split-YFP screen for telomere regulators; MDH1 recovered as a TERF1-associating protein. Underpins only the uninformative "protein binding" annotation; biological significance unclear.

title: Comparison of tear protein levels in breast cancer patients and healthy controls using a de novo proteomic approach.
review_notes: Tear-fluid proteomics; MDH1 detected and noted as a glycolysis/TCA enzyme. Supports only the over-annotated extracellular-region localization.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Prostatic-secretion exosome proteomics; MDH1 among ~900 detected proteins. Supports only the over-annotated exosome localization.

title: Biochemical and genetic identity of alpha-keto acid reductase and cytoplasmic malate dehydrogenase from human erythrocytes.
review_notes: Establishes that human cytosolic malate dehydrogenase and the historically described aromatic alpha-keto acid reductase are the same protein; cited by UniProt for EC 1.1.1.37. Supports both the core MDH activity and the promiscuous KAR side activity. Abstract-only cache.

title: MDH1 deficiency is a metabolic disorder of the malate-aspartate shuttle associated with early onset severe encephalopathy.
review_notes: Establishes recessive MDH1 deficiency (DEE88) as a malate-aspartate shuttle disorder, cited by UniProt for FUNCTION and the disease association. Not cached locally; not manually verified.

title: The metabolite alpha-KG induces GSDMC-dependent pyroptosis through death receptor 6-activated caspase-8.
review_notes: UniProt reference for MDH1's reduction of 2-oxoglutarate to 2-hydroxyglutarate (basis of the (S)-2-hydroxyglutarate dehydrogenase side activity). Not cached locally; not manually verified.

title: A hydride transfer complex reprograms NAD metabolism and bypasses senescence.
review_notes: Reports a cytosolic MDH1/ME1/pyruvate-carboxylase hydride transfer complex that transfers reducing equivalents from NADH to NADP+ in cancer/hypoxic cells. Basis for the NAD+/NADP+ metabolic-process and cytoplasm IDA annotations. Abstract-only cache.

title: The malate-aspartate shuttle is important for de novo serine biosynthesis.
review_notes: Genetic disruption of MAS components in HEK293 cells; MDH1-deficient cells show the most severe metabolic disruption, providing IMP support for MDH1's role in the malate-aspartate shuttle. Abstract-only cache.

title: Molecular cloning and mapping of a human cDNA for cytosolic malate dehydrogenase (MDH1).
review_notes: cDNA cloning and chromosomal mapping (2p15) of cytosolic MDH1; supports the cytosol localization. Does NOT support the "malic enzyme activity" molecular function it is cited for (that MF is EC 1.1.1.40, a different enzyme).

title: An NADH-tetrazolium-coupled sensitive assay for malate dehydrogenase in mitochondria and crude tissue homogenates.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false); a sensitive spectrophotometric assay for mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase activity. Used by Reactome as evidence that the MDH2 dimer dehydrogenates malate; supports the NAD-dependent malate dehydrogenase activity annotation.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary-exosome proteomics; detects MDH2 as a background hit. Supports only a likely-contaminant extracellular-exosome location.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: High-throughput B-cell exosome proteomics; MDH2 detected as background. Supports only a likely-contaminant extracellular-exosome location.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial phosphoproteomics; corroborates mitochondrial localization of MDH2.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: High-throughput sperm-nucleus proteomics; the resulting "nucleus" annotation for a mitochondrial matrix enzyme most likely reflects contamination, not a functional nuclear pool.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: mRNA-interactome capture identifying MDH2 as an RNA-binding protein; corroborates the moonlighting RNA-binding activity later validated directly (PMID:38609156).

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: mRNA-bound-proteome capture identifying MDH2 as an RNA-binding protein; corroborates the moonlighting RNA-binding activity.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; MDH2 detected as background. Supports only a likely-contaminant extracellular-exosome location.

title: Mutations in MDH2, Encoding a Krebs Cycle Enzyme, Cause Early-Onset Severe Encephalopathy.
review_notes: Full text available; primary disease/functional paper. Directly establishes MDH2's NAD-dependent malate dehydrogenase activity, its TCA and malate-aspartate-shuttle roles, and support for aerobic respiration.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput high-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization of MDH2.

title: The malate-aspartate shuttle is important for de novo serine biosynthesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Provides IMP evidence for MDH2 involvement in the malate-aspartate shuttle (MDH2 is one of the disrupted MAS components).

title: Cytosolic RNA binding of the mitochondrial TCA cycle enzyme malate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes the moonlighting RNA-binding activity (kept as non-core) and confirms mitochondrial-matrix localization of the metabolic enzyme.

title: Studies on mitochondrial and cytoplasmic malate dehydrogenase in childhood myelodysplastic syndrome.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Old (1983) case study; provides IMP/dosage support linking the chromosome-7 MDH2 locus to mitochondrial malate dehydrogenase activity and malate metabolism.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid interactome map; correctly cited as the source of an IPI row whose partner (UniProtKB:P63010, AP2B1) is now known to be a real, if secondary, MEA1 client. Useful corroboration rather than a functional study.

title: Male-enhanced antigen gene is phylogenetically conserved and expressed at late stages of spermatogenesis.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Lau YF, Chan KM, Sparkes R, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 1989 Nov;86(21):8462-6, doi 10.1073/pnas.86.21.8462; abstract only in the cache. The identifier and title are correct, but the paper does not support the two biological-process annotations drawn from it. It reports cloning, conservation and an expression pattern, and states its functional claim explicitly as a hypothesis; it contains no functional assay of MEA1 in spermatogenesis or gonad development. Flagged MISCITED on that basis rather than for any defect in the paper itself.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Records MEA1 with UniProtKB:Q9BXS5 (AP1M1, the mu1 subunit), which the 2026 mechanistic work confirms as a direct client - an early and correct observation buried under a bare protein binding term.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex affinity-purification interactomes; records both AP1M1 and AP2B1 as MEA1 partners, both independently confirmed in PMID:41559075.

title: Regulation of AP1 adaptor assembly by the bi-handed chaperone MEA1.
review_notes: Verified against PubMed as Wan C, Wu J, Ouyang Y, Puscher H, Tian Y, Li S, Yin Q, Shen J, Nat Commun 2026 Jan 20;17(1), doi 10.1038/s41467-026-68662-3, PMC12923701; full text cached. The sole primary source for MEA1's molecular function, and a well-controlled one: heterologous reconstitution in E. coli, domain mapping with interface point mutants, endogenous co-IP, knockout-and-rescue in two human cell lines, and cargo-trafficking readouts. The AlphaFold-derived interface details are predictions, but each was tested by mutagenesis. Still a single study and a single laboratory; independent replication of the dual-chaperone collision model is not yet available.

title: Cryopyrin and pyrin activate caspase-1, but not NF-kappaB, via ASC oligomerization.
review_notes: Establishes the pro-inflammatory pyrin-ASC-caspase-1 axis (core sensor function). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Familial Mediterranean fever mutations lift the obligatory requirement for microtubules in Pyrin inflammasome activation.

title: Cloning and expression of N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase I, the medial Golgi transferase that initiates complex N-linked carbohydrate formation.

Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text is a verbatim quote from the abstract. Basis of the IDA MF and BP annotations.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: High-throughput parotid-gland exosome proteomics; basis of an HDA "extracellular exosome" location, an over-annotation for a Golgi enzyme.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.

title: Golgi N-glycosyltransferases form both homo- and heterodimeric enzyme complexes in live cells.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.

review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Calcium 2016). The paper is about EFHD1; MICU1 appears only as one of five siRNA screen hits. Correctly cited, but too thin to carry the GO:1900069 salinity-response term mapped from it.

title: High-affinity cooperative Ca(2+) binding by MICU1-MICU2 serves as an on-off switch for the uniporter.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO Rep 2017). Reconstitution of the MICU1-MICU2 heterodimer and measurement of cooperative Ca2+ binding matched to the disinhibition threshold; the strongest single support for calcium ion sensor activity.

title: MICU1 controls cristae junction and spatially anchors mitochondrial Ca(2+) uniporter complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Rep 2019). Independent group, converging conclusion on cristae junction stabilisation and inner boundary membrane localisation.

title: Mechanisms and significance of tissue-specific MICU regulation of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Cell 2022). Source for tissue-specific MICU1 homodimers and the intersubunit disulfide; used to justify keeping the homo-oligomerisation terms as non-core rather than removing them.

title: Evidence supporting the MICU1 occlusion mechanism and against the potentiation model in the mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2023, doi 10.1073/pnas.2217665120). Written specifically to adjudicate the occlusion-versus-potentiation dispute and reports direct patch-clamp evidence for occlusion. Correctly cited for GO:0019855.

title: MICU1 regulates mitochondrial cristae structure and function independently of the mitochondrial Ca(2+) uniporter channel.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Signal 2023, doi 10.1126/scisignal.abi8948). Establishes the MICOS/cristae role and states explicitly that it is independent of matrix Ca2+ uptake. Important context: MCU-independent MICU1 function was already published three years before the 2026 metabolon proposal.

title: MICU1 occludes the mitochondrial calcium uniporter in divalent-free conditions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2023, doi 10.1073/pnas.2218999120). Independent support for occlusion from a different assay (divalent-free Na+ flux), with the useful caveat that a fraction of the uniporter appears to escape MICU1-dependent gating.

title: MICU proteins facilitate calcium-dependent mitochondrial metabolon formation to regulate cellular energetics independently of MCU.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Metab 2026;8:1106-1123, PMC13310417, doi 10.1038/s42255-026-01513-z). The contested claim of this review. Correctly cited and methodologically substantial, but it is a single-laboratory study with no independent replication - a PubMed search for 'MICU metabolon' returns only this paper and its own Research Square preprint (PMID:40678212) - and no published rebuttal. Its headline assertion of primacy over matrix-Ca2+-dependent dehydrogenase activation is framed as a proposal, and the paper itself continues to describe MICU1 as the primary regulator of uniporter-mediated uptake, so no existing annotation is retracted on its basis.

title: Asymmetric distribution of mitochondrial Ca(2+) regulators specifies compartment-specific mitochondrial function and neuronal development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Exp Mol Med 2026;58:2688-2700, doi 10.1038/s12276-026-01803-2). Not used for any annotation; cited only to record that work published after the metabolon proposal still treats MICU1 and MICU2 as gatekeepers of the uniporter.

title: Isolation of cDNA clones coding for IgE autoantigens with serum IgE from atopic dermatitis patients.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Invest Dermatol 1998) and correctly identified as the paper that cloned this cDNA, but it does not support the GO:0006952 defense response annotation drawn from it. MICU1/CBARA1 appears there only as one of four IgE autoantigens recovered from an expression library; IgE reactivity is a property of the patients' sera, not a function of the protein.

title: Structures of the human mitochondrial ribosome in native states of assembly.
review_notes: Brown et al. 2017 (Nat Struct Mol Biol 24:866). Discovery of L0R8F8 as an mt-LSU assembly factor in the MALSU1-L0R8F8-mt-ACP module, with a de novo model and the LYR contact with the 4-PP arm. Full text read from PMC.

title: Deep transcriptome annotation enables the discovery and functional characterization of cryptic small proteins.
review_notes: Samandi et al. 2017 (eLife). First functional study of AltMiD51: matrix localisation and fission upon overexpression. The fission evidence is gain-of-function only. Full text read.

title: The Protein Coded by a Short Open Reading Frame, Not by the Annotated Coding Sequence, Is the Main Gene Product of the Dual-Coding Gene MIEF1.
review_notes: Delcourt et al. 2018 (Mol Cell Proteomics). Absolute quantification shows that AltMiD51 is 2-6 times more abundant than MiD51. Describes uORF-specific CRISPR knockout cells. No GOA rows cite it. Full text read.

title: MIEF1 Microprotein Regulates Mitochondrial Translation.
review_notes: Rathore et al. 2018 (Biochemistry 57:5564). Proteinase K matrix localisation, APEX2 and BioPlex mitoribosome interactions, and translation-rate effects with knockdown/rescue. Full text read from PMC. The abstract's expansion "mitochondrial elongation factor 1 microprotein" is a misnomer; MIEF1 stands for mitochondrial elongation factor 1, a name for the fission adaptor MiD51.

title: The Mitochondrial Acyl-carrier Protein Interaction Network Highlights Important Roles for LYRM Family Members in Complex I and Mitoribosome Assembly.
review_notes: Dibley et al. 2020 (Mol Cell Proteomics 19:65). Abstract-only in cache; full text could not be retrieved. The abstract supports the mt-LSU assembly role but not the complex I assembly claim for AltMiD51.

title: Structural basis for late maturation steps of the human mitoribosomal large subunit.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of GTPBP5-associated mt-LSU intermediates containing the MALSU1:L0R8F8:mt-ACP module. Full text read.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput MitoCoP proteome. L0R8F8 is not named in the article text; it is present only in the supplementary dataset.

title: A late-stage assembly checkpoint of the human mitochondrial ribosome large subunit.
review_notes: Rebelo-Guiomar et al. 2022 (Nat Commun). MRM2-deficient mt-LSU intermediates all retain the MALSU1:L0R8F8:mtACP anti-association module. No GOA rows cite it. Full text read.

title: Structural insights into the role of GTPBP10 in the RNA maturation of the mitoribosome.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of GTPBP7/GTPBP10-bound mt-LSU intermediates. The MALSU1-L0R8F8-mtACP module binds early and persists. Full text read.

title: A micropeptide encoded by lncRNA MIR155HG suppresses autoimmune inflammation via modulating antigen presentation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; Sci Adv 2020;6(21):eaaz2059, PMC7314557 (note the journal is Science Advances, not Nature Communications as sometimes cited). Full text cached. Sole source of every experimental annotation on this entry: endogenous translation of the ORF, HSPA8 binding and domain mapping, ATPase inhibition, antigen-trafficking and MHC class II effects, and the two mouse disease models. Two interpretive limits worth recording: all functional experiments used exogenous synthetic peptide at 25 uM rather than loss of the endogenous peptide, and the cellular and in vivo work was largely done in mouse cells although the authors report the coding sequence is absent from the mouse genome.

title: Evidence That Regulation of Pri-miRNA/miRNA Expression Is Not a General Rule of miPEPs Function in Humans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; Int J Mol Sci 2021;22(7):3432, PMC8038077. Full text cached. Independent confirmation that the spliced pri-miR-155 transcript is translated into the peptide in HeLa cells, and the source of the important negative result that the peptide does not regulate its own pri-miRNA or miR-155 activity, unlike plant miPEPs and human miPEP133. Also the source of the conservation caveat, describing the peptide as extremely well conserved in primates and only partially conserved in mouse.

title: Mutation of a gene encoding a putative chaperonin causes McKusick-Kaufman syndrome.
review_notes: Gene-discovery paper; establishes MKKS as a putative chaperonin and links it to McKusick-Kaufman syndrome. Supports the chaperone/protein-folding and disease- developmental annotations (TAS).

title: Dissection of epistasis in oligogenic Bardet-Biedl syndrome.
review_notes: Identifies CCDC28B/MGC1203 as a pericentriolar protein interacting and colocalizing with BBS proteins; supports the MKKS-CCDC28B IPI.

title: Recruitment of PCM1 to the centrosome by the cooperative action of DISC1 and BBS4: a candidate for psychiatric illnesses.
review_notes: Primarily about DISC1/BBS4/PCM1 centrosomal recruitment; MKKS-PCM1 IPI is a peripheral, centrosomal-context interaction.

title: BBS6, BBS10, and BBS12 form a complex with CCT/TRiC family chaperonins and mediate BBSome assembly.
review_notes: Key paper establishing the BBS6/BBS10/BBS12 + CCT/TRiC chaperonin complex that mediates BBSome assembly; underpins the core chaperone-mediated complex assembly annotation.

title: Direct role of Bardet-Biedl syndrome proteins in transcriptional regulation.
review_notes: Demonstrates a direct nuclear/transcriptional-regulation role for BBS proteins; abstract foregrounds BBS7 but indicates a similar role for other BBS proteins. Full text not cached; supports MKKS nuclear/TF-binding IPI assigned by MGI.

title: Combining Cep290 and Mkks ciliopathy alleles in mice rescues sensory defects and restores ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Shows MKKS directly interacts with CEP290 and that BBS mutations disrupt this interaction; supports the MKKS-CEP290 IPI within ciliary biology.

title: Intrinsic protein-protein interaction-mediated and chaperonin-assisted sequential assembly of stable bardet-biedl syndrome protein complex, the BBSome.
review_notes: Defines the sequential BBSome-assembly pathway; the BBS-chaperonin complex (incl. MKKS) stabilizes BBS7 and nucleates the BBS7-BBS2-BBS9 core. Confirms MKKS is an assembly factor, not a stable BBSome subunit.

title: A novel H395R mutation in MKKS/BBS6 causes retinitis pigmentosa and polydactyly without other findings of Bardet-Biedl or McKusick-Kaufman syndrome.
review_notes: Disease-allele study; H395R reduces MKKS-BBS12 interaction, supporting the MKKS-BBS12 IPI and the functional importance of the chaperonin interaction.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS (BioPlex 2.0); source of a high-throughput MKKS-BBS12 interaction. Supports complex membership but provides no specific function.

title: Nuclear/cytoplasmic transport defects in BBS6 underlie congenital heart disease through perturbation of a chromatin remodeling protein.
review_notes: Establishes active nuclear-cytoplasmic transport of BBS6, the SMARCC1 interaction, and a transcriptional/chromatin-remodeling arm relevant to congenital heart disease; supports nucleus/cytoplasm IDA, SMARCC1 IPI, and cilium-assembly IMP.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome map (HuRI); source of low-specificity MKKS-CDR2 and MKKS-ZBED1 interactions of uncertain biological relevance.

title: Dlec1 is required for spermatogenesis and male fertility in mice.
review_notes: Mouse spermatogenesis study reporting a Dlec1-Mkks interaction; source of the MKKS-DLEC1 IPI. Peripheral to MKKS core function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS (BioPlex 3.0); source of a high-throughput MKKS-BBS12 interaction corroborating complex membership.

title: Falcon deep research report for MKKS
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Falcon/Edison) over recent reviews (Alvarez-Satta 2017, Tian 2023, Gupta 2022, etc.). Correctness left UNVERIFIED because the underlying review papers are not in the local cache and the synthesis was machine-generated. MKKS-CHAPERONIN-SPECIFIC claims that are well anchored and consistent with the curated literature: (1) MKKS is a chaperonin-LIKE assembly factor, NOT a stable/core BBSome subunit; (2) MKKS does not perform canonical ATP-dependent protein folding - its ATP-hydrolysis motif is divergent and the actual folding is executed by the associated canonical CCT/TRiC chaperonins; (3) MKKS/BBS12 act as substrate-binding units mediating association of CCT with the client BBS7, stabilizing BBS7 for the BBS2-BBS7-BBS9 core; (4) basal-body/ centrosome-centered localization, and chaperonin-like BBS proteins are generally NOT detected along the cilium itself. These are used to STRENGTHEN existing annotations only, not to add new ones. CLAIMS to treat with caution as BBSome/CCT GENERALIZATION rather than direct MKKS evidence: BBSome cargo-adaptor trafficking, Hedgehog/GPCR/ARL6 trafficking detail, and SMARCC1/nuclear moonlighting (the report itself flags these as less established); these were not used to alter MKKS molecular-function calls.

title: Differential regulation of p53 and p21 by MKRN1 E3 ligase controls cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title and GOA anchors this PMID to IDA for GO:0061630 (ubiquitin protein ligase activity) and GO:0000209; establishes MKRN1's core E3 ligase function on p53/p21.

title: The RNA-binding ubiquitin ligase MKRN1 functions in ribosome-associated quality control of poly(A) translation.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title and content describes MKRN1 binding PABPC1/polysomes and ubiquitinating RPS10/PABPC1; establishes the RNA-binding ubiquitin-ligase role in poly(A) RQC.

title: Huntingtin interacting proteins are genetic modifiers of neurodegeneration.
review_notes: High-throughput huntingtin interactome screen; a passing/contextual capture of MKRN2, not informative about its core molecular function. Not cached; relevance to MKRN2 function is low.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; GOA anchors this PMID to HDA for GO:0003723 (RNA binding). It is a global mRNA-interactome screen, not a dedicated MKRN2 study, so it supports (but does not by itself establish) the RNA-binding core function. No dedicated experimental paper establishes human MKRN2's core E3 ligase activity in this review.

title: An Upstream Open Reading Frame in Phosphatase and Tensin Homolog Encodes a Circuit Breaker of Lactate Metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary characterization (Cell Metab 2021); abstract only in cache, no PMC record. Erratum PMID:33535099. Source of all GOA experimental rows.

title: Upstream open reading frame-encoded MP31 disrupts the mitochondrial quality control process and inhibits tumorigenesis in glioblastoma.
review_notes: PubMed-verified follow-up from the same group (Neuro Oncol 2023), full text in PMC. Corroborates mitochondrial localization and LDHB binding; mitophagy/lysosome effects are indirect phenotypes.

title: Novel Insights Into Small Open Reading Frame-Encoded Micropeptides in Glioblastoma.
review_notes: PubMed-verified 2025 review of glioblastoma micropeptides naming MP31; background only.

title: The pseudokinase MLKL mediates necroptosis via a molecular switch mechanism.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Mouse MLKL knockout and structure; pseudokinase domain binds ATP but is catalytically inactive.

title: A robust methodology to subclassify pseudokinases based on their nucleotide-binding properties.
review_notes: Full text. Human MLKL is a cation-independent ATP-binding (Class 2) pseudokinase; earlier reported kinase activity attributed to a contaminating protein.

title: Mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein MLKL causes necrotic membrane disruption upon phosphorylation by RIP3.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Phospho-MLKL oligomers bind PI lipids and cardiolipin; MLKL lacks kinase activity.

title: MLKL compromises plasma membrane integrity by binding to phosphatidylinositol phosphates.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. 4HB binds PIPs; recombinant MLKL permeabilizes PIP-containing liposomes.

title: Activation of the pseudokinase MLKL unleashes the four-helix bundle domain to induce membrane localization and necroptotic cell death.
review_notes: Full text, mostly mouse MLKL. 4HB residue clusters needed for membrane localization and killing.

title: Sequential Engagement of Distinct MLKL Phosphatidylinositol-Binding Sites Executes Necroptosis.
review_notes: Full text. Hierarchical PIP binding by the N-terminal bundle; PI(4,5)P2 preferred.

title: Conformational switching of the pseudokinase domain promotes human MLKL tetramerization and cell death by necroptosis.
review_notes: Full text. Human MLKL tetramers permeabilize liposomes; species differences in activation.

title: Structures of the human GTPase MMAA and vitamin B12-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and insight into their complex formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Structural/biochemical study establishing MMAA as a GTPase modulated by MUT, homodimer (PDB 2WWW), and its GTP-dependent gatekeeping role for AdoCbl assembly into MUT.

title: Protection and reactivation of human methylmalonyl-CoA mutase by MMAA protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Demonstrates MMAA's dual protectase/reactivase role toward MCM and the GTP-hydrolysis-dependent cofactor exchange.

title: Protein destabilization and loss of protein-protein interaction are fundamental mechanisms in cblA-type methylmalonic aciduria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Large patient/mutant series showing intrinsic GTPase is retained while MUT-stimulated GTPase, MUT binding, and AdoCbl gating are lost in disease variants.

title: Human MMAA induces the release of inactive cofactor and restores methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity through their complex formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Shows OH2Cbl accumulation causes MCM inactivation, MMAA complex slows this, and MMAA removes the damaged cofactor via GTP hydrolysis; first in vivo mito colocalization of hMMAA with hMCM.

title: Allosteric Regulation of Oligomerization by a B(12) Trafficking G-Protein Is Corrupted in Methylmalonic Aciduria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Human MCM-CblA form nucleotide-sensitive interconverting oligomers; GTPase-driven resolution to the loading-ready state is needed for AdoCbl loading; cblA switch III mutations reduce the fibroblast AdoCbl pool.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Large-scale mitochondrial proteomics; corroborates mitochondrial localization of MMAA but does not directly address molecular function.

title: Identification of the human and bovine ATP:Cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase cDNAs based on complementation of a bacterial mutant.
review_notes: Defining functional study of human MMAB/ATR; directly establishes corrinoid adenosyltransferase activity, the AdoCbl-synthesis role, and the link to cblB methylmalonic aciduria. Abstract-only in cache but supporting quotes verified verbatim against the cached record.

title: Spectroscopic evidence for the formation of a four-coordinate Co2+ cobalamin species upon binding to the human ATP:cobalamin adenosyltransferase.
review_notes: Spectroscopy of the human ATR mechanism (cobalamin binding, ATP-dependent coordination chemistry); supports the adenosyltransferase activity and cobalamin binding.

title: Structure of ATP-bound human ATP:cobalamin adenosyltransferase.
review_notes: Crystal structure of ATP-bound human MMAB (PDB 2IDX), establishing the homotrimer and ATP binding site; cited by UniProt for ATP-binding features and SUBUNIT. Used to support the NEW ATP binding annotation.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome perturbation study; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (CBY2). Does not characterize MMAB function.

title: Protein destabilization and loss of protein-protein interaction are fundamental mechanisms in cblA-type methylmalonic aciduria.
review_notes: Primarily an MMAA (cblA) study, but assays MMAB adenosylcobalamin binding and the MMAB->MUT AdoCbl transfer; UniProt cites it for MMAB adenosylcobalamin-binding. Abstract-only in cache; supporting quotes verified verbatim.

title: Sacrificial Cobalt-Carbon Bond Homolysis in Coenzyme B(12) as a Cofactor Conservation Strategy.
review_notes: Full text available; directly documents MMAB/ATR AdoCbl synthesis, direct delivery to MCM, and the sacrificial Co-C homolysis cofactor-conservation activity.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of generic protein-binding IPIs (CALR, DLST, NEK7, OPTN). No functional MMAB characterization.

title: Redox-Linked Coordination Chemistry Directs Vitamin B(12) Trafficking.
review_notes: Authoritative account of the mitochondrial B12 trafficking pathway; describes MMAB/ATR as the homotrimeric adenosyltransferase and escort in the matrix. Full text available; quotes verified.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (DBT). No functional MMAB characterization.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome supporting MMAB mitochondrial localization (HTP).

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map resource; source of a generic protein-binding IPI (DBT). No functional MMAB characterization.

title: Decyanation of vitamin B12 by a trafficking chaperone.
review_notes: Founding paper establishing MMACHC reductive decyanation of cyanocobalamin to cob(II)alamin; directly supports the core cyanocobalamin reductase function and the "most common inborn error" framing. Abstract-only cache, PubMed-verified title.

title: Mechanism of vitamin B12-responsiveness in cblC methylmalonic aciduria with homocystinuria.
review_notes: Shows base-off cobalamin binding, NADPH/FAD-dependent decyanation, and combined MMA + homocystinuria in cblC; supports decyanase activity, cobalamin binding, FAD binding, and the disease framing.

title: A human vitamin B12 trafficking protein uses glutathione transferase activity for processing alkylcobalamins.
review_notes: Defines the glutathione-dependent alkylcobalamin dealkylase (S-alkyltransferase) activity (EC 2.5.1.151) and that cysteine/homocysteine cannot substitute; supports GO:0016765 and the demethylase/demethylation over-annotation reasoning.

title: Structural basis of multifunctionality in a vitamin B12-processing enzyme.
review_notes: Crystal structures (with MeCbl) establishing the divergent flavin-reductase scaffold, FMN/FAD use, and dual decyanation/dealkylation chemistry; supports decyanase, alkyltransferase, and FAD binding functions.

title: Structure of MMACHC reveals an arginine-rich pocket and a domain-swapped dimer for its B12 processing function.
review_notes: Defines the arginine-rich glutathione-binding pocket, GSH-dependent dealkylation, and the substrate/cofactor-triggered domain-swapped homodimer; supports glutathione binding, dealkylase activity, and homodimerization annotations.

title: Subcellular location of MMACHC and MMADHC, two human proteins central to intracellular vitamin B(12) metabolism.
review_notes: Definitive subcellular-localization study showing MMACHC is cytoplasmic/cytosolic (vs the partly mitochondrial MMADHC); supports the cytosol core location and argues against a nuclear pool.

title: The C-terminal domain of CblD interacts with CblC and influences intracellular cobalamin partitioning.
review_notes: Establishes the MMACHC(CblC)-MMADHC(CblD) interaction and CblD's adapter role in partitioning cobalamin between AdoCbl and MeCbl routes; supports the protein-binding IPI (as MMADHC partner).

title: Interaction between methionine synthase isoforms and MMACHC: characterization in cblG-variant, cblG and cblC inherited causes of megaloblastic anaemia.
review_notes: Documents MMACHC-methionine synthase interaction and that cblC mutations disrupt cob(II)alamin formation; supports the cobalamin metabolic process IMP and the MTR protein-binding IPI.

title: Purification and interaction analyses of two human lysosomal vitamin B12 transporters: LMBD1 and ABCD4.
review_notes: Shows cytoplasmic MMACHC interacts with lysosomal exporters LMBD1 and ABCD4 with nanomolar affinity, delivering cobalamin to the cytosol; supports the corresponding protein-binding IPI.

title: Pathogenic mutations differentially affect the catalytic activities of the human B12-processing chaperone CblC and increase futile redox cycling.

title: Methionine synthase and methionine synthase reductase interact with MMACHC and with MMADHC.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.

title: Interaction between MMACHC and MMADHC, two human proteins participating in intracellular vitamin B₁₂ metabolism.

title: Molecular mechanisms leading to three different phenotypes in the cblD defect of intracellular cobalamin metabolism.

title: Subcellular location of MMACHC and MMADHC, two human proteins central to intracellular vitamin B(12) metabolism.

title: The C-terminal domain of CblD interacts with CblC and influences intracellular cobalamin partitioning.

title: Characterization of functional domains of the cblD (MMADHC) gene product.

title: Methionine synthase and methionine synthase reductase interact with MMACHC and with MMADHC.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: An Interprotein Co-S Coordination Complex in the B(12)-Trafficking Pathway.
