MMGT1-specific host-pathogen phenotype (lipid droplet/persistence axis); the study does not resolve whether the mechanism is via EMC function, magnesium transport, or another pathway, so recorded as informative context rather than a core molecular function.

title: EMC rectifies the topology of multipass membrane proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Struct Mol Biol 2023/2024). Expands the EMC client repertoire and topology-completion role; supports the stop-transfer/multipass insertion processes to which EMC5 contributes as a core subunit.

title: Structural insights into human EMC and its interaction with VDAC.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Aging 2024). Human EMC structure; EMC5 used as the affinity handle for native complex purification, confirming EMC5 as a stable core membrane subunit; also documents an EMC-VDAC interaction at MERCs.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: SLC interactome; SLC partners are plausible EMC clients; source of an IPI protein-binding annotation.

title: The EMC acts as a chaperone for membrane proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2025). Defines an additional EMC chaperone mode (client features, EMC1-mediated TMD engagement); supports the broader membrane-protein biogenesis role of the EMC of which EMC5 is a core member.

title: Cloning and expression of a mutant methylmalonyl coenzyme A mutase with altered cobalamin affinity that causes mut- methylmalonic aciduria.
review_notes: Human MCM expressed and assayed; characterizes the G717V mut- variant with ~1000-fold elevated Km for adenosylcobalamin. Supports mutase activity and cofactor binding.

title: Primary structure and activity of mouse methylmalonyl-CoA mutase.
review_notes: Establishes MCM as an adenosylcobalamin-dependent isomerase (MM-CoA to succinyl-CoA); mouse enzyme is 94% identical to human and complements human deficiency.

title: Novel associations of CPS1, MUT, NOX4, and DPEP1 with plasma homocysteine in a healthy population: a genome-wide evaluation of 13 974 participants in the Women's Genome Health Study.
review_notes: A GWAS associating a MUT-locus SNP with plasma homocysteine. The paper itself states MUT's catalytic activity is "hardly related to homocysteine"; it does not support direct involvement of MMUT in homocysteine metabolic process or binding of a modified amino acid, so the IDA annotations to GO:0050667 and GO:0072341 are over-interpretations.

title: Structures of the human GTPase MMAA and vitamin B12-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and insight into their complex formation.
review_notes: Crystal structures of human MUT (apo/holo/ternary with AdoCbl and malonyl-CoA) and MMAA; MUT is a homodimer and forms a GTP-dependent complex with MMAA. Note the GTPase activity characterized is MMAA's (modulated by MUT), not MUT's own activity.

title: Protection and reactivation of human methylmalonyl-CoA mutase by MMAA protein.
review_notes: In vitro assays of purified recombinant hMCM and hMMAA; MMAA protects/reactivates MCM by cofactor exchange via GTP hydrolysis. Supports mutase activity, cobalamin binding, and the MMAA interaction.

title: Intracellular localization of hepatic propionyl-CoA carboxylase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase in humans and normal and vitamin B12 deficient rats.
review_notes: Subcellular fractionation localizes all MCM activity to the mitochondria, loosely bound to the inner membrane-matrix compartment. Supports mitochondrial-matrix localization and mutase activity.

title: Molecular cloning of L-methylmalonyl-CoA mutase: gene transfer and analysis of mut cell lines.
review_notes: Cloning of human MCM cDNA; gene transfer into COS cells constitutes increased MCM enzymatic activity. Supports the identity and mutase activity of the gene product.

title: Functional characterization and categorization of missense mutations that cause methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (MUT) deficiency.
review_notes: Full text available; comprehensive enzymology of 23 recombinant MUT variants (activity, thermostability, Km for AdoCbl and MM-CoA). Excellent verbatim support for the core mutase function, cofactor requirement, and propionate-catabolism context.

title: Cloning of full-length methylmalonyl-CoA mutase from a cDNA library using the polymerase chain reaction.
review_notes: Full-length cloning that defined the N-terminal mitochondrial transit peptide; basis of the TAS mitochondrial localization.

title: Molecular Genetic Characterization of 151 Mut-Type Methylmalonic Aciduria Patients and Identification of 41 Novel Mutations in MUT.
review_notes: Large mut-type MMA cohort; MUT mutations cause loss of function (reduced protein, propionate incorporation). Supports mutase activity via IMP.

title: Eight novel MUT loss-of-function missense mutations in Chinese patients with isolated methylmalonic academia.
review_notes: Functional (HEK293T) assays show patient missense mutations reduce MCM protein/activity. Supports mutase activity via IMP.

title: Protein destabilization and loss of protein-protein interaction are fundamental mechanisms in cblA-type methylmalonic aciduria.
review_notes: MMAA-focused study; MMAA GTPase activity is stimulated by interaction with MUT, and cblA-type mutations reduce this. Supports the positive-regulation-of-GTPase annotation (MUT as the stimulator of MMAA).

title: Human MMAA induces the release of inactive cofactor and restores methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity through their complex formation.
review_notes: Recombinant hMCM enzymology; identifies OH2Cbl as the inactivating oxidized cofactor and MMAA-mediated cofactor exchange; demonstrates mitochondrial colocalization of hMCM and hMMAA. Supports mutase activity, cobalamin binding, and localization.

title: The Human Knockout Gene CLYBL Connects Itaconate to Vitamin B(12).
review_notes: Full text available; recombinant human MUT enzymology and clear statement of MUT as the mitochondrial-matrix B12-dependent mutase converting MM-CoA to succinyl-CoA; identifies itaconyl-CoA as a cofactor-inactivating inhibitor. Strong core-function support.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput neurodegenerative-disease interactome/aggregation map; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (partner HTT). Does not inform MMUT's core function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS interactome dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (partner CRYZ). Does not inform MMUT's core function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP) includes MMUT; corroborates mitochondrial localization (HTP).

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Large-scale multimodal cell-mapping dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (partner CRYZ). Does not inform MMUT's core function.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline. Maps InterPro IPR005302 (MoCF_Sase_C domain) to the generic root MF GO:0003824 catalytic activity. Correct but uninformative parent term.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the family molybdenum cofactor sulfurtransferase activity and the general molybdopterin cofactor metabolic process, consistent with the experimentally characterized MOCOS function.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by transferring manual GO annotations between related proteins based on shared sequence features
review_notes: UniRule sequence-feature transfer that yields GO:0016829 lyase activity for MOCOS. MOCOS is a sulfurtransferase (EC 2.8.1.9); the terminal reaction transfers sulfur to the Moco rather than performing a lyase (bond-cleaving, non-hydrolytic) reaction, so the lyase MF is an incorrect over-propagation for this protein.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning IEA to GO:0032324 molybdopterin cofactor biosynthetic process. Correct but a more general relative of the specific GO:0006777 term.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: UniRule/HAMAP (MF_03050) combined IEA. Recovers the core sulfurtransferase activity, PLP binding, Mo-molybdopterin cofactor biosynthetic process, and molybdenum ion binding, all consistent with the HAMAP MOCOS rule and the experimental literature.

title: Mutation of human molybdenum cofactor sulfurase gene is responsible for classical xanthinuria type II.
review_notes: Establishes MOCOS as the type II xanthinuria gene and its sulfur-donor role for the MoCo of XDH and AO. Basis of the IMP annotations. Cached record is abstract-only; the IMP curator read the full text.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome dataset; source of an IntAct MOCOS-PARVA (Q9NVD7) IPI. No functional characterization relating the interaction to MoCo sulfuration.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Systematic binary interactome map; source of a MOCOS-PARVA (Q9NVD7) IPI. Not functionally informative for the enzymatic role of MOCOS.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Interactome community-architecture study; source of a MOCOS-PARVA (Q9NVD7) IPI. Not functionally informative for the core MoCo sulfurase function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary (Y2H) interactome reference map; source of a MOCOS-ARL8A (Q96BM9) IPI. No functional link to MoCo sulfuration established.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex-type) study; source of MOCOS-PARVA (Q9NVD7) and MOCOS-ARL8A (Q96BM9) IPIs. High-throughput data, not functionally characterized.

title: Classical Xanthinuria in Nine Israeli Families and Two Isolated Cases from Germany: Molecular, Biochemical and Population Genetics Aspects.
review_notes: Full text available (PMC8301430). Provides the direct catalytic/IDA evidence and the PLP-dependent L-cysteine desulfurase mechanism; source of the UniProt catalytic-activity, PLP cofactor, pathway and EC 2.8.1.9 assignments.

title: Exchange of oxygen with sulfur in MoCo
review_notes: Reactome reaction for MoCo oxygen-to-sulfur exchange; supports the sulfurtransferase activity and cytosolic location TAS annotations.

title: Molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis
review_notes: Reactome MoCo biosynthesis pathway; supports the molybdopterin cofactor biosynthetic process TAS annotation.

title: Mutations in the molybdenum cofactor biosynthetic genes MOCS1, MOCS2, and GEPH.
review_notes: Review (abstract-only in cache) establishing MOCS1 encodes the first two enzymes of Moco biosynthesis and the bicistronic architecture; supports the GO:0006777 TAS annotation.

title: Characterization of MOCS1A, an oxygen-sensitive iron-sulfur protein involved in human molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis.
review_notes: Biochemical characterization of human MOCS1A as an oxygen-sensitive radical-SAM protein binding two [4Fe-4S] clusters; conserved cysteines essential for precursor-Z synthesis. Directly supports the 4Fe-4S binding and Moco-biosynthesis annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Ten novel mutations in the molybdenum cofactor genes MOCS1 and MOCS2 and in vitro characterization of a MOCS2 mutation that abolishes the binding ability of molybdopterin synthase.
review_notes: Disease-mutation study of MOCS1/MOCS2; supports MOCS1 involvement in Moco biosynthesis (GO:0006777 IMP). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Identification of a cyclic nucleotide as a cryptic intermediate in molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis.
review_notes: Full text available. Isolates 3',8-cH2GTP as the MoaA product and shows the human homolog MOCS1B converts it to cPMP (Km 0.79 uM); primary experimental support for the MOCS1B cPMP synthase activity (GO:0061799, EC 4.6.1.17).

title: A mild case of molybdenum cofactor deficiency defines an alternative route of MOCS1 protein maturation.
review_notes: Mild MoCD case; functional studies confirm activity of a residual MOCS1B protein produced by translation re-initiation. Supports GO:0061799 (IGI) and GO:0006777 (IMP). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Alternative splicing of the bicistronic gene molybdenum cofactor synthesis 1 (MOCS1) uncovers a novel mitochondrial protein maturation mechanism.
review_notes: Establishes mitochondrial-matrix localization of MOCS1A/MOCS1B (with cytosolic exon-1b variants) and the proteolytic maturation of MOCS1AB; UniProt cites it for the EC 4.1.99.22 MOCS1A activity. Supports GO:0061798 (EXP), GO:0005759 and GO:0005737. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial-proteome study; detects MOCS1 in mitochondria (HTP, GO:0005739). Corroborates but does not by itself establish the specific matrix localization.

title: Mutations in a polycistronic nuclear gene associated with molybdenum cofactor deficiency.
review_notes: Original identification of MOCS1 (bicistronic moaA/moaC homolog) as the molybdenum cofactor deficiency gene; mutations in both ORFs confirm their functional role. Supports GO:0006777 (IMP). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Genomic structure and mutational spectrum of the bicistronic MOCS1 gene defective in molybdenum cofactor deficiency type A.
review_notes: Genomic structure and mutational spectrum of MOCS1 in MoCD type A; MOCS1A and MOCS1B are the first two enzymes of the pathway in a single transcript. Supports GO:0006777 (IMP). Abstract-only in cache.

title: Mechanistic studies of human molybdopterin synthase reaction and characterization of mutants identified in group B patients of molybdenum cofactor deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary characterization of human MPT synthase catalytic mechanism and disease mutants; directly supports the core catalytic/complex annotations (abstract-only in cache).

title: Evidence for the physiological role of a rhodanese-like protein for the biosynthesis of the molybdenum cofactor in humans.
review_notes: Establishes the physiological sulfur-delivery pathway to MOCS2A and the cytosolic localization of MPT synthase (abstract-only in cache).

title: Ten novel mutations in the molybdenum cofactor genes MOCS1 and MOCS2 and in vitro characterization of a MOCS2 mutation that abolishes the binding ability of molybdopterin synthase.
review_notes: Basis of the ComplexPortal IDA/IPI annotations; verifies MOCS2B-MOCS2A/precursor Z interactions (abstract-only in cache).

title: Investigation of molybdenum cofactor deficiency due to MOCS2 deficiency in a newborn baby.
review_notes: Full text available; provides the direct human recombinant evidence underlying the 2025 IDA MF/BP/CC annotations for MOCS2B.

title: Moco biosynthesis and the ATAC acetyltransferase engage translation initiation by inhibiting latent PKR activity.
review_notes: Supports the secondary/moonlighting annotations (nucleus, PKR binding, negative regulation of signal transduction), not the core MoCo-biosynthesis function (abstract-only in cache).

title: Evidence for the physiological role of a rhodanese-like protein for the biosynthesis of the molybdenum cofactor in humans.
review_notes: Establishes MOCS3's physiological role in human Moco biosynthesis; identifies Cys412 as the essential persulfide-forming active-site cysteine and cytosolic localization. Abstract-only in cache; claims anchored to GOA IDA/IMP evidence codes.

title: Molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis in humans: identification of a persulfide group in the rhodanese-like domain of MOCS3 by mass spectrometry.
review_notes: Mass spectrometry pinpoints the catalytic persulfide on Cys412 and the C316-C324 disulfide. Directly supports the sulfurtransferase mechanism. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Site-directed mutagenesis of the active site loop of the rhodanese-like domain of the human molybdopterin synthase sulfurase MOCS3. Major differences in substrate specificity between eukaryotic and bacterial homologs.
review_notes: Establishes that thiosulfate is not the physiological sulfur donor for MOCS3 in eukaryotes, motivating the NFS1 sulfur-donor model. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The sulfurtransferase activity of Uba4 presents a link between ubiquitin-like protein conjugation and activation of sulfur carrier proteins.
review_notes: Characterizes yeast Uba4 (MOCS3 ortholog): N-terminal adenylation then thiocarboxylation of MOCS2A/Urm1, no thioester intermediate. Basis of the ISO annotation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A novel role for human Nfs1 in the cytoplasm: Nfs1 acts as a sulfur donor for MOCS3, a protein involved in molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis.
review_notes: Identifies cytosolic NFS1 as the physiological sulfur donor to MOCS3-RLD and documents specific NFS1-MOCS3 interaction. Supports EXP/IDA MF and Moco BP and the NFS1 (Q9Y697) IPI. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A functional proteomics approach links the ubiquitin-related modifier Urm1 to a tRNA modification pathway.
review_notes: Establishes the URM1 thiocarboxylate as sulfur donor for tRNA thiolation, the basis for the URM1 activating enzyme activity and tRNA thio-modification annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Role of the ubiquitin-like protein Urm1 as a noncanonical lysine-directed protein modifier.
review_notes: Shows URM1 is conjugated to lysines of its own-pathway components including MOCS3 under oxidative stress; source of the URM1 (Q9BTM9) IPI and relevant to protein urmylation. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Dual role of the molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis protein MOCS3 in tRNA thiolation and molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis in humans.
review_notes: Definitive demonstration that MOCS3 is shared between Moco biosynthesis and tRNA thiolation, activating both MOCS2A and URM1 by adenylation plus sulfur transfer. Anchors multiple EXP/IDA MF and BP annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The L-cysteine desulfurase NFS1 is localized in the cytosol where it provides the sulfur for molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis in humans.
review_notes: Full text available; demonstrates cytosolic NFS1-MOCS3 interaction via the MOCS3 rhodanese domain (KD ~28 nM) and cytosolic localization. Supports cytosol CC and the NFS1 (Q9Y697) IPI.

title: Analysis of the Cellular Roles of MOCS3 Identifies a MOCS3-Independent Localization of NFS1 at the Tips of the Centrosome.
review_notes: MOCS3 CRISPR knockout in HEK293T abolishes sulfite oxidase activity (no Moco) and mcm5s2U-modified tRNAs, confirming the dual in-vivo role. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale neurodegenerative-disease yeast two-hybrid interactome; source of the candidate MOCS3-ATXN1 (P54253) and MOCS3-TARDBP (Q13148) IPIs. No dedicated functional characterization of MOCS3; bare protein-binding annotation only.

title: Requirement of the Lec35 gene for all known classes of monosaccharide-P-dolichol-dependent glycosyltransferase reactions in mammals.
review_notes: Definitive functional paper (hamster Lec35 = human MPDU1). PubMed-verified; establishes the non-catalytic Dol-P-Man/Dol-P-Glc utilization role and ER-membrane localization. Abstract-only in cache but the assayed molecular role is clearly stated.

title: MPDU1 mutations underlie a novel human congenital disorder of glycosylation, designated type If.
review_notes: Establishes MPDU1 as the CDG-If disease gene and links loss of function to defective dolichol-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis. Basis for the TAS/IGI BP annotations.

title: Screening of hepatocyte proteins binding to F protein of hepatitis C virus by yeast two-hybrid system.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid screen with HCV F protein as bait (UniProtKB:P0C045); MPDU1 appears only as a screen hit. Supports only a bare, non-core protein-binding annotation of unclear physiological relevance.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput MS membrane proteome of an NK-like cell line; supports only a generic "membrane" localization, not a specific compartment or function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome; the MPDU1-MANBAL interaction is corroborated in UniProt but only supports a generic (non-core) protein-binding annotation.

title: Perforin-2 restricts growth of Chlamydia trachomatis in macrophages.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Infect Immun 2013). Primary evidence that perforin-2 knockdown permits Chlamydia trachomatis growth in macrophages; supports the Gram-negative defence annotation.

title: Perforin-2 is essential for intracellular defense of parenchymal cells and phagocytes against pathogenic bacteria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (eLife 2015). In vivo Mpeg1 knockout phenotype plus EM of 100 A pores on bacterial surfaces; the strongest single source for the antibacterial role.

title: Regulation of expression and trafficking of perforin-2 by LPS and TNF-α.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Immunol 2017). Establishes the two human isoforms and that only TM-containing perforin-2a reaches vesicle membranes while perforin-2b is secreted; the basis for treating the extracellular annotation as isoform-specific and non-core.

title: Single cell analyses reveal specific distribution of anti-bacterial molecule Perforin-2 in human skin and its modulation by wounding and Staphylococcus aureus infection.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Exp Dermatol 2019). Human skin expression and anti-S. aureus activity; supports the Gram-positive defence annotation.

title: The cryo-EM structure of the acid activatable pore-forming immune effector Macrophage-expressed gene 1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2019). Source of the GO:0022829 IDA and of the acid-activation and MABP-orientation model that PMID:42618800 revisits.

title: MPEG1/Perforin-2 Haploinsufficiency Associated Polymicrobial Skin Infections and Considerations for Interferon-γ Therapy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Front Immunol 2020). Human MPEG1 haploinsufficiency with impaired phagocyte bacterial killing; the only human genetic evidence.

title: Perforin-2 is a pore-forming effector of endocytic escape in cross-presenting dendritic cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2023). Genetic screen identifying perforin-2 as the endocytic-escape effector of cross-presentation. Its released-ectodomain model is partly superseded by the same laboratory in PMID:42618800; the requirement for perforin-2 in cross-presentation is not in dispute.

title: Perforin-2 enhances antigen-specific CTL immune response by promoting cross presentation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Death Dis 2026). Independent replication that P2 loss impairs dendritic-cell cross-presentation and CD8+ T cell priming, though it attributes this to antigen uptake and restraint of endosomal acidification rather than to escape.

title: Anchoring of perforin-2 via the transmembrane domain is required for antigen escape into the cytosol.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (EMBO J 2026, Laub/Chatterjee/Kozik). Abstract-only in the cache. Argues that endocytic escape uses full-length membrane-anchored perforin-2 rather than the released ectodomain and is pH-independent, and concludes that pore formation in antibacterial defence and in cross-presentation proceed by distinct mechanisms. Single paper, no published rebuttal; weighed accordingly.

title: A micropeptide encoded by a putative long noncoding RNA regulates muscle performance.
review_notes: Founding paper (Cell 2015;160:595-606), cited in the UniProt entry. Full text cached. All functional experiments are on the mouse peptide or in mouse cells and animals. This is the source of the mouse IDA/IMP annotations transferred by ISS to human.

title: Widespread control of calcium signaling by a family of SERCA-inhibiting micropeptides.
review_notes: Sci Signal 2016. Source of the mouse IDA for GO:1901895 and GO:0005789. The work is primarily about ALN/ELN, with MLN included as a comparator.

title: Early vertebrate origin and diversification of small transmembrane regulators of cellular ion transport.
review_notes: J Physiol 2017. Evolutionary context only.

title: Newly Discovered Micropeptide Regulators of SERCA Form Oligomers but Bind to the Pump as Monomers.
review_notes: J Mol Biol 2019. FRET and co-IP in heterologous cells. Supports the UniProt SUBUNIT text.

title: Nothing Regular about the Regulins: Distinct Functional Properties of SERCA Transmembrane Peptide Regulatory Subunits.
review_notes: Int J Mol Sci 2021, a review containing new primary data. The finding that inhibition works through Vmax conflicts with the KCa mechanism reported in PMID:25640239 and stated in UniProt. Both agree that MLN inhibits SERCA. The synthetic MLN peptide's species is not stated in the cached text (the MD models were human).

title: NR1D1 controls skeletal muscle calcium homeostasis through myoregulin repression.
review_notes: JCI Insight 2022. One of only two sources of human-cell loss-of-function data for MRLN (shRNA in immortalized human DMD myoblasts and myotubes). The authors note that no specific anti-MLN antibody was available, so protein-level validation is lacking.

title: Functional Role of an Unusual Transmembrane Acidic Residue in the Calcium Pump Regulator Myoregulin.
review_notes: Biochemistry 2023. Simulations plus ATPase assays of the co-reconstituted protein.

title: Replacement of Lys27 by asparagine in the SERCA regulator myoregulin: A Ca(2+) affinity modulator or a catalytic activity switch?
review_notes: BBA Mol Cell Res 2024. Rabbit SERCA1a with synthetic MLN.

title: Cardiac effects of myoregulin in ischemia-reperfusion.
review_notes: Peptides 2024, abstract only. A preliminary report of human heart mRNA and of exogenous peptide effects in the rat Langendorff heart. Not used for any annotation.

title: Canonical Wnt signaling affects calcium homeostasis in serum-treated AC16 cells through MLN-mediated SERCA2a regulation.
review_notes: J Mol Cell Biol 2026. Human-cell loss-of-function evidence for SERCA inhibition. The AC16 line is transformed and serum-conditioned, and MLN expression in cardiomyocytes is not physiological in mouse, so the result supports the molecular activity but not a cardiac role.

title: Store-operated cation entry mediated by CD20 in membrane rafts.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes CD20 as a raft-associated component of BCR-activated SOC entry (siRNA and heterologous expression).

title: Mouse CD20 expression and function.
review_notes: CD20-/- mice: reduced CD19-induced calcium responses; otherwise normal B cell development and proliferation.

title: CD20 homo-oligomers physically associate with the B cell antigen receptor. Dissociation upon receptor engagement and recruitment of phosphoproteins and calmodulin-binding proteins.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; CD20 homo-oligomers associate with IgM BCR and dissociate upon BCR engagement.

title: CD20 deficiency in humans results in impaired T cell-independent antibody responses.
review_notes: Human loss-of-function (CVID5) establishing CD20 role in T-independent antibody responses; also CD20-deficient mouse data.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: B-cell exosome proteomics; CD20 co-IP with exosomal MHC II.

title: Proteomic analysis of S-acylated proteins in human B cells reveals palmitoylation of the immune regulators CD20 and CD23.
review_notes: Full text; CD20 S-palmitoylation and topology.

title: Comparison of tear protein levels in breast cancer patients and healthy controls using a de novo proteomic approach.
review_notes: Tear proteomics; CD20 not discussed in body text; localization implication weak.

title: Expression of MS4A and TMEM176 Genes in Human B Lymphocytes.
review_notes: Full text; GFP-CD20 imaged at plasma membrane in BJAB cells.

title: Isolation and structure of a cDNA encoding the B1 (CD20) cell-surface antigen of human B lymphocytes.
review_notes: cDNA cloning of CD20; functional statements are speculative (NAS).

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: HI-II-14 Y2H interactome; uninformative generic protein binding.

title: Structure of CD20 in complex with the therapeutic monoclonal antibody rituximab.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure: CD20 is a compact double-barrel dimer.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI Y2H interactome; uninformative generic protein binding.

title: Binding mechanisms of therapeutic antibodies to human CD20.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of CD20 with type I/II therapeutic mAbs.

title: CD20 as a gatekeeper of the resting state of human B cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMC7896350; full text cached). CRISPR KO/re-expression in Ramos and rituximab treatment of naive human B cells show CD20 maintains nanoscale receptor organization and the resting state, restraining IgM-BCR/CD19 signaling.

title: The B cell surface molecule B1 is functionally linked with B cell activation and differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; antibody-perturbation evidence for roles in B cell activation/differentiation, not loss of function.

title: Transfection of the CD20 cell surface molecule into ectopic cell types generates a Ca2+ conductance found constitutively in B lymphocytes.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; electrophysiology showing CD20 expression generates a Ca2+ conductance.

title: Falcon deep research report for human MS4A1
review_notes: Generated late (after the review was drafted). Its gatekeeper claim was verified against PMID:33563755. Its claims that the Rouge 2020 cryo-EM structure lacks a plausible ion-permeation pathway and that CD20-deficient patient B-cell lines retain BCR-induced Ca2+ flux (Kuijpers 2010) could not be checked here (both cached papers are abstract-only) and were not used to change actions.

title: Expression of MS4A and TMEM176 Genes in Human B Lymphocytes.
review_notes: Cached full text supports MS4A family/tetraspanning context and MS4A4A expression analysis; useful for family context and localization but not a normal B-cell function.

title: A protein-interaction network of interferon-stimulated genes extends the innate immune system landscape.
review_notes: Cached abstract describes a high-throughput interferon-stimulated-gene interaction network; supports only generic interaction evidence.

title: The MS4A gene cluster is a key modulator of soluble TREM2 and Alzheimer's disease risk.
review_notes: Cached full text directly supports MS4A4A/TREM2 colocalization at plasma membrane lipid rafts, MS4A4A perturbation effects on sTREM2, and the AD-risk/sTREM2 genetic context.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached full text describes a broad binary interactome reference map; supports only generic interaction evidence.

title: Expression of MS4A and TMEM176 Genes in Human B Lymphocytes.
review_notes: Cached full text directly supports MS4A6A expression testing and GFP-MS4A6A trans-Golgi localization, and cautions against normal plasma-membrane localization in B cells.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Cached full text describes the HuRI binary interactome reference map; for MS4A6A it supports only a generic high-throughput protein-interaction annotation.

title: Mutations in the human SC4MOL gene encoding a methyl sterol oxidase cause psoriasiform dermatitis, microcephaly, and developmental delay.
review_notes: PubMed-verified index paper establishing MSMO1/SC4MOL function and disease (MCCPD). Abstract-only in cache; full text read by curators for EXP annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Genome-scale binary interactome (HuRI); source of the uninformative bare protein-binding IPI annotations. Verified PMID/title against PubMed.

title: Characterization of yeast methyl sterol oxidase (ERG25) and identification of a human homologue.
review_notes: Original identification of the human ERG25 homologue (MSMO1); basis of the older ProtInc TAS annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The mitochondrial-derived peptide MOTS-c promotes metabolic homeostasis and reduces obesity and insulin resistance.
review_notes: Original characterisation of the peptide; full text in the cache. Verified that it establishes the 12S rRNA ORF, the obligate cytosolic translation, the exclusion of NUMT sources, plasma detection by ELISA, and the folate-AICAR-AMPK cascade. Soundness caveat recorded in the annotation reviews rather than here - the functional work uses stable overexpression, exogenous peptide and injected mice, and no direct molecular target in the folate cycle is identified.

title: MOTS-c peptide increases survival and decreases bacterial load in mice infected with MRSA.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; title and abstract confirmed against PubMed. Independent group (Fourth Military Medical University), which makes it the only non-Cohen/Lee corroboration of an in vivo antibacterial effect. The paper attributes protection largely to immunomodulation and enhanced macrophage bactericidal capacity rather than to direct killing, so it is cited as corroboration of the in vivo outcome, not of the mechanism.

title: The Mitochondrial-Encoded Peptide MOTS-c Translocates to the Nucleus to Regulate Nuclear Gene Expression in Response to Metabolic Stress.
review_notes: Source of every molecular-function and nuclear annotation on this entry; re-fetched so the full text is cached, and the EMSA, ChIP-qPCR and co-immunoprecipitation results were read directly rather than inferred from the abstract. The specificity limitation of the EMSA controls (alanine substitution of the very residues that confer charge and hydrophobicity) is a soundness caveat recorded in the GO:0003677 review.

title: MOTS-c improves osteoporosis by promoting osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells via TGF-β/Smad pathway.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; title and abstract verified against PubMed. Correctly cited for what it reports, but methodologically thin for a GO process annotation - synthetic peptide applied to rat BMSCs, marker and staining readouts, no endogenous peptide manipulation and no molecular target. Supports the MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED call on GO:0001649 rather than a core function.

title: MOTS-c improves osteoporosis by promoting the synthesis of type I collagen in osteoblasts via TGF-β/SMAD signaling pathway.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; title and abstract verified against PubMed. The GO:0033687 osteoblast proliferation annotation traces to a CCK-8 viability assay in the hFOB1.19 line after micromolar peptide addition, which is weak support for a proliferation process term; the paper's own conclusion concerns collagen synthesis.

title: Increased expression of the mitochondrial derived peptide, MOTS-c, in skeletal muscle of healthy aging men is associated with myofiber composition.
review_notes: Full text cached. Cited for endogenous expression in human skeletal muscle and plasma and for the opposite age trends in the two compartments, from a group only partly overlapping with the originating laboratory. Observational human data, so it supports location and expression claims, not function; it also reports that muscle MOTS-c expression does not track ARE-related gene expression in vivo.

title: A pro-diabetogenic mtDNA polymorphism in the mitochondrial-derived peptide, MOTS-c.
review_notes: Full text cached. Verified that the m.1382A>C variant produces a K14Q peptide, is associated with type 2 diabetes in men across three Japanese and multi-ethnic cohorts, and that the variant peptide is less effective than wild type in mice and in vitro. Used for the sequence-variant statement in the description; it is genetic association plus pharmacology, not direct evidence of a molecular function.

title: MOTS-c is an exercise-induced mitochondrial-encoded regulator of age-dependent physical decline and muscle homeostasis.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Verified that exercise raises endogenous MOTS-c in human muscle and plasma, that injected peptide improves rodent physical performance, and that nuclear entry of exogenous FITC-peptide was imaged. The nuclear-localisation support here is exogenous peptide only, so it is treated as corroboration of PMID:29983246 rather than as independent evidence.

title: MOTS-c reduces myostatin and muscle atrophy signaling.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Correctly cited for the CK2-PTEN-mTORC2-AKT-FOXO1-myostatin cascade in peptide-injected mice. Two problems traced to the GOA rows derived from it and recorded in the reviews - GO:2001145 names PIP3 5-phosphatase activity whereas PTEN is a 3-phosphatase, and the muscle-mass effect behind GO:0048630 appears only after body-weight adjustment, with absolute masses unchanged.

title: MOTS-c is a mitochondrial-encoded interferon-linked host defense peptide.
review_notes: Full text cached and read; eLife reviewed preprint from the originating laboratory, with an earlier bioRxiv version. Verified the amphipathicity and charge analysis, dose-dependent aggregation of E. coli and MRSA, loss of activity in the YIFY and RKLR mutants, protection in mouse peritonitis, and induction of endogenous peptide in human monocytes by IFN-gamma and LPS. Basis for the three NEW host-defence annotations. Caveat - in vitro assays use up to 100 micromolar peptide, far above circulating levels.

title: Mechanisms of neuroprotection by a novel rescue factor humanin from Swedish mutant amyloid precursor protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Early mechanistic follow-up on protection against Swedish-mutant APP, with two separable targets of inhibition.

title: A rescue factor abolishing neuronal cell death by a wide spectrum of familial Alzheimer's disease genes and Abeta.
review_notes: Founding study; PubMed-verified. Full text cached. Source of the secretion and neuroprotection evidence and of the original 24-residue assignment.

title: Evidence for in vivo production of Humanin peptide, a neuroprotective factor against Alzheimer's disease-related insults.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only cache. The in vivo detection study UniProt cites for its CAUTION on this entry: HN immunoreactivity in mouse testis and colon, which cannot distinguish the mitochondrial product from the nuclear MT-RNR2-like paralogs.

title: A tripartite motif protein TRIM11 binds and destabilizes Humanin, a neuroprotective peptide against Alzheimer's disease-relevant insults.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. TRIM11 binds and destabilises humanin; relevant to humanin turnover (and its intracellular pool) rather than to a humanin activity.

title: Humanin peptide suppresses apoptosis by interfering with Bax activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2003, Guo et al.). Abstract-only cache. Establishes BAX binding and the block on BAX translocation, and explicitly notes that the mitochondrial genome carries an identical ORF.

title: Two serine residues distinctly regulate the rescue function of Humanin, an inhibiting factor of Alzheimer's disease-related neurotoxicity: functional potentiation by isomerization and dimerization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Ser7-dependent homodimerization and the 2-3 orders of magnitude potency difference between humanin and its D-Ser14/S14G forms - the key caveat on all synthetic-peptide work.

title: Identification of essential amino acids in Humanin, a neuroprotective factor against Alzheimer's disease-relevant insults.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Residue-level mapping of secretion and neuroprotection determinants.

title: Interaction between the Alzheimer's survival peptide humanin and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 3 regulates cell survival and apoptosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Founding IGFBP3 interaction study; maps the binding site and the F6A requirement.

title: Humanin, a newly identified neuroprotective factor, uses the G protein-coupled formylpeptide receptor-like-1 as a functional receptor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. FPRL1-dependent monocyte chemotaxis and competition with amyloid-beta 42 for the receptor; source of both the chemotaxis and the receptor antagonist activity annotations.

title: N-Formylated humanin activates both formyl peptide receptor-like 1 and 2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct binding and activation of FPRL1/FPRL2 with nanomolar EC50 values; the best evidence for the GPCR-ligand annotations.

title: Increased expression of humanin peptide in diffuse-type pigmented villonodular synovitis: implication of its mitochondrial abnormality.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Descriptive pathology of pigmented villonodular synovitis. Supports a mitochondrial pool by EM-immunohistochemistry, but the iron-deposit observation that generated the NAS GO:0006879 row supports no iron-homeostasis function.

title: Interaction of the spectrin-like repeats of alpha-actinin-4 with humanin peptide.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Bacterial two-hybrid screen for actinin-4 ligands; incidental GFP-fusion colocalization. Source of the two rows (ACTN4 protein binding, perinuclear region) recommended for removal or downgrade.

title: Cytoprotective peptide humanin binds and inhibits proapoptotic Bcl-2/Bax family protein BimEL.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Isoform-selective BimEL binding and bax-independent protection.

title: Humanin binds and nullifies Bid activity by blocking its activation of Bax and Bak.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. BID/tBID binding and block of apoptogenic protein release. Note that GOA also uses this reference for a GO:0005102 signaling receptor binding TAS row, which the paper does not itself establish.

title: Involvement of tyrosine kinases and STAT3 in Humanin-mediated neuroprotection.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. STAT3 and tyrosine-kinase dependence, and the explicit negative result that FPR2 knockdown does not abolish neuroprotection in F11 cells.

title: Humanin inhibits neuronal cell death by interacting with a cytokine receptor complex or complexes involving CNTF receptor alpha/WSX-1/gp130.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Identifies the CNTFR/WSX-1/gp130 receptor complex; the basis of the receptor ligand activity annotation.

title: Evidence for potential functionality of nuclearly-encoded humanin isoforms.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only cache. Describes the thirteen nuclear MT-RNR2-like loci and their predicted humanin-like peptides; the basis of the unresolved coding question and of the antibody-specificity caveat applied to the localization rows.

title: Humanin: a novel central regulator of peripheral insulin action.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Central (ICV) humanin improves insulin sensitivity and documents the age-related decline in circulating humanin.

title: Immunolocalization of humanin in human sperm and testis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Two-page immunolocalization report; the only evidence for a nuclear pool and the reason that row is marked over-annotated.

title: VSTM2L is a novel secreted antagonist of the neuroprotective peptide Humanin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies VSTM2L as a secreted humanin antagonist; the functional assertion belongs on VSTM2L.

title: Neuroprotective Peptide humanin inhibits inflammatory response in astrocytes induced by lipopolysaccharide.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Astrocyte LPS model with humanin at 5-20 micromolar, well above the measured receptor potencies; partial effect, no mechanism.

title: Humanin binds MPP8: mapping interaction sites of the peptide and protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. MPP8 interaction mapping with no functional consequence demonstrated.

title: Humanin Peptide Binds to Insulin-Like Growth Factor-Binding Protein 3 (IGFBP3) and Regulates Its Interaction with Importin-β.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Quantifies humanin-IGFBP3 affinity (Kd 5.05 micromolar) and competition with importin-beta1.

title: The Mitochondrial-Derived Peptide Humanin Protects RPE Cells From Oxidative Stress, Senescence, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. RPE protection, STAT3 phosphorylation, and uptake of exogenous labelled peptide into mitochondria - the latter shows import, not synthesis in the organelle.

title: Naturally occurring mitochondrial-derived peptides are age-dependent regulators of apoptosis, insulin sensitivity, and inflammatory markers.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cobb et al., Aging (Albany NY) 2016); full text cached from PMC4925829. The founding description of SHLP1-6: in silico identification of the six ORFs, antibody detection of SHLP1-4 and 6 in mouse tissues (no specific antibody could be raised against SHLP5), and a panel of viability, apoptosis and proliferation assays with synthetic peptides at 100 nM. It is the only publication covering SHLP1, SHLP4, SHLP5 and SHLP6, and for those four peptides it reports a cell-culture phenotype without any molecular mechanism, receptor or binding partner.

title: Solution NMR structure and inhibitory effect against amyloid-β fibrillation of Humanin containing a d-isomerized serine residue.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. NMR structure of humanin D-Ser14 and its amyloid-beta binding and anti-fibrillation activity.

title: Humanin Protects RPE Cells from Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress-Induced Apoptosis by Upregulation of Mitochondrial Glutathione.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. ER-stress protection via mitochondrial glutathione in RPE cells; exogenous peptide.

title: Humanin Specifically Interacts with Amyloid-β Oligomers and Counteracts Their in vivo Toxicity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct SPR binding to amyloid-beta 42 oligomers and thioflavin-T inhibition of fibril formation; supports the amyloid-beta binding replacement term.

title: The Mitochondrial-Derived Peptides, HumaninS14G and Small Humanin-like Peptide 2, Exhibit Chaperone-like Activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Rep 2017); full text cached. Cell-free IAPP misfolding assays with HNG and SHLP2, including the conformer-selectivity controls (EPR, CD) that distinguish seed binding from monomer binding. Supports the misfolded protein binding and anti-fibrillation proposals.

title: Humanin promotes mitochondrial biogenesis in pancreatic MIN6 β-cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. PGC1A-driven mitochondrial biogenesis markers in MIN6 cells after exogenous peptide; the source of the GO:0007005 row judged an over-annotation here.

title: Interaction of Insulin-Like Growth Factor-Binding Protein 3 With Hyaluronan and Its Regulation by Humanin and CD44.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Humanin and hyaluronan compete for the same IGFBP3 segment; supports the IGFBP3 interaction but adds no new humanin activity.

title: Characterizing the protective effects of SHLP2, a mitochondrial-derived peptide, in macular degeneration.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Rep 2018); full text cached. Exogenous SHLP2 in a transmitochondrial AMD ARPE-19 cell model: OXPHOS subunit stabilisation, mtDNA copy number, viability and apoptosis. Phenotypic, single-model, no mechanism; used for context only.

title: Humanin levels in human seminal plasma and spermatozoa are related to sperm quality.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. ELISA quantification in 164 patients plus immunofluorescence; independent replication of the sperm midpiece localization.

title: Humanin induces conformational changes in the apoptosis regulator BAX and sequesters it into fibers, preventing mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. In vitro humanin-BAX co-fibrillation; mechanism for the BAX arm.

title: Humanin Ameliorates Free Fatty Acid-Induced Endothelial Inflammation by Suppressing the NLRP3 Inflammasome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Single HUVEC study with exogenous peptide that generates five GOA process rows (IL1B production, IL18 production, inflammatory response, NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, response to oxidative stress). Sound as far as it goes, but the derived annotation set over-represents it.

title: Humanin selectively prevents the activation of pro-apoptotic protein BID by sequestering it into fibers.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. In vitro humanin-BID co-fibrillation.

title: Mitochondria-derived peptide SHLP2 regulates energy homeostasis through the activation of hypothalamic neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2023); full text cached. Receptor deorphanization by arrayed beta-arrestin screening, direct CXCR7 binding by pulldown, receptor-selective internalisation, patch-clamp and DREADD evidence that POMC neurons mediate the metabolic effect. The strongest mechanistic paper on any SHLP; all peptide work is with synthetic SHLP2.

title: A naturally occurring variant of SHLP2 is a protective factor in Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Psychiatry 2024); full text cached. Source of the inner-membrane localisation (fractionation, Na2CO3 extraction, APEX2 topology) and of the complex I interactome. Its disease claim (the m.2158T>C/K4R variant as a Parkinson protective factor) is disputed by PMID:38940474 and is not used here for any annotation.

title: Investigating the Protective Role of the Mitochondrial 2158 T > C Variant in Parkinson's Disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mov Disord 2024); full text cached. The dispute of the m.2158T>C Parkinson association; cited to record that the variant claim is contested.

title: Mitochondrial-derived peptides, HNG and SHLP3, protect cochlear hair cells against gentamicin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Death Discov 2024); full text cached. Mouse organ-of-Corti explants treated with exogenous HNG or SHLP3 against gentamicin: reduced hair cell loss, oxidative stress and inflammatory gene induction, with AKT/AMPK-alpha modulation. Phenotypic and ex vivo; it identifies no SHLP3 target, so it supports the description but no GO annotation.

title: Sequence and organization of the human mitochondrial genome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Anderson et al., Nature 1981). Cited by UniProt as the genomic sequence source for the MT-RNR2 locus; provides the sequence, not functional information about the peptide.

title: Identification of a novel PSD-95/Dlg/ZO-1 (PDZ)-like protein interacting with the C terminus of presenilin-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 1999;274:32543-6). Correctly cited as the origin of the PSAP name and the presenilin-1 interaction, but its PDZ-like domain assignment has not been borne out and its closing speculation is the sole basis for two NAS annotations that are recommended for removal.

title: The novel presenilin-1-associated protein is a proapoptotic mitochondrial protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2002;277:48913-22). Establishes mitochondrial localisation and an overexpression-induced apoptosis phenotype; the apoptosis result is a gain-of-function readout, so it supports a non-core rather than a core assignment.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; supports the compartment only.

title: MTCH2 is a mitochondrial outer membrane protein insertase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2022). Established the MTCH insertase class. Caveat recorded: the reconstitution evidence in this paper is for MTCH2; for MTCH1 it shows an additive depletion phenotype and a proposal, which is thinner than the IDA code on the MTCH1 annotation implies.

title: Triaging of α-helical proteins to the mitochondrial outer membrane by distinct chaperone machinery based on substrate topology.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Cell 2024;84:1101-1119.e9). Cached entry is abstract-only, so the MTCH1-specific data behind the FlyBase IMP annotations could not be inspected directly; the genome-wide CRISPRi framing is consistent with the annotations and the conclusion is independently confirmed elsewhere.

title: Definition of the human mitochondrial TOM interactome reveals TRABD as a new interacting protein.
review_notes: Source of the MUL1/MAPL interaction; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: The mammalian protein MTCH1 can function as an insertase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Cell Sci 2025;138:jcs263736, PMC12401536). The single most MTCH1-specific functional study available. Its headline contrast - MTCH1 but not MTCH2 rescues the yeast MIM complex - does not contradict MTCH2 insertase activity: the authors attribute the MTCH2 failure to toxicity and ER mislocalisation in yeast, and MTCH2 activity rests on reconstitution with purified protein, which this assay does not address.

title: MTCH2 modulates CPT1 activity to regulate lipid metabolism of adipocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2025). Paralog context only - a reported MTCH2-CPT1 interaction. Not tested on MTCH1 and deliberately not transferred to it.

title: MTCH2 promotes BAX and BAK self-assembly and apoptotic pore growth.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Struct Mol Biol 2026;33:824-837). Paralog context only. Cited to mark the boundary. MTCH1 has its own, older and weaker proapoptotic literature, and the two should not be merged.

title: Structural evolution of the MTCH family of mitochondrial insertases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Adv 2026;12:eaeh2957, PMC13274618). Provides the family-level structural argument that the MTCH clade has diverged from SLC25 transporters, and an independent human-cell demonstration that MTCH1 partially rescues loss of MTCH2.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Membrane proteomics dataset; supports only a root-level membrane location.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Source of the nucleus HDA annotation. Correctly cited, but a sperm-nucleus fraction is exactly where mitochondrial carry-over is expected, and no nuclear function has ever been reported for MTCH2.

title: tBid undergoes multiple conformational changes at the membrane required for Bax activation.
review_notes: Source of the IMP for tBid recruitment to mitochondria. Supports the tBID-platform role, which is distinct from the later-established effect on BAX/BAK self-assembly.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; the source of two bare protein-binding rows and of no functional information about MTCH2.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; supports the compartment only.

title: MTCH2 is a mitochondrial outer membrane protein insertase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2022;378:317-322). The landmark paper for the core molecular function; it is also the source of the MTCH1 annotations, where the evidence is thinner (see the MTCH1 review).

title: Definition of the human mitochondrial TOM interactome reveals TRABD as a new interacting protein.
review_notes: Source of the MUL1/MAPL interaction; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: The mammalian protein MTCH1 can function as an insertase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Cell Sci 2025;138:jcs263736, PMC12401536). Awkward for a framing in which MTCH2 is "the" insertase, but it does not contradict MTCH2 insertase activity: the authors attribute the failure to complement to toxicity and endoplasmic-reticulum mislocalisation in yeast, and MTCH2 activity rests on reconstitution with purified protein, which this heterologous assay does not test. Read the same way in the MTCH1 review.

title: MTCH2 modulates CPT1 activity to regulate lipid metabolism of adipocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2025, PMC12494973). Gives the lipid-homeostasis annotation a concrete mechanism - a direct CPT1 interaction - rather than leaving it as an unexplained knockout phenotype. Whether the effect is separable from insertase activity was not tested.

title: MTCH2 promotes BAX and BAK self-assembly and apoptotic pore growth.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Struct Mol Biol 2026;33:824-837, PMC13186707). The key paper for this update: it refutes the assumption, made in the previous version of this review, that the apoptotic role of MTCH2 is downstream of its insertase activity, and shows instead that it is a separable, lipid-linked function. The molecular activity responsible is still undefined.

title: Structural evolution of the MTCH family of mitochondrial insertases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Adv 2026;12:eaeh2957, PMC13274618). Supplies the structural mechanism for the insertase activity and the strongest evidence that the MTCH family has diverged from SLC25 transport rather than retaining it.

title: Falcon deep research report for human MTCH2
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis, current to roughly 2025. Useful for the insertase framing and the LPA/fusion link; it predates the 2026 structural and BAX/BAK work, and its treatment of the apoptotic role as secondary to insertion has since been superseded.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO electronic pipeline. Maps MTHFD1 to root 'catalytic activity' and 'ATP binding'; correct but uninformative relative to the experimental specific-MF annotations.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer, mostly from mouse Mthfd1 (UniProtKB:Q922D8) and Q3V3R1. Catalytic and one-carbon-metabolism transfers are sound; developmental/craniofacial transfers are whole-animal phenotypes of the ortholog, appropriate to keep as non-core.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central IBA. The phylogenetic backbone correctly reconstructs the two catalytic MFs of the D/C domain, tetrahydrofolate interconversion, and cytosol for this well-characterized enzyme family.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell mapping to cytoplasm; consistent with the experimental cytosol location.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence IDA localizing MTHFD1 to the cytosol; matches known biology.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara ortholog transfer from mouse Mthfd1 (Q922D8). Sources phenotypic developmental BPs (neural tube closure, heart/somite development, neutrophil homeostasis) and transsulfuration; the first are legitimate downstream/pleiotropic consequences, transsulfuration is mis-scoped for this enzyme.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning IEA; cytosol and folic acid metabolic process, both correct but redundant with experimental annotations.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA (ARBA/InterPro/RHEA/EC/ortholog). Reproduces the catalytic MFs and one-carbon BPs electronically; correct but redundant with the experimental record.

title: Structures of three inhibitor complexes provide insight into the reaction mechanism of the human methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase/cyclohydrolase.
review_notes: Structural/mechanistic study of the human enzyme; direct support for the dehydrogenase (GO:0004488) and cyclohydrolase (GO:0004477) activities. Abstract-only in cache but title and content match.

title: The MTHFD1 p.Arg653Gln variant alters enzyme function and increases risk for congenital heart defects.
review_notes: Functional characterization of the human enzyme and R653Q variant; supports the synthetase and dehydrogenase activities and the purine-biosynthesis role.

title: Expression of active domains of a human folate-dependent trifunctional enzyme in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Foundational study defining the two-domain, three-activity architecture of human MTHFD1 by independent domain expression in E. coli. Abstract-only in cache; content matches.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics detecting MTHFD1 in urinary exosome fractions; HDA localization, not indicative of the enzyme's functional compartment.

title: MTRNR2L12: A Candidate Blood Marker of Early Alzheimer's Disease-Like Dementia in Adults with Down Syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Alzheimers Dis 2015;46:145-150, PMCID PMC4878308), full text cached. The only paper named after this locus. Its primary result is sound as far as it goes: microarray plus SYBR Green RQ-PCR in blood mononuclear cells of 48 adults with Down syndrome identified MTRNR2L12 transcript as the single discriminating gene. Three caveats make it unusable as functional evidence. First, it measures transcript, not peptide. Second, it designed its own primers from ENST00000600213 because no commercial assay exists, and does not demonstrate specificity against the twelve near-identical nuclear copies or the mitochondrial rRNA. Third, and the reason for the DISPUTED flag, its discussion asserts without any citation that the presence of the MTRNR2L12 peptide has been confirmed in brain tissue; I could find no primary report of an HN12 peptide, and that sentence should not be propagated into annotation.

title: Methionine synthase and methionine synthase reductase interact with MMACHC and with MMADHC.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes MSR interactions with MMACHC and MMADHC and the cytosolic multiprotein Cbl-processing complex (MS, MSR, MMACHC, MMADHC); supports the protein-binding IPI and cobalamin-metabolism annotations.

title: Cloning and mapping of a cDNA for methionine synthase reductase, a flavoprotein defective in patients with homocystinuria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Cloning of MTRR as the reducing system maintaining methionine synthase; cblE mutations confirm identity; FNR-family membership; cytosolic targeting predicted. Foundational reference.

title: Falcon deep research report for MVB12A
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep research report (Edison/Falcon). Useful as a structured synthesis that is consistent with the primary literature already cited in this review (Morita 2007, Audhya 2007, Boura/Hurley 2012, Flower 2020). It correctly anchors MVB12A as a structural/adapter fourth subunit of ESCRT-I (UMA domain) with an N-terminal MABP membrane-targeting domain, and it adds one genuinely new MVB12A-specific finding: the 2025 Zhang et al. study (mBio, doi:10.1128/mbio.00979-25) showing MVB12A knockdown impairs beta-coronavirus virion egress without blocking assembly. CAUTION: many statements in the report ascribe whole-ESCRT-I-complex or pan-MVB12-family functions (cytokinesis/abscission, membrane repair, autophagosome closure, exosome biogenesis, ubiquitin-dependent MVB sorting) to MVB12A by inference from the holo-complex or from the MVB12B/UBAP1 paralogs rather than from MVB12A-specific perturbation; e.g. UBAP1-, not MVB12A-, containing ESCRT-I is the one shown to be required for ubiquitin-dependent MVB sorting (Stefani 2011), and the autophagosome-closure assay perturbed VPS28, not MVB12A (Flower 2020). MVB12A-specific claims are kept anchored; holo-complex/paralog inferences are not used to upgrade annotations. Identifier and supporting-text claims have not been independently verified against the cited primary papers, hence UNVERIFIED.

title: Falcon deep research report for MVB12B
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report (Edison/Falcon); not independently verified against primary full text, so marked UNVERIFIED. MVB12B-SPECIFIC and well-anchored: (1) MVB12B is a fourth-subunit ESCRT-I member that acts as a structural/adaptor subunit in sorting ubiquitinated cargo into MVBs, and (2) the TBK1/STING-dependent phosphorylation of MVB12B (S222) that drives sorting of DNA into extracellular vesicles for paracrine cGAS-STING signaling (Nandakumar 2019; Kuchitsu 2023) -- this immune/EV-sorting axis is a genuine MVB12B-specific function not currently captured in the GOA rows. CAUTION: many statements about cytokinesis/abscission, autophagosome closure, membrane repair, and broad enveloped-virus egress are explicitly flagged in the report as ESCRT-I holo-complex level (or MVB12A-paralog structural inference, e.g. the human ESCRT-I head structure was solved with MVB12A not MVB12B) rather than MVB12B-specific, and should not be attributed to the MVB12B subunit. Used here only to corroborate the MVB12B adaptor/cargo-sorting and ESCRT-I-membership annotations, not to add holo-complex processes.

title: Absence of functional peroxisomes does not lead to deficiency of enzymes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis.
review_notes: Shows MVD (and other MVA-pathway enzymes) retain activity in peroxisome-deficient cells; supports cytosolic function, not a specific catalytic characterization of MVD.

title: Mortalin-MPD (mevalonate pyrophosphate decarboxylase) interactions and their role in control of cellular proliferation.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid / co-IP interaction between MPD (MVD) and mortalin (mot-2/GRP75, an HSP70-family protein). Supports the Hsp70-binding IPI but this is an interaction finding, not MVD's core molecular function.

title: Cholesterol biosynthesis is not defective in peroxisome biogenesis defective fibroblasts.
review_notes: Measures MVD (MPD) activity among five presqualene MVA/isoprenoid enzymes in PBD fibroblasts; supports enzymatic activity and cytosolic function.

title: Human mevalonate pyrophosphate decarboxylase is localized in the cytosol.
review_notes: Definitive subcellular localization study; MVD is cytosolic with no peroxisomal localization. Directly supports the cytosol/NOT-peroxisome annotations.

title: Human mevalonate diphosphate decarboxylase: characterization, investigation of the mevalonate diphosphate binding site, and crystal structure.
review_notes: Full text available. Recombinant human MDD characterization, kinetics, active-site mutagenesis (R161, N17) and 2.4 A crystal structure (3D4J). Directly establishes the diphosphomevalonate decarboxylase activity and reaction.

title: Molecular cloning and expression of the cDNAs encoding human and yeast mevalonate pyrophosphate decarboxylase.
review_notes: Cloning and expression of human MVD; recombinant enzyme is a homodimer of 43-kDa subunits with measurable decarboxylase activity. Supports catalytic activity and homodimerization.

title: Regulation of proliferation and Ras localization in transformed cells by products of mevalonate metabolism.
review_notes: Uses 6-fluoromevalonate (Fmev, an MVD inhibitor) to block downstream mevalonate products and Ras prenylation, suppressing proliferation. Supports a pathway-level role in proliferation but the effect is indirect (via prenylated products), not a direct MVD signalling function.

title: Post-translational regulation of mevalonate kinase by intermediates of the cholesterol and nonsterol isoprene biosynthetic pathways.
review_notes: Expressed and assayed recombinant human MDDase (MVD) alongside MKase and PMKase; the focus is feedback inhibition of MKase, but MVD activity and kinetics (KM for mevalonate diphosphate) were determined. Supports catalytic activity.

title: Mutations in MVK, encoding mevalonate kinase, cause hyperimmunoglobulinaemia D and periodic fever syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes that MVK loss-of-function mutations reduce MK activity and cause HIDS; supports the mevalonate kinase activity IMP.

title: Investigation of invariant serine/threonine residues in mevalonate kinase. Tests of the functional significance of a proposed substrate binding motif and a site implicated in human inherited disease.
review_notes: Mutagenesis of Ser-146/T243 defines catalytic and substrate-binding roles in the human enzyme; supports mevalonate kinase activity.

title: Molecular cloning of human mevalonate kinase and identification of a missense mutation in the genetic disease mevalonic aciduria.
review_notes: Cloning and functional expression of human MVK; links enzyme to mevalonic aciduria.

title: Cholesterol biosynthesis is not defective in peroxisome biogenesis defective fibroblasts.
review_notes: Measured MK activity directly and showed the presqualene enzymes function independent of peroxisomes; supports cytosolic activity.

title: Mevalonate kinase is a cytosolic enzyme in humans.
review_notes: Definitive multi-method demonstration that human MK is cytosolic, not peroxisomal; grounds the cytosol annotations and the NOT peroxisome call.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map recording the MK self-interaction; consistent with homodimer but low individual informativeness.

title: AA amyloidosis complicating hyperimmunoglobulinemia D with periodic fever syndrome: a report of two cases.
review_notes: Cited to support GO:0050728 negative regulation of inflammatory response, but this is a two-patient AA amyloidosis case report and does not demonstrate a direct MK-mediated regulation of inflammation; the inflammatory phenotype is a downstream consequence of MKD.

title: Biochemical and structural basis for feedback inhibition of mevalonate kinase and isoprenoid metabolism.
review_notes: Crystal structure (PDB 2R3V) and biochemistry of human MK; defines competitive feedback inhibition at the ATP site.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Identification of catalytic residues in human mevalonate kinase.
review_notes: Direct characterization of recombinant human MK as a homodimer and identification of catalytic residues (Asp-204, Glu-193).

title: Post-translational regulation of mevalonate kinase by intermediates of the cholesterol and nonsterol isoprene biosynthetic pathways.

title: Evolution of the holozoan ribosome biogenesis regulon.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Brown, Cole & Erives 2008 BMC Genomics), full text cached. Comparative promoter analysis (computational only) linking CACGTG E-boxes in ribosome biogenesis gene promoters to Myc-bearing holozoan genomes, including Monosiga; no functional test in choanoflagellates.

The GOA rows citing it (protein binding with RAB3A, lysosome localization, regulated exocytosis, regulation of plasma membrane repair) exactly match PMID:27325790 (Rab3a/Slp4-a/NMHC-IIA complex), which is also cited by GOA with the same RAB3A partner; the cited id is a truncation of 27325790.

review_notes: Full text cached; identifies NMHC-IIA as a Rab3a effector required for lysosome positioning, lysosome exocytosis and plasma membrane repair.
