review_notes: Mouse dendritic cells and Dictyostelium; MYH9-GFP enriched behind the nucleus during nucleokinesis and myosin II inhibition impairs it. Pharmacological inhibition is not paralog specific.

title: Control of muscle formation by the fusogenic micropeptide myomixer.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2017;356:323-327). One of three independent 2017 discovery papers for this gene; source of the mouse plasma membrane localisation, the embryonic knockout phenotype and the MYMK co-immunoprecipitation. Full text available in the cache.

title: The microprotein Minion controls cell fusion and muscle formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2017;8:15664). The paper that identified the human ORF (KY857877) and showed it rescues fusion, with frameshift controls proving the activity is protein-borne. Note that its ER/Golgi evidence is a mixed membrane fraction, which is the root of the ER and Golgi annotations reviewed here. The task brief attributed this work to Genes Dev; PubMed places it in Nat Commun.

title: Myomerger induces fusion of non-fusogenic cells and is required for skeletal muscle development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2017;8:15665). The third independent discovery paper; source of the muscle-specific expression pattern and of the reconstitution of fusion in non-fusogenic fibroblasts together with myomaker.

title: Requirement of the fusogenic micropeptide myomixer for muscle formation in zebrafish.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2017;114:11950-11955). Establishes that the fusion requirement is conserved in zebrafish and that fish and reptile orthologs substitute for the mammalian protein, which supports the IBD node placement behind the IBA rows. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Fusogenic micropeptide Myomixer is essential for satellite cell fusion and muscle regeneration.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2018;115:3864-3869). This is the experimental basis of the mouse regeneration annotations (GO:0014905, GO:0043403) that reach human MYMX by orthology; it is not the paper GOA cites on the human gene. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Myomaker and Myomerger Work Independently to Control Distinct Steps of Membrane Remodeling during Myoblast Fusion.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Dev Cell 2018;46:767-780.e7). The mechanistic core of this review: establishes cell-surface topology, the hemifusion/pore division of labour with MYMK, rescue by purified ectodomain in trans, and MYMK-independent activity. Full text cached.

title: Myomerger promotes fusion pore by elastic coupling between proximal membrane leaflets and hemifusion diaphragm.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2021;12:495). Provides the biophysical measurement - positive spontaneous curvature generated by the isolated ectodomain - that underpins the proposed molecular function. Full text cached.

title: Impaired activity of the fusogenic micropeptide Myomixer causes myopathy resembling Carey-Fineman-Ziter syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Clin Invest 2022;132:e159002) and the correct, indeed the only, paper for human MYMX loss of function; it establishes CFZS2. It is flagged MISCITED only with respect to the specific GOA row that uses it as IMP evidence for GO:0014905 myoblast fusion involved in skeletal muscle regeneration: the full text contains no injury or regeneration experiment, and regeneration is mentioned only in the introduction citing the earlier mouse satellite-cell study. The paper fully supports GO:0007520 myoblast fusion, which is the proposed replacement.

title: Evolution of a chordate-specific mechanism for myoblast fusion.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Sci Adv 2022;8:eadd2696). Background for the description: MYMX arose de novo in early vertebrates whereas MYMK predates it, which explains the narrow phylogenetic scope of the PANTHER family. Full text cached.

title: Phosphatidylserine orchestrates Myomerger membrane insertions to drive myoblast fusion.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2022;119:e2202490119). Defines the roles of the two ectodomain helices and shows that externalised phosphatidylserine licenses their membrane insertion, which is how the destabilising activity is confined to fusion sites. Full text cached.

title: Mutations of the protocadherin gene PCDH15 cause Usher syndrome type 1F.
review_notes: The identifier resolves to the intended paper by Ahmed et al. 2001 on PCDH15 and USH1F, but that paper is an experimental study of PCDH15, not of MYO7A; MYO7A appears only in background statements about known Usher genes. It is therefore a weak citation for the two MYO7A IMP annotations (GO:0007605 and GO:0050953) made against it. The underlying claims are correct and are properly supported by PMID:7870171.

title: MyRIP, a novel Rab effector, enables myosin VIIa recruitment to retinal melanosomes.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms yeast two-hybrid identification of MYRIP as a myosin-VIIa tail ligand, co-immunoprecipitation and direct in vitro binding, GTP-dependent RAB27A binding, and immunoelectron-microscopic colocalisation of MYRIP, RAB27A and myosin VIIa on retinal melanosomes.

title: Impaired calmodulin binding of myosin-7A causes autosomal dominant hearing loss (DFNA11).
review_notes: Abstract-only in the local cache. Supports calmodulin binding by the MYO7A IQ5 motif and its loss in the DFNA11 p.R853C variant. The assay used IQ5-containing peptides expressed in smooth muscle cells, a heterologous system, so the cytosol localisation annotated against it is weakly grounded.

title: The unconventional myosin-VIIa associates with lysosomes.
review_notes: Full text confirms myosin-VIIa association with cathepsin D- and RAB7-positive lysosomes in human ARPE-19 cells, co-purification on density gradients, and tight association with the lysosome surface.

title: Function of MYO7A in the human RPE and the validity of shaker1 mice as a model for Usher syndrome 1B.
review_notes: Human primary RPE cells with RNAi knockdown of MYO7A. Establishes that the motor constrains long-range melanosome movements in human cells, matching the mouse phenotype. Used here to support a new melanosome localization annotation.

title: Functional characterization of the human myosin-7a motor domain.
review_notes: Full text confirms the kinetic characterisation of the human myosin-7a motor domain, with rate-limiting ADP release, a high duty ratio, high F-actin affinity, Mg2+-sensitive regulation and in vitro actin sliding. The construct is the isolated motor domain fused to an artificial lever arm, so the measurements describe the motor module rather than the autoinhibited full-length molecule.

title: Myosin VIIa and sans localization at stereocilia upper tip-link density implicates these Usher syndrome proteins in mechanotransduction.
review_notes: Full text confirms immunolocalisation of MYO7A and sans to the upper tip-link density in hair cells and the tripartite MYO7A, sans and harmonin-b complex in a heterologous system. The hair cells are rodent, hence ISS rather than IDA for the human protein.

title: Alterations of the CIB2 calcium- and integrin-binding protein cause Usher syndrome type 1J and nonsyndromic deafness DFNB48.
review_notes: Full text confirms an interaction between CIB2 and myosin VIIa. The focus of the paper is CIB2 rather than MYO7A, and it also reports that CIB2 localisation at stereocilia tips is unaffected in Myo7a mutant mice.

title: The giant spectrin βV couples the molecular motors to phototransduction and Usher syndrome type I proteins along their trafficking route.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the local cache, but the abstract explicitly reports spectrin betaV as a myosin VIIa- and rhodopsin-interacting partner in photoreceptor cells, supporting the spectrin binding annotation.

title: Defective myosin VIIA gene responsible for Usher syndrome type 1B.
review_notes: The founding human genetic evidence linking MYO7A loss of function to USH1B, comprising deafness, vestibular dysfunction and retinitis pigmentosa. Abstract-only in the cache but unambiguous.

title: Human Usher 1B/mouse shaker-1: the retinal phenotype discrepancy explained by the presence/absence of myosin VIIA in the photoreceptor cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Establishes myosin-VIIA expression in human but not rodent photoreceptors and its localisation to the inner segment, base of the outer segment and synaptic ending region. The developmental interpretation annotated as IC (GO:0042462) goes beyond what the localisation data show.

title: N-terminal acetylation shields proteins from degradation and promotes age-dependent motility and longevity.

title: Falcon deep research report for NAA30
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) deep-research report; not independently verified against primary full text and treated as UNVERIFIED. NAA30-catalytic-specific claims used here (GNAT-fold acetyl-CoA-dependent transfer to the N-terminal alpha-amino group; NatC Met-hydrophobic substrate class distinct from NatA/NatB; ribosome co-sedimentation; N-degron shielding) are consistent with the cached primary literature (PMID:19398576, PMID:37891180) and with UniProt. The report also generalizes across the NatC complex and other NATs and attributes some functions to auxiliary subunits (e.g. NAA35 as ribosome anchor, NAA38 broadening substrate specificity/thermostability) and to broader NatC biology (mitochondrial integrity, Golgi/vesicle trafficking, cullin neddylation via UBE2M/UBE2F, cancer/development) - these are complex-level or pathway-level claims and were NOT used to assert new NAA30-specific catalytic molecular functions.

title: Knockdown of human N alpha-terminal acetyltransferase complex C leads to p53-dependent apoptosis and aberrant human Arl8b localization.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches the YAML title; GOA anchors this PMID to IDA for GO:0031417 (NatC complex) and IMP for GO:0043066 (negative regulation of apoptosis) for NAA35. This is the NatC complex-characterization paper establishing NAA35 (hMak10) as an auxiliary/scaffold subunit, the gene's core function.

title: N-terminal acetylation shields proteins from degradation and promotes age-dependent motility and longevity.

title: Falcon deep research report for NAA35
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report. It correctly and repeatedly states that NAA35 does NOT itself catalyze N-terminal acetylation and that catalysis resides exclusively in NAA30 (GNAT fold); NAA35's role is architectural/scaffolding and ribosome-binding. No mis-attribution of catalytic acetyltransferase activity to the auxiliary subunit was detected. Underlying primary sources (Grunwald 2020 NatC crystal structure; Varland 2023 N-degron shielding) are consistent with the NatC literature, but the specific structural/genetic-interaction claims were not independently verified against full text here, so correctness is left UNVERIFIED.

title: Falcon deep research report for NAALADL2
review_notes: LLM-synthesized report (Edison/falcon); its own header notes "no contexts were retrieved" and that key primary papers (e.g. Whitaker et al. 2014) were inaccessible, so cited DOIs are not independently confirmed here. Usefully, it does NOT over-assert peptidase/NAALADase catalytic activity by homology -- it explicitly affirms NAALADL2 is inactive ("structure-related homology without validated enzyme activity"), consistent with UniProt. Disease associations (prostate/breast cancer, Kawasaki GWAS, NAALADL2-AS2 biomarker) are correctly flagged by the report as associative/expression-level and not mechanistic; treat them as background, not as evidence for a molecular function. Catalytic-activity-by-homology and disease-mechanism claims remain UNVERIFIED pending primary-source review.

title: Quantitative nucleotide resolution profiling of RNA cytidine acetylation by ac4C-seq.

title: [Profanities and the profane person].

It is cited in GOA as the IDA support for GO:0060090 and GO:0030674 and is a digit-dropped form of PMID:31189953 (Sharif et al., Nature 2019, NEK7-licensed activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome), which supports the neighbouring annotations made on the same dates. Correctly cited and scientifically sound, but the annotations derived from it (GO:0032691, GO:0050728) invert the direction of the biology: the mutations are gain-of-function and the patients are hyper-inflammatory. Correctly identified, and reasonable as TAS support for the general cytoplasm and defense-response annotations, but it is cited in GOA as the support for GO:0042834 peptidoglycan binding, a ligand-binding molecular function for which neither this review nor any primary study provides direct evidence. That is the basis for the REMOVE on that annotation.

title: Silica crystals and aluminum salts activate the NALP3 inflammasome through phagosomal destabilization.
review_notes: Hornung et al. 2008. Cited in GOA as IDA support for molecular sensor activity, but the paper's own conclusion is that what NLRP3 senses is lysosomal damage downstream of phagocytosis, not the crystal itself - which is why that annotation is marked over-annotated. Note PubMed records a 2026 erratum for this article (Nat Immunol 27(4):881).

title: The receptor NLRP3 is a transcriptional regulator of TH2 differentiation.
review_notes: Bruchard et al., Nat Immunol 2015, doi 10.1038/ni.3202 - PubMed-verified. The sole primary source behind every DNA-binding, IRF4-binding, nuclear and T helper 2 annotation on human NLRP3, all of which reach the human gene by IBA or ISS from mouse Nlrp3. Single laboratory, mouse only, carries a published corrigendum (PMID:26580508), and no NLRP3 DNA-binding domain or NLRP3-DNA structure has been reported since despite extensive structural work. Flagged DISPUTED rather than MISCITED: the citation is correct, the claim is uncorroborated.

title: Corrigendum: The receptor NLRP3 is a transcriptional regulator of TH2 differentiation.
review_notes: Corrigendum to PMID:26098997 (Nat Immunol 2015). Cited so that the correction is visible alongside the primary claim; the corrigendum text itself was not available.

review_notes: Sharif et al., Nature 2019, NEK7-licensed NLRP3 activation. Verified; also the paper that PMID:1189953 in GOA is a corrupted reference to.

Bears on cellular-component and assembly annotations; makes no molecular-function claim, and is not used here to change one.

title: The centrosomal hub unifies regulatory factors of NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PNAS 2026, doi 10.1073/pnas.2612800123, Wu M & Wu H). PubMed indexes the abstract but PMC access is restricted, so only the abstract was read. Supports the centrosomal condensate framing and the finding that NLRP3 overexpression can bypass both NEK7 and priming for K+-efflux-driven activation. Partly in tension with PMID:42215451 over NEK7 dependence; both are cited and the tension is stated rather than resolved.

title: NLRX1 is a mitochondrial NOD-like receptor that amplifies NF-kappaB and JNK pathways by inducing reactive oxygen species production.

review_notes: Source of the NLRX1-TUFM protein-binding annotation; the TUFM interaction is the mechanistic link to NLRX1's autophagy role (TUFM recruits ATG5-ATG12).

title: Falcon deep research report for NLRX1
review_notes: LLM synthesis (Edison/Falcon) built almost entirely from recent secondary reviews (Bi 2024, Pickering 2021, Chou 2023/2022, Jewell 2024) and very recent primary papers (Xiao 2025 mPTP; Zhang 2026 acetyl-CoA; Song 2024 SLC39A7) that are NOT in the local publications cache, so the cited claims could not be verified against primary text and are marked UNVERIFIED. Several claims are debated or go beyond what the cached primary literature shows: (1) Localization - falcon asserts NLRX1 is in the matrix and inner mitochondrial membrane in addition to the outer membrane, whereas the foundational cached papers (PMID:18200010, PMID:22749352) place its MAVS-regulatory activity at the mitochondrial outer membrane; the matrix/inner-membrane and mPTP claims rest on uncached 2024-2025 work. (2) Mitophagy - falcon frames direct NLRX1-LC3 binding and mitophagy as the overarching function, but the cached full-text PMID:22749352 states mitophagy "was not occurring under these test conditions" and that NLRX1 promotes (non-selective) autophagy indirectly via TUFM/ATG5-ATG12, not by direct LC3 binding; the LC3-receptor/acetyl-CoA model is newer and not independently verified here. (3) NF-kappaB - falcon (citing reviews) reports NLRX1 NEGATIVELY regulates NF-kappaB, which contradicts the human-specific cached primary report (PMID:18219313) that NLRX1 AMPLIFIES NF-kappaB/JNK via ROS; this confirms the field is genuinely mixed. Useful as a pointer to recent literature and to flag controversy, but not used as sole support for any annotation action change.

title: IgSF21 promotes differentiation of inhibitory synapses via binding to neurexin2α.
review_notes: Tanabe et al. 2017; full text. IgSF21 binds only neurexin-2-alpha (LNS1) and recruits axonal NRX2alpha in trans to induce inhibitory presynaptic differentiation.

title: Neurexin-2: An inhibitory neurexin that restricts excitatory synapse formation in the hippocampus.
review_notes: Lin et al. 2023 Sci Adv; full text. Neuronal Nrxn2 deletion increases CA1 excitatory synapse density and release probability. A 2025 editorial expression of concern was removed in 2026 with an erratum (PMID:41824587) and the conclusions were maintained, but the companion PNAS paper (PMID:36961922) was retracted, and the finding conflicts with Born et al. 2015 (whose mouse line this paper disputes). Single-laboratory result; used with that caveat.

title: Advances in neurexin studies and the emerging role of neurexin-2 in autism spectrum disorder.
review_notes: Khoja et al. 2023 review of NRXN2 mouse models; used for retrieval, claims checked against primary papers.

title: Conditional deletion of Neurexin-2 alters neuronal network activity in hippocampal circuitries and leads to spontaneous seizures.
review_notes: Haile et al. 2023; Emx1-Cre Nrxn2 cKO: reduced social preference, increased network activity, spontaneous seizures.

title: Conditional deletion of neurexin-2 impaired behavioral flexibility to alterations in action-outcome contingency.
review_notes: Khoja and Chen 2024; Nrxn2 cKO impairs reversal learning and goal-directed/habitual discrimination.

title: Falcon deep research report on NRXN2
review_notes: LLM-generated literature synthesis used only as retrieval support; claims checked against primary papers. It presents the anti-synaptogenic role as established without noting the conflicting data or the retraction of the companion PNAS paper.

title: Mints as adaptors. Direct binding to neurexins and recruitment of munc18.
review_notes: Biederer and Sudhof 2000 (abstract only); Mint1/Mint2 bind neurexin tails directly via PDZ domains.

title: A stoichiometric complex of neurexins and dystroglycan in brain.
review_notes: Sugita et al. 2001; LNS2 of all alpha-neurexins, including neurexin-3-alpha, binds dystroglycan Ca2+-dependently.

title: Structure and evolution of neurexin genes: insight into the mechanism of alternative splicing.
review_notes: Tabuchi and Sudhof 2002 (abstract only); neurexin gene structure, alpha/beta promoters, extensive splicing.

title: Identification and characterization of heart-specific splicing of human neurexin 3 mRNA (NRXN3).
review_notes: Occhi et al. 2002 (abstract only); NRXN3 expression outside brain and heart-specific splice variants.

title: Alpha-neurexins couple Ca2+ channels to synaptic vesicle exocytosis.
review_notes: Missler et al. 2003 (abstract only); alpha-neurexin triple knockouts (including Nrxn3-alpha) show impaired Ca2+-triggered release.

title: Neurexins induce differentiation of GABA and glutamate postsynaptic specializations via neuroligins.
review_notes: Graf et al. 2004; family-level neurexin induction of GABAergic and glutamatergic postsynaptic differentiation.

title: Neurexins: synaptic cell surface proteins related to the alpha-latrotoxin receptor and laminin.
review_notes: Ushkaryov et al. 1992 Science (abstract only); neurexin discovery paper reporting at least two neurexin genes. Supports family membrane/synaptic localization; does not characterize neurexin-3; the axon-guidance statement is only sequence similarity.

title: Deletion of alpha-neurexins does not cause a major impairment of axonal pathfinding or synapse formation.
review_notes: Dudanova et al. 2007 (abstract only); alpha-neurexins not required for axon pathfinding or most synapse formation.

title: Genomewide suggestive linkage of opioid dependence to chromosome 14q.
review_notes: Lachman et al. 2007 (abstract only); suggestive linkage of opioid dependence to a broad 14q region encompassing NRXN3, driven by one ancestry subset.

title: Neurexin 3 polymorphisms are associated with alcohol dependence and altered expression of specific isoforms.
review_notes: Hishimoto et al. 2007 (abstract only); candidate-gene SNP association with alcohol dependence near SS5 (P = 0.0007, not genome-wide) and allele-associated isoform expression differences in postmortem cortex.

title: Neuroligins and neurexins link synaptic function to cognitive disease.
review_notes: Sudhof 2008 review (abstract only); family-level framing of neurexins as synaptic adhesion molecules.

title: NRXN3 is a novel locus for waist circumference: a genome-wide association study from the CHARGE Consortium.
review_notes: Heard-Costa et al. 2009 PLoS Genet; NRXN3 locus associated with waist circumference (genome-wide significant only in combined analysis); no mechanism.

title: Rare deletions at the neurexin 3 locus in autism spectrum disorder.
review_notes: Vaags et al. 2012 AJHG; full text. Four ASD probands with NRXN3 exonic deletions (one de novo), incomplete penetrance; source of the BHF-UCL IGI behaviour rows. No learning or vocalization phenotype is characterized.

title: High affinity neurexin binding to cell adhesion G-protein-coupled receptor CIRL1/latrophilin-1 produces an intercellular adhesion complex.
review_notes: Boucard et al. 2012; neurexin-3-beta (SS4-) binds CL1/latrophilin-1 (about 10-fold lower affinity than neurexin-1/2-beta) and mediates cell aggregation.

title: Presynaptic neurexin-3 alternative splicing trans-synaptically controls postsynaptic AMPA receptor trafficking.
review_notes: Aoto et al. 2013 Cell; Nrxn3 SS4 knockin mice; presynaptic SS4 inclusion decreases postsynaptic AMPA receptors and blocks LTP. No correction or retraction found.

title: Distinct circuit-dependent functions of presynaptic neurexin-3 at GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses.
review_notes: Aoto et al. 2015 Nat Neurosci; Nrxn3 alpha/beta cKO. Hippocampus: extracellular Nrxn3 stabilizes postsynaptic AMPARs; olfactory bulb: intracellular sequences needed for GABA release. Source of SynGO mouse Nrxn3 annotations.

title: Human neurexin-3α antibodies associate with encephalitis and alter synapse development.
review_notes: Gresa-Arribas et al. 2016 Neurology; neurexin-3-alpha autoantibody encephalitis; patient IgG reduces neurexin-3-alpha clusters and synapse number in developing cultures.

title: A Missense Variant at the Nrxn3 Locus Enhances Empathy Fear in the Mouse.
review_notes: Keum et al. 2018 Neuron (abstract only); Nrxn3 R498W variant and SST+ ACC deletion enhance observational fear.

title: Alternative Splicing of Presynaptic Neurexins Differentially Controls Postsynaptic NMDA and AMPA Receptor Responses.
review_notes: Dai, Aoto and Sudhof 2019 Neuron; SS4 of Nrxn1, Nrxn2 and Nrxn3 have distinct effects. Carries a 2024 erratum (PMID:38330900); the Nrxn3 AMPAR finding agrees with Aoto 2013/2015.

title: Modeling a Neurexin-3α Human Mutation in Mouse Neurons Identifies a Novel Role in the Regulation of Transsynaptic Signaling and Neurotransmitter Release at Excitatory Synapses.
review_notes: Restrepo et al. 2019 J Neurosci (Aoto lab); human-patient A687T neurexin-3-alpha variant modelled in mouse neurons; cell aggregation with NLGN1-3/LRRTM2; presynaptic gain of function.

title: GluD1 is a signal transduction device disguised as an ionotropic receptor.
review_notes: Dai et al. 2021 Nature; Nrxn3SS4+-Cbln2-GluD1 suppresses AMPARs. Carries a 2025 erratum (PMID:40481306); no retraction. Source of the mouse Nrxn3 GO:0099557 IDA.

title: Neurexin-3 defines synapse- and sex-dependent diversity of GABAergic inhibition in ventral subiculum.
review_notes: Boxer et al. 2021 Cell Rep (Aoto lab); sex- and synapse-dependent Nrxn3 functions at PV synapses in ventral subiculum.

title: Targeted proteoform mapping uncovers specific Neurexin-3 variants required for dendritic inhibition.
review_notes: Hauser et al. 2022 Neuron (Scheiffele lab); GPI-anchored NRXN3 AS5 proteoform required at dendrite-targeting interneuron synapses.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Gogl et al. 2022; high-throughput PBM-PDZ affinity mapping (erratum PMID:36477203). NRXN3 is not named in the narrative; source of the IntAct IPI rows with APBA1, PATJ, LNX1, GRIP2.

title: Distinct neurexin-cerebellin complexes control AMPA- and NMDA-receptor responses in a circuit-dependent manner.
review_notes: Dai et al. 2022 eLife; circuit-dependent Nrxn3SS4+-cerebellin signalling (correction PMID:37943030).

title: A combinatorial code of neurexin-3 alternative splicing controls inhibitory synapses via a trans-synaptic dystroglycan signaling loop.
review_notes: Trotter et al. 2023 Nat Commun; Nrxn3 SS2/SS4 splicing and dystroglycan binding set inhibitory release probability in olfactory bulb and PFC. No correction found.

title: Neurexin-3 subsynaptic densities are spatially distinct from Neurexin-1 and essential for excitatory synapse nanoscale organization in the hippocampus.
review_notes: Lloyd et al. 2023 Nat Commun (Aoto lab); dSTORM shows Nrxn3 subsynaptic densities opposite postsynaptic ligands.

title: Regulation of hippocampal mossy fiber-CA3 synapse function by a Bcl11b/C1ql2/Nrxn3(25b+) pathway.
review_notes: Koumoundourou et al. 2024 eLife; C1ql2 acts through the Nrxn3(25b+) splice variant at mossy fibre synapses.

title: A Systematic Structure-Function Characterization of a Human Mutation in Neurexin-3α Reveals an Extracellular Modulatory Sequence That Stabilizes Neuroligin-1 Binding to Enhance the Postsynaptic Properties of Excitatory Synapses.
review_notes: Stokes et al. 2024 J Neurosci; A687 residue of neurexin-3-alpha modulates neuroligin-1/3 binding.

title: Presynaptic Nrxn3 is essential for ribbon-synapse maturation in hair cells.
review_notes: Jukic et al. 2024 Development; Nrxn3 required for ribbon-synapse maturation in hair cells (mouse, zebrafish).

title: CASK: a novel dlg/PSD95 homolog with an N-terminal calmodulin-dependent protein kinase domain identified by interaction with neurexins.
review_notes: Hata et al. 1996 (abstract only); CASK binding to neurexin I requires the C-terminal residues shared by NRXN3.

title: The gene mutated in bare patches and striated mice encodes a novel 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Identifies the gene and establishes its role in cholesterol biosynthesis via mouse Bpa/Str alleles; abstract-only cache.

title: Mutations in the NSDHL gene, encoding a 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, cause CHILD syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes NSDHL-CHILD syndrome link and cholesterol-pathway role; abstract-only cache.

title: Identification of major proteins in the lipid droplet-enriched fraction isolated from the human hepatocyte cell line HuH7.
review_notes: Lipid-droplet proteomics; the abstract does not name NSDHL specifically (curator full-text-based IDA), so treated as supporting the LD localization only.

title: Hypomorphic temperature-sensitive alleles of NSDHL cause CK syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Basis for the EXP ER-membrane localization and CK syndrome association; abstract-only cache.

title: Human lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferases 1 and 2 are located in lipid droplets where they catalyze the formation of phosphatidylcholine.
review_notes: About LPCAT1/2; the abstract does not mention NSDHL (curator full-text IDA). Supports the LD localization context.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; correctly cited but yields only uninformative 'protein binding'.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome screen; correctly cited but uninformative for MF.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO mapping. Correctly applied, but produces only generic parents where the exact reaction is known from experiment.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Orthology transfers from mouse Nsun2. Appropriate for the tRNA stabilisation and for the skin and stem-cell phenotypes, which are genuine mouse knockout results.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The tRNA-related IBAs on this gene are sound. Three others (rRNA C5 methyltransferase activity, rRNA processing, mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit assembly) name mouse Nsun4 as the donor in the GOA WITH/FROM column and appear to carry a paralogue-specific function onto NSUN2.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Subcellular-location mapping. Nucleolus, cytoplasm and mitochondrion are right; extracellular region is an over-reach from the exosome observation.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning annotations. tRNA methylation is right; mRNA processing is the wrong branch for what NSUN2 does to mRNA.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automatic methods; consistent with the manual annotations on this gene.

title: Identification of human tRNA:m5C methyltransferase catalysing intron-dependent m5C formation in the first position of the anticodon of the pre-tRNA Leu (CAA).
review_notes: Full text available and read. Founding identification of the human Trm4 orthologue, with single-nucleotide substrate specificity and yeast complementation. Basis of the core molecular function.

title: The tRNA methyltransferase NSun2 stabilizes p16INK⁴ mRNA by methylating the 3'-untranslated region of p16.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Reports in vitro methylation of the p16 3'UTR and an mRNA half-life effect, but the site is given as "A988", and the paper carries an erratum (Nat Commun 2013;4:2703). Supports the mRNA activity in principle while illustrating why site-level claims in this literature need orthogonal confirmation.

title: Whole exome sequencing identifies a splicing mutation in NSUN2 as a cause of a Dubowitz-like syndrome.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Human loss-of-function genetics: patient cells lack NSUN2 and lose m5C at C47/C48 of tRNA-Asp, confirming the substrate in vivo.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. High-throughput mRNA interactome capture; supports RNA binding but no NSUN2-specific conclusion.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Second, independent mRNA-bound proteome survey.

title: Cytosolic YB-1 and NSUN2 are the only proteins recognizing specific motifs present in mRNAs enriched in exosomes.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. NSUN2 recognises one of three exosome-enrichment motifs and is present in HEK293 exosomes. Peripheral to the enzymatic function.

title: 5-methylcytosine promotes mRNA export - NSUN2 as the methyltransferase and ALYREF as an m(5)C reader.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The best-controlled of the mRNA m5C studies, because the export phenotype is rescued by wild-type but not methyltransferase-dead NSUN2.

title: Loss of 5-methylcytosine alters the biogenesis of vault-derived small RNAs to coordinate epidermal differentiation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Establishes vault RNA VTRNA1.1 C69 as an NSUN2-exclusive substrate, a third non-mRNA substrate class.

title: NSUN2 introduces 5-methylcytosines in mammalian mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Mitochondrial import by proximity labelling, plus mt-tRNA m5C in three genetic models. Also the source of the useful negative result that NSUN2 loss does not much perturb mitochondrial translation.

title: Mammalian NSUN2 introduces 5-methylcytidines into mitochondrial tRNAs.
review_notes: Full text available and read. In vitro reconstitution with purified NSUN2 and SAM, with product positions mapped by mass spectrometry - the strongest evidence for the core activity.

title: 5-methylcytosine promotes pathogenesis of bladder cancer through stabilizing mRNAs.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Influential single-nucleotide mRNA m5C map in bladder cancer and the source of the YBX1 reader model. The site-level conclusions depend on bisulfite mapping whose specificity is questioned in PMID:42587746.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Full text available and read. BioPlex-style proteome-scale interactome; the resulting annotation is bare protein binding and carries no functional content.

title: Activity-based RNA-modifying enzyme probing reveals DUS3L-mediated dihydrouridylation.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Mechanism-based covalent capture plus oligo-dT selection, a rare piece of orthogonal evidence for mRNA methylation, and notable for stating its own polyA-purity caveat explicitly.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Full text available and read. High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; corroborative only.

title: The RNA methyltransferase NSUN2 catalyzes 5-methylcytosine (m(5)C) on IL1B mRNA to promote transcript stability.
review_notes: Full text available. Representative of the recent single-transcript m5C literature (IL1B, read by YBX1). Cited here as an example of the pattern, not as support for any annotation; no orthogonal, site-resolved validation is presented.

title: m5C Methylation of mRNA: Still More Questions Than Answers.
review_notes: Full text available and read. The main source for the methodological dispute recorded in this review. Note that it does not deny that NSUN2 methylates mRNA - it accepts NSUN2 and NSUN6 as the mRNA m5C writers - but it argues that the site maps, the stoichiometry and the reader mechanisms are unresolved.

title: NSUN2 methylates cytidine-40, cytidine-48, cytidine-49, cytidine-50 of tRNA(GLY)(GCC)
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing NSUN2 methylation of tRNA-Gly(GCC); consistent with the experimental literature.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The InterPro2GO mapping is correctly applied as a procedure, but IPR001678 fires on the NOL1/NOP2/Sun fold and cannot see that NSUN7's motif IV has lost the SAM-binding aspartate. The resulting methyltransferase-activity assertion is refuted by direct assay.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Transfer from mouse Nsun7 (UniProtKB:Q14AW5) is appropriate; the mouse phenotype and localisation data are strong and the human gene is a clear one-to-one orthologue.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Cytoplasm and motile cilium follow correctly from the UniProt subcellular location lines for this entry.

title: Sperm motility defects and infertility in male mice with a mutation in Nsun7, a member of the Sun domain-containing family of putative RNA methyltransferases.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. The founding ENU forward-genetic identification of Nsun7; note the authors already hedged with "putative RNA methyltransferases".

title: T26248G-transversion mutation in exon7 of the putative methyltransferase Nsun7 gene causes a change in protein folding associated with reduced sperm motility in asthenospermic men.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Small candidate-gene association study in one Iranian cohort with in silico folding predictions rather than functional work; supports human relevance but should not be treated as establishing a mechanism.

title: Positioning of sperm tail longitudinal columns depends on NSUN7, an RNA-binding protein destabilizing elongated spermatid transcripts.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Source of the direct RNA-binding evidence (UV CLIP-seq from testis). Its own bisulfite sequencing found no NSUN7-dependent methylation that correlated with binding, which the authors state explicitly.

title: Testis-specific RNA methyltransferase NSUN7 contains a re-arranged catalytic site.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache. Independent laboratory, and a stronger genetic design than a null - a knock-in of the putative catalytic cysteine to alanine, which produced no phenotype. Title still calls NSUN7 a methyltransferase while the content argues the opposite.

title: NSUN7-mediated m5C methylation of NLRP3 promotes pyroptosis in ovarian granulosa cells in polycystic ovary syndrome.
review_notes: Knockdown plus MeRIP and actinomycin D chase in a granulosa cell line. Catalysis is assumed rather than tested.

title: NSUN7-mediated m(5)C modification of circNTRK2 regulates stemness properties of glioblastoma cells by activating STK31.
review_notes: Uses the word "catalyzes" of a knockdown-plus-m5C-mapping result in glioblastoma lines. No direct test of catalysis, and NSUN7 is not appreciably expressed outside testis.

title: NSUN7 is a catalytically inactive RNA m(5)C methyltransferase essential for sperm flagellum assembly.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Decisive for catalytic inactivity - ITC on purified mouse and human NSUN domains plus transcriptome-wide m5C mass spectrometry and bisulfite sequencing in the knockout. The authors are also candid that they could not perform RIP or IP because no usable antibody was available, so the mechanism downstream of NSUN7 remains open.

title: NSUN7 Regulates Sperm Flagella Formation at All Stages of Spermiogenesis.
review_notes: Proteomics of sorted spermatid populations from Nsun7 knockout mice; supports a flagellar-assembly role and a protein-complex-stabilising model rather than an RNA-turnover model.

title: The m5C orchestrator NSUN7 drives SPARC/HMGB1 axis-mediated inflammation to exacerbate kidney injury.
review_notes: Abstract only in our cache (PMC full text is publisher-restricted). Asserts that NSUN7 is the main driver of kidney m5C, which conflicts with the direct biochemistry and with the testis-restricted expression of NSUN7. A fall in bulk m5C after deleting a protein does not establish that the protein is the methyltransferase; the abstract reports no SAM binding, no in vitro methylation and no catalytically dead rescue.

title: Human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase I: characterization and role in nucleoside analog resistance.
review_notes: Primary characterization of the human enzyme; PubMed-verified. Underlies the UniProt FUNCTION, catalytic activity, ADP activation and tissue-specificity calls.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome (Rolland 2014). Source of a bare protein-binding (NTAQ1) IPI; no NT5C1A-specific functional data.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Systematic SNV interaction-perturbation study (Fragoza 2019). Source of a bare protein-binding (NTAQ1) IPI; no NT5C1A-specific functional characterization.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome (Luck 2020). Source of bare protein-binding IPIs (CDC37, NTAQ1); systematic mapping only.

title: The decreased serum activity of cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase IA as a potential marker of breast cancer-associated muscle inflammation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; measures serum cN-IA activity and states the AMP->adenosine function and autoantigen role. Supports GO:0008253 and GO:0046085.

title: Regulation of the fatty acid composition of alkyl ether phospholipid in Ehrlich ascites tumor cells. The substrate specificities of 1-O-alkylglycerol 3-phosphate and 1-O-alkylglycero-3-phosphocholine acyltransferases.
review_notes: PMID:599155 (Waku & Nakazawa 1977, J Biochem) is an Ehrlich-ascites acyltransferase paper unrelated to NT5C1A. It is a transcription error in GOA for PMID:7599155 (Tavenier 1995, "Kinetics of adenylate metabolism in human and rat myocardium"), the paper UniProt actually cites (ECO:0000305|PubMed:7599155) for 5'-nucleotidase activity and cytoplasmic location. Annotations citing PMID:599155 are marked UNDECIDED pending correction of the identifier.

title: Kinetics of adenylate metabolism in human and rat myocardium.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the paper UniProt cites for cN-I 5'-nucleotidase activity and cytoplasmic location. This is the correct target of the mis-entered PMID:599155.

title: Soluble forms of 5'-nucleotidase in rat and human heart.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports GO:0008253 (IDA), GO:0000287 (Mg2+, IDA) and the adenosine-generation biological role in ischemic heart.

title: ATP and phosphate reciprocally affect subunit association of human recombinant High Km 5'-nucleotidase. Role for the C-terminal polyglutamic acid tract in subunit association and catalytic activity.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes catalytic activity, ATP/phosphate regulation and the role of the C-terminal acidic tail in tetramer assembly. Consistent with the IDA annotations attributed to it.

title: Cytosolic and mitochondrial deoxyribonucleotidases: activity with substrate analogs, inhibitors and implications for therapy.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Supports 5'-nucleotidase activity on (deoxy)purine analog substrates and the drug-inactivation role.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Large-scale Y2H interactome screen; source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations only. Uninformative about molecular function.

title: Nucleoside phosphotransferase activity of human colon carcinoma cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase.
review_notes: Abstract-only. Foundational characterization of both the 5'-nucleotidase and phosphotransferase activities and their allosteric activation.

title: Crystal structure of human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase II: insights into allosteric regulation and substrate recognition.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; structural basis of catalysis and allosteric regulation.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: Structural basis for the allosteric regulation and substrate recognition of human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase II.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports ATP binding (allosteric activator site), the homotetramer (identical protein binding), and Mg2+ dependence.

title: Suppression of 5'-nucleotidase enzymes promotes AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and metabolism in human and mouse skeletal muscle.
review_notes: Full text available. Direct genetic (IMP) evidence for cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase activity and IMP catabolism; source of the MGI-curated BP/CC annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome map; source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Interactome community study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome reference map; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cell-specific interactome study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation.

title: TRIM22 orchestrates the proliferation of GBMs and the benefits of TMZ by coordinating the modification and degradation of RIG-I.
review_notes: Full text available. Sole source of the ubiquitin-ligase (GO:0061630), K48-linked ubiquitination (GO:0070936) and antiviral (GO:0050689) annotations. This is a moonlighting claim well outside the enzyme's HAD-fold metabolic role (no recognizable E3 domain; interaction with RIG-I is indirect via TRIM22) and is not independently corroborated; treated as a likely over-annotation.

title: Molecular cloning of human cytosolic purine 5'-nucleotidase.
review_notes: Original cloning of human NT5C2; basis of the TAS 5'-nucleotidase activity annotation.

title: Bovine cytosolic IMP/GMP-specific 5'-nucleotidase: cloning and expression of active enzyme in Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Bovine ortholog 99.5% identical to human; curator source for several IDA annotations on the human enzyme (5'-nucleotidase, phosphotransferase, cytosol, IMP/GMP metabolic).

title: carbovir + IMP => carbovir monophosphate + inosine
review_notes: Reactome reaction (abacavir/carbovir metabolism) placing NT5C2 in the cytosol; illustrates the phosphotransferase activity on a nucleoside-analog prodrug.

title: (d)GMP or (d)IMP + H2O => (2'-deoxy)guanosine or (2'-deoxy)inosine + orthophosphate (NT5C2)
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the core (d)GMP/(d)IMP dephosphorylation by NT5C2 in the cytosol.

title: NT5C2 tetramer phosphorylates RBV
review_notes: Reactome reaction (ribavirin metabolism); NT5C2 tetramer, cytosol.

title: NT5C2 tetramer dephosphorylates RBV-MP
review_notes: Reactome reaction (ribavirin metabolism); NT5C2 tetramer dephosphorylating ribavirin monophosphate in the cytosol.

title: Human erythrocyte pyrimidine 5-nucleotidase, PN-I, is identical to p36, a protein associated to lupus inclusion formation in response to alpha-interferon.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes PN-I (= NT5C3A) as an active pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase and its identity with p36. Supports the 5'-nucleotidase MF calls.

title: Human erythrocyte pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase, PN-I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (abstract only). Primary biochemical characterization; underpins the 5'-nucleotidase MF, Mg2+ dependence, and UMP/CMP/dTMP/dUMP catabolic-process annotations (all curated by MGI from this paper).

title: Molecular characterization of six unrelated Italian patients affected by pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase deficiency.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; disease/genetics context confirming the physiological importance of the enzyme's pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase activity.

title: Evidence for essential catalytic determinants for human erythrocyte pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the EXP source for the 5'-nucleotidase activity annotation. Defines the HAD catalytic mechanism and separates nucleotidase from phosphotransferase activity.

title: A diverse range of gene products are effectors of the type I interferon antiviral response.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. NT5C3A ("NT5C3") appears only as a weak/non-hit in the screen; the "defense response to virus" IDA is at best a peripheral role, not core.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; high-throughput binary interactome. Supports only uninformative "protein binding"; interactors match the UniProt INTERACTION block.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HTP spatial-proteome hit; inconsistent with the well-established cytosolic localization, so treated as non-core.

title: Purification, microsequencing, and immunolocalization of p36, a new interferon-alpha-induced protein that is associated with human lupus inclusions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; source of the ER/cytoplasm IDA localization. ER localization is isoform-2-specific.

title: Pyrimidine nucleotidases from human erythrocyte possess phosphotransferase activities specific for pyrimidine nucleotides.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited as support for GO:0000215 (tRNA 2'-phosphotransferase activity), but the paper describes a pyrimidine-nucleotide phosphotransferase, not a tRNA 2'-phosphotransferase; the GO:0000215 annotation is a mis-mapping.
