title: Centrobin controls mother-daughter centriole asymmetry in Drosophila neuroblasts.
review_notes: Drosophila neuroblast Centrobin/POLO study; cited by GOA for human PLK1 'identical protein binding'. Correct paper, but its relevance to human PLK1 function is minimal.

title: Structure and expression of the variant melanin-concentrating hormone genes: only PMCHL1 is transcribed in the developing human brain and encodes a putative protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Biol Evol 2000). Abstract only in cache. Describes the 5'-truncation, sense and antisense PMCHL1 RNAs in brain, and VMCH-p8 translation only in vitro and in transfected COS cells.

title: Birth of two chimeric genes in the Hominidae lineage.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2001). Abstract only in cache. Origin of PMCHL1 by retroposition of antisense PMCH mRNA and exon shuffling; PMCHL2 by later duplication.

title: Primate-specific spliced PMCHL RNAs are non-protein coding in human and macaque tissues.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (BMC Evol Biol 2008), full text cached. Key paper. An anti-VMCH-p8 antiserum detected no protein in human testis, human brain or macaque brain, nor in HEK293 cells transfected with ORF1-bearing sequences. The authors note that expression below the detection threshold cannot be excluded.

title: Assignment of the human pro-melanin-concentrating hormone gene (PMCH) to chromosome 12q23-q24 and two variant genes (PMCH1 and PMCHL2) to chromosome 5p14 and 5q12-q13.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Genomics 1994). Chromosomal mapping only; defines the PMCHL1 (5p14) and PMCHL2 (5q12-q13) loci.

title: Isolation and characterization of the human melanin-concentrating hormone gene and a variant gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Brain Res Mol Brain Res 1993). First description of the variant MCH gene; its statement that the variant expresses a prohormone predates the later structural and protein-detection work, which does not support it.

title: Antisense expression of the human pro-melanin-concentrating hormone genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Brain Res 1998). Hypothalamic RT-PCR shows only antisense PMCHL1 transcripts; basis of the UniProt CAUTION.

title: Structure and expression of the variant melanin-concentrating hormone genes: only PMCHL1 is transcribed in the developing human brain and encodes a putative protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Biol Evol 2000). Abstract only in cache. Shows that PMCHL2 is not expressed in fetal, newborn or adult brain, and that both variant genes are 5'-truncated copies of PMCH.

title: Birth of two chimeric genes in the Hominidae lineage.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2001). Abstract only in cache. PMCHL2 cloned from testis (UniProt RN[1]); origin by segmental duplication of the PMCHL1 locus.

title: Primate-specific spliced PMCHL RNAs are non-protein coding in human and macaque tissues.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (BMC Evol Biol 2008), full text cached. Key paper. PMCHL2 transcripts are found only in testis and use a gene-specific splice donor. Western blots with anti-VMCH-p8 antiserum (raised against the PMCHL1 N-terminal epitope; PMCHL2 differs at one position, KTKKK versus KPKKK) detected no protein in adult testis or in transfected HEK293 cells. Detection of PMCHL2-specific product is therefore slightly less direct than for PMCHL1.

title: Assignment of the human pro-melanin-concentrating hormone gene (PMCH) to chromosome 12q23-q24 and two variant genes (PMCH1 and PMCHL2) to chromosome 5p14 and 5q12-q13.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Genomics 1994). Chromosomal mapping that defined the PMCHL2 locus at 5q12-q13.

title: Antisense expression of the human pro-melanin-concentrating hormone genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Brain Res 1998). Hypothalamic variant-locus transcripts are antisense and come from the 5p (PMCHL1) locus, not 5q (PMCHL2).

title: The X-ray crystal structures of human alpha-phosphomannomutase 1 reveal the structural basis of congenital disorder of glycosylation type 1a.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structural/kinetic study. Abstract foregrounds PMM1 crystal structures but explicitly compares both isozymes and underpins the EC 5.4.2.8 ECO:0000269 evidence UniProt assigns to PMM2; per guidelines not removed as 'wrong gene'.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome screen; supports only a generic, uninformative 'protein binding' annotation with no demonstrated functional relevance to PMM2.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome screen; supports only a generic 'protein binding' annotation, not a core function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome; generic 'protein binding' hits with no functional meaning for a cytosolic metabolic enzyme.

title: Evolutionary rescue of phosphomannomutase deficiency in yeast models of human disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:36214454, eLife 2022). Yeast SEC53/PMM2 model; corroborates that PMM2 loss-of-function impairs N-linked glycosylation and that the common p.Phe119Leu/F126L allele acts via dimer/stability defects. Added by Falcon integration to strengthen the N-glycosylation (non-core) and homodimer evidence.

title: Tracer metabolomics reveals the role of aldose reductase in glycosylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:37257447, Cell Rep Med 2023). Confirms PMM2 deficiency depletes GDP-mannose (supports the core GDP-mannose biosynthetic process role) and explicitly states PMM2 is NOT directly involved in polyol metabolism, supporting the decision NOT to annotate polyol/metabolic-rewiring as a PMM2 function. The aldose-reductase axis is a downstream/compensatory metabolic effect, not a PMM2 molecular function. Added by Falcon integration.

title: In Silico Analysis of Phosphomannomutase-2 Dimer Interface Stability and Heterodimerization with Phosphomannomutase-1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:40572562, Molecules 2025). In silico/structural study; supports the homodimer quaternary structure asserted in core_functions and the catalytic- vs interface-defect distinction (R141H vs F119L). Predicted PMM1/PMM2 heterodimer is computational only and PMM1 does not compensate in vivo, so it does NOT justify a PMM1-containing-complex annotation. Added by Falcon integration.

title: Mutations in PMM2, a phosphomannomutase gene on chromosome 16p13, in carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein type I syndrome (Jaeken syndrome).
review_notes: Foundational PMM2 cloning/disease paper; PubMed-verified. Anchors the gene's catalytic identity and disease association.

title: Carbohydrate-deficient glycoprotein syndrome type Ib. Phosphomannose isomerase deficiency and mannose therapy.
review_notes: Cited as the IMP source for PMM2 GDP-mannose biosynthetic process, but the paper is about phosphomannose isomerase (PMI/MPI) deficiency / CDG-Ib and mannose therapy - a different enzyme catalyzing F6P<->Man6P and a different gene (MPI). The GO term is still correct for PMM2 and is strongly supported by other references, so the annotation was kept; the citation itself appears mis-attributed. Recommendation: FlyBase should re-examine and correct this IMP annotation, since its supporting evidence derives from a different enzyme (PMI/MPI, CDG-Ib) and does not assay the PMM2 mutase step.

title: Defective PMM2 does not isomerise Man6P to Man1P
review_notes: Reactome-curated reaction; consistent with UniProt and primary literature.

title: PMM1,2 isomerise Man6P to Man1P
review_notes: Reactome-curated; supports cytosolic localization and catalytic activity.

title: Synthesis of GDP-mannose
review_notes: Reactome-curated pathway context for the GDP-mannose biosynthetic process annotation.

title: Phosphomevalonate kinase is a cytosolic protein in humans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; definitive multi-technique demonstration that human PMVK is exclusively cytosolic, the basis for the NOT|peroxisome and cytosol annotations.

title: Phosphomevalonate kinase: functional investigation of the recombinant human enzyme.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary characterization of recombinant human PMVK establishing the phosphomevalonate kinase activity, ATP binding, and monomeric state.

title: Localization of the pre-squalene segment of the isoprenoid biosynthetic pathway in mammalian peroxisomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified citation, but its conclusion of peroxisomal localization of presqualene enzymes (including PMVK) is contradicted by PMID:14729858 and PMID:27052676 and by the UniProt CAUTION note; the field consensus is cytosolic.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI interactome map. The PMVK interactors it reports are high-throughput Y2H hits with no functional follow-up; supports only a bare, and uninformative, protein-binding annotation.

title: UniProtKB Q15126 (PMVK_HUMAN) record
review_notes: Curated UniProt entry; source for the EC 2.7.4.2 catalytic activity, the isoprenoid/IPP PATHWAY statement, the cytosolic subcellular location, the ATP-binding features, and the CAUTION note reconciling the peroxisome-vs-cytosol history.

title: Human phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase pharmacogenomics: gene re-sequencing and functional genomics.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary study on human PNMT; the IMP annotation for PNMT activity is supported by functional assay of wild-type and variant allozymes.

title: Mode of binding of methyl acceptor substrates to the adrenaline-synthesizing enzyme phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase: implications for catalysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structural/mechanistic study of human PNMT; directly supports the EXP annotation for catalytic activity.

title: Discovery of novel human phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (hPNMT) inhibitors using 3D pharmacophore-based in silico, biophysical screening and enzymatic activity assays.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports the IMP annotation for PNMT activity via direct enzymatic assay of recombinant enzyme.

title: Transgenic mice express the human phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase gene in adrenal medulla and retina.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes the expression pattern (adrenal medulla, retina) and the enzyme's role, supporting the TAS activity annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified systematic interactome paper, but the PNMT binary interactions are high-throughput screen hits with no functional context; basis for a bare protein-binding annotation only.

title: Recombinant human phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase: overproduction in Escherichia coli, purification, and characterization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; foundational biochemical characterization of purified human PNMT supporting the IDA annotation.

title: Noradrenaline is converted to adrenaline
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly describing the PNMT-catalyzed step and its cytosolic location.

title: Catecholamine biosynthesis
review_notes: Reactome pathway placing PNMT as the terminal enzyme of catecholamine biosynthesis, supporting the catecholamine biosynthetic process annotation.

title: Role of purine nucleoside phosphorylase in interactions between 2',3'-dideoxyinosine and allopurinol, ganciclovir, or tenofovir.
review_notes: Full text cached; establishes PNP-dependent phosphorolysis/clearance of the antiviral ddI, supporting the response-to-xenobiotic annotation.

title: Intracellular delivery of purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) fused to protein transduction domain corrects PNP deficiency in vitro.
review_notes: Enzyme-replacement study confirming PNP activity, cytoplasmic localization, and correction of T-lymphocyte function/IL-2 in PNP-deficient cells.

title: TAT-mediated intracellular delivery of purine nucleoside phosphorylase corrects its deficiency in mice.
review_notes: In vivo mouse enzyme replacement; ties PNP activity to correction of nucleoside homeostasis and T-cell immunodeficiency (downstream immune/urate annotations).

title: Effect of the phosphate substrate on drug-inhibitor binding to human purine nucleoside phosphorylase.
review_notes: ITC study of human PNP; supports phosphate-ion binding and enzymatic activity; confirms trimer with catalytic sites at subunit interfaces.

title: Nicotinamide riboside and nicotinic acid riboside salvage in fungi and mammals. Quantitative basis for Urh1 and purine nucleoside phosphorylase function in NAD+ metabolism.
review_notes: Full text cached; demonstrates mammalian PNP (not MTAP) as the NR phosphorylase feeding NAD+ salvage; supports NR catabolism annotation.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports incidental exosome detection, not a functional localization.

review_notes: Structural study of human PNP transition-state analogue inhibitors; used here as an IntAct self-interaction source consistent with the homotrimer.

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; incidental detection of a cytosolic enzyme.

title: Catalytic site conformations in human PNP by 19F-NMR and crystallography.
review_notes: Full text cached; establishes reversible phosphorolysis of purine (deoxy)ribonucleosides, homotrimeric structure, and catalytic mechanism.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; incidental detection.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Large-scale variant/interaction pipeline; used as an IntAct self-interaction source consistent with the homotrimer.

review_notes: Identifies the E89K deficiency mutation abolishing PNP activity; supports catalytic activity, cytoplasmic localization, and PNP-deficiency biology.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome-perturbation study; IntAct self-interaction source.

review_notes: Binary interactome map (HuRI); IntAct self-interaction source consistent with homotrimer.

review_notes: Y2H neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of non-specific protein binding IPIs flagged as over-annotation.

title: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase activity of human erythrocytes in iron deficiency anaemia.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; human erythrocyte PNP activity assay supporting the catalytic-activity annotation.

title: Characterization of purine nucleoside phosphorylase from human granulocytes and its metabolism of deoxyribonucleosides.
review_notes: Key experimental characterization: purified human PNP is a trimer and phosphorolyses inosine, deoxyinosine, guanosine and deoxyguanosine; adenine and pyrimidine (deoxy)nucleosides are not substrates.

title: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase. 1. Structure-function studies.
review_notes: Active-site mutagenesis (Asn243, Glu201, His86) defining substrate/base binding and catalysis; supports nucleoside and purine-nucleobase binding.

title: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase. 3. Reversal of purine base specificity by site-directed mutagenesis.
review_notes: Establishes 6-oxopurine specificity (inosine kcat/KM ~350,000-fold over adenosine) and kinetic parameters; N243D reverses specificity to 6-aminopurines.

title: Identification, cloning, expression, and purification of three novel human calcium-independent phospholipase A2 family members possessing triacylglycerol lipase and acylglycerol transacylase activities.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2004;279:48968-75). Cached record is abstract-only. It is the founding biochemistry for TAG lipase and acylglycerol transacylase activity of PNPLA3. The 'calcium-independent phospholipase A2' in the title is a family label based on sequence motifs; the abstract reports no PLA2 assay for these three proteins, which is why the GO:0004623 annotation drawn from this paper is flagged as over-annotated.

title: A sequence variation (I148M) in PNPLA3 associated with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease disrupts triglyceride hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2010;285:6706-15). Establishes TG hydrolase activity and its loss in I148M, plus the membrane/lipid-droplet partitioning.

title: Expression and characterization of a PNPLA3 protein isoform (I148M) associated with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2011;286:37085-93), full text available. The most complete substrate survey of purified PNPLA3. It reports the glycerolipid hydrolase activities and explicit negatives for GPAT, LPAAT, DGAT, phospholipids, cholesteryl esters and retinyl esters. The citation itself is correct; what is wrong is GOA's use of it as EXP evidence for GO:0003841, a reaction this paper could not detect.

title: Adiponutrin functions as a nutritionally regulated lysophosphatidic acid acyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Metab 2012;15:691-702). Correctly cited, but the central claim - that PNPLA3 is a CoA-dependent LPA acyltransferase, and that I148M increases that activity - is directly contradicted by PMID:21878620, which assayed the same reaction with CGI-58 as a positive control and detected nothing. The disagreement also runs the opposite way on the direction of the variant's effect. Retained; the annotations derived from it are marked over-annotated rather than removed.

title: PNPLA3/adiponutrin functions in lipid droplet formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biol Cell 2013;105:219-233). Cached record is abstract-only. Supports lipid droplet targeting and the effect of PNPLA3 dosage on droplet size; also an early report that co-expressed ABHD5/CGI-58 reverses PNPLA3-induced droplet enlargement.

title: PNPLA3 mediates hepatocyte triacylglycerol remodeling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Lipid Res 2014;55:739-46). The cellular evidence for acyl-chain remodelling, and for the shift of I148M protein towards lipid droplets.

title: PNPLA3 is a triglyceride lipase that mobilizes polyunsaturated fatty acids to facilitate hepatic secretion of large-sized very low-density lipoprotein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Commun 2024;15:4847). Not cited by any current GOA row; added here because it is the loss-of-function pole of the dispute. Its in vivo findings - hepatic Pnpla3 knockout aggravating steatosis and lowering VLDL-TG - are explicitly contradicted by PMID:39550037, which reports no hepatic phenotype in Pnpla3-null mice and increased rather than decreased phospholipid PUFA in 148M animals. Cited as one side of an open disagreement.

title: PNPLA3(148M) is a gain-of-function mutation that promotes hepatic steatosis by inhibiting ATGL-mediated triglyceride hydrolysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Hepatol 2025;82:871-881), full text available. The strongest current evidence for the ABHD5-sequestration model, and also the first demonstration that ABHD5 directly activates PNPLA3's own TG hydrolase activity. Its central claim is a gain-of-function interpretation that PMID:38844467 rejects, so it is scientifically contested even though the citation is sound.

title: Lipid droplet targeting of the lipase coactivator ABHD5 and the fatty liver disease-causing variant PNPLA3 I148M is required to promote liver steatosis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2025;301:108186), full text available. Independent support for the ABHD5 interaction and for lipid droplet targeting being required for it. Reports greater association of I148M than wild-type PNPLA3 with ABHD5, which PMID:39550037 attributes largely to higher I148M protein levels.

title: Loss or gain of function: The functional complexity of the PNPLA3 I148M variant.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Hepatol 2025;82:778-780), an editorial accompanying PMID:39550037. PubMed holds no abstract and no full text is available, so it is cited only as evidence that the loss-of-function versus gain-of-function question is recognised as unresolved by the field, with no supporting_text quoted from it.

title: PNPLA3-I148M is a neomorph that interferes with two primary hepatic triglyceride clearance pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Rep 2025;44:116371). Cached record is abstract-only, so claims are anchored to the abstract. Proposes a third mechanism distinct from both loss- and gain-of-function, converging on ABHD5/CGI-58 and adding impaired ApoB/VLDL secretion.

title: Structure and properties of recombinant human pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; abstract directly supports catalytic activity, FMN cofactor, homodimer and PLP-binding claims. PDB 1NRG derives from this work.

title: Genomic organization, tissue distribution and deletion mutation of human pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports the EXP catalytic-activity annotation and the N-terminal-dispensable truncation biology.

title: Neonatal epileptic encephalopathy caused by mutations in the PNPO gene encoding pyridox(am)ine 5'-phosphate oxidase.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes disease mechanism and directly supports the IDA catalytic-activity annotation via human-variant expression assays.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome screen; source of a bare GO:0005515 IPI (partner AGTRAP). Not informative for PNPO's molecular function.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; source of a bare GO:0005515 IPI (partner MTERF1). Not informative for function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome reference map; source of bare GO:0005515 IPI (partners AGTRAP, LIME1). Not informative for function.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interaction network; source of bare GO:0005515 IPI (partner MTERF1). Not informative for function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Large-scale mitochondrial proteome study; used to support a mitochondrion localization for PNPO, but PNPO is a canonical cytosolic enzyme and the cached full text does not specifically establish PNPO as a mitochondrial resident. Likely reflects cytosolic contamination; annotation flagged as over-annotation.

title: 2xPNPO:2xFMN oxidizes PDXP to PXLP
review_notes: Reactome reaction for PNP to PLP oxidation, localized to cytosol; supports the cytosol and PLP-biosynthesis annotations.

title: 2xPNPO:2xFMN oxidizes PXAP to PXLP
review_notes: Reactome reaction for PMP to PLP oxidation, localized to cytosol; supports the cytosol and PLP-biosynthesis annotations.

title: Modification of epidermal growth factor-like repeats with O-fucose. Molecular cloning and expression of a novel GDP-fucose protein O-fucosyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed/UniProt-verified primary cloning and enzymatic characterization of human POFUT1 (Wang et al. 2001, JBC). Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text is a verbatim quote from the abstract. Anchors the core MF and O-fucosylation process annotations. Note the abstract predicts a type-II TM anchor, but the active enzyme is later shown to be soluble ER-luminal (PMID:15653671).

title: Composition of Drosophila melanogaster proteome involved in fucosylated glycan metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, but this is a Drosophila genome bioinformatics survey, not a study of human POFUT1 enzymatic activity. It is a weak/inappropriate basis for a TAS human peptide-O-fucosyltransferase-activity annotation; the same MF term is far better supported by human IDA (PMID:11524432, PMID:9023546, PMID:15653671).

title: O-fucosylation of notch occurs in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary localization study (Luo & Haltiwanger 2005, JBC). Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text quotes are verbatim from the abstract. Definitive evidence for soluble ER-luminal localization and KDEL-like retention; basis for treating ER as core and Golgi/membrane as incorrect/uninformative.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput membrane-proteome MS study. POFUT1's presence in a crude membrane fraction is the basis of the HDA "membrane" annotation but is not informative of its true soluble ER-luminal localization; contributes only a generic, over-annotated location.

title: Structure of human POFUT1, its requirement in ligand-independent oncogenic Notch signaling, and functional effects of Dowling-Degos mutations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available in cache. Provides the human POFUT1 crystal structures (GDP-fucose complex), the IMP evidence for regulation of Notch signaling, and functional analysis of Dowling-Degos mutations. Anchors the Notch-regulation annotation and the cautious (non-core) treatment of a mammalian chaperone role.

title: Identification of a GDP-L-fucose:polypeptide fucosyltransferase and enzymatic addition of O-linked fucose to EGF domains.
review_notes: PubMed-verified original enzyme-activity characterization (Wang et al. 1996, Glycobiology). Abstract-only in cache; supporting_text quotes are verbatim. Establishes the core peptide-O-fucosyltransferase activity and the folded-EGF-domain acceptor requirement.

title: FutureHouse Falcon deep-research report for POFUT1
review_notes: FutureHouse Falcon deep-research report. Conclusions are concordant with the curated review and with the primary literature. Used only to anchor the ER-localization synthesis; all substantive annotations are cited to the cached primary PMIDs rather than to Falcon's (largely review-derived, unverified) citation list. One Falcon claim (Ajima 2017 attributed to uterine/placental angiogenesis via uPA/RhoA) appears to be a citation mismatch and was rejected.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Proteome-scale AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (PPAT-NUDT5); no functional consequence established for PPAT's catalytic role.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Second proteome-scale BioPlex interactome. Source of a bare "protein binding" IPI (PPAT-NUDT5); uninformative about molecular function.

title: Two genes for de novo purine nucleotide synthesis on human chromosome 4 are closely linked and divergently transcribed.
review_notes: Primary human cloning/expression paper establishing PPAT (GPAT) as the step-1 de novo purine enzyme; supports the TAS MF and process annotations.

title: Complete reconstitution of the human coenzyme A biosynthetic pathway via comparative genomics.

title: Phosphoserine Aminotransferase Pathogenetic Variants in Serine Deficiency Disorders: A Functional Characterization.
