title: PSAT1 impairs ferroptosis and reduces immunotherapy efficacy via GPX4 hydroxylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports both the core catalytic MF (K200A mutagenesis) and the noncanonical negative regulation of ferroptosis annotation.

title: PXLP-K200-PSAT1 dimer transfers amino group from L-Glu to 3POPA
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the PSAT1 step of serine biosynthesis; supports the cytosolic localization and the catalytic reaction.

title: Purification and characterization of the human gamma-secretase complex.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; exact abstract text supports gamma-secretase complex composition and APP/Notch substrate cleavage.

title: Presenilins form ER Ca2+ leak channels, a function disrupted by familial Alzheimer's disease-linked mutations.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports presenilin ER calcium leak biology, treated as non-core because the normal in-vivo scope is less settled than gamma-secretase proteolysis.

title: An atomic structure of human γ-secretase.
review_notes: Cached full text verified; supports PSEN1 catalytic aspartates in the human gamma-secretase transmembrane active site.

title: A loss of function mutation of presenilin-2 interferes with amyloid beta-peptide production and notch signaling.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports PSEN2 catalytic-site dependence for APP processing and Notch signaling.

title: The transmembrane aspartates in presenilin 1 and 2 are obligatory for gamma-secretase activity and amyloid beta-protein generation.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports the PSEN2 transmembrane aspartates as required for gamma-secretase activity and amyloid-beta generation.

title: Purification and characterization of the human gamma-secretase complex.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports gamma-secretase complex composition and APP/Notch substrate cleavage used for PSEN2 core-function synthesis.

title: Presenilin 2 modulates endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria interactions and Ca2+ cross-talk.
review_notes: Cached abstract/title verified; supports PSEN2 ER-mitochondria calcium-coupling biology, treated as non-core pending stronger normal in-vivo evidence.

title: Restricted Location of PSEN2/γ-Secretase Determines Substrate Specificity and Generates an Intracellular Aβ Pool.
review_notes: Cached full text verified; directly supports AP-1-dependent late endosome/lysosome enrichment and PSEN2 substrate specificity.

title: PEN-2 is an integral component of the gamma-secretase complex required for coordinated expression of presenilin and nicastrin.
review_notes: Cached abstract directly identifies PEN-2 as an integral gamma-secretase component required for coordinated presenilin/nicastrin complex expression.

title: PEN-2 and APH-1 coordinately regulate proteolytic processing of presenilin 1.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports PEN-2 interaction with presenilin 1 holoprotein and a direct role in presenilin endoproteolysis.

title: The role of presenilin cofactors in the gamma-secretase complex.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports PEN-2 requirement for presenilin endoproteolysis and conferring gamma-secretase activity to the complex.

title: APH1, PEN2, and Nicastrin increase Abeta levels and gamma-secretase activity.
review_notes: Cached abstract includes PEN2 as a gamma-secretase complex component and supports its contribution to Abeta levels and gamma-secretase activity.

title: Purification and characterization of the human gamma-secretase complex.
review_notes: Cached abstract identifies Pen-2 with presenilin, nicastrin, and APH-1 as components of purified active human gamma-secretase.

title: Three-dimensional structure of human γ-secretase.
review_notes: Cached full-text record supports the four-subunit human gamma-secretase structural model containing Pen-2/PSENEN.

title: An atomic structure of human γ-secretase.
review_notes: Cached full-text record supports atomic gamma-secretase structure and membrane-embedded complex organization including PSENEN.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Basis for the three rat-ortholog IEA response-phenotype annotations (response to mechanical stimulus / nutrient levels / testosterone). The transferred terms are regulatory-context phenotypes of the rat ortholog, not molecular functions of human PSPH; flagged as over-annotations.

title: Molecular basis for the local conformational rearrangement of human phosphoserine phosphatase.
review_notes: Crystal structures and active-site mutagenesis of human PSPH; establishes the catalytic mechanism and residues (E29, R65, T182, R202) and the homodimer.

title: High-resolution structure of human phosphoserine phosphatase in open conformation.
review_notes: High-resolution structure; explicitly describes PSPH as a dimeric enzyme catalyzing the third/final step of L-serine biosynthesis. Supports the homodimerization annotation.

title: Mutations responsible for 3-phosphoserine phosphatase deficiency.
review_notes: Identifies and functionally characterizes the D32N and M52T disease variants on recombinant enzyme; basis for the IMP catalytic-activity and L-serine biosynthesis annotations.

title: How calcium inhibits the magnesium-dependent enzyme human phosphoserine phosphatase.
review_notes: Structural/biochemical basis for Mg2+ dependence and Ca2+ inhibition; supports the magnesium ion binding and catalytic-activity annotations.

title: Phosphoserine phosphatase of human brain: partial purification, characterization, regional distribution, and effect of certain modulators including psychoactive drugs.
review_notes: Purification of PSPH from human brain; establishes it as a cytosolic enzyme specific for phosphoserine (both L and D enantiomers), inhibited by L-serine.

title: Phosphoserine phosphatase (PSPH) gene mutation in an intellectual disability family from Pakistan.
review_notes: Reports a PSPH (A35T) variant with decreased phosphatase activity in an intellectual-disability family; cached record is a Letter (abstract-only).

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome map; source of a PSPH self-interaction (identical protein binding) consistent with the known homodimer, but PSPH is not individually discussed.

title: A massively parallel pipeline to clone DNA variants and examine molecular phenotypes of human disease mutations.
review_notes: Methods paper (Clone-seq / comparative interactome scanning); IntAct curated a PSPH self-interaction from it. PSPH is not named in the abstract or the text I reviewed; the self-interaction is consistent with the homodimer.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Characterizes the PSPH self-interaction and shows a dimerization-disrupting rare variant (T152I) reduces phosphatase activity to ~59% of wild-type - functional evidence that homodimerization is required for catalysis.

title: Human L-3-phosphoserine phosphatase: sequence, expression and evidence for a phosphoenzyme intermediate.
review_notes: Cloning and biochemical characterization of the human enzyme; demonstrates Mg2+-dependent L-phosphoserine hydrolysis and a phosphoenzyme (aspartyl/glutamyl) intermediate.

title: Phosphoserine phosphatase deficiency in a patient with Williams syndrome.
review_notes: First report of phosphoserine phosphatase deficiency; patient cells had ~25% of normal PSPH activity and responded to oral serine.

title: PSPH:Mg2+ dimer dephosphorylates O-P-Ser
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the PSPH:Mg2+ dimer dephosphorylation of O-phospho-L-serine; basis for the cytosol TAS annotation.

title: Identification and characterization of phosphoseryl-tRNA[Ser]Sec kinase
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Carlson et al., PNAS 2004;101(35):12848-53). Foundational discovery and characterization of PSTK / phosphoseryl-tRNA[Ser]Sec kinase, establishing the seryl-tRNA(Sec) -> O-phosphoseryl-tRNA(Sec) phosphorylation step in selenocysteine biosynthesis. Full text is not in the local publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text is drawn from it; all quotes come from the UniProt record.

title: The sonic hedgehog-patched-gli pathway in human development and disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. A review article used as a TAS source for PTCH1's repressive role; the cached entry carries no abstract, so no supporting text is quoted from it. The claim it supports is independently established by seven IDAs in this same annotation set.

title: Expression of the developmental Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signalling pathway is up-regulated in chronic lung fibrosis and the Shh receptor patched 1 is present in circulating T lymphocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached entry is abstract-only. Establishes Patched protein at the surface of human peripheral CD4/CD8 lymphocytes and alveolar macrophages - adequate for the plasma-membrane location, incidental to PTCH1's mechanism.

title: Inhibition of GLI1 gene activation by Patched1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Both GOA rows it supports are present in the paper - the GLI1 transcription result in the abstract, the osteogenic differentiation result in the full text (Figure 10). Overexpression-based, hence kept as non-core.

title: Immunohistochemical analysis of Sonic hedgehog signalling in normal human urinary tract development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Descriptive immunohistochemistry of human urinary tract development; the authors present the findings as hypothesis-generating, which is the basis for flagging its two IEP-derived process rows as over-annotated while accepting the apical localisation IDA.

title: Kinase activity-independent regulation of cyclin pathway by GRK2 is essential for zebrafish early development.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. A zebrafish GRK2 study; PTCH1 appears as the cyclin B1 regulator whose association with GRK2 and with cyclin B1 was directly measured. Supports the cyclin binding and protein kinase binding replacements but not a core PTCH1 function.

title: The structure of SHH in complex with HHIP reveals a recognition role for the Shh pseudo active site in signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primarily an HHIP-SHH structure; PTCH1 enters via ectodomain peptide-binding comparisons ('patch for Patched'). Adequate support for retermiing the SHH protein-binding row to hedgehog family protein binding, but not a PTCH1-centred study.

title: The hedgehog receptor patched is involved in cholesterol transport.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Supports cholesterol binding by purified Patched and transport-like behaviour in yeast. Its 'efflux from cells' framing predates the accessible-cholesterol model, which is why the GO:0010875 row is re-termed rather than accepted.

title: Ligand binding to WW tandem domains of YAP2 transcriptional regulator is under negative cooperativity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached entry is abstract-only. A biophysical study of YAP2 WW tandem-domain cooperativity. The PTCH1 link is an interaction datum with no connection to an established PTCH1 function, which is why the bare protein-binding row it supports is removed as uninformative.

title: Structures of human Patched and its complex with native palmitoylated sonic hedgehog.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Cryo-EM of human PTCH1 with natively lipidated SHH-N; the source of the palmitate-in-cavity interface description used throughout this review and in modules/hedgehog_signaling.yaml.

title: The morphogen Sonic hedgehog inhibits its receptor Patched by a pincer grasp mechanism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Establishes the cholesteroyl arm of the pincer grasp and links ligand binding to closure of the PTCH1 sterol conduit; the IDA basis for GO:0140303.

title: The energetics and ion coupling of cholesterol transport through Patched1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Simulation plus in vivo mutant assays on cholesterol transport energetics and ion coupling; second IDA basis for GO:0140303.

title: Characterization of two patched receptors for the vertebrate hedgehog protein family.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The primary source for PTCH1 binding all three mammalian Hedgehog ligands and for PTCH1/PTCH2 complex formation with SMO; underpins five GOA rows.

title: p48 subunit of mouse PTF1 binds to RBP-Jkappa/CBF-1, the intracellular mediator of Notch signalling, and is expressed in the neural tube of early stage embryos.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Establishes Ptf1a-RBPJ binding, PTF1-motif transcriptional activation, and that retinoic acid treatment induces Ptf1a rather than demonstrating Ptf1a as a retinoic-acid receptor pathway component.

title: The role of the transcriptional regulator Ptf1a in converting intestinal to pancreatic progenitors.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; directly supports pancreatic progenitor fate specification and loss-of-function diversion to duodenal fates.

title: Mutations in PTF1A cause pancreatic and cerebellar agenesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; directly links human biallelic truncating variants to pancreatic and cerebellar agenesis and reports confirming Ptf1a-null mouse pathology.

title: PTF1 is an organ-specific and Notch-independent basic helix-loop-helix complex containing the mammalian Suppressor of Hairless (RBP-J) or its paralogue, RBP-L.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; defines the PTF1 trimer, its E-protein and RBPJ/RBPJL subunits, and its Notch-independent activity.

title: Ptf1a determines horizontal and amacrine cell fates during mouse retinal development.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; mouse lineage tracing and knockout directly support retinal horizontal/amacrine fate and neural-retina annotations transferred to human.

title: Cerebellar GABAergic progenitors adopt an external granule cell-like phenotype in the absence of Ptf1a transcription factor expression.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; directly supports Ptf1a-dependent specification of Purkinje cells and cerebellar interneurons and suppression of the granule-cell program in VZ cells.

title: Early pancreatic development requires the vertebrate Suppressor of Hairless (RBPJ) in the PTF1 bHLH complex.
review_notes: Full text verified; establishes the stable PTF1-J DNA-binding complex, the later RBPJ-to-RBPJL switch, promoter occupancy, and pancreatic developmental consequences.

title: A nonclassical bHLH Rbpj transcription factor complex is required for specification of GABAergic neurons independent of Notch signaling.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; establishes that Ptf1a-Rbpj complex formation is required for GABAergic specification independently of canonical Notch signaling.

title: Transcriptional autoregulation controls pancreatic Ptf1a expression during development and adulthood.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; supports PTF1 trimer composition, transcriptional activation, autoregulation, and the acinar differentiation/maintenance program.

title: The genesis of cerebellar GABAergic neurons: fate potential and specification mechanisms.
review_notes: Full-text cerebellar synthesis verified; directly places Ptf1a-positive ventricular-zone progenitors upstream of cerebellar GABAergic projection neurons and interneurons.

title: Specification of spatial identities of cerebellar neuron progenitors by ptf1a and atoh1 for proper production of GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache verified; reciprocal knock-in and electroporation experiments support Ptf1a as necessary and sufficient for cerebellar GABAergic versus glutamatergic identity.

title: Impact of cytosine methylation on DNA binding specificities of human transcription factors.
review_notes: Full text verifies the 542-transcription-factor methyl-SELEX study, but the cached article does not expose a PTF1A-specific measurement or motif in accessible prose or tables. The associated PTF1A IDA annotation is therefore left UNDECIDED.

title: Regulation of neutrophil adhesion by pituitary growth hormone accompanies tyrosine phosphorylation of Jak2, p125FAK, and paxillin.
review_notes: Abstract describes Jak2 (Janus kinase) association with FAK via STAT3; the GOA row is JUN kinase binding, a possible JAK/JNK mix-up.

title: Role of dystrophins and utrophins in platelet adhesion process.
review_notes: Abstract does not mention FAK; supports actin binding and utrophin binding rows only if the full text does.

title: Ancient origin of the integrin-mediated adhesion and signaling machinery.
review_notes: Full text read. Source for presence of canonical FAK in Capsaspora and its absence (FAK-related kinase domain only) in M. brevicollis and Proterospongia.

title: Integrin-Mediated Adhesion in the Unicellular Holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki.
review_notes: Abstract only. Shows integrin/vinculin-based substrate adhesion in Capsaspora; does not test FAK.

title: Mutations in PTPN11, encoding the protein tyrosine phosphatase SHP-2, cause Noonan syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Human genetics establishes PTPN11 gain-of-function variants in Noonan syndrome; developmental GO terms remain broad outputs.

title: Sprouty proteins are in vivo targets of Corkscrew/SHP-2 tyrosine phosphatases.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Directly identifies Sprouty as a physiological SHP2/Corkscrew substrate and explains positive RTK signaling.

title: Shp2-dependent ERK signaling is essential for induction of Bergmann glia and foliation of the cerebellum.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Conditional genetics establishes the FGF8-SHP2-ERK requirement in radial glia/Bergmann glia and cerebellar foliation.

title: Siglec1 suppresses antiviral innate immune response by inducing TBK1 degradation via the ubiquitin ligase TRIM27.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Establishes a context-specific scaffolding/adaptor role for SHP2 in innate immunity.

title: Determination of the catalytic activity of LEOPARD syndrome-associated SHP2 mutants toward parafibromin, a bona fide SHP2 substrate involved in Wnt signaling.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Biochemical work on a physiological substrate confirms SHP2 tyrosine-phosphatase activity and variant effects.

title: Structural, Functional, and Clinical Characterization of a Novel PTPN11 Mutation Cluster Underlying Noonan Syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Biochemical and cellular analyses connect altered SHP2 activity to MAPK output.

title: Interaction of SHP-2 SH2 domains with PD-1 ITSM induces PD-1 dimerization and SHP-2 activation.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Full text directly defines tandem-SH2 phosphotyrosine binding, autoinhibition release, and activation.

title: Adapter function of protein-tyrosine phosphatase 1D in insulin receptor/insulin receptor substrate-1 interaction.
review_notes: PubMed identifier/title confirmed against NCBI ESummary on 2026-07-14. Directly demonstrates a non-catalytic adaptor function between insulin receptor and IRS1.

title: Falcon deep research report for human PTPRC
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/falcon, 29 cited passages, mostly reviews plus 2019-2024 primary papers). Used as leads only. Core content (D1 catalytic/D2 inactive, LCK Y505 and Y394, ITAM restraint, ectodomain-size segregation, JAK phosphatase as less secure, human SCID) is consistent with primary papers cited in this review; four primary leads (PMID:31641081, PMID:23580664, PMID:39454026, PMID:11145714) were verified and cached. Clinical/therapeutic sections (CAR T, radioimmunotherapy, base editing) are outside GO scope and were not used.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: Machine-source identity verified. The securin family mapping captures chromosome biology but its chromosome-organization term is too broad for the direct PTTG1 mechanism.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Machine-source identity verified; the inferred inhibitor, nuclear, and meiotic segregation annotations are compatible with securin orthology.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas immunofluorescence source for cytosolic localization.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Automated nucleus and cytoplasm calls agree with direct human fractionation.

title: Identification of a vertebrate sister-chromatid separation inhibitor involved in transformation and tumorigenesis.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. It identifies human PTTG as securin and supplies foundational vertebrate functional evidence; some perturbation experiments use Xenopus securin.

title: Securin is required for chromosomal stability in human cells.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. This directly establishes the activating/chaperone requirement and chromosome-stability consequence in human cells.

title: Regulation of human separase by securin binding and autocleavage.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The source directly supports ESPL1 binding and inhibitor activity; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Human full-length Securin is a natively unfolded protein.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The paper directly establishes intrinsic disorder but its accessible experimental summary does not establish molecular-function activator activity; direct activation support comes from PMID:11371342 and PMID:23798554.

title: Systematic analysis of human protein complexes identifies chromosome segregation proteins.
review_notes: PubMed identity and platform description were verified. The exact PTTG1-ESPL1 pair is present in GOA/IntAct but not in the locally accessible abstract, so pair-level verification remains incomplete.

title: Critical differences between isoforms of securin reveal mechanisms of separase regulation.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The human experiments provide the most direct support for a specific cysteine-endopeptidase activator replacement term; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: PP2A delays APC/C-dependent degradation of separase-associated but not free securin.
review_notes: PubMed identity and cached full text were verified. This directly supports the PTTG1-ESPL1 interaction and regulated maintenance of the inhibited complex before anaphase.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: PubMed identity and platform-level abstract were verified; the exact PTTG1-ESPL1 pair is represented in GOA/IntAct but not in the cached text.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and cached full text were verified at the platform level. The exact PTTG1-ESPL1 pair is encoded in GOA/IntAct but not discussed in the accessible article prose.

title: Structural basis of human separase regulation by securin and CDK1-cyclin B1.
review_notes: PubMed identity and full PMC text were verified. This is the decisive human structural source for complex membership and inhibitor mechanism.

title: hpttg, a human homologue of rat pttg, is overexpressed in hematopoietic neoplasms. Evidence for a transcriptional activation function of hPTTG.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The fractionation result directly supports both cytoplasmic/cytosolic and nuclear localization; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Pituitary tumor-transforming gene protein associates with ribosomal protein S10 and a novel human homologue of DnaJ in testicular cells.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The study supports a testis/spermatogenesis context, but the functional inference is indirect and substantially based on rat expression plus transfected-cell binding.

title: Association of cell cycle proteins with the APC/C:Cdh1 complex
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; supports the curated cytosolic APC/C substrate context.

title: Degradation of multiubiquitinated cell cycle proteins
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; represents proteasomal turnover of APC/C substrates.

title: Association of Securin with Cdc20:APC/C complex
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; directly concerns securin recognition by APC/C:Cdc20.

title: Ubiquitination of Securin by phospho-APC/C:Cdc20 complex
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; directly represents regulated PTTG1 ubiquitination.

title: Ubiquitination of cell cycle proteins targeted by the APC/C:Cdh1complex
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; explicitly supports the cytosolic compartment.

title: Degradation of multiubiquitinated Securin
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; directly represents the PTTG1 destruction step.

title: PTTG1 (Securin) sequesters ESPL1 (Separase)
review_notes: Local Reactome cache inspected; this database reaction directly matches the core separase-securin inhibitory mechanism.

title: Manual deep-research synthesis for human PTTG1
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the complete GOA set, reviewed UniProt record, locally cached publications, and explicit evidence limitations.

title: Manual PTTG1 curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored decision log recording source access, OpenScientist status, GO-term verification, and annotation-level judgments.

title: UniProtKB record for human PTTG1 (O95997)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project and inspected in full.

title: Crystal structure of human pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase.
review_notes: First human PYCR1 crystal structure; decameric (five homodimers) architecture, Rossmann motif and Glu221 catalytic role, and NAD(P)H-dependent P5C-to-proline catalysis. Directly supports the core MF, homo-oligomerization, and complex.

title: Cloning human pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase cDNA by complementation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Original human PYCR1 cDNA cloning by complementation of yeast proline auxotrophy; establishes the gene identity, EC 1.5.1.2 activity, and role in proline biosynthesis.

title: Mutations in PYCR1 cause cutis laxa with progeroid features.
review_notes: Landmark disease paper linking PYCR1 loss-of-function to ARCL2B/ARCL3B; demonstrates mitochondrial localization, altered mitochondrial morphology/membrane potential, and increased apoptosis under oxidative stress in patient fibroblasts.

title: Functional specialization in proline biosynthesis of melanoma.
review_notes: Full-text available; isotope-tracing and kinetic dissection of PYCR1/PYCR2/PYCRL. Shows PYCR1 is mitochondrial and contributes primarily to proline production from glutamate, with NADH preference and product (proline) inhibition.

title: DJ-1 cooperates with PYCR1 in cell protection against oxidative stress.
review_notes: Reports a direct DJ-1(PARK7)-PYCR1 interaction that enhances PYCR1 activity, joint mitochondrial co-localization, and a shared anti-oxidative-stress pathway; basis for the oxidative-stress and membrane-potential annotations. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Frequent amplification of ORAOV1 gene in esophageal squamous cell cancer promotes an aggressive phenotype via proline metabolism and ROS production.
review_notes: ORAOV1/LTO1 binds PYCR (peptide mass fingerprinting) and modulates proline metabolism and ROS in esophageal cancer; source of the LTO1 protein-binding annotation. The binding is real but the plain "protein binding" MF term is uninformative.

title: Purified human erythrocyte pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase. Preferential oxidation of NADPH.
review_notes: Early biochemical purification of human P5C reductase; native 10-12-mer assembly, NADH/NADPH kinetics and cofactor preference. Supports homo-oligomerization and the catalytic activity.

title: Resolving the cofactor-binding site in the proline biosynthetic enzyme human pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase 1.
review_notes: Definitive structural/kinetic study locating the NADPH cofactor site in the N-terminal Rossmann fold, confirming the decameric (pentamer-of-dimers) assembly, and validating catalysis via the T238A mutant. Supports core MF, complex, and BP.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI high-throughput yeast two-hybrid interactome (source of the TNPO2 binary interaction). Provides only a generic "protein binding" datapoint with no functional annotation for PYCR1.

title: PYCR1 decamer reduces (S)-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate to L-Pro
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing the PYCR1 decamer reaction in the mitochondrial matrix; supports the core catalytic activity and the mitochondrial matrix localization.

title: UniProtKB P32322 (P5CR1_HUMAN) record
review_notes: Authoritative UniProt record; establishes the core catalytic activity (EC 1.5.1.2), NADH cofactor preference, mitochondrial localization, homodecamer assembly, proline biosynthesis pathway (step 1/1), and the ARCL2B/ARCL3B disease associations.

title: Functional specialization in proline biosynthesis of melanoma.
review_notes: Full text available and cached. Directly establishes PYCR2's catalytic activity, mitochondrial localization and role in the glutamate route of proline biosynthesis; the primary experimental basis for the core MF, BP and location annotations. Supporting quotes verified verbatim.

title: Frequent amplification of ORAOV1 gene in esophageal squamous cell cancer promotes an aggressive phenotype via proline metabolism and ROS production.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. The paper's primary focus is ORAOV1; it reports a physical interaction with "PYCR" generically. Supports the PYCR2 IPI (GO:0005515) but "protein binding" is uninformative; the interaction is non-core. Interaction partner recorded in UniProt as LTO1.

title: Mutations in PYCR2, encoding pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase 2, cause microcephaly and hypomyelination.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but abstract is detailed. Establishes disease (HLD10), mitochondrial localization, and the oxidative-stress/redox role (IMP GO:0034599). Supporting quotes verified verbatim against the abstract.

title: Purified human erythrocyte pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase. Preferential oxidation of NADPH.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Cited by UniProt for FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION. Characterizes the erythrocyte enzyme; basis for the EXP catalytic-activity and (erythrocyte) cytoplasm annotations. Quote verified verbatim.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput (HTP) mitochondrial-proteome dataset supporting the mitochondrial localization; corroborative rather than primary.

title: Pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase in human erythrocytes.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Cited by UniProt for FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, ACTIVITY REGULATION and TISSUE SPECIFICITY. Supports the EXP catalytic activity and the redox interpretation. Quote verified verbatim.

title: PYCR2 decamer reduces (S)-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate to L-Pro
review_notes: Reactome reaction record; supports the catalytic activity but asserts a cytosolic localization at odds with the mitochondrial localization established experimentally for PYCR2 in nucleated cells.

title: Regulation of glycogen phosphorylase. Role of the peptide region surrounding the phosphoserine residue in determining enzyme properties.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Supports catalytic activity, allosteric regulation, and the homodimer subunit structure of the muscle enzyme (UniProt cites it for CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, ACTIVITY REGULATION, SUBUNIT, and Ser-15 phosphorylation).

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput exosome proteomics; supports only the (over-annotated) extracellular exosome detection, not a functional role.

title: Protein interaction network of alternatively spliced isoforms from brain links genetic risk factors for autism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Large-scale isoform interactome; source of an uninformative bare protein binding IPI (PRKAB2).

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Proteome-scale interactome screen; source of bare protein binding IPIs (PRKAB2, NTAQ1).

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Systematic interaction-perturbation study; source of a bare protein binding IPI (NTAQ1).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (HuRI). Binary interactome map; source of bare protein binding IPIs, several with paralogous phosphorylases (PYGL, PYGB).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Proteome-scale interactome study; source of a bare protein binding IPI (PYGB paralog).

title: A proteome-scale map of the SARS-CoV-2-human contactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Virus-host contactome; source of a bare (xeno) protein binding IPI with SARS-CoV-2 rep, not a native function.

title: Molecular genetic heterogeneity of myophosphorylase deficiency (McArdle's disease).
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Establishes PYGM loss-of-function as the cause of McArdle disease (GSD5) and underpins the FUNCTION/CATALYTIC ACTIVITY and IMP glycogen-catabolism annotations.

title: Molecular diagnosis of McArdle disease: revised genomic structure of the myophosphorylase gene and identification of a novel mutation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Focused on genomic structure and mutation detection; TAS source for glycogen phosphorylase activity and glycogen metabolic process.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO_Central PAN-GO phylogenetic pipeline; the IBA annotations it supports (DHPR activity, cytoplasm, tetrahydrobiopterin biosynthetic process, NAD(P)H binding) are all consistent with the experimentally characterized function of this well-studied enzyme.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Genuine urinary-exosome proteomics dataset that includes QDPR; supports a non-core extracellular-exosome localization, not a functional role.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Exosome shotgun proteomics from expressed prostatic secretions; supports a non-core extracellular-exosome localization datum.

title: Structure and expression of human dihydropteridine reductase.
review_notes: Primary paper cloning/expressing human DHPR and establishing its NADH- dependent reductase function and role in the aromatic amino acid hydroxylating systems. Abstract uses the older EC 1.6.99.7; the current EC is 1.5.1.34 (same activity).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial-proteome mapping in which QDPR is detected; weak, single-source evidence for organellar residence of an abundant cytosolic SDR enzyme lacking mitochondrial targeting features. Treated as over-annotation, not core localization.

title: The crystallographic structure of a human dihydropteridine reductase NADH binary complex expressed in Escherichia coli by a cDNA constructed from its rat homologue.
review_notes: Structural/kinetic characterization of human DHPR as an NADH binary complex; supports the EXP molecular-function annotation and NADH binding.

title: q-dihydrobiopterin + NADH + H+ => tetrahydrobiopterin + NAD+
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the DHPR-catalyzed regeneration of BH4 in the cytosol; supports cytosolic localization and the core reductase reaction.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline; yields the over-general pentosyltransferase activity term. Mechanically correct but uninformative relative to the specific MF.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic inference; supports the correct catalytic MF and NAD/quinolinate process terms.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: ARBA/EC/RHEA-based electronic annotation re-deriving the correct catalytic MF and NAD biosynthetic process.

title: Structural and kinetic characterization of quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (hQPRTase) from homo sapiens.
review_notes: Full-text available; primary structural and kinetic characterization of human QPRT. Directly grounds the catalytic MF, catalytic-complex, and homo-oligomer annotations.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports only the HDA extracellular-exosome detection, which is non-core for a cytosolic enzyme.

title: The crystal structure of human quinolinic acid phosphoribosyltransferase in complex with its inhibitor phthalic acid.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache but establishes catalytic activity, quinolinate catabolism, and the hexameric assembly.

title: Novel interactive partners of neuroligin 3: new aspects for pathogenesis of autism.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports a single QPRT-NLGN3 PPI (bare protein binding) of unclear functional significance for QPRT.

title: Structural Insights into the Quaternary Catalytic Mechanism of Hexameric Human Quinolinate Phosphoribosyltransferase, a Key Enzyme in de novo NAD Biosynthesis.
review_notes: Full-text available; grounds the hexameric catalytic-complex and identical-protein-binding annotations and the de novo NAD role.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome; QPRT self-interaction is consistent with homo-oligomerization, but the heterologous partners lack functional relevance.

title: Quinolinic-phosphoribosyl transferase activity is decreased in epileptic human brain tissue.
review_notes: Abstract-only; direct assay of endogenous human QPRTase activity and quinolinate catabolism in brain.

title: Characterization and functional expression of the cDNA encoding human brain quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase.
review_notes: Abstract-only; functional-complementation evidence directly establishing the catalytic activity and quinolinate catabolic role of human QPRT.

title: QPRT transfers PRIB to QUIN to form NAMN
review_notes: Reactome reaction supporting the cytosol location and de novo NAD+ from tryptophan process; also notes Mg2+ dependence.

title: Glycosylated queuosines in tRNAs optimize translational rate and post-embryonic growth.
review_notes: Abstract-only (no PMC record). The defining biochemistry and knockout paper.

title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for QTGAL (human)
review_notes: Trust gates clear; its single citation (PMID:37992713) is cached and quoted.

title: UniProt entry Q67FW5 (QTGAL_HUMAN)
review_notes: Function, Rhea reaction, kinetics and location from PMID:37992713. The FUNCTION text contains an apparent slip: it says 'Mannosylation of queuosine(34) in tRNA(Tyr)' slows UAC elongation, where galactosylation is meant (tRNA(Tyr) carries galQ; mannosylation is QTMAN's tRNA(Asp) reaction). That sentence is not used here.

title: The CAP superfamily: cysteine-rich secretory proteins, antigen 5, and pathogenesis-related 1 proteins--roles in reproduction, cancer, and immune defense.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This family review supports topology and functional-diversity context, not a specific R3HDML molecular activity.

title: R3hdml regulates satellite cell proliferation and differentiation.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and the cached full text were checked. Mouse knockout, knockdown, extracellular-protein rescue, injury, and expression experiments directly establish the secreted myogenic role while explicitly leaving the molecular mechanism open.

title: Falcon deep research report for RAB24
review_notes: LLM synthesis of secondary reviews; not independently verified against the primary papers, which are not all in the publications cache (e.g. Amaya 2016 Traffic, Ylä-Anttila 2018 Small GTPases). The report's RAB24-specific points (low GTPase activity, predominant GTP-bound state, prenylation-dependent targeting, late-stage basal-autophagic-compartment clearance, Rab7/RILP interaction, inner/outer autophagic-vacuole membranes) are consistent with the curated UniProt and PMID:26325487 / PMID:10660536 evidence. However, the report repeatedly imposes the canonical Rab GEF/GAP/GDI/effector cycle and a definitive autophagosome-lysosome "fusion" step onto RAB24 despite its atypical, GTP-locked, poorly-hydrolysing, partly-non-prenylated biochemistry; those canonical-mechanism generalizations are not anchored to RAB24-specific data and were not adopted.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis run: RAB9A GEF/GAP switch-control gap
review_notes: Directly inspected; supports the existing residual switch-control knowledge gap and the caution against curating RUTBC1/RUTBC2 as RAB9A GAPs.

title: Protein farnesyltransferase and geranylgeranyltransferase share a common alpha subunit.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Foundational paper on the shared prenyltransferase alpha subunit. Note that the FTase/GGTase-I shared alpha is FNTA; RABGGTA is the distinct Rab (type II) alpha subunit. The TAS annotations were curated to RABGGTA by PINC.

title: Comprehensive mutation analysis (20 families) of the choroideremia gene reveals a missense variant that prevents the binding of REP1 with Rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports the physiological RABGGTA-CHM/REP1 interaction (GOA IPI WITH P24386), though the paper's focus is the REP1/CHM side.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome (BioPlex). Source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations with CHM (P24386) and RABGGTB (P53611); interactors are physiologically plausible but the annotation is uninformative as a stand-alone MF.

title: GGTase3 is a newly identified geranylgeranyltransferase targeting a ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The IPI WITH/FROM is RABGGTB (P53611), the beta subunit that dimerizes with RABGGTA; the paper itself is primarily about the GGTase3 = PTAR1 + RABGGTB complex.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary (Y2H) interactome. Source of a bare protein-binding IPI with RABGGTB (P53611), the catalytic beta subunit. Uninformative as a stand-alone MF.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 AP-MS interactome. Source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations with CHM (P24386) and RABGGTB (P53611). Physiologically plausible interactors; uninformative as a stand-alone MF.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging IP-MS. Source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations with CHM (P24386) and RABGGTB (P53611). Uninformative as a stand-alone MF.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map interactome. Source of bare protein-binding IPI annotations with CHM (P24386) and RABGGTB (P53611). Uninformative as a stand-alone MF.

title: Rab geranylgeranyl transferase catalyzes the geranylgeranylation of adjacent cysteines in the small GTPases Rab1A, Rab3A, and Rab5A.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary experimental reference for the catalytic activity (UniProt EXP). Directly supports the core Rab geranylgeranyltransferase function.

title: Retinal degeneration in choroideremia: deficiency of rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the choroideremia link, but attributes the defect to component A (REP1/CHM). The RABGGTA visual-perception and protein-modification TAS annotations derived from this paper are best treated as over-annotations of the wrong subunit.

title: Novel raf kinase protein-protein interactions found by an exhaustive yeast two-hybrid analysis.
review_notes: Yeast two-hybrid screen for Raf kinase interactors; reports that the Raf cysteine-rich domain (CRD) bound all 20 proteins recovered, indicating a low-specificity interaction surface. Supports only a bare GO:0005515 "protein binding" (ARAF, P10398) with no functional context for RABGGTB.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome map; source of several bare protein binding IPI annotations (WDR4, TAFA1, TMEM25, B4GALT7) that are not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome (BioPlex-type) study; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations including RABGGTA (Q92696) and PTAR1 (Q7Z6K3). The RABGGTA/PTAR1 partnerships are biologically meaningful but are better captured by the complex-membership terms.

title: GGTase3 is a newly identified geranylgeranyltransferase targeting a ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Identifies GGTase-III as a heterodimer of the orphan alpha subunit PTAR1 and the catalytic beta subunit of GGTase2 (RABGGTB); reports that GGTase-III geranylgeranylates FBXL2. Crystal structure of the GGTase3-FBXL2-SKP1 complex. Abstract-only in cache but PMID/title verified.

title: A SNARE geranylgeranyltransferase essential for the organization of the Golgi apparatus.
review_notes: Full text available. Defines GGTase-III (PTAR1 + beta subunit of RabGGTase) and shows it geranylgeranylates mono-farnesylated YKT6 at Cys194 to produce doubly prenylated YKT6 required for Golgi SNARE assembly. Mutagenesis of RABGGTB Gly49 abolishes YKT6 modification. Also questions whether FBXL2 is a physiological GGTase-III substrate.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (IGFBP6, WDR4, RABGGTA, B4GALT7). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex 3.0 interactome; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (PTAR1, RABGGTA). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging proximity interactome; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (PTAR1, RABGGTA). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell map interactome; source of bare protein binding IPI annotations (PTAR1, RABGGTA). Not gene-specific functional evidence.

title: Rab geranylgeranyl transferase catalyzes the geranylgeranylation of adjacent cysteines in the small GTPases Rab1A, Rab3A, and Rab5A.
review_notes: Direct biochemical demonstration (mass spectrometry of tryptic peptides) of di-geranylgeranylation of Rab substrates by RabGGTase; the EXP evidence underpinning the enzyme's molecular function. Abstract-only in cache but PMID/title verified and this is the reference cited by UniProt for the catalytic activity / EC 2.5.1.60.

title: Retinal degeneration in choroideremia: deficiency of rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
review_notes: This paper is about component A (REP1/CHM), the choroideremia disease gene, and explicitly finds that component B (which contains RABGGTB) is NOT deficient. It is therefore the wrong reference to attribute "visual perception" and "protein modification process" to RABGGTB; the visual phenotype maps to CHM, not to this catalytic subunit.

title: Structures of the human and Drosophila 80S ribosome.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed ("Structures of the human and Drosophila 80S ribosome"); cryo-EM structure places RACK1 as an integral 40S subunit component, establishing the core ribosome-binding/structural-subunit function (GO:0043022, GO:0022627).

title: ZNF598 and RACK1 Regulate Mammalian Ribosome-Associated Quality Control Function by Mediating Regulatory 40S Ribosomal Ubiquitylation.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; Results show RACK1 (with ZNF598) is required for regulatory 40S ubiquitylation that resolves stalled/collided ribosomes, establishing RACK1's ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) scaffold role.

title: RACK1, a receptor for activated C kinase and a homolog of the beta subunit of G proteins, inhibits activity of src tyrosine kinases and growth of NIH 3T3 cells.
review_notes: GOA-anchored (this PMID supports GO:0030292 protein tyrosine kinase inhibitor activity in RACK1-goa.tsv); seminal paper establishing RACK1's Src-family kinase inhibition / signaling-scaffold core function.

title: Human chromatid cohesin component hRad21 is phosphorylated in M phase and associated with metaphase centromeres.
review_notes: Abstract checked; directly supports nuclear localisation, M-phase phosphorylation, prometaphase chromosome association and retention at metaphase centromeres of human RAD21.

title: Cohesin cleavage by separase required for anaphase and cytokinesis in human cells.
review_notes: Abstract checked (abstract-only cache); identifies the two separase cleavage sites in human SCC1/RAD21 and shows cleavage is essential for sister separation and cytokinesis.

title: A potential role for human cohesin in mitotic spindle aster assembly.
review_notes: Abstract checked; supports nuclear-matrix and spindle-pole localisation of the human complex containing Scc1/Rad21; the spindle-aster role remains a single-study proposal.

title: Functional contribution of Pds5 to cohesin-mediated cohesion in human cells and Xenopus egg extracts.
review_notes: Abstract checked; Scc1 RNAi produces severe cohesion defects in HeLa cells and PDS5 associates with chromatin cohesin-dependently.

title: Cohesin mediates transcriptional insulation by CCCTC-binding factor.
review_notes: Abstract checked; cohesin binding sites coincide with CTCF and cohesin mediates CTCF insulation at H19/IGF2, the basis of the transcriptional/looping role.

title: The cohesin complex is required for the DNA damage-induced G2/M checkpoint in mammalian cells.
review_notes: Full text checked; Scc1/RAD21 depletion abolishes the DNA damage-induced G2/M checkpoint and leaves broken chromosomes unrepaired, supporting the repair and checkpoint roles.

title: Releasing cohesin from chromosome arms in early mitosis: opposing actions of Wapl-Pds5 and Sgo1.
review_notes: Full text checked; maps the RAD21 central region (287-449) required for SA1, WAPL and PDS5B binding and shows WAPL/PDS5B bind RAD21 directly.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: NK-cell membrane proteome; RAD21 identification in a membrane fraction is a contaminant-level observation and does not support a membrane localisation.

title: Structure of cohesin subcomplex pinpoints direct shugoshin-Wapl antagonism in centromeric cohesion.
review_notes: Full text checked; crystal structure of the human SA2-Scc1 subcomplex defining the RAD21 docking surface for STAG2 and the shared SGO1/WAPL site.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale Y2H map; the RAD21-FHL3 pair has no functional follow-up.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Variant-interaction screen built on the Y2H map; the RAD21-FHL3 pair has no functional follow-up.

title: Cryo-EM structure of the human cohesin-NIPBL-DNA complex.
review_notes: Abstract checked; cryo-EM of human cohesin-NIPBL-DNA establishing the ring architecture, RAD21 head contacts and DNA entrapment.

title: Sequence conservation of the rad21 Schizosaccharomyces pombe DNA double-strand break repair gene in human and mouse.
review_notes: Abstract checked; the cloning paper only infers repair/recombination roles from S. pombe homology and expression pattern, so its TAS annotations were graded on later direct evidence.

title: Ca2+ activates human homologous recombination protein Rad51 by modulating its ATPase activity.
review_notes: Bugreev & Mazin; RAD51 DNA-dependent ATPase; Ca2+ modulation of ATP hydrolysis stimulates strand exchange. Full text available; quotes confirmed.

title: RECQL5/Recql5 helicase regulates homologous recombination and suppresses tumor formation via disruption of Rad51 presynaptic filaments.
review_notes: RECQL5 disrupts RAD51 presynaptic (nucleoprotein) filaments — confirms the GO:0099182 annotation is a misnomer-driven mis-mapping, not a neuronal-synapse localization.

title: Discovery of a novel function for human Rad51: maintenance of the mitochondrial genome.
review_notes: Sage et al.; RAD51/RAD51C/XRCC3 maintain mtDNA copy number under oxidative stress; identifies mtDNA as a RAD51 substrate.

title: Purified human BRCA2 stimulates RAD51-mediated recombination.
review_notes: Jensen, Carreira & Kowalczykowski; full-length BRCA2 promotes assembly of RAD51 onto ssDNA, targets RAD51 to ssDNA over dsDNA, displaces RPA and stabilizes RAD51-ssDNA filaments by blocking ATP hydrolysis. Verified against cached full text; corroborates the Affinage narrative on BRCA2-mediated RAD51 loading. Cited here only under the over-annotated generic protein-binding rows.

title: RAD51 mutants cause replication defects and chromosomal instability.
review_notes: RAD51 mutants cause replication defects and chromosomal instability; supports fork-processing role.

title: A Dominant Mutation in Human RAD51 Reveals Its Function in DNA Interstrand Crosslink Repair Independent of Homologous Recombination.
review_notes: Dominant RAD51 variant (FANCR) with a role in interstrand crosslink repair separable from HR. Quote confirmed.

title: A novel Fanconi anaemia subtype associated with a dominant-negative mutation in RAD51.
review_notes: Dominant-negative RAD51 mutation defining a novel Fanconi anemia subtype (FANCR). Full text available.

title: TOPBP1 regulates RAD51 phosphorylation and chromatin loading and determines PARP inhibitor sensitivity.
review_notes: Moudry et al.; TOPBP1 promotes PLK1-mediated RAD51 Ser14 phosphorylation required for RAD51 chromatin loading and foci formation in HR. Verified against cached record; supports the DSB-repair and chromosome-localization rows for which it is the original reference.

title: The β-isoform of BCCIP promotes ADP release from the RAD51 presynaptic filament and enhances homologous DNA pairing.
review_notes: Describes RAD51 presynaptic filament, homology search, strand invasion and D-loop formation. Full text; quote confirmed.

title: Cryo-EM structures of RAD51 assembled on nucleosomes containing a DSB site.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of RAD51 assembled on DSB-containing nucleosomes; filament binds and peels nucleosomal DNA. Quote confirmed.

title: Purification and characterization of the human Rad51 protein, an analogue of E. coli RecA.
review_notes: Baumann et al.; establishes human RAD51 ss/dsDNA binding, DNA-dependent ATPase and helical nucleoprotein filament formation. Verbatim quote confirmed.

title: Human Rad51 protein promotes ATP-dependent homologous pairing and strand transfer reactions in vitro.
review_notes: Baumann & West; human RAD51 promotes ATP-dependent homologous pairing and strand transfer in vitro. Verbatim quote confirmed.

title: Activities of human recombination protein Rad51.
review_notes: Gupta, Bazemore, Golub & Radding (1997 PNAS); purified human RAD51 catalyzes DNA-dependent ATP hydrolysis, homologous pairing and strand exchange, and forms stable presynaptic complexes, with homologous pairing/strand exchange more tightly coupled to ATP hydrolysis than in RecA. Foundational human-RAD51 recombinase paper surfaced by the Affinage record; verified against cached full text and attached to core_functions (strand exchange, ATP hydrolysis).

title: Identification and purification of two distinct complexes containing the five RAD51 paralogs.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified. Establishes the two RAD51C-containing complexes (BCDX2 and CX3) by purification and shows BCDX2 binds ssDNA, ss gaps and nicks. Foundational for the complex and DNA-binding annotations.

title: Mediator function of the human Rad51B-Rad51C complex in Rad51/RPA-catalyzed DNA strand exchange.
review_notes: Verified (PubMed abstract). Original biochemical demonstration that the RAD51B-RAD51C complex has ssDNA-binding and ssDNA-stimulated ATPase activity and acts as a recombination mediator by partially relieving RPA competition for ssDNA, promoting RAD51-ssDNA filament assembly. Primary support for the BCDX2 HR-mediator core function (previously supported only by the later cryo-EM and epistasis papers).

title: Mammalian Rad51C contributes to DNA cross-link resistance, sister chromatid cohesion and genomic stability.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). RAD51C-mutant hamster CL-V4B cells show cross-link (MMC/cisplatin) hypersensitivity, impaired RAD51 focus formation, genomic instability, and a reduced level of sister chromatid cohesion (complemented by Rad51C cDNA). Direct experimental support for the sister-chromatid-cohesion (GO:0007062) and ICL-repair annotations.

title: Identification of functional domains in the RAD51L2 (RAD51C) protein and its requirement for gene conversion.
review_notes: Verified. Shows RAD51C ATP-binding domain (K131) is required for function, nuclear localization with a C-terminal NLS, and a requirement for gene conversion (HR).

title: RAD51C is required for Holliday junction processing in mammalian cells.
review_notes: Verified. RAD51C depletion reduces branch migration/HJ resolvase activity in extracts. Supports RAD51C's role in HJ processing, but the endonucleolytic catalysis was later attributed to GEN1; hence the crossover-junction endonuclease MF is marked over-annotated.

title: Cellular localization of human Rad51C and regulation of ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis of Rad51.
review_notes: Verified. Detects endogenous RAD51C in nucleus, cytoplasm and perinuclear region and shows RAD51C regulates ubiquitin-mediated RAD51 proteolysis.

title: Role of RAD51C and XRCC3 in genetic recombination and DNA repair.
review_notes: Verified (PubMed abstract). Shows RAD51C localizes to mouse meiotic chromosomes at pachytene/diplotene and that Holliday-junction resolvase activity co-elutes with the CX3 (RAD51C-XRCC3) complex, which associates with crossovers. Supports the non-core meiotic reciprocal-recombination annotation.

title: RAD51C deficiency in mice results in early prophase I arrest in males and sister chromatid separation at metaphase II in females.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Hypomorphic Rad51c mice show sexually dimorphic meiotic defects: early prophase I arrest in spermatocytes (early RAD51-mediated recombination role) and precocious sister-chromatid separation/aneuploidy in oocytes. Supports the non-core meiotic recombinase-assembly annotation.

title: RAD51C facilitates checkpoint signaling by promoting CHK2 phosphorylation.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Establishes RAD51C's early DDR role: recruitment dependent on ATM/NBS1/RPA and requirement for CHK2 activation and cell-cycle arrest.

title: Ring-shaped Rad51 paralog protein complexes bind Holliday junctions and replication forks as visualized by electron microscopy.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Direct EM evidence that BCDX2 and CX3 bind Holliday junctions and replication forks with high specificity as ring-shaped complexes.

title: Mutation of the RAD51C gene in a Fanconi anemia-like disorder.
review_notes: Verified (PubMed abstract). Identifies a homozygous RAD51C missense mutation in a consanguineous FA-like family, establishing RAD51C as the Fanconi anemia complementation group O (FANCO) gene; patient cells lose RAD51 focus formation and are hypersensitive to MMC and camptothecin. Primary support for the NEW interstrand-cross-link-repair (GO:0036297) annotation.

title: Discovery of a novel function for human Rad51: maintenance of the mitochondrial genome.
review_notes: Verified. Demonstrates mitochondrial localization of RAD51C (with RAD51/XRCC3) and a role in maintaining mtDNA copy number under oxidative stress. Supports the non-core mitochondrial annotations.

title: The RAD51 paralogs ensure cellular protection against mitotic defects and aneuploidy.
review_notes: Verified. RAD51B/RAD51C depletion causes G2/M arrest; XRCC3 acts with GEN1 at HJ resolution. Supports the non-core G2/M annotation and the reassignment of resolvase catalysis to GEN1.

title: Rad51 paralog complexes BCDX2 and CX3 act at different stages in the BRCA1-BRCA2-dependent homologous recombination pathway.
review_notes: Verified (PMC). Epistasis places BCDX2 downstream of BRCA2/upstream of RAD51 and CX3 downstream of RAD51 within BRCA-dependent HR. Core evidence for the DSB-repair-via-HR role.

title: Breast cancer-associated missense mutants of the PALB2 WD40 domain, which directly binds RAD51C, RAD51 and BRCA2, disrupt DNA repair.
review_notes: Verified. Shows RAD51C is part of a PALB2-BRCA2-containing HR complex and characterizes FANCO/BROVCA3 variants that disrupt these interactions.

title: Mammalian RAD51 paralogs protect nascent DNA at stalled forks and mediate replication restart.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Directly demonstrates RAD51C protects nascent DNA at stalled forks and promotes ATP-hydrolysis-dependent restart; patient mutations abolish fork protection.

title: A human interactome in three quantitative dimensions organized by stoichiometries and abundances.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: Sequential role of RAD51 paralog complexes in replication fork remodeling and restart.
review_notes: Supports the sequential action of RAD51 paralog complexes at replication forks and the replication-fork localization annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: A protein interaction landscape of breast cancer.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only (uninformative MF).

title: Structure and function of the RAD51B-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2 tumour suppressor.
review_notes: Verified (PMC full text). Cryo-EM/biochemistry showing BCDX2 stimulates RAD51 filament nucleation and extension via coupled RAD51B/RAD51C ATPases. Key structural support for the RAD51-filament-mediator core function.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: High-throughput cell-map interactome; supports a protein-binding IPI only.

title: Isolation and characterization of RAD51C, a new human member of the RAD51 family of related genes.
review_notes: Verified. Original RAD51C isolation; family membership, testis-high expression, and Y2H interactions with XRCC3 and RAD51B. Supports the historical DNA-binding/repair/recombination TAS annotations.

title: 14-3-3Gamma interacts with and is phosphorylated by multiple protein kinase C isoforms in PDGF-stimulated human vascular smooth muscle cells.
review_notes: Cached text directly describes the RAF1 finding used here (study of 14-3-3gamma in PDGF-stimulated vascular smooth muscle cells).

title: JSAP1, a novel jun N-terminal protein kinase (JNK)-binding protein that functions as a Scaffold factor in the JNK signaling pathway.
review_notes: Cached text directly describes the RAF1 finding used here (study identifying the mouse JNK scaffold JSAP1 (Mapk8ip3), which also coprecipitated Raf-1).

title: Hepatitis C virus core protein interacts with 14-3-3 protein and activates the kinase Raf-1.
review_notes: Cached abstract/text checked; supports the RAF1 annotation reviewed.

title: Functional conservation of 14-3-3 isoforms in inhibiting bad-induced apoptosis.
review_notes: Cached text directly describes the RAF1 finding used here (study of functional conservation of 14-3-3 isoforms binding Bad, Raf-1 and Cbl).

title: Identification of interaction between MEK2 and A-Raf-1.
review_notes: Cached text directly describes the RAF1 finding used here (MEK2-bait yeast two-hybrid screen that recovered c-Raf, KSR and A-Raf).

title: Di-Ras, a distinct subgroup of ras family GTPases with unique biochemical properties.
review_notes: Correctly shows Di-Ras does not bind the Raf RBD; the NOT annotation to the general small GTPase binding term overstates this.

title: Structure of a RING E3 trapped in action reveals ligation mechanism for the ubiquitin-like protein NEDD8.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structure of the trapped RBX1-UBC12~NEDD8-CUL1-DCN1 intermediate; direct mechanistic evidence for RBX1-catalysed NEDD8 ligation.

title: Arsenite Targets the RING Finger Domain of Rbx1 E3 Ubiquitin Ligase to Inhibit Proteasome-Mediated Degradation of Nrf2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; arsenite binding to the RBX1 RING suppresses CUL3-RBX1-KEAP1 activity toward NRF2 - chemical-biology support for the RING as the catalytic site of K48 chain formation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified HuRI binary interactome map; a legitimate source of interaction data but not of functional information about RBX1.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified BioPlex proteome-scale affinity-purification network; same caveat as the other high-throughput interactome sources.

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage.
review_notes: The identifier resolves to the cryo-EM structure of the human signal peptidase complex, which contains no RBX1 or centrosome data; it cannot support the GO:0051298 centrosome duplication annotation it is cited for. The same misattribution is recorded in the CUL1 review.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO (IPR039731) pipeline reference. The CAAX-box protein processing mapping it produces is correct, but the metalloendopeptidase activity mapping from the same reference is the wrong catalytic class for this glutamate-type protease.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO phylogenetic (IBA) reference. The ER-membrane and CAAX-box protein processing inferences are correct, but the metalloendopeptidase-activity inference propagated in the same tree assigns the wrong catalytic class.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA electronic annotations (endopeptidase activity, CAAX-box protein maturation). Both are correct, if general; endopeptidase is refined here to the glutamic-type class.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Automated multi-method IEA producing the ER-membrane location (via UniProtKB-SubCell SL-0097), consistent with the experimental localization.

title: Cloning and characterization of a mammalian prenyl protein-specific protease.
review_notes: Foundational RCE1 characterization paper; PubMed-verified. Establishes the CAAX-processing protease function, prenyl-substrate specificity, and substrate range. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false); experimental IDA annotations derive from the full text read by the curator.

title: USP17 regulates Ras activation and cell proliferation by blocking RCE1 activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Supports RCE1 endopeptidase activity, ER-membrane localization, the CAAX/Ras-processing role, and ubiquitination-dependent activity regulation. Abstract-only in the cache; IDA/IMP annotations derive from the full text.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput proteomics dataset (HDA). Provides only a generic membrane-localization datapoint, uninformative relative to the specific ER-membrane annotations.

title: RAF/MAP kinase cascade
review_notes: Reactome pathway. RCE1 is connected only indirectly (via processing of its Ras substrates upstream of the cascade), so the MAPK-cascade annotation is downstream/non-core.

title: USP17 deubiquitinates RCE1, CDC25A, DDX58, IFIH1
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing USP17-mediated deubiquitination/inhibition of RCE1. Supports the regulation biology; its cytosol compartment placement is a reaction abstraction, not RCE1 residence.

title: RCE1 cleaves S-Farn proRAS proteins
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly modeling the RCE1 CAAX-cleavage step at the ER membrane. Note the associated Reactome molecular-function call (cysteine-type endopeptidase) is the wrong catalytic class.

title: USP17L2 deubiquitinates RCE1
review_notes: Reactome reaction for USP17L2-mediated deubiquitination/inactivation of RCE1 at the ER membrane; supports the ER localization and activity-regulation biology.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS pipeline reference; the WITH/FROM source is the paralog RDH12 (Q96NR8). The transferred retinol-metabolic-process BP is independently correct for RDH11, but the NAD+-cofactor MF term is mis-transferred (RDH11 prefers NADP).

title: Automatic Gene Ontology annotation based on Rhea mapping
review_notes: Rhea-mapped enzymatic terms; chemically correct for the NADP-dependent retinol dehydrogenase reactions.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods

review_notes: Characterizes the MOUSE ortholog (SCALD). Source of the aldehyde-detoxification and retinal-metabolism annotations; abstract-only. Human RDH11 is weaker on toxic aldehydes (UniProt CAUTION), so detox terms are non-core for the human gene.

review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes cis-retinol substrate specificity and NAD+ preference; key evidence that the all-trans-retinol dehydrogenase term is the wrong substrate for RDH5.

title: Activity of human 11-cis-retinol dehydrogenase (Rdh5) with steroids and retinoids and expression of its mRNA in extra-ocular human tissue.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the retinoid and steroid (androsterone / androstanediol) dehydrogenase IDA annotations.

title: Identification and characterization of all-trans-retinol dehydrogenase from photoreceptor outer segments, the visual cycle enzyme that reduces all-trans-retinal to all-trans-retinol.
review_notes: Cached abstract-only record (full_text_available: false); title matches UniProt reference [1]. review_notes: Full-text mouse study supports a narrowly scoped cerebellar layer-forming outcome; it does not justify generalizing the mechanism to every Purkinje cell or directly to human development.
