review_notes: Full text available. Establishes RETREG2/FAM134A-specific ER-phagy function, stress-activation, ER membrane localization, and collagen quality control role.

title: Crystal structure of human riboflavin kinase reveals a beta barrel fold and a novel active site arch.
review_notes: PubMed-verified structure paper on human RFK (PDB 1NB0/1NB9/1P4M/1Q9S). Establishes the beta-barrel fold and confirms the riboflavin-kinase catalytic function; abstract supports the function and localization (cytoplasm) claims. GOA reuses it as the NAS source. The riboflavin biosynthetic process NAS is a minor mislabel (should be riboflavin metabolic process for a human salvage/utilization enzyme).

title: Riboflavin kinase couples TNF receptor 1 to NADPH oxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Primary experimental source for human RFK riboflavin kinase activity (IDA), the TNFRSF1A/CYBA physical interactions, and the NADPH-oxidase/ROS moonlighting role. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false); quoted claims are verbatim from the abstract.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome (Y2H) reference map; source of the RFK-CNTLN protein-binding IPI (also recorded in UniProt). Large-scale interaction screen with no RFK-specific functional characterization; contextual/background relevance only.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: Large-scale human mitochondrial-proteome dataset; source of the HTP mitochondrion localization. Such datasets can include cytosolic proteins, and RFK's curated location is cytoplasm/cytosol, so this is treated as a non-core localization.

title: Translocation of lipid-linked oligosaccharides across the ER membrane requires Rft1 protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The founding genetic paper for the flippase model. Correctly cited, but its conclusion is the contested one - the authors show Rft1 is "required for" translocation in vivo, which later biochemistry (PMID:18668045, PMID:19494107) and genetics (PMID:23720757) showed does not entail that Rft1 catalyses the step. A formal Brief Communication Arising was published against it.

title: Human RFT1 deficiency leads to a disorder of N-linked glycosylation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the index RFT1-CDG paper and the source of the IMP and IGI rows in GOA. The mutant-phenotype and rescue data are solid and uncontested; only the mechanistic gloss ("translocation") inherits the family controversy.

title: Does Rft1 flip an N-glycan lipid precursor?
review_notes: PubMed-verified Nature Brief Communication Arising against PMID:11807558. This is the paper that opened the controversy and it is essential context for any RFT1 molecular function annotation; it was absent from the previous version of this review.

title: Specific transbilayer translocation of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides by an endoplasmic reticulum flippase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Characterizes a specific ER M5-DLO flippase activity biochemically; relevant as background for the claim that flipping activity exists independently of Rft1, but does not assay RFT1 itself.

title: Suppression of Rft1 expression does not impair the transbilayer movement of Man5GlcNAc2-P-P-dolichol in sealed microsomes from yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct counter-evidence to the catalytic-flippase reading of the yeast genetics; the key observation is that the same Rft1-depleted cells that accumulate M5-DLO have undiminished flippase activity in sealed microsomes.

title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited by UniProt for Q96AA3 but missing from the previous version of this review. Independent replication of the RFT1-CDG phenotype and rescue across three additional patients and two novel alleles.

title: Glycoprotein biosynthesis in a eukaryote lacking the membrane protein Rft1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The strongest in-vivo argument against the obligate-flippase model - an entire eukaryote lives, flips M5-DLO and N-glycosylates without Rft1. Also the origin of the chaperone hypothesis.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Correctly cited for the HuRI Y2H interactions, but it is a systematic screen with no RFT1-specific follow-up; it supports only the uninformative GO:0005515 term, which this review removes.

title: Rft1 catalyzes lipid-linked oligosaccharide translocation across the ER membrane.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text checked. Importantly for the human annotation, recombinant human RFT1 was assayed alongside the yeast and archaeal proteins, so the human IDA is not a cross-species transfer. The title states the strongest reading; the data establish the in-vitro activity, and later work (PMID:42417535) accepts the activity while contesting that it is the essential cellular role.

title: Molecular characterization of Rft1, an ER membrane protein associated with congenital disorder of glycosylation RFT1-CDG.
review_notes: PubMed-verified peer-reviewed JBC version (the bioRxiv preprint is PMID:38617304). Published after PMID:38886340 and still treating the essential role as unknown, which is the clearest evidence that the controversy was not closed by the reconstitution paper. Also the source of direct human topology and localization data.

title: Mechanism-guided mutagenesis of Rft1 to test its role as a dolichol-linked oligosaccharide scramblase in cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the most recent primary evidence on this question and decisive for how the molecular function should be curated. It concedes the reconstituted scramblase activity but shows that a portal-blocking mutant predicted to lack that activity still supports growth, separating the biochemical capacity from the essential in-vivo role.

title: Defective RFT1 does not flip the N-glycan precursor
review_notes: The reaction name asserts the canonical flippase model as settled. That model is contested in the primary literature (PMID:19494107, PMID:23720757, PMID:42417535), so the two GOA rows sourced from it should not be read as independent confirmation of the mechanism.

title: RFT1 side-chain orientation - resolving a conflict between two structural analyses
review_notes: Local reproducible check written to settle a direct contradiction between the two OpenScientist runs over whether E298 faces the central axis or the lipid. Recomputes the membrane normal from helix geometry and tests the sign of each side-chain orientation under 24 perturbed axes.

title: Cyberian deep research on RFT1 function
review_notes: Machine-generated. Explicitly frames the controversy as resolved in 2024 ("This controversy persisted for over two decades until 2024"), which the 2026 primary literature contradicts.

title: Deep research on RFT1 function (falcon)
review_notes: Machine-generated. Useful on topology and general background, but it presents the flippase question as closed by the 2024 reconstitution and does not surface PMID:19494107, PMID:23720757 or PMID:42417535. Do not rely on it for the molecular function call.

title: OpenScientist family-constraint analysis - is the substrate cavity or the lipid portal the conserved surface of the RFT1 fold?
review_notes: Second independent computational run, framed on wild-type family constraint with disease variants excluded as both input and selection criterion. Unlike the first run this one performed real statistics - a 3,826-sequence Pfam PF04506 alignment, Henikoff-weighted Kullback-Leibler constraint per column, geometric classification against the AlphaFold model with stated criteria, and four controls (second metric, composition, 20,000-draw permutation null, membrane-axis perturbation), plus axis-independent continuous correlations. The Pfam family identity and its eukaryote-only taxonomic spread were checked against InterPro. One caveat the run does not draw itself is recorded in the gene notes - lipid-facing transmembrane residues are the fastest-evolving class in essentially every membrane protein, which the run confirms as its own frame sanity check, so low constraint at portal-lining positions has limited power to show the portal is non-functional. Its numbers live only in the report prose - unlike the first run it emitted no data artifacts, and no citations file was written.

title: OpenScientist structural analysis - do RFT1-CDG residues line the substrate cavity or the lipid portal?
review_notes: Independent computational run commissioned for this review, deliberately framed with both mechanistic models stated symmetrically rather than reusing this review's rationale. Its literature citations were spot-checked and resolve correctly, including PMID:19267216. Its central negative result - that residue mapping cannot discriminate the two models because headgroup binding is required under both - is a correction to the premise the run was given, and is recorded here rather than being quietly dropped. One secondary claim is wrong and was not imported - it flags human Q9NWF4 and mouse Q9D8F3 as divergent RFT1 paralogs at risk of annotation transfer, but those are SLC52A1/Slc52a2 riboflavin transporters that merely carry RFT1 as a legacy gene symbol; the transfer hazard is real but is nomenclature, not paralogy. No local bioinformatics holdout existed for this gene, so nothing was leaked into the prompt. Superseded in one respect - its classification of E298 as exposed and outward-facing is not reproducible and is contradicted both by the family-constraint run and by the local check in RFT1-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md. That E298 call has therefore been withdrawn from the findings list below rather than carried forward as a structured assertion; the retraction is recorded here and in RFT1-notes.md.

title: Analysis of the human E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H map of E2 conjugating enzymes; supports an RFWD3-UBE2N (UBC13) interaction consistent with RFWD3 using K63-forming E2 machinery, but is a systematic interaction screen, not a functional study of RFWD3.

title: RFWD3-Mdm2 ubiquitin ligase complex positively regulates p53 stability in response to DNA damage.
review_notes: Establishes the secondary RFWD3-MDM2-p53 axis; RFWD3 forms a complex with MDM2 and p53, synergistically ubiquitinates p53, and stabilizes it late after IR in an ATM/ATR-phosphorylation-dependent manner. Single-group work; abstract-only in cache.

title: E3 ligase RFWD3 participates in replication checkpoint control.
review_notes: Identifies RFWD3 as a direct RPA2-interacting protein recruited to stalled forks and required for ATR-dependent CHK1 activation. Full text available; verified.

title: RING finger and WD repeat domain 3 (RFWD3) associates with replication protein A (RPA) and facilitates RPA-mediated DNA damage response.
review_notes: Companion study confirming RFWD3-RPA association, S-G2 up-regulation, partial PML-body localization, and a role in the RPA-mediated DNA damage response.

title: hPrimpol1/CCDC111 is a human DNA primase-polymerase required for the maintenance of genome integrity.
review_notes: Primarily a PRIMPOL study; the RFWD3 annotation derives from a detected RFWD3-RPA2 (P15927) interaction, contextual rather than an RFWD3 functional characterization.

title: The MEKK1 PHD ubiquitinates TAB1 to activate MAPKs in response to cytokines.
review_notes: MEKK1/TAB1 study; RFWD3 annotation derives from a detected RFWD3-UBE2N (P61088) interaction, not an RFWD3-focused experiment.

title: RFWD3-Dependent Ubiquitination of RPA Regulates Repair at Stalled Replication Forks.
review_notes: Landmark paper: RFWD3 mediates RPA ubiquitination (non-degradative), required for fork restart and HR at stalled forks. Full text verified.

title: RPA-Mediated Recruitment of the E3 Ligase RFWD3 Is Vital for Interstrand Crosslink Repair and Human Health.
review_notes: Demonstrates that WD40-mediated RPA binding recruits RFWD3 to ICLs and that the FA patient I639K mutation abolishes this; ICL repair is a major RFWD3 function. Full text verified.

title: RFWD3-Mediated Ubiquitination Promotes Timely Removal of Both RPA and RAD51 from DNA Damage Sites to Facilitate Homologous Recombination.
review_notes: Identifies RAD51 as a second RFWD3 substrate; RFWD3 polyubiquitinates RPA and RAD51 (ATR/ATM-phosphorylation-dependent) driving VCP/p97-mediated removal to enable late-phase HR. Abstract-only in cache but definitive for the core function.

title: Biallelic mutations in the ubiquitin ligase RFWD3 cause Fanconi anemia.
review_notes: Defines RFWD3 as Fanconi anemia gene FANCW via a patient with biallelic mutations; HR disrupted by impaired chromatin relocation and defective RPA interaction; supported by a knockout mouse. Full text verified.

title: PCNA-mediated stabilization of E3 ligase RFWD3 at the replication fork is essential for DNA replication.
review_notes: RFWD3-focused functional study (full text available). Shows that in unperturbed cells RFWD3 localizes at replication forks and binds PCNA via a PIP motif; this association stabilizes RFWD3 and supports normal fork progression / DNA replication, with reduced RPA ubiquitination in RFWD3-null cells. Corroborates the replication-fork-processing role and adds an unperturbed-fork context beyond the stalled-fork core function.

title: The ubiquitin ligase RFWD3 is required for translesion DNA synthesis.
review_notes: Shows RFWD3 promotes ubiquitylation of proteins on ssDNA, required for PCNA ubiquitylation and translesion synthesis across diverse lesions.

title: RFWD3 promotes ZRANB3 recruitment to regulate the remodeling of stalled replication forks.
review_notes: RFWD3-focused functional study (full text available). RFWD3 promotes recruitment of the DNA translocase ZRANB3 to stalled forks and stimulates fork remodeling (reversal) in a ZRANB3-epistatic manner, via RFWD3-dependent PCNA ubiquitination. Corroborates and mechanistically extends the replication-fork-processing role.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Systems-level multimodal interaction/localization mapping; the RFWD3 annotation is a detected RFWD3-RPA2 (P15927) interaction, contextual not functional.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput yeast two-hybrid interactome screen (CCSB-HI1). Source of the bare GO:0005515 protein-binding IPI (interactor KIFBP/Q96EK5, matching the UniProt INTERACTION section). Abstract-only cache; no RGR-specific interaction detail beyond the interactome dataset. Uninformative for RGR's molecular function.

title: Retinal pigment epithelium-retinal G protein receptor-opsin mediates light-dependent translocation of all-trans-retinyl esters for synthesis of visual chromophore in retinal pigment epithelial cells.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP high-throughput mitochondrial proteome; RPIA is an HTP hit only. Given the cytosolic localisation and absence of a transit peptide, the mitochondrial signal likely reflects co-purification rather than a genuine mitochondrial pool.

title: The ribose 5-phosphate isomerase-encoding gene is located immediately downstream from that encoding murine immunoglobulin kappa.
review_notes: Cloned the mouse/human RPI gene and showed a recombinant GST-RPI fusion is enzymatically active; basis for the NAS molecular-function annotation.

title: UniProtKB entry P49247 (RPIA_HUMAN)
review_notes: Swiss-Prot record; establishes EC 5.3.1.6, the RHEA:14657 reaction, the non-oxidative PPP pathway step, cytosolic family membership, and RPIA deficiency (MIM:608611).

title: Characterization and analysis of posttranslational modifications of the human large cytoplasmic ribosomal subunit proteins by mass spectrometry and Edman sequencing.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The study characterizes post-translational modifications of human large-subunit proteins and supports composition by inference; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The mRNA interactome supports association with polyadenylated-RNA-containing complexes but not a separable RPL36A RNA-binding mechanism; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Structures of the human and Drosophila 80S ribosome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. Human 80S cryo-EM directly supports cytosolic ribosome and large-subunit membership; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Host factors that interact with the pestivirus N-terminal protease, Npro, are components of the ribonucleoprotein complex.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. RPL36A is one of many ribosomal proteins recovered in the viral Npro pulldown, and the authors explicitly allow indirect complex capture.

title: Structure of the human 80S ribosome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The human 80S structure supports cytoplasmic ribosome membership and translation; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Structural snapshots of actively translating human ribosomes.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. Cryo-EM structures of actively translating human ribosomes support large-subunit membership and cytoplasmic translation.

title: Expression of Muscle-Specific Ribosomal Protein L3-Like Impairs Myotube Growth.
review_notes: PubMed identity and full text were verified. The experiments perturb RPL3L in mouse myoblasts and never assay RPL36A; the paper does not support assigning the RPL3L fusion phenotype to RPL36A.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. HuRI is a systematic binary-interaction resource; its RPL36A record is retained as interaction data but not an informative molecular function.

title: Structural snapshots of human pre-60S ribosomal particles before and after nuclear export.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were verified. Human pre-60S structures support eL42 incorporation into the large ribosomal subunit.

title: Knockdown of Muscle-Specific Ribosomal Protein L3-Like Enhances Muscle Function in Healthy and Dystrophic Mice.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. This mouse study knocks down Rpl3l and does not assay RPL36A, so it cannot support an RPL36A striated-muscle-contraction annotation.

title: Characterisation of an mRNA encoding a human ribosomal protein homologous to the yeast L44 ribosomal protein.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were verified. The early cloned cDNA establishes the human L44/eL42 homolog but is weaker than current structural evidence; locally cached content is abstract-only.

title: Manual deep-research synthesis for human RPL36A
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the complete GOA set, reviewed UniProt, cached structural and interaction papers, and the RPL3L citation mismatch.

title: Manual RPL36A curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored decision log with provider failures, action rationale, citation boundaries, and experimental priorities.

title: UniProtKB record for human RPL36A (P83881)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project; used for identity, family, length, cytoplasmic localization, and experimentally supported large-subunit membership.

title: Functional second genes generated by retrotransposition of the X-linked ribosomal protein genes.
review_notes: PMID and title were verified against the cached record, and the open article was manually inspected. This study distinguishes RPL36AL from X-linked RPL36A at the gene and expression levels; it does not directly demonstrate incorporation of the encoded protein into ribosomes.

title: Lys53 of ribosomal protein L36AL and the CCA end of a tRNA at the P/E hybrid site are in close proximity on the human ribosome.
review_notes: PMID, title, and abstract were verified. The paper explicitly names RPL36AL and maps a ribosome-bound tRNA contact to Lys53, providing direct support for ribosomal tRNA binding; only the abstract is cached.

title: The CCA-end of P-tRNA Contacts Both the Human RPL36AL and the A-site Bound Translation Termination Factor eRF1 at the Peptidyl Transferase Center of the Human 80S Ribosome.
review_notes: PMID, title, methods, results, and discussion were verified in the cached full text. The recombinant construct is explicitly RPL36AL, making the tRNA-binding result paralog-specific. Claims of an independent peptidyl-tRNA-hydrolase activity were not converted into GO annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: PMID, title, and full text were verified. The GOA row records a high-throughput RPL36AL-KRTAP10-7 binary interaction, but the study does not define a ribosomal or partner-specific molecular activity for RPL36AL.

title: E-cadherin interactome complexity and robustness resolved by quantitative proteomics.
review_notes: PMID, title, full narrative, and localization methodology were verified. The RPL36AL-specific nuclear call is not stated in the narrative and resides in a supplementary candidate table that was not accessible, so the citation is not fully adjudicated for this gene.

title: Functional involvement of a conserved motif in the middle region of the human ribosomal protein eL42 in translation.
review_notes: PMID, title, and abstract were verified. The abstract calls the construct human eL42 but does not provide an accession or distinguish the single-residue RPL36A/RPL36AL paralogs, so this family-level result was not used to create a paralog-specific elongation annotation.

title: Manual deep research synthesis for human RPL36AL
review_notes: Reviewer-authored synthesis of the fetched records, cached publications, open primary literature, current QuickGO term record, and explicit RPL36A sequence comparison.

title: Manual RPL36AL curation notes
review_notes: Reviewer-authored decision log with inline provenance and explicit exclusion of unsupported RPL36A transfers.

title: UniProtKB record for human RPL36AL (Q969Q0)
review_notes: Reviewed UniProt record fetched by the project and used for accession, sequence, family, modification, expression, complex, and localization metadata. Its RPL36AL sequence differs from RPL36A at residue 38 only.

title: Proteomic analysis of early melanosomes: identification of novel melanosomal proteins.
review_notes: Correctly cited proteomics of melanosome fractions; supports the melanosome CC annotation but as an ER-contaminant co-purification rather than a genuine RPN1 functional site.

title: Proteomic analysis of mammalian oligosaccharyltransferase reveals multiple subcomplexes that contain Sec61, TRAP, and two potential new subunits.
review_notes: Biochemical proteomics of mammalian OST; explicitly lists ribophorin I as an OST subunit. Basis of the contributes_to GO:0004579 TAS annotation.

title: Proteomic and bioinformatic characterization of the biogenesis and function of melanosomes.
review_notes: Correctly cited melanosome proteomics; supports the melanosome CC as a co-purified ER protein, not a core localization.

title: Ribophorin I acts as a substrate-specific facilitator of N-glycosylation.
review_notes: Directly about RPN1 function; establishes the substrate-specific facilitator model. Supports the IMP for protein N-linked glycosylation and the facilitator core function.

title: Cotranslational and posttranslational N-glycosylation of polypeptides by distinct mammalian OST isoforms.
review_notes: Full text assays ribophorin I directly; supports OST membership and interaction with STT3A/ STT3B. Basis of the STT3B IPI annotation.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: Correctly cited high-throughput RBP atlas, but the RNA-binding assignment is a screen-level call without a defined molecular function for RPN1; treated as an over-annotation.

title: Malectin forms a complex with ribophorin I for enhanced association with misfolded glycoproteins.
review_notes: Directly about the RPN1-malectin complex; supports a glycoprotein quality-control adapter role. Basis of the MLEC IPI annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
TMEM258 Is a Component of the Oligosaccharyltransferase Complex Controlling ER Stress and Intestinal Inflammation.
Histone Interaction Landscapes Visualized by Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry in Intact Cell Nuclei.
Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
Cryo-electron microscopy structures of human oligosaccharyltransferase complexes OST-A and OST-B.
review_notes: Structural basis for RPN1 membership in both OST complexes and its cotranslational substrate-presentation role. Supports GO:0160226/GO:0160227 IDAs.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
Visualization of translation and protein biogenesis at the ER membrane.
Positive selection CRISPR screens reveal a druggable pocket in an oligosaccharyltransferase required for inflammatory signaling to NF-κB.
Interleukin-2 induces N-glycosylation in T-cells: characterization of human lymphocyte oligosaccharyltransferase.
review_notes: Biochemical purification directly identifying ribophorin I in the human OST enzyme. Supports the IDA for OST complex membership and N-linked glycosylation.

title: Retention of subunits of the oligosaccharyltransferase complex in the endoplasmic reticulum.
review_notes: Identifies ER-retention determinants in ribophorin I, ribophorin II (RII) and OST48; confirms RII is an OST subunit and an ER membrane protein. Used by GOA only for the broad "protein modification process" TAS annotation, which understates the specific role.

title: Proteomic analysis of mammalian oligosaccharyltransferase reveals multiple subcomplexes that contain Sec61, TRAP, and two potential new subunits.
review_notes: Proteomic dissection of mammalian OST subcomplexes; supports RPN2 as a component of the OST enzyme and its contribution to the complex-level glycotransferase activity.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput NK-cell membrane proteome; RPN2 detected as a membrane protein. Only supports the generic "membrane" localization, not a specific function.

title: Host factors that interact with the pestivirus N-terminal protease, Npro, are components of the ribonucleoprotein complex.
review_notes: Pestivirus Npro interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI annotation. Interaction is in an infection context and does not define RPN2's endogenous molecular function.

title: Armc5 deletion causes developmental defects and compromises T-cell immune responses.
review_notes: ARMC5 knockout / T-cell study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (RPN2-ARMC5). Does not inform RPN2's core molecular function.

title: Removal of RTF2 from Stalled Replisomes Promotes Maintenance of Genome Integrity.
review_notes: Replisome/genome-integrity study; source of the RPN2-DDI2 protein-binding IPI, also recorded in UniProt as "Interacts with DDI2". Interaction is real but does not define RPN2's molecular function.

title: Cryo-electron microscopy structures of human oligosaccharyltransferase complexes OST-A and OST-B.
review_notes: Definitive structural characterization of both human OST complexes; establishes RPN2 as a core subunit of OST-A and OST-B and its role in N-linked glycosylation. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false).

title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
review_notes: High-throughput kinase interaction network; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (RPN2-POMK). Does not inform RPN2's core molecular function.

title: Visualization of translation and protein biogenesis at the ER membrane.
review_notes: Cryo-ET of the native ER translocon; resolves the SEC61-OSTA-TRAP translocon (with RPN2 in OSTA) as the most abundant translocon and confirms OST-A's co-translational N-glycosylation role.

title: Positive selection CRISPR screens reveal a druggable pocket in an oligosaccharyltransferase required for inflammatory signaling to NF-κB.
review_notes: CRISPR/cryo-EM study of the STT3A-containing OST-A complex; supports RPN2 as an OST-A subunit and OST-A's role in N-glycosylation of TLR4. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Interleukin-2 induces N-glycosylation in T-cells: characterization of human lymphocyte oligosaccharyltransferase.
review_notes: Biochemical purification of human lymphocyte OST; N-terminal sequencing identified ribophorin I and ribophorin II as OST components. Direct experimental support for OST membership and N-glycosylation involvement. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Annexin II light chain regulates sensory neuron-specific sodium channel expression.
review_notes: Abstract-only; p11 binds NaV1.8 N-terminus and promotes functional surface expression.

title: p11, an annexin II subunit, an auxiliary protein associated with the background K+ channel, TASK-1.
review_notes: Abstract-only; p11 binds TASK-1 C-terminus and is essential for its surface trafficking.

title: Functional expression of the epithelial Ca(2+) channels (TRPV5 and TRPV6) requires association of the S100A10-annexin 2 complex.
review_notes: Abstract-only; S100A10-annexin 2 required for TRPV5/TRPV6 routing to plasma membrane.

title: Alterations in 5-HT1B receptor function by p11 in depression-like states.
review_notes: Abstract-only; p11 binds 5-HT1B receptor and increases its surface localization; KO depression-like phenotype.

title: Regulation of fibrinolysis by S100A10 in vivo.
review_notes: Abstract-only; S100A10-null mice show impaired fibrinolysis.

title: Structure of an asymmetric ternary protein complex provides insight for membrane interaction.
review_notes: Abstract-only; structural basis of AHNAK recruitment; does not address exocytosis directly.

title: S100A10 is required for the organization of actin stress fibers and promotion of cell spreading.
review_notes: Abstract-only; single siRNA study of indirect actin/spreading phenotypes.

title: Lipid segregation and membrane budding induced by the peripheral membrane binding protein annexin A2.
review_notes: Abstract-only; activity described is ANXA2's; S100A10 dispensable for lipid clustering/budding.

title: A novel Munc13-4/S100A10/annexin A2 complex promotes Weibel-Palade body exocytosis in endothelial cells.
review_notes: Identified via falcon deep research; abstract confirms S100A10-Munc13-4 interaction and role in WPB exocytosis.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI high-throughput Y2H; source of generic protein binding rows.

title: Interactions between the Cell Membrane Repair Protein S100A10 and Phospholipid Monolayers and Bilayers.
review_notes: Model-membrane study reporting weak direct S100A10-lipid interactions; contrasts with NOT lipid binding (PMID:23861394).

title: The p11 subunit of the annexin II tetramer plays a key role in the stimulation of t-PA-dependent plasminogen activation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; direct biochemical evidence that p11 C-terminal lysines bind plasminogen and stimulate t-PA activation.

title: The crystal structure of a complex of p11 with the annexin II N-terminal peptide.
review_notes: Abstract-only; crystal structures of p11 dimer and p11-ANXA2 peptide complex; loss of Ca2+ binding.

title: Sphingomyelin synthase related protein is a mammalian phosphatidylethanolamine phospholipase C.
review_notes: Full primary read. Recombinant human cDNA expressed in Sf9 supports PE-PLC/CPE activity and condition-specific negative SMS/PC/PA assays; mouse liver work establishes in-vivo PE/DAG effects. Broader specificity differs from PMID:33621517; the PI comparison is limited by spontaneous TopFluor-PI hydrolysis.

title: Sphingomyelin Synthase Family and Phospholipase Cs.
review_notes: Secondary review supports PE-PLC physiology, but its universal PE-only and absent-in-vivo-ceramide-regulation framing requires qualification by conflicting human PMID:33621517 and conditional mouse PMID:40998032 results.

title: Cryo-EM structure of human sphingomyelin synthase and its mechanistic implications for sphingomyelin synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed abstract and primary structural accession confirm human SMSr PE-hydrolysis/CPE-transfer mechanism. Full Results and mutant/wild-type activity panels remain inaccessible, so no universal residual-SMS exclusion is inferred.

title: Sphingomyelin synthase-related protein is a regulator of serine palmitoyltransferase.
review_notes: Full primary methods, results and figure captions read. Human liver/adipose findings are observational expression analyses; mouse overexpression, high-fat-diet knockout, PE intervention, liver microsomal SPT assay and tagged co-IP support a conditional regulatory mechanism. Co-IP is not direct binary binding; exact PE-to-SPT mechanism remains unresolved. Low/undetectable CPE does not revoke independently demonstrated human CPE catalytic capacity.

title: Falcon (Edison) deep research on SAMD8/SMSr function
review_notes: Useful PLC/ER/DGK synthesis critically reused. Dominant PE-PLC physiology remains tissue- and condition-dependent; it does not invalidate measured CPE transfer or broad human substrate assays.

title: Deep research on SAMD8 function
review_notes: Useful synthesis, but universal PE-only/predominant-in-vivo activity, exclusive ER residency and universal apoptosis dependence are too strong. Primary PMID:33621517 shows broader human hydrolysis; PMID:28120887 shows a minor wild-type Golgi pool and viable stable knockout cells.

title: OpenScientist focused SAMD8 reaction-spectrum, pathway and compartment report
review_notes: Report body and all three artifacts read. Supports PE-dependent CPE, ER residence and broad hydrolase capacity, but GO:0002950 and GO:0047493 recommendations conflate donor chemistry; wild-type Golgi is misread as mutant-only; pairwise identity is not PAINT topology; physiological negatives omit the conditional 2025 SPT evidence. Explicitly could not retrieve 34332077/38388831. No alignment script or sequence output accompanies its percentage table.

title: Identification of endothelial cell genes expressed in an in vitro model of angiogenesis: induction of ESM-1, (beta)ig-h3, and NrCAM.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. SAT1 is a co-identified transcript upregulated in an in-vitro angiogenesis model; the paper foregrounds ESM-1/betaig-h3/NrCAM and does not establish a causal enzymatic role for SAT1 in angiogenesis. Supports only a context-specific expression association (IEP), not a core function.

title: Spermidine/spermine-N1-acetyltransferase-2 (SSAT2) acetylates thialysine and is not involved in polyamine metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Primary subject is the paralog SSAT2 (SAT2), which the paper concludes is NOT a polyamine catabolic enzyme; SSAT1 (this gene, P21673) is used throughout as the well-characterized reference standard and its polyamine KM/kcat are reported. UniProt cites this PMID as EXP evidence for SAT1 catalytic activity, so the GOA IDA to SAT1 diamine N-acetyltransferase activity is appropriate. The IDA to polyamine biosynthetic process is wrong-direction (SSAT1 is catabolic).

title: A human protein-protein interaction network: a resource for annotating the proteome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome dataset; supports only a bare, uninformative protein-binding annotation.

title: Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein interaction network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale Y2H interactome (CCSB-HI1). Supports uninformative bare protein-binding hits; its SAT1 self-hit is consistent with the validated homodimer (identical protein binding).

title: Structures of wild-type and mutant human spermidine/spermine N1-acetyltransferase, a potential therapeutic drug target.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. High-resolution crystal structures of human SSAT with CoA, acetyl-CoA, spermine and inhibitor; establishes the catalytic MF, the homodimer, the Y140 catalytic residue, and the role in polyamine level control and export.

title: Mechanistic and structural analysis of human spermidine/spermine N1-acetyltransferase.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Definitive kinetic and mechanistic characterization of human SSAT1 (random sequential mechanism, ternary complex, Tyr140/Glu92 catalytic residues); directly supports the core diamine N-acetyltransferase activity.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome study; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Isolation and characterization of a cDNA clone that codes for human spermidine/spermine N1-acetyltransferase.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Original cloning/characterization of the human SSAT1 cDNA; establishes the encoded protein as an active enzyme and the rate-limiting enzyme of polyamine catabolism. Basis of the TAS diamine N-acetyltransferase annotation.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome dataset; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome map. Supports uninformative bare protein-binding hits; the SAT1 self-hit is consistent with the validated homodimer.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-perturbation screen; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Variant-interactome study; supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Reference binary interactome map (HuRI) with a large heterogeneous partner list; supports only bare protein-binding annotations.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration interactome study (partner APP); supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cell-specific proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex); supports only a bare protein-binding annotation.

title: Interconversion of polyamines
review_notes: Reactome pathway describing polyamine back-conversion via SAT1-mediated N1-acetylation followed by PAOX/SMOX oxidation. The pathway is catabolic/interconversion; the GOA mapping of this reference to polyamine biosynthetic process is a wrong-direction term.

title: Spermine => N-acetylated spermine
review_notes: Reactome reaction; SAT1 acetylates spermine to N-acetylspermine, the rate-limiting step of polyamine catabolism. Supports the core MF and cytosol location.

title: Spermidine => N-acetylated spermidine
review_notes: Reactome reaction; SAT1 acetylates spermidine to N-acetylspermidine, the rate-limiting step of polyamine catabolism. Supports the core MF and cytosol location.

title: cDNA cloning of the mammalian sterol C5-desaturase and the expression in yeast mutant.
review_notes: Cloning and yeast-complementation study establishing SC5D catalytic activity and ER-membrane localization; source of the UniProt RecName, EC number, and subcellular location. Abstract-only in cache but claims confirmed against the UniProt record.

title: Lathosterolosis, a novel multiple-malformation/mental retardation syndrome due to deficiency of 3beta-hydroxysteroid-delta5-desaturase.
review_notes: First human lathosterolosis patient (R29Q, G211D); documents block in lathosterol to 7-DHC conversion and deficient SC5D activity.

title: Lathosterolosis: an inborn error of human and murine cholesterol synthesis due to lathosterol 5-desaturase deficiency.
review_notes: Sc5d-null mouse and human Y46S patient; states SC5D catalyzes the next-to-last step of cholesterol synthesis; elevated lathosterol / reduced cholesterol on loss.

title: 7-Dehydrocholesterol is an endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis.
review_notes: Nature study characterizing SC5D function/catalytic activity/pathway and the anti-ferroptotic role of its product 7-DHC. Abstract-only in cache; the ferroptosis role is indirect (via 7-DHC), hence treated as non-core.

title: 7-Dehydrocholesterol dictates ferroptosis sensitivity.
review_notes: Full text available; genome-wide CRISPR screen shows SC5D is an anti-ferroptotic distal-cholesterol-biosynthesis gene whose product 7-DHC suppresses ferroptosis. Supports GO:0110076 as a non-core role.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis run: SCGB1C1 ligand specificity
review_notes: Directly inspected; refutes odorant-binding annotation without direct purified-SCGB1C1 ligand assays and preserves the remaining immunomodulatory mechanism gap.

title: Electrophysiological properties of mutant Nav1.7 sodium channels in a painful inherited neuropathy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports plasma-membrane localization and gain-of-function mechanism in inherited erythromelalgia.

title: SCN9A mutations in paroxysmal extreme pain disorder: allelic variants underlie distinct channel defects and phenotypes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract; establishes Nav1.7 channel activity and pain-perception role via PEPD gain-of-function mutations.

title: An SCN9A channelopathy causes congenital inability to experience pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; decisive loss-of-function human genetics for the core pain-perception role.

title: Early- and late-onset inherited erythromelalgia: genotype-phenotype correlation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract-only; supports plasma-membrane localization via EXP annotation.

title: Inherited pain: sodium channel Nav1.7 A1632T mutation causes erythromelalgia due to a shift of fast inactivation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports plasma-membrane localization and gain-of-function mechanism.

title: Protein kinase C enhances human sodium channel hNav1.7 resurgent currents via a serine residue in the domain III-IV linker.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports plasma-membrane localization and post-translational regulation of channel activity.

title: Structural basis of Nav1.7 inhibition by an isoform-selective small-molecule antagonist.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract-only; supports plasma-membrane localization and channel pharmacology.

title: Structures of human Na(v)1.7 channel in complex with auxiliary subunits and animal toxins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; structural basis for VGSC complex membership and membrane-depolarization function.

title: Defining the Functional Role of Na(V)1.7 in Human Nociception.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; primary human evidence for neuronal action potential, pain perception, and subcellular localization (node of Ranvier, axon terminus).

title: Pain-causing stinging nettle toxins target TMEM233 to modulate Na(V)1.7 function.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available; underlying interaction (TMEM233) is real but the generic protein binding term is uninformative.

title: Structure and functional expression of a new member of the tetrodotoxin-sensitive voltage-activated sodium channel family from human neuroendocrine cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract-only; founding functional study establishing channel activity, plasma-membrane localization, and absence from heart.

title: Falcon deep research report for human SCN9A
review_notes: LLM-generated literature synthesis (Edison/falcon); used only as corroborating context. Its core-function, localization, and TMEM233-accessory claims are consistent with the primary literature and UniProt cited elsewhere in this review; the NEDD4L/trafficking point is supported by UniProt's curated SUBUNIT annotation (interaction with NEDD4/NEDD4L).

title: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation disorders and 58 kDa sterol carrier protein X (SCPx). Activity measurements in liver and fibroblasts using a newly developed method.
review_notes: Abstract-only; establishes SCPx's role in branched-chain fatty acid oxidation and the specific bile-acid thiolase assay. PubMed-verified.

title: Identification of the peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of docosahexaenoic acid.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports SCPx participation in peroxisomal beta-oxidation during DHA synthesis (ALA metabolism annotation). PubMed-verified.

title: Subcellular localisation and processing of non-specific lipid transfer protein are not aberrant in Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata fibroblasts.
review_notes: Abstract-only; direct evidence for peroxisomal localization and precursor processing of nsLTP/SCP2. PubMed-verified.

title: Sterol carrier protein-2 directly interacts with caveolin-1 in vitro and in vivo.
review_notes: Abstract-only; supports cholesterol/PI binding and the caveolin-1 interaction (basis of two IPI protein binding annotations). PubMed-verified.

title: Sterol carrier protein-2-facilitated intermembrane transfer of cholesterol- and phospholipid-derived hydroperoxides.
review_notes: Abstract-only; primary support for the sterol/phospholipid transfer activity and the lipid-hydroperoxide-transport / cholesterol-transport-regulation annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Mutations in the gene encoding peroxisomal sterol carrier protein X (SCPx) cause leukencephalopathy with dystonia and motor neuropathy.
review_notes: Full text (abstract identical) available; disease-defining loss-of-function evidence for the SCPx thiolase and the LKDMN phenotype. PubMed-verified.

title: Recognition of a functional peroxisome type 1 target by the dynamic import receptor pex5p.
review_notes: Full text available; source of the two-product bifunctional gene model and the PEX5/PTS1 import mechanism; supports cytoplasm/mitochondrion localization annotations. PubMed-verified.

title: Investigation of the ligand spectrum of human sterol carrier protein 2 using a direct mass spectrometry assay.
review_notes: Abstract-only; direct support for long-chain fatty-acyl-CoA binding (IDA). PubMed-verified.

title: Structure and function of the sterol carrier protein-2 N-terminal presequence.
review_notes: Abstract-only; basis for cholesterol binding, fatty-acyl-CoA binding and oleic acid binding IDAs, and for the mitochondrial/peroxisomal targeting behavior. PubMed-verified.

title: Solution structure of human Pex5.Pex14.PTS1 protein complexes obtained by small angle X-ray scattering.
review_notes: Full text available; basis of the protein-containing-complex (IDA) and a PEX5 protein-binding (IPI) annotation; the interaction is import-machinery cargo loading, not a core functional complex. PubMed-verified.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only; high-throughput proteomics source of the generic membrane (HDA) annotation; not specific to SCP2 function. PubMed-verified.

title: The Peroxisomal Targeting Signal 1 in sterol carrier protein 2 is autonomous and essential for receptor recognition.
review_notes: Full text available; direct peroxisomal-import evidence (IDA peroxisome) and the PEX5 interaction annotated as signaling receptor binding (mischaracterized MF). PubMed-verified.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.

title: Cerberus is a feedback inhibitor of Nodal asymmetric signaling in the chick embryo.
