title: Hhat is a palmitoylacyltransferase with specificity for N-palmitoylation of Sonic Hedgehog.
review_notes: Abstract directly establishes HHAT-mediated SHH N-palmitoylation during secretory-pathway transit.

title: The structure of SHH in complex with HHIP reveals a recognition role for the Shh pseudo active site in signaling.
review_notes: Abstract and structure directly establish the human SHH-HHIP complex and zinc-coordinating interface.

title: A new role for Hedgehogs in juxtacrine signaling.
review_notes: Full text directly analyzes human SHH precursor processing, secretion, and signaling and describes its autoprocessing/cholesterol-transfer domain.

title: Wnt signaling in midbrain dopaminergic neuron development and regenerative medicine for Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: The cached abstract is a Wnt-focused review and does not expose the basis for the SHH-specific dopaminergic annotations; full text is unavailable.

title: Proteomic characterization of human multiple myeloma bone marrow extracellular matrix.
review_notes: The cached abstract describes a multiple-myeloma ECM proteome but does not enumerate SHH; full text is unavailable, so the SHH ECM localization cannot be checked.

title: Structural basis for the recognition of Sonic Hedgehog by human Patched1.
review_notes: Abstract directly reports the human PTCH1-SHH-N structure and structure-guided interaction assays.

title: Structures of human Patched and its complex with native palmitoylated sonic hedgehog.
review_notes: Full text directly reports native dually lipidated human SHH-N bound to human PTCH1 and associated signaling assays.

title: Two Patched molecules engage distinct sites on Hedgehog yielding a signaling-competent complex.
review_notes: Full text directly resolves two PTCH1 molecules engaging SHH-N and tests the signaling contribution of both interfaces.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/IBA pipeline; correctly recovers the core SHMT function (glycine hydroxymethyltransferase activity, PLP binding, glycine/serine/THF metabolism) but also propagates a spurious "mitochondrion" localization from mitochondrial SHMT orthologs onto the cytosolic isozyme.

title: Human cytoplasmic serine hydroxymethyltransferase is an mRNA binding protein.
review_notes: Establishes SHMT1's moonlighting RNA-binding role: it binds its own 5'-UTR and represses translation. Supports GO:0048027, GO:0000900, GO:0017148 (all non-core moonlighting).

title: Heavy chain ferritin enhances serine hydroxymethyltransferase expression and de novo thymidine biosynthesis.
review_notes: Links cSHMT expression to folate-dependent de novo thymidylate synthesis; supports the folic acid metabolic process annotation.

title: The role of serine hydroxymethyltransferase isozymes in one-carbon metabolism in MCF-7 cells as determined by (13)C NMR.
review_notes: 13C-NMR flux study; notably concludes cytosolic SHMT is NOT a major one-carbon source for purine/thymidylate in MCF-7, arguing the GO:0009113 purine-biosynthesis annotation is an over-annotation.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis in mammals.
review_notes: Review of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis; Reactome uses it as source for the broad aldehyde-lyase (HTMLA-step) activity annotation. Background/pathway context.

title: Evidence for small ubiquitin-like modifier-dependent nuclear import of the thymidylate biosynthesis pathway.
review_notes: Shows SUMO-dependent, cell-cycle-restricted (S/G2-M) nuclear import of cSHMT; supports the non-core nuclear localization.

title: Effect of vitamin B6 availability on serine hydroxymethyltransferase in MCF-7 cells.
review_notes: Characterizes PLP dependence (Kd=850 nM) and cytosolic localization of cSHMT; supports core PLP-binding, cytosol, and SHMT activity annotations.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput urinary exosome proteome; source of the extracellular exosome (over-annotation) call.

title: Serine hydroxymethyltransferase anchors de novo thymidylate synthesis pathway to nuclear lamina for DNA synthesis.
review_notes: Key paper for the nuclear scaffold/lamin-binding role: SHMT1 is essential for assembling the DHFR-SHMT-TYMS de novo thymidylate complex at the nuclear lamina/replication forks.

title: In-depth proteomic analyses of exosomes isolated from expressed prostatic secretions in urine.
review_notes: High-throughput prostatic-secretion exosome proteome; source of an extracellular exosome (over-annotation) call.

title: Distinct biochemical properties of human serine hydroxymethyltransferase compared with the Plasmodium enzyme: implications for selective inhibition.
review_notes: Detailed biochemical characterization of human cytosolic SHMT (kinetics, PLP/serine binding, THF substrate inhibition); supports core catalytic, PLP-binding, serine-binding and THF-interconversion annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of generic "protein binding" and self-interaction (identical protein binding) IPI calls.

title: The catalytic activity of serine hydroxymethyltransferase is essential for de novo nuclear dTMP synthesis in lung cancer cells.
review_notes: Shows the catalytic activity (not just oligomeric state/scaffolding) of SHMT1 is required for de novo nuclear dTMP synthesis; RAN-dependent nuclear import. Supports core catalytic and non-core nuclear/thymidylate annotations.

title: IDH3α regulates one-carbon metabolism in glioblastoma.
review_notes: Reports a specific IDH3A-cSHMT interaction regulating one-carbon metabolism; underlies one of the generic "protein binding" IPI annotations.

title: Affinity purification and characterization of serine hydroxymethyltransferases from rat liver.
review_notes: Classic biochemical characterization of rat-liver cytosolic/mitochondrial SHMT (tetramer, 4 PLP/enzyme). Reactome uses it for the broad aldehyde-lyase activity annotation.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Interaction-perturbation study; source of a generic "protein binding" (with MAPK9) IPI call.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Binary interactome map; source of generic "protein binding" and self-interaction IPI calls.

title: One substrate many enzymes virtual screening uncovers missing genes of carnitine biosynthesis in human and mouse.
review_notes: Experimentally demonstrates HTMLA and threonine/allo-threonine aldolase activities of human SHMT1; explicitly frames the carnitine (HTMLA) role as low-efficiency partial compensation for a lost dedicated gene (Tha1), justifying non-core treatment.

title: Structure-based mechanism of riboregulation of the metabolic enzyme SHMT1.
review_notes: cryo-EM structures of free and RNA-bound human SHMT1; RNA acts as an allosteric switch competing with polyglutamylated folates and biasing the enzyme toward glycine->serine, coordinating cytosolic/mitochondrial one-carbon flux. Supports core catalytic and non-core riboregulation annotations.

title: Purification and characterization of cytosolic and mitochondrial serine hydroxymethyltransferases from rat liver.
review_notes: Biochemical characterization of rat-liver SHMT isozymes (tetramer, 4 PLP/mol, allothreonine reactivity). Reactome uses it for the broad aldehyde-lyase activity annotation.

title: Cloning of human cDNAs encoding mitochondrial and cytosolic serine hydroxymethyltransferases and chromosomal localization.
review_notes: Original cloning of human cSHMT by functional complementation of an E. coli glyA mutant, directly demonstrating SHMT activity; chromosome 17p11.2. Supports the core activity.

title: The crystal structure of human cytosolic serine hydroxymethyltransferase: a target for cancer chemotherapy.
review_notes: Crystal structure (1BJ4) of human cytosolic SHMT: alpha-class PLP fold, tetramer as a "dimer of dimers", active site at the tight-dimer interface. Supports core PLP-binding and homodimer/tetramer annotations.

title: The role of serine hydroxymethyltransferase isozymes in one-carbon metabolism in MCF-7 cells as determined by (13)C NMR.
review_notes: 13C-NMR tracing in MCF-7 cells; establishes that mitochondrial serine (carbon 3) is the major source of the cellular one-carbon pool. Supports core one-carbon/matrix annotations.

title: Effect of vitamin B6 availability on serine hydroxymethyltransferase in MCF-7 cells.
review_notes: Measures mitochondrial vs cytosolic SHMT activity/stability under vitamin B6 (PLP) restriction; supports PLP-dependence and the catalytic MF.

title: The layered structure of human mitochondrial DNA nucleoids.
review_notes: mtDNA nucleoid proteomics/cross-linking; cited by UniProt for SHMT2 association with mitochondrial DNA. Basis for the mitochondrial nucleoid localization (and the chromatin binding IDA, better read as mtDNA/nucleoid association). Abstract does not name SHMT2 explicitly; full text read by curator.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput exosome proteomics; basis for the extracellular exosome HDA call, an over-annotation for a mitochondrial matrix enzyme.

title: Defining the human deubiquitinating enzyme interaction landscape.
review_notes: DUB-interactome screen; SHMT2 interaction with BRCC3/BRCC36 reflects BRISC-complex association. Basis for a bare protein-binding IPI (over-annotated as MF).

title: MHC class II-associated proteins in B-cell exosomes and potential functional implications for exosome biogenesis.
review_notes: High-throughput B-cell exosome proteomics; basis for the extracellular exosome HDA (over-annotation).

title: Identification of a de novo thymidylate biosynthesis pathway in mammalian mitochondria.
review_notes: Establishes de novo mitochondrial thymidylate synthesis via SHMT2/TYMS/DHFRL1 and localizes SHMT2 to mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane; prevents uracil accumulation in mtDNA.

title: A BRISC-SHMT complex deubiquitinates IFNAR1 and regulates interferon responses.
review_notes: Primary evidence for SHMT2's catalysis-independent moonlighting role as a BRISC-complex component that deubiquitinates IFNAR1 and regulates type I interferon responses; also confirms catalytic activity and mitochondrial/cytoplasmic/nuclear localization. Basis for BRISC/K63-deubiquitination/type-I-IFN annotations.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome map; basis for bare protein-binding IPIs (uninformative MF).

title: How pyridoxal 5'-phosphate differentially regulates human cytosolic and mitochondrial serine hydroxymethyltransferase oligomeric state.
review_notes: Crystal structure and biochemistry of human SHMT2; PLP binding drives a dimer-to-tetramer transition; reports kinetics (KM 278 uM serine, 23 uM THF). Supports core catalytic MF, PLP binding, and tetramerization.

title: Autism and Intellectual Disability-Associated KIRREL3 Interacts with Neuronal Proteins MAP1B and MYO16 with Potential Roles in Neurodevelopment.
review_notes: Reports a SHMT2-KIRREL3 interaction (also in UniProt SUBUNIT); basis for a bare protein-binding IPI. Biological significance for SHMT2 function unclear.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Alternative-splicing interactome map; basis for bare protein-binding IPIs (uninformative MF).

title: SHMT2 Desuccinylation by SIRT5 Drives Cancer Cell Proliferation.
review_notes: SIRT5 desuccinylates SHMT2 at Lys-280 to activate it; hypersuccinylation inhibits activity. Confirms the catalytic MF (rate-limiting step of serine catabolism) and PLP-dependent homotetramerization; links SHMT2 activity to cancer-cell proliferation (indirect, non-core).

title: Mitochondrial translation requires folate-dependent tRNA methylation.
review_notes: Shows SHMT2 catalytic loss impairs mitochondrial translation (taurinomethyluridine tRNA wobble modification) and hence oxidative phosphorylation. Supports core catalytic MF/one-carbon and the downstream (non-core) translation/OXPHOS/respiration regulation annotations.

title: Serine Catabolism by SHMT2 Is Required for Proper Mitochondrial Translation Initiation and Maintenance of Formylmethionyl-tRNAs.
review_notes: SHMT2 serine catabolism is required for robust mitochondrial oxygen consumption and proper mitochondrial translation initiation / fMet-tRNA maintenance. Supports the downstream (non-core) translation/OXPHOS annotations.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-perturbation screen; basis for a bare protein-binding IPI (uninformative MF).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome map; basis for a bare protein-binding IPI (uninformative MF).

title: Impairment of the mitochondrial one-carbon metabolism enzyme SHMT2 causes a novel brain and heart developmental syndrome.
review_notes: Biallelic SHMT2 variants cause NEDCASB; patient fibroblasts show decreased glycine/serine ratio and altered 5-methyl-THF, and variant P499A shows decreased hydroxymethyltransferase activity. Strong IMP support for the core catalytic MF and one-carbon/serine/glycine BP annotations.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BRCC3 interaction, i.e. BRISC association); basis for a bare protein-binding IPI.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports the core mitochondrion localization (HTP).

title: AI-guided pipeline for protein-protein interaction drug discovery identifies a SARS-CoV-2 inhibitor.
review_notes: AI-guided PPI pipeline; SHMT2 appears with a BRCC3 interaction and a self (identical-protein-binding) interaction. Basis for a bare protein-binding IPI and the identical-protein-binding IPI.

title: One substrate many enzymes virtual screening uncovers missing genes of carnitine biosynthesis in human and mouse.
review_notes: Structure-based screen showing SHMT1/2 catalyze the hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase (HTMLA) reaction of carnitine biosynthesis, only partially compensating for a dedicated (mouse) threonine aldolase. Basis for the promiscuous, secondary (non-core) HTMLA activity annotation.

title: Cloning of human cDNAs encoding mitochondrial and cytosolic serine hydroxymethyltransferases and chromosomal localization.
review_notes: Cloned human mitochondrial (and cytosolic) SHMT cDNAs by functional complementation of an E. coli glyA (SHMT-deficient) mutant, directly demonstrating hydroxymethyltransferase activity and defining the gene.

title: PXLP-K280-SHMT2 tetramer transfers CH2OH group to Gly to form L-Ser
review_notes: Reactome reaction of the PLP(K280)-SHMT2 tetramer catalyzing the SHMT reaction; supports the core catalytic MF.

title: LONP1 binds mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: Generic LONP1 substrate-binding reaction listing SHMT2 as an inner-membrane-associated substrate; basis for an inner-membrane localization TAS (non-core).

title: LONP1 degrades mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: Generic LONP1 substrate-degradation reaction listing SHMT2; basis for an inner-membrane localization TAS (non-core).

title: Siah-1 mediates a novel beta-catenin degradation pathway linking p53 to the adenomatous polyposis coli protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; establishes the SIAH1 beta-catenin degradation pathway.

title: Regulation of BOB.1/OBF.1 stability by SIAH.
review_notes: Establishes BOB.1/OBF.1 (POU2AF1) as a SIAH substrate; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: An anthropoid-specific locus of orphan C to U RNA-editing enzymes on chromosome 22.
review_notes: The cited paper (APOBEC RNA-editing enzymes) has no relation to SIAH1 - the cached abstract contains zero mention of SIAH1/seven-in-absentia. The zinc ion binding annotation citing this PMID appears to use a wrong identifier; SIAH1 zinc binding is independently supported by PMID:16085652.

title: Structural analysis of Siah1-Siah-interacting protein interactions and insights into the assembly of an E3 ligase multiprotein complex.
review_notes: Full text available; source of zinc ion binding (IDA) and beta-catenin destruction complex annotations.

title: Siah1 interacts with the scaffold protein POSH to promote JNK activation and apoptosis.
review_notes: Establishes the SIAH1-POSH-JNK apoptosis link; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Synphilin-1A inhibits seven in absentia homolog (SIAH) and modulates alpha-synuclein monoubiquitylation and inclusion formation.
review_notes: Full text available; experimental (EXP) support for SIAH1 ligase activity on alpha-synuclein/synphilin-1.

title: Analysis of the human E2 ubiquitin conjugating enzyme protein interaction network.
review_notes: High-throughput E2 interaction network; source of a bare protein binding annotation, consistent with SIAH1 binding E2 enzymes.

title: Comparison of an expanded ataxia interactome with patient medical records reveals a relationship between macular degeneration and ataxia.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: ARTS and Siah collaborate in a pathway for XIAP degradation.
review_notes: Full text available; establishes the SIAH1-ARTS-XIAP apoptosis pathway.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: E3 ubiquitin ligase Siah-1 facilitates poly-ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of the hepatitis B viral X protein.
review_notes: Establishes HBx as a SIAH1 substrate; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.
review_notes: High-throughput liver interactome; source of bare protein binding and identical protein binding (self-association) annotations.

title: Systematic analysis of dimeric E3-RING interactions reveals increased combinatorial complexity in human ubiquitination networks.
review_notes: Source of the identical protein binding (SIAH1 self-association/dimerization) annotation; consistent with SIAH1 functioning as a homodimer.

title: Polycystin-1 regulates the stability and ubiquitination of transcription factor Jade-1.
review_notes: Full text available; IDA support for SIAH1 ligase activity and ubiquitin-dependent catabolism of Jade-1.

title: MOR is not enough: identification of novel mu-opioid receptor interacting proteins using traditional and modified membrane yeast two-hybrid screens.
review_notes: High-throughput interaction screen; source of a bare protein binding annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; source of bare protein binding and identical protein binding annotations.

title: The SIAH E3 ubiquitin ligases promote Wnt/β-catenin signaling through mediating Wnt-induced Axin degradation.
review_notes: Full text available; establishes the SIAH1-AXIN1 axis and the positive (feed-forward) Wnt-signaling role.

title: De novo variants in SIAH1, encoding an E3 ubiquitin ligase, are associated with developmental delay, hypotonia and dysmorphic features.
review_notes: Disease-variant evidence; source of a canonical Wnt signaling annotation.

title: DAZAP2 acts as specifier of the p53 response to DNA damage.
review_notes: Full text available; IDA support for SIAH1-mediated proteasomal degradation of HIPK2 in the DNA-damage/p53 response.

title: Mammalian homologs of seven in absentia regulate DCC via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
review_notes: Full text available; foundational study establishing SIAH1 as a cytoplasmic RING E3 that binds E2 enzymes and degrades DCC via the proteasome.

title: Characterization of human homologs of the Drosophila seven in absentia (sina) gene.
review_notes: Source of the apoptosis and anatomical-structure-morphogenesis TAS annotations.

title: Selective Sirt2 inhibition by ligand-induced rearrangement of the active site.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-resolution human Sirt2 structures (PDB 4RMG/4RMJ) resolving the NAD+-dependent deacylase active site, the NAD+/cofactor pocket and the structural zinc-binding domain.

title: Structure of the Cul1-Rbx1-Skp1-F boxSkp2 SCF ubiquitin ligase complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified crystal structure of Cul1-Rbx1-Skp1-F box(Skp2); directly supports SCF complex membership and the substrate-receptor role.

title: Structural basis of the Cks1-dependent recognition of p27(Kip1) by the SCF(Skp2) ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Skp1-Skp2-Cks1/phospho-p27 structure; supports the CKS1-dependent phosphodegron recognition of p27.

title: Acute myelogenous leukemia-derived SMAD4 mutations target the protein to ubiquitin-proteasome degradation.
review_notes: Correct paper, but its mechanism is degradation of mutant SMAD4 by SCF(beta-TrCP1); it does not support a SKP2-specific function, so the bare protein-binding annotation drawn from it was removed as uninformative.

title: SNIP1 is a candidate modifier of the transcriptional activity of c-Myc on E box-dependent target genes.
review_notes: Cached record is an abstract about SNIP1 and c-Myc transcriptional activity and does not itself mention SKP2; the SKP2-MYC relationship used in this review is taken from PMID:16376880 and PMID:23277542.

title: Skp2 E3 ligase integrates ATM activation and homologous recombination repair by ubiquitinating NBS1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; supports SKP2-dependent K63-linked ubiquitination of NBS1 and the HR-repair requirement. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Acetylation-dependent regulation of Skp2 function.
review_notes: Full text cached; supports NLS acetylation, cytoplasmic retention, E-cadherin degradation and acetylation-dependent SKP2 dimerisation.

title: ISG12a Restricts Hepatitis C Virus Infection through the Ubiquitination-Dependent Degradation Pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; identifies SKP2 as the E3 ligase for HCV NS5A recruited by ISG12a/IFI27. Cached record is abstract-only, so the K48 linkage claim was accepted on the curator's full-text reading.

title: p19Skp1 and p45Skp2 are essential elements of the cyclin A-CDK2 S phase kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified founding p45(SKP2) paper; supports the requirement of SKP2 for S-phase entry.

title: Falcon deep research report for human SKP2
review_notes: LLM-generated (Falcon/Edison) synthesis. Its high-confidence section matches the primary literature used here (SCF substrate receptor, CKS1-dependent p27 recognition, nuclear canonical activity, K63 branch). Several cited secondary reviews are not in the local cache and were not independently verified.

title: Ethnicity-dependent polymorphism in Na+-taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (SLC10A1) reveals a domain critical for bile acid substrate recognition.
review_notes: Establishes human substrate specificity and that loss-of-function variants can act through reduced plasma-membrane expression.

title: Homo- and hetero-dimeric architecture of the human liver Na⁺-dependent taurocholate co-transporting protein.
review_notes: Source of the IDA plasma-membrane and bile acid transporter annotations; abstract-only in the cache but the assays named (FRET, co-IP, cross-linking, uptake) support both terms.

title: Sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide is a functional receptor for human hepatitis B and D virus.
review_notes: Full text cached; the primary evidence for the proposed virus receptor activity and symbiont entry annotations.

title: Sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (SLC10A1) deficiency: conjugated hypercholanemia without a clear clinical phenotype.
review_notes: First description of human NTCP deficiency; the mild phenotype with intact bile salt synthesis and FGF19 signalling is also the evidence against nutrient/hormone response process terms.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI systematic yeast two-hybrid map; correctly cited but functionally uninformative, and the source of 87 generic protein binding rows recommended for removal.

title: Targeting the Four Pillars of Enterohepatic Bile Salt Cycling; Lessons From Genetics and Pharmacology.
review_notes: Review placing NTCP as one of the four transport pillars of enterohepatic cycling; used for pathway context, not for primary functional claims.

title: Functional and Pharmacological Comparison of Human and Mouse Na(+)/Taurocholate Cotransporting Polypeptide (NTCP).
review_notes: Supports the basolateral plasma membrane location and the drug-transport (xenobiotic) component of substrate specificity.

title: Structural basis of sodium-dependent bile salt uptake into the liver.
review_notes: Full text cached; links the transport cycle mechanistically to the viral receptor function.

title: Structure of the bile acid transporter and HBV receptor NTCP.
review_notes: Independent cryo-EM study of human NTCP supporting both the transport and receptor functions.

title: Structural insights into the HBV receptor and bile acid transporter NTCP.
review_notes: Third 2022 cryo-EM structure of NTCP; cited as corroborating structural evidence for the dual transporter/receptor function.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: Interaction-proteomics survey of 396 SLCs; correctly cited but assigns no molecular function to SLC10A1.

title: Molecular cloning, chromosomal localization, and functional characterization of a human liver Na+/bile acid cotransporter.
review_notes: Cloning and first functional characterization of human NTCP; directly establishes the Na+-dependent bile acid symporter activity annotated by TAS.

title: Expression and transport properties of the human ileal and renal sodium-dependent bile acid transporter.
review_notes: Primarily about SLC10A2 (ileal ASBT), but its explicit contrast with the multispecific liver transporter is the basis for treating organic anion/xenobiotic uptake as a genuine NTCP activity.

title: Topology scanning and putative three-dimensional structure of the extracellular binding domains of the apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter (SLC10A2).
review_notes: Supports the multi-pass membrane architecture and provides a structural rationalization of the P290S transport-null allele. Not the source of any GOA row; used here as corroborating structural context.

title: Bile acid transporters.
review_notes: Authoritative review by the group that cloned the human transporter; used for the pathway position and tissue breadth statements rather than as primary evidence.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI systematic yeast two-hybrid map; correctly cited but functionally uninformative, and the source of ten generic protein binding rows recommended for removal.

title: Targeting the Four Pillars of Enterohepatic Bile Salt Cycling; Lessons From Genetics and Pharmacology.
review_notes: Full text available in the cache. Cited by UniProt for the statement that SLC10A2 works together with NTCP, OST-alpha/beta and BSEP in enterohepatic recycling; also the source for ASBT as a drug target. Supports the apical localization of the human protein.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Verified as the Huttlin et al. Cell 2021 BioPlex 3.0/HCT116 paper, a proteome-wide AP-MS interactome resource. It is correctly cited for the SLC10A2-CLPTM1 co-purification but assigns no molecular function to SLC10A2, so it cannot license an informative replacement term.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: Interaction-proteomics survey of 396 SLCs; correctly cited, and it independently reproduces the SLC10A2-CLPTM1 interaction, but it assigns no molecular function to SLC10A2.

title: Identification of a mutation in the ileal sodium-dependent bile acid transporter gene that abolishes transport activity.
review_notes: Cloning and first loss-of-function characterization of the human ileal transporter; directly supports the TAS transporter-activity and plasma-membrane annotations assigned by PINC. Abstract-only in the cache, but the assays named (chimeras, transfected COS-1 uptake, sequencing) match what was annotated.

title: Primary bile acid malabsorption caused by mutations in the ileal sodium-dependent bile acid transporter gene (SLC10A2).
review_notes: Disease-gene paper for PBAM1 (MIM 613291) and the source of the PINC TAS rows for bile acid sodium symporter activity and plasma membrane. Abstract-only in the cache; the trafficking-versus-transport dissection stated in the abstract is exactly what the plasma-membrane annotation rests on.

title: Expression and transport properties of the human ileal and renal sodium-dependent bile acid transporter.
review_notes: Primary characterization of substrate specificity, ion dependence and tissue distribution of the human ileal/renal transporter. This is the reference that establishes the specificity contrast with SLC10A1/NTCP, and therefore why no xenobiotic- or organic-anion transport term is appropriate for SLC10A2.

title: Bile acid uptake via the human apical sodium-bile acid cotransporter is electrogenic.
review_notes: Direct electrophysiological determination of the sodium stoichiometry of the human protein in stably transfected CHO cells lacking other bile acid transporters. This is the evidence that the sodium leg of the symport is work the protein itself performs, and so the basis for the proposed GO:0098719 annotation. Abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract states the method, the result and the control.

title: Recycling of bile acids and salts
review_notes: Pathway-level Reactome entry supporting the TAS row for GO:0015721; places SLC10A2 correctly as the apical uptake step of the enterohepatic cycle.

title: SLC10A2 transports bile salts and acids and Na+ from extracellular region to cytosol
review_notes: Reactome reaction underlying the TAS rows for GO:0008508 and GO:0005886. One caveat that does not affect the GO terms: the reaction is written with a single sodium ion, whereas the human protein was measured at a 2:1 Na+ to bile acid stoichiometry [PMID:9856990] and UniProt's curated RHEA reactions use two Na+.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard PAINT/IBA reference. Sound as a method; the individual propagations it carries are judged per row — two accepted or corrected in place (GO:0022857, GO:0005886) and one removed (GO:0015721).

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mechanical SL-keyword-to-GO mapping. Verified against the Q96EP9 UniProt record, which does carry a SUBCELLULAR LOCATION of Cell membrane with ECO:0000269|PubMed:23589386.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Deterministic MF-to-BP inter-ontology inference; correct given the source molecular function.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: InterPro/ARBA-based automatic annotation. IPR002657 is genuinely present in SLC10A4, so the generic membrane assignment is correct.

title: Cloning and expression of SLC10A4, a putative organic anion transport protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. First cloning and functional characterization of human SLC10A4; the earliest independent negative result for bile acid transport, and one source of the plasma-membrane localization claim.

title: Cloning and molecular characterization of the orphan carrier protein Slc10a4: expression in cholinergic neurons of the rat central nervous system.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cited in the UniProt entry for TISSUE SPECIFICITY. Establishes the topology, the cholinergic-neuron expression, and a second independent negative transport result. Abstract-only in the cache but the assays are named explicitly.

title: Co-expression studies of the orphan carrier protein Slc10a4 and the vesicular carriers VAChT and VMAT2 in the rat central and peripheral nervous system.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. The primary evidence for synaptic vesicle and mast cell granule localization, which underpins the proposed GO:0030672 replacement. An erratum exists (Neuroscience 2012;212:226) but does not affect these conclusions.

title: Homo- and hetero-dimeric architecture of the human liver Na⁺-dependent taurocholate co-transporting protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only in the cache. Relevant to SLC10A4 only through its effect on a partner. The sign is negative and the system is forced co-expression in U2OS cells, so it does not support involved_in bile acid transport for SLC10A4; raised under suggested_questions instead.

title: The synaptic protein encoded by the gene Slc10A4 suppresses epileptiform activity and regulates sensitivity to cholinergic chemoconvulsants.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Knockout-phenotype evidence establishing necessity for normal cholinergic signalling. Per the participation test this does not identify SLC10A4 as the entity performing any step, so no process annotation is proposed from it.

title: SLC10A4 is a protease-activated transporter that transports bile acids.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cited in the UniProt entry for FUNCTION, PROTEOLYTIC CLEAVAGE, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and TOPOLOGY. Abstract-only in the cache. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because the title's positive claim that SLC10A4 transports bile acids is contested — including by the abstract's own opening sentence and hedged conclusion, by UniProt's FUNCTION comment drawn from this same paper ("No significant bile acid transporter activity could be measured despite its similarity to bile acid:sodium symporters", ECO:0000269|PubMed:23589386), and by four independent transport studies [PMID:17106928, PMID:18355966, PMID:26084360, PMID:28439090]. It is correctly cited for the negated GO:0008508 annotation and for the cell-membrane localization, which is how GOA uses it.

title: Distribution of SLC10A4, a synaptic vesicle protein in the human brain, and the association of this protein with Alzheimer's disease-related neuronal degeneration.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. The only report of SLC10A4 protein distribution in human rather than rodent brain, so it is what justifies carrying the rodent localization conclusions over to the human gene. The Alzheimer association is correlative and no disease annotation is proposed.

title: SLC10A4 is a vesicular amine-associated transporter modulating dopamine homeostasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. The most informative functional study. Note that it explicitly reports failure to demonstrate direct dopamine transport, so despite the word transporter in its title it supports a modulatory role rather than a dopamine transporter annotation.

title: A role for solute carrier family 10 member 4, or vesicular aminergic-associated transporter, in structural remodelling and transmitter release at the mouse neuromuscular junction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Knockout-phenotype evidence extending the modulatory role to the peripheral cholinergic synapse. Necessity evidence only, so no process annotation is proposed from it.

title: Expression, sorting and transport studies for the orphan carrier SLC10A4 in neuronal and non-neuronal cell lines and in Xenopus laevis oocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available in the cache. The decisive negative study, because it closes the trafficking escape hatch with the NTCP C-terminal chimera. The authors themselves qualify the result as holding at least in the transport assays used, which is why GO:0022857 is accepted rather than challenged.

title: SLC10A4 regulates IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation in vitro and mast cell-mediated reactions in vivo.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available in the cache. Extends the secretory-vesicle modulatory role beyond neurons, and is the source of the field's own explicit statement that the substrate is unknown — the key fact behind accepting the uninformative GO:0022857 parent.

title: Homo- and heterodimerization is a common feature of the solute carrier family SLC10 members.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only. Independent replication of the SLC10A4-NTCP heterodimer and its negative effect on NTCP transport, and a family-level confirmation that SLC10A4 is still classified as an orphan carrier.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Correctly cited for five IPI protein-binding rows, but a systematic interactome screen supports no informative molecular function for SLC10A4, which is why all five rows are removed as uninformative rather than modified.

title: SLC10 pocket-conservation analysis: NTCP sodium and preS1 sites across the human family
review_notes: Local reproducible analysis written for this review round; sites are defined from ligand contacts in experimental NTCP cryo-EM structures and the residue correspondence passes a method control on the SLC10A1 model itself. Two OpenScientist hypothesis jobs run blind to this analysis reached the same verdict (REFUTED for the degeneration hypothesis). It supports the structural premise of the GO:0022857 argument; it is prediction-based for every paralogue and no review action rests on it.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT phylogenetic annotation method; the substantive judgment under review is the placement of the IBD at PANTHER:PTN000040759/PTN000040761, not the method itself.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara orthology transfer method; here the donor is the true rat ortholog Soat (UniProtKB:Q70EX6), so the transfer is sound.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined automated IEA method; supports only the broad GO:0016020 membrane term from InterPro:IPR002657 and UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0162.

title: Cloning and functional characterization of human sodium-dependent organic anion transporter (SLC10A6).
review_notes: Primary cloning and functional characterization of human SOAT; PubMed-verified. Abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract itself states both the steroid-sulfate kinetics and the negative bile-acid result that the review turns on.

title: Homo- and hetero-dimeric architecture of the human liver Na⁺-dependent taurocholate co-transporting protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the abstract itself names SLC10A6 in both the co-IP result and the functional-interference result. This is the informative interaction evidence for SOAT, in contrast to the HuRI rows, but it is not the source of any GOA annotation.

title: Membrane transporters for sulfated steroids in the human testis--cellular localization, expression pattern and functional analysis.
review_notes: Full text cached. Source of the UniProt subcellular-location evidence and of the germ-cell localization; extends the substrate list by mass spectrometry rather than radiotracer uptake.

title: Transport of the placental estriol precursor 16α-hydroxy-dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (16α-OH-DHEAS) by stably transfected OAT4-, SOAT-, and NTCP-HEK293 cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the abstract states the sodium dependence, the kinetics and the placental localization used here.

title: Sodium-dependent organic anion transporter (Slc10a6(-/-)) knockout mice show normal spermatogenesis and reproduction, but elevated serum levels for cholesterol sulfate.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. The negative reproductive phenotype is the main reason no spermatogenesis or hormone-biosynthesis process term is proposed for this gene.

title: Transport of steroid 3-sulfates and steroid 17-sulfates by the sodium-dependent organic anion transporter SOAT (SLC10A6).
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Defines the chemical scope of the activity (mono-sulfate at 3' or 17'), which is what a molecular-function term for SOAT needs to capture.

title: Estrone-3-Sulfate Stimulates the Proliferation of T47D Breast Cancer Cells Stably Transfected With the Sodium-Dependent Organic Anion Transporter SOAT (SLC10A6).
review_notes: Full text cached. Shows a downstream cellular consequence of SOAT-mediated substrate uptake; it establishes drug-target interest rather than a separate SOAT activity, so no proliferation-related process term is proposed.

title: Homo- and heterodimerization is a common feature of the solute carrier family SLC10 members.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Relevant to SOAT's oligomeric state; it is not the source of any GOA row, and the evidence is systematic Y2H plus co-localization rather than a defined complex, so no complex annotation is proposed.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Full text cached. Correctly cited, high-quality resource, but a proteome-scale binary interactome map; for SLC10A6 it supports only the generic GO:0005515 rows and no specific molecular function.

title: Substrate Specificities and Inhibition Pattern of the Solute Carrier Family 10 Members NTCP, ASBT and SOAT.
review_notes: Full text cached; the single most decision-relevant reference for this review. It both confirms that SOAT is not a bile acid transporter in the NTCP/ASBT sense and shows that one bile salt (taurolithocholate) is a genuine sodium-coupled substrate, which is why the family-level bile-acid terms are kept as non-core rather than removed.

title: Role of the Sodium-Dependent Organic Anion Transporter (SOAT/SLC10A6) in Physiology and Pathophysiology.
review_notes: Full text cached. Authoritative 2023 review by the group that cloned the carrier; used for the consensus statement of substrate specificity and for plasma-membrane localization.

title: SOAT can transport taurolithocholate-3-sulphate
review_notes: Cached Reactome reaction, grounded in PMID:17491011. The reaction itself (taurolithocholate-3-sulphate uptake) is correct, but its own summary states SOAT has no affinity for bile acids, which argues against treating the derived GO:0008508 annotation as this gene's core function.

title: SLC-mediated bile acid transport
review_notes: Cached Reactome pathway. A grouping node rather than a SOAT-specific statement; SOAT's only member reaction in it is the sulfoconjugated bile salt R-HSA-433089.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA methodology reference behind the plasma-membrane IBA at node PANTHER:PTN000428041. The method is sound; the node's compartment assertion does not transfer to the human member, which localizes to the Golgi.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Mapping reference for the three UniProt subcellular-location IEAs (SL-0134 Golgi apparatus membrane, SL-0097 ER membrane, SL-0039 Cell membrane). The mappings are mechanically correct; the evidential strength is inherited from the UniProt statements.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Orthology-transfer reference for the two annotations propagated from mouse Slc10a7 (Q5PT53). The one-to-one orthology is uncontroversial; one of the two transferred terms (GO:0030210) is mis-scoped at source.

title: Molecular and phylogenetic characterization of a novel putative membrane transporter (SLC10A7), conserved in vertebrates and bacteria.
review_notes: The founding molecular characterization of SLC10A7 and the source of the ER and plasma-membrane localizations. Abstract-only in the cache, and the abstract reports only the plasma membrane, so the ER observations in the full text could not be checked - hence UNDECIDED on the two ER rows rather than any stronger action. Its negative transport result is the firmest thing known about the protein.

title: Homo- and hetero-dimeric architecture of the human liver Na⁺-dependent taurocholate co-transporting protein.
review_notes: Not an SLC10A7-focused study (abstract-only here) but a useful negative datum - SLC10A7 neither co-localizes nor co-complexes with the family prototype NTCP, supporting its functional and compartmental separation from the bile acid carriers.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Correctly cited for a high-throughput interaction, but the cached full text never mentions SLC10A7 and the study supports no molecular function for it. Basis for REMOVE of the generic protein-binding row rather than for any replacement term.

title: Integrating glycomics and genomics uncovers SLC10A7 as essential factor for bone mineralization by regulating post-Golgi protein transport and glycosylation.
review_notes: The only study that asks directly where the human protein resides, and the source of the Golgi annotations. Abstract-only in the cache, but the Golgi statement and the post-Golgi transport defect are explicit in the abstract. Decisive for resolving the localization conflict in favour of the Golgi as the physiological compartment.

title: SLC10A7 mutations cause a skeletal dysplasia with amelogenesis imperfecta mediated by GAG biosynthesis defects.
review_notes: Full text available and the source of five of the eighteen annotations. Verified by reading - the calcium and heparan sulfate data are solid, but the plasma-membrane assignment is an over-expression immunofluorescence result without a surface marker, and heparin itself was never assayed - both findings drive the actions taken here.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Correctly cited for a high-throughput interaction only. The cached full text does not mention SLC10A7 and no molecular function can be drawn from it.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: The most relevant of the three interaction screens, since SLC10A7 was in its bait set, and the third independent detection of the DPY19L4 interaction. Still supports no informative molecular function, so it cannot rescue the generic protein-binding rows.

title: SLC10A7 sodium-site conservation against the ligand-bound NTCP cryo-EM structures
review_notes: Local reproducible analysis written for this review round; the pipeline and its method control live in genes/human/SLC10A4/SLC10A4-bioinformatics/. It independently supports keeping the molecular function at the substrate-agnostic parent, but it is prediction-based and no review action rests on it.

title: The gene mutated in thiamine-responsive anaemia with diabetes and deafness (TRMA) encodes a functional thiamine transporter.
review_notes: Founding functional study identifying SLC19A2 as the TRMA gene encoding thiamine transporter-1; abstract confirms thiamine-transport function. Abstract-only in cache (full_text_available false) but the IMP annotation matches the abstract.

title: Cloning of the human thiamine transporter, a member of the folate transporter family.
review_notes: Cloning paper establishing direct, Na+-independent, thiamine-specific uptake. Note that the "folate transporter family" in the title is a sequence-homology statement; the same paper shows the transporter is specific to thiamine, so the derived folate-transport annotations are over-annotations.

title: Tspan-1 interacts with the thiamine transporter-1 in human intestinal epithelial cells and modulates its stability.
review_notes: Provides the IDA for plasma-membrane localization and thiamine transporter activity, and the IPI for the functional TSPAN1 interaction (stabilization).

title: pH-dependent pyridoxine transport by SLC19A2 and SLC19A3: Implications for absorption in acidic microclimates.
review_notes: Directly demonstrates human SLC19A2 pyridoxine transport (IDA) and reports thiamine and pyridoxine KM values; abstract in cache supports both annotations.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput BioPlex interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI to ENDOD1. SLC19A2 pair is in the large-scale supplementary network, not the cached text; no established functional consequence.

title: Animal species differences in the pyridoxine transport function of SLC19A3: Absence of Slc19a3-mediated pyridoxine uptake in the rat small intestine.
review_notes: Although titled for SLC19A3, the study also assays SLC19A2 orthologs (including human), showing all transport thiamine and that SLC19A2 transports pyridoxine. Supports the thiamine (IDA) and pyridoxine (IDA) annotations.

title: Identification of the amino acid residues involved in the species-dependent differences in the pyridoxine transport function of SLC19A3.
review_notes: Full text available; directly assays human SLC19A2 (hSLC19A2-ma3-7AA mutant) showing pyridoxine transport can be abolished while thiamine uptake is retained. Supports the IMP thiamine-transport annotation.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput SLC-superfamily interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (ENDOD1). Individual pair is in supplementary network data, not the cached text.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline reference; supports the general vitamin transmembrane transporter activity IEA (parent of the specific thiamine term).

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Curator ISS transfer from mouse Slc19a3 (Q99PL8); consistent with human experimental thiamine-transport data.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) inference; supports the core thiamine transporter activity and plasma-membrane location.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl-Compara transfer from mouse ortholog; supports thiamine transmembrane transport.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Combined IEA methods; recapitulate the correct core thiamine transporter activity and thiamine transport, redundant with experimental records.

title: Identification and characterization of the human and mouse SLC19A3 gene: a novel member of the reduced folate family of micronutrient transporter genes.
review_notes: Original cloning/characterization of human+mouse SLC19A3: 496 aa, 12 TM, reduced-folate family, widely expressed (most abundant placenta/kidney/liver). Basis of the NAS "membrane" annotation and tissue specificity.

title: SLC19A3 encodes a second thiamine transporter ThTr2.
review_notes: Foundational functional study: SLC19A3 transfectants take up [3H]thiamine but not folate/methotrexate; high specificity for vitamin B1; establishes ThTr2. Directly supports the core thiamine transporter activity.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI systematic high-throughput Y2H interactome; source of the 11 bare GO:0005515 IPI hits. Citation is correct but the interactions are proteome- scale screen hits with no SLC19A3-specific functional interpretation.

title: pH-dependent pyridoxine transport by SLC19A2 and SLC19A3: Implications for absorption in acidic microclimates.
review_notes: Demonstrates SLC19A3-mediated pH-dependent pyridoxine uptake (Km 18.5 uM) plus thiamine transport; Caco-2 siRNA knockdown reduces carrier-mediated pyridoxine uptake. Supports both thiamine-transport and pyridoxine-transport IDAs.

title: Animal species differences in the pyridoxine transport function of SLC19A3: Absence of Slc19a3-mediated pyridoxine uptake in the rat small intestine.
review_notes: Human SLC19A3 transports both thiamine and pyridoxine; rat/mouse Slc19a3 transport thiamine but not pyridoxine (species-restricted secondary activity).

title: Identification of the amino acid residues involved in the species-dependent differences in the pyridoxine transport function of SLC19A3.
review_notes: Full text. Mutagenesis identifies 7 residues (Gln86, Gly87, Ile91, Thr93, Trp94, Ser168, Asn173) required for human pyridoxine but not thiamine transport; confirms conserved thiamine transport. Supports thiamine (IMP) and pyridoxine (IMP) transport.

title: Disrupted in renal carcinoma 2 (DIRC2/SLC49A4) is an H(+)-driven lysosomal pyridoxine exporter.
review_notes: Primarily about DIRC2; SLC19A3 used as a plasma-membrane pyridoxine-transport positive control that drives cellular pyridoxine accumulation. Supports the pyridoxine-transport IDA.

title: Vitamin B1 (thiamin) metabolism
review_notes: Pathway-level placement of SLC19A3 in vitamin B1 metabolism; supports the thiamine-containing compound metabolic process TAS (retained as non-core context).

title: SLC19A2/3 transport extracellular THMN to cytosol
review_notes: Directly describes SLC19A3/THTR2 at the plasma membrane mediating uptake of extracellular thiamine into the cytosol; supports the core thiamine transporter activity and plasma-membrane location TAS annotations. Notes SLC19A3 has no affinity for biotin.

title: Functional characteristics and tissue distribution pattern of organic cation transporter 2 (OCTN2), an organic cation/carnitine transporter.
review_notes: Abstract confirms OCTN2 as a dual Na+-independent organic cation / Na+-dependent carnitine transporter; PMID matches title.

title: Functional and pharmacological characterization of human Na(+)-carnitine cotransporter hOCTN2.
review_notes: Electrophysiological characterization; supports the Na+-symport mechanism and betaine transport.

title: L-Carnitine transport in human placental brush-border membranes is mediated by the sodium-dependent organic cation transporter OCTN2.
review_notes: Supports carnitine transporter activity and brush-border (apical) localization.

title: PDZK1 directly regulates the function of organic cation/carnitine transporter OCTN2.
review_notes: Establishes the functionally meaningful PDZ-domain (PDZK1) interaction; supersedes the bare protein-binding IPI.

title: OCTN2-mediated carnitine uptake in a newly discovered human proximal tubule cell line (Caki-1).
review_notes: Supports apical/renal localization and carnitine reabsorption role.

title: OCTN2VT, a splice variant of OCTN2, does not transport carnitine because of the retention in the endoplasmic reticulum caused by insertion of 24 amino acids in the first extracellular loop of OCTN2.
review_notes: Distinguishes plasma-membrane functional OCTN2 from ER-retained, transport-dead isoform 3.

title: Transport of butyryl-L-carnitine, a potential prodrug, via the carnitine transporter OCTN2 and the amino acid transporter ATB(0,+).
review_notes: Supports acyl-carnitine (butyryl-carnitine) transport by OCTN2.

title: The Bacillus subtilis quorum-sensing molecule CSF contributes to intestinal homeostasis via OCTN2, a host cell membrane transporter.
review_notes: Supports apical intestinal localization and a polyspecific cationic-peptide transport role (non-core).

title: Expression and localization of carnitine/organic cation transporter OCTN1 and OCTN2 in ocular epithelium.
review_notes: Supports apical localization in ocular epithelia.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: High-throughput proteomics; exosome detection is incidental, not a functional localization.

title: Cytokine regulation of OCTN2 expression and activity in small and large intestine.
review_notes: Full text available; supports carnitine transport, apical localization, and cytokine (IFN-gamma/TNF) regulation.

title: Transport of gabapentin by LAT1 (SLC7A5).
review_notes: Paper is about LAT1/gabapentin; the ARUK-UCL OCTN2 IDA cannot be verified from the abstract-only cache (full text unavailable). Annotation left UNDECIDED.

title: Functional expression of organic cation/carnitine transporter 2 (OCTN2/SLC22A5) in human brain capillary endothelial cell line hCMEC/D3, a human blood-brain barrier model.
review_notes: Experimental (siRNA) evidence for OCTN2 carnitine transport at the BBB; underpins the BBB-transport annotations.

title: Establishment and Dysfunction of the Blood-Brain Barrier.
review_notes: Review-based NAS support; weak. The experimental BBB evidence is PMID:23877104.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; the OCTN2 interaction is uninformative bare protein binding.

title: Blood-Brain Barrier: From Physiology to Disease and Back.
review_notes: Review-based NAS support; weak. Experimental BBB evidence is PMID:23877104.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H; keratin/KAP partners are common artifacts; uninformative bare protein binding.

title: Deorphaning a solute carrier 22 family member, SLC22A15, through functional genomic studies.
review_notes: Full text available; OCTN2 is a comparator. Betaine transport by OCTN2 is directly shown in PMID:10966938; dimethylglycine interaction is cited here.

title: Cholesterol stimulates the cellular uptake of L-carnitine by the carnitine/organic cation transporter novel 2 (OCTN2).
review_notes: Full text available; supports plasma-membrane localization and carnitine transporter activity (cholesterol-regulated).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; uninformative bare protein binding.

title: Localization of Xenobiotic Transporters Expressed at the Human Blood-Testis Barrier.
review_notes: Full text available; supports basal-membrane (Sertoli cell) localization at the blood-testis barrier.

title: cDNA sequence, transport function, and genomic organization of human OCTN2, a new member of the organic cation transporter family.
review_notes: Original human OCTN2 cloning; supports organic cation (quaternary ammonium) transport and multipass membrane topology.

title: Molecular and functional identification of sodium ion-dependent, high affinity human carnitine transporter OCTN2.
review_notes: Foundational identification of OCTN2 as the Na+-dependent carnitine transporter.

title: Primary systemic carnitine deficiency is caused by mutations in a gene encoding sodium ion-dependent carnitine transporter.
review_notes: Establishes SLC22A5 as the systemic carnitine deficiency gene via loss of carnitine transport.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline reference; maps the mitochondrial carrier domain to the generic "transmembrane transport" process. Correct but non-specific.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS pipeline reference supporting the mitochondrial inner membrane location by transfer from the mouse ortholog (Q8JZU2); consistent with the SLC25 family localization.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic pipeline; correctly assigns the core citrate transporter MF, citrate-transport BP, and mitochondrial location for SLC25A1.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: SubCell-mapping pipeline supporting the mitochondrial inner membrane location.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology logical-inference pipeline; derives "succinate transmembrane transport" from the citrate:succinate antiporter term, but succinate is only a minor substrate, so the inferred BP over-states this transport role.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary-exosome proteomics catalogue; supports only a mass-spec detection of SLC25A1 in exosomes, not a functional extracellular location.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteomics; supports only a mass-spec detection in a nuclear fraction. No biological support for a nuclear function of this inner-membrane carrier.

title: Pathogenic mutations of the human mitochondrial citrate carrier SLC25A1 lead to impaired citrate export required for lipid, dolichol, ubiquinone and sterol synthesis.
review_notes: Key functional paper. Reconstituted SLC25A1 and measured transport for all known pathogenic variants; established substrate specificity (predominantly citrate, isocitrate, cis-aconitate, PEP and malate) and Km(citrate)=7.5 uM. Directly supports the core transport MF and BP.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial-proteome study; corroborates mitochondrial localization at the organelle level (broader than the inner-membrane annotation).

title: SLC25A1 and ACLY maintain cytosolic acetyl-CoA and regulate ferroptosis susceptibility via FSP1 acetylation.
review_notes: Full-text available. CRISPR screen identifying SLC25A1 as a ferroptosis regulator; shows SLC25A1-driven citrate export fuels ACLY/acetyl-CoA to sustain FSP1 acetylation. Supports the (non-core, downstream) negative-regulation-of-ferroptosis annotation and reinforces the core citrate-export function.

title: Localization of the human mitochondrial citrate transporter protein gene to chromosome 22Q11 in the DiGeorge syndrome critical region.
review_notes: Original identification/cloning paper mapping the human mitochondrial citrate transporter gene to 22q11 (DiGeorge critical region); source of the TAS citrate-transporter-activity annotation.

title: SLC25A1 may exchange mitochondrial PEP for cytosolic anion
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the hypothetical PEP/citrate exchange; consistent with UniProt's report that SLC25A1 can exchange citrate for phosphoenolpyruvate.

title: SLC25A1 exchanges CIT and MAL
review_notes: Reactome reaction capturing the core citrate/malate exchange (citrate-malate shuttle with ACLY); directly reflects the primary physiological function of SLC25A1.

title: SLC-mediated transport of organic anions
review_notes: Generic Reactome collection pathway for SLC-mediated organic-anion transport; supports only the broad transmembrane-transport process annotation.

title: An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome method paper; source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Not informative about DIC's molecular function.

title: Shifted Transversal Design smart-pooling for high coverage interactome mapping.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome-mapping method; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (MDFI). Non-physiological for an inner-membrane transporter.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome dataset method; source of a bare protein-binding IPI. Uninformative for DIC function.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome; underlies the nucleus HDA annotation. For a mitochondrial inner-membrane transporter this is a co-purification or contaminant artifact and does not support a genuine nuclear localization.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale Y2H interactome; source of multiple bare protein-binding IPIs to keratins/KRTAPs and other non-mitochondrial partners (classic high-throughput false positives). Uninformative for function.

title: SLC25A10 biallelic mutations in intractable epileptic encephalopathy with complex I deficiency.
review_notes: Full text available; directly establishes human DIC transport function (via reconstituted transport assay), disease association, and lack of glutathione transport.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Allelic interactome perturbation study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (NOTCH2NLA). Non-mitochondrial partner; uninformative for DIC function.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial localization (supports the mitochondrion HTP annotation).

title: A mitochondrial carrier transports glycolytic intermediates to link cytosolic and mitochondrial glycolysis in the human gut parasite Blastocystis.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt for FUNCTION, SUBSTRATE SPECIFICITY and TRANSPORTER ACTIVITY of human SLC25A10 (multiple RHEA-referenced exchange reactions). Not in local cache; title taken from UniProt reference record.

title: Human mitochondrial carriers of the SLC25 family function as monomers exchanging substrates with a ping-pong kinetic mechanism.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt for FUNCTION and SUBUNIT (monomer; ping-pong mechanism). Not in local cache; title taken from UniProt reference record.

title: The sequence, bacterial expression, and functional reconstitution of the rat mitochondrial dicarboxylate transporter cloned via distant homologs in yeast and Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Foundational functional-reconstitution study of the DIC (rat ortholog); establishes dicarboxylate transport activity and the gluconeogenesis/ureogenesis physiological context. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Sequences of the human and bovine genes for the mitochondrial 2-oxoglutarate carrier.
review_notes: Original human/bovine OGC gene sequence paper; abstract establishes electroneutral 2-oxoglutarate/malate exchange across the inner membrane. The plasma-membrane annotation attributed to this paper is not supported by the abstract and is flagged as over-annotated.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
