review_notes: Full text available (PMC5840878); PCH1E disease association and independent confirmation of pro-fission function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source for a bare "protein binding" IPI. Correctly cited but not gene-function-specific.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization only.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO pipeline; assigns only the high-level "transmembrane transport" parent process.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: ISS transfer from the well-characterized paralog P51881; correctly assigns the core antiporter MF, inner-membrane location and ADP/ATP transport processes, plus the secondary uncoupling/mPTP/mitophagy roles.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAN-GO/GO_Central phylogenetic annotations; correctly captures the core antiporter MF, inner-membrane location, ATP-transport process and the mPTP- associated roles.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curation of immunofluorescence data
review_notes: HPA immunofluorescence supporting mitochondrial localization.

title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: Ensembl Compara transfer from the mouse orthologue; provides the secondary uncoupler/proton-transport/mPTP/mitophagy/thermogenesis and differentiation annotations, all By-similarity and treated here as non-core.

title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: Inter-ontology inference produced "adenine transport" from the incorrect "adenine transmembrane transporter activity"; ANT transports adenine nucleotides, not free adenine, so the inferred term has the wrong substrate.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA-assigned mitochondrion localization; correct compartment.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Multiple-method IEA pipeline; correctly assigns the core antiporter MF, inner- membrane location and mitochondrial ADP/ATP transport processes.

title: Regulation of insulin secretion by SIRT4, a mitochondrial ADP-ribosyltransferase.
review_notes: Source of a SIRT4-ANT2 IntAct interaction; the paper is primarily about SIRT4 and insulin secretion. Supports only an uninformative "protein binding".

title: The layered structure of human mitochondrial DNA nucleoids.
review_notes: ANT co-purifies with mtDNA nucleoids but the study notes several metabolic proteins in native nucleoids did not cross-link to mtDNA; association rather than functional nucleoid membership.

title: Capsaicin binds to prohibitin 2 and displaces it from the mitochondria to the nucleus.
review_notes: This capsaicin/prohibitin-2 paper is cited (IMP) for ANT2 nucleotide-transport activity and adenine nucleotide transport, but it does not measure ANT2 transport; it supports only a prohibitin-2 co-purification (protein binding).

title: Enzymatically inactive adenylate kinase 4 interacts with mitochondrial ADP/ATP translocase.
review_notes: Full text available; demonstrates co-immunoprecipitation of ANT with AK4, a physiologically plausible adenine-nucleotide-handling interaction. Supports only "protein binding" as an MF.

title: Identification of C2orf18, termed ANT2BP (ANT2-binding protein), as one of the key molecules involved in pancreatic carcinogenesis.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; identifies the ANT2-binding protein ANT2BP/C2orf18/SLC35F6 and links ANT2 to PDAC-cell proliferation and apoptosis. Source of the proliferation and OMM-permeabilization/apoptosis IMP annotations.

title: Proteomic analysis of increased Parkin expression and its interactants provides evidence for a role in modulation of mitochondrial function.
review_notes: Tandem-affinity-purification/MS lists SLC25A5 among Parkin (E3 ligase) interactants; supports the specific "ubiquitin protein ligase binding" MF.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane-proteome detection; supports only the over-general "membrane" location.

title: MMXD, a TFIIH-independent XPD-MMS19 protein complex involved in chromosome segregation.
review_notes: Directly identifies ANT2 as a component of the MMXD (MMS19-MIP18-XPD) complex implicated in chromosome segregation; basis of the GO:0071817 IDA annotation.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial phosphoproteome; supports mitochondrial localization.

title: Expression of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) inhibits the processing of uMtCK to induce cell death in a cell culture model system.
review_notes: Source of an LRRK2-ANT2 IntAct interaction; supports only "protein binding".

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome; the "nucleus" localization for this abundant mitochondrial carrier is most likely a co-purification background hit.

title: The human fibroblast adenine nucleotide translocator gene. Molecular cloning and sequence.
review_notes: Genomic cloning/sequence of the fibroblast (ANT2) gene; no transport assay and no localization experiment, yet cited (TAS) for "adenine transmembrane transporter activity" (wrong substrate) and "plasma membrane" location.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: High-throughput mRNA-interactome capture; abundant mitochondrial membrane proteins are frequent nonspecific hits, so the "RNA binding" MF is not a credible molecular function for ANT2.

title: Ribosomal protein s15 phosphorylation mediates LRRK2 neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: Source of an LRRK2-ANT2 IntAct interaction; supports only "protein binding".

title: Mitochondrial Protein Interaction Mapping Identifies Regulators of Respiratory Chain Function.
review_notes: Source of an ADCK2-ANT2 IntAct interaction; supports only "protein binding".

title: TSPO ligands stimulate ZnPPIX transport and ROS accumulation leading to the inhibition of P. falciparum growth in human blood.
review_notes: Full text available; detects ANT isoforms in erythrocyte (non-mitochondrial) membranes as part of a TSPO2-VDAC complex, the basis for UniProt's note that ANT2 may localize to non-mitochondrial membranes (the GO:0016020 IDA).

title: Human-Specific ARHGAP11B Acts in Mitochondria to Expand Neocortical Progenitors by Glutaminolysis.
review_notes: Shows human-specific ARHGAP11B enters mitochondria, interacts with ANT and inhibits the mPTP to expand basal progenitors; the key experimental support for ANT2's mPTP/apoptosis role in human cells.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization.

title: The E3 ligase TRIM1 ubiquitinates LRRK2 and controls its localization, degradation, and toxicity.
review_notes: Source of an LRRK2-ANT2 IntAct interaction; supports only "protein binding".

title: SLC25A5,6 dimers exchange ATP for ADP across the mitochondrial inner membrane
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the ADP/ATP exchange at the inner membrane; directly supports the core antiporter function and inner-membrane location.

title: Association of Vpr with ANT1
review_notes: Reactome host-virus reaction (HIV-1 Vpr/ANT); used here only to place ANT2 at the mitochondrial inner membrane.

title: LONP1 binds mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing ANT2 among LONP1-bound inner-membrane proteins; supports inner-membrane location.

title: LONP1 degrades mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome reaction placing ANT2 among LONP1-degraded inner-membrane proteins; supports inner-membrane location.

title: Influenza virus PB1-F2 protein induces cell death through mitochondrial ANT3 and VDAC1.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Identifies ANT3 as a direct interactor of influenza PB1-F2 and states its antiporter function and role in the permeability transition pore; supports the antiporter MF and the mPTP/apoptosis non-core annotations.

title: Phosphoproteome analysis of functional mitochondria isolated from resting human muscle reveals extensive phosphorylation of inner membrane protein complexes and enzymes.
review_notes: High-throughput mitochondrial phosphoproteome; supports mitochondrial localization (HDA) only, not a specific function.

title: Expression of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) inhibits the processing of uMtCK to induce cell death in a cell culture model system.
review_notes: Abstract-only; LRRK2-focused. Source of bare protein-binding IPI (VDAC1/LRRK2) via IntAct; does not inform ANT3 core function.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome methodology paper; source of a bare protein-binding IPI only.

title: Proteomic characterization of the human sperm nucleus.
review_notes: Sperm-nucleus proteome; ANT3 detection is most likely mitochondrial contamination. Basis for the nucleus HDA annotation, which is treated as over-annotation.

title: Ribosomal protein s15 phosphorylation mediates LRRK2 neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
review_notes: Abstract-only; LRRK2/Parkinson's study. Source of a bare protein-binding IPI (LRRK2) via IntAct; does not inform ANT3 core function.

title: DNA sequences of two expressed nuclear genes for human mitochondrial ADP/ATP translocase.
review_notes: Classic human ANT gene/sequence paper (Walker lab). Abstract states the ADP/ATP translocase transport role, supporting the core antiporter MF (NAS). Its use as the TAS reference for TIM23-complex membership is questionable.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome (BioPlex-type); source of multiple bare protein-binding IPIs. High-throughput, uninformative for core function.

title: TSPO ligands stimulate ZnPPIX transport and ROS accumulation leading to the inhibition of P. falciparum growth in human blood.
review_notes: Full text available. Detects ANT3 at protein level in erythrocyte membranes, supporting UniProt's TISSUE SPECIFICITY and the (over-general) 'membrane' IDA localization.

title: A Map of Human Mitochondrial Protein Interactions Linked to Neurodegeneration Reveals New Mechanisms of Redox Homeostasis and NF-κB Signaling.
review_notes: Mitochondrial interaction map; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (VDAC1). Consistent with ANT-VDAC association but uninformative as an MF.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: Interactome-perturbation dataset; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (AP2B1).

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (SLC25A4/ANT1).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome; supports mitochondrial localization (HTP) only.

title: The E3 ligase TRIM1 ubiquitinates LRRK2 and controls its localization, degradation, and toxicity.
review_notes: LRRK2/TRIM1 study; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (LRRK2) via IntAct.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: SLC superfamily interactome; source of a bare protein-binding IPI (SLC25A4/ANT1).

title: SLC25A5,6 dimers exchange ATP for ADP across the mitochondrial inner membrane
review_notes: Reactome reaction directly describing ANT3 (SLC25A6) ADP/ATP exchange at the inner membrane; supports both the core MF and the inner-membrane localization.

title: PB1-F2 binds to the mitochondrial adenine nucleotide translocator 3 ANT3, inducing apoptosis
review_notes: Reactome reaction for PB1-F2/ANT3 apoptosis; supports the inner-membrane localization TAS and the non-core apoptosis/mPTP annotations.

title: Association of Vpr with ANT1
review_notes: Reactome reaction (HIV-1 Vpr/ANT); used only as a TAS source for inner-membrane localization.

title: TIMM9:TIMM10 transfers proteins to TIMM22
review_notes: Reactome mitochondrial-import reaction; used only as a TAS source for inner-membrane localization. Notably this is the TIM22 (carrier) pathway, of which ANT is a substrate.

title: LONP1 binds mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome reaction; used only as a TAS source for inner-membrane localization.

title: LONP1 degrades mitochondrial inner membrane proteins
review_notes: Reactome reaction; used only as a TAS source for inner-membrane localization.

title: Human liver-specific very-long-chain acyl-coenzyme A synthetase: cDNA cloning and characterization of a second enzymatically active protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cloning and biochemical characterization of the human enzyme's acyl-CoA synthetase activity and ER localization.

title: The human liver-specific homolog of very long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase is cholate:CoA ligase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; establishes the defining cholate-CoA ligase activity.

title: Participation of two members of the very long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase family in bile acid synthesis and recycling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; broadens substrate profile and defines the recycling role.

title: FATP2 is a hepatic fatty acid transporter and peroxisomal very long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the knockdown assays are on FATP2 (SLC27A2), but the paper frames the FATP-family transporter/synthetase duality relevant to FATP5.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; high-throughput Y2H screen, no functional interpretation for SLC27A5.

title: Bile-acyl-CoA conjugation reaction (SLC27A5 BACS)
review_notes: Reactome reaction id returns 404 in the current ContentService and the local cache is empty (likely retired/renumbered); title is descriptive.

title: Genetic complementation reveals a novel human congenital disorder of glycosylation of type II, due to inactivation of the Golgi CMP-sialic acid transporter.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; primary IDA source establishing SLC35A1 as the CMP-sialic acid transporter and defining CDG2F. Abstract-only in cache; claims anchored to the GOA IDA evidence code and the abstract text.

title: Intellectual disability and bleeding diathesis due to deficient CMP--sialic acid transport.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; EXP source for Golgi localization and CDG2F. Confirms the disease variant impairs transport without mislocalizing the protein.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified high-throughput interactome; correctly cited but supports only uninformative bare protein-binding annotations, treated here as over-annotation.

title: Functional expression of human golgi CMP-sialic acid transporter in the Golgi complex of a transporter-deficient Chinese hamster ovary cell mutant.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; foundational functional/localization paper. Note the ProtInc TAS plasma-membrane annotation derived from this reference is not supported by the paper, which localizes the protein to the Golgi.

title: DAG1 glycosylations
review_notes: Reactome pathway used as TAS source for the protein O-linked glycosylation annotation; SLC35A1's role here is indirect (substrate supply), hence non-core.

title: SLC35A1,4 import CDP-ribitol
review_notes: Supports the secondary CDP-ribitol import activity (By-similarity in UniProt); basis for the non-core pyrimidine-nucleotide transporter annotation.

title: Molecular cloning and identification of 3'-phosphoadenosine 5'-phosphosulfate transporter.
review_notes: Original functional characterization of SLC35B2/PAPST1 as the Golgi PAPS transporter; abstract-only cache but the assay results are stated directly. Basis for the IDA MF/BP/CC annotations.

title: Large-scale identification and characterization of human genes that activate NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but this high-throughput overexpression screen is the sole basis for the NF-kappaB annotation and is mechanistically unlinked to the PAPS-transport function; treated as over-annotation.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Full text available. Large-scale interactome screen supporting only bare "protein binding"; no specific molecular function derivable for SLC35B2.

title: Biallelic variants in SLC35B2 cause a novel chondrodysplasia with hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
review_notes: Establishes human disease (HLD26) and links loss of SLC35B2 function to a proteoglycan sulfation defect; basis for the Golgi CC (EXP/IDA) and chondroitin sulfate PG biosynthesis (IMP) annotations.

title: The solute carrier superfamily interactome.
review_notes: Full text available. Large-scale AP-MS interactome supporting only bare "protein binding"; no specific molecular function derivable for SLC35B2.

title: SLC35B2,3 exchange cytosolic PAPS with Golgi PAP
review_notes: Accurately describes the PAPS:PAP antiport function. Note the derived GOA term GO:1902558 (5'-adenylyl sulfate/APS transport) uses the wrong metabolite versus the PAPS described here; reviewed as MODIFY to the PAPS transport term.

title: Molecular cloning and characterization of a novel 3'-phosphoadenosine 5'-phosphosulfate transporter, PAPST2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary characterization of SLC35B3/PAPST2. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false); the abstract directly supports the Golgi localization, PAPS transport activity (Km 2.2 uM), and role in sulfated-glycoconjugate synthesis. Underpins the IDA annotations (GO:0000139, GO:0046964).

title: SLC35B2,3 exchange cytosolic PAPS with Golgi PAP
review_notes: Reactome reaction describing SLC35B2/SLC35B3 exchanging cytosolic PAPS for Golgi PAP; supports the Golgi-membrane location and PAPS transporter activity. The companion GO:1902558 (5'-adenylyl sulfate / APS) process term names the wrong substrate (APS not PAPS) and is flagged as an over-annotation.

title: Inactivation of the glucose 6-phosphate transporter causes glycogen storage disease type 1b.
review_notes: Foundational functional characterization of recombinant G6PT; establishes that GSD-1b mutations disrupt G6P transport. Directly supports the antiporter/transport annotations.

title: Human variant glucose-6-phosphate transporter is active in microsomal transport.
review_notes: Shows isoform 2 (vG6PT) is an active microsomal G6P transporter working with glucose-6-phosphatase for glucose homeostasis; source of the isoform-2 annotations.

title: The signature motif in human glucose-6-phosphate transporter is essential for microsomal transport of glucose-6-phosphate.
review_notes: Signature-motif mutants lack microsomal G6P uptake; supports G6P transmembrane transporter activity and the G6P transport process.

title: The glucose-6-phosphate transporter is a phosphate-linked antiporter deficient in glycogen storage disease type Ib and Ic.
review_notes: Reconstituted-proteoliposome demonstration of the dual G6P/Pi antiport function and that GSD-Ib and GSD-Ic map to the same G6PT gene. Primary support for GO:0061513.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane proteomics of an NK-like cell line; only supports the generic "membrane" term, which is subsumed by the specific ER membrane localization.

title: A new variant of glycogen storage disease type I probably due to a defect in the glucose-6-phosphate transport system.
review_notes: Early clinical description of a GSD type I variant attributed to defective G6P transport; historical support for the ER/transport role.

title: SLC37A1 and SLC37A2 are phosphate-linked, glucose-6-phosphate antiporters.
review_notes: Although the title foregrounds SLC37A1/A2, the full text extensively characterizes G6PT/SLC37A4 as the physiological ER G6P:Pi antiporter (positive control), including CHA sensitivity, coupling to G6Pase-α, and ER localization. Strongly supports the SLC37A4 MF, BP and CC annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI high-throughput Y2H interactome; source of the bare "protein binding" (BIK) IPI. No established functional consequence for the antiporter; flagged as over-annotated.

title: SLC37A4-CDG: Mislocalization of the glucose-6-phosphate transporter to the Golgi causes a new congenital disorder of glycosylation.
review_notes: Establishes ER localization of wild-type SLC37A4 and that the dominant R423* variant mislocalizes to the Golgi causing CDG-IIw. Supports ER membrane localization.

title: A mutation in SLC37A4 causes a dominantly inherited congenital disorder of glycosylation characterized by liver dysfunction.
review_notes: Describes SLC37A4 as an ER-localized multitransmembrane protein required for transporting G6P into the ER; the dominant CDG variant. Supports transport and ER membrane annotations.

title: Sequence of a putative glucose 6-phosphate translocase, mutated in glycogen storage disease type Ib.
review_notes: Original cDNA cloning; identifies the protein as the G6P translocase functionally associated with glucose-6-phosphatase, with a C-terminal ER retention motif.

title: Luminal heterodimeric amino acid transporter defective in cystinuria.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and locally available full text were checked. The study directly separates the catalytic light-chain role from rBAT complex membership.

title: Differential influence of the 4F2 heavy chain and the protein related to b(0,+) amino acid transport on substrate affinity of the heteromeric b(0,+) amino acid transporter.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The co-expression study supports functional complex formation and a heavy-chain effect on substrate affinity, but it does not make SLC3A1 the catalytic permease.

title: rBAT-b(0,+)AT heterodimer is the main apical reabsorption system for cystine in the kidney.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Biochemical analysis of human and mouse kidney directly establishes the native brush-border heterodimer and its reabsorptive role.

title: The structural and functional units of heteromeric amino acid transporters. The heavy subunit rBAT dictates oligomerization of the heteromeric amino acid transporters.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. Native-state and functional assays establish rBAT-dependent heterotetramerization while delimiting the minimal transport unit to one heterodimer.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked, but the locally available text does not expose the SLC3A1 peptide-level result. The HDA localization is left undecided rather than overruled.

title: Cryo-EM structure of the human heteromeric amino acid transporter b(0,+)AT-rBAT.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC identity and full text were checked. Cryo-EM, biochemical transport, mutagenesis, and enzymatic assays define the heavy-chain role and exclude the InterPro-derived carbohydrate-metabolism interpretation.

title: Structural basis for amino acid exchange by a human heteromeric amino acid transporter.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The structure paper states the catalytic/accessory subunit boundary explicitly; full text was unavailable locally.

title: Cystinuria caused by mutations in rBAT, a gene involved in the transport of cystine.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. The genetics and oocyte phenotype establish SLC3A1 involvement in cystine/dibasic-amino-acid transport, but later work shows that the endogenous or coexpressed SLC7 light chain is catalytic.

title: Regional and subcellular distribution of a neutral and basic amino acid transporter in forebrain neurons containing nitric oxide synthase.
review_notes: PubMed identity and abstract were checked. This rat study is the experimental source behind the transferred human vacuolar-membrane annotation; relevance to normal human SLC3A1 biology remains context-specific.

title: Proton-associated sucrose transport of mammalian solute carrier family 45: an analysis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Bartolke et al., Biochem J 464(2):193-201, 2014. Correctly cited and not retracted, but methodologically weak as the sole basis of a molecular-function call: sucrose uptake was measured only in Saccharomyces cerevisiae heterologously expressing mouse SLC45A2/3/4, with Km around 5 mM. It is the seed for every sucrose annotation in this family, including the mouse IDAs that the human IBA and ISS derive from, and it is directly contradicted for the human protein by PMID:40836097 and PMID:41266324. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: Cached record title matches. High-throughput quantitative PDZ-domain holdup screen; supports a C-terminal PDZ-binding motif but gives no functional information about transport.

title: SLC45A4 is a pain gene encoding a neuronal polyamine transporter.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Middleton et al., Nature 646(8084):404-412, 2025 (Epub 2025 Aug 20), PMC12507699. The primary source for the plasma-membrane polyamine transporter assignment, the cryo-EM structure and the pain phenotype, and for the direct negative result on sucrose. Full text available and read.

title: Machine-learning-guided discovery of SLC25A45 as a mediator of mitochondrial methylated amino acid import and carnitine synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Khan et al., Cell Metab 37(11):2220-2232.e8, 2025, PMC12768559. The title names SLC25A45, not SLC45A4, so the GOA citation looks transposed - it is not. SLC45A4 is a co-equal subject of the paper, named in the abstract as a candidate plasma-membrane polyamine transporter and validated by isotope tracing in HEK293T knockout cells. Relevance marked MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the SLC45A4 evidence is metabolite-pool based, the authors state that definitive oocyte and proteoliposome assays remain to be done, and their observed direction (acetylpolyamine efflux) is not obviously the uptake the annotations imply.

title: SLC45A4 encodes a peroxisomal putrescine transporter that promotes GABA de novo synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Colson et al., Nat Commun 16(1):10198, 2025 (Nov 20), PMC12634670. Correctly cited and methodologically careful - endogenous protein, validated antibody, two independent peroxisome isolation methods. Marked DISPUTED because its central localisation claim (peroxisome membrane) is incompatible, as stated, with the plasma-membrane localisation reported three months earlier in Nature, and neither group has addressed the other. Not yet used by GOA.

title: Identification of receptors for pig endogenous retrovirus.
review_notes: Original identification of SLC52A1 (huPAR-2) as a PERV-A receptor; establishes it is a widespread, multi-membrane-spanning plasma-membrane protein whose biological function was then unknown. Abstract-only cache.

title: Identification and functional characterization of a novel human and rat riboflavin transporter, RFT1.
review_notes: Cloning and functional characterization of hRFT1 (SLC52A1) as a riboflavin transporter; plasma-membrane localization of GFP-tagged protein and increased [3H]riboflavin accumulation on overexpression. Abstract-only cache.

title: Identification and comparative functional characterization of a new human riboflavin transporter hRFT3 expressed in the brain.
review_notes: Comparative characterization of hRFT1/2/3; provides hRFT1 riboflavin uptake kinetics (KM ~1.38 uM) and plasma-membrane localization. Abstract-only cache.

title: Differential expression of human riboflavin transporters -1, -2, and -3 in polarized epithelia: a key role for hRFT-2 in intestinal riboflavin uptake.
review_notes: Full text available; live-cell confocal imaging places hRFT-1 (SLC52A1) mainly at the basolateral membrane of polarized Caco-2/MDCK cells and demonstrates RFVT1-mediated riboflavin uptake.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale HuRI binary (Y2H) interactome; source of the IntAct "protein binding" IPI annotations for SLC52A1. The hits (e.g. SLC7A1, IFNGR2, GJA8) are high-throughput and uncharacterized for RFVT1 function; supports only bare, uninformative protein binding.

title: SLC52A1 is a neofunctionalized primate urate transporter enabling intestinal urate secretion.
review_notes: Full text available; demonstrates primate/human SLC52A1 transports urate as well as riboflavin and, basolaterally in enterocytes, works with ABCG2 to secrete urate into the intestine. Basis of the urate-transport IDA annotations.

title: Cloning and functional characterization of a gamma-hydroxybutyrate receptor identified in the human brain.
review_notes: Cloned GPR172A/GHBh1 (= SLC52A2) as a putative GHB receptor. The GHB-receptor function is now superseded by the protein's identity as riboflavin transporter RFVT2; UniProt retains it only as "Probable". Basis of the GO:0062124 IDA (marked over-annotated) and one plasma-membrane IDA (accepted; localization is sound).

title: Identification and comparative functional characterization of a new human riboflavin transporter hRFT3 expressed in the brain.
review_notes: "hRFT3" in this paper is SLC52A2/RFVT2 (older Inui-lab nomenclature; KM 0.33 uM matches UniProt). Directly establishes Na+-independent riboflavin transport and brain-enriched expression. Abstract only (full text unavailable); claims anchored to abstract text and UniProt.

title: Differential expression of human riboflavin transporters -1, -2, and -3 in polarized epithelia: a key role for hRFT-2 in intestinal riboflavin uptake.
review_notes: Nomenclature caution: this paper's "hRFT-3" is SLC52A2 (this gene), while "hRFT-2" is SLC52A3. The GO:0016323 basolateral IDA to Q9HAB3 corresponds to hRFT-3, described as mostly intracellular vesicles with some BLM signal. Full text available and consistent.

title: Treatable childhood neuronopathy caused by mutations in riboflavin transporter RFVT2.
review_notes: Definitive RFVT2/SLC52A2 study: BVVLS2 gene, in-vitro 3H-riboflavin transport assays for 7 mutants, plasma-membrane expression of WT and W31S, and clinical response to high-dose riboflavin. Full text available.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Systematic human interactome map; source of the bare "protein binding" IPI with CDC23. Interactor matches UniProt INTERACTION; provides no functional insight for SLC52A2 (annotation marked over-annotated).

title: SLC52A2 [p.P141T] and SLC52A3 [p.N21S] causing Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere Syndrome in an Indian patient: First genetically proven case with mutations in two riboflavin transporters.
review_notes: Case with SLC52A2 p.P141T; 3H-RF uptake and confocal imaging show WT hRFVT-2 (SLC52A2) is membrane-localized and transports riboflavin (mutant slightly reduced). Full text available.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome; source of the bare "protein binding" IPI with FAM209A (matches UniProt INTERACTION). No functional insight for SLC52A2 (annotation marked over-annotated).

title: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) metabolism
review_notes: Pathway context. SLC52A2 is a transporter, not a metabolic enzyme; the GO:0006771 "riboflavin metabolic process" TAS derived from this pathway is marked over-annotated in favor of GO:0032218 riboflavin transport.

title: SLC52A1,2,3 transport RIB from extracellular region to cytosol
review_notes: Reactome reaction correctly modelling SLC52A2 as a plasma-membrane riboflavin transporter; supports the core MF and CC.

title: Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere syndrome, a ponto-bulbar palsy with deafness, is caused by mutations in c20orf54.
review_notes: Disease-gene discovery paper identifying C20orf54 (SLC52A3) mutations as the cause of Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere syndrome. Supports the disease association. Abstract-only in cache. The derived GO annotation "sensory perception of sound" is a phenotype-to- process over-annotation (deafness is a downstream consequence of riboflavin transporter deficiency), not a molecular hearing role.

title: Identification and comparative functional characterization of a new human riboflavin transporter hRFT3 expressed in the brain.
review_notes: Cloning and functional characterization of the human riboflavin transporter that UniProt/GOA map to SLC52A3 (Q9NQ40). The paper's local name "hRFT3" corresponds to SLC52A3/RFVT3. Supports core transporter activity, riboflavin transport, membrane localization, and kinetics. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Differential expression of human riboflavin transporters -1, -2, and -3 in polarized epithelia: a key role for hRFT-2 in intestinal riboflavin uptake.
review_notes: Full text available. Uses the Said-lab nomenclature in which "hRFT-2" is the 469-aa C20orf54 product = SLC52A3/RFVT3 (exclusively apical, key intestinal transporter); note that this paper's separate "hRFT-3" is a different SLC52 member. GOA correctly attributes the apical-localization and intestinal-uptake data for "hRFT-2" to Q9NQ40 (SLC52A3).

title: Effect of clinical mutations on functionality of the human riboflavin transporter-2 (hRFT-2).
review_notes: Full text available. "hRFT-2" here = C20orf54 = SLC52A3. Functional characterization of BVVLS clinical mutations in Caco-2 cells (uptake, membrane targeting) supports RFVT3 riboflavin transport activity, plasma-membrane localization, and the disease mechanism.

title: Functional involvement of RFVT3/SLC52A3 in intestinal riboflavin absorption.
review_notes: Directly names RFVT3/SLC52A3. Apical riboflavin uptake in T84 cells and mouse jejunum/ileum, methylene-blue inhibition, RFVT3 siRNA. Strongly supports apical localization, transporter activity, and intestinal absorption. Abstract-only in cache.

title: SLC52A2 [p.P141T] and SLC52A3 [p.N21S] causing Brown-Vialetto-Van Laere Syndrome in an Indian patient: First genetically proven case with mutations in two riboflavin transporters.
review_notes: Full text available. Functional characterization of the SLC52A3 p.N21S variant (drastically reduced RF uptake, ER retention / loss of membrane expression), supporting plasma-membrane localization and the transport/disease mechanism.

title: SLC52A3 expression is activated by NF-κB p65/Rel-B and serves as a prognostic biomarker in esophageal cancer.
review_notes: Full text available. Establishes the two transcript variants (SLC52A3a isoform 1, SLC52A3b isoform 2), their differential localization (isoform 2 cytoplasmic), and a cancer/NF-kB context. Basis for the cytoplasm/nuclear-membrane localizations, which are non-core (isoform- and cancer-context specific).

title: Identification of transmembrane protein 237 as a novel interactor with the intestinal riboflavin transporter-3 (RFVT-3): role in functionality and cell biology.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Identifies TMEM237 (Q96Q45) as a functional RFVT-3 interactor that modulates RF uptake and RFVT-3 stability; supports transporter activity, riboflavin transport and intestinal absorption. The IPI "protein binding" to TMEM237 is a real interaction but generic; flagged as over-annotated.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Large-scale yeast two-hybrid neurodegeneration interactome; the RFVT3 interactions (ATXN3, DNM2, TOR1A) are screen-scale and yield only the uninformative "protein binding" term (over-annotated). Not informative about RFVT3's molecular function.

title: Human placental taurine transporter in uncomplicated and IUGR pregnancies: cellular localization, protein expression, and regulation.
review_notes: Supports microvillous (apical) plasma-membrane localization of placental TAUT by immunocytochemistry; abstract-only cache but title/finding match.

title: Taurine uptake across the human intestinal brush-border membrane is via two transporters: H+-coupled PAT1 (SLC36A1) and Na+- and Cl(-)-dependent TauT (SLC6A6).
review_notes: Full text available; directly characterizes TauT as a Na+/Cl−-dependent, high-affinity, low-capacity taurine and beta-alanine transporter at the intestinal apical membrane.

title: Taurine transport in human placental trophoblast is important for regulation of cell differentiation and survival.
review_notes: Full text available; RNAi TauT knockdown reduces intracellular taurine and compromises trophoblast differentiation and survival (IMP source).

title: Neurotransmitter transporter family including SLC6A6 and SLC6A13 contributes to the 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA)-induced accumulation of protoporphyrin IX and photodamage, through uptake of ALA by cancerous cells.
review_notes: Establishes SLC6A6-mediated uptake of the amino-acid analogue ALA in cancer cells (substrate promiscuity / drug delivery), not a canonical physiological taurine role.

title: Establishment and Dysfunction of the Blood-Brain Barrier.
review_notes: General BBB review; cached text does not specifically establish SLC6A6 as a blood-brain-barrier taurine transporter. Weak support for the NAS transport-across-BBB annotation.

title: LC-MS/MS Based Quantitation of ABC and SLC Transporter Proteins in Plasma Membranes of Cultured Primary Human Retinal Pigment Epithelium Cells and Immortalized ARPE19 Cell Line.
review_notes: Quantitative proteomics detecting TAUT in RPE plasma membranes; supports plasma-membrane localization.

title: Blood-Brain Barrier: From Physiology to Disease and Back.
review_notes: Comprehensive BBB physiology review; cached text does not specifically establish an SLC6A6 BBB transport role. Weak support for the NAS annotation.

title: Biallelic mutation of human SLC6A6 encoding the taurine transporter TAUT is linked to early retinal degeneration.
review_notes: HTRDC patient study; variant A78E severely decreases taurine transport, establishes disease link and plasma-membrane localization.

title: Quantitative Protein Expression in the Human Retinal Pigment Epithelium: Comparison Between Apical and Basolateral Plasma Membranes With Emphasis on Transporters.
review_notes: Quantitative apical/basolateral RPE membrane proteomics; supports apical and basolateral plasma-membrane localization of TAUT.

title: Taurine treatment of retinal degeneration and cardiomyopathy in a consanguineous family with SLC6A6 taurine transporter deficiency.
review_notes: HTRDC family; variant G399V decreases taurine transport, and taurine supplementation treats the phenotype. Supports core MF/BP/CC.

title: Structural basis of augmenting taurine uptake by the taurine transporter in alleviating cellular senescence.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure and functional data on taurine uptake by TauT; links augmented taurine uptake to senescence alleviation.

title: Dimerization and substrate recognition of human taurine transporter.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structures of TauT bound to taurine and GABA; substrate recognition and (unconfirmed) dimerization. Supports core MF and GABA activity.

title: Molecular basis of human taurine transporter uptake and inhibition.
review_notes: Eleven cryo-EM structures with taurine and analogues (beta-alanine, guanidinoacetate, GABA) and inhibitors; confirms Na+/Cl−-dependent taurine uptake and substrate specificity residues.

title: Structural determination of the human taurine transporter TauT reveals the mechanism of substrate and inhibitor recognition.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structures of the Na+/Cl−-dependent TauT (KM 7.62 uM) bound to taurine and analogues; supports core MF and secondary beta-alanine/GABA activities.

title: SLC6A6 imports taurine into mitochondria to sustain mitochondrial translation and tumour growth.
review_notes: Establishes a mitochondrial-inner-membrane pool of SLC6A6 importing taurine for mt-tRNA modification/mitochondrial translation; PKA controls plasma-membrane vs mitochondrial localization.

title: Functional characterization and chromosomal localization of a cloned taurine transporter from human placenta.
review_notes: Original functional cloning of the human placental taurine transporter; Na+/Cl−-dependent, 2:1:1 stoichiometry, high affinity, tissue expression.

title: Cloning of the human taurine transporter and characterization of taurine uptake in thyroid cells.
review_notes: Original cloning from human thyroid; expression confers taurine uptake, which is regulated by thyrotropin via cAMP.

title: Isolation of a cDNA encoding a taurine transporter in the human retinal pigment epithelium.
review_notes: RPE clone; Na+/Cl−-dependent taurine uptake (KM ~2 uM) inhibited by taurine, beta-alanine and GABA but not alpha-alanine — establishes beta-amino-acid specificity.

title: Human, rat and chicken small intestinal Na+ - Cl- -creatine transporter: functional, molecular characterization and localization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; directly establishes transport stoichiometry, substrate specificity (no GABA/choline transport), and apical localization.

title: Functional characterization of missense variants in the creatine transporter gene (SLC6A8): improved diagnostic application.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; functional creatine-uptake assays of SLC6A8 variants (IMP support for the symporter activity).

title: Functional and electrophysiological characterization of four non-truncating mutations responsible for creatine transporter (SLC6A8) deficiency syndrome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; electrophysiology + transport assays; IMP for symporter activity and plasma membrane localization.

title: Negative regulation of the creatine transporter SLC6A8 by SPAK and OSR1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; SPAK/OSR1 (WNK-controlled) kinases negatively regulate SLC6A8 activity. Basis of the ISS symporter annotation.

title: Estimated carrier frequency of creatine transporter deficiency in females in the general population using functional characterization of novel missense variants in the SLC6A8 gene.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; functional creatine-uptake characterization of novel SLC6A8 variants (IMP for symporter activity and creatine transport).

title: The cloning and expression of a human creatine transporter.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; original cloning and IDA of sodium-dependent creatine uptake.

title: Cloning, pharmacological characterization, and genomic localization of the human creatine transporter.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; original cloning, IDA of creatine uptake, substrate specificity, tissue expression.

title: Identification of a testis-expressed creatine transporter gene at 16p11.2 and confirmation of the X-linked locus to Xq28.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cited for NAS creatine transporter activity/transport; distinguishes the X-linked SLC6A8 locus (Xq28) from the testis CT2 gene.

title: The genomic organization of a human creatine transporter (CRTR) gene located in Xq28.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as a genomic-organization paper; cited as TAS for muscle contraction (GO:0006936), which it does not directly establish. The muscle-contraction link is an indirect physiological inference, kept as non-core.

title: Molecular characterization of the human CRT-1 creatine transporter expressed in Xenopus oocytes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; IDA of Na+/Cl--dependent creatine symport with kinetic parameters.

title: Lithium-calcium exchange is mediated by a distinct potassium-independent sodium-calcium exchanger.
review_notes: J Biol Chem 2004; verified. Founding characterisation of NCLX as a K+-independent exchanger that uniquely catalyses Li+/Ca2+ exchange - the earliest signal that its monovalent selectivity is not canonical. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: NCLX is an essential component of mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchange.
review_notes: PNAS 2010; verified. The paper that identified NCLX as the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchanger and the source of most of this gene's experimental annotations. Correctly cited, but its central identification is now directly challenged by PMID:40931067, which reports intact mito-NCX in four independent NCLX-knockout lines.

title: The mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchanger upregulates glucose dependent Ca2+ signalling linked to insulin secretion.
review_notes: PLoS One 2012; verified. Supports the mitochondrial location and the beta-cell insulin-secretion phenotype.

title: NCLX protein, but not LETM1, mediates mitochondrial Ca2+ extrusion, thereby limiting Ca2+-induced NAD(P)H production and modulating matrix redox state.
review_notes: J Biol Chem 2014; verified. Independent replication that NCLX, and not LETM1, carries matrix calcium extrusion, and links it to NAD(P)H and matrix redox.

title: Identification of residues that control Li(+) versus Na(+) dependent Ca(2+) exchange at the transport site of the mitochondrial NCLX.
review_notes: Biochim Biophys Acta 2017; verified. Mutagenesis identifying separate Na+- and Li+-selective residues in the NCLX transport site. Important counter-evidence to the structural claim that NCLX has no monovalent-selective sites. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: Mitochondria control store-operated Ca(2+) entry through Na(+) and redox signals.
review_notes: EMBO J 2017; verified. Establishes the NCLX-dependent redox link to store-operated calcium entry through Orai1.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial residence.

title: TMEM65 regulates and is required for NCLX-dependent mitochondrial calcium efflux.
review_notes: Nat Metab 2025; verified. Cited here for context: TMEM65 is reported as an NCLX binding partner required for NCLX-dependent mitochondrial calcium efflux, which bears on whether NCLX is the transporter.

title: TMEM65 functions as the mitochondrial Na(+)/Ca(2+) exchanger.
review_notes: Nat Cell Biol 2025; verified. Cited here for context: it assigns mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchange to TMEM65 rather than NCLX. Its conclusion is contradicted by PMID:40200126, and its liposome assay measures 45Ca2+ accumulation rather than transmembrane flux (PMID:41061666).

title: Structure and mechanism of the mitochondrial calcium transporter NCLX.
review_notes: Nature 2025; verified (title, journal and year match the cached record). Cryo-EM structures plus functional reassignment of NCLX to H+/Ca2+ exchange, and the report that mito-NCX survives NCLX knockout. Correctly cited, but contradicted on the counterion by PMID:42431881 and on the transport-site residues by PMID:28130126. Note that it shares senior authors with PMID:40691517 (TMEM65 as mito-NCX); the two papers are one model, not two independent challenges.

title: Mitochondrial sodium-calcium exchange-Can TMEM65 do it alone?
review_notes: Cell Metab 2025 commentary; verified. Frames the TMEM65-versus-NCLX dispute and identifies the binding-versus-translocation gap in the TMEM65 liposome assay. Written by the authors of PMID:40200126, so not a neutral referee.

title: Molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial Ca(2+) exchanger NCLX.
review_notes: Nat Commun 2026; verified. Independent cryo-EM study that reproduces the structural observation (missing Na+-coordinating residues, trimeric assembly) but concludes broader selectivity rather than H+ specificity, and explicitly declines to adjudicate the TMEM65 question.

title: Expression and localization of the uptake transporters OATP2B1, OATP3A1 and OATP5A1 in non-malignant and malignant breast tissue.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Kindla et al., Cancer Biol Ther 11(6):584-91, 2011. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false). Supports plasma membrane localisation of endogenous OATP5A1 in human breast ductal epithelium, which is the strongest localisation evidence in the record because it is neither heterologous nor overexpressed. Says nothing about substrates or polarity. Same group as PMID:42231149, so not fully independent of it.

title: Deorphanisation and functional characterisation of OATP5A1 as transport protein for amino acids and vitamins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Kohlmann et al., Cell Mol Biol Lett 31(1):75, 2026 (Jun 2), PMC13231527. Full text available and read. The sole source for every substrate claim about OATP5A1, and correctly cited for all of them. Marked LOW_QUALITY not because the work is poorly done - the controls (4 degree Celsius counter-controls, saturation kinetics with six biological replicates, inhibitor panels, thiamine background depletion) are appropriate - but because the entire substrate profile rests on one laboratory and one heterologous overexpression system, and because the paper itself reports that its flagship substrate, estrone-3-sulfate, was NOT taken up in two earlier oocyte studies. The single-lab status is the reason the specific molecular functions are recorded here as NEW reviewer proposals rather than asserted.

title: Secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor mediates non-redundant functions necessary for normal wound healing.
review_notes: Slpi-null mice show impaired cutaneous wound healing with increased inflammation and elastase activity and enhanced local TGF-beta activation.

title: Conversion of proepithelin to epithelins: roles of SLPI and elastase in host defense and wound repair.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Documents that SLPI forms complexes with proepithelin (progranulin, GRN) and protects it from elastase-mediated conversion to epithelins, linking SLPI's antiprotease activity to wound repair.

title: Secretory leucoprotease inhibitor binds to NF-kappaB binding sites in monocytes and inhibits p65 binding.
review_notes: SLPI enters monocytes, localizes to cytoplasm and nucleus, and inhibits NF-kappaB activation partly by binding NF-kappaB consensus DNA sites and blocking p65. Provides sequence-specific support for nuclear DNA binding distinct from the nonspecific charge binding of PMID:2467900.

title: Complex of human neutrophil elastase with 1/2SLPI.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human neutrophil elastase with the recombinant C-terminal domain of SLPI; confirms the C-terminal domain is sufficient for elastase inhibition and identifies the P1 and selectivity residues.

title: The major bactericidal activity of human seminal plasma is zinc-dependent and derived from fragmentation of the semenogelins.
review_notes: Full text available. SLPI was identified among antibacterial polypeptides in seminal plasma gel-overlay clearance zones, but the authors state its contribution to bactericidal activity is minor relative to semenogelin peptides. Supports presence/secretion and a contributory antibacterial role.

title: Proteomic analysis of human parotid gland exosomes by multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
review_notes: High-throughput proteomic detection of SLPI in parotid exosome fractions; supports an extracellular/exosome localization but not a specific function.

title: The phospholipid scramblases 1 and 4 are cellular receptors for the secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor and interact with CD4 at the plasma membrane.
review_notes: Full text available. SLPI binds PLSCR1 and PLSCR4 and disrupts the PLSCR1-CD4 association, a mechanism for its anti-HIV-1 activity at a post-binding, pre-reverse-transcription step.

title: Proteomics characterization of extracellular space components in the human aorta.
review_notes: High-throughput ECM proteomics of human aorta; supports extracellular/ECM localization only.

title: A lack of secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor (SLPI) causes defects in granulocytic differentiation.
review_notes: SLPI knockdown in CD34+ progenitors impairs myeloid differentiation via NF-kappaB/ERK/LEF-1; a reciprocal regulatory relationship with neutrophil elastase (ELANE). Supports a role in myelopoiesis, likely indirect.

title: Secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor binding to mRNA and DNA as a possible cause of toxicity to Escherichia coli.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but describes a recombinant-overexpression artifact: the cationic SLPI binds mRNA and DNA via nonspecific charge interactions (like lysozyme) when overexpressed in E. coli, inhibiting translation and causing host toxicity. The authors frame this as a general problem of basic recombinant proteins, not a physiological nucleic-acid-binding function.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Systematic high-throughput Y2H interactome map; SLPI interactions reported here are generic binary hits without functional interpretation.

title: Characterization of the Extracellular Matrix of Normal and Diseased Tissues Using Proteomics.
review_notes: High-throughput ECM proteomics; supports extracellular/ECM localization only.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Systematic high-throughput binary interactome (HuRI); the SLPI interactions are generic, functionally uninterpreted hits.

title: The 2.5 A X-ray crystal structure of the acid-stable proteinase inhibitor from human mucous secretions analysed in its complex with bovine alpha-chymotrypsin.
review_notes: Crystal structure of SLPI with chymotrypsin; localizes the elastase/ chymotrypsin reactive-site loop (scissile Leu-Met bond) to the second (C-terminal) domain.

title: Isolation, properties, and complete amino acid sequence of human secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor, a potent inhibitor of leukocyte elastase.
review_notes: Foundational paper: purification from parotid secretions and demonstration that SLPI is a potent inhibitor of leukocyte elastase, cathepsin G and trypsin, with the inhibitory activities assigned to the two domains.

title: The acid-stable proteinase inhibitor of human mucous secretions (HUSI-I, antileukoprotease). Complete amino acid sequence as revealed by protein and cDNA sequencing and structural homology to whey proteins and Red Sea turtle proteinase inhibitor.
review_notes: Complete amino acid sequence and two-domain four-disulfide-core architecture; establishes the WAP/whey-protein family relationship.

title: Secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor: a human saliva protein exhibiting anti-human immunodeficiency virus 1 activity in vitro.
review_notes: Identifies SLPI as the salivary factor responsible for anti-HIV-1 activity, targeting a host-cell-associated molecule rather than the virus directly.

title: Antibacterial activity of antileukoprotease.
review_notes: Recombinant SLPI (ALP) kills E. coli and S. aureus in vitro; the antibacterial activity resides largely in the N-terminal domain, which is distinct from the C-terminal antiprotease domain.

title: Secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor: a macrophage product induced by and antagonistic to bacterial lipopolysaccharide.
review_notes: SLPI is an LPS-induced macrophage product; transfection suppresses LPS-induced NF-kappaB activation and production of NO and TNF-alpha. Basis for the response-to-LPS and anti-inflammatory annotations (mouse, By similarity to human).

title: Inhibition of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 infectivity by secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor occurs prior to viral reverse transcription.
review_notes: SLPI blocks HIV-1 infection of monocytes at or before viral DNA synthesis (after virus binding, before reverse transcription), via a host-cell receptor and independently of antiprotease activity.

title: Falcon deep research report for human SLPI
review_notes: Provider-generated literature synthesis that completed after the review was written. Reconciled against the review: consistent with the C-terminal WAP domain serine protease inhibitor (P1 Leu72; neutrophil elastase and cathepsin G as principal targets), extracellular mucosal location, nuclear NF-kappaB-site competition (PMID:16352738), and secondary antimicrobial and anti-HIV activities already anchored to cached primary papers. Its additional items (Eisenberg 1990 Leu72 mutagenesis, NE cleavage of SLPI in CF airways, 2024 mouse airway model, clinical registry entries) did not warrant annotation changes; it is not used as sole evidence for any GO decision.

title: Coordination of structure-specific nucleases by human SLX4/BTBD12 is required for DNA repair.
review_notes: Primary paper identifying human SLX4 as a scaffold for XPF-ERCC1, MUS81-EME1 and SLX1 and showing SLX4 enhances their nuclease activity; supporting quotes verified verbatim against the cached record.

title: Drosophila MUS312 and the vertebrate ortholog BTBD12 interact with DNA structure-specific endonucleases in DNA repair and recombination.
review_notes: Establishes orthology of BTBD12/SLX4 to MUS312/Slx4 and its role directing HJ resolution and ICL repair; quotes verified.

title: Mammalian BTBD12/SLX4 assembles a Holliday junction resolvase and is required for DNA repair.
review_notes: Defines the SLX4 multiprotein complex and the SLX1-SLX4 HJ resolvase; source of the enzyme activator activity and complex-membership annotations. Quotes verified verbatim.

title: Human SLX4 is a Holliday junction resolvase subunit that binds multiple DNA repair/recombination endonucleases.
review_notes: Independently identifies SLX4 as a docking platform for XPF-ERCC1, MUS81-EME1 and SLX1 required for ICL repair; quotes verified.

title: Mutations of the SLX4 gene in Fanconi anemia.
review_notes: Establishes biallelic SLX4 mutations as a Fanconi anemia subtype (FANCP) and that SLX4 loss does not affect FANCD2 monoubiquitination; full text verified.

title: SLX4, a coordinator of structure-specific endonucleases, is mutated in a new Fanconi anemia subtype.
review_notes: Companion FANCP-defining paper describing the first individuals with biallelic SLX4 mutations; abstract verified.

title: FBH1 co-operates with MUS81 in inducing DNA double-strand breaks and cell death following replication stress.
review_notes: Cited by MGI for the SLX4 GO:0072429 (intra-S checkpoint) annotation, but the cached abstract concerns FBH1 and MUS81, not SLX4, and full text is unavailable; SLX4-specific support could not be verified.

title: SLX4 assembles a telomere maintenance toolkit by bridging multiple endonucleases with telomeres.
review_notes: Source of the telomere-maintenance / t-circle / D-loop annotations; shows the SLX4-TRF2 scaffold bridges SLX1/XPF/MUS81 to telomeres. Quotes verified.

title: XPF-ERCC1 acts in Unhooking DNA interstrand crosslinks in cooperation with FANCD2 and FANCP/SLX4.
review_notes: Xenopus egg-extract reconstitution showing XPF-ERCC1 cooperates with SLX4/FANCP to perform the unhooking incisions of replication-coupled ICL repair, and that XPF-ERCC1/SLX4 recruitment depends on ubiquitylated FANCD2. Provides the mechanistic basis for SLX4's core ICL-repair role; supporting quote verified verbatim against the cached full text.

title: Mouse SLX4 is a tumor suppressor that stimulates the activity of the nuclease XPF-ERCC1 in DNA crosslink repair.
review_notes: Demonstrates that the N-terminal mini-SLX4 (XPF-ERCC1-binding only) is sufficient for crosslink resistance and enhances XPF-ERCC1 nuclease activity up to 100-fold, directing fork specificity and stimulating dual incisions at a crosslink. Directly quantifies SLX4's enzyme-activator function; quote verified verbatim against the cached full text.

title: The SLX4 complex is a SUMO E3 ligase that impacts on replication stress outcome and genome stability.
review_notes: Primary biochemical/cell-biological evidence that the SLX4 complex is a SUMO E3 ligase (SUMOylating SLX4 and XPF via a specific SLX4-UBC9 interaction, SIMs and BTB domain). Source of the NEW SUMO ligase activity annotation; SIMs are dispensable for ICL repair but the activity prevents mitotic catastrophe at common fragile sites. Quote verified verbatim against the cached abstract.

title: Integrative analysis of kinase networks in TRAIL-induced apoptosis provides a source of potential targets for combination therapy.
review_notes: High-throughput kinase-network study; source of a generic PLK1 protein-binding IPI, uninformative for SLX4 molecular function.

title: An interactome perturbation framework prioritizes damaging missense mutations for developmental disorders.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome dataset; generic protein-binding IPI only.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI proteome-scale two-hybrid map; generic protein-binding IPI only.

title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
review_notes: Large-scale kinase interaction network; generic protein-binding IPI only.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex proteome-scale AP-MS network; generic protein-binding IPI only.

title: Exploring the Structures and Functions of Macromolecular SLX4-Nuclease Complexes in Genome Stability.
review_notes: Review of SLX4-nuclease complexes; cited (NAS) for a broad DNA replication annotation that over-annotates SLX4's replication-associated repair role.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Multimodal cell-map foundation dataset; generic protein-binding IPI only.

title: Development of a yeast-based system to identify new hBRAFV600E functional interactors.
review_notes: Abstract only. It is the only study of SMIM10 protein. Its effects come from overexpression and are described as indirect, so they support no MF or BP term. The mitochondrial localization is asserted, but the method cannot be checked from the abstract.

title: From PREDs and open reading frames to cDNA isolation: revisiting the human chromosome 21 transcription map.
review_notes: Abstract only. Establishes that the transcript exists; contains nothing on protein function.

title: Ubiquilins Chaperone and Triage Mitochondrial Membrane Proteins for Degradation.
review_notes: Not about SMIM11; cited to interpret the UBQLN2 interaction as transmembrane-domain client recognition.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI yeast two-hybrid map; source of all three SMIM11 IPI rows. High-throughput, no functional follow-up on SMIM11.

title: SMIM12 - The Human Protein Atlas
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas record inspected programmatically on 2026-10-03 (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000163866.json): immunofluorescence main location Mitochondria, reliability Approved; RNA low tissue specificity, detected in all tissues.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Source of the three yeast two-hybrid protein binding rows (matches the GOA reference and the UniProt INTERACTION block). Abstract-only in cache; SMIM12 is not mentioned in the abstract. High-throughput screen with no SMIM12-specific follow-up.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: MitoCoP proteome; source of the HTP mitochondrion row. SMIM12 appears only in supplementary data, not in the main text.

title: SMIM13 - The Human Protein Atlas
review_notes: Human Protein Atlas record inspected programmatically on 2026-10-03 (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000224531.json): immunofluorescence reliability Approved, main location Nucleoplasm, additional Nuclear membrane and Golgi apparatus; RNA tissue enhanced in brain. Single-antibody data, not used to support an annotation.

title: SMIM14 - The Human Protein Atlas
review_notes: Inspected programmatically on 2026-10-03 (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000163683.json): RNA tissue enhanced in liver; single-cell enhanced in hepatocytes, goblet cells and oesophageal apical cells. No immunofluorescence localisation data.

title: Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets.
review_notes: Stitch-seq Y2H method paper; source of the FATE1 protein binding row (matches GOA). SMIM14 is not discussed in the text.

title: Characterization of the cellular localization of C4orf34 as a novel endoplasmic reticulum resident protein.
review_notes: The only study of SMIM14 itself (full text cached). Localisation and topology data are sound for overexpressed constructs. The proposed roles in Ca2+ homeostasis and ER stress are speculative and untested (the single ER-stress experiment was negative). The abstract's claim of conservation to invertebrates is not shown for C4orf34, whose alignment covers only vertebrates.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI; source of four protein binding rows (FATE1, SGTA, SLPI, TMEM42), matching GOA and the UniProt INTERACTION block.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Source of the SPRED1 protein binding row. Abstract-only in cache.

title: SMIM15 - The Human Protein Atlas

review_notes: PubMed-verified (PMID:39261662, doi:10.1038/s44318-024-00193-3, EMBO J 2024). Notable new finding - SPCS3 acts as an antiviral restriction factor against CHIKV (an alphavirus, distinct from the flaviviral host-factor role) via E1 binding; Falcon reports this is peptidase-independent (overexpression did not alter CHIKV polyglycoprotein cleavage). A secondary host-pathogen/innate-immunity role, not the core SPC function. Not in publications cache, so no verbatim supporting_text added.

title: Cloning of ACP33 as a novel intracellular ligand of CD4.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2001;276:9123-32). Correctly cited and not contradicted; the CD4 interaction and the domain mapping are real. Its limitation is scope, not soundness - one screen, one cell context, no replication in twenty-five years - which is why the annotations derived from it are kept as non-core. Its most durable contribution is the observation that the alpha/beta hydrolase fold of this protein is non-catalytic and serves as an interaction module. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: Maspardin is mutated in mast syndrome, a complicated form of hereditary spastic paraplegia associated with dementia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Am J Hum Genet 2003;73:1147-56). The origin of both the gene-disease link and the catalytic-triad claim. The triad analysis is an alignment argument, explicitly hedged in the paper as 'suggests that it is unlikely to possess enzymatic function'; every later source traces back to it.

title: Interaction of the SPG21 protein ACP33/maspardin with the aldehyde dehydrogenase ALDH16A1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neurogenetics 2009;10:217-28). Cited here for its localisation data and its statement of the catalytic-triad inference. The ALDH16A1 interaction it reports has not been connected to the RAB7A effector mechanism and is not used to support any annotation in this review.

title: Targeted disruption of the Mast syndrome gene SPG21 in mice impairs hind limb function and alters axon branching in cultured cortical neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neurogenetics 2010;11:369-78). Used for the explicit admission that the absence of enzymatic activity remains to be confirmed - the field's own statement of the knowledge gap. Note that its axon-branching phenotype is reported in the opposite direction to a later study (PMID:26978163), which is why no axon-branching annotation is proposed here.

title: Characterization of maspardin, responsible for human Mast syndrome, in an insect species and analysis of its evolution in metazoans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Naturwissenschaften 2012;99:537-43). Relevant chiefly for two contextual points: it restates the hedged pseudoenzyme inference, and it documents that maspardin is conserved across metazoans including insects - which is what makes a CD4-binding family-level assertion implausible. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: Loss of Maspardin Attenuates the Growth and Maturation of Mouse Cortical Neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Neurodegener Dis 2016;16:260-72). Reports reduced axonal branching in SPG21-null mouse cortical neurons - the opposite direction to PMID:20661613, which reported increased branching in the same knockout. The 2026 J Cell Biol paper notes the discrepancy explicitly. Cited here only to record that the neuronal morphology phenotype is unsettled; no annotation is derived from it. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: The hereditary spastic paraplegia type 21 (SPG21) protein is a RAB7A effector that promotes noncanonical mTORC1-catalyzed TFEB phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Biol Cell 2025;36:ar123, PMC12483374). One of the two independent 2025-2026 studies that establish the RAB7A effector function; includes the specificity control showing canonical mTORC1 substrates are unaffected. Published a few months before PMID:41400694 and reaching the same conclusion by different methods, which is why the effector call is treated as solid rather than provisional.

title: Maspardin/SPG21 controls lysosome motility and TFEB phosphorylation through RAB7 positioning.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Cell Biol 2026;225(2):e202501135, PMC12707310). Independent confirmation of the RAB7 effector function with a CRISPR knockout model, and the source of the lysosome-motility and RAB7-positioning mechanism. Its own discussion is careful about what is not established - it reports no maspardin interaction with VPS35 or TBC1D5 - which is the basis of the second knowledge gap here.

title: Expression and subcellular localization of Spred proteins in mouse and human tissues.

title: Distinct requirements for the Sprouty domain for functional activity of Spred proteins.

title: Spred2 interaction with the late endosomal protein NBR1 down-regulates fibroblast growth factor receptor signaling.
review_notes: Full text read. EVH1 domain of Spred2 binds NBR1; Spred2 inhibition of FGF2-ERK depends on NBR1 and lysosomal routing of FGFR.

review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Human SPRED1/SPRED2 bind DYRK1A via the SPR (CRD) domain and inhibit DYRK1A substrate phosphorylation by substrate competition. Abstract does not mention p53/DNA damage.

title: A shared molecular mechanism underlies the human rasopathies Legius syndrome and Neurofibromatosis-1.
review_notes: Fetched and full text read (Stowe et al. 2012 Genes Dev). Primarily SPRED1, but shows SPRED2 associates with neurofibromin, ectopic SPRED2 relocates neurofibromin to membrane fraction, SPRED1+SPRED2 knockdown reduces membrane neurofibromin; Sprouty proteins do not bind neurofibromin.

title: SPRED2 loss-of-function causes a recessive Noonan syndrome-like phenotype.
review_notes: Cached text = abstract + introduction only. Biallelic SPRED2 LoF causes recessive Noonan-like syndrome; variants impair membrane targeting/NF1 binding and fail to suppress EGF-induced RAF1/MEK/ERK; patient fibroblasts show prolonged MAPK activation; zebrafish rescue.

title: Mammalian sprouty-1 and -2 are membrane-anchored phosphoprotein inhibitors of growth factor signaling in endothelial cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1083/jcb.152.5.1087; full text read. Endogenous human SPRY1 localisation in HUVECs, palmitoylation, caveolin-1 association, FGF2/VEGF-ERK inhibition, no effect on EGF-ERK.

title: Mammalian sprouty proteins inhibit cell growth and differentiation by preventing ras activation.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Supports prevention of Ras activation by Sprouty1, but places the block downstream of SNT-GRB2-SOS complex formation, conflicting with Hanafusa 2002 on the exact step.

title: Sprouty1 and Sprouty2 provide a control mechanism for the Ras/MAPK signalling pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Cell Biol 2002, DOI 10.1038/ncb867). Abstract-only cache. Key mechanistic source: membrane translocation, Tyr phosphorylation, GRB2 binding and block of GRB2-SOS recruitment to FRS2/SHP2.

title: Sprouty1 is a critical regulator of GDNF/RET-mediated kidney induction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Dev Cell 2005). Abstract-only cache. Mouse Spry1-/- supernumerary ureteric buds rescued by reducing Gdnf dosage; developmental outcome of RTK feedback.

title: Efficient suppression of FGF-2-induced ERK activation by the cooperative interaction among mammalian Sprouty isoforms.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1242/jcs.02711. Abstract-only cache. SPRY1-GRB2 interaction; SPRY1-SPRY4 hetero-oligomer most potent ERK inhibitor.

title: Sprouty proteins are in vivo targets of Corkscrew/SHP-2 tyrosine phosphatases.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache. Drosophila and mammalian-cell study; SHP-2 associates with and dephosphorylates the critical tyrosine of Sprouty 1; source of the GOA IMP for FGFR negative regulation.

title: Direct binding of PP2A to Sprouty2 and phosphorylation changes are a prerequisite for ERK inhibition downstream of fibroblast growth factor receptor stimulation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Lao et al. 2007, JBC). Describes the SPRY2-exclusive C-terminal PXXPXR motif and argues GRB2 binding is necessary for SPRY2 inhibition; contrasts with PMID:17689925.

title: Sprouty2 binds Grb2 at two different proline-rich regions, and the mechanism of ERK inhibition is independent of this interaction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Martinez et al. 2007, Cell Signal). A GRB2-binding-dead SPRY2 mutant still inhibits FGFR-ERK signalling, which weakens GRB2 sequestration as the Sprouty mechanism; contrasts with PMID:17255109.

title: Overexpression of Spry1 in chondrocytes causes attenuated FGFR ubiquitination and sustained ERK activation resulting in chondrodysplasia.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2008.05.555; full text. Overexpression context where Spry1 prolongs ERK by reducing FGFR2 ubiquitination.

title: MicroRNA-21 contributes to myocardial disease by stimulating MAP kinase signalling in fibroblasts.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; mouse cardiac fibroblasts, miR-21 augments ERK by repressing Spry1; source of mouse ERK negative-regulation IMP.

title: Kidney development in the absence of Gdnf and Spry1 requires Fgf10.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1371/journal.pgen.1000809; full text. Mouse genetic epistasis showing Spry1 restrains FGF10/FGFR2 as well as GDNF/RET signalling in ureteric bud.

title: Sprouty1, a new target of the angiostatic agent 16K prolactin, negatively regulates angiogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1186/1476-4598-9-231; full text. Endogenous SPRY1 knockdown in primary human endothelial cells increases ERK activation, migration and network formation.

title: Toward an understanding of the protein interaction network of the human liver.

title: Spry1 as a novel regulator of erythropoiesis, EPO/EPOR target, and suppressor of JAK2.

title: Protein interactions of the transcription factor Hoxa1.

review_notes: Abstract-only; TESK1, PP2A, GRB2 and CBL interactions; SPRY2 inhibits CBL-mediated EGFR ubiquitination.

title: Human sprouty 4, a new ras antagonist on 5q31, interacts with the dual specificity kinase TESK1.
