title: Mammalian Sprouty4 suppresses Ras-independent ERK activation by binding to Raf1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Cell Biol 2003, DOI 10.1038/ncb978). Abstract-only cache; abstract states 'mammalian Sprouty4' without species. Key source for RAF1 binding via cysteine-rich domain.

title: Sprouty-4 negatively regulates cell spreading by inhibiting the kinase activity of testicular protein kinase.
review_notes: Full text read. Direct in vitro TESK1 kinase inhibition by GST-SPRY4; ERK- and Tyr75-independent inhibition of cell spreading; Tyr75 required for FGF-ERK inhibition.

title: Efficient suppression of FGF-2-induced ERK activation by the cooperative interaction among mammalian Sprouty isoforms.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1242/jcs.02711. Abstract-only cache. Supports SPRY4-SOS1 association and SPRY1/SPRY4 suppression of GRB2-SOS1 recruitment to FRS2 (co-IP based).

title: Structural basis for a novel intrapeptidyl H-bond and reverse binding of c-Cbl-TKB domain substrates.
review_notes: Structural study of CBL TKB domain with phospho-Sprouty peptides; SPRY4 as CBL ligand.

title: Analysis of the myosin-II-responsive focal adhesion proteome reveals a role for β-Pix in negative regulation of focal adhesion maturation.
review_notes: Focal adhesion proteome (HDA); SPRY4 not discussed in the cached text.

title: The palmitoyl acyltransferase HIP14 shares a high proportion of interactors with huntingtin: implications for a role in the pathogenesis of Huntington's disease.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; SPRY4 not individually discussed.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; SPRY4 not individually discussed.

title: Sprouty4 correlates with favorable prognosis in perihilar cholangiocarcinoma by blocking the FGFR-ERK signaling pathway and arresting the cell cycle.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2019.11.021. Human SPRY4 knockdown/overexpression in PHCC cells supports FGFR-ERK negative regulation; prognosis data observational.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; SPRY4 not individually discussed.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; SPRY4 not individually discussed.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput interactome; SPRY4 not individually discussed.

title: Role of SPRY4 in health and disease.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.3389/fonc.2024.1376873. Review; used for mechanistic summary (SOS1/GRB2, RAF1, PIP2), not as primary evidence.

title: Mdm2 requires Sprouty4 to regulate focal adhesion formation and metastasis independent of p53.
review_notes: PubMed-verified via DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-51488-2. Shows ERK-independent SPRY4 role in focal adhesion/RhoA in p53-null cells; SPRY4 knockdown did not alter ERK phosphorylation in HT1080 cells.

title: Identification of small subunits of mammalian serine palmitoyltransferase that confer distinct acyl-CoA substrate specificities.
review_notes: Primary experimental identification of the human SPT complex and its small subunits; supports the core catalytic-activity and complex annotations for SPTLC1.

title: Orm family proteins mediate sphingolipid homeostasis.
review_notes: Establishes the Orm/ORMDL-SPT (SPOTS) complex; supports SPTLC1 complex membership and ORMDL interaction.

title: Characterization of two mutations in the SPTLC1 subunit of serine palmitoyltransferase associated with hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type I.
review_notes: HSAN1 SPTLC1 mutant characterization; cited by UniProt for the ER membrane subcellular location.

title: Autophagy regulates sphingolipid levels in the liver.
review_notes: Mouse-liver study; SPT overexpression elevates de novo sphingolipids and induces autophagy. Supports flux/biosynthetic-process annotations; the lipophagy link is indirect.

title: ORMDL/serine palmitoyltransferase stoichiometry determines effects of ORMDL3 expression on sphingolipid biosynthesis.
review_notes: SPT/ORMDL stoichiometry and complex formation; supports complex membership and serine C-palmitoyltransferase activity annotations.

title: Complex formation of sphingomyelin synthase 1 with glucosylceramide synthase increases sphingomyelin and decreases glucosylceramide levels.
review_notes: Full text is about SMS1 (SGMS1) and GCS (UGCG); it does not mention SPTLC1 or serine palmitoyltransferase. Used to annotate SPTLC1 to sphingomyelin biosynthetic process, a downstream terminus not assayed here; the SPTLC1 annotation is over-annotated/miscited.

title: Structural insights into the regulation of human serine palmitoyltransferase complexes.
review_notes: Cryo-EM of the human SPT holocomplex (SPTLC1/SPTLC2/ssSPTa/ORMDL3); supports complex membership and catalytic-core role.

title: Structural insights into the assembly and substrate selectivity of human SPT-ORMDL3 complex.
review_notes: Cryo-EM showing SPTLC1-SPTLC2 form a dimer of heterodimers as the catalytic core; supports complex and MF annotations.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: Large-scale endogenous-tagging interactome; detects SPTLC1-SPTLC2 association. Supports only a bare protein-binding annotation (over-annotated).

title: Human and murine serine-palmitoyl-CoA transferase--cloning, expression and characterization of the key enzyme in sphingolipid synthesis.
review_notes: Founding cloning/characterization of human/murine SPT (LCB1/LCB2); defines the PLP-dependent serine + palmitoyl-CoA condensation reaction.

title: Identification of small subunits of mammalian serine palmitoyltransferase that confer distinct acyl-CoA substrate specificities.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes the SPTLC1/SPTLC2 catalytic core, SPT complex composition, and acyl-CoA substrate specificity determined by small subunits. Primary support for catalytic activity, complex membership, and sphingoid base biosynthesis.

title: Mutations in the SPTLC2 subunit of serine palmitoyltransferase cause hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type I.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HSAN1C-causing SPTLC2 variants; disease variants cause loss of normal SPT activity and accumulation of neurotoxic 1-deoxysphinganine.

title: Autophagy regulates sphingolipid levels in the liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Mouse-liver study; SPT overexpression elevates de novo sphingolipid synthesis and induces autophagy. Basis for the (non-core) lipophagy and adipose/sphingolipid annotations; effect is indirect/downstream.

title: ORMDL/serine palmitoyltransferase stoichiometry determines effects of ORMDL3 expression on sphingolipid biosynthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. ORMDLs are negative homeostatic regulators of SPT, the initiating enzyme of sphingolipid biosynthesis. Supports the SPT catalytic and upstream-of-ceramide roles.

title: The Variant p.(Arg183Trp) in SPTLC2 Causes Late-Onset Hereditary Sensory Neuropathy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. HSAN1C variant p.(Arg183Trp); variant protein produced elevated 1-deoxysphingolipids in vitro, confirming altered SPT activity of SPTLC2.

title: Complex formation of sphingomyelin synthase 1 with glucosylceramide synthase increases sphingomyelin and decreases glucosylceramide levels.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Concerns the Golgi SMS1-GCS complex (downstream sphingomyelin/glucosylceramide branching), not SPTLC2 directly; cited for de novo ceramide originating at the ER by condensation of serine and palmitoyl-CoA. Supports keeping the sphingomyelin-biosynthesis annotation as non-core.

title: Structural insights into the regulation of human serine palmitoyltransferase complexes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM structures of the human SPT holocomplex (SPTLC1, SPTLC2, ssSPTa, ORMDL3); establishes complex composition, ER localization, and the rate-limiting nature of the SPT step.

title: Structural insights into the assembly and substrate selectivity of human SPT-ORMDL3 complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM of the human SPT-ORMDL3 complex; SPTLC1 and SPTLC2 form a dimer of heterodimers as the catalytic core; substrate binding (PLP-L-serine, palmitoyl-CoA analogue) and mutagenesis (incl. K379) support catalytic and PLP-binding functions.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput endogenous-tagging interactome/localization resource; source of the IntAct SPTLC1 interaction call. Uninformative as a bare 'protein binding' annotation on its own.

title: Human and murine serine-palmitoyl-CoA transferase--cloning, expression and characterization of the key enzyme in sphingolipid synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Original cloning/characterization establishing that human/murine LCB2 (SPTLC2) encodes serine palmitoyltransferase catalyzing PLP-dependent condensation of L-serine and palmitoyl-CoA to 3-oxosphinganine.

title: Identification of small subunits of mammalian serine palmitoyltransferase that confer distinct acyl-CoA substrate specificities.
review_notes: Primary discovery paper for ssSPTa/SPTSSA as an SPT activator subunit; cached entry is abstract-only but abstract directly supports the activation and substrate-specificity claims.

title: Identification of small subunit of serine palmitoyltransferase a as a lysophosphatidylinositol acyltransferase 1-interacting protein.
review_notes: Establishes experimental ER membrane localization and an SPT-independent role in MBOAT7/LPIAT1 localization to mitochondria-associated membranes.

title: ORMDL/serine palmitoyltransferase stoichiometry determines effects of ORMDL3 expression on sphingolipid biosynthesis.
review_notes: Studies SPT activity in the SPT-ORMDL context (which includes ssSPTa); cited by MGI IDA annotations. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: Complex formation of sphingomyelin synthase 1 with glucosylceramide synthase increases sphingomyelin and decreases glucosylceramide levels.
review_notes: Full text does not mention SPTSSA/ssSPTa; the paper concerns the SMS1-GCS Golgi complex. The GOA sphingomyelin biosynthetic process IDA citing this paper is an over-annotation for SPTSSA.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI large-scale binary interactome; source of several uninformative protein binding IPI hits of uncertain physiological relevance.

title: Structural insights into the regulation of human serine palmitoyltransferase complexes.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structures confirming SPT complex membership and the substrate-specificity role of ssSPTa (engages SPTLC2, shapes the tunnel).

title: Structural insights into the assembly and substrate selectivity of human SPT-ORMDL3 complex.
review_notes: Structural and biochemical confirmation of the activator / substrate-selectivity role of SPTssa; MUTAGEN M28K abolishes complex activity.

title: Ceramide sensing by human SPT-ORMDL complex for establishing sphingolipid homeostasis.
review_notes: Confirms SPT complex composition (SPTLC1, SPTLC2/3, SPTssa/ssb) and pathway context; ceramide-sensing regulation is mediated by ORMDL rather than SPTSSA.

title: SPTLC complexes transfer acyl-CoA onto serine
review_notes: Reactome reaction for the SPT-catalyzed condensation step; source of the TAS ER membrane localization annotation.

title: UniProtKB Q969W0 (SPTSA_HUMAN) Serine palmitoyltransferase small subunit A
review_notes: UniProt curated record; source for localization, topology, complex composition, interactions, and disease.

title: Cloning, heterologous expression, and enzymological characterization of human squalene monooxygenase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cloning, expression, purification and kinetics of human SQLE; establishes the core squalene monooxygenase activity with FAD and NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase.

title: The Regulatory Domain of Squalene Monooxygenase Contains a Re-entrant Loop and Senses Cholesterol via a Conformational Change.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Maps SQLE N-terminal topology to the ER membrane and shows cholesterol-induced conformational change driving proteasomal degradation.

title: The cancer-associated microprotein CASIMO1 controls cell proliferation and interacts with squalene epoxidase modulating lipid droplet formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes SQLE-CASIMO1 (SMIM22) interaction and its effects on lipid droplet formation and proliferation; supports the non-core proliferation/lipid-droplet annotations.

title: Structure and inhibition mechanism of the catalytic domain of human squalene epoxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text available. Crystal structures (PDB 6C6N/6C6P/6C6R) with FAD, kinetics, and mechanism; the definitive structural/biochemical reference for the core catalytic function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: Acceptor substrate specificity of a cloned GD3 synthase that catalyzes the biosynthesis of both GD3 and GD1c/GT1a/GQ1b.
review_notes: Defines acceptor-substrate specificity (GM3, GM1b, GD1a, GT1b); supports the core MF and the enzyme's broader alpha-2,8-sialyltransferase acceptor range.

title: The steroidogenic acute regulatory protein, StAR, works only at the outer mitochondrial membrane.
review_notes: Establishes that StAR acts only at the outer mitochondrial membrane despite being targeted to the matrix; source for OMM site-of-action and matrix non-core localization.

title: Steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (StAR), a novel mitochondrial cholesterol transporter.
review_notes: Review establishing StAR's cholesterol transfer activity and exclusive action on the outer membrane; supports MF and transport annotations.

title: Intracellular cholesterol transporter StarD4 binds free cholesterol and increases cholesteryl ester formation.
review_notes: Primarily a StarD4 (paralog) paper. It names StarD1/STAR only as the reference cholesterol-binding START protein, which supports the STAR cholesterol-binding IDA. Its bile-acid biosynthesis phenotype is a StarD4 property and does not support the STAR bile-acid regulation annotation (flagged over-annotated).

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale interactome; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI (MAGEA11). No functional relevance established.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Systematic interactome study; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI.

title: Widespread Expansion of Protein Interaction Capabilities by Alternative Splicing.
review_notes: Alternative-splicing interactome; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference interactome; source of several uninformative StAR protein-binding IPIs.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegenerative-disease interactome; source of an uninformative StAR protein-binding IPI (HTT).

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence mitochondrial proteome (MitoCoP); supports the HTP mitochondrion localization.

title: Human steroidogenic acute regulatory protein: functional activity in COS-1 cells, tissue-specific expression, and mapping of the structural gene to 8p11.2 and a pseudogene to chromosome 13.
review_notes: Original human StAR functional characterization: >4-fold increase in pregnenolone with P450scc/adrenodoxin; tissue expression; gene mapping.

title: Role of steroidogenic acute regulatory protein in adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis.
review_notes: Human loss-of-function (lipoid CAH) evidence that StAR is indispensable for adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis.

title: UniProtKB entry STAR_HUMAN (P49675)
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; FUNCTION, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY (cholesterol transport reaction), PATHWAY and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION statements used as supporting text.

title: Arginine/lysine-rich structural element is involved in interferon-induced nuclear import of STATs.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms experimental cytoplasm and nucleus localization of STAT2 and IFN-induced nuclear import; supports the localization annotations.

title: Affinity of Stat2 for the subunits of the interferon alpha receptor.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms SH2-dependent STAT2 docking to phospho-IFNAR1 (Tyr466) and constitutive IFNAR2 binding; supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: Identification of STAT2 serine 287 as a novel regulatory phosphorylation site in type I interferon-induced cellular responses.
review_notes: Cached full text confirms STAT2 as a positive modulator of type I IFN transcription and identifies Ser287 as a negative regulatory phosphosite; supports localization and transcription annotations.

title: STAT2 deficiency and susceptibility to viral illness in humans.
review_notes: Cached full text; human STAT2 deficiency causes profound failure of type I IFN signaling and viral susceptibility, with loss of ISGF3-dependent ISG induction. Strongly supports defense response to virus and type I IFN signaling.

title: IFNβ-dependent increases in STAT1, STAT2, and IRF9 mediate resistance to viruses and DNA damage.
review_notes: Cached abstract supports STAT2 membership in ISGF3/U-ISGF3 and its role in driving antiviral ISG transcription.

title: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 2 deficiency is a novel disorder of mitochondrial fission.
review_notes: Cached full text; STAT2 deficiency reduces DRP1 (DNM1L) Ser616 phosphorylation and impairs mitochondrial fission. Supports the non-core mitochondrial fission and protein phosphorylation annotations.

title: PIPINO: A Software Package to Facilitate the Identification of Protein-Protein Interactions from Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry Data.
review_notes: Methods/software paper; source of an uninformative high-throughput protein binding annotation.

title: Global functional profiling of human ubiquitome identifies E3 ubiquitin ligase DCST1 as a novel negative regulator of Type-I interferon signaling.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms DCST1 as an E3 ligase that binds and ubiquitinates STAT2 to negatively regulate type I IFN signaling; supports GO:0044389 and cytoplasm annotations.

title: STAT2 is an essential adaptor in USP18-mediated suppression of type I interferon signaling.
review_notes: Cached full text; establishes STAT2 both as a positive effector and as the essential adaptor recruiting USP18 to IFNAR2 for negative feedback. Key support for core functions and GO:0060339.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome study; source of an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: Histone deacetylase 4 promotes type I interferon signaling, restricts DNA viruses, and is degraded via vaccinia virus protein C6.
review_notes: Cached full text; ChIP shows STAT2 recruitment to ISRE-containing ISG promoters and that the STAT2 transactivation domain mediates HDAC4 interaction. Supports DNA-binding TF activity and chromatin annotations.

title: Severe type I interferonopathy and unrestrained interferon signaling due to a homozygous germline mutation in STAT2.
review_notes: Cached full text; homozygous STAT2 variant causes unrestrained IFN signaling by compromising USP18-mediated negative regulation. Supports type I IFN signaling and negative-feedback roles.

title: Homozygous STAT2 gain-of-function mutation by loss of USP18 activity in a patient with type I interferonopathy.
review_notes: Cached full text; STAT2 R148Q is a GOF that fails to traffic USP18 to IFNAR2, preventing negative regulation of IFN-I. Supports type I IFN signaling and USP18-adaptor core functions.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Large-scale interactome study; source of an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: Unresolvable identifier - no record in NCBI PubMed (likely a GOA data error)
review_notes: Verified via NCBI eutils esummary that PMID:34521819 returns "cannot get document summary" - the identifier does not resolve to any PubMed record and is most likely an error in the GOA source. The entry is retained only because a GOA annotation (existing_annotations[32], a generic uninformative protein binding IPI already marked MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED) references it, so it cannot be deleted without failing reference-integrity validation. Carries no supporting_text and informs no core function.

title: Human transcription factor protein interaction networks.
review_notes: Large-scale TF interaction network study; source of an uninformative protein binding annotation.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Large-scale cell-map study; source of uninformative protein binding and identical protein binding annotations.

title: Phosphorylated interferon-alpha receptor 1 subunit (IFNaR1) acts as a docking site for the latent form of the 113 kDa STAT2 protein.
review_notes: Cached abstract confirms SH2-dependent docking of latent STAT2 to phospho-IFNAR1 (Tyr466); supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: The SH2 domains of Stat1 and Stat2 mediate multiple interactions in the transduction of IFN-alpha signals.
review_notes: Confirms SH2-mediated STAT1/STAT2 homo- and heterodimerization; supports identical protein binding (homodimerization) annotation.

title: Stat2 is a transcriptional activator that requires sequence-specific contacts provided by stat1 and p48 for stable interaction with DNA.
review_notes: Cached abstract; establishes that STAT2 is a potent transactivator that cannot stably contact DNA alone and requires STAT1/p48(IRF9) within ISGF3. Central to the DNA-binding/transactivation core function.

title: Functional subdomains of STAT2 required for preassociation with the alpha interferon receptor and for signaling.
review_notes: Maps STAT2 subdomains required for IFNAR preassociation and signaling; supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: Identification of amino acid residues critical for the Src-homology 2 domain-dependent docking of Stat2 to the interferon alpha receptor.
review_notes: Maps SH2 residues for STAT2-IFNAR1 docking; supports receptor-interaction annotation.

title: Estrogen inhibits GH signaling by suppressing GH-induced JAK2 phosphorylation, an effect mediated by SOCS-2.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. The paper studies GH/JAK2/STAT5 signaling and its suppression by estradiol via SOCS-2; supports the GH receptor signaling, response to estradiol and cellular response to hormone IDA annotations. However the cached abstract does not mention the GO:0035259 glucocorticoid receptor binding annotation, which is BHF-UCL curator judgment from full text (not cached) - left UNDECIDED rather than removed.

title: ZFP36L1 negatively regulates erythroid differentiation of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells by interfering with the Stat5b pathway.
review_notes: Full text cached. Supports the GO:0045648 positive regulation of erythrocyte differentiation annotation - ZFP36L1 binds the Stat5b mRNA 3'UTR and down-regulation of Stat5b drastically reduces erythroid colony formation in human hematopoietic progenitors, demonstrating STAT5B promotes erythroid differentiation.

title: The tumor suppressor hTid1 inhibits STAT5b activity via functional interaction.
review_notes: Full text cached. hTid1/DNAJA3 binds specifically to the STAT5b (not STAT5a) transactivation domain and negatively regulates STAT5b expression and transcriptional activity. Supports a GO:0005515 interaction (marked over-annotated as bare protein binding).

title: Dominant-negative STAT5B mutations cause growth hormone insensitivity with short stature and mild immune dysregulation.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read. Directly establishes STAT5B as the key GH signal transducer; provides experimental evidence for GH-induced Tyr phosphorylation, homo/heterodimerization (co-IP), nuclear translocation (IF), GHRE/GAS DNA binding (EMSA) and reporter transactivation, plus dominant-negative disease variants. Supports the GO:0001228, GO:0042803, nucleus and cytoplasm IDA annotations.

title: Structural and functional consequences of the STAT5B(N642H) driver mutation.
review_notes: Full text cached. Structural/functional study of the SH2-domain N642H oncogenic driver mutation; source of the ABL1 and self-association (GO:0042802) IntAct interactions. Informs STAT5B's role in leukemia/lymphoma but not its core physiological function.

title: Cloning of human Stat5B. Reconstitution of interleukin-2-induced Stat5A and Stat5B DNA binding activity in COS-7 cells.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Original cloning/characterization of human STAT5B; shows IL-2 activation via JAK1/JAK3 and the IL-2R beta/gamma chains and that Tyr-699 is required for dimerization. Supports the TAS JAK-STAT and transcription-factor annotations. Cached as abstract-only.

title: Erythropoietin induces tyrosine phosphorylation of Jak2, STAT5A, and STAT5B in primary cultured human erythroid precursors.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. Directly supports the GO:0038162 erythropoietin-mediated signaling pathway IDA annotation - EPO induces JAK2, STAT5A and STAT5B tyrosine phosphorylation and nuclear translocation in primary human erythroid precursors. Cached as abstract-only.

title: Functional association of Nmi with Stat5 and Stat1 in IL-2- and IFNgamma-mediated signaling.
review_notes: Abstract verified against PubMed. NMI (Q13287) was found via yeast two-hybrid using the STAT5b coiled-coil region and augments STAT5/STAT1 transcription by enhancing CBP/p300 recruitment. Supports the GO:0005515 NMI interaction (marked over-annotated as bare protein binding). Cached as abstract-only.

title: The adaptor protein MITA links virus-sensing receptors to IRF3 transcription factor activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Zhong B et al., Immunity 2008;29(4):538-50 (the MITA paper) - the identifier and title are correct and the paper is a landmark for this gene. Flagged MISCITED because of what two of the annotations drawn from it assert, not because of the citation itself: GO:0003713 transcription coactivator activity and GO:0005741 mitochondrial outer membrane. The paper's own abstract says MITA 'was found to localize to the outer membrane of mitochondria' and that it 'interacted with IRF3', but neither supports a nuclear coactivator role for a four-pass ER membrane protein, and the mitochondrial localisation has not been sustained. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so these judgements rest on the term definitions and on the subsequent literature, not on re-reading the curator's source.

title: Human STING is a proton channel.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Liu B et al., Science 2023 Aug 4;381(6657):508-514, doi 10.1126/science.adf8974. Origin of the GO:0015252 proton channel activity annotation. Liposome reconstitution of purified STING makes this a property of the protein rather than an indirect cellular readout, and C53 blockade provides specificity.

title: A TBK1-independent primordial function of STING in lysosomal biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Lv B et al., Mol Cell 2024, doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2024.08.026. Independent requirement for the STING proton channel in TBK1-independent TFEB activation and lysosome biogenesis; supports GO:0015252, GO:1905673 and GO:1904262.

title: ArfGAP2 promotes STING proton channel activity, cytokine transit, and autoinflammation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Poddar S et al., Cell 2025, doi 10.1016/j.cell.2025.01.027. Third independent laboratory relying on and regulating STING proton channel activity (ArfGAP2); supports GO:0015252 and GO:0001819.

title: STING mediates lysosomal quality control and recovery through its proton channel function and TFEB activation in lysosomal storage disorders.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Tang Z et al., Mol Cell 2025;85(8):1624-1639.e5, doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2025.03.008. Fourth independent laboratory (Yan lab, UTSW) requiring STING proton channel function, here for lysosomal quality control in lysosomal storage disorder models. Cited in this review only as corroboration for GO:0015252; not a GOA source.

title: Beyond interferons: Non-canonical roles of MITA/STING.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Yang Y et al. (Cell Insight 2025), 'Beyond interferons: Non-canonical roles of MITA/STING', doi 10.1016/j.cellin.2025.100266. A review, and the sole support for four NAS annotations (GO:0006914, GO:0045820, GO:0055088, GO:0090398). Correctly cited, but review prose is weak evidence for process annotations; two of the four (glycolysis, lipid homeostasis) are marked as over-annotation here.

title: Regulation of STING activation by phosphoinositide and cholesterol.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Li J et al., Nature 2026 Apr;652(8109):499-507, doi 10.1038/s41586-025-10076-0, PMC13224288. Cryo-EM structures of STING1 with PtdIns(3,5)P2, PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdIns4P plus a cholesterol-like molecule at the dimer-dimer interface, with lipid-strip binding and mutational validation. Source of both the GO:0015485 cholesterol binding IDA and the proposed GO:0005546. Companion to PMID:41639454 with overlapping authorship: corroboration, not independent replication.

title: PtdIns(3,5)P(2) is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Tan JX et al., Nature 2026 Apr;652(8109):490-498, doi 10.1038/s41586-025-10084-0, PMC13222494. Establishes PtdIns(3,5)P2 as a direct STING1 ligand (FRET, PIKFYVE interaction and knockout, lipid-binding mutants). Sound, but note it is co-submitted with PMID:41639452 and shares authors (Tan, Chen, Bai); the cryo-EM structure it cites is that companion paper, so the two are not independent. Carries a Publisher Correction, PMID:41721038, whose content I could not retrieve.

title: Publisher Correction: PtdIns(3,5)P(2) is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Publisher Correction to PMID:41639454, Nature 2026 Mar;651(8105):E11, doi 10.1038/s41586-026-10280-6. The correction's content could NOT be retrieved: PubMed carries only the erratum notice with no descriptive text, Europe PMC returns no abstract, and the Nature page is behind an authentication redirect. Springer Nature reserves 'Publisher Correction' for errors introduced in production, as opposed to 'Author Correction', so on its face it does not affect the data or conclusions - but this is a categorical inference, not something I was able to read. No annotation in this review depends on it.

title: Glues that can STING: Lipids in innate immunity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Debiasi-Anders G & de Oliveira Mann CC, Mol Cell 2026 Apr 16;86(8):1425-1426. Independent commentary (TU Munich) on the two Nature papers. Useful as evidence that the field has not raised a methodological objection, but a commentary is not replication and carries no primary data.

title: Membrane lipids regulate the STING pathway and type I interferon responses.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Messaoud-Nacer Y, Guha S & Laguette N, Cell Chem Biol 2026 Apr 16;33(4):430-432. Second independent commentary (IGMM Montpellier) on the same pair of papers. PubMed types it as 'Journal Article' but the text is a preview/commentary, so it is treated as such here - no primary data.

title: C92, a proton channel-blocking allosteric STING agonist generates robust antitumor activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: Banerjee M et al., J Immunother Cancer 2026;14(6), doi 10.1136/jitc-2026-015242. Industry medicinal-chemistry paper describing an allosteric agonist series that binds within the STING transmembrane proton channel. Cited only as evidence that the channel is a tractable, reproducible structural feature; contributes no GOA annotation.

title: A quantitative chaperone interaction network reveals the architecture of cellular protein homeostasis pathways.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; the quantitative chaperone-interaction network places HOP/STIP1 as a hub co-chaperone of the HSP90 module interacting with HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1, supporting its core Hsp70-Hsp90 organizing/adaptor function (GO:0051879).

title: Tumor suppressor Tsc1 is a new Hsp90 co-chaperone that facilitates folding of kinase and non-kinase clients.
review_notes: GOA-anchored (this PMID supports GO:0051879 Hsp90 protein binding, IPI, and GO:0101031 chaperone complex in STIP1-goa.tsv); corroborates STIP1/HOP as a component of the HSP70-HSP90 multichaperone machine maturing kinase/non-kinase clients.

title: The Ste20-like kinase Mst2 activates the human large tumor suppressor kinase Lats1.
review_notes: Abstract only; MST2 phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2.

title: A conserved MST-FOXO signaling pathway mediates oxidative-stress responses and extends life span.
review_notes: Abstract describes MST1 only; full text not cached, so MST2 involvement in FOXO nuclear translocation could not be checked.

title: Structural insight into dimeric interaction of the SARAH domains from Mst1 and RASSF family proteins in the apoptosis pathway.
review_notes: MST1 SARAH homodimer and RASSF5 SARAH heterodimer structures; SARAH is a dimerization module (paralog STK4 data).

title: Components of the Hippo pathway cooperate with Nek2 kinase to regulate centrosome disjunction.
review_notes: Full text cached; Mst2 phosphorylates Nek2A at centrosomes for centrosome disjunction.

title: Mammalian ste20-like kinase and SAV1 promote 3T3-L1 adipocyte differentiation by activation of PPARγ.
review_notes: Full text; MST2/SAV1 effects on PPARgamma are indirect via SAV1 and the mechanism is unresolved.

title: Premetazoan origin of the hippo signaling pathway.
review_notes: Capsaspora Hpo activates the Drosophila Warts-Yorkie cascade heterologously.

title: Structural basis for autoactivation of human Mst2 kinase and its regulation by RASSF5.
review_notes: Full text cached; crystal structures of human MST2 kinase domain and MST2-RASSF5 SARAH complex; SARAH homodimerization required for trans-autophosphorylation.

title: Structural basis of the heterodimerization of the MST and RASSF SARAH domains in the Hippo signalling pathway.
review_notes: MST2 SARAH homodimer and MST1-RASSF5 heterodimer crystal structures.

title: SAV1 promotes Hippo kinase activation through antagonizing the PP2A phosphatase STRIPAK.
review_notes: Full text cached; SAV1-MST2 SARAH heterodimer, 2:2 heterotetramer via SAV1 WW domains, SLMAP-STRIPAK dephosphorylation of MST2.

title: The Hippo kinase cascade regulates a contractile cell behavior and cell density in a close unicellular relative of animals.
review_notes: Capsaspora coHpo/coWts knockouts; ortholog evidence for ancestral restraint of Yorkie.

title: Assembling a Hippo: the evolutionary emergence of an animal developmental signaling pathway.
review_notes: Review of the evolutionary assembly of the Hippo pathway; source for ancestral vs co-opted functions.

title: Gli regulation by the opposing activities of fused and suppressor of fused.
review_notes: The founding characterisation of human Fused homolog, cited by GOA for six rows (GO:0001222, two TAS rows, the SUFU IPI, and the nucleus and cytoplasm IDAs). The cached record contains title and citation metadata only - no abstract - so the paper could not be read here. Each row citing it was adjudicated against the structured UniProt annotations that cite it with experimental evidence codes (SUBUNIT, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION, BINDING 33, and the reference-block RP line naming MUTAGENESIS OF LYS-33), and every conclusion is independently corroborated by a later experimental row, so no action depends on the missing text.

title: Loss of the serine/threonine kinase fused results in postnatal growth defects and lethality due to progressive hydrocephalus.
review_notes: The mouse knockout: normal embryonic Hedgehog responses, postnatal failure to thrive from communicating hydrocephalus. Abstract-only in the cache (PMC blocks full text). This is the mouse source behind the GO:0009791 rows, and reading it is what shows those rows sit at the end of a long causal chain the paper itself describes only as a possibility.

title: A possible role of mouse Fused (STK36) in Hedgehog signaling and Gli transcription factor regulation.
review_notes: Mouse Fu cloning and RNAi study; the experimental grounding of the mouse GO:0007224 and GO:0045880 IMP rows from which the human ISS rows are transferred. Full text in the cache. Its finding that the Hedgehog requirement appears in some cell lines and not others prefigures the redundancy later demonstrated by epistasis.

title: Fused has evolved divergent roles in vertebrate Hedgehog signalling and motile ciliogenesis.
review_notes: The paper that separated the two functions: mouse Fu is dispensable for Hedgehog signalling but essential for central-pair construction in motile 9+2 cilia, interacts with KIF27, and can rescue both the Hedgehog-dependent and -independent defects of zebrafish fu mutants. Full text in the cache. Load-bearing for the motile-cilium-specific reading of the cilium-assembly rows and for the redundancy argument.

title: Congenital hydrocephalus in genetically engineered mice.
review_notes: A survey of congenital hydrocephalus in engineered mouse lines, not cited by any human STK36 row. Consulted only for the comparator check on ciliary-movement terms: it is the source of the single cilium-movement annotation (GO:0003351) anywhere on the Stk36 family record, in mouse, which is the evidence that GO has not treated STK36 as a participant in ciliary beating. Abstract-only.

title: Using an in situ proximity ligation assay to systematically profile endogenous protein-protein interactions in a pathway network.
review_notes: Systematic in situ proximity ligation survey of pathway interactions. Contributes one STK36-SUFU row. Methodologically the strongest evidence for that pair because it reports on endogenous untagged protein; abstract-only in the cache, and the abstract describes the method but names no individual pair, so the STK36-SUFU detection itself is corroborated through IntAct rather than read here.

title: Mutation of serine/threonine protein kinase 36 (STK36) causes primary ciliary dyskinesia with a central pair defect.
review_notes: Human disease evidence for the Hedgehog-independent function: biallelic loss of function causing primary ciliary dyskinesia with a central-pair defect, with electron microscopy placing STK36 between the radial spokes and the central pair. Abstract-only. Source of the GO:0035082 and GO:0060271 IMP rows and of the UniProt axoneme location.

title: Phosphorylation of Ci/Gli by Fused Family Kinases Promotes Hedgehog Signaling.
review_notes: Establishes Fused-family phosphorylation of Ci/GLI as the conserved Hedgehog activation mechanism, mapping the fly sites and then showing ULK3 and mFu/STK36 act on the corresponding Gli2 sites. Abstract-only in the cache; quotes are from that abstract. Source of the human GO:0004674 and GO:0007224 IMP rows, which FlyBase curators made on the human gene because the paper does both halves.

title: Kinase Interaction Network Expands Functional and Disease Roles of Human Kinases.
review_notes: Mass-spectrometry kinase interaction network covering over 300 kinases. Contributes the STK36-ULK4 row. Full text in the cache. The interaction it reports has since been validated by targeted experiments and given a mechanism, which is why the row is modified rather than removed.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Systematic yeast two-hybrid interactome of neurodegeneration-related proteins. Contributes five bare protein-binding rows for STK36 (DMWD, KLF11, GFAP, ATXN3, SPRED1), all removed as uninformative. The measurements are not disputed and IntAct records three experiments each; none has functional follow-up linking the partner to STK36 activity. Abstract-only.

title: The putative protein kinase Stk36 is essential for ciliogenesis and CSF flow by associating with Ulk4.
review_notes: Maps the STK36-ULK4 interaction to their N-terminal kinase domains by yeast two-hybrid and co-IP, and shows the Stk36 hypomorph phenocopies the Ulk4 hypomorph in motile-cilia defects, CSF flow and Foxj1-pathway expression. Abstract-only. Source of one of the two ULK4 protein-binding rows.

title: Ulk4 promotes Shh signaling by regulating Stk36 ciliary localization and Gli2 phosphorylation.
review_notes: The central mechanistic paper: in vitro kinase assays with defined substrates, activation-loop autophosphorylation as the activity readout, kinase-dead and phospho-mutant controls, the ULK4 bridging mechanism, mutual ciliary-tip dependence, and the epistasis that separates the STK36-ULK4 pathway from ULK3. Full text available in the cache and quoted directly.

title: A peptide encoded by a transcript annotated as long noncoding RNA enhances SERCA activity in muscle.
review_notes: Discovery paper (Science 2016). Primary source of mouse function, localization and KO/Tg data underlying the ISS rows. Studies the murine peptide; human data limited to mRNA in failing hearts. Full text cached.

title: Early vertebrate origin and diversification of small transmembrane regulators of cellular ion transport.
review_notes: J Physiol 2017. Evolutionary context for the regulin/FXYD small TM regulators.

title: The DWORF micropeptide enhances contractility and prevents heart failure in a mouse model of dilated cardiomyopathy.
review_notes: eLife 2018 (mouse). Overexpression prevents DCM in MLP KO mice; reports no direct activation without PLN.

title: Newly Discovered Micropeptide Regulators of SERCA Form Oligomers but Bind to the Pump as Monomers.
review_notes: J Mol Biol 2019. FRET oligomerization of regulins (mouse sequences, per PMID:36523160); background.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI (Nature 2020). High-throughput Y2H; source of all 45 protein binding rows. No SERCA or regulin partner detected for DWORF.

title: The transmembrane peptide DWORF activates SERCA2a via dual mechanisms.
review_notes: JBC 2021. Uses the human DWORF and human SERCA2a sequences in HEK293 cells; Ca-ATPase assays and FRET; P15/W22 mutagenesis. Direct human experimental evidence for activation not yet used in GOA.

title: Dwarf open reading frame (DWORF) is a direct activator of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA.
review_notes: eLife 2021. Purified recombinant human DWORF with rabbit SERCA1a in proteoliposomes. Correctly cited; the direct-activation claim conflicts with the Olson lab results (PMID:26816378, PMID:30299255).

title: A kink in DWORF helical structure controls the activation of the sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+)-ATPase.
review_notes: Structural NMR/MD study (PDB 7MPA); background only.

title: Inhibitory and stimulatory micropeptides preferentially bind to different conformations of the cardiac calcium pump.
review_notes: JBC 2022. DWORF binds E1P/E2P SERCA states preferentially; notes the anti-mouse-DWORF antibody does not detect human DWORF.

title: Micropeptide hetero-oligomerization adds complexity to the calcium pump regulatory network.
review_notes: Biophys J 2023. FRET with human sequences of PLB, SLN, DWORF, ALN, ELN: homo- and hetero-oligomerization; SERCA competes with PLB-DWORF hetero-oligomers.

title: Interaction of DWORF with SERCA and PLB as determined by EPR spectroscopy.
review_notes: Biophysical study; background only.

title: Phosphorylation of phospholamban promotes SERCA2a activation by dwarf open reading frame (DWORF).
review_notes: Cell Calcium 2024. HEK293 with human SERCA2a; DWORF activation is revealed when PLB is phosphorylated.

title: Structural Elements of Dwarf Open Reading Frame Required for Activation of the Sarco-Endoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Pump.
review_notes: Biochemistry 2025. Leu12/Pro15 required for activation; Pro15 substitutions convert DWORF into an inhibitor.

title: Cotranslational and posttranslational N-glycosylation of polypeptides by distinct mammalian OST isoforms.
review_notes: Foundational functional study establishing that STT3A is the OST catalytic subunit responsible for co-translational N-glycosylation, via isoform-specific siRNA knockdown. PubMed-verified; full text available and supports the catalytic MF and co-translational BP.

title: Quantitative glycoproteomics reveals new classes of STT3A- and STT3B-dependent N-glycosylation sites.
review_notes: SILAC glycoproteomics in STT3A/STT3B knockout cells; directly quantifies STT3A-dependent sequons and documents STT3A's role in preventing GRP94 hyperglycosylation. Full text available; supports catalytic MF, co-translational transfer BP, and N-linked glycosylation BP.

title: Positive selection CRISPR screens reveal a druggable pocket in an oligosaccharyltransferase required for inflammatory signaling to NF-κB.
review_notes: CRISPR base-editing plus cryo-EM identifying STT3A as the OST-A catalytic subunit and NGI-1 target; shows OST-A is required for TLR4 N-glycosylation and NF-kB signaling. Abstract only in cache, but the STT3A active-site/OST-A findings are stated in the abstract and match UniProt.

title: Oligosaccharyltransferase isoforms that contain different catalytic STT3 subunits have distinct enzymatic properties.
review_notes: Kelleher et al. 2003 established that mammals express two STT3 homologs (STT3A/STT3B) assembled into OST complexes with distinct enzymatic properties; source of the ER subcellular-location annotation for STT3B.

title: Cotranslational and posttranslational N-glycosylation of polypeptides by distinct mammalian OST isoforms.
review_notes: Ruiz-Canada et al. 2009 (full text available). Isoform-specific siRNA knockdowns show STT3A is the primary cotranslational enzyme while STT3B mediates post-translational glycosylation of skipped sites in unfolded proteins (e.g. Factor VII N360). Primary support for STT3B catalytic activity, N-linked glycosylation and post-translational roles.

title: Defining the membrane proteome of NK cells.
review_notes: High-throughput membrane-proteome (HDA) detection; supports membrane localization only, not function.

title: The oligosaccharyltransferase subunits OST48, DAD1 and KCP2 function as ubiquitous and selective modulators of mammalian N-glycosylation.
review_notes: Roboti & High 2012 (abstract only in cache). Studies non-catalytic OST subunits; shows OST48/DAD1 are required for assembly of both STT3A- and STT3B-containing complexes. Supports STT3B complex membership and its catalytic activity indirectly via subunit-depletion glycosylation defects.

title: STT3B-dependent posttranslational N-glycosylation as a surveillance system for secretory protein.
review_notes: Sato et al. 2012 (abstract only in cache). Demonstrates STT3B-dependent post-translational glycosylation of cryptic sequons in unfolded TTR, routing it to EDEM3-mediated N-glycan-dependent ERAD; primary support for the ERAD/surveillance roles.

title: ZMPSTE24 defends against influenza and other pathogenic viruses.
review_notes: ZMPSTE24 antiviral study; STT3B appears as a co-purifying protein-containing complex partner (IDA to GO:0032991). Not informative about STT3B's own function.

title: Histone Interaction Landscapes Visualized by Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry in Intact Cell Nuclei.
review_notes: Crosslinking mass-spectrometry interaction screen; source of a bare protein-binding (IPI) annotation. Not informative about STT3B function.

title: Quantitative glycoproteomics reveals new classes of STT3A- and STT3B-dependent N-glycosylation sites.
review_notes: Cherepanova et al. 2019 (full text available). SILAC glycoproteomics in CRISPR STT3A/STT3B/MAGT1-TUSC3 knockouts defines STT3B-dependent site classes (short loops of multispanning membrane proteins) and confirms the STT3B complex catalyzes N-glycosylation of sites skipped by STT3A.

title: Cryo-electron microscopy structures of human oligosaccharyltransferase complexes OST-A and OST-B.
review_notes: Ramirez et al. 2019 (abstract only in cache; PDB 6S7T). Cryo-EM structures of OST-A and OST-B; STT3B is the catalytic subunit of OST-B with an acceptor peptide and dolichylphosphate bound. Primary support for complex B membership and ER-membrane localization.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome (Y2H) map; source of a bare protein-binding (IPI) annotation (INCA1/Q0VD86). Not informative about STT3B function.

title: OpenCell: Endogenous tagging for the cartography of human cellular organization.
review_notes: OpenCell endogenous-tagging interactome/localization resource; source of a bare protein-binding (IPI) annotation (RPN1/P04843, a genuine OST subunit).

title: Regulated N-glycosylation controls chaperone function and receptor trafficking.
review_notes: Ma et al. 2024 (full text available). Shows N-glycosylation by the OST complexes is regulated by ER specificity factors (CCDC134/HSP90B1); disruption impairs WNT/IGF1R signaling and causes osteogenesis imperfecta. Supports STT3B catalytic activity and N-glycosylation in a physiological regulatory context.

title: BAG-2 acts as an inhibitor of the chaperone-associated ubiquitin ligase CHIP.
review_notes: GOA-anchored (this PMID supports GO:0061630 ubiquitin protein ligase activity, GO:0051087 protein-folding chaperone binding, and GO:0101031 protein folding chaperone complex in STUB1-goa.tsv); supports CHIP/STUB1 as the chaperone-associated ubiquitin ligase, anchoring its E3 ligase and co-chaperone core functions.

title: CHIP participates in protein triage decisions by preferentially ubiquitinating Hsp70-bound substrates.
review_notes: Cached publication title matches PubMed; establishes CHIP/STUB1's protein-quality-control triage role - preferentially ubiquitinating misfolded chaperone substrates for degradation, a core function.

title: Hsp70 and Hsp90 oppositely regulate TGF-β signaling through CHIP/Stub1.
review_notes: GOA-anchored (this PMID supports GO:0061630 ubiquitin protein ligase activity IDA, GO:0030544 Hsp70 protein binding IPI, and GO:0043161 proteasome-mediated degradation in STUB1-goa.tsv); directly establishes all three CHIP/STUB1 core functions - E3 ligase activity, Hsp70 co-chaperone binding, and chaperone-coupled proteasomal degradation.

title: Mammalian suppressor-of-fused modulates nuclear-cytoplasmic shuttling of Gli-1.
review_notes: Cloning and characterisation of human SUFU; the source of the sequestration model and of the nucleus/cytoplasm localisation. Cached record is abstract-only; every claim used here is quoted verbatim from that abstract.

title: Characterization of the human suppressor of fused, a negative regulator of the zinc-finger transcription factor Gli.
review_notes: Independent characterisation of human SUFU by the Genentech group; source of the GLI repression, GLI1/2/3 binding, Slimb/BTRC interaction and adaptor readings. Abstract-only in the cache.

title: Gli regulation by the opposing activities of fused and suppressor of fused.

The claims it is cited for are corroborated by UniProt experimental evidence codes and by other rows, so no action depends on it.

review_notes: A review of the SHH-PTCH-GLI pathway, cited as TAS for four terms. The cached record has no abstract or full text, so the author statements behind the TAS rows cannot be read. All four terms are independently supported by experimental rows, so the review is redundant rather than load-bearing.

review_notes: Proteome-scale yeast two-hybrid map. Contributes six bare protein-binding rows, all removed as uninformative; the underlying measurements are not disputed.

title: Dual function of UNC-51-like kinase 3 (Ulk3) in the Sonic hedgehog signaling pathway.
review_notes: Establishes the SUFU-ULK3 interaction and, importantly, its direction: SUFU inhibits the kinase. Sole basis for the GO:0019901 row. Abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract states the interaction and its consequence explicitly.

review_notes: mTOR/S6K1-Hedgehog crosstalk; relevant to SUFU only through the demonstration that phosphorylated GLI1 is released from SUFU. Supports the interaction, not a distinct SUFU function.

review_notes: Full-length human and Drosophila Sufu structures plus the Sufu-Gli complex. The key reference for treating repression, tethering and degradation-protection as one binding event; the abstract states this directly.

review_notes: Crystal and SAXS structures of human SUFU and its complex with the GLI SYGHL motif, plus reporter assays with interface mutants. Full text available and used for verbatim quotes.

title: SCF (Fbxl17) ubiquitylation of Sufu regulates Hedgehog signaling and medulloblastoma development.
review_notes: SCF(FBXL17) ubiquitylation of SUFU. Provides the loss-of-SUFU-raises-pathway-output logic behind the IMP row and the basis for the ubiquitin protein ligase binding replacement. Full text available.

title: Hypomorphic Recessive Variants in SUFU Impair the Sonic Hedgehog Pathway and Cause Joubert Syndrome with Cranio-facial and Skeletal Defects.
review_notes: Human recessive hypomorphic SUFU variants causing Joubert syndrome; the strongest human genetic evidence in this record, and the direct human support for the GLI3R-processing role. Abstract-only in the cache but the abstract carries the functional results.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI reference binary interactome. Contributes 27 bare protein-binding rows; the GLI1 row is promoted to a specific term and the remainder removed as uninformative.

title: Systematic discovery of mutation-directed neo-protein-protein interactions in cancer.
review_notes: A screen for neo-interactions gained by mutant proteins in cancer, cited for a bare SUFU-BRAF protein-binding row. The dataset does not support a claim about wild-type SUFU, so the row is removed rather than promoted; the reference is not wrong, but it is the wrong evidence for a general molecular-function assertion.

title: ERK2 MAP kinase regulates SUFU binding by multisite phosphorylation of GLI1.
review_notes: Quantitative measurement of how ERK2 phosphorylation of GLI1 weakens SUFU binding. The title foregrounds ERK2, but SUFU binding is the measured variable throughout, which is why the IDA rows citing it are accepted rather than questioned.

review_notes: DYRK2 phosphorylation of GLI2/GLI3 at the ciliary base and the resulting SUFU dissociation, with SPR affinity measurements using SUFU as analyte. Also the clearest single statement of the retention mechanism. Full text available.

review_notes: PAINT/IBA method reference. The SULT1 IBD node is seeded by a broad set of characterized vertebrate and invertebrate members, and SULT1A1 has its own experimental grounding for all three IBA terms.

review_notes: Maps UniProt SL-0086 (Cytoplasm) to GO:0005737. The underlying UniProt statement itself carries ECO:0000269|PubMed:8093002, so the transfer is sound.

title: Automatic Gene Ontology annotation based on Rhea mapping
review_notes: Source of the steroid sulfotransferase IEA via RHEA:52372, which carries ECO:0000269|PubMed:16221673. Chemically correct; the activity is peripheral rather than core, which the review captures with KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: Source of the very general sulfur compound metabolic process assertion. Correct but uninformative given the specific sulfation annotations already present.

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Draws on EC 2.8.2.1, six RHEA reactions and InterPro IPR000863, all of which are correct for this protein.

title: Characterization of human iodothyronine sulfotransferases.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Directly establishes the highest-affinity substrate class for SULT1A1 and is the source of the thyroid hormone metabolic process IDA and the UniProt iodothyronine RHEA reactions. Also supplies the field's own statement of the open question about in vivo dominance.

title: Characterization of human liver thermostable phenol sulfotransferase (SULT1A1) allozymes with 3,3',5-triiodothyronine as the substrate.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; PubMed record checked (Li et al., J Endocrinol 2001). Added on review of PR #2835, which flagged that this paper was fetched but never cited. It is the independent replication that the proposed_new_terms entry needed: the same 3,3'-T2 > rT3 > T3 > T4 ordering measured in a different laboratory with recombinant allozymes, plus the 3,5-T2 result that the PMID:10199779 abstract does not report. Note on a correction: an earlier draft of this entry described 3,5-T2 as lacking the outer-ring hydroxyl and cited it as licensing the 4'-regiospecificity clause of the proposed term. That was wrong. Thyronine is 4-(4-hydroxyphenoxy)-L-phenylalanine, so the 4'-phenolic hydroxyl is part of the scaffold and is present in every iodothyronine including 3,5-T2 - verified against ChEBI:89575, whose SMILES NC(Cc1cc(I)c(Oc2ccc(O)cc2)c(I)c1)C(=O)O shows an intact 4-hydroxyphenoxy outer ring with both iodines on the inner tyrosyl ring. 3,5-T2 is itself sulfated at the 4'-OH; it is simply a poor SULT1A1 acceptor. The series is re-read here as evidence about outer-ring iodination.

title: Structure of a human carcinogen-converting enzyme, SULT1A1. Structural and kinetic implications of substrate inhibition.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Source of the PAPS-binding IDA, the PAPS metabolic process IDA, the xenobiotic metabolic process IDA and the aryl sulfotransferase IDA, and one of the three UniProt references for the homodimer.

title: Human thyroid phenol sulfotransferase enzymes 1A1 and 1A3: activities in normal and diseased thyroid glands, and inhibition by thyroid hormones and phytoestrogens.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; PubMed record checked (Ebmeier & Anderson, JCEM 2004). Added on review of PR #2835. Partially answers the knowledge_gaps concern that the iodothyronine chemistry rests on recombinant enzyme: the activity is measurable in native human thyroid cytosol. It does not close the gap, because the assay reports tissue SULT1A1 activity rather than attributing the activity to the SULT1A1 gene product by knockdown or immunodepletion, so no annotation action is changed on the strength of it. Also the source for adding thyroid to the description tissue list.

title: The structure of human SULT1A1 crystallized with estradiol. An insight into active site plasticity and substrate inhibition with multi-ring substrates.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Source of the steroid sulfotransferase and estrogen metabolic process IDAs and of RHEA:52372. Read carefully it argues for treating estradiol as a poor-fit, substrate-inhibited acceptor rather than a core substrate, which is the basis of the KEEP_AS_NON_CORE calls.

title: Inhibitory effects of kynurenic acid, a tryptophan metabolite, and its derivatives on cytosolic sulfotransferases.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. An inhibitor-characterization study rather than a substrate study; supports the generic sulfotransferase activity annotation but the abstract does not name the acceptor used for the hSULT1A1 assays, so no more specific term can be drawn from it here.

title: Phase II metabolism of hesperetin by individual UDP-glucuronosyltransferases and sulfotransferases and rat and human tissue samples.
review_notes: Correctly identified, directly relevant, and sound. It supports all three annotations drawn from it at the level of flavonoid sulfation: the flavonoid metabolic process and xenobiotic metabolic process rows are accepted as-is. The problem with the GO:0047894 row is term selection by the curator, not the citation - GO:0047894 flavonol 3-sulfotransferase activity is defined by the quercetin to quercetin 3-sulfate reaction, whereas hesperetin is a flavanone lacking the C-ring 3-hydroxyl and the SULT1A1 product named in the abstract is the B-ring 3'-O-sulfate - so it is recorded as a MODIFY on that annotation rather than as a defect of this reference. Abstract-only: the article is not open access and has no PMC record, so the full methods could not be inspected.

title: Crystal structures of SULT1A2 and SULT1A1 *3: insights into the substrate inhibition and the role of Tyr149 in SULT1A2.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. One of the three UniProt ECO:0000269 references for the homodimer, and the source of the Phe247 selectivity-switch result. Surfaced by the OpenScientist iodothyronine run; the quoted sentence was checked verbatim against the freshly fetched abstract rather than taken from the report on trust.

title: Directed evolution of sulfotransferases and paraoxonases by ancestral libraries.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache, so the per-enzyme assay detail is not visible; UniProt cites it with ECO:0000269 for EC 2.8.2.1 and the curator will have read the full text. A protein-engineering study rather than a physiology study, so it supports the catalytic activity but says nothing about biological role.

title: The molecular basis for the broad substrate specificity of human sulfotransferase 1A1.
review_notes: Full text available in cache. The single most informative reference for the enzyme's molecular function; supplies the mechanistic account of broad specificity, PAP binding and substrate inhibition, and the explicit SULT1A1-versus-SULT1E1 substrate-preference contrast used to scope the steroid annotations.

title: Ethanol sulfation by the human cytosolic sulfotransferases: a systematic analysis.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Correctly cited and scientifically sound, but the terms drawn from it overreach: ethanol is an aliphatic alcohol, so it does not demonstrate aryl sulfotransferase activity, and the authors' own framing of ethyl sulfate as a minor metabolite argues against an ethanol catabolic process annotation.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Proteome-scale binary interactome map; source of a bare protein binding IPI with WITH/FROM UniProtKB:O00204 (SULT2B1). No molecular function content for SULT1A1.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Interaction-perturbation screen; redetects the same SULT1A1-SULT2B1 pair. Uninformative for molecular function.

title: The classic pathways of thyroid hormone metabolism.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; PubMed record checked (van der Spek et al., Mol Cell Endocrinol 2017). Added on review of PR #2835. Background review, not primary evidence for SULT1A1 - it is cited only for pathway orientation and carries no annotation.

title: Extensive disruption of protein interactions by genetic variants across the allele frequency spectrum in human populations.
review_notes: Population-scale variant-interaction survey; redetects the same SULT1A1-SULT2B1 pair. Uninformative for molecular function.

title: Interaction of the Brain-Selective Sulfotransferase SULT4A1 with Other Cytosolic Sulfotransferases: Effects on Protein Expression and Function.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache, but the abstract is explicit about the mechanism. Unlike the four large-scale interactome references, this one identifies the interaction surface and therefore supports a specific molecular function term (heterodimerization) rather than bare protein binding.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Cell-line-resolved affinity-purification interactome; redetects the same SULT1A1-SULT2B1 pair. Uninformative for molecular function.

title: A gut-derived metabolite alters brain activity and anxiety behaviour in mice.
review_notes: Full text available. UniProt cites it with ECO:0000269 for 4-ethylphenol sulfation (RHEA:70607) but GOA has no corresponding annotation, so this is an annotation gap rather than a citation problem. Note the paper is a mouse study and the SULT1A1 attribution rests on in vitro biochemistry; the authors state the in vivo site of sulfation is unknown.

title: Metabolic activation of N-hydroxy arylamines and N-hydroxy heterocyclic amines by human sulfotransferase(s).
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Establishes the procarcinogen-bioactivation role that makes SULT1A1 toxicologically important; uses the pre-SULT nomenclature (TS-PST), which is unambiguously SULT1A1.

title: Functional characterization of two human sulphotransferase cDNAs that encode monoamine- and phenol-sulphating forms of phenol sulphotransferase: substrate kinetics, thermal-stability and inhibitor-sensitivity studies.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache (PMC full text is publisher-restricted). The defining kinetic characterization of SULT1A1 and the source of both the cytoplasm EXP and the dopamine catabolic process IDA. The paper's own framing - phenol-sulfating versus monoamine-sulfating forms, with cross-reactions two orders of magnitude weaker - is the direct basis for treating the dopamine annotation as an over-annotation.

title: Human phenol sulfotransferase STP2 gene: molecular cloning, structural characterization, and chromosomal localization.
review_notes: The PMID resolves to the intended paper, but the paper characterizes the paralogous gene and contains no enzymology, so it supports neither annotation drawn from it for SULT1A1. Two independent lines confirm this. (1) Gene identity, checkable against UniProt without the full text: this is reference 4 of P50226 (SULT1A2), whose gene-name line reads "Name=SULT1A2; Synonyms=STP2", while P50225 (SULT1A1) lists "Synonyms=STP, STP1". (2) Content, from the project curator's reading of the full text: STP2/SULT1A2 is the only gene newly characterized experimentally, with STP1/SULT1A1 (96% identical protein), STM/SULT1A3, STE/SULT1E1 and rat and guinea-pig genes appearing only as comparisons; and there is no new enzymology anywhere in the paper - no recombinant assays, substrate specificity, kinetics, thermostability, or STP1-versus-STP2 functional comparison. The amine metabolic process term therefore has no traceable statement behind it beyond a generic family-level background clause about sulfonation acting on neurotransmitters. The sulfotransferase activity term happens to be true of SULT1A1 on abundant independent evidence and is retained on that basis, but should be re-sourced. Note on full_text_unavailable: that flag describes the cached record, which is abstract-only (not open access, no PMC record) and is what the quote validator reasons about; it does not mean the full text was never consulted.

title: In vitro inhibition of thyroid hormone sulfation by polychlorobiphenylols: isozyme specificity and inhibition kinetics.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; PubMed record checked (Schuur et al., Toxicol Sci 1998). Added on review of PR #2835. An inhibition study rather than a substrate study, so it supports no annotation on its own, but the hSULT1A1-versus-hSULT1A3 contrast is the isozyme discrimination the review otherwise argues only from Km ratios.

title: A single amino acid, glu146, governs the substrate specificity of a human dopamine sulfotransferase, SULT1A3.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache. Gives the structural basis for the SULT1A1/SULT1A3 division of labour and is the strongest single argument that catecholamine disposal belongs to SULT1A3 - the residue that makes an enzyme a dopamine sulfotransferase is exactly the one SULT1A1 lacks. Surfaced independently by two OpenScientist runs; the quoted sentence was checked verbatim against the freshly fetched abstract rather than taken from the reports on trust. Note the switch was characterized for dopamine-versus-phenol selectivity, not for iodothyronine affinity.

review_notes: Reactome reaction placing a major SULT1A1 drug-conjugation step in the cytosol and modelling the enzyme as a dimer.

title: Phenol can form a sulfate conjugate
review_notes: Directly states both the location and the catalytic form (homodimer), supporting the cytosol annotations and the proposed homodimerization annotation.

title: SULT1A1 dimer sulfonates NHABP
review_notes: Pathway-level corroboration of the procarcinogen-bioactivation core function.

review_notes: Reactome reaction for the highest-affinity SULT1A1 substrate, placed in the cytosol.

review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biochem J 2009;422:455-62). Supports that recombinant hSULT1B1 is catalytically active and pharmacologically distinguishable from SULT1A enzymes; the paper's subject is inhibitor characterization rather than SULT1B1 function per se.

title: Phase II metabolism of hesperetin by individual UDP-glucuronosyltransferases and sulfotransferases and rat and human tissue samples.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Drug Metab Dispos 2010;38:617-25). Supports SULT1B1 activity on a phenolic flavonoid in a 12-enzyme panel; note the in vivo role is inferred from expression level rather than from catalytic efficiency, which is why the flavonoid annotation is kept as non-core.

title: Genome-wide YFP fluorescence complementation screen identifies new regulators for telomere signaling in human cells.
review_notes: Correctly cited high-throughput interaction screen, but it supports only a bare protein binding annotation and says nothing about SULT1B1 function.

title: Analysis of proteomic changes induced upon cellular differentiation of the human intestinal cell line Caco-2.
review_notes: The paper is correctly identified, but it reports differential abundance of SULT1B1 between proliferating and differentiated Caco-2 cells. That is an expression correlation and does not support involved_in epithelial cell differentiation.

title: Ethanol sulfation by the human cytosolic sulfotransferases: a systematic analysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Biol Pharm Bull 2012;35:2180-5). Correct paper, but it is used to support an ethanol catabolic process annotation for SULT1B1 when its own summary names SULT1A1, SULT1A2, SULT1A3 and SULT1C4 as the ethanol-sulfating enzymes among the eleven SULTs assayed. Cached record is abstract-only, so the full-text panel data could not be checked.

title: A proteome-scale map of the human interactome network.
review_notes: Correctly cited binary interactome map; supports only bare protein binding.

title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.
review_notes: Correctly cited interactome study; supports only bare protein binding.

title: A high frequency missense SULT1B1 allelic variant (L145V) selectively expressed in African descendants exhibits altered kinetic properties.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Xenobiotica 2018;48:79-88), full text available. Directly establishes the phenolic substrate preference, tissue distribution and PAPS/PAP kinetics of human SULT1B1.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: Correctly cited HuRI interactome map; supports only bare protein binding.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Correctly cited interactome study; supports only bare protein binding.

title: Histone tyrosine sulfation by SULT1B1 regulates H4R3me2a and gene transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2023;19:855-864). The claim that SULT1B1 is a histone sulfotransferase acting on H3 Tyr99 is formally contested by PMID:40890505, which reannotated the original raw mass spectra as a phosphotyrosine peptide and found no sulfation of recombinant histone H3.2 by recombinant SULT1B1. The authors replied (PMID:40890506) and an Author Correction was published (PMID:40890508); the paper has not been retracted. Cited here only to document the dispute - no GO annotation derives from it.

title: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:1667-1670), full text available via PMC12978989. A formal Matters Arising refuting PMID:36805701 on three independent grounds: sulfotyrosine is too labile to give the 100% sulfate-retaining HCD fragments reported, the reported fragment masses fit phosphotyrosine to <3 ppm versus 12.5-31.5 ppm for sulfotyrosine, and a recombinant SULT1B1 assay that efficiently sulfated T3 gave no histone H3.2 sulfation. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because the original authors contest it in PMID:40890506, not because of any problem with the citation.

title: Reply to: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:1671-1674). The original authors' reply to PMID:40890505. Cached record is abstract-only and PubMed carries no abstract for it, so the substance of their rebuttal could not be assessed here. Its existence is why this review treats the question as open rather than settled.

title: Author Correction: Histone tyrosine sulfation by SULT1B1 regulates H4R3me2a and gene transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as an erratum to PMID:36805701 (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:2014). The correction notice has no abstract in PubMed and the cached record is abstract-only, so what was corrected could not be determined. Recorded for completeness; a curator should read the correction before acting on the 2023 paper.

title: GAL3ST1-Mediated Histone Tyrosine Sulfation Induced by Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Promotes Gastric Cancer Metastasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cancer Res 2026;86:2429-2446), full text available via PMC13176828. Relevant to SULT1B1 because it attributes the same H3Y99sulf mark to a different enzyme, GAL3ST1, and reports SULT1B1 levels unchanged under the inducing conditions. It cites PMID:36805701 as settled background and does not cite the refutation PMID:40890505, and its H3Y99sulf readouts rest on the antibody class that the refutation says needs further validation.

title: Molecular cloning and characterization of rat ST1B1 and human ST1B2 cDNAs, encoding thyroid hormone sulfotransferases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biochem 1997;122:1052-61). Founding characterization of human SULT1B1 (ST1B2). Note the internal conflict with PMID:9463486 on dopamine: this paper reports dopamine sulfation, the other reports none.

title: Expression and characterization of a novel thyroid hormone-sulfating form of cytosolic sulfotransferase from human liver.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Mol Pharmacol 1998;53:274-82). Founding characterization establishing the phenol and iodothyronine substrate range, the absence of steroid activity and the cytosolic localization of human SULT1B1.
