title: TMEM106a is a Novel Tumor Suppressor in Human Renal Cancer.
review_notes: Primary study for the renal-cancer tumor-suppressor claim (proliferation, migration, caspase-3-dependent apoptosis). Its "key factor to regulate macrophage activation" sentence sits in BACKGROUND/AIMS and restates prior mouse work; the paper assays no macrophages, so it is not independent support for GO:0042116. Abstract-only in cache.

title: TMEM106A inhibits cell proliferation, migration, and induces apoptosis of lung cancer cells.
review_notes: Primary study; TMEM106A tumor suppressor in NSCLC, represses EMT and PI3K/AKT/NF-kB signaling. Abstract-only in cache.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary reference interactome (Y2H). Source of a generic protein-binding IPI annotation; no gene-specific functional insight for TMEM106A.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS proteome-scale interactome. Source of a generic protein-binding IPI annotation; not a focused study of TMEM106A function.

title: Functional chimeric mRNAs encode proteins in mammalian immunity.
review_notes: Venezia/Kane et al., Nature 2026 (PubMed-verified). Describes the mouse Gsdmd-Tmem106a trans-spliced chimeric mRNA, whose TMEM106A contribution is an out-of-frame reading of the Tmem106a mRNA (not the canonical protein). Relevant as context / knowledge gap; does not change the review of canonical TMEM106A. Human orthologous chimera not yet established.

title: TMEM120A and B: Nuclear Envelope Transmembrane Proteins Important for Adipocyte Differentiation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Batrakou et al., PLoS One 2015). Source of the nuclear envelope (NET29) assignment, the adipocyte-differentiation role, and the homo/heterooligomerization annotations. Correctly cited; its compartment assignment is contested by later work but the experiments themselves are not in dispute.

title: TACAN Is an Ion Channel Involved in Sensing Mechanical Pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., Cell 2020). This is the origin of the TACAN name and of every channel-related annotation on this gene, including the mouse donor annotation behind the human GO_REF:0000024 ISS rows. The channel claim was not reproduced by four independent groups in 2021, and GO now carries three human NOT|enables annotations against the same term. Correctly cited but the central claim is contested; the in vivo nociceptor knockout phenotype is a separate matter and is not itself refuted.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput binary interactome map; the source of 24 bare protein-binding rows. Correctly cited but contributes no functional information about TMEM120A.

title: Involvement of TACAN, a Mechanotransducing Ion Channel, in Inflammatory But Not Neuropathic Hyperalgesia in the Rat.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Pain 2020). Antisense knockdown in rat supports a contribution to inflammatory mechanical hyperalgesia, which is relevant to the pain-process annotations. Marked DISPUTED only because the paper adopts the mechanotransducing-ion-channel framing that has since been refuted; the behavioural observation stands independently of that framing.

title: Analysis of the mechanosensor channel functionality of TACAN.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Niu et al., eLife 2021). Independent failure to detect mechanosensitive channel activity, plus native mass spectrometry confirming co-purified coenzyme A. Not currently cited in GOA but directly load-bearing for the removal of the positive ISS channel annotation.

title: TMEM120A is a coenzyme A-binding membrane protein with structural similarities to ELOVL fatty acid elongase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Xue et al., eLife 2021). Supports both the positive coenzyme A binding IDA and the negated ion channel IMP carried in GOA; verified that the paper reports both the CoA-bound structure and the failure to reproduce mechanosensitive currents.

title: TMEM120A contains a specific coenzyme A-binding site and might not mediate poking- or stretch-induced channel activities in cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Rong et al., eLife 2021). The negative electrophysiology used proper positive controls (Piezo channels, HsTMEM63a) in Piezo1-knockout HEK cells, which makes it a strong negative rather than an insensitive assay. Identifies the tryptophan required for CoASH binding.

title: Cryo-EM structures of human TMEM120A and TMEM120B.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Discov 2021). Supports the negated ion channel IDA. Notably careful - the authors observed conductance in a bilayer system yet declined to conclude channel identity because non-channel proteins also conduct in that assay.

title: Gain-of-function genetic screening identifies the antiviral function of TMEM120A via STING activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Li et al., Nat Commun 2022). Source of the antiviral innate immune response IMP and of the ER and plasma membrane IDA rows. Single-laboratory result, but includes a mouse knockout and a mechanistically coherent ER-export readout.

title: Genomic loci mispositioning in Tmem120a knockout mice yields latent lipodystrophy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Czapiewski et al., Nat Commun 2022). Adipocyte-specific knockout gives a lipodystrophy syndrome, supporting the fat-cell and lipid-homeostasis annotations. Interprets the phenotype through nuclear envelope genome organisation, which competes with the ER lipid-flux interpretation of PMID:41423633; both are recorded rather than adjudicated here.

title: TMEM120A/TACAN inhibits mechanically activated PIEZO2 channels.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Del Rosario et al., J Gen Physiol 2022). Provides the alternative account of the mechanosensory phenotype - TMEM120A as a negative modulator of PIEZO2 rather than a channel - and explicitly states the data do not support channel identity.

title: Regulation of PKD2 channel function by TACAN.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available false), so the supporting evidence for the PKD2 interaction was not read. Cited in GOA only for a bare protein-binding row; not relied on for any action in this review beyond that row.

title: Phosphatidic acid is an endogenous negative regulator of PIEZO2 channels and mechanical sensitivity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Gabrielle et al., Nat Commun 2024). Identifies the mediator linking TMEM120A to PIEZO2 inhibition - TMEM120A expression raises phosphatidic acid and lysophosphatidic acid. This is the key reconciliation between the lipid-metabolic function and the mechanosensory phenotypes, since lysophosphatidic acid is the product of the GPAT4 reaction TMEM120A activates.

title: TMEM120A maintains adipose tissue lipid homeostasis through ER CoA channeling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cho et al., Nat Commun 2025, PMC12855804). Establishes the ER-resident CoA-binding role, the CoA-site-dependent interaction with ACSL1 and ACSL3, and the adipose phenotype of the adipocyte-specific knockout. Note that the authors hedge the transport mechanism themselves ("possibly through recycling CoA in ER"), so no CoA transporter term is proposed on its basis.

title: From nociception to therapy: The expanding role of TMEM proteins in pain.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Life Sci 2026); cached record is abstract-only. A narrative review that still lists TMEM120A/TACAN among pain-relevant TMEM proteins. Its own wording is "modulating ion channels", which is compatible with the PIEZO2 model rather than with TMEM120A being a channel. Recorded to document that the channel framing persists in secondary literature; it presents no new data and is not a basis for reinstating the channel annotation.

title: A conserved ER protein prevents lipotoxicity by stimulating the key enzyme in glycerolipid synthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Li et al., Nat Commun 2026, PMC13365615). Identifies TMEM120A as a GPAT4-activating protein acting with CHP1, with an in vitro acyltransferase assay, split-GFP and co-immunoprecipitation evidence, ER localisation of endogenously tagged C. elegans TMEM-120, and a conserved high-fat-diet phenotype. Basis for the proposed enzyme-activator terms.

title: Biolayer Interferometry for Investigating Membrane Protein-Inhibitor Binding: TACAN Mutant and GsMTx4 As a Model System.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Vis Exp 2026); cached record is abstract-only. A methods paper demonstrating a biolayer-interferometry protocol, using detergent-solubilised TMEM120A M207A and the gating-modifier peptide GsMTx4 as a convenient model pair. It measures binding kinetics, not channel gating, and the authors describe TMEM120A as "multifunctional" rather than as a channel. Flagged MISCITED in the sense that its use of a mechanosensitive-channel toxin should not be read as evidence that TMEM120A is a mechanosensitive channel.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2020). Correctly cited as the source of the bare protein binding row, but it is a systematic binary-interactome screen and none of the partners it reports for TMEM187 has been followed up or connected to a function. Contributes no functional information about this gene.

title: TMEM187 is a novel brakelike modulator in the regulation of erythropoiesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Blood 2026;148(3):361-375, PMC13386088), with an accompanying Blood commentary (PMID:42461672). Essentially the entire functional literature on this gene. The cellular-component and biological-process claims are well supported - loss and gain of function in human cells, zebrafish and humanised mice, in both directions. The molecular mechanism is the weaker part: the GEF-competition model is inferred from co-immunoprecipitation, colocalisation and expression changes, with no nucleotide-exchange assay, and the paper itself notes that its observed nucleotide-state preference for GRAB is opposite to earlier reports. This is a single study from one laboratory and has not yet been independently replicated.

title: The fellowship of the ring: TMEM187 guides iron to heme.
review_notes: Identifier verified against PubMed (Blood 2026;148:271-2, an Editorial/Comment by Y.Y. Yien accompanying PMID:41824385), but PubMed carries no abstract and no full text was retrievable, so its content could not be read. Listed for provenance only - that Blood commissioned a commentary indicates the finding was considered notable - and it is not used to support any annotation.

title: Integral and associated lysosomal membrane proteins.
review_notes: Lysosomal membrane proteomics; correctly cited, supports the lysosomal membrane location but carries no functional information.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary exosome shotgun proteomics; correctly cited but a high-throughput co-purification dataset with no functional content for this gene.

title: The N- and C-terminal carbohydrate recognition domains of Haemonchus contortus galectin bind to distinct receptors of goat PBMC and contribute differently to its immunomodulatory functions in host-parasite interactions.
review_notes: Correctly cited, but a Haemonchus contortus galectin host-parasite interaction study; it identifies TMEM63A as a binding partner on goat PBMC and says nothing about the normal function of the human protein. Basis for marking GO:0005515 over-annotated.

title: OSCA/TMEM63 are an Evolutionarily Conserved Family of Mechanically Activated Ion Channels.
review_notes: Murthy et al. 2018 eLife; PubMed-verified. Founding demonstration that OSCA/TMEM63 proteins confer mechanosensitivity to naive cells.

title: Heterozygous Variants in the Mechanosensitive Ion Channel TMEM63A Result in Transient Hypomyelination during Infancy.
review_notes: Yan et al. 2019; PubMed-verified. Human genetics establishing TMEM63A variants as a cause of transient infantile hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.

title: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2023 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Structures and electrophysiology of TMEM63A and TMEM63B establishing monomeric architecture and bona fide mechanosensitivity.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 Nat Struct Mol Biol; PubMed-verified. About the paralog TMEM63B, cited here only for the paralog contrast.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase activity of the TMEM63/OSCA family.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 FEBS Lett; PubMed-verified. Source of the NOT|enables phospholipid scramblase annotation on TMEM63A: a deliberate paralog/ortholog comparison in Tmem63b-deficient pro-B cells in which scramblase activity tracked with TMEM63B orthology. Cached abstract only.

title: Structural and functional basis of mechanosensitive TMEM63 channelopathies.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2025 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM of the TMEM63A V53M lipid-open state; the V-to-M substitutions evoke constitutive scrambling without enhancing channel activity, which presupposes that wild-type TMEM63A does not scramble.

title: Oligodendrocyte mechanotransduction channel TMEM63A regulates myelin sheath geometry.
review_notes: Dereddi et al. 2026 Neuron; PubMed-verified (Neuron 114(4):699-723.e11, doi 10.1016/j.neuron.2025.11.009). Cached abstract only - full_text_available is false - so only the abstract has been used. Frames TMEM63A purely as a mechanotransduction channel in oligodendrocytes.

title: TMEM63 proteins act as mechanically activated cholesterol modulated lipid scramblases contributing to membrane mechano-resilience.
review_notes: Lin et al. 2026 Nat Commun; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Reports lipid translocation by reconstituted hTMEM63A in GUVs while explicitly stating that this does not occur in the cellular context - the key text for reconciling the NOT|enables scramblase annotation.

title: OSCA/TMEM63 are an Evolutionarily Conserved Family of Mechanically Activated Ion Channels.
review_notes: Murthy et al. 2018 eLife; PubMed-verified. Founding demonstration that OSCA/TMEM63 proteins confer mechanosensitivity; supports the mechanosensitive channel core function.

title: Overexpression of Osmosensitive Ca(2+)-Permeable Channel TMEM63B Promotes Migration in HEK293T Cells.
review_notes: Marques et al. 2019 Biochemistry; PubMed-verified. This is the mouse IDA source behind GO:0005227. Its own title and text describe TMEM63B as Ca2+-PERMEABLE and osmosensitive, not Ca2+-activated, which is the basis for the MODIFY on that term.

title: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration.
review_notes: Vetro et al. 2023 Am J Hum Genet; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Defines the TMEM63B developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and characterises variant conductance; this is the source of the GO:0005227 IDA whose term choice is challenged here.

title: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2023 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM structures and electrophysiology establishing TMEM63A/B as monomeric, small-conductance, high-threshold mechanosensitive channels.

title: Mechanosensitive channels TMEM63A and TMEM63B mediate lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion.
review_notes: Chen et al. 2024 J Clin Invest; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. In vivo demonstration that TMEM63A/B mechanotransduction drives lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion; source of the GO:0140135 IDA and the lamellar body membrane location.

title: Phospholipid scrambling induced by an ion channel/metabolite transporter complex.
review_notes: Niu et al. 2024 Nat Commun; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Unbiased CRISPR revival screen identifying Tmem63b as a phospholipid-scrambling factor acting with Slc19a2; independent assay system from the Segawa-lab work.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 Nat Struct Mol Biol; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Purified-protein scramblase assays plus open and closed cryo-EM structures resolving the lipid translocation pathway. Strongest single piece of evidence for the scramblase core function.

title: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase activity of the TMEM63/OSCA family.
review_notes: Miyata et al. 2025 FEBS Lett; PubMed-verified. Paralog and ortholog survey in Tmem63b-null pro-B cells; grounds both the positive scramblase annotation on TMEM63B and the NOT annotation on TMEM63A. Cached abstract only.

title: Structural and functional basis of mechanosensitive TMEM63 channelopathies.
review_notes: Zheng et al. 2025 Neuron; PubMed-verified. Cryo-EM of the TMEM63A V53M lipid-open state; establishes that the V-to-M channelopathy variants evoke constitutive scrambling without enhancing channel activity, and states that the physiological relevance of WT scramblase activity is still open.

title: TMEM63 proteins act as mechanically activated cholesterol modulated lipid scramblases contributing to membrane mechano-resilience.
review_notes: Lin et al. 2026 Nat Commun; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. GUV reconstitution plus coarse-grained MD showing mechanically activated lipid scrambling by TMEM63A/B and separable ion/lipid bottleneck residues.

title: Autoinhibition of the mechanosensitive lipid scramblase TMEM63B by its C-terminal tail.
review_notes: Nishimura et al. 2026 J Biol Chem; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Maps a C-terminal autoinhibitory motif that holds TMEM63B scrambling off at rest.

title: A TMEM63B variant with enhanced mechanosensitive channel activity and acquired lipid scramblase function.
review_notes: Lowry et al. 2026 J Gen Physiol; PubMed-verified, full text in PMC. Characterises I475del as a gain-of-function mechanosensitive channel variant that also acquires constitutive and osmotically potentiated scramblase activity; the clearest statement of the channel-to-scramblase switch.

title: TMEM65 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane protein.
review_notes: PeerJ 2014; verified against the cached record. Establishes mitochondrial import and inner-membrane integration, and the cleaved N-terminal targeting sequence.

title: Evolutionarily conserved intercalated disc protein Tmem65 regulates cardiac conduction and connexin 43 function.
review_notes: Nat Commun 2015; verified. Correctly cited for the intercalated-disc/connexin-43 role, but the surface localisation it reports has not been reproduced by any subsequent mitochondrial study of TMEM65 and is hard to reconcile with a cleaved mitochondrial targeting sequence. Cached record is abstract-only.

title: A mutation in the TMEM65 gene results in mitochondrial myopathy with severe neurological manifestations.
review_notes: Eur J Hum Genet 2017; verified. Confirms inner-membrane localisation and links a homozygous TMEM65 splice variant to mitochondrial encephalomyopathy.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI binary interactome. Correctly cited, but yields only bare protein binding with no functional interpretation for TMEM65.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: High-confidence human mitochondrial proteome; corroborates mitochondrial residence.

title: TMEM65 regulates and is required for NCLX-dependent mitochondrial calcium efflux.
review_notes: Nat Metab 2025; verified (title, journal and year match the cached record). Source of the NOT|enables GO:0005432 annotation. Correctly cited and methodologically sound, but its central conclusion - TMEM65 is a regulator of NCLX, not the exchanger - is directly contradicted by PMID:40691517. Recorded as DISPUTED rather than MISCITED: the paper is cited for exactly what it claims.

title: TMEM65 functions as the mitochondrial Na(+)/Ca(2+) exchanger.
review_notes: Nat Cell Biol 2025; verified (title, journal and year match the cached record). Source of the positive enables GO:0005432 annotation. Correctly cited, but the key liposome reconstitution measures 45Ca2+ accumulation rather than transmembrane flux, a limitation raised in PMID:41061666, and the conclusion is contradicted by PMID:40200126. Note also that this paper shares senior authors with PMID:40931067, which reassigns NCLX to H+/Ca2+ exchange; the two form one model rather than two independent lines of evidence.

title: Structure and mechanism of the mitochondrial calcium transporter NCLX.
review_notes: Nature 2025; verified. Cited here for context only - it does not assay TMEM65 (the word does not appear in the paper). Relevant because it reassigns NCLX to H+/Ca2+ exchange, which would remove the alternative candidate for mito-NCX and so indirectly supports Position A.

title: Mitochondrial sodium-calcium exchange-Can TMEM65 do it alone?
review_notes: Cell Metab 2025 commentary; verified. Frames the TMEM65 dispute and identifies the specific experimental gap (binding versus translocation in the proteoliposome assay). Written by the authors of PMID:40200126, so not a neutral referee, but the methodological point is concrete and checkable.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis run: TMEM70 c-ring versus complex-I boundary
review_notes: Directly inspected; supports the accepted ATP-synthase c-ring scaffold role and the existing unresolved complex-I direct-versus-secondary knowledge gap.

title: Expression of the Bcl-2 protein BAD promotes prostate cancer growth.
review_notes: Full text cached (Expression of the Bcl-2 protein BAD promotes prostate cancer growth); it contains no mechanical-stimulation experiment and does not mention TNFRSF1A. UniProt assigned IEP GO:0071260 cellular response to mechanical stimulus from this PMID to 36 human genes in one batch dated 2011-03-15 (QuickGO), while its only content-matching annotation is the BAD IMP row; almost certainly a batch identifier error. Intended paper not identified. See projects/MISCITATIONS.md.

title: Enhanced CD4+ T cell proliferation and Th2 cytokine production in DR6-deficient mice.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Immunity 2001, Liu et al.). Founding DR6 knockout study; experimental basis, via the mouse ortholog, for the T cell proliferation and Th2 cytokine annotations.

title: Enhanced B cell expansion, survival, and humoral responses by targeting death receptor 6.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Exp Med 2003). DR6-null B cell hyperproliferation, reduced apoptosis, enhanced germinal centres and antibody titres; basis for the B cell and humoral immune response annotations.

title: APP binds DR6 to trigger axon pruning and neuron death via distinct caspases.
review_notes: RETRACTED. PubMed-verified as Nikolaev et al., Nature 2009, "APP binds DR6 to trigger axon pruning and neuron death via distinct caspases"; retracted January 2024 (see PMID:38110576) for image duplication, statistical errors and superseded mechanistic conclusions. Listed here only because it is the origin of the APP-receptor model for DR6. Critically, it is cited by no GO annotation on this gene or on the mouse ortholog, so the retraction does not invalidate anything in existing_annotations.

title: Functional analysis of the posttranslational modifications of the death receptor 6.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Klima et al., Biochim Biophys Acta 2009, on DR6 post-translational modification. The plasma membrane IDA it supports is well matched to the abstract. The cellular response to tumor necrosis factor IDA drawn from the same paper could not be connected to any experiment described in the abstract, and the cached record is abstract-only; flagged as UNDECIDED in that annotation rather than removed.

title: Death receptor 6 negatively regulates oligodendrocyte survival, maturation and myelination.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Med 2011, Mi et al.). DR6 as negative regulator of oligodendrocyte survival, maturation and myelination, with overexpression, antagonist-antibody and knockout evidence; independent of the APP/axon-degeneration disputes.

title: Death receptor 6 induces apoptosis not through type I or type II pathways, but via a unique mitochondria-dependent pathway by interacting with Bax protein.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Biol Chem 2012). Correctly cited, but the apoptosis it reports depends on ectopic overexpression of a death-domain receptor, which is weak evidence for a physiological role; hence KEEP_AS_NON_CORE for the apoptotic process annotation.

title: A DR6/p75(NTR) complex is responsible for β-amyloid-induced cortical neuron death.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Death Dis 2013, Hu et al.). DR6/p75NTR complex mediating amyloid-beta-induced cortical neuron death; the real experimental basis for the neuron apoptotic process annotation, and independent of the retracted Nature paper.

title: Genetic analysis reveals that amyloid precursor protein and death receptor 6 function in the same pathway to control axonal pruning independent of β-secretase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Neurosci 2014, Olsen et al.). The non-retracted in vivo genetic analysis that the retraction notice relies on: APP and DR6 act in the same pathway to control retinal axon pruning, while beta-secretase activity is not required. Shares authorship with the retracted paper and has not been independently replicated.

title: Death Receptor 6 and Caspase-6 Regulate Prion Peptide-Induced Axonal Degeneration in Rat Spinal Neurons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Wang et al., J Mol Neurosci 2015, on DR6 and caspase-6 in prion-peptide-induced axonal degeneration in rat spinal neurons. It is the sole source of the rat IMP that the human GO:0007413 axonal fasciculation IEA is propagated from, and its subject (axonal degeneration) does not match that term (collection of axons into a fascicle). Not cited directly by the human GOA row, listed here to document the provenance.

title: Death Receptor 6 Promotes Wallerian Degeneration in Peripheral Axons.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Curr Biol 2017, Gamage et al.). The claim that DR6 is required for Wallerian degeneration and Schwann cell remodelling after axotomy. Directly non-replicated by PMID:41891813 using two knockout lines including the original.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2020, HuRI). High-throughput yeast two-hybrid; source of a bare protein binding annotation with SGTA. Contributes no functional information.

title: A physical wiring diagram for the human immune system.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nature 2022). Systematic extracellular-protein interactome of the human immune system; the source of the APP (P05067) and PI16 (Q6UXB8) protein binding rows. Independent redetection of the DR6-APP interaction, obtained without reference to the retracted work.

title: Retraction Note: APP binds DR6 to trigger axon pruning and neuron death via distinct caspases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified retraction notice, Nature 2024, retracting PMID:19225519. Documents both the anomalies and the authors’ position that the DR6-APP genetic interaction itself still stands via later work.

title: Death receptor 6 does not regulate axon degeneration and Schwann cell injury responses during Wallerian degeneration.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (eLife 2026, Beirowski/Huang/Babetto). Full text cached. Non-replication of PMID:28285993 across two independent DR6 knockout lines, in vivo and in culture. Covers injury-induced Wallerian degeneration in peripheral nerve only; does not test developmental CNS axon pruning, trophic-deprivation degeneration, or the immune and oligodendrocyte roles.

title: TOM20-driven E3 ligase recruitment regulates mitochondrial dynamics through PLD6.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structures (PDB 9J79, 9J7A, 9J7B, 9JCE) show the TOM20 cytosolic four-helix bundle directly binding the FEM1B ANK1 repeat, defining a TOM20-dependent recruitment of the CRL2-FEM1B E3 ubiquitin ligase to the outer mitochondrial membrane that drives PLD6 degradation and regulates mitochondrial dynamics, distinct from TOM20's canonical presequence import-receptor role.

title: Structure of human PINK1 at a mitochondrial TOM-VDAC array.
review_notes: Cryo-EM structure (PDB 9EIH/9EII/9EIJ) of dimeric human PINK1 stabilized at an endogenous TOM-VDAC array; TOMM5 appears incidentally as a TOM core subunit that, with TOM20, facilitates the symmetric two-TOM/VDAC2 arrangement and binds the PINK1 kinase C-lobes.

title: The p53 tumor suppressor-like protein nvp63 mediates selective germ cell death in the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis.
review_notes: Full text cached; experimental (RNAi, EMSA, reporter assays) on a cnidarian p63-like paralog, not a TP53 ortholog. Used for evolutionary context only.

title: Early diversification and complex evolutionary history of the p53 tumor suppressor gene family.
review_notes: Abstract only. Sequence and phylogeny study; the p53-type versus p63/p73-type label rests on presence or absence of the SAM domain and does not imply orthology to vertebrate TP53. Used for evolutionary context only.

title: The genome of the choanoflagellate Monosiga brevicollis and the origin of metazoans.
review_notes: Full text cached; establishes p53-family presence in a unicellular choanoflagellate. No functional data; used for evolutionary context only.

title: Mdm2 and p53 are highly conserved from placozoans to man.
review_notes: Abstract only; sequence analysis. Supports an early-animal origin of the p53-MDM2 interaction. Used for evolutionary context only.

title: The origins and evolution of the p53 family of genes.
review_notes: Review, abstract only. Its statement that the family is first detected in sea anemones predates or ignores the choanoflagellate homologs (PMID:17924139, PMID:31861340).

title: Characterization of p53 Family Homologs in Evolutionary Remote Branches of Holozoa.
review_notes: Full text cached; bioinformatic and structure-prediction study only, no experiments. Used for evolutionary context only.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.
review_notes: BioPlex AP-MS interactome screen; TPH1 appears only in high-throughput supplementary data, not in the paper text. Supports a bare "protein binding" IPI that is uninformative for TPH1 function.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI Y2H binary interactome map; TPH1 appears only in high-throughput data. Supports a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation.

title: Interactome Mapping Provides a Network of Neurodegenerative Disease Proteins and Uncovers Widespread Protein Aggregation in Affected Brains.
review_notes: Neurodegeneration-focused Y2H interactome; full text not available in cache. Supports a bare, uninformative "protein binding" annotation for TPH1.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.
review_notes: Second BioPlex AP-MS dataset; with-from DNAJC12 (Q9UKB3), a hydroxylase co-chaperone. Interaction itself is plausible but "protein binding" is uninformative as a molecular function.

title: The A328 V/E (rs2887147) polymorphisms in human tryptophan hydroxylase 2 compromise enzyme activity.
review_notes: PMC full text available and read. Primary biochemical characterization of recombinant full-length human TPH2: establishes wild-type tryptophan 5-monooxygenase kinetics (with BH4 and O2) and shows A328E abolishes and A328V reduces activity. Directly supports the IDA tryptophan 5-monooxygenase activity annotation and the description of TPH2 as the rate-limiting brain serotonin-synthesis enzyme.

title: Tryptophan is hydroxylated
review_notes: Reactome reaction record for the tryptophan-hydroxylation step of serotonin biosynthesis; identifies it as the first and rate-limiting step requiring iron(II), tetrahydrobiopterin and dioxygen. Supports the cytosol location (TAS) and the serotonin biosynthetic process assignment.

title: Isolation and characterization of a human thiamine pyrophosphokinase cDNA.
review_notes: Founding cloning and functional characterization of human TPK1 (hTPK1); recombinant enzyme showed thiamine pyrophosphokinase activity and the gene was mapped to 7q34. Abstract-only in the cache (full_text_available: false); supports the enzyme's core catalytic function and biosynthetic role.

title: Thiamine pyrophosphokinase deficiency in encephalopathic children with defects in the pyruvate oxidation pathway.
review_notes: Cited in UniProt as the source of the THMD5 disease variants (Pro-40, His-50, Ser-219). title: Falcon deep research report for TRAPPC1
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) deep-research report compiling current understanding of TRAPPC1. Useful corroboration for established TRAPP-complex biology (core subunit membership with TRAPPC3/TRAPPC4 at the Rab-binding/GEF site; TRAPPIII activates RAB1 for ER-to-Golgi transport and autophagy; TRAPPII activates RAB11; Golgi/ER-Golgi and cis-Golgi localization). IMPORTANT caveat: the report repeatedly attributes whole-TRAPP holo-complex functions (GEF activity, Rab specificity, autophagosome formation) to the TRAPPC1 subunit specifically. Subunit-specific evidence for TRAPPC1 is limited to its structural placement in the conserved core (consistent with PMID:16828797 Bet3-Tpc6B-Mum2 sub-complex) and to patient-variant studies (Zykaj 2024; Van Bergen 2020) showing reduced TRAPPC1 destabilizes the complex and impairs trafficking/autophagy. GEF catalysis is a holo-complex property, not an independent TRAPPC1 activity. Citations are secondary reviews (Galindo & Munro 2023; Bagde & Fromme 2023; Sacher 2019; Hall 2024) not independently verified here.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis run: TRAPPC12 kinetochore moonlighting

title: Falcon deep research report for TRAPPC13
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) literature report. It is internally careful to distinguish TRAPPC13 subunit-specific evidence from holo-complex inference: it correctly states TRAPPC13 does NOT itself catalyze nucleotide exchange and that a recombinant "miniTRAPPIII" lacking TRAPPC12/TRAPPC13 still retains Rab1 GEF activity in vitro (subunit-specific, structural/accessory role at the TRAPPC8/TRAPPC11 arm vertex), while attributing Rab1 GEF activity, ER-to-Golgi transport, Golgi homeostasis, and autophagosome formation to the TRAPPIII complex as a whole. Those complex-level claims should be read as holo-complex inference, not TRAPPC13-specific function. The report frames TRAPPC13 primarily as a TRAPPIII subunit (metazoan TRAPPC8/11/12/13), whereas the existing GOA/ComplexPortal annotations also place it in TRAPPII; this TRAPPII/TRAPPIII partition remains source-dependent and unresolved. Underlying primary sources (Galindo 2021 EMBO J cryo-EM; Galindo & Munro 2023 and Bagde & Fromme 2023 FEBS Lett reviews; Hall 2024 TRAPPopathies; Maeda 2025) are not in the publications/ cache and have not been independently verified here, so correctness is left UNVERIFIED.

title: The bipartite structure of the tRNA m1A58 methyltransferase from S. cerevisiae is conserved in humans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (RNA 2005, 11(8), 1281-90). The cached entry is abstract-only.

title: Insights into RNA biology from an atlas of mammalian mRNA-binding proteins.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell 2012, 149(6), 1393-406). Correctly cited proteome-wide mRNA interactome capture; TRMT6 is one of 860 proteins recovered. title: Crystal Structure of the Human tRNA m(1)A58 Methyltransferase-tRNA(3)(Lys) Complex: Refolding of Substrate tRNA Allows Access to the Methylation Target.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (J Mol Biol 2015, 427(24), 3862-76). The definitive reference for TRMT6's molecular function. It shows the non-catalytic chain acting as the tRNA-binding subunit, working in trans across the dimer interface, and remodelling the T- and D-loops so that the buried A58 reaches the partner active site.

Marked DISPUTED because the underlying claim of internal mRNA m1A is contested by later biochemical validation (PMID:42337368), not because the citation is wrong. The cached entry is abstract-only.

It also reports m1A destabilising its target, the opposite direction to PMID:41103012 and PMID:42003777. Cited for completeness of the disputed literature only; no annotation in this review rests on it.

title: Falcon deep research report for TTC8
review_notes: LLM (Edison/Falcon) synthesis of secondary reviews (Tian 2023, Melluso 2023, Florea 2021) and cryo-EM structural papers (Chou 2019, Singh 2020, Klink 2020, Yang 2020) plus Dilan 2018; none of these primary/review sources are in our publications cache, so claims are UNVERIFIED pending full-text checking. TTC8-subunit-specific claims that align with the structural literature and are retained here are (i) TTC8 is a non-catalytic TPR/alpha-solenoid (~12-TPR) structural subunit, (ii) loss of TTC8 destabilizes the BBSome, and (iii) the IVS1-2A>G splice variant causes photoreceptor-specific BBS8 ablation and non-syndromic RP. Claims framed as whole-BBSome (holo-complex) activities -- GPCR/SMO/GPR161/SSTR3 cargo recognition, ARL6/BBS3-dependent activation, transition-zone crossing, IFT coupling, and Hedgehog/Wnt/insulin/leptin signaling outputs -- are properties of the assembled octamer, NOT autonomous molecular functions of TTC8, and are not transferred to TTC8 as enables MF annotations. The report's label of TTC8 as a "peripheral" subunit is a structural-position descriptor, not a statement that TTC8 is dispensable.

review_notes: Relevance is MEDIUM because the report plausibly identifies the relevant biological context (UMA-domain ESCRT-I accessory subunit family) and a primary functional study (Glover et al. 2023) that, if verified, would substantially inform UMAD1 function. Correctness is UNVERIFIED: the strong claims ("Primary Function: Role in Cytokinetic Abscission" and "Functional Redundancy with ALIX") rest almost entirely on the Glover 2023 paper, which is not in the local cache and was not read; the report's per-claim "citations" are page-range tags rather than checkable quotes. The abscission, CEP55/TSG101-stabilization, ESCRT-III-turnover, and ALIX-redundancy claims should be treated as DISPUTED/unverified pending direct reading of Glover 2023, and were NOT promoted into accepted GO functions, core_functions, or the description in this review.

title: Falcon deep research report for USP21
review_notes: LLM-synthesized (Edison/Falcon) literature report; useful for substrate breadth and chain-type/pathway context, but treated as UNVERIFIED. USP21-SPECIFIC substrate evidence that the report attributes to dedicated primary papers includes: RIG-I deubiquitination / negative regulation of antiviral RIG-I-IFN signaling (Fan et al. 2014, J Exp Med, doi:10.1084/jem.20122844), MEK2 stabilization driving ERK/MAPK signaling (Li et al. 2018, doi:10.1038/s41419-018-0523-z), Nanog stabilization in ESC pluripotency (Liu et al. 2016), histone H2A K119ub deubiquitination, MARK3/macropinocytosis in pancreatic cancer (Hou et al. 2021), TCF7, and microtubule/centrosome association (Urbe et al. 2012). These primary papers are NOT in the local publications cache and could not be verified here, so substrate identities and chain-type assignments are recorded but not used to change existing experimental annotations. DUB-FAMILY-LEVEL inference (broad chain-type promiscuity, ISG15 cross-reactivity, general USP catalytic mechanism) should not be over-read as USP21-specific physiological function. NOTE a conflict to flag for experts: this report (citing Ye et al. 2011 structural work) states USP21 is "inactive against NEDD8 conjugates", whereas the curated IDA annotation GO:0019784 (PMID:10799498) records deNEDDylase activity; the existing experimental deNEDDylase annotation is retained and NOT weakened on the basis of this report.

review_notes: Cached full text of this blood-brain barrier review does not mention vinculin; it does not support the NAS maintenance of blood-brain barrier annotation.

title: Bioinformatics analysis of VCP domains, motifs, disease mutations, and cofactor interfaces
review_notes: Directly inspected; reproducible local sequence/UniProt analysis that corroborates the accepted ATPase-domain architecture, disease-mutation clustering, and cofactor-interface model but does not by itself change GO annotation calls.

title: Vezatin, a novel transmembrane protein, bridges myosin VIIA to the cadherin-catenins complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. The defining paper for VEZT; establishes myosin VIIA binding, adherens junction localization and the stereocilia ankle-link site.

title: Unconventional myosin VIIa and vezatin, two proteins crucial for Listeria entry into epithelial cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Source of the UniProt EXP plasma-membrane annotation for Q9HBM0. Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract nonetheless states the junctional localization directly.

title: Vezatin, a protein associated to adherens junctions, is required for mouse blastocyst morphogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract only. Identified as the likely experimental basis for the mouse nucleus location that is transferred to human VEZT by ISS and by UniProt subcellular-location mapping.

title: Vezatin, a ubiquitous protein of adherens cell-cell junctions, is exclusively expressed in germ cells in mouse testis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract only. Underpins the acrosomal vesicle location, which is mouse germ-cell specific and treated here as non-core.

title: Conditional knock-out reveals that zygotic vezatin-null mouse embryos die at implantation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract only. Strongest loss-of-function evidence that vezatin is required for cadherin-dependent intercellular adhesion.

title: Molecular characterization of the ankle-link complex in cochlear hair cells and its role in the hair bundle functioning.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Primary evidence for the stereocilia ankle link complex annotation; also the source of the vezatin-usherin direct interaction.

title: Vezatin, an integral membrane protein of adherens junctions, is required for the sound resilience of cochlear hair cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Establishes membrane topology, the late-recruitment and stability role at adherens junctions, and the radixin interaction.

title: Vezatin is essential for dendritic spine morphogenesis and functional synaptic maturation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Context for the synaptic role; no corresponding human GOA line at present.

title: Endometrial vezatin and its association with endometriosis risk.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached abstract only. A regulatory and disease-association result, not evidence of a molecular function, and deliberately not used to support any GO annotation.

title: Vezatin is required for the maturation of the neuromuscular synapse.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Not the basis of any current human GOA line; recorded as context for the general role of vezatin in stabilizing specialized membrane assemblies.

title: A Conserved Role for Vezatin Proteins in Cargo-Specific Regulation of Retrograde Axonal Transport.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Invertebrate and fish genetics; tagged human VEZT did not rescue the fly phenotype, so this is not used to support any human annotation here.

title: Falcon deep research for VEZT
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis. Every claim used here was independently checked against the primary papers (PMID:11080149, PMID:20049712, PMID:17567809, PMID:15090598) before being relied on.

title: Falcon deep research report for VPS37D
review_notes: LLM-synthesized deep-research report. The VPS37D-specific claims it makes are appropriately hedged and consistent with the existing review: VPS37D is the least functionally characterized of the four human VPS37 paralogs, is a bona fide core ESCRT-I structural subunit, does NOT show the SH3YL1/CDIP1 selective interactions reported for VPS37B/C, and has no VPS37A-like autophagy UEVL specialization established in the cited literature; it explicitly states that direct VPS37D-specific mechanistic evidence remains limited. The one novel VPS37D-specific assertion (breast-cancer biomarker association from chen2025escrtmayfunction; negligible VPS37D expression in colorectal tissue from kolmus2021) is disease/expression context, not a molecular-function or core-process claim, and was not used to change any GO annotation. All other pathway content (autophagosome closure, cytokinetic abscission, membrane/NE repair, viral budding) is ESCRT-I holo-complex or VPS37A-C paralog inference and is NOT attributed to the VPS37D subunit. Underlying primary PMIDs were not independently re-verified here, hence UNVERIFIED.

title: CRIg: a macrophage complement receptor required for phagocytosis of circulating pathogens.
review_notes: Discovery paper (Cell 2006), PubMed-verified; knockout data are in mouse. Abstract-only in cache.

title: VSIG4, a B7 family-related protein, is a negative regulator of T cell activation.
review_notes: Full text cached; evidence relies on soluble Ig fusion proteins, and the T cell counter-receptor is not identified.

title: Structure of C3b in complex with CRIg gives insights into regulation of complement activation.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache; PubMed metadata confirmed (Nature 2006). Primary source for C3b binding and AP convertase inhibition.

title: A novel inhibitor of the alternative pathway of complement reverses inflammation and bone destruction in experimental arthritis.
review_notes: Shows that AP inhibition is conserved between human and mouse CRIg; uses soluble CRIg-Fc.

title: Complement receptor of the Ig superfamily enhances complement-mediated phagocytosis in a subpopulation of tissue resident macrophages.
review_notes: Mouse peritoneal macrophages; CRIg binds opsonized targets independently of divalent cations.

title: CRIg signals induce anti-intracellular bacterial phagosome activity in a chloride intracellular channel 3-dependent manner.
review_notes: CLIC3 binds the CRIg cytoplasmic domain; supports signaling receptor activity.

title: CRIg Functions as a Macrophage Pattern Recognition Receptor to Directly Bind and Capture Blood-Borne Gram-Positive Bacteria.
review_notes: Mouse intravital study; complement-independent LTA recognition. Single study, so not annotated.

title: Extracellular stimulation of VSIG4/complement receptor Ig suppresses intracellular bacterial infection by inducing autophagy.
review_notes: VSIG4 engagement induces autophagosome formation in macrophages and in VSIG4-expressing HeLa cells.

title: VSIG4 inhibits proinflammatory macrophage activation by reprogramming mitochondrial pyruvate metabolism.
review_notes: Vsig4-/- mice plus human VSIG4+ THP-1 cells; PI3K/Akt-STAT3-PDK2 axis.

title: VSIG4 mediates transcriptional inhibition of Nlrp3 and Il-1β in macrophages.
review_notes: The MS4A6D partner is a mouse protein (no direct human ortholog with an established role).

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI Y2H screen; source of generic protein binding rows (VAMP5, JAGN1, FATE1) with no functional follow-up.

title: Binding of ADAMTS13 to von Willebrand factor.
review_notes: ADAMTS13-VWF binding kinetics; VWF as substrate.

title: Two Cys residues essential for von Willebrand factor multimer assembly in the Golgi.
review_notes: Full text; defines Cys1099/Cys1142 in D3 multimerization.

title: Large-scale proteomics and phosphoproteomics of urinary exosomes.
review_notes: Urinary exosome proteome; high-throughput detection only.

title: von Willebrand factor, Jedi knight of the bloodstream.
review_notes: Full-text review (Springer, Blood 2014); verified statements on FVIII binding by D'D3, alphaIIb-beta3 RGD binding in C4, and shear-dependent VWF-mediated aggregation.

title: Novel factor VIII variants with a modified furin cleavage site improve the efficacy of gene therapy for hemophilia A.
review_notes: FVIII gene-therapy variant paper; VWF appears only as the SPR binding partner of FVIII variants.

title: The relationship of N-linked glycosylation and heavy chain-binding protein association with the secretion of glycoproteins.
review_notes: Abstract states VWF associates transiently with BiP (immunoglobulin heavy chain binding protein); it supports chaperone binding, not the GO:0019865 immunoglobulin binding annotation derived from it.

title: Biochemistry and genetics of von Willebrand factor.
review_notes: Sadler 1998 review; abstract supports hemostasis, adhesion bridging and FVIII carrier roles.

title: Protein-protein interactions between large proteins: two-hybrid screening using a functionally classified library composed of long cDNAs.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H screen among large KIAA proteins (whirlin = KIAA1526); establishes only that whirlin engages in binary interactions, no whirlin-specific functional insight in the abstract (cached record is abstract-only).

title: Myosin-XVa is required for tip localization of whirlin and differential elongation of hair-cell stereocilia.
review_notes: Founding paper for the stereocilium tip module; shows myosin-XVa interacts with whirlin's third PDZ domain via its C-terminal PDZ-ligand and delivers whirlin to stereocilia tips, and that GFP-Myo15a transfection into shaker-2 hair cells restores hair-bundle architecture by recruiting endogenous whirlin to tips. Abstract-only in cache but the abstract states these findings verbatim.

title: The DFNB31 gene product whirlin connects to the Usher protein network in the cochlea and retina by direct association with USH2A and VLGR1.
review_notes: Founding paper for whirlin's direct association with USH2A and VLGR1b (ADGRV1) and its co-localization at synapses and the photoreceptor connecting cilium region; abstract-only in cache but abstract explicitly supports the claims cited here.

title: A novel gene for Usher syndrome type 2: mutations in the long isoform of whirlin are associated with retinitis pigmentosa and sensorineural hearing loss.
review_notes: Defines USH2D; human genetic (IMP) evidence that long-isoform whirlin is required for both hearing and retinal function. Abstract-only in cache but the abstract states the key findings verbatim.

title: MPP1 links the Usher protein network and the Crumbs protein complex in the retina.
review_notes: Direct, strong whirlin-MPP1/p55 interaction and retinal co-localization (OLM, synaptic layer, basal body, ciliary axoneme); links Usher and Crumbs networks. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Regulation of stereocilia length by myosin XVa and whirlin depends on the actin-regulatory protein Eps8.
review_notes: Full text in cache. Establishes Eps8 as the third integral component of the stereocilia tip complex with MyoXVa and whirlin, shows Eps8 tip localization depends on MyoXVa and is reduced without whirlin, and concludes whirlin serves as a scaffold for the assembly, stability, and targeting of the MyoXVa:Eps8 complex; directly supports the tip elongation-module core function.

title: Guanylate kinase domains of the MAGUK family scaffold proteins as specific phospho-protein-binding modules.
review_notes: Whirlin appears as a phospho-dependent ligand of the CASK SH3-GK module (pSer685 peptide); mechanistically interesting for CASK, marginal for defining whirlin's own function.

title: Alterations of the CIB2 calcium- and integrin-binding protein cause Usher syndrome type 1J and nonsyndromic deafness DFNB48.
review_notes: Shows CIB2-whirlin interaction and whirlin localization at stereocilia tips; also shows whirlin is not required for CIB2 tip localization in vivo.

title: Whirlin and PDZ domain-containing 7 (PDZD7) proteins are both required to form the quaternary protein complex associated with Usher syndrome type 2.
review_notes: Full text cached; systematic demonstration of the WHRN-PDZD7-USH2A-GPR98 quaternary USH2 complex, WHRN's preference for USH2A, and WHRN-PDZD7 bridging; key mechanistic reference for the ankle-link/USH2 complex annotations.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: HuRI proteome-scale Y2H map; source of multiple uninformative 'protein binding' IPI lines for WHRN.

title: Quantitative fragmentomics allow affinity mapping of interactomes.
review_notes: In vitro holdup/fragmentomics affinity mapping of PDZ-motif interactions; source of >400 'protein binding' GOA lines for WHRN plus the identical-protein-binding annotation. Demonstrates binding capability, not physiological interaction.

title: Subcellular localization of xanthine oxidase in rat hepatocytes: high-resolution immunoelectron microscopic study combined with biochemical analysis.
review_notes: Rat hepatocyte immunoelectron microscopy localizing XO to the cytosol; the MGI-assigned reference for the human XDH cytosol IDA and the array of purine catabolic-process IDAs. Directly supports cytosolic localization and argues against peroxisomal/organellar XO. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Human colostrum: identification of minor proteins in the aqueous phase by proteomics.
review_notes: Proteomics identification of XDH as a minor protein in human colostrum; supports the secreted/extracellular (milk) pool. Contextual, not central to the enzyme's core catalytic function.

title: Human xanthine oxidase changes its substrate specificity to aldehyde oxidase type upon mutation of amino acid residues in the active site: roles of active site residues in binding and activation of purine substrate.
review_notes: Crystal structure of human XOR (E803V mutant) in complex with FAD, 2Fe-2S, molybdopterin and salicylate; directly establishes the cofactor complement, homodimeric subunit structure, active-site purine-binding residues and allopurinol interaction. Cited by UniProt for COFACTOR, CATALYTIC ACTIVITY, FUNCTION and SUBUNIT.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput Y2H interactome (HuRI); source of the bare protein-binding IPI (interactor GRIP1 isoform Q9Y3R0-3). Systematic screen, not focused on XDH function; yields an uninformative molecular-function term.

title: Cloning and expression in vitro of human xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase.
review_notes: Cloning and heterologous expression of the complete human XDH/XO coding sequence with measured XDH/XO enzyme activity; the enzyme was expressed predominantly in the dehydrogenase form. UniProt CATALYTIC ACTIVITY reference for EC 1.17.1.4. Directly supports xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase activity in human.

title: The XRCC2 and XRCC3 repair genes are required for chromosome stability in mammalian cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Establishes XRCC2's requirement for chromosome stability; irs1 (XRCC2-mutant) cells accumulate breaks/deletions/translocations. Supports the DNA repair IGI annotation.

title: Mammalian XRCC2 promotes the repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Johnson, Liu, Jasin, Nature 1999). Classic demonstration that XRCC2-deficient hamster cells show >100-fold decrease in DSB-induced HR between sister chromatids while NHEJ is normal. Direct experimental support for the DSBR-HR annotation.

title: XRCC2 is a nuclear RAD51-like protein required for damage-dependent RAD51 focus formation without the need for ATP binding.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (O'Regan et al., JBC 2001). XRCC2 localizes to the nucleus and is required for damage-dependent RAD51 focus formation, yet P-loop (ATP-binding) mutants still complement irs1. Supports the mediator (not ATP-dependent damage-sensor) role and the MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED call on GO:0140664.

title: Identification and purification of two distinct complexes containing the five RAD51 paralogs.
review_notes: Full text verified. Defines the BCDX2 complex (RAD51B-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2) and shows it binds ssDNA and ssDNA gaps. Primary evidence for the GO:0033063 complex annotation.

title: Homologous pairing and ring and filament structure formation activities of the human Xrcc2*Rad51D complex.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Purified Xrcc2*Rad51D subcomplex catalyzes homologous pairing between ssDNA and dsDNA and forms ssDNA-dependent filaments. Supports DNA strand invasion.

title: Ring-shaped Rad51 paralog protein complexes bind Holliday junctions and replication forks as visualized by electron microscopy.
review_notes: Full text verified. Direct EM shows BCDX2 binds Holliday junctions and replication forks with high specificity. Supports four-way junction DNA binding and replication-fork localization.

title: Homologous recombination proteins are associated with centrosomes and are required for mitotic stability.
review_notes: Abstract verified. Shows XRCC2 centrosome co-localization and mitotic-stability requirement; supports the (non-core) centrosome, centrosome cycle and mitotic cell cycle annotations.

title: Rad51 paralog complexes BCDX2 and CX3 act at different stages in the BRCA1-BRCA2-dependent homologous recombination pathway.
review_notes: Verified. Places BCDX2 downstream of BRCA2 and upstream of RAD51 recruitment in HR; supports the DSBR-HR IMP annotation and the mediator model.

title: Complementation of hypersensitivity to DNA interstrand crosslinking agents demonstrates that XRCC2 is a Fanconi anaemia gene.
review_notes: Full text verified (Park et al., J Med Genet 2016; PMC5035190). Establishes XRCC2 as Fanconi anemia complementation group U (FANCU): wild-type XRCC2 corrects MMC hypersensitivity, chromosome breakage and G2-M accumulation of patient cells with biallelic XRCC2 mutation; XRCC2 acts late in the FA-BRCA pathway (FANCD2 monoubiquitination normal). Primary evidence for the new interstrand cross-link repair annotation.

title: XRCC2 mutation causes meiotic arrest, azoospermia and infertility.
review_notes: Full text verified (Yang et al., J Med Genet 2018; PMC6119352). Homozygous XRCC2 p.Leu14Pro causes meiotic arrest, azoospermia and infertility in a consanguineous family; a knockin mouse reproduces meiotic arrest, azoospermia and premature ovarian failure. Direct human/mouse evidence strengthening the (non-core) meiotic cell cycle annotation beyond the original testis-expression inference.

title: XRCC2 Regulates Replication Fork Progression during dNTP Alterations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Saxena, Somyajit, Nagaraju, Cell Rep 2018). XRCC2 (FANCU) and RAD51D restrain active DNA synthesis during dNTP alterations independently of HDR, via ATR-mediated phosphorylation of XRCC2 Ser247. XRCC2-specific corroboration of the replication-fork localization/function annotation.

title: Sequential role of RAD51 paralog complexes in replication fork remodeling and restart.
review_notes: Verified. Shows the BCDX2 subcomplex restrains fork progression and promotes fork reversal under replication stress. Supports replication-fork localization/function.

title: Structure and function of the RAD51B-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2 tumour suppressor.
review_notes: Full text verified. Definitive cryo-EM structure/function of BCDX2: RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2 mimic three aligned RAD51 protomers; BCDX2 stimulates RAD51 filament nucleation/extension in an ATP-hydrolysis-dependent manner (RAD51B/RAD51C ATPases); XRCC2 binds ATP via Walker A K54/T55, Walker B D149. Primary evidence for the mediator core function.

title: The XRCC2 DNA repair gene from human and mouse encodes a novel member of the recA/RAD51 family.
review_notes: Verified. Original identification of XRCC2 as a recA/RAD51-family DNA-repair gene; testis-elevated expression suggests a meiotic role. Supports DNA repair and meiotic cell cycle annotations.

title: Premetazoan origin of the hippo signaling pathway.
review_notes: Capsaspora coYki/coSd/coHpo assayed in Drosophila cells and tissue; establishes ancestral TEAD-coactivator function. Full text cached.

title: Genome editing in the unicellular holozoan Capsaspora owczarzaki suggests a premetazoan role for the Hippo pathway in multicellular morphogenesis.
review_notes: coYki knockout in Capsaspora: cortical blebbing and altered aggregate shape, no proliferation phenotype. Evolutionary context for YAP1.

title: The Hippo kinase cascade regulates a contractile cell behavior and cell density in a close unicellular relative of animals.
review_notes: coHpo/coWts knockouts make coYki nuclear; hyperactive coYki phenotypes need the TEAD-binding residue.

title: Assembling a Hippo: the evolutionary emergence of an animal developmental signaling pathway.
review_notes: Review of Hippo pathway evolution; argues proliferation control is a later co-option.

title: Global landscape of HIV-human protein complexes.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Supports a physical association with HIV-1 capsid, but only as a bare protein-binding datum.

title: Topology of the human and mouse m6A RNA methylomes revealed by m6A-seq.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, and the cached text does not mention YTHDF3, so the IDA drawn from it could not be checked. Not flagged as miscited - the curator read the full text and the annotation is corroborated by five other IDAs to the same term.

title: The mRNA-bound proteome and its global occupancy profile on protein-coding transcripts.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. High-throughput mRNA interactome capture; supports generic RNA binding only.

title: N6-methyladenosine-dependent regulation of messenger RNA stability.
review_notes: Full text cached. The abstract is about YTHDF2, but the methods section contains a GST-YTHDF3 construct and an anti-YTHDF3 antibody, confirming that YTHDF3 was directly assayed. Verified as correctly cited for YTHDF3.

title: YTHDF3 facilitates translation and decay of N(6)-methyladenosine-modified RNA.
review_notes: Full text cached. Correctly cited and a primary source for YTHDF3 function, but its translation-promoting conclusion is directly contradicted by PMID:32492408; the mRNA-decay conclusion is not.

title: Cytoplasmic m(6)A reader YTHDF3 promotes mRNA translation.

title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks.

title: m(6)A enhances the phase separation potential of mRNA.
review_notes: Full text cached. Establishes multivalent m6A-driven condensation of YTHDF proteins and their partitioning into P-bodies, stress granules and neuronal RNA granules.

title: Antibody cross-reactivity accounts for widespread appearance of m(1)A in 5'UTRs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Grozhik et al., Nat Commun 2019). Full text cached. Not about YTHDF3, but load-bearing for the review because it shows that the mRNA m1A substrate underlying the YTHDF3 m1A-reader claim was largely an antibody cap-binding artifact.

title: Cytoplasmic m(1)A reader YTHDF3 inhibits trophoblast invasion by downregulation of m(1)A-methylated IGF1R.
review_notes: Full text cached. Correctly cited for YTHDF3, and the IGF1R turnover and trophoblast phenotypes are real; but the m1A-reader framing depends on m1A-seq, whose specificity was challenged the previous year (PMID:31719534).

title: No evidence for DNA N (6)-methyladenine in mammals.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Douvlataniotis et al., Sci Adv 2020). Full text cached. Not about YTHDF3, but cited as part of the evidence that the substrate of the proposed DNA-6mA-reader role is largely artifactual.

title: A reference map of the human binary protein interactome.

title: m(6)A-binding YTHDF proteins promote stress granule formation.

title: Dual proteome-scale networks reveal cell-specific remodeling of the human interactome.

title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics.
review_notes: Full text cached. Interactome/cell-map dataset; supports the YTHDF1 interaction as a bare binding datum.

title: YTHDF3 recognizes DNA N6-methyladenine and recruits ALKBH1 for 6mA removal from genomic DNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Chen et al., EMBO J 2025). Full text cached. Proposes an entirely new substrate class for YTHDF3 - N6-methyladenine in genomic DNA. Recorded here because it is the most recent functional claim about this gene, but not annotated: the mark being read is itself contested (PMID:32206710, PMID:32203414, PMID:35113693, PMID:41254163), the paper's own abstract concedes that the ALKBH1 dsDNA demethylase activity remains largely debated, and its senior authorship overlaps with the original human genomic 6mA study rather than constituting independent confirmation. title: Mapping the Zap-70 phosphorylation sites on LAT (linker for activation of T cells) required for recruitment and activation of signalling proteins in T cells.

title: The mammalian-membrane two-hybrid assay (MaMTH) for probing membrane-protein interactions in human cells.

title: Extensive rewiring of the EGFR network in colorectal cancer cells expressing transforming levels of KRAS(G13D).

title: ZAP-70 augments tonic B-cell receptor and CCR7 signaling in IGHV-unmutated chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

title: Sequential interactions of the TCR with two distinct cytoplasmic tyrosine kinases.

title: ZAP-70 binding specificity to T cell receptor tyrosine-based activation motifs: the tandem SH2 domains of ZAP-70 bind distinct tyrosine-based activation motifs with varying affinity.
review_notes: Direct binding assays: tandem SH2 domains bind doubly phosphorylated zeta/CD3 epsilon TAMs.

title: Essential role for ZAP-70 in both positive and negative selection of thymocytes.

title: Human and mouse killer-cell inhibitory receptors recruit PTP1C and PTP1D protein tyrosine phosphatases.

title: LAT: the ZAP-70 tyrosine kinase substrate that links T cell receptor to cellular activation.

title: Falcon deep research report for human ZAP70
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis citing 11 distinct sources (mostly 2021-2024 reviews and three bioRxiv preprints). Core content (tandem SH2 binding of doubly phosphorylated ITAMs, LCK-dependent activation via Y319/Y493, LAT and SLP-76 as principal substrates, electrostatic substrate selection, inability to phosphorylate ITAMs) agrees with primary literature checked here (PMID:27700984, PMID:34923645, PMID:37313400). Weaknesses: it repeatedly asserts robust ZAP70 autophosphorylation, which PMID:27700984 contradicts; it relies on unrefereed preprints (thermodynamic brake, kinetic avidity, allosteric hot spot); it gives no PMIDs; it says nothing about THEMIS, VAV1 direct phosphorylation evidence or DUSP3.

title: IFNbeta responses induced by intracellular bacteria or cytosolic DNA in different human cells do not require ZBP1 (DLM-1/DAI).
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell Microbiol 2008;10:2579-88). Directly tests the human protein and reports a negative result for the interferon arm, which is the key human-specific counterweight to the mouse-derived GO:0060340 annotations.

title: An orthogonal proteomic-genomic screen identifies AIM2 as a cytoplasmic DNA sensor for the inflammasome.

title: DAI/ZBP1 recruits RIP1 and RIP3 through RIP homotypic interaction motifs to activate NF-kappaB.

title: Bcl2 regulation by the melanocyte master regulator Mitf modulates lineage survival and melanoma cell viability.

title: During negative selection, Nur77 family proteins translocate to mitochondria where they associate with Bcl-2 and expose its proapoptotic BH3 domain.

title: A short Nur77-derived peptide converts Bcl-2 from a protector to a killer.
review_notes: Full Results/Fig1E–G,6J,8C–F independently read. WT versus Bcl2-knockout MEFs show Bcl2-dependent NuBCP9 death; biochemical mechanism exposes a BH3 activity that neutralizes BCLXL, not direct BAX activation. Cross-species and recombinant experiments distinguished.

title: T cell-specific inhibition of multiple apoptotic pathways blocks negative selection and causes autoimmunity.

title: Expression of Bcl-2 protein in murine neural cells in culture.
review_notes: Identifier and abstract inspected; full source-specific Bcl2 assay could not be verified. An abstract focused on another protein is not proof of misattribution. Biological claims may be supported independently, with narrow unverified assertions left unresolved.
