title: Automatic assignment of GO terms using logical inference, based on on inter-ontology links
review_notes: The rule (phenylalanine 4-monooxygenase activity implies involvement in L-tyrosine biosynthesis) is itself correct but was applied to a false premise, since GO:0004505 does not hold for Pcbd2. The resulting GO:0006571 annotation is recommended for removal.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA00029278 assigns GO:0004505 phenylalanine 4-monooxygenase activity to Pcbd2 and Pcbd1. Contradicted by UniProt's own experimentally-supported EC 4.2.1.96 and Lyase assignment on this entry. Recommended for removal, with review of the rule's condition set.

title: Mirk protein kinase is activated by MKK3 and functions as a transcriptional activator of HNF1alpha.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Lim, Jin, Friedman; J Biol Chem 2002). The paper that cloned DCoHm, which is PCBD2, as a Mirk/DYRK1B-binding protein, and showed it enhances HNF1alpha transcriptional activity like DCoH. This is the source of human PCBD2's GO:0045893 IDA and therefore the upstream evidence for the mouse ISO. Abstract-only in cache; the coactivation statement is in the abstract. Title foregrounds Mirk rather than DCoHm, which is normal and not a citation problem.

title: Biochemical and structural basis for partially redundant enzymatic and transcriptional functions of DCoH and DCoH2.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Rose, Pullen, Bayle, Crabtree, Alber; Biochemistry 2004). The source reference for the MGI IDA that geneontology/go-annotation#6591 asks to correct, and for the Pcbd2 crystal structures. The abstract states the enzymology for this protein - "Like DCoH, DCoH2 ... displays pterin-4alpha-carbinolamine dehydratase activity" - an exact synonym of GO:0008124 and not of GO:0004505. Cached abstract-only, so the PhhB complementation assay the issue describes is in full text I could not read; UniProt read it and assigned EC 4.2.1.96 to this entry with ECO:0000269 from this reference, which corroborates the issue's reading.

title: A mitochondrial protein compendium elucidates complex I disease biology.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Pagliarini et al., Cell 2008); the MitoCarta compendium and the sole source of the mitochondrion annotation. Marked LOW_QUALITY in the specific sense that it is a high-throughput MS inventory whose own text notes that published MS-based reports show up to 41% false positive rates, and the cached text does not name Pcbd2 (the gene list is supplementary). The annotation is retained as non-core rather than removed because three further organellar datasets and a presequence-like N-terminal extension support it; see Pcbd2-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md.

title: Label-free quantitative proteomics of the lysine acetylome in mitochondria identifies substrates of SIRT3 in metabolic pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Rardin et al., PNAS 2013). Cited here only as corroborating detection of Pcbd2 in a liver mitochondrial preparation: UniProt's K120/K124/K131 acetylation sites on Q9CZL5 carry ECO:0007744 from this study. The cached text does not name Pcbd2, so the checkable fact is the UniProt evidence tag rather than a quotable sentence. Contributes no GO annotation of its own.

title: SIRT5-mediated lysine desuccinylation impacts diverse metabolic pathways.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Park et al., Mol Cell 2013). Cited here only as corroborating detection of Pcbd2 in a liver mitochondrial preparation: UniProt's K120/K124/K131 succinylation sites on Q9CZL5 carry ECO:0007744 from this study. The cached text does not name Pcbd2, so the checkable fact is the UniProt evidence tag rather than a quotable sentence. Contributes no GO annotation of its own.

title: Intestine-specific deletion of SIRT1 in mice impairs DCoH2-HNF-1α-FXR signaling and alters systemic bile acid homeostasis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kazgan et al., Gastroenterology 2014); full text cached. The most informative mouse-specific paper on this gene: direct nucleus/cytoplasm immunofluorescence in Hepa1-6 cells, an FXR-promoter reporter assay showing that an acetylation-mimicking DCoH2 mutant loses coactivation, and the SIRT1-dependent regulation of the Hnf1a interaction. It is UniProt's source for both FUNCTION and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION on this entry yet supports no GOA annotation at all, which is the main curation gap identified by this review and the basis of the proposed NEW GO:0003713.

title: Quantitative high-confidence human mitochondrial proteome and its dynamics in cellular context.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Morgenstern et al., Cell Metab 2021). Not a mouse paper and not a source of any mouse annotation; cited because QuickGO records human PCBD2 (Q9H0N5) as located_in GO:0005739 with HTP evidence from it, which makes the mitochondrial claim for this family considerably harder to dismiss than the 2008 MitoCarta row alone. The cached text does not name PCBD2 - the MitoCoP membership list is supplementary - so the checkable fact is the GOA annotation, verified via QuickGO.

title: Does the Pcbd2-specific N-terminal extension look like a mitochondrial presequence? (this repository)
review_notes: Analysis written for this review. Scores the Pcbd2-specific N-terminal 32 residues against 259 reviewed mouse mitochondrial transit peptides and 300 reviewed mouse cytosolic N-termini, with mouse Pcbd1 as an internal negative control and alanine content reported as an explicit confounder. Reproducible from Pcbd2-bioinformatics/nterm_mts_analysis.py; no thresholds are asserted and no targeting predictor was run, so it establishes compatibility with a presequence, not import.

title: UniProtKB entry Q9CZL5 (PHS2_MOUSE), repository snapshot
review_notes: Curated UniProt record for the gene under review, and decisive for the molecular function question: EC 4.2.1.96 and the RHEA:11920 CATALYTIC ACTIVITY block are both tagged ECO:0000269|PubMed:15182178, i.e. experimental evidence from the very reference MGI cites for GO:0004505. Also the source for the acetylation sites, the Cytoplasm/Nucleus location, and the Erroneous initiation flags on the two mRNAs that bear on the N-terminal extension.

title: SUMO modification of STAT1 and its role in PIAS-mediated inhibition of gene activation.
review_notes: STAT1 inhibition by PIAS1 does not require STAT1 sumoylation; PIAS1 is not the STAT1 E3.

title: The negative regulator of Gli, Suppressor of fused (Sufu), interacts with SAP18, Galectin3 and other nuclear proteins.
review_notes: Sufu Y2H screen; PIAS1 only listed among unconfirmed prey (abstract-only).

title: Transcriptional activity of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma is modulated by SUMO-1 modification.
review_notes: Abstract states PIAS1 and PIASxbeta are E3 ligases for PPARgamma.

title: Control of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma2 stability and activity by SUMOylation.
review_notes: Abstract-only; abstract does not mention PIAS1. EXP SUMO transferase annotation accepted by deferring to the curator.

title: PIAS1 selectively inhibits interferon-inducible genes and is important in innate immunity.
review_notes: Pias1-/- mice: PIAS1 restrains STAT1 promoter recruitment and a subset of IFN-inducible genes.

title: The transactivating function of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma is negatively regulated by SUMO conjugation in the amino-terminal domain.
review_notes: Abstract-only; abstract does not mention PIAS1. EXP SUMO transferase annotation accepted by deferring to the curator.

title: Negative regulation of NF-kappaB signaling by PIAS1.
review_notes: PIAS1 binds p65 and blocks its DNA binding; Pias1-/- cells/mice show enhanced NF-kB responses. Basis for the NEW annotation.

title: A SUMOylation-dependent pathway mediates transrepression of inflammatory response genes by PPAR-gamma.
review_notes: Full text: PIAS1 binds and sumoylates PPARgamma; siRNA knockdown abolishes PPARgamma transrepression of iNOS in macrophages.

title: Interaction of protein inhibitor of activated STAT (PIAS) proteins with the TATA-binding protein, TBP.
review_notes: Full text: direct PIAS1-TBP interaction mapped to a conserved 39-aa C-terminal region; endogenous co-IP from mouse tissues.

title: PIAS1 confers DNA-binding specificity on the Msx1 homeoprotein.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; PIAS1 tethers Msx1 to the nuclear periphery and confers DNA-binding specificity, independent of Msx1 sumoylation.

title: The interaction of Piasy with Trim32, an E3-ubiquitin ligase mutated in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2H, promotes Piasy degradation and regulates UVB-induced keratinocyte apoptosis through NFkappaB.
review_notes: Abstract-only; abstract concerns Trim32-Piasy. PIAS1 IPI retained deferring to the curator.

title: SUMOylation of Tr2 orphan receptor involves Pml and fine-tunes Oct4 expression in stem cells.
review_notes: Abstract-only; abstract does not name PIAS1. UniProt cites it for the PIAS1-NR2C1 interaction promoting Tr2 sumoylation.

title: Proinflammatory stimuli induce IKKalpha-mediated phosphorylation of PIAS1 to restrict inflammation and immunity.
review_notes: IKKalpha phosphorylates PIAS1 Ser90 to switch on repression; requires PIAS1 ligase activity.

title: Sumoylation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma by apoptotic cells prevents lipopolysaccharide-induced NCoR removal from kappaB binding sites mediating transrepression of proinflammatory cytokines.
review_notes: PIAS1 knockdown in RAW264.7 cells eliminates apoptotic-cell/PPARgamma suppression of NF-kB.

title: Mammalian SUMO E3-ligases PIAS1 and PIAS4 promote responses to DNA double-strand breaks.
review_notes: Human cells: PIAS1 and PIAS4 promote DSB repair; supports ISO DNA damage rows.

title: The SUMO E3-ligase PIAS1 regulates the tumor suppressor PML and its oncogenic counterpart PML-RARA.
review_notes: Full text: PIAS1 SUMOylates PML/PML-RARA and promotes their degradation; PML-NB interaction. Experiments mostly in human cell lines.

title: PIAS1 is a GATA4 SUMO ligase that regulates GATA4-dependent intestinal promoters independent of SUMO ligase activity and GATA4 sumoylation.
review_notes: Full text: PIAS1 is a SUMO ligase and ligase-independent coactivator for GATA4; ChIP in mouse enterocytes.

title: Forkhead box protein A2 (FOXA2) protein stability and activity are regulated by sumoylation.
review_notes: PIAS1 but not a ligase-dead mutant enhances FOXA2 sumoylation.

title: Protein inhibitor of activated STAT 1 (PIAS1) is identified as the SUMO E3 ligase of CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (C/EBPβ) during adipogenesis.
review_notes: Full text: PIAS1 is the SUMO E3 for C/EBPbeta in 3T3-L1 adipogenesis; E3 activity needed to restrain adipogenesis.

title: SUMO Ligase Protein Inhibitor of Activated STAT1 (PIAS1) Is a Constituent Promyelocytic Leukemia Nuclear Body Protein That Contributes to the Intrinsic Antiviral Immune Response to Herpes Simplex Virus 1.
review_notes: PIAS1 is a constituent PML-NB protein.

title: Super-resolution study of PIAS SUMO E3-ligases in hippocampal and cortical neurons.
review_notes: SIM imaging: partial colocalization of PIAS1 with synaptic markers in cultured hippocampal neurons.

title: Crosstalk between SUMOylation and ubiquitylation controls DNA end resection by maintaining MRE11 homeostasis on chromatin.
review_notes: Human cells: PIAS1 is the major SUMO E3 for MRE11 during end resection; supports ISO DSB rows.

title: Inhibition of Stat1-mediated gene activation by PIAS1.
review_notes: Discovery of PIAS1 as a specific inhibitor of STAT1 DNA binding (human PIAS1; source of ISO rows).

title: OpenScientist deep research report for Pias1 (mouse)
review_notes: Automated synthesis. Claims used were checked against cached primary sources (PMID:15311277, PMID:15657437, PMID:12764129, PMID:17540171, PMID:27099310, PMID:24061474). Substrate claims for PNKP, Hes-1, AICD and MK2/HECTD2 regulation were not verified and not used. Omits that PIAS1 is not the STAT1 E3 (PMID:12764129).

title: Regulation of TH2 responses by the pulmonary Clara cell secretory 10-kd protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; primary source for the Th2-cytokine and GATA-3/mRNA stability annotations. Abstract directly contradicts the negative-regulation- of-IFN-gamma annotation (reports induction in naive T cells), which is flagged UNDECIDED.

title: Mouse Clara cell 10-kDa (CC10) protein: cDNA nucleotide sequence and molecular basis for the variation in progesterone binding of CC10 from different species.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; basis for treating progesterone/steroid binding as weak and of doubtful physiological relevance in mouse.

title: Thyroid transcription factor-1, hepatocyte nuclear factor-3beta, surfactant protein B, C, and Clara cell secretory protein in developing mouse lung.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; supports the cytoplasmic (biosynthetic-compartment) localization in club cells.

title: UniProt entry Q06318 (UTER_MOUSE), uteroglobin / Scgb1a1
review_notes: Curated UniProt record; source for the NEW phospholipase A2 inhibitor and phospholipid binding molecular functions, PCB binding, secretion, club cell expression and glucocorticoid induction.

title: Succinate dehydrogenase 5 (SDH5) regulates glycogen synthase kinase 3β-β-catenin-mediated lung cancer metastasis.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: Drp1 controls complex II assembly and skeletal muscle metabolism by Sdhaf2 action on mitochondria.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: Inhibition of cysteine proteinases by autolytic digestion is mediated by CBP2/Hsp47.
review_notes: Relevant as corroborating evidence against GO:0004867; its cysteine-proteinase finding does not support serine-type endopeptidase inhibitor activity.

title: Hsp47 as a collagen-specific molecular chaperone.
review_notes: PubMed-cached review directly states that HSP47 lacks serine protease inhibitory activity.

title: Biology of Hsp47 (Serpin H1), a collagen-specific molecular chaperone.
review_notes: PubMed-cached review directly supports the non-inhibitory-serpin interpretation for HSP47/Serpinh1.

title: Serpinh1 GOA annotation snapshot
review_notes: Local GOA snapshot identifies the exact propagated IBA and InterPro IEA rows under review.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis review of Serpinh1 GO:0004867
review_notes: OpenScientist report is used for provenance-focused hypothesis review; its key biological claim was checked against PubMed-cached primary/review literature in PMID:27838364, PMID:21683254, and PMID:12685865.

title: Manual transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs by curator judgment of sequence similarity
review_notes: Methodological GO_REF describing curator-judged ortholog transfer; the annotation it supports (basolateral plasma membrane, from rat P26435) is itself sound.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Methodological GO_REF for PAINT/IBA inference; the three IBA node placements used here (PTN000040759, PTN000040761, PTN002570905) are appropriate for this gene.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Methodological GO_REF; the mapped UniProt location (SL-0039, Cell membrane) is correct for Ntcp.

title: Automated transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to mouse-rat orthologs
review_notes: Methodological GO_REF for MGI/RGD orthology transfer; the donor rat Slc10a1 (RGD:3681) annotations carried over here are IDA-grade.

title: Automated transfer of experimentally-verified manual GO annotation data to mouse-human orthologs
review_notes: Methodological GO_REF for mouse-human orthology transfer; the donor human SLC10A1 (Q14973) annotations carried over here are IDA-grade (PMID:22029531).

title: Combined Automated Annotation using Multiple IEA Methods
review_notes: Methodological GO_REF; the InterPro IPR002657 / ARBA route to a generic membrane term is correct though uninformative.

title: Molecular cloning and functional characterization of two alternatively spliced Ntcp isoforms from mouse liver1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the primary functional characterization of the mouse protein and the direct experimental basis for the bile acid:sodium symporter activity. Cached abstract-only, but the assay (oocyte uptake, saturation kinetics) is stated and UniProt cites it for the curated taurocholate reaction and Km values.

title: Hepatocyte nuclear factor-1alpha is an essential regulator of bile acid and plasma cholesterol metabolism.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; the paper is about Hnf1a, but Slc10a1 is one of the transporters directly assayed and the abstract explicitly assigns it to the basolateral membrane. Cached abstract-only, so the MGI curator saw assay detail not visible here, and the IDA localization call is deferred to.

title: Sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide is a functional receptor for human hepatitis B and D virus.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cited only as the human-side comparator for the species difference, and it does not support any annotation on the mouse protein.

title: Molecular determinants of hepatitis B and D virus entry restriction in mouse sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available in the cache. Establishes the species divergence that blocks transfer of the human virus-receptor terms to mouse, and independently confirms that mouse Ntcp is a fully functional sodium-dependent taurocholate transporter.

title: Functional and Pharmacological Comparison of Human and Mouse Na(+)/Taurocholate Cotransporting Polypeptide (NTCP).
review_notes: PubMed-verified; directly compares human and mouse NTCP in the same assay system, so it is the key reference establishing that the mouse transport function matches the human donor annotations being transferred.

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: Structural basis of signal peptide recognition by the signal peptidase complex.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: A toll-like receptor that prevents infection by uropathogenic bacteria.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. The paper is sound, but on the sequence evidence its receptor is the paralogue Q6QNU9 (MGI Tlr12) rather than this entry: MGI's note on the allele used (MGI:3045751) states that the sequence information indicates a Tlr12 allele although the references call it Tlr11, and UniProt cites this paper under Q6QNU9. Flagged rather than removed because the identity question is for MGI and GO to settle.

title: UNC93B1 is essential for TLR11 activation and IL-12-dependent host resistance to Toxoplasma gondii.
review_notes: Full text read. Concerns the paralogue, since its cloning primer encodes the Q6QNU9 N-terminus, but is cited here for the UNC93B1 dependence of the pair and as a third independent primer-level check on the naming inversion.

title: A mouse model of Salmonella typhi infection.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Establishes flagellin as the ligand of the receptor the authors call TLR11; the same sequence argument places that receptor on Q6QNU9, so the interaction row on this entry is probably on the wrong paralogue.

title: Recognition of profilin by Toll-like receptor 12 is critical for host resistance to Toxoplasma gondii.
review_notes: Full text read. The receptor characterised here as TLR12 is this entry: the cloned open reading frame is NP_991388.1 with a 30-residue signal peptide, matching Q6R5P0. Primary evidence for profilin recognition, endolysosomal trafficking via UNC93B1, obligate heterodimerisation with the paralogue, and the IL-12 and host-resistance phenotype.

title: Combined action of nucleic acid-sensing Toll-like receptors and TLR11/TLR12 heterodimers imparts resistance to Toxoplasma gondii in mice.
review_notes: Full text read; independent support that both members of the pair are endosomal receptors acting as heterodimers, used here for the location call.

title: Cooperation of TLR12 and TLR11 in the IRF8-dependent IL-12 response to Toxoplasma gondii profilin.
review_notes: Full text read. Direct profilin binding by both receptors, UNC93B1 interaction, and the finding that only the paralogue recruits MyD88. Also the cleanest source for the naming inversion, since both cloning primers are given and their reading frames match the two UniProt N-termini unambiguously.

title: A toll-like receptor that prevents infection by uropathogenic bacteria.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but the claims used here are in the abstract. UniProt cites this paper under Q6QNU9 for FUNCTION and DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE, and MGI records the allele used as Tlr12<tm1Gho>, so despite the paper calling the receptor TLR11 it is about this entry.

title: TLR11 activation of dendritic cells by a protozoan profilin-like protein.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; the chemically defined profilin ligand and the in vivo IL-12 requirement are both stated in the abstract.

title: Recognition of Toxoplasma gondii by TLR11 prevents parasite-induced immunopathology.
review_notes: Full text read. Toxoplasma immunopathology study using the knockout of this gene's allele; supports the accepted GO:0042832 row and names profilin as the ligand.

title: UNC93B1 is essential for TLR11 activation and IL-12-dependent host resistance to Toxoplasma gondii.
review_notes: Full text read. Establishes the ER residence and the direct UNC93B1 interaction of this receptor, and its cloning primer encodes the Q6QNU9 N-terminus, which is one of the checks fixing the direction of the naming inversion.

title: A mouse model of Salmonella typhi infection.
review_notes: Full text read. Identifies flagellin as the ligand of the receptor called TLR11 and shows direct binding; the receptor is this entry on the primer and allele evidence.

title: Recognition of profilin by Toll-like receptor 12 is critical for host resistance to Toxoplasma gondii.
review_notes: Full text read. Principally about the paralogue Q6R5P0, whose open reading frame it gives as NP_991388.1; cited here for the obligate heterodimerisation of the pair and as part of the nomenclature argument.

title: Combined action of nucleic acid-sensing Toll-like receptors and TLR11/TLR12 heterodimers imparts resistance to Toxoplasma gondii in mice.
review_notes: Full text read; independent support that both members of the pair act as endosomal receptors, used for the location call.

title: Cooperation of TLR12 and TLR11 in the IRF8-dependent IL-12 response to Toxoplasma gondii profilin.
review_notes: Full text read. Shows that of the pair only this receptor recruits MyD88, and gives both cloning primers, whose reading frames match the two UniProt N-termini and settle which entry each literature name denotes.

title: Toll-Like Receptor 11 (TLR11) Interacts with Flagellin and Profilin through Disparate Mechanisms.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. Shows that one receptor binds both flagellin and Toxoplasma profilin, through different ectodomain regions and with different pH and cleavage requirements, which is the strongest single support for the pattern recognition receptor activity call on this entry. The receptor studied is this one: the authors give the signal sequence as M1 to S21 and the ectodomain as T22 to S709, matching Q6QNU9's UniProt features (SIGNAL 1..21, TOPO_DOM 22..709) and not Q6R5P0's 1..30 signal, so this is a fourth independent check on the direction of the naming inversion.

title: Twelve toll-like receptor (TLR) genes in the family Equidae - comparative genomics, selection and evolution.
review_notes: Full text fetched during the deep-research cross-check and used only for the statement in the description that the pair is not confined to rodents; the paper sequences equine TLR11 and TLR12 cDNAs and confirms their expression in white blood cells.

title: The interaction between the ER membrane protein UNC93B and TLR3, 7, and 9 is crucial for TLR signaling.
review_notes: Full text read. The receptor is not in the title but is identified with 26 peptides in the UNC93B immunoprecipitate, which is what the interaction row rests on.

title: A novel Toll-like receptor that recognizes vesicular stomatitis virus.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Sound for the MyD88 and TAK1 dependence and for the intracellular localisation; the vesicular stomatitis virus claim it makes is the weakest part of this gene's record and is flagged as such by UniProt, so rows resting on it are kept as non-core.

title: TLR13 recognizes bacterial 23S rRNA devoid of erythromycin resistance-forming modification.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but the ligand identification and the methylation-escape result are both stated there. Primary evidence for rRNA binding and for the receptor-specific pathway term.

title: Cutting edge: TLR13 is a receptor for bacterial RNA.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Independent identification of the receptor as a bacterial RNA sensor, plus the endosomal localisation UniProt cites.

title: Structural basis for specific recognition of single-stranded RNA by Toll-like receptor 13.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Crystal structure of the ectodomain with a 13-nucleotide single-stranded RNA; supports both the homodimerisation calls and the sequence- and conformation-specific recognition, and is the only support for a viral single-stranded RNA activating the receptor.

title: Nucleic Acid-Sensing Toll-Like Receptors Play a Dominant Role in Innate Immune Recognition of Pneumococci.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. Single-knockout and triple-knockout mouse phenotypes in pneumococcal infection, with the cell-level readouts in alveolar macrophages and microglia. Basis for the proposed GO:0050830 annotation, and the source of the observation that human TLR8 recognises the bacterial species that stimulate this receptor in mouse cells.

title: Combining antibiotic with anti-TLR2/TLR13 therapy prevents brain pathology in pneumococcal meningitis.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. Double-knockout animals show that this receptor and TLR2 are the dominant pneumococcal sensors in the subarachnoid space, and that the same signalling drives the brain pathology of meningitis. Supports the proposed GO:0050830 row and the description's note that the contribution is protective in the lung and damaging in the central nervous system.

title: RNase T2 deficiency promotes TLR13-dependent replenishment of tissue-protective Kupffer cells.
review_notes: Full text read; fetched during the deep-research cross-check. Shows that the receptor is activated in vivo by ribosomal RNA of microbiota origin when endosomal RNase T2 is absent, driving accumulation of tissue-protective macrophages. Cited as in vivo support that ribosomal RNA is the physiological ligand; the macrophage-accumulation phenotype is described but not annotated, since it was obtained in an RNase-deficient background.

title: Falcon deep research report on mouse Tlr13
review_notes: Machine-generated literature synthesis, read during the cross-check. It surfaced the pneumococcal-infection, meningitis and microbiome-sensing literature that the review had not used; every claim taken from it was verified in the primary paper before use, and it is cited here only for its framing of the receptor's core activity.

title: Structural insights into the activation of metabotropic glutamate receptors.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: A novel family of putative pheromone receptors in mammals with a topographically organized and sexually dimorphic distribution.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: ALDH1L2 is the mitochondrial homolog of 10-formyltetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Checked the primary cached source. Full-text comparison distinguishes ALDH1L2 mitochondrial targeting from cytosolic ALDH1L1; evidence is interpreted at the paralog/targeting level, without treating compartment names alone as proof.

title: Enzymatic properties of ALDH1L2, a mitochondrial 10-formyltetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase.
review_notes: Checked the primary cached source. Full-text comparison distinguishes ALDH1L2 mitochondrial targeting from cytosolic ALDH1L1; evidence is interpreted at the paralog/targeting level, without treating compartment names alone as proof.

title: OpenScientist assessment of rat Aldh1l1 cofactor specificity and mitochondrial localization
review_notes: Read the complete output and inspected its N-terminal CSV. The mitochondrial targeting distinction was verified against the rat P28037 N terminus and primary PMID:20498374/21238436. The report headline overstates NAD+ refutation: its own limitations acknowledge no NAD+ kinetics, and the structural study says NADP preference rather than zero NAD usage. Its repeated weaker-evidence-code framing and untraced generic-ALDH ISO explanation are not adopted; the actual ISO donor is mouse Aldh1l1 MGI:MGI:1340024. This report was incorporated substantively rather than accepted wholesale.

title: Enzymic changes in the cervix of the rat and hamster during the oestrous cycle and the effect of steroids.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Shows estrogen-induced upregulation of cervical arylsulphatase B activity in ovariectomised rats. Supports a tissue-specific hormonal regulation observation but not a core Arsb function.

title: Inability of thiol compounds to restore CNS arylsulfatases inhibited by methyl mercury.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Shows methylmercury inhibits rat CNS arylsulfatase activity; used to support GO:0051597 response to methylmercury but the evidence is a toxicology observation, not evidence of Arsb participating in a biological response process.

title: Cell-surface arylsulfatase A and B on sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatocytes, and Kupffer cells in mammalian livers.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Direct immunohistochemistry/EM evidence for cell-surface localisation of ARSA and ARSB in liver parenchymal and sinusoidal cell types. Supports the extra-lysosomal cell-surface annotation.

title: Characterization of liver lysosomal enzyme activity in hepatocytes, Kupffer and endothelial cells during aging: effect of dietary restriction.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Shows age- and diet-dependent changes in hepatic lysosomal enzyme activities (including Arsb) but does not demonstrate that Arsb is a component of a nutrient-response pathway.

title: Arylsulfatase B modulates neurite outgrowth via astrocyte chondroitin-4-sulfate: dysregulation by ethanol.
review_notes: PubMed-verified with PMC full text. Mechanistically links astrocyte Arsb activity to chondroitin-4-sulfate and neurocan levels and to hippocampal neurite outgrowth; identifies ethanol-induced Arsb inhibition as a candidate mechanism for FASD.

title: Isolation and characterization of rat hepatic ascorbic acid-2-sulfatases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Biochemical demonstration that rat arylsulfatase B hydrolyses ascorbic acid-2-sulfate (as a minor substrate), supporting the sulfuric ester hydrolase MF.

title: The effect of pH on the kinetics of arylsulphatases A and B.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Enzyme-kinetics study of pH dependence of rat liver arylsulphatases; used incorrectly to support GO:0009268 response to pH.

title: Autophagy-related changes of arylsulphatases A and B in rat liver lysosomes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Sanghavi & Koenig 1976 describes arylsulphatase A/B activity ratio changes during hepatic autophagocytosis, with A converted to B by other lysosomal hydrolases active in autophagic vacuoles. title: An autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease gene homolog is involved in intraflagellar transport in C. elegans ciliated sensory neurons.
review_notes: Primary paper directly identifying CHE-11 as one of two Complex A (IFT-A) polypeptides that move along C. elegans sensory cilia at the IFT rate. Note the title's "ARPKD gene homolog" refers to osm-5/IFT88, not che-11; the che-11 evidence is in the body (Complex A subunit, IFT motility).

title: Mutations in chemosensory cilia cause resistance to paraquat in nematode Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Identifies the paraquat-resistant, long-lived mutant mev-4 as a che-11 nonsense allele with a Dyf phenotype. Supports stress/lifespan phenotypes that are downstream consequences of ciliary/sensory dysfunction rather than molecular functions of CHE-11.

title: Genetic analysis of chemosensory control of dauer formation in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Classic genetic study placing che-11 among the cilium-structure genes whose mutations give structurally defective chemosensory cilia and block chemosensation; basis for the dauer-entry (IGI) and cilium-assembly (IGI) annotations.

title: Mutation of the MAP kinase DYF-5 affects docking and undocking of kinesin-2 motors and reduces their speed in the cilia of Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Study of the DYF-5 MAP kinase that also imaged IFT proteins in cilia; source of the IDA non-motile cilium localization for CHE-11. Abstract-only cache does not name che-11, but the curator read the full text.

title: Functional interactions between the ciliopathy-associated Meckel syndrome 1 (MKS1) protein and two novel MKS1-related (MKSR) proteins.
review_notes: MKS1/MKSR transition-zone study; source of a WB IMP determination-of-adult- lifespan annotation for a che-11 variant. Lifespan is a downstream sensory consequence, not a core CHE-11 function.

title: Whole-Organism Developmental Expression Profiling Identifies RAB-28 as a Novel Ciliary GTPase Associated with the BBSome and Intraflagellar Transport.
review_notes: Uses che-11(e1810) as an IFT-A loss-of-function background and describes CHE-11 as the IFT140 component of IFT-A essential for IFT; RAB-28 IFT movement is abolished in che-11 mutant truncated cilia. Basis for the positive-regulation-of-IFT annotations.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.
review_notes: Retrograde (dynein-2/IFT-A) transport study; cited by ComplexPortal (CPX-1289) for the NAS IFT-A complex-membership and retrograde-transport annotations. The abstract discusses IFT-A subunits IFT-139/IFT-43 and dynein-2, not che-11 by name.

title: Identification of CHE-13, a novel intraflagellar transport protein required for cilia formation.
review_notes: Haycraft et al. 2003 (Exp Cell Res); abstract-only in cache. The defining che-13 cloning/characterization paper. Source of IFT-B membership, ciliary base/axoneme localization, DAF-19-dependent expression, the anterograde/retrograde IEP annotations and the OSM-5/OSM-6 mislocalization (protein-localization) evidence.

title: Caenorhabditis elegans DYF-2, an orthologue of human WDR19, is a component of the intraflagellar transport machinery in sensory cilia.
review_notes: Efimenko et al. 2006; abstract-only. Primarily a DYF-2/WDR19 paper that does not foreground che-13; it is the GOA reference for the che-13(WBVar00144317) IMP to intracellular protein localization. Not overruled (curator full-text evidence).

title: Sensory ciliogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans: assignment of IFT components into distinct modules based on transport and phenotypic profiles.
review_notes: Ou et al. 2007 (Mol Biol Cell); abstract-only. Source of the IDA IFT particle B membership annotation for che-13.

title: Genetic analysis of chemosensory control of dauer formation in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Vowels & Thomas 1992; abstract-only. Basis for the che-13 cilium-assembly IGI as a genetic requirement for functional chemosensory cilia in the dauer pathway.

title: Functional redundancy of the B9 proteins and nephrocystins in Caenorhabditis elegans ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Williams et al. 2008; abstract-only. Primarily a B9/nephrocystin paper that does not foreground che-13; it is the GOA reference for one of the che-13 axoneme IDA annotations. Not overruled (curator full-text evidence).

title: The BBSome controls IFT assembly and turnaround in cilia.
review_notes: Wei et al. 2012 (Nat Cell Biol); full text available. The paper is about DYF-2 and the BBSome and does not name che-13; it is the MGI reference for the che-13 ciliary basal body IDA. Basal-body localization is independently established for che-13 (concentrates at the ciliary base, PMID:12651157), so the annotation is not overruled.

title: Mutant sensory cilia in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Perkins et al. 1986 (Dev Biol); abstract-only. Foundational ultrastructural characterization of the che-13 ciliary phenotype and its dye-filling/chemosensory defects.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.
review_notes: Yi et al. 2017 (Curr Biol); abstract-only. Identifies che-13 in IFT complex B by mass spectrometry (UniProt SUBUNIT) and underlies the ComplexPortal NAS annotations for IFT particle B membership, intraciliary transport, cilium assembly and cilium.

title: Differential requirements for clathrin in receptor-mediated endocytosis and maintenance of synaptic vesicle pools.
review_notes: Full text cached; chc-1 paper cited for the heavy chain/light chain relationship.

title: Endocytosis genes facilitate protein and membrane transport in C. elegans sensory cilia.
review_notes: Abstract only, but the abstract names the clathrin light chain explicitly; the only primary clic-1 record in GOA.

title: CLK-1 controls respiration, behavior and aging in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Direct evidence that active CLK-1-GFP localizes to mitochondria; establishes the respiration/behavior/aging phenotypes. Title-verified.

title: Altered quinone biosynthesis in the long-lived clk-1 mutants of Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Biochemical proof that clk-1 is required for UQ9 synthesis and that DMQ9 accumulates and can substitute as an electron carrier; anchors the DMQ-vs-Q knowledge gap. Title-verified.

title: CLK-1 protein has DNA binding activity specific to O(L) region of mitochondrial DNA.
review_notes: Correctly cited but an isolated 2002 in-vitro study of mtDNA (O_L) binding, not widely replicated; basis for the debated transcription cis-regulatory region binding annotation. Treated as a possible moonlighting activity, non-core.

title: Silencing of ubiquinone biosynthesis genes extends life span in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: RNAi of clk-1 (among eight CoQ genes) lowers quinone and extends lifespan; supports the ubiquinone biosynthetic role. Title-verified.

title: Molecular mechanism of maternal rescue in the clk-1 mutants of Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: clk-1 encodes the UQ-biosynthesis hydroxylase; UQ replaced by DMQ in mutants; establishes maternal rescue and uncoupling of longevity from developmental phenotypes. Title-verified.

title: Mitochondrial complex I function modulates volatile anesthetic sensitivity in C. elegans.
review_notes: clk-1 is one of several ETC/CoQ mutants tested; supports the indirect OXPHOS/ anesthetic-sensitivity (xenobiotic-response) annotations as downstream effects.

title: Knockdown of mitochondrial heat shock protein 70 promotes progeria-like phenotypes in caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Uses CLK-1 as a mitochondrial protein whose level falls with hsp-6 knockdown; supports mitochondrial localization only.

title: eIF4E function in somatic cells modulates ageing in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: clk mutants used as long-lived partners in a translation/ageing study; supports the non-core lifespan-determination annotations.

title: Life-span extension by dietary restriction is mediated by NLP-7 signaling and coelomocyte endocytosis in C. elegans.
review_notes: Cached abstract discusses long-lived electron-transport-chain mutants without naming clk-1; full-text curator classed clk-1 in this group. Supports the non-core lifespan annotations; not removed on abstract-only grounds.

title: A nuclear role for the respiratory enzyme CLK-1 in regulating mitochondrial stress responses and longevity.
review_notes: Full-text primary paper reporting a distinct nuclear CLK-1/COQ7 pool that regulates ROS metabolism, the UPRmt, transcription, and longevity independently of ubiquinone. The data are genuine but the nuclear/non-mitochondrial model is debated (worm N-terminus lacks the COQ7 NTS; limited independent confirmation). Underlies the nucleus, ROS-regulation, and transcription-regulation annotations, which are retained as non-core.

title: Structural and functional conservation of the Caenorhabditis elegans timing gene clk-1.
review_notes: Founding paper: cloned clk-1, showed conservation to yeast Cat5p/Coq7p, and demonstrated shared biochemical function by cross-complementation. PubMed title-verified; supports the core CoQ7-family molecular function.

title: Deep research report (Edison/falcon): C. elegans CLK-1 (COQ7)
review_notes: AI-generated Edison/falcon deep-research synthesis (40 cited sources) used only as corroborating context. It independently reproduces the di-iron DMQ9->UQ9 hydroxylase function, the COQ metabolon/CoQ-synthome membership, and the debated (explicitly unconfirmed) nuclear moonlighting role. Its underlying citations were not individually verified, so it is marked UNVERIFIED; every review claim is anchored to cached primary PMIDs, not to this file.

title: Complexin has opposite effects on two modes of synaptic vesicle fusion.
review_notes: Full text cached; the defining functional study of worm complexin.

title: Deep research report for cpx-1 (falcon / Edison Scientific Literature)
review_notes: LLM literature synthesis, consistent with the cached primary paper (Martin 2011) on every point used here.

title: Arginine methylation promotes siRNA-binding specificity for a spermatogenesis-specific isoform of the Argonaute protein CSR-1.
review_notes: Full isoform-specific Results and small-RNA Methods read. CSR-1A N-terminal dimethylarginines regulate relative spermatogenic versus oogenic 22G guide specificity. Polyphosphatase-treated libraries and gene-feature enrichment do not by themselves establish a negative miRNA-loading assay; separate physiological miRNA enrichment remains unresolved.

title: Falcon report generated from the original Q17370/NHR-47 input, retained for provenance
review_notes: Full report read. It explicitly researches nuclear receptor nhr-47/C24G6.4, including NHR domains and toxicology/transcription evidence, because the original supplied accession was Q17370. Those substantive findings concern NHR-47, not the F20D12.1 Argonaute; none is transferred as CSR-1 functional evidence. The source is retained unchanged as an identity-provenance artifact.

title: OpenScientist focused assessment of CSR-1 miRNA-binding specificity
review_notes: Full report body, evidence/decision CSVs and corresponding HTML read. Useful identity verification and 22G/isoform specificity synthesis are retained. The recommendation to REMOVE or add NOT is not supported by its admitted absence of a miRNA-binding exclusion test; IBA-only status is not evidence against the ancestral assertion. The report used PubMed abstracts and did not independently dereference the target leaf. The CSVs are evidence summaries, not a reproducible guide-loading analysis. Its siRNA-binding NEW would duplicate an existing RNA-binding ancestor; tuning and silencing need not be mutually exclusive.

title: OpenScientist CSR-1 identity and transcription-factor/metabolic-prediction adjudication
review_notes: Full body and HTML artifact read. Identity independently checked against live UniProt/UniParc; report-generated 6-mer comparisons are not represented as a new local analysis. The report does not authorize claiming all CSR-1 regulation is post-transcriptional: direct RNA tethering supports transcriptional licensing without DNA-sequence-specific TF activity.

title: Regulation of the Caenorhabditis elegans longevity protein DAF-16 by insulin/IGF-1 and germline signaling.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only. Establishes that sensory neurons and germline activity regulate DAF-16 nuclear accumulation systemically. Grounds the IGI regulation-of-insulin-receptor-signaling annotation, but the effect of daf-10 is an indirect, whole-organism sensory input into insulin/IGF signaling, not a molecular function of an IFT-A structural subunit.

title: The molecular identities of the Caenorhabditis elegans intraflagellar transport genes dyf-6, daf-10 and osm-1.
review_notes: Founding molecular-identity paper for daf-10: the daf-10 product contains WD and WAA repeats and (per the full text, which the automated validator can only access as the PubMed abstract) is classified with che-11 as an IFT complex A component. Loss of daf-10/che-11 gives thicker-than-wild-type OSM-6::GFP patches in the ciliary endings (IFT-B accumulation), the classic IFT-A retrograde-defect signature. Supports the IFT-A membership and non-motile cilium assembly annotations.

title: Genetic analysis of chemosensory control of dauer formation in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only. Classic epistasis study placing daf-10 among the dauer-defective genes whose mutations cause structurally defective chemosensory cilia; supports both the cilium-assembly (structural) role and the downstream dauer-formation role.

title: Localization of a guanylyl cyclase to chemosensory cilia requires the novel ciliary MYND domain protein DAF-25.
review_notes: Full text available and read. States that daf-10/IFT122 mutations disrupt ciliogenesis and genetically suppress the daf-25 dauer-constitutive phenotype, confirming daf-10 = IFT122 and its ciliogenesis role, and grounding the IGI regulation-of-dauer annotation (genetic interaction with daf-25).

title: Diverse cell type-specific mechanisms localize G protein-coupled receptors to Caenorhabditis elegans sensory cilia.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only; describes the proteins required to localize GPCRs to AWB/ASK sensory cilia. daf-10 is not named in the abstract, but the WormBase IMP (receptor localization to non-motile cilium) reflects the full-text result; consistent with the established IFT-A requirement for ciliary import of membrane GPCRs.

title: A Conserved Role for Girdin in Basal Body Positioning and Ciliogenesis.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract is about Girdin and basal-body positioning and does not name daf-10. The UniProt IDA (ciliary basal body) rests on the full text (DAF-10 likely used/scored as a ciliary-base marker). Basal-body/ciliary-base localization is biologically consistent with an IFT-A subunit (IFT proteins dock at transition fibres before axonemal entry), so the annotation is retained, but the daf-10-specific datum could not be independently verified from the cached abstract.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.
review_notes: Affinity purification / mass spectrometry defined the worm IFT-A complex (che-11, daf-10, dyf-2, ift-139, ift-43, ifta-1); basis for the ComplexPortal (CPX-1289) NAS annotations placing DAF-10 in IFT-A and in retrograde transport. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false); the abstract confirms the affinity-purification definition of IFT-A subunits but does not name daf-10, so the daf-10 datum rests on the full text / UniProt SUBUNIT curation.

title: A pheromone-induced developmental switch in Caenorhabditis elegans: Temperature-sensitive mutants reveal a wild-type temperature-dependent process.
review_notes: Cached record is abstract-only; the abstract foregrounds daf-4/daf-7 dauer-constitutive genes and states that dauer-defective mutants fail to respond to added pheromone. WormBase attaches a specific daf-10 allele (WBVar00143964) IMP for positive regulation of dauer larval development; the dauer role is well-established (gene name = abnormal DAuer Formation) but is a downstream sensory consequence of the ciliary defect, not a core molecular function.

title: A seven-transmembrane receptor that mediates avoidance response to dihydrocaffeic acid, a water-soluble repellent in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Aoki et al., J Neurosci 2011). Original identification of DCAR-1 as a 7-TM receptor for the repellent DHCA expressed in ASH sensory neurons; establishes the neuronal chemosensory role and the receptor's small-molecule ligand. Cached copy is abstract-only (full text unavailable), so the non-motile cilium localization it supports cannot be re-verified from the cache and is deferred to the WormBase curator.

title: Activation of a G protein-coupled receptor by its endogenous ligand triggers the innate immune response of Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Zugasti et al., Nat Immunol 2014); full text available in cache. Flagship paper establishing DCAR-1 as the epidermal innate-immune GPCR, identifying HPLA as its endogenous DAMP ligand, the apical hyp7 localization, and the GPA-12/p38-MAPK signalling context. Directly supports the defense-response, wounding, GPCR-signalling and apical plasma membrane annotations.

title: Deep research report (Edison/falcon) for C. elegans dcar-1
review_notes: Automated Edison/falcon deep-research report (19 citations). Content was inspected and corroborates the primary literature: DCAR-1 as an apical epidermal HPLA/DAMP-sensing GPCR driving the GPA-12 -> PLC/DAG -> TPA-1 -> TIR-1 -> p38/PMK-1 -> STA-2 antimicrobial-peptide pathway, and the neuronal DHCA-avoidance origin. Used only for corroboration; all primary evidence in this review is PMID-anchored, and the single file quote used was grep-verified (the reference validator skips file: prefixes).

title: Caenorhabditis elegans auxilin: a J-domain protein essential for clathrin-mediated endocytosis in vivo.
review_notes: Abstract only in cache; the primary characterization of the worm auxilin (dnj-25/W07A8.3).

title: Control of clathrin-mediated endocytosis by NIMA family kinases.
review_notes: Full text cached; identified through the falcon deep-research report; cites DNJ-25 phenotypes as a comparator for nekl mutants.

title: Human dolichol-phosphate-mannose synthase consists of three subunits, DPM1, DPM2 and DPM3.
review_notes: Primary report checked against the cached abstract/full text; the evidence scope is stated in the finding.

title: Receptor-mediated endocytosis in the Caenorhabditis elegans oocyte.
review_notes: Full text cached; the paper foregrounds other coat components but assays mu2 RNAi directly.

title: C. elegans AP-2 and retromer control Wnt signaling by regulating mig-14/Wntless.
review_notes: Full text cached; establishes the MIG-14 endocytosis requirement.

title: Mu2 adaptin facilitates but is not essential for synaptic vesicle recycling in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Primary characterisation of the dpy-23/apm-2 mutants; full text cached and quotes checked.

title: Endocytosis and intracellular trafficking contribute to necrotic neurodegeneration in C. elegans.
review_notes: Abstract only; dpy-23 is not mentioned in the abstract so the IGI cannot be checked.

title: Endocytosis genes facilitate protein and membrane transport in C. elegans sensory cilia.
review_notes: Abstract only in cache; the abstract explicitly names AP-2 mutants.

title: Clathrin and AP2 are required for phagocytic receptor-mediated apoptotic cell clearance in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Full text cached.

review_notes: Full text cached; worm genetics of AP-2 activation.

title: The Caenorhabditis elegans Tubby homolog dynamically modulates olfactory cilia membrane morphogenesis and phospholipid composition.
review_notes: Full text cached; dpy-23 is a secondary subject of this Tubby study.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard GO_Central IBA pipeline. The phylogenetic inferences (IFT complex B membership, intraciliary transport, IFT-B binding, axonemal microtubule) are all corroborated by C. elegans experimental data, so the IBA transfers are sound.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Electronic mapping of the UniProt "Cilium" subcellular-location keyword to GO:0005929; redundant with the experimental IDA cilium annotation but not incorrect.

title: Functional genomics of the cilium, a sensory organelle.
review_notes: Blacque et al. 2005 SAGE/DAF-19 ciliary-transcriptome screen; source of the UniProt tissue-specificity statement that dyf-1 is expressed in amphid, phasmid and labial-quadrant sensory neurons. Background/expression context, not an annotation source.

title: Functional coordination of intraflagellar transport motors.
review_notes: Founding functional paper for dyf-1 (Ou et al. 2005, Nature). The abstract directly establishes that DYF-1 is specifically required for OSM-3 kinesin to dock onto and move IFT particles and that OSM-3 is inactive in dyf-1 mutants. Correctly supports the intraciliary-transport and OSM-3-activation core function. The same PMID is also the GOA citation for the protein-polyglutamylation and plasma-membrane-localization IMP rows, which its abstract does not itself address (see those annotations).

title: The zebrafish fleer gene encodes an essential regulator of cilia tubulin polyglutamylation.
review_notes: Pathak et al. 2007. Establishes the DYF-1/fleer family role in cilia tubulin polyglutamylation and states explicitly that C. elegans dyf-1 is also required for tubulin polyglutamylation in sensory-neuron cilia; also confirms fleer/DYF1 orthology. This is the definitive supporting reference for the protein-polyglutamylation annotation (which GOA cites to PMID:16049494 instead).

title: The BBSome controls IFT assembly and turnaround in cilia.
review_notes: Wei et al. 2012. A C. elegans IFT paper whose main text (cached) concerns dyf-2 and bbs-1 IFT turnaround; DYF-1 is not named in the cached main text (dyf-2/bbs-1 are the subjects). It is the assigned reference for the ciliary-basal-body IDA (assigned_by MGI); the basal-body localization is biologically expected for any IFT-B protein, but the dyf-1-specific evidence could not be verbatim-verified here (may reside in a supplement). Deferred to the experimental curator; retained as ACCEPT on biological grounds.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.
review_notes: Yi et al. 2017. Identifies DYF-1 as a component of IFT complex B by mass spectrometry (basis of ComplexPortal CPX-1290 and the UniProt SUBUNIT list) and shows IFT-B is required for ciliary entry of dynein-2. Supports the IFT-B membership, intraciliary transport, cilium-localization and cilium-assembly (NAS) annotations.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: InterPro2GO mapping of the TRAF3IP1 family (IPR018799) to microtubule binding (GO:0008017). The family is named for its microtubule-interacting property (MIP-T3 = Microtubule-Interacting Protein associated with TRAF3) and human MIP-T3 was shown to bind microtubules, so the molecular-function transfer is reasonable at the family level.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard GO_Central IBA pipeline. The phylogenetic inferences (IFT complex B membership, intraciliary transport, cilium assembly, axoneme and basal body localization) are all independently corroborated by C. elegans experimental data, so the IBA transfers are sound. The "regulation of microtubule cytoskeleton organization" transfer over-generalizes the axoneme-assembly role.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: Electronic mapping of the UniProt cilium-axoneme subcellular-location keyword to GO:0005930; redundant with the experimental IDA axoneme annotation but not incorrect.

title: Electronic Gene Ontology annotations created by ARBA machine learning models
review_notes: ARBA machine-learning annotations. The "animal organ development" and "system development" terms are over-general electronic inferences that are not informative for a nematode sensory-cilium protein; "regulation of microtubule cytoskeleton organization" over-generalizes the structural axoneme-assembly role.

title: The conserved proteins CHE-12 and DYF-11 are required for sensory cilium function in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Bacaj, Lu & Shaham 2008 (Genetics), independent characterization of dyf-11. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), but the abstract directly establishes that dyf-11 mutant cilia lack medial and distal segments, that DYF-11 undergoes IFT-like movement and may act at an early stage of IFT-B particle assembly, and that DYF-11 is expressed in all ciliated neurons. The four WormBase IMP annotations to this PMID (chemotaxis, hyperosmotic response, dauer entry, non-motile cilium assembly) rest on full-text assays not in the cached abstract.

title: An essential role for DYF-11/MIP-T3 in assembling functional intraflagellar transport complexes.
review_notes: Li et al. 2008 (PLoS Genet, PMC2268012), the primary cloning and functional characterization paper. Full text available. Establishes dyf-11 = the C. elegans MIP-T3/TRAF3IP1 ortholog, its localization to transition zone/basal body and axoneme, its bidirectional IFT movement, its identity as a novel IFT-B component, and its requirement for assembly/integrity of the motor-IFT machinery. Supports the core cellular-component, transport, and cilium-assembly annotations.

title: Reversal of salt preference is directed by the insulin/PI3K and Gq/PKC signaling in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Adachi et al. 2010 (Genetics). The PMID resolves to the correct paper on ASE salt-chemotaxis plasticity, but the cached record is abstract-only and the abstract does not mention dyf-11; the associative-learning IMP therefore cannot be verified from the cache. Any dyf-11 salt-learning phenotype is an indirect consequence of loss of functional sensory cilia rather than a core function.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.
review_notes: Yi et al. 2017 (Curr Biol). Source of the ComplexPortal (CPX-1290) NAS annotations placing DYF-11 in IFT complex B. Abstract-only cache, but the abstract confirms that an intact IFT-B complex is required for dynein-2 ciliary entry, consistent with DYF-11's IFT-B membership.

title: Functional genomics of the cilium, a sensory organelle.
review_notes: Primary paper that clones dyf-13 (C27H5.7a) and establishes it as a novel core IFT component required for cilia function; the ciliary structural defect of dyf-13(mn396) is caused by a mutation in C27H5.7a. Verbatim quotes confirmed against the cached record.

title: Caenorhabditis elegans DYF-2, an orthologue of human WDR19, is a component of the intraflagellar transport machinery in sensory cilia.
review_notes: Background/context reference for the dyf IFT gene class; primarily about the paralog dyf-2/WDR19 (IFT complex-B associated). Only the abstract is cached, so supporting_text is quoted verbatim from the abstract; the dyf-13-specific X-box cloning detail is not stated in the cached abstract and is not asserted here.

title: The Caenorhabditis elegans nephrocystins act as global modifiers of cilium structure.
review_notes: Full-text (PMC) paper using DYF-13::GFP as an IFT reporter; supports ciliary localization/IFT and a distal-segment cargo (OSM-6) defect in dyf-13 mutants.

title: An essential role for DYF-11/MIP-T3 in assembling functional intraflagellar transport complexes.
review_notes: Corroborates evolutionary conservation of DYF-13 as an IFT component; the paper itself is about the IFT-B protein DYF-11.

title: Overall Architecture of the Intraflagellar Transport (IFT)-B Complex Containing Cluap1/IFT38 as an Essential Component of the IFT-B Peripheral Subcomplex.
review_notes: Mammalian IFT-B interaction-map paper; supports the family-level IFT-B (TTC26/IFT56) assignment used for the orthology-based annotations. Ortholog evidence, not C. elegans-specific.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.
review_notes: Source of the UniProt IFT-B SUBUNIT composition (lists dyf-13) and of the ComplexPortal NAS annotations. Abstract-only in cache; the IFT-B membership and dynein-2-entry roles are stated in the abstract and match the annotations.

title: Caenorhabditis elegans DYF-2, an orthologue of human WDR19, is a component of the intraflagellar transport machinery in sensory cilia.
review_notes: Founding paper that identified dyf-2 as the WDR19 ortholog and an IFT component in C. elegans sensory cilia (transgenic rescue + allele sequencing). Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available: false), so experimental IDA/IMP annotations from this paper rest on the full text the WormBase curator read; the abstract independently confirms the IFT-machinery-integrity role and cilia/chemosensation phenotypes.

title: The BBSome controls IFT assembly and turnaround in cilia.
review_notes: Full text available and read. Establishes DYF-2 = WDR19/IFT144 as an IFT structural protein whose WD40 domain is required for IFT turnaround and retrograde IFT, and for BBSome docking onto IFT particles (WDR19–BBS1 interaction). Directly supports the retrograde-transport and cilium-assembly IMP annotations.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.

title: The intraflagellar transport protein IFT27 promotes BBSome exit from cilia through the GTPase ARL6/BBS3.
review_notes: Full-text cached. Confirms co-purification of CLUAP1/DYF-3/qilin with the IFT-B complex, corroborating IFT-B membership; the paper's primary focus (IFT27/ARL6/BBSome) is otherwise tangential to dyf-3.

title: Dynein-Driven Retrograde Intraflagellar Transport Is Triphasic in C. elegans Sensory Cilia.

Abstract-only in cache; quotes verified verbatim.

title: Mutation of the MAP kinase DYF-5 affects docking and undocking of kinesin-2 motors and reduces their speed in the cilia of Caenorhabditis elegans.

Establishes DYF-5 as a ciliary kinase controlling cilium length/morphology and coordinating the kinesin-II to OSM-3 anterograde-IFT handover. Cached record is abstract-only; the experimental IDA/IMP/IGI annotations were made by WormBase/UniProt curators from the full text.

title: DYF-5/MAK-dependent phosphorylation promotes ciliary tubulin unloading.

Underpins one of the IDA GO:0004674 annotations.

title: Neurons dispose of hyperactive kinesin into glial cells for clearance.

Underpins the IDA GO:0004674 annotation. The paper's headline topic is kinesin disposal into glia; DYF-5 is characterized as a cell-autonomous regulator of OSM-3.

title: Deep research report (Falcon/Edison): DYF-6/IFT46 in Caenorhabditis elegans
review_notes: AI-generated (Falcon/Edison) deep-research synthesis. Also surfaces worm-specific literature (Cevik et al. 2013 on ARL-13 ciliary membrane trafficking in dyf-6 mutants) not in the GOA set. Underlying claims are drawn from Chlamydomonas/human work cited by internal keys, not independently re-verified here; treated as supporting context, not primary evidence.

title: Genetic interactions due to constitutive and inducible gene regulation mediated by the unfolded protein response in C. elegans.
review_notes: PMC full text confirmed (full_text_available: true). This is a transcriptional-profiling study of the C. elegans UPR; fis-2 appears only as a high-throughput expression-profiling (HEP) target in supplementary data. No verbatim fis-2 quote is available. title: Mutations in Fis1 disrupt orderly disposal of defective mitochondria.
review_notes: PMC full text confirmed. Directly characterizes C. elegans fis-2 using the fis-1(tm1867); fis-2(gk414) double mutant (called the "Fis1 mutant" throughout) plus drp-1 fis-1 fis-2 and pink-1 fis-1 fis-2 triple mutants. Establishes that fis-2 is dispensable for fission and contributes REDUNDANTLY (only demonstrated in the double mutant) to orderly disposal of defective mitochondria. Not in the GOA seed set; added here because it is the primary loss-of-function characterization of worm fis-2.

title: Ubiquitination is required for the initial removal of paternal organelles in C. elegans.
review_notes: Abstract-only in cache but PubMed-verified (Molina, Lim & Boyd, Dev Biol 2019). title: Fndc-1 contributes to paternal mitochondria elimination in C. elegans.

review_notes: PubMed-verified, abstract-only. Crystal structure of yeast Sse1p (Hsp110) bound to the Hsp70 NBD; ATP-bound HSP110 NBD embraces the Hsp70 NBD to release ADP, and NEF activity is essential. Conserved-mechanism support for the worm ortholog; also documents direct substrate binding by Hsp110.

title: Mitochondrial electron transport is a key determinant of life span in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Feng, Bussiere & Hekimi 2001 (Dev Cell). PubMed-verified (note: an initially mis-recollected PMID, 11740940, is a different Drosophila paper; corrected to 11709184).

title: Two modes of mitochondrial dysfunction lead independently to lifespan extension in Caenorhabditis elegans.

title: A mitochondrial superoxide signal triggers increased longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Yang & Hekimi 2010 (PLoS Biol). Establishes that isp-1 (and nuo-6) are complex III/I subunits whose partial loss decreases electron transport, and that an elevated mitochondrial superoxide signal is necessary and sufficient for the longevity. PubMed-verified; full text cached.

title: Tether mutations that restore function and suppress pleiotropic phenotypes of the C. elegans isp-1(qm150) Rieske iron-sulfur protein.

title: Innate Immunity Promotes Sleep through Epidermal Antimicrobial Peptides.

title: Regulation of response properties and operating range of the AFD thermosensory neurons by cGMP signaling.
review_notes: Full text states tax-4 CNG-channel mutations abolish AFD thermosensitivity and isothermal tracking. Support for the thermosensory core role (the paper centers on the upstream gcy receptor guanylyl cyclases).

title: Temperature, oxygen, and salt-sensing neurons in C. elegans are carbon dioxide sensors that control avoidance behavior.
review_notes: Shows CO2-evoked Ca2+ responses in AFD and BAG require cGMP-gated channels, and CO2 avoidance requires channels containing the TAX-2 and TAX-4 subunits. Grounds the CO2/chemotaxis non-core annotations and corroborates the abstract-only PMID:24240097.

title: Cell- and subunit-specific mechanisms of CNG channel ciliary trafficking and localization in C. elegans.
review_notes: Defines cis-sequences and trans-factors for ciliary targeting of the TAX-4 CNGA and TAX-2 CNGB subunits, and reports heterogeneous, cell- and subunit-specific channel composition across the cilium. Grounds ciliary localization and the in vivo stoichiometry/composition knowledge gap.

title: In vivo genetic dissection of O2-evoked cGMP dynamics in a Caenorhabditis elegans gas sensor.
review_notes: In vivo cGMP/Ca2+ imaging showing cGMP-gated channels are required for the sustained Ca2+ response and participate in negative-feedback loops. Supports the response-to-oxygen and negative-regulation-of-rGC-signaling annotations.

title: A chemoreceptor that detects molecular carbon dioxide.
review_notes: Primary focus is the GCY-9 receptor guanylyl cyclase in BAG CO2 sensing; the cached record is abstract-only and does not itself mention tax-4. The tax-4 requirement for CO2-evoked responses is independently supported (PMID:21435556), so the IMP CO2/Ca2+/detection annotations are retained (non-core) rather than removed.

title: Chemosensation of bacterial secondary metabolites modulates neuroendocrine signaling and behavior of C. elegans.
review_notes: ASJ chemosensory detection of P. aeruginosa metabolites induces DAF-7/TGF-beta expression; TAX-4 is the chemosensory channel upstream. Supports the positive-regulation-of-gene-expression non-core annotation.

title: Ciliopathy proteins establish a bipartite signaling compartment in a C. elegans thermosensory neuron.
review_notes: Shows NPHP-2/inversin anchors the cGMP-gated ion channel within the proximal ciliary (inversin) compartment of AFD. Directly grounds the ciliary inversin compartment and non-motile cilium localizations.

title: Structure of a eukaryotic cyclic-nucleotide-gated channel.
review_notes: cryo-EM structure of the C. elegans TAX-4 channel (homotetramer) in the cGMP-bound open state; documents the unusual voltage-sensor-like domain with deficient voltage dependence (basis for removing the voltage-gated K+ channel IEA term) and the selectivity-filter glutamate.

title: The Caenorhabditis elegans Tubby homolog dynamically modulates olfactory cilia membrane morphogenesis and phospholipid composition.

title: Mechanism of ligand activation of a eukaryotic cyclic nucleotide-gated channel.
review_notes: cryo-EM of the C. elegans TAX-4 channel in cGMP-bound and unbound states; defines the ligand-activation mechanism and central-gate residues. Grounds the cGMP-binding core function and the gating knowledge gap.

title: Mutations in a cyclic nucleotide-gated channel lead to abnormal thermosensation and chemosensation in C. elegans.
review_notes: Foundational paper: tax-4 mutants fail thermo- and chemosensory behaviors; TAX-4 is homologous to vertebrate CNG channels and functions as a CNG channel in cultured cells; TAX-4::GFP localizes to sensory endings. Anchors the core molecular function, localization and sensory-behavior annotations.

title: A cyclic nucleotide-gated channel inhibits sensory axon outgrowth in larval and adult Caenorhabditis elegans: a distinct pathway for maintenance of sensory axon structure.
review_notes: Shows tax-2/tax-4 are required to maintain correct sensory axon structure (late-larval/adult axon-outgrowth phenotype). Supports the non-core regulation-of-axon-extension annotation.

title: Genetic and structural characterization of the human mitochondrial inner membrane translocase.
review_notes: Human/yeast Tim44 characterization (abstract only). Establishes the conserved Tim23/Tim17/Tim44 + mtHsp70 matrix-import mechanism that is the by-similarity basis for the worm annotations, and reports that human Tim44 is matrix-localized and only loosely membrane-associated — the source for the submitochondrial-topology knowledge gap.

title: Activation of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response does not predict longevity in Caenorhabditis elegans.
review_notes: Genome-wide hsp-6p::gfp UPRmt RNAi screen (full text, verified). Directly assays tin-44: T09B4.9 (TIM44) is recovered as a UPRmt-inducing clone, grouped with the TIM23-complex import components, and is among the mitochondrial-import knockdowns that shorten lifespan. This is the strongest direct worm loss-of-function evidence that tin-44 acts in mitochondrial protein import. NOTE: a falcon deep-research summary claimed tin-44 RNAi "extended lifespan by 11.1%"; the paper's verified text instead groups tin-44 with the lifespan-SHORTENING import knockdowns, so that falcon claim was not used.

title: The UPRmt preserves mitochondrial import to extend lifespan.
review_notes: Only direct-worm reference for tin-44 (full text, PMC-available). Explicitly identifies tin-44 as the C. elegans homolog of mammalian tim44, places it at the matrix-pulling step of import with mtHSP70/HSP-6, and shows it is transcriptionally co-induced with the rest of the TIM/TOM import machinery upon UPRmt activation. Quoted sentences are verbatim from the cached full text. Note: the worm data here are transcriptional, not biochemical.

title: Probable mitochondrial import inner membrane translocase subunit tin-44 (C. elegans)
