title: Intermembrane space proteome of yeast mitochondria.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Targeted Bax-release IMS proteomics with >90% coverage of the known soluble IMS proteome; the strongest single localization evidence. Coa4 appears in the protein tables rather than the body text.

title: Inaccurately assembled cytochrome c oxidase can lead to oxidative stress-induced growth arrest.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. Supplies an independent IMP for complex IV assembly, the CMC1 genetic interaction, and the important caveat that reductant rescue of respiratory growth does not restore assembly.

title: A yeast suppressor screen links Coa4 to the mitochondrial copper delivery pathway for cytochrome c oxidase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text cached. The strongest functional evidence for Coa4 and the direct antecedent of the 2026 interaction work. Not currently cited by any GOA row for this gene, which is a gap worth reporting to SGD.

title: MIA40:ERV1 oxidizes cysteine residues to cystine disulfide bonds
review_notes: Reactome traceable author statement. Consistent with the direct evidence but adds nothing independent.

title: A family of tetraspans organizes cargo for sorting into multivesicular bodies.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified primary paper (MacDonald et al., Dev Cell 2015; PMC4421094). It is the source of the COS9 endosome and MVB-sorting ISS annotations, propagated via WITH/FROM SGD:S000003922 (COS5, the experimentally studied representative). The paper characterizes the COS family (COS1-COS10 and COS12) collectively via a whole-family cosΔ deletion and Cos5 as the representative; single-gene tests used COS1, COS2, COS4, COS5, COS6. COS9 (YKL219W) is not individually assayed, so its annotations are homology-based rather than direct experimental evidence for Cos9.

title: Isolation of a human cDNA for heme A:farnesyltransferase by functional complementation of a yeast cox10 mutant.
review_notes: PubMed-verified: the record is the COX10 (heme A:farnesyltransferase) cloning paper, not a COX17 study. It sources both the GO:0018343 protein farnesylation row and the GO:0005739 row on COX17, assigned by MGI against a S. cerevisiae accession. GO:0018343 is wrong even for COX10, since heme A:farnesyltransferase farnesylates heme rather than protein. Recommend retraction by the assigning group.

title: Prolyl isomerases in yeast.
review_notes: Arevalo-Rodriguez, Wu, Hanes & Heitman (2004) Frontiers in Bioscience; PubMed-verified (PMID:15353296, DOI:10.2741/1405); abstract-only in cache. Background/context review for the yeast prolyl-isomerase family; not used for a load-bearing CPR4-specific verbatim claim beyond the title.

title: The cyclophilins.
review_notes: Wang & Heitman (2005) Genome Biology review; PubMed-verified (PMID:15998457, DOI:10.1186/gb-2005-6-7-226); full text in cache. Makes explicit CPR4-specific statements (vacuolar localization, signal peptide, octuple-mutant viability, NinaA=CypC). Used for localization and non-essentiality/redundancy claims.

title: The nucleotide sequence of a third cyclophilin-homologous gene from Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Original cloning/sequencing paper for SCC3/CPR4 (P25334, YCR069W). PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache. Primary source for the signal-peptide + C-terminal TM topology and the NinaA structural parallel. Consistent with the UniProt feature table.

title: One library to make them all: streamlining the creation of yeast libraries via a SWAp-Tag strategy.
review_notes: Yofe et al. (2016) Nat Methods; PubMed-verified; full text in cache. A genome-wide library/methods paper that does not discuss CPR4 individually; it is the dataset source for the SGD HDA fungal-type vacuole annotation. Localization datapoint only.

title: All cyclophilins and FK506 binding proteins are, individually and collectively, dispensable for viability in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Dolinski, Muir, Cardenas & Heitman (1997) PNAS; PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache (full_text_available: false). Directly names Cpr4 as the secretory-pathway cyclophilin, establishes non-essentiality of all cyclophilins/FKBPs, and frames the "unknown physiological function / unique partners" gap. Source of the ISS PPIase annotation.

title: Falcon deep research report for CPR4 (Edison Scientific Literature)
review_notes: Falcon (Edison) deep-research synthesis. Its W121-to-glutamate claim independently corroborates this review's own sequence analysis (whole cyclophilin domain lacks a Trp; the human CypA W121-homologous position is not a Trp in CPR4). Cited claims grep-verified as verbatim substrings of the cached report.

title: A chemical-genetic screen to unravel the genetic network of CDC28/CDK1 links ubiquitin and Rad6-Bre1 to cell cycle progression.
review_notes: Source identity and abstract verified; target-specific genetic phenotype is curated by UniProt. The locally accessible abstract does not identify DCV1; do not treat the screen as a directly verified localization or defined molecular-activity assay.

title: The Sur7/PalI family transmembrane protein Tos7 (Yol019w) plays a role in secretion in budding yeast.
review_notes: Cited by SGD for the DCV1 nuclear-envelope IDA (GO:0005635). The cached record is abstract-only and its title/abstract concern the paralog Tos7 (Yol019w) localizing to plasma-membrane MCC/eisosome microdomains; I could not access the full text to confirm that DCV1/YFR012W was assayed for nuclear-envelope localization. Retained per policy (do not overrule an experimental annotation from incomplete evidence); marked UNVERIFIED.

title: A member of the claudin superfamily influences formation of the front domain in pheromone-responding yeast cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, target-specific primary paper. Its abstract directly reports Dcv1 plasma-membrane localization in vegetative cells, rear localization during pheromone response, and dcv1 loss-of-function effects on plasma-membrane lipids and mating polarity proteins.

title: Falcon research report on yeast DCV1
review_notes: Actual complete narrative and artifact table read. Correctly labels most proposals as family inference; it misses the PMID:33002606 curated nuclear-envelope source and PMID:22042866 genetic-screen source. Therefore its claim that no direct cell-biological characterization exists is incomplete, and its specific Rim101/scaffold assignments cannot be promoted to target molecular functions. Existing focused request addresses these uncovered source experiments.

title: OpenScientist focused report on DCV1 secondary membrane localizations
review_notes: The focused report was read and its decisive lead, PMID:36601911, was verified against the cached PubMed abstract. Its full-text caveat for PMID:33002606 is preserved, and its plasma-membrane and growing-tip recommendations are incorporated.

title: Regulation of the Dot1 histone H3K79 methyltransferase by histone H4K16 acetylation
review_notes: PubMed-verified cryo-EM structure (PDB 7K6P) of the yeast Dot1 catalytic domain bound to the nucleosome with the SAM cofactor, providing a structural basis for H3K79 methyltransferase activity.

title: Suppressor analysis of the mpt5/htr1/uth4/puf5 deletion in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache (full_text_available: false). PubMed-verified. This is the paper that named DSF2 and is the primary DSF2-specific functional report, but it only demonstrates a genetic suppressor relationship with mpt5/puf5; it does not assign DSF2 a molecular function or a direct biological process. Note dsf1 and dsf2 are unrelated genes co-recovered in the same screen.

title: Dissecting DNA damage response pathways by analysing protein localization and abundance changes during DNA replication stress.
review_notes: PMC full text confirmed. This is a large-scale GFP localization screen; DSF2 is not discussed by name in the main text (it is one of hundreds of scored strains in the supplementary tables). It legitimately supports the HDA "cellular bud tip" localization annotation but does not provide a dedicated functional characterization of DSF2.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Huh et al. global GFP-localization study; source of the HDA cytoplasm annotation (GO:0005737) and the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION Cytoplasm {ECO:0000269|PubMed:14562095}. Cached record is abstract-only but the localization datum is a curated high-throughput result.

title: Large-scale phosphorylation analysis of alpha-factor-arrested Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Large-scale phosphoproteomics; contributes a phosphosite (Ser1065) but no functional insight into ECM30.

title: A multidimensional chromatography technology for in-depth phosphoproteome analysis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Phosphosite Ser635; no functional insight.

title: Global analysis of Cdk1 substrate phosphorylation sites provides insights into evolution.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Cdk1 substrate phosphoproteome (Holt et al.); phosphosites only, regulatory significance for ECM30 not established.

title: Large scale identification of genes involved in cell surface biosynthesis and architecture in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Lussier et al. 1997; SGD attributes the ECM30 gene name to this paper and it is the ECO:0000269 source for UniProt's cell-wall FUNCTION line. Cached entry is abstract-only (full_text_available: false); the abstract describes the screen but does not name ECM30 individually, so the gene-specific cell-wall data reside in the full text (not read here). Not contradicted.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for ECM30 HID1-family Golgi inheritance
review_notes: Focused report read. It correctly highlights the lack of direct S. cerevisiae Golgi localization and the target-divergence question raised by PMID:40899782, but it treats absence of a target-specific assay and metazoan dense-core-vesicle biology as refutation despite actual descent from PTN000491103, a PomBase Golgi-organization donor and no demonstrated target-specific loss. Retain the current IBA actions.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO_Central IBA pipeline reference for the phylogenetically inferred protein methyltransferase activity annotation; consistent with the experimentally established protein-lysine methyltransferase function.

title: Automated identification of putative methyltransferases from genomic open reading frames.
review_notes: Abstract-only, but this is the well-known Katz/Dlakic/Clarke yeast MTase catalog; it correctly predicts EFM6 as a SAM-dependent methyltransferase, a prediction later experimentally confirmed by PMID:26115316. Supports the general SAM-MTase activity annotation, not a specific substrate.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; the Huh et al. global GFP localization dataset is the standard source for the cytoplasm HDA annotation. Cytoplasmic localization is consistent with a translation-machinery-associated methyltransferase.

title: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Eukaryotic Elongation Factor 1A (eEF1A) Is Methylated at Lys-390 by a METTL21-Like Methyltransferase.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified primary research article (Jakobsson et al. 2015, PLoS ONE). This is the defining functional characterization of EFM6/YNL024C. Full text read; all supporting_text quotes are verbatim substrings. The Lys390 substrate is uniquely and experimentally attributed to YNL024C, distinct from the other Efm enzymes (Efm1/4/5 on other eEF1A lysines; Efm2/3 on eEF2).

title: Structural genomics of enzymes involved in sterol/isoprenoid biosynthesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Bonanno et al. 2001 PNAS; source of PDB 1FI4 and the homodimer (SUBUNIT) assignment in UniProt.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Huh et al. 2003 Nature GFP localization atlas; basis for the HDA cytoplasm annotation.

title: Identification of active site residues in mevalonate diphosphate decarboxylase: implications for a family of phosphotransferases.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified; directly assays the diphosphomevalonate decarboxylase active site and ATP utilization.

title: Sterol pathway in yeast. Identification and properties of mutant strains defective in mevalonate diphosphate decarboxylase and farnesyl diphosphate synthetase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Chambon et al. 1991; the founding genetic evidence that erg19 mutants lack MDD activity.

title: Recent Advances in Ergosterol Biosynthesis and Regulation Mechanisms in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified review (Hu et al. 2017). Source of the NAS vacuole annotation; a review-level compartmentalization statement, not a direct localization assay of MDD.

title: Molecular cloning and expression of the cDNAs encoding human and yeast mevalonate pyrophosphate decarboxylase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Toth & Huwyler 1996; direct demonstration of catalytic activity of the cloned yeast enzyme.

title: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae mevalonate diphosphate decarboxylase is essential for viability, and a single Leu-to-Pro mutation in a conserved sequence leads to thermosensitivity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Berges et al. 1997; establishes essentiality and the role of MDD in sterol biosynthesis by mutant phenotype.

title: Deep research report (falcon / Edison Scientific Literature) for yeast ERG19/MVD1
review_notes: Automated deep-research report; cited primary/review sources (Cordier 1999, Johnston 2020, Jorda & Puig 2020, Garay 2026 preprint) are consistent with the UniProt record and the cached publications used in this review. Used for corroboration, not as primary evidence for any single annotation.

title: Sequence analysis of the right end of chromosome XV in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: an insight into the structural and functional significance of sub-telomeric repeat sequences.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; this is the foundational report defining the three ERR enolase-related genes and their sub-telomeric location. Abstract-only in our cache (full text not available). It establishes DNA sequence identity to ENO1/ENO2 and genomic copy number/location, NOT enzymatic activity; the SGD ISA annotation to phosphopyruvate hydratase activity uses this paper as the sequence-similarity source.

title: Global analysis of protein expression in yeast.
review_notes: Cached abstract and matching UniProt reference metadata checked. Gene-specific abundance/phosphosite statements are available in UniProt, not in the cached primary abstract; those findings are attributed separately to that record.

title: A multidimensional chromatography technology for in-depth phosphoproteome analysis.
review_notes: Cached abstract and matching UniProt reference metadata checked. Gene-specific abundance/phosphosite statements are available in UniProt, not in the cached primary abstract; those findings are attributed separately to that record.

title: Functional analysis of the single Est1/Ebs1 homologue in Kluyveromyces lactis reveals roles in both telomere maintenance and rapamycin resistance.
review_notes: Fetched PubMed/PMC3416500 record and read assay Results and Discussion: UV crosslinking provides binding evidence despite unsuccessful EMSA; TPR/DSH mutants constrain the KlEst1 interface. No Esl1 construct is tested. This comparator can guide a target assay but does not establish an Esl1 loss.

title: Yeast hEST1A/B (SMG5/6)-like proteins contribute to environment-sensing adaptive gene expression responses.
review_notes: Dedicated primary full text read, including methods and Figures 2–6. Ade2-1 and pre-CYH2 RNA measurements with upf1 controls provide scoped NMD-negative evidence. Telomere-length, senescence, silencing and transcript measurements provide functional negatives but do not measure Esl1 nucleic-acid binding or holoenzyme membership. Transcriptomic and genetic effects motivate adaptive-regulation hypotheses but do not identify the biochemical step performed by Esl1.

title: Falcon literature report for yeast ESL1
review_notes: Read full scientific body. Useful EST/SMG/PIN background, but it missed PMID:23893744 and Esl2 and therefore cannot adjudicate the target negatives or establish target telomere/NMD/nuclease functions. The dedicated full-text study takes precedence. No exact OpenScientist report existed at the initial cache check; the newly generated focused report is separately assessed here.

title: OpenScientist focused assessment of ESL1 telomerase association and nucleic-acid binding
review_notes: Entire report, HTML version and all three CSV artifacts read. The actual PAINT lineage already verifies positive IBD PTN000403280 above target PTN007651903; a family/subfamily label is not the origin or validity test of that assertion. Zero STRING experimental-channel scores mean no recorded positive link, not tested noninteraction; uniform database scores do not identify their underlying source. Low global identity does not establish interface loss. NMD-substrate negatives do not negate another function by parity. Primary PMID:23893744 full experiments and newly fetched PMID:22544908 KlEst1 binding results do not test Esl1 binding or complex association. Retain all three UNDECIDED calls and manual follow-up rather than REMOVE/NOT or another duplicate report.

title: ESL1: inspected PAINT ancestry
review_notes: Actual nested PANTHER tree retrieved by POST; lineage, target accession, ancestral rows and response hash retained in sibling JSON. Related loss assertions outside the target lineage are distinguished from inherited losses.

review_notes: InterPro2GO source of the endopeptidase and proteolysis inferences; both correct for separase.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt

review_notes: Establishes Rec8 as a second Esp1 substrate; the abstract foregrounds meiosis I, so the 'meiosis II' rows are graded MODIFY to meiotic chromosome separation rather than removed.

title: A novel role of the budding yeast separin Esp1 in anaphase spindle elongation: evidence that proper spindle association of Esp1 is regulated by Pds1.
review_notes: Full text cached; source of the nucleus, cytoplasm, spindle and SPB localisations.

title: The dual mechanism of separase regulation by securin.

title: The role of the polo kinase Cdc5 in controlling Cdc14 localization.
review_notes: Full text cached; the title foregrounds Cdc5 but the paper directly assays esp1-1 mutants.

title: The proteome of Saccharomyces cerevisiae mitochondria.
review_notes: Correct identifier, but a high-throughput organellar proteome is weak evidence for localisation of a nuclear/spindle protein; mitochondrion HDA rows graded REMOVE.

title: Downregulation of PP2A(Cdc55) phosphatase by separase initiates mitotic exit in budding yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; mechanistic basis of the FEAR role (source of the Cdc55 IPI).

title: Toward the complete yeast mitochondrial proteome: multidimensional separation techniques for mitochondrial proteomics.
review_notes: As for PMID:14576278; high-throughput organellar proteome, mitochondrion HDA graded REMOVE.

title: Cleavage of Mcd1 by caspase-like protease Esp1 promotes apoptosis in budding yeast.
review_notes: Full text cached; single study of a stress-specific role, graded KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.

title: The protease activity of yeast separase (esp1) is required for anaphase spindle elongation independently of its role in cleavage of cohesin.
review_notes: Full text cached; source of the regulation of mitotic spindle elongation rows.

title: High-quality binary protein interaction map of the yeast interactome network.

title: Separase cooperates with Zds1 and Zds2 to activate Cdc14 phosphatase in early anaphase.
review_notes: Full text cached; source of the second Cdc55 IPI and of the mechanistic caveat on direct PP2A inhibition.

title: Dissecting DNA damage response pathways by analysing protein localization and abundance changes during DNA replication stress.
review_notes: High-throughput localisation dataset; calls agree with directed studies.

title: Positive feedback promotes mitotic exit via the APC/C-Cdh1-separase-Cdc14 axis in budding yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; independent support for the mitotic-exit role.

title: Molecular mechanism for the regulation of yeast separase by securin.
review_notes: Full text cached; atomic-resolution basis for the separase-securin complex annotation.

title: Rewiring of the phosphoproteome executes two meiotic divisions in budding yeast.
review_notes: Identifier resolves to the intended paper, but the Esp1-specific statement is not in the cached text (likely a figure legend or supplementary table); the annotated function is independently established by PMID:11081626.

title: An ESP1/PDS1 complex regulates loss of sister chromatid cohesion at the metaphase to anaphase transition in yeast.
review_notes: Founding description of the Esp1-Pds1 complex and of Esp1 as the sister-separating protein (abstract-only cache).

title: Deep research report (Edison/falcon): ESP1 (YGR098C; UniProt Q03018) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
review_notes: Claims cross-checked against the cached primary papers (Ciosk 1998, Uhlmann 2000, Buonomo 2000, Jensen 2001, Hornig 2002, Baskerville 2008); the Ty1 and Cdk1-phosphosite claims rest on papers not cached here and are not used for annotation decisions.

title: Functional differences in yeast protein disulfide isomerases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified genetic analysis central to defining Eug1p as a cooperative auxiliary component of the ER redox-folding network. The cache is abstract-only, so assay-level claims defer to curator review.

title: Mutation of yeast Eug1p CXXS active sites to CXXC results in a dramatic increase in protein disulphide isomerase activity.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary biochemical study that directly distinguishes native Eug1p from engineered CXXC variants. The cache is abstract-only.

title: The yeast EUG1 gene encodes an endoplasmic reticulum protein that is functionally related to protein disulfide isomerase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary characterization of EUG1. The cache is abstract-only; conclusions are limited to statements visible in that abstract.

title: Interactions among yeast protein-disulfide isomerase proteins and endoplasmic reticulum chaperone proteins influence their activities.
review_notes: PubMed-verified biochemical and interaction study. The cache is abstract-only; it supports weak Eug1p oxidative-refolding activity but is silent on whether Eug1p itself has chaperone activity.

title: Synergistic computational and experimental proteomics approaches for more accurate detection of active serine hydrolases in yeast.
review_notes: Defines the eukaryotic Fsh (family of serine hydrolase) group and detects FSH3 as a catalytically active serine hydrolase by combined chemical/computational activity-based proteomics. This is the paper UniProt cites for FUNCTION ("Serine hydrolase of unknown specificity"). Abstract-only in cache; the FSH3 identification is in the full text/supplementary of this yeast serine-hydrolase survey. Anchored to the yeast serine-hydrolase-family framing and the UniProt FUNCTION evidence tag ECO:0000269|PubMed:14645503.

title: Identification of new genes regulated by the Crt1 transcription factor, an effector of the DNA damage checkpoint pathway in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Experimentally confirms FSH3 is a transcriptional target of Crt1p (RFX1) by RT-PCR in wild-type vs crt1-delta strains (source of UniProt INDUCTION). NOTE: this paper's suggestion that FSH3 acts in folate metabolism / with DHFR is explicit speculation from OVCA2/DYR-SCHPO sequence similarity, not experimental data; it must not be used to annotate folate metabolism.

title: Screening for hydrolytic enzymes reveals Ayr1p as a novel triacylglycerol lipase in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Background/contextual: characterizes GXSXG serine-hydrolase enzymes acting in yeast peroxisomal and lipid-droplet lipid metabolism (Ayr1p, Lpx1p). Does not assay FSH3 or assign it a substrate; supports the plausibility of a peroxisomal serine-hydrolase acting in lipid metabolism.

title: FSH3 mediated cell death is dependent on NUC1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: FSH3-specific study: H2O2 induces FSH3; overexpression causes ROS accumulation and NUC1-dependent apoptosis; single deletion is viable (grows better under H2O2); fsh double deletions grow faster, indicating partial redundancy among FSH paralogs. Establishes phenotype without assigning a molecular substrate.

title: Systematic multi-level analysis of an organelle proteome reveals new peroxisomal functions.
review_notes: Systematic peroxisome-proteome study; basis of the SGD IDA C:peroxisome annotation for FSH3 and reports that FSH3 overexpression gives the strongest lipidome change (reduction of phosphatidylcholine) among dark peroxisomal proteins. It also reports a deletion-based phenotype: a Fsh3/Lpx1 double deletion (but neither single mutant) has reduced peroxisomal beta-oxidation activity, suggesting FSH3 has an overlapping role with the peroxisomal lipase Lpx1 in fatty-acid beta-oxidation. The PC lipid effect is an overexpression phenotype, not proof of a direct PC-hydrolase activity.

title: Molecular analysis of Saccharomyces cerevisiae chromosome I. On the number of genes and the identification of essential genes using temperature-sensitive-lethal mutations.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary source that named FUN19 ("Function UNknown 19"); establishes non-essentiality and the historical absence of homology, underpinning the "dark gene" framing.

title: Structure and function of the SWIRM domain, a conserved protein module found in chromatin regulatory complexes.
review_notes: Domain-level source (does not study FUN19 itself). Justifies the chromatin/nucleosome-association inference from FUN19's SWIRM domain while making clear the domain is a shared module that does not specify a complex.

title: A multidimensional chromatography technology for in-depth phosphoproteome analysis.
review_notes: Proteome-scale phosphosite dataset; the FUN19 phosphosites are recorded in UniProt (Thr194/Ser207/Ser211). Establishes expression, not function.

title: Global analysis of Cdk1 substrate phosphorylation sites provides insights into evolution.
review_notes: Large-scale Cdk1 substrate map; FUN19 Ser207 is one of 547 sites. Recorded in UniProt as a Cdk1 site. Establishes phosphoregulation potential, not a specific molecular function.

title: The SAGA HAT module is tethered by its SWIRM domain and modulates activity of the SAGA DUB module.
review_notes: Primary mechanistic Ada2/SAGA study. It does not assay Fun19, but it shows that the SWIRM domain retained by Fun19 is a SAGA-HAT tether in Ada2, not a standalone coactivator module.

title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for FUN19 Ada2/SAGA coactivation divergence
review_notes: Focused report read. Its negative conclusion on Fun19 coactivator activity and positive regulation is supported by PMID:36965704 and by the Fun19 subfamily's loss of SAGA-type complex membership. The report overstates the weakness of the neutral chromatin and Rpd3L IBAs, which remain plausible PAINT inferences pending direct target experiments.

title: Fus3 controls Ty1 transpositional dormancy through the invasive growth MAPK pathway.
review_notes: Abstract verified: Fus3 kinase activity inhibits invasive growth and Ty1 transposition (supports negative, not positive, regulation of invasive growth).

title: Specificity of MAP kinase signaling in yeast differentiation involves transient versus sustained MAPK activation.
review_notes: Abstract verified: active Fus3 limits Kss1 activation.

title: MAP kinase dynamics in response to pheromones in budding yeast.

review_notes: Abstract verified: Fus3-dependent Tec1 degradation; active Fus3 phosphorylates Tec1 T273 in vitro; fus3 deletion causes loss of specificity.

title: Signal transduction in Saccharomyces cerevisiae requires tyrosine and threonine phosphorylation of FUS3 and KSS1.

review_notes: InterPro2GO electronic pipeline. Correctly transfers GATA/zinc-finger domain terms (zinc ion binding, sequence-specific DNA binding, regulation of transcription) from IPR000679/IPR013088, which GAT2 genuinely carries. Domain- level, not GAT2-specific functional evidence.

title: Use of the ND evidence code for Gene Ontology (GO) terms
review_notes: Standard GO_REF documenting the ND (no biological data) evidence code, used here for the root cellular_component placeholder.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PAINT/IBA phylogenetic pipeline. The IBA terms on GAT2 propagate from PANTHER family PTHR45658 (with_from lists Arabidopsis AGI codes and Dictyostelium genes), i.e. from the plant/Dictyostelium GATA cluster, NOT from the yeast NCR GATA factors (which are in the separate family PTHR10071). Appropriate for generic GATA-TF terms; does not establish GAT2's specific process.

title: Genome-wide transcriptional analysis in S. cerevisiae by mini-array membrane hybridization.
review_notes: Methods paper (Cox, Pinchak & Cooper 1999) validating mini-array membrane hybridization using the GATA-factor/nitrogen-control network as a test case. Abstract-only in cache. It does not demonstrate GAT2-specific function; SGD used it as the anchor for ISA (inferred from sequence alignment) annotations whose with_from fields point to OTHER GATA-factor genes. Correctly cited but only weakly relevant to GAT2's own function.

title: The cellular economy of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae zinc proteome.
review_notes: Wang et al. 2018 (Metallomics). Bioinformatic + mass-spec survey defining the yeast zinc proteome via combined domain and motif searches. GAT2's inclusion as a zinc-binding protein is a reasonable computational (RCA) inference from its GATA zinc finger; not a direct GAT2 metal-binding measurement.

title: GAT2 bioinformatics — GATA zinc-finger confirmation and paralog relationships
review_notes: In-repo reproducible analysis (this review). Confirms domain presence and quantifies paralog divergence; supports the MF domain terms while cautioning against transferring NCR-factor process functions to GAT2. file: reference — not auto quote-checked; quotes verified by hand against RESULTS.md.

title: Structural basis for activation of SAGA histone acetyltransferase Gcn5 by partner subunit Ada2.
review_notes: Crystal structures (PDB 6CW2/6CW3) of the yeast Gcn5 HAT domain bound to its partner subunit Ada2 show that the Ada2 SANT domain activates Gcn5 HAT activity by enhancing binding of the acetyl-CoA cosubstrate.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: Source of the experimental (HDA) cytoplasm localization for GPM3 in GOA. Abstract-only in cache; the per-protein call resides in the study's database, recorded by SGD.

title: Global analysis of protein expression in yeast.
review_notes: Basis for the UniProt statement that GPM3 is present at ~3730 molecules/cell in log-phase SD medium (ECO:0000269|PubMed:14562106); establishes that GPM3 is a genuinely expressed, stable protein despite lacking demonstrated activity.

title: Investigation of two yeast genes encoding putative isoenzymes of phosphoglycerate mutase.
review_notes: Definitive characterization of GPM2 and GPM3. PubMed-verified; abstract-only in cache but the abstract contains the load-bearing experimental findings (no detectable mutase activity even on forced expression; phenotypically silent deletions; probable non-functional homologs). Directly grounds the over-annotation calls on the transferred mutase/glycolysis terms.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified genome-wide GFP localization study (Huh et al., Nature 2003); it is the ECO:0000269 source cited by UniProt for Gtt3's nuclear-membrane location. The cached entry is abstract-only, but the per-protein localization is captured in the UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION annotation.

title: One library to make them all: streamlining the creation of yeast libraries via a SWAp-Tag strategy.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. This is the high-throughput N'-GFP localization resource from which SGD derived Gtt3's nuclear-periphery (GO:0034399, HDA) annotation; the paper describes the localization category set but does not name GTT3 in the cached text (per-gene calls are in the library data).

title: UniProtKB entry for GTT3_YEAST (P39996)
review_notes: UniProt record for the target protein; supports the membrane topology and nuclear-membrane localization used in this review. The RecName "Glutathione transferase 3" is a name/family assignment, not experimentally demonstrated activity.

title: Falcon deep research report for GTT3 (YEL017W)
review_notes: Genuine Edison/falcon deep-research report (17 citations). Used for its well-supported "no direct evidence" statements about GTT3 and the paralog contrast. Note one factual error: it states GTT3 is "285 amino acids", whereas UniProt P39996 is 337 aa; that length claim was not propagated into this review.

title: Osmotic stress-induced gene expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae requires Msn1p and the novel nuclear factor Hot1p.
review_notes: Full text: identifies Hot1 by two-hybrid with Hog1; biochemical confirmation of the interaction failed in this paper.

title: Rck2 kinase is a substrate for the osmotic stress-activated mitogen-activated protein kinase Hog1.
review_notes: Full text: Rck2 is a direct Hog1 substrate; in vitro kinase assays with Pbs2(EE)-activated Hog1.

title: Two protein tyrosine phosphatases, Ptp2 and Ptp3, modulate the subcellular localization of the Hog1 MAP kinase in yeast.
review_notes: Full text: Hog1 nuclear accumulation and Ptp2/Ptp3-dependent localization.

title: Regulation of the Sko1 transcriptional repressor by the Hog1 MAP kinase in response to osmotic stress.
review_notes: Full text: Hog1 phosphorylates Sko1 in vitro and converts the Sko1-Ssn6-Tup1 repressor.

title: Systematic identification of protein complexes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by mass spectrometry.
review_notes: High-throughput AP-MS interactome; source of a Hog1-Rck2 IPI.

title: Subcellular localization of the yeast proteome.
review_notes: High-throughput localization study; source of cytoplasm HDA.

title: Targeting the MEF2-like transcription factor Smp1 by the stress-activated Hog1 mitogen-activated protein kinase.
review_notes: Full text: Smp1 is a Hog1 substrate controlling osmostress genes.

title: Osmostress-induced transcription by Hot1 depends on a Hog1-mediated recruitment of the RNA Pol II.
review_notes: Full text: Hot1 recruits Hog1 to promoters; Hog1 needed for Pol II recruitment.

title: Hog1 mediates cell-cycle arrest in G1 phase by the dual targeting of Sic1.
review_notes: Abstract only: Hog1 binds and phosphorylates Sic1 for G1 arrest.

title: Phosphorylation of Hsl1 by Hog1 leads to a G2 arrest essential for cell survival at high osmolarity.
review_notes: Full text: Hog1 phosphorylates Hsl1 causing G2 arrest.

title: Deletion of HOG1 leads to Osmosensitivity in starvation-induced, but not rapamycin-dependent Atg8 degradation and proteolysis: further evidence for different regulatory mechanisms in yeast autophagy.
review_notes: Abstract only; an addendum/commentary on hog1-dependent osmosensitivity of starvation-induced autophagy.

title: An in vivo map of the yeast protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput PCA interactome; source of a Hog1-Rck2 IPI.

title: A global protein kinase and phosphatase interaction network in yeast.
review_notes: High-throughput kinase/phosphatase AP-MS network; source of Hog1 IPIs with Ste7, Rck2, Hot1.

title: Control of Ubp3 ubiquitin protease activity by the Hog1 SAPK modulates transcription upon osmostress.
review_notes: Full text: Hog1 phosphorylates Ubp3 Ser695 to modulate osmostress transcription.

title: Coordinated control of replication and transcription by a SAPK protects genomic integrity.
review_notes: Abstract only: Hog1 phosphorylates Mrc1 to delay replication during osmostress.

title: Activator and repressor functions of the Mot3 transcription factor in the osmostress response of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Full text: Mot3-activated osmostress genes depend on Hog1.

title: Control of Cdc28 CDK1 by a stress-induced lncRNA.
review_notes: Full text: Hog1 associates with chromatin and induces lncRNAs/CDC28.

title: Regulation of MAP kinase Hog1 by calmodulin during hyperosmotic stress.
review_notes: Abstract only: single study reporting calmodulin binding to Hog1.

title: Hog1 activation delays mitotic exit via phosphorylation of Net1.
review_notes: Full text: Hog1 phosphorylates Net1 T62/S385 and delays mitotic exit.

title: The social and structural architecture of the yeast protein interactome.
review_notes: High-throughput AE-MS interactome; source of a Hog1-Rck2 IPI.

title: Proline-directed yeast and human MAP kinases phosphorylate the Dot1p/DOT1L histone H3K79 methyltransferase.
review_notes: Abstract only: Hog1 phosphorylates Dot1 in vitro and in vivo.

title: An osmosensing signal transduction pathway in yeast.
review_notes: Founding paper identifying HOG1 and PBS2 as MAPK and MAPKK of the osmosensing pathway (abstract checked).

title: Reconstitution of G1 cyclin ubiquitination with complexes containing SCFGrr1 and Rbx1.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; abstract states the Rbx1 reconstitution of SCF(Grr1)/Cln1 ubiquitination and Cdc34 recruitment. The glucose-transport IDA cannot be checked from the abstract.

title: ROC1, a homolog of APC11, represents a family of cullin partners with an associated ubiquitin ligase activity.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; abstract states the yeast ROC1 essentiality/Sic1-Cln2 accumulation result and the RING-mutant loss of ligase activity.

title: Cdc53/cullin and the essential Hrt1 RING-H2 subunit of SCF define a ubiquitin ligase module that activates the E2 enzyme Cdc34.
review_notes: Full text cached (PMC316801). The defining Hrt1 paper: MS identification, essentiality, hrt1-ts G1/S arrest, direct binding to Cdc53/Cdc4/Cdc34, >5-fold stimulation of Sic1 ubiquitination, NEM-insensitive Cdc34 activation, human HRT1 complementation.

title: Nuclear-specific degradation of Far1 is controlled by the localization of the F-box protein Cdc4.
review_notes: Full text cached; GFP-Hrt1 nucleus+cytoplasm localisation is stated explicitly.

title: A role for Saccharomyces cerevisiae Cul8 ubiquitin ligase in proper anaphase progression.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; states Cul3/Cul8 ligase activity and the Roc1-binding requirement of Cul8.

title: ELA1 and CUL3 are required along with ELC1 for RNA polymerase II polyubiquitylation and degradation in DNA-damaged yeast cells.
review_notes: Full text cached; Roc1 participation in the Elc1-Ela1-Cul3 ligase is explicitly presumed, not tested.

title: Cullin neddylation and substrate-adaptors counteract SCF inhibition by the CAND1-like protein Lag2 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Full text cached; purified Cdc53/Hrt1 heterodimers, Lag2 sequestration and Rub1 modification.

title: Cul8/Rtt101 forms a variety of protein complexes that regulate DNA damage response and transcriptional silencing.
review_notes: Full text cached; Cul8 complex composition and phenotypes, Hrt1 never tested (only 'Rbx1' in the introduction).

title: The SCFDia2 ubiquitin E3 ligase ubiquitylates Sir4 and functions in transcriptional silencing.
review_notes: Full text cached; SCF(Dia2)/Sir4 study that never mentions Hrt1.

title: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae F-box protein Dia2 is a mediator of S-phase checkpoint recovery from DNA damage.
review_notes: Full text cached; SCF(Dia2)/Mrc1 study that mentions Rbx1 only as a generic SCF subunit.

title: Proteome-wide protein interaction measurements of bacterial proteins of unknown function.
review_notes: Full text cached; the paper concerns Streptococcus pneumoniae proteins and never mentions Hrt1, Cdc4 or Cdc53, so the two IPI rows citing it cannot be verified here.

title: Cdc53 is a scaffold protein for multiple Cdc34/Skp1/F-box proteincomplexes that regulate cell division and methionine biosynthesis in yeast.
review_notes: Full text cached; predates the discovery of Hrt1 and does not mention it; supports SCF architecture generally.

title: Falcon deep research report for yeast HRT1
review_notes: LLM-generated (Falcon/Edison) synthesis built almost entirely on Seol et al. 1999 (cached, full text) plus Scott et al. 2010 and a 2023 review that are not in the local cache; its RING-E3/E2-facing framing and its Rub1/Dcn1 dual-E3 summary agree with UniProt and the cached papers. Its localisation caveat was checked against PMID:11080155.

title: UniProtKB record for yeast HRT1 (Q08273)
review_notes: Swiss-Prot entry; function, subunit, neddylation and localisation (PMID:10880467) annotations agree with the cached primary literature.

title: The hsp90 molecular chaperone modulates multiple telomerase activities.
review_notes: The cached abstract supports a family-level yeast-Hsp90 contribution to telomere maintenance but names Hsp82p in the mechanistic assays; HSC82-specific support has not been verified in-repository.

title: Intra- and intermonomer interactions are required to synergistically facilitate ATP hydrolysis in Hsp90.
review_notes: Full text is cached and directly reports biochemical ATPase assays on purified yeast Hsc82.

title: Molecular mechanism governing heme signaling in yeast: a higher-order complex mediates heme regulation of the transcriptional activator HAP1.
review_notes: The cached abstract identifies Hsp82, not Hsc82, in the purified HAP1 complex. The HSC82 annotation is retained as a plausible family-level paralog extrapolation but is not directly verified.

title: Swapping the gene-specific and regional silencing specificities of the Hst1 and Sir2 histone deacetylases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary study; directly distinguishes Hst1-Rfm1-Sum1 gene-specific repression from Sir2-Sir3-Sir4 regional silencing.

title: Control of replication initiation by the Sum1/Rfm1/Hst1 histone deacetylase.
review_notes: Full text verified; directly supports Hst1-dependent replication-origin control and the H4K5-predominant substrate-specificity conclusions.

title: HST1, a new member of the SIR2 family of genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary study; the abstract directly reports the negative HST1 results for HML regional silencing and rDNA recombination used in this review.

title: PubMed figure-caption evidence for Hst1 in PMID:27185881
review_notes: Exact figure-caption excerpt read from the official PubMed page; the usual cached publication remains abstract-only after retrieval attempts.

title: OpenScientist GO-focused literature synthesis for yeast HST1
review_notes: Actual report reviewed with primary sources. Its opening H3K9/K14/H4K16 list derives partly from Sir2/Hst2; it is not a direct site-specific Hst1 assay. Its native-role language must not erase conditional SUM1-1 silencing or the H4K16-positive loci in PMID:18990212.

title: Screening and characterization of transposon-insertion mutants in a pseudohyphal strain of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Suzuki et al. 2003 Yeast. The cached abstract describes the screen generally and does not name ICY1; the ICY1-specific phenotype is in the full-text tables read by the UniProt curator. Supports a phenotype, not a molecular function.

title: Suppression of a defect in mitochondrial protein import identifies cytosolic proteins required for viability of yeast cells lacking mitochondrial DNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Dunn & Jensen 2003 Genetics; primary source for the UniProt FUNCTION statement "Required for viability of cells lacking mtDNA". Provides only a genetic/indirect link, not a molecular function; also describes ICY1 as cytosolic (a localization discrepancy with the vacuole-membrane GFP call).

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Huh et al. 2003 Nature GFP localization study; source of the HDA fungal-type vacuole membrane annotation. Abstract is method-level; the ICY1-specific call is in the accompanying dataset, which the SGD curator used.

title: Transcriptional profiling of Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells under adhesion-inducing conditions.
review_notes: PubMed-verified Kleinschmidt et al. 2005. Abstract confirms the amino-acid-starvation/Gcn4 induction paradigm; the ICY1-specific induction is in the full-text gene tables. Regulatory context only, not a function.

title: The switch from fermentation to respiration in Saccharomyces cerevisiae is regulated by the Ert1 transcriptional activator/repressor.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Gasmi et al. 2014, Genetics). The cached full text does not contain the string "ICY1"/"YMR195W"; the ICY1-as-Ert1-target detail is in the supplementary target lists. Cited for regulatory context only; no ICY1-specific verbatim quote is anchored to this reference.

title: Atg41/Icy2 regulates autophagosome formation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Yao et al. 2015, Autophagy). The cached record is abstract-only and is about the paralog Atg41/Icy2, not ICY1; the ICY1-specific comparison (low similarity, no autophagy defect) is in the full text. Cited to support the paralog framing, not to assign ICY1 a function.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only cache. High-throughput localisation, consistent with the single-gene nucleus annotation and with the protein's nuclear and cytoplasmic targets.

title: Initiation of the TORC1-regulated G0 program requires Igo1/2, which license specific mRNAs to evade degradation via the 5'-3' mRNA decay pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only cache (PMC2919320 exists). The paper that named IGO1/IGO2, mapped Rim15 phosphorylation to Ser64 and established the G0 and mRNA-protection phenotypes; source of the P-body, nucleus, mRNA stabilization, deadenylation-dependent decay and G1-to-G0 annotations.

title: Yeast endosulfines control entry into quiescence and chronological life span by inhibiting protein phosphatase 2A.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; abstract-only cache. Establishes the PP2A-Cdc55 inhibitor mechanism for the yeast endosulfines (purified-protein inhibition, Ser64-dependent Cdc55 binding, cdc55/pph21 but not rts1 epistasis); source of the IDA/IMP inhibitor rows and two G1-to-G0 IGI rows.

title: Budding yeast greatwall and endosulfines control activity and spatial regulation of PP2A(Cdc55) for timely mitotic progression.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; full text cached. Independent confirmation of the Ser64-dependent PP2A-Cdc55 binding and in vitro inhibition, plus the paradoxical in vivo positive role in mitotic entry; source of one IDA inhibitor row and the mitotic phase-transition IGI row.

title: Deep research report for IGO1 (yeast), Falcon provider
review_notes: Falcon (Edison) literature synthesis; claims about Bontron 2013 and Juanes 2013 were checked against the cached abstracts/full text. Its summaries of Sarkar 2014, Talarek 2017 and Hollenstein 2021 (not cached here) are used only for context in the description and core-function narrative, and it correctly flags the 2024 Nature Communications study as fission-yeast igo1, not P53897.

title: Natural Variation in the Multidrug Efflux Pump SGE1 Underlies Ionic Liquid Tolerance in Yeast.
review_notes: PMC full text available (PMC6116967). Verified against PubMed; this is the paper that named ILT1/YDR090C and provides the only experimental functional data (deletion sensitivity to cationic compounds, complementation, plasma-membrane localization, SGE1-independence). Supports the tolerance and localization claims verbatim; it does NOT establish a molecular transport function for Ilt1.

title: Improving ionic liquid tolerance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae through heterologous expression and directed evolution of an ILT1 homolog from Yarrowia lipolytica.
review_notes: PubMed-verified abstract-only cache. This 2019 follow-up is directly relevant to ILT engineering and confirms endogenous ScILT1/YDR090C as the comparison point for the evolved Yarrowia homolog, but it still does not identify Ilt1's direct substrate or mechanism.

title: Falcon literature report for yeast ILT1
review_notes: Full body reviewed. Its identity/domain and comparative transporter synthesis is informative, but its assertion of no target localization and its naming history miss PMID:30045857. Primary PM microscopy supplements rather than excludes the inherited vacuolar role. No exact cached OpenScientist report was found.

title: ILT1: inspected PAINT ancestry
review_notes: Actual nested PANTHER tree retrieved by POST; lineage, target accession, ancestral rows and response hash retained in sibling JSON. Related loss assertions outside the target lineage are distinguished from inherited losses.

title: Use of the ND evidence code for Gene Ontology (GO) terms
review_notes: GO_REF documenting the ND (No biological Data available) evidence code. Correctly applied by SGD to the three root-term annotations for this uncharacterized gene.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: Standard GO_REF for phylogenetically inferred (IBA) annotations from GO_Central. Correctly identifies the method; the biological transfer of the specific SRRM1 splicing function to yeast JIP4 is questionable (see per-annotation reasons), but the reference itself is valid.

title: Quantitative phosphoproteomics applied to the yeast pheromone signaling pathway.
review_notes: Pheromone-signaling phosphoproteome study; JIP4 Ser-577 detected as a phosphosite. Corroborates phosphoprotein status. Verified via UniProt MOD_RES cross-reference.

title: A multidimensional chromatography technology for in-depth phosphoproteome analysis.
review_notes: Methods-focused large-scale phosphoproteome study; JIP4 (Ser-48, Ser-360, Ser-552) appears as a mapped phosphoprotein. Corroborates the phosphoprotein status only. Verified via UniProt MOD_RES cross-references.

title: Global analysis of Cdk1 substrate phosphorylation sites provides insights into evolution.
review_notes: Large-scale identification of Cdk1 substrate phosphorylation sites in S. cerevisiae; JIP4 (Ser-48, Ser-51, Ser-510, Ser-552, Ser-775) is one of many phosphoproteins cataloged. Supports that JIP4 is an in vivo phosphoprotein and a likely Cdk1 substrate, but does not assign a molecular function. Verified via UniProt MOD_RES cross-references to this PMID.

title: Falcon (Edison) deep-research report on S. cerevisiae JIP4/YDR475C
review_notes: Automated Edison deep-research report (20 citations). Reconfirms merged-ORF status, non-essentiality, the YOR019W paralog, and the Ser/Arg repetitive matrix domain, and treats a splicing/RNA-processing role as a low-to-moderate-confidence, domain-based inference only. Adds a naming-origin hypothesis that JIP4 is a Gis1-associated factor. NOTE: its "165 aa" size claim is inconsistent with the authoritative UniProt length (876 aa) and is not used.

title: UniProtKB entry Q03361 (JIP4_YEAST), including PANTHER family assignment and sequence features
review_notes: Cached UniProt record for JIP4/YDR475C. Source for the domain/composition analysis (intrinsic disorder, compositionally biased low-complexity tracts, yeast JIP4_N/JIP4_helical Pfam cross-references, absence of a PWI/RRM domain), the PANTHER PTHR23148 family assignment, and the phosphosite features.

title: A yeast strain biosensor to detect cell wall-perturbing agents.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Rodriguez-Pena et al., J Biotechnol 2008). Directly documents stress-inducible KDX1/Mlp1 accumulation and its use as a CWI biosensor; supports the INDUCTION annotation in UniProt.

title: Yeast Mpk1 mitogen-activated protein kinase activates transcription through Swi4/Swi6 by a noncatalytic mechanism that requires upstream signal.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kim, Truman & Levin, MCB 2008). The pivotal paper establishing KDX1/Mlp1 as a "pseudokinase paralog" that activates transcription non-catalytically via Swi4/Swi6. Cached abstract-only, but the abstract itself carries the load-bearing statements quoted.

title: A global protein kinase and phosphatase interaction network in yeast.
review_notes: The existing source row explicitly uses ISS from SLT2 (SGD:S000001072); it is a similarity transfer, not an experimental Kdx1 phosphotransfer measurement. The cached abstract describes the interaction-network study. Target-specific primary pseudokinase evidence contradicts the catalytic transfer.

title: Transcriptional reporters for genes activated by cell wall stress through a non-catalytic mechanism involving Mpk1 and SBF.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Kim & Levin, Yeast 2011). Full text cached. States KDX1/Mlp1 is catalytically inactive, redundant with Mpk1 in the non-catalytic SBF branch, and itself an Mpk1->Rlm1 target. Strongly informs both core function and the redundancy knowledge gap.

title: Hsp90 and phosphorylation of the Slt2(Mpk1) MAP kinase activation loop are essential for catalytic, but not non-catalytic, Slt2-mediated transcription in yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Millson, Truman & Piper, Cell Stress Chaperones 2022). Full text cached. Independently corroborates KDX1/Mlp1 as a catalytically inactive pseudokinase participating in the non-catalytic SBF transcriptional branch.

title: Characterization of a serum response factor-like protein in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Rlm1, which has transcriptional activity regulated by the Mpk1 (Slt2) mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Watanabe et al., MCB 1997). Establishes the KDX1(Mlp1)-Rlm1 physical interaction (UniProt SUBUNIT) and its genetic role in CWI signaling. Notably the authors hedge on catalysis, calling Mlp1 a "MAP kinase-like kinase" rather than a kinase.

title: Specificity of MAP kinase signaling in yeast differentiation involves transient versus sustained MAPK activation.
review_notes: Full text cached: Kss1 is activated by pheromone in wild-type cells; Fus3 limits Kss1 activation.

title: MAP kinase dynamics in response to pheromones in budding yeast.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt for Kss1 subcellular location including Periplasm; abstract concerns Fus3/Ste5/Ste7 localization and does not support a periplasmic location for Kss1.

title: Global analysis of protein phosphorylation in yeast.
review_notes: Proteome-chip kinase substrate screen; supports generic protein kinase activity.

title: Analysis of the yeast kinome reveals a network of regulated protein localization during filamentous growth.
review_notes: Full text cached: Kss1-vYFP nuclear during filamentous growth.

title: The Ste5 scaffold directs mating signaling by catalytically unlocking the Fus3 MAP kinase for activation.
review_notes: Full text cached: Kss1 is an intrinsically good Ste7 substrate, independent of Ste5.

title: Proteome-wide protein interaction measurements of bacterial proteins of unknown function.
review_notes: Bacterial (S. pneumoniae) interaction study; the cached text does not mention Kss1/Ste12 (likely an assay control); curator annotation retained as the basis of the row.

title: Exploitation of latent allostery enables the evolution of new modes of MAP kinase regulation.
review_notes: Full text cached: Kss1 functions independently of Ste5 allosteric regulation.

title: Phosphorylation of Bni4 by MAP kinases contributes to septum assembly during yeast cytokinesis.
review_notes: Abstract only; multicopy suppression by Kss1 of slt2 rim101 lethality via Bni4.

title: Phosphorylation and localization of Kss1, a MAP kinase of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae pheromone response pathway.
review_notes: Abstract verified: Thr183/Tyr185 phosphorylation, Ste11->Ste7->Kss1 order, nuclear localization.

title: Elements of a single MAP kinase cascade in Saccharomyces cerevisiae mediate two developmental programs in the same cell type: mating and invasive growth.
review_notes: Abstract only; defines haploid invasive growth as a MAPK cascade-dependent program; KSS1 data in full text.

title: Signaling in the yeast pheromone response pathway: specific and high-affinity interaction of the mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinases Kss1 and Fus3 with the upstream MAP kinase kinase Ste7.
review_notes: Abstract verified: specific high-affinity Ste7-Kss1 complex and reciprocal phosphorylation.

title: Two novel targets of the MAP kinase Kss1 are negative regulators of invasive growth in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Abstract verified: identifies Dig1/Dig2 as Kss1 partners and substrates.

title: MAP kinases with distinct inhibitory functions impart signaling specificity during yeast differentiation.
review_notes: Abstract verified: Kss1 is the filamentation MAPK with a kinase-independent inhibitory role.

title: Repression of yeast Ste12 transcription factor by direct binding of unphosphorylated Kss1 MAPK and its regulation by the Ste7 MEK.
review_notes: Full text cached: direct binding of unphosphorylated Kss1 to Ste12 mediates repression.

title: Differential regulation of transcription: repression by unactivated mitogen-activated protein kinase Kss1 requires the Dig1 and Dig2 proteins.
review_notes: Abstract verified: Dig1/Dig2 are required cofactors for Kss1-imposed repression.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: Global GFP-tag localization survey. SGD reports LEE1 cytoplasmic localization from this study, but the cached PubMed record is abstract-only and does not expose the gene-specific table, so the paper is used here only as database-supported localization context rather than as direct support for a GO cellular-component assertion.

title: Effect of 21 different nitrogen sources on global gene expression in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Transcriptome study that (per its full text, surfaced by deep research) highlighted LEE1/YPL054W as one of a few nitrogen-responsive regulator-encoding genes of unknown function, describing it as a protein with two tandem CCCH-type zinc fingers. Marked UNVERIFIED because the cached record is abstract-only and the LEE1-specific statement is in the full text, which could not be re-read here; it is the best current source for LEE1's nitrogen-source-responsive (NCR) expression but assigns no molecular function.

title: Global analysis of Cdk1 substrate phosphorylation sites provides insights into evolution.
review_notes: UniProt source for the LEE1 phosphoserine sites (Ser-21, Ser-30, Ser-282) from large-scale phosphoproteomics; contextual, does not define LEE1 function.

title: A Whole Genome Screen for Minisatellite Stability Genes in Stationary-Phase Yeast Cells.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified whole-genome screen for mutants with stationary-phase minisatellite instability. Supports that the lee1/ypl054w deletion was a high-throughput ade2-h7.5 screen hit, but does not define LEE1's molecular function or justify a direct minisatellite-stability biological-process annotation.

title: The cellular economy of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae zinc proteome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (title matches). Proteome-wide zinc-proteome survey; supports LEE1's classification as a predicted zinc-binding protein via its CCCH zinc fingers, but does not assign a specific molecular or biological function. It is the assigned SGD source for the RCA GO:0008270 (zinc ion binding) annotation. Cached entry is abstract-only.

title: The reference genome sequence of Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Then and now.
review_notes: Reference-genome reannotation; source of the 2011 sequence revision at residues 14 and 66. No functional characterization of LIH1.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of a Yeast Lipase Family in the Yarrowia Clade.
review_notes: PMC full text verified. This is the source UniProt cites (ECO:0000303 / ECO:0000305) for the LIH1 name and the EC 3.1.1.3 designation. Confirms that the lipase assignment for LIH1 is homology-based, not experimental: LIH1 is only mentioned as a distant (26% identity) Saccharomycetaceae relative of the Yarrowia LIP family and was not expressed or assayed.

title: Complete nucleotide sequence of Saccharomyces cerevisiae chromosome X.

This is the genetic study directly linking MNN14 to N-glycan mannosylphosphorylation and the source of the SGD IGI annotation to GO:0006491. It establishes, by genetic-interaction/ deletion analysis, that MNN14 (an MNN4 paralog) is required for full N-glycan mannosylphosphorylation and that the MNN4+MNN14 double deletion abolishes it. It does NOT assay a molecular activity for MNN14, so it does not distinguish a transferase from a regulator role.

title: In Vitro N-Glycan Mannosyl-Phosphorylation of a Therapeutic Enzyme by Using Recombinant Mnn14 Produced from Pichia pastoris.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified primary research (Kang et al. 2021, J Microbiol Biotechnol; full text available, PMC9705852). This is the decisive molecular-function paper: recombinant soluble MNN14 (rMnn14 77-935) secreted from Pichia pastoris directly transfers mannosyl-phosphate from GDP-mannose to high-mannose N-glycans (Man8GlcNAc2 and the Man7-9GlcNAc2 glycans of rhGAA), producing mono- and bis-mannosyl-phosphorylated products, requires Mn2+, and is optimal at pH 7.5 / 30 C. It establishes an intrinsic mannosylphosphate transferase (mannosylphosphorylation enzyme, MPE) activity for MNN14 in vitro, and (with its companion Kim et al. 2017) that MNN14 is a main MPE in S. cerevisiae. It does not resolve the in-vivo division of labour between MNN14 and MNN4.

title: Mannosylphosphate transfer to cell wall mannan is regulated by the transcriptional level of the MNN4 gene in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Odani et al. 1997, FEBS Lett). Not about MNN14 directly, but load-bearing for the molecular-function reasoning: it establishes the MNN4-family paradigm in which MNN4 is a positive regulator whose amount is rate-limiting for mannosylphosphorylation, while the catalytic mannosylphosphate transferase is a separate enzyme (Mnn6/Ktr6). This is the basis for treating MNN14's own transferase-vs-regulator activity as an open molecular-function gap rather than assigning it the transferase term.

This regulator-vs-catalyst distinction relative to the intrinsic in-vitro catalytic activity of the paralogous DXD-containing MNN14 is the basis of the in-vivo division-of-labour knowledge gap.
