review_notes: Zhang, Shibahara, Stillman 2000; PCNA mutants defective in CAF-1 binding reduce silencing and CAF-1 chromatin association. Abstract-only cache.

title: The silencing complex SAS-I links histone acetylation to the assembly of repressed chromatin by CAF-I and Asf1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Meijsing & Ehrenhofer-Murray 2001; Sas2 interacts with Cac1 and Asf1, linking SAS-I to CAF-I-dependent silent chromatin assembly. Abstract-only cache.

title: Chromatin assembly factor I mutants defective for PCNA binding require Asf1/Hir proteins for silencing.
review_notes: Krawitz, Kama, Kaufman 2002; cac1 alleles defective in Cac3 or PCNA binding; weak Asf1-Cac2 interaction. Abstract-only cache.

title: Chromatin assembly factor I and Hir proteins contribute to building functional kinetochores in S. cerevisiae.
review_notes: Sharp et al. 2002; CAF-I and Hir proteins contribute to centromeric chromatin; CAF-I subunits enriched at centromeres. Abstract-only cache.

title: Systematic identification of protein complexes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by mass spectrometry.
review_notes: Ho et al. 2002 HMS-PCI complex survey; source of a generic protein binding row.

title: The yeast histone chaperone chromatin assembly factor 1 protects against double-strand DNA-damaging agents.
review_notes: Linger & Tyler 2005; CAF-1 protects against DSB agents, not required for repair per se; PCNA binding needed. Full text cached.

title: Proteome survey reveals modularity of the yeast cell machinery.
review_notes: Gavin et al. 2006 TAP proteome survey; source of generic protein binding rows among CAF-1 subunits.

title: Chromatin assembly factor 1 interacts with histone H3 methylated at lysine 79 in the processes of epigenetic silencing and DNA repair.
review_notes: Zhou et al. 2006; CAF-1 purified from yeast with H3/H4 bearing new-histone marks; basis of the contributes_to histone binding rows. Abstract-only cache.

title: Yeast two-hybrid analysis of the origin recognition complex of Saccharomyces cerevisiae: interaction between subunits and identification of binding proteins.
review_notes: Matsuda et al. 2007 two-hybrid survey of ORC-binding proteins; source of a Cac1-Orc3 protein binding row.

title: Subtle alterations in PCNA-partner interactions severely impair DNA replication and repair.
review_notes: Fridman et al. 2010; PCNA-partner interactions, includes Cac1-PCNA binding. Full text cached.

title: Defining the budding yeast chromatin-associated interactome.
review_notes: Lambert et al. 2010 chromatin-associated interactome; source of generic protein binding rows.

title: CDC28 phosphorylates Cac1p and regulates the association of chromatin assembly factor I with chromatin.
review_notes: Jeffery et al. 2015; Cdc28 phosphorylation of Cac1p regulates CAF-I chromatin association.

title: A DNA binding winged helix domain in CAF-1 functions with PCNA to stabilize CAF-1 at replication forks.
review_notes: Zhang et al. 2016 NAR; crystal structure of the Cac1 C-terminal winged helix domain and sequence-independent DNA binding needed for silencing and damage resistance. Full text cached.

title: DNA-mediated association of two histone-bound complexes of yeast Chromatin Assembly Factor-1 (CAF-1) drives tetrasome assembly in the wake of DNA replication.
review_notes: Mattiroli et al. 2017 eLife; yeast CAF-1 binds one H3-H4 dimer and two complexes assemble a tetrasome on DNA; Cac1 WHD activation. Full text cached.

title: Insights into the molecular architecture and histone H3-H4 deposition mechanism of yeast Chromatin assembly factor 1.
review_notes: Sauer et al. 2017 eLife; architecture of yeast CAF1, Cac1 KER DNA-binding domain, Cac1 scaffolds Cac2 and Cac3. Full text cached.

title: The Cac2 subunit is essential for productive histone binding and nucleosome assembly in CAF-1.
review_notes: Mattiroli et al. 2017 Sci Rep; HX-MS mapping of yeast CAF-1 subunit interfaces; Cac2 indispensable for productive H3-H4 binding, Cac3 only moderately required. Full text cached.

title: Mechanistic insights into histone deposition and nucleosome assembly by the chromatin assembly factor-1.
review_notes: Sauer et al. 2018 NAR review of CAF-1 mechanism (full text cached). Cited by Complex Portal for several rows; it supports the chaperone function but not part_of nucleosome.

title: The social and structural architecture of the yeast protein interactome.
review_notes: Michaelis et al. 2023 yeast interactome; source of generic protein binding rows among CAF-1 subunits.

title: Ultraviolet radiation sensitivity and reduction of telomeric silencing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells lacking chromatin assembly factor-I.
review_notes: Founding purification of yeast CAF-I (Kaufman, Kobayashi, Stillman 1997); identifies CAC1/RLF2, CAC2 and CAC3/MSI1, UV sensitivity and telomeric silencing phenotypes. Abstract-only cache; claims used are stated in the abstract.

title: RLF2, a subunit of yeast chromatin assembly factor-I, is required for telomeric chromatin function in vivo.
review_notes: Enomoto et al. 1997; identifies RLF2 as CAC1 and shows telomeric chromatin defects. Abstract-only cache.

title: Chromatin assembly factor I contributes to the maintenance, but not the re-establishment, of silencing at the yeast silent mating loci.
review_notes: Enomoto & Berman 1998; CAF-I needed for maintenance but not re-establishment of HM silencing; all three subunit deletions give the shmoo-cluster phenotype. Abstract-only cache.

title: Role of Saccharomyces cerevisiae chromatin assembly factor-I in repair of ultraviolet radiation damage in vivo.
review_notes: Game & Kaufman 1999; genetic role of CAF-I in UV damage repair pathways. Abstract-only cache.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/PAINT reference for the four ROF1 IBA rows; all current inferences trace to PTN001997771 in PTHR28027. The node supports conserved WOPR-family DNA-binding transcription-factor activity, sequence-specific DNA binding, and nuclear activity, but its positive Pol-II regulation term overtransfers the sign of the Candida Wor1 seed to budding-yeast Rof1.

title: A conserved transcriptional regulator governs fungal morphology in widely diverged species.
review_notes: PubMed-verified; cached record abstract-only. Establishes the Wor1/Mit1/Ryp1 WOPR family as sequence-specific transcriptional regulators recognizing the same DNA motif and that Mit1 (ROF1's paralog) is a master regulator of pseudohyphal growth. Cited by Cromie 2017 for YHR177W/ROF1 DNA-binding properties. Directly about the paralog Mit1, so relevance to ROF1 itself is corroborative rather than primary.

title: Structure of a new DNA-binding domain which regulates pathogenesis in a wide variety of fungi.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Reports the 2.6 A co-crystal structure of the WOPR domain bound to DNA (PDB 4M8B is the YHR177W/ROF1 WOPR domain, residues 6-201, per UniProt), the direct experimental basis for the IDA DNA-binding annotation. Cached record is abstract-only (full_text_available:false); the structural assay of the ROF1 fragment is in the full text and is trusted per curator IDA.

title: Transcriptional Profiling of Biofilm Regulators Identified by an Overexpression Screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Names YHR177W as ROF1 (Regulator Of Fluffy 1), identifies it as a repressor of complex/fluffy colony morphology (overexpression reduces, deletion increases colony structure), and shows the overexpression profile represses FLO11/FLO10/TEC1 and filamentation-MAPK genes. Establishes the S. cerevisiae biological-process context and the paralog (MIT1)/ ortholog (WOR1) relationships.

title: A genome-scale yeast library with inducible expression of individual genes.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. Uses an inducible Z3pr-ROF1 allele in phosphate-limited chemostats to identify a rapidly repressed, WOPR-motif-enriched Rof1 regulon, strengthening the evidence that budding-yeast Rof1 can function as a transcriptional repressor.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PANTHER/PAINT reference for the four ROT1 IBA rows. The current PTHR28090 cache retains PTN001999053 for ER membrane and de novo protein folding and PTN001999057 for budding cell apical bud growth; the GO:0051082 IBA traces to PTN001999053 in GOA but that obsolete term no longer appears on the current PAINT node.

title: UPR deficiency leads to poor growth, aneuploidy, and a trade-off between ER and general proteostasis in yeast.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, full text available. This newer yeast work used inducible Rot1 expression as a UPR-independent ER folding-capacity tool; it reinforces Rot1's ER chaperone role but does not alter the GO calls made for the IBA rows.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO Consortium PAINT reference supporting the three RPD3 IBA rows re-reviewed against PTHR10625 in this pass.

title: PKA plays a conserved role in regulating gene expression and metabolic adaptation by phosphorylating Rpd3/HDAC1.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2025 primary study of Tpk2-dependent phosphorylation of Rpd3 and Ash1 in the Rpd3L-SAGA regulatory circuit.

title: Transcriptional memory dampens heat shock responses in yeast: functional role of Mip6 and its interaction with Rpd3.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2025 primary study; relevant to heat-shock transcriptional memory as a peripheral Rpd3 regulatory context.

title: Chromatin context-dependent deacetylation by the asymmetric Rpd3L.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2026 full-text primary study of S. cerevisiae Rpd3L nucleosome engagement and chromatin-context-dependent deacetylation.

title: Rpd3L regulates transcription-replication conflict via H3K4 methylation-dependent and -independent chromatin mechanisms.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2026 primary study extending Rpd3L's chromatin role to replication-fork progression and transcription-replication conflict buffering.

title: Yeast Rpd3L histone deacetylase couples nutrient shifts to genome-wide chromatin reprogramming.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2026 primary study showing Rpd3L-dependent promoter deacetylation during nutrient-shift transcriptional reprogramming.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO Consortium PAINT reference supporting the two PTN000523093 RRB1 IBA rows re-reviewed against PTHR45903.

title: Dedicated chaperones coordinate co-translational regulation of ribosomal protein production with ribosome assembly to preserve proteostasis.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2022 primary study that extends the Rrb1/Rpl3 dedicated chaperone model to co-translational regulation of RPL3 mRNA levels.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO_REF for PAINT/IBA propagation; the three RTT109 IBA rows were checked against the cached PTHR31571 PAINT file and all trace to fungal RTT109 node PANTHER:PTN001586545 with SGD RTT109 among the experimentally grounded descendants.

title: The Rtt109-Vps75 histone acetyltransferase complex acetylates non-nucleosomal histone H3.
review_notes: Abstract-only cached primary paper supporting the Rtt109-Vps75 non-nucleosomal H3 acetyltransferase complex.

title: Acetylation of lysine 56 of histone H3 catalyzed by RTT109 and regulated by ASF1 is required for replisome integrity.
review_notes: Abstract-only cached primary paper supporting Rtt109 as the H3K56 acetyltransferase catalytic subunit and Asf1 as the H3/H4-presenting chaperone.

title: Molecular basis for the autoregulation of the protein acetyl transferase Rtt109.
review_notes: PubMed-verified crystal structure (PDB 3CZ7) of Rtt109 in complex with acetyl-CoA at 2.0-A resolution, supporting histone acetyltransferase activity and acetyl-CoA cofactor binding.

title: A role for the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Rtt109 histone acetyltransferase in R-loop homeostasis and associated genome instability.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified, full text cached. Establishes a distinct RTT109 function (R-loop/DNA-RNA hybrid suppression via H3K14/H3K23ac) that was already asserted in this review's description and core_functions text but previously lacked any supporting citation; this review's own curation notes (RTT109-CURATION-REVIEW.md) had already flagged the gap. No single existing GO term captures "prevention of R-loop formation" (GO:0062176 R-loop processing is R-loop disassembly, the opposite direction), so this is recorded as a proposed_new_terms entry rather than forced onto an ill-fitting existing id.

title: RNA Polymerase II Dependent Crosstalk between H4K16 Deacetylation and H3K56 Acetylation Promotes Transcription of Constitutively Expressed Genes.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified, full text cached. Supports a secondary, transcription-coupled context for Rtt109 recruitment and H3K56 acetylation.

title: IMD2, located near the boundary of heterochromatin regions, is regulated by multiple HAT-related factors.
review_notes: PubMed-verified but abstract-only in the local cache. Peripheral support for Rtt109 in a subtelomeric boundary-expression context; no existing RTT109 action depends on this paper.

title: Repair of replication-dependent double-strand breaks differs between the leading and lagging strands.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified, full text cached. Reinforces RTT109's replication-associated DNA damage response role by placing RCNA-pathway H3K56 acetylation in leading-strand fork-collapse repair.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: GO_REF for PAINT/IBA propagation. The refreshed PTHR15710 export resolves SAN1's E3 ligase row to PANTHER:PTN001864905, the non-core cytoplasm row to PANTHER:PTN004565028, and the newer fungal response-to-misfolded-protein and ERAD rows to PANTHER:PTN008581526; the old catabolic-process IBA is no longer asserted in the current PAINT export.

title: Role of the San1 ubiquitin ligase in the heat stress-induced degradation of nonnative Nup1 in the nuclear pore complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified but abstract-only in the local cache. Extends San1 nuclear PQC to nonnative nuclear-pore-complex substrates.

title: Quiescent cells maintain active degradation-mediated protein quality control requiring proteasome, autophagy, and nucleus-vacuole junctions.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified, full text cached. Shows that San1 remains part of degradation-mediated PQC in quiescent yeast, although Ubr1 dominates the tested tGnd1/stGnd1 model substrates.

title: TAP-MS analysis of FACT interactions and regulation by a ubiquitin ligase, San1.
review_notes: PubMed-verified but abstract-only in the local cache. Updates the older Spt16 substrate literature by examining FACT interactions in the presence or absence of San1-dependent regulation.

title: Aberrant cohesin function in Saccharomyces cerevisiae activates Mcd1 degradation to promote cell lethality.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified, full text cached. Identifies Mcd1/cohesin as a new San1-linked degradation context, but the mechanism is a substrate-specific extension of the core E3 PQC activity.

title: Proteasomal Degradation of Mutant Huntingtin Exon1 Regulates Autophagy.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified, full text cached. Relevant as a synthetic/model substrate that depends on San1, but not a native San1 substrate or a new core process for SAN1.

title: Blocking protein quality control degradation leads to structural stabilization of DHFR indel variants.
review_notes: PubMed-verified but abstract-only in the local cache. Relevant as a model PQC-reporter study using SAN1 deletion, but not a native substrate or new SAN1 mechanism.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: PTHR10615 PAINT node PTN007449682 supports SAS2's inherited H4K16 acetyltransferase activity but over-propagates NuA4 complex membership from KAT5/TIP60 descendants to the S. cerevisiae Sas2/SAS-I paralog.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The SAS3 PAINT assertions resolve to PTHR10615 nodes PTN004172926 and PTN008308138. Both are biologically aligned with Sas3 as the conserved MYST-family catalytic subunit of NuA3a/NuA3b chromatin HAT complexes.

title: The yeast SAS (something about silencing) protein complex contains a MYST-type putative acetyltransferase and functions with chromatin assembly factor ASF1.
review_notes: Correct paper (Osada et al. 2001, PMC312835), but it does not support the two SGD IMP annotations that cite it for SAS3 (GO:0030466, GO:0031509). Full text read at PMC312835 (the local cache is abstract-only): Table 1 lists sas2, sas4, sas5, sir1 and asf1 alleles and the SAS2 M1-M3 acetyl-CoA-motif point mutants, but no sas3 allele, and no SAS3 mutant phenotype is reported. The IMP most likely belongs to SAS2/SAS4/SAS5. To be reported to SGD.

title: Methylation of histone H3 mediates the association of the NuA3 histone acetyltransferase with chromatin.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Martin et al. 2006, Mol Cell Biol 26:3018-28); second UniProt source for SAS3 involvement in HMR silencing. The local cache is abstract-only; the full text was read at PMC1446952. Fig. 4B and text show that deleting NuA3 components, including sas3, rescues the silencing defect of HMR-E silencer mutants, i.e. SAS3 opposes silencing at a weakened HMR. No SAS3 telomeric phenotype is reported. Supports SAS3/NuA3 as an H3K14 acetyltransferase recruited by H3K4/H3K36 methylation in vivo; does not support GO:0030466 or GO:0031509.

title: Molecular insight into interactions between the Taf14, Yng1 and Sas3 subunits of the NuA3 complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified 2024 primary paper; provides direct structural, biochemical, mutational, and in vivo yeast evidence for Sas3/Yng1/Taf14 assembly contacts within NuA3.

title: Mechanistic insights into histone recognition and H3K14 acetylation by the NuA3 histone acetyltransferase complex.
review_notes: PubMed-verified 2025 primary paper with full text in PMC; directly reconstitutes the S. cerevisiae NuA3 complex and explains H3K14 substrate recognition by Sas3/Nto1.

title: Yeast SAS silencing genes and human genes associated with AML and HIV-1 Tat interactions are homologous with acetyltransferases.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Reifsnyder et al. 1996, Nat Genet 14:42-49); the SAS3 naming paper and the UniProt source for SAS3 involvement in HMR silencing. The abstract reports SAS2 and SAS3 as enhancers of sir1 silencing defects. Only the abstract is cached, so the specific sas3 alleles and silencing assays were not read. PubMed and UniProt list a published erratum, PMID:9140406 (Nat Genet 16:109, 1997). It was checked but its content could not be read: the PubMed record has no abstract or erratum text, and its DOI (10.1038/ng0597-106) returns 404. Whether it bears on the SAS3 silencing data is therefore unknown.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees
review_notes: The GO_REF correctly identifies PAINT/IBA annotations. For SBP1, the local PTHR23003 PAINT export places mRNA binding, nucleus, and cytoplasm on PTN002345455 and ribonucleoprotein complex on PTN000543776; these propagations are compatible with the reviewed Sbp1 literature. The current rRNA-processing row from PTN000543777 is marked over-annotated, and the nuclear-mRNA-surveillance row from the same node is marked REMOVE, because that process node is not supported for the functionally divergent Sbp1/SF56 branch.

title: Scd6 targets eIF4G to repress translation: RGG motif proteins as a class of eIF4G-binding proteins.
review_notes: The paper is relevant and correctly cited. Its translation-repression result remains supported, while the narrower direct-eIF4G claim is marked DISPUTED at finding level because PMID:28986506 did not reproduce it with purified proteins.

title: Translation control of autophagy genes modulates cellular response to hydroxyurea-induced genotoxic stress.
review_notes: PubMed-verified 2026 primary yeast SBP1 paper found in the rerun literature search; it reinforces Sbp1's core translation-repression function in the hydroxyurea/replication-stress context.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms.
review_notes: Standard InterPro2GO electronic-annotation reference. Underlies the generic metal ion binding IEA term, which is consistent with the M16 zincin domain.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on curatorial statement evidence.
review_notes: Standard reference for ND (no biological data) root annotations. Honestly reflects that no biological process has been assigned to SDD3.

title: Global analysis of protein localization in budding yeast.
review_notes: Huh et al. 2003 Nature; the source of the experimental (HDA) cytoplasm localization annotation. Abstract-only in cache but this is a canonical, high-coverage yeast localization dataset. The single most solid experimental annotation for SDD3.

title: A cytosolic network suppressing mitochondria-mediated proteostatic stress and cell death.
review_notes: Wang & Chen 2015 Nature (full text cached, PMC4582408); the paper that named SDD3. Establishes only an overexpression/gain-of-function genetic phenotype for SDD3 as one of 40 suppressors and one of eight uncharacterized ones (SDD1-4); SDD3 itself is not individually mechanistically characterized.

title: The cellular economy of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae zinc proteome.
review_notes: Wang et al. 2018 Metallomics; source of the RCA zinc ion binding annotation. The zinc-proteome membership is a computational prediction, not a direct binding measurement for SDD3.

title: Chemogenomic profiling: identifying the functional interactions of small molecules in yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; source of the only reported SET6 phenotype (drug-conditional fitness). UniProt itself notes deletion has no effect absent the compounds, so SET6 is more likely involved in compound availability than in a defined process.

title: The cellular economy of the Saccharomyces cerevisiae zinc proteome.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; this is the computational (RCA) source for the zinc-ion-binding annotation. Corroborated independently by the Cys-rich SMYD zinc-knot/post-SET architecture in the local bioinformatics analysis.

title: Using Yeast to Define the Regulatory Role of Protein Lysine Methylation.
review_notes: Full-text review; supports SMYD-family placement, the histone/non-histone substrate range of the family, and that Set6 localization is unmeasured.

title: Function of the MYND Domain and C-Terminal Region in Regulating the Subcellular Localization and Catalytic Activity of the SMYD Family Lysine Methyltransferase Set5.
review_notes: Abstract-only cache; establishes the Set5/Set6 SMYD paralog pair (family/context for SET6). The paper's experimental focus is Set5, not Set6.

title: The protein methylation network in yeast: A landmark in completeness for a eukaryotic post-translational modification.
review_notes: Full-text PNAS review/analysis; directly adjudicates Set6 as the most-likely genuine yeast protein-lysine methyltransferase with an unknown substrate. Primary literature support for the putative-KMT MF call and the substrate/activity knowledge gaps.

title: SET6 SET-domain integrity, SMYD-family and zinc-architecture analysis (this review)
review_notes: Local reproducible bioinformatics analysis; independently reproduces PMID:37252976 on the SET6 sequence and corroborates the RCA zinc-binding annotation. Motif conservation is necessary but not sufficient for activity; no substrate is inferred.

title: Human SHQ1 variants R335C and A426V lead to severe ribosome biogenesis defects when expressed in yeast.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2023 yeast complementation study; corroborates the conserved SHQ1-Cbf5 carrier-chaperone model but does not alter the yeast GO action calls.

title: ER-localized Shr3 is a selective co-translational folding chaperone necessary for amino acid permease biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2023 primary paper that directly refines the Shr3 amino acid permease folding-chaperone mechanism.

title: Characterization of Shy1, the Schizosaccharomyces pombe homolog of human SURF1.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2024 fission-yeast homolog paper; corroborates SURF1-family conservation but is not direct evidence for S. cerevisiae Shy1 action calls.

title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms.
review_notes: InterPro2GO electronic pipeline; source of the IEA GO:0016787 (hydrolase activity) annotation from IPR004843. Domain-based, not gene-specific evidence.

title: Gene Ontology annotation based on ND (No biological Data available) records.
review_notes: SGD ND placeholders for the molecular_function and cellular_component root terms, recording that no data are available for these aspects. Consistent with SIA1 being a dark gene.

title: Annotation inferences using phylogenetic trees.
review_notes: PAINT/GO_Central phylogenetic (IBA) pipeline; source of the IBA GO:0004721 (phosphoprotein phosphatase activity) annotation, propagated across PANTHER family PTHR32440. Family-level inference; not experimentally verified for SIA1, and several close family members are predicted inactive purple acid phosphatases.

title: Global gene expression during short-term ethanol stress in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Cited by UniProt for the INDUCTION (ethanol up-regulation) statement. Relevant to expression regulation/stress response, not to SIA1 molecular function. Abstract not in cache; provenance anchored to the UniProt curated INDUCTION line rather than to a verbatim publication quote (full_text_unavailable).

title: Genetic interactions of yeast eukaryotic translation initiation factor 5A (eIF5A) reveal connections to poly(A)-binding protein and protein kinase C signaling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Genetics 2002); abstract cached (full text unavailable). This is the origin of the gene name SIA1 = "Suppressor of eIF5A" (confirmed against the SGD locus record, which cites this paper for the name). The abstract names five of the six suppressors and links eIF5A to WSC/PKC1 signalling; SIA1 is the sixth suppressor, described in the full text (not in the cached abstract) - a case where the abstract foregrounds other genes. Cited here for the eIF5A-suppressor / PKC1-signalling context, not for a specific SIA1 molecular function.

title: Phosphoregulation of the yeast Pma1 H+-ATPase autoinhibitory domain involves the Ptk1/2 kinases and the Glc7 PP1 phosphatase and is under TORC1 control.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2024 primary paper that clarifies the Pma1 phosphoregulatory circuit downstream of glucose and TORC1. Useful for the SIA1 knowledge gap, but not direct evidence for any SIA1 molecular function.

title: Yeast gene YOR137c is involved in the activation of the yeast plasma membrane H+-ATPase by glucose.
review_notes: PubMed-verified primary paper (FEBS Lett 1997); abstract cached (full text unavailable). This is the sole experimental functional characterization of SIA1 and is the basis of the curated SGD/UniProt FUNCTION line and the IMP GO:1902600 annotation. Establishes a requirement (deletion phenotype), not a molecular mechanism.

title: Falcon (Edison) deep-research report for SIA1 (YOR137C).
review_notes: Genuine Falcon/Edison deep-research report (32 citations, ~26 min run). Cross-checked against the cached primary papers: it corroborates (does not extend beyond) the evidence used here - metallophosphoesterase domain, genetic-only implication in Pma1 activation, and unresolved mechanism. Some of its downstream citations (e.g. Mira 2009 RIM101, Guarini 2024 phosphoregulation) were not independently fetched; used for context only, not as primary support for any GO action.

title: UniProt entry Q12212 (SIA1_YEAST) - domain and feature annotations.
review_notes: Machine-fetched UniProt record used for inline domain analysis. Establishes the signal peptide and the metallophosphatase fold that underlie the hydrolase/phosphatase family-level annotations.

title: Nuclear-specific degradation of Far1 is controlled by the localization of the F-box protein Cdc4.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. The paper is about Far1 and Cdc4, but it directly shows a functional Sic1-GFP fusion in the nucleus and that cytoplasm-forced Cdc4 fails to degrade Sic1, which is exactly what the nucleus IDA annotation cites.

title: Characterization of the Net1 cell cycle-dependent regulator of the Cdc14 phosphatase from budding yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Sic1 appears as one of five in vitro Cdc14 substrates used to characterise Net1 inhibition; it supports the Cdc14-Sic1 enzyme-substrate relationship but no Sic1 molecular function.

title: Cdc6 cooperates with Sic1 and Hct1 to inactivate mitotic cyclin-dependent kinases.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Establishes Cdc6 as a Sic1-like contributor to late-mitotic CDK inactivation and shows that loss of the Cdc6 CDK-interacting domain causes a mitotic-exit delay that is exacerbated by loss of Sic1 or of cyclin degradation.

title: Relationship between the function and the location of G1 cyclins in S. cerevisiae.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache, but the abstract states the Sic1 result directly (present in both nucleus and cytoplasm), which is all the two localisation annotations require.

title: Hog1 mediates cell-cycle arrest in G1 phase by the dual targeting of Sic1.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Establishes Sic1 as the direct Hog1 target (Thr173 phosphorylation, stabilisation) in osmostress G1 arrest; the Cdc4 co-interaction row from this paper could not be checked against the full text and is resolved on the strength of independent Cdc4-binding evidence.

title: Subcellular localization of the cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor Sic1 is modulated by the carbon source in budding yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache. Identifies the bipartite NLS, carbon-source modulation of Sic1 amount and localisation, and cytoplasmic accumulation of Clb5 upon SIC1 shut-off (proposed Cip/Kip-like escort role).

title: A refined two-hybrid system reveals that SCF(Cdc4)-dependent degradation of Swi5 contributes to the regulatory mechanism of S-phase entry.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Its subject is Swi5 degradation, but it validates the refined two-hybrid assay on the phosphorylation-dependent Sic1-Cdc4 interaction (abolished by sic1-0p) and shows that persistent SIC1 transcription antagonises Sic1 turnover and delays S phase.

title: Dynamic equilibrium engagement of a polyvalent ligand with a single-site receptor.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Definitive biophysical characterisation of the phospho-Sic1(1-90)-Skp1-Cdc4 interaction (Kd about 0.6 uM, dynamic polyvalent binding of suboptimal CPDs, no binding without phosphorylation). Source of the SCF ubiquitin ligase complex binding annotations.

title: Positive or negative roles of different cyclin-dependent kinase Pho85-cyclin complexes orchestrate induction of autophagy in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Thorough genetic analysis showing Sic1 as a negative regulator of autophagy acting upstream of Rim15 and destabilised by Clg1/Pcl1/Pho80-Pho85; the Sic1-Rim15 mechanism is left open (only weak co-IP).

title: A global protein kinase and phosphatase interaction network in yeast.
review_notes: Abstract-only in the cache; a proteome-scale AP-MS survey. Source of a Cdc14-Sic1 interaction that is consistent with, but adds nothing beyond, the known enzyme-substrate relationship.

title: An inhibitor of p34CDC28 protein kinase activity from Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

title: Falcon deep research report for SIC1
review_notes: LLM-generated synthesis (Edison/Falcon). Left UNVERIFIED because its citations are internal document keys, several of them an unpublished thesis, and could not be resolved against the publication cache.

title: Sir2 is required for the quiescence-specific condensed three-dimensional chromatin structure of rDNA.

title: Nej1p, a cell type-specific regulator of nonhomologous end joining in yeast.

title: Distinguishing between recruitment and spread of silent chromatin structures in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

title: Role of yeast SIR genes and mating type in directing DNA double-strand breaks to homologous and non-homologous repair paths.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Lee SE, Pâques F, Sylvan J, Haber JE; Curr Biol 1999). Establishes that the sir mutant NHEJ defect reported by Boulton & Jackson is largely attributable to derepression of the silent mating-type loci rather than a direct Sir role at the break, and quantifies the residual direct contribution. Abstract-only in cache.

title: Nej1p, a cell type-specific regulator of nonhomologous end joining in yeast.

Same reference used for the identical adjudication merged on SIR3. Abstract-only in cache.

title: The mitochondrial proteins Ssq1 and Jac1 are required for the assembly of iron sulfur clusters in mitochondria.

title: Ssq1, a mitochondrial Hsp70 involved in iron-sulfur (Fe/S) center biogenesis. Similarities to and differences from its bacterial counterpart.
review_notes: Full author PDF read, including Methods and Figures1-8. Ssq1 purified from yeast, at least 85% purity; single-turnover ATPase, Isu binding by SPR/gradient, Mge1 nucleotide release. Figure8 tests Mdj1 stimulation, not global folding loss. Mature Yfh1/Nfu1 fail ATPase stimulation; precursor binding is not thereby excluded.

title: An interaction between frataxin and Isu1/Nfs1 that is crucial for Fe/S cluster synthesis on Isu1.
review_notes: Abstract and indexed full Results sections on Isu1-GST purification/competition verified. Isu1-GST copurifies Ssq1 and competes with native Isu1. Frataxin-focused title does not make the Ssq1 interaction miscited. Complete PDF remained unavailable.

title: The Hsp70 chaperone Ssq1p is dispensable for iron-sulfur cluster formation on the scaffold protein Isu1p.
review_notes: Full author PDF Methods, Results and Discussion read. Figure 4C measures denatured bovine rhodanese aggregation by 500 nm light scattering and establishes antiaggregation capacity, not refolding/activity recovery. Ssq1 also preserves purified Nfs1 activity without ATP/Jac1, but native lysate desulfurase activity is unchanged by Ssq1 depletion. Fe-S synthesis on Isu and subsequent transfer are separable.

title: Global landscape of protein complexes in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Abstract verifies TAP-MS complex mapping in budding yeast. The target-pair supplementary record was not independently recovered for this paper. Later PMID:19536198 contains exact Ssq1/Nop1 evidence and shares the data lineage; do not count these citations as proven independent binary binding assays.

title: Toward the complete yeast mitochondrial proteome: multidimensional separation techniques for mitochondrial proteomics.

title: An atlas of chaperone-protein interactions in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: implications to protein folding pathways in the cell.
review_notes: Full methods and exact supplement read. Table S1 row 39 maps Ssq1 to YLR369W; Table S2 AI7=Ssq1 and AI44=Nop1,b, with row 6 legend b:bait/p:prey. Whole-cell TAP-MS and spoke inference establish association, not direct binary contact, native nuclear localization or Nop1 refolding. Ssq1 has 97 nonchaperone and 5 chaperone interactors in this table.

title: Co-evolution-driven switch of J-protein specificity towards an Hsp70 partner.
review_notes: Full text read. Jac1/Hsp70 coevolution is supported by cross-species complementation and ATPase stimulation. Introductory folding-loss inference rests on failure of Mdj1/Pam18 stimulation; the paper does not demonstrate universal loss of refolding capacity on all Ssq1 clients.

title: The mitochondrial Hsp70 chaperone Ssq1 facilitates Fe/S cluster transfer from Isu1 to Grx5 by complex formation.
review_notes: Full text read. Target Grx5 binding by co-IP/MST at a site distinct from LPPVK-client binding; Figure 3D also detects recombinant Cia1 binding displaced by LPPVK. The transfer sequence is a working mechanistic model supported by native depletion and complex evidence. Its folding interpretation of Cia1 binding is not a refolding assay; its bacterial orthologue wording should be read as functional analogy, since Ssq1 derives from mitochondrial-Hsp70 duplication.

title: Quantitative variations of the mitochondrial proteome and phosphoproteome during fermentative and respiratory growth in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
review_notes: Abstract verifies isolated yeast mitochondria across fermentative/respiratory media. Specific Ssq1 phosphopeptides/protein entry were not rechecked; the annotation is retained based also on independent native localization.

title: Iron-Sulfur Cluster Biogenesis Chaperones: Evidence for Emergence of Mutational Robustness of a Highly Specific Protein-Protein Interaction.

title: The social and structural architecture of the yeast protein interactome.

review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2025 full-text paper. YDJ1 plus SSA1 overexpression improved heterologous aspulvinone E production, which is consistent with Ydj1's general Hsp70 co-chaperone activity but is a biotechnological client-folding use rather than evidence for an additional endogenous GO annotation.

title: BAP31 interacts with Sec61 translocons and promotes retrotranslocation of CFTRDeltaF508 via the derlin-1 complex.
review_notes: Wang et al. 2008 (Cell) is the human BCAP31 source-side evidence behind the broad BAP29/BAP31-family ERAD IBDs; it supports the PAINT placement at the ancestral node, but does not constitute direct yeast YET2 evidence.

title: Yet1p and Yet3p, the yeast homologs of BAP29 and BAP31, interact with the endoplasmic reticulum translocation apparatus and are required for inositol prototrophy.
review_notes: Wilson & Barlowe 2010 (J Biol Chem). The key mechanistic paper on the yeast BAP31 family, but it characterizes the Yet1p-Yet3p complex, not Yet2p. The abstract establishes that the Yet complex associates with the Sec translocation apparatus, that this association increases under ER stress, and that yet1/yet3 deletions cause inositol-starvation growth defects; the PMC full text further shows that Yet2p has only minor co-association with Yet1p and the Sec complex. This reference directly informs the YET2-vs-paralog attribution and the knowledge gaps. (The original naming paper, Toikkanen et al. 2006, J. Biol. Sci. Faisalabad, DOI 10.3923/jbs.2006.446.456, which assigned YMR040W=YET2 and reported a yet2 yet3 double-deletion growth phenotype, is not PubMed-indexed and its text is not retrievable, so it is described in prose but not cited as a validated reference.)

title: One library to make them all: Streamlining the creation of yeast libraries via a SWAp-Tag strategy.
review_notes: High-throughput N-terminal SWAp-Tag localization library (Yofe et al., Nat Methods 2016). Source of the HDA endoplasmic reticulum localization annotation (ECO:0007005). Supports ER localization of Yet2p as a systematic observation; not a functional characterization of the gene.

title: The molecular mechanism of on-demand sterol biosynthesis at organelle contact sites.
review_notes: PubMed/PMC-verified 2024 bioRxiv preprint. The study primarily characterizes Yet3p as an ER contact-site scaffold for post-squalene ergosterol biosynthesis enzymes, but it directly compares the three budding-yeast BAP31 paralogs and reports that Yet2p is low-abundance and non-constitutive relative to Yet1p/Yet3p.

title: Falcon (Edison) deep-research report for YET2 (Q04210), synthesizing BAP31-family and Yet-paralog literature.
review_notes: Falcon/Edison deep-research synthesis. Its most useful YET2-specific content derives from Zung et al. 2024 (bioRxiv 2024.05.09.593285, "The molecular mechanism of on-demand sterol biosynthesis at organelle contact sites"), which reports that Yet2 is low-abundance and non-constitutively expressed relative to Yet1/Yet3 and is therefore likely NOT simply redundant with the Yet1-Yet3 branch — corroborating the paralog-distinction and functional-role knowledge gaps here. The report otherwise characterizes the well-studied Yet3 (ergosterol/ERGosome scaffold) and Yet1-Yet3 (Opi1/inositol) functions, which are paralog context, not YET2 evidence. Quotes used as supporting_text were grep-verified against the cached report file.

title: UniProtKB entry Q04210 (YET2_YEAST) - domain, topology, and family annotation.
review_notes: UniProt record used for inline domain/topology analysis: BCAP29/BCAP31 family membership, three TM helices, lumenal N-terminus, cytoplasmic C-terminal tail, and C-terminal di-lysine ER-retrieval motif. UniProt cites Toikkanen et al. 2006 as its Ref. 3 FUNCTION source.

title: Parallel analysis of tagged deletion mutants efficiently identifies genes involved in endoplasmic reticulum biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. High-throughput deletion screen implicating yfh7Δ (among many) in ER/karmellae biogenesis; provides a phenotypic association only, not a molecular function. Cited here for the ER-biogenesis knowledge-gap context.

title: Crystal structure and functional analysis identify the P-loop containing protein YFH7 of Saccharomyces cerevisiae as an ATP-dependent kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified crystal-structure + enzymology paper (Gueguen-Chaignon et al., Proteins 2008; PDB 2GA8/2GAA). Establishes the P-loop kinase fold and the ATP-dependent-kinase activity but explicitly leaves the substrate undetermined ("new substrate specificity"). This is the primary source for the MF/BP annotations.

title: Computationally driven, quantitative experiments discover genes required for mitochondrial biogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (full text cached). Basis for UniProt's DISRUPTION PHENOTYPE "Increases frequency of mitochondrial genome loss" and the AIM ("altered inheritance of mitochondria") alias. Supports a mitochondrial-maintenance phenotype but does not determine YFH7's substrate or direct molecular role.

title: YFH7 bioinformatics analysis (P-loop / Walker-A motif scan, PRK/URK/PANK family signature, domain architecture, and taxonomic conservation).
review_notes: Reproducible in-repo analysis (scripts + control tests in YFH7-bioinformatics/). NOTE: file: references are not verbatim-quote-checked by the reference validator; the quoted supporting_text was confirmed by hand to be a verbatim substring of RESULTS.md. Corroborates the intact P-loop kinase scaffold and lineage restriction.

title: Novel role for an HPt domain in stabilizing the phosphorylated state of a response regulator domain.
review_notes: Full text: Ypd1 extends phospho-Ssk1-R2 half-life ~200-fold.

title: The yeast YPD1/SLN1 complex: insights into molecular recognition in two-component signaling systems.
review_notes: Abstract only cached: Ypd1-Sln1 receiver domain co-crystal structure.

title: Saccharomyces cerevisiae histidine phosphotransferase Ypd1p shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm for SLN1-dependent phosphorylation of Ssk1p and Skn7p.
review_notes: Full text: GFP localization of Ypd1 in cytoplasm and nucleus, NLS/NES/CaaX and heterokaryon shuttling experiments.

title: Kinetic analysis of YPD1-dependent phosphotransfer reactions in the yeast osmoregulatory phosphorelay system.
review_notes: Abstract: kinetics of Sln1-R1 -> Ypd1 -> Ssk1-R2/Skn7-R3 phosphotransfer and His64-flanking mutants.

title: An in vivo map of the yeast protein interactome.
review_notes: Abstract only: genome-wide PCA interactome; source of the Ypd1-Ssk1 protein binding row.

title: High-quality binary protein interaction map of the yeast interactome network.
review_notes: Abstract only: HT Y2H binary interactome; source of the Ypd1-Ssk1 protein binding row.

title: Yeast HOG1 MAP kinase cascade is regulated by a multistep phosphorelay mechanism in the SLN1-YPD1-SSK1 "two-component" osmosensor.
review_notes: Abstract: defines the Sln1-His576 -> Asp1144 -> Ypd1-His64 -> Ssk1-Asp554 phosphorelay; founding paper for YPD1.

title: The yeast histidine protein kinase, Sln1p, mediates phosphotransfer to two response regulators, Ssk1p and Skn7p.
review_notes: Abstract: establishes Skn7 as the second response regulator downstream of Sln1-Ypd1.
